The Provider and Model Registries identify eligible resources.

The project Quality Contract defines acceptable character and story quality.

The Production Envelope defines cost and retry boundaries.

6.240 Nova and Pling Character Consistency Capability

A specialised Capability may be defined as:

media.character_consistency.evaluate

Inputs may include:

- canonical character references,

- generated image or video,

- approved style profile.

Outputs may include:

- consistency score,

- detected deviations,

- frame references,

- pass or fail,

- human-review recommendation.

Quality Dimensions may include:

- face,

- body proportions,

- colours,

- clothing,

- accessories,

- style,

- and scene continuity.

This Capability remains provider-independent.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 6.241 Nova and Pling Video Capability Requirements
6.242 Applied Example — The Prompt News Production
text:
6.241 Nova and Pling Video Capability Requirements

The video.image_to_video request may require Features such as:

- characterReferenceSupport,

- multipleCharacterSupport,

- aspectRatio16x9,

- commercialUse,

- minimumDuration,

- childSafeOutput,

- and asynchronousJobTracking.

A provider lacking multiple-character support may remain eligible for scenes containing only Nova.

It may be ineligible for scenes containing Nova and Pling together.

6.242 Applied Example — The Prompt News Production

A The Prompt episode may require:

- research.search_current

- research.source_assess

- research.verify_sources

- text.news_script_generate

- evaluation.factual_grounding

- speech.synthesise

- video.avatar_generate

- media.broll_generate

- video.caption

- video.compose

- publication.prepare

The Capability Registry ensures that factual verification remains separate from video presentation.

A capable avatar provider does not become the research authority.

6.243 The Prompt Source Verification Capability

research.verify_sources may define:

Inputs

- claims,

- source references,

- time range,

- topic.

Outputs

- supported claims,

- unsupported claims,

- source quality,

- date relevance,

- uncertainty,

- citations.

Quality Dimensions

- accuracy,

- source authority,

- recency,

- completeness,

- quotation integrity.

The capability must not be implemented as fluent summarisation alone.

6.244 Applied Example — GainPilot Reel

A GainPilot reel may require:

- text.exercise_script_generate

- image.generate

- speech.synthesise

- media.motion_graphics_create

- video.caption

- evaluation.brand_alignment

- publication.prepare

The routing profile may prefer:

- local text generation,

- low-cost image generation,

- and local video composition.

The Capability contracts remain the same even when cheaper resources are used.

6.245 Applied Example — Omnira Code Work

An Omnira code task may require:

- repository.analyse_readonly

- code.generate

- code.review

- code.test_generate

- evaluation.code_test

- evaluation.architecture_conformance

Separate capabilities would be required for:

- repository.write,

- repository.commit,

- repository.push,

- pull_request.create,

- pull_request.merge,

- deployment.execute.

The Capability Registry prevents analysis permission from silently becoming deployment authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 6.249 Anti-Pattern — One Capability Per Provider Endpoint
6.251 Anti-Pattern — Claimed Support Equals Verified Support
6.252 Anti-Pattern — Capability Availability as Global Boolean
text:
6.246 Applied Example — Local Confidential Analysis

A Confidential request may use:

- document.extract_text

- retrieval.embed

- retrieval.search_project

- reasoning.general

- text.summarise

All resource mappings must support:

- Local Only placement,

- approved local Runtime Node,

- and restricted evidence.

The same Capabilities may also be available externally for Public data.

Availability is request-specific.

6.247 Anti-Pattern — Provider as Capability Name

The Registry must not define Capabilities such as:

- use_openart,

- call_claude,

- use_gemini,

- run_eleventlabs.

These are provider or implementation instructions.

Canonical Capabilities should express the operation.

6.248 Anti-Pattern — One Generic AI Capability

A single Capability named:

ai.execute

is insufficient.

It prevents meaningful:

- routing,

- quality,

- policy,

- cost,

- and authority.

The Registry shall preserve semantic distinctions.

6.249 Anti-Pattern — One Capability Per Provider Endpoint

The Registry must not mirror every provider endpoint as a canonical Capability.

Provider endpoints belong in Adapter Mappings.

Canonical capability identity should remain stable when APIs change.

6.250 Anti-Pattern — Capability Without Contract

A name and description alone are not enough.

Executable Capabilities require:

- input,

- output,

- risk,

- quality,

- authority,

- and evidence semantics.

6.251 Anti-Pattern — Claimed Support Equals Verified Support

Provider marketing or documentation is not sufficient proof of conformance.

Claims may create experimental mappings.

Production routing requires appropriate verification.

6.252 Anti-Pattern — Capability Availability as Global Boolean

Availability depends on:

- tenant,

- project,

- environment,

- provider account,

- policy,

- budget,

- data,

- and health.

The Registry must not expose one misleading universal available flag.

6.253 Anti-Pattern — Quality-Free Capability Mapping

A model that technically outputs the correct format may still be unsuitable.

Capability support shall include relevant quality evidence.

6.254 Anti-Pattern — Hidden Feature Loss

Adapters must not ignore requested Features silently.

If character references are unsupported, the mapping must report incompatibility or degradation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 6.258 Anti-Pattern — Manual Workflow Presented as Automated Capability
6.259 Anti-Pattern — Capability Registry as Static Documentation
text:
6.255 Anti-Pattern — Capability Version Rewrite

A Capability Version used by historical Executions must not be rewritten to a new meaning.

Create a new Version.

Preserve historical interpretation.

6.256 Anti-Pattern — Project-Specific Core Duplication

Familje-Stunden, The Prompt and GainPilot should not create separate incompatible definitions of:

- image.generate,

- speech.synthesise,

- or video.compose.

Projects may add:

- project Quality Contracts,

- project policies,

- and specialised extensions.

Core Capability meaning should remain shared.

6.257 Anti-Pattern — Capabilities Granting Authority

The existence or discovery of a Capability must not grant permission to use it.

Capability definition and Authority remain separate.

6.258 Anti-Pattern — Manual Workflow Presented as Automated Capability

A human-operated provider interface shall be registered as:

- human-assisted,

- manual external,

- or partially automated.

It must not appear as a fully controlled API integration.

6.259 Anti-Pattern — Capability Registry as Static Documentation

The Registry must support operational use.

It shall not exist only as a document that runtime systems ignore.

The authoritative Registry must be queryable by:

- request validation,

- planning,

- routing,

- policy,

- and evidence systems.

6.260 Anti-Pattern — Runtime Configuration Without Architecture

A collection of model names and endpoints is not a Capability Registry.

The Registry defines semantic contracts.

Runtime configuration maps resources to them.

6.261 Capability Registry Performance

Registry queries should be efficient enough for planning and routing.

The architecture may use:

- cached read models,

- indexed database tables,

- in-memory snapshots,

- or generated configuration.

Performance optimisation must preserve:

- version,

- freshness,

- and authority.

6.262 Registry Cache

A Registry Cache may accelerate reads.

It shall include:

- source version,

- generated time,

- expiry,

- and invalidation.

Stale cache must not claim current capability availability without freshness disclosure.

6.263 Registry Consistency

Control-plane changes may propagate asynchronously.

The Fabric shall define consistency expectations.

Critical changes such as:

- Capability retirement,

- rights restriction,

- or security disablement

should propagate quickly and fail safely.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
6.264 Registry Snapshot

A Registry Snapshot is an immutable view of Capability definitions and mappings at a point in time.

Execution evidence may reference the Snapshot used for planning.

Snapshots support:

- audit,

- reproduction,

- and rollback.

6.265 Registry Rollback

A faulty Registry update may require rollback.

Rollback shall preserve:

- invalid version,

- reason,

- affected executions,

- and restored version.

Historical evidence must not be deleted.

6.266 Registry Integrity

Registry data should support integrity verification.

Controls may include:

- checksums,

- signed releases,

- schema validation,

- approval records,

- and protected storage.

Risk increases if agents can rewrite Capability definitions directly.

6.267 Registry Backup

Capability definitions and history shall be backed up.

Backup must preserve:

- versions,

- lifecycle,

- mappings,

- approvals,

- and provenance.

A Registry loss would make historical Executions difficult to interpret.

6.268 Registry Export

The Registry may be exported for:

- documentation,

- testing,

- Atlas Knowledge,

- developer SDK generation,

- or disaster recovery.

Exports shall declare:

- source version,

- generated time,

- scope,

- and completeness.

6.269 Registry Import

Imported Capability definitions shall be validated.

External packages must not activate Capabilities automatically.

Import stages may include:

- parsed,

- quarantined,

- reviewed,

- approved,

- and activated.

6.270 Registry Federation

Future Omnira deployments may federate Capability Registries across:

- local node,

- tenant,

- Omnira-managed cloud,

- and customer environments.

Federation shall preserve:

- canonical identifiers,

- local restrictions,

- version compatibility,

- and authority.

Federation must not permit one tenant to redefine global Capability meaning.

6.271 Local Registry Extension

A user-controlled node may declare local Resource support.

It shall map to approved Capabilities.

Local extension may remain:

- private,

- tenant-specific,

- and unavailable to other users.

Local declarations require conformance evidence appropriate to their scope.

6.272 Tenant Capability Extension

A Tenant may define specialised Capabilities when core contracts are insufficient.

Tenant extensions should use a namespaced identifier.

They shall not conflict with global Capabilities.

Promotion to the core Registry requires architecture review.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
6.273 Project Capability Extension

A Project may define highly specialised operations.

Examples include:

project.familje_stunden.story_activity_align

project.gainpilot.exercise_form_visualise

Project extensions may later become reusable core Capabilities if they prove broadly valuable.

6.274 Provider Capability Extension

Provider-specific Features may be represented through namespaced extensions.

Examples include:

provider.openart.director_project_create

provider.elevenlabs.voice_settings_special

These should be used only when the provider-specific operation has no stable canonical equivalent.

Core workflows should prefer canonical Capabilities.

6.275 Future Capability Marketplace

Omnira may later support installable Capability packages.

A package may include:

- Capability definitions,

- Adapter mappings,

- tests,

- policies,

- documentation,

- and UI metadata.

Marketplace installation shall not automatically grant:

- credentials,

- authority,

- production admission,

- or cross-project access.

6.276 Capability Package Trust

Capability packages may be:

- Omnira official,

- provider official,

- verified partner,

- community,

- local private,

- or untrusted.

Trust level shall affect:

- review,

- sandboxing,

- permissions,

- and production admission.

6.277 Capability Package Dependency

Packages may depend on:

- core Capability Version,

- Adapter framework,

- provider,

- Runtime Node,

- or Tool.

Dependencies shall be explicit and versioned.

6.278 Capability Package Removal

Removing a package must not destroy historical interpretation.

Capability definitions used by historical Executions may remain archived even when the package is no longer active.

6.279 Capability Registry Success Criteria

The Capability Registry succeeds when:

- callers request outcomes without provider coupling,

- new providers can map to existing Capabilities,

- resource support can be compared honestly,

- policies can target stable operations,

- quality remains task-specific,

- availability is represented truthfully,

- historical Executions remain interpretable,

- and project workflows survive provider change.

6.280 Capability Registry Failure Conditions

The Registry is non-conformant when:

- provider names become canonical Capability identifiers,

- Capabilities lack input or output contracts,

- availability is treated as one global boolean,

- claimed support is treated as verified support,

- versions are rewritten,

- project scope is absent,

- capability discovery grants authority,

- manual execution is presented as autonomous,

- or runtime systems bypass Registry validation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
6.281 Canonical Capability Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Capability contract:

1. Every Capability SHALL have stable provider-independent identity.

2. Capability identifiers SHALL use governed namespaces.

3. Canonical identifiers SHALL remain language-independent.

4. Every Executable Capability SHALL have a versioned Input Contract.

5. Every Executable Capability SHALL have a versioned Output Contract.

6. Capabilities SHALL declare modality.

7. Capabilities SHALL declare execution pattern.

8. Capabilities SHALL declare risk and consequence.

9. Capabilities SHALL declare relevant Quality Dimensions.

10. Capabilities SHALL declare minimum evidence requirements.

11. Capabilities SHALL declare applicable authority requirements.

12. Capabilities SHALL declare data-placement considerations.

13. Capabilities SHALL declare rights and consent requirements where applicable.

14. Capabilities SHALL remain distinct from Providers, Models, Agents, Tools and Workflows.

15. Provider-specific behaviour SHALL remain in Adapters or namespaced extensions.

16. Capability Versions used by historical Executions SHALL remain interpretable.

17. Material semantic changes SHALL create new Capability Versions.

18. Claimed support SHALL remain distinct from verified support.

19. Partial support SHALL remain distinct from full support.

20. Availability SHALL remain distinct from lifecycle.

21. Capability discovery SHALL NOT grant execution authority.

22. Capability support SHALL be scoped and version-specific.

23. Resource compatibility SHALL include policy, quality, rights, placement and cost.

24. Unsupported constraints SHALL NOT be silently ignored.

25. Human-assisted execution SHALL be represented honestly.

26. Side-effect Capabilities SHALL declare authority and verification requirements.

27. Publication SHALL remain separate from generation.

28. Local resources SHALL be first-class Capability providers.

29. Capability changes SHALL be attributable and versioned.

30. Capability deprecation SHALL include migration guidance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
6.282 Canonical Registry Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Capability Registry contract:

1. The Capability Registry SHALL be the authoritative catalogue of canonical Capability definitions.

2. The Registry SHALL support versioned Capability entries.

3. The Registry SHALL preserve lifecycle history.

4. The Registry SHALL support Resource Support Mappings.

5. The Registry SHALL preserve support evidence.

6. The Registry SHALL distinguish architectural definition from operational availability.

7. The Registry SHALL expose governed discovery.

8. The Registry SHALL support request validation.

9. The Registry SHALL support compatibility evaluation.

10. The Registry SHALL remain provider-independent.

11. The Registry SHALL support project, tenant and provider extensions through namespaces.

12. Extensions SHALL NOT redefine core Capability semantics.

13. Administrative mutation SHALL require explicit authority.

14. Registry changes SHALL preserve provenance.

15. Registry caches and projections SHALL declare freshness.

16. Historical Capability Versions SHALL remain resolvable after retirement.

17. The Registry SHALL support explicit missing-capability and capability-gap records.

18. The Registry SHALL support Stage-based production admission.

19. The Registry SHALL NOT treat documentation as proof of runtime availability.

20. The Registry SHALL remain usable by both human and machine consumers.

6.283 Capability Registry Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No Provider becomes the canonical definition of a Capability.

- No Model becomes the identity of a Capability.

- No Agent gains identity from a Capability.

- No Capability grants authority merely by existing.

- No Capability is considered available without an eligible supporting resource.

- No Resource is considered compatible by technical format alone.

- No unsupported Feature is silently ignored.

- No provider claim becomes verified support without evidence.

- No Capability Version changes historical meaning.

- No retired Capability disappears from historical evidence.

- No project extension silently replaces a core Capability.

- No manual process is labelled fully automated.

- No availability projection hides its freshness.

- No quality judgment becomes universal across unrelated Capabilities.

- No fallback weakens the original Capability Contract.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
6.284 Closing Statement

The Capability Registry is the semantic foundation through which Omnira understands intelligence work.

It defines what can be requested without defining who must provide it.

It separates human and project intent from provider implementation.

It allows Atlas, Managers, agents and workflows to communicate through one stable language.

It allows Providers, Models, Tools and local resources to remain replaceable.

It allows policy to target meaningful operations.

It allows quality to remain task-specific.

It allows cost, rights, privacy and authority to be evaluated before execution.

It allows capability gaps to be identified honestly.

It allows manual pilots to coexist with governed production without confusing their maturity.

For Familje-Stunden, it means that Nova and Pling production is defined through capabilities such as story segmentation, character-aware animation, Swedish narration and child-facing review rather than through one permanent vendor.

For The Prompt, it means that current research, source verification, scripting and reporter production remain separate governed capabilities.

For GainPilot, it means that lower-cost image, narration and short-form media resources can be used without creating a separate intelligence architecture.

For Omnira, it means that code, research, memory, media, voice and future modalities can all pass through one shared semantic contract.

The Capability Registry shall answer:

What kind of intelligence work does Omnira understand?

The Provider Registry shall answer:

Who may supply it?

The Model and Resource Registries shall answer:

Which resources can perform it?

Policy shall answer:

Which resources may be used here?

Routing shall answer:

Which eligible resource should be selected now?

Evidence shall answer:

What actually happened?

The Capability Registry gives stable meaning to every one of those decisions.

Without it, the Fabric would be a collection of connections.

With it, the Fabric becomes an intelligence architecture.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical architecture, governance model, lifecycle, contracts and operational responsibilities of the Omnira Intelligence Fabric Model Registry.

It establishes:

- what a Model represents within Omnira,

- how Models differ from Providers, Deployments, Agents and Capabilities,

- how Model Families and Model Versions are identified,

- how provider aliases and silent provider updates are handled,

- how capabilities, context limits, modalities and execution properties are declared,

- how quality, cost, safety, privacy and rights evidence are attached,

- how local and externally hosted models are represented consistently,

- how model deployments are separated from abstract model identity,

- how model support is verified,

- how Models are activated, restricted, deprecated and retired,

- how historical Executions remain interpretable,

- and how Stage 1 shall implement a bounded but extensible registry.

The Model Registry is a foundational Intelligence Fabric control-plane component.

It is the authoritative catalogue of model identities, versions and deployment relationships known to Omnira.

It is not, by itself, proof that a Model can currently be used.

A Model may be:

- known,

- proposed,

- experimental,

- approved,

- active,

- restricted,

- degraded,

- deprecated,

- retired,

- or historically referenced.

Operational eligibility also depends on:

- Provider Account,

- Connection,

- Model Deployment,

- Adapter,

- Capability support,

- policy,

- data classification,

- authority,

- budget,

- health,

- region,

- and current availability.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

Runtime implementation and conformance must be verified separately.

7.2 Purpose of the Model Registry

The Intelligence Fabric requires a stable internal understanding of the Models that may execute intelligence work.

Providers frequently expose Models through:

- changing names,

- aliases,

- preview labels,

- dated identifiers,

- deployment identifiers,

- product tiers,

- or generic endpoints that silently change their underlying implementation.

Without a canonical Model Registry, Omnira would be unable to determine reliably:

- which model performed an Execution,

- which capabilities the model actually supports,

- which version was tested,

- which limits applied,

- whether pricing changed,

- whether quality evidence remains valid,

- whether a workflow depends on a deprecated resource,

- whether a local deployment is equivalent to an external one,

- or whether a provider silently changed model behaviour.

The Model Registry provides a canonical layer between provider naming and Omnira execution.

It allows Models to be:

- understood,

- compared,

- governed,

- selected,

- replaced,

- benchmarked,

- deprecated,

- and historically interpreted.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.3 Model as an Execution Resource

A Model is an intelligence execution resource.

It may perform operations such as:

- text generation,

- reasoning,

- code generation,

- image generation,

- image editing,

- speech synthesis,

- speech recognition,

- video generation,

- embedding,

- reranking,

- multimodal analysis,

- or evaluation.

The Model does not own:

- user intent,

- Agent identity,

- project context,

- long-term memory,

- authority,

- provider selection,

- budget,

- or strategic direction.

The Model receives a bounded execution context through the Fabric.

It returns output or execution evidence.

Omnira remains responsible for governance.

7.4 Model Is Not Provider

A Provider is the organisation or platform supplying access to a resource.

A Model is the intelligence resource itself.

One Provider may expose many Models.

The same Model Family may be available through:

- its original Provider,

- a third-party hosting platform,

- a local runtime,

- an Omnira-managed deployment,

- or a user-controlled private server.

Provider identity and Model identity shall remain separate.

For example:

Provider

NVIDIA-hosted service.

Model

A specific open or proprietary language Model Version.

Deployment

The provider-hosted operational endpoint through which that Model Version is accessed.

These concepts must not be collapsed.

7.5 Model Is Not Provider Account

A Provider Account represents a specific connected billing, credential or workspace relationship.

A Model may be accessible through several Provider Accounts.

The same Provider Account may expose many Models.

Model eligibility therefore requires both:

- eligible Model or Model Version,

- and eligible Provider Account.

The Model Registry shall not store account credentials or project billing authority as properties of the abstract Model.

7.6 Model Is Not Deployment

A Model represents a logical intelligence resource or family.

A Model Deployment represents one operational instance or access path.

The same Model Version may be deployed:

- in several regions,

- under several Provider Accounts,

- on different local nodes,

- with different quantisation,

- through different runtimes,

- or under different safety and performance configurations.

Deployment determines practical properties such as:

- endpoint,

- region,

- hardware,

- latency,

- context capacity,

- throughput,

- privacy boundary,

- and cost.

Model identity must remain stable across Deployments where semantic equivalence is sufficiently established.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.7 Model Is Not Agent

A Model is not an Omnira Agent.

An Agent has:

- identity,

- role,

- purpose,

- behavioural policy,

- authority,

- project relationships,

- tools,

- and governed memory access.

A Model is one resource an Agent may use.

Atlas does not become a different Agent when a different reasoning Model is selected.

Arnold does not cease to be Arnold when GainPilot changes its execution provider.

The Model Registry shall never be used as the Agent Registry.

7.8 Model Is Not Capability

A Capability defines what kind of operation Omnira understands.

A Model declares support for one or more Capabilities.

One Model may support several Capabilities.

One Capability may be supported by many Models.

Capability identity remains provider- and Model-independent.

The Model Registry shall reference canonical Capability Versions from the Capability Registry.

7.9 Model Is Not Adapter

An Adapter translates between Omnira’s canonical contracts and a provider-specific interface.

A Model may be accessible through several Adapters.

An Adapter may support several Models.

Adapter behaviour may affect:

- supported parameters,

- error mapping,

- streaming,

- tool calling,

- usage reporting,

- and output normalisation.

Model identity shall not be tied permanently to one Adapter implementation.

7.10 Model Is Not Endpoint

A provider endpoint is an operational address or routing target.

An endpoint may expose:

- one Model,

- several Models,

- a moving alias,

- or a provider-managed router.

The endpoint shall belong to a Connection or Model Deployment.

It shall not become the canonical Model identifier.

7.11 Model Family

A Model Family groups related Model Versions that share a recognised lineage or product identity.

A Model Family may include:

- major generations,

- dated versions,

- preview versions,

- specialised variants,

- context variants,

- speed-optimised variants,

- or provider-managed releases.

The Model Family provides continuity.

It does not imply that all Versions are interchangeable.

7.12 Model

The canonical Model object represents the stable logical identity under which one or more Versions are grouped.

A Model shall include or reference:

- modelId,

- canonical name,

- Model Family,

- originating Provider where known,

- model type,

- primary modalities,

- broad purpose,

- ownership or licence class,

- lifecycle,

- and provenance.

The Model object should not contain volatile operational properties that belong to Versions or Deployments.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.13 Model Version

A Model Version represents a specific release or materially distinct implementation of a Model.

It shall include or reference:

- modelVersionId,

- modelId,

- provider version identifier,

- release date where known,

- knowledge or training cutoff where declared,

- supported Capabilities,

- modality support,

- context limits,

- output limits,

- tool support,

- safety properties,

- pricing references,

- quality evidence,

- lifecycle,

- and provenance.

Historical Executions shall reference the exact Model Version used where this can be determined.

7.14 Model Variant

A Model Variant is a specialised form of a Model Version.

Variants may differ by:

- size,

- speed,

- quality,

- quantisation,

- context window,

- safety configuration,

- modality,

- region,

- or hardware optimisation.

Examples may include:

- small,

- medium,

- large,

- fast,

- reasoning,

- vision,

- instruct,

- code,

- real-time,

- or distilled.

A Variant may be modelled as:

- separate Model Version,

- Variant metadata,

- or Deployment property,

depending on whether the semantic behaviour differs materially.

The distinction must remain consistent.

7.15 Model Alias

A Model Alias is a provider or user-facing name that resolves to a Model Version or provider-managed target.

Aliases may include:

- latest,

- production,

- preview,

- default,

- fast,

- or dated shorthand.

Aliases are not stable evidence of Model Version.

The Registry shall record:

- alias,

- Provider,

- resolution state,

- observed target,

- and observation time.

Executions using a moving alias shall preserve the alias and any resolved Version evidence available.

7.16 Moving Alias

A Moving Alias may change its underlying Model Version without changing its name.

Moving aliases reduce reproducibility.

The Fabric shall:

- identify them explicitly,

- avoid treating historical quality evidence as automatically current,

- record observed provider metadata,

- and increase verification when material behaviour may have changed.

A moving alias must not be represented as a fixed Version.

7.17 Unknown Model Version

A Provider may not disclose the exact Model Version behind an endpoint or alias.

The Registry shall support an explicit Unknown Model Version state.

Execution evidence should preserve:

- Provider,

- endpoint or alias,

- observation time,

- declared product name,

- and any response metadata.

Unknown shall not be replaced with an assumed Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.18 Model Identity

Every Model shall have a stable canonical identifier.

The identifier shall remain independent of:

- provider endpoint,

- display name,

- project,

- local filename,

- account,

- or mutable alias.

A Model may also have:

- provider names,

- community names,

- repository names,

- local runtime names,

- and deprecated names.

These shall be represented as aliases or external identifiers.

7.19 Model Version Identity

Every Model Version shall have a stable canonical identifier.

The identifier should distinguish:

- provider-declared releases,

- materially changed hidden releases where detectable,

- local builds,

- quantised builds where behaviour differs,

- and fine-tuned or adapted versions.

A checksum or artefact digest may assist identification for self-hosted Models.

7.20 Model Naming Convention

Canonical Model names should be:

- recognisable,

- stable,

- provider-aware where appropriate,

- and separate from mutable marketing labels.

The canonical identifier may use a structured namespace such as:

provider.model_family

or:

origin.model_family

Model Version identifiers may append a governed Version reference.

The exact naming syntax may evolve.

Meaning must remain stable.

7.21 Provider Model Name

The Provider Model Name is the identifier required by the Provider API or service.

It shall be stored separately from the canonical Model identifier.

Adapter code may use the Provider Model Name.

Callers and business logic should use canonical resource references or capability requests.

7.22 External Model Identifier

A Model may have external identifiers such as:

- provider API ID,

- model repository ID,

- NIM identifier,

- Hugging Face repository,

- Ollama tag,

- container image,

- or local artefact path.

Each external identifier shall include:

- source,

- identifier type,

- value,

- validity,

- and observed time where relevant.

7.23 Model Type

The Registry shall classify Models by Model Type.

Types may include:

- foundation language model,

- reasoning model,

- code model,

- embedding model,

- reranking model,

- image generation model,

- image editing model,

- video generation model,

- speech synthesis model,

- speech recognition model,

- music generation model,

- multimodal model,

- evaluator model,

- moderation model,

- classifier,

- or tool-routing model.

A Model may have several types when justified.

Types support discovery.

Capabilities remain the authoritative execution contract.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.24 Model Modality

Each Model Version shall declare accepted and produced modalities.

Accepted Modalities may include:

- text,

- image,

- audio,

- video,

- document,

- code,

- structured data,

- or embedding vectors.

Produced Modalities may include:

- text,

- structured output,

- image,

- audio,

- video,

- embedding,

- ranking,

- or tool calls.

Multimodal must be represented precisely.

7.25 Input Modality

Input Modality describes what the Model Version can consume.

A Model accepting text and one image is not necessarily equivalent to a Model designed for:

- many images,

- video,

- audio,

- or interleaved multimodal context.

The Registry shall capture practical limits.

7.26 Output Modality

Output Modality describes what the Model Version can produce directly.

A text Model whose output is later converted to audio shall not be registered as a native speech synthesis Model.

Post-processing must remain explicit.

7.27 Native Capability

A Native Capability is performed directly by the Model Version.

Examples include:

- text generation,

- image generation,

- embedding,

- speech synthesis,

- or image understanding.

Native support should remain distinct from support created through:

- Adapter transformation,

- tool composition,

- workflow composition,

- or human assistance.

7.28 Composed Capability Support

A Model may participate in a composed Capability without performing the whole operation.

For example, a text Model may create:

- motion instructions for video generation,

- but not the video itself.

The Model Registry shall not claim support for the final video Capability merely because the Model contributed to the workflow.

7.29 Model Capability Declaration

A Model Capability Declaration connects one Model Version to one Capability Version.

It shall include:

- capabilityId,

- Capability Version,

- support state,

- supported Features,

- constraints,

- context limits,

- output limits,

- quality evidence,

- known limitations,

- and verification state.

Declarations may originate from:

- Provider documentation,

- Adapter metadata,

- testing,

- benchmark,

- or operational evidence.

7.30 Claimed Model Capability

Claimed support means a Provider or source states that the Model supports the Capability.

Claimed support may be used for:

- discovery,

- experimentation,

- and test planning.

It shall not automatically be treated as production-verified.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.31 Observed Model Capability

Observed support means Omnira has executed the Capability successfully under recorded conditions.

Observed support shall identify:

- Capability Version,

- Model Version,

- Deployment,

- Adapter,

- inputs,

- environment,

- and output evidence.

One success does not prove universal compatibility.

7.32 Verified Model Capability

Verified support means the Model Version has passed the applicable Capability conformance and quality tests.

Verification shall be:

- Capability-specific,

- Version-specific,

- Deployment-aware where needed,

- Adapter-specific,

- and time-aware.

Verification may expire.

7.33 Partial Model Capability

Partial support means the Model Version satisfies only part of the Capability Contract.

Examples include:

- supports image input but not multiple images,

- supports speech synthesis but not Swedish,

- supports structured output but not strict schema adherence,

- supports image-to-video but not reusable character references.

Partial support must not be presented as full support.

7.34 Restricted Model Capability

Restricted support means the Capability is supported only under specific conditions.

Restrictions may include:

- Public data only,

- one Project,

- one region,

- one Provider Account,

- one duration limit,

- mandatory human review,

- or no commercial use.

Restrictions shall be routable metadata.

7.35 Unsupported Model Capability

Unsupported means the Model Version cannot satisfy the Capability contract.

Unsupported declarations may still be preserved to prevent repeated invalid selection.

7.36 Unknown Model Capability

Unknown support means insufficient evidence exists.

Unknown may be acceptable for controlled experimentation.

It should not be treated as verified production support.

7.37 Capability Feature Support

Model Capability Declarations shall identify supported Features.

For a text Model, Features may include:

- structured output,

- function calling,

- tool calling,

- streaming,

- reasoning mode,

- system instructions,

- image input,

- document input,

- citation output,

- or deterministic seed support.

For video, Features may include:

- image reference,

- multiple-character reference,

- first and last frame,

- camera control,

- motion control,

- lip sync,

- extension,

- or resolution options.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.38 Mandatory Feature Compatibility

If a Capability Request requires a Feature, a Model lacking verified support is ineligible.

The Fabric must not assume that a Model supports a Feature because a related Model in the same Family supports it.

7.39 Tool-Calling Support

Tool-calling support shall describe:

- whether tools are supported,

- schema restrictions,

- parallel calls,

- streaming tool calls,

- tool-choice control,

- argument reliability,

- and provider limitations.

Tool support is not authority to use tools.

Authority remains a separate Fabric decision.

7.40 Structured Output Support

Structured output support shall describe:

- JSON mode,

- schema enforcement,

- response validation,

- retry requirements,

- maximum schema complexity,

- and known failure behaviour.

A Model producing JSON-like text is not equivalent to strict schema support.

7.41 Reasoning Support

Reasoning support may include:

- general reasoning,

- extended reasoning,

- hidden reasoning mode,

- visible rationale summary,

- planning,

- or specialised mathematical reasoning.

The Registry shall not require or store private chain-of-thought content.

It may record:

- reasoning mode,

- declared effort level,

- latency impact,

- cost impact,

- and quality evidence.

7.42 Grounding and Citation Support

Some Models or provider systems may support:

- web grounding,

- document grounding,

- source citations,

- or retrieval integration.

Grounding support shall identify:

- source type,

- freshness,

- citation traceability,

- provider control,

- and limitations.

Citation appearance alone does not prove source correctness.

7.43 Context Window

The Context Window describes the maximum amount of input context supported by a Model Version or Deployment.

The Registry should distinguish:

- advertised maximum,

- verified practical maximum,

- project-approved maximum,

- and recommended operating range.

Larger context does not guarantee better quality.

7.44 Input Token Limit

For token-based Models, the Registry shall record the maximum supported input size where known.

Provider counting methods may differ.

The Adapter shall preserve provider-specific token estimation where required.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.45 Output Token Limit

The Registry shall record output limits separately from input limits.

A large context window does not imply equally large output support.

Output limits influence:

- Capability compatibility,

- planning,

- document generation,

- and cost.

7.46 Total Context Limit

Some Providers apply one total limit across input and output.

The Registry shall represent whether limits are:

- input-only,

- output-only,

- combined,

- dynamic,

- or unknown.

Adapters must not assume one universal counting model.

7.47 Media Limits

Multimodal Model Versions may have limits such as:

- image count,

- image dimensions,

- audio duration,

- video duration,

- frame count,

- file size,

- or document page count.

These limits belong to Version or Deployment metadata.

7.48 Context Quality Profile

The Registry may record practical evidence about performance across context lengths.

A Model may technically accept a long context while showing degraded:

- retrieval,

- instruction adherence,

- accuracy,

- or latency.

Routing should use measured quality where available.

7.49 Knowledge Cutoff

Where declared, the Registry may record a Model Version’s knowledge cutoff.

The cutoff is not evidence that every fact before that date is known or correct.

The Fabric shall still use current research tools for time-sensitive requests.

7.50 Training Data Disclosure

The Registry may preserve Provider-declared information about:

- training sources,

- licences,

- synthetic data,

- opt-out mechanisms,

- and limitations.

Unknown training provenance shall remain unknown.

The Registry shall not invent certainty.

7.51 Model Ownership Class

A Model may be classified as:

- proprietary,

- open-weight,

- open-source,

- source-available,

- research-only,

- custom private,

- fine-tuned,

- distilled,

- or unknown.

Ownership class affects:

- deployment options,

- rights,

- cost,

- privacy,

- and maintenance.

7.52 Model Licence

Open or self-hosted Models shall reference the applicable licence.

The Registry may record:

- licence name,

- version,

- commercial-use permission,

- redistribution terms,

- attribution,

- acceptable-use restrictions,

- and uncertainty.

Open weights do not automatically mean unrestricted commercial use.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.53 Provider Terms Relationship

Externally hosted Model use may be governed by Provider terms in addition to Model licence.

The Registry shall preserve the distinction between:

- Model licence,

- Provider service terms,

- Provider Account agreement,

- and project input rights.

7.54 Commercial Use Eligibility

The Registry may record whether output from a Model Version is:

- eligible for commercial use,

- conditionally eligible,

- restricted,

- unknown,

- or prohibited.

Eligibility may vary by:

- Provider Account tier,

- Provider terms,

- region,

- use case,

- and input rights.

The Model Registry alone cannot prove the complete rights chain.

7.55 Data Retention Profile

A Model Deployment or Provider relationship may declare:

- prompt retention,

- output retention,

- abuse-monitoring retention,

- human-review possibility,

- training use,

- and deletion support.

Retention is often Deployment- or Account-specific rather than Model-specific.

The Registry shall place data at the correct object level.

7.56 Training-Use Profile

The Registry may record whether Provider-submitted data may be used for:

- model training,

- service improvement,

- safety review,

- or no such use.

This property may differ by:

- account tier,

- contract,

- region,

- and endpoint.

It shall not be assumed from general Provider reputation.

7.57 Safety Profile

A Model Safety Profile may include:

- built-in moderation,

- refusal behaviour,

- harmful-content controls,

- age-related restrictions,

- prompt-injection resilience,

- known jailbreak sensitivity,

- and Provider enforcement.

Safety claims require evidence.

A strict refusal profile may make a Model unsuitable for some benign tasks.

A permissive profile may require stronger Fabric controls.

7.58 Content Policy Profile

The Registry may preserve Provider- or Model-specific content restrictions.

Restrictions may affect:

- image generation,

- child-facing media,

- health,

- finance,

- politics,

- likeness,

- copyrighted characters,

- or voice cloning.

Policy restrictions influence eligibility.

They must not be confused with Omnira’s own policies.

7.59 Privacy Profile

A Model Deployment Privacy Profile may describe:

- execution location,

- Provider access,

- encryption,

- retention,

- training use,

- regional processing,

- local ownership,

- and auditability.

Privacy belongs primarily to Deployment and Provider Account context.

The abstract Model may support several privacy profiles through different Deployments.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.60 Risk Classification

Each Model Version may receive a Risk Classification based on:

- autonomy,

- tool use,

- modality,

- external side effects,

- data handling,

- output unpredictability,

- and known defects.

Risk classification informs:

- production admission,

- approval,

- evaluation,

- and monitoring.

Capability risk and Model risk shall both be considered.

7.61 Model Trust Level

The Registry may assign a Trust Level such as:

- untrusted,

- experimental,

- reviewed,

- production approved,

- restricted production,

- high assurance,

- or retired.

Trust Level shall be based on evidence.

It shall not be inherited automatically across Model Family Versions.

7.62 Model Maturity

Model Maturity may include:

- preview,

- beta,

- stable,

- generally available,

- legacy,

- or unknown.

Provider labels are evidence, not absolute truth.

Preview status may require:

- lower spending limits,

- stronger review,

- and reduced data eligibility.

7.63 Model Lifecycle

Canonical Model lifecycle states may include:

- proposed,

- discovered,

- experimental,

- approved,

- active,

- restricted,

- degraded,

- deprecated,

- disabled,

- retired,

- and archived.

Lifecycle shall be version-specific where appropriate.

7.64 Proposed Model

Proposed means the Model has been identified for possible addition.

It may have incomplete metadata.

It shall not be used for production execution.

7.65 Discovered Model

Discovered means the Model was detected through:

- Provider metadata,

- API listing,

- repository scan,

- user connection,

- or manual research.

Discovery does not imply trust or approval.

7.66 Experimental Model

Experimental means the Model Version may be used in bounded tests.

Experimental use should normally require:

- sandbox environment,

- restricted data,

- limited budget,

- mandatory evaluation,

- and no automatic publication.

7.67 Approved Model

Approved means architecture, policy and risk review have accepted the Model Version for defined use.

Approved does not mean every Deployment or Account is active.

7.68 Active Model

Active means the Model Version is available through at least one production-admitted Deployment and may be selected for eligible requests.

Active state shall include:

- supported environments,

- supported scopes,

- and restrictions.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.69 Restricted Model

Restricted means the Model Version may be used only under declared conditions.

Restrictions may include:

- specific Capabilities,

- specific Projects,

- Public data,

- low budget,

- human review,

- or no side effects.

7.70 Degraded Model

Degraded means the Model remains selectable for limited use but current evidence shows reduced:

- quality,

- availability,

- latency,

- reliability,

- or capability support.

Degradation must be visible to routing.

7.71 Deprecated Model

Deprecated means the Model Version should not be selected for new ordinary work.

Deprecation shall identify:

- reason,

- replacement,

- affected Capabilities,

- migration plan,

- and retirement date where known.

7.72 Disabled Model

Disabled means selection is blocked immediately.

Reasons may include:

- security incident,

- rights issue,

- severe quality regression,

- Provider outage,

- cost anomaly,

- or administrative decision.

Disabled status may be temporary.

7.73 Retired Model

Retired means the Model Version is no longer eligible for new execution.

Historical evidence must remain resolvable.

7.74 Archived Model

Archived means the Model record is retained primarily for historical interpretation.

Archived Models may no longer appear in ordinary discovery.

7.75 Model Lifecycle Transition

Lifecycle transitions shall record:

- previous state,

- new state,

- actor,

- reason,

- evidence,

- effective time,

- and affected scopes.

A Model shall not move directly from discovered to active without required review.

7.76 Model Owner

Every Model Registry entry shall have an accountable governance Owner or Steward.

Responsibilities may include:

- metadata quality,

- lifecycle,

- capability mappings,

- benchmark coverage,

- deprecation,

- and review.

Ownership does not grant unrestricted execution authority.

7.77 Model Provenance

Model records shall preserve provenance such as:

- Provider documentation,

- repository metadata,

- Model card,

- licence,

- API observation,

- benchmark,

- test execution,

- and human review.

Conflicting source claims shall remain visible.

7.78 Model Card

The Registry may include or reference a Model Card.

A Model Card may describe:

- intended use,

- limitations,

- training information,

- safety,

- evaluation,

- licence,

- and known risks.

Provider or community Model Cards are evidence sources.

They are not automatically canonical truth.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.79 Canonical Model Record

A canonical Model record should contain or reference:

- stable identity,

- Family,

- Provider origin,

- Model Type,

- modality,

- ownership class,

- licence,

- broad purpose,

- lifecycle,

- aliases,

- Versions,

- and provenance.

Volatile operational data should remain in Version or Deployment objects.

7.80 Canonical Model Version Record

A Model Version record should contain or reference:

- stable Version identity,

- Model identity,

- Provider version identifier,

- release date,

- Capability Declarations,

- Features,

- limits,

- quality evidence,

- cost references,

- safety profile,

- rights profile,

- lifecycle,

- and known limitations.

7.81 Model Deployment

A Model Deployment represents an operationally selectable instance or access path.

It shall include or reference:

- deploymentId,

- Model Version,

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Connection,

- region,

- endpoint reference,

- environment,

- configuration,

- runtime,

- capacity,

- health,

- privacy profile,

- pricing reference,

- and lifecycle.

Routing shall select a Deployment, not only an abstract Model.

7.82 External Model Deployment

An External Model Deployment executes on infrastructure controlled by an external Provider.

It shall identify:

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- region,

- endpoint,

- service tier,

- account terms,

- retention profile,

- and current health.

7.83 Omnira-Managed Deployment

An Omnira-Managed Deployment executes on infrastructure controlled or operated by Omnira.

It may use:

- proprietary Models,

- licensed open Models,

- containerised NIM resources,

- or managed compute.

It shall still have:

- explicit ownership,

- budget,

- capacity,

- security,

- and operational evidence.

7.84 User-Managed Deployment

A User-Managed Deployment runs on infrastructure controlled by the user.

Examples include:

- local workstation,

- private rig,

- home server,

- or user cloud account.

The Fabric shall record:

- node owner,

- connectivity,

- capacity,

- trust,

- and permitted scope.

7.85 Local Model Deployment

A Local Deployment executes on a user-controlled device or private node.

It may provide:

- privacy,

- offline use,

- predictable ownership,

- and lower marginal cost.

It may also have:

- limited performance,

- energy cost,

- reduced availability,

- hardware dependency,

- and maintenance burden.

Local shall not be treated as automatically free or superior.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.86 Edge Model Deployment

An Edge Deployment runs on a constrained device such as:

- mobile phone,

- tablet,

- vehicle,

- wearable,

- or embedded node.

Edge deployment may support:

- low latency,

- offline processing,

- privacy,

- and limited capabilities.

The Registry shall preserve hardware and battery constraints.

7.87 Deployment Configuration

Deployment Configuration may include:

- quantisation,

- precision,

- context setting,

- safety setting,

- system prompt layer,

- batching,

- concurrency,

- temperature defaults,

- or hardware allocation.

Configuration materially affecting behaviour shall be versioned.

7.88 Quantisation

For locally hosted Models, Quantisation may affect:

- memory use,

- speed,

- quality,

- and hardware compatibility.

Quantised variants should be represented at Version or Deployment level according to semantic impact.

Benchmark evidence shall identify the actual quantisation used.

7.89 Fine-Tuned Model

A Fine-Tuned Model is derived from another Model Version through additional training or adaptation.

The Registry shall record:

- base Model Version,

- training owner,

- training data provenance where governed,

- intended purpose,

- evaluation,

- licence compatibility,

- and scope.

Fine-tuned Models may be project-specific.

7.90 Adapter-Tuned or Prompt-Tuned Model

Some apparent specialisation may result from:

- system instructions,

- adapters,

- retrieval,

- or prompt templates

rather than changed Model weights.

The Registry shall not register a new Model Version when only execution configuration changed unless the behaviour is governed as a distinct Deployment or packaged resource.

7.91 Distilled Model

A Distilled Model derives behaviour from another Model or training process.

The Registry shall record available lineage.

Distillation does not guarantee equivalent quality or rights.

7.92 Model Lineage

Model Lineage may represent:

- derived from,

- fine-tuned from,

- distilled from,

- quantised from,

- converted from,

- or supersedes.

Lineage supports:

- rights,

- reproducibility,

- quality interpretation,

- and migration.

7.93 Model Artefact

A self-hosted Model may have one or more artefacts.

Artefact metadata may include:

- file or container reference,

- checksum,

- size,

- format,

- source,

- licence,

- and integrity verification.

Artefact identity supports secure deployment.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.94 Model Checksum

Checksums should be preserved for self-hosted Model artefacts where practical.

Checksum mismatch may indicate:

- corruption,

- unapproved modification,

- or wrong version.

External hosted Models may not expose equivalent artefact verification.

7.95 Runtime

A Runtime is the software environment that loads or accesses a Model Deployment.

Examples include:

- Ollama,

- vLLM,

- NVIDIA NIM,

- provider-hosted API,

- custom inference server,

- mobile runtime,

- or browser runtime.

Runtime identity shall remain separate from Model identity.

7.96 Runtime Version

Runtime Version may materially affect:

- performance,

- supported context,

- tool calling,

- quantisation,

- and output.

Execution evidence should preserve Runtime Version for local or self-hosted Deployments where relevant.

7.97 Hardware Profile

Local and managed Deployments shall reference a Hardware Profile.

It may include:

- CPU,

- GPU,

- accelerator,

- RAM,

- VRAM,

- storage,

- architecture,

- and energy constraints.

Hardware Profile informs:

- compatibility,

- load time,

- throughput,

- and model placement.

7.98 Hardware Requirement

A Model Deployment may declare minimum and recommended hardware.

Requirements may include:

- VRAM,

- system RAM,

- storage,

- GPU compute capability,

- operating system,

- runtime,

- and driver.

The Fabric shall not schedule a Model to an incompatible node.

7.99 Node Compatibility

Node Compatibility determines whether a Runtime Node can operate the Model Deployment.

It shall consider:

- hardware,

- runtime,

- storage,

- power state,

- network,

- privacy,

- and environment.

Compatibility may change dynamically.

7.100 Model Load State

Local Models may have states such as:

- not installed,

- installed,

- loading,

- loaded,

- idle,

- unloading,

- unavailable,

- or corrupted.

Load State affects latency and availability.

7.101 Model Installation State

Installation shall preserve:

- source,

- artefact,

- checksum,

- licence acceptance,

- node,

- installedAt,

- and installer identity.

Automatic Model installation may require approval due to:

- storage,

- bandwidth,

- licence,

- and security.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.102 Model Removal

Removing a local Model artefact shall require authority.

Removal must distinguish:

- unload,

- uninstall,

- archive,

- and physical deletion.

Historical execution evidence shall remain interpretable after removal.

7.103 Capacity

Model Deployment Capacity may include:

- concurrent requests,

- tokens per minute,

- images per minute,

- audio seconds per minute,

- video queue capacity,

- or local GPU availability.

Capacity is operational state.

It shall not be stored as a permanent abstract Model property.

7.104 Throughput

Throughput evidence may include:

- tokens per second,

- requests per second,

- images per minute,

- or media processing rate.

Throughput shall identify:

- Deployment,

- input conditions,

- hardware,

- Adapter,

- and time.

7.105 Latency

Latency evidence may include:

- queue latency,

- first-token latency,

- total response time,

- job completion time,

- and callback delay.

Latency is Capability- and Deployment-specific.

7.106 Availability

Model availability depends on:

- lifecycle,

- Deployment,

- Provider Account,

- Connection,

- health,

- capacity,

- quota,

- policy,

- and scope.

The Registry shall not expose one misleading universal available flag.

7.107 Model Health

Model Health is the current derived condition of a Model Deployment.

Expected states may include:

- healthy,

- degraded,

- unavailable,

- unknown,

- warming,

- rate limited,

- exhausted,

- authentication required,

- and maintenance.

Health is not the same as eligibility.

7.108 Health Observation

Health Observations may include:

- successful request,

- failed request,

- latency,

- rate limit,

- capacity,

- Provider status,

- or local node telemetry.

Health state shall be derived from observations with declared freshness.

7.109 Health Freshness

Health data shall include:

- observedAt,

- source,

- expected refresh,

- and stale threshold.

Stale health data must not be represented as current certainty.

7.110 Model Quality Evidence

Model quality shall be represented through capability-specific evidence.

Evidence may include:

- benchmarks,

- test executions,

- human review,

- project outcomes,

- error rates,

- acceptance rates,

- and operational learning.

The Registry shall not assign one universal quality score to every Model.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.111 Benchmark Relationship

Benchmark Results shall reference:

- Model Version,

- Model Deployment,

- Capability Version,

- Adapter Version,

- test conditions,

- cost,

- latency,

- and date.

Results shall remain contextual.

7.112 External Benchmark

External Benchmarks may be useful evidence.

They shall preserve:

- source,

- methodology,

- date,

- tested Version,

- and limitations.

External rankings must not be treated as permanent or universally applicable.

7.113 Internal Benchmark

Internal Benchmarks shall reflect Omnira tasks and requirements.

Examples include:

- Nova and Pling character consistency,

- Swedish narration quality,

- TypeScript architecture conformance,

- source-grounded news synthesis,

- or local retrieval performance.

Internal benchmarks may be more useful for routing than generic leaderboards.

7.114 Project-Specific Benchmark

A Project may define benchmarks reflecting its own Quality Contracts.

Project-specific evidence shall not automatically become platform-wide ranking.

7.115 Human Evaluation Evidence

Human review may record:

- reviewer,

- criteria,

- score,

- comments,

- acceptance,

- and date.

Human evaluation should preserve reviewer scope and potential subjectivity.

7.116 Automated Evaluation Evidence

Automated evaluation may use:

- deterministic tests,

- another Model,

- rules,

- or external metrics.

The evaluator and Version shall be recorded.

7.117 Acceptance Rate

The Registry may derive Model acceptance rates by:

- Capability,

- Project,

- routing profile,

- and time period.

Acceptance rate shall not be interpreted without considering:

- task difficulty,

- reviewer standards,

- and retry policy.

7.118 Retry Rate

High retry rate may indicate:

- weak quality,

- unstable Provider,

- poor Adapter mapping,

- or unsuitable prompt strategy.

Retry evidence shall remain Capability-specific.

7.119 Unknown-Outcome Rate

Asynchronous or external Models may have unknown outcomes.

The Registry may track unknown-outcome frequency by Deployment.

This affects reliability ranking and retry policy.

7.120 Model Cost Profile

Cost belongs primarily to:

- Deployment,

- Provider Account,

- pricing version,

- and usage.

The Model Registry may reference cost profiles but shall not store one permanent universal price.

Cost may include:

- per token,

- per image,

- per second,

- per job,

- subscription capacity,

- local compute,

- energy,

- or bundled credits.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.121 Pricing Reference

A Pricing Reference shall identify:

- Provider,

- Provider Account class,

- Model Deployment,

- pricing version,

- effective date,

- currency,

- usage units,

- and source.

Historical Executions shall preserve the pricing basis used for estimates where possible.

7.122 Cost Estimate Evidence

Model selection may use Cost Estimates based on:

- expected input,

- expected output,

- retries,

- conversion,

- and Provider pricing.

Estimates must remain separate from confirmed usage.

7.123 Local Execution Cost

Local execution may have:

- zero direct provider charge,

- energy cost,

- hardware depreciation,

- opportunity cost,

- and maintenance.

Stage 1 may initially report local cost as:

- zero marginal provider cost,

- estimated compute cost,

- or unknown internal cost.

It shall not claim universally free execution.

7.124 Subscription-Included Capacity

Some Provider Accounts include Model use within a subscription.

The Registry or Account state may record:

- included quota,

- reset period,

- API availability,

- and marginal cost.

Subscription inclusion does not make usage unbounded.

7.125 Free-Tier Model Access

Free-tier access may have:

- lower rate limits,

- reduced quality,

- watermarking,

- restricted commercial rights,

- or no API.

Free-tier status belongs to Provider Account and Deployment context.

It shall not define the abstract Model.

7.126 Model Selection Score

Routing may derive a Model Selection Score using:

- capability compatibility,

- policy,

- quality,

- cost,

- latency,

- reliability,

- privacy,

- and user preference.

The score shall not override mandatory eligibility.

A high-scoring ineligible Model remains unselectable.

7.127 Model Ranking

Rankings shall be scoped to:

- Capability,

- request conditions,

- Project,

- routing profile,

- and time.

The Fabric shall not maintain one simplistic global “best model” list.

7.128 Economy Suitability

A Model may be suitable for Economy routing when it:

- meets the Quality Floor,

- has acceptable reliability,

- satisfies rights and privacy,

- and offers lower total cost.

Economy suitability is Capability-specific.

7.129 Balanced Suitability

Balanced suitability considers:

- quality,

- cost,

- latency,

- reliability,

- and historical acceptance.

The weighting shall be versioned.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.130 Premium Suitability

Premium suitability reflects evidence that the Model can produce superior required quality within budget.

Premium does not mean highest price.

7.131 Private Suitability

Private suitability depends on:

- local or approved private Deployment,

- data controls,

- retention,

- region,

- and ownership.

The same Model Family may have both private and external Deployments.

7.132 Pinned Suitability

A Pinned request may require a specific Model Version or Deployment.

Pinned selection must still verify:

- authority,

- availability,

- safety,

- rights,

- and budget.

Pinning does not convert an ineligible Model into an eligible one.

7.133 Model Fallback

Fallback may select another:

- Model Version,

- Model Family,

- Deployment,

- Provider,

- or composed Capability path.

Fallback shall preserve mandatory constraints.

Model fallback must be evidenced.

7.134 Same-Family Fallback

A newer or older Version in the same Family may be a fallback.

The Registry must not assume semantic equivalence.

Quality, cost and compatibility must be evaluated.

7.135 Cross-Provider Model Fallback

An equivalent or related Model may be hosted by another Provider.

Cross-Provider fallback changes:

- account,

- terms,

- region,

- pricing,

- and operational trust.

It must be evaluated as a distinct Resource Candidate.

7.136 Local Fallback

External failure may permit local fallback when:

- local Capability support exists,

- quality floor is met,

- deadline permits,

- and policy allows.

Local fallback may be slower or lower quality.

Material degradation must be disclosed.

7.137 External Fallback From Local

A local failure must not automatically route externally when data is Local Only.

External fallback requires compatible classification and authority.

7.138 Model Substitution

Model substitution occurs when a selected Model is replaced before or during execution.

Substitution shall record:

- original selection,

- replacement,

- reason,

- cost change,

- quality change,

- and approval impact.

Silent material substitution is prohibited.

7.139 Model Deprecation Trigger

Deprecation may be triggered by:

- Provider retirement notice,

- quality regression,

- high cost,

- security issue,

- licence change,

- better replacement,

- or unsupported Adapter.

Deprecation shall not erase historical evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.140 Model Retirement Migration

Retirement planning shall identify:

- affected Capabilities,

- Workflows,

- Agents,

- Provider Accounts,

- and stored prompts or configurations.

Migration should use Capability contracts rather than provider-specific rewrite where possible.

7.141 Model Version Drift

Version Drift occurs when observed behaviour changes while the declared Version remains stable.

Signals may include:

- benchmark regression,

- changed refusal behaviour,

- changed output format,

- pricing changes,

- or Provider announcement.

Drift may require creating an observed sub-version or restricting the alias.

7.142 Silent Provider Update

When a Provider silently updates a stable Model name, Omnira shall:

- preserve the alias used,

- record the observation period,

- re-run critical conformance tests,

- reduce reproducibility confidence,

- and update quality evidence.

The Registry shall not pretend that past and current behaviour are identical.

7.143 Model Behaviour Fingerprint

The Fabric may derive a Behaviour Fingerprint using controlled tests.

A fingerprint may help detect:

- silent update,

- Adapter change,

- or configuration drift.

A fingerprint is evidence.

It is not proof of underlying weights.

7.144 Model Reproducibility Profile

A Reproducibility Profile may include:

- fixed Version availability,

- seed support,

- deterministic settings,

- provider alias behaviour,

- local artefact checksum,

- and observed variance.

Reproducibility requirements may affect routing.

7.145 Determinism

Models may be:

- deterministic,

- configurable,

- stochastic,

- provider-dependent,

- or unknown.

Determinism claims shall identify conditions.

Temperature zero does not always guarantee identical output.

7.146 Seed Support

Generative media Models may support seeds.

Seed support may improve repeatability.

The Registry shall record:

- seed availability,

- seed range,

- provider consistency,

- and limitations.

Seed support does not guarantee identical output after a Model update.

7.147 Parameter Profile

Model Versions may support canonical parameters such as:

- temperature,

- top-p,

- maximum output,

- seed,

- aspect ratio,

- duration,

- guidance,

- voice settings,

- or reasoning effort.

Provider-specific parameter names belong in Adapter mappings.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.148 Parameter Compatibility

A Model Capability Declaration shall identify which canonical parameters are:

- supported,

- ignored,

- transformed,

- bounded,

- or unsupported.

Adapters must not silently discard material parameters.

7.149 Default Parameter Set

Deployments may define safe default parameters.

Defaults shall be:

- versioned,

- Capability-specific,

- and scoped.

A Provider’s generic default is not automatically Omnira’s approved default.

7.150 Project Parameter Profile

Projects may define preferred parameter profiles.

For example:

- Familje-Stunden child-safe motion settings,

- The Prompt newsroom voice pacing,

- GainPilot short-form visual format.

Project profiles shall not alter canonical Model identity.

7.151 Model Prompt Compatibility

Models may respond differently to:

- system instructions,

- structured prompts,

- examples,

- long context,

- tool schemas,

- and multilingual input.

Prompt compatibility evidence may be captured in operational learning.

It should not become part of immutable Model identity unless contractually relevant.

7.152 Instruction Hierarchy Support

The Registry may record whether a Model or Provider supports:

- system instructions,

- developer instructions,

- user messages,

- tool messages,

- or equivalent roles.

Adapter mappings shall preserve the strongest available instruction hierarchy.

7.153 Multilingual Support

Model Versions may declare language support.

Support should distinguish:

- understands,

- generates,

- transcribes,

- synthesises,

- translates,

- and maintains quality.

“Supports Swedish” is too broad without capability context.

7.154 Swedish Quality Evidence

For Omnira, Swedish quality may require dedicated tests for:

- grammar,

- tone,

- pronunciation,

- transcription,

- child-facing language,

- technical terminology,

- and naturalness.

Generic multilingual claims are insufficient for critical workflows.

7.155 Model Locale Support

Locale support may include:

- language,

- regional spelling,

- date format,

- pronunciation,

- and cultural context.

Locale is often a request constraint rather than separate Capability.

7.156 Code Model Profile

Code Models may declare support for:

- languages,

- frameworks,

- repository size,

- tool use,

- patch generation,

- test generation,

- code review,

- and architecture reasoning.

Code quality shall be verified through tests and review.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.157 Image Model Profile

Image Models may declare support for:

- text-to-image,

- image editing,

- inpainting,

- outpainting,

- text rendering,

- transparency,

- reference consistency,

- style control,

- and resolution.

Provider claims shall be tested for project-critical features.

7.158 Video Model Profile

Video Models may declare:

- text-to-video,

- image-to-video,

- video-to-video,

- duration,

- resolution,

- aspect ratio,

- reference support,

- motion control,

- camera control,

- lip sync,

- sound,

- extension,

- and asynchronous job behaviour.

7.159 Speech Model Profile

Speech Models may declare:

- text-to-speech,

- speech-to-speech,

- transcription,

- language,

- voice cloning,

- emotion,

- pronunciation,

- streaming,

- latency,

- and output formats.

Voice identity and consent remain separate governed objects.

7.160 Embedding Model Profile

Embedding Models may declare:

- vector dimensions,

- supported languages,

- context length,

- normalisation,

- retrieval domain,

- similarity metric guidance,

- and migration compatibility.

Changing Embedding Model may require re-embedding data.

7.161 Embedding Compatibility

Embeddings produced by different Models or Versions are not assumed compatible.

The Registry shall preserve:

- Model Version,

- dimensions,

- normalisation,

- and index relationship.

A retrieval index shall identify the Embedding Model used.

7.162 Reranking Model Profile

Reranking Models may declare:

- input count,

- language,

- document length,

- scoring semantics,

- latency,

- and domain evidence.

Reranking scores from different Models may not be directly comparable.

7.163 Evaluation Model Profile

Evaluator Models shall declare:

- evaluated Capabilities,

- criteria,

- independence,

- bias,

- calibration,

- and known limitations.

The generating Model should not always be its own sole evaluator.

7.164 Moderation Model Profile

Moderation Models may support:

- text,

- image,

- audio,

- or video safety assessment.

Moderation output is evidence.

It does not replace human review where policy requires it.

7.165 Model Bias and Limitation Record

The Registry may preserve known:

- biases,

- failure modes,

- cultural weaknesses,

- language weaknesses,

- visual artefacts,

- hallucination tendencies,

- or safety limitations.

Limitations should remain evidence-based and Version-specific.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.166 Known Defect

A Known Defect records a reproducible or credible Model issue.

It should include:

- Capability,

- conditions,

- severity,

- evidence,

- workaround,

- and status.

Known defects may affect eligibility.

7.167 Model Incident

A Model Incident may involve:

- severe quality regression,

- data leakage,

- unexpected cost,

- unsafe output,

- Provider misrouting,

- or false Version identification.

Incidents shall reference affected Versions and Deployments.

7.168 Model Incident Containment

Containment may include:

- disable Version,

- restrict Capability,

- block Project use,

- require human review,

- disable fallback,

- or pin a safer Version.

Containment shall be scoped where possible.

7.169 Model Incident Recovery

Recovery requires:

- root-cause evidence,

- corrected configuration,

- renewed conformance tests,

- review,

- and controlled reactivation.

Provider reassurance alone may be insufficient.

7.170 Model Monitoring

The Fabric should monitor production Models for:

- availability,

- latency,

- error rate,

- cost,

- quality acceptance,

- retry rate,

- unknown outcomes,

- and drift.

Monitoring shall respect privacy.

7.171 Quality Monitoring

Quality Monitoring may use:

- sampled evaluation,

- deterministic tests,

- user feedback,

- human rejection,

- or project outcomes.

Monitoring must remain Capability-specific.

7.172 Cost Monitoring

Cost Monitoring may detect:

- pricing change,

- unexpected usage,

- retry loops,

- account misattribution,

- or Model substitution.

Material anomalies may trigger Incident or restriction.

7.173 Terms Monitoring

Provider terms affecting Model use may change.

The Fabric should track:

- effective date,

- changed rights,

- retention,

- training use,

- prohibited use,

- and review status.

A terms change may make a previously eligible Deployment ineligible.

7.174 Licence Monitoring

For open Models, licence updates or interpretation changes may affect:

- redistribution,

- commercial use,

- hosting,

- or derivative models.

Licence uncertainty shall trigger review.

7.175 Model Discovery

Model Discovery may occur through:

- Provider API,

- Provider documentation,

- local runtime listing,

- repository metadata,

- installed artefacts,

- user connection,

- or manual research.

Discovered Models shall enter a non-active state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.176 Automated Discovery

Automated discovery may collect:

- identifiers,

- names,

- context limits,

- modalities,

- and Provider metadata.

Automated discovery must not activate Models automatically.

7.177 Manual Model Registration

An authorised operator may register a Model manually.

Manual registration shall preserve:

- source,

- reason,

- known uncertainty,

- and review status.

7.178 Model Import

Model metadata packages may be imported.

Imported records shall be:

- validated,

- namespaced,

- checked for duplicates,

- and quarantined until approved.

7.179 Duplicate Model Detection

The Registry shall attempt to detect duplicates caused by:

- different Provider aliases,

- different host names,

- local tags,

- renamed Versions,

- or community metadata.

Duplicate detection may use:

- lineage,

- Provider identifiers,

- artefact checksum,

- release metadata,

- and semantic comparison.

7.180 Model Merge

Duplicate Model records may be merged when evidence confirms one identity.

The merge shall preserve:

- aliases,

- external identifiers,

- provenance,

- historical references,

- and superseded record IDs.

7.181 Model Split

A Model record may be split when one identity incorrectly grouped materially different Versions or variants.

Historical executions must remain mapped correctly.

7.182 Model Rename

Display names may change without changing identity.

Canonical identifier change should occur only when necessary.

Old names shall remain aliases.

7.183 Model Registry Source of Truth

The Model Registry shall have one authoritative governed source.

Derived views may exist in:

- runtime cache,

- documentation,

- Atlas Knowledge,

- Intelligence Graph,

- or user interfaces.

Derived views shall declare:

- source version,

- freshness,

- and completeness.

7.184 Model Registry API

The Registry should expose governed operations such as:

- get Model,

- get Model Version,

- list Versions,

- list Deployments,

- query by Capability,

- query by modality,

- query by lifecycle,

- inspect quality evidence,

- inspect limits,

- and inspect current availability.

Mutation shall require privileged authority.

7.185 Human Model Discovery

Human-facing discovery should explain Models through:

- capabilities,

- strengths,

- limitations,

- privacy,

- expected cost,

- and approved use.

Users should not need to compare every Model manually for ordinary tasks.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
7.186 Machine Model Discovery

Machine consumers may receive structured metadata needed for planning.

Discovery shall not expose:

- raw credentials,

- secret endpoints,
