- payment required,

- exhausted,

- suspended,

- revoked,

- disconnected,

- and archived.

Account lifecycle is distinct from Provider lifecycle.

8.105 Connecting State

Connecting means authentication or setup is underway.

The account must not be represented as ready before verification.

8.106 Connected State

Connected means the technical relationship exists.

Connected does not prove:

- eligible terms,

- available credits,

- correct scope,

- or production approval.

8.107 Active Account

Active means the account is eligible for defined governed use.

Eligibility remains request-specific.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.108 Authentication Required

Authentication Required means the account relationship exists but current credentials cannot be used.

Reasons may include:

- expiry,

- revocation,

- user re-consent,

- changed OAuth scopes,

- or multi-factor requirement.

8.109 Payment Required

Payment Required means execution is blocked by:

- failed payment,

- expired subscription,

- required upgrade,

- or missing billing method.

The system shall not classify this as a generic Provider outage.

8.110 Exhausted Account

Exhausted means relevant credits or quota are unavailable.

Exhaustion may be temporary.

It shall affect account eligibility without retiring the Provider.

8.111 Suspended Account

A Provider or Omnira may suspend the account.

The Registry shall preserve:

- reason,

- detected time,

- affected workflows,

- and recovery path.

8.112 Revoked Account

Revoked means authorisation has been withdrawn.

No new execution may use the account.

Existing external jobs may require reconciliation.

8.113 Disconnected Account

Disconnected means Omnira no longer has an active Connection.

Provider-side assets or data may still exist.

The system shall not imply Provider deletion merely because local credentials were removed.

8.114 Provider Connection

A Provider Connection defines how Omnira communicates with a Provider Account or service.

It shall include:

- connectionId,

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- protocol,

- endpoint reference,

- environment,

- credential reference,

- permitted operations,

- lifecycle,

- health,

- and provenance.

8.115 API Connection

An API Connection uses a documented or approved programmatic interface.

It shall declare:

- base endpoint reference,

- API version,

- authentication,

- rate limits,

- supported operations,

- and error behaviour.

8.116 MCP Connection

An MCP Connection exposes Provider or Tool capabilities through the Model Context Protocol.

It shall declare:

- server identity,

- transport,

- tool catalogue,

- authentication,

- permissions,

- integration owner,

- lifecycle,

- and trust.

MCP availability does not imply that all exposed tools are authorised.

8.117 OAuth Connection

An OAuth Connection shall preserve:

- authorising Principal,

- scopes,

- Account,

- refresh behaviour,

- expiry,

- revocation,

- and environment.

OAuth scope changes may require reapproval.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.118 Webhook Connection

A Webhook Connection receives Provider events.

It shall define:

- callback endpoint,

- signature verification,

- event types,

- secret reference,

- replay protection,

- deduplication,

- and rotation.

8.119 Queue Connection

A Provider may communicate through:

- message queue,

- event bus,

- or asynchronous job channel.

Queue integration shall preserve:

- identity,

- ordering assumptions,

- retry,

- and dead-letter handling.

8.120 Local Connection

A Local Connection may use:

- process invocation,

- local API,

- socket,

- command-line tool,

- or runtime library.

Local does not remove permission, evidence or sandbox requirements.

8.121 Human-Assisted Connection

A Human-Assisted Connection represents a governed handoff rather than direct automation.

It may include:

- operator instructions,

- approved Provider Account,

- expected settings,

- budget,

- file-transfer method,

- and output-ingestion procedure.

8.122 Connection Lifecycle

Connection states may include:

- proposed,

- configuring,

- validating,

- active,

- degraded,

- authentication required,

- disabled,

- revoked,

- disconnected,

- and archived.

8.123 Connection Health

Connection Health may include:

- healthy,

- degraded,

- unavailable,

- unknown,

- rate limited,

- authentication required,

- and misconfigured.

Health shall include freshness.

8.124 Connection Permission

Connections shall expose only permitted operations.

A Connection may be approved for:

- generation,

- but not deletion;

- reading credits,

- but not changing billing;

- creating Assets,

- but not publishing.

Permissions shall be explicit.

8.125 Connection Environment

A Connection shall belong to an Environment.

A development Connection must not silently execute production work.

Callbacks must resolve the same Environment.

8.126 Connection Scope

Connection scope may be:

- Provider Account,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Capability,

- or service-specific.

Scope must propagate into execution.

8.127 Provider Adapter Relationship

Each Provider operation exposed through the Fabric shall use an approved Adapter or equivalent compatibility boundary.

The Adapter shall define:

- canonical Capability mapping,

- request translation,

- output normalisation,

- error mapping,

- usage mapping,

- and Provider-specific limitations.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.128 Provider Capability Claim

A Provider Capability Claim records what the Provider states it can do.

It shall include:

- Provider,

- Product,

- claimed Capability,

- source,

- date,

- limitations,

- and confidence.

Claims are not production-verification evidence.

8.129 Provider Capability Support

Provider Capability Support is established through one or more:

- Models,

- Tools,

- External Agent Resources,

- Adapters,

- or human-assisted processes.

Support shall remain Resource-specific.

The Provider itself does not perform every claimed Capability uniformly.

8.130 Provider Service Catalogue

The Registry may expose a Service Catalogue containing:

- Products,

- Models,

- Tools,

- Capabilities,

- Accounts,

- and integration states.

The catalogue is a Provider-oriented view.

Canonical Capability meaning remains in the Capability Registry.

8.131 Provider Capability Coverage

Coverage may be measured across:

- Capability families,

- modalities,

- environments,

- data classes,

- and account tiers.

Coverage breadth is not quality proof.

8.132 Provider Capability Verification

Provider support shall be verified through:

- Adapter conformance,

- test Executions,

- quality evaluation,

- rights review,

- privacy review,

- cost mapping,

- and failure testing.

Verification shall be scoped.

8.133 Provider Quality Evidence

Provider-level quality evidence may include:

- account reliability,

- operational support,

- service consistency,

- asset handling,

- and cross-Model behaviour.

Model-level quality remains separate.

8.134 Provider Reliability Profile

The Provider Reliability Profile may include:

- uptime,

- outage history,

- latency,

- queue stability,

- callback reliability,

- API consistency,

- support responsiveness,

- and unknown-outcome rate.

Reliability shall be time-aware.

8.135 Provider Health

Provider Health is the current derived operational condition.

Expected states may include:

- healthy,

- degraded,

- partially unavailable,

- unavailable,

- maintenance,

- unknown,

- billing restricted,

- or incident active.

Provider Health does not prove a specific Model or Account is available.

8.136 Provider Health Observation

Health Observations may originate from:

- official status page,

- test request,

- Account response,

- API error,

- user report,

- callback delay,

- or monitoring system.

Each Observation shall preserve:

- source,

- time,

- target,

- and confidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.137 Official Status Evidence

Official status information is useful but not sufficient.

A Provider may report healthy while:

- one Account is blocked,

- one region is degraded,

- one Model is unavailable,

- or one API endpoint is failing.

The Fabric shall combine official and observed evidence.

8.138 Synthetic Provider Check

The Fabric may execute low-cost or non-consequential tests to assess health.

Synthetic checks shall:

- use approved test data,

- have bounded cost,

- avoid production side effects,

- and remain distinguishable from user work.

8.139 Provider Availability

Availability shall be evaluated across:

- Provider lifecycle,

- Product,

- Account,

- Connection,

- Model Deployment,

- Capability,

- region,

- quota,

- budget,

- policy,

- and health.

There is no single universal Provider available flag.

8.140 Provider Capacity

Provider capacity may include:

- requests per minute,

- concurrent jobs,

- token throughput,

- image generation quota,

- audio minutes,

- video queue,

- storage,

- or account seats.

Capacity belongs to Product, Account or Deployment context.

8.141 Provider Rate Limit

Rate limits may be:

- documented,

- dynamic,

- account-specific,

- Model-specific,

- region-specific,

- or unknown.

The Fabric shall preserve:

- limit,

- remaining capacity,

- reset,

- source,

- and freshness where available.

8.142 Provider Quota

Quota differs from monetary budget.

A paid Account may have:

- daily request quota,

- monthly video seconds,

- storage limit,

- or concurrent-job limit.

Quota exhaustion must be classified accurately.

8.143 Provider Queue

Some Providers expose queue state.

Queue evidence may include:

- current wait,

- priority tier,

- job position,

- estimated completion,

- or unavailable estimate.

Queue estimates are not guarantees.

8.144 Provider Maintenance

Planned maintenance may affect:

- routing,

- deadlines,

- recurring work,

- and fallback.

Maintenance windows should be represented when known.

8.145 Provider Outage

An outage may be:

- global,

- regional,

- Product-specific,

- Model-specific,

- Account-specific,

- Connection-specific,

- or partial.

The Incident model shall preserve scope.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.146 Provider Incident

A Provider Incident may involve:

- security,

- privacy,

- outage,

- incorrect billing,

- data leakage,

- rights change,

- account compromise,

- Provider drift,

- or destructive tool behaviour.

The Incident shall reference affected:

- Provider,

- Products,

- Accounts,

- Connections,

- Models,

- Projects,

- and Executions.

8.147 Provider Incident Severity

Severity should consider:

- protected data,

- affected Tenants,

- public consequence,

- financial impact,

- duration,

- and recoverability.

8.148 Provider Incident Containment

Containment may include:

- disable Provider,

- restrict one Account,

- block one Capability,

- disable one Connection,

- require local routing,

- suspend publication,

- or revoke credentials.

Containment should be narrowly scoped where safe.

8.149 Provider Incident Recovery

Recovery should include:

- evidence,

- root cause,

- Provider response,

- credential action,

- data impact,

- cost impact,

- conformance testing,

- and controlled reactivation.

8.150 Provider Security Incident

A security Incident may require:

- immediate credential revocation,

- audit of recent Executions,

- Project notification,

- Provider suspension,

- and evidence preservation.

Secret rotation must not erase historical connection evidence.

8.151 Provider Privacy Incident

A privacy Incident may involve:

- unexpected retention,

- wrong region,

- cross-account exposure,

- data used for training,

- or unauthorised human review.

Protected workloads may require immediate suspension.

8.152 Provider Billing Incident

Billing incidents may include:

- duplicate charges,

- unexpected credits,

- wrong Project attribution,

- pricing mismatch,

- hidden retry cost,

- or subscription failure.

Billing Incident must remain separate from generic execution failure.

8.153 Provider Quality Incident

A Provider may experience broad quality regression.

The Registry may mark:

- Product degraded,

- Resource mappings restricted,

- or Quality evidence stale.

Model-level investigation remains required.

8.154 Provider Terms Incident

A material terms change may create an Incident when it conflicts with:

- Project rights,

- privacy,

- commercial use,

- or existing production.

New execution may be suspended during review.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.155 Provider Monitoring

The Fabric should monitor Providers for:

- health,

- terms,

- pricing,

- Models,

- Products,

- quotas,

- credits,

- incidents,

- and lifecycle changes.

Monitoring cadence should reflect Provider criticality.

8.156 Provider Terms Monitoring

Terms monitoring may detect:

- revised Terms Version,

- changed privacy,

- changed commercial rights,

- new training use,

- or changed jurisdiction.

Automated detection should create a review task, not autonomous legal acceptance.

8.157 Provider Pricing Monitoring

Pricing monitoring may detect:

- Model price changes,

- credit-value changes,

- subscription changes,

- free-tier changes,

- and currency changes.

Current pricing belongs to cost architecture.

The Registry preserves source and relationship.

8.158 Provider Product Monitoring

Providers may:

- add Products,

- retire Products,

- rename tools,

- change API access,

- or move Capabilities between tiers.

Changes must not silently alter execution.

8.159 Provider Model Monitoring

The Provider may add, update or retire Models.

Discovered changes shall update:

- Provider metadata,

- Model Registry proposals,

- and migration analysis.

They shall not automatically activate new Models.

8.160 Provider Account Monitoring

Account monitoring may include:

- authentication,

- subscription,

- credits,

- quota,

- workspace,

- and billing state.

Monitoring shall respect account privacy.

8.161 Provider Asset Monitoring

Some Providers store:

- images,

- voices,

- videos,

- threads,

- projects,

- or generation history.

Asset monitoring may support:

- reconciliation,

- export,

- cost,

- and deletion.

Provider asset libraries shall not become Omnira’s canonical Asset Library.

8.162 Provider Support Channel

The Registry may record support paths such as:

- email,

- ticket portal,

- enterprise contact,

- emergency channel,

- status page,

- or community support.

Support availability may affect criticality decisions.

8.163 Provider Service-Level Commitment

A Provider may offer formal or informal service-level commitments.

The Registry may record:

- uptime target,

- response time,

- support tier,

- exclusions,

- and contractual source.

Service commitment is evidence.

It does not guarantee actual availability.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.164 Provider Recovery Objective

For critical Providers, Omnira may define:

- maximum tolerated outage,

- fallback deadline,

- data-recovery expectation,

- and migration trigger.

These are Omnira governance expectations, not necessarily Provider promises.

8.165 Provider Account Cost Attribution

Every paid Provider execution shall identify:

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Project,

- Budget Source,

- usage,

- pricing reference,

- and Cost Record.

Shared accounts must still preserve Project attribution.

8.166 Provider Pricing Model

Pricing models may include:

- per token,

- per request,

- per image,

- per video second,

- per audio minute,

- per generation,

- per compute second,

- subscription,

- seat,

- credits,

- storage,

- or hybrid.

Pricing models shall be versioned.

8.167 Provider Credit Conversion

Where Providers use credits, the Fabric should preserve:

- purchased credit cost,

- included credit source,

- Product usage rate,

- effective currency value,

- and uncertainty.

Credit systems may change over time.

8.168 Provider Minimum Charge

Some Providers may round usage or impose minimum charges.

The cost estimator shall account for this where known.

8.169 Provider Retry Cost

Provider retries may create full additional charges.

The Registry or pricing metadata should identify:

- failed-job charging,

- cancellation refund,

- retry policy,

- and credit return behaviour.

8.170 Provider Cancellation Economics

Cancellation may:

- prevent charge,

- partially charge,

- fully charge,

- or be unavailable.

The Fabric must not promise cost recovery without evidence.

8.171 Provider Refund Behaviour

Refunds or credit returns may be:

- automatic,

- manual,

- conditional,

- delayed,

- or unavailable.

Refund state belongs to cost reconciliation.

8.172 Provider Currency

Provider billing currency may differ from Project budget currency.

The cost system shall preserve exchange-rate assumptions separately.

8.173 Provider Tax Treatment

Taxes, VAT and invoice handling belong to financial systems.

The Registry may reference:

- invoice availability,

- tax region,

- and billing entity.

8.174 Provider Cost Transparency

Provider cost transparency may be classified as:

- exact pre-execution,

- estimated,

- usage-based,

- delayed,

- opaque,

- or unknown.

Opaque pricing increases approval and reservation risk.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.175 Provider Economic Suitability

Economic suitability shall consider:

- direct price,

- retries,

- correction cost,

- Account capacity,

- subscription value,

- quality,

- and operational burden.

Cheapest advertised price is not sufficient.

8.176 Provider Routing Preference

A Provider may receive a preference based on:

- user choice,

- Project policy,

- quality evidence,

- cost,

- privacy,

- or strategic relationship.

Preference remains subordinate to eligibility.

8.177 Provider Pinning

A request may pin:

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Product,

- Model,

- or Connection.

Pinning shall identify:

- reason,

- fallback,

- validity,

- and mandatory or preferred state.

8.178 Provider Allowlist

Policies may define approved Providers or Accounts.

Allowlist membership does not prove current compatibility.

8.179 Provider Denylist

Denied Providers shall remain excluded through fallback.

Deny reasons may include:

- privacy,

- rights,

- cost,

- security,

- quality,

- user preference,

- or Incident.

8.180 Provider Data-Class Eligibility

A Provider may be eligible for:

- Public,

- Project Internal,

- Confidential,

- or no protected data.

Eligibility may differ by:

- Account,

- Product,

- region,

- contract,

- and Connection.

8.181 Public Data Eligibility

Public data may use a wider Provider set.

Other constraints still apply.

8.182 Project Internal Eligibility

Project Internal data may require:

- approved Account,

- acceptable retention,

- no unauthorised training use,

- and Project scope.

8.183 Confidential Eligibility

Confidential data may require:

- enterprise terms,

- approved region,

- private Deployment,

- zero or bounded retention,

- and explicit approval.

8.184 Local Only Eligibility

External Providers are normally ineligible for Local Only data.

A local runtime Provider may be eligible when execution remains user-controlled.

8.185 Prohibited Data

Prohibited data shall not be sent to any Provider through the Fabric.

The Provider Registry shall not create exceptions to prohibited classification.

8.186 Provider Rights Eligibility

Provider eligibility may depend on:

- commercial-use terms,

- derivative rights,

- attribution,

- watermarking,

- output ownership,

- and Project purpose.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.187 Provider Child-Facing Eligibility

Child-facing content may require:

- Provider policy compatibility,

- visual safety,

- stronger review,

- rights,

- and publication controls.

A Provider generally supporting video is not automatically approved for child-facing production.

8.188 Provider Voice Eligibility

Voice Provider eligibility may require:

- consent enforcement,

- voice ownership,

- cloning controls,

- account security,

- and commercial rights.

8.189 Provider Code Eligibility

Code Providers may require:

- repository privacy,

- data-retention review,

- tool restrictions,

- and protected branch controls.

A coding Provider shall not gain repository-write authority automatically.

8.190 Provider Publication Eligibility

Providers exposing publication tools require:

- target account mapping,

- explicit publication authority,

- audit,

- idempotency,

- and verification.

Publishing shall remain a distinct Capability.

8.191 Provider Administrative Eligibility

Administrative Provider operations include:

- changing billing,

- adding users,

- deleting workspace,

- accepting terms,

- rotating keys,

- and changing permissions.

These operations require privileged authority.

8.192 Provider Onboarding

Provider onboarding shall follow a controlled process.

Expected phases include:

1. Proposal.

2. Research.

3. Risk and terms review.

4. Capability mapping.

5. Account planning.

6. Credential setup.

7. Connection configuration.

8. Adapter integration.

9. Test execution.

10. Conformance review.

11. Production admission.

12. Monitoring activation.

8.193 Provider Proposal

A Provider Proposal should include:

- Provider identity,

- intended Capabilities,

- Projects,

- expected value,

- access model,

- pricing,

- privacy,

- rights,

- integration method,

- and alternatives.

8.194 Provider Need Assessment

Before integration, Omnira should determine:

- which Capability gap exists,

- whether existing Providers can satisfy it,

- whether local execution is possible,

- whether the Provider creates meaningful value,

- and whether ongoing maintenance is justified.

Provider count is not a success metric.

8.195 Provider Research

Provider research should examine:

- official documentation,

- terms,

- privacy,

- pricing,

- API or MCP access,

- commercial rights,

- Models,

- limits,

- operational maturity,

- and exportability.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.196 Provider Risk Review

Risk review should evaluate:

- protected data,

- jurisdiction,

- security,

- rights,

- account controls,

- billing,

- lock-in,

- and operational dependency.

8.197 Provider Capability Mapping

The onboarding process shall map Provider resources to canonical Capabilities.

Provider terminology shall remain in Adapter metadata.

The Provider shall not redefine Omnira Capability names.

8.198 Provider Account Plan

Before connection, the system should determine:

- account owner,

- account type,

- Project scope,

- environment,

- billing source,

- credential owner,

- and recovery owner.

8.199 Provider Credential Setup

Credentials shall be created or connected through an approved secure process.

The Provider Registry receives only references and status metadata.

8.200 Provider Connection Validation

Connection validation should test:

- identity,

- Account,

- permissions,

- environment,

- basic read operation,

- billing visibility,

- and safe revocation.

8.201 Provider Adapter Validation

Adapter validation shall test:

- canonical request translation,

- output normalisation,

- errors,

- usage,

- retries,

- callbacks,

- and unsupported constraints.

8.202 Provider Sandbox Test

Initial Provider testing should use:

- approved test data,

- low budget,

- no public publication,

- and isolated environment.

8.203 Provider Conformance Review

Production admission shall require evidence that:

- scope,

- authority,

- cost,

- data placement,

- rights,

- errors,

- and provenance

are handled correctly.

8.204 Provider Production Admission

A Production Admission Record shall identify:

- Provider,

- Products,

- Accounts,

- Connections,

- Adapters,

- Capabilities,

- environments,

- data classes,

- restrictions,

- approver,

- and evidence.

8.205 Provider Re-Certification

Re-certification may be required after:

- major terms change,

- privacy change,

- API change,

- Adapter change,

- security Incident,

- acquisition,

- or extended inactivity.

8.206 Provider Offboarding

Provider offboarding shall be controlled.

Expected phases may include:

1. Stop new execution.

2. Reconcile running jobs.

3. Export required Assets and evidence.

4. Migrate workflows.

5. Revoke credentials.

6. Disconnect Connections.

7. Settle costs.

8. Request Provider deletion where appropriate.

9. Preserve historical records.

10. Archive the Provider relationship.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.207 Stop-New-Execution Boundary

Offboarding should first prevent new ordinary work while allowing:

- reconciliation,

- export,

- recovery,

- and required deletion actions.

8.208 Running Job Reconciliation

Active Provider jobs must be classified as:

- cancellable,

- completing,

- failed,

- unknown,

- or requiring manual inspection.

Offboarding must not abandon paid or consequential jobs silently.

8.209 Provider Asset Export

Provider-side Assets may need export before disconnection.

Export should preserve:

- files,

- metadata,

- Provider IDs,

- provenance,

- and ownership.

8.210 Provider Workflow Migration

Pinned workflows shall be reviewed and migrated to:

- alternative Provider,

- alternative Model,

- human-assisted path,

- or retired Capability.

8.211 Credential Revocation

Credentials shall be revoked after the required operational steps.

Revocation must be evidenced.

8.212 Provider Data Deletion

Where policy requires it, Omnira may request deletion of:

- Inputs,

- Outputs,

- threads,

- assets,

- or account data.

Deletion state shall distinguish:

- requested,

- accepted,

- completed,

- verified,

- failed,

- and unknown.

8.213 Provider Account Closure

Closing the Provider Account is separate from disconnecting Omnira.

Account closure may require:

- owner approval,

- billing settlement,

- asset export,

- and Provider confirmation.

8.214 Provider Historical Preservation

Offboarding shall not delete:

- Execution Receipts,

- Cost Records,

- Provider Receipts,

- Model references,

- provenance,

- incidents,

- or accepted learning

required for historical truth.

8.215 Provider Registry Governance

Material Registry operations include:

- create Provider,

- add legal identity,

- add Product,

- add Account,

- approve,

- restrict,

- suspend,

- deprecate,

- retire,

- merge,

- split,

- and offboard.

All operations shall be attributable.

8.216 Provider Owner

Every Provider relationship shall have an accountable Owner or Steward.

Responsibilities may include:

- metadata,

- terms review,

- Account health,

- incidents,

- integrations,

- cost oversight,

- and offboarding.

8.217 Provider Steward

A Steward may maintain operational Provider information without possessing authority to accept terms or approve spending.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.218 Separation of Duties

Higher-risk Provider actions may require separation between:

- proposer,

- technical integrator,

- terms approver,

- security reviewer,

- and production approver.

8.219 Provider Registry Access

Read, use and administration permissions shall remain distinct.

Many systems may discover approved Providers.

Few Principals should modify lifecycle or legal metadata.

8.220 Provider Visibility

Provider visibility may be:

- platform-wide,

- Tenant-visible,

- Project-visible,

- administrative,

- experimental,

- or hidden internal.

Visibility does not imply use permission.

8.221 Provider Discovery

Atlas, Managers and authorised users may discover Providers through Capability-oriented views.

Ordinary users should not need to compare every Provider manually.

8.222 Machine Provider Discovery

Machine consumers may receive:

- Provider ID,

- type,

- lifecycle,

- integration maturity,

- supported resource classes,

- and request-relevant eligibility metadata.

They shall not receive raw secrets.

8.223 Provider Search

Search may support:

- name,

- alias,

- Capability,

- modality,

- region,

- Provider Type,

- lifecycle,

- integration maturity,

- and Account availability.

8.224 Provider Registry API

The Registry should expose governed operations such as:

- get Provider,

- list Providers,

- query by Capability,

- get Products,

- list Provider Accounts,

- inspect integration maturity,

- inspect terms status,

- inspect health summary,

- and inspect lifecycle.

Administrative mutation requires privileged authority.

8.225 Registry Source of Truth

The Provider Registry shall have an authoritative governed source.

Derived views may exist in:

- runtime cache,

- documentation,

- Atlas Knowledge,

- Intelligence Graph,

- dashboards,

- and SDKs.

Derived views shall declare freshness.

8.226 Provider Registry Snapshot

An immutable Snapshot may preserve:

- Provider metadata,

- Account relationships,

- lifecycle,

- terms versions,

- and integration states

at a point in time.

Executions may reference the relevant Snapshot or component versions.

8.227 Provider Registry Cache

Caches may accelerate routing.

Critical changes such as:

- suspension,

- credential compromise,

- rights restriction,

- or Provider disablement

must invalidate caches rapidly.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.228 Provider Registry Backup

Provider identity, Account history, terms, incidents and provenance shall be backed up.

Loss would impair:

- cost reconciliation,

- historical execution,

- rights,

- and provider migration.

8.229 Provider Registry Export

Exports may support:

- documentation,

- disaster recovery,

- audit,

- SDK generation,

- and Atlas Knowledge.

Exports shall declare scope and freshness.

8.230 Provider Registry Import

Imported Provider definitions shall be:

- validated,

- checked for duplicates,

- reviewed,

- and prevented from automatic production admission.

8.231 Provider Registry Federation

Future Omnira deployments may federate Provider metadata across:

- user nodes,

- Tenants,

- customer environments,

- and Omnira-managed cloud.

Federation must preserve:

- local Account privacy,

- canonical Provider identity,

- restrictions,

- and authority.

8.232 Tenant-Private Provider

A Tenant may connect a Provider unavailable to other Tenants.

The Provider identity may be global while the Account and integration remain private.

In some cases, the Provider itself may remain Tenant-private.

8.233 Project-Private Provider

A Project may use a specialised Provider relationship not visible elsewhere.

Its credentials, Accounts, Assets and cost remain Project-scoped.

8.234 Local Provider Registration

A local runtime or service may be registered as a Provider relationship for one user or Tenant.

The Registry shall preserve:

- operator,

- Node,

- Runtime,

- scope,

- and trust.

8.235 Provider Package

Future integrations may be distributed as Provider Packages containing:

- Provider metadata,

- Adapter,

- Capability mappings,

- schemas,

- tests,

- and documentation.

Installing a package shall not automatically:

- connect credentials,

- accept terms,

- grant permissions,

- or activate production.

8.236 Provider Package Trust

Packages may be:

- Omnira official,

- Provider official,

- verified partner,

- community,

- local private,

- or untrusted.

Trust affects review and sandboxing.

8.237 Provider Package Update

Updates may change:

- Adapter,

- tools,

- permissions,

- Capability mappings,

- or security.

Material update requires review before production activation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.238 Provider Package Removal

Removing an integration package must not erase historical Provider or Execution identity.

8.239 Provider Recommendation

The Fabric may recommend Provider classes or specific Providers during approval.

Recommendations should explain relevant trade-offs such as:

- quality,

- cost,

- privacy,

- reliability,

- commercial rights,

- and lock-in.

Recommendations are not authority.

8.240 Provider Explanation

The system should be able to explain:

- why a Provider is eligible,

- why it was selected,

- which Account will be used,

- what data will be sent,

- what it may cost,

- and what restrictions apply.

8.241 Provider Selection Decision

Provider selection shall be recorded through a Selection Decision.

The decision should reference:

- Capability,

- eligible Providers,

- Provider Accounts,

- Models or Tools,

- policy,

- quality,

- cost,

- latency,

- health,

- and fallback.

8.242 Provider Eligibility Decision

Eligibility shall consider:

- lifecycle,

- Account,

- Connection,

- Capability support,

- data class,

- region,

- rights,

- authority,

- budget,

- health,

- and restrictions.

8.243 Provider Ranking

Ranking occurs only after eligibility.

A high-ranked but ineligible Provider shall not be selected.

8.244 Provider Fallback

Fallback may move to another Provider when:

- original Provider fails,

- Account exhausts credits,

- Model becomes unavailable,

- or deadline risk rises.

Fallback shall preserve:

- data classification,

- rights,

- quality,

- budget,

- and approval.

8.245 Same-Provider Fallback

Fallback may remain within one Provider by changing:

- Model,

- Product,

- Account,

- Deployment,

- or region.

These changes still require eligibility evaluation.

8.246 Cross-Provider Fallback

Cross-Provider fallback changes:

- terms,

- Account,

- pricing,

- data processing,

- and Provider evidence.

It must be recorded.

8.247 Provider Substitution Disclosure

Material Provider substitution should be disclosed when it affects:

- user expectation,

- privacy,

- cost,

- quality,

- rights,

- or reproducibility.

8.248 No Commission-Driven Provider Routing

Omnira shall not prefer a Provider merely because Omnira receives:

- commission,

- margin,

- credit,

- referral benefit,

- or commercial partnership.

Commercial benefit must not silently override user value.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.249 Provider Commercial Relationship

The Registry may record:

- partner,

- reseller,

- affiliate,

- customer,

- negotiated contract,

- or ordinary subscriber relationship.

Commercial relationships shall remain transparent to governance.

8.250 Provider Conflict of Interest

A conflict may exist when Provider recommendation benefits Omnira financially.

Relevant decision systems should preserve and disclose the conflict where material.

8.251 Provider Marketplace Governance

A future Provider marketplace shall not:

- grant automatic production access,

- hide Provider margin,

- weaken quality,

- or reduce user control.

Marketplace discovery and Fabric eligibility remain separate.

8.252 Provider Competition

The Fabric should preserve multiple eligible Providers where this improves:

- resilience,

- cost,

- quality,

- and negotiation.

Provider diversity shall not be pursued at the expense of governance or maintainability.

8.253 Provider Consolidation

Using fewer Providers may reduce:

- complexity,

- contracts,

- credentials,

- and maintenance.

Consolidation may be appropriate when it does not create unacceptable lock-in or quality loss.

8.254 Provider Portfolio

Omnira may maintain a Provider Portfolio balancing:

- local resources,

- user-owned Accounts,

- managed Providers,

- premium specialists,

- and fallback services.

The Portfolio shall reflect actual Capability needs.

8.255 Provider Portfolio Review

Portfolio review may assess:

- unused Providers,

- duplicate subscriptions,

- cost,

- lock-in,

- security,

- quality,

- and current demand.

8.256 Unused Provider

A Provider relationship with no current justified use may be:

- restricted,

- disconnected,

- or retired.

Credentials should not remain active without need.

8.257 Duplicate Provider Coverage

Several Providers may supply the same Capability.

The Fabric should determine whether each relationship creates distinct value.

8.258 Provider Cost Duplication

Multiple subscriptions may create unnecessary fixed cost.

The Fabric may recommend consolidation while respecting:

- fallback,

- rights,

- and Project requirements.

8.259 Provider Asset Portability

Provider-stored Assets should be exportable where possible.

Portability metadata may include:

- export format,

- metadata export,

- batch export,

- API support,

- and deletion.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.260 Provider Prompt Portability

Provider-specific prompt formats may reduce portability.

Canonical prompts and Instruction Sets should remain in Omnira.

Provider adaptations belong in Adapters.

8.261 Provider Voice Portability

Voice Assets may be:

- exportable,

- Provider-locked,

- reproducible,

- or legally restricted.

This dependency must be visible.

8.262 Provider Character-System Portability

Creative Providers may store:

- character references,

- style profiles,

- or project-specific training.

The Registry should record:

- exportability,

- ownership,

- reusability,

- and Provider lock-in.

8.263 Provider Thread Portability

Provider-hosted threads or assistants may contain useful context.

They shall not become the only canonical Project memory.

Export and deletion behaviour should be known.

8.264 Provider Data Custody

Custody describes which Provider currently stores:

- Inputs,

- Outputs,

- Assets,

- threads,

- or metadata.

Custody is separate from ownership.

8.265 Provider Data Return

The Provider may return data through:

- synchronous response,

- callback,

- download URL,

- Asset library,

- export,

- or manual delivery.

The Fabric shall verify receipt and integrity.

8.266 Provider Download Link

Temporary Provider download links may expire.

The Adapter shall record:

- expiry,

- authentication,

- checksum where possible,

- and ingestion status.

8.267 Provider Asset Ingestion

Provider output shall be ingested into Omnira-controlled storage when required.

Ingestion should preserve:

- Provider Asset ID,

- Execution,

- checksum,

- format,

- rights,

- and provenance.

8.268 Provider Asset Deletion After Ingestion

Provider-side deletion may be required after successful ingestion.

Deletion must remain a separate governed action.

8.269 Provider Callback Security

Callbacks shall require:

- authentication or signature validation,

- replay protection,

- correlation,

- deduplication,

- and schema validation.

Provider callback content is untrusted until verified.

8.270 Provider Callback Failure

Callback failure may require:

- polling,

- reconciliation,

- manual inspection,

- or unknown-outcome state.

The system shall not assume job failure.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.271 Provider Polling

Polling policy should consider:

- rate limit,

- latency,

- cost,

- Provider guidance,

- and deadline.

8.272 Provider Job Reconciliation

Reconciliation compares:

- Omnira Execution state,

- Provider job state,

- Provider Assets,

- usage,

- and billing.

Discrepancies shall be evidenced.

8.273 Provider Error Mapping

Adapters shall map Provider errors into canonical categories.

The Registry may preserve Provider-level error patterns.

Errors may include:

- authentication,

- quota,

- billing,

- policy rejection,

- unsupported Capability,

- rate limit,

- outage,

- malformed request,

- timeout,

- and unknown outcome.

8.274 Provider Error Ownership

The system shall distinguish:

- Provider failure,

- Account failure,

- Connection failure,

- Adapter defect,

- request defect,

- and policy rejection.

A generic Provider error is insufficient.

8.275 Provider Retry Guidance

Provider documentation may recommend retries.

Fabric retry policy remains authoritative.

Provider guidance is evidence, not permission to exceed budget or idempotency limits.

8.276 Provider Idempotency Support

The Registry or Adapter metadata shall record whether the Provider supports:

- idempotency key,

- duplicate suppression,

- job correlation,

- or no such control.

8.277 Provider Cancellation Support

Cancellation support shall describe:

- which job states are cancellable,

- effect on cost,

- response evidence,

- and completion verification.

8.278 Provider Unknown Outcome

Unknown outcome may occur when:

- request timed out,

- callback failed,

- Provider state unavailable,

- or billing appeared without output.

The Fabric shall preserve uncertainty until reconciliation.

8.279 Provider Manual Verification

Some outcomes may require a human to inspect:

- Provider dashboard,

- Account assets,

- billing,

- or public result.

Manual verification shall be recorded honestly.

8.280 Provider Documentation

Provider documentation should be linked or summarised through governed records.

Documentation may cover:

- APIs,

- Models,

- tools,

- terms,

- pricing,

- limits,

- and incidents.

Documentation freshness must be visible.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.281 Provider Knowledge for Atlas

Atlas may receive approved Provider knowledge sufficient to:

- explain broad trade-offs,

- understand integration state,

- and formulate Capability Requests.

Atlas should not need:

- raw keys,

- secret endpoints,

- or unrestricted account administration.

8.282 Provider Knowledge for Developers

Developers may require:

- Adapter contracts,

- sandbox setup,

- test Account,

- error mapping,

- and conformance requirements.

Production secrets remain inaccessible unless explicitly required.

8.283 Provider Knowledge for Operators

Operators may need:

- Account health,

- credits,

- running jobs,

- incidents,

- and recovery actions.

Operator views should remain Project- and Tenant-scoped.

8.284 Provider Knowledge for Approvers

Approvers should receive:

- proposed Provider,

- Account owner,

- data use,

- cost,

- rights,

- quality,

- and restrictions.

They do not need every technical endpoint detail.

8.285 Provider Registry and Capability Registry

The Capability Registry defines operations.

The Provider Registry identifies suppliers.

Capability Support Mappings connect Provider resources to canonical Capability Versions.

8.286 Provider Registry and Model Registry

The Model Registry defines Models, Versions and Deployments.

The Provider Registry defines the Provider and Account relationships through which those Models may be accessed.

8.287 Provider Registry and Credential Service

The Credential Service owns raw secrets.

The Provider Registry references:

- credential identity,

- status,

- owner,

- expiry,

- and scope.

8.288 Provider Registry and Adapter Registry

Adapters define Provider-specific execution translation.

The Provider Registry records which Adapters are approved for which Provider Products and Connections.

8.289 Provider Registry and Cost System

The Cost System owns:

- estimates,

- Usage Records,

- Cost Records,

- reservations,

- and reconciliation.

The Provider Registry supplies:

- Provider identity,

- Account,

- Product,

- credit system,

- and pricing references.

8.290 Provider Registry and Policy Engine

Policies may target:

- Provider,

- Provider Type,

- Account,

- region,

- Product,

- or integration maturity.

Policy evaluation occurs per request.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 8.298 Applied Example — OpenArt as a Multimodal Provider
text:
8.291 Provider Registry and Asset System

The Asset System owns durable Omnira Assets.

The Provider Registry preserves Provider custody, export and deletion relationships.

8.292 Provider Registry and Intelligence Graph

The Graph may represent:

- Provider,

- legal entity,

- Account,

- Product,

- Model,

- Connection,

- Adapter,

- Capability,

- Execution,

- Asset,

- Incident,

- and terms.

The Registry remains authoritative for Provider identity.

8.293 Provider Registry and Atlas Memory

Memory may contain governed Provider learnings.

The Provider Registry should reference accepted learning rather than store every execution observation as permanent Provider truth.

8.294 Provider Registry and Executive Intelligence

Executive Intelligence may use Provider evidence to assess:

- strategic dependency,

- cost,

- risk,

- and portfolio direction.

The Provider Registry does not decide business strategy.

8.295 Provider Registry and Managers

Managers may request Capabilities and review Provider trade-offs.

They do not own credentials or Provider governance.

8.296 Provider Registry and Agents

Agents may discover eligible Provider classes through the Fabric.

They shall not directly own Provider Accounts.

8.297 Provider Registry and Workflows

Workflows should reference Capabilities.

Provider pinning shall be explicit and validated through the Registry.

8.298 Applied Example — OpenArt as a Multimodal Provider

OpenArt may be represented as:

Provider

A specialised multimodal creative-production Provider.

Possible Service Families

- image generation,

- image editing,

- video generation,

- character-consistent production,

- and creative project tools.

Provider Accounts

- user-owned experimental account,

- future Familje-Stunden production account,

- or future Omnira-managed account.

Connections

- experimental MCP Connection,

- API Connection where supported,

- and human-assisted web workflow.

Models or Routed Resources

- specific selectable Models where visible,

- Provider-managed routed resources where exact Model identity is hidden.

Capability Mappings

- image.generate,

- image.edit,

- video.image_to_video,

- video.text_to_video,

- and potentially character-reference-related features.

Integration Maturity

An experimental Claude MCP connection shall remain classified as experimental or human-supervised until Omnira controls:

- identity,

- credentials,

- scope,

- cost,

- execution receipts,

- output ingestion,

- and failure handling.

The Provider Registry must not claim full Omnira production integration merely because Claude can invoke the service.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 8.301 Applied Example — ElevenLabs as a Voice Provider
8.302 Applied Example — Ideogram or Equivalent Image Provider
text:
8.299 OpenArt Account Boundary

The Provider Registry shall distinguish:

- André’s user-owned OpenArt Account,

- any Project-specific Workspace,

- any future Omnira-managed Account,

- and any development session.

Credits shall not be assumed interchangeable.

Project Assets shall not be mixed by convenience.

8.300 OpenArt Character Asset Boundary

Nova and Pling references may be stored or used through the Provider.

The Provider record shall preserve:

- Provider custody,

- Project ownership,

- input rights,

- reference versions,

- and exportability.

Provider-side character configuration shall not become the only canonical character source.

8.301 Applied Example — ElevenLabs as a Voice Provider

ElevenLabs or an equivalent voice Provider may be represented through:

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- speech Model or routed voice resource,

- approved Voice Asset,

- Consent Record,

- Subscription,

- credit balance,

- and speech Capabilities.

The Registry shall distinguish:

- Provider,

- speech Model,

- Voice identity,

- Project,

- and Account.

Voice cloning shall require stronger authority than ordinary synthesis.

8.302 Applied Example — Ideogram or Equivalent Image Provider

An image Provider may support:

- image.generate,

- image.edit,

- text rendering,

- brand graphics,

- and commercial image production.

The Provider Registry shall preserve:

- Product,

- Account,

- terms,

- Models,

- watermarking,

- rights,

- and integration maturity.

Provider popularity does not prove eligibility for every Project.

8.303 Applied Example — External Text Providers

Stage 1 may use at least two external text or reasoning Provider paths.

Each shall remain separate by:

- Provider,

- Account,

- Models,

- pricing,

- privacy,

- rights,

- and health.

The purpose is to prove:

- Provider independence,

- routing,

- fallback,

- and evidence.

8.304 Applied Example — Local Ollama Provider

Ollama or an equivalent local runtime may be represented as:

Provider Type

Local runtime Provider.

Provider Account

Not necessarily a commercial account.

Connection

Local API or command-line relationship.

Deployments

Specific local Models on a Runtime Node.

Data Boundary

User-controlled local processing.

Cost

No direct Provider charge, with local compute cost represented separately.

The runtime is the Provider relationship.

The installed Model remains a separate Model Version and Deployment.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 8.305 Applied Example — NVIDIA-Hosted and Local Resources
8.307 Applied Example — The Prompt Provider Policy
8.311 Anti-Pattern — One Provider Entry Per API Key
text:
8.305 Applied Example — NVIDIA-Hosted and Local Resources

NVIDIA-related resources may appear through:

- hosted API,

- NIM container,

- local GPU Deployment,

- or partner platform.

The Registry shall distinguish:

- NVIDIA as Provider or technology supplier,

- actual hosting Provider,

- Model creator,

- Runtime,

- Deployment operator,

- and Provider Account.

8.306 Applied Example — Familje-Stunden Provider Policy

Familje-Stunden may permit:

- OpenArt for approved creative production,

- ElevenLabs for approved Swedish narration,

- another image Provider for selected graphics,

- and local tools for composition.

Its Provider policy may require:

- child-facing review,

- commercial rights,

- Project-specific Accounts,

- bounded cost,

- no publication without approval,

- and strong provenance.

8.307 Applied Example — The Prompt Provider Policy

The Prompt may permit:

- current-search Provider,

- external reasoning Providers,

- avatar Provider,

- voice Provider,

- and local editing tools.

Research Providers must be evaluated for:

- source freshness,

- citation quality,

- and reliability.

Visual Providers do not become factual authorities.

8.308 Applied Example — GainPilot Provider Policy

GainPilot may use:

- local or inexpensive text Providers,

- image Provider,

- voice Provider,

- and local composition tools.

The policy may optimise for Economy while preserving:

- brand quality,

- commercial rights,

- and Project isolation.

8.309 Applied Example — Omnira Development Providers

Omnira development may use:

- Claude,

- Codex,

- Gemini,

- local Models,

- repository tools,

- and search Providers.

The Provider Registry shall preserve:

- provider identity,

- connected Account,

- environment,

- code-data policy,

- and side-effect authority.

Access to code reasoning shall not imply permission to merge or deploy.

8.310 Anti-Pattern — Provider Name as Architecture

The Fabric must not define Project workflows directly around one Provider’s current product structure.

Provider integration belongs behind canonical Capabilities and Adapters.

8.311 Anti-Pattern — One Provider Entry Per API Key

API keys are credentials.

They do not create separate Provider identities.

Separate Provider Accounts may be appropriate when ownership or scope differs.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 8.314 Anti-Pattern — Provider Account as Agent Identity
8.315 Anti-Pattern — Provider Workspace as Project Authority
8.316 Anti-Pattern — Provider Marketing as Verified Capability
8.318 Anti-Pattern — One Global Provider Eligibility Flag
8.319 Anti-Pattern — Personal Credits as Silent Fallback
8.321 Anti-Pattern — Development Session as Production Integration
8.323 Anti-Pattern — Provider Health as Capability Eligibility
8.326 Anti-Pattern — Provider Asset Library as Canonical Storage
text:
8.312 Anti-Pattern — Provider Equals Account

Combining Provider and Account would destroy:

- ownership,

- billing,

- region,

- scope,

- and lifecycle distinctions.

8.313 Anti-Pattern — Connected Means Approved

A successful OAuth or MCP Connection does not prove:

- production admission,

- acceptable terms,

- correct scope,

- or safe data processing.

8.314 Anti-Pattern — Provider Account as Agent Identity

A Provider assistant or Account name must not become an Omnira Agent identity.

8.315 Anti-Pattern — Provider Workspace as Project Authority

A workspace label is not sufficient to establish Project scope.

Scope must resolve through Omnira identity.

8.316 Anti-Pattern — Provider Marketing as Verified Capability

Marketing claims may support research.

They do not establish verified Capability support.

8.317 Anti-Pattern — Provider Terms as Permanent

Terms change.

The Registry must preserve versions and review.

8.318 Anti-Pattern — One Global Provider Eligibility Flag

Eligibility depends on:

- request,

- Project,

- Account,

- Capability,

- data,

- rights,

- budget,

- region,

- and health.

8.319 Anti-Pattern — Personal Credits as Silent Fallback

The Fabric shall not silently use the user’s personal Provider credits when Project or Omnira capacity is exhausted.

8.320 Anti-Pattern — Shared Account Without Attribution

Shared Accounts must preserve:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- usage,

- and cost attribution.

8.321 Anti-Pattern — Development Session as Production Integration

A Claude or IDE MCP session shall not be treated as the Omnira production Provider integration.

8.322 Anti-Pattern — Human-Assisted as Fully Automated

Manual Provider steps must remain visible.

8.323 Anti-Pattern — Provider Health as Capability Eligibility

A healthy Provider may be ineligible.

An eligible Provider may be temporarily unhealthy.

8.324 Anti-Pattern — Provider Retirement Deletes History

Retirement must preserve:

- accounts,

- costs,

- assets,

- terms,

- incidents,

- and Executions.

8.325 Anti-Pattern — Commercial Partnership Controls Routing

Provider margin or referral benefit shall not silently determine selection.

8.326 Anti-Pattern — Provider Asset Library as Canonical Storage

Provider Assets must be ingested or referenced through the Asset architecture.

The Provider dashboard is not Omnira’s canonical Asset system.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 8.327 Anti-Pattern — Provider Thread as Long-Term Memory
8.328 Anti-Pattern — Broad OAuth Scope by Convenience
8.330 Anti-Pattern — Opaque Provider Router as Fixed Model
text:
8.327 Anti-Pattern — Provider Thread as Long-Term Memory

Provider-hosted conversations shall not become the only persistent Project memory.

8.328 Anti-Pattern — Broad OAuth Scope by Convenience

Connections should request the minimum permissions necessary.

8.329 Anti-Pattern — Provider Deletion Assumed

Disconnecting credentials does not prove that Provider-side data was deleted.

8.330 Anti-Pattern — Opaque Provider Router as Fixed Model

Provider-managed routing opacity must remain visible.

8.331 Stage 1 Provider Registry Objective

Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy Provider Registry required to support representative intelligence Providers.

The objective is not to integrate every Provider.

Stage 1 shall prove:

- stable Provider identity,

- Account separation,

- Connection separation,

- terms and privacy metadata,

- Capability relationships,

- lifecycle,

- health references,

- cost attribution,

- and governed production admission.

8.332 Stage 1 Initial Provider Classes

Stage 1 should include representative Provider classes such as:

- local runtime Provider,

- at least two external text or reasoning Providers,

- voice Provider,

- image Provider,

- multimodal or video Provider,

- and simulation or test Provider.

8.333 Stage 1 Provider Objects

Stage 1 should implement or represent:

- Provider,

- Provider Product,

- Provider Account,

- Provider Workspace reference,

- Provider Subscription,

- Provider Connection,

- Provider Terms Record,

- Privacy Profile,

- Trust Level,

- Lifecycle,

- Capability Claim,

- Health State,

- and Production Admission Record.

8.334 Stage 1 Provider Fields

Stage 1 Provider entries should include at least:

- providerId,

- canonical name,

- Provider Type,

- legal or service identity where known,

- lifecycle,

- trust,

- risk,

- regions,

- terms reference,

- privacy reference,

- integration maturity,

- supported resource classes,

- and provenance.

8.335 Stage 1 Account Fields

Stage 1 Provider Account records should include:

- providerAccountId,

- providerId,

- owner,

- Tenant,

- Project restrictions,

- environment,

- subscription tier,

- billing relationship,

- region,

- credential reference,

- Connection references,

- lifecycle,

- credits or quota reference,

- and provenance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.336 Stage 1 Connection Fields

Stage 1 Connections should include:

- connectionId,

- Provider Account,

- protocol,

- environment,

- credential reference,

- permission scope,

- lifecycle,

- health,

- and Adapter reference.

8.337 Stage 1 Terms Fields

Stage 1 should preserve:

- Terms Version or retrieval date,

- commercial-use status,

- retention summary,

- training-use summary,

- region summary,

- prohibited-use summary,

- and review status.

8.338 Stage 1 Integration Maturity

Stage 1 shall distinguish:

- manual external,

- human-assisted,

- experimental MCP,

- experimental API,

- production MCP,

- production API,

- and local production.

8.339 Stage 1 Provider API

The Registry should support:

- get Provider,

- list approved Providers,

- get Provider Account,

- list Accounts by Project or Tenant,

- get Connection status,

- inspect terms review status,

- inspect integration maturity,

- inspect current health,

- and query Providers by Capability.

8.340 Stage 1 Selection Support

The Registry shall provide routing with:

- Provider identity,

- eligible Accounts,

- environment,

- region,

- integration maturity,

- terms status,

- trust,

- health reference,

- and restrictions.

8.341 Stage 1 OpenArt Classification

Until Omnira controls a production-grade connection, OpenArt should be represented according to actual maturity, such as:

- Provider approved for pilot,

- user-owned experimental Account,

- experimental MCP or human-assisted Connection,

- selected creative Capabilities,

- paid execution requiring bounded approval,

- and no automatic publication.

8.342 Stage 1 Voice Provider Classification

The first voice Provider should be represented with:

- Account,

- speech resource,

- Voice Asset relationships,

- consent requirements,

- credits,

- rights,

- and human review.

8.343 Stage 1 Image Provider Classification

The first image Provider should include:

- commercial-use review,

- Account scope,

- Model or routed resource relationship,

- image Capabilities,

- output rights,

- and quality evidence.

8.344 Stage 1 Local Provider Classification

The local Provider should include:

- Runtime,

- Runtime Node,

- local Connection,

- privacy boundary,

- installed Models,

- health,

- and no direct Provider billing.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.345 Stage 1 Provider Acceptance Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Provider remains distinct from Provider Account.

2. Provider Account remains distinct from Connection.

3. Provider remains distinct from Model.

4. Provider remains distinct from Adapter.

5. Connected Account is not automatically production approved.

6. Personal and Project Accounts remain distinct.

7. Shared Account usage is attributed by Project.

8. Missing account scope does not become global.

9. Provider terms are versioned or date-preserved.

10. Privacy metadata remains Account- and Product-aware.

11. Moving Provider data is marked stale when not refreshed.

12. Provider lifecycle remains distinct from health.

13. Provider health remains distinct from Capability eligibility.

14. Experimental MCP remains classified as experimental.

15. Manual integration remains human-assisted.

16. Provider suspension blocks new execution.

17. Provider retirement preserves historical evidence.

18. Provider Account exhaustion affects only relevant routing.

19. Cross-Provider fallback is evidenced.

20. Provider selection identifies the exact Account used.

8.346 Stage 1 Security Tests

Representative security tests should include:

1. Raw secrets do not appear in Registry records.

2. Provider Accounts cannot be read across Tenants.

3. Project Account credentials cannot be used by another Project.

4. Development Connection cannot execute production work.

5. Broad MCP tools require explicit permissions.

6. Callback signatures are verified.

7. Duplicate callbacks do not duplicate outputs.

8. Revoked credentials block new work.

9. Provider discovery does not grant connection authority.

10. Provider Package installation does not activate credentials.

11. Local Providers do not expose private Node data globally.

12. Suspended Provider cache entries invalidate safely.

13. Provider Workspace name does not establish Project scope.

14. Provider output remains subject to validation.

15. Terms acceptance requires authorised Principal.

8.347 Stage 1 Privacy Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Local Only data excludes external Providers.

2. Confidential data requires approved Provider configuration.

3. Unknown processing region blocks restricted routing.

4. Training-use prohibition is enforced.

5. Provider retention incompatibility blocks the request.

6. Provider-side deletion remains separate from local disconnection.

7. Project data does not enter another Project workspace.

8. Operational logs do not expose full protected Provider payloads.

9. Account owner and data owner remain separate.

10. Provider privacy change triggers review.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.348 Stage 1 Cost Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Provider Account identifies billing source.

2. Credits are observed with freshness.

3. Personal credits are not silent fallback.

4. Project cost attribution survives shared Account use.

5. Estimated and confirmed Provider cost remain separate.

6. Retry cost is recorded.

7. Account exhaustion blocks or reroutes safely.

8. Subscription-included capacity is not treated as unlimited.

9. Promotional-credit expiry is represented.

10. Billing Incident remains distinct from Provider outage.

8.349 Stage 1 Reliability Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Provider outage affects health without retiring Provider.

2. Account authentication failure remains Account-scoped.

3. Connection failure remains Connection-scoped.

4. Model failure does not mark every Provider Product unavailable.

5. Cross-Provider fallback respects policy.

6. Provider timeout may become unknown outcome.

7. Callback failure triggers reconciliation.

8. Provider recovery requires fresh evidence.

9. Rate limits affect scheduling.

10. Maintenance state is visible.

8.350 Stage 1 Governance Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Discovered Provider cannot be selected for production.

2. Experimental Provider is limited to approved data and budget.

3. Production admission identifies exact Accounts and Connections.

4. Terms change can suspend affected execution.

5. Provider deprecation includes migration.

6. Offboarding revokes credentials after reconciliation.

7. Historical terms remain queryable.

8. Provider merge preserves aliases and history.

9. Provider commercial relationship does not alter mandatory routing.

10. Administrative mutation requires privileged authority.

8.351 Provider Registry Conformance Requirements

An implementation conforms to this chapter only when:

- Provider identity is stable,

- Provider Accounts are explicit,

- Connections are explicit,

- credentials remain external,

- integration maturity is truthful,

- terms and privacy are version-aware,

- Account ownership and scope are explicit,

- Capability claims remain separate from verified support,

- health remains separate from eligibility,

- cost is attributable,

- lifecycle is governed,

- and Provider removal preserves historical truth.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.352 Canonical Provider Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Provider contract:

1. A Provider SHALL represent a stable supplier identity.

2. Provider SHALL remain distinct from Provider Account.

3. Provider SHALL remain distinct from Model.

4. Provider SHALL remain distinct from Connection.

5. Provider SHALL remain distinct from Adapter.

6. Provider SHALL remain distinct from credential.

7. Provider SHALL remain distinct from Agent and Project.

8. Every persistent Provider SHALL have stable canonical identity.

9. Provider aliases and legal names SHALL remain separately represented.

10. Provider Type SHALL be explicit.

11. Provider lifecycle SHALL be explicit and versioned.

12. Provider trust and risk SHALL be evidence-based.

13. Provider terms SHALL preserve version or retrieval evidence.

14. Provider privacy SHALL remain Product-, Account- and region-aware.

15. Provider capability claims SHALL remain distinct from verified support.

16. Provider health SHALL remain distinct from eligibility.

17. Provider availability SHALL remain request-specific.

18. Provider commercial relationships SHALL NOT silently control routing.

19. Provider lock-in SHALL remain visible.

20. Provider exit and portability SHOULD be evaluated.

21. Provider Incidents SHALL preserve scope and evidence.

22. Provider deprecation and retirement SHALL preserve history.

23. Provider discovery SHALL NOT create production admission.

24. Provider integration maturity SHALL be represented truthfully.

25. External Providers SHALL remain outside Omnira’s trusted core.

8.353 Canonical Provider Account Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Provider Account contract:

1. Every operational Provider relationship SHALL use an explicit Provider Account or equivalent governed account context.

2. Provider Account SHALL identify its owner.

3. Provider Account SHALL identify Tenant scope.

4. Project restrictions SHALL be explicit.

5. Provider Account SHALL identify environment.

6. Provider Account SHALL identify billing relationship.

7. Provider Account SHALL identify subscription or Product where relevant.

8. Provider Account SHALL reference credentials without exposing secrets.

9. Provider Account SHALL reference active Connections.

10. Provider Account lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

11. Account quota and credit evidence SHALL declare freshness.

12. Personal Accounts SHALL NOT be used as silent fallback.

13. Shared Accounts SHALL preserve Project cost attribution.

14. Sandbox and production Accounts SHALL remain distinct.

15. Revoked Accounts SHALL block new execution.

16. Disconnecting Omnira SHALL NOT be represented as Provider-side data deletion.

17. Account ownership SHALL remain separate from Project data ownership.

18. Account substitution SHALL be evidenced.

19. Account scope SHALL fail closed when unresolved.

20. Historical Account relationships SHALL remain interpretable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.354 Canonical Provider Connection Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Connection contract:

1. Every automated Provider access path SHALL use an explicit Connection.

2. Connection SHALL identify Provider and Account.

3. Connection SHALL identify protocol.

4. Connection SHALL identify environment.

5. Connection SHALL reference credential identity.

6. Connection SHALL define permitted operations.

7. Connection lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

8. Connection health SHALL declare freshness.

9. API, MCP, OAuth, webhook, local and human-assisted Connections SHALL remain distinguishable.

10. Connected SHALL NOT mean production approved.

11. Development Connections SHALL NOT silently execute production work.

12. Callback Connections SHALL verify authenticity and deduplicate events.

13. Connection failure SHALL NOT redefine Provider identity.

14. Revoked Connections SHALL block new execution.

15. Human-assisted Connections SHALL remain truthfully labelled.

8.355 Canonical Provider Registry Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Provider Registry contract:

1. The Provider Registry SHALL be the authoritative catalogue of Provider identities known to Omnira.

2. The Registry SHALL preserve Provider lifecycle history.

3. The Registry SHALL preserve Provider Products and Service Families where material.

4. The Registry SHALL preserve Provider Account relationships.

5. The Registry SHALL preserve Connection relationships.

6. The Registry SHALL preserve terms, privacy and trust evidence.

7. The Registry SHALL reference canonical Capabilities.

8. The Registry SHALL reference Model, Tool and Adapter resources.

9. The Registry SHALL support governed discovery.

10. Discovery SHALL NOT grant execution authority.

11. Registry mutation SHALL require governance authority.

12. Registry projections and caches SHALL declare freshness.

13. Historical Providers SHALL remain resolvable after retirement.

14. The Registry SHALL support Incidents, restriction and suspension.

15. The Registry SHALL support Provider onboarding and offboarding.

16. The Registry SHALL support Tenant-, Project- and user-owned Accounts.

17. The Registry SHALL support local, external, managed and human-assisted Providers.

18. The Registry SHALL NOT contain raw secrets.

19. The Registry SHALL distinguish architectural definition from operational availability.

20. The Registry SHALL remain suitable for human and machine consumers.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.356 Provider Registry Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No Provider becomes an Agent identity.

- No Provider Account becomes the Provider itself.

- No Connection becomes proof of production approval.

- No credential becomes Provider identity.

- No Provider claim becomes verified Capability support without evidence.

- No healthy Provider bypasses data, rights or authority policy.

- No shared Account hides Project usage.

- No personal Account becomes silent platform capacity.

- No development MCP session becomes a hidden production dependency.

- No manual Provider workflow is represented as autonomous.

- No Provider Workspace name replaces canonical Project scope.

- No Provider terms are treated as permanently stable.

- No Provider retirement deletes historical provenance.

- No commercial relationship silently overrides user value.

- No Provider-side Asset library becomes Omnira’s canonical Asset system.

- No Provider-hosted thread becomes the only long-term memory.

- No unknown region or retention state becomes favourable by default.

- No Provider fallback weakens the original request contract.

- No Provider disconnection is misrepresented as verified data deletion.

- No Provider receives authority beyond the bounded execution submitted to it.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
8.357 Closing Statement

The Provider Registry gives Omnira a governed understanding of the organisations, services, runtimes and operational relationships that supply intelligence resources.

It separates:

- Provider from Account,

- Account from Connection,

- Connection from credential,

- Provider from Model,

- Model from Deployment,

- Provider from Adapter,

- and Provider access from execution authority.

This separation is essential because Provider relationships are not static.

Brands change.

Terms change.

Products change.

Prices change.

Models appear and disappear.

Credits expire.

Sessions break.

Accounts become suspended.

APIs evolve.

MCP servers expose new tools.

Provider workspaces accumulate Assets.

Commercial partnerships create incentives.

A development integration may appear functional long before it is safe for production.

The Provider Registry ensures that these changes remain governed at the supplier layer rather than leaking into every Project, Agent and Workflow.

For Familje-Stunden, it allows OpenArt, ElevenLabs and image Providers to support Nova and Pling production without owning the characters, the Project, the memory or the publication authority.

For The Prompt, it allows research, reasoning, avatar, voice and media Providers to remain separate from editorial truth.

For GainPilot, it allows economical Provider choices without creating an isolated provider architecture.

For Omnira, it allows local Models, user-owned subscriptions, managed credits and external services to coexist within one controlled intelligence portfolio.

The Capability Registry defines what must be done.

The Model Registry defines which intelligence resources may perform it.

The Provider Registry defines who supplies access and under which relationship.

The Provider Account defines whose access and billing are used.

The Connection defines how Omnira communicates.

The Adapter defines how canonical meaning is translated.

Policy defines whether the relationship is permitted.

Routing selects the eligible path.

Evidence records what actually occurred.

The Provider supplies capability.

The Provider does not own the intent.

The Provider does not own the Agent.

The Provider does not own the Project.

The Provider does not own Omnira’s intelligence architecture.

The user retains direction.

Omnira retains governance.

The Fabric retains the boundary.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical architecture, object model, lifecycle, governance boundaries and Registry contracts for Agents, Tools and Execution Resources within the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

It establishes:

- how Agents are represented as persistent Omnira identities rather than Model instances,

- how Agent identity remains independent from Provider, Model, Runtime and Session,

- how Tools are represented as governed executable resources,

- how deterministic Tools remain distinct from Models and Agents,

- how MCP-discovered Tools enter the same canonical Tool model,

- how local commands, APIs, browser actions, databases, search systems and device operations may become Tools,

- how execution infrastructure is represented independently from the intelligence it hosts,

- how Runtime Nodes, Runtime Services, Execution Environments and Resource Pools are registered,

- how local, cloud, private, edge and human-assisted resources coexist,

- how capabilities are bound to Agents, Tools and execution resources,

- how resource ownership, Project scope, Tenant scope and Environment remain explicit,

- how lifecycle, Version, availability, health and qualification remain separate concepts,

- how discovery differs from registration,

- how registration differs from approval,

- how approval differs from execution eligibility,

- how execution eligibility depends on current policy and context,

- how authority remains external to resource existence,

- how side effects are classified,

- how permissions and access requirements are represented without embedding raw Secrets,

- how resource dependencies are represented,

- how scheduling and placement metadata are exposed,

- how cost and capacity metadata are attached,

- how trust and certification evidence are represented,

- how resource drift is detected,

- how compromised or stale resources are suspended,

- how resources are deprecated and retired,

- how Agents may call Tools only through governed Plans and authority,

- how Tools may never self-authorise,

- how Tools may never become policy simply because they describe themselves as capable,

- how Agent-to-Agent execution resources are represented,

- how human operators and human-assisted execution are represented truthfully,

- how Stage 1 shall implement the minimum viable Registry foundation,

- and how future resources can be introduced without altering the canonical architecture.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

Chapter 10 defines how registered capabilities and resources are assembled into Intelligence Plans and Execution Graphs.

Later chapters define Routing, cost, Quality, reliability, scheduling, integrations, Credentials, local intelligence, authority, observability and conformance in greater depth.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.2 Purpose

Omnira must understand not only which Models and Providers exist.

It must also understand:

- which Agents exist,

- which Tools exist,

- where work may execute,

- which Runtime hosts which resource,

- which resources are available now,

- which resources are allowed for one Project,

- which resources produce side effects,

- which resources require approval,

- which resources are local,

- which resources are external,

- which resources are human-operated,

- and which resources remain safe and qualified for use.

Without canonical resource Registries, Omnira could:

- confuse an Agent with the Model currently powering it,

- grant new authority merely because a new Tool appears,

- expose arbitrary MCP Tools automatically,

- call local commands outside their intended Project,

- send a job to an offline Node,

- choose a Runtime that lacks required hardware,

- execute a publication Tool when only generation was authorised,

- mix personal and Project browser Sessions,

- treat a human-assisted service as autonomous,

- or allow a compromised resource to remain eligible because it still responds.

The Registry architecture exists so the Fabric can answer:

- What resource is this?

- Who owns it?

- What type of resource is it?

- What Version is active?

- What Capabilities does it expose?

- Under which conditions?

- In which Environment?

- For which Tenant and Project?

- Through which Runtime?

- With which dependencies?

- What side effects can it create?

- What authority is required?

- What data may it process?

- What does it cost?

- What capacity does it have?

- Is it healthy?

- Is it certified?

- Has it drifted?

- Is it currently eligible?

9.3 Resource

A Resource is a registered entity that may participate in intelligence planning or execution.

9.4 Resource Classes

Canonical Resource classes include:

- Agent Resource,

- Tool Resource,

- Model Resource,

- Provider Resource,

- Execution Resource,

- Runtime Node,

- Runtime Service,

- Human Resource,

- External Agent Resource,

- and Resource Pool.

9.5 Registry

A Registry is the canonical source of metadata describing one Resource class or related resource domain.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.6 Resource Registration

Registration makes a Resource known to Omnira.

Registration does not make the Resource automatically eligible for production use.

9.7 Discovery

Discovery identifies a possible Resource.

Discovery is not registration.

9.8 Qualification

Qualification evaluates whether a registered Resource satisfies defined requirements.

9.9 Certification

Certification provides evidence-backed eligibility for defined scopes and uses.

9.10 Execution Eligibility

Execution Eligibility is a contextual Decision that a Resource may participate in one specific Plan or Attempt.

Eligibility is determined at execution time from:

- Registry state,

- policy,

- Classification,

- authority,

- health,

- capacity,

- certification,

- Budget,

- and Request constraints.

9.11 Resource Identity

Every canonical Resource shall have a stable Resource identity.

9.12 Resource Version
