Every materially mutable Resource definition shall have a Version.

9.13 Resource Instance

A Resource Instance is one concrete operational instance of a Resource definition.

9.14 Resource Definition Versus Instance

A Tool definition may describe one operation.

Several deployed Tool Instances may implement it.

A Model definition may describe one Model.

Several Deployments may serve it.

An Agent definition may describe one Agent identity.

Several Sessions or Runtime processes may execute it.

9.15 Resource Ownership

Every Resource shall identify an ownership model.

9.16 Ownership Types

Ownership may include:

- user-owned,

- Project-owned,

- Tenant-owned,

- Omnira-owned,

- Provider-owned,

- device-owned,

- organisation-owned,

- and externally-operated.

9.17 Ownership Is Not Authority

Owning a Resource does not automatically authorise every operation through it.

9.18 Resource Scope

Resources may be scoped by:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- device,

- Account,

- Runtime,

- region,

- or Capability.

9.19 Global Resource

A Resource may be globally discoverable while remaining conditionally eligible.

9.20 Project Resource

A Project Resource is intended for one Project or defined Project set.

9.21 Tenant Resource

A Tenant Resource may be shared among authorised Projects within one Tenant.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.22 Personal Resource

A Personal Resource belongs to one user.

Personal ownership shall not make it available to Projects automatically.

9.23 Environment Scope

Resource definitions shall distinguish:

- development,

- test,

- staging,

- production,

- recovery,

- and other governed Environments.

9.24 Cross-Environment Use

A production Plan shall not use a development Resource merely because schemas are compatible.

9.25 Resource State

Every Resource shall have a lifecycle state.

9.26 Canonical Resource Lifecycle

States may include:

- discovered,

- proposed,

- registered,

- validating,

- qualified,

- active,

- degraded,

- suspended,

- deprecated,

- retired,

- revoked,

- unavailable,

- and archived.

9.27 Discovered

The Resource has been observed but not admitted.

9.28 Proposed

The Resource is being considered for registration.

9.29 Registered

The Resource exists in the canonical Registry.

9.30 Validating

Technical and governance validation is in progress.

9.31 Qualified

Required baseline checks have passed.

9.32 Active

The Resource may become eligible when contextual policy permits.

9.33 Degraded

The Resource remains partially usable but has known limitations.

9.34 Suspended

The Resource shall not receive new production work until reviewed.

9.35 Deprecated

The Resource remains supported temporarily but should not receive new adoption.

9.36 Retired

The Resource shall not receive new work.

9.37 Revoked

The Resource has lost authority, trust or access and is explicitly blocked.

9.38 Unavailable

The Resource cannot currently execute.

Unavailability is operational rather than necessarily governance-related.

9.39 Archived

The Resource remains available for historical interpretation only.

9.40 Resource Lifecycle Evidence

Every material state transition shall be attributable.

9.41 Availability

Availability describes whether a Resource can currently receive work.

9.42 Availability Is Not Lifecycle

An active Resource may be unavailable.

A deprecated Resource may still be technically available.

9.43 Health

Health describes observed fitness to serve.

9.44 Health Is Not Eligibility

A healthy Resource may still be ineligible because of:

- privacy,

- Project scope,

- authority,

- Budget,

- rights,

- or policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.45 Capability Binding

A Capability Binding declares that a Resource may satisfy a canonical Capability under stated conditions.

9.46 Binding Identity

Every material Capability Binding should have stable identity and Version.

9.47 Binding Conditions

Conditions may include:

- supported Input types,

- Output types,

- context limits,

- required Runtime,

- required Account,

- Classification maximum,

- side effects,

- cost model,

- and certification.

9.48 Binding Claim

A Resource owner or Adapter may claim support for a Capability.

Claims do not become trusted production facts without validation.

9.49 Binding Evidence

Capability Bindings should reference supporting evidence.

9.50 Unsupported Capability

A Resource shall reject unsupported Capability use before consequential execution.

9.51 Resource Metadata

Canonical resource metadata should include:

- identity,

- type,

- Version,

- owner,

- scope,

- lifecycle,

- capabilities,

- dependencies,

- Runtime,

- health,

- cost,

- authority requirements,

- side effects,

- Classification limits,

- provenance,

- and certification.

9.52 Resource Tag

Tags may assist search and administration.

Tags shall not determine authority by themselves.

9.53 Resource Label

Human-readable labels may change without changing identity.

9.54 Resource Alias

Aliases may exist for convenience.

Canonical identity shall remain stable.

9.55 Alias Collision

Aliases shall not create ambiguous resource resolution.

9.56 Resource Provenance

The Registry should preserve how and when a Resource definition entered Omnira.

9.57 Resource Source

Sources may include:

- manual registration,

- Adapter discovery,

- MCP discovery,

- local Runtime discovery,

- deployment manifest,

- configuration,

- or migration import.

9.58 Imported Resource

Imported legacy Resources shall retain import provenance and uncertainty.

9.59 Agent Resource

An Agent Resource represents a persistent Omnira intelligence actor with:

- identity,

- role,

- policy,

- Memory access,

- Tool access,

- authority boundaries,

- and operational configuration.

9.60 Agent Identity

Agent identity is owned by Omnira.

9.61 Agent Identity Independence

Agent identity shall remain independent from:

- Provider,

- Model,

- Deployment,

- Runtime,

- Session,

- Tool set,

- and physical Node.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.62 Agent Example

Atlas remains Atlas when execution changes from one external reasoning Model to another.

9.63 Agent Example Two

Arnold remains Arnold when coaching reasoning moves from cloud inference to a local Model.

9.64 Agent Definition

An Agent Definition describes the canonical Agent.

It should include:

- agentId,

- name,

- role,

- owner,

- Tenant,

- default Project relationships,

- policy profile,

- Memory Domains,

- Tool policy,

- Authority Level,

- escalation rules,

- lifecycle,

- and Version.

9.65 Agent Definition Identity

Every Agent Definition shall have stable identity and Version.

9.66 Agent Role

The role defines the Agent’s intended function.

Examples include:

- executive coordinator,

- coach,

- researcher,

- creative producer,

- reviewer,

- coding Agent,

- and workflow operator.

9.67 Role Is Not Authority

A descriptive role shall not grant permissions automatically.

9.68 Agent Version

Material changes to:

- system instructions,

- role policy,

- allowed Tool classes,

- Memory access,

- or operating constraints

should create a new Agent Version.

9.69 Model Swap

Changing the Model serving an Agent shall not necessarily create a new Agent identity.

9.70 Agent Session

An Agent Session represents one bounded interaction or execution context.

9.71 Agent Session Identity

Every material Session should have stable identity.

9.72 Agent Session State

Session state is temporary unless admitted into governed Memory.

9.73 Agent Session Scope

Session scope shall include:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- user,

- purpose,

- and current authority context.

9.74 Agent Runtime

An Agent Runtime is the execution environment hosting the Agent’s current process or inference orchestration.

9.75 Agent Runtime Mobility

The same Agent may execute on different Runtime Nodes over time.

9.76 Agent Model Binding

An Agent may have:

- preferred Model classes,

- minimum capabilities,

- prohibited Providers,

- or default Routing Profiles.

These are preferences or constraints, not identity.

9.77 Agent Provider Binding

Hard binding an Agent identity to one Provider should be avoided unless the user intentionally requires Pinned execution.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
sectionTitles: 9.80 Potential Access Is Not Current Permission
9.93 External Agent Is Not Omnira Agent
text:
9.78 Agent Tool Access

Tool access shall be represented as governed policy or Grant references.

9.79 Agent Tool Inventory

The Agent Registry may expose which Tool classes the Agent is potentially eligible to use.

9.80 Potential Access Is Not Current Permission

Registry metadata showing a Tool relationship does not authorise one invocation.

9.81 Agent Memory Access

The Agent definition shall identify permitted Memory Domains or retrieval classes.

9.82 Agent Memory Boundary

The Agent Registry shall not embed raw Memory content.

9.83 Agent Authority Metadata

The Agent definition may reference:

- default Authority Level,

- permitted action classes,

- required approval classes,

- and maximum operating boundaries.

9.84 Agent Cannot Self-Modify Authority

An Agent shall not modify its own authority through ordinary execution.

9.85 Agent Cannot Self-Register Tools

An Agent may propose a discovered Tool.

It shall not make that Tool production-eligible by itself.

9.86 Agent Cannot Self-Certify

An Agent may produce test evidence.

Certification remains a separate governance process.

9.87 Agent Lifecycle

Agent lifecycle states may include:

- draft,

- active,

- observe-only,

- suspended,

- degraded,

- retired,

- and archived.

9.88 Observe-Only Agent

An observe-only Agent may:

- inspect,

- analyse,

- recommend,

- and prepare

without executing consequential actions.

9.89 Suspended Agent

A suspended Agent shall not initiate new execution.

9.90 Agent Incident Suspension

An Agent may be suspended after:

- policy violation,

- repeated boundary attempts,

- compromised Runtime,

- or material Incident.

9.91 Agent Historical Identity

Retired Agents remain resolvable in historical Execution Evidence.

9.92 External Agent Resource

An External Agent Resource represents an Agent operated outside Omnira.

9.93 External Agent Is Not Omnira Agent

An external Agent shall not receive Omnira Agent trust merely because it speaks an Agent protocol.

9.94 External Agent Definition

It should include:

- externalAgentResourceId,

- operator,

- endpoint,

- protocol,

- Version,

- capabilities,

- authentication profile reference,

- trust state,

- data policy,

- and lifecycle.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.95 External Agent Capability

Capabilities claimed by an external Agent require validation.

9.96 External Agent Authority

External Agent access shall be bounded to the exact delegated task.

9.97 External Agent Output

External Agent output remains untrusted until canonical validation.

9.98 Agent-to-Agent Delegation

Delegation shall create explicit execution and authority context.

9.99 Delegation Is Not Identity Transfer

One Agent does not become another Agent because it performs delegated work.

9.100 Tool Resource

A Tool Resource is a governed executable capability that performs a defined operation.

9.101 Tool Versus Model

A Tool primarily performs a bounded operation.

A Model primarily produces inference.

A Tool may internally use a Model, but its canonical Tool contract remains distinct.

9.102 Tool Versus Agent

A Tool executes an operation.

An Agent interprets intent and coordinates behaviour.

9.103 Tool Definition

A Tool Definition should include:

- toolId,

- name,

- Version,

- owner,

- type,

- Capability Bindings,

- input schema,

- output schema,

- side-effect class,

- Runtime requirements,

- permissions,

- data limits,

- timeout,

- reliability profile,

- lifecycle,

- and provenance.

9.104 Tool Definition Identity

Every Tool Definition shall have stable identity and Version.

9.105 Tool Instance

A Tool Instance is one deployed or configured implementation of a Tool Definition.

9.106 Tool Instance Identity

Every governed Tool Instance should have stable identity.

9.107 Tool Types

Tool types may include:

- API Tool,

- MCP Tool,

- local process Tool,

- filesystem Tool,

- database Tool,

- search Tool,

- browser Tool,

- publication Tool,

- communication Tool,

- commerce Tool,

- device Tool,

- code execution Tool,

- Asset transformation Tool,

- and deterministic computation Tool.

9.108 API Tool

An API Tool invokes one governed external or internal service operation.

9.109 MCP Tool

An MCP Tool is a canonical Tool derived from an approved MCP server capability.

9.110 Local Process Tool

A Local Process Tool executes a governed local command or process.

9.111 Filesystem Tool

A Filesystem Tool operates on approved files or directories.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.112 Database Tool

A Database Tool performs governed read or write operations against a registered database resource.

9.113 Search Tool

A Search Tool retrieves information from an approved search system.

9.114 Browser Tool

A Browser Tool performs bounded browser observation or action.

9.115 Publication Tool

A Publication Tool creates or modifies externally visible content.

9.116 Communication Tool

A Communication Tool sends or modifies messages.

9.117 Commerce Tool

A Commerce Tool may create:

- purchases,

- subscriptions,

- refunds,

- or financial commitments.

It requires elevated governance.

9.118 Device Tool

A Device Tool operates on a registered Node or device capability.

9.119 Code Execution Tool

A Code Execution Tool executes user or Agent-produced code in a governed environment.

9.120 Transformation Tool

A Transformation Tool performs deterministic or specialised transformation of Assets.

9.121 Deterministic Tool

A deterministic Tool should produce materially identical results for identical controlled Inputs and state.

9.122 Probabilistic Tool

A Tool may contain probabilistic behaviour.

That fact shall be represented.

9.123 Tool Input Schema

Every production Tool shall have a validated Input schema.

9.124 Tool Output Schema

Every production Tool shall have a validated Output schema or bounded Output contract.

9.125 Tool Description

Tool descriptions are metadata.

They are not authority or system instructions.

9.126 Tool Self-Description

A Tool-provided description shall be treated as untrusted until validated.

9.127 Tool Side-Effect Class

Every Tool shall declare its side-effect class.

9.128 Canonical Tool Side-Effect Classes

Classes may include:

- none,

- read,

- local write,

- Project write,

- external write,

- communication,

- publication,

- deletion,

- financial,

- identity or permission change,

- system control,

- and unknown.

9.129 Unknown Side Effect

Unknown side effect shall be treated restrictively.

9.130 Side-Effect Escalation

A Tool invocation whose actual side effect exceeds its registered class is a conformance defect and may be an Incident.

9.131 Read Tool

A read Tool shall not mutate protected external state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.132 Local Write Tool

A local write Tool may modify approved local Project state.

9.133 External Write Tool

An external write Tool modifies a remote system.

9.134 Publication Tool Authority

Publication requires distinct authority even when the Tool is already registered.

9.135 Deletion Tool Authority

Deletion requires distinct authority from ordinary write.

9.136 Financial Tool Authority

Financial side effects require bounded economic authority.

9.137 Tool Permission Requirement

Tool definitions shall declare required permission classes.

9.138 Permission Reference

Permission requirements shall reference governance objects.

Raw Credentials shall not appear in the Tool definition.

9.139 Tool Runtime Requirement

A Tool may require:

- specific Node,

- operating system,

- container,

- browser,

- network,

- library,

- GPU,

- Account,

- or Connector.

9.140 Tool Data Requirement

A Tool may declare eligible:

- Data Categories,

- Classifications,

- Input media types,

- and maximum payload size.

9.141 Tool Data Prohibition

A Tool shall not receive data above its allowed Classification.

9.142 Tool Network Policy

Tools with network access shall declare or inherit permitted network scope.

9.143 Tool Filesystem Policy

Filesystem Tools shall declare allowed roots or Asset scopes.

9.144 Tool Environment Variables

Tools shall receive only required Environment variables.

9.145 Tool Secret Exposure

Broad inheritance of process Secrets is prohibited.

9.146 Tool Timeout

Each Tool operation should define a timeout or bounded execution policy.

9.147 Tool Cancellation

Tool cancellation semantics shall be explicit.

9.148 Tool Idempotency

Tools creating side effects shall declare idempotency semantics.

9.149 Tool Retryability

Retry safety shall be represented separately from transient failure detection.

9.150 Tool Cost

Tools may carry:

- estimated invocation cost,

- variable cost model,

- local resource cost,

- or unknown cost.

9.151 Tool Capacity

Tool capacity may include:

- concurrency,

- throughput,

- queue limit,

- rate limit,

- and resource reservation.

9.152 Tool Health

Tool health shall be observable.

9.153 Tool Drift

Tool drift may occur through:

- new Version,

- changed dependency,

- changed permissions,

- changed schema,

- changed external service,

- or changed side effect.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.154 Tool Drift Response

Material drift shall trigger revalidation.

9.155 Tool Deprecation

Deprecated Tools should not receive new Agent bindings.

9.156 Tool Retirement

Retired Tools shall remain resolvable historically.

9.157 Tool Discovery

Tools may be discovered from:

- MCP,

- local Runtime,

- API manifests,

- configuration,

- plugin packages,

- or manual registration.

9.158 Discovery Record

Discovery should preserve:

- source,

- time,

- Version information,

- raw metadata reference,

- and trust state.

9.159 Discovery Is Not Admission

Discovered Tools shall not become executable by Agents automatically.

9.160 Tool Admission

Tool admission should require:

- identity,

- schema validation,

- side-effect classification,

- permissions,

- Runtime,

- data policy,

- testing,

- and governance review.

9.161 Tool Qualification

Qualification should verify that the Tool behaves according to its registered contract.

9.162 Tool Certification

High-risk production Tools shall require current conformance evidence.

9.163 MCP Discovery

MCP server capability discovery shall create candidate Tool definitions.

9.164 MCP Tool Identity

MCP Tool identity shall include:

- canonical Tool ID,

- server identity,

- server Version or discovery snapshot,

- native Tool name,

- and schema Version.

9.165 MCP Tool Rename

A native Tool rename shall not silently change canonical identity.

9.166 MCP Schema Drift

Changed MCP Tool schema shall trigger new Version or revalidation.

9.167 MCP Tool Removal

Removed Tools shall become unavailable or retired rather than disappearing historically.

9.168 MCP Prompt Separation

MCP Prompts are not Tools unless explicitly wrapped as governed operations.

9.169 MCP Resource Separation

MCP Resources are data sources, not Tool authority.

9.170 Local Tool Discovery

Local executable discovery shall be restricted to approved directories or manifests.

9.171 Arbitrary PATH Discovery Prohibition

Omnira shall not expose every executable on a Node automatically.

9.172 Shell Tool

A Shell Tool should expose bounded operations rather than unrestricted shell access where possible.

9.173 Unrestricted Shell

Unrestricted shell execution is a high-risk Tool class and shall require strong isolation and authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.174 Code Execution Tool Sandbox

Code execution shall occur inside a Sandbox appropriate to risk.

9.175 Sandbox Profile

A Sandbox Profile should declare:

- filesystem,

- network,

- process,

- device,

- memory,

- CPU,

- execution time,

- and Secret boundaries.

9.176 Browser Tool Profile

Browser Tools should declare:

- browser profile,

- Account,

- allowed domains,

- read/write actions,

- download policy,

- upload policy,

- and Session scope.

9.177 Browser Profile Identity

Every automation browser profile should have stable identity.

9.178 Browser Project Isolation

Project browser Sessions shall not share personal or unrelated Project state.

9.179 Database Resource

A registered database may participate as both Execution Resource and Tool dependency.

9.180 Database Tool Scope

Database Tools shall define:

- database,

- schema,

- tables,

- query class,

- read/write,

- Tenant isolation,

- and transaction expectations.

9.181 Search Resource

A search system may be a Tool dependency or direct execution resource.

9.182 Search Scope

Search shall preserve source, retrieval scope and data policy.

9.183 Human Resource

A Human Resource represents a person or governed human role that may perform a Step.

9.184 Human Resource Is Not Agent

A human operator remains a human Principal even when participating in an Execution Graph.

9.185 Human Resource Definition

It may include:

- humanResourceId,

- Principal,

- role,

- organisation,

- skills,

- availability,

- Project eligibility,

- review classes,

- and lifecycle.

9.186 Human Skill

Skill metadata may influence assignment.

It does not create authority.

9.187 Human Availability

Human availability may include:

- online,

- available,

- busy,

- offline,

- scheduled,

- and unknown.

9.188 Human Capacity

Capacity may include:

- concurrent tasks,

- working hours,

- queue limit,

- and expected turnaround.

9.189 Human-Assisted Resource

A Human-Assisted Resource combines a human operator with an external platform or manual process.

9.190 Human-Assisted Truthfulness

Human-assisted execution shall not be represented as autonomous API execution.

9.191 Human-Assisted Resource Definition

It should include:

- resourceId,

- operator role,

- required external Account,

- instructions,

- Inputs,

- Outputs,

- evidence requirements,

- expected turnaround,

- cost model,

- and lifecycle.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.192 Human Evidence

Human Steps shall preserve:

- assignee,

- start,

- result,

- output,

- and evidence.

9.193 Human Account Scope

Manual external actions shall use the correct registered Account.

9.194 Human Error

Human error remains possible and shall be observable and recoverable.

9.195 Execution Resource

An Execution Resource is infrastructure capable of hosting or performing one or more operations.

9.196 Execution Resource Classes

Classes may include:

- Runtime Node,

- Runtime Service,

- Model Deployment,

- Tool Runtime,

- Browser Runtime,

- Container Runtime,

- GPU Resource,

- CPU Resource,

- Queue Worker,

- Human-Assisted Runtime,

- and external execution endpoint.

9.197 Execution Resource Definition

It should include:

- executionResourceId,

- type,

- owner,

- Tenant,

- Environment,

- Location,

- Runtime,

- Capabilities,

- capacity,

- health,

- data policy,

- network policy,

- cost,

- dependencies,

- lifecycle,

- and Version.

9.198 Execution Resource Identity

Every Execution Resource shall have stable identity.

9.199 Execution Resource Versus Provider

A Provider is an organisational or service boundary.

An Execution Resource is a concrete place or mechanism where work may run.

9.200 Execution Resource Versus Model

A Model is an intelligence artefact.

An Execution Resource may host that Model.

9.201 Runtime Node

A Runtime Node is a registered compute device or execution host.

9.202 Runtime Node Examples

Examples include:

- laptop,

- desktop,

- workstation,

- private server,

- cloud VM,

- mobile device,

- edge device,

- and container host.

9.203 Node Identity

Every Runtime Node shall have stable identity independent from its current IP address.

9.204 Node Definition

A Node should include:

- nodeId,

- owner,

- Tenant,

- device class,

- operating system,

- architecture,

- hardware,

- location class,

- trust state,

- available Runtimes,

- network,

- power state,

- lifecycle,

- and Version.

9.205 Node Owner

Node ownership shall be explicit.

9.206 Node Tenant Scope

A Node may belong to one Tenant or approved shared platform scope.

9.207 Node Project Scope

A Node may restrict which Projects may dispatch work to it.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.208 Node Environment

Development and production Node eligibility shall remain separate.

9.209 Node Location

Location may be represented at the minimum granularity needed for:

- residency,

- network,

- latency,

- and availability.

Precise location shall not be collected unnecessarily.

9.210 Node Trust State

Trust states may include:

- unverified,

- enrolled,

- trusted,

- degraded,

- quarantined,

- revoked,

- and retired.

9.211 Node Enrollment

New Nodes shall require controlled enrollment.

9.212 Node Attestation

Attestation may strengthen trust.

It shall not replace policy or Quality validation.

9.213 Node Health

Node health may include:

- CPU,

- RAM,

- GPU,

- VRAM,

- storage,

- network,

- process state,

- battery,

- thermal state,

- and Runtime state.

9.214 Node Availability

Personal Nodes shall not be assumed continuously online.

9.215 Node Heartbeat

Nodes should publish a bounded heartbeat.

9.216 Heartbeat Timeout

Loss of heartbeat shall transition availability to unknown or unavailable after policy-defined timeout.

9.217 Node Capacity

Node capacity may include:

- CPU cores,

- RAM,

- GPU type,

- VRAM,

- disk,

- active jobs,

- and concurrency limits.

9.218 Node Resource Reservation

Heavy tasks may reserve Node capacity.

9.219 Node Power State

Power state may include:

- online,

- sleeping,

- offline,

- starting,

- shutting down,

- and unknown.

9.220 Node Start Requirement

The Fabric may request the user to start a required Node.

The Fabric shall not fabricate availability.

9.221 Node Loss

Node loss shall not produce automatic external fallback when policy prohibits it.

9.222 Runtime Service

A Runtime Service is software running on an Execution Resource that exposes one or more governed execution capabilities.

9.223 Runtime Service Examples

Examples include:

- Ollama,

- local inference server,

- code Sandbox,

- browser automation Runtime,

- vector service,

- media renderer,

- and Tool host.

9.224 Runtime Service Definition

It should include:

- runtimeServiceId,

- Node,

- Runtime type,

- Version,

- endpoint or transport reference,

- capabilities,

- health,

- capacity,

- network exposure,

- and lifecycle.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.225 Runtime Version

Runtime Version shall be explicit where behaviour may change.

9.226 Runtime Endpoint

Endpoint metadata shall remain inside execution infrastructure.

Agents shall not require it.

9.227 Runtime Transport

Transports may include:

- local process,

- stdio,

- Unix socket,

- HTTP,

- gRPC,

- queue,

- or another governed protocol.

9.228 Runtime Locality

Runtime locality may be:

- same process,

- same Node,

- private network,

- public cloud,

- external Provider,

- or human-assisted.

9.229 Runtime Locality Is Not Trust

Local execution shall not automatically receive unrestricted trust.

9.230 Runtime Process Identity

Important Runtime processes should have Service Principal identity.

9.231 Runtime Restart

Restart shall not change canonical Resource identity unnecessarily.

9.232 Runtime Upgrade

A material Runtime upgrade may trigger revalidation of hosted resources.

9.233 Runtime Health

Runtime health shall remain separate from Node health.

9.234 Model Deployment

A Model Deployment binds a registered Model to one concrete execution environment.

9.235 Model Deployment Identity

Every production Model Deployment should have stable identity.

9.236 Model Deployment Fields

It should include:

- deploymentId,

- modelId,

- Runtime Service,

- Node or Provider Product,

- Version,

- configuration,

- context limit,

- quantisation where relevant,

- concurrency,

- health,

- cost,

- and lifecycle.

9.237 Deployment Configuration

Configuration may include:

- inference parameters,

- quantisation,

- precision,

- context allocation,

- batching,

- and hardware settings.

9.238 Deployment Identity Versus Model Identity

Two Deployments of the same Model remain different Resources.

9.239 Local Deployment

A local Deployment shall preserve:

- Model checksum where practical,

- Runtime Version,

- quantisation,

- and Node.

9.240 External Deployment

An external Deployment may be represented using Provider Product, Model, region and Account configuration without claiming access to Provider-internal infrastructure details.

9.241 Tool Runtime

A Tool Runtime hosts one or more executable Tool Instances.

9.242 Tool Runtime Definition

It should identify:

- runtimeId,

- Runtime Service,

- hosted Tool Instances,

- Sandbox,

- identity,

- capacity,

- permissions,

- network scope,

- and health.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.243 Browser Runtime

A Browser Runtime is an execution environment for governed browser operations.

9.244 Browser Runtime State

It may include:

- browser engine,

- Version,

- profile,

- active Session,

- Account context,

- tabs,

- download directory,

- and health.

9.245 Browser Runtime Isolation

One Project shall not inherit another Project’s browser Session unless explicitly authorised.

9.246 Container Runtime

A Container Runtime executes workloads inside governed container boundaries.

9.247 Container Image

Container images should have:

- identity,

- Version,

- digest,

- source,

- vulnerability state,

- and lifecycle.

9.248 Mutable Container Tag

Mutable tags shall not replace immutable digest identity in high-assurance execution evidence.

9.249 GPU Resource

A GPU Resource represents allocatable accelerator capacity.

9.250 GPU Resource Fields

It may include:

- GPU identity,

- Node,

- model,

- memory,

- compute capability,

- utilisation,

- reservation,

- and health.

9.251 GPU Is Not Model

The accelerator hardware shall not be conflated with the Model it currently hosts.

9.252 CPU Resource

CPU capacity may also be represented where scheduling materially depends on it.

9.253 Memory Resource

System or accelerator memory may be represented as schedulable capacity where relevant.

9.254 Storage Resource

Storage may become an Execution Resource dependency when:

- Models,

- Assets,

- or temporary working sets

require bounded capacity.

9.255 Network Resource

Network availability may influence execution placement and scheduling.

9.256 Resource Pool

A Resource Pool groups interchangeable or schedulable Resource Instances.

9.257 Resource Pool Identity

Every governed Resource Pool shall have stable identity.

9.258 Pool Examples

Examples include:

- text reasoning pool,

- image generation pool,

- local GPU pool,

- browser worker pool,

- human review pool,

- and Project-specific Tool pool.

9.259 Pool Membership

Membership shall be explicit and Versioned where material.

9.260 Pool Eligibility

Pool membership does not guarantee that every member is eligible for every Request.

9.261 Pool Selection

Routing and scheduling select eligible Pool members according to policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.262 Pool Scope

Pools may be scoped to:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- Capability,

- region,

- or trust class.

9.263 Pool Health

Pool health shall derive from member health and capacity rather than one synthetic binary state alone.

9.264 Pool Capacity

Pool capacity may aggregate:

- concurrency,

- throughput,

- GPU memory,

- rate limits,

- and human availability.

9.265 Shared Pool

A shared Pool shall preserve Project isolation during scheduling and execution.

9.266 Dedicated Pool

A dedicated Pool serves one Tenant, Project or workload class.

9.267 Worker Resource

A Worker Resource executes queued Fabric work.

9.268 Worker Identity

Every production Worker shall operate through a Service Principal.

9.269 Worker Definition

It should identify:

- workerId,

- service Version,

- Environment,

- supported Step types,

- queue bindings,

- capacity,

- health,

- and lifecycle.

9.270 Worker Capability

A Worker may be technically able to run an operation while policy still makes the operation ineligible.

9.271 Worker Lease

Workers should use leases, locks or equivalent concurrency controls.

9.272 Worker Loss

Worker loss shall not erase canonical execution state.

9.273 Worker Upgrade

Worker Versions should be visible in execution evidence where behaviour may differ.

9.274 Scheduler Resource

A Scheduler is a governed execution service that admits work at a selected time.

9.275 Scheduler Is Not Authority

A schedule does not create current authority.

9.276 Scheduled Resource Eligibility

Resources shall be re-evaluated when scheduled work actually begins.

9.277 Execution Environment

An Execution Environment is the bounded context in which a Resource runs.

9.278 Environment Identity

Every governed Execution Environment should have stable identity or reproducible definition.

9.279 Environment Types

Types may include:

- host process,

- container,

- virtual machine,

- browser profile,

- secure enclave,

- remote Provider,

- and human-assisted workspace.

9.280 Environment Profile

An Environment Profile should define:

- trust,

- network,

- filesystem,

- Secrets,

- process,

- device,

- data,

- logging,

- and cleanup policies.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.281 Environment Version

Material Environment changes should create a new Version or Configuration Version.

9.282 Environment Drift

Unexpected Runtime or dependency change shall be detectable where risk is material.

9.283 Resource Dependency

A Resource Dependency is another Resource or condition required for execution.

9.284 Dependency Types

Dependencies may include:

- Model,

- Runtime,

- Node,

- Tool,

- Connector,

- Account,

- network,

- storage,

- browser profile,

- queue,

- and human operator.

9.285 Hard Dependency

A hard dependency is mandatory for execution.

9.286 Optional Dependency

An optional dependency may enhance execution but is not required.

9.287 Alternative Dependency

Alternative dependencies may satisfy the same requirement through approved substitutes.

9.288 Dependency Version

Version constraints shall be explicit where incompatibility is possible.

9.289 Dependency Health

Eligibility shall consider the health of required dependencies.

9.290 Dependency Chain

The Fabric should be able to reconstruct the Resource dependency chain for material execution.

9.291 Dependency Cycle

Dependency cycles that prevent safe resource resolution shall be rejected.

9.292 Resource Placement Constraint

A Placement Constraint restricts where a Resource may execute.

9.293 Placement Examples

Constraints may include:

- same Node,

- private network,

- Local Only,

- specific region,

- GPU required,

- browser profile required,

- or human operator required.

9.294 Placement Preference

A preference influences ranking but is not mandatory.

9.295 Placement Requirement

A requirement makes non-matching Resources ineligible.

9.296 Resource Data Boundary

Every Resource shall expose or inherit data-processing constraints.

9.297 Classification Eligibility

Resources may declare maximum eligible Classification.

The effective limit may be tightened by policy.

9.298 Local Only Eligibility

Only approved local or private execution resources may process Local Only data.

9.299 Prohibited Data

Prohibited data shall not become eligible merely because a local Resource exists.

9.300 Data Minimisation

Resource registration does not justify sending every available Project field to the Resource.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.301 Resource Input Contract

A Resource Input Contract shall describe what input types the Resource accepts.

9.302 Resource Output Contract

A Resource Output Contract shall describe what outputs the Resource may produce.

9.303 Resource Format

File format support is an implementation property.

It shall not substitute for canonical Capability or Asset Type.

9.304 Resource Constraint

A Resource Constraint describes a non-negotiable technical or governance limitation.

9.305 Constraint Examples

Examples include:

- maximum context,

- supported image dimensions,

- maximum file size,

- no streaming,

- no cancellation,

- no external network,

- or no Confidential data.

9.306 Resource Limitation

Known limitations shall remain visible to Planning and Routing.

9.307 Resource Capability Confidence

A capability claim may have confidence based on evidence freshness and quality.

9.308 Resource Cost Profile

A Resource may have a Cost Profile.

9.309 Cost Profile Types

Cost may be:

- per invocation,

- per token,

- per character,

- per second,

- per image,

- per job,

- subscription-allocated,

- hardware-allocated,

- human-time-based,

- or unknown.

9.310 Cost Profile Is Not Budget

Resource cost describes expected economic consumption.

Budget defines authorised spend.

9.311 Local Cost

Local Resources may have non-zero cost through:

- power,

- hardware,

- storage,

- rented infrastructure,

- and opportunity cost.

9.312 Human Cost

Human-assisted Resources may include:

- labour,

- external credits,

- turnaround,

- and review overhead.

9.313 Resource Capacity Profile

Capacity describes how much work a Resource may support.

9.314 Capacity Dimensions

Dimensions may include:

- concurrency,

- requests per interval,

- tokens per interval,

- GPU memory,

- queue depth,

- working hours,

- and storage.

9.315 Static Capacity

Static capacity derives from configuration or hardware.

9.316 Dynamic Capacity

Dynamic capacity changes with current load and health.

9.317 Capacity Observation

Capacity observations shall include freshness.

9.318 Stale Capacity

Stale capacity shall not be treated as current fact.

9.319 Resource Availability Window

Some Resources may have scheduled availability.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
sectionTitles: 9.329 Registry Does Not Own Evaluation Truth
text:
9.320 Availability Window Examples

Examples include:

- office hours,

- local Node powered hours,

- Provider maintenance,

- human operator shift,

- or reserved GPU windows.

9.321 Deadline Eligibility

A Resource unable to satisfy the expected deadline may be excluded.

9.322 Resource Latency Profile

Latency evidence may be attached by Capability and operation class.

9.323 Latency Is Contextual

Latency may depend on:

- region,

- Account,

- Model,

- payload,

- queue,

- Node,

- and time.

9.324 Resource Reliability Profile

Reliability evidence may include:

- success rate,

- timeout rate,

- retry rate,

- unknown outcome rate,

- and recovery characteristics.

9.325 Reliability Is Not Static Trust

Past reliability informs Routing but does not create permanent eligibility.

9.326 Resource Quality Profile

Quality evidence may be attached to Resource Capability Bindings.

9.327 Quality Is Task-Specific

One Tool, Model or Agent may perform well on one task and poorly on another.

9.328 Resource Evaluation Record

Evaluation shall remain in the evaluation architecture and be referenced from the Registry.

9.329 Registry Does Not Own Evaluation Truth

The Registry indexes current evidence.

It does not replace Evaluation Records.

9.330 Resource Rights Profile

Resources creating or transforming Assets may reference rights and commercial-use constraints.

9.331 Rights Eligibility

A Tool or external production Resource may be ineligible if required rights cannot be established.

9.332 Resource Consent Requirement

A Resource may require consent for specific operations such as:

- Voice identity,

- likeness,

- biometric processing,

- or personalisation.

9.333 Consent Is Contextual

Consent validity must be checked at execution time.

9.334 Resource Trust Profile

A Trust Profile describes evidence relevant to technical and organisational trust.

9.335 Trust Profile Inputs

It may include:

- owner,

- operator,

- source,

- signature,

- package integrity,

- test results,

- certification,

- Incident history,

- and last review.

9.336 Trust Is Not Authority

Trust evidence does not create permission.

9.337 Trust Is Not Capability

A trusted Tool may still lack the required Capability.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.338 Trust Is Not Health

A trusted Tool may be offline.

9.339 Resource Certification

A Resource may reference one or more current Certifications.

9.340 Certification Scope

Certification may be limited by:

- Capability,

- Environment,

- Project,

- data class,

- operation,

- or Version.

9.341 Certification Expiry

Expired certification shall not be treated as current.

9.342 Certification Suspension

Material drift or Incident may suspend eligibility immediately.

9.343 Resource Incident Link

Resources should link to active Incidents that may affect eligibility.

9.344 Resource Quarantine

A quarantined Resource shall not receive new execution.

9.345 Automatic Quarantine

Policy may quarantine after signals such as:

- integrity failure,

- unexpected side effect,

- Secret exposure,

- malware detection,

- cross-Project access,

- or severe schema drift.

9.346 Quarantine Release

Return from quarantine shall require verification.

9.347 Resource Drift

Resource Drift is a material difference between registered assumptions and observed reality.

9.348 Drift Types

Drift may include:

- Version drift,

- schema drift,

- capability drift,

- permission drift,

- endpoint drift,

- dependency drift,

- policy drift,

- quality drift,

- and side-effect drift.

9.349 Drift Observation

Drift shall preserve:

- observed value,

- expected value,

- source,

- time,

- severity,

- and Resource identity.

9.350 Drift Severity

Severity may be:

- informational,

- minor,

- material,

- critical,

- and unknown.

9.351 Material Drift

Material drift should trigger revalidation.

9.352 Critical Drift

Critical drift should suspend production eligibility automatically where safe.

9.353 Unknown Drift

Unknown but potentially high-risk drift shall be treated conservatively.

9.354 Resource Refresh

Discovery or health processes may refresh operational metadata.

9.355 Refresh Does Not Rewrite History

Current metadata updates shall not alter historical Execution Evidence.

9.356 Registry Projection

Operational views may project current eligible Resources.

The source Registry history remains Versioned.

9.357 Registry Search

Registry interfaces should allow lookup by:

- identity,

- type,

- Capability,

- Project,

- owner,

- Environment,

- health,

- lifecycle,

- and certification.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.358 Registry Search Is Not Routing

Search returns possible Resources.

Routing determines contextual selection.

9.359 Registry API

The Resource Registry should expose governed operations such as:

- discover,

- propose,

- register,

- inspect,

- update,

- Version,

- qualify,

- activate,

- suspend,

- deprecate,

- retire,

- and archive.

9.360 Registry Mutation Authority

Resource mutation shall require explicit administrative or governance authority.

9.361 Agent Registration Authority

Agents shall not register themselves as production Agents automatically.

9.362 Tool Registration Authority

Tools shall not activate themselves.

9.363 Node Registration Authority

New Nodes shall require enrollment authority.

9.364 Runtime Registration

Runtime Services may self-report technical metadata after authenticated enrollment.

Self-reporting does not create trust.

9.365 Discovery Principal

Automated discovery shall operate through a Service Principal.

9.366 Registry Audit

Material Registry mutations shall be audited.

9.367 Registry History

Historical Versions shall remain queryable.

9.368 Registry Deletion

Canonical Resource identity should rarely be hard-deleted.

Retirement or archival is preferred.

9.369 Secret Exclusion

Registry records shall not contain raw Secrets.

9.370 Credential Reference

Resources may reference a governed Credential Requirement or Connection.

Raw Credential values belong outside this Registry.

9.371 Account Reference

Tools requiring an external Account shall reference canonical Account or Connection identity.

9.372 Connection Dependency

An API Tool may depend on an active Connection.

9.373 Connection Health

Connection health shall influence Tool eligibility.

9.374 Credential Rotation

Credential rotation shall not change Tool identity unnecessarily.

9.375 Agent Credential Isolation

Agents shall never need raw Credential material merely because their Tool bindings reference external services.

9.376 Resource Invocation

Invocation is the act of executing one registered Resource under a Plan.

9.377 Resource Invocation Record

Every material invocation should link:

- Execution,

- Step,

- Attempt,

- Resource,

- Resource Version,

- Principal,

- authority,

- Inputs,

- Outputs,

- and Evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.378 Invocation Eligibility Check

Eligibility shall be evaluated before dispatch.

9.379 Final Execution Boundary Check

High-risk Tools should receive a final authority and scope check immediately before side effect.

9.380 Registry Snapshot

A Plan may preserve a Registry Snapshot or exact Resource Versions used during Planning.

9.381 Snapshot Is Not Permanent Eligibility

Current policy and health may invalidate a Resource before execution.

9.382 Late Binding

The Fabric may delay exact Resource selection until execution.

Capability and constraints remain stable.

9.383 Early Binding

Pinned or scarce resources may be bound earlier when required.

9.384 Resource Reservation

A scarce Resource may be reserved before execution.

9.385 Reservation Is Not Authority

Reservation does not permit execution by itself.

9.386 Reservation Expiry

Reservations shall expire when not consumed.

9.387 Resource Lock

Exclusive Resource access may require a lock or lease.

9.388 Lock Expiry

Stale locks shall not block resources indefinitely.

9.389 Resource Concurrency

Concurrency limits shall be explicit where exceeding them causes instability or policy risk.

9.390 Resource Preemption

Low-priority work may be preempted where the Runtime supports safe pause or cancellation.

9.391 Preemption and Side Effects

Consequential operations shall not be preempted blindly after external side effects may have occurred.

9.392 Agent Resource Selection

An Agent shall not select itself as an execution resource in a way that bypasses Planning or authority.

9.393 Tool Chaining

A Tool Output may feed another Tool only through an explicit Plan dependency or controlled orchestration.

9.394 Recursive Tool Use

Unbounded recursive Tool invocation is prohibited.

9.395 Agent Loop

Agentic loops shall be:

- bounded,

- observable,

- Budget-aware,

- authority-aware,

- and terminable.

9.396 Agent Delegation Loop

Agents shall not delegate indefinitely among themselves.

9.397 Tool-Generated Tool Request

A Tool may return data suggesting another Tool action.

That suggestion shall not become execution authority.

9.398 Agent-Generated Tool Definition

An Agent may draft a Tool manifest.

Registration and qualification remain separate.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.399 Dynamic Code Tool

Generated code intended for execution shall be treated as new untrusted Input.

9.400 Dynamic Tool Package

Agent-generated executable packages shall not become persistent Tools without admission and testing.

9.401 Ephemeral Tool

An Ephemeral Tool is a bounded one-time executable operation created for a specific Plan.

9.402 Ephemeral Tool Governance

It shall still define:

- identity,

- scope,

- permissions,

- Sandbox,

- side effect,

- and expiry.

9.403 Ephemeral Tool Persistence

Enough metadata shall remain to reconstruct material execution.

9.404 Ephemeral Does Not Mean Ungoverned

Short lifetime does not justify broader permissions.

9.405 Composite Resource

A Composite Resource represents a governed collection of resources exposed as one higher-level execution option.

9.406 Composite Resource Example

A multimodal production Resource may combine:

- text generation,

- image generation,

- Voice,

- transformation,

- and human review.

The underlying resources remain separately attributable.

9.407 Composite Resource Transparency

Composition shall not hide:

- cost,

- data transfer,

- Providers,

- side effects,

- or provenance.

9.408 Resource Bundle

A Resource Bundle groups Resources that are normally deployed or qualified together.

9.409 Bundle Is Not Pool

A Bundle describes composition.

A Pool describes selectable members.

9.410 Resource Dependency Manifest

A deployment or Tool package may provide a Resource Dependency Manifest.

9.411 Manifest Validation

Manifest claims shall be validated before production use.

9.412 Resource Signature

Packages or manifests may be signed.

Signature verification proves origin or integrity, not behavioural safety.

9.413 Resource Checksum

Executable packages and local Model artefacts should preserve checksums where practical.

9.414 Resource Supply Chain

Supply-chain metadata should include:

- source,

- publisher,

- Version,

- dependencies,

- digest,

- signature,

- licence,

- and scan state.

9.415 Supply-Chain Incident

Compromised package evidence may suspend every dependent Tool or Runtime.

9.416 Dependency Blast Radius

The Registry should support identifying Resources affected by one compromised dependency.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.417 Reverse Dependency Query

Operators should be able to identify which Agents, Tools, Runtimes and Plans depend on a Resource.

9.418 Resource Usage Query

Operators should be able to determine where a Resource is used.

9.419 Historical Usage

Historical usage shall remain queryable after Resource retirement.

9.420 Resource Owner Notification

Material drift or deprecation should notify accountable owners.

9.421 Resource Steward

A Resource Steward may maintain:

- metadata,

- tests,

- lifecycle,

- and operational review.

Stewardship does not create execution authority.

9.422 Provider-Owned Tool

A Provider may expose Tools.

They still require canonical registration.

9.423 Project-Owned Tool

A Project may define custom Tools.

Cross-Project use shall not occur automatically.

9.424 Tenant-Shared Tool

A Tenant may provide shared Tools with Project-scoped invocation.

9.425 Omnira Platform Tool

Platform Tools may be shared across Projects while enforcing scope structurally.

9.426 Personal Tool

Personal Tools shall not become Project Tools by convenience.

9.427 Sensitive Tool

A Sensitive Tool can access or modify protected resources.

9.428 High-Risk Tool

High-Risk Tools include operations involving:

- publication,

- communication,

- finance,

- identity,

- deletion,

- system control,

- private data,

- and broad code execution.

9.429 High-Risk Registration

High-Risk Tools require stronger review and conformance.

9.430 High-Risk Invocation

High-Risk Tool invocation shall require current authority immediately before execution.

9.431 Unknown Tool Class

Unknown Tool class shall default to restrictive governance.

9.432 Tool Capability Granularity

Capabilities should be narrow enough to govern side effects meaningfully.

9.433 Broad Tool Anti-Pattern

A Tool named “do_anything” with unrestricted permissions is not an acceptable default architecture.

9.434 Tool Operation

One Tool may expose multiple Operations.

9.435 Tool Operation Identity

Material Operations should have stable identity within the Tool Version.

9.436 Operation-Level Authority

Different Operations from one Tool may require different authority.

9.437 Operation-Level Data Policy

Different Operations may accept different Classifications.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.438 Operation-Level Side Effect

Side-effect classification should occur at Operation level where one Tool mixes read and write behaviour.

9.439 Operation-Level Cost

Cost may differ by Operation.

9.440 Operation-Level Capability

Capability Bindings should map to specific Operations where practical.

9.441 Agent Capability

An Agent itself may be registered as capable of higher-level tasks.

9.442 Agent Capability Is Composite

Agent Capability may depend on:

- Models,

- Tools,

- Memory,

- and authority.

The Agent Registry shall not conceal these dependencies.

9.443 Agent Capability Evidence

Agent Capability claims should reference Evaluation and Conformance evidence.

9.444 Agent Quality Profile

Quality evidence may be task-specific to one Agent Version.

9.445 Agent Cost Profile

Agent execution cost may aggregate multiple underlying resources.

9.446 Agent Capacity

Agent concurrency may be limited by:

- Runtime,

- Model,

- Tool access,

- human review,

- or Project policy.

9.447 Agent Availability

Agent availability depends on required underlying resources.

9.448 Agent Degraded State

An Agent may remain available for some Capabilities while degraded for others.

9.449 Agent Partial Capability

Capability-specific health shall be preferred over one simplistic global status where useful.

9.450 External Agent Cost

External Agent Resources may expose:

- fixed,

- per-task,

- usage-based,

- or unknown cost.

9.451 External Agent Data Policy

External Agents shall declare or inherit explicit data custody and Classification limits.

9.452 External Agent Tool Use

An external Agent shall not receive Omnira Tool authority automatically.

Delegated Tool access requires separate governed mechanisms.

9.453 Human Review Tool

Human review may be represented as a Human Resource Step rather than pretending it is deterministic Tool execution.

9.454 Human Approval Versus Human Review

Review evaluates content or state.

Approval grants authority.

They shall remain distinct.

9.455 Human Resource Privacy

Human operators shall receive only data required for the task.

9.456 Human Resource Project Isolation

A human operator working across Projects shall still receive Project-scoped assignments.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.457 Human Resource Revocation

Loss of role or employment shall revoke future assignment eligibility.

9.458 Human-Assisted Provider

A Provider accessible only through a website may be represented through:

- Human Resource,

- Browser Runtime,

- Provider Account,

- and Human-Assisted Resource.

No fictional API is required.

9.459 Manual Evidence

Manual execution may preserve:

- screenshot,

- receipt,

- downloaded Asset,

- Provider job identifier,

- and operator confirmation.

Evidence requirements depend on risk.

9.460 Human Latency

Human turnaround is part of scheduling and planning.

9.461 Human Queue

Human review or assisted work may use a governed queue.

9.462 Human Queue Priority

Priority shall remain policy-controlled.

9.463 Human Capacity Unknown

Unknown availability shall remain unknown rather than assumed.

9.464 Resource Federation

Future external resource Registries may expose candidate Resources to Omnira.

9.465 Federated Discovery

Federated discovery shall not create local trust automatically.

9.466 Federated Resource Identity

External Resource identity shall map to one local canonical representation.

9.467 Federated Resource Authority

Local Omnira policy remains authoritative for local execution.

9.468 Resource Marketplace

A future marketplace may list:

- Tools,

- Agents,

- Runtimes,

- and Adapters.

Marketplace presence shall not equal qualification.

9.469 Marketplace Publisher

Publisher identity shall remain separate from Resource operator and user authority.

9.470 Resource Import

Importing a Resource package shall create a proposed or registered state, not immediate production activation.

9.471 Resource Export

Exported Resource definitions shall exclude Secrets and unrelated Project data.

9.472 Resource Template

Templates may define reusable Resource configurations.

9.473 Template Is Not Resource

Instantiation creates a concrete Resource identity.

9.474 Resource Clone

Cloning a Resource definition shall create a distinct identity when ownership, Environment or configuration differs materially.

9.475 Shared Definition

Several Instances may legitimately reference one immutable definition.

9.476 Resource Version Pinning

Critical workflows may pin exact Resource Versions.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.477 Resource Version Range

Low-risk workflows may permit compatible Version ranges under Conformance policy.

9.478 Automatic Upgrade

Automatic Resource upgrade shall not occur for high-risk production dependencies without defined policy.

9.479 Resource Rollback

A Resource may roll back to an older qualified Version where safe.

9.480 Rollback Is New Current State

Historical execution continues to reference the Version actually used.

9.481 Resource Replacement

A replacement Resource may satisfy the same Capability without assuming identical behaviour.

9.482 Replacement Evaluation

Migration should compare:

- Capability,

- Quality,

- privacy,

- cost,

- latency,

- rights,

- and reliability.

9.483 Resource Equivalence

Two Resources shall not be labelled equivalent merely because they accept similar Inputs.

9.484 Routing Group

Resources may be grouped for routing after eligibility criteria are satisfied.

9.485 Preferred Resource

A preferred Resource influences ranking.

It does not override mandatory policy.

9.486 Prohibited Resource

A prohibited Resource is removed before ranking.

9.487 Pinned Resource

A Pinned Request names one exact Resource or constrained set.

Silent fallback is prohibited.

9.488 Private Resource

A private Resource is one whose custody and execution boundary meet defined private-placement requirements.

Private is not synonymous with local.

9.489 Local Resource

A local Resource executes on a Node under local or user-controlled infrastructure.

Local is not synonymous with trusted.

9.490 Cloud Resource

A cloud Resource may be public, private or dedicated.

Cloud location alone does not determine data eligibility.

9.491 Edge Resource

An Edge Resource executes near the user, device or data source.

It still requires identity and governance.

9.492 Dedicated Resource

A dedicated Resource is reserved for one Tenant or workload class.

9.493 Shared Resource

A shared Resource serves several scopes while enforcing isolation.

9.494 Shared Resource Isolation

Sharing shall not allow:

- cross-Tenant state,

- cross-Project cache,

- cross-Project browser Session,

- or cross-Project Memory.

9.495 Resource Observability

Resource status should expose:

- health,

- capacity,

- lifecycle,

- current Version,

- active Incidents,

- drift,

- and certification.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
sectionTitles: 9.500 Synthetic Check Is Not Full Quality Proof
text:
9.496 Resource Health Observation

Every material Health Observation should include:

- resourceId,

- observation type,

- value,

- timestamp,

- source,

- freshness,

- and severity.

9.497 Health Observation Identity

Material observations may have stable identity for audit and incident correlation.

9.498 Health Freshness

Routing shall not rely indefinitely on old Health Observations.

9.499 Synthetic Health Check

A Resource may be probed with safe synthetic operations.

9.500 Synthetic Check Is Not Full Quality Proof

Health checks verify availability or contract behaviour, not full task Quality.

9.501 Passive Health

Operational telemetry may provide passive Health Observations.

9.502 Active Health

Explicit probes may provide active Health Observations.

9.503 Resource Circuit State

Reliability systems may attach circuit-breaker state to one Resource or dependency.

9.504 Circuit State Is Operational

Circuit state does not mutate Resource identity.

9.505 Resource Incident State

An Incident may:

- degrade,

- suspend,

- quarantine,

- or revoke

a Resource.

9.506 Resource Recovery

Recovery from Incident shall require updated Health and applicable Conformance evidence.

9.507 Resource Audit Events

Material events should include:

- registration,

- activation,

- suspension,

- permission change,

- Version change,

- certification,

- deprecation,

- retirement,

- and revocation.

9.508 Registry Observability

The Registry itself shall expose:

- mutation rate,

- stale records,

- unresolved drift,

- missing owners,

- expired certifications,

- and unavailable dependencies.

9.509 Registry Integrity

Registry data is security- and execution-relevant state.

Unauthorised mutation is a serious control failure.

9.510 Registry Backup

Resource metadata shall be backed up according to platform recovery policy.

9.511 Registry Restore

Restore shall reapply current:

- revocations,

- deletions,

- certification suspensions,

- and policy restrictions.

9.512 Stale Backup Protection

A restored old Registry shall not reactivate Resources that have since been revoked.

9.513 Registry Migration

Schema migration shall preserve Resource identity and historical Versions.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
sectionTitles: 9.519 Policy Does Not Belong in Registry Alone
9.529 No Raw Derived Learning in Registry
text:
9.514 Imported Legacy Tool

A legacy Tool with incomplete history may be registered as imported and restricted until verified.

9.515 Imported Legacy Agent

A legacy Agent may preserve identity while its Provider-specific configuration is migrated out.

9.516 Imported Legacy Node

A known machine shall not become trusted solely because it existed before the Registry.

9.517 Imported Legacy Runtime

Legacy Runtime metadata may be incomplete.

Unknown properties shall remain unknown.

9.518 Resource Policy Hook

The Registry shall expose enough metadata for Policy to determine contextual eligibility.

9.519 Policy Does Not Belong in Registry Alone

Registry fields may describe requirements.

Current Decisions remain in the Policy layer.

9.520 Planner Use

The Planner queries possible Resources and their constraints when constructing Plans.

9.521 Planner Shall Not Assume Availability

Planning-time availability may change before execution.

9.522 Router Use

The Router ranks currently eligible Resources.

9.523 Scheduler Use

The Scheduler uses:

- capacity,

- locality,

- availability,

- deadline,

- and queue state.

9.524 Cost Engine Use

The Cost Engine reads Resource Cost Profiles and current Provider pricing evidence.

9.525 Quality Engine Use

Evaluation systems update or reference Resource Quality evidence.

9.526 Incident System Use

Incident systems may suspend or quarantine Resources.

9.527 Conformance System Use

Certification status feeds Resource eligibility.

9.528 Memory System Use

Memory may store reviewed learning about Resource performance.

The Registry remains the source for current Resource metadata.

9.529 No Raw Derived Learning in Registry

Informal operational beliefs shall not be written directly as authoritative Resource facts.

9.530 Resource Reputation

Future reputation scores may summarise evidence.

They shall not override categorical policy.

9.531 Resource Preference Learning

Project-specific preferences may evolve from repeated evidence.

They shall remain scoped.

9.532 Global Preference Promotion

Project-specific observations shall not become global Registry truth automatically.

9.533 Stage 1 Resource Registry Objective

Stage 1 shall implement the minimum Resource Registry required for governed Planning and execution.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.534 Stage 1 Agent Registry

Stage 1 shall register at minimum:

- Atlas,

- Arnold where integrated,

- any Project-specific Agent used in production,

- and coding or operational Agents requiring Fabric resources.

9.535 Stage 1 Agent Fields

The Stage 1 Agent record should include:

- agentId,

- name,

- Version,

- role,

- Tenant,

- Project relationships,

- Authority Level,

- Memory policy reference,

- Tool policy reference,

- lifecycle,

- and owner.

9.536 Stage 1 Tool Registry

Stage 1 shall register all production Tools exposed to Agents or workflows.

9.537 Stage 1 Tool Fields

The Stage 1 Tool record should include:

- toolId,

- name,

- Version,

- type,

- Capability Bindings,

- Input schema,

- Output schema,

- side-effect class,

- authority requirement,

- Runtime requirement,

- Project scope,

- lifecycle,

- and certification.

9.538 Stage 1 Execution Resource Registry

Stage 1 shall register execution resources required for:

- local inference,

- Tool execution,

- MCP,

- browser-assisted work where used,

- and asynchronous Workers.

9.539 Stage 1 Node Fields

Node records should include:

- nodeId,

- owner,

- Tenant,

- Environment,

- hardware profile,

- Runtime services,

- trust state,

- availability,

- health,

- and lifecycle.

9.540 Stage 1 Runtime Fields

Runtime records should include:

- runtimeServiceId,

- Node,

- Runtime type,

- Version,

- transport,

- capability classes,

- health,

- capacity,

- and lifecycle.

9.541 Stage 1 Model Deployment Fields

Deployments should include:

- deploymentId,

- Model,

- Runtime,

- Node or Provider Product,

- configuration,

- health,

- capacity,

- and certification.

9.542 Stage 1 Resource Pools

Stage 1 may create simple Pools for:

- external text reasoning,

- local text reasoning,

- image generation,

- Voice,

- Tools,

- and human review.

9.543 Stage 1 Resource Discovery

Automated discovery may initially support:

- local Models,

- MCP Tools,

- and registered Runtime services.

9.544 Stage 1 Discovery Admission

All discovered Resources shall remain non-active until validation succeeds.

9.545 Stage 1 Health

Stage 1 shall support Resource health for:

- Nodes,

- Runtime Services,

- Tool Instances,

- Connections,

- and Model Deployments.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.546 Stage 1 Capacity

At minimum, capacity should represent:

- online/offline,

- concurrency,

- queue state,

- and relevant GPU or rate-limit constraints.

9.547 Stage 1 Drift

Stage 1 shall detect at least:

- Tool schema drift,

- Runtime Version drift,

- Model alias drift,

- local Model installation drift,

- and MCP discovery drift.

9.548 Stage 1 Audit

Resource activation, suspension, deprecation and authority-relevant modification shall be audited.

9.549 Stage 1 Resource Conformance

Production Resources shall pass the applicable Conformance Profile defined later in this book.

9.550 Stage 1 Agent Test

Agent tests shall verify identity remains stable across Model changes.

9.551 Stage 1 Tool Test

Tool tests shall verify:

- schemas,

- side effects,

- Project scope,

- permission boundaries,

- and failure states.

9.552 Stage 1 Node Test

Node tests shall verify:

- enrollment,

- identity,

- health,

- scope,

- offline state,

- and revocation.

9.553 Stage 1 Runtime Test

Runtime tests shall verify:

- Version,

- capabilities,

- execution,

- cancellation,

- health,

- and isolation.

9.554 Stage 1 MCP Test

MCP-discovered Tools shall not become automatically active.

9.555 Stage 1 Human-Assisted Test

Human-assisted Resources shall preserve explicit manual state and evidence.

9.556 Stage 1 Browser Test

Browser Runtime tests shall verify Project and Account isolation.

9.557 Stage 1 Shell Test

Unrestricted shell access shall not be exposed to ordinary Agents by default.

9.558 Stage 1 Local Model Test

Local Model Deployments shall use registered Model, Node and Runtime identity.

9.559 Stage 1 Offline Node Test

An offline required Node shall produce:

- wait,

- blocked,

- or unavailable

rather than silent external fallback.

9.560 Stage 1 Cross-Project Tool Test

A Tool scoped to GainPilot shall fail when invoked from Familje-Stunden without explicit cross-Project authority.

9.561 Stage 1 Agent Authority Test

Changing an Agent Model shall not change the Agent’s Authority Level.

9.562 Stage 1 Tool Drift Test

A changed Tool schema shall prevent stale unvalidated execution.

9.563 Stage 1 Resource Retirement Test

A retired Resource shall remain historical but receive no new work.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.564 Stage 1 Resource Revocation Test

A revoked Resource shall disappear from execution eligibility immediately.

9.565 Applied Example — Atlas

Atlas is registered as:

Agent Resource:

- identity: Atlas,

- role: central Omnira intelligence coordinator,

- owner: Omnira,

- Model: not part of identity,

- Provider: not part of identity,

- Tool policy: governed reference,

- Memory policy: governed reference,

- authority: separate canonical Grants and Mandates.

Atlas may use several Model Deployments over time while remaining one Agent.

9.566 Applied Example — Atlas Provider Swap

Atlas requests:

text.reason.

The Registry exposes several possible Model Deployments.

The Router selects one according to policy.

Atlas receives the result without changing Agent identity or storing Provider Credentials.

9.567 Applied Example — Atlas Tool Discovery

An MCP server suddenly advertises:

delete_repository.

The Tool appears as a discovered candidate.

It does not become active.

Omnira requires:

- server identity,

- schema review,

- side-effect classification,

- filesystem scope,

- authority requirements,

- testing,

- and explicit admission.

9.568 Applied Example — Arnold

Arnold is registered as a GainPilot coaching Agent.

His identity persists across:

- local Model,

- external Model,

- laptop,

- workstation,

- or future private server.

His coaching role does not grant unrestricted file or health-data access.

9.569 Applied Example — GainPilot Local Tool

A Tool reads current workout-plan data from the GainPilot Project.

It is registered as:

- Project-scoped,

- read operation,

- Confidential-capable,

- GainPilot only,

- no external network,

- and bounded database access.

Familje-Stunden cannot invoke it merely because Atlas knows that it exists.

9.570 Applied Example — Programme Mutation Tool

A GainPilot Tool can change a training programme.

The Tool is classified:

Project write.

Changing one exercise may fall inside one bounded Mandate.

Changing programme structure may require higher authority.

The Tool definition describes the operation.

Authority is evaluated separately.

9.571 Applied Example — Familje-Stunden Image Tool

An image-generation Tool exposes:

image.generate.

Its Tool Definition references:

- Adapter-backed external execution,

- generated Asset output,

- Project scope,

- Budget requirements,

- and human QA before publication.

The Tool itself cannot publish the result.

9.572 Applied Example — Familje-Stunden Publication Tool

A separate Tool exposes:

publication.publish.

It has:

- external write,

- publication side effect,

- exact Account requirement,

- exact Asset Version requirement,

- and elevated approval requirement.

Image generation authority does not grant publication authority.

9.573 Applied Example — Nova Reference Assets

Nova reference images are Assets.

They are not Tools.

An image Tool may receive them as governed Input references.

The distinction preserves:

- identity,

- provenance,

- scope,

- and rights.

9.574 Applied Example — ElevenLabs Voice Tool

A Voice Tool may expose:

voice.generate.

It references:

- ElevenLabs Connector,

- Voice Profile requirement,

- Consent requirement,

- character or narrator context,

- cost profile,

- audio Asset output,

- and Project scope.

The API Credential remains outside the Tool metadata.

9.575 Applied Example — Voice Profile Provider ID

A Provider-native Voice ID is an integration-side reference.

The canonical Voice Profile remains an Omnira resource or governed identity object.

Changing Provider does not require changing the story identity attached to the Voice Profile.

9.576 Applied Example — The Prompt Search Tool

A search Tool exposes:

search.web.

It declares:

- external read,

- public or eligible Input,

- source-linked Output,

- network requirement,

- and no Memory write.

Search results remain untrusted external content.

9.577 Applied Example — The Prompt Publication Browser

A Browser Runtime uses a dedicated Project profile.

The publication Tool references that Runtime and exact social Account.

A personal browser Session is not eligible.

9.578 Applied Example — OpenArt Human-Assisted Resource

OpenArt is used through a manual workflow.

The Registry represents:

- external platform,

- required Account,

- Human-Assisted Resource,

- human operator,

- image-generation capability,

- credit cost,

- evidence requirement,

- and expected turnaround.

It does not claim an API that does not exist.

9.579 Applied Example — Ollama Runtime

A local Runtime Service is registered:

- Runtime type: Ollama,

- Node: approved workstation,

- transport: local HTTP,

- installed Model Deployments,

- health,

- capacity,

- and Local Only eligibility.

Atlas sees local intelligence capability rather than a raw localhost endpoint.

text:
9.580 Applied Example — Local Model Upgrade

A local Model tag now resolves to different content.

The Registry detects changed digest.

The Deployment becomes drifted.

Production eligibility may pause until evaluation and conformance are updated.

9.581 Applied Example — Local Node Offline

A Local Only GainPilot Request requires a local Node.

The Node heartbeat expires.

The Node becomes unavailable.

The Fabric does not route the sensitive Request to an external Provider.

It waits, blocks or asks for the Node to be started.

9.582 Applied Example — Windows Workstation

A Windows workstation may expose:

- NVIDIA GPU,

- local inference Runtime,

- Tool Runtime,

- file-processing Tools,

- and media transformation.

Each remains a separately registered Resource or dependency.

The machine itself does not gain arbitrary Project file access.

9.583 Applied Example — Mac Laptop

A Mac laptop may serve as:

- developer Node,

- local lightweight Model Node,

- Tool host,

- and approval interface.

Production eligibility depends on current trust, Environment and Project scope.

9.584 Applied Example — Coding Agent

A coding Agent is registered with:

- repository role,

- allowed Tool classes,

- no default commit authority,

- no default push authority,

- and constrained filesystem paths.

Its underlying coding Model may change without expanding these limits.

9.585 Applied Example — Git Tool

A Git Tool may expose separate Operations:

- status,

- diff,

- stage,

- commit,

- push.

These Operations shall not share one authority class automatically.

Read operations may be lower risk.

Commit and push require distinct authority.

9.586 Applied Example — Wrong Repository

The coding Agent is instructed to work in one repository.

The filesystem or Git Tool reports another.

The Resource execution shall fail or pause before mutation.

Tool availability does not override task scope.

9.587 Applied Example — Database Read Tool

A Project database Tool supports read-only queries.

The Tool is healthy.

A user asks it to delete a row.

The operation is unsupported.

The Fabric shall not reinterpret health as mutation permission.

9.588 Applied Example — Database Write Tool

A write Tool exists separately.

Its use requires:

- correct Project,

- transaction scope,

- write authority,

- and audit.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
