text:
9.589 Applied Example — Device Screenshot Tool

A mobile Node exposes a screenshot Capability.

The Tool is classified as privacy-sensitive system observation.

The user’s device ownership does not grant Atlas unrestricted screenshot authority.

9.590 Applied Example — Location Tool

A device may expose bounded location information.

The Resource shall identify:

- device,

- granularity,

- permission,

- Project or purpose,

- and retention.

Precise location shall not be collected simply because the device can provide it.

9.591 Applied Example — Human Reviewer

A Familje-Stunden human Reviewer evaluates a generated child-facing illustration.

The human is assigned through a Human Resource queue.

Review does not itself publish the Asset.

Publication remains a separate governed Tool action.

9.592 Applied Example — Resource Degradation

An image Tool still responds but generates malformed files intermittently.

Health becomes degraded.

Routing may reduce or stop use depending on Quality and reliability evidence.

9.593 Applied Example — Resource Incident

A Tool accesses a directory outside its registered scope.

The system:

- records Incident evidence,

- quarantines the Tool,

- stops new invocations,

- identifies dependent workflows,

- and requires verification before reactivation.

9.594 Applied Example — Tool Version Update

A Provider integration adds a new optional parameter.

If semantics remain backward compatible, one compatible Version update may be sufficient.

If the parameter changes side effects or data exposure, revalidation is required.

9.595 Applied Example — MCP Tool Disappears

An approved MCP server no longer advertises a registered Tool.

The Resource becomes unavailable or drifted.

Historical Executions continue referencing its prior Tool Version.

9.596 Applied Example — Human Operator Unavailable

A Human-Assisted Resource requires one operator pool.

The human queue is unavailable.

Planning may:

- wait,

- select another approved human resource,

- or present the task as blocked.

The system shall not pretend the manual task completed.

9.597 Applied Example — Shared Provider Tool

Two Projects use the same external search Provider.

The Provider Tool may be shared.

Each invocation still carries:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Account or Connection,

- Classification,

- and Evidence.

9.598 Applied Example — Personal Account

A user has a personal design-platform Account.

A Project requests production work.

The Account is not automatically eligible.

The user must intentionally connect or authorise its Project use.

9.599 Applied Example — Retired Tool

A publication Tool is replaced by a safer Connector.

The old Tool becomes retired.

Past publication Evidence can still resolve it.

New Plans cannot select it.

9.600 Applied Example — External Agent

An external specialist Agent offers video-editing Capability.

It is registered as an External Agent Resource.

It receives only:

- exact task,

- approved Assets,

- Project scope,

- Budget,

- and bounded authority.

It does not gain Atlas’s identity, Memory or Tools.

9.601 Anti-Pattern — Agent Equals Model

An Agent shall never be represented only by the Model currently serving it.

9.602 Anti-Pattern — Agent Equals Provider Session

Provider conversation IDs are not Agent identity.

9.603 Anti-Pattern — Model Swap Creates New Agent

Changing intelligence implementation shall not erase persistent Agent identity.

9.604 Anti-Pattern — Agent Role Creates Authority

Role names do not grant permissions.

9.605 Anti-Pattern — Agent Owns API Keys

Credentials belong at the governed execution boundary.

9.606 Anti-Pattern — Agent Registers Its Own Tools

Discovery and admission remain separate.

9.607 Anti-Pattern — Agent Self-Certifies

Conformance remains separate from execution.

9.608 Anti-Pattern — Tool Description Is Trusted Instruction

Tool metadata is data.

9.609 Anti-Pattern — MCP Discovery Is Permission

Protocol discovery does not create authority.

9.610 Anti-Pattern — Every Executable Is a Tool

Local PATH contents shall not become automatic Agent capabilities.

9.611 Anti-Pattern — Unrestricted Shell as Default Tool

Narrow operations are preferred.

9.612 Anti-Pattern — Tool Has No Input Schema

Production Tools require bounded Inputs.

9.613 Anti-Pattern — Tool Has No Output Contract

Outputs shall be validated.

9.614 Anti-Pattern — Tool Side Effect Unknown but Treated Read-Only

Unknown side effects require restrictive handling.

9.615 Anti-Pattern — One Tool Mixes Read and Delete Under One Permission

Operation-level authority should distinguish consequences.

9.627 Anti-Pattern — Model Deployment Equals Model

9.628 Anti-Pattern — GPU Equals Intelligence Resource

9.629 Anti-Pattern — Pool Membership Equals Eligibility

9.630 Anti-Pattern — Human Work Hidden From Execution Graph

9.631 Anti-Pattern — Human Review Equals Approval

9.632 Anti-Pattern — Human-Assisted Provider Labelled Automated

Execution truth matters.

9.633 Anti-Pattern — Resource Exists Therefore Agent May Use It

9.638 Anti-Pattern — Resource Label Used as Stable ID

9.667 Future Agent Registry Architecture

Future Agent Registry versions may support:

- richer roles,

- Agent teams,

- capability profiles,

- performance evidence,

- portable Runtime state,

- delegated authority graphs,

- and external Agent federation.

9.668 Agent Team

An Agent Team may coordinate several persistent Agent identities.

9.669 Team Is Not One Agent

Team membership shall not collapse accountability.

9.670 Team Role

Each Agent retains its own:

- role,

- authority,

- Memory scope,

- and Tool access.

9.671 Agent Supervisor

A supervisor Agent may coordinate others under explicit delegation.

9.672 Supervisor Cannot Grant Authority It Does Not Possess

Delegation shall remain bounded.

9.673 Agent Capability Reputation

Future systems may track task-specific Agent performance.

9.674 Reputation Scope

Performance evidence shall remain:

- task-specific,

- Project-aware,

- Version-aware,

- and time-aware.

9.675 Agent Runtime Portability

Agents may move among cloud, local and edge Runtimes.

9.676 Portable Agent State

Portable state shall exclude raw Secrets and unauthorised Memory.

9.677 External Agent Federation

External Agents may become routable resources after identity, trust and Conformance mature.

9.678 Agent Protocol Independence

A future Agent protocol shall not redefine canonical Agent identity.

9.679 Future Tool Registry Architecture

The Tool Registry may support:

- signed packages,

- marketplaces,

- dynamic sandbox creation,

- capability negotiation,

- remote Tools,

- local Tools,

- edge Tools,

- and policy-generated Tool Views.

9.680 Tool View

A Tool View is the exact subset of Tool Operations exposed to one Agent or Plan.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.681 Tool View Is Contextual

Tool Views may differ by:

- Project,

- user,

- authority,

- Environment,

- and task.

9.682 Tool View Minimisation

Agents should receive only Tools relevant to current work.

9.683 Dynamic Tool Exposure

Dynamic exposure may reduce context size and risk.

It shall still derive from registered Tools and current policy.

9.684 Tool Marketplace

A marketplace may distribute Tool packages.

Installation and production admission remain separate.

9.685 Tool Package Certification

Packages may carry signed Conformance evidence.

Local policy must still verify applicability.

9.686 Future Execution Resource Architecture

Execution Resources may expand to:

- private GPU clusters,

- confidential compute,

- mobile NPUs,

- edge devices,

- serverless functions,

- specialised accelerators,

- and federated compute.

9.687 Confidential Resource

A confidential-compute Resource may provide attestation evidence.

Data eligibility still depends on Project policy.

9.688 Serverless Resource

Serverless execution may be represented as Runtime Service with:

- Provider,

- region,

- Runtime,

- limits,

- and cost.

9.689 Edge Accelerator

An edge accelerator may host local Model Deployments under the same Node contract.

9.690 Federated Resource Pool

Several independent Nodes may form one policy-governed Pool.

9.691 Resource Handoff

Future execution may hand work among Nodes.

Identity, state, authority and Evidence shall survive handoff.

9.692 Cross-Node Continuation

Continuation shall not duplicate side effects.

9.693 Resource Attestation Evolution

Node and Runtime trust may incorporate:

- hardware attestation,

- secure boot,

- signed Runtime,

- and workload identity.

9.694 Resource Energy Profile

Future scheduling may consider:

- energy use,

- battery impact,

- thermal impact,

- and carbon estimates.

9.695 Energy Is Ranking Input

Sustainability may influence ranking only after mandatory eligibility.

9.696 User Activity Awareness

Personal-device scheduling may consider whether the user is actively using the machine.

9.697 Foreground Protection

Heavy Fabric work should not silently degrade critical user activity where policy requires protection.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.698 Resource Lease Market

Future shared infrastructure may allocate scarce compute through governed internal reservations.

Economic optimisation shall not override Project priority or privacy.

9.699 Future Human Resource Architecture

Human Resources may support:

- skills,

- queues,

- shifts,

- Project clearance,

- reviewer calibration,

- and multi-party review.

9.700 Reviewer Calibration

Human evaluation quality may itself receive evidence and training.

Reviewer scoring shall not become authority.

9.701 Multi-Reviewer Requirement

High-impact content may require more than one independent Reviewer.

9.702 Human Escalation Pool

Specialists may receive escalated tasks when ordinary automation lacks confidence.

9.703 Human Privacy Clearance

Human access to sensitive Project data may require explicit clearance.

9.704 Future Resource Graph

The Registry may project a Resource Graph containing:

- dependencies,

- capabilities,

- owners,

- deployments,

- Pools,

- Agents,

- Tools,

- and Nodes.

9.705 Resource Graph Is Projection

The graph does not replace canonical Resource records.

9.706 Resource Graph Use

It may support:

- blast-radius analysis,

- Planning,

- migration,

- security review,

- and Incident Response.

9.707 Resource Graph Access

Protected relationships shall remain Tenant- and Project-scoped.

9.708 Canonical Agent Resource Contract

The following requirements define Agent Resources:

1. Every Agent SHALL have stable canonical identity.

2. Agent identity SHALL be independent from Model.

3. Agent identity SHALL be independent from Provider.

4. Agent identity SHALL be independent from Runtime.

5. Agent identity SHALL be independent from Session.

6. Every material Agent definition SHALL have Version.

7. Role SHALL be explicit.

8. Owner SHALL be explicit.

9. Tenant SHALL be explicit.

10. Project relationships SHALL be explicit.

11. Memory access policy SHALL be explicit.

12. Tool policy SHALL be explicit.

13. Authority metadata SHALL be explicit.

14. Role SHALL NOT create authority.

15. Tool availability SHALL NOT create authority.

16. Model swap SHALL NOT expand authority.

17. Provider swap SHALL NOT expand authority.

18. Agent SHALL NOT self-authorise.

19. Agent SHALL NOT self-certify.

20. Historical Agent identity SHALL remain resolvable after retirement.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.709 Canonical Tool Resource Contract

The following requirements define Tool Resources:

1. Every Tool SHALL have stable identity.

2. Every material Tool definition SHALL have Version.

3. Tool type SHALL be explicit.

4. Owner SHALL be explicit.

5. Capability Bindings SHALL be explicit.

6. Input schema SHALL be explicit.

7. Output contract SHALL be explicit.

8. Side-effect class SHALL be explicit.

9. Unknown side effects SHALL be restrictive.

10. Runtime requirements SHALL be explicit.

11. permission requirements SHALL be explicit.

12. data eligibility SHALL be explicit.

13. Project scope SHALL be explicit where applicable.

14. network scope SHALL be explicit where material.

15. filesystem scope SHALL be explicit where material.

16. retry semantics SHALL be explicit.

17. cancellation semantics SHALL be explicit.

18. raw Secrets SHALL NOT appear in Tool metadata.

19. registration SHALL NOT create invocation authority.

20. Tool self-description SHALL NOT become policy.

9.710 Canonical Tool Operation Contract

The following requirements define Tool Operations:

1. Every material Operation SHALL be identifiable inside one Tool Version.

2. Capability SHALL be explicit.

3. Input schema SHALL be explicit.

4. Output schema or contract SHALL be explicit.

5. side-effect class SHALL be explicit.

6. authority requirement SHALL be explicit.

7. Classification limit SHALL be explicit.

8. idempotency SHALL be explicit where relevant.

9. retry safety SHALL be explicit.

10. timeout SHALL be bounded.

11. cancellation semantics SHALL be explicit.

12. cost MAY be operation-specific.

13. capacity MAY be operation-specific.

14. unsupported Operation SHALL fail before dispatch.

15. changed side effect SHALL require revalidation.

16. changed permissions SHALL require revalidation.

17. changed schema SHALL require Version or compatibility review.

18. invocation SHALL be attributable.

19. historical Operation Versions SHALL remain resolvable.

20. One broad Tool permission SHALL NOT silently authorise every Operation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.711 Canonical Resource Discovery Contract

The following requirements define Resource Discovery:

1. Every Discovery event SHOULD identify source.

2. discovery time SHALL be explicit.

3. candidate Resource type SHALL be explicit.

4. native identity SHALL be preserved.

5. raw metadata MAY be retained as bounded evidence.

6. discovery SHALL NOT equal registration.

7. registration SHALL NOT equal qualification.

8. qualification SHALL NOT equal authority.

9. discovered Tools SHALL NOT become Agent-visible automatically.

10. discovered Nodes SHALL NOT become trusted automatically.

11. discovered Models SHALL NOT become production-eligible automatically.

12. discovered MCP Capabilities SHALL require schema validation.

13. discovery SHALL avoid unnecessary Secret exposure.

14. discovery scope SHALL be bounded.

15. local executable discovery SHALL use approved paths.

16. drift between discoveries SHALL be detectable.

17. removed Resources SHALL remain historically resolvable.

18. discovery failure SHALL remain explicit.

19. automated discovery SHALL use Service Principal identity.

20. Discovery convenience SHALL NOT become a trust shortcut.

9.712 Canonical Runtime Node Contract

The following requirements define Runtime Nodes:

1. Every Node SHALL have stable identity.

2. Node identity SHALL not depend on IP address.

3. owner SHALL be explicit.

4. Tenant SHALL be explicit.

5. Project eligibility SHALL be explicit or derivable.

6. Environment SHALL be explicit.

7. device class SHALL be explicit.

8. operating system SHALL be explicit where relevant.

9. hardware profile SHALL be attributable.

10. trust state SHALL be explicit.

11. lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

12. Runtime Services SHALL be discoverable.

13. health SHALL be observable.

14. availability SHALL be observable.

15. heartbeat freshness SHALL be bounded.

16. capacity SHALL be observable where schedulable.

17. Node loss SHALL become explicit.

18. Local Only policy SHALL survive Node failure.

19. revocation SHALL prevent new execution.

20. Device ownership SHALL NOT create unrestricted execution authority.

9.713 Canonical Runtime Service Contract

The following requirements define Runtime Services:

1. Every Runtime Service SHALL have stable identity.

2. Runtime type SHALL be explicit.

3. Runtime Version SHALL be explicit.

4. hosting Node or Provider context SHALL be explicit.

5. transport SHALL be explicit.

6. capabilities SHALL be explicit.

7. health SHALL be observable.

8. capacity SHALL be observable where material.

9. network exposure SHALL be bounded.

10. process identity SHOULD be explicit.

11. lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

12. upgrade SHALL be attributable.

13. material upgrade SHALL trigger revalidation.

14. restart SHALL NOT create new canonical identity unnecessarily.

15. endpoint SHALL remain inside infrastructure boundary.

16. Agent SHALL NOT depend directly on endpoint.

17. Secret access SHALL be minimal.

18. failure SHALL remain distinct from Node failure.

19. historical Runtime Version SHALL remain reconstructable.

20. Local Runtime SHALL NOT become a governance bypass.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.714 Canonical Model Deployment Contract

The following requirements define Model Deployments:

1. Every production Deployment SHALL have stable identity.

2. canonical Model SHALL be explicit.

3. Runtime SHALL be explicit.

4. Node or Provider execution context SHALL be explicit.

5. configuration SHALL be explicit.

6. context limit SHALL be explicit or verified.

7. quantisation SHALL be explicit where relevant.

8. health SHALL be observable.

9. capacity SHALL be observable where material.

10. cost SHALL be attributable where relevant.

11. Capability Bindings SHALL reference deployment constraints.

12. Deployment SHALL remain distinct from Model identity.

13. two Deployments of one Model MAY have different eligibility.

14. local Deployments SHOULD preserve checksum.

15. external Deployments SHALL preserve Provider and Account context as available.

16. Version changes SHALL be detectable.

17. certification SHALL be scope-specific.

18. retired Deployments SHALL remain historical.

19. Agent identity SHALL remain independent from Deployment.

20. Deployment availability SHALL NOT create invocation authority.

9.715 Canonical Resource Pool Contract

The following requirements define Resource Pools:

1. Every governed Pool SHALL have stable identity.

2. Pool purpose SHALL be explicit.

3. member Resources SHALL be explicit.

4. membership Version SHALL be attributable.

5. Capability scope SHALL be explicit.

6. Tenant scope SHALL be explicit.

7. Project scope SHALL be explicit where relevant.

8. Environment SHALL be explicit.

9. member health SHALL remain visible.

10. aggregate capacity MAY be exposed.

11. pool membership SHALL NOT equal Request eligibility.

12. Routing SHALL still evaluate individual contextual eligibility.

13. shared Pools SHALL preserve Tenant and Project isolation.

14. dedicated Pools SHALL preserve owner scope.

15. retired members SHALL not receive new work.

16. suspended members SHALL not receive new work.

17. member drift SHALL affect Pool eligibility.

18. historical membership SHALL remain queryable.

19. Pool selection SHALL remain explainable.

20. A Pool SHALL NOT hide underlying data custody or side effects.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.716 Canonical Human Resource Contract

The following requirements define Human Resources:

1. Every governed human operator SHALL map to a Principal.

2. Human Resource role SHALL be explicit.

3. skills MAY be registered.

4. skills SHALL NOT create authority.

5. Project eligibility SHALL be explicit.

6. availability SHALL be observable where required.

7. capacity MAY be represented.

8. assignment SHALL be attributable.

9. data minimisation SHALL apply.

10. Confidential access SHALL require appropriate authority.

11. review SHALL remain distinct from approval.

12. manual execution SHALL remain truthful.

13. external Account used by the human SHALL be explicit.

14. cost or time MAY be represented.

15. completion SHALL require evidence appropriate to risk.

16. human error SHALL remain attributable.

17. revocation SHALL stop new assignment.

18. historical assignments SHALL remain queryable.

19. Human-Assisted work SHALL remain visible in Evidence.

20. Human involvement SHALL NOT be hidden merely to make automation appear more complete.

9.717 Canonical External Agent Resource Contract

The following requirements define External Agent Resources:

1. Every external Agent Resource SHALL have stable local canonical identity.

2. external operator SHALL be explicit.

3. protocol SHALL be explicit.

4. endpoint SHALL remain integration-side.

5. Version SHALL be explicit where available.

6. claimed Capabilities SHALL require validation.

7. data policy SHALL be explicit.

8. trust state SHALL be explicit.

9. authentication reference SHALL be explicit.

10. Tenant and Project delegation SHALL be bounded.

11. external Agent SHALL NOT inherit Omnira Agent identity.

12. external Agent SHALL NOT receive Omnira Memory automatically.

13. external Agent SHALL NOT receive Omnira Tool authority automatically.

14. Output SHALL remain untrusted until validated.

15. cost SHALL be attributable where applicable.

16. lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

17. Conformance SHALL precede high-risk use.

18. revocation SHALL be supported.

19. historical delegated work SHALL remain attributable.

20. Protocol compatibility SHALL NOT create trust or authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.718 Canonical Resource Health Contract

The following requirements define Resource Health:

1. Health SHALL be Resource-specific.

2. health observation time SHALL be explicit.

3. source SHALL be explicit.

4. freshness SHALL be considered.

5. health SHALL remain distinct from lifecycle.

6. health SHALL remain distinct from authority.

7. health SHALL remain distinct from Quality.

8. health SHALL remain distinct from certification.

9. degraded state SHALL be representable.

10. unavailable state SHALL be representable.

11. unknown state SHALL be representable.

12. synthetic probes MAY inform health.

13. operational telemetry MAY inform health.

14. stale observations SHALL NOT be treated as current fact indefinitely.

15. severe health failure MAY remove Resource eligibility.

16. recovery SHALL require new evidence.

17. health history SHOULD remain queryable.

18. incidents SHALL link to relevant health changes.

19. health updates SHALL NOT rewrite historical Execution state.

20. A healthy Resource SHALL NOT become eligible if other mandatory requirements fail.

9.719 Canonical Resource Drift Contract

The following requirements define Resource Drift:

1. Every material drift event SHOULD have stable identity.

2. Resource SHALL be explicit.

3. expected state SHALL be explicit.

4. observed state SHALL be explicit.

5. observation time SHALL be explicit.

6. source SHALL be explicit.

7. drift type SHALL be explicit.

8. severity SHALL be explicit.

9. capability drift SHALL be detectable.

10. schema drift SHALL be detectable.

11. permission drift SHALL be detectable.

12. Runtime drift SHALL be detectable.

13. dependency drift SHALL be detectable.

14. side-effect drift SHALL be treated as high risk.

15. material drift SHALL trigger review.

16. critical drift MAY suspend Resource automatically.

17. resolution SHALL be attributable.

18. historical drift SHALL remain queryable.

19. current metadata updates SHALL NOT rewrite past Evidence.

20. Drift SHALL NOT be ignored merely because the Resource still responds.

9.720 Canonical Registry Governance Contract

The following requirements define Registry governance:

1. Every canonical Resource SHALL have stable identity.

2. every material Resource definition SHALL have Version.

3. ownership SHALL be explicit.

4. Tenant SHALL be explicit.

5. Project scope SHALL be explicit where applicable.

6. Environment SHALL be explicit.

7. lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

8. discovery SHALL remain distinct from registration.

9. registration SHALL remain distinct from qualification.

10. qualification SHALL remain distinct from execution authority.

11. health SHALL remain distinct from eligibility.

12. Capability claims SHALL require evidence.

13. raw Secrets SHALL be prohibited.

14. material Registry mutations SHALL be audited.

15. historical Versions SHALL remain queryable.

16. revocation SHALL propagate to eligibility.

17. retirement SHALL prevent new work.

18. restore SHALL preserve current revocations.

19. policy SHALL remain external to Registry facts.

20. Registry existence SHALL NOT become execution permission.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
sectionTitles: 9.721 Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Invariants
text:
9.721 Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No Agent identity depends on one Model.

- No Agent identity depends on one Provider.

- No Agent identity depends on one Runtime.

- No Agent role creates authority.

- No Agent self-authorises.

- No Agent self-certifies.

- No Tool exists in production without stable identity.

- No discovered Tool becomes automatically active.

- No MCP discovery becomes permission.

- No Tool side effect remains implicitly trusted.

- No raw Secret belongs in Resource metadata.

- No Tool receives unrestricted filesystem or network access by default.

- No Runtime endpoint becomes an Agent dependency.

- No local Node becomes trusted merely because it is local.

- No Node being online makes it automatically eligible.

- No Model Deployment becomes the Model identity itself.

- No Resource Pool membership becomes execution eligibility.

- No Human-Assisted work is represented as API automation.

- No Resource remains production-eligible after critical unreviewed drift.

- No Resource registration becomes execution authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
9.722 Closing Statement

The Intelligence Fabric cannot route, schedule or govern intelligence reliably unless the things capable of doing work have stable canonical identity.

Models are only one class of resource.

Providers are only one class of resource.

Agents, Tools, Runtimes, Nodes, humans and execution infrastructure are equally important parts of the operational intelligence system.

The Agent Registry ensures that Atlas, Arnold and future Agents retain persistent Omnira identity independently from whatever Model happens to serve them.

The Tool Registry ensures that useful operations become explicit, bounded and reviewable instead of appearing as arbitrary capabilities inside prompts or protocols.

The Execution Resource Registry ensures that Omnira understands where work can actually run, what dependencies exist, what capacity is available and which environments are safe for each workload.

The Runtime Node gives compute a stable identity.

The Runtime Service describes the software that exposes execution.

The Model Deployment binds intelligence to a concrete execution environment.

The Tool Instance binds an operation to a concrete Runtime.

The Human Resource makes manual intelligence and review truthful.

The Human-Assisted Resource allows Omnira to govern workflows that are not yet fully automated.

The External Agent Resource allows future Agent ecosystems to participate without receiving automatic trust.

The Resource Pool creates schedulable groups without hiding member identity.

The Capability Binding describes what each Resource may be able to do.

The Health Observation describes whether it appears capable of doing it now.

The Conformance evidence describes whether the implementation has been verified.

Policy determines whether it may do it for this Request.

Authority determines whether the action may occur.

Routing determines which eligible Resource should be selected.

Execution creates the actual Attempt.

Evidence records what really happened.

For Familje-Stunden, this means that:

- Nova and Pling remain Project Assets rather than Provider concepts,

- image generation remains a Tool or Model Capability,

- Voice production remains separately governed,

- publication remains a distinct Tool class,

- human creative review remains visible,

- and no Provider can become the owner of the Project’s creative identity.

For The Prompt, this means that:

- search,

- reasoning,

- visual generation,

- browser operations,

- and publication

can be composed from different registered Resources while retaining Project scope and source evidence.

For GainPilot, this means that:

- Arnold remains Arnold across Model changes,

- local health-sensitive reasoning can use approved Nodes,

- Project Tools remain isolated,

- programme mutation can be separated from ordinary read access,

- and no local or external resource gains broader health-data access merely because it is technically capable.

For Atlas, this means that:

- Atlas can discover what Omnira is capable of without learning raw infrastructure details,

- it can request Capabilities rather than endpoints,

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Agent, Tool and Execution Resource Registry
text:
- it can receive governed Tool Views rather than unrestricted Tool inventories,

- and it can change Models, Providers and execution locations without changing its identity.

For Omnira, this creates one common language for every actor and mechanism capable of participating in intelligence work.

No Agent without identity.

No Tool without a contract.

No Operation without side-effect classification.

No Runtime without scope.

No Node without ownership.

No discovered Resource without admission.

No admitted Resource without qualification where required.

No healthy Resource without contextual eligibility.

No Resource without lifecycle.

No Resource drift without evidence.

No Human-Assisted work without truth.

No external Agent without bounded delegation.

No execution Resource without governance.

The user retains authority.

The Project retains scope.

The Agent retains identity.

The Tool retains bounded purpose.

The Runtime retains operational identity.

Omnira retains canonical resource truth.

The Fabric may choose among intelligence resources without allowing the resources themselves to determine who they are allowed to serve, what they are allowed to access or what they are allowed to do.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical architecture, governance model, lifecycle, contracts and operational responsibilities for Intelligence Planning and Execution Graphs within the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

It establishes:

- how validated Capability Requests become executable plans,

- how complex intent is decomposed into bounded work,

- how execution dependencies are represented,

- how mandatory, optional, conditional and fallback paths are modelled,

- how models, providers, tools, local resources and human steps are combined,

- how budgets, authority, data classification, rights and quality remain attached throughout planning,

- how parallelism and sequencing are determined,

- how iterative refinement and retries remain bounded,

- how side effects and irreversible actions are isolated,

- how plans are versioned, approved, activated, revised and retired,

- how partial execution and unknown outcomes are reconciled,

- how planning remains separate from execution,

- and how Stage 1 shall implement a minimal but trustworthy planning architecture.

The Intelligence Planner transforms approved intent into a governed description of how work may proceed.

The Planner does not receive authority to change the user’s objective.

It does not receive permission to weaken mandatory policy.

It does not receive unlimited budget.

It does not receive the right to perform every step it can imagine.

The Planner may select and organise eligible implementation paths only inside the boundaries of the Capability Request, Authority Envelope, Budget Envelope, Quality Contract and current policy.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

Implementation and conformance must be verified separately.

10.2 Purpose of Intelligence Planning

A Capability Request describes what Omnira is expected to achieve.

A Provider call describes one technical operation.

Complex work usually requires something between them.

That intermediate layer is the Execution Plan.

The Execution Plan determines:

- which capabilities are required,

- how they depend on one another,

- which resources are eligible,

- where approvals are required,

- how much cost may be consumed,

- how quality will be evaluated,

- how failure will be handled,

- and what evidence proves completion.

Without a planning layer, complex intent would become:

- one oversized prompt,

- hard-coded provider workflow,

- uncontrolled agent improvisation,

- or a sequence of disconnected API calls.

The planning layer allows Omnira to preserve human intent while adapting implementation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.3 Planning Is Not Execution

Planning determines what may be attempted.

Execution performs the approved work.

A Planner may:

- analyse requirements,

- decompose work,

- identify dependencies,

- compare resources,

- estimate cost,

- propose fallback,

- and define checkpoints.

Planning shall not:

- consume production credits unnecessarily,

- publish content,

- mutate canonical Assets,

- send external messages,

- modify production systems,

- or perform another consequential side effect

unless that operation is itself an explicitly authorised planning-stage capability.

A plan may be complete while no execution has begun.

10.4 Planning Is Not Intent

Intent describes the desired outcome.

Planning describes one permitted implementation of that outcome.

Several valid plans may satisfy the same Intent.

For example, a Nova and Pling episode may be produced through:

- premium scene-by-scene video generation,

- lower-cost image animation plus local composition,

- motion-comic production,

- or a human-assisted creative workflow.

The Intent may remain unchanged while the selected plan changes.

10.5 Planning Is Not Authority

The existence of a technically valid plan does not authorise execution.

The plan must remain inside the effective Authority Envelope.

A Planner may identify that publication would complete a production.

It shall not add publication authority when the request authorises only generation.

A Planner may estimate that an additional premium retry would improve quality.

It shall not increase the retry budget without approval.

10.6 Planning Is Not Routing

Planning defines the required work and candidate structure.

Routing selects eligible resources for specific Execution Steps.

Planning may identify:

- required Capability,

- resource constraints,

- preferred execution pattern,

- and fallback class.

Routing evaluates current:

- Provider Accounts,

- Models,

- Deployments,

- cost,

- health,

- capacity,

- quality evidence,

- and policy.

Planning and routing may interact iteratively.

They shall remain conceptually distinct.

10.7 Planning Is Not Workflow Definition

A Workflow Definition is a reusable governed template.

An Execution Plan is a request-specific plan created for one Capability Request, Production or Workflow Run.

The Workflow may define:

- expected steps,

- decision points,

- dependencies,

- and policies.

The Execution Plan resolves:

- current Inputs,

- current resource candidates,

- current budget,

- current approvals,

- and current operational state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.8 Planning Is Not Agent Autonomy

An Agent may assist with planning.

The canonical plan remains an Omnira-governed object.

Agent reasoning shall not become invisible runtime authority.

The plan must expose:

- steps,

- constraints,

- dependencies,

- cost,

- authority,

- and completion requirements

in a form that can be validated independently of the Agent’s internal reasoning.

10.9 Intelligence Planner

The Intelligence Planner is the Fabric component or governed service responsible for constructing Execution Plans.

The Planner may use:

- deterministic rules,

- reusable templates,

- graph algorithms,

- policy evaluation,

- cost estimation,

- resource discovery,

- AI-assisted decomposition,

- historical evidence,

- and human input.

The Planner shall have a stable Service Principal identity.

It shall operate with limited authority.

It shall not directly own Provider credentials.

10.10 Planner Responsibilities

The Planner is responsible for:

- receiving a validated Capability Request,

- resolving applicable planning templates,

- decomposing the request,

- identifying required and optional Capability Steps,

- attaching Inputs and Output Contracts,

- defining dependencies,

- defining approval boundaries,

- defining evaluation requirements,

- allocating budget,

- identifying eligible resource classes,

- estimating cost and latency,

- defining retry and fallback policies,

- defining Completion Contract,

- and producing a versioned Execution Plan.

The Planner shall preserve all mandatory request constraints.

10.11 Planner Non-Responsibilities

The Planner is not responsible for:

- owning Project strategy,

- approving its own budget expansion,

- accepting Provider terms,

- creating unrestricted credentials,

- overriding Data Classification,

- granting publication authority,

- or declaring output accepted without evaluation.

These responsibilities belong to other governed components or human authorities.

10.12 Planning Input

The Planner shall receive a canonical Planning Input Package.

The package should include:

- Capability Request ID and Version,

- Intent reference,

- caller,

- initiator,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- Authority Envelope,

- Policy Decisions,

- Routing Profile,

- Budget Envelope,

- Capability Requirements,

- Input references,

- Output Contract,

- Quality Contract,

- Completion Contract,

- rights and consent references,

- deadline,

- priority,

- and permitted assumptions.

The Planner shall not reconstruct authoritative constraints from informal conversation when canonical request data exists.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.13 Planning Context

Planning Context may also include:

- Capability Registry Snapshot,

- Model Registry Snapshot,

- Provider Registry Snapshot,

- Tool Registry Snapshot,

- available Workflow templates,

- historical performance evidence,

- current quotas,

- current capacity,

- and relevant governed learning.

Planning Context shall declare freshness.

Stale operational information may support estimation.

It must not be represented as current certainty.

10.14 Planning Output

The primary output of planning is an Execution Plan.

Planning may also produce:

- Plan Alternatives,

- Cost Estimates,

- Latency Estimates,

- Resource Requirements,

- Approval Requests,

- Capability Gap Records,

- Planning Warnings,

- Assumption Register,

- and Human Decision Points.

A failed planning attempt shall produce evidence explaining why no valid plan could be created.

10.15 Execution Plan

An Execution Plan is a versioned canonical object describing how one request may be fulfilled.

It shall include or reference:

- planId,

- planVersion,

- requestId,

- requestVersion,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- objective,

- plan status,

- planning strategy,

- Execution Graph,

- step definitions,

- dependency definitions,

- resource requirements,

- selected or deferred resources,

- budget allocation,

- expected cost,

- expected latency,

- approval points,

- quality gates,

- retry policies,

- fallback policies,

- compensation policies,

- Completion Contract,

- assumptions,

- warnings,

- and provenance.

10.16 Plan Identity

Every persistent Execution Plan shall have stable identity.

Plan identity shall remain separate from:

- Capability Request,

- Workflow,

- Execution,

- and plan version.

One Capability Request may have several competing or sequential plans.

10.17 Plan Version

Material changes shall create a new Plan Version.

A Plan Version shall preserve:

- exact request version,

- policy context,

- registry snapshots,

- assumptions,

- estimated cost,

- step graph,

- and approval state.

Executions shall reference the Plan Version under which they were created.

10.18 Plan Revision

A Plan Revision may correct non-semantic metadata such as:

- display description,

- formatting,

- or documentation.

A change affecting:

- steps,

- resources,

- budget,

- authority,

- quality,

- data placement,

- or Completion Contract

requires a new Plan Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.19 Plan Alternative

A Plan Alternative is one possible implementation path for the same request.

Alternatives may differ by:

- providers,

- cost,

- quality,

- privacy,

- latency,

- automation maturity,

- or operational risk.

Alternatives should remain comparable through structured trade-offs.

10.20 Preferred Plan

The Preferred Plan is the currently recommended valid plan.

It is not necessarily approved.

Preference may be based on:

- Routing Profile,

- quality evidence,

- cost,

- deadline,

- privacy,

- and reliability.

10.21 Approved Plan

An Approved Plan has received any required human or policy approval for its exact version and boundaries.

Approval does not guarantee resource availability at execution time.

Current eligibility must still be revalidated.

10.22 Active Plan

An Active Plan is the Plan Version currently governing one or more Executions.

A Capability Request should normally have one active Plan Version at a time unless the architecture explicitly permits parallel alternatives.

10.23 Superseded Plan

A Superseded Plan has been replaced for future execution.

Executions already created under it remain historically valid.

Supersession does not erase prior evidence.

10.24 Abandoned Plan

An Abandoned Plan was considered but intentionally not selected.

The reason may include:

- excessive cost,

- insufficient quality,

- unavailable Provider,

- policy conflict,

- deadline,

- or user preference.

Abandoned alternatives may support future explanation and learning.

10.25 Rejected Plan

A Rejected Plan was explicitly denied by an approver or policy.

Rejection evidence shall remain immutable.

10.26 Execution Graph

The Execution Graph is the canonical dependency graph within an Execution Plan.

It represents:

- work units,

- data dependencies,

- control dependencies,

- approval boundaries,

- evaluation gates,

- fallback branches,

- compensation paths,

- and completion logic.

The Execution Graph shall be machine-readable and human-explainable.

10.27 Graph Node

A Graph Node represents one bounded planning element.

Node types may include:

- Capability Step,

- Data Transformation,

- Resource Selection,

- Approval,

- Human Action,

- Evaluation,

- Decision,

- Wait,

- Side Effect,

- Compensation,

- Aggregation,

- Publication,

- Notification,

- or Completion Gate.

Each Node shall have stable identity within the Plan Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.28 Graph Edge

A Graph Edge represents a relationship between Nodes.

Edge types may include:

- depends on,

- provides input to,

- triggers,

- conditional on,

- fallback from,

- compensates,

- waits for,

- aggregates,

- approves,

- rejects,

- or completes.

Edge meaning shall be explicit.

10.29 Directed Graph

The Execution Graph shall normally be directed.

Direction represents control or data progression.

The graph need not be strictly linear.

It may contain:

- branches,

- joins,

- parallel groups,

- bounded loops,

- and conditional paths.

10.30 Acyclic Default

The default planning structure should be acyclic.

Cycles may exist only when they represent explicitly bounded behaviour such as:

- retry,

- iterative refinement,

- review correction,

- or repeated polling.

Unbounded cycles are prohibited.

10.31 Bounded Loop

A Bounded Loop shall define:

- entry condition,

- maximum iterations,

- budget limit,

- deadline,

- exit condition,

- and failure behaviour.

A loop shall not expand its own limit.

10.32 Execution Step

An Execution Step is a Node representing one bounded unit of governed work.

It shall include:

- stepId,

- planId,

- step type,

- Capability Requirement,

- Input references,

- Output Contract,

- Quality Contract,

- Authority requirement,

- Data Classification,

- rights requirement,

- Resource Requirement,

- budget allocation,

- retry policy,

- fallback policy,

- timeout,

- dependencies,

- and Completion Criteria.

10.33 Step Identity

Step identity shall remain stable within one Plan Version.

A revised Plan may retain logical continuity through:

- predecessorStepId,

- supersedesStepId,

- or equivalent relationship.

Executions shall reference the exact Step definition used.

10.34 Step Type

Canonical Step Types may include:

- intelligence execution,

- tool execution,

- deterministic transformation,

- human review,

- approval,

- wait,

- evaluation,

- side effect,

- aggregation,

- reconciliation,

- and compensation.

10.35 Intelligence Execution Step

An Intelligence Execution Step invokes a Model or External Agent Resource through a canonical Capability.

Examples include:

- reasoning,

- script generation,

- image generation,

- speech synthesis,

- video generation,

- embedding,

- reranking,

- or multimodal evaluation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.36 Tool Execution Step

A Tool Execution Step invokes a governed Tool.

Examples include:

- file conversion,

- repository read,

- frame extraction,

- audio mixing,

- storage ingestion,

- or publication submission.

Tool permissions shall remain explicit.

10.37 Deterministic Transformation Step

A Deterministic Transformation Step performs a predictable operation such as:

- schema conversion,

- resizing,

- document parsing,

- checksum generation,

- format conversion,

- or metadata extraction.

Deterministic does not mean risk-free.

The operation may still modify data or create side effects.

10.38 Human Action Step

A Human Action Step requires a person to perform a defined task.

It shall include:

- responsible role,

- instructions,

- Inputs,

- expected Output or decision,

- deadline,

- evidence requirement,

- and escalation.

Human-assisted work shall remain visible in the graph.

10.39 Approval Step

An Approval Step pauses progression until a valid Approval Decision exists.

It shall define:

- approver class,

- approval subject,

- summary,

- scope,

- budget,

- conditions,

- validity,

- and rejection path.

10.40 Evaluation Step

An Evaluation Step assesses an Output or intermediate result.

It shall define:

- target,

- criteria,

- evaluator,

- method,

- thresholds,

- failure path,

- and acceptance authority.

10.41 Wait Step

A Wait Step pauses execution until:

- a time,

- callback,

- external state,

- dependency,

- human response,

- or condition

is satisfied.

Wait Steps shall be durable.

They must not rely on one process remaining active.

10.42 Decision Step

A Decision Step chooses among defined branches.

It shall include:

- decision inputs,

- decision logic,

- authority,

- possible outcomes,

- and evidence.

A Decision Step may be:

- deterministic,

- policy-driven,

- model-assisted,

- or human.

10.43 Aggregation Step

An Aggregation Step combines several Outputs.

Examples include:

- join scene videos,

- combine research findings,

- merge evaluation results,

- assemble a document,

- or summarise batch status.

Aggregation shall preserve provenance from all source Outputs.

10.44 Side-Effect Step

A Side-Effect Step changes external or durable state.

Examples include:

- publish,

- send,

- commit,

- delete,

- modify configuration,

- create Provider Asset,

- or charge a transaction.

Side effects require explicit authority, idempotency and verification.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.45 Compensation Step

A Compensation Step reverses or mitigates an earlier side effect.

It shall define:

- triggering condition,

- target action,

- authority,

- expected restoration,

- residual risk,

- and evidence.

Compensation may fail.

It must not be represented as guaranteed rollback.

10.46 Reconciliation Step

A Reconciliation Step compares Omnira state with an external system.

It may resolve:

- unknown Provider job,

- uncertain publication,

- cost discrepancy,

- missing Asset,

- or callback failure.

10.47 Completion Gate

A Completion Gate determines whether the request or parent step satisfies its Completion Contract.

It shall inspect:

- mandatory Outputs,

- Evaluation Results,

- Approval Decisions,

- cost,

- unresolved unknown outcomes,

- and required side-effect verification.

10.48 Node Input

Every executable Node shall define its Inputs.

Inputs may reference:

- request Inputs,

- Outputs from predecessor Nodes,

- Assets,

- Data Items,

- governed memory,

- policy results,

- human decisions,

- or external events.

Input lineage shall remain traceable.

10.49 Node Output

Every executable Node shall define its expected Output.

Outputs may be:

- data,

- Asset candidate,

- decision,

- approval,

- receipt,

- status,

- cost,

- or side-effect evidence.

Output existence does not automatically mean acceptance.

10.50 Data Edge

A Data Edge identifies Output from one Node as Input to another.

It shall define:

- source Output,

- destination Input,

- transformation,

- classification,

- rights inheritance,

- and version.

10.51 Control Edge

A Control Edge determines execution order without necessarily transferring data.

Examples include:

- execute after approval,

- execute after deadline,

- or execute only when evaluation passes.

10.52 Conditional Edge

A Conditional Edge is traversed only when a defined condition is satisfied.

The condition shall be:

- explicit,

- machine-evaluable where possible,

- versioned,

- and evidenced.

10.53 Fallback Edge

A Fallback Edge leads to an alternative step or resource after defined failure or ineligibility.

It shall preserve mandatory request constraints.

10.54 Compensation Edge

A Compensation Edge identifies which corrective action follows a failed or cancelled side effect.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.55 Join Edge

A Join waits for defined predecessor conditions.

Join policies may include:

- all mandatory predecessors,

- any one predecessor,

- minimum count,

- quorum,

- or explicitly selected subset.

10.56 Split Edge

A Split creates parallel or conditional branches.

Split conditions shall define:

- branch count,

- budget allocation,

- and later join behaviour.

10.57 Mandatory Step

A Mandatory Step must complete according to its Completion Criteria for the parent request to complete.

The Planner shall not silently remove it.

10.58 Optional Step

An Optional Step may improve output or create derivatives.

Its omission shall be allowed by the parent Completion Contract.

Optional Steps shall still have cost and authority boundaries.

10.59 Conditional Step

A Conditional Step becomes active only when a defined condition is true.

Examples include:

- premium retry after failed quality evaluation,

- translation when target language differs,

- human review for child-facing output,

- or external search when internal sources are insufficient.

10.60 Deferred Step

A Deferred Step is defined but not yet scheduled because:

- a decision is pending,

- a future Input is missing,

- budget is not yet approved,

- or a prior result determines its necessity.

10.61 Disabled Step

A Disabled Step remains in the Plan for history or possible future activation but cannot execute under the current Plan Version.

10.62 Composite Step

A Composite Step contains a subgraph.

It may represent:

- one scene production,

- one research package,

- one publication package,

- or one software-delivery phase.

Composite Steps support hierarchical planning.

10.63 Atomic Step

An Atomic Step is the smallest unit the current Planner schedules independently.

Atomic does not mean one provider call.

An Adapter may internally perform bounded technical operations.

Material governance boundaries must remain visible at Plan level.

10.64 Hierarchical Execution Graph

Complex Plans may use a hierarchy:

- Plan,

- Phase,

- Composite Step,

- Atomic Step,

- Execution,

- Attempt.

Hierarchy supports explanation without losing detail.

10.65 Phase

A Phase groups Steps with a shared purpose.

Example phases may include:

- preparation,

- research,

- generation,

- evaluation,

- assembly,

- approval,

- publication,

- and verification.

Phase names are organisational.

Step contracts remain authoritative.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.66 Planning Template

A Planning Template is a reusable structure for common requests.

It may define:

- standard Steps,

- dependencies,

- approvals,

- Quality Gates,

- retry limits,

- and Completion Contract.

Templates shall be versioned and scoped.

10.67 Project Planning Template

Projects may define specialised templates.

Examples include:

- Familje-Stunden monthly episode,

- The Prompt news segment,

- GainPilot short-form reel,

- Omnira code audit.

Templates shall reference canonical Capabilities.

10.68 Platform Planning Template

Platform templates may define reusable patterns such as:

- research and verification,

- generate and evaluate,

- preview then premium,

- draft and human review,

- or side-effect with verification.

10.69 Template Instantiation

Instantiating a Template creates a request-specific Plan.

The Plan shall resolve:

- Inputs,

- Project,

- budget,

- current policies,

- resource requirements,

- deadlines,

- and approvals.

The Template itself is not an active Plan.

10.70 Template Version

Plans shall reference the exact Template Version used.

A Template update shall not rewrite active Plans.

10.71 Template Override

A request may override approved Template fields.

Overrides shall remain within:

- authority,

- policy,

- and schema.

Material overrides may require review.

10.72 Planning Strategy

A Plan shall identify the strategy used.

Strategies may include:

- template-based,

- deterministic decomposition,

- AI-assisted decomposition,

- hybrid,

- manually authored,

- imported,

- or recovery-generated.

10.73 Deterministic Planning

Deterministic Planning uses predefined rules and templates.

It is suitable when:

- request type is stable,

- steps are known,

- and variation is limited.

It offers strong predictability.

10.74 AI-Assisted Planning

AI-Assisted Planning may interpret complex intent and propose Steps.

Its output shall be validated against:

- Capability Registry,

- authority,

- policy,

- budget,

- and graph rules.

The AI Planner cannot create new authority.

10.75 Hybrid Planning

Hybrid Planning combines:

- deterministic boundaries,

- reusable templates,

- and AI-generated detail.

This is likely appropriate for many Omnira workflows.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.76 Manual Planning

An authorised human may create or edit a Plan.

Manual Plans remain subject to the same validation and evidence requirements.

10.77 Imported Plan

A Plan may be imported from:

- external workflow system,

- provider agent,

- code package,

- or partner integration.

Imported Plans shall be treated as untrusted until validated.

10.78 Plan Validation

Before approval or activation, the Plan shall be validated.

Validation should include:

- graph structure,

- Capability existence,

- scope,

- Inputs,

- authority,

- policy,

- budget,

- data placement,

- rights,

- quality,

- side effects,

- retry,

- fallback,

- and Completion Contract.

10.79 Structural Graph Validation

Structural validation shall detect:

- missing Node,

- invalid Edge,

- unreachable mandatory Step,

- orphaned Step,

- unbounded cycle,

- impossible join,

- duplicate identifier,

- and invalid dependency.

10.80 Semantic Plan Validation

Semantic validation shall detect conflicts such as:

- publication before acceptance,

- evaluation before Output exists,

- narration before final script when sequence requires final text,

- Local Only Input routed to external step,

- or deletion without target.

10.81 Scope Validation

Every Step shall remain within the request’s permitted Tenant, Project and Environment scope.

Cross-Project Steps require explicit authority.

10.82 Authority Validation

Each Step shall identify the authority required.

The Plan shall not rely on one broad approval when action-specific authority is required.

10.83 Policy Validation

Current policies shall be evaluated against:

- Step Capability,

- selected or candidate resource,

- Inputs,

- Outputs,

- data class,

- rights,

- and side effects.

10.84 Budget Validation

The sum of planned maximum spending shall fit within the Budget Envelope.

The Plan shall account for:

- mandatory Steps,

- approved optional Steps,

- retries,

- fallbacks,

- evaluation,

- post-processing,

- and Provider minimum charges.

10.85 Budget Allocation

The Planner may allocate budget by:

- Step,

- Phase,

- modality,

- Provider class,

- retry pool,

- or reserve.

Allocation shall not exceed the parent envelope.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.86 Hard Step Budget

A Hard Step Budget is the maximum amount one Step may consume.

The Executor shall stop before knowingly exceeding it.

10.87 Shared Retry Budget

Several Steps may share one retry reserve.

The Plan shall define:

- total reserve,

- allocation rules,

- priority,

- and exhaustion behaviour.

10.88 Contingency Reserve

A Plan may reserve budget for:

- fallback,

- correction,

- or uncertain Provider pricing.

Unused reserve shall be released.

10.89 Cost Estimate

The Plan shall include an estimated cost or cost range.

The estimate should identify:

- assumptions,

- pricing versions,

- expected usage,

- retry allowance,

- and uncertainty.

10.90 Minimum Cost Plan

A Minimum Cost Plan represents the cheapest currently valid execution path.

It must still satisfy mandatory requirements.

10.91 Expected Cost Plan

An Expected Cost Plan represents likely cost under ordinary success and expected retries.

10.92 Maximum Authorised Cost

Maximum Authorised Cost is the hard approved boundary.

It shall remain distinct from expected cost.

10.93 Cost Uncertainty

Cost uncertainty may be:

- low,

- moderate,

- high,

- or unknown.

High uncertainty may require conservative reservation or stronger approval.

10.94 Latency Estimate

The Plan should estimate:

- queue time,

- execution time,

- review time,

- retry time,

- and final delivery.

Latency estimates must remain distinct from guarantees.

10.95 Critical Path

The Critical Path is the longest dependency path determining earliest completion.

The Planner may optimise the Critical Path through:

- parallelism,

- resource choice,

- preparation,

- or early validation.

10.96 Deadline Feasibility

The Plan shall evaluate whether the request deadline is feasible.

It should include:

- Provider latency,

- human review,

- fallback,

- and final verification.

An impossible deadline shall be reported before unnecessary spending.

10.97 Earliest Start

Some Steps may have an earliest start based on:

- schedule,

- Input availability,

- human availability,

- Provider window,

- or policy.

10.98 Latest Start

A Step may have a latest start to preserve the request deadline.

Missing the latest start may trigger:

- escalation,

- degraded alternative,

- or failure.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.99 Step Timeout

Each external or long-running Step should define a timeout.

Timeout does not always mean failure.

It may produce unknown outcome.

10.100 Plan Expiry

A Plan may expire because:

- approval expires,

- registry state changes materially,

- pricing becomes stale,

- deadline passes,

- Inputs change,

- or Provider terms change.

Expired Plans shall not start new execution without revalidation.

10.101 Resource Requirement

A Resource Requirement defines the properties needed for a Step.

It may include:

- Capability Version,

- mandatory Features,

- modality,

- quality floor,

- data placement,

- Provider restrictions,

- Model restrictions,

- region,

- context capacity,

- latency,

- cost,

- rights,

- and integration maturity.

10.102 Resource Candidate

A Resource Candidate combines the operational objects needed to execute a Step.

It may include:

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Model Version,

- Model Deployment,

- Adapter,

- Connection,

- Runtime Node,

- Tool,

- or External Agent Resource.

10.103 Candidate Generation

The Planner or Router may generate candidates from the current registries.

Candidate generation shall exclude resources that are structurally incompatible.

Full eligibility remains a separate decision.

10.104 Candidate Eligibility

Eligibility shall consider:

- Capability compatibility,

- policy,

- data class,

- rights,

- authority,

- Account,

- Connection,

- health,

- capacity,

- quota,

- budget,

- and deadline.

10.105 Candidate Ranking

Only eligible candidates may be ranked.

Ranking may use:

- quality,

- cost,

- latency,

- reliability,

- privacy,

- and Routing Profile.

10.106 Selected Resource

A Plan may contain:

- fully selected Resource Candidate,

- ranked candidate set,

- deferred selection,

- or pinned resource.

The choice depends on how far in advance the Plan is created.

10.107 Early Binding

Early Binding selects a resource during planning.

It may be useful for:

- fixed Provider contract,

- exact reproducibility,

- reserved capacity,

- unique Capability,

- or approval clarity.

10.108 Late Binding

Late Binding selects the resource near execution time.

It allows the Fabric to use current:

- health,

- pricing,

- quota,

- capacity,

- and quality evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.109 Hybrid Binding

A Plan may bind:

- Provider class early,

- Account during approval,

- and exact Model Deployment at execution.

Binding level shall be explicit.

10.110 Resource Pinning

A Step may pin:

- Provider,

- Account,

- Model,

- Deployment,

- Adapter,

- Tool,

- or Node.

Pinning shall identify:

- reason,

- fallback,

- validity,

- and whether the pin is mandatory.

10.111 Resource Reservation

The Plan may reserve:

- local compute,

- Provider capacity,

- budget,

- or human review slot.

Reservation state shall remain separate from execution.

10.112 Resource Unavailability

If a selected resource becomes unavailable before execution, the Plan shall follow its:

- fallback policy,

- replanning policy,

- approval policy,

- or failure path.

10.113 Planning With Unknown Resource

A Plan may define a Resource Requirement without identifying a current eligible resource.

Such a Plan may remain:

- incomplete,

- blocked,

- or awaiting Capability gap resolution.

It shall not be activated as executable.

10.114 Capability Gap During Planning

A Capability Gap exists when no valid resource path can satisfy a mandatory Step.

The Planner shall produce:

- missing Capability or support,

- conflicting constraint,

- possible alternatives,

- and whether human-assisted execution is available.

10.115 Human-Assisted Alternative

A human-assisted path may bridge a Capability Gap.

It shall define:

- operator,

- Provider or Tool,

- manual instructions,

- cost,

- evidence,

- and quality review.

10.116 Plan Decomposition

Decomposition divides a broad request into bounded Steps.

The Planner should decompose when:

- different Capabilities are required,

- different authority applies,

- different data placement applies,

- separate quality evaluation is needed,

- different resources are optimal,

- or partial completion has value.

10.117 Decomposition Boundary

A boundary should be created when one part of work has a distinct:

- identity,

- lifecycle,

- authority,

- budget,

- Input,

- Output,

- side effect,

- or failure behaviour.

10.118 Over-Decomposition

A Plan is over-decomposed when trivial technical details become separate governed Steps without meaningful boundary.

Over-decomposition increases:

- latency,

- state complexity,

- cost,

- and failure surface.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.119 Under-Decomposition

A Plan is under-decomposed when materially different work is hidden inside one opaque Step.

Under-decomposition weakens:

- authority,

- provenance,

- cost,

- evaluation,

- and recovery.

10.120 Provider Call Boundary

One Step may result in several Provider calls when the Adapter performs bounded internal operations.

Material calls involving separate:

- cost,

- authority,

- output,

- or retry

should normally remain visible as separate Executions or Attempts.

10.121 Multi-Provider Plan

A Plan may use several Providers.

Each Step shall preserve:

- Provider eligibility,

- Account,

- cost,

- terms,

- data transfer,

- and provenance.

10.122 Local and External Composition

A Plan may combine:

- local preprocessing,

- external premium generation,

- local evaluation,

- and human review.

Data Classification shall determine what may cross each boundary.

10.123 Data Localisation Step

A Plan may include a Step to:

- redact,

- summarise,

- anonymise,

- extract,

- or transform data locally

before external use.

Transformation must not automatically lower classification without policy.

10.124 Data Transfer Boundary

Every transfer between custody or processing locations should be explicit when material.

The Plan should identify:

- source location,

- destination,

- classification,

- rights,

- encryption,

- and retention.

10.125 Context Assembly Step

A Context Assembly Step builds the bounded context used by a Model or Agent.

It may include:

- retrieved memory,

- selected Assets,

- request instructions,

- evidence,

- and policy summaries.

The resulting Context Package shall be scoped and classified.

10.126 Retrieval Step

A Retrieval Step obtains relevant information from:

- Project data,

- Memory,

- Intelligence Graph,

- external search,

- or Provider storage.

Retrieval authority and freshness remain explicit.

10.127 Prompt Construction Step

Prompt construction may be represented when it materially affects:

- provenance,

- quality,

- privacy,

- or reproducibility.

Prompt Templates and runtime substitutions shall be versioned.

10.128 Prompt Adaptation

Adapters may transform canonical instructions into Provider-specific format.

Material omissions or changes shall be evidenced.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.129 Output Ingestion Step

External Provider output may require ingestion into Omnira-controlled storage.

The Step shall verify:

- file integrity,

- type,

- checksum,

- classification,

- provenance,

- and storage destination.

10.130 Output Normalisation Step

Output may require:

- schema conversion,

- encoding conversion,

- media conversion,

- or metadata normalisation.

Normalisation must preserve original evidence where relevant.

10.131 Quality Gate

A Quality Gate blocks progression until defined criteria pass.

It shall identify:

- target Output,

- criteria,

- evaluator,

- threshold,

- and failure path.

10.132 Deterministic Quality Gate

A deterministic gate may test:

- schema,

- file format,

- dimensions,

- duration,

- compilation,

- type checking,

- or unit tests.

10.133 Model-Based Quality Gate

A Model-based gate may assess:

- relevance,

- style,

- factual support,

- visual consistency,

- or safety.

Evaluator identity and Version shall be preserved.

10.134 Human Quality Gate

A Human Quality Gate requires an authorised reviewer.

The Plan shall define:

- reviewer role,

- checklist,

- decision options,

- and correction path.

10.135 Composite Quality Gate

A Composite Gate combines several evaluations.

It may require:

- all mandatory checks,

- minimum score,

- and human approval.

10.136 Gate Failure

When a Quality Gate fails, the Plan may:

- retry,

- refine,

- use fallback,

- route to human correction,

- accept partial result if permitted,

- or fail.

10.137 Revision Loop

A Revision Loop may:

1. evaluate Output,

2. identify defects,

3. refine instructions,

4. execute again,

5. re-evaluate.

The loop shall have bounded:

- iterations,

- budget,

- time,

- and authority.

10.138 Same-Resource Retry

The Plan may retry the same resource for transient failure or stochastic variation.

Retry must remain idempotency- and cost-aware.

10.139 Resource Fallback

The Plan may switch to another eligible resource.

The fallback may alter:

- cost,

- quality,

- latency,

- or reproducibility.

Material changes require disclosure or approval according to policy.

10.140 Capability Alternative Fallback

The Plan may switch to an alternative Capability path.

Example:

- premium image-to-video fails,

- motion-comic composition becomes the approved alternative.

The alternative must still satisfy the Completion Contract or produce approved degradation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.141 Human Escalation

Repeated failure may escalate to a human.

Escalation should present:

- failed Steps,

- Outputs,

- cost,

- remaining budget,

- alternatives,

- and required decision.

10.142 Retry Policy

Each retryable Step shall have a Retry Policy defining:

- retryable conditions,

- non-retryable conditions,

- maximum attempts,

- backoff,

- idempotency,

- budget,

- deadline,

- and unknown-outcome handling.

10.143 Failure Category

Retry decisions shall distinguish:

- validation failure,

- policy rejection,

- authentication failure,

- rate limit,

- Provider outage,

- timeout,

- quality failure,

- rights restriction,

- safety refusal,

- and internal defect.

10.144 Transient Failure

Transient failures may include:

- temporary outage,

- rate limit,

- short network interruption,

- or temporary capacity issue.

They may permit bounded retry.

10.145 Permanent Failure

Permanent failures may include:

- unsupported Capability,

- policy prohibition,

- expired rights,

- missing consent,

- or retired Model.

They shall not be retried without changed conditions.

10.146 Unknown Outcome

Unknown outcome means the system cannot confirm whether an operation completed.

The Plan shall not automatically retry a non-idempotent or paid Step.

It may require reconciliation first.

10.147 Unknown-Outcome Branch

A Plan should define a branch for uncertain external operations.

The branch may include:

- Provider status lookup,

- Asset listing,

- billing inspection,

- delayed callback wait,

- human verification,

- or Incident.

10.148 Retry Backoff

Retry timing may use:

- fixed delay,

- exponential backoff,

- jitter,

- Provider guidance,

- or scheduled retry.

Backoff shall respect deadlines.

10.149 Retry Budget

Retry cost shall be reserved or bounded.

The system shall stop when the retry budget is exhausted.

10.150 Attempt Limit

Attempt limit shall count all relevant Attempts across:

- same resource,

- fallback resource,

- and revision loops

according to the Plan’s defined semantics.

10.151 Infinite Retry Prohibition

No Plan may retry indefinitely.

Every retry path requires a terminal or escalation state.

10.152 Fallback Policy

A Fallback Policy defines:

- trigger,

- candidate alternatives,

- ordering,

- quality floor,

- budget,

- data policy,

- approval,

- and disclosure.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.153 Fallback Eligibility Revalidation

Fallback resources shall be evaluated under current conditions.

Previous eligibility does not guarantee current eligibility.

10.154 Fallback Ordering

Fallback may be ordered by:

- same Model different Deployment,

- same Provider different Model,

- different Provider same Capability,

- local resource,

- human-assisted path,

- or approved degraded Capability.

10.155 No Policy Escape

Fallback shall not weaken:

- data classification,

- rights,

- consent,

- authority,

- or hard budget.

10.156 Degradation Plan

A Degradation Plan defines a reduced outcome that may be offered when full completion is impossible.

Examples include:

- lower resolution,

- fewer variants,

- delayed completion,

- partial episode,

- manual review,

- or draft-only delivery.

Material degradation requires approval where policy demands it.

10.157 Graceful Degradation

Graceful degradation shall preserve:

- truth,

- minimum value,

- and mandatory safety.

The system shall not claim full completion.

10.158 Partial Completion

A Plan may permit partial completion.

The Completion Contract shall define:

- which Steps are mandatory,

- minimum output count,

- acceptable omissions,

- and approval requirements.

10.159 Partial Output Preservation

Successful Outputs should remain preserved when later Steps fail, unless retention policy prohibits it.

They shall be marked with truthful lifecycle state.

10.160 Partial Cost

Cost incurred by partial work shall remain recorded.

Failure does not erase spending.

10.161 Parent Completion Logic

A Parent Plan or Composite Step may complete when:

- all mandatory children pass,

- defined optional threshold is met,

- required approval exists,

- and no blocking unknown outcomes remain.

10.162 Child Failure Propagation

A Child Step failure may:

- fail the parent,

- trigger fallback,

- create partial completion,

- or remain isolated.

Propagation rules shall be explicit.

10.163 Parallel Execution

Independent Steps may run in parallel.

Parallelism can reduce latency.

It may increase:

- concurrent cost,

- quota pressure,

- complexity,

- and partial-state handling.

10.164 Parallel Group

A Parallel Group defines Steps allowed to execute concurrently.

It shall include:

- concurrency limit,

- shared budget,

- join condition,

- and cancellation behaviour.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.165 Concurrency Limit

Concurrency may be limited by:

- Project,

- Provider Account,

- Model Deployment,

- Runtime Node,

- Capability,

- budget,

- or Workflow.

10.166 Parallel Cost Reservation

The Plan shall reserve enough budget for concurrently launched paid work.

It must not assume later Steps can be cancelled without cost.

10.167 Speculative Execution

Speculative Execution runs several alternatives before one is known to be necessary.

It may improve latency or quality.

It also increases cost.

Speculation requires explicit policy and budget.

10.168 Candidate Race

A Candidate Race submits the same bounded task to several eligible resources and selects the best accepted result.

It shall define:

- maximum candidates,

- budget,

- evaluation,

- cancellation,

- and provenance.

Candidate races should not be default behaviour.

10.169 Hedged Request

A Hedged Request submits a second attempt after the first exceeds a latency threshold.

Hedging requires:

- idempotency analysis,

- cost allowance,

- and duplicate-result handling.

10.170 Sequential Execution

Sequential Steps execute in dependency order.

Sequence should be used when:

- Output is required,

- authority boundary exists,

- or cost should be deferred until prior validation passes.

10.171 Preview-First Strategy

Preview-first planning generates a cheaper or lower-resolution result before full production.

It may reduce waste for:

- image,

- video,

- voice,

- design,

- and long-form media.

10.172 Premium-Escalation Strategy

A Plan may start with an economical resource and escalate to premium only when:

- quality fails,

- importance warrants it,

- and budget permits.

The escalation threshold shall be explicit.

10.173 Premium-First Strategy

Critical outputs may use a premium resource immediately when:

- quality risk is high,

- retries are expensive,

- deadline is tight,

- or failure consequence is significant.

10.174 Local-First Strategy

A Local-First Plan prefers local or private resources.

External fallback shall remain prohibited unless the request permits it.

10.175 Free-Capacity-First Strategy

A Plan may prefer:

- included credits,

- free tiers,

- or local resources

before paid execution.

The strategy shall still respect quality, rights and reliability.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.176 Mixed-Tier Strategy

A production may use:

- premium resources for master Assets,

- economical resources for derivatives,

- local resources for conversion,

- and human review for acceptance.

10.177 Planning for Human Review

Human review shall be scheduled as a real dependency.

The Plan should estimate:

- reviewer availability,

- review duration,

- and correction cycle.

10.178 Reviewer Assignment

The Plan may identify:

- named reviewer,

- reviewer role,

- reviewer pool,

- or Project owner.

Assignment shall respect scope and authority.

10.179 Review Timeout

A Human Review Step may have:

- reminder,

- escalation,

- expiry,

- and cancellation behaviour.

No decision shall be fabricated when the reviewer does not respond.

10.180 Conditional Approval

The Plan may receive approval with conditions.

Conditions shall become enforceable Plan constraints.

10.181 Plan Approval Summary

Before approval, the Plan should present:

- objective,

- phases,

- providers or resource classes,

- data transfers,

- expected cost,

- maximum cost,

- retries,

- expected duration,

- quality gates,

- human steps,

- side effects,

- and prohibited actions.

10.182 Plan Approval Granularity

Approval may cover:

- complete Plan,

- one Phase,

- one expensive branch,

- one Provider,

- one side effect,

- or one retry envelope.

Granularity shall be explicit.

10.183 Plan Approval Version Binding

Approval shall bind to the exact Plan Version.

Material replanning may invalidate it.

10.184 Approval Invalidation

Approval may become invalid after:

- budget increase,

- Provider change,

- data-placement change,

- publication addition,

- new side effect,

- rights change,

- or expanded retry.

10.185 Bounded Plan Autonomy

An approved Plan may allow autonomous execution within:

- defined Steps,

- budget,

- Providers,

- retry limits,

- deadline,

- and quality gates.

Autonomy ends at the Plan boundary.

10.186 Plan Activation

A Plan may activate only when:

- validation passes,

- required approval exists,

- required Inputs exist,

- budget can be reserved,

- and no blocking policy conflict remains.

10.187 Activation Record

Activation shall record:

- Plan Version,

- actor,

- time,

- approvals,

- budget reservation,

- registry snapshots,

- and initial state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.188 Plan Execution State

Plan states may include:

- draft,

- constructing,

- validating,

- awaiting clarification,

- awaiting approval,

- approved,

- activating,

- active,

- paused,

- replanning,

- partially completed,

- completed,

- failed,

- cancelled,

- expired,

- superseded,

- and archived.

10.189 Draft Plan

Draft means the Plan is still being edited and cannot execute.

10.190 Constructing Plan

Constructing means decomposition, candidate generation or cost estimation is underway.

10.191 Validating Plan
