Validating means structural, semantic and governance checks are running.

10.192 Awaiting Clarification Plan

The Plan requires additional authoritative information.

10.193 Awaiting Approval Plan

The Plan is valid but lacks required approval.

10.194 Approved Plan State

Approved means the current Plan Version may proceed when activation conditions are satisfied.

10.195 Activating Plan

Activating means:

- budget,

- resources,

- queues,

- and execution records

are being prepared.

10.196 Active Plan State

Active means at least one Step may execute or wait according to the graph.

10.197 Paused Plan

A Plan may pause because of:

- approval,

- budget,

- Incident,

- human review,

- Provider outage,

- or user action.

10.198 Replanning State

Replanning means current execution conditions require a new Plan Version or adjusted future Steps.

10.199 Partially Completed Plan

Some Outputs satisfy parts of the Completion Contract.

Remaining mandatory work is incomplete or blocked.

10.200 Completed Plan

Completed means the Plan-level Completion Contract is satisfied.

Completion does not imply every optional Step executed.

10.201 Failed Plan

Failed means the Plan cannot fulfil its mandatory Completion Contract under current approved boundaries.

10.202 Cancelled Plan

Cancelled means an authorised Principal stopped future progression.

Running external jobs may remain subject to reconciliation.

10.203 Expired Plan

Expired means the Plan is no longer valid for new execution.

10.204 Superseded Plan State

A new Plan Version governs future work.

Existing Executions remain linked to the old Version.

10.205 Plan Pause

Pause shall prevent new Steps from starting.

It may allow:

- in-flight jobs to complete,

- reconciliation,

- safe cancellation,

- or compensation

according to policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.206 Hard Pause

A Hard Pause stops all possible activity immediately.

It may be required for:

- security Incident,

- rights violation,

- credential compromise,

- or severe budget anomaly.

10.207 Soft Pause

A Soft Pause stops new work while allowing current safe operations to settle.

10.208 Plan Resume

Resume requires:

- valid Plan Version,

- current authority,

- current policy,

- valid credentials,

- budget,

- and resolved pause reason.

10.209 Plan Cancellation

Cancellation shall define:

- which Steps stop,

- which external jobs are cancelled,

- which Outputs are retained,

- whether compensation runs,

- and how cost is reconciled.

10.210 User Cancellation

A user with authority may cancel the Plan.

The system shall report what cannot be undone.

10.211 Automatic Cancellation

Policy may automatically cancel after:

- approval expiry,

- deadline,

- severe Incident,

- or repeated failure.

Automatic cancellation rules shall be explicit.

10.212 Replanning

Replanning creates a new Plan Version when the active plan can no longer continue as designed.

Triggers may include:

- Provider unavailability,

- cost change,

- quality failure,

- changed Input,

- deadline risk,

- policy change,

- or user amendment.

10.213 Replanning Boundary

Replanning shall preserve completed work where safe.

It shall not rewrite prior Executions.

10.214 Material Replanning

Material replanning changes:

- Provider class,

- budget,

- data placement,

- quality,

- side effects,

- mandatory Step,

- or Completion Contract.

It may require renewed approval.

10.215 Non-Material Replanning

Non-material replanning may adjust:

- queue order,

- equivalent Deployment,

- or timing

within the approved envelope.

10.216 Replanning Decision

A Replanning Decision shall record:

- trigger,

- old Plan Version,

- new Plan Version,

- preserved Steps,

- cancelled Steps,

- cost impact,

- approval impact,

- and actor.

10.217 Mid-Execution Resource Change

A future Step may use a different resource without changing completed history.

The new selection shall remain evidenced.

10.218 Input Change During Execution

Material Input changes may invalidate:

- downstream Steps,

- Evaluations,

- Outputs,

- and approval.

The Planner shall determine the affected subgraph.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.219 Selective Invalidation

Only Steps dependent on changed information should be invalidated where safe.

Selective invalidation reduces unnecessary cost.

10.220 Output Reuse

Accepted Outputs from a superseded Plan may be reused when:

- Inputs remain valid,

- classification permits,

- quality remains sufficient,

- and provenance is preserved.

10.221 Cached Result Reuse

A cached Output may satisfy a Step only when:

- request semantics match,

- Project and Tenant scope permit,

- freshness is valid,

- rights permit,

- and provenance is complete.

10.222 Plan Determinism

The same Planning Input may produce different valid Plans when:

- current resources differ,

- prices change,

- health changes,

- or AI-assisted planning is non-deterministic.

The Planner shall preserve the actual Plan Version and decision evidence.

10.223 Planning Reproducibility

Reproduction may require:

- request version,

- policy versions,

- registry snapshots,

- planning strategy,

- template version,

- assumptions,

- and Planner version.

10.224 Planner Version

Every Plan shall identify the Planner implementation or service version.

Material Planner changes may affect decomposition and cost.

10.225 Planning Policy Version

The Plan shall reference relevant planning-policy versions.

Examples include:

- decomposition rules,

- approval rules,

- retry defaults,

- and fallback defaults.

10.226 Plan Provenance

Plan Provenance should include:

- request,

- Planner,

- human editor,

- template,

- registry snapshots,

- policy,

- assumptions,

- cost sources,

- and revision history.

10.227 Plan Evidence

Planning evidence should answer:

- Why were these Steps created?

- Why are these dependencies required?

- Why were these resource classes considered?

- What assumptions were made?

- What may the Plan cost?

- Which approvals are required?

- What happens if a Step fails?

10.228 Human-Readable Plan

The system should provide a concise human-readable representation.

It may show:

- phases,

- providers,

- costs,

- reviews,

- and side effects

without overwhelming the user with every internal field.

10.229 Machine-Readable Plan

The canonical Plan shall have a structured machine-readable form suitable for:

- validation,

- scheduling,

- execution,

- audit,

- and simulation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.230 Plan Visualisation

The Execution Graph may be visualised as:

- flow diagram,

- dependency graph,

- timeline,

- phase view,

- or cost tree.

Visualisation is a derived view.

The canonical graph remains authoritative.

10.231 Plan Simulation

A Plan may be simulated before execution.

Simulation may evaluate:

- policy,

- candidate resources,

- cost,

- latency,

- failure,

- and fallback.

10.232 Simulation State

Simulation shall remain clearly separated from production state.

It shall not create real Provider jobs or charges.

10.233 Cost Simulation

Cost simulation may compare:

- Economy,

- Balanced,

- Premium,

- Private,

- and Pinned alternatives.

10.234 Failure Simulation

Failure simulation may test:

- Provider outage,

- callback loss,

- quality failure,

- quota exhaustion,

- and credential expiry.

10.235 Policy Simulation

Policy simulation may show why resources are:

- eligible,

- blocked,

- or approval-required.

10.236 Dry Run

A Dry Run validates Plan activation without performing consequential execution.

It may:

- resolve candidates,

- reserve simulated budget,

- validate Inputs,

- and test graph transitions.

10.237 Test Plan

A Test Plan uses approved test data and non-production resources.

It shall not be confused with the production Plan.

10.238 Planning Metrics

Planning metrics may include:

- plan creation latency,

- validation failures,

- number of alternatives,

- estimated versus actual cost,

- replan rate,

- approval delay,

- graph size,

- and Capability gaps.

10.239 Plan Quality

Plan quality may be assessed through:

- successful completion,

- cost variance,

- unnecessary Steps,

- retry rate,

- replan rate,

- deadline performance,

- and human intervention.

10.240 Over-Planning Signal

Over-planning may be indicated by:

- excessive graph size,

- long planning latency,

- high administrative burden,

- or negligible benefit from detailed decomposition.

10.241 Under-Planning Signal

Under-planning may be indicated by:

- hidden side effects,

- repeated rework,

- unexplained costs,

- broad opaque Agent steps,

- or frequent unknown outcomes.

10.242 Planning Learning Candidate

The Fabric may create Learning Candidates such as:

- preview-first reduces failed premium video cost,

- parallel research and Asset preparation reduce production latency,

- one review checkpoint catches most Nova consistency defects,

- or local preprocessing reduces external context cost.

Learning shall remain scoped and evidence-based.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.243 Plan Outcome Comparison

Expected and actual outcomes may be compared for:

- cost,

- latency,

- quality,

- retries,

- fallback,

- and human effort.

10.244 Planning Calibration

The Planner should improve estimates based on governed evidence.

Calibration shall not modify completed Plan history.

10.245 Plan Recommendation

The Fabric may present several Plan Alternatives.

Recommendations should explain trade-offs.

Example:

Economy Plan

- lower cost,

- more local work,

- lower video consistency confidence,

- longer manual review.

Balanced Plan

- mixed Providers,

- preview-first,

- premium escalation for failed scenes.

Premium Plan

- premium video resource for all character scenes,

- higher cost,

- lower expected correction burden.

10.246 User Plan Selection

The user may select an alternative.

Selection remains subject to mandatory policy and budget.

10.247 User Plan Override

A user may override a recommendation.

The override shall preserve:

- chosen Plan,

- reason where material,

- cost,

- risk,

- and policy constraints.

10.248 Planner Conflict

The Planner may identify that no Plan can satisfy all requirements.

It shall not silently discard constraints.

It should present:

- conflicting requirements,

- minimum necessary change,

- and possible alternatives.

10.249 Planning Clarification

The Planner may request focused clarification when a decision materially affects:

- cost,

- quality,

- privacy,

- rights,

- deadline,

- or side effects.

10.250 Planning Without Excessive Questions

The Planner should use:

- Project defaults,

- approved Templates,

- and safe assumptions

for low-risk details.

It should not require the user to design the technical graph manually.

10.251 Cross-Project Planning

A Plan involving multiple Projects shall explicitly identify:

- participating Projects,

- data flows,

- shared resources,

- cost attribution,

- Outputs,

- and authority.

Shared ownership does not create automatic permission.

10.252 Platform-Global Planning

Platform-global Plans may include:

- Provider health testing,

- model benchmarking,

- registry maintenance,

- and infrastructure recovery.

They shall prohibit unnecessary Project-content access.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.253 Tenant Planning

Tenant-wide Plans may coordinate:

- shared budgets,

- Provider Accounts,

- policy changes,

- or portfolio analysis.

Project context shall remain isolated.

10.254 User-Private Planning

User-private Plans shall remain separate from Project Plans.

They may use user-owned credentials and local resources.

10.255 Long-Running Plan

A long-running Plan shall support:

- durable graph state,

- authority revalidation,

- policy revalidation,

- credential renewal,

- budget tracking,

- and cancellation.

10.256 Scheduled Plan

A scheduled Plan may activate at a future time.

It shall revalidate:

- Inputs,

- policy,

- authority,

- credentials,

- budget,

- and resource eligibility

before execution.

10.257 Recurring Plan Template

Recurring work should create separate Plan instances or versions for each occurrence.

One permanently active Plan should not hide changing Inputs and costs.

10.258 Condition-Triggered Plan

A Plan may wait for:

- new source,

- approval,

- Provider recovery,

- Asset completion,

- or threshold.

Condition evaluation shall be scoped and durable.

10.259 Event-Triggered Plan

Internal or external events may initiate planning.

Events shall be authenticated, deduplicated and correlated.

10.260 Planning and Scheduling

Planning determines dependencies and constraints.

Scheduling determines when executable Steps run.

The scheduler shall not alter Plan meaning.

10.261 Scheduler

The Scheduler assigns eligible Steps to time and capacity.

It considers:

- dependencies,

- priority,

- deadline,

- capacity,

- quotas,

- concurrency,

- and environment.

10.262 Scheduler Authority

The Scheduler may delay or order work.

It shall not add Capabilities, increase budget or weaken policy.

10.263 Ready Step

A Step is Ready when:

- all dependencies are satisfied,

- required Inputs exist,

- approvals are valid,

- budget is available,

- and current policy permits execution.

10.264 Blocked Step

A Step is Blocked when one or more readiness conditions are missing.

The block reason shall be explicit.

10.265 Queued Step

A Ready Step may be queued for:

- capacity,

- schedule,

- concurrency,

- or Provider availability.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.266 Running Step

A Running Step has one or more active Executions.

10.267 Awaiting External Step

A Step may await:

- Provider job,

- callback,

- human action,

- or external condition.

10.268 Completed Step

A Step completes only when its Completion Criteria are met.

10.269 Failed Step

A Step fails when it cannot meet its Completion Criteria under the current Plan boundaries.

10.270 Cancelled Step

A cancelled Step shall preserve:

- reason,

- active Attempts,

- Outputs,

- cost,

- and compensation status.

10.271 Skipped Step

A Step may be skipped when:

- optional,

- condition false,

- superseded,

- or approved degradation.

Skip reason shall be recorded.

10.272 Step State Machine

Each Step Type shall define valid state transitions.

Invalid transitions shall be rejected.

10.273 Execution Creation

When a Step begins, the execution layer creates an Execution object referencing:

- Plan Version,

- Step,

- request,

- selected resource,

- authority,

- policy,

- and budget.

10.274 Multiple Executions Per Step

One Step may produce several Executions because of:

- retry,

- fallback,

- parallel candidates,

- batch items,

- or revision.

All shall remain linked to the Step.

10.275 Attempt History

Each Execution shall preserve its Attempts.

Planning shall not collapse retry history.

10.276 Step Completion Evidence

Step completion may require:

- Execution Receipt,

- Output,

- Evaluation,

- Approval,

- Side-Effect Receipt,

- or reconciliation.

10.277 Graph Progress

Graph progress should distinguish:

- planned,

- ready,

- running,

- blocked,

- completed,

- failed,

- skipped,

- and cancelled Steps.

10.278 Progress Percentage

A percentage may be shown for user convenience.

It shall not replace truthful state.

Progress should consider:

- Step weight,

- mandatory work,

- and uncertainty.

10.279 Cost Progress

The Plan should expose:

- reserved,

- estimated,

- provisional,

- confirmed,

- and remaining budget.

10.280 Time Progress

The Plan may expose:

- elapsed time,

- expected remaining time,

- deadline risk,

- and blocked duration.

10.281 Plan Observability

Observability should include:

- graph state,

- Step state,

- Execution state,

- budget,

- latency,

- resource choice,

- and incidents.

Sensitive Input content shall not be broadly logged.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.282 Trace Correlation

All Plan-related events should preserve:

- planId,

- requestId,

- productionId where applicable,

- traceId,

- correlationId,

- and causationId.

10.283 Plan Event

Material Plan events may include:

- PlanCreated,

- PlanValidated,

- PlanApprovalRequested,

- PlanApproved,

- PlanActivated,

- StepReady,

- StepStarted,

- StepCompleted,

- StepFailed,

- PlanPaused,

- PlanReplanned,

- PlanCompleted,

- and PlanCancelled.

10.284 Event Ordering

The system shall not assume global event ordering.

Object revisions and state-transition validation shall prevent late events from corrupting current state.

10.285 Duplicate Plan Event

Consumers shall handle duplicate events idempotently.

10.286 Plan Incident

A Plan Incident may involve:

- invalid authority,

- runaway retry,

- budget overrun,

- wrong Project data,

- incorrect resource selection,

- lost callback,

- or false completion.

10.287 Planning Incident

A Planning Incident occurs when the Plan itself violates or misrepresents architecture.

Examples include:

- omitted mandatory review,

- hidden publication,

- unsupported Capability,

- unbounded loop,

- or cost underestimation caused by defect.

10.288 Execution Incident

An Execution Incident occurs while performing a valid Plan.

The distinction helps identify whether the defect belongs to planning or execution.

10.289 Incident Containment

Containment may:

- pause Plan,

- block affected Step,

- revoke resource,

- disable fallback,

- freeze budget,

- or cancel side effects.

10.290 Plan Recovery

Recovery may involve:

- resume,

- retry,

- replan,

- compensate,

- reconcile,

- accept partial,

- or cancel.

10.291 Recovery Plan

A Recovery Plan may be created for a failed or uncertain Plan.

It shall reference original evidence.

It shall not rewrite original state.

10.292 Plan Archive

Completed, cancelled, rejected and superseded Plans may be archived according to retention policy.

Historical interpretation must remain possible.

10.293 Plan Retention

Retention may depend on:

- Project,

- commercial use,

- cost,

- classification,

- incident,

- and Output provenance.

10.294 Plan Redaction

A redacted Plan view may hide:

- sensitive Inputs,

- Provider details,

- cost,

- or credentials.

The canonical Plan remains unchanged.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.295 Plan Export

Plans may be exported for:

- review,

- audit,

- documentation,

- simulation,

- or recovery.

Exports shall preserve:

- Version,

- scope,

- and integrity.

10.296 Plan Import Security

Imported Plans shall not execute before:

- schema validation,

- policy validation,

- Capability validation,

- and authority review.

10.297 Plan Integrity

Important Plan Versions should preserve:

- checksum,

- immutable revision,

- author,

- and approval linkage.

10.298 Plan Mutation

Plan mutation shall use:

- expected Version,

- acting Principal,

- reason,

- and validation.

Concurrent silent overwrite is prohibited.

10.299 Plan Access Control

Read access may differ from edit or approve access.

A reviewer may inspect Outputs without seeing all confidential Inputs.

A Project operator may view progress without administering Providers.

10.300 Plan Search

Plan search shall remain Tenant- and Project-scoped.

Search indexes shall not leak cross-Project data.

10.301 Plan Graph Projection

Plans may be projected into the Intelligence Graph.

Relationships may include:

- fulfils Request,

- requires Capability,

- contains Step,

- depends on,

- uses Provider,

- produces Output,

- evaluated by,

- and approved by.

The canonical Plan remains authoritative.

10.302 Plan and Atlas

Atlas may:

- formulate Intent,

- request planning,

- explain alternatives,

- and monitor progress.

Atlas shall not bypass the Plan to call Providers directly.

10.303 Plan and Executive Intelligence

Executive Intelligence may evaluate:

- expected business value,

- cost,

- risk,

- and strategic trade-offs.

It may recommend a Plan.

It does not automatically approve execution.

10.304 Plan and Managers

Managers may coordinate Plans within their authorised Project scope.

They may create child requests and monitor Outcomes.

They shall not expand authority.

10.305 Plan and Specialist Agents

Specialist Agents may execute or assist with specific Steps.

Their authority shall remain Step-scoped.

10.306 Plan and Memory

Plans may retrieve governed memory.

They may also produce Learning or Memory Candidates.

The complete raw Plan shall not automatically become semantic memory.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.307 Plan and Intelligence Graph

The Graph may support:

- dependency navigation,

- provenance,

- explanation,

- and impact analysis.

It shall not be the sole execution state store unless designed and governed for that role.

10.308 Plan and Capability Registry

Every Capability Step shall reference an approved Capability Version.

Unknown or retired Capabilities block activation.

10.309 Plan and Model Registry

Model requirements and selected Versions shall resolve through the Model Registry.

10.310 Plan and Provider Registry

Provider, Account, Product and Connection eligibility shall resolve through the Provider Registry.

10.311 Plan and Credential Service

The Plan may reference Connections.

It shall not contain raw credentials.

10.312 Plan and Cost System

The cost system shall own:

- reservations,

- usage,

- cost records,

- and reconciliation.

The Plan defines budget boundaries and estimates.

10.313 Plan and Approval System

Approval Decisions shall bind to:

- Plan Version,

- scope,

- cost,

- and conditions.

10.314 Plan and Asset System

Plans may consume Assets and produce Asset candidates.

Canonicalisation remains separate.

10.315 Plan and Publication System

Publication shall be represented as a separate Side-Effect Step.

Generation completion shall not imply publication.

10.316 Plan and Repository System

Code Plans shall separate:

- analyse,

- write,

- test,

- commit,

- push,

- pull request,

- merge,

- and deploy.

Each action requires appropriate authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 10.317 Applied Example — Nova and Pling Episode Plan
text:
10.317 Applied Example — Nova and Pling Episode Plan

A Familje-Stunden monthly episode Plan may contain:

Phase 1 — Preparation

1. Resolve approved story manuscript.

2. Resolve canonical Nova and Pling Asset Versions.

3. Validate scene illustration completeness.

4. Validate commercial rights and child-facing policy.

5. Assemble Project Instruction Set.

Phase 2 — Scene Planning

6. Segment story into scenes.

7. Match narration to scene duration.

8. Classify scenes by complexity.

9. Identify character-critical scenes.

10. Estimate preview and production cost.

Phase 3 — Approval

11. Present Production Plan.

12. Approve maximum budget.

13. Approve Providers or Provider classes.

14. Confirm no publication authority.

Phase 4 — Preview Generation

15. Generate low-cost preview for each complex scene.

16. Evaluate Nova consistency.

17. Evaluate Pling consistency.

18. Evaluate child-appropriate motion.

19. Route failed previews to revision.

Phase 5 — Final Scene Production

20. Use economical accepted previews where quality permits.

21. Escalate character-critical failed scenes to premium resource.

22. Ingest Provider videos.

23. Verify format, duration and integrity.

Phase 6 — Narration and Audio

24. Generate or ingest approved Swedish narration.

25. Validate pronunciation.

26. Generate or select approved sound.

27. Mix audio.

Phase 7 — Composition

28. Assemble master video.

29. Add titles and captions.

30. Validate sequence and timing.

Phase 8 — Review

31. Automated technical evaluation.

32. Human child-facing review.

33. Human brand and story review.

34. Revision loop within approved budget.

Phase 9 — Derivatives

35. Create trailer.

36. Create five short clips.

37. Create thumbnail candidates.

38. Preserve derivative provenance.

Phase 10 — Delivery

39. Store accepted master Asset candidate.

40. Prepare Publication Package.

41. Stop before publication unless separately authorised.

The Plan may execute scene previews in parallel.

Premium scene generation may remain conditional.

The complete production remains bounded by one Production Envelope.

10.318 Nova and Pling Scene Subgraph

Each scene may use a Composite Step containing:

1. Resolve scene Input.

2. Resolve character references.

3. Select eligible video resource.

4. Reserve Step budget.

5. Submit generation.

6. Wait for Provider job.

7. Ingest output.

8. Evaluate character consistency.

9. Evaluate technical quality.

10. Accept, retry or escalate.

11. Store accepted scene Output.

The subgraph preserves scene-specific cost and provenance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric

10.322 Applied Example — Omnira Code Audit Plan
text:
10.319 Nova and Pling Premium Escalation

A premium fallback may activate only when:

- preview fails mandatory character criteria,

- scene is character-critical,

- remaining Production budget permits,

- premium resource is eligible,

- and retry count remains within the approved envelope.

Premium use shall not become the default for every scene merely because it is available.

10.320 Applied Example — The Prompt News Plan

A The Prompt AI-news Plan may contain:

Phase 1 — Topic Discovery

1. Search approved current sources.

2. identify candidate developments.

3. remove duplicates.

4. assess date relevance.

Phase 2 — Verification

5. Retrieve primary sources.

6. verify claims.

7. identify uncertainty.

8. reject unsupported developments.

Phase 3 — Editorial Planning

9. Rank stories by importance.

10. Create two-minute structure.

11. distinguish fact from interpretation.

12. generate source-linked script.

Phase 4 — Factual Evaluation

13. Evaluate claim support.

14. verify quotations.

15. confirm dates.

16. require human editorial review.

Phase 5 — Media Production

17. Generate narration or reporter performance.

18. Generate or retrieve approved visual support.

19. Create captions.

20. Compose video.

Phase 6 — Final Review

21. Verify factual consistency with final media.

22. review title and thumbnail.

23. prepare Publication Package.

24. stop before publication unless authorised.

Research, verification and media production remain separate graph branches.

A media Provider never becomes the source authority.

10.321 Applied Example — GainPilot Reel Plan

A GainPilot reel Plan may use:

1. Retrieve approved Arnold brand rules.

2. Generate short Swedish script locally or economically.

3. Validate exercise claim.

4. Generate one image.

5. Generate Swedish narration.

6. Create animated captions locally.

7. Compose 20-second video.

8. Evaluate brand alignment.

9. Request human review.

10. Prepare publication package.

The Plan may use Economy routing because the Output Contract is simpler.

10.322 Applied Example — Omnira Code Audit Plan

An Omnira code audit Plan may include:

1. Resolve repository and branch.

2. verify read-only scope.

3. inspect architecture documents.

4. search relevant files.

5. identify isolation defects.

6. generate audit report.

7. propose patch.

8. generate tests.

9. evaluate architecture conformance.

10. deliver patch candidate.

The Plan shall explicitly exclude:

- commit,

- push,

- pull request,

- merge,

- and deployment.

Those actions require separate Steps and authority.

text:
10.323 Applied Example — Private Local Analysis Plan

A Local Only document Plan may include:

1. Validate local Node.

2. verify local Model Deployment.

3. extract document locally.

4. create local embeddings.

5. retrieve relevant sections.

6. perform local reasoning.

7. create local summary.

8. evaluate output locally.

9. store output in private Project location.

No external fallback branch exists.

If local quality is insufficient, the Plan pauses for revised authority.

10.324 Applied Example — Human-Assisted OpenArt Plan

Before a production API exists, a human-assisted Plan may include:

1. Prepare approved scene package.

2. select approved OpenArt Account.

3. present maximum spend.

4. generate operator instructions.

5. human performs Provider operation.

6. human records credits consumed.

7. human downloads output.

8. Omnira ingests output.

9. preserve Provider job or Asset reference.

10. evaluate quality.

11. accept or repeat within budget.

The Plan is governed.

The central Provider action remains human-assisted.

10.325 Applied Example — Mixed Local and External Research

A Confidential Project request may:

1. extract and summarise confidential documents locally,

2. remove protected identifiers,

3. classify the derived question,

4. search public external sources,

5. combine public research with local summary,

6. perform final synthesis locally,

7. preserve separate provenance.

The Plan shall not send raw confidential documents externally.

10.326 Anti-Pattern — One Giant Prompt as Plan

A complex production shall not be represented only as one prompt asking an Agent to “handle everything.”

This hides:

- authority,

- cost,

- dependencies,

- side effects,

- and failure.

10.327 Anti-Pattern — Provider Workflow as Canonical Plan

A Provider’s internal workflow may assist execution.

It shall not replace Omnira’s canonical Plan when governance boundaries matter.

10.328 Anti-Pattern — Planner Grants Itself Authority

The Planner shall not add:

- publication,

- deletion,

- spending,

- or cross-Project access

because those actions appear useful.

10.329 Anti-Pattern — Hidden Side Effect

Side effects shall not be buried inside:

- generate,

- complete task,

- or run agent

Steps.

sectionTitles: 10.334 Anti-Pattern — Optional Step Presented as Mandatory Cost
10.342 Anti-Pattern — Plan Completion Equals Business Outcome
text:
10.330 Anti-Pattern — Unbounded Agent Loop

An Agent shall not iterate until satisfied without:

- attempt limit,

- budget,

- time,

- and acceptance criteria.

10.331 Anti-Pattern — Retry Every Error

Permanent rejection, policy failure and unknown outcome require different handling from transient failure.

10.332 Anti-Pattern — Fallback Without Revalidation

Fallback resources must satisfy the original constraints.

10.333 Anti-Pattern — Quality Review After Publication

Required evaluation and approval must occur before public side effect.

10.334 Anti-Pattern — Optional Step Presented as Mandatory Cost

Optional work shall remain distinguishable so users understand what can be omitted.

10.335 Anti-Pattern — Mandatory Step Silently Skipped

The Plan cannot claim completion when a mandatory Step was omitted.

10.336 Anti-Pattern — Cost Estimate Without Retry

Expected and maximum cost shall account for the permitted retry strategy.

10.337 Anti-Pattern — Parallel Everything

Uncontrolled parallelism may waste credits and overload review.

Parallelism shall be intentional.

10.338 Anti-Pattern — Sequential Everything

Unnecessary sequential execution increases latency.

Independent Steps may run concurrently within limits.

10.339 Anti-Pattern — Early Binding Every Resource

Binding every Provider and Model long before execution may use stale information.

10.340 Anti-Pattern — Late Binding Consequential Resources

Publication Account, sensitive Provider or contractually pinned resource may require early explicit approval.

10.341 Anti-Pattern — Replanning Rewrites History

A new Plan Version shall not alter the meaning of completed Executions.

10.342 Anti-Pattern — Plan Completion Equals Business Outcome

A production Plan may complete while:

- publication remains pending,

- audience outcome remains unknown,

- or strategic benefit remains unmeasured.

Completion Contract must define the boundary.

10.343 Anti-Pattern — Simulation Presented as Execution

Simulated cost, output or Provider choice shall remain clearly labelled.

10.344 Anti-Pattern — Human Step Hidden

Manual intervention must be visible in the graph.

10.345 Anti-Pattern — Human Approval as Comment

Approval conditions must become enforceable Plan constraints.

10.354 Anti-Pattern — Planner Uses Stale Registry as Current Truth
text:
10.346 Anti-Pattern — Project Scope From Prompt

Each Step shall inherit or declare canonical Project scope.

10.347 Anti-Pattern — Plan Contains Raw Credential

Plans reference Connections.

They never contain raw secret material.

10.348 Anti-Pattern — One Universal Planning Template

Different requests require different:

- quality,

- rights,

- risk,

- and completion structures.

10.349 Anti-Pattern — Provider Success Ends Plan

Provider success may still require:

- ingestion,

- validation,

- review,

- and storage.

10.350 Anti-Pattern — Unknown Outcome Treated as Failure

Unknown external state requires reconciliation before unsafe retry.

10.351 Anti-Pattern — Failed Plan Deletes Accepted Outputs

Useful accepted Outputs should remain available where policy permits.

10.352 Anti-Pattern — Graph Without Lifecycle

Nodes and Edges require state and transition semantics.

A static diagram is not an executable Plan.

10.353 Anti-Pattern — Graph as Uncontrolled Code

Arbitrary executable code shall not be treated as a valid Plan without canonical validation.

10.354 Anti-Pattern — Planner Uses Stale Registry as Current Truth

Registry and health freshness shall be visible.

10.355 Stage 1 Planning Objective

Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy planning system capable of converting representative Capability Requests into governed Execution Plans.

The objective is not to support unrestricted dynamic agent planning.

Stage 1 shall prove:

- canonical Plan identity,

- request decomposition,

- Execution Graph,

- Step contracts,

- budget allocation,

- approval boundaries,

- resource requirements,

- retries,

- fallback,

- evaluation,

- and Completion Contracts.

10.356 Stage 1 Minimum Plan Types

Stage 1 should support:

- simple single-Step Plan,

- sequential multi-Step Plan,

- parallel Plan,

- preview-and-evaluate Plan,

- bounded retry Plan,

- Provider fallback Plan,

- local private Plan,

- human-assisted Plan,

- and side-effect-separated Plan.

10.357 Stage 1 Plan Object

The Stage 1 Plan object should include:

- planId,

- planVersion,

- requestId,

- requestVersion,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- status,

- graph,

- expected cost,

- maximum cost,

- expected latency,

- approvals,

- assumptions,

- Completion Contract,

- and provenance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.358 Stage 1 Step Object

The Stage 1 Step object should include:

- stepId,

- stepType,

- Capability,

- dependencies,

- Inputs,

- Output Contract,

- Quality Contract,

- Resource Requirement,

- budget,

- retry policy,

- fallback policy,

- authority,

- and status.

10.359 Stage 1 Edge Object

The Stage 1 Edge object should include:

- edgeId,

- sourceStep,

- targetStep,

- edgeType,

- condition,

- and provenance.

10.360 Stage 1 Planner

Stage 1 may use a hybrid Planner consisting of:

- predefined Templates,

- deterministic validation,

- registry lookup,

- cost estimation,

- and bounded AI assistance.

AI-generated Plans shall not activate before deterministic validation.

10.361 Stage 1 Planning Templates

Initial Templates may include:

- text generation,

- research and verification,

- image generation and review,

- voice generation and review,

- video preview and final generation,

- local private analysis,

- and human-assisted production.

10.362 Stage 1 Resource Binding

Stage 1 should support:

- pinned resource,

- preferred candidate list,

- and late-bound selection.

The binding mode shall be explicit.

10.363 Stage 1 Cost Planning

Stage 1 Plans shall include:

- estimated cost,

- maximum approved cost,

- retry allowance,

- and budget source.

10.364 Stage 1 Approval Planning

Paid or consequential Plans shall produce an Approval Summary.

Approval shall bind to the Plan Version.

10.365 Stage 1 Retry Planning

Retries shall be bounded by:

- count,

- cost,

- timeout,

- and failure category.

10.366 Stage 1 Fallback Planning

Fallback shall support at least:

- second external text Provider,

- local text alternative where eligible,

- and human-assisted multimodal alternative where automation is incomplete.

10.367 Stage 1 Evaluation Planning

Representative Quality Gates should include:

- schema validation,

- source-grounding review,

- code test,

- image review,

- voice review,

- and human media approval.

10.368 Stage 1 Human Step

Stage 1 shall support explicit Human Action and Human Review Steps.

10.369 Stage 1 Side-Effect Separation

Publication, repository push, deletion and Account administration shall remain separate from ordinary generation Plans.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.370 Stage 1 Plan API

Stage 1 should support:

- create Plan,

- validate Plan,

- estimate Plan,

- list alternatives,

- request approval,

- activate,

- inspect graph,

- pause,

- resume,

- cancel,

- replan,

- and retrieve Plan receipt.

10.371 Stage 1 Graph Execution

The execution engine shall activate only Ready Steps.

Readiness shall require:

- dependencies,

- approvals,

- budget,

- policy,

- Inputs,

- and resource eligibility.

10.372 Stage 1 Plan Acceptance Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Plan remains separate from Capability Request.

2. Plan remains separate from Execution.

3. Plan references exact Request Version.

4. Plan Version changes after material graph change.

5. Mandatory Step cannot be silently removed.

6. Optional Step may be skipped according to Completion Contract.

7. Publication remains separate from generation.

8. Plan cannot activate without required approval.

9. Plan cannot exceed the Request Budget Envelope.

10. Plan graph rejects unbounded cycles.

11. Plan graph rejects unreachable mandatory Steps.

12. Dependencies prevent early execution.

13. Parallel Steps respect concurrency limits.

14. Human-assisted Step remains visible.

15. Unknown Capability blocks activation.

16. Retired resource is not selected.

17. Local Only Step excludes external resources.

18. Plan references Connections rather than raw credentials.

19. Completed Plan preserves its exact Version.

20. Superseded Plan remains historically interpretable.

10.373 Stage 1 Retry Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Transient failure retries within limit.

2. Permanent policy rejection does not retry.

3. Unknown outcome enters reconciliation.

4. Retry cost counts against budget.

5. Retry exhaustion produces terminal or escalation state.

6. Idempotency key prevents duplicate side effect.

7. Retry history remains visible.

8. Quality retry remains separate from transport retry.

9. Fallback may occur after retry policy permits it.

10. Infinite retry is impossible.

10.374 Stage 1 Fallback Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Fallback resource is revalidated.

2. Fallback preserves Data Classification.

3. Fallback preserves commercial-rights requirement.

4. Fallback preserves Quality Floor.

5. Fallback remains inside budget.

6. Pinned mandatory Provider blocks silent substitution.

7. Material fallback creates disclosure or approval.

8. Local Only Plan has no external fallback.

9. Human-assisted fallback is labelled honestly.

10. Fallback selection is evidenced.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.375 Stage 1 Budget Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Sum of maximum Step budgets does not exceed Plan budget.

2. Shared retry reserve cannot be overspent.

3. Parallel paid Steps reserve budget before launch.

4. Confirmed cost reduces remaining budget.

5. Unknown cost remains provisional.

6. Optional Steps stop when discretionary budget is exhausted.

7. Plan pauses before material overrun.

8. Replanning recalculates cost.

9. Approval invalidates after material budget increase.

10. Personal Provider credits are not used silently.

10.376 Stage 1 Authority Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Planner cannot add publication authority.

2. Planner cannot add cross-Project access.

3. Planner cannot lower Data Classification.

4. Step authority cannot exceed parent request.

5. Delegated Planner authority remains traceable.

6. Human approval binds to exact Plan Version.

7. Expired approval blocks activation.

8. Approval conditions become Step constraints.

9. Administrative Step requires privileged authority.

10. Planner Service Principal cannot retrieve raw Provider secrets.

10.377 Stage 1 Graph Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Directed dependencies execute in correct order.

2. Parallel branch joins according to defined rule.

3. Conditional branch executes only when condition is true.

4. Fallback Edge activates only after defined trigger.

5. Compensation Edge does not run without triggering failure.

6. Bounded loop stops at maximum iterations.

7. Late event cannot revert completed Step.

8. Duplicate event does not duplicate execution.

9. Orphaned Node fails validation.

10. Completion Gate rejects missing mandatory evidence.

10.378 Stage 1 Replanning Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Provider outage may create new Plan Version.

2. Completed Steps remain preserved.

3. Changed Input invalidates dependent Steps.

4. Unaffected Steps remain reusable.

5. Material Provider change may require approval.

6. Cost is recalculated.

7. Old Plan remains immutable.

8. New Executions reference new Plan Version.

9. Cancelled old Steps cannot restart.

10. Replanning reason is evidenced.

10.379 Stage 1 Privacy Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Step Inputs remain Project-scoped.

2. Data transfer boundaries are explicit.

3. Confidential Inputs cannot enter unapproved external Step.

4. Local preprocessing does not automatically declassify data.

5. Plan visualisation can redact protected content.

6. Search does not expose other Tenant Plans.

7. Human reviewer sees only authorised data.

8. Context Package contains minimum necessary information.

9. Provider payload is not copied into broad logs.

10. Plan export preserves classification.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.380 Stage 1 Reliability Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Plan state survives process restart.

2. Wait Step survives long delay.

3. Callback correlates to correct Step and Execution.

4. Provider timeout produces truthful state.

5. Paused Plan starts no new Steps.

6. Resume revalidates policy and credentials.

7. Cancellation preserves active-job reconciliation.

8. Partial Outputs remain available after failure.

9. Scheduler does not execute blocked Step.

10. Critical Provider disable propagates to Ready Steps.

10.381 Stage 1 Observability Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Plan progress distinguishes blocked and running.

2. Cost progress distinguishes estimated and confirmed.

3. Step resource selection is visible.

4. Approval state is visible.

5. Retry count is visible.

6. Fallback use is visible.

7. Human Action remains visible.

8. Unknown outcomes are visible.

9. Plan events preserve correlation.

10. Logs do not expose secrets.

10.382 Planning Conformance Requirements

An implementation conforms to this chapter only when:

- Plans remain separate from Requests and Executions,

- graph structure is explicit,

- every Step has bounded meaning,

- mandatory constraints propagate,

- authority remains attached,

- cost remains bounded,

- data placement remains enforceable,

- side effects remain explicit,

- retries and loops remain bounded,

- fallback remains policy-compliant,

- Plan changes are versioned,

- and Completion requires defined evidence.

A visual workflow editor alone does not prove conformance.

The runtime must enforce the canonical Plan.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.383 Canonical Planning Contract

The following requirements define the canonical planning contract:

1. Every complex governed Capability Request SHALL be translated into an Execution Plan or approved equivalent.

2. Planning SHALL remain separate from execution.

3. Planning SHALL remain separate from authority.

4. Planning SHALL preserve human Intent.

5. The Planner SHALL NOT weaken mandatory request constraints.

6. Every Plan SHALL have stable identity.

7. Every material Plan change SHALL create a new Plan Version.

8. Every Plan SHALL reference the exact Request Version.

9. Every Plan SHALL define an Execution Graph.

10. Every executable Step SHALL have stable identity within the Plan Version.

11. Every Step SHALL declare its Capability or action type.

12. Every Step SHALL declare Inputs and expected Outputs.

13. Every Step SHALL declare applicable authority.

14. Every Step SHALL declare applicable data classification.

15. Every paid Step SHALL have budget allocation.

16. Every external Step SHALL identify resource requirements.

17. Side effects SHALL remain explicit.

18. Publication SHALL remain separate from generation.

19. Human actions SHALL remain visible.

20. Quality Gates SHALL be represented before acceptance.

21. Mandatory and optional Steps SHALL remain distinguishable.

22. Dependencies SHALL be explicit.

23. Loops SHALL be bounded.

24. Retries SHALL be bounded.

25. Fallback SHALL preserve mandatory policy.

26. Unknown outcomes SHALL trigger reconciliation rather than unsafe assumption.

27. Partial completion SHALL remain truthful.

28. Replanning SHALL preserve completed history.

29. Plan approval SHALL bind to an exact Plan Version.

30. Plan activation SHALL require validation and current eligibility.

10.384 Canonical Execution Graph Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Execution Graph contract:

1. The Execution Graph SHALL be directed.

2. Nodes SHALL have explicit types.

3. Edges SHALL have explicit semantics.

4. Mandatory Nodes SHALL be reachable.

5. Unbounded cycles SHALL be prohibited.

6. Bounded loops SHALL declare limits and exit conditions.

7. Data Edges SHALL preserve lineage.

8. Control Edges SHALL preserve execution order.

9. Conditional Edges SHALL declare evaluable conditions.

10. Fallback Edges SHALL declare triggers and constraints.

11. Compensation Edges SHALL declare corrective purpose.

12. Join behaviour SHALL be explicit.

13. Parallel groups SHALL declare concurrency and budget.

14. Graph state SHALL be durable.

15. Duplicate events SHALL NOT duplicate effects.

16. Late events SHALL NOT silently corrupt newer state.

17. Completion Gates SHALL inspect mandatory evidence.

18. Graph visualisations SHALL remain derived views.

19. Graph imports SHALL be validated before execution.

20. Graph execution SHALL enforce scope and authority at every Step.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.385 Canonical Step Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Step contract:

1. Every Step SHALL identify its parent Plan Version.

2. Every Step SHALL identify its Step Type.

3. Every intelligence Step SHALL reference a Capability Version.

4. Every Step SHALL identify required Inputs.

5. Every Step SHALL define expected Outputs.

6. Every Step SHALL define Completion Criteria.

7. Every Step SHALL identify dependencies.

8. Every Step SHALL identify authority requirements.

9. Every Step SHALL identify data-placement requirements.

10. Every paid Step SHALL identify budget.

11. Every retryable Step SHALL identify Retry Policy.

12. Every fallback-capable Step SHALL identify Fallback Policy.

13. Every long-running Step SHALL identify timeout and reconciliation behaviour.

14. Every human Step SHALL identify responsible role and evidence.

15. Every side-effect Step SHALL identify idempotency and verification.

16. Every Step state transition SHALL be valid and attributable.

17. Step Outputs SHALL preserve provenance.

18. Step failure SHALL preserve incurred cost.

19. Step cancellation SHALL preserve residual state.

20. Step completion SHALL NOT be inferred from Provider acceptance alone.

10.386 Planning Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No Plan changes the user’s Intent silently.

- No Planner grants itself new authority.

- No mandatory Step disappears for convenience.

- No optional Step becomes hidden mandatory cost.

- No Plan exceeds its approved budget.

- No raw credential enters the Plan.

- No protected data crosses an unapproved boundary.

- No side effect hides inside a generic intelligence Step.

- No publication occurs under generation-only authority.

- No retry loop is unbounded.

- No fallback weakens policy.

- No unknown outcome becomes assumed failure or success.

- No Provider success becomes automatic acceptance.

- No Plan Version rewrites completed history.

- No human-assisted Step is represented as automated.

- No simulation is represented as production.

- No Project scope is inferred only from prompt content.

- No inactive or retired resource becomes selectable.

- No Plan completes without its defined Completion Contract.

- No execution path expands beyond the approved envelope.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
10.387 Closing Statement

The Intelligence Planner is the component that turns governed intent into governed action structure.

It allows Omnira to move beyond isolated prompts and provider calls without surrendering control to opaque agent autonomy.

The user defines the objective.

The Capability Request defines what the Fabric may attempt.

The Planner decomposes the work.

The Execution Graph defines dependencies.

The Steps define bounded operations.

The Resource Requirements define what implementation is needed.

Routing chooses the eligible resources.

The Budget Envelope limits spending.

The Authority Envelope limits action.

The Quality Gates define acceptance.

The Retry Policies define bounded recovery.

The Fallback Policies define eligible alternatives.

The Completion Gate determines whether the promised result was actually achieved.

For Familje-Stunden, this architecture allows one Nova and Pling episode to coordinate story, scene planning, character references, video, voice, sound, composition, evaluation and human review without handing the entire Project to one Provider.

For The Prompt, it keeps research, verification, editorial reasoning, media creation and publication as separate governed responsibilities.

For GainPilot, it enables economical mixed-resource production without creating a second orchestration architecture.

For Omnira, it allows code, research, media, local Models, external Providers, human work and future agent systems to participate in one versioned execution structure.

The Plan may change.

The Provider may change.

The Model may change.

The user’s approved objective and authority boundary remain stable.

No complex execution without a Plan.

No Plan without scope.

No Step without purpose.

No side effect without authority.

No retry without a bound.

No fallback without policy.

No completion without evidence.

The user retains direction.

Omnira retains orchestration.

The Fabric turns intention into governed execution.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical architecture, governance model, decision order, lifecycle, contracts and operational responsibilities for routing within the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

It establishes:

- how eligible intelligence resources are discovered,

- how mandatory constraints are separated from preferences,

- how Providers, Provider Accounts, Models, Deployments, Tools, local resources, External Agent Resources and human-assisted paths are compared,

- how the canonical Routing Profiles Economy, Balanced, Premium, Private and Pinned behave,

- how security, privacy, data classification, rights, authority, quality, deadline and budget outrank ordinary optimisation,

- how local, user-owned and Omnira-managed capacity coexist,

- how resource candidates are excluded, ranked, selected and substituted,

- how profile defaults and Project-specific policy are applied,

- how current health, quotas, credits, latency and capacity affect decisions,

- how fallback and retry remain governed,

- how routing decisions remain explainable,

- how commercial conflicts of interest are controlled,

- how routing learning is admitted without creating unbounded self-modification,

- and how Stage 1 shall implement a bounded but extensible routing system.

Routing is the process through which the Fabric selects an eligible execution path for a specific bounded Step or request.

Routing does not determine the user’s intent.

Routing does not define Capability meaning.

Routing does not create execution authority.

Routing does not lower Data Classification.

Routing does not grant commercial rights.

Routing does not approve spending.

Routing operates only after mandatory eligibility conditions have been resolved.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

Runtime implementation and conformance must be verified separately.

11.2 Purpose of Routing

The Intelligence Fabric may have many ways to fulfil the same Capability.

A text Capability may be available through:

- a local Model,

- a user-owned external subscription,

- an Omnira-managed Provider Account,

- a specialist external Provider,

- or a human-assisted workflow.

A video Capability may be available through:

- one economical Model,

- one premium Provider,

- one Provider-managed router,

- one local composition workflow,

- or one manually operated creative platform.

Without a canonical routing layer, resource selection would tend to become:

- hard-coded in Project code,

- embedded inside Agent prompts,

- determined by whichever Provider was connected first,

- chosen manually for every task,

- based on Provider popularity,

- or driven by hidden commercial incentives.

The routing architecture exists to choose the best eligible path for the current request while preserving:

- user control,

- Project isolation,

- quality,

- cost,

- privacy,

- rights,

- reliability,

- deadline,

- and truthful evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 11.9 Routing Is Not Global Best-Resource Selection
text:
11.3 Routing Is Not Planning

Planning defines:

- which Steps are required,

- what Capabilities they need,

- what dependencies exist,

- what budgets apply,

- and what Completion Contract must be satisfied.

Routing selects the current eligible resource for a Step.

A Plan may state:

Generate one Swedish narration track using speech.synthesise.

Routing determines whether that Step uses:

- a local speech Model,

- ElevenLabs,

- another Provider,

- an Omnira-managed voice service,

- or a human-assisted path.

The Plan defines the need.

Routing selects the implementation.

11.4 Routing Is Not Capability Resolution

Capability Resolution determines which canonical operation is required.

Routing occurs only after the Capability is known.

The Router shall not replace:

video.image_to_video

with:

image.generate

merely because an image Model is cheaper.

A materially different Capability path requires:

- approved alternative,

- replanning,

- or degraded-outcome approval.

11.5 Routing Is Not Authority

A Router may identify a technically attractive Provider.

It shall not select that Provider if:

- the Principal lacks authority,

- the Provider Account is outside Project scope,

- spending is unapproved,

- or the requested side effect is prohibited.

Routing cannot expand the Authority Envelope.

11.6 Routing Is Not Policy Creation

Routing applies current policy.

It does not invent policy dynamically.

The Router may produce a Policy Gap when rules are incomplete.

It shall not assume that missing policy means permission.

11.7 Routing Is Not Provider Preference

A Provider Preference may influence ranking.

It is not the same as routing.

Routing considers all applicable mandatory and optimisation dimensions.

11.8 Routing Is Not Model Popularity

A widely known or expensive Model is not automatically the correct resource.

Suitability depends on:

- Capability,

- Inputs,

- Quality Contract,

- Project,

- privacy,

- rights,

- budget,

- latency,

- and current evidence.

11.9 Routing Is Not Global Best-Resource Selection

There is no universal best resource.

A resource may be best for:

- Swedish technical reasoning,

- but not image editing;

- low-cost captioning,

- but not child-facing narration;

- local confidential analysis,

- but not premium video production.

Routing decisions shall remain request-specific.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.10 Intelligence Router

The Intelligence Router is the Fabric component or governed service responsible for selecting eligible Resource Candidates.

The Router may use:

- deterministic policy,

- Registry data,

- current operational state,

- cost estimates,

- quality evidence,

- routing profile,

- historical outcomes,

- and bounded learned preferences.

The Router shall operate as an identifiable Service Principal.

It shall not own unrestricted Provider credentials.

11.11 Router Responsibilities

The Router is responsible for:

- receiving a Routing Request,

- resolving applicable policy,

- generating Resource Candidates,

- evaluating hard eligibility,

- excluding incompatible candidates,

- scoring eligible candidates,

- selecting a candidate or ranked set,

- identifying fallback candidates,

- preserving decision evidence,

- and returning a Selection Decision.

The Router shall distinguish:

- eligible,

- ineligible,

- conditionally eligible,

- unavailable,

- and unresolved candidates.

11.12 Router Non-Responsibilities

The Router is not responsible for:

- changing the user objective,

- creating new Capabilities,

- accepting Provider terms,

- granting credentials,

- raising the budget,

- lowering the Quality Floor,

- changing Data Classification,

- granting publication authority,

- or declaring an Output accepted.

These responsibilities remain outside routing.

11.13 Routing Request

A Routing Request is a canonical request to select one or more eligible execution resources.

It shall include or reference:

- routingRequestId,

- Capability Requirement,

- Plan Version,

- Step ID,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- initiating Principal,

- Authority Envelope,

- Data Classification,

- Rights Profile,

- Consent requirements,

- Quality Contract,

- Budget allocation,

- deadline,

- latency requirement,

- Routing Profile,

- Provider constraints,

- Model constraints,

- placement constraints,

- required Features,

- Inputs,

- output requirements,

- retry context,

- and policy versions.

11.14 Routing Request Identity

Every material Routing Request shall have stable identity.

A Step may produce several Routing Requests because of:

- initial selection,

- retry,

- fallback,

- replanning,

- or changed operational conditions.

Each decision shall remain traceable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.15 Routing Context

Routing Context may include:

- Capability Registry Snapshot,

- Model Registry Snapshot,

- Provider Registry Snapshot,

- Tool Registry Snapshot,

- Connection state,

- Credential state,

- Provider Account state,

- Runtime Node state,

- current pricing,

- current quota,

- current credit balance,

- current health,

- benchmark evidence,

- Project preferences,

- and governed learning.

Every operational input shall declare freshness.

11.16 Routing Output

The primary routing output is a Selection Decision.

Routing may also produce:

- ranked candidates,

- exclusions,

- warnings,

- approval requirement,

- budget conflict,

- no-route result,

- degraded alternatives,

- and fallback chain.

11.17 Selection Decision

A Selection Decision shall include or reference:

- selectionDecisionId,

- routingRequestId,

- selected Resource Candidate,

- selected Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Connection,

- Model Version or Tool,

- Deployment or Runtime Node,

- Adapter,

- Capability Version,

- Routing Profile,

- eligibility results,

- score components,

- expected cost,

- expected latency,

- quality evidence,

- privacy and rights status,

- fallback set,

- decision time,

- data freshness,

- and provenance.

11.18 Decision Version

Material changes to routing logic or candidate state may produce a new Selection Decision.

The execution shall reference the exact Selection Decision used when the Provider operation began.

11.19 Decision Finality

A Selection Decision is valid only for a bounded time and context.

It may become invalid because of:

- Provider outage,

- Account exhaustion,

- credential expiry,

- price change,

- policy change,

- Model retirement,

- or deadline shift.

The Executor shall revalidate material conditions before use.

11.20 Selection Window

A Selection Window defines how long a decision may be used without full rerouting.

The window should reflect:

- operational volatility,

- cost sensitivity,

- Provider health,

- and request consequence.

11.21 Early Routing

Early Routing selects resources during planning or approval.

It may be appropriate when:

- the exact Provider must be approved,

- the resource is pinned,

- capacity must be reserved,

- or cost must be known.

Early Routing is more exposed to stale operational state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.22 Late Routing

Late Routing selects resources shortly before execution.

It can use current:

- health,

- pricing,

- quota,

- and capacity.

Late Routing may be unsuitable when the user expects exact Provider disclosure before approval.

11.23 Hybrid Routing

Hybrid Routing may decide:

- Provider class during planning,

- Account during approval,

- Model Family during scheduling,

- and exact Deployment at execution.

The binding level shall remain explicit.

11.24 Candidate Resource

A Candidate Resource is a complete or partial path capable of performing the requested Step.

A Candidate may include:

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Connection,

- Model Version,

- Model Deployment,

- Adapter,

- Tool,

- External Agent Resource,

- Runtime Node,

- human-assisted process,

- or composed resource path.

11.25 Complete Resource Candidate

A Complete Resource Candidate contains every operational object required to execute the Step.

For an external Model request, this may include:

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Connection,

- Model Version,

- Deployment,

- Adapter,

- and pricing reference.

11.26 Partial Candidate

A Partial Candidate lacks one or more unresolved elements.

Examples include:

- Provider selected but exact Model late-bound,

- local Model selected but Runtime Node unavailable,

- human-assisted path without assigned operator,

- or Model known but no active Connection.

Partial Candidates shall not be executed until complete.

11.27 Composite Candidate

A Composite Candidate satisfies one Step through several resources.

For example:

- local document extraction,

- external reasoning,

- local validation,

- and human review.

Composite candidates may require replanning when the composition changes the Step boundary materially.

11.28 Human-Assisted Candidate

A Human-Assisted Candidate includes one or more required human operations.

It shall declare:

- operator,

- Provider Account,

- manual action,

- expected cost,

- output handoff,

- and evidence.

It shall not be scored as fully autonomous.

11.29 Simulated Candidate

A Simulated Candidate exists only for:

- testing,

- cost comparison,

- or policy simulation.

It shall not be selected for production execution.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.30 Candidate Generation

Candidate Generation discovers resources that may structurally support the requested Capability.

It may query:

- Capability Registry,

- Model Registry,

- Provider Registry,

- Tool Registry,

- Runtime Node Registry,

- and approved human-assisted procedures.

Candidate Generation is broad.

Eligibility evaluation narrows the set.

11.31 Candidate Discovery Scope

Candidate discovery shall respect:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- visibility,

- and administrative restrictions.

A private Tenant resource shall not appear as a candidate for another Tenant.

11.32 Candidate Set

The Candidate Set is the complete set considered by the Router for one decision.

The decision record should preserve:

- candidates discovered,

- candidates excluded before scoring,

- candidates scored,

- and candidates selected.

11.33 Candidate Deduplication

Equivalent candidate paths may appear through:

- aliases,

- duplicate Model records,

- several Adapter views,

- or Provider routing products.

The Router should deduplicate only when equivalence is sufficiently established.

11.34 Eligibility Before Ranking

The Router shall evaluate eligibility before optimisation.

A resource that violates a mandatory constraint shall not receive a score that could overcome the violation.

The decision sequence is:

1. Resolve mandatory policy.

2. Generate candidates.

3. Evaluate hard eligibility.

4. Exclude ineligible candidates.

5. Score eligible candidates.

6. Select according to profile.

7. preserve fallback.

8. revalidate before execution.

11.35 Hard Constraint

A Hard Constraint is a requirement that cannot be traded away through scoring.

Examples include:

- Local Only processing,

- valid commercial rights,

- mandatory consent,

- required Capability Feature,

- explicit Provider deny,

- maximum authorised cost,

- production-approved Connection,

- and required publication authority.

11.36 Soft Constraint

A Soft Constraint expresses preference rather than absolute eligibility.

Examples include:

- prefer local,

- prefer included credits,

- prefer lower latency,

- prefer one Provider,

- or prefer higher quality.

Soft constraints may influence ranking.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.37 Mandatory Requirement

A Mandatory Requirement shall fail closed when unsatisfied.

The Router must not convert a mandatory requirement into a preference because few candidates remain.

11.38 Preferred Requirement

A Preferred Requirement should influence ranking.

The decision record should show when a preferred requirement was not satisfied and why.

11.39 Optional Feature

An Optional Feature may improve suitability.

Its absence shall not create ineligibility unless the request marks it mandatory.

11.40 Eligibility Result

Candidate eligibility may be:

- eligible,

- eligible with conditions,

- ineligible,

- unavailable,

- unresolved,

- approval required,

- or requires replanning.

11.41 Eligible Candidate

An Eligible Candidate satisfies all hard constraints under current evidence.

11.42 Conditionally Eligible Candidate

A Conditionally Eligible Candidate may be used only when defined conditions are satisfied.

Conditions may include:

- human review,

- separate approval,

- lower data class,

- limited duration,

- or bounded retry.

11.43 Ineligible Candidate

An Ineligible Candidate violates at least one mandatory condition.

Its exclusion reason shall be recorded.

11.44 Unavailable Candidate

An Unavailable Candidate may be structurally and policy compatible but cannot currently execute because of:

- outage,

- quota,

- credits,

- capacity,

- authentication,

- or maintenance.

11.45 Unresolved Candidate

An Unresolved Candidate lacks sufficient evidence for a safe decision.

Unknown shall not be treated as eligible.

11.46 Approval-Required Candidate

A Candidate may be otherwise eligible but require:

- Provider approval,

- cost approval,

- data-placement approval,

- voice consent,

- or premium escalation approval.

The Router shall return the required approval boundary.

11.47 Replanning-Required Candidate

A Candidate requires a materially different Capability path or graph structure.

Routing shall not perform that substitution silently.

11.48 Policy Precedence

Mandatory policy shall be applied before optimisation.

The canonical precedence order is:

1. Law and mandatory external obligations.

2. Platform security and safety policy.

3. Tenant isolation and Project scope.

4. Data Classification and privacy.

5. Rights, consent and commercial-use requirements.

6. Authority and approval.

7. Capability and Feature compatibility.

8. Quality Floor and mandatory evaluation.

9. Hard deadline and operational feasibility.

10. Maximum budget and cost authority.

11. Provider, Model and placement restrictions.

12. Routing Profile.

13. Project and user preferences.

14. Learned optimisation.

15. Tie-breaking policy.

A lower level shall not override a higher mandatory level.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.49 Legal Constraint

Where a legal or contractual requirement is known and applicable, it shall be enforced before routing preference.

The Fabric shall not invent legal conclusions.

Unresolved legal uncertainty may require human review.

11.50 Security Constraint

Security policy may exclude resources because of:

- compromised Credential,

- unsafe Model artefact,

- untrusted Adapter,

- active Provider Incident,

- or excessive administrative scope.

11.51 Tenant Isolation Constraint

A resource belonging to another Tenant is ineligible unless an explicit managed shared-service architecture permits isolated use.

11.52 Project Scope Constraint

A Project-owned Account, Asset, Credential or local Node shall not be used by another Project without explicit authority.

11.53 Data Classification Constraint

The Candidate shall be compatible with the effective Data Classification.

The Router shall use the most restrictive unresolved classification.

11.54 Privacy Constraint

Privacy may require:

- Local Only execution,

- approved region,

- no training use,

- zero or bounded retention,

- private Deployment,

- or user-controlled infrastructure.

11.55 Rights Constraint

The Candidate shall support required:

- commercial use,

- modification,

- distribution,

- attribution,

- and derivative rights.

11.56 Consent Constraint

Voice, likeness or personal-data use may require valid consent.

No score may compensate for missing consent.

11.57 Authority Constraint

The acting Principal and Plan shall have authority for:

- Capability,

- Project,

- Provider class,

- cost,

- side effect,

- and retry.

11.58 Capability Compatibility Constraint

The Candidate shall support the exact Capability Version or an approved compatible version.

11.59 Feature Compatibility Constraint

Mandatory Features shall be supported.

A base-capability claim is insufficient.

11.60 Quality Floor Constraint

The Candidate shall have sufficient evidence to meet the minimum Quality Floor.

Unknown quality may be treated as:

- experimental,

- approval required,

- or ineligible

depending on consequence.

11.61 Deadline Constraint

The Candidate shall have a feasible chance of meeting a Hard Deadline.

Routing shall include:

- queue,

- execution,

- review,

- and fallback time.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 11.70 No-Route Is Not Failure of Intent
text:
11.62 Budget Constraint

Expected and maximum candidate cost shall remain inside the approved Step and Plan budgets.

11.63 Provider Restriction

Provider allowlists, denylists and pinning shall be enforced.

11.64 Model Restriction

Model Family, Version, ownership class or licence restrictions shall be enforced.

11.65 Placement Restriction

Execution may be restricted to:

- local Node,

- user-managed Provider,

- approved region,

- Omnira-managed cloud,

- or external Provider class.

11.66 Integration Maturity Constraint

Production work may require:

- production API,

- production MCP,

- local production,

- or approved human-assisted process.

An experimental connection may remain ineligible.

11.67 Evidence Sufficiency

Eligibility requires sufficient evidence.

The required evidence strength shall increase with:

- consequence,

- cost,

- privacy,

- public exposure,

- and irreversibility.

11.68 Fail-Closed Routing

When a mandatory eligibility property cannot be resolved, the Router shall fail closed.

It may:

- request clarification,

- request approval,

- recommend a safer Candidate,

- or return no route.

11.69 No-Route Result

A No-Route Result means no current Candidate satisfies all mandatory conditions.

It shall identify:

- violated constraints,

- unavailable resources,

- unresolved evidence,

- and possible next actions.

11.70 No-Route Is Not Failure of Intent

The user’s Intent may remain valid when no route exists.

The request may:

- wait,

- amend constraints,

- add Provider access,

- use human assistance,

- or be deferred.

11.71 Routing Profile

A Routing Profile is a canonical policy preset describing how eligible candidates should be optimised.

The canonical profiles are:

- Economy,

- Balanced,

- Premium,

- Private,

- and Pinned.

A Routing Profile applies only after mandatory eligibility.

11.72 Profile Identity

Every Routing Profile shall have stable canonical identity and version.

The profile shall define:

- objective,

- weighting,

- tie-breaking,

- permissible strategies,

- fallback behaviour,

- and disclosure requirements.

11.73 Profile Version

Material changes to profile behaviour require a new Profile Version.

Executions shall preserve which profile version influenced selection.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.74 Profile Inheritance

A Routing Profile may be selected through:

- request-explicit setting,

- Production Envelope,

- Project policy,

- Tenant policy,

- user preference,

- Workflow Template,

- or safe platform default.

11.75 Profile Resolution Order

The effective profile should be resolved in this order:

1. Request-explicit profile.

2. Approved Production Envelope.

3. Workflow or Plan requirement.

4. Project default.

5. Tenant default.

6. User preference.

7. Platform safe default.

Mandatory policy may override any profile behaviour.

11.76 Default Profile

Balanced should normally be the default for ordinary governed production unless Project or Tenant policy defines another default.

The default shall be explicit.

Missing profile shall not create undefined behaviour.

11.77 Profile Override

A user or authorised system may override the default profile within policy.

The override shall preserve:

- actor,

- reason where material,

- scope,

- and validity.

11.78 Profile Restriction

A Project may prohibit certain profiles.

Examples include:

- Premium prohibited for routine tasks,

- Pinned prohibited without architecture reason,

- External Balanced prohibited for Local Only work.

11.79 Profile Combination

One Step shall have one effective primary Routing Profile.

Additional constraints such as:

- local-first,

- included-credit preference,

- or approved Provider preference

may be expressed separately.

Profiles shall not be combined ambiguously.

11.80 Economy Profile

Economy optimises for the lowest expected total eligible cost.

Economy shall preserve:

- Quality Floor,

- privacy,

- rights,

- authority,

- deadline,

- reliability minimum,

- and required evidence.

Economy does not mean:

- lowest advertised unit price,

- free at any quality,

- unlimited local execution,

- or skipping evaluation.

11.81 Economy Objective

The Economy objective is:

Select the lowest expected total-cost Candidate that satisfies all mandatory constraints and has acceptable reliability.

11.82 Economy Cost Definition

Total expected cost may include:

- direct Provider charge,

- expected retry cost,

- post-processing cost,

- human correction cost,

- transfer cost,

- local compute estimate,

- and deadline risk.

The cheapest initial generation may not be the cheapest completed result.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.83 Economy Candidate Preference

Economy may prefer:

- included subscription capacity,

- free eligible quota,

- local resources,

- lower-cost Providers,

- smaller Models,

- fewer variants,

- reusable Outputs,

- and preview-first strategies.

11.84 Economy Quality Rule

Economy shall not lower the Quality Floor.

It may accept lower performance above the floor when the user has not requested premium optimisation.

11.85 Economy Reliability Rule

A very cheap Candidate with high expected failure or retry rate may be more expensive overall.

Economy scoring shall consider reliability.

11.86 Economy Latency Rule

Economy may accept slower execution when the deadline permits.

It shall not miss a Hard Deadline merely to save cost.

11.87 Economy Privacy Rule

Economy shall not route protected data to a cheaper but ineligible external Provider.

11.88 Economy Included-Credit Rule

Included credits may be preferred when:

- Capability and quality are sufficient,

- rights are valid,

- and the credits belong to the authorised Account.

11.89 Economy Local Rule

Local execution may receive a preference for zero marginal Provider charge.

The Router shall still consider:

- local quality,

- energy,

- hardware occupancy,

- and completion time.

11.90 Economy Optional-Work Rule

Economy may omit Optional Steps when the Completion Contract permits it.

The omission shall remain visible.

11.91 Economy Premium Escalation

Economy may escalate to a higher-cost Candidate only when:

- cheaper eligible paths failed,

- the Quality Floor remains unmet,

- remaining budget permits,

- and policy authorises the escalation.

11.92 Economy Fallback

Economy fallback should ordinarily proceed from lower expected total cost to higher cost while preserving eligibility.

11.93 Balanced Profile

Balanced optimises across:

- quality,

- expected total cost,

- latency,

- reliability,

- privacy,

- and operational fit.

Balanced is intended for ordinary production where no single dimension dominates.

11.94 Balanced Objective

The Balanced objective is:

Select the eligible Candidate with the strongest overall expected value for the current request.

11.95 Balanced Weighting

Balanced weighting shall be versioned.

A representative weighting may consider:

- quality,

- cost,

- reliability,

- latency,

- privacy,

- operational maturity,

- and Project evidence.

Exact weights belong to implementation policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.96 Balanced Quality Rule

Balanced should prefer resources with stronger evidence when the expected benefit justifies the cost difference.

11.97 Balanced Cost Rule

Balanced shall avoid unnecessary premium spending.

It may select a more expensive Candidate when expected:

- acceptance,

- reliability,

- or deadline performance

is materially better.

11.98 Balanced Latency Rule

Balanced should avoid both:

- slow inexpensive paths that threaten delivery,

- and fast premium paths with little added value.

11.99 Balanced Reliability Rule

Candidates with stable:

- API,

- callbacks,

- Account state,

- and historical success

may outrank less reliable alternatives.

11.100 Balanced Privacy Rule

Privacy may influence ranking even when several candidates are legally eligible.

A local or low-retention Candidate may receive a preference.

11.101 Balanced Project Evidence

Project-specific evidence may influence selection.

For Familje-Stunden, character consistency may receive greater weight.

For The Prompt, factual grounding may receive greater weight.

For GainPilot, economical short-form completion may receive greater weight.

11.102 Balanced Fallback
