Balanced fallback should preserve overall expected value rather than follow cost or quality alone.

11.103 Premium Profile

Premium optimises for the strongest justified expected quality within the approved budget and deadline.

Premium does not mean:

- highest price,

- unlimited variants,

- unlimited retries,

- or automatic use of the most famous Provider.

11.104 Premium Objective

The Premium objective is:

Select the eligible Candidate with the strongest expected ability to satisfy or exceed the Quality Target while remaining inside the approved envelope.

11.105 Premium Quality Rule

Premium shall prioritise:

- task-specific benchmark evidence,

- Project acceptance evidence,

- stronger Features,

- and lower quality-failure risk.

11.106 Premium Budget Rule

Premium remains bounded by:

- Step budget,

- Plan budget,

- retry budget,

- and maximum authorised cost.

11.107 Premium Reliability Rule

A premium resource shall not be selected merely for advertised quality when operational reliability is inadequate.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.108 Premium Latency Rule

Premium may accept additional latency when the deadline permits and expected quality improvement is meaningful.

11.109 Premium Candidate Count

Premium may permit:

- additional variants,

- candidate races,

- or independent evaluation

only when explicitly included in budget and policy.

11.110 Premium Evaluation

Premium production may require stronger evaluation to ensure the additional cost produced additional value.

11.111 Premium Fallback

Fallback should prefer the next strongest eligible quality path.

Material quality reduction shall be disclosed.

11.112 Premium for Master Assets

Premium routing may be appropriate for:

- canonical character Assets,

- master video,

- high-visibility campaign,

- critical architecture reasoning,

- or reusable commercial output.

11.113 Premium for Derivatives

Derivatives should not automatically inherit Premium.

A lower-cost profile may be used when the derivative Quality Contract permits it.

11.114 Private Profile

Private optimises for approved privacy, custody and placement.

The meaning of Private shall be resolved explicitly.

Private may require:

- Local Only execution,

- user-managed infrastructure,

- Tenant-controlled server,

- specified region,

- no Provider retention,

- no training use,

- or private contractual Provider path.

11.115 Private Objective

The Private objective is:

Select the most private eligible execution path satisfying the request’s required Capability and Quality Floor.

11.116 Private Is Not One Location

Private does not always mean local device.

Depending on policy, Private may include:

- local Runtime Node,

- home server,

- Tenant server,

- private cloud Deployment,

- enterprise zero-retention API,

- or Omnira-managed isolated environment.

11.117 Private Placement Definition

The request or Project policy shall define acceptable placement classes.

The Router shall not infer that any encrypted cloud service satisfies Private.

11.118 Private Data Rule

Private routing shall preserve the effective Data Classification.

Local Only data normally requires user- or Tenant-controlled execution.

11.119 Private Quality Rule

Private shall not pretend that a weak local resource satisfies a stronger Quality Floor.

When no private Candidate meets quality, the Router shall return:

- no route,

- human-assisted private path,

- or request for revised authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.120 Private Cost Rule

Private may select a more expensive resource when privacy is the primary profile objective.

The maximum budget remains binding.

11.121 Private External Fallback

External fallback is prohibited unless the Private profile definition explicitly includes eligible external private services.

11.122 Private Local-First Rule

Where several private candidates exist, the Router may prefer:

- user-controlled local,

- Tenant-controlled private,

- Omnira-managed isolated,

- and approved external private

according to Project policy.

11.123 Private Evidence Rule

Privacy eligibility shall rely on:

- Deployment,

- Account,

- region,

- retention,

- training use,

- and contract evidence.

Provider brand reputation is insufficient.

11.124 Private Logging Rule

Private execution may require reduced or local evidence storage.

Routing evidence shall still preserve enough information for governance.

11.125 Private Fallback

Fallback shall remain inside the accepted privacy class.

It shall not silently route protected data to ordinary external Providers.

11.126 Pinned Profile

Pinned requires or strongly prefers a specified resource.

The pin may target:

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Product,

- Model,

- Model Version,

- Deployment,

- Tool,

- Adapter,

- Runtime Node,

- or human-assisted procedure.

11.127 Pinned Objective

The Pinned objective is:

Use the specified resource when it remains eligible under all mandatory policy and request constraints.

11.128 Mandatory Pin

A Mandatory Pin prohibits substitution.

If the pinned resource is unavailable or ineligible, the result is:

- wait,

- fail,

- request amendment,

- or reapproval.

No silent fallback is permitted.

11.129 Preferred Pin

A Preferred Pin influences ranking but permits substitution under defined conditions.

11.130 Pin Reason

Every material Pin should preserve a reason such as:

- reproducibility,

- unique Capability,

- contractual requirement,

- existing Provider Asset,

- user choice,

- benchmark,

- or migration constraint.

11.131 Pin Scope

A Pin shall define whether it applies to:

- one request,

- one Step,

- one Workflow,

- one Production,

- one Project,

- or one time period.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.132 Pin Validity

Pins may expire after:

- Model update,

- benchmark review,

- Project milestone,

- Provider migration,

- or defined date.

11.133 Pinned Moving Alias

Pinning to a moving Provider alias shall preserve:

- drift risk,

- observed target,

- and reproducibility uncertainty.

11.134 Pinned Provider Account

A Pin may require one Account because of:

- credits,

- Assets,

- terms,

- or Project ownership.

The Account must still have valid budget and credentials.

11.135 Pinned Local Node

A request may require execution on one local Node.

Node availability and capacity must be validated.

11.136 Pinned Failure

When a mandatory Pin fails, the Router shall explain:

- unavailability,

- policy conflict,

- cost conflict,

- or Capability mismatch.

11.137 Pinned Fallback

Fallback exists only when the Pin explicitly permits it.

11.138 Profile Priority

Routing Profiles guide optimisation.

They do not outrank:

- security,

- privacy requirements,

- rights,

- authority,

- Quality Floor,

- deadline,

- or budget maximum.

11.139 Profile Conflict

A profile may conflict with request constraints.

Examples include:

- Economy with mandatory premium-only Feature,

- Private with external-only Capability,

- Pinned with denied Provider,

- Premium with insufficient budget.

The Router shall surface the conflict.

11.140 Profile Degradation

The Router shall not silently reinterpret one profile as another.

A proposed profile change requires:

- disclosure,

- approval where material,

- and new Selection Decision.

11.141 Resource-Origin Classes

Omnira shall recognise several resource-origin classes:

- local user-controlled,

- user-owned external,

- Project-owned external,

- Tenant-owned external,

- Omnira-managed,

- shared managed,

- human-assisted,

- and public or free service.

11.142 Local User-Controlled Resource

A Local User-Controlled Resource runs on infrastructure controlled by the user.

It may receive preference for:

- privacy,

- ownership,

- offline use,

- and low marginal charge.

11.143 User-Owned External Resource

A User-Owned External Resource uses the user’s Provider Account or subscription.

Use shall preserve:

- explicit permission,

- Project scope,

- and cost attribution.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.144 Project-Owned External Resource

A Project-Owned Resource should be preferred when:

- the work belongs to that Project,

- the Account terms are suitable,

- and sufficient capacity exists.

11.145 Tenant-Owned External Resource

A Tenant-owned Account may serve several Projects.

Routing shall preserve Project attribution and policy.

11.146 Omnira-Managed Resource

An Omnira-managed resource may be selected when:

- the user has allocated managed credits,

- the Provider is eligible,

- and the Project or Tenant permits it.

11.147 Shared Managed Resource

Shared resources require strong:

- Tenant isolation,

- Project attribution,

- quotas,

- and privacy controls.

11.148 Human-Assisted Resource

A human-assisted path may be selected when:

- no automation exists,

- quality is superior,

- Provider access is manual,

- or the user requires direct creative control.

Human effort and delay shall be included in scoring.

11.149 Free Public Resource

Free or unauthenticated resources may be considered only when:

- terms are acceptable,

- data is eligible,

- rights are adequate,

- reliability is sufficient,

- and evidence can be preserved.

11.150 Resource-Origin Preference

Project or user policy may define an order such as:

1. Local eligible capacity.

2. Included Project capacity.

3. User-owned Account.

4. Omnira-managed credits.

5. Paid external on-demand.

6. Human-assisted alternative.

This order is a preference, not a universal law.

11.151 Cost Ownership

Routing shall identify who bears the cost:

- user,

- Project,

- Tenant,

- Omnira,

- customer,

- or included subscription.

A cheaper resource for Omnira may be more expensive for the user.

The cost owner must remain explicit.

11.152 User-Owned Credit Protection

The Router shall not use user-owned credits as silent fallback when another Account is exhausted.

11.153 Project Budget Preference

A Project-owned budget should normally fund Project work.

Cross-Project budget use requires explicit authority.

11.154 Managed Credit Preference

Managed credits may be preferred when:

- they reduce user friction,

- remain transparent,

- and do not create hidden Provider bias.

11.155 Included Capacity Preference

Subscription-included capacity may be used before metered charges when it remains the best eligible path.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.156 Credit Expiry Preference

Credits nearing expiry may influence ranking only when:

- quality remains acceptable,

- use is authorised,

- and selection still serves user value.

Avoiding credit waste shall not override Project needs.

11.157 Local Capacity Cost

Local capacity may have:

- no direct Provider charge,

- but real compute, energy and opportunity cost.

The scoring model may use an internal estimate.

11.158 Total Expected Cost

Total Expected Cost should include:

- initial execution,

- likely retries,

- required evaluation,

- post-processing,

- human correction,

- transfer,

- storage,

- and likely fallback.

11.159 Cost Confidence

Cost estimates shall include confidence or uncertainty.

Opaque Provider pricing reduces routing certainty.

11.160 Cost Normalisation

Different Provider billing units shall be normalised into comparable expected cost.

The original units shall remain preserved.

11.161 Currency Normalisation

Where currencies differ, the Router may use a current exchange rate or budget conversion.

The conversion source and time shall be preserved.

11.162 Quality Evidence

Quality scoring shall rely on Capability-specific evidence.

Evidence may include:

- internal benchmark,

- external benchmark,

- Project acceptance rate,

- human review,

- retry rate,

- and recent operational outcomes.

11.163 Quality Confidence

Quality evidence shall include:

- scope,

- freshness,

- sample size,

- and confidence.

Sparse evidence shall not be represented as certainty.

11.164 Quality Floor

The Quality Floor is mandatory.

A candidate below the floor is ineligible.

11.165 Quality Target

The Quality Target influences ranking above the floor.

Premium routing may weight it strongly.

11.166 Expected Acceptance Probability

The Router may estimate the probability that a candidate will pass required evaluation.

This estimate should be evidence-based.

11.167 Correction Cost

A candidate with low initial price but frequent manual correction may have high total cost.

11.168 Project-Specific Quality

Project evidence may outweigh generic benchmarks when:

- the evidence is sufficient,

- current,

- and relevant.

Nova and Pling consistency tests are more relevant to Familje-Stunden video routing than generic cinematic benchmark scores.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.169 User Preference Evidence

A user may prefer a Provider’s output style.

Preference may influence ranking after mandatory quality.

11.170 Reliability Evidence

Reliability may include:

- success rate,

- Provider uptime,

- callback reliability,

- unknown-outcome rate,

- retry rate,

- and Account stability.

11.171 Reliability Floor

High-consequence work may require a minimum reliability level.

11.172 Provider Reliability

Provider-level reliability and Model-level quality shall remain distinct.

11.173 Account Reliability

One Provider Account may have:

- exhausted quota,

- authentication issues,

- or lower tier

while another Account remains healthy.

11.174 Connection Reliability

A Provider may be healthy while one MCP or API Connection is degraded.

11.175 Deployment Reliability

A Model Deployment may be unavailable while another Deployment remains eligible.

11.176 Local Reliability

Local reliability may depend on:

- Node power,

- hardware health,

- storage,

- Runtime,

- and network.

11.177 Human-Assisted Reliability

Human-assisted execution may have strong quality but uncertain availability and latency.

11.178 Latency Evidence

Latency shall consider:

- queue,

- first response,

- total execution,

- upload,

- download,

- evaluation,

- and human handoff.

11.179 Latency Floor

Interactive and real-time Capabilities may require a maximum latency.

11.180 Deadline Risk

The Router may score the probability of meeting the deadline.

A high-quality candidate with high queue risk may be unsuitable.

11.181 Queue-Aware Routing

Current Provider queue state may influence selection.

Queue evidence shall declare freshness.

11.182 Warm-Resource Preference

A loaded local Model or warm Deployment may outperform a theoretically faster cold resource.

11.183 Capacity-Aware Routing

The Router shall consider:

- concurrency,

- quota,

- rate limits,

- GPU capacity,

- and reserved workload.

11.184 Load Balancing

Several equivalent resources may be balanced to improve:

- throughput,

- resilience,

- and quota utilisation.

Load balancing shall preserve cost and Project policy.

11.185 Sticky Routing

Some workflows may prefer the same resource across related Steps for:

- style consistency,

- context continuity,

- or Provider Asset reuse.

Sticky routing shall be explicit.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.186 Non-Sticky Routing

Related Steps may use different resources when:

- Capabilities differ,

- cost improves,

- privacy differs,

- or quality evidence supports specialisation.

11.187 Session Affinity

Provider threads or real-time sessions may require affinity to one Deployment or Account.

Affinity shall not become permanent Agent identity.

11.188 Asset Affinity

A Provider-side character, voice or Project Asset may require routing to the Provider or Account holding it.

The lock-in implication shall remain visible.

11.189 Context Affinity

A persistent Provider context may reduce cost or improve continuity.

It shall not override Project isolation or memory governance.

11.190 Privacy Score

Eligible candidates may receive a privacy score based on:

- custody,

- region,

- retention,

- training use,

- contractual controls,

- and user control.

11.191 Privacy Score Limitation

Privacy scoring occurs only after mandatory privacy requirements.

A high privacy score cannot make an otherwise prohibited candidate eligible.

11.192 Rights Score

Candidates may differ in:

- commercial clarity,

- attribution burden,

- watermarking,

- and output ownership.

Rights may influence ranking after mandatory eligibility.

11.193 Operational Maturity Score

Production API or local production resources may outrank experimental integrations.

Maturity may include:

- conformance,

- monitoring,

- support,

- and recovery.

11.194 Automation Maturity Score

Fully governed automation may reduce human effort.

Human-assisted routes may still win when quality or unique Capability justifies them.

11.195 Portability Score

Candidates may be compared by:

- output export,

- open format,

- Asset portability,

- and lock-in.

Portability may influence long-term routing.

11.196 Strategic Dependency Score

A Candidate creating severe single-source dependency may receive a penalty where alternatives exist.

11.197 Energy and Resource Score

Local and managed compute may consider:

- energy,

- device battery,

- heat,

- and resource contention.

This may be important for mobile or edge routing.

11.198 Routing Score

The Routing Score is a calculated value used to rank eligible candidates.

It may combine:

- quality,

- cost,

- reliability,

- latency,

- privacy,

- rights,

- maturity,

- portability,

- and preference.

The score shall not include ineligible candidates.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.199 Score Component

Every material score component should have:

- value,

- weight,

- evidence,

- confidence,

- and version.

11.200 Score Normalisation

Different dimensions shall be normalised consistently.

Normalisation logic shall be versioned.

11.201 Profile Weights

Each Routing Profile shall define how dimensions are weighted.

Weights may be adjusted by:

- Capability,

- Project,

- consequence,

- and deadline

within governed limits.

11.202 Hard Constraint Exclusion

A candidate excluded by hard constraint shall not receive an overall score.

11.203 Score Explainability

The decision should explain the dominant reasons for selection.

Example:

Selected Candidate B because it met the mandatory multi-character Feature, had the strongest recent Familje-Stunden consistency score, remained within budget and had acceptable queue time.

11.204 Score Uncertainty

When evidence is weak, the Router should expose uncertainty.

It may choose:

- safer known candidate,

- bounded experiment,

- human review,

- or no route.

11.205 Deterministic Tie-Breaking

When candidates have equivalent scores, tie-breaking should be deterministic where practical.

Possible order:

1. Stronger privacy.

2. Lower expected total cost.

3. Higher reliability.

4. Lower latency.

5. Existing Project Account.

6. Greater portability.

7. Stable canonical identifier.

11.206 Randomised Tie-Breaking

Randomised selection may be used for:

- experiments,

- load distribution,

- or evidence gathering

only when explicitly governed.

11.207 Exploration

Exploration selects a less-proven eligible Candidate to gather evidence.

It shall use:

- low-risk tasks,

- bounded budget,

- explicit experiment policy,

- and mandatory evaluation.

11.208 Exploitation

Exploitation selects the strongest currently evidenced Candidate.

Ordinary production should usually favour exploitation.

11.209 Exploration Budget

Exploration shall consume a separately bounded budget or experiment allowance.

11.210 Production Exploration

High-consequence production should not be used as uncontrolled experimentation.

11.211 A/B Routing

A/B Routing may compare Candidates across equivalent tasks.

It shall define:

- population,

- metrics,

- duration,

- budget,

- and user-impact controls.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.212 Shadow Routing

Shadow Routing evaluates a Candidate without using its Output for the production result.

It may estimate:

- quality,

- latency,

- or compatibility.

Shadow execution still consumes resources and data.

It requires authority.

11.213 Offline Evaluation

Offline evaluation may compare historical Outputs without new Provider execution.

11.214 Routing Experiment

Every Routing Experiment shall have:

- experimentId,

- hypothesis,

- scope,

- candidates,

- metrics,

- data policy,

- budget,

- start,

- end,

- and approval.

11.215 Learned Routing

Learned Routing uses governed historical evidence to adjust candidate ranking.

It may improve:

- cost,

- quality,

- reliability,

- and Project fit.

11.216 Learned Routing Boundary

Learned Routing shall not change:

- mandatory policy,

- authority,

- Data Classification,

- rights,

- budget maximum,

- or Quality Floor.

11.217 Routing Learning Candidate

A Learning Candidate may state:

Provider Resource A performs better for Capability X under Project Y conditions.

It shall include:

- evidence,

- scope,

- confidence,

- validity,

- and review status.

11.218 Learning Admission

Routing learning shall enter production only after governed admission.

Raw outcome correlation shall not automatically rewrite routing policy.

11.219 Learning Scope

Learning may be:

- global,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Capability,

- Provider Account,

- Model Version,

- or Workflow-specific.

11.220 Learning Expiry

Routing learning shall expire or be reviewed after:

- Model change,

- Adapter change,

- Provider update,

- terms change,

- Project style change,

- or defined time.

11.221 Negative Learning

The Fabric may learn that a Candidate performs poorly under defined conditions.

Negative learning shall not become an unjustified global ban.

11.222 Confidence Decay

Confidence may decay as evidence becomes stale.

11.223 Model Drift

Model drift may invalidate routing evidence.

The Router shall reduce confidence or trigger revalidation.

11.224 Provider Drift

Provider changes in:

- queue,

- pricing,

- terms,

- or routing

may change suitability.

11.225 Project Drift

Project requirements may evolve.

Old routing preferences may no longer match current quality standards.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.226 Feedback Signal

Routing feedback may include:

- accepted Output,

- rejected Output,

- retry,

- user override,

- cost variance,

- latency,

- Incident,

- and publication outcome.

11.227 Explicit User Feedback

Explicit feedback should normally receive greater weight than inferred satisfaction.

It shall remain scoped.

11.228 Implicit Feedback

Implicit signals such as reuse or acceptance may help.

They shall not be overinterpreted.

11.229 Human Reviewer Feedback

Reviewer decisions may improve routing evidence.

Reviewer identity and criteria shall be preserved.

11.230 Business Outcome Feedback

Long-term outcomes such as engagement or conversion may inform routing only when causation is treated carefully.

11.231 Cost Feedback

Estimated versus actual cost shall calibrate future decisions.

11.232 Latency Feedback

Actual queue and completion time shall update routing evidence.

11.233 Reliability Feedback

Timeouts, unknown outcomes and Provider errors shall update reliability.

11.234 Routing Override

An authorised user may override the selected Candidate.

The override shall remain subject to mandatory eligibility.

11.235 Override Reason

Material overrides should preserve a reason such as:

- creative preference,

- known Provider strength,

- contractual obligation,

- or experiment.

11.236 Unsafe Override

The system shall reject an override that violates mandatory policy.

11.237 Override Learning

An override shall not automatically become a permanent preference.

Repeated accepted overrides may create a Learning Candidate.

11.238 User Preference

A user may express preferences for:

- local,

- Provider,

- Model,

- price,

- quality,

- privacy,

- or speed.

Preferences shall remain distinguishable from pins and policies.

11.239 Project Preference

A Project may define preferred:

- Providers,

- Models,

- Accounts,

- regions,

- and routing profiles.

11.240 Tenant Preference

Tenant preferences may optimise shared capacity and Provider relationships.

11.241 Preference Conflict

When preferences conflict, the Router should apply:

1. mandatory policy,

2. request-explicit preference,

3. Production Envelope,

4. Project preference,

5. Tenant preference,

6. user global preference,

7. platform default.

The effective source shall be recorded.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.242 Provider Bias Control

The Router shall not favour a Provider because:

- it was integrated first,

- its Adapter is easier,

- it has stronger marketing,

- or Omnira receives commercial benefit.

11.243 Commercial Conflict of Interest

A commercial relationship may include:

- commission,

- margin,

- affiliate payment,

- bundled credits,

- or strategic partnership.

The relationship shall be visible to governance.

11.244 Conflict Disclosure

Where a commercial relationship materially influences recommendation, it shall be disclosed.

11.245 User-Value Priority

Routing shall optimise user and Project value within policy.

Provider or Omnira financial benefit is subordinate.

11.246 Managed-Margin Routing

Future Omnira-managed credits may include margin.

Margin shall not permit lower-quality or more expensive routing when a better eligible path exists under the user’s chosen profile.

11.247 Neutral Candidate Evaluation

Candidates should be evaluated through consistent canonical dimensions.

11.248 Provider-Specific Exception

A Provider-specific routing exception requires:

- explicit reason,

- scope,

- validity,

- and review.

11.249 Routing Policy

Routing Policy defines mandatory and optimisation rules.

It may exist at:

- platform,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Capability,

- Provider,

- Workflow,

- Production,

- and request level.

11.250 Policy Composition

Effective Routing Policy is the composition of all applicable rules.

The most restrictive mandatory rule shall prevail.

11.251 Policy Conflict

Conflicting mandatory rules shall produce:

- no route,

- clarification,

- or governance escalation.

The Router shall not choose one silently.

11.252 Policy Rule

A Routing Policy Rule may include:

- ruleId,

- scope,

- condition,

- effect,

- priority,

- version,

- owner,

- effective period,

- and provenance.

11.253 Allow Rule

An Allow Rule permits a Candidate class when all other requirements are satisfied.

Allow does not override higher restrictions.

11.254 Deny Rule

A Deny Rule excludes a Candidate.

Deny rules shall propagate through fallback.

11.255 Require Rule

A Require Rule mandates:

- Provider class,

- region,

- privacy level,

- review,

- or another property.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.256 Prefer Rule

A Prefer Rule influences ranking.

11.257 Penalise Rule

A Penalise Rule lowers ranking without creating ineligibility.

11.258 Approval Rule

An Approval Rule marks a Candidate or profile transition as requiring approval.

11.259 Budget Rule

A Budget Rule may limit:

- cost,

- profile,

- Provider,

- Model tier,

- or retry.

11.260 Time Rule

A Time Rule may apply during:

- business hours,

- maintenance,

- campaign period,

- or scheduled window.

11.261 Environment Rule

An Environment Rule may prohibit production resources in development.

11.262 Data-Class Rule

A Data-Class Rule maps classifications to permitted placement and Provider types.

11.263 Capability Rule

A Capability Rule may require:

- evaluation,

- minimum Model class,

- or specific Provider maturity.

11.264 Child-Facing Rule

Child-facing media may require:

- approved Provider set,

- stronger visual evaluation,

- and human review.

11.265 Code Rule

Code execution may require:

- private Provider,

- no repository mutation,

- or separate credentials.

11.266 Publication Rule

Publication routing requires:

- approved target Account,

- publication Connection,

- idempotency,

- and verification.

11.267 Voice Rule

Voice routing may require:

- approved Voice Asset,

- consent,

- and cloning restriction.

11.268 Local-Only Rule

Local Only data shall route only to approved local or private resources.

11.269 Policy Version

Every Selection Decision shall reference relevant policy versions.

11.270 Policy Effective Time

Rules may have:

- future start,

- expiry,

- or temporary Incident window.

11.271 Emergency Routing Policy

During Incident response, emergency policy may:

- disable Provider,

- force local,

- prohibit publication,

- or require human approval.

Emergency rules shall be attributable and reviewed.

11.272 Routing Lifecycle

Routing lifecycle states may include:

- requested,

- evaluating,

- awaiting data,

- awaiting approval,

- candidate set ready,

- selected,

- revalidating,

- invalidated,

- superseded,

- failed,

- and archived.

11.273 Requested State

A Routing Request has been created.

11.274 Evaluating State

Candidates and policies are being evaluated.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.275 Awaiting Data State

Fresh operational or governance data is missing.

11.276 Awaiting Approval State

One or more Candidates require approval.

11.277 Candidate-Set-Ready State

Eligible candidates have been resolved and may be scored.

11.278 Selected State

A Selection Decision exists.

11.279 Revalidating State

The selected Candidate is being checked before execution.

11.280 Invalidated State

The decision can no longer be used.

11.281 Superseded State

A newer Selection Decision applies.

11.282 Failed State

No valid decision could be produced.

11.283 Archived State

The routing record is retained for history.

11.284 Pre-Execution Revalidation

Before Provider execution, the system shall revalidate:

- selected resource lifecycle,

- Account,

- Connection,

- Credential,

- health,

- quota,

- budget,

- authority,

- and policy.

11.285 Lightweight Revalidation

For low-risk immediate execution, revalidation may use cached state within a defined freshness window.

11.286 Full Revalidation

High-risk or delayed execution may require full current-state evaluation.

11.287 Selection Invalidation

A decision may invalidate when:

- Candidate disabled,

- Credential revoked,

- Account exhausted,

- price exceeds budget,

- policy changes,

- or deadline becomes infeasible.

11.288 Rerouting

Rerouting creates a new Selection Decision for the same Step.

It shall preserve:

- previous decision,

- invalidation reason,

- and cost impact.

11.289 Rerouting Without Replanning

Equivalent resource substitution inside the approved Plan may occur without replanning when all material boundaries remain unchanged.

11.290 Rerouting With Replanning

A different Capability path, privacy class, quality contract or side effect requires replanning.

11.291 Retry Routing

A retry may route to:

- the same Candidate,

- another Deployment,

- another Model,

- another Provider,

- or human-assisted path.

The Retry Policy determines permitted options.

11.292 Same-Candidate Retry

Same-Candidate retry may be suitable for:

- transient failure,

- stochastic variation,

- or rate limit after delay.

11.293 Same-Provider Fallback

The Router may change:

- Model,

- Deployment,

- Account,

- region,

- or Product

inside one Provider.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.294 Cross-Provider Fallback

Cross-Provider fallback changes:

- terms,

- processing location,

- Account,

- pricing,

- and operational evidence.

It requires full eligibility evaluation.

11.295 Local Fallback

External failure may route locally only when local quality and policy are sufficient.

11.296 External Fallback

Local failure may route externally only when classification and authority permit it.

11.297 Human-Assisted Fallback

Automation failure may route to a human-assisted path within budget and deadline.

11.298 No-Fallback Condition

Fallback may be prohibited by:

- mandatory Pin,

- Local Only policy,

- rights,

- user instruction,

- or unique Capability.

11.299 Fallback Chain

A Fallback Chain defines ordered eligible alternatives.

It shall include:

- trigger,

- maximum depth,

- approval conditions,

- and quality implications.

11.300 Fallback Depth

Fallback depth shall be bounded.

The system shall not cycle through unlimited resources.

11.301 Fallback Cost

Fallback cost counts against the approved budget.

11.302 Fallback Disclosure

Material fallback shall be disclosed when it affects:

- Provider,

- privacy,

- quality,

- cost,

- or user expectation.

11.303 Hedged Routing

Hedged Routing may launch a second Candidate after a delay to reduce tail latency.

It requires:

- budget,

- idempotency,

- cancellation,

- and duplicate handling.

11.304 Speculative Routing

Speculative Routing launches several Candidates before one is known to be necessary.

It shall not be used by default.

11.305 Candidate Race

A Candidate Race may be permitted for:

- premium creative selection,

- high-value reasoning,

- or latency-critical work.

It requires explicit limits.

11.306 Multi-Resource Voting

Several Models may produce or evaluate responses.

Voting shall be represented as a composite Plan, not hidden Router behaviour when it materially changes cost or evidence.

11.307 Router-Managed Micro-Fallback

The Router or Adapter may perform bounded micro-fallback only when:

- alternatives are semantically equivalent,

- cost remains inside the Step budget,

- policy permits,

- and evidence preserves the substitution.

Material Provider changes should remain visible.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.308 Provider Router

A Provider-managed router may choose an underlying Model.

The Fabric shall represent:

- routing opacity,

- declared candidates,

- quality evidence,

- and reproducibility limits.

11.309 Omnira Meta-Router

The Omnira Router may choose between Provider routers and fixed resources.

It shall not claim control over the Provider’s hidden internal choice.

11.310 Routing Explainability

Every meaningful Selection Decision should be explainable.

The explanation should answer:

- Which resource was selected?

- Why was it eligible?

- Which candidates were excluded?

- Which Routing Profile applied?

- What is the expected cost?

- What quality evidence mattered?

- What privacy and rights conditions apply?

- Which fallback is permitted?

11.311 Human-Readable Explanation

User-facing explanation should be concise and consequence-focused.

Example:

Balanced routing selected the Project-owned voice Provider because it supports approved Swedish narration, uses included credits, has stronger recent pronunciation scores and remains within the approved budget.

11.312 Machine-Readable Explanation

The canonical decision shall expose structured:

- rules,

- exclusions,

- scores,

- evidence,

- and versions.

11.313 Exclusion Explanation

Material candidate exclusions should identify the exact reason.

Examples include:

- Local Only conflict,

- commercial rights unknown,

- insufficient quality evidence,

- expired Credential,

- or cost above limit.

11.314 Profile Explanation

The system should explain what the selected profile optimised.

Economy:

Lowest expected total eligible cost.

Balanced:

Best overall expected value.

Premium:

Strongest expected quality within budget.

Private:

Strongest eligible privacy and placement.

Pinned:

Specified resource subject to mandatory policy.

11.315 Uncertainty Explanation

When routing evidence is weak, the decision should state uncertainty.

11.316 Approval Explanation

When approval is required, the system should explain:

- what changes,

- why it matters,

- and the maximum consequence.

11.317 Routing Receipt

A Routing Receipt may provide a durable summary containing:

- request,

- Plan Step,

- profile,

- candidates,

- exclusions,

- selected Candidate,

- expected cost,

- fallback,

- and decision provenance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.318 Routing Provenance

Routing provenance should include:

- Router version,

- profile version,

- policy versions,

- Registry snapshots,

- pricing sources,

- health observations,

- quality evidence,

- and learning references.

11.319 Router Version

The Selection Decision shall identify the Router implementation version.

11.320 Scoring Version

Material changes to score calculation require a new scoring version.

11.321 Policy Snapshot

The decision should preserve the policy state used.

11.322 Registry Snapshot

The decision should preserve the relevant Registry versions or identifiers.

11.323 Health Snapshot

Current health observations used in selection should be referenced.

11.324 Pricing Snapshot

Expected cost should reference pricing evidence.

11.325 Quality Snapshot

Quality scoring should reference benchmark and operational evidence.

11.326 Routing Audit

Routing audit should allow reconstruction of:

- candidates,

- rules,

- scores,

- decision,

- and later substitution.

11.327 Routing Privacy

Routing evidence may contain sensitive:

- Account,

- Project,

- Provider,

- and cost information.

Access shall be scoped.

11.328 Redacted Routing View

A redacted view may hide:

- exact Account,

- protected Provider relationship,

- confidential Inputs,

- or internal scoring detail.

The canonical record remains unchanged.

11.329 Routing Metrics

Routing metrics may include:

- profile usage,

- selection distribution,

- no-route rate,

- fallback rate,

- override rate,

- estimated versus actual cost,

- quality acceptance,

- latency,

- and Project outcomes.

11.330 Profile Usage Metric

The system may measure which profiles are used by:

- Project,

- Capability,

- and user.

11.331 Candidate Exclusion Metric

Frequent exclusions may reveal:

- missing rights,

- stale credentials,

- Provider gaps,

- or overly restrictive policy.

11.332 No-Route Metric

No-route frequency may identify Capability or integration gaps.

11.333 Fallback Metric

High fallback rate may indicate unreliable primary selection.

11.334 Override Metric

Frequent human overrides may indicate poor preferences or scoring.

11.335 Cost Variance Metric

Estimated and confirmed cost differences should calibrate routing.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.336 Quality Acceptance Metric

Acceptance should be measured by:

- Capability,

- Model,

- Provider,

- Project,

- and profile.

11.337 Latency Variance Metric

Actual completion time should calibrate future choices.

11.338 Routing Regret

Routing Regret represents the estimated difference between the selected Candidate’s result and a better eligible alternative.

It may be measured only when comparable evidence exists.

11.339 Routing Efficiency

Efficiency may combine:

- accepted quality,

- total cost,

- latency,

- and human effort.

11.340 Profile Effectiveness

Profile effectiveness should be evaluated against its intended objective.

Economy should minimise completed cost.

Premium should improve quality.

Private should preserve approved custody.

Pinned should honour the selected resource.

11.341 Routing Incident

A Routing Incident may involve:

- ineligible Provider selection,

- wrong Project Account,

- privacy violation,

- cost overrun,

- hidden fallback,

- wrong Model,

- or commercial bias.

11.342 Selection Incident

A Selection Incident occurs when the decision itself was invalid.

11.343 Execution Incident

An execution may fail despite a valid selection.

The distinction shall remain explicit.

11.344 Wrong-Account Incident

Using the wrong Provider Account is a routing or execution-control Incident even if the output quality is correct.

11.345 Wrong-Project Incident

Using another Project’s Account, Asset or local resource is a severe isolation defect.

11.346 Privacy Routing Incident

Protected data sent to an ineligible Provider is a privacy Incident.

11.347 Rights Routing Incident

Selecting a Provider with incompatible commercial terms is a rights Incident.

11.348 Budget Routing Incident

Selecting a Candidate whose expected cost exceeds approved limits is a budget Incident.

11.349 Hidden-Fallback Incident

Substituting a materially different Provider or privacy class without evidence is an Incident.

11.350 Routing Incident Containment

Containment may include:

- disable Candidate,

- block Provider,

- freeze profile,

- require manual routing,

- revoke Connection,

- or pause affected Plans.

11.351 Routing Incident Recovery

Recovery should include:

- corrected policy,

- evidence review,

- affected Executions,

- cost and privacy impact,

- tests,

- and controlled reactivation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.352 Routing Policy Rollback

A faulty policy or scoring update may require rollback.

Historical Selection Decisions shall remain linked to the faulty version.

11.353 Routing Canary

New routing logic may be tested on:

- low-risk requests,

- limited Projects,

- or shadow evaluation.

Canary use shall be bounded.

11.354 Routing Feature Flag

Routing features may be enabled by:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Capability,

- or environment.

Flags shall not bypass canonical policy.

11.355 Routing Cache

Candidate and eligibility data may be cached.

Caches shall preserve:

- source,

- version,

- freshness,

- and invalidation.

11.356 Eligibility Cache

Eligibility caching may be safe only when:

- policy,

- Account,

- credential,

- and resource state remain sufficiently stable.

11.357 Health Cache

Health data may expire quickly.

Stale health shall not be represented as current.

11.358 Pricing Cache

Pricing cache shall include effective date and uncertainty.

11.359 Quality Cache

Benchmark evidence may remain valid longer but shall still be Version-specific.

11.360 Routing Consistency

The system shall define consistency requirements for:

- Provider disable,

- credential revocation,

- budget exhaustion,

- and policy changes.

Security-critical changes should propagate rapidly.

11.361 Routing Availability

The Router itself is a critical Fabric service.

Its failure must not cause Agents to bypass routing.

11.362 Router Failure

When the Router is unavailable, permitted behaviour may include:

- use a recently valid pinned Decision,

- pause execution,

- or use a narrowly approved emergency route.

Direct Provider calls are not the safe default.

11.363 Emergency Static Route

A critical Workflow may have a pre-approved emergency route.

It shall remain:

- bounded,

- versioned,

- monitored,

- and policy-compliant.

11.364 Router Recovery

Recovery shall preserve pending Routing Requests and avoid duplicate execution.

11.365 Routing Idempotency

Repeated submission of the same Routing Request Version should return the same decision when relevant state has not materially changed.

Dynamic state may legitimately produce a new decision.

11.366 Routing Correlation

Routing records shall preserve:

- requestId,

- planId,

- stepId,

- executionId where created,

- correlationId,

- and causationId.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.367 Routing Event

Material events may include:

- RoutingRequested,

- CandidatesGenerated,

- CandidateExcluded,

- ApprovalRequired,

- ResourceSelected,

- SelectionInvalidated,

- ReroutingRequested,

- FallbackSelected,

- and NoRouteFound.

11.368 Routing Event Deduplication

Consumers shall process routing events idempotently.

11.369 Routing Event Ordering

Late events shall not overwrite newer decisions.

11.370 Routing Access Control

Permissions may include:

- request routing,

- inspect decision,

- view cost,

- override,

- modify policy,

- modify profile,

- and administer scoring.

11.371 Routing Request Permission

A Principal may request routing only for authorised:

- Project,

- Capability,

- and Plan Step.

11.372 Routing View Permission

Users may receive a simplified decision view.

Operators may receive Account and health details.

Developers may inspect technical scoring.

Access shall remain scoped.

11.373 Routing Override Permission

Only authorised Principals may override selection.

11.374 Routing Policy Administration

Policy modification requires privileged governance authority.

11.375 Scoring Administration

Changing scoring logic is a material platform action.

11.376 Profile Administration

Creating or changing canonical profiles requires architecture governance.

11.377 Project Routing Administration

Project owners may configure preferences and allowed resources within Tenant policy.

11.378 Tenant Routing Administration

Tenant administrators may define shared Provider and privacy rules.

11.379 Global Routing Administration

Platform-global rules shall be narrowly controlled.

11.380 Routing and Atlas

Atlas may:

- express Capability requirements,

- request routing,

- explain trade-offs,

- and present user choices.

Atlas shall not hard-code Provider names or retrieve credentials.

11.381 Routing and Executive Intelligence

Executive Intelligence may influence:

- strategic importance,

- budget posture,

- and Quality Target.

It shall not bypass eligibility.

11.382 Routing and Managers

Managers may define Project preferences and Production profiles within authority.

11.383 Routing and Specialist Agents

Agents receive the selected execution path indirectly through the Fabric.

They should not select unrestricted Providers independently.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.384 Routing and Capability Registry

The Capability Registry defines required operation and Features.

11.385 Routing and Model Registry

The Model Registry supplies:

- Versions,

- Capability support,

- limits,

- quality evidence,

- and Deployments.

11.386 Routing and Provider Registry

The Provider Registry supplies:

- Provider,

- Account,

- Connection,

- terms,

- trust,

- health,

- and integration maturity.

11.387 Routing and Credential Service

Routing checks credential status through references.

It does not retrieve raw secrets.

11.388 Routing and Planning

Planning defines resource requirements and permitted fallback.

Routing selects the current resource.

11.389 Routing and Execution

Execution uses the selected Candidate after revalidation.

11.390 Routing and Cost System

The cost system supplies:

- pricing,

- budget,

- credits,

- reservations,

- and confirmed cost.

11.391 Routing and Policy Engine

The Policy Engine evaluates mandatory rules.

The Router may orchestrate policy calls but shall not replace policy governance.

11.392 Routing and Quality System

The Quality System supplies benchmark and acceptance evidence.

11.393 Routing and Memory

Governed memory may supply routing preferences and accepted learning.

Raw execution logs do not become routing policy automatically.

11.394 Routing and Intelligence Graph

The Graph may represent:

- candidate,

- selected resource,

- exclusion,

- fallback,

- quality evidence,

- and Project outcome.

The canonical routing record remains authoritative.

11.395 Routing and Observability

Observability shall expose:

- selection latency,

- candidate count,

- exclusions,

- score,

- profile,

- fallback,

- and current validity.

11.396 Routing and Incident Response

Incident response may override ordinary optimisation through emergency mandatory policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric

11.399 Applied Example — Nova and Pling Master Versus Derivatives
11.400 Applied Example — The Prompt Research Routing
text:
11.397 Applied Example — Nova and Pling Scene Routing

A Familje-Stunden scene requires:

Capability

video.image_to_video.

Mandatory requirements

- approved Nova and Pling references,

- multi-character support,

- commercial-use eligibility,

- child-facing review,

- 16:9 output,

- bounded cost,

- and asynchronous job evidence.

Candidate A

Low-cost Provider Model.

Strengths:

- low price,

- short queue.

Weaknesses:

- weak multi-character evidence.

Candidate B

Premium Provider Model.

Strengths:

- strongest recent character-consistency evidence,

- reliable reference support.

Weaknesses:

- higher cost.

Candidate C

Provider-managed router.

Strengths:

- moderate cost,

- broad video support.

Weaknesses:

- exact Model unknown,

- weaker reproducibility.

Candidate D

Local video Model.

Strengths:

- private,

- no direct Provider charge.

Weaknesses:

- fails the character-consistency Quality Floor.

Eligibility result:

- Candidate A may be ineligible for scenes containing both Nova and Pling.

- Candidate B is eligible.

- Candidate C may be conditionally eligible for preview.

- Candidate D is ineligible for final character-critical production.

Balanced routing may select Candidate B for character-critical scenes.

Economy routing may select Candidate C for low-risk preview scenes.

Premium routing may select Candidate B immediately.

Private routing may return no route if no private Candidate meets quality.

Pinned routing uses the specified Candidate only when eligible.

11.398 Applied Example — Nova Background Scene

A scene containing only:

- background motion,

- no visible character,

- and no dialogue

may use an economical video resource.

The Quality Contract differs from a close-up character scene.

Routing shall remain Step-specific rather than applying one Provider to the entire episode.

11.399 Applied Example — Nova and Pling Master Versus Derivatives

The master episode may use:

- Balanced or Premium routing.

Short derivatives may use:

- Economy routing,

- local format conversion,

- and lower-cost caption generation.

Derivative routing shall preserve master provenance.

11.400 Applied Example — The Prompt Research Routing

A The Prompt research Step requires:

- current public sources,

- source citations,

- recency,

- and factual grounding.

Candidate A

Fast low-cost language Model without current search.

Candidate B

Search-grounded reasoning Provider.

Candidate C

Local Model with no current internet access.

Candidate D

External search Tool plus separate reasoning Model.

Candidate A and C may be ineligible for the complete current-research Capability.

Candidate B and D may remain eligible.

Balanced routing may choose D when it offers stronger source control and lower total cost.

Premium routing may choose B or D based on factual benchmark evidence.

The visual avatar Provider is not considered for research routing.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 11.401 Applied Example — The Prompt Script Draft
text:
11.401 Applied Example — The Prompt Script Draft

After verified research exists, a script-drafting Step may use a lower-cost text Model.

The research Capability and script Capability have different routing requirements.

11.402 Applied Example — GainPilot Reel Routing

A GainPilot reel may require:

- short Swedish script,

- one still image,

- narration,

- captions,

- and local composition.

Economy routing may choose:

- local text Model,

- low-cost image Provider,

- included voice credits,

- and local media tools.

Premium video generation would be unnecessary when motion graphics satisfy the Output Contract.

11.403 Applied Example — Omnira Code Analysis

A read-only code audit may require:

- large repository context,

- TypeScript reasoning,

- private code handling,

- and architecture evidence.

A local Model may be eligible for preliminary search.

A stronger external Model may be eligible only when Project policy permits code processing.

A coding Provider with repository-write tools shall still use a read-only Connection for this Step.

11.404 Applied Example — Confidential Local Analysis

A request has:

- Local Only classification,

- Private profile,

- local document Inputs,

- and no external fallback.

The Router considers only:

- eligible local Models,

- local Tools,

- and user-controlled Runtime Nodes.

When no local Model meets the Quality Floor, the result is No Route.

The system may propose:

- weaker draft with disclosure,

- human local review,

- or revised data authority.

It shall not route externally.

11.405 Applied Example — User-Owned OpenArt Credits

A user-owned OpenArt Account has remaining credits.

A Familje-Stunden request may use them only when:

- the user authorised that Account for the Project,

- the selected Capability is eligible,

- cost is visible,

- and no Project-owned or managed policy conflicts.

The existence of credits does not create silent preference.

11.406 Applied Example — Omnira-Managed Credits

A future Omnira-managed Provider Account may offer lower effective cost.

Balanced routing may select it when:

- quality is equivalent,

- Tenant isolation is proven,

- the cost is transparent,

- and no user-owned preference is violated.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 11.409 Applied Example — Local Versus External Embeddings
text:
11.407 Applied Example — Pinned Voice

A Familje-Stunden narration may pin one approved Voice Asset and Provider Account for continuity.

The Pin applies to:

- voice identity,

- Provider Account,

- and synthesis Capability.

The speech Model may still change if the Provider exposes a compatible approved Model and the Pin does not require an exact Version.

11.408 Applied Example — Human-Assisted OpenArt Director

Before a full production integration exists, the Router may consider:

Candidate

Human-assisted OpenArt Director workflow.

The Candidate may score:

- high creative quality,

- moderate or high cost,

- slower latency,

- lower automation maturity,

- strong user control.

It may be eligible for Premium or Pinned production.

It shall not be represented as autonomous API execution.

11.409 Applied Example — Local Versus External Embeddings

A retrieval workflow may compare:

- local multilingual embedding Model,

- external premium embedding API,

- and existing Project index compatibility.

If the Project index already uses the local Model, migration cost and vector compatibility may make local routing preferable even when an external benchmark is stronger.

11.410 Anti-Pattern — Provider First

The Fabric shall not begin routing with:

Which Provider should we use?

It shall begin with:

Which candidates satisfy the Capability and mandatory constraints?

11.411 Anti-Pattern — Cheapest Unit Price

The lowest per-token or per-generation price may produce higher total cost through:

- retries,

- correction,

- and failure.

11.412 Anti-Pattern — Most Expensive Means Premium

Premium means strongest justified expected quality.

It does not mean selecting the highest price.

11.413 Anti-Pattern — Local Always First

Local-first may be a preference.

It shall not override quality or deadline unless privacy requires local execution.

11.414 Anti-Pattern — Cloud Always Better

External Providers do not automatically outperform local resources for every Capability.

11.415 Anti-Pattern — Free Means Eligible

A free resource may have:

- weak rights,

- poor reliability,

- data-training use,

- or no commercial permission.

11.416 Anti-Pattern — Connected Means Candidate

A connected Provider Account remains ineligible when:

- policy,

- Capability,

- quality,

- rights,

- or budget

do not match.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 11.423 Anti-Pattern — Personal Credits as Platform Pool
11.431 Anti-Pattern — Stale Benchmark as Current Truth
text:
11.417 Anti-Pattern — Healthy Means Eligible

Provider health does not override governance.

11.418 Anti-Pattern — One Score Overrides Policy

Scoring shall never compensate for a mandatory violation.

11.419 Anti-Pattern — One Universal Score

Scores shall remain Capability- and context-specific.

11.420 Anti-Pattern — Global Best Model List

No leaderboard shall replace request-specific routing.

11.421 Anti-Pattern — Hidden Provider Preference

Provider preferences shall be visible and attributable.

11.422 Anti-Pattern — Commercial Bias

Provider margin, affiliate income or partnership shall not silently influence selection.

11.423 Anti-Pattern — Personal Credits as Platform Pool

User-owned credits shall not become silent shared capacity.

11.424 Anti-Pattern — Project Account Mixing

One Project’s Provider Account shall not be used for another Project by convenience.

11.425 Anti-Pattern — Profile Lowers Quality Floor

Economy shall not redefine acceptable quality.

11.426 Anti-Pattern — Private Equals Encrypted Cloud

Private must be defined through actual custody, region, retention and control.

11.427 Anti-Pattern — Pinned Overrides Security

A Pin cannot force use of a compromised, prohibited or unauthorised resource.

11.428 Anti-Pattern — Silent Profile Change

The Router shall not switch from Economy to Premium or Private to ordinary external routing without evidence and approval where material.

11.429 Anti-Pattern — Stale Price as Current

Pricing evidence shall declare freshness.

11.430 Anti-Pattern — Stale Health as Current

Health evidence shall declare freshness.

11.431 Anti-Pattern — Stale Benchmark as Current Truth

Model or Provider updates may invalidate quality evidence.

11.432 Anti-Pattern — Unverified Model Family Inheritance

Capability and quality evidence shall not be inherited automatically across Model Versions.

11.433 Anti-Pattern — Unknown Treated as Good

Unknown privacy, rights or quality shall not receive favourable defaults.

11.434 Anti-Pattern — Retry Reuses Ineligible Candidate

Every retry and fallback shall revalidate eligibility.

11.435 Anti-Pattern — Fallback Escapes Denylist

Denied Providers remain denied through fallback.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 11.446 Anti-Pattern — No-Route Hidden as Generic Failure
text:
11.436 Anti-Pattern — Router Creates Capability Alternative

A materially different Capability path requires Plan authority.

11.437 Anti-Pattern — Human-Assisted Hidden in Score

Human effort, delay and manual risk shall remain visible.

11.438 Anti-Pattern — Routing Decision Without Account

External execution shall identify the exact Provider Account.

11.439 Anti-Pattern — Routing Decision Without Connection

The selected operational path shall identify the approved Connection.

11.440 Anti-Pattern — Routing Decision Contains Secret

Routing references credentials indirectly.

It never contains raw secrets.

11.441 Anti-Pattern — Router Owns Provider Credentials

The Router shall not retrieve or store raw Provider secrets.

11.442 Anti-Pattern — Override Becomes Permanent Learning

One user override shall not silently rewrite Project policy.

11.443 Anti-Pattern — Outcome Correlation Equals Causation

Business performance shall not be attributed solely to one Provider without sufficient evidence.

11.444 Anti-Pattern — Exploration on High-Risk Production

Experiments shall not use consequential work without explicit approval.

11.445 Anti-Pattern — Candidate Race by Default

Parallel premium generation can waste budget.

It requires explicit strategy.

11.446 Anti-Pattern — No-Route Hidden as Generic Failure

The system shall explain the blocking constraints.

11.447 Anti-Pattern — Router Bypass During Outage

Router failure shall not cause direct uncontrolled Provider calls.

11.448 Anti-Pattern — Routing Cache Ignores Revocation

Credential revocation and Provider suspension must invalidate cached eligibility.

11.449 Anti-Pattern — Selection History Rewritten

New routing decisions shall supersede, not overwrite, prior decisions.

11.450 Stage 1 Routing Objective

Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy Router capable of selecting among representative local and external resources.

The objective is not to create a fully autonomous global optimisation engine.

Stage 1 shall prove:

- mandatory eligibility,

- canonical Routing Profiles,

- candidate generation,

- deterministic exclusion,

- bounded scoring,

- Provider Account selection,

- Model or Tool selection,

- cost awareness,

- fallback,

- explanation,

- and historical evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.451 Stage 1 Profiles

Stage 1 shall support:

- Economy,

- Balanced,

- Premium,

- Private,

- and Pinned.

Each shall have explicit versioned behaviour.

11.452 Stage 1 Default Profile

Balanced should be the default unless Project or request policy specifies another profile.

11.453 Stage 1 Candidate Types

Stage 1 should support candidates using:

- local Model Deployment,

- external text Provider,

- external image Provider,

- external voice Provider,

- multimodal or video Provider,

- local Tool,

- and human-assisted process.

11.454 Stage 1 Routing Request Object

The Stage 1 Routing Request should include:

- routingRequestId,

- Plan Version,

- Step ID,

- Capability,

- required Features,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- profile,

- Data Classification,

- Authority Envelope,

- Quality Floor,

- Budget,

- deadline,

- Provider restrictions,

- Model restrictions,

- and placement.

11.455 Stage 1 Candidate Object

The Stage 1 Candidate should include:

- candidateId,

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Connection,

- Model Version or Tool,

- Deployment or Runtime Node,

- Adapter,

- Capability support,

- cost estimate,

- quality evidence,

- latency estimate,

- health,

- and eligibility state.

11.456 Stage 1 Selection Decision Object

The Stage 1 Selection Decision should include:

- selectionDecisionId,

- selected Candidate,

- Routing Profile,

- excluded Candidates,

- score summary,

- expected cost,

- fallback candidates,

- policy versions,

- Router version,

- and decision time.

11.457 Stage 1 Mandatory Eligibility Checks

Stage 1 shall check at minimum:

- Capability support,

- mandatory Features,

- Tenant and Project scope,

- Environment,

- Data Classification,

- Provider and Model lifecycle,

- Provider Account,

- Connection,

- Credential status,

- rights,

- authority,

- Quality Floor,

- budget,

- health,

- and deadline.

11.458 Stage 1 Economy Behaviour

Stage 1 Economy should:

- choose the lowest expected eligible completed cost,

- prefer included or local capacity where suitable,

- preserve Quality Floor,

- and use bounded escalation.

11.459 Stage 1 Balanced Behaviour

Stage 1 Balanced should compare:

- quality,

- cost,

- reliability,

- latency,

- and privacy

through a simple versioned scoring model.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.460 Stage 1 Premium Behaviour

Stage 1 Premium should prioritise:

- strongest task-specific quality evidence,

- reliable Feature support,

- and lower expected quality-failure risk

within budget.

11.461 Stage 1 Private Behaviour

Stage 1 Private should require an explicit allowed placement class.

It shall not route externally unless that class permits the external Candidate.

11.462 Stage 1 Pinned Behaviour

Stage 1 Pinned should support:

- mandatory Provider pin,

- preferred Provider pin,

- mandatory Model pin,

- preferred Model pin,

- and no-fallback option.

11.463 Stage 1 Local Routing

Stage 1 shall support routing to at least one local text or reasoning Deployment.

Local eligibility shall include:

- Node,

- Runtime,

- installed Model,

- health,

- Capability,

- and quality.

11.464 Stage 1 External Text Routing

Stage 1 shall support at least two external text or reasoning Provider paths to prove:

- selection,

- fallback,

- and independence.

11.465 Stage 1 Voice Routing

Stage 1 should support one voice Provider path with:

- approved Voice Asset,

- consent-aware policy,

- Account,

- credits,

- and pronunciation quality evidence.

11.466 Stage 1 Image Routing

Stage 1 should support:

- primary image Provider,

- alternative image Provider or path,

- and Project quality evidence.

11.467 Stage 1 Video Routing

Stage 1 may support:

- one primary multimodal or video Provider,

- one human-assisted alternative,

- and truthful routed-resource identity.

11.468 Stage 1 Human-Assisted Routing

The Router shall be able to return a human-assisted Candidate when no production automation exists.

11.469 Stage 1 Cost Input

Stage 1 cost may use:

- exact pricing,

- estimated pricing,

- Provider credits,

- subscription inclusion,

- and local zero-marginal-charge classification.

Uncertainty shall remain visible.

11.470 Stage 1 Quality Input

Stage 1 quality may use:

- manual test results,

- small internal benchmarks,

- Project acceptance,

- and known limitations.

The system shall not require a perfect benchmark platform before beginning.

11.471 Stage 1 Reliability Input

Stage 1 reliability should include:

- current health,

- recent success,

- rate-limit state,

- and authentication state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.472 Stage 1 Routing API

Stage 1 should support:

- create Routing Request,

- generate Candidates,

- evaluate eligibility,

- score Candidates,

- return Selection Decision,

- revalidate,

- reroute,

- inspect explanation,

- and retrieve Routing Receipt.

11.473 Stage 1 Policy API

Stage 1 should support querying effective:

- Provider allowlist,

- Provider denylist,

- Model restrictions,

- placement,

- data-class eligibility,

- and profile default.

11.474 Stage 1 Explainability

Every Stage 1 Selection Decision should provide a concise human-readable explanation.

11.475 Stage 1 No-Route Response

No-route response should include:

- blocking constraints,

- unavailable Candidates,

- and safe alternatives.

11.476 Stage 1 Fallback

Stage 1 should support:

- same Provider alternative,

- second external text Provider,

- eligible local fallback,

- and human-assisted fallback.

11.477 Stage 1 Rerouting

Stage 1 shall reroute after:

- Provider outage,

- Account exhaustion,

- credential failure,

- or resource retirement.

11.478 Stage 1 Routing Acceptance Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Ineligible Candidate is excluded before scoring.

2. Economy does not lower Quality Floor.

3. Balanced uses versioned score components.

4. Premium remains inside budget.

5. Private excludes unapproved external resources.

6. Mandatory Pin blocks silent substitution.

7. Preferred Pin permits governed fallback.

8. Provider denylist propagates through fallback.

9. Model retirement removes Candidate from new routing.

10. Provider Account scope is enforced.

11. Environment mismatch blocks selection.

12. Connection status is validated.

13. Credential expiry blocks selection.

14. Data Classification is enforced.

15. Commercial-rights requirement is enforced.

16. Consent requirement is enforced.

17. Deadline feasibility affects eligibility.

18. Health affects availability but not identity.

19. Exact selected Account is recorded.

20. Routing Decision references the Plan Step.

11.479 Stage 1 Economy Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Lowest unit price does not win when retry cost is higher.

2. Included credits are preferred only when eligible.

3. Local resource wins when quality and deadline are sufficient.

4. Optional variants may be omitted when permitted.

5. Economy does not use prohibited free service.

6. Economy escalation remains bounded.

7. Economy stops before budget overrun.

8. Economy preserves rights.

9. Economy preserves privacy.

10. Economy explanation identifies total expected cost.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.480 Stage 1 Balanced Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Higher-quality Candidate may win despite moderate cost increase.

2. Unreliable cheap Candidate receives lower ranking.

3. Slow Candidate loses when deadline risk is high.

4. Stronger privacy may improve ranking.

5. Project-specific quality evidence influences score.

6. Score weights are versioned.

7. Tie-breaking is deterministic.

8. Ineligible Candidate never wins through score.

9. Unknown evidence lowers confidence.

10. Decision explanation identifies dominant dimensions.

11.481 Stage 1 Premium Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Highest price does not automatically win.

2. Strongest task-specific quality evidence receives priority.

3. Premium remains inside maximum budget.

4. Premium may permit additional evaluation when approved.

5. Premium Master Asset routing does not force premium derivatives.

6. Unreliable premium Provider may lose.

7. Premium fallback discloses quality reduction.

8. Candidate race requires explicit policy.

9. Premium cannot bypass rights.

10. Premium cannot bypass deadline.

11.482 Stage 1 Private Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Private profile resolves allowed placement.

2. Local Only request considers only local or approved private resources.

3. Unknown Provider retention blocks protected routing.

4. Private does not claim a weak Model meets Quality Floor.

5. No private Candidate returns No Route.

6. External fallback requires explicit permission.

7. Private evidence includes Deployment and Account.

8. Private logs remain appropriately restricted.

9. Private routing still records cost.

10. Private profile remains distinct from Provider preference.

11.483 Stage 1 Pinned Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Mandatory Provider Pin is enforced.

2. Mandatory Model Version Pin is enforced.

3. Preferred Pin may fall back.

4. Pinned Candidate remains subject to security.

5. Pinned Candidate remains subject to budget.

6. Pinned Candidate remains subject to rights.

7. Pinned moving alias preserves uncertainty.

8. Pin scope and expiry are enforced.

9. No-fallback Pin returns No Route when unavailable.

10. Pin reason is preserved.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.484 Stage 1 Fallback Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Fallback Candidate is fully revalidated.

2. Same-Provider fallback records Model change.

3. Cross-Provider fallback records Provider and Account change.

4. Fallback stays inside budget.

5. Fallback preserves Quality Floor.

6. Fallback preserves Data Classification.

7. Fallback preserves rights.

8. Fallback depth is bounded.

9. Human-assisted fallback is labelled.

10. Hidden fallback is impossible.

11.485 Stage 1 Security Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Router never retrieves raw Credential.

2. Compromised Credential excludes related Candidate.

3. Suspended Provider excludes all affected Candidates.

4. Project Account cannot route another Project.

5. Tenant-private resource is invisible to other Tenants.

6. Development Connection cannot serve production.

7. Administrative Connection is excluded from ordinary generation.

8. Callback Incident can invalidate a Candidate.

9. Cached eligibility invalidates after revocation.

10. Router Service Principal cannot alter Provider terms.

11.486 Stage 1 Privacy Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Data Classification is evaluated before scoring.

2. Unknown processing region fails closed.

3. No-training requirement is enforced.

4. Retention requirement is enforced.

5. Confidential data excludes unapproved Provider Account.

6. Local preprocessing does not lower classification automatically.

7. Routing explanation does not expose protected Input.

8. Project-private Candidate remains scoped.

9. Provider preference cannot override privacy.

10. Fallback cannot weaken privacy.

11.487 Stage 1 Cost Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Cost estimate references pricing version.

2. Credit balance declares freshness.

3. Personal credits require explicit permission.

4. Shared managed credits preserve Project attribution.

5. Local cost is not falsely represented as universally free.

6. Retry cost is included.

7. Candidate race cost is reserved before launch.

8. Exchange-rate conversion is preserved.

9. Opaque pricing increases uncertainty.

10. Actual cost can calibrate future routing.

11.488 Stage 1 Quality Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Quality evidence references Capability.

2. Quality evidence references Model Version.

3. Project-specific evidence remains scoped.

4. Stale benchmark confidence decreases.

5. Quality Floor excludes weak Candidate.

6. Quality Target affects Premium ranking.

7. Human rejection updates evidence.

8. Provider marketing is not verified quality.

9. Model Family reputation does not replace Version evidence.

10. Quality evaluation remains separate from routing selection.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.489 Stage 1 Reliability Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Provider outage marks Candidate unavailable.

2. Account authentication failure remains Account-scoped.

3. One Deployment failure does not disable the Model globally.

4. Local Node offline state excludes local Candidate.

5. Rate limit affects latency or availability.

6. Unknown outcome affects reliability evidence.

7. Recovery restores Candidate after fresh validation.

8. Stale health is not treated as current.

9. Router failure does not trigger direct Provider bypass.

10. Repeated failures trigger fallback or no route.

11.490 Stage 1 Explainability Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Decision identifies selected Candidate.

2. Decision identifies Routing Profile.

3. Decision identifies dominant score reasons.

4. Decision identifies material exclusions.

5. Decision identifies expected cost.

6. Decision identifies fallback.

7. Decision identifies uncertainty.

8. Decision identifies Provider Account.

9. Decision identifies policy versions.

10. Redacted view hides protected details without changing canonical record.

11.491 Stage 1 Governance Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Profile changes are versioned.

2. Routing policy changes are attributable.

3. Commercial relationship is represented.

4. Provider commission cannot override user value.

5. User override cannot violate mandatory policy.

6. One override does not become permanent policy.

7. Routing learning requires admission.

8. Learning expires after Model change.

9. Emergency policy is temporary and reviewed.

10. Historical Selection Decisions remain immutable.

11.492 Routing Conformance Requirements

An implementation conforms to this chapter only when:

- mandatory eligibility occurs before ranking,

- profiles guide optimisation rather than authority,

- all selected external paths identify Provider Account and Connection,

- local and external resources use one decision model,

- Project and Tenant scope are enforced,

- cost and quality remain Capability-specific,

- privacy and rights fail closed,

- fallback is revalidated,

- routing decisions are versioned and explainable,

- and no commercial incentive silently controls selection.

A Provider dropdown is not a routing architecture.

A weighted score alone is not a routing architecture.

A canonical Router must enforce eligibility, policy, evidence and bounded optimisation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.493 Canonical Routing Request Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Routing Request contract:

1. Every Routing Request SHALL identify a Capability Requirement.

2. Every Routing Request SHALL identify its Plan Version and Step where applicable.

3. Every Routing Request SHALL identify Tenant.

4. Every Project request SHALL identify Project.

5. Every Routing Request SHALL identify Environment.

6. Every Routing Request SHALL identify effective Authority.

7. Every Routing Request SHALL identify Data Classification.

8. Every Routing Request SHALL identify required rights and consent.

9. Every Routing Request SHALL identify Quality Floor.

10. Every paid Routing Request SHALL identify budget.

11. Every Routing Request SHALL identify Routing Profile.

12. Required Features SHALL be explicit.

13. Provider and Model restrictions SHALL be explicit.

14. Placement restrictions SHALL be explicit.

15. Deadline and latency requirements SHALL be explicit where material.

16. Routing Requests SHALL NOT contain raw credentials.

17. Routing Requests SHALL preserve provenance.

18. Material changes SHALL create a new Routing Request or version.

19. Routing Context freshness SHALL remain visible.

20. Unresolved mandatory fields SHALL fail closed.

11.494 Canonical Candidate Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Candidate contract:

1. Every Candidate SHALL identify the resource path it represents.

2. External Candidates SHALL identify Provider.

3. External Candidates SHALL identify Provider Account.

4. Automated Candidates SHALL identify Connection.

5. Model Candidates SHALL identify Model Version where known.

6. Model Candidates SHALL identify Deployment or routed-resource identity.

7. Tool Candidates SHALL identify Tool and runtime.

8. Local Candidates SHALL identify Runtime Node.

9. Human-assisted Candidates SHALL identify the human boundary.

10. Candidates SHALL identify Capability support.

11. Candidates SHALL identify mandatory Feature support.

12. Candidates SHALL identify expected cost.

13. Candidates SHALL identify relevant quality evidence.

14. Candidates SHALL identify current health or availability.

15. Candidates SHALL identify privacy and rights context.

16. Candidate state SHALL distinguish eligible, unavailable and unresolved.

17. Unknown properties SHALL remain unknown.

18. Candidate records SHALL NOT expose raw secrets.

19. Candidate identity SHALL remain stable within the Routing Request.

20. Composite Candidates SHALL preserve every material resource boundary.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.495 Canonical Eligibility Contract

The following requirements define canonical eligibility:

1. Eligibility SHALL be evaluated before ranking.

2. Law and mandatory obligations SHALL outrank optimisation.

3. Security SHALL outrank profile preference.

4. Tenant and Project isolation SHALL fail closed.

5. Data Classification SHALL fail closed.

6. Privacy requirements SHALL be mandatory.

7. Rights and consent SHALL be mandatory.

8. Authority SHALL be mandatory.

9. Capability and Feature compatibility SHALL be mandatory.

10. Quality Floor SHALL be mandatory.

11. Hard deadline feasibility SHALL be mandatory.

12. Maximum budget SHALL be mandatory.

13. Provider and Model deny rules SHALL propagate through fallback.

14. Integration maturity requirements SHALL be enforced.

15. Unknown mandatory evidence SHALL NOT become favourable.

16. An ineligible Candidate SHALL NOT receive an optimisation score.

17. Conditional eligibility SHALL identify enforceable conditions.

18. Approval-required Candidates SHALL NOT execute before approval.

19. Availability SHALL be revalidated before execution.

20. Eligibility decisions SHALL preserve reasons and evidence.

11.496 Canonical Routing Profile Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Routing Profiles:

1. Economy SHALL minimise expected total eligible cost.

2. Economy SHALL preserve Quality Floor.

3. Economy SHALL preserve privacy, rights, authority and deadline.

4. Balanced SHALL optimise overall expected value.

5. Balanced SHALL use versioned quality, cost, reliability, latency and privacy weights.

6. Premium SHALL prioritise strongest justified expected quality.

7. Premium SHALL remain inside budget.

8. Premium SHALL NOT mean highest price.

9. Private SHALL optimise approved custody and placement.

10. Private SHALL define acceptable placement explicitly.

11. Private SHALL NOT silently route externally.

12. Pinned SHALL honour the specified resource only when eligible.

13. Mandatory Pinned routing SHALL prohibit silent substitution.

14. Preferred Pinned routing MAY permit governed fallback.
