15. Every profile SHALL have stable identity and version.

16. Profile selection SHALL remain visible.

17. Profiles SHALL NOT override mandatory policy.

18. Profile changes SHALL be attributable.

19. Project and Tenant defaults SHALL remain explicit.

20. Balanced SHOULD be the ordinary safe default unless policy defines otherwise.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.497 Canonical Selection Decision Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Selection Decision:

1. Every Selection Decision SHALL have stable identity.

2. It SHALL identify the Routing Request.

3. It SHALL identify the selected Candidate.

4. It SHALL identify the Routing Profile and version.

5. It SHALL identify excluded material Candidates and reasons.

6. It SHALL identify expected cost.

7. It SHALL identify quality evidence.

8. It SHALL identify current operational evidence and freshness.

9. It SHALL identify Provider Account and Connection for external execution.

10. It SHALL identify Model Version, Tool or routed resource where known.

11. It SHALL identify fallback policy or no-fallback state.

12. It SHALL identify applicable policy versions.

13. It SHALL identify Router and scoring versions.

14. It SHALL preserve uncertainty.

15. It SHALL remain valid only for a bounded context and time.

16. It SHALL be revalidated before consequential execution.

17. Material substitution SHALL create a new Decision or evidenced fallback.

18. Historical Decisions SHALL remain immutable.

19. The Decision SHALL NOT contain raw credentials.

20. The Decision SHALL be human- and machine-explainable.

11.498 Canonical Fallback Contract

The following requirements define canonical routing fallback:

1. Fallback SHALL be explicitly permitted.

2. Fallback SHALL have bounded depth.

3. Every fallback Candidate SHALL be revalidated.

4. Fallback SHALL preserve Data Classification.

5. Fallback SHALL preserve rights and consent.

6. Fallback SHALL preserve Authority.

7. Fallback SHALL preserve Quality Floor.

8. Fallback SHALL remain within budget.

9. Fallback SHALL respect Provider and Model denylists.

10. Mandatory Pins SHALL block unapproved substitution.

11. Cross-Provider fallback SHALL preserve changed terms and Account evidence.

12. Local-to-external fallback SHALL require eligible data placement.

13. External-to-local fallback SHALL require sufficient Capability and quality.

14. Human-assisted fallback SHALL remain truthfully labelled.

15. Material fallback SHALL be disclosed.

16. Fallback cost SHALL be recorded.

17. Unknown outcome SHALL be reconciled before unsafe retry or fallback.

18. Fallback SHALL NOT change Capability meaning silently.

19. Fallback history SHALL remain traceable.

20. Exhausted fallback SHALL produce No Route or escalation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.499 Canonical Routing Governance Contract

The following requirements define routing governance:

1. Routing Policy SHALL be versioned.

2. Canonical Profiles SHALL be versioned.

3. Scoring logic SHALL be versioned.

4. Router implementation SHALL be identifiable.

5. Routing changes SHALL be attributable.

6. Commercial Provider relationships SHALL remain visible.

7. Commercial benefit SHALL NOT silently override user value.

8. User-owned credits SHALL remain user-owned.

9. Project-owned resources SHALL remain Project-scoped.

10. Tenant-owned resources SHALL preserve Project attribution.

11. Omnira-managed resources SHALL preserve Tenant isolation.

12. Routing learning SHALL require governed admission.

13. Routing learning SHALL remain scoped and expirable.

14. User overrides SHALL preserve evidence.

15. Unsafe overrides SHALL be rejected.

16. Exploration SHALL use bounded risk and budget.

17. Emergency routing policy SHALL be temporary and reviewable.

18. Routing Incidents SHALL preserve affected decisions and Executions.

19. Routing caches SHALL invalidate after critical governance changes.

20. Router failure SHALL NOT authorise direct Provider bypass.

11.500 Routing Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No ineligible Candidate is scored into eligibility.

- No Routing Profile overrides mandatory policy.

- No Economy route lowers the Quality Floor.

- No Premium route exceeds the approved budget.

- No Private route silently changes custody.

- No mandatory Pin silently falls back.

- No Provider preference becomes authority.

- No Provider commission silently controls selection.

- No user-owned credit becomes shared capacity without permission.

- No Project Account serves another Project by convenience.

- No local resource is assumed free, private or sufficient without evidence.

- No external resource is assumed current, secure or rights-compatible by reputation.

- No stale health, pricing or quality evidence is presented as current certainty.

- No fallback escapes Data Classification, rights or authority.

- No Routing Decision hides its Provider Account or Connection.

- No Router receives raw Provider secrets.

- No user override bypasses mandatory governance.

- No learned preference rewrites policy automatically.

- No Selection Decision rewrites historical routing truth.

- No Router failure creates uncontrolled direct execution.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
11.501 Closing Statement

Routing is the decision layer through which the Intelligence Fabric turns interchangeable resource potential into a specific governed execution path.

The Capability defines what must be done.

The Plan defines where the work belongs.

The Routing Request defines the constraints.

The Candidate Set defines what may be possible.

Eligibility removes what is not permitted.

The Routing Profile defines how the remaining candidates should be optimised.

The Selection Decision defines which resource shall be used now.

The Executor performs the bounded work.

The Evaluation system determines whether the result is acceptable.

The Evidence Plane records what happened.

For Familje-Stunden, routing allows one Nova and Pling production to use:

- premium character-aware video for critical scenes,

- economical motion for backgrounds,

- approved Swedish voice,

- local media composition,

- and human child-facing review

without permanently binding the Project to one Provider.

For The Prompt, routing keeps:

- current search,

- factual verification,

- editorial reasoning,

- voice,

- avatar,

- and media production

assigned to the resources best suited to each responsibility.

For GainPilot, routing allows routine content to use economical local and external resources while preserving quality and commercial rights.

For Omnira, routing allows:

- local Models,

- user-owned subscriptions,

- Project Accounts,

- Omnira-managed credits,

- external specialists,

- private infrastructure,

- Tools,

- MCP servers,

- and human-assisted providers

to coexist under one policy-controlled decision model.

Economy shall reduce completed cost.

Balanced shall optimise total value.

Premium shall pursue justified quality.

Private shall preserve custody and placement.

Pinned shall preserve deliberate resource choice.

None shall override:

- security,

- scope,

- privacy,

- rights,

- authority,

- Quality Floor,

- deadline,

- or budget.

The Provider may change.

The Model may change.

The Account may change.

The current health may change.

The user’s approved constraints remain binding.

No routing before eligibility.

No scoring before policy.

No profile above authority.

No fallback outside scope.

No selection without explanation.

No execution without a traceable path.

The user retains preference.

The Project retains its boundaries.

Omnira retains neutrality.

The Fabric selects intelligence without surrendering governance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical architecture, governance model, lifecycle, contracts and operational responsibilities for cost, credits, budgets, pricing, reservations, usage and financial accountability within the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

It establishes:

- how estimated, reserved, provisional and confirmed cost remain distinct,

- how user-owned, Project-owned, Tenant-owned and Omnira-managed funding sources coexist,

- how subscriptions, credits, quotas, local compute and direct charges are represented,

- how spending authority remains separate from technical Provider access,

- how budgets are defined, allocated, reserved, consumed, released and reconciled,

- how paid retries, fallbacks, variants and speculative execution remain bounded,

- how cost is attributed to the correct Tenant, Project, Plan, Step, Execution and Provider Account,

- how currency conversion and Provider credit systems are normalised,

- how refunds, failed charges, delayed usage and disputed amounts are handled,

- how local and self-hosted execution receives honest economic treatment,

- how economic routing remains subordinate to quality, rights, privacy, security and authority,

- how users receive transparent explanations before and after spending,

- how Omnira-managed plans and future commercial margins remain governed,

- how economic learning may improve estimates without gaining authority,

- and how Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy economic control plane.

Economic governance exists to help Omnira use intelligence resources efficiently without allowing convenience, automation or Provider billing systems to become uncontrolled spending authority.

A connected Provider Account does not create permission to spend.

Available credits do not create permission to consume them.

A subscription does not create unlimited capacity.

A local Model does not create zero total cost.

A cheap resource does not create permission to lower quality, privacy, rights or safety.

A high-value request does not create unlimited budget.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

Implementation and financial conformance must be verified independently.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.2 Purpose of Economic Governance

The Intelligence Fabric may execute work through resources with very different economic models.

These may include:

- usage-based APIs,

- monthly subscriptions,

- prepaid credits,

- promotional credits,

- bundled Omnira capacity,

- enterprise contracts,

- free tiers,

- local Models,

- private servers,

- human-assisted services,

- marketplace products,

- and Provider interfaces whose true cost is visible only after completion.

Without one canonical economic architecture, spending would become distributed across:

- Provider dashboards,

- personal subscriptions,

- Project accounts,

- local hardware,

- Agent decisions,

- hidden retries,

- browser sessions,

- and manual workflows.

This would make it difficult to answer:

- Who paid?

- Which Project consumed the value?

- What was approved?

- What was estimated?

- What was actually charged?

- Which retries consumed cost?

- Which Provider Account was used?

- Did the result meet the Quality Contract?

- Was a cheaper eligible path available?

- Did Omnira or a Provider receive a commercial benefit?

- Can the cost be reproduced or disputed?

The economic control plane exists to make those questions answerable.

12.3 Economic Governance Is Not Accounting

The Intelligence Fabric economic architecture governs intelligence-resource spending.

It is not a complete:

- bookkeeping system,

- tax system,

- payroll system,

- invoice-payment platform,

- or corporate accounting ledger.

It may produce records consumed by those systems.

It shall not silently claim to replace them.

12.4 Economic Governance Is Not Routing

Routing compares eligible resources and may use economic evidence.

The cost system defines and verifies that evidence.

Routing may select the lowest expected total-cost Candidate under Economy.

It may not invent:

- Provider price,

- available credits,

- exchange rate,

- approved budget,

- or spending authority.

12.5 Economic Governance Is Not Authority

A Budget describes how much may be spent within a defined scope.

It does not prove that the action itself is authorised.

A request may have sufficient budget but still lack:

- publication authority,

- data-processing permission,

- commercial rights,

- consent,

- or Provider approval.

Financial permission and operational authority shall remain separate.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 12.6 Economic Governance Is Not Provider Billing
12.7 Economic Governance Is Not Business Value
text:
12.6 Economic Governance Is Not Provider Billing

Provider billing records what the Provider claims or charges.

Omnira economic governance records:

- what was approved,

- what was estimated,

- what was attempted,

- what the Provider reported,

- what Omnira attributed,

- and what remains unresolved.

Provider billing is evidence.

It is not the only source of economic truth.

12.7 Economic Governance Is Not Business Value

Cost measures resource consumption.

Business Value measures the expected or realised benefit of the work.

A low-cost Output may have low value.

A high-cost Output may be justified by:

- strategic importance,

- reuse,

- conversion,

- quality,

- risk reduction,

- or time saved.

Cost and value shall remain distinct.

12.8 Economic Control Plane

The Economic Control Plane is the collection of governed services and canonical objects responsible for:

- budgets,

- funding sources,

- pricing,

- cost estimation,

- reservations,

- usage,

- cost confirmation,

- credits,

- quotas,

- reconciliation,

- alerts,

- and reporting.

It shall interact with:

- Capability Requests,

- Plans,

- Routing,

- Provider Accounts,

- Connections,

- Executions,

- Approvals,

- Assets,

- and Evidence.

It shall not expose raw payment credentials to Agents or Models.

12.9 Economic Object Model

The canonical economic object model should include or reference:

- Funding Source,

- Budget,

- Budget Allocation,

- Budget Envelope,

- Budget Reservation,

- Pricing Record,

- Pricing Unit,

- Cost Estimate,

- Cost Range,

- Usage Record,

- Provider Charge,

- Cost Record,

- Cost Adjustment,

- Credit System,

- Credit Balance,

- Credit Reservation,

- Quota,

- Subscription,

- Refund Record,

- Financial Approval,

- Cost Anomaly,

- and Reconciliation Record.

12.10 Funding Source

A Funding Source identifies the economic source expected to pay for an intelligence execution.

A Funding Source may be:

- user-owned,

- Project-owned,

- Tenant-owned,

- Omnira-managed,

- customer-managed,

- subscription-included,

- prepaid credit,

- promotional credit,

- local compute allocation,

- or external partner-funded.

Every paid Execution shall identify a Funding Source or explicitly unresolved funding state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.11 Funding Source Identity

Every persistent Funding Source shall have stable identity.

Its identity shall remain separate from:

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Budget,

- Credit Balance,

- and payment method.

One Funding Source may support several Provider Accounts.

One Provider Account may draw from several Funding Sources only when the Provider permits it and attribution remains clear.

12.12 Funding Source Owner

Every Funding Source shall have an explicit owner.

Possible owners include:

- human user,

- Project,

- Tenant,

- Omnira,

- customer organisation,

- or external partner.

Ownership determines who may:

- allocate,

- approve,

- suspend,

- and review spending.

12.13 User-Owned Funding Source

A User-Owned Funding Source belongs directly to the user.

Examples include:

- personal subscription,

- personal Provider credits,

- personal API billing,

- or personal local hardware.

The Fabric shall not use it silently for Project work.

Explicit permission and Project attribution are required.

12.14 Project-Owned Funding Source

A Project-Owned Funding Source exists primarily for one Project.

Its use shall remain:

- Project-scoped,

- budgeted,

- and attributable.

Familje-Stunden funds shall not be consumed for GainPilot merely because one person owns both Projects.

12.15 Tenant-Owned Funding Source

A Tenant-Owned Funding Source may support several Projects.

Project-level attribution remains mandatory.

12.16 Omnira-Managed Funding Source

An Omnira-Managed Funding Source uses capacity, credits or contracts controlled by Omnira.

It may support:

- bundled plans,

- shared Provider Accounts,

- internal compute,

- or future customer subscriptions.

It shall preserve:

- Tenant isolation,

- Project attribution,

- transparent pricing,

- and commercial-interest disclosure.

12.17 Customer-Managed Funding Source

A future customer may connect their own billing relationship.

Omnira shall preserve:

- customer ownership,

- billing scope,

- Project allocation,

- and revocation rights.

12.18 Partner-Funded Source

An external partner may fund experimentation or production.

The relationship shall identify:

- scope,

- conditions,

- expiry,

- commercial influence,

- and data implications.

Partner funding shall not silently control Provider selection.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.19 Local Compute Allocation

Local compute may be represented through a Local Compute Funding Source or Allocation.

It may track:

- energy,

- hardware use,

- storage,

- GPU time,

- and opportunity cost.

Stage 1 may use simplified estimates.

It shall not claim that local execution has no cost merely because no Provider invoice exists.

12.20 Budget

A Budget is a governed limit on permitted economic consumption within a defined scope and period.

A Budget shall include or reference:

- budgetId,

- owner,

- Funding Source,

- currency or accounting unit,

- total limit,

- remaining amount,

- effective period,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- permitted Capabilities,

- permitted Providers,

- permitted cost classes,

- approval rules,

- and lifecycle.

12.21 Budget Identity

Every persistent Budget shall have stable identity.

A Budget may receive new versions or periods.

Historical Executions shall remain linked to the Budget in effect at execution time.

12.22 Budget Owner

The Budget Owner is responsible for:

- purpose,

- limit,

- scope,

- renewal,

- and policy.

The Budget Owner need not possess raw Provider billing credentials.

12.23 Budget Scope

Budget Scope may include:

- Platform,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Production,

- Workflow,

- Plan,

- Phase,

- Step,

- Capability,

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Model class,

- or Environment.

Scope shall be explicit.

Missing scope shall fail closed.

12.24 Platform Budget

A Platform Budget governs Omnira-wide economic consumption.

It may support:

- registry benchmarking,

- infrastructure,

- shared evaluation,

- or managed services.

It shall not become a substitute for Project attribution.

12.25 Tenant Budget

A Tenant Budget governs aggregated Tenant spending.

Project sub-budgets may draw from it.

12.26 Project Budget

A Project Budget governs spending for one Project.

It may contain:

- monthly operating budget,

- campaign budget,

- media budget,

- research budget,

- or development budget.

12.27 Production Budget

A Production Budget applies to one bounded deliverable such as:

- Nova and Pling episode,

- The Prompt news video,

- GainPilot reel,

- or Omnira architecture audit.

Production Budgets should include retries and derivatives where authorised.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.28 Plan Budget

A Plan Budget is the maximum amount authorised for one Plan Version.

Material Plan changes may require a new Budget Envelope or approval.

12.29 Step Budget

A Step Budget is the maximum cost one Step may consume.

It may include:

- first attempt,

- retry allowance,

- fallback allowance,

- and evaluation cost.

12.30 Capability Budget

A Capability Budget limits cost for a class of operations such as:

- video generation,

- speech synthesis,

- current search,

- or code analysis.

12.31 Provider Budget

A Provider Budget limits spending with one Provider or Provider Account.

It may reduce exposure to:

- unexpected charges,

- single-source dependence,

- or Provider pricing errors.

12.32 Environment Budget

Development, staging and production budgets shall remain separate where appropriate.

Development experiments shall not consume production capacity without explicit authority.

12.33 Periodic Budget

A Periodic Budget resets or renews on a schedule such as:

- daily,

- weekly,

- monthly,

- quarterly,

- or annually.

Reset behaviour shall be explicit.

12.34 Fixed Budget

A Fixed Budget applies to a bounded initiative and does not automatically renew.

12.35 Rolling Budget

A Rolling Budget covers a moving time window.

The calculation method shall be explicit.

12.36 Budget Version

Material changes to:

- limit,

- scope,

- owner,

- Funding Source,

- or approval rules

shall create a new Budget Version or attributable amendment.

12.37 Budget Lifecycle

Budget lifecycle states may include:

- proposed,

- awaiting approval,

- active,

- partially reserved,

- fully reserved,

- nearing limit,

- exhausted,

- suspended,

- expired,

- closed,

- and archived.

12.38 Proposed Budget

A Proposed Budget has not yet been approved for spending.

12.39 Awaiting-Approval Budget

The amount and scope are defined but authority remains incomplete.

12.40 Active Budget

An Active Budget may support eligible reservations and spending.

12.41 Partially Reserved Budget

Part of the Budget is committed to pending work.

12.42 Fully Reserved Budget

The available amount is fully reserved.

No additional spending may begin unless reservations are released or the Budget is increased.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.43 Nearing-Limit Budget

The remaining amount has crossed a defined warning threshold.

12.44 Exhausted Budget

No additional cost may be authorised under the Budget.

Existing paid external jobs may still need reconciliation.

12.45 Suspended Budget

New reservations are blocked temporarily.

Suspension may result from:

- anomaly,

- Incident,

- review,

- or owner action.

12.46 Expired Budget

The Budget period has ended.

New work requires a new active Budget.

12.47 Closed Budget

The Budget has completed its economic lifecycle and all known charges have been reconciled.

12.48 Archived Budget

The Budget remains for history and audit.

12.49 Budget Envelope

A Budget Envelope is the request- or Plan-specific economic boundary derived from one or more Budgets and Funding Sources.

It shall include or reference:

- budgetEnvelopeId,

- parent Budgets,

- maximum authorised cost,

- expected cost,

- currency,

- Step allocations,

- retry allocation,

- fallback allocation,

- optional-work allocation,

- approval validity,

- Funding Source priority,

- and overrun behaviour.

12.50 Budget Envelope Identity

A Budget Envelope shall have stable identity and version.

Approval shall bind to the exact Envelope Version.

12.51 Maximum Authorised Cost

Maximum Authorised Cost is the hard upper boundary for the approved scope.

The Fabric shall stop before knowingly exceeding it.

12.52 Expected Cost

Expected Cost is the estimated likely total under ordinary execution.

It shall remain distinct from the maximum.

12.53 Minimum Estimated Cost

Minimum Estimated Cost represents the lowest plausible valid cost under favourable conditions.

12.54 Cost Range

A Cost Range may include:

- minimum,

- expected,

- maximum,

- and confidence.

Ranges are appropriate when Provider usage or retries are uncertain.

12.55 Budget Headroom

Budget Headroom is the difference between:

- maximum authorised cost,

- and current confirmed plus reserved cost.

Headroom may be allocated to:

- retries,

- fallback,

- or optional work.

12.56 Budget Allocation

A Budget Allocation assigns part of a Budget to a narrower scope.

It may be created for:

- Project,

- Plan,

- Step,

- Provider,

- Capability,

- or time period.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.57 Allocation Hierarchy

Allocations may form a hierarchy such as:

Tenant Budget

→ Project Budget

→ Production Budget

→ Plan Budget

→ Step Budget

Child allocations shall not exceed available parent capacity.

12.58 Hard Allocation

A Hard Allocation cannot be exceeded without amendment or new approval.

12.59 Soft Allocation

A Soft Allocation is a planning target that may draw from shared reserve when policy permits.

12.60 Shared Reserve

A Shared Reserve supports unexpected but approved:

- retries,

- fallback,

- or corrections.

The reserve shall remain bounded.

12.61 Optional-Work Allocation

Optional variants, derivatives or enhancements should use a separate discretionary allocation where practical.

12.62 Retry Allocation

Retry budget shall remain explicit.

Retries shall not silently consume unrelated Project funds.

12.63 Fallback Allocation

Fallback budget may be reserved separately when alternative Providers have higher costs.

12.64 Human-Correction Allocation

Plans involving review or manual production may allocate expected human effort or external service cost.

12.65 Budget Priority

When several Funding Sources are eligible, the Budget Envelope may define priority.

Examples include:

1. Project-included capacity.

2. Project-owned credits.

3. Tenant shared allocation.

4. User-owned credits with permission.

5. Omnira-managed credits.

6. Paid on-demand source.

Priority remains subordinate to routing eligibility and user choice.

12.66 Funding Source Substitution

Changing Funding Source after approval may be material.

The system shall evaluate:

- owner,

- price,

- Provider Account,

- commercial relationship,

- and user expectation.

12.67 Budget Reservation

A Budget Reservation temporarily commits capacity before cost is confirmed.

It prevents several concurrent operations from overspending the same Budget.

A Reservation shall include or reference:

- reservationId,

- Budget Envelope,

- Plan,

- Step,

- selected Candidate,

- expected cost,

- maximum reservable cost,

- currency,

- expiration,

- status,

- and provenance.

12.68 Reservation Identity

Every Reservation shall have stable identity.

12.69 Reservation Purpose

The Reservation purpose shall identify the exact work being protected.

Generic permanent reservations are discouraged.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.70 Reservation Amount

The reserved amount should reflect:

- expected Provider charge,

- retry allowance,

- minimum charge,

- and uncertainty.

It shall not exceed the Step or Plan boundary.

12.71 Reservation Currency

Reservation currency shall match the parent Budget or use an explicit conversion basis.

12.72 Reservation Lifecycle

Reservation states may include:

- proposed,

- pending,

- active,

- partially consumed,

- fully consumed,

- released,

- expired,

- cancelled,

- and disputed.

12.73 Active Reservation

An Active Reservation reduces available Budget capacity.

12.74 Partial Consumption

Part of the reserved amount has become provisional or confirmed cost.

12.75 Full Consumption

The full reserved amount has been consumed or allocated to confirmed charge.

12.76 Reservation Release

Unused reservation capacity shall be released when:

- work completes,

- work is cancelled,

- cost is lower than expected,

- or the reservation expires safely.

12.77 Reservation Expiry

Reservations shall have expiry or explicit long-running status.

Expired reservations must not disappear while active external jobs remain unresolved.

12.78 Reservation Renewal

Long-running jobs may renew reservations before expiry.

Renewal shall remain inside the Budget Envelope.

12.79 Concurrent Reservation Control

Reservation creation shall use concurrency-safe checks.

Two workers shall not reserve the same remaining budget simultaneously beyond the allowed limit.

12.80 Reservation Idempotency

Repeated Reservation requests for the same Step and attempt shall not duplicate committed capacity.

12.81 Reservation Before Paid Execution

Paid execution should normally require an active Reservation before Provider submission.

12.82 Reservation for Subscription Capacity

Even when no marginal charge is expected, a logical Reservation may protect:

- included quota,

- concurrency,

- or monthly capacity.

12.83 Reservation for Local Compute

Local jobs may reserve:

- GPU time,

- battery allowance,

- energy allocation,

- or node capacity.

This may be operational rather than financial.

12.84 Reservation for Human-Assisted Work

Manual Provider work may reserve the approved maximum spend before the operator begins.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.85 Pricing Record

A Pricing Record represents Provider, local or managed pricing evidence.

It shall include or reference:

- pricingRecordId,

- Provider,

- Provider Account class,

- Product,

- Model or Capability,

- region,

- Pricing Unit,

- currency,

- effective time,

- expiry or review,

- source,

- confidence,

- and provenance.

12.86 Pricing Record Identity

Every material Pricing Record shall have stable identity and version.

12.87 Pricing Source

Pricing sources may include:

- official Provider price list,

- Provider API,

- contract,

- invoice,

- subscription dashboard,

- manually verified terms,

- or local cost model.

Source quality and freshness shall remain visible.

12.88 Pricing Effective Date

Pricing shall include an effective date where known.

12.89 Pricing Retrieval Date

When effective date is unknown, retrieval date shall be preserved.

12.90 Pricing Expiry

Volatile pricing may expire quickly.

Stale pricing shall not be represented as current certainty.

12.91 Pricing Confidence

Pricing confidence may be:

- exact,

- high,

- moderate,

- low,

- opaque,

- or unknown.

12.92 Pricing Unit

A Pricing Unit defines the Provider billing measure.

Examples include:

- input token,

- output token,

- cached token,

- image,

- megapixel,

- video second,

- audio second,

- character,

- request,

- job,

- compute second,

- GPU minute,

- credit,

- seat,

- storage unit,

- or subscription period.

12.93 Composite Pricing

A Provider may charge through several units.

For example:

- input tokens,

- output tokens,

- tool use,

- storage,

- and search calls.

The estimate shall include every material component.

12.94 Tiered Pricing

Pricing may change after volume thresholds.

The Pricing Record shall represent the tier logic.

12.95 Regional Pricing

Price may vary by region.

The selected Deployment or Account shall determine the applicable record.

12.96 Account-Tier Pricing

Subscription or enterprise tiers may alter:

- unit price,

- included quota,

- and rights.

Pricing shall remain Account-aware.

12.97 Promotional Pricing

Promotional prices shall include:

- expiry,

- restrictions,

- and applicable Products.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.98 Minimum Charge

Some Provider operations impose minimum billable amounts.

The estimate shall include them.

12.99 Rounded Usage

Providers may round:

- tokens,

- seconds,

- compute,

- or storage.

Rounding rules shall be represented where material.

12.100 Failed-Request Pricing

Providers may charge for:

- rejected requests,

- partial generations,

- failed jobs,

- or moderation checks.

The system shall not assume failed means free.

12.101 Cancellation Pricing

Cancellation may result in:

- no charge,

- partial charge,

- full charge,

- or unknown charge.

The Provider-specific behaviour shall be preserved.

12.102 Retry Pricing

Every retry may create a new charge.

Retry cost shall be estimated and recorded separately.

12.103 Fallback Pricing

Fallback to another Provider or Model shall use its own Pricing Record.

12.104 Subscription

A Subscription represents recurring access purchased from a Provider or through Omnira.

It shall include or reference:

- subscriptionId,

- owner,

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Product,

- tier,

- billing period,

- recurring price,

- included capacity,

- overage rules,

- renewal,

- cancellation,

- rights,

- and lifecycle.

12.105 Subscription Ownership

Subscription ownership shall remain explicit.

A personal subscription shall not become a shared Project asset automatically.

12.106 Subscription Billing Period

The billing period may be:

- monthly,

- annual,

- prepaid term,

- or custom contract.

12.107 Subscription Included Capacity

Included capacity may consist of:

- credits,

- tokens,

- jobs,

- media duration,

- storage,

- seats,

- priority,

- or API access.

12.108 Subscription Marginal Cost

Usage within included capacity may have zero immediate marginal Provider charge.

It still consumes limited value.

12.109 Subscription Allocation

A subscription may be allocated across:

- Projects,

- users,

- Capabilities,

- or environments.

Allocation shall be governed when capacity is shared.

12.110 Subscription Renewal

Renewal is a financial commitment.

Automatic renewal policy shall remain explicit.

12.111 Subscription Upgrade

Upgrades may change:

- price,

- rights,

- capacity,

- retention,

- or API access.

Material upgrades require authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.112 Subscription Downgrade

Downgrade impact shall be assessed for:

- running workflows,

- commercial rights,

- and capacity.

12.113 Subscription Cancellation

Cancellation shall preserve:

- end-of-service date,

- remaining credits,

- export deadlines,

- and affected Plans.

12.114 Subscription Expiry

Expired subscription status shall affect Provider Account eligibility.

12.115 Credit System

A Credit System is a Provider- or Omnira-defined unit system through which capacity is purchased or consumed.

It shall include or reference:

- creditSystemId,

- issuer,

- unit definition,

- applicable Products,

- purchase conversion,

- usage conversion,

- expiry,

- transferability,

- refundability,

- and provenance.

12.116 Provider Credit

A Provider Credit is issued by one Provider and normally usable only within that Provider ecosystem.

12.117 Omnira Credit

A future Omnira Credit may represent managed capacity across one or more Providers.

Its conversion, margin, expiry and permitted use shall be transparent.

12.118 Promotional Credit

Promotional credits may have:

- expiry,

- Provider restrictions,

- non-commercial conditions,

- or Product limits.

12.119 Non-Transferable Credit

Credits may be bound to:

- Account,

- user,

- workspace,

- or Product.

The system shall not assume transferability.

12.120 Credit Balance

A Credit Balance records observed available credits.

It shall include:

- balanceId,

- Credit System,

- Provider Account,

- observed balance,

- reserved amount,

- available amount,

- observedAt,

- source,

- and confidence.

12.121 Credit Balance Freshness

Credit balance is dynamic.

The system shall expose freshness.

12.122 Stale Credit Balance

A stale balance shall not be used as exact current capacity for high-cost work without revalidation.

12.123 Credit Reservation

Credit Reservation commits Provider or managed credits for planned work.

It shall remain linked to the Budget Reservation.

12.124 Credit Consumption

Credit consumption shall be linked to:

- Execution,

- Attempt,

- Provider job,

- and Provider Account.

12.125 Credit Expiry

Credits nearing expiry may influence Economy routing only when:

- the work is authorised,

- quality is sufficient,

- and user value remains primary.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.126 Credit Purchase

Purchasing new credits is a financial side effect.

It requires separate authority from consuming already approved credits.

12.127 Automatic Credit Purchase

Automatic top-up shall be disabled by default unless explicitly governed.

Where enabled, it shall have:

- maximum amount,

- period limit,

- Funding Source,

- approval,

- and alerting.

12.128 Credit Transfer

Credit transfer between Accounts or Projects requires explicit Provider support and governance.

12.129 Credit Refund

Credit refunds shall be recorded separately from cash refunds.

12.130 Credit Value

The effective currency value of one credit may depend on:

- purchase package,

- subscription tier,

- promotion,

- and time.

One universal credit-to-currency value may be inaccurate.

12.131 Credit Normalisation

The Fabric may normalise expected credit consumption into budget currency while preserving original Provider units.

12.132 Quota

A Quota limits usage independently of financial budget.

Quota may include:

- requests,

- tokens,

- images,

- audio minutes,

- video seconds,

- concurrent jobs,

- storage,

- or seats.

12.133 Quota Identity

Every governed Quota shall identify:

- Provider Account,

- Product,

- limit,

- period,

- current usage,

- reset,

- source,

- and freshness.

12.134 Quota Versus Budget

Quota answers:

Can the Provider Account perform more work?

Budget answers:

May Omnira spend or allocate more value?

Both may be required.

12.135 Quota Reset

Reset timing shall be explicit where known.

12.136 Quota Reservation

For scarce quotas, Omnira may reserve capacity before scheduling work.

12.137 Quota Exhaustion

Quota exhaustion shall be classified separately from budget exhaustion.

12.138 Rate Limit

Rate limits affect scheduling and latency.

They are not direct financial limits.

12.139 Cost Estimate

A Cost Estimate predicts the economic consumption of a planned operation.

It shall include or reference:

- estimateId,

- Plan,

- Step,

- Candidate,

- Pricing Records,

- expected usage,

- retry assumptions,

- fallback assumptions,

- currency,

- minimum,

- expected,

- maximum,

- confidence,

- and createdAt.

12.140 Cost Estimate Identity

Each material estimate shall have stable identity and version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.141 Estimate Scope

The estimate may apply to:

- request,

- Plan,

- Phase,

- Step,

- Execution,

- retry,

- fallback,

- or derivative set.

12.142 Estimate Inputs

Estimate Inputs may include:

- token count,

- media duration,

- resolution,

- variant count,

- document size,

- context size,

- expected attempts,

- evaluation cost,

- and Provider minimum charges.

12.143 Pre-Execution Estimate

A pre-execution estimate is generated before resource use.

12.144 Updated Estimate

An estimate may be updated after:

- exact resource selection,

- known Input size,

- Provider queue,

- or first-stage result.

Material increases may require new approval.

12.145 Estimate Confidence

Estimate confidence depends on:

- pricing certainty,

- Input certainty,

- Provider billing transparency,

- and retry uncertainty.

12.146 Exact Estimate

An Exact Estimate is possible only when all billing inputs are known and the Provider pricing model is deterministic.

It remains an estimate until confirmed.

12.147 Range Estimate

Range estimates are appropriate for variable outputs or uncertain retries.

12.148 Opaque Estimate

Some Provider products expose only approximate or post-hoc pricing.

The estimate shall be labelled opaque or low confidence.

12.149 No Estimate

When meaningful estimation is impossible, paid execution should normally require:

- conservative maximum,

- explicit approval,

- or refusal.

12.150 Estimate Currency

Every estimate shall identify currency.

12.151 Base Currency

A Budget may use a canonical Base Currency.

For André’s current context, Swedish kronor may be the user-facing default where appropriate.

Provider charges may remain in other currencies.

12.152 Provider Currency

Original Provider currency shall always be preserved.

12.153 Currency Conversion

Currency conversion shall include:

- exchange rate,

- source,

- timestamp,

- and rounding.

12.154 Exchange-Rate Risk

Material foreign-currency uncertainty may require additional headroom.

12.155 Currency Rounding

Rounding rules shall be consistent and versioned.

12.156 Tax and Fee Treatment

Estimates may include or exclude:

- VAT,

- taxes,

- card fees,

- currency fees,

- and platform fees.

The treatment shall be explicit.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.157 Usage Record

A Usage Record represents measured resource consumption.

It shall include or reference:

- usageRecordId,

- Execution,

- Attempt,

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Model or Tool,

- Pricing Unit,

- quantity,

- measurement source,

- observedAt,

- status,

- and provenance.

12.158 Usage Record Identity

Every Usage Record shall have stable identity.

12.159 Usage Source

Usage may be reported by:

- Provider response,

- Provider dashboard,

- invoice,

- local telemetry,

- Adapter calculation,

- or manual operator.

12.160 Provider-Reported Usage

Provider-reported usage shall preserve the Provider’s original units.

12.161 Locally Measured Usage

Local telemetry may measure:

- token estimates,

- GPU time,

- CPU time,

- energy,

- media duration,

- and storage.

12.162 Estimated Usage

Estimated Usage is not confirmed usage.

It shall remain distinct.

12.163 Provisional Usage

Provisional Usage has stronger evidence but may still change before final billing.

12.164 Confirmed Usage

Confirmed Usage is reconciled with authoritative Provider or local evidence.

12.165 Usage Timing

Usage may be reported:

- synchronously,

- after job completion,

- later through billing,

- or only through monthly invoice.

12.166 Delayed Usage

Delayed Provider usage shall keep cost provisional until reconciliation.

12.167 Missing Usage

Missing usage shall not be assumed to be zero.

12.168 Duplicate Usage Record

Duplicate Provider usage events shall be deduplicated through stable correlation.

12.169 Usage Correction

Corrected usage shall create an adjustment or new revision.

Historical evidence shall remain visible.

12.170 Provider Charge

A Provider Charge represents an amount claimed or charged by a Provider.

It shall include or reference:

- providerChargeId,

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Product,

- Provider job or transaction,

- amount,

- currency,

- tax or fee treatment,

- status,

- source,

- and time.

12.171 Charge Status

Charge states may include:

- expected,

- pending,

- authorised,

- provisional,

- settled,

- refunded,

- partially refunded,

- disputed,

- reversed,

- failed,

- and unknown.

12.172 Pending Charge

The Provider or payment system has indicated a charge but settlement remains incomplete.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.173 Settled Charge

The charge is considered final under available evidence.

12.174 Unknown Charge

The Fabric cannot determine whether a charge occurred.

This state requires reconciliation.

12.175 Duplicate Charge

A duplicate charge is a billing anomaly or potential Provider Incident.

12.176 Cost Record

A Cost Record is Omnira’s canonical attributed economic record for one bounded scope.

It shall include or reference:

- costRecordId,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Plan,

- Step,

- Execution,

- Attempt,

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Funding Source,

- Usage Records,

- Provider Charges,

- amount,

- currency,

- cost state,

- attribution,

- and provenance.

12.177 Cost Record Identity

Every Cost Record shall have stable identity.

12.178 Cost State

Cost states may include:

- estimated,

- reserved,

- provisional,

- confirmed,

- adjusted,

- refunded,

- disputed,

- written off,

- and unknown.

12.179 Estimated Cost

Estimated cost is predictive.

12.180 Reserved Cost

Reserved cost represents committed Budget capacity.

12.181 Provisional Cost

Provisional cost is based on usage or Provider evidence that may still change.

12.182 Confirmed Cost

Confirmed cost has completed reconciliation under current economic policy.

12.183 Adjusted Cost

Adjusted cost reflects a correction after prior confirmation or provisional state.

12.184 Refunded Cost

Refunded cost has been returned through currency, credits or billing reversal.

12.185 Disputed Cost

Disputed cost remains unresolved with the Provider, payment system or internal attribution.

12.186 Unknown Cost

Unknown cost shall remain visible.

It shall not be converted to zero.

12.187 Cost Attribution

Every paid cost shall be attributed to:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Plan or operational purpose,

- Provider Account,

- and Funding Source.

Attribution shall be preserved even when the Account is shared.

12.188 Attempt-Level Cost

Retry and fallback Attempts shall have separate cost attribution.

12.189 Step-Level Cost

Step cost aggregates Attempts and related evaluation or transformation cost.

12.190 Plan-Level Cost

Plan cost aggregates all Step costs.

12.191 Production-Level Cost

Production cost may aggregate:

- master generation,

- retries,

- review,

- derivatives,

- and publication preparation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.192 Project-Level Cost

Project cost supports:

- reporting,

- budgeting,

- and economic learning.

12.193 Tenant-Level Cost

Tenant cost aggregates Projects while preserving Project detail.

12.194 Provider-Level Cost

Provider cost supports portfolio and dependency analysis.

12.195 Capability-Level Cost

Capability-level cost supports comparison across Providers and Models.

12.196 Model-Level Cost

Model-level cost shall remain Deployment- and Account-aware.

12.197 Asset Cost

An Asset may reference the costs required to create, modify and validate it.

Asset cost should preserve:

- original master,

- derivatives,

- retries,

- and rejected attempts where relevant.

12.198 Rejected-Output Cost

Rejected Outputs still consume cost.

The cost shall not disappear because quality failed.

12.199 Cancelled-Job Cost

Cancelled jobs may still incur partial or full cost.

12.200 Failed-Execution Cost

Failed execution cost shall remain recorded.

12.201 Unknown-Outcome Cost

Unknown-outcome executions shall reserve or provisionally record the maximum plausible charge until reconciled.

12.202 Cost Adjustment

A Cost Adjustment modifies the economic interpretation without rewriting the original record.

Adjustment reasons may include:

- Provider correction,

- refund,

- exchange-rate update,

- attribution correction,

- duplicate removal,

- or invoice reconciliation.

12.203 Positive Adjustment

A positive adjustment increases recognised cost.

12.204 Negative Adjustment

A negative adjustment reduces recognised cost.

12.205 Attribution Adjustment

Cost may move between Project or Funding Source only through attributable correction.

The original attribution history shall remain visible.

12.206 Refund Record

A Refund Record represents value returned by:

- cash,

- credit,

- invoice reduction,

- or Provider balance.

It shall identify the original charge and affected Budget.

12.207 Partial Refund

Partial refunds shall preserve the remaining confirmed cost.

12.208 Credit Refund

Provider credits returned after failure shall restore the Credit Balance after verification.

12.209 Refund Pending

Refund promises shall remain pending until confirmed.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.210 Refund Failure

A failed or denied refund may produce a dispute.

12.211 Reconciliation

Reconciliation compares Omnira economic state with Provider or financial evidence.

It may compare:

- Reservations,

- Usage Records,

- Provider Charges,

- credit balances,

- invoices,

- and Budget consumption.

12.212 Reconciliation Record

A Reconciliation Record shall include:

- reconciliationId,

- scope,

- expected values,

- observed values,

- discrepancies,

- resolution,

- actor or service,

- time,

- and provenance.

12.213 Execution Reconciliation

Execution reconciliation confirms whether the Provider charged and delivered the expected Output.

12.214 Provider Account Reconciliation

Account reconciliation compares Omnira usage with Provider dashboard or invoice.

12.215 Credit Reconciliation

Credit reconciliation compares expected and observed balance changes.

12.216 Subscription Reconciliation

Subscription reconciliation checks:

- recurring price,

- included usage,

- overage,

- and renewal.

12.217 Local Compute Reconciliation

Local compute reconciliation may compare estimated and measured:

- GPU time,

- energy,

- and resource occupancy.

12.218 Manual Workflow Reconciliation

Human-assisted execution shall reconcile:

- operator-reported spend,

- Provider evidence,

- downloaded Output,

- and Budget Reservation.

12.219 Reconciliation Frequency

Frequency should reflect:

- Provider criticality,

- cost,

- billing delay,

- and usage volume.

12.220 Real-Time Reconciliation

Some Providers expose immediate usage and charge data.

12.221 Deferred Reconciliation

Other Providers may reconcile:

- daily,

- weekly,

- or at invoice time.

12.222 Reconciliation Discrepancy

Discrepancy types may include:

- missing charge,

- unexpected charge,

- quantity mismatch,

- currency mismatch,

- credit mismatch,

- duplicate charge,

- wrong Project attribution,

- and unknown Provider job.

12.223 Reconciliation Tolerance

Small rounding differences may be accepted within a defined tolerance.

Tolerance shall be versioned.

12.224 Reconciliation Failure

Unresolved material discrepancy shall remain open.

It may trigger:

- Cost Anomaly,

- Budget suspension,

- Provider Incident,

- or human review.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.225 Cost Anomaly

A Cost Anomaly is an observed or predicted economic condition outside expected boundaries.

Examples include:

- unexpected price,

- rapid spending,

- repeated failed generations,

- duplicate charges,

- unexplained credit loss,

- wrong Provider Account,

- or budget overrun.

12.226 Cost Anomaly Identity

Every material anomaly shall have stable identity and severity.

12.227 Cost Anomaly Severity

Severity may depend on:

- absolute amount,

- percentage variance,

- Project importance,

- recurrence,

- and fraud or compromise risk.

12.228 Estimate Variance

Estimate Variance is the difference between estimated and actual cost.

12.229 Warning Variance

A warning threshold may trigger explanation or recalibration.

12.230 Critical Variance

A critical threshold may pause new spending.

12.231 Spending Velocity

Spending Velocity measures cost over time.

Unexpected acceleration may indicate:

- retry loop,

- Candidate race,

- compromised Credential,

- or Provider pricing change.

12.232 Cost Spike

A Cost Spike is a sudden increase compared with normal scope-specific patterns.

12.233 Repeated-Failure Spend

Repeated paid failures may trigger automatic pause before the full Budget is exhausted.

12.234 Wrong-Account Cost

Using the wrong Provider Account is both an attribution defect and possible governance Incident.

12.235 Shadow Spend

Shadow Spend occurs outside governed Fabric Connections.

Examples include:

- personal browser generation,

- direct script,

- unregistered API call,

- or hidden subscription use.

Shadow Spend shall be reconciled or explicitly excluded from canonical project economics.

12.236 Cost Incident

A Cost Incident may involve:

- unauthorised spending,

- budget bypass,

- duplicate Provider charge,

- compromised payment path,

- wrong Account,

- concealed margin,

- or unbounded retry.

12.237 Cost Incident Containment

Containment may include:

- suspend Budget,

- disable Connection,

- revoke Credential,

- stop retries,

- block Provider,

- or freeze managed credits.

12.238 Cost Incident Recovery

Recovery may include:

- reconciliation,

- refund request,

- attribution correction,

- new Budget control,

- and routing-policy update.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.239 Spending Authority

Spending Authority determines who may approve economic consumption.

It shall remain separate from:

- Provider credential ownership,

- technical execution,

- and Output approval.

12.240 Spending Authority Scope

Scope may include:

- maximum amount,

- period,

- Project,

- Capability,

- Provider,

- risk class,

- and action type.

12.241 Human Spending Authority

A human may approve one:

- request,

- Plan,

- Production,

- subscription,

- Provider Account,

- or Budget period.

12.242 Delegated Spending Authority

A human may delegate bounded spending authority to:

- Manager,

- Service Principal,

- Workflow,

- or Agent.

Delegation shall preserve:

- maximum amount,

- scope,

- expiry,

- and revocation.

12.243 Agent Spending Authority

An Agent may receive only bounded economic authority.

It shall not hold unrestricted purchase or billing permissions.

12.244 Service Spending Authority

A service may reserve and consume budget only for authorised Plans and Steps.

12.245 Approval Threshold

Approval may be required when:

- expected cost exceeds threshold,

- maximum cost exceeds threshold,

- premium resource is selected,

- Funding Source changes,

- new Provider is used,

- or opaque pricing applies.

12.246 Per-Action Approval

High-cost or high-risk work may require approval for every execution.

12.247 Bounded Job Approval

Bounded Job Approval authorises:

- defined objective,

- maximum cost,

- permitted Providers or classes,

- retry limit,

- fallback limit,

- and validity period.

The Fabric may operate autonomously inside those bounds.

12.248 Production Approval

A Production Approval may cover a complete media or document production.

It shall identify:

- expected cost,

- maximum cost,

- optional derivatives,

- retries,

- and stop conditions.

12.249 Subscription Approval

Starting or changing a subscription is separate from approving one execution.

12.250 Credit-Purchase Approval

Purchasing credits is a financial side effect requiring explicit authority.

12.251 Auto-Renewal Approval

Subscription auto-renewal shall be governed separately.

12.252 Auto-Top-Up Approval

Auto-top-up shall require:

- per-top-up limit,

- period limit,

- Funding Source,

- and notification.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.253 Approval Binding

Economic Approval shall bind to:

- Budget Envelope Version,

- Plan Version,

- scope,

- and expiry.

12.254 Approval Expiry

Approval may expire after:

- time,

- price change,

- Plan change,

- Provider change,

- or Budget amendment.

12.255 Approval Invalidation

Approval shall be invalidated by material increase in:

- cost,

- retries,

- Candidate count,

- Provider risk,

- or Funding Source impact.

12.256 Approval Conditions

Conditions such as:

- no more than two video retries,

- use Project credits first,

- no subscription purchase,

- or stop before premium fallback

shall become enforceable controls.

12.257 Approval Summary

The user-facing economic summary should include:

- what will be produced,

- expected cost,

- maximum cost,

- Funding Source,

- Provider Accounts or classes,

- retry allowance,

- optional work,

- and stop conditions.

12.258 Spend Disclosure

Before material paid execution, the system should disclose:

- expected charge,

- maximum charge,

- who pays,

- and what may cause cost variation.

12.259 Post-Execution Disclosure

After completion, the system should report:

- estimated cost,

- confirmed cost,

- retries,

- refunds,

- and remaining budget.

12.260 Small-Cost Autonomy

Low-cost recurring work may operate without per-action approval when covered by an active bounded Budget and Authority policy.

12.261 High-Cost Autonomy

High-cost work should require stronger:

- approval,

- evaluation,

- and anomaly controls.

12.262 Unclear-Cost Autonomy

Opaque pricing reduces permitted autonomous scope.

12.263 Spend Stop

A Spend Stop prevents new cost-incurring operations.

It may be:

- user initiated,

- Budget initiated,

- Incident initiated,

- or policy initiated.

12.264 Soft Spend Stop

A Soft Spend Stop blocks new work while allowing:

- in-flight completion,

- reconciliation,

- and refunds.

12.265 Hard Spend Stop

A Hard Spend Stop attempts to cancel all cancellable paid operations immediately.

12.266 Spend Resume

Resuming requires:

- active Budget,

- resolved anomaly,

- valid approval,

- and current pricing.

12.267 Budget Overrun

A Budget Overrun occurs when confirmed or unavoidable cost exceeds the approved maximum.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.268 Prevented Overrun

The preferred behaviour is to stop before overrun.

12.269 Unavoidable Overrun

An external Provider may charge beyond estimate despite controls.

The overrun shall be:

- recorded,

- explained,

- reconciled,

- and reviewed.

12.270 Intentional Overrun

Intentional overrun requires new approval before spending where possible.

12.271 Overrun Attribution

Overrun shall identify:

- trigger,

- Provider,

- Attempt,

- pricing evidence,

- and control failure.

12.272 Economic Routing

Routing may optimise economic outcomes only after mandatory eligibility.

Economy routing should minimise expected completed cost.

Balanced routing should optimise overall value.

Premium routing should maximise justified quality within Budget.

Private routing should preserve privacy even if cost is higher.

Pinned routing should honour the specified resource when eligible and affordable.

12.273 Cost Before Quality Floor Prohibition

No cost saving may justify falling below the mandatory Quality Floor.

12.274 Cost Before Privacy Prohibition

No cheaper Candidate may bypass Data Classification or privacy requirements.

12.275 Cost Before Rights Prohibition

No cheaper Candidate may use unclear or incompatible commercial rights.

12.276 Cost Before Security Prohibition

No cheaper Candidate may use compromised credentials or untrusted resources.

12.277 Cost Before Authority Prohibition

Available credits shall not create authority.

12.278 Cheapest Advertised Price

Cheapest advertised price is not equivalent to lowest expected completed cost.

12.279 Expected Completed Cost

Expected Completed Cost may include:

- generation,

- retries,

- correction,

- evaluation,

- post-processing,

- and human effort.

12.280 Quality-Adjusted Cost

Quality-Adjusted Cost compares cost with the probability of passing the Quality Contract.

12.281 Reliability-Adjusted Cost

Reliability-Adjusted Cost includes expected cost of failures and fallbacks.

12.282 Latency-Adjusted Cost

A cheaper resource that misses a deadline may have higher practical cost.

12.283 Privacy-Adjusted Cost

A private resource may have higher direct cost but lower privacy risk.

12.284 Lock-In Cost

Provider lock-in may create future migration and Asset-portability cost.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.285 Human-Effort Cost

Manual review and correction should be considered where material.

12.286 Opportunity Cost

Local compute or human time may prevent other valuable work.

Opportunity cost may remain estimated.

12.287 Economic Preference

Users and Projects may prefer:

- lower direct spend,

- included subscriptions,

- local capacity,

- or predictable billing.

Preferences do not override mandatory policy.

12.288 Free-First Principle

The Fabric may prefer free or already-included eligible capacity where it satisfies:

- Quality Floor,

- rights,

- privacy,

- reliability,

- and deadline.

Free-first does not mean free-only.

12.289 Local-First Economic Principle

Local execution may be preferred for:

- privacy,

- ownership,

- and low marginal charge.

It shall still be evaluated for:

- quality,

- energy,

- latency,

- and hardware impact.

12.290 User-Owned Capacity Preference

The user may choose to use their own subscription or credits.

The choice shall remain explicit.

12.291 Omnira-Managed Capacity Preference

Omnira-managed capacity may be used when:

- allocated,

- transparent,

- and competitive under the selected Routing Profile.

12.292 Mixed Funding

One Plan may use several Funding Sources.

For example:

- local compute for preprocessing,

- Project subscription for voice,

- user-owned credits for experimental video,

- and Omnira-managed credits for fallback.

Every Step shall identify its Funding Source.

12.293 Funding Waterfall

A Funding Waterfall defines the order in which eligible Funding Sources are used.

The waterfall shall be:

- explicit,

- approved,

- and Project-scoped.

12.294 Funding Waterfall Stop

If the next Funding Source requires new authority, execution shall pause rather than substitute silently.

12.295 Subscription Optimisation

The Fabric may recommend:

- using existing subscriptions,

- cancelling unused subscriptions,

- consolidating duplicate plans,

- or changing tier.

Recommendations are not automatic financial actions.

12.296 Duplicate Subscription

Duplicate subscriptions may create unnecessary fixed cost.

The system may identify overlap while preserving resilience needs.

12.297 Underused Subscription

A subscription may be underused relative to its fixed cost.

The analysis shall consider:

- strategic availability,

- rights,

- and fallback value.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.298 Overused Subscription

Frequent overage may justify tier review.

12.299 Subscription Break-Even

The Fabric may estimate when a subscription becomes cheaper than usage-based access.

The estimate shall preserve assumptions.

12.300 Provider Portfolio Cost

Provider Portfolio Cost includes:

- subscriptions,

- usage,

- local compute,

- maintenance,

- and human-assisted services.

12.301 Provider Concentration Risk

Heavy spending with one Provider may create dependency.

Economic optimisation may consider diversification when justified.

12.302 Provider Switching Cost

Switching cost may include:

- migration,

- retesting,

- Asset export,

- prompt adaptation,

- and quality loss.

12.303 Model Switching Cost

Changing an Embedding Model may require re-embedding data.

Changing a creative Model may require style recalibration.

12.304 Cost of Reproducibility

Pinned or fixed-version execution may cost more than routed execution.

The value of reproducibility may justify it.

12.305 Cost of Evaluation

Evaluation consumes:

- Models,

- Tools,

- human effort,

- and time.

Evaluation cost shall be included in the Plan.

12.306 Cost of Provenance

Evidence and storage create operational cost.

They remain necessary for meaningful Outputs.

12.307 Cost of Rejected Variants

Candidate races and variant generation shall include all rejected-output costs.

12.308 Cost of Derivatives

Trailers, thumbnails, captions and alternate formats shall have separate or allocated cost.

12.309 Cost of Publication

Publication may incur:

- platform fees,

- advertising cost,

- delivery services,

- or tool usage.

Publication cost remains outside generation unless explicitly included.

12.310 Cost of Storage

Provider and Omnira storage may incur recurring cost.

Long-lived Assets should preserve storage attribution.

12.311 Cost of Retention

Retention policy may affect ongoing storage and compliance cost.

12.312 Cost of Deletion

Deletion may incur:

- Provider API cost,

- operator effort,

- or migration effort.

It remains a separate governed action.

12.313 Cost of Recovery

Incident recovery, reruns and migration may consume budget.

Recovery cost shall be attributed separately.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.314 Economic Learning

The Fabric may improve:

- usage estimates,

- retry probability,

- local compute estimates,

- Provider total-cost estimates,

- and subscription recommendations.

Learning shall remain evidence-based.

12.315 Cost Learning Candidate

A Cost Learning Candidate may state:

- Provider A averages 18 percent more cost than estimate for five-second video jobs.

- Local Model B has lower marginal cost but higher review cost for Swedish scripts.

- Preview-first reduces premium video waste for Familje-Stunden.

It shall include:

- scope,

- evidence,

- confidence,

- and validity.

12.316 Estimate Calibration

Estimate models should compare expected and confirmed cost.

12.317 Calibration Scope

Calibration shall remain scoped to:

- Provider,

- Account tier,

- Model,

- Capability,

- Input class,

- and Project where relevant.

12.318 Learning Expiry

Cost learning may expire after:

- pricing change,

- Model change,

- Provider billing change,

- or workflow update.

12.319 Cost Prediction Model

A cost prediction model may assist estimation.

It shall not create spending authority.

12.320 Economic Recommendation

The system may recommend:

- cheaper eligible Candidate,

- subscription change,

- budget increase,

- lower variant count,

- local processing,

- or delayed execution.

Recommendations require user or policy acceptance where material.

12.321 Savings Estimate

A Savings Estimate should compare equivalent eligible outcomes.

It shall not claim savings by lowering required quality.

12.322 Avoided Cost

Avoided Cost may result from:

- cache reuse,

- local preprocessing,

- early validation,

- cancelled optional work,

- or successful refund.

12.323 False Savings

A cheaper attempt that requires repeated correction may not represent true savings.

12.324 Economic Efficiency

Economic Efficiency may combine:

- accepted quality,

- confirmed cost,

- latency,

- and human effort.

12.325 Cost per Accepted Output

Cost per Accepted Output includes failed and rejected Attempts required to obtain one accepted result.

12.326 Cost per Capability

Cost per Capability may compare resource paths over time.

12.327 Cost per Project Outcome

Business outcomes may be compared with cost cautiously.

Correlation shall not be treated as certain causation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.328 Budget Utilisation

Budget Utilisation measures:

- confirmed cost,

- provisional cost,

- reservations,

- and remaining capacity.

12.329 Budget Burn Rate

Burn Rate measures spending over time.

12.330 Forecast

A Forecast estimates future spend based on:

- active Plans,

- recurrence,

- current usage,

- and subscription commitments.

12.331 Forecast Confidence

Forecasts shall expose uncertainty.

12.332 Forecast Horizon

Forecasts may be:

- daily,

- weekly,

- monthly,

- quarterly,

- or initiative-based.

12.333 Recurring-Cost Forecast

Recurring Provider subscriptions and scheduled work shall be included.

12.334 Scenario Forecast

Scenario forecasts may compare:

- Economy,

- Balanced,

- Premium,

- Private,

- and Provider migration.

12.335 Economic Dashboard

A user-facing dashboard may show:

- Project spend,

- Provider spend,

- remaining Budgets,

- subscription commitments,

- credits,

- anomalies,

- and forecasts.

The dashboard is a projection.

Canonical records remain authoritative.

12.336 Budget Alert

Alerts may trigger at thresholds such as:

- 50 percent,

- 75 percent,

- 90 percent,

- and 100 percent utilisation.

Thresholds shall be configurable.

12.337 Credit Alert

Credit alerts may trigger before:

- exhaustion,

- expiry,

- or unusual consumption.

12.338 Subscription Alert

Subscription alerts may cover:

- renewal,

- price change,

- low utilisation,

- and cancellation deadline.

12.339 Cost Anomaly Alert

Material anomalies shall notify the appropriate owner.

12.340 Alert Fatigue Control

Economic alerts should be prioritised by consequence.

Routine low-value changes should not overwhelm the user.

12.341 Economic Reporting

Reports may be produced by:

- Project,

- Tenant,

- Provider,

- Capability,

- Model,

- Funding Source,

- and period.

12.342 Project Cost Report

A Project Cost Report should include:

- total confirmed cost,

- provisional cost,

- Provider distribution,

- Capability distribution,

- failed-attempt cost,

- and Budget status.

12.343 Provider Cost Report

A Provider Cost Report should include:

- subscriptions,

- usage,

- credits,

- refunds,

- anomalies,

- and Project attribution.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.344 Capability Cost Report

A Capability Cost Report supports resource comparison.

12.345 Model Cost Report

Model cost reports shall preserve:

- Deployment,

- Account,

- pricing version,

- and quality context.

12.346 Local Compute Report

Local reports may include:

- runtime hours,

- estimated energy,

- hardware occupancy,

- and avoided Provider spend.

12.347 Human-Assisted Cost Report

Manual workflows should include:

- Provider spend,

- operator time where tracked,

- and review cost.

12.348 Cost Export

Economic records may be exported to accounting or analysis systems.

Exports shall preserve:

- source,

- currency,

- scope,

- and confirmation state.

12.349 Cost Import

Provider invoices or billing exports may be imported.

Imports shall be validated and reconciled.

12.350 Invoice Relationship

An invoice may cover several Provider Accounts or Projects.

Omnira shall preserve internal attribution.

12.351 Tax Classification

Tax and accounting classifications may be attached by downstream financial systems.

The Fabric shall not invent them without policy.

12.352 Payment Method

Payment methods belong to financial systems or Provider Accounts.

Raw card or bank credentials shall not enter the Intelligence Fabric.

12.353 Payment Credential Prohibition

The Fabric shall not expose:

- card numbers,

- bank credentials,

- or unrestricted financial credentials

to Agents or Models.

12.354 Purchase Capability

Purchasing subscription or credits is a financial side-effect Capability.

It shall remain separate from ordinary execution.

12.355 Billing Administration

Changing:

- payment method,

- billing address,

- tax details,

- or invoice contact

requires administrative authority.

12.356 Commercial Margin

Omnira may later include a margin in managed plans.

Margin shall be:

- disclosed,

- governed,

- and separated from Provider base cost.

12.357 Margin Transparency

The user should be able to understand whether a managed price includes:

- Provider cost,

- Omnira service fee,

- risk reserve,

- or support.

12.358 Hidden Margin Prohibition

Omnira shall not silently inflate cost while presenting it as direct Provider price.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.359 Routing Neutrality

Commercial margin shall not cause routing to an inferior or more expensive eligible resource against the user’s selected profile.

12.360 Affiliate Relationship

Affiliate income shall be disclosed where it materially affects recommendations.

12.361 Managed Plan

A Managed Plan may bundle:

- credits,

- routing,

- support,

- storage,

- and platform services.

Its limits and pricing shall be explicit.

12.362 Managed Plan Budget

The user’s managed allowance shall remain separate from Omnira’s internal Provider procurement cost.

12.363 Managed Credit Expiry

Managed credit expiry shall be clear and fair.

12.364 Managed Credit Portability

Whether managed credits can be transferred, refunded or rolled over shall be explicit.

12.365 Managed Capacity Isolation

Tenant and Project usage shall remain isolated even when one Omnira Provider Account is shared.

12.366 Economic Conflict of Interest

A conflict exists when Omnira benefits financially from one routing choice.

The conflict shall remain visible to governance.

12.367 User-Benefit Rule

The selected resource shall serve the user’s approved profile and constraints.

Omnira’s margin is subordinate.

12.368 Economic Governance Roles

Relevant roles may include:

- Budget Owner,

- Funding Source Owner,

- Spending Approver,

- Economic Administrator,

- Project Manager,

- Cost Analyst,

- Reconciliation Service,

- and Incident Responder.

12.369 Budget Owner Responsibilities

The Budget Owner defines:

- purpose,

- amount,

- period,

- and scope.

12.370 Funding Source Owner Responsibilities

The Funding Source Owner controls whether the source may be used.

12.371 Spending Approver Responsibilities

The Spending Approver authorises bounded consumption.

12.372 Economic Administrator Responsibilities

The Economic Administrator manages:

- Budgets,

- pricing records,

- subscriptions,

- and economic policy.

They shall not necessarily approve every Project outcome.

12.373 Cost Analyst Responsibilities

The Cost Analyst may inspect:

- trends,

- forecasts,

- and anomalies.

They shall not receive payment credentials unnecessarily.

12.374 Reconciliation Service Responsibilities

The Reconciliation Service compares Provider and Omnira economic evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.375 Separation of Duties

High-risk financial actions may require separation between:

- requester,

- approver,

- executor,

- and reconciler.

12.376 Budget Creation Authority

Creating a Budget requires authority appropriate to its scope.

12.377 Budget Amendment Authority

Increasing a Budget requires new approval.

Reducing or suspending may use broader safety authority.

12.378 Funding Source Connection Authority

Connecting a paid Provider Account does not automatically approve its use.

12.379 Subscription Purchase Authority

Subscription purchase requires explicit authority.

12.380 Refund Request Authority

Requesting a refund may be delegated.

Accepting settlement terms may require owner authority.

12.381 Economic Policy

Economic Policy may define:

- default Routing Profile,

- maximum autonomous spend,

- approval thresholds,

- permitted Funding Sources,

- subscription rules,

- credit rules,

- and anomaly thresholds.

12.382 Platform Economic Policy

Platform policy may define universal controls such as:

- no hidden spend,

- no raw payment credential exposure,

- and no Budget bypass.

12.383 Tenant Economic Policy

Tenant policy may define:

- monthly limits,

- managed Provider use,

- and Project allocation.

12.384 Project Economic Policy

Project policy may define:

- maximum production cost,

- allowed Providers,

- preferred Funding Sources,

- and approval thresholds.

12.385 Capability Economic Policy

Capability policy may define:

- video generation requires reservation,

- low-cost text may use autonomous allowance,

- credit purchases require approval,

- or premium candidate races are prohibited.

12.386 Provider Economic Policy

Provider policy may define:

- maximum monthly spend,

- no auto-top-up,

- or restricted subscription tier.

12.387 Environment Economic Policy

Development environments may have low hard limits.

Production may have larger but stricter approved Budgets.

12.388 Economic Policy Version

Economic policy shall be versioned.

12.389 Policy Conflict

Conflicting budget and Funding Source rules shall fail closed.

12.390 Emergency Economic Policy

Emergency policy may:

- freeze spending,

- block one Provider,

- disable auto-renewal,

- or reduce autonomous thresholds.

Emergency rules shall be temporary and attributable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.391 Economic Event

Material economic events may include:

- BudgetCreated,

- BudgetApproved,

- BudgetReserved,

- ReservationReleased,

- UsageReported,

- ChargeObserved,

- CostConfirmed,

- CreditConsumed,

- CreditRefunded,

- BudgetExhausted,

- CostAnomalyDetected,

- and ReconciliationCompleted.

12.392 Economic Event Identity

Events shall preserve:

- eventId,

- object version,

- correlation,

- causation,

- and time.

12.393 Event Deduplication

Duplicate Provider billing events shall not duplicate cost.

12.394 Event Ordering

Late usage or refund events shall not corrupt newer confirmed state.

They shall create valid adjustments.

12.395 Economic State Durability

Budget, Reservation and Cost state shall survive process restarts.

12.396 Economic Idempotency

Repeated cost-record creation for the same Provider usage shall remain idempotent.

12.397 Economic Concurrency

Concurrent reservations and charges require consistency controls.

12.398 Budget Ledger

A Budget Ledger may represent:

- allocations,

- reservations,

- releases,

- confirmed cost,

- and adjustments.

It shall be append-oriented or preserve equivalent immutable history.

12.399 Economic Source of Truth

Canonical economic records shall have an authoritative governed source.

Provider dashboards and user interfaces are projections or evidence.

12.400 Economic Snapshot

A Snapshot may preserve:

- Budget,

- pricing,

- credits,

- and policy

at a point in time.

12.401 Pricing Snapshot

Executions shall preserve the Pricing Record or Snapshot used for estimation.

12.402 Credit Snapshot

Credit-based approvals should preserve the observed balance and freshness.

12.403 Economic Audit Trail

The audit trail shall preserve:

- Budget creation,

- approval,

- reservation,

- use,

- adjustment,

- refund,

- and closure.

12.404 Economic Data Classification

Economic records may contain:

- Provider relationships,

- Project strategy,

- spending,

- and account information.

They should normally be Project Internal or Confidential according to scope.

12.405 Payment Data Isolation

Sensitive payment information shall remain in approved financial systems.

12.406 Economic Access Control

Permissions may include:

- view own spend,

- view Project spend,

- create Budget,

- approve spend,

- administer Funding Source,

- reconcile,

- and export.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.407 User Cost Visibility

The user should be able to see costs they own or authorised.

12.408 Project Cost Visibility

Project operators may see Project cost without access to unrelated Projects.

12.409 Tenant Cost Visibility

Tenant administrators may see aggregated cost according to role.

12.410 Provider Cost Visibility

Provider cost may reveal contract terms and require restricted access.

12.411 Margin Visibility

Internal procurement margin may be restricted operationally.

User-facing managed price and service fee shall still be transparent.

12.412 Economic Redaction

Redacted views may hide:

- contract rate,

- Provider Account identifier,

- or other protected commercial details.

The canonical record remains unchanged.

12.413 Economic Retention

Retention shall support:

- audit,

- disputes,

- accounting export,

- and historical provenance.

Retention periods may differ by record type.

12.414 Budget Retention

Closed Budgets shall remain historically interpretable.

12.415 Pricing Retention

Historical pricing shall remain available for cost reconstruction.

12.416 Usage Retention

Usage evidence shall remain linked to Executions.

12.417 Refund Retention

Refund and adjustment records shall remain linked to original charges.

12.418 Economic Backup

Economic records shall be backed up according to criticality.

12.419 Economic Recovery

Recovery shall preserve:

- outstanding reservations,

- unresolved costs,

- and Budget state.

12.420 Disaster Recovery

Economic recovery must avoid:

- double reservation,

- duplicate charge attribution,

- and lost Budget consumption.

12.421 Economic API

The control plane should expose governed operations such as:

- create Budget,

- approve Budget,

- get remaining Budget,

- create Reservation,

- consume Reservation,

- release Reservation,

- create Cost Estimate,

- record Usage,

- confirm Cost,

- record Refund,

- reconcile,

- and inspect anomaly.

12.422 Budget Query API

The Budget API should support:

- get active Budget,

- list Budgets by Project,

- inspect allocations,

- inspect reservations,

- and inspect remaining capacity.

12.423 Pricing API

The Pricing API should support:

- retrieve current Pricing Record,

- retrieve historical record,

- estimate usage cost,

- and expose confidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
12.424 Credit API

The Credit API should support:
