- benchmarkId,

- purpose,

- scope,

- Capability,

- Test Suite,

- metrics,

- thresholds,

- sampling,

- evaluator requirements,

- version,

- lifecycle,

- and provenance.

13.140 Benchmark Identity

Every Benchmark shall have stable identity and version.

13.141 Benchmark Purpose

A Benchmark shall state what it is intended to measure.

Examples include:

- Swedish reasoning,

- code architecture conformance,

- Nova and Pling character consistency,

- speech naturalness,

- retrieval relevance,

- or Provider callback reliability.

13.142 Benchmark Scope

Benchmarks may be:

- global,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Capability,

- Model,

- Provider,

- Tool,

- Workflow,

- or production-specific.

13.143 General Benchmark

A General Benchmark measures broad capability.

Its results may have limited Project relevance.

13.144 Project Benchmark

A Project Benchmark reflects real Project requirements.

Project results shall not automatically become universal rankings.

13.145 Production Benchmark

A Production Benchmark uses realistic or historical tasks to predict production suitability.

13.146 Synthetic Benchmark

A Synthetic Benchmark uses generated or constructed Test Cases.

It may improve coverage.

It may not reflect real user distribution.

13.147 Historical Benchmark

A Historical Benchmark uses past requests or accepted Outputs.

Data reuse shall respect classification and rights.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.148 Adversarial Benchmark

An Adversarial Benchmark targets known failure modes.

13.149 Regression Benchmark

A Regression Benchmark detects whether a resource or system became worse after change.

13.150 Conformance Benchmark

A Conformance Benchmark tests whether a resource satisfies a Capability Contract.

13.151 Benchmark Version

Changes to:

- Test Cases,

- labels,

- metrics,

- rubrics,

- thresholds,

- or sampling

shall create a new Benchmark Version.

13.152 Benchmark Lifecycle

Benchmark states may include:

- proposed,

- drafting,

- calibrating,

- approved,

- active,

- restricted,

- deprecated,

- retired,

- and archived.

13.153 Benchmark Owner

Every Benchmark shall have an accountable Owner or Steward.

13.154 Test Case

A Test Case is one bounded evaluation item.

It shall include or reference:

- testCaseId,

- Input,

- expected properties,

- reference answer or rubric,

- classification,

- difficulty,

- tags,

- applicability,

- and provenance.

13.155 Test Case Identity

Every persistent Test Case shall have stable identity and version.

13.156 Test Case Input

Input may be:

- prompt,

- document,

- image,

- audio,

- video,

- repository state,

- structured data,

- or combined multimodal package.

13.157 Reference Answer

A Reference Answer may define:

- exact expected output,

- acceptable range,

- key facts,

- required structure,

- or exemplar.

Reference answers are not always appropriate for creative tasks.

13.158 Reference Asset

Creative benchmarks may use approved reference Assets.

Examples include canonical Nova and Pling images.

13.159 Test Case Difficulty

Difficulty may be classified as:

- basic,

- standard,

- challenging,

- adversarial,

- or expert.

13.160 Test Case Tags

Tags may include:

- language,

- modality,

- Project,

- domain,

- risk,

- Feature,

- and known failure mode.

13.161 Test Case Classification

Test data shall preserve Data Classification.

Protected Test Cases shall not be sent to ineligible Providers.

13.162 Test Case Rights

Benchmark Inputs require valid rights and usage permission.

13.163 Test Case Leakage

Public or repeated Test Cases may become memorised by Models.

Leakage risk shall be considered.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.164 Hidden Test Case

Some Tests may remain hidden from the generation system to preserve validity.

13.165 Test Suite

A Test Suite is a versioned collection of Test Cases.

It shall define:

- inclusion,

- weighting,

- sampling,

- expected coverage,

- and exclusions.

13.166 Test Suite Coverage

Coverage should represent relevant:

- Inputs,

- difficulty,

- languages,

- Features,

- risks,

- and Project conditions.

13.167 Coverage Gap

A Coverage Gap exists when important requirements lack sufficient Tests.

13.168 Test Suite Balance

The Suite should avoid over-representing easy or repetitive cases.

13.169 Test Case Weight

Some Cases may receive greater weight because of:

- frequency,

- consequence,

- or Project importance.

13.170 Benchmark Run

A Benchmark Run executes one Benchmark Version against one or more targets.

It shall include or reference:

- benchmarkRunId,

- Benchmark Version,

- targets,

- environment,

- resource configuration,

- Evaluators,

- start,

- completion,

- cost,

- and provenance.

13.171 Benchmark Target

Targets may include:

- Model Version,

- Deployment,

- Provider Product,

- Tool Version,

- Adapter Version,

- Agent configuration,

- Workflow Version,

- or Routing Policy.

13.172 Benchmark Configuration

The Run shall preserve:

- prompts,

- parameters,

- context limits,

- Tool access,

- temperature,

- seed,

- Runtime,

- hardware,

- and Adapter.

13.173 Benchmark Reproducibility

A reproducible Run requires sufficient configuration evidence.

External moving aliases may reduce reproducibility.

13.174 Benchmark Cost

Benchmarking may consume substantial cost.

Budget and authority remain required.

13.175 Benchmark Sampling

Large Test Suites may use sampling.

Sampling method shall be explicit.

13.176 Full Benchmark Run

A full Run executes every applicable Test Case.

13.177 Incremental Benchmark Run

An incremental Run executes changed or high-risk Cases.

13.178 Canary Benchmark

A Canary Benchmark checks a small critical subset before broader admission.

13.179 Benchmark Metric

A Benchmark Metric aggregates Evaluation Results.

Metrics may include:

- pass rate,

- average score,

- median,

- percentile,

- defect rate,

- cost per pass,

- latency,

- and confidence interval.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.180 Metric Identity

Reusable Metrics shall have stable identity and definition.

13.181 Pass Rate

Pass Rate is the proportion of applicable Test Cases meeting criteria.

13.182 Critical-Failure Rate

Critical-Failure Rate measures blocking failures.

A high average score may still be unacceptable when critical failures exist.

13.183 Average Score

Average Score may hide outliers.

It should be interpreted with distribution evidence.

13.184 Median Score

Median may reduce sensitivity to extreme values.

13.185 Percentile Score

Percentiles may expose lower-tail quality.

13.186 Worst-Case Score

Worst-case performance may matter for safety-critical or public work.

13.187 Cost per Passing Case

This metric combines quality and economic efficiency.

13.188 Latency per Passing Case

This metric measures completed quality rather than raw response speed.

13.189 Human Correction Rate

Correction Rate estimates how often human intervention is required.

13.190 Retry Rate

Retry Rate may reveal resource or prompt weakness.

13.191 Unknown-Outcome Rate

Unknown outcomes affect operational suitability.

13.192 Acceptance Rate

Acceptance Rate reflects real or benchmark acceptance under defined criteria.

13.193 Composite Benchmark Score

A composite score may combine several metrics.

Its weights and limitations shall be explicit.

13.194 Benchmark Confidence

Confidence depends on:

- sample size,

- evaluator reliability,

- test coverage,

- variance,

- and leakage risk.

13.195 Statistical Significance

Comparative claims should consider whether differences are meaningful rather than random variation.

13.196 Practical Significance

A statistically significant difference may be too small to matter operationally.

Practical significance shall be considered.

13.197 Benchmark Ranking

Rankings shall identify:

- Benchmark Version,

- scope,

- date,

- and uncertainty.

No ranking is universally valid.

13.198 Tied Result

Ties or near-equivalence shall remain visible.

13.199 Benchmark Winner

A Benchmark winner is the strongest target under the exact benchmark conditions.

It is not automatically the best production resource.

13.200 Benchmark Interpretation

Interpretation shall consider:

- Capability fit,

- Project fit,

- cost,

- latency,

- privacy,

- rights,

- and operational reliability.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.201 Benchmark Admission

A Model or Provider may require benchmark evidence before production admission.

13.202 Benchmark Expiry

Evidence may expire after:

- Model update,

- Provider drift,

- Adapter change,

- Prompt change,

- or defined period.

13.203 Benchmark Drift

Changes in score over time may indicate drift.

13.204 Benchmark Contamination

A Benchmark may become invalid when:

- answers leak,

- Models are trained on the Test Cases,

- evaluators are tuned to the benchmark,

- or the Suite no longer reflects production.

13.205 Benchmark Gaming

Systems may optimise specifically for a known metric while harming real quality.

The architecture shall use:

- hidden Tests,

- rotating Tests,

- operational evidence,

- and human review

where appropriate.

13.206 Benchmark Retirement

A Benchmark shall be retired when:

- obsolete,

- contaminated,

- redundant,

- or no longer aligned with the Project.

13.207 Historical Benchmark Preservation

Retired Benchmarks and Runs shall remain historically interpretable.

13.208 Resource Evaluation

The Quality System may evaluate:

- Model Versions,

- Deployments,

- Providers,

- Tools,

- Adapters,

- Agents,

- and Workflows.

13.209 Model Evaluation

Model evaluation shall remain:

- Version-specific,

- Capability-specific,

- parameter-aware,

- and Deployment-aware where material.

13.210 Provider Evaluation

Provider evaluation may include:

- reliability,

- callback quality,

- Asset handling,

- consistency,

- billing accuracy,

- and support.

It shall remain distinct from Model output quality.

13.211 Deployment Evaluation

The same Model Version may perform differently across:

- runtime,

- quantisation,

- hardware,

- region,

- and Provider.

13.212 Tool Evaluation

Tools may be evaluated for:

- correctness,

- determinism,

- safety,

- performance,

- and side-effect control.

13.213 Adapter Evaluation

Adapters may be evaluated for:

- request translation,

- parameter preservation,

- output normalisation,

- usage reporting,

- error mapping,

- and callback handling.

13.214 Agent Evaluation

Agent evaluation may assess:

- role adherence,

- tool selection,

- planning,

- authority compliance,

- memory use,

- and completion quality.

Agent identity remains separate from Model performance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.215 Workflow Evaluation

Workflow evaluation may assess:

- completion rate,

- cost,

- latency,

- quality,

- retries,

- human effort,

- and side-effect safety.

13.216 Routing Evaluation

Routing may be evaluated by comparing:

- selected Candidate,

- accepted quality,

- cost,

- fallback,

- and available alternatives.

13.217 Planner Evaluation

Planning may be evaluated for:

- unnecessary Steps,

- missing gates,

- cost accuracy,

- replan rate,

- and successful completion.

13.218 Prompt Evaluation

Prompt or Instruction Set Versions may be evaluated independently from Models.

A poor prompt shall not be misclassified as a Model defect without evidence.

13.219 Retrieval Evaluation

Retrieval quality may include:

- precision,

- recall,

- relevance,

- freshness,

- source quality,

- and citation traceability.

13.220 Memory Retrieval Evaluation

Memory retrieval shall assess:

- correct scope,

- relevance,

- freshness,

- privacy,

- and avoidance of stale or unrelated memory.

13.221 Text Quality

Text quality may include:

- instruction adherence,

- factual accuracy,

- relevance,

- completeness,

- structure,

- clarity,

- tone,

- grammar,

- and audience fit.

13.222 Factual Accuracy

Factual Accuracy measures whether claims are correct under available evidence.

13.223 Groundedness

Groundedness measures whether claims are supported by supplied or retrieved sources.

13.224 Citation Correctness

Citation Correctness measures whether citations support the associated claims.

13.225 Source Quality

Source Quality considers:

- authority,

- primary versus secondary status,

- freshness,

- and reliability.

13.226 Hallucination

A Hallucination is an unsupported or fabricated claim presented as true.

Hallucination severity depends on:

- consequence,

- prominence,

- and correctability.

13.227 Uncertainty Expression

High-quality factual output should express uncertainty when evidence is incomplete.

13.228 Completeness

Completeness measures whether mandatory content is present.

13.229 Relevance

Relevance measures alignment with the actual request and intended use.

13.230 Instruction Adherence

Instruction Adherence measures whether the Output follows applicable instructions and constraints.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.231 Tone

Tone quality is Project- and audience-specific.

13.232 Language Quality

Language quality may include:

- grammar,

- spelling,

- naturalness,

- terminology,

- and locale.

13.233 Swedish Language Quality

Swedish evaluation may include:

- idiomatic phrasing,

- compound words,

- punctuation,

- terminology,

- readability,

- and regional appropriateness.

13.234 Child-Facing Language

Child-facing language shall be assessed for:

- age appropriateness,

- emotional safety,

- clarity,

- warmth,

- and absence of inappropriate complexity.

13.235 Structured Output Quality

Structured output quality may include:

- valid schema,

- required fields,

- correct types,

- semantic correctness,

- and no forbidden fields.

13.236 Code Quality

Code quality may include:

- compilation,

- type correctness,

- tests,

- security,

- maintainability,

- architecture conformance,

- performance,

- and scope compliance.

13.237 Code Syntax

Syntax validation is necessary but insufficient.

13.238 Type Safety

Type checking should use the Project’s actual toolchain where possible.

13.239 Unit Tests

Unit tests validate bounded behaviour.

13.240 Integration Tests

Integration tests validate component interaction.

13.241 End-to-End Tests

End-to-end tests validate complete workflows.

They may be costly and slower.

13.242 Security Tests

Security evaluation may include:

- injection,

- permission bypass,

- secret exposure,

- unsafe file access,

- and dependency risk.

13.243 Architecture Conformance

Code may work while violating:

- Tenant isolation,

- authority boundaries,

- canonical object ownership,

- or repository structure.

Architecture evaluation remains required.

13.244 Patch Scope

A code patch shall be evaluated for whether it changes only the authorised scope.

13.245 Regression Risk

Evaluation shall assess whether existing behaviour was unintentionally changed.

13.246 Repository State

Code evaluation shall preserve:

- branch,

- commit,

- worktree,

- dependency state,

- and test environment.

13.247 Image Quality

Image quality may include:

- composition,

- anatomy,

- identity,

- text rendering,

- resolution,

- artefacts,

- style,

- colour,

- and Project alignment.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.248 Character Identity

Character Identity measures whether a visual Output preserves canonical character features.

13.249 Character Consistency

Character Consistency measures identity stability across:

- poses,

- scenes,

- angles,

- expressions,

- and Outputs.

13.250 Multi-Character Consistency

A scene containing several characters shall preserve each identity without blending or substitution.

13.251 Visual Artefact

Visual artefacts may include:

- malformed limbs,

- merged objects,

- inconsistent eyes,

- broken text,

- duplicate features,

- or background distortion.

13.252 Composition Quality

Composition evaluates:

- framing,

- subject placement,

- balance,

- readability,

- and intended focal point.

13.253 Brand Alignment

Brand alignment measures conformance with:

- visual identity,

- style,

- palette,

- tone,

- and recurring Project patterns.

13.254 Text Rendering

Image text shall be evaluated for:

- spelling,

- legibility,

- placement,

- and style.

13.255 Transparency Quality

Transparent Assets shall preserve:

- clean edges,

- correct alpha,

- and no unintended background.

13.256 Image Edit Fidelity

Image editing shall preserve elements that were not authorised to change.

13.257 Reference Fidelity

Reference-based generation shall be evaluated against the approved reference version.

13.258 Video Quality

Video quality may include:

- identity stability,

- temporal coherence,

- motion,

- camera behaviour,

- frame integrity,

- timing,

- resolution,

- audio synchronisation,

- and artefacts.

13.259 Temporal Consistency

Temporal Consistency measures whether objects and identities remain stable over time.

13.260 Motion Coherence

Motion shall appear physically and narratively coherent for the intended style.

13.261 Camera Consistency

Camera movement shall match the requested direction and avoid unintended jumps.

13.262 Frame Artefact

Frame-level defects may include:

- flicker,

- morphing,

- duplication,

- missing objects,

- and sudden style change.

13.263 Lip Synchronisation

Lip sync shall be evaluated against:

- timing,

- phoneme alignment,

- and naturalness.

13.264 Audio-Visual Synchronisation

Narration, music, effects and visual events shall remain aligned.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.265 Scene Continuity

Adjacent scenes should preserve:

- character state,

- location,

- clothing,

- time,

- and narrative sequence.

13.266 Video Duration

Duration shall satisfy the Output Contract within allowed tolerance.

13.267 Video Resolution

Resolution and aspect ratio shall be validated deterministically.

13.268 Child-Facing Video Review

Child-facing video should receive review for:

- frightening artefacts,

- unsafe motion,

- inappropriate expressions,

- accidental text,

- and emotional tone.

13.269 Voice Quality

Voice quality may include:

- intelligibility,

- pronunciation,

- naturalness,

- identity consistency,

- pacing,

- emotion,

- noise,

- and audience fit.

13.270 Pronunciation

Pronunciation evaluation may use:

- expert review,

- dictionary references,

- automated phonetic comparison,

- or targeted Test Cases.

13.271 Swedish Pronunciation

Swedish voice evaluation should include:

- names,

- compounds,

- place names,

- technical terms,

- and child-facing phrasing.

13.272 Voice Identity

Voice Identity measures consistency with an approved Voice Asset.

It does not prove consent.

13.273 Pacing

Pacing shall match:

- target duration,

- audience,

- emotional tone,

- and media format.

13.274 Emotional Delivery

Emotion should be appropriate and not exaggerated beyond Project intent.

13.275 Audio Artefact

Audio artefacts may include:

- clipping,

- distortion,

- unnatural breath,

- robotic transitions,

- or background noise.

13.276 Speech Timing

Speech timing should align with scene duration and captions.

13.277 Transcription Quality

Transcription may be evaluated through:

- word error rate,

- entity accuracy,

- punctuation,

- speaker attribution,

- and language handling.

13.278 Music Quality

Music quality may include:

- composition,

- loop continuity,

- mood,

- mix,

- originality evidence,

- and rights.

13.279 Sound-Effect Quality

Sound effects should align with:

- action,

- timing,

- volume,

- and audience suitability.

13.280 Multimodal Quality

Multimodal evaluation shall consider consistency across modalities.

Examples include:

- script matches image,

- narration matches text,

- captions match speech,

- video matches story,

- and citations match claims.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.281 Cross-Modal Consistency

A high-quality component may still create a low-quality production when modalities conflict.

13.282 Asset Package Quality

A complete Asset Package may require:

- correct files,

- correct versions,

- correct metadata,

- correct rights,

- and complete provenance.

13.283 Research Quality

Research quality may include:

- source coverage,

- primary sources,

- recency,

- factual support,

- uncertainty,

- and claim traceability.

13.284 Currentness

Time-sensitive work shall evaluate whether information is current enough for the intended use.

13.285 Source Diversity

Source diversity may reduce dependence on one perspective.

It shall not replace source quality.

13.286 Claim-Level Support

Material factual claims should map to supporting evidence.

13.287 Quote Accuracy

Direct quotations shall match the source within permitted use.

13.288 Date Accuracy

Dates and time context shall be verified.

13.289 Entity Accuracy

Names, organisations, products and places shall be verified.

13.290 Numerical Accuracy

Numbers, calculations and comparisons should receive deterministic verification where possible.

13.291 Recommendation Quality

Recommendations may be evaluated for:

- constraint fit,

- evidence,

- cost awareness,

- risk,

- and clarity.

13.292 Decision Quality

Decision-support quality may include:

- alternatives,

- assumptions,

- uncertainty,

- consequences,

- and reversibility.

13.293 Plan Quality

Execution Plans may be evaluated for:

- complete Steps,

- correct dependencies,

- bounded cost,

- bounded retries,

- explicit approvals,

- and Completion Contract.

13.294 Agent Quality

Agent quality may include:

- role fidelity,

- authority compliance,

- memory correctness,

- tool discipline,

- planning quality,

- and truthful state reporting.

13.295 Authority Compliance Evaluation

An Output or action shall be evaluated for whether it stayed inside approved authority.

13.296 Truthful-State Evaluation

The system shall not claim:

- completed,

- published,

- saved,

- approved,

- or verified

without evidence.

13.297 Evaluation Disagreement

Evaluators may disagree.

Disagreement shall be preserved rather than averaged away automatically.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.298 Disagreement Types

Disagreement may result from:

- subjective preference,

- ambiguous rubric,

- evaluator bias,

- insufficient context,

- or genuine uncertainty.

13.299 Disagreement Resolution

Resolution may use:

- additional evaluator,

- expert reviewer,

- clarified rubric,

- or limited-use acceptance.

13.300 Majority Vote

Majority vote may be appropriate for some subjective comparisons.

It shall not override a critical deterministic failure.

13.301 Expert Override

An authorised expert may override lower-confidence evaluators.

The override shall be attributable.

13.302 Reviewer Tie

A tie may result in:

- unresolved state,

- additional review,

- or conservative rejection.

13.303 Inter-Rater Agreement

Agreement metrics may help assess Rubric clarity and Evaluator consistency.

13.304 Model Evaluator Bias

Model Evaluators may favour:

- verbose Outputs,

- familiar style,

- same-Provider generations,

- or certain languages.

Bias shall be tested.

13.305 Position Bias

Pairwise evaluators may prefer the first or second option.

Candidate order should be randomised where practical.

13.306 Length Bias

Longer Outputs may receive inflated scores despite lower relevance.

Rubrics should control for this.

13.307 Style Bias

Evaluators may confuse style preference with correctness.

13.308 Provider Bias

Provider or Model identity should be hidden when not relevant.

13.309 Self-Preference Bias

A Model may prefer Outputs generated by itself or similar Models.

13.310 Human Reviewer Bias

Human review may be affected by:

- fatigue,

- expectation,

- familiarity,

- and creator relationship.

13.311 Bias Mitigation

Mitigation may include:

- blind review,

- calibration,

- multiple evaluators,

- deterministic checks,

- and periodic audit.

13.312 Evaluation Uncertainty

Every non-deterministic Evaluation should preserve uncertainty.

13.313 Confidence Calibration

A stated confidence should correspond meaningfully to observed correctness or agreement.

13.314 Overconfidence

An Evaluator repeatedly expressing high confidence in wrong results is degraded.

13.315 Underconfidence

An Evaluator may be accurate but overly uncertain.

Calibration should distinguish this from poor quality.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.316 Production Evaluation

Production Outputs should be evaluated according to the exact Quality Contract used for delivery.

13.317 Pre-Execution Quality Evidence

Routing may use historical quality evidence before execution.

13.318 In-Execution Evaluation

Evaluation may occur during:

- generation,

- iterative refinement,

- or streaming.

It shall remain bounded.

13.319 Post-Execution Evaluation

The completed Output shall be evaluated before acceptance.

13.320 Pre-Publication Evaluation

Public-facing Output should receive final review after all composition and transformations.

13.321 Post-Publication Monitoring

Published Output may receive later quality or outcome monitoring.

This shall not retroactively change the original Acceptance Decision.

13.322 Sampled Production Review

High-volume low-risk work may use sampled human review.

Sampling rules shall be explicit.

13.323 Full Production Review

High-consequence or child-facing work may require review of every Output.

13.324 Continuous Evaluation

Continuous evaluation monitors production quality over time.

13.325 Evaluation Sampling Policy

Sampling may depend on:

- risk,

- Provider,

- Model,

- Project,

- novelty,

- and recent drift.

13.326 New Resource Sampling

New Models or Providers should receive higher review rates.

13.327 Stable Resource Sampling

Stable resources may receive reduced human sampling while deterministic and automated checks continue.

13.328 Incident Sampling

After a Quality Incident, review rates should increase.

13.329 Quality Monitoring

Quality Monitoring observes:

- acceptance,

- defects,

- retries,

- reviewer disagreement,

- drift,

- and user feedback.

13.330 Quality Trend

Trends may be measured by:

- Dimension,

- Model Version,

- Provider,

- Project,

- Capability,

- and time.

13.331 Quality Drift

Quality Drift is a material change in observed performance.

It may be:

- positive,

- negative,

- sudden,

- gradual,

- global,

- or scoped.

13.332 Drift Signal

Signals may include:

- lower benchmark score,

- higher rejection rate,

- changed refusal behaviour,

- more artefacts,

- worse pronunciation,

- or increased correction effort.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.333 Drift Cause

Possible causes include:

- Model update,

- Provider routing change,

- Adapter change,

- prompt change,

- Project standard change,

- input distribution shift,

- or Evaluator drift.

13.334 Drift Detection

Detection may use:

- control charts,

- threshold comparison,

- periodic benchmark,

- user feedback,

- and manual review.

13.335 Drift Record

A Drift Record shall include:

- driftRecordId,

- target,

- affected Dimensions,

- evidence,

- start time,

- severity,

- suspected cause,

- and status.

13.336 Drift Response

Response may include:

- reduce routing score,

- increase review,

- restrict resource,

- rerun benchmark,

- revert Adapter,

- or suspend production use.

13.337 Quality Incident

A Quality Incident is a material failure affecting trust, user value or public consequence.

Examples include:

- unsupported public claim,

- severe character corruption,

- unsafe child-facing output,

- broken production code,

- wrong language,

- false completion,

- or systematic evaluator failure.

13.338 Quality Incident Severity

Severity may consider:

- audience,

- publication status,

- repeatability,

- cost,

- safety,

- and reversibility.

13.339 Quality Incident Containment

Containment may include:

- stop publication,

- suspend Model,

- disable Provider path,

- increase review,

- withdraw Asset,

- or pause Workflow.

13.340 Quality Incident Investigation

Investigation should inspect:

- Input,

- Plan,

- Routing Decision,

- Model,

- Provider,

- Adapter,

- prompt,

- Evaluations,

- reviewer,

- and Acceptance Decision.

13.341 Quality Incident Recovery

Recovery may require:

- corrected Output,

- new evaluation,

- retraction,

- Model restriction,

- Rubric update,

- or benchmark expansion.

13.342 False Acceptance Incident

A target was accepted despite failing mandatory criteria.

13.343 False Rejection Incident

A valid target was rejected incorrectly.

Repeated false rejection may waste cost and reduce throughput.

13.344 Evaluator Incident

An Evaluator may be systematically incorrect, biased or unavailable.

13.345 Benchmark Incident

A Benchmark may be contaminated, mislabeled or misleading.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.346 Quality Policy

Quality Policy defines mandatory standards and governance.

It may exist at:

- Platform,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Capability,

- audience,

- environment,

- and publication level.

13.347 Platform Quality Policy

Platform policy may require:

- truthful state,

- traceable evaluation,

- and no acceptance without evidence.

13.348 Project Quality Policy

Project policy may define:

- required Dimensions,

- thresholds,

- reviewers,

- and canonical references.

13.349 Capability Quality Policy

Capability policy may define standard evaluation methods.

13.350 Audience Quality Policy

Child-facing and public content may require stronger review.

13.351 Publication Quality Policy

Publication policy may require a final composite Gate.

13.352 Model Admission Quality Policy

New Models may require minimum benchmark evidence.

13.353 Provider Admission Quality Policy

Providers may require operational-quality validation.

13.354 Evaluator Admission Policy

Evaluators shall be calibrated and approved for their scope.

13.355 Quality Policy Version

Every Evaluation and Acceptance Decision shall reference applicable policy versions.

13.356 Emergency Quality Policy

Emergency policy may:

- increase human review,

- prohibit one Model,

- or require expert approval.

It shall be attributable and temporary.

13.357 Quality Evidence

Quality Evidence is the canonical body of information supporting a quality claim or decision.

It may include:

- Evaluation Results,

- Benchmark Runs,

- Human Reviews,

- Test outputs,

- defects,

- user feedback,

- and operational metrics.

13.358 Evidence Scope

Every quality claim shall identify its scope.

13.359 Evidence Freshness

Evidence shall identify when it was produced and when review is due.

13.360 Evidence Confidence

Confidence shall reflect:

- sample size,

- evaluator quality,

- relevance,

- and recency.

13.361 Evidence Conflict

Conflicting evidence shall remain visible.

13.362 Evidence Aggregation

Aggregated evidence shall preserve the underlying results.

13.363 Evidence Weight

Evidence may receive different weight based on:

- directness,

- Project relevance,

- recency,

- independence,

- and sample size.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.364 External Benchmark Evidence

External benchmarks may support discovery and comparison.

They shall preserve source and methodology.

13.365 Internal Benchmark Evidence

Internal evidence should reflect Omnira requirements.

13.366 Production Evidence

Real production acceptance may be highly relevant but affected by selection bias.

13.367 Human Preference Evidence

Human preference is important for creative work.

It remains subjective and scoped.

13.368 User Complaint Evidence

Complaints may signal defects or changing expectations.

13.369 Absence of Complaint

No complaint does not prove high quality.

13.370 Evaluation Learning

The Fabric may create governed Learning Candidates from quality evidence.

Examples include:

- Model A is stronger for Swedish architecture chapters.

- Provider B creates fewer Nova identity defects.

- Evaluation prompt C over-rewards verbosity.

- Preview-first reduces final video rejection.

13.371 Learning Candidate Structure

A Quality Learning Candidate shall include:

- claim,

- target,

- Capability,

- Project scope,

- evidence,

- confidence,

- validity,

- and proposed use.

13.372 Learning Admission

Learning shall not affect routing or policy until admitted through governance.

13.373 Learning Scope

Learning may be:

- global,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Capability,

- Workflow,

- Model Version,

- or Provider Account-specific.

13.374 Learning Expiry

Learning shall expire or be reviewed after relevant changes.

13.375 Negative Quality Learning

A weak result shall not automatically create a permanent global ban.

13.376 Positive Quality Learning

A strong result shall not automatically create universal preference.

13.377 Evaluator Learning

Evaluator calibration may improve based on expert-labelled Cases.

13.378 Benchmark Evolution

Benchmarks may evolve to include newly discovered defects.

13.379 Memory Admission

Accepted quality learning may enter governed Memory.

Raw Evaluations shall remain in the evidence system unless separately admitted.

13.380 Intelligence Graph Relationship

The Intelligence Graph may represent:

- target,

- evaluated by,

- passed,

- failed,

- benchmarked against,

- contains defect,

- accepted by,

- and supersedes.

The Quality System remains authoritative for Evaluation state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.381 Routing Relationship

Routing uses quality evidence.

Routing does not own or redefine the evidence.

13.382 Planning Relationship

Planning defines required Quality Gates.

The Quality System executes and records them.

13.383 Execution Relationship

Execution produces the Outputs and evidence to be evaluated.

13.384 Asset Relationship

Accepted Outputs may become Asset Candidates.

Asset canonicalisation remains separate.

13.385 Provider Relationship

Provider success and Provider metadata are evidence.

They do not replace evaluation.

13.386 Model Registry Relationship

Model quality claims shall reference exact Model Version and relevant Deployment.

13.387 Capability Registry Relationship

Evaluation shall reference the Capability Version being tested.

13.388 Cost Relationship

Evaluation cost and cost per accepted Output shall remain measurable.

13.389 Approval Relationship

Quality acceptance and user approval may be separate Decisions.

13.390 Publication Relationship

Publication requires accepted final Output and publication authority.

13.391 Observability Relationship

Quality metrics and drift signals shall integrate with Observability.

13.392 Quality API

The Quality Control Plane should expose governed operations such as:

- create Quality Contract,

- create Evaluation Plan,

- register Evaluator,

- create Test Case,

- create Benchmark,

- run Evaluation,

- run Benchmark,

- record Human Review,

- create Acceptance Decision,

- inspect Defects,

- detect drift,

- and retrieve evidence.

13.393 Quality Contract API

The API should support:

- get effective Contract,

- resolve composition,

- inspect Floors,

- inspect Targets,

- and inspect required Evaluators.

13.394 Evaluation API

The API should support:

- submit target,

- execute method,

- retrieve Results,

- retry evaluator,

- and dispute Result.

13.395 Benchmark API

The API should support:

- create Version,

- execute Run,

- compare targets,

- inspect coverage,

- and retire Benchmark.

13.396 Acceptance API

The API should support:

- evaluate Gate,

- record Decision,

- apply conditions,

- and supersede after target change.

13.397 Quality Access Control

Permissions may include:

- view evidence,

- create Contract,

- run Evaluation,

- review,

- accept,

- waive Defect,

- administer Benchmark,

- and alter thresholds.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.398 Reviewer Permission

A reviewer may evaluate only authorised:

- Projects,

- data,

- Dimensions,

- and consequence levels.

13.399 Acceptance Permission

Acceptance authority may be narrower than review authority.

13.400 Benchmark Administration Permission

Changing Test Cases, labels or thresholds requires governance authority.

13.401 Quality Data Classification

Evaluation Inputs and Results inherit appropriate classification from:

- target,

- Project,

- and evidence.

13.402 Reviewer Data Access

Reviewers shall receive only the data necessary for their evaluation.

13.403 External Evaluator Privacy

Sending protected Outputs to an external Evaluator requires separate eligibility.

13.404 Benchmark Data Isolation

Private Benchmark cases shall remain isolated by Tenant and Project.

13.405 Quality Logging

Logs shall preserve identifiers and status without exposing protected Inputs unnecessarily.

13.406 Evaluation Retention

Retention shall preserve enough evidence for:

- audit,

- routing,

- Incident review,

- and historical interpretation.

13.407 Benchmark Retention

Historical Benchmark Versions and Runs shall remain queryable.

13.408 Human Review Retention

Review notes may contain sensitive or subjective content.

Access shall be scoped.

13.409 Quality Backup

Quality Contracts, Results, Benchmarks and Acceptance Decisions shall be backed up according to criticality.

13.410 Quality Integrity

Important quality records should support:

- immutable versioning,

- checksums,

- signed events,

- or equivalent integrity protection.

13.411 Quality Event

Material events may include:

- EvaluationRequested,

- EvaluationStarted,

- EvaluationCompleted,

- DefectDetected,

- QualityGatePassed,

- QualityGateFailed,

- AcceptanceGranted,

- AcceptanceRejected,

- BenchmarkCompleted,

- DriftDetected,

- and QualityIncidentOpened.

13.412 Quality Event Identity

Events shall preserve:

- eventId,

- target,

- object version,

- correlation,

- causation,

- and time.

13.413 Event Deduplication

Duplicate Evaluation events shall not duplicate Acceptance Decisions.

13.414 Event Ordering

Late Results shall not overwrite newer target versions or Decisions.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.415 Quality State Durability

Evaluation and Gate state shall survive process restarts.

13.416 Evaluation Idempotency

Repeated request for the same deterministic evaluation should not create conflicting duplicate results.

13.417 Concurrent Evaluation

Several Evaluators may run in parallel.

Their Results shall remain separately attributable.

13.418 Quality Performance

The evaluation system should be fast enough to support production without weakening required assurance.

13.419 Evaluation Latency

Evaluation latency shall be included in deadline planning.

13.420 Evaluation Availability

If a required Evaluator is unavailable, the Gate shall:

- wait,

- use an approved alternate Evaluator,

- or fail closed.

13.421 Evaluator Fallback

Fallback Evaluators shall be qualified for the same Dimensions and consequence level.

13.422 Evaluation Retry

Evaluator technical failure may be retried within bounded policy.

13.423 Evaluation Unknown Outcome

Unknown evaluator state shall not become pass or fail without reconciliation.

13.424 Quality Cache

Deterministic Evaluation Results may be cached when the target is immutable.

Cache keys shall include:

- target version,

- Evaluation Method,

- Evaluator Version,

- and Quality Contract Version.

13.425 Cached Evaluation Invalidation

Target mutation or evaluator change shall invalidate cached Results.

13.426 Human Review Cache Prohibition

A previous human review shall not automatically accept a modified target.

13.427 Stage 1 Quality Objective

Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy quality system capable of evaluating representative Omnira Outputs and resource candidates.

The objective is not to build a universal benchmark laboratory.

Stage 1 shall prove:

- Quality Contracts,

- Quality Floors,

- Evaluation Plans,

- deterministic checks,

- Model-based evaluation,

- Human Review,

- Quality Gates,

- Acceptance Decisions,

- Project benchmarks,

- quality evidence for routing,

- and drift-aware lifecycle.

13.428 Stage 1 Quality Objects

Stage 1 should implement or represent:

- Quality Dimension,

- Quality Contract,

- Evaluation Plan,

- Evaluator,

- Evaluation Run,

- Evaluation Result,

- Defect,

- Quality Gate,

- Acceptance Decision,

- Test Case,

- Test Suite,

- Benchmark,

- Benchmark Run,

- and Quality Evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.429 Stage 1 Quality Contract Object

The Stage 1 Quality Contract should include:

- qualityContractId,

- scope,

- Capability,

- Dimensions,

- Floors,

- Targets,

- Acceptance Criteria,

- required Evaluators,

- lifecycle,

- and version.

13.430 Stage 1 Evaluation Plan Object

The Stage 1 Evaluation Plan should include:

- evaluationPlanId,

- target type,

- Quality Contract,

- Methods,

- Evaluators,

- thresholds,

- human-review requirement,

- and version.

13.431 Stage 1 Evaluation Result Object

The Stage 1 Evaluation Result should include:

- evaluationResultId,

- target,

- Evaluator,

- Dimension,

- Score,

- confidence,

- pass state,

- evidence,

- and createdAt.

13.432 Stage 1 Defect Object

The Stage 1 Defect should include:

- defectId,

- target,

- Dimension,

- severity,

- description,

- evidence,

- status,

- and provenance.

13.433 Stage 1 Acceptance Decision Object

The Stage 1 Acceptance Decision should include:

- acceptanceDecisionId,

- target,

- Quality Contract Version,

- Evaluation Results,

- decision,

- conditions,

- approver or policy,

- intended use,

- and time.

13.434 Stage 1 Benchmark Object

The Stage 1 Benchmark should include:

- benchmarkId,

- purpose,

- Capability,

- Test Suite,

- metrics,

- Evaluators,

- lifecycle,

- and version.

13.435 Stage 1 Benchmark Run Object

The Stage 1 Benchmark Run should include:

- benchmarkRunId,

- Benchmark Version,

- target resource,

- configuration,

- environment,

- Results,

- cost,

- and time.

13.436 Stage 1 Deterministic Evaluations

Stage 1 should support deterministic checks such as:

- JSON schema validation,

- file existence,

- checksum,

- image dimensions,

- video duration,

- audio format,

- TypeScript type checking,

- unit tests,

- and required-section detection.

13.437 Stage 1 Model-Based Evaluations

Stage 1 may use approved Models for:

- relevance,

- factual support,

- style,

- character consistency,

- and rubric conformance.

Model-based Results shall preserve evaluator Version.

13.438 Stage 1 Human Reviews

Stage 1 shall support Human Review for:

- child-facing media,

- public factual content,

- canonical architecture approval,

- voice quality,

- and final creative acceptance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.439 Stage 1 Quality Gates

Stage 1 should support:

- automatic technical Gate,

- automated semantic Gate,

- Human Review Gate,

- and Composite Gate.

13.440 Stage 1 Benchmark Categories

Stage 1 should include representative benchmarks for:

- external text or reasoning,

- local text or reasoning,

- Swedish language,

- image generation,

- voice synthesis,

- video or multimodal production,

- and code generation.

13.441 Stage 1 Project Benchmarks

Stage 1 should include at least one Project-specific benchmark for:

- Familje-Stunden,

- The Prompt,

- GainPilot,

- and Omnira software.

13.442 Stage 1 Familje-Stunden Benchmark

The Familje-Stunden benchmark should include:

- Nova identity,

- Pling identity,

- multi-character consistency,

- child-safe expression,

- colour consistency,

- Swedish narration,

- and scene continuity.

13.443 Stage 1 The Prompt Benchmark

The Prompt benchmark should include:

- source recency,

- primary-source use,

- claim support,

- citation correctness,

- Swedish script clarity,

- and fact versus interpretation separation.

13.444 Stage 1 GainPilot Benchmark

The GainPilot benchmark should include:

- exercise terminology,

- Swedish clarity,

- brand tone,

- practical usefulness,

- and short-form production fit.

13.445 Stage 1 Omnira Code Benchmark

The Omnira code benchmark should include:

- TypeScript correctness,

- test success,

- Tenant isolation,

- authority boundaries,

- repository scope,

- and architecture conformance.

13.446 Stage 1 Resource Admission

A production Model or Provider path should require:

- Capability conformance,

- minimum benchmark evidence,

- no unresolved critical defects,

- and approved lifecycle.

13.447 Stage 1 Routing Evidence

Routing should receive:

- Capability-specific quality score,

- confidence,

- evidence freshness,

- Project scope,

- and acceptance rate.

13.448 Stage 1 Quality Monitoring

Stage 1 should monitor:

- rejection rate,

- retry rate,

- critical defect rate,

- reviewer disagreement,

- and Model or Provider drift.

13.449 Stage 1 Evaluation API

Stage 1 should support:

- create Evaluation Run,

- execute Evaluator,

- record Human Review,

- retrieve Results,

- create Defect,

- evaluate Gate,

- and create Acceptance Decision.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.450 Stage 1 Benchmark API

Stage 1 should support:

- register Test Cases,

- create Benchmark Version,

- run Benchmark,

- compare targets,

- and retrieve score summary.

13.451 Stage 1 Quality Acceptance Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Quality Contract references exact Capability.

2. Quality Floor remains distinct from Quality Target.

3. Acceptance Criteria remain distinct from individual Scores.

4. Evaluation references exact target version.

5. Evaluator identity is recorded.

6. Model Evaluator Version is recorded.

7. Tool Evaluator Version is recorded.

8. Human Reviewer identity is recorded.

9. Unknown score does not become pass.

10. Blocking Defect prevents acceptance.

11. Advisory Defect does not automatically block.

12. Accepted-with-conditions state enforces conditions.

13. Limited-use acceptance cannot become publication approval.

14. Modified Output invalidates prior acceptance.

15. Rejected Output remains preserved where policy permits.

16. Evaluation cost is attributable.

17. Quality Gate cannot pass without required Results.

18. Human-review timeout does not fabricate approval.

19. Acceptance Decision references Quality Contract Version.

20. Historical Decisions remain immutable.

13.452 Stage 1 Deterministic Evaluation Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Invalid schema fails.

2. Missing required field fails.

3. Wrong image dimensions fail.

4. Wrong video aspect ratio fails.

5. Wrong audio format fails.

6. Missing required chapter section fails.

7. Type-check failure blocks code acceptance.

8. Unit-test failure creates Defect.

9. Checksum mismatch fails Asset integrity.

10. Deterministic rerun produces the same Result.

11. Tool Version is preserved.

12. Target mutation invalidates cached Result.

13. Error output is preserved without secrets.

14. Evaluation timeout produces failure or unknown, not pass.

15. Deterministic Result remains linked to exact target.

13.453 Stage 1 Model-Evaluator Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Evaluator Model Version is explicit.

2. Evaluation prompt or Rubric Version is explicit.

3. Temperature and relevant settings are preserved.

4. Same generator is not sole high-risk evaluator.

5. Provider identity may be hidden for blind review.

6. Unknown evaluator result remains unknown.

7. Evaluator refusal does not become target failure automatically.

8. Evaluator drift triggers recalibration.

9. Pairwise candidate order is randomised where required.

10. Length bias is tested.

11. Self-preference bias is tested.

12. Model-based Result includes explanation.

13. Protected target is sent only to eligible Evaluator.

14. Evaluation cost is reserved.

15. Evaluator fallback is qualified.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.454 Stage 1 Human Review Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Reviewer has Project scope.

2. Reviewer has required role.

3. Reviewer sees only necessary data.

4. Review uses exact Rubric Version.

5. Review decision is attributable.

6. Reviewer conflict is disclosed.

7. Reviewer may request revision.

8. Reviewer may accept with conditions where authorised.

9. Reviewer cannot waive critical policy requirement.

10. Review timeout remains unresolved.

11. Modified target requires new review.

12. Reviewer disagreement remains visible.

13. Expert override is attributable.

14. Human notes retain classification.

15. Human approval remains separate from Provider success.

13.455 Stage 1 Benchmark Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Benchmark has stable identity and version.

2. Test Cases have stable identity.

3. Test Suite preserves coverage metadata.

4. Benchmark target identifies exact Model Version.

5. Deployment and Adapter are recorded.

6. Parameters are recorded.

7. Hidden Tests remain protected.

8. Protected Test Cases respect data policy.

9. Full and sampled Runs remain distinguishable.

10. Critical-failure rate is reported.

11. Average score does not hide critical failures.

12. Benchmark confidence is reported.

13. Benchmark cost is recorded.

14. Benchmark change creates new Version.

15. Retired Benchmark remains historically queryable.

13.456 Stage 1 Routing Quality Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Quality evidence is Capability-specific.

2. Quality evidence is Project-scoped where appropriate.

3. Stale evidence lowers confidence.

4. Candidate below Quality Floor is ineligible.

5. Premium prioritises stronger quality evidence within Budget.

6. Economy cannot lower the Floor.

7. Unknown quality does not receive favourable score.

8. One accepted Output does not create global preference.

9. Repeated rejection lowers candidate suitability.

10. Model update invalidates stale evidence.

11. Project benchmark may outweigh generic benchmark.

12. Critical defect can disable candidate.

13. Human preference remains distinct from factual correctness.

14. Provider reputation is not sufficient evidence.

15. Routing Decision references the quality evidence used.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.457 Stage 1 Text Quality Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Required sections are present.

2. Instruction adherence is evaluated.

3. Unsupported factual claims are detected.

4. Citations support associated claims.

5. Dates are verified.

6. Numbers are checked.

7. Uncertainty is expressed appropriately.

8. Swedish grammar is evaluated.

9. Project tone is evaluated.

10. Excessive verbosity may be detected when relevant.

11. Missing source support creates blocking Defect for public news.

12. Creative writing is not incorrectly judged by factual rubric.

13. Structured Output remains valid.

14. Human reviewer can identify subtle tone failure.

15. Acceptance remains use-specific.

13.458 Stage 1 Code Quality Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Code compiles.

2. Type checks pass.

3. Unit tests pass.

4. Integration tests pass where required.

5. No unauthorised files changed.

6. Tenant isolation is preserved.

7. Authority checks are preserved.

8. Secrets are not introduced.

9. Architecture contracts are followed.

10. Regression risk is assessed.

11. Repository branch and commit are recorded.

12. Generated patch remains reviewable.

13. Test environment is identified.

14. Code success does not imply merge authority.

15. Acceptance does not imply deployment authority.

13.459 Stage 1 Image Quality Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Required dimensions are correct.

2. Aspect ratio is correct.

3. Nova identity is preserved.

4. Pling identity is preserved.

5. Multi-character scenes preserve both characters.

6. No severe anatomy defects exist.

7. Text is legible and correctly spelled.

8. Background matches request.

9. Colour and style align with Project.

10. Transparency is correct where required.

11. Reference image version is recorded.

12. Image edit preserves protected elements.

13. Child-facing content receives human review.

14. Commercial rights remain separately validated.

15. Accepted image version remains immutable.

13.460 Stage 1 Video Quality Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Duration matches contract.

2. Resolution matches contract.

3. Aspect ratio matches contract.

4. Character identity remains stable across frames.

5. Motion is coherent.

6. No severe morphing exists.

7. Camera movement matches request.

8. Scene continuity is preserved.

9. Narration and video timing align.

10. Captions match spoken content.

11. Child-facing review passes.

12. Provider completion does not equal quality acceptance.

13. Preview acceptance does not automatically accept final render.

14. Premium retry requires new evaluation.

15. Final composed master receives complete review.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.461 Stage 1 Voice Quality Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Audio format is correct.

2. Duration is within tolerance.

3. Swedish pronunciation is acceptable.

4. Names are pronounced correctly.

5. Pacing matches intended audience.

6. Voice identity is consistent.

7. No severe artefacts exist.

8. Emotional delivery matches the script.

9. Audio level is acceptable.

10. Speech aligns with captions.

11. Voice quality remains distinct from consent.

12. New Voice Version requires evaluation.

13. Model update may require recalibration.

14. Human reviewer may request pronunciation correction.

15. Accepted narration remains linked to exact Voice and Model.

13.462 Stage 1 Multimodal Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Script matches final narration.

2. Narration matches captions.

3. Visuals match story sequence.

4. Character references match final scenes.

5. Final composition uses accepted component versions.

6. No rejected component enters the master.

7. Provenance links every modality.

8. Rights remain valid across all components.

9. Timing is coherent.

10. Final master receives a composite Gate.

11. Derivatives preserve master relationship.

12. Modified derivative receives relevant evaluation.

13. One strong modality does not hide another modality’s failure.

14. Cross-modal contradictions create Defect.

15. Production acceptance remains separate from publication.

13.463 Stage 1 Drift Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Model Version change triggers benchmark review.

2. Moving alias reduces evidence confidence.

3. Adapter update triggers regression tests.

4. Provider quality regression increases review rate.

5. Evaluator drift triggers recalibration.

6. Project standard change creates new Quality Contract Version.

7. Increased rejection rate creates drift signal.

8. Drift remains scoped to affected Capability.

9. Drift response does not erase prior evidence.

10. Resource may be restricted pending review.

11. Recovery requires fresh evidence.

12. False drift alert may be closed with reason.

13. Benchmark contamination triggers retirement.

14. Quality trend remains time-aware.

15. Production monitoring preserves privacy.

sectionTitles: 13.465 Applied Example — Nova and Pling Character Benchmark
text:
13.464 Stage 1 Quality Incident Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. False public claim opens Quality Incident.

2. Severe child-facing visual defect blocks publication.

3. Broken production code blocks delivery.

4. False acceptance is traced to Evaluator and Gate.

5. Affected Outputs and Assets are identified.

6. Routing Candidate may be suspended.

7. Review sampling increases after Incident.

8. Corrected Output receives new Evaluation.

9. Original Acceptance Decision remains historical.

10. Retraction or replacement is recorded.

11. Cost of failed quality remains attributed.

12. Provider and Model impact remain distinct.

13. Root cause may be prompt rather than Model.

14. Incident closure requires evidence.

15. Learning Candidate may be created after review.

13.465 Applied Example — Nova and Pling Character Benchmark

The Familje-Stunden character benchmark may contain Test Cases for:

- Nova alone in several poses,

- Pling alone in several poses,

- Nova and Pling together,

- close-up expressions,

- movement,

- changing camera angle,

- indoor and outdoor scenes,

- school clothing,

- seasonal clothing,

- and interaction with objects.

Quality Dimensions may include:

- face identity,

- body proportions,

- colour consistency,

- clothing consistency,

- expression,

- species or character integrity,

- multi-character separation,

- and child-facing suitability.

The benchmark should use approved canonical reference Assets.

Generic image aesthetics shall not outweigh character identity.

13.466 Nova Identity Evaluation

A Nova evaluation may compare:

- face shape,

- hair,

- eyes,

- proportions,

- clothing,

- expression,

- and recurring visual markers.

The exact canonical Asset Version shall be recorded.

13.467 Pling Identity Evaluation

A Pling evaluation may compare:

- body shape,

- colours,

- facial features,

- size relative to Nova,

- and recurring design markers.

13.468 Multi-Character Evaluation

The evaluator shall verify that:

- Nova remains Nova,

- Pling remains Pling,

- neither character merges into the other,

- relative scale remains plausible,

- and interaction remains readable.

13.469 Nova and Pling Video Gate

A character-critical scene may require:

1. Technical video checks pass.

2. Nova identity passes.

3. Pling identity passes.

4. Temporal consistency passes.

5. No severe artefact exists.

6. Child-facing review passes.

7. Human Project review accepts the scene.

A Provider success state is insufficient.

text:
13.470 Nova and Pling Premium Escalation Evaluation

A failed Economy preview may be retried or escalated only when the Evaluation Result identifies a defect that premium routing is expected to improve.

Premium escalation shall not occur merely because the reviewer prefers a different style.

13.471 Applied Example — Familje-Stunden Narration

The narration Quality Contract may require:

- correct Swedish pronunciation,

- warm child-facing tone,

- no frightening delivery,

- correct names,

- target duration,

- clear pauses,

- and acceptable noise level.

Human review may be mandatory for the final master narration.

13.472 Applied Example — The Prompt Research Evaluation

A The Prompt research Output may require:

- primary or authoritative sources,

- current dates,

- claim-level support,

- clear distinction between fact and interpretation,

- no unsupported quotation,

- and explicit uncertainty.

A fluent script shall be rejected when source support fails.

13.473 The Prompt Citation Gate

The Gate may require:

- every material claim maps to a source,

- citations support the exact claim,

- sources are current enough,

- and conflicting evidence is disclosed.

13.474 The Prompt Final Media Gate

After narration, avatar and editing, the final video shall be checked again for:

- factual consistency,

- caption accuracy,

- title accuracy,

- and removal of obsolete statements.

13.475 Applied Example — GainPilot Exercise Content

A GainPilot Quality Contract may require:

- correct exercise terminology,

- no unsupported medical claim,

- clear Swedish instructions,

- practical usefulness,

- brand tone,

- and correct visual exercise identification.

A visually strong reel may still fail when the exercise advice is wrong.

13.476 GainPilot Short-Form Quality

Short-form media may use a lower production complexity than Familje-Stunden.

The Quality Floor remains appropriate to the intended use.

13.477 Applied Example — Omnira Architecture Chapter

A canonical Omnira chapter may be evaluated for:

- completeness,

- consistency with earlier chapters,

- correct object boundaries,

- normative clarity,

- absence of implementation overclaim,

- Stage 1 usefulness,

- and internal terminology.

A long chapter may still fail if it contradicts canonical ownership boundaries.

text:
13.478 Omnira Chapter Gate

The Gate may require:

- filename and title correct,

- all required domains covered,

- canonical contracts included,

- anti-patterns included,

- Stage 1 requirements included,

- no contradiction with approved doctrine,

- and human approval.

13.479 Applied Example — Omnira Code Patch

A code patch may require:

- exact repository scope,

- type checking,

- tests,

- no secret exposure,

- correct Tenant isolation,

- and architecture conformance.

The patch may be accepted as a candidate while still lacking:

- commit,

- push,

- merge,

- or deployment authority.

13.480 Applied Example — Local Confidential Analysis

A private local analysis may use local Evaluators.

The Quality Contract may require:

- source section traceability,

- factual consistency,

- no external processing,

- and explicit uncertainty.

If no eligible local Evaluator exists, the result may require human local review.

13.481 Applied Example — Provider Comparison

A comparison between two video Providers should preserve:

- same Test Cases,

- same reference Assets,

- comparable duration,

- comparable resolution,

- same Quality Contract,

- full cost,

- and evaluator blindness.

Different conditions invalidate simplistic ranking.

13.482 Applied Example — Human-Assisted Creative Review

A human-assisted OpenArt workflow may generate several variants.

The Evaluation system shall preserve:

- every variant,

- Provider cost,

- reviewer selection,

- rejection reasons,

- and accepted Output.

The chosen variant shall not erase the cost or provenance of rejected variants.

13.483 Anti-Pattern — One Universal Quality Score

No single global score shall represent every Capability and Project.

13.484 Anti-Pattern — Provider Success Equals Acceptance

Provider completion is only execution evidence.

13.485 Anti-Pattern — Expensive Equals High Quality

Price shall not replace evaluation.

13.486 Anti-Pattern — Famous Model Equals Suitable Model

13.487 Anti-Pattern — Generator Grades Itself

Self-evaluation shall not be the only high-consequence Gate.

13.488 Anti-Pattern — Human Approval Without Criteria

Human review shall use a defined purpose or Rubric.

13.527 Future Quality Architecture

Future versions may support:

- automated multimodal defect detection,

- expert-review marketplaces,

- continuous benchmark generation,

- privacy-preserving federated evaluation,

- active learning,

- causal quality analysis,

- synthetic adversarial Test generation,

- user-personalised preference models,

- real-time voice quality monitoring,

- and automated benchmark contamination detection.

Future evolution must preserve:

- explicit Quality Contracts,

- evaluator identity,

- evidence,

- uncertainty,

- Project scope,

- and human authority.

Future Tenants may share aggregate benchmark evidence without sharing protected Test Cases or Outputs.

13.529 Privacy-Preserving Benchmarking

Secure aggregation or local evaluation may allow comparison while preserving confidential data.

13.530 Active Test Selection

The system may choose high-information Test Cases based on uncertainty.

Selection shall remain governed.

13.531 Adaptive Sampling

Review rate may change based on:

- drift,

- confidence,

- novelty,

- and consequence.

13.532 Personal Preference Model

A user-specific preference model may help creative evaluation.

It shall remain separate from factual and safety criteria.

13.533 Project Aesthetic Model

A Project may develop a governed aesthetic evaluator.

It shall preserve:

- training evidence,

- scope,

- and human override.

13.534 Automated Character Validator

Future systems may compare generated characters with canonical embeddings or visual identity models.

Automated Results shall remain subject to human review for critical Assets.

13.535 Automated Factual Verifier

A future verifier may map claims to sources automatically.

Source quality and currentness shall remain explicit.

13.536 Quality Forecast

The system may estimate acceptance probability before execution.

Forecasts shall not replace actual evaluation.

13.537 Quality-Cost Frontier

The Fabric may model the trade-off between:

- expected quality,

- cost,

- latency,

- and privacy.

The frontier supports routing.

It does not change mandatory Floors.

13.538 Quality Success Criteria

The quality architecture succeeds when:

- every meaningful Output has a clear intended Quality Contract,

- acceptance is evidence-based,

- deterministic and subjective checks remain distinct,

- Project-specific requirements are preserved,

- evaluators are identifiable,

- benchmarks remain versioned,

- drift is detectable,

- rejected Outputs remain attributable,

- routing receives trustworthy evidence,

- and publication cannot occur by Provider success alone.

13.539 Quality Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- one universal score drives every task,

- Provider success becomes acceptance,

- evaluation target version is unknown,

- evaluator identity is missing,

- benchmark scope is hidden,

- human approval lacks criteria,

- critical defects are averaged away,

- child-facing content bypasses review,

- stale evidence is presented as current,

- or acceptance is reused after material mutation.

13.540 Canonical Quality Dimension Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Quality Dimension contract:

1. Every reusable Quality Dimension SHALL have stable identity.

2. Every Dimension SHALL have a clear definition.

3. Every Dimension SHALL identify applicable Capabilities.

4. Every Dimension SHALL define measurement direction.

5. Every Dimension SHALL remain distinct from Evaluator.

6. Every Dimension SHALL remain distinct from Metric.

7. Critical and advisory Dimensions SHALL remain distinguishable.

8. Dimension interpretation SHALL remain Project- and use-aware.

9. Dimension changes SHALL be versioned.

10. Unknown applicability SHALL NOT become automatic inclusion.

11. Factual, stylistic, safety and rights properties SHALL remain distinct.

12. Composite quality SHALL preserve underlying Dimensions.

13. Dimension evidence SHALL remain traceable.

14. Project-specific Dimensions SHALL remain scoped.

15. Historical Dimension definitions SHALL remain interpretable.

13.541 Canonical Quality Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Quality Contract:

1. Every meaningful production Output SHALL reference a Quality Contract or approved equivalent.

2. Every Quality Contract SHALL have stable identity and version.

3. Every Contract SHALL identify its scope.

4. Every Contract SHALL identify Capability or Output type.

5. Every Contract SHALL identify mandatory Dimensions.

6. Every Contract SHALL identify Quality Floors.

7. Every Contract SHOULD identify Quality Targets where useful.

8. Acceptance Criteria SHALL remain explicit.

9. Required Evaluators SHALL remain explicit.

10. Required Human Review SHALL remain explicit.

11. Critical defects SHALL block acceptance unless policy explicitly permits a scoped waiver.

12. Lower-level Contracts SHALL NOT silently weaken mandatory higher-level Floors.

13. Contract composition SHALL remain traceable.

14. Project-specific requirements SHALL remain Project-scoped.

15. Contract changes SHALL create new Versions.

16. Executions and Evaluations SHALL reference the exact Version.

17. Quality Contract SHALL remain separate from rights and authority.

18. Quality Contract SHALL remain separate from Routing Profile.

19. Expired or superseded Contracts SHALL remain historically resolvable.

20. Contracts SHALL be human- and machine-readable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric

13.542 Canonical Evaluation Plan Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Evaluation Plan:

1. Every Evaluation Plan SHALL have stable identity and version.

2. It SHALL identify the Evaluation Target type.

3. It SHALL reference the applicable Quality Contract.

4. It SHALL identify Evaluation Methods.

5. It SHALL identify Evaluators or evaluator classes.

6. It SHALL identify thresholds and decision logic.

7. It SHALL identify sampling where applicable.

8. It SHALL identify required human review.

9. It SHALL identify disagreement handling.

10. It SHALL identify cost and deadline considerations.

11. It SHALL preserve data-classification requirements.

12. It SHALL NOT expose raw credentials.

13. It SHALL identify provenance.

14. Material method changes SHALL create a new Version.

15. High-consequence evaluation SHOULD include independent evidence.

16. Evaluation depth SHALL reflect consequence.

17. Generator self-evaluation SHALL NOT be the sole high-assurance method.

18. Unknown evaluator state SHALL NOT produce acceptance.

19. Imported Evaluation Plans SHALL be validated.

20. Historical Plans SHALL remain interpretable.

13.543 Canonical Evaluator Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Evaluator:

1. Every Evaluator SHALL have stable identity.

2. Evaluator SHALL remain distinct from Evaluation Method.

3. Evaluator SHALL identify type.

4. Model Evaluators SHALL identify exact Model Version and Deployment where material.

5. Tool Evaluators SHALL identify Tool Version.

6. Human Evaluators SHALL identify Reviewer Principal.

7. Evaluator scope SHALL be explicit.

8. Evaluator qualification SHALL be evidence-based.

9. Evaluator lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

10. Evaluator configuration SHALL be versioned.

11. Model evaluation prompts and Rubrics SHALL be versioned.

12. Evaluator bias and limitations SHALL remain visible.

13. Evaluator drift SHALL trigger review.

14. Evaluator fallback SHALL require equivalent qualification.

15. External Evaluators SHALL remain subject to data policy.

16. Evaluators SHALL NOT create publication authority.

17. Evaluators SHALL NOT alter the target.

18. Evaluation Attempts SHALL remain attributable.

19. Retired Evaluators SHALL remain historically resolvable.

20. Evaluator confidence SHALL NOT replace evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric

13.544 Canonical Evaluation Result Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Evaluation Result:

1. Every Evaluation Result SHALL have stable identity.

2. It SHALL identify the exact target version.

3. It SHALL identify the Evaluator.

4. It SHALL identify the Evaluation Method and version.

5. It SHALL identify the Quality Dimension.

6. It SHALL identify Score or categorical result.

7. It SHALL identify confidence where applicable.

8. It SHALL identify evidence.

9. It SHALL identify detected Defects.

10. Unknown SHALL remain a valid result.

11. Failed evaluator execution SHALL NOT become target failure automatically.

12. Result correction SHALL preserve prior history.

13. Results SHALL remain scoped to their target and criteria.

14. Results SHALL NOT automatically propagate to derivatives.

15. Result cost SHALL remain attributable.

16. Protected Results SHALL remain access-controlled.

17. Duplicate Results SHALL be deduplicated where semantically identical.

18. Late Results SHALL NOT overwrite newer target Decisions.

19. Historical Results SHALL remain queryable.

20. Results SHALL be human- and machine-interpretable.

13.545 Canonical Acceptance Decision Contract

The following requirements define canonical Acceptance Decisions:

1. Every Acceptance Decision SHALL have stable identity.

2. It SHALL identify the exact target version.

3. It SHALL identify the Quality Contract Version.

4. It SHALL reference supporting Evaluation Results.

5. It SHALL identify the decision state.

6. It SHALL identify approver or policy.

7. It SHALL identify intended use.

8. It SHALL identify conditions and exceptions.

9. It SHALL identify validity.

10. Blocking Defects SHALL prevent ordinary acceptance.

11. Limited-use acceptance SHALL NOT become final-publication acceptance.

12. Accepted-with-conditions SHALL enforce the conditions.

13. Target mutation SHALL invalidate or supersede prior acceptance.

14. Acceptance SHALL remain separate from rights approval.

15. Acceptance SHALL remain separate from publication authority.

16. Rejection SHALL preserve incurred cost and evidence.

17. Human timeout SHALL NOT fabricate acceptance.

18. Historical Decisions SHALL remain immutable.

19. New Decisions SHALL supersede rather than rewrite.

20. Acceptance SHALL be explainable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.546 Canonical Benchmark Contract

The following requirements define canonical Benchmarks:

1. Every Benchmark SHALL have stable identity and version.

2. Every Benchmark SHALL state its purpose.

3. Every Benchmark SHALL identify scope.

4. Every Benchmark SHALL identify Capability.

5. Every Benchmark SHALL reference a Test Suite.

6. Every Test Case SHALL have stable identity.

7. Benchmark configuration SHALL be reproducible where possible.

8. Benchmark target SHALL identify exact resource version.

9. Deployment, Adapter and parameters SHALL be recorded where material.

10. Metrics SHALL have explicit definitions.

11. Critical failures SHALL remain visible.

12. Benchmark confidence SHALL be reported.

13. Benchmark cost SHALL be recorded.

14. Protected Test Cases SHALL preserve data policy.

15. Benchmark leakage and contamination SHALL be monitored.

16. Benchmark results SHALL NOT become universal rankings.

17. Project Benchmarks SHALL remain Project-scoped.

18. Benchmark changes SHALL create new Versions.

19. Retired Benchmarks SHALL remain historically queryable.

20. Benchmark evidence SHALL be interpreted with cost, latency, privacy and operational context.

13.547 Canonical Quality Gate Contract

The following requirements define canonical Quality Gates:

1. Every Quality Gate SHALL have stable identity.

2. It SHALL identify target.

3. It SHALL reference a Quality Contract.

4. It SHALL identify required Evaluation Results.

5. It SHALL define pass and fail logic.

6. Blocking and advisory Gates SHALL remain distinct.

7. Gate state SHALL be durable.

8. Gate timeout SHALL NOT create automatic pass.

9. Gate re-evaluation SHALL use the new target version.

10. Gate failure path SHALL be explicit.

11. Human Review Gates SHALL identify reviewer role.

12. Composite Gates SHALL preserve underlying Results.

13. Provider success SHALL NOT bypass the Gate.

14. Publication SHALL NOT proceed past a failed required Gate.

15. Gate override SHALL require explicit authority.

16. Gate conditions SHALL remain enforceable.

17. Gate events SHALL be attributable.

18. Gate history SHALL remain immutable.

19. Quality Gate SHALL NOT replace rights or authority checks.

20. Completion SHALL require all mandatory Gates.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.548 Canonical Quality Governance Contract

The following requirements define overall quality governance:

1. Quality SHALL be contextual and Capability-specific.

2. Quality Floors SHALL be mandatory.

3. Quality Targets SHALL guide optimisation above the Floor.

4. Provider reputation SHALL NOT replace evidence.

5. Price SHALL NOT replace evaluation.

6. User preference SHALL remain distinct from correctness and safety.

7. Evaluation SHALL preserve target, evaluator and method identity.

8. High-consequence work SHOULD use independent evaluation.

9. Human review SHALL be attributable and criteria-based.

10. Benchmark evidence SHALL be versioned and scoped.

11. Project-specific quality SHALL remain Project-scoped.

12. Critical Defects SHALL remain visible.

13. Evaluator disagreement SHALL remain visible.

14. Unknown quality SHALL NOT become favourable by default.

15. Drift SHALL trigger review.

16. Quality learning SHALL require governed admission.

17. Evaluation cost SHALL remain economically governed.

18. Accepted Outputs SHALL NOT bypass rights or publication authority.

19. Quality Incidents SHALL preserve evidence and affected scope.

20. Historical quality truth SHALL remain reconstructable.

13.549 Quality Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No Provider success becomes quality acceptance.

- No universal score replaces Capability-specific evaluation.

- No expensive resource becomes high quality by price alone.

- No famous Model becomes suitable without evidence.

- No generator becomes its own sole high-assurance evaluator.

- No unknown result becomes pass.

- No critical defect disappears inside an average.

- No human review occurs without attributable decision.

- No Project benchmark becomes universal truth.

- No benchmark change rewrites prior Runs.

- No modified target reuses stale acceptance.

- No child-facing final media bypasses required review.

- No factual fluency substitutes for source support.

- No citation presence substitutes for citation correctness.

- No compiling code substitutes for architecture conformance.

- No visual beauty substitutes for canonical character identity.

- No natural voice substitutes for correct pronunciation and consent.

- No evaluation learning rewrites routing policy automatically.

- No accepted Output gains publication authority automatically.

- No quality-system failure creates false completion.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
13.550 Closing Statement

Quality is the boundary between a Provider-produced result and an Omnira-accepted result.

The Capability defines what kind of result is required.

The Quality Contract defines what acceptable means.

The Plan defines where evaluation occurs.

The Evaluator measures one or more Dimensions.

The Evaluation Result preserves the evidence.

The Quality Gate enforces the criteria.

The Acceptance Decision determines whether the exact target may advance.

The Benchmark compares resources under controlled conditions.

Production Monitoring determines whether past evidence remains trustworthy.

For Familje-Stunden, quality means more than attractive media.

Nova must remain Nova.

Pling must remain Pling.

Their identities must remain stable together and across frames.

The language must suit children.

The narration must sound natural in Swedish.

The final story must feel safe, warm and coherent.

For The Prompt, quality means more than fluent reporting.

Claims must be current.

Sources must support them.

Fact and interpretation must remain distinguishable.

The final video must preserve the same factual meaning as the verified research.

For GainPilot, quality means more than energetic media.

Exercise language must be accurate.

Advice must be useful.

The brand tone must remain clear.

Economical production must still meet the defined Floor.

For Omnira, quality means more than code that appears to work.

Architecture boundaries must remain intact.

Tenant and Project isolation must survive.

Authority must remain explicit.

Tests must pass.

The repository state must remain truthful.

The Provider creates an Output.

The Evaluator creates evidence.

The Gate applies the Contract.

The human retains judgement where human judgement matters.

No quality without context.

No acceptance without criteria.

No benchmark without scope.

No score without an Evaluator.

No Gate without evidence.

No publication from Provider success alone.

The user retains taste.

The Project retains identity.

Omnira retains standards.

The Fabric turns generated possibility into evaluated, accepted and trustworthy output.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
14.1 Chapter Status
