Both outbound and inbound payloads shall be validated.

16.68 Provider Schema Drift

Unexpected schema changes shall produce:

- Adapter error,

- degraded state,

- Incident,

- or controlled compatibility handling.

They shall not be accepted silently.

16.69 Response Normalisation

Response Normalisation converts Provider output into canonical Output structures.

It shall preserve:

- Provider response ID,

- job ID,

- Model identity where known,

- timing,

- usage,

- finish reason,

- content,

- Asset references,

- warnings,

- and raw-evidence reference.

16.70 Output Type Mapping

The Adapter shall map Provider outputs to canonical types such as:

- Text Output,

- Structured Output,

- Code Output,

- Image Output,

- Audio Output,

- Video Output,

- Tool Result,

- Search Result,

- or External Action Result.

16.71 Output Type Integrity

A Provider response shall not be labelled as a canonical type when mandatory properties are missing.

16.72 Text Normalisation

Text normalisation may include:

- encoding,

- line endings,

- Unicode handling,

- and Provider wrapper removal.

It shall not rewrite meaning.

16.73 Structured Output Normalisation

Structured Outputs shall preserve:

- raw Provider text where relevant,

- parsed object,

- schema-validation result,

- and parse error.

16.74 Code Output Normalisation

Code output shall preserve:

- language,

- file context,

- patch format,

- and Provider metadata.

Code shall not be applied automatically by the Adapter.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.75 Image Output Normalisation

Image output shall preserve:

- Provider Asset ID,

- URL or binary reference,

- dimensions,

- format,

- generation metadata,

- and expiry.

16.76 Audio Output Normalisation

Audio output shall preserve:

- format,

- sample rate,

- duration,

- channels,

- Voice Asset,

- and Provider metadata.

16.77 Video Output Normalisation

Video output shall preserve:

- duration,

- dimensions,

- frame rate where known,

- Provider job,

- Asset reference,

- and processing state.

16.78 Search Output Normalisation

Search output shall preserve:

- query,

- result identity,

- source URL or source reference,

- title,

- snippet,

- retrieval time,

- ranking,

- and Provider.

16.79 Tool Result Normalisation

Tool results shall preserve:

- Tool identity,

- Tool Version,

- input fingerprint,

- output,

- side effects,

- exit state,

- and logs reference.

16.80 Finish Reason Mapping

Provider finish reasons may include:

- completed,

- length limit,

- content filter,

- tool call,

- cancellation,

- error,

- or unknown.

They shall map to canonical state without losing Provider detail.

16.81 Provider Warning

Provider warnings shall be preserved.

Warnings may affect:

- quality,

- rights,

- safety,

- cost,

- or future availability.

16.82 Raw Response Preservation

The complete raw response may be retained as protected evidence when policy permits.

Canonical operation shall not depend on indefinite raw retention.

16.83 Raw Response Redaction

Secrets, tokens, personal data or restricted Provider fields may require redaction before evidence storage.

16.84 State Mapping

State Mapping converts implementation-specific lifecycle states into canonical Execution or Provider Job states.

It shall preserve both:

- canonical interpretation,

- and original external state.

16.85 Canonical Job States

Representative canonical states may include:

- submitted,

- accepted,

- queued,

- running,

- partially complete,

- succeeded,

- failed,

- cancelled,

- cancellation pending,

- expired,

- unknown,

- and reconciliation required.

16.86 Provider-Specific Job State

Provider state names shall be stored as evidence.

They shall not replace canonical state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.87 Ambiguous State Mapping

When a Provider state cannot be mapped safely, the canonical state shall be:

- unknown,

- unresolved,

- or provider-specific pending

rather than an invented completion.

16.88 Terminal State

A Provider terminal state does not automatically imply canonical Completion.

Required Output ingestion, cost, evaluation and verification may remain.

16.89 Cancellation Mapping

Cancellation states shall distinguish:

- cancellation requested,

- cancellation accepted,

- cancelled,

- and cancellation unknown.

16.90 Expired Provider Job

Provider expiry may mean:

- result deleted,

- job cancelled,

- status unavailable,

- or access expired.

The Adapter shall not assume one interpretation.

16.91 Error Mapping

An Error Mapping converts implementation-specific failures into canonical Error Classification.

It shall include:

- Provider error code,

- HTTP or protocol status,

- message pattern,

- canonical category,

- retryability,

- severity,

- and Version.

16.92 Error Mapping Identity

Every reusable Error Mapping shall have stable identity or versioned rule identity.

16.93 Authentication Error Mapping

Authentication failures shall remain distinct from:

- Account suspension,

- missing permission,

- expired session,

- and Provider outage.

16.94 Authorisation Error Mapping

Permission errors shall identify:

- Principal,

- Connection,

- Account,

- resource,

- and required scope where known.

16.95 Rate-Limit Error Mapping

Rate-limit errors shall preserve:

- limit type,

- retry-after,

- scope,

- and reset time.

16.96 Quota Error Mapping

Quota exhaustion shall remain distinct from rate limiting and Budget failure.

16.97 Validation Error Mapping

Provider validation errors shall preserve which translated field failed.

16.98 Unsupported-Feature Error Mapping

Feature incompatibility shall update or challenge the relevant Capability Mapping.

16.99 Content-Policy Error Mapping

Provider content-policy rejection shall remain Provider-specific evidence.

It shall not automatically become Omnira safety judgement.

16.100 Provider Internal Error Mapping

Provider internal failures may be retryable according to Reliability Policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.101 Network Error Mapping

Network errors shall preserve whether request submission may have occurred.

16.102 Timeout Error Mapping

Timeout shall not be mapped directly to confirmed failure when external state is uncertain.

16.103 Unknown Error Mapping

Unknown Provider errors shall remain unknown and may reduce Connector maturity.

16.104 Error Detail Protection

Error evidence shall not expose:

- raw secrets,

- full protected payloads,

- or unnecessary personal data.

16.105 Usage Mapping

Usage Mapping translates Provider or local measurements into canonical Usage Records.

It may include:

- tokens,

- characters,

- images,

- video seconds,

- audio seconds,

- GPU time,

- requests,

- search calls,

- storage,

- or credits.

16.106 Usage Mapping Version

Usage interpretation shall be versioned.

Provider billing models may change.

16.107 Input Usage

Input usage shall remain separate from output usage where the Provider distinguishes them.

16.108 Output Usage

Output usage shall remain separate from input usage.

16.109 Cached Usage

Cached tokens or reused context may have different economic meaning.

16.110 Tool Usage

Tool invocations and search calls may create separate usage components.

16.111 Estimated Usage

Locally estimated usage shall remain distinct from Provider-reported usage.

16.112 Provisional Usage

Provider response usage may remain provisional until billing reconciliation.

16.113 Missing Usage

Missing usage shall remain unknown.

It shall not become zero.

16.114 Credit Usage

Provider credits shall preserve original credit units and conversion evidence.

16.115 Usage Correlation

Every Usage Record shall correlate to:

- Execution,

- Attempt,

- Provider Account,

- Model or Tool,

- and Provider job or request.

16.116 Cost Mapping

An Adapter may extract or calculate cost evidence.

It shall not create economic authority.

Cost Mapping may include:

- unit price reference,

- Provider-reported charge,

- credit consumption,

- or estimated cost.

16.117 Cost Mapping Limitation

The economic control plane remains authoritative for:

- Budget,

- Reservation,

- Cost Record,

- and reconciliation.

16.118 Asset Mapping

Asset Mapping translates external or local files and references into canonical Output and Asset-candidate structures.

It shall preserve:

- source,

- external Asset ID,

- download location,

- expiration,

- format,

- checksum where available,

- and provenance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.119 External Asset Reference

An External Asset Reference may point to Provider-hosted content.

It shall identify:

- Provider,

- Account,

- external ID,

- retrieval method,

- expiry,

- and access constraints.

16.120 Temporary Asset URL

Temporary URLs shall not be treated as durable Asset storage.

16.121 Asset Ingestion

The Connector or downstream Asset Service shall ingest required content before expiry when policy permits.

16.122 Asset Checksum

Downloaded content should receive a checksum or equivalent integrity evidence.

16.123 Asset Format Validation

The actual file format shall be validated.

Filename extension alone is insufficient.

16.124 Asset Metadata Validation

Dimensions, duration, encoding and other metadata should be validated against the Output Contract.

16.125 Provider Project Asset

Some Providers store reusable Project Assets such as:

- voice,

- character,

- style,

- image reference,

- or workspace file.

The Connector shall preserve Account and Project affinity.

16.126 Asset Ownership Boundary

Provider-hosted Asset ownership and Omnira canonical Asset ownership shall remain distinct.

16.127 Asset Deletion Boundary

Deleting a Provider Asset is a consequential side effect.

The Adapter shall not delete automatically during ordinary cleanup without authority.

16.128 Asset Portability

The Connector should expose whether Assets can be:

- downloaded,

- exported,

- migrated,

- or reused outside the Provider.

16.129 Asset Expiry

Provider-hosted Outputs may expire.

Expiry shall influence ingestion and recovery.

16.130 Multimodal Payload

A Multimodal Payload may include:

- text,

- image,

- audio,

- video,

- document,

- or structured data.

The Connector shall preserve modality boundaries and references.

16.131 Inline Payload

Small payloads may be embedded directly where protocol permits.

16.132 Referenced Payload

Large or protected payloads should use governed references.

16.133 Payload Size Limit

Every Connector shall expose relevant size limits.

16.134 Payload Compression

Compression may be used when:

- supported,

- loss is acceptable,

- and format remains valid.

16.135 Lossy Transformation

Lossy conversion shall require explicit permission when it may affect quality.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.136 Payload Chunking

Large Inputs may be chunked only when the Capability and Plan permit decomposition.

16.137 Chunk Identity

Every chunk shall preserve:

- source,

- order,

- boundaries,

- and relation to the original Asset.

16.138 Chunk Reassembly

Reassembly shall validate:

- completeness,

- order,

- and integrity.

16.139 Streaming

Streaming allows partial data exchange before complete execution finishes.

The integration architecture shall distinguish:

- token streaming,

- audio streaming,

- event streaming,

- partial Asset streaming,

- and status streaming.

16.140 Streaming Capability Mapping

Streaming support shall be explicit.

A synchronous-only Provider shall not be represented as streaming.

16.141 Stream Session

A Stream Session shall include:

- sessionId,

- Connection,

- Execution,

- protocol,

- start,

- state,

- sequence,

- and closure.

16.142 Stream Event

Every Stream Event should preserve:

- event type,

- sequence,

- time,

- payload reference,

- and correlation.

16.143 Stream Ordering

Ordering guarantees shall be explicit.

16.144 Stream Gap

Missing sequence or corrupted stream shall produce:

- gap,

- retry,

- reconciliation,

- or failure

according to policy.

16.145 Stream Resume

Resume may be supported only when the external protocol provides sufficient state.

16.146 Stream Cancellation

Local stream closure does not necessarily cancel external execution.

16.147 Stream Finalisation

Partial streamed content shall not become final Output until completion conditions are satisfied.

16.148 Stream Backpressure

Adapters shall respect downstream capacity.

Unbounded buffering is prohibited.

16.149 Stream Error

Stream errors shall preserve whether:

- partial content is usable,

- external job continues,

- or retry is safe.

16.150 Pagination

Pagination is required when external systems return bounded subsets.

The Connector shall preserve:

- page identity,

- cursor,

- limit,

- order,

- and completion status.

16.151 Cursor Pagination

Cursor tokens shall be treated as opaque Provider state.

16.152 Offset Pagination

Offset-based pagination may be unstable under concurrent mutation.

16.153 Page Deduplication

Repeated or overlapping pages shall not duplicate canonical records.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.154 Pagination Completion

The system shall distinguish:

- complete enumeration,

- partial enumeration,

- interrupted enumeration,

- and unknown completeness.

16.155 Pagination Limit

Maximum pages or items shall be bounded by:

- request,

- Budget,

- latency,

- and policy.

16.156 Search Pagination

Search result pagination shall preserve ranking and retrieval context.

16.157 Asset Listing Pagination

Provider Asset reconciliation may require complete or scoped pagination.

16.158 Tool Invocation

A Tool Invocation translates a canonical Tool Call into an implementation-specific operation.

It shall preserve:

- Tool identity,

- input schema,

- authority,

- target,

- side-effect class,

- timeout,

- and evidence.

16.159 Tool Input Mapping

Tool Inputs shall be validated against:

- canonical schema,

- Tool schema,

- and policy.

16.160 Tool Output Mapping

Tool Outputs shall be normalised without hiding:

- exit status,

- side effects,

- warnings,

- or partial state.

16.161 Tool Side Effect

The Connector shall declare whether a Tool may:

- read,

- write,

- create,

- delete,

- publish,

- send,

- purchase,

- or execute code.

16.162 Tool Read-Only Mode

A read-only Connection shall block mutation even if the underlying Tool supports it.

16.163 Tool Target Scope

Tool invocation shall identify exact target such as:

- repository,

- branch,

- file,

- calendar,

- account,

- or publication channel.

16.164 Tool Confirmation

Consequential Tool actions may require pre-execution confirmation and post-execution verification.

16.165 Tool Sandbox

Untrusted or experimental Tools should run in a sandbox or constrained Environment.

16.166 Tool Process Adapter

A local process Adapter shall manage:

- executable path,

- arguments,

- environment,

- working directory,

- standard input,

- standard output,

- standard error,

- exit code,

- and timeout.

16.167 Shell Invocation

Shell invocation shall avoid unsafe string concatenation.

Arguments should be structured.

16.168 Working Directory

The working directory shall be explicit and Project-scoped.

16.169 Environment Variable Protection

Sensitive environment variables shall not be exposed to Tools unnecessarily.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.170 Process Exit State

Exit code shall remain distinct from semantic success.

16.171 Process Output Limit

Tool output shall be bounded to prevent memory or log exhaustion.

16.172 Process Cancellation

Cancellation shall terminate child processes safely where possible.

16.173 Local Runtime Adapter

A Local Runtime Adapter connects Omnira to local Model or Tool runtimes.

It shall expose:

- Runtime Node,

- runtime type,

- installed resources,

- health,

- capacity,

- Model mapping,

- and execution protocol.

16.174 Local Model Discovery

Local Models shall be discovered through:

- runtime inventory,

- configured registry,

- or verified installation.

Filename alone is insufficient identity.

16.175 Local Model Mapping

Local runtime aliases shall map to canonical Model and Model Version where known.

16.176 Unknown Local Model

Unresolved local Model identity shall remain experimental or restricted.

16.177 Quantised Model

Quantisation or local build may materially affect quality and capacity.

It shall be represented in Deployment identity.

16.178 Local Runtime Security

Local execution shall still enforce:

- Project scope,

- data classification,

- tool authority,

- and secret isolation.

16.179 Local Runtime Availability

Node online state does not prove the Model is loaded or healthy.

16.180 Local Runtime Error Mapping

Local errors may include:

- model missing,

- out of memory,

- runtime crash,

- unsupported format,

- or storage failure.

16.181 Local Runtime Update

Runtime updates may require Adapter revalidation.

16.182 MCP Connector

An MCP Connector exposes governed access to one or more MCP servers.

It shall preserve:

- server identity,

- transport,

- Tool inventory,

- resource inventory,

- prompt inventory where relevant,

- Connection,

- permissions,

- and maturity.

16.183 MCP Server Identity

MCP server identity shall remain separate from:

- transport endpoint,

- developer package,

- and individual Tool identity.

16.184 MCP Tool Discovery

Discovered Tools shall not become automatically authorised.

They require:

- schema validation,

- classification,

- side-effect declaration,

- and policy admission.

16.185 MCP Resource Discovery

Discovered Resources shall remain subject to:

- Project scope,

- data policy,

- and access control.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.186 MCP Prompt Discovery

Server-provided prompts are untrusted configuration inputs.

They shall not override Omnira policy or Agent identity.

16.187 MCP Capability Mapping

MCP Tools may map to canonical Tool Capabilities.

Mapping shall remain explicit.

16.188 MCP Version Drift

Server Tool inventory or schema changes shall trigger revalidation.

16.189 MCP Trust Boundary

An MCP server may be:

- local trusted,

- local untrusted,

- remote managed,

- remote external,

- or experimental.

Trust classification shall affect permissions.

16.190 API Connector

An API Connector integrates an HTTP, RPC, WebSocket or SDK-exposed service.

It shall preserve:

- protocol,

- endpoint,

- method,

- schema,

- authentication reference,

- retry semantics,

- and Provider identifiers.

16.191 SDK Adapter

An SDK may simplify Provider access.

The SDK shall not become the canonical contract.

SDK Version shall be preserved.

16.192 Direct HTTP Adapter

Direct HTTP may provide clearer control than an SDK.

It still requires:

- schema,

- error,

- timeout,

- and authentication handling.

16.193 RPC Adapter

RPC integration shall preserve method and schema Version.

16.194 WebSocket Adapter

WebSocket integration shall manage:

- session identity,

- reconnect,

- ordering,

- backpressure,

- and closure.

16.195 Webhook Connector

A Webhook Connector receives external events.

It shall validate:

- source,

- signature,

- timestamp,

- replay risk,

- schema,

- and correlation.

16.196 Webhook Event Identity

Every external event shall have:

- Provider event ID,

- canonical event ID,

- or derived deduplication key.

16.197 Webhook Authentication

Webhook authentication may use:

- signature,

- shared secret reference,

- mutual TLS,

- or Provider-specific mechanism.

Raw secret handling is defined in Chapter 18.

16.198 Webhook Replay Protection

Repeated valid webhooks shall not duplicate canonical effects.

16.199 Webhook Ordering

Events may arrive out of order.

State transitions shall use Version and lifecycle validation.

16.200 Webhook Missing Event

Missing webhook shall trigger polling or reconciliation where required.

16.201 Queue Connector

A Queue Connector integrates message brokers or asynchronous work queues.

It shall expose:

- topic or queue identity,

- delivery semantics,

- ordering,

- retry,

- dead-letter behaviour,

- and tenant isolation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.202 Delivery Semantics

Delivery semantics may be:

- at most once,

- at least once,

- or Provider-defined.

The Connector shall not claim universal exactly-once behaviour.

16.203 Queue Message Mapping

Queue payloads shall map to versioned canonical event or command schemas.

16.204 Queue Consumer Identity

Consumer identity and ownership shall remain visible.

16.205 Queue Redelivery

Consumers shall be idempotent.

16.206 Queue Dead Letter

Dead-lettered messages shall retain:

- original payload reference,

- failure history,

- and remediation state.

16.207 File-Exchange Connector

A File-Exchange Connector transfers data through:

- watched folder,

- upload,

- export,

- removable storage,

- cloud drive,

- or manual file handoff.

It shall preserve:

- source,

- destination,

- checksum,

- version,

- and operator where applicable.

16.208 File Drop

A file appearing in a folder shall not be trusted automatically.

It requires:

- identity,

- format validation,

- classification,

- and provenance.

16.209 Export Package

An Export Package may contain:

- Assets,

- metadata,

- manifest,

- checksums,

- and instructions.

16.210 Import Package

Imported packages shall be validated before canonical admission.

16.211 Browser-Assisted Connector

A Browser-Assisted Connector supports systems without suitable production API access.

It may use:

- human operator,

- browser automation,

- guided procedure,

- or supervised session.

It shall preserve truth about its maturity.

16.212 Browser Automation

Browser automation shall be classified separately from official API integration.

It may be vulnerable to:

- interface change,

- session expiry,

- anti-automation controls,

- and ambiguous outcomes.

16.213 Browser Session

A browser session shall be scoped to:

- user,

- Project,

- Provider Account,

- and task.

16.214 Browser Action Evidence

Evidence may include:

- action log,

- screenshot,

- downloaded Asset,

- Provider job ID,

- and human confirmation.

16.215 Browser Terms

Automation eligibility shall consider Provider terms and restrictions.

16.216 Browser Fragility

Browser-assisted paths should receive lower automation maturity unless repeatedly verified.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.217 Human-Assisted Connector

A Human-Assisted Connector defines a structured manual procedure as a governed integration.

It shall include:

- task package,

- required role,

- Account,

- instructions,

- expected Output,

- cost boundary,

- evidence requirements,

- and Completion Contract.

16.218 Manual Procedure

A Manual Procedure shall have stable identity and Version.

16.219 Human Operator Identity

The operator shall be recorded as a Principal.

16.220 Manual Provider Account

The exact Provider Account used manually shall remain explicit.

16.221 Manual Cost

Operator-reported spend shall be reconciled when possible.

16.222 Manual Evidence

Human-assisted completion should include:

- exported file,

- Provider reference,

- screenshot,

- receipt,

- or external status.

16.223 Manual Uncertainty

When exact external state cannot be verified, the result shall remain:

- human-reported,

- provisional,

- or unknown.

16.224 Manual Procedure Drift

Interface or Provider changes may invalidate instructions.

Procedures require review dates.

16.225 Provider-Managed Router

Some Providers expose a routing product that selects an underlying Model or Tool.

The Connector shall represent:

- Provider-managed routing,

- declared candidate set where known,

- selected underlying resource where reported,

- opacity,

- reproducibility limits,

- and cost.

16.226 Hidden Model Selection

When the Provider does not disclose the exact Model, Omnira shall not fabricate identity.

16.227 Moving Alias

A Provider alias may map to changing underlying resources.

The Connector shall preserve:

- alias,

- observed behaviour,

- date,

- and uncertainty.

16.228 Routed Resource Disclosure

Where the Provider returns actual resource identity, the Adapter shall record it.

16.229 Provider Router Eligibility

A Provider-managed router may be ineligible when the request requires:

- exact Model,

- deterministic reproduction,

- fixed region,

- or transparent rights.

16.230 Integration Maturity

Integration Maturity describes production readiness.

Canonical maturity levels may include:

- discovered,

- experimental,

- development,

- controlled preview,

- production,

- restricted,

- degraded,

- deprecated,

- and retired.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.231 Discovered

The integration exists but has not been validated.

16.232 Experimental

Basic functionality has been demonstrated.

Production trust is insufficient.

16.233 Development

The integration supports developer use with bounded non-production data.

16.234 Controlled Preview

Limited production-like use may occur under stronger review.

16.235 Production

The integration satisfies approved conformance, security, reliability and evidence requirements.

16.236 Restricted

Use is limited by:

- Project,

- Capability,

- data class,

- Environment,

- or approval.

16.237 Degraded

The integration remains available with known operational limitation.

16.238 Deprecated

New use should migrate away.

16.239 Retired

New execution is prohibited.

Historical evidence remains resolvable.

16.240 Maturity Evidence

Maturity shall be based on:

- conformance tests,

- security review,

- reliability,

- error mapping,

- cost mapping,

- operational experience,

- and recovery readiness.

16.241 Maturity Is Not Provider Reputation

A famous Provider may have an immature Omnira integration.

16.242 Connection Lifecycle

Connection lifecycle may include:

- proposed,

- configuring,

- validating,

- active,

- restricted,

- degraded,

- suspended,

- expired,

- revoked,

- deprecated,

- retired,

- and archived.

16.243 Proposed Connection

The connection has not yet been approved or completed.

16.244 Configuring Connection

Required endpoint, Account and Credential References are being established.

16.245 Validating Connection

Health, scope, permissions and Capability support are being tested.

16.246 Active Connection

The Connection may be considered for eligible execution.

16.247 Restricted Connection

Use is limited by explicit policy.

16.248 Degraded Connection

The Connection remains usable with reduced capability or reliability.

16.249 Suspended Connection

New execution is blocked temporarily.

16.250 Expired Connection

The Connection’s validity period ended.

16.251 Revoked Connection

Authority or Provider access has been withdrawn.

16.252 Deprecated Connection

New use should migrate to a replacement.

16.253 Retired Connection

The Connection may not be selected for new execution.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.254 Archived Connection

The historical record remains available.

16.255 Connection Activation

Activation shall require:

- valid Connector Version,

- valid Adapter Version,

- valid Provider Account,

- valid Credential Reference,

- policy approval,

- health validation,

- and conformance state.

16.256 Connection Restriction

Restrictions may include:

- read-only,

- no public data,

- no confidential data,

- development only,

- one Project,

- one Capability,

- or no consequential side effect.

16.257 Connection Suspension

Suspension may result from:

- Incident,

- credential compromise,

- Provider change,

- billing issue,

- quality drift,

- or owner action.

16.258 Connection Reactivation

Reactivation shall require fresh validation.

16.259 Connection Retirement

Retirement should identify:

- replacement,

- migration status,

- affected Plans,

- and historical retention.

16.260 Connection Discovery

Connections may be discovered through:

- configuration,

- Provider Account onboarding,

- local runtime scan,

- MCP inventory,

- or human registration.

Discovery shall not create active status automatically.

16.261 Connection Ownership

Every Connection shall identify an owner such as:

- user,

- Project,

- Tenant,

- Omnira,

- or customer organisation.

16.262 Connection Scope

Connection scope shall identify:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- Capability,

- and data class restrictions.

16.263 Cross-Project Connection

A shared Connection may serve several Projects only when:

- ownership permits,

- attribution remains exact,

- and data isolation is enforced.

16.264 Shared Managed Connection

Omnira-managed shared Connections require:

- Tenant isolation,

- per-Project attribution,

- quota,

- and Budget controls.

16.265 Personal Connection

A personal Provider Connection shall not become platform-wide capacity by convenience.

16.266 Connection Alias

Human-friendly aliases may exist.

Canonical identity shall remain stable.

16.267 Connection Priority

Connection preference may influence routing.

It shall not override eligibility.

16.268 Connection Region

Region shall be selected and preserved where material.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.269 Connection Endpoint Rotation

Endpoint changes shall be attributable.

They may require new validation.

16.270 Adapter Deployment

An Adapter may be deployed as:

- library,

- service,

- sidecar,

- worker,

- local process,

- plugin,

- or serverless function.

Deployment form shall not change canonical semantics.

16.271 Adapter Service

A shared Adapter Service may serve multiple Connectors or Accounts.

It shall preserve isolation and exact Connection identity.

16.272 Adapter Library

An embedded library may reduce network latency.

It still requires Version evidence and policy.

16.273 Adapter Sidecar

A sidecar may isolate Provider SDK or protocol concerns.

16.274 Adapter Worker

A worker may execute asynchronous integration operations.

16.275 Adapter Plugin

A plugin may extend the Fabric dynamically.

Plugin admission requires trust and conformance.

16.276 Adapter Isolation

Adapters handling external or untrusted payloads should run with least privilege.

16.277 Adapter Resource Limits

Adapters shall have bounded:

- memory,

- CPU,

- concurrency,

- payload size,

- and execution time.

16.278 Adapter Network Access

Network access should be limited to required endpoints.

16.279 Adapter File Access

Local file access shall be restricted to authorised paths.

16.280 Adapter Secret Access

Adapters should receive only short-lived or narrowly scoped credential material required for one operation.

16.281 Adapter Logging

Adapter logs shall preserve:

- request ID,

- Connection,

- operation,

- state,

- timing,

- and error class

without exposing secrets or full protected payloads.

16.282 Adapter Determinism

Request translation should be deterministic for the same:

- canonical input,

- Adapter Version,

- Connection configuration,

- and policy.

16.283 Provider Non-Determinism

Provider output may remain stochastic even when translation is deterministic.

16.284 Request Fingerprint

The Adapter may create a fingerprint of canonical and translated requests for:

- idempotency,

- audit,

- and debugging.

Protected content should be hashed or referenced safely.

16.285 Correlation

Every integration call shall preserve:

- requestId,

- planId,

- stepId,

- executionId,

- attemptId,

- routingDecisionId,

- and Provider request or job ID where applicable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.286 Causation

Callbacks, retries, fallback and downstream Asset events shall preserve causation.

16.287 Trace Context

Trace context may cross external boundaries when supported and safe.

16.288 Provider Request ID

Provider request IDs shall be preserved exactly.

16.289 Provider Job ID

Asynchronous job IDs shall remain durable and queryable.

16.290 External Asset ID

External Asset IDs shall remain linked to the exact Provider Account and Connection.

16.291 Integration Evidence

Integration Evidence may include:

- translated request summary,

- endpoint,

- Adapter Version,

- Connection,

- Provider identifiers,

- response state,

- usage,

- warnings,

- and raw-evidence references.

16.292 Translation Evidence

The system should preserve which mapping rules were applied.

16.293 Omitted-Feature Evidence

When an optional Feature is omitted, the decision shall remain visible.

16.294 Provider Mutation Evidence

Any external side effect shall preserve target and result.

16.295 Integration Receipt

An Integration Receipt may summarise:

- canonical operation,

- Connector,

- Adapter,

- Connection,

- Provider,

- Account,

- resource,

- external identifiers,

- timing,

- cost evidence,

- result,

- and warnings.

16.296 Observability

Integration observability shall expose:

- request volume,

- success,

- failure,

- timeout,

- schema error,

- callback delay,

- usage-mapping confidence,

- Asset-ingestion status,

- and Connection health.

16.297 Adapter Metric

Metrics may include:

- translation latency,

- validation failure,

- parsing failure,

- unknown-error rate,

- and schema-drift rate.

16.298 Connector Metric

Connector metrics may include:

- Capability success,

- Connection distribution,

- fallback,

- maturity,

- and conformance.

16.299 Connection Metric

Connection metrics may include:

- health,

- authentication failure,

- rate limit,

- quota,

- latency,

- and Provider Incident impact.

16.300 Error-Mapping Coverage

The system should measure the proportion of errors mapped to known canonical categories.

16.301 Unknown-Error Rate

High unknown-error rate reduces integration maturity.

16.302 Schema-Drift Metric

Unexpected fields, missing fields and parse failures should be monitored.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.303 Usage-Mapping Variance

Mapped usage should be compared with Provider billing evidence.

16.304 Asset-Ingestion Failure Rate

External completion without durable Asset ingestion is a material integration metric.

16.305 Callback Reliability

Callback receipt and processing should be measured separately.

16.306 Manual-Procedure Reliability

Human-assisted integration should measure:

- completion,

- error,

- delay,

- and evidence quality.

16.307 Integration Health

Integration Health is derived from:

- Adapter,

- Connection,

- endpoint,

- credential,

- Provider,

- and operational evidence.

16.308 Adapter Health

Adapter Health may include:

- process availability,

- dependency availability,

- schema compatibility,

- and error rate.

16.309 Connector Health

Connector Health aggregates integration capability state.

It shall preserve component detail.

16.310 Connection Health

Connection Health is specific to:

- Account,

- endpoint,

- credential,

- region,

- and configuration.

16.311 Provider Health

Provider Health remains separate from Connection Health.

16.312 Health Freshness

Every integration health state shall identify observation time.

16.313 Health Probe

A probe shall avoid:

- expensive side effects,

- sensitive data,

- or unintended Provider charges.

16.314 Synthetic Probe

A synthetic probe may test a safe no-op or low-cost operation.

16.315 Credential Probe

Credential validation should use a minimally privileged operation.

16.316 Capability Probe

Capability probes may verify Feature support in controlled Environment.

16.317 Probe Cost

Probe cost shall remain recorded where non-zero.

16.318 Probe Rate

Excessive probing may consume quota or trigger Provider limits.

16.319 Integration Policy

Integration Policy defines mandatory rules for Connector, Adapter and Connection use.

It may include:

- allowed Projects,

- allowed data classes,

- allowed Environments,

- allowed Capabilities,

- side-effect limits,

- required maturity,

- required evidence,

- and approval.

16.320 Platform Integration Policy

Platform policy may require:

- versioned Adapters,

- no raw secrets,

- canonical error mapping,

- and durable external identifiers.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.321 Tenant Integration Policy

Tenant policy may restrict:

- Providers,

- regions,

- shared Connections,

- and data handling.

16.322 Project Integration Policy

Project policy may define:

- approved Connections,

- preferred Accounts,

- manual procedures,

- and Capability restrictions.

16.323 Capability Integration Policy

Capability policy may require:

- production API,

- human review,

- exact resource identity,

- or asynchronous callback.

16.324 Environment Integration Policy

Development and production Connections shall remain distinct.

16.325 Data-Class Integration Policy

Data Classification may constrain:

- Connector type,

- Provider,

- region,

- retention,

- and external processing.

16.326 Side-Effect Integration Policy

Consequential Connectors may require:

- read-before-write,

- idempotency,

- approval,

- and verification.

16.327 Maturity Policy

Production execution may require minimum integration maturity.

16.328 Adapter-Allow Policy

Only approved Adapter Versions may run in production.

16.329 Connector-Deny Policy

A Connector may be blocked during Incident or deprecation.

16.330 Connection-Allow Policy

Specific Connections may be allowlisted.

16.331 Policy Version

Every Integration Decision and Execution shall reference applicable policy Versions.

16.332 Security Boundary

Adapters and Connectors are security-sensitive because they translate canonical authority into external action.

They shall use:

- least privilege,

- explicit scope,

- data minimisation,

- input validation,

- output validation,

- and secret isolation.

16.333 Untrusted External Input

All Provider responses, callbacks and discovered Tool schemas shall be treated as untrusted until validated.

16.334 Prompt Injection Boundary

External text, Tool descriptions, MCP prompts and search content may contain malicious instructions.

Adapters shall not merge them into authority or system policy.

16.335 Tool Description Trust

Discovered Tool descriptions are metadata.

They are not executable authority.

16.336 Callback Trust

A valid signature confirms source possession of a signing secret.

It does not prove semantic correctness.

16.337 Provider Metadata Trust

Provider metadata may be incomplete or inaccurate.

Critical claims require validation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.338 Input Sanitisation

Canonical data shall be encoded safely for the target protocol.

Sanitisation shall not alter required meaning.

16.339 Output Sanitisation

Returned content may require:

- schema validation,

- encoding validation,

- malware scanning,

- or content isolation.

16.340 File Security

Downloaded files should be scanned or sandboxed according to type and risk.

16.341 Archive Security

Compressed archives may contain:

- path traversal,

- excessive expansion,

- or hidden files.

Import shall be constrained.

16.342 URL Security

Provider-returned URLs shall be validated before server-side retrieval.

The system shall protect against:

- internal-network access,

- unsupported schemes,

- and redirect abuse.

16.343 Network Egress Policy

Adapters shall access only approved network destinations.

16.344 DNS and Endpoint Drift

Endpoint identity changes may affect trust and region.

They should be monitored where material.

16.345 Certificate Validation

TLS or equivalent transport validation shall not be disabled by convenience.

16.346 Local Trust Boundary

Local does not automatically mean trusted.

A local MCP server or executable may be malicious or misconfigured.

16.347 Plugin Trust Boundary

Third-party plugins require:

- provenance,

- permissions,

- review,

- and revocation capability.

16.348 Multi-Tenant Isolation

Shared Adapters shall prevent:

- request mixing,

- response mixing,

- credential mixing,

- log leakage,

- and cache leakage.

16.349 Project Isolation

Project-specific Accounts, Assets and data shall remain scoped.

16.350 Cache Isolation

Adapter caches shall include:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Connection,

- resource,

- and Version

where relevant.

16.351 Session Isolation

Provider threads, sessions and browser state shall not cross Project boundaries.

16.352 Temporary Storage

Temporary files shall be:

- scoped,

- access-controlled,

- cleaned safely,

- and retained only as required.

16.353 Data Retention

Connector retention shall respect:

- Data Classification,

- Provider policy,

- and canonical evidence requirements.

16.354 Provider Retention

Provider-side retention terms shall be represented in eligibility.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.355 Training Use

Whether Provider data may be used for training shall remain Connection- and Account-aware.

16.356 Region and Residency

Actual processing and storage regions shall remain explicit where known.

16.357 Privacy-Preserving Translation

The Adapter should avoid sending fields not required by the Provider operation.

16.358 Metadata Minimisation

Internal identifiers should not reveal unnecessary personal or strategic information externally.

16.359 Credential Reference

The Connection shall reference credentials indirectly.

Credential mechanics are defined in Chapter 18.

16.360 Credential Scope

The Adapter shall request only the credential scope required for the operation.

16.361 Short-Lived Credential

Short-lived credentials should be preferred where supported.

16.362 Credential Rotation

Adapters shall support rotation without rewriting historical Execution evidence.

16.363 Credential Failure

Credential failure shall map to canonical state and may suspend the Connection.

16.364 Credential Revocation

Revocation shall invalidate cached authorisation rapidly.

16.365 Credential Leakage Prevention

Credentials shall never appear in:

- prompts,

- canonical Outputs,

- user-facing errors,

- or ordinary logs.

16.366 Provider Account Identity

The exact Provider Account shall be recorded for every external operation.

16.367 Account Workspace

Workspace, organisation or team identity shall remain explicit where Provider scope depends on it.

16.368 Account Tier

Account tier may affect:

- Features,

- pricing,

- capacity,

- retention,

- and rights.

16.369 Account Ownership

Account ownership shall remain distinct from Connection ownership when relevant.

16.370 Account Switching

Changing Account for retry or fallback is material and shall be recorded.

16.371 Integration Reliability

The Adapter architecture shall support:

- timeout,

- retry,

- idempotency,

- callback reconciliation,

- and recovery.

It shall not hide distributed-system uncertainty.

16.372 Adapter Retry Boundary

The Adapter may perform bounded transport-level retry only when:

- policy permits,

- idempotency is preserved,

- and no ambiguous external side effect exists.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.373 Router Retry Boundary

Resource-level retry or fallback belongs to the Execution and Reliability architecture.

Adapters shall not silently change Provider or Model.

16.374 Provider SDK Retry

Automatic SDK retries shall be disabled, configured or observed explicitly.

Hidden SDK retry may create:

- cost,

- duplicate effects,

- and unknown state.

16.375 Connection Retry

Retry shall use the same Connection unless a new Routing or Fallback Decision selects another.

16.376 Idempotency-Key Mapping

Canonical idempotency keys shall map to Provider mechanisms where available.

16.377 Provider Without Idempotency

The Adapter shall use internal duplicate protection and reconciliation where Provider support is absent.

16.378 Callback Reconciliation

Missing or duplicate callbacks shall be handled through durable external identifiers.

16.379 Async Job Polling

Polling shall be bounded and coordinated with:

- callback,

- timeout,

- rate limit,

- and cost.

16.380 Polling Interval

Polling interval may adapt to Provider guidance and expected job duration.

16.381 Polling Stop

Polling shall stop on:

- terminal state,

- cancellation,

- expiry,

- or escalation.

Unknown state may remain after polling ends.

16.382 Long-Running Job

Long-running jobs require durable:

- Provider job ID,

- Connection,

- Adapter Version,

- Reservation,

- and reconciliation state.

16.383 Worker Restart

Adapter-worker restart shall not lose external job correlation.

16.384 Adapter Circuit Breaker

Circuit breakers may protect:

- Provider,

- Connection,

- endpoint,

- or Adapter Version.

16.385 Schema-Failure Circuit

Repeated parse or schema failures may open an Adapter-specific circuit.

16.386 Provider-Failure Circuit

Provider service failure should not be misclassified as Adapter defect.

16.387 Integration Recovery

Recovery may require:

- Adapter restart,

- Connection revalidation,

- Provider reconciliation,

- schema rollback,

- or alternate Adapter Version.

16.388 Adapter Rollback

A faulty Adapter Version may be rolled back.

New and historical Executions shall remain linked to their actual Versions.

16.389 Connection Failover

Connection failover requires routing or approved fallback.

It shall not occur invisibly inside the Adapter.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.390 Protocol Fallback

Switching from API to browser-assisted or human-assisted execution is material.

It requires a new or pre-approved execution path.

16.391 Quality Boundary

Adapters shall preserve output faithfully.

They do not determine final quality acceptance.

16.392 Adapter-Level Validation

Adapters may perform:

- schema,

- format,

- and basic integrity validation.

Semantic quality belongs to the Quality system.

16.393 Provider Moderation Output

Provider moderation or safety classification may be preserved as evidence.

It does not replace Omnira policy or evaluation.

16.394 Rights Boundary

Provider rights and licensing metadata shall be preserved.

The Adapter shall not invent commercial-use permission.

16.395 Consent Boundary

A Provider allowing voice cloning does not prove valid consent.

Consent remains a canonical policy requirement.

16.396 Economic Boundary

Adapters may report usage and Provider charges.

They shall not reserve Budget or approve spending independently.

16.397 Scheduling Boundary

Adapters may expose capacity and rate-limit evidence.

They shall not grant unrestricted scheduling priority.

16.398 Planning Boundary

Adapters shall not decompose user intent into hidden business Steps.

Material multi-operation behaviour belongs in the Execution Plan.

16.399 Hidden Provider Workflow

Some Provider Products perform several internal operations.

The Connector shall represent opacity and known boundaries.

It shall not claim visibility it does not have.

16.400 Internal Provider Tool Use

If the Provider may use hidden search, tools or submodels, the integration shall record that uncertainty where relevant.

16.401 Data-Processing Boundary

The Connector shall identify what data crosses the Provider boundary.

Derived prompts and transformed media remain data processing.

16.402 Integration Testing

Every production Adapter and Connector shall have governed tests.

Test categories should include:

- unit,

- contract,

- schema,

- conformance,

- integration,

- sandbox,

- fault,

- security,

- performance,

- and recovery.

16.403 Adapter Unit Test

Unit tests validate:

- parameter mapping,

- schema mapping,

- error mapping,

- and response parsing.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.404 Contract Test

Contract tests verify canonical interface behaviour.

16.405 Provider Sandbox Test

Sandbox tests use Provider development or test Environments where available.

16.406 Live Integration Test

Live tests verify real Provider behaviour.

They require:

- Budget,

- safe data,

- and cleanup policy.

16.407 Mock Provider

A Mock Provider may simulate responses for deterministic testing.

16.408 Mock Limitation

Mock success does not prove live Provider conformance.

16.409 Recorded Fixture

Recorded Provider fixtures may support regression testing.

Fixtures shall be:

- redacted,

- versioned,

- and rights-compatible.

16.410 Replay Test

Recorded payloads may test parsing without repeating external side effects.

16.411 Schema Fuzzing

Fuzz tests may introduce:

- missing fields,

- extra fields,

- wrong types,

- and malformed payloads.

16.412 Error Injection

Tests should simulate:

- timeout,

- rate limit,

- invalid credential,

- Provider error,

- duplicate callback,

- and missing usage.

16.413 Asset Test

Asset integration tests should verify:

- download,

- expiry,

- checksum,

- format,

- and metadata.

16.414 Streaming Test

Streaming tests should verify:

- ordering,

- interruption,

- backpressure,

- and finalisation.

16.415 Pagination Test

Pagination tests should verify:

- complete enumeration,

- cursor expiry,

- duplicates,

- and mutation during listing.

16.416 Tool Side-Effect Test

Consequential Tool tests should use:

- sandbox,

- dry run,

- or isolated target.

16.417 Multi-Tenant Test

Shared Adapters shall receive isolation tests.

16.418 Secret-Leak Test

Tests shall verify secrets do not appear in:

- logs,

- errors,

- Outputs,

- or traces.

16.419 Policy-Enforcement Test

Adapters shall not invoke a target when canonical policy blocks execution.

16.420 Adapter Conformance

Adapter Conformance measures whether an Adapter satisfies the canonical integration contract.

16.421 Connector Conformance

Connector Conformance measures whether the governed integration provides:

- declared Capabilities,

- Features,

- maturity,

- security,

- evidence,

- and recovery.

16.422 Conformance Result

A Conformance Result shall include:

- conformanceResultId,

- Adapter or Connector Version,

- Test Suite,

- Environment,

- results,

- defects,

- decision,

- and time.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.423 Conformance States

States may include:

- conformant,

- conformant with restrictions,

- non-conformant,

- unresolved,

- expired,

- and superseded.

16.424 Restricted Conformance

An integration may be conformant only for:

- one Capability,

- one Project,

- one Environment,

- or one data class.

16.425 Conformance Expiry

Conformance may expire after:

- Provider API change,

- Adapter update,

- SDK change,

- or defined review period.

16.426 Certification

A production Connector may be certified after successful conformance and governance review.

Certification is not permanent.

16.427 Certification Revocation

Certification may be revoked after Incident or drift.

16.428 Integration Defect

An Integration Defect is a specific failure in:

- translation,

- mapping,

- protocol handling,

- security,

- evidence,

- or recovery.

16.429 Defect Severity

Severity may include:

- informational,

- minor,

- major,

- critical,

- and blocking.

16.430 Blocking Integration Defect

A blocking defect prevents production use.

16.431 Defect Ownership

Defect ownership may lie with:

- Adapter,

- Connector,

- Provider,

- SDK,

- Connection,

- schema,

- or configuration.

16.432 Integration Incident

An Integration Incident is a material failure affecting trustworthy external or local execution.

Examples include:

- wrong Provider Account,

- malformed request translation,

- missing Output ingestion,

- duplicate publication,

- raw secret in logs,

- schema drift,

- wrong cost mapping,

- or cross-Project response leakage.

16.433 Integration Incident Scope

Incident scope shall identify:

- Adapter Version,

- Connector Version,

- Connection,

- Provider,

- Account,

- Capabilities,

- Projects,

- and time.

16.434 Integration Incident Containment

Containment may include:

- suspend Adapter Version,

- suspend Connection,

- open circuit,

- block Capability,

- stop callbacks,

- or enter manual mode.

16.435 Integration Incident Recovery

Recovery may include:

- rollback,

- schema fix,

- replay parsing,

- reconciliation,

- Asset recovery,

- or credential rotation.

16.436 Integration Incident Review

Review should inspect:

- canonical request,

- translated request,

- Provider evidence,

- Adapter logs,

- mapping Version,

- and downstream state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.437 Translation Incident

A Translation Incident occurs when canonical intent or constraint is changed incorrectly.

16.438 Account-Mixing Incident

Using the wrong Provider Account is a severe integration and isolation defect.

16.439 Response-Mixing Incident

Returning another Tenant’s or Project’s response is a critical Incident.

16.440 Usage-Mapping Incident

Incorrect usage mapping may cause economic misattribution.

16.441 Asset-Loss Incident

Provider Output existed but Omnira failed to ingest or preserve it.

16.442 Callback-Trust Incident

An invalid or spoofed callback affected canonical state.

16.443 Browser-Automation Incident

A browser-assisted path may click or submit the wrong target after interface change.

16.444 Manual-Procedure Incident

A human-assisted procedure may use the wrong Account, Asset or instructions.

16.445 Integration Governance

Adapter and Connector changes are architectural changes.

They shall be governed through:

- Versioning,

- review,

- test,

- release,

- rollback,

- and retirement.

16.446 Adapter Ownership

Every Adapter shall have an accountable owner or steward.

16.447 Connector Ownership

Every Connector shall have a business and technical owner where appropriate.

16.448 Connection Ownership

Every Connection shall identify the responsible owner.

16.449 Mapping Ownership

Capability and Feature mappings require an accountable steward.

16.450 Release Approval

Production Adapter releases should require:

- conformance,

- security review,

- migration assessment,

- and rollback readiness.

16.451 Mapping Change Approval

Changing a mapping may alter output or Provider behaviour.

Material changes require review.

16.452 Provider API Change

Provider API changes shall trigger impact assessment.

16.453 Provider Deprecation

Deprecation shall identify:

- replacement,

- deadline,

- affected Connections,

- and migration path.

16.454 Adapter Deprecation

Deprecated Adapter Versions should be removed from new Routing Candidates.

16.455 Connection Migration

Migration shall preserve:

- Account ownership,

- Project scope,

- credentials,

- Model mapping,

- Assets,

- and historical evidence.

16.456 Parallel Adapter Versions

Several Adapter Versions may coexist during migration.

Routing and Execution shall identify the selected Version exactly.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.457 Canary Release

A new Adapter Version may receive limited traffic.

16.458 Shadow Translation

A new Adapter may translate requests without dispatching them to compare behaviour.

16.459 Dual Read

During migration, the system may compare states through old and new Connectors.

Dual read shall not duplicate side effects.

16.460 Dual Write Prohibition

Dual writing consequential actions to two integrations is prohibited unless explicitly designed and idempotent.

16.461 Rollback Readiness

A release shall define how to return to a safe prior Version.

16.462 Compatibility

Compatibility may be:

- backward,

- forward,

- bidirectional,

- or none.

The claim shall be tested.

16.463 Canonical Schema Evolution

Canonical schema evolution shall avoid forcing every Adapter to update simultaneously without migration support.

16.464 Required-Field Introduction

New mandatory fields require:

- default,

- migration,

- compatibility layer,

- or coordinated release.

16.465 Optional-Field Introduction

Optional fields may be ignored only when their semantics are truly optional.

16.466 Field Deprecation

Deprecated fields shall retain a transition period and mapping guidance.

16.467 Enum Expansion

External Adapters shall handle unknown enum values safely.

16.468 Unknown Enum

Unknown enum values shall not crash or map to incorrect canonical state silently.

16.469 Provider Schema Evolution

Provider schema updates shall be isolated within the relevant Adapter.

16.470 Protocol Evolution

Protocol Version changes may require new Connector or Adapter Version.

16.471 Integration Documentation

Every production Connector should have documentation covering:

- purpose,

- supported Capabilities,

- configuration,

- limitations,

- policy,

- failure modes,

- cost mapping,

- and recovery.

16.472 Adapter Specification

The Adapter specification should define:

- canonical input,

- Provider operation,

- mappings,

- response,

- errors,

- usage,

- and evidence.

16.473 Connection Runbook

Critical Connections should have a runbook for:

- authentication failure,

- Provider outage,

- schema change,

- and suspension.

16.474 Manual Procedure Documentation

Human-assisted procedures shall include:

- exact steps,

- target Account,

- expected evidence,

- failure path,

- and review date.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.475 Documentation Version

Documentation shall align with the Adapter and Connector Versions.

16.476 Developer Experience

The integration architecture should make it possible to add a new Provider without modifying every Project or Agent.

A developer should implement:

- canonical Capability mappings,

- Adapter translations,

- Connection requirements,

- tests,

- and evidence

rather than Provider-specific business logic.

16.477 Adapter Interface

A canonical Adapter interface should support operations such as:

- validate,

- prepare request,

- dispatch,

- stream,

- poll,

- cancel,

- parse response,

- map error,

- map usage,

- collect evidence,

- and health check.

16.487 Integration Graph

16.488 Routing Relationship

- Connection eligibility,

- maturity,

- health,

- cost,

- streaming,

- callback,

16.491 Reliability Relationship

- timeout,

- retry,

- circuit,

- fallback,

- and reconciliation.

16.492 Cost Relationship

The economic system consumes usage and cost evidence from the integration.

16.493 Quality Relationship

The Quality system evaluates the returned Output.

Adapter conformance remains separate from Output quality.

16.494 Asset Relationship

The Asset system ingests and governs external Outputs and reusable Provider Assets.

16.495 Identity Relationship

Identity and credentials are resolved through governed references.

The Adapter does not own them.

16.496 Approval Relationship

Connection use and consequential Tool actions may require approval.

16.497 Observability Relationship

Integration traces and metrics feed the Observability system.

16.498 Stage 1 Integration Objective

Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy integration foundation capable of supporting representative:

- local,

- external,

- API,

- MCP,

- Tool,

- multimodal,

- asynchronous,

- and human-assisted paths.

The objective is not to integrate every Provider.

Stage 1 shall prove:

- canonical Adapter and Connector contracts,

- Connection identity and scope,

- Capability and Feature mapping,

- request and response normalisation,

- error and usage mapping,

- Asset transfer,

- health,

- Versioning,

- conformance,

- and truthful manual fallback.

- image Provider Adapter,

- voice Provider Adapter,

- local Tool Adapter,

- MCP Connector,

16.524 Stage 1 Connector Acceptance Tests

15. Connection retirement preserves historical Executions.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.526 Stage 1 Capability-Mapping Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Mapping references exact canonical Capability.

2. Mapping references canonical Version.

11. Unknown finish reason remains unknown.

13. Raw response is access-controlled.

14. Secret fields are redacted.

15. Output remains linked to Adapter and Connection.

Capability

text.reason.

text.reason

to the Provider’s chat or responses operation.

- role names,

execution mode

human-assisted.

16.548 Applied Example — ElevenLabs Voice Connector

A speech-synthesis request may include:

- approved Voice Asset,

16.549 Applied Example — Video Provider Async Job

A video request is translated into an asynchronous Provider job.

The Adapter:

1. validates Input Assets.

2. submits the job with canonical idempotency correlation.

3. stores Provider job ID.

4. maps queued and running states.

5. receives or polls for completion.

6. validates the returned Asset.

7. records usage and warnings.

8. ingests the video before URL expiry.

Provider completion alone does not satisfy the Quality Gate.

An MCP server exposes repository Tools.

The Connector discovers:

- read file,

- search,

- inspect Git status,

- modify file,

- and commit.

The Project policy permits only:

- read file,

- search,

- and inspect Git status

for one audit Plan.

The read-only Connection shall prevent modification and commit even though the server exposes them.

- transcode,

- working directory,

- input checksums,

- output checksum,

search.current

- image Provider Connector,

- voice Connector,

- local media Tool Adapter,

- and publication Connector.

Each Step uses a separate governed Connection.

No single Provider SDK controls the full production.

text:
16.559 Applied Example — Nova and Pling Scene

A Familje-Stunden scene may require:

- canonical Nova reference Asset,

- canonical Pling reference Asset,

- multi-character support,

- 16:9 video,

- and bounded duration.

The video Connector’s Capability Mapping shall declare whether:

- two reference Assets are supported,

- identity preservation is tested,

- duration is exact or approximate,

- and callback is production-ready.

A generic image-to-video claim is insufficient.

16.560 Applied Example — Adapter Schema Drift

A Provider changes the completion payload field from:

output_url

to:

assets[0].url.

The old Adapter fails response validation.

The correct response is:

- mark the Attempt as integration failure or unresolved according to external state,

- open an Adapter defect,

- suspend affected Adapter Version if necessary,

- create a new mapping Version,

- run regression tests,

- and deploy through controlled release.

The system shall not guess silently from unrelated fields.

16.561 Applied Example — Wrong Account Prevention

Two Projects use the same Provider.

Familje-Stunden and GainPilot have separate Accounts.

The Routing Decision for a Familje-Stunden scene selects the Familje-Stunden Connection.

The Adapter receives only that Connection’s short-lived credential material.

It cannot choose the GainPilot Account by Provider name alone.

16.562 Applied Example — Duplicate Callback

A video Provider sends the same completion webhook three times.

The Webhook Connector validates:

- signature,

- event ID,

- timestamp,

- and job correlation.

Deduplication ensures one:

- state transition,

- Asset ingestion,

- Usage Record,

- and completion event.

All callback receipts may remain evidence.

16.563 Applied Example — Missing Usage

A Provider returns a completed image but no usage field.

The Adapter records:

- Output received,

- usage unknown,

- pricing reference,

- and reconciliation required.

It shall not create zero usage.

16.564 Applied Example — Provider Asset URL Expiry

A Provider video URL expires after twenty-four hours.

The Connection and Connector metadata expose that constraint.

The Plan and Scheduler shall ensure timely ingestion.

If ingestion fails before expiry, the Integration state remains incomplete even when the Provider job succeeded.

16.615 Future Integration Architecture

Future versions may support:

- standard Agent-to-Agent protocols,

- dynamic Connector discovery,

- signed Connector manifests,

- verified plugin marketplaces,

- policy-carrying requests,

- confidential-compute Connectors,

- federated edge Connectors,

- self-describing Provider capabilities,

- automated mapping generation,

- and protocol-neutral execution contracts.

Future evolution must preserve:

- canonical semantics,

- explicit trust boundaries,

- Versioning,

- authority,

- and provenance.

16.616 Signed Connector Manifest

A signed manifest may declare:

- identity,

- Capabilities,

- permissions,

- schema,

- owner,

- and Version.

Signatures do not replace conformance testing.

16.617 Dynamic Discovery

The Fabric may discover new:

- MCP Tools,

- local Models,

- Provider Products,

- or Connectors.

Discovery shall not create production eligibility automatically.

16.618 Automated Mapping Suggestion

AI may propose Capability or parameter mappings.

Human or governed conformance review remains required.

16.619 Generated Adapter

Code generation may accelerate Adapter creation.

Generated code shall meet the same testing and security requirements.

16.620 Confidential-Compute Connector

Future Connectors may target trusted execution environments.

Actual guarantees shall be evidenced rather than assumed.

16.621 Federated Edge Connector

User-controlled Nodes may expose governed local Capabilities across encrypted channels.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.622 Agent Protocol Connector

Future external Agent protocols may expose:

- goals,

- tasks,

- delegation,

- and results.

External Agent autonomy shall remain bounded by canonical authority.

16.623 Portable Connector Package

Connectors may become portable deployment packages containing:

- Adapter,

- manifest,

- tests,

- schemas,

- and documentation.

16.624 Connector Marketplace

A future marketplace may distribute approved Connectors.

Installation shall not equal permission.

16.625 Integration Success Criteria

The integration architecture succeeds when:

- Projects request Capabilities rather than Providers,

- Adapter logic contains Provider-specific translation,

- Connections preserve exact Account and scope,

- local and external resources use one canonical model,

- errors and usage are normalised truthfully,

- external Assets become durable only through validated ingestion,

- manual paths remain honest,

- and integrations can evolve without rewriting Project architecture.

16.626 Integration Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- Provider schema becomes canonical business logic,

- raw credentials enter Connector records,

- Provider Account is missing,

- unsupported Features are ignored,

- Provider success becomes quality acceptance,

- temporary URLs become canonical Assets,

- callbacks create duplicate effects,

- manual work is represented as automation,

- or Adapter changes rewrite historical execution truth.

16.627 Canonical Adapter Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Adapter contract:

1. Every Adapter SHALL have stable identity.

2. Every Adapter release SHALL have an explicit Version.

3. Every Adapter SHALL reference a governed Connector.

4. Every Adapter SHALL identify its target Product, protocol, runtime or procedure.

5. Every Adapter SHALL translate canonical requests deterministically where practical.

6. Every Adapter SHALL validate mandatory canonical fields.

7. Every Adapter SHALL preserve request correlation.

8. Every Adapter SHALL preserve Provider or external identifiers.

9. Every Adapter SHALL normalise responses into canonical Output types.

10. Every Adapter SHALL map errors into canonical categories.

11. Every Adapter SHALL preserve Provider-native error evidence.

12. Every Adapter SHALL map usage where available.

13. Missing usage SHALL remain unknown.

14. Every Adapter SHALL preserve Adapter Version in execution evidence.

15. Adapters SHALL NOT own Agent identity.

16. Adapters SHALL NOT choose unrestricted fallback resources.

17. Adapters SHALL NOT grant authority.

18. Adapters SHALL NOT contain raw credentials.

19. Adapters SHALL NOT silently alter Capability meaning.

20. Historical Adapter Versions SHALL remain resolvable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.628 Canonical Connector Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Connector contract:

1. Every Connector SHALL have stable identity.

2. Every Connector SHALL have explicit Version.

3. Every Connector SHALL identify supported protocol classes.

4. Every Connector SHALL identify supported canonical Capabilities.

5. Every Connector SHALL identify supported Features.

6. Every Connector SHALL identify required Connection properties.

7. Every Connector SHALL identify maturity.

8. Every Connector SHALL identify lifecycle.

9. Every Connector SHALL reference approved Adapter Versions.

10. Every Connector SHALL identify policy restrictions.

11. Connector SHALL remain distinct from Provider.

12. Connector SHALL remain distinct from Model.

13. Connector SHALL remain distinct from Connection.

14. Unsupported Capabilities SHALL fail explicitly.

15. Approximate mappings SHALL be labelled.

16. Connector health SHALL preserve component detail.

17. Connector changes SHALL be versioned.

18. Deprecated Connectors SHALL be excluded from new routing.

19. Retired Connectors SHALL remain historically queryable.

20. Connector capability claims SHALL require evidence.

16.629 Canonical Connection Contract

The following requirements define the canonical Connection contract:

1. Every persistent Connection SHALL have stable identity.

2. Every Connection SHALL reference Connector Version.

3. Every Connection SHALL reference Adapter Version or permitted Adapter set.

4. Every Connection SHALL identify owner.

5. Every Connection SHALL identify Tenant.

6. Every Project-scoped Connection SHALL identify Project.

7. Every Connection SHALL identify Environment.

8. External Connections SHALL identify Provider Account.

9. Local Connections SHALL identify Runtime Node or target.

10. Every Connection SHALL identify endpoint or invocation target.

11. Region SHALL be explicit where material.

12. Connection SHALL reference credentials indirectly.

13. Connection scope SHALL identify permitted Capabilities.

14. Connection scope SHALL identify data restrictions.

15. Connection lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

16. Suspended, revoked, expired or retired Connections SHALL NOT execute.

17. Shared Connections SHALL preserve Tenant and Project attribution.

18. Personal Connections SHALL NOT become shared silently.

19. Connection changes SHALL be attributable.

20. Historical Connections SHALL remain resolvable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.630 Canonical Capability-Mapping Contract

The following requirements define canonical Capability Mapping:

1. Every Capability Mapping SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Mapping SHALL reference one canonical Capability.

3. Mapping SHALL identify canonical Capability Version or compatible range.

4. Mapping SHALL reference Connector Version.

5. Mapping SHALL identify implementation operation.

6. Mapping SHALL identify supported Features.

7. Mandatory Features SHALL require verified support.

8. Unsupported mandatory Features SHALL fail.

9. Optional unsupported Features SHALL be disclosed.

10. Approximate mappings SHALL remain labelled.

11. Composite mappings SHALL disclose hidden composition.

12. Mapping constraints SHALL be explicit.

13. Mapping maturity SHALL be explicit.

14. Mapping evidence SHALL be attributable.

15. Provider drift SHALL trigger review.

16. Mapping changes SHALL create a new Version.

17. Project-specific mappings SHALL remain scoped.

18. Mapping SHALL NOT create authority.

19. Mapping SHALL NOT lower Quality Floor.

20. Historical mappings SHALL remain interpretable.

16.631 Canonical Translation Contract

The following requirements define canonical translation:

1. Translation SHALL preserve user intent.

2. Translation SHALL preserve mandatory constraints.

3. Translation SHALL preserve data classification.

4. Translation SHALL preserve authority boundaries.

5. Translation SHALL preserve Project and Tenant scope.

6. Translation SHALL preserve idempotency correlation.

7. Translation SHALL preserve exact Connection identity.

8. Provider-specific fields SHALL remain inside the integration boundary.

9. Canonical defaults SHALL remain distinct from Provider defaults.

10. Unsupported mandatory parameters SHALL fail.

11. Unit conversions SHALL be explicit.

12. Derived fields SHALL preserve provenance.

13. Ignored optional fields SHALL be visible.

14. Outbound payloads SHALL be validated.

15. Inbound payloads SHALL be validated.

16. Schema drift SHALL fail safely.

17. Unknown enum values SHALL remain unknown.

18. Translation rules SHALL be versioned.

19. Translation SHALL NOT expose raw secrets.

20. Translation evidence SHALL remain queryable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.632 Canonical Response-Normalisation Contract

The following requirements define response normalisation:

1. Every external response SHALL remain linked to exact Execution and Attempt.

2. Provider request or job ID SHALL be preserved.

3. Provider-native lifecycle state SHALL be preserved.

4. Canonical lifecycle interpretation SHALL be explicit.

5. Output type SHALL match actual returned content.

6. Missing mandatory Output SHALL prevent canonical success.

7. Finish reason SHALL be preserved.

8. Provider warnings SHALL remain visible.

9. Structured-output parse state SHALL be explicit.

10. External Asset references SHALL preserve Provider and Account.

11. Temporary URL expiry SHALL be explicit.

12. Raw response MAY be retained as protected evidence.

13. Raw response SHALL be redacted where required.

14. Provider success SHALL NOT become quality acceptance.

15. Provider completion SHALL NOT become durable Asset automatically.

16. Unknown state SHALL remain valid.

17. Response mapping SHALL be versioned.

18. Duplicate responses SHALL NOT duplicate canonical effects.

19. Historical normalised results SHALL remain immutable.

20. Normalisation SHALL be human- and machine-interpretable.

16.633 Canonical Error-Mapping Contract

The following requirements define canonical error mapping:

1. Every material Provider error SHALL preserve original code or category.

2. Every mapped error SHALL identify canonical category.

3. Retryability SHALL be explicit.

4. Severity SHALL be explicit.

5. Validation errors SHALL remain distinct from Provider failure.

6. Authentication errors SHALL remain distinct from authorisation errors.

7. Rate limits SHALL remain distinct from quota exhaustion.

8. Account failure SHALL remain distinct from Provider outage.

9. Timeout SHALL NOT become confirmed failure automatically.

10. Network failure SHALL preserve submission uncertainty.

11. Unsupported Feature SHALL challenge Capability evidence.

12. Unknown errors SHALL remain unknown.

13. Error Mapping SHALL be versioned.

14. Error detail SHALL NOT expose raw secrets.

15. Provider messages SHALL be treated as untrusted text.

16. Mapping changes SHALL NOT rewrite historical Attempts.

17. High unknown-error rate SHOULD reduce maturity.

18. Errors SHALL remain linked to Connection and Adapter Version.

19. Error evidence SHALL remain queryable.

20. Error Mapping SHALL support Reliability Policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.634 Canonical Usage-Mapping Contract

The following requirements define canonical usage mapping:

1. Usage SHALL remain linked to Execution and Attempt.

2. Usage SHALL identify Provider Account.

3. Usage SHALL identify Model, Tool or Product.

4. Provider-native units SHALL be preserved.

5. Canonical units MAY be derived transparently.

6. Input and output usage SHALL remain distinct.

7. Cached usage SHALL remain distinct.

8. Tool or search usage SHALL remain distinct where billed separately.

9. Credit usage SHALL preserve original units.

10. Estimated usage SHALL remain distinct from reported usage.

11. Provisional usage SHALL remain distinct from confirmed usage.

12. Missing usage SHALL remain unknown.

13. Duplicate callbacks SHALL NOT duplicate usage.

14. Usage Mapping SHALL be versioned.

15. Usage confidence SHALL be explicit where inferred.

16. Usage SHALL NOT create Budget authority.

17. Usage SHALL support cost reconciliation.

18. Account-tier context SHALL remain visible where material.

19. Historical usage SHALL remain queryable.

20. Usage records SHALL NOT expose credentials.

16.635 Canonical Asset-Integration Contract

The following requirements define canonical Asset integration:

1. External Asset identity SHALL be preserved.

2. Provider Account SHALL be preserved.

3. Temporary and durable references SHALL remain distinct.

4. Temporary URL expiry SHALL be explicit.

5. Required Assets SHALL be ingested or durably referenced before canonical completion.

6. Downloaded content SHOULD receive checksum.

7. Actual file format SHALL be validated.

8. Required metadata SHALL be validated.

9. Failed ingestion SHALL remain incomplete state.

10. Duplicate callback SHALL NOT duplicate Asset admission.

11. Provider-hosted and Omnira-hosted Assets SHALL remain distinct.

12. Provider Project Asset affinity SHALL remain explicit.

13. Asset deletion SHALL require authority.

14. Asset portability SHALL be represented.

15. Asset expiry SHALL influence scheduling and recovery.

16. Asset mapping SHALL preserve provenance.

17. Protected Assets SHALL preserve classification.

18. Imported files SHALL be treated as untrusted until validated.

19. Historical external references SHALL remain queryable.

20. Quality acceptance SHALL remain separate from ingestion.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.636 Canonical Human-Assisted Integration Contract

The following requirements define human-assisted integration:

1. Every Manual Procedure SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Procedure SHALL identify required operator role.

3. Procedure SHALL identify Project and Tenant scope.

4. Procedure SHALL identify exact Provider Account or target.

5. Procedure SHALL identify instructions.

6. Procedure SHALL identify expected Output.

7. Procedure SHALL identify maximum spend where paid.

8. Procedure SHALL identify required evidence.

9. Procedure SHALL identify failure and escalation paths.

10. Human-assisted execution SHALL remain labelled.

11. Human completion SHALL remain attributable.

12. Manual uncertainty SHALL remain visible.

13. Manual cost SHALL be reconciled where possible.

14. Wrong Account use SHALL create Incident.

15. Missing evidence SHALL block full completion where required.

16. Procedure drift SHALL trigger review.

17. Human-assisted path SHALL remain subject to policy.

18. Human-assisted path SHALL remain subject to Quality Gates.

19. Procedure history SHALL remain queryable.

20. Human-assisted integration SHALL NOT be represented as autonomous API execution.

16.637 Canonical MCP Integration Contract

The following requirements define canonical MCP integration:

1. Every MCP server SHALL have stable identity.

2. Transport SHALL be explicit.

3. Connection scope SHALL be explicit.

4. Tool discovery SHALL NOT create authority.

5. Tool schemas SHALL be validated.

6. Tool side-effect classes SHALL be declared.

7. Project and Tenant scope SHALL be enforced.

8. Read-only Connections SHALL block mutation.

9. Server prompts SHALL be treated as untrusted metadata.

10. Server resources SHALL remain subject to data policy.

11. Local MCP servers SHALL NOT be trusted automatically.

12. Remote MCP servers SHALL remain external trust boundaries.

13. Inventory drift SHALL trigger review.
