14. Tool invocation SHALL preserve server and Tool identity.

15. MCP errors SHALL map canonically.

16. MCP Connection lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

17. Suspended MCP Connections SHALL NOT execute.

18. MCP events SHALL preserve correlation.

19. MCP integration SHALL NOT expose raw credentials.

20. Historical Tool schemas and executions SHALL remain queryable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.638 Canonical Integration Conformance Contract

The following requirements define integration conformance:

1. Every production Adapter SHALL have a Conformance Result.

2. Every production Connector SHALL have supported-Capability evidence.

3. Conformance SHALL identify exact Version.

4. Conformance SHALL identify Test Suite.

5. Conformance SHALL identify Environment.

6. Conformance SHALL identify restrictions.

7. Security tests SHALL be included.

8. Isolation tests SHALL be included for shared components.

9. Error and schema tests SHALL be included.

10. Recovery tests SHALL be included for long-running integrations.

11. Asset tests SHALL be included for multimodal integrations.

12. Secret-leak tests SHALL be included.

13. Live Provider tests SHOULD supplement mocks where practical.

14. Mock success SHALL NOT prove production compatibility.

15. Conformance SHALL expire after material drift.

16. Non-conformant Versions SHALL NOT serve production.

17. Restricted conformance SHALL be enforced.

18. Certification revocation SHALL affect routing.

19. Historical Conformance Results SHALL remain immutable.

20. Conformance evidence SHALL remain human- and machine-readable.

16.639 Canonical Integration Governance Contract

The following requirements define overall integration governance:

1. Provider-specific schemas SHALL NOT become canonical Project contracts.

2. Adapters SHALL isolate implementation variation.

3. Connectors SHALL expose governed integration capability.

4. Connections SHALL preserve exact operational scope.

5. Provider Accounts SHALL remain explicit.

6. Credentials SHALL remain indirect references.

7. Local and external integrations SHALL use one canonical object model.

8. Manual paths SHALL remain truthful.

9. Capability mappings SHALL be evidence-based.

10. Integration maturity SHALL be explicit.

11. Adapter and Connector changes SHALL be versioned.

12. Production releases SHALL be tested and reversible.

13. Cross-Tenant and cross-Project isolation SHALL be enforced.

14. External Inputs SHALL be treated as untrusted.

15. Integration failure SHALL NOT bypass the Fabric.

16. Usage and cost evidence SHALL remain attributable.

17. External Assets SHALL require validated ingestion or durable reference.

18. Protocol drift SHALL trigger review.

19. Historical integration truth SHALL remain reconstructable.

20. Omnira SHALL remain Provider-independent at canonical boundaries.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
16.640 Integration Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No Provider schema becomes the canonical Project schema.

- No Adapter becomes a Provider.

- No Connector becomes a Connection.

- No Connection hides its Provider Account or Runtime Node.

- No Adapter owns Agent identity.

- No Connector stores raw credentials.

- No active Connection becomes automatically eligible.

- No discovered Tool becomes automatically authorised.

- No MCP prompt overrides Omnira policy.

- No local integration becomes trusted by location alone.

- No browser-assisted workflow is represented as an API.

- No human-assisted execution is represented as autonomous.

- No mandatory parameter is dropped silently.

- No missing usage becomes zero.

- No timeout becomes confirmed failure automatically.

- No Provider success becomes quality acceptance.

- No temporary URL becomes a durable Asset automatically.

- No duplicate callback creates duplicate canonical effect.

- No Adapter silently chooses an unapproved fallback.

- No Adapter or Connector change rewrites historical execution evidence.

16.641 Closing Statement

The Adapter and Connector architecture is the boundary that allows Omnira to use many forms of intelligence without allowing any one Provider, protocol or tool to define the platform.

The Capability defines what must be achieved.

The Plan defines which bounded operation is required.

The Routing Decision selects an eligible resource path.

The Connector defines the governed integration capability.

The Connection identifies the exact operational target.

The Adapter translates canonical meaning into implementation-specific action.

The Provider, Tool, Runtime or human operator performs the work.

The Adapter translates the result back into canonical evidence.

The Asset system preserves durable Outputs.

The Cost system reconciles usage.

The Quality system determines acceptance.

The Reliability system handles uncertainty and recovery.

For Familje-Stunden, this architecture allows Nova and Pling production to combine:

- an external image Provider,

- an asynchronous video Provider,

- an approved voice service,

- local media tools,

- and human creative review

without embedding those Provider interfaces into the Project’s canonical design.

For The Prompt, it allows:

- current search,

- source retrieval,

- reasoning,

- voice,

- avatar,

- composition,

- and publication

to remain separate governed integrations.

For GainPilot, it allows economical local and external resources to be substituted without rewriting the Project’s workflows.

For Omnira, it allows:

- APIs,

- MCP,

- local Models,

- local Tools,

- webhooks,

- queues,

- browser-assisted systems,

- human-assisted Providers,

- and future Agent protocols

to coexist behind one canonical boundary.

The Provider may change.

The endpoint may change.

The SDK may change.

The protocol may change.

The Model may change.

The Provider Account may change.

The user’s intent and Omnira’s governance shall not.

No integration without a boundary.

No boundary without identity.

No Connection without scope.

No Adapter without Version.

No Capability claim without evidence.

No external action without authority.

No response without validation.

No Asset without provenance.

No manual work without truth.

The user retains control.

The Project retains its architecture.

Omnira retains canonical meaning.

The Fabric connects intelligence without becoming owned by its integrations.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical architecture, governance model, object model, lifecycle, contracts and operational responsibilities for APIs, Model Context Protocol integrations, webhooks, event delivery, polling, streaming and asynchronous jobs within the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

It establishes:

- how synchronous and asynchronous integration patterns remain distinct,

- how API operations are described independently from Provider SDKs,

- how canonical request, response, command, event and callback envelopes are represented,

- how long-running Provider jobs are submitted, tracked, reconciled and completed,

- how polling and callbacks cooperate without duplicating state,

- how webhooks are authenticated, validated, deduplicated and ordered,

- how MCP servers, Tools, Resources and prompts remain governed external capabilities,

- how MCP discovery remains separate from MCP authority,

- how sessions, transports and server inventory changes are handled,

- how queue and event delivery semantics are represented truthfully,

- how at-least-once delivery is made safe through idempotency and deduplication,

- how correlation, causation, tracing and provenance cross protocol boundaries,

- how pagination, rate limits, quotas and backpressure are handled,

- how streaming results remain partial until finalisation,

- how asynchronous work survives worker, service and network failure,

- how unknown outcomes remain explicit,

- how callbacks and events remain subordinate to canonical state machines,

- how external payloads are treated as untrusted data,

- how Project, Tenant, Environment and authority scope remain preserved,

- how protocol versioning and schema evolution are governed,

- how APIs, MCP, webhooks and queues remain implementation mechanisms rather than business architecture,

- and how Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy protocol foundation.

An API response is not automatically an accepted Output.

A webhook is not automatically trusted.

A callback is not automatically unique.

A successful HTTP status is not automatically business success.

A timeout is not automatically Provider failure.

A queued external job is not automatically durable inside Omnira.

An MCP Tool is not automatically authorised because a server exposes it.

An event is not automatically current merely because it arrived later.

A retried message is not automatically a new logical operation.

A streaming fragment is not automatically a final result.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

Credential, identity and secret mechanics are defined in Chapter 18.

Implementation and conformance must be verified separately.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.2 Purpose of Protocol Governance

The Intelligence Fabric communicates with:

- external AI Providers,

- local Model runtimes,

- MCP servers,

- search services,

- media-generation platforms,

- repository systems,

- publication platforms,

- internal platform services,

- human-assisted procedures,

- queues,

- event buses,

- and future Agent protocols.

Those systems use different interaction patterns.

Some return immediately.

Some stream partial data.

Some create jobs that finish minutes or hours later.

Some send callbacks.

Some require polling.

Some expose discovered Tools.

Some deliver duplicate events.

Some lose callbacks.

Some return temporary Asset URLs.

Some change schemas without warning.

Some retry automatically.

Some provide incomplete usage or billing evidence.

The protocol architecture exists to ensure that these differences do not weaken:

- authority,

- policy,

- cost control,

- reliability,

- Project isolation,

- quality,

- provenance,

- or truthful state.

17.3 Protocol Is Not Capability

A protocol describes how communication occurs.

A Capability describes what can be achieved.

The same Capability may be accessed through:

- synchronous API,

- asynchronous API,

- streaming API,

- MCP Tool,

- local process,

- queue,

- browser-assisted procedure,

- or human-assisted operation.

The protocol shall not become the Capability identity.

17.4 Protocol Is Not Provider

One Provider may expose several protocols.

Several Providers may expose equivalent protocol patterns.

Protocol identity and Provider identity shall remain separate.

17.5 Protocol Is Not Authority

A technically callable endpoint does not create permission to use it.

A discovered MCP Tool does not create authority.

A valid webhook signature does not grant permission to perform a downstream action.

Authority remains governed by Omnira.

17.6 Protocol Is Not Completion

A transport-level success indicates only that one communication phase succeeded.

Canonical completion may still require:

- external processing,

- Output retrieval,

- Asset ingestion,

- usage capture,

- quality evaluation,

- approval,

- side-effect verification,

- and reconciliation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.7 Protocol Is Not Reliability

HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, queue and webhook mechanisms expose different reliability characteristics.

The protocol alone does not guarantee:

- delivery,

- ordering,

- uniqueness,

- durability,

- or completion.

17.8 Protocol Control Plane

The Protocol Control Plane is the governed collection of services and canonical objects responsible for:

- API contracts,

- protocol negotiation,

- request and response envelopes,

- asynchronous job tracking,

- callback registration,

- webhook receipt,

- event validation,

- polling,

- streaming,

- message delivery,

- MCP sessions,

- Tool invocation,

- schema versioning,

- correlation,

- deduplication,

- and protocol observability.

It shall integrate with:

- Adapters,

- Connectors,

- Connections,

- Planning,

- Routing,

- Execution,

- Scheduling,

- Reliability,

- Cost,

- Quality,

- Assets,

- Policy,

- and Identity.

17.9 Canonical Protocol Objects

The canonical protocol object model should include or reference:

- Protocol Profile,

- API Contract,

- API Operation,

- Request Envelope,

- Response Envelope,

- Command Envelope,

- Event Envelope,

- Callback Contract,

- Webhook Endpoint,

- Webhook Subscription,

- Webhook Receipt,

- Delivery Attempt,

- Polling Policy,

- Stream Session,

- Stream Event,

- Asynchronous Job,

- External Job Reference,

- Job Status Observation,

- Queue Message,

- Queue Subscription,

- MCP Server,

- MCP Session,

- MCP Tool Definition,

- MCP Resource Definition,

- MCP Prompt Definition,

- MCP Invocation,

- Protocol Error,

- Schema Version,

- Correlation Context,

- and Protocol Receipt.

17.10 Protocol Profile

A Protocol Profile defines the communication properties of one integration mode.

It should include or reference:

- protocolProfileId,

- protocol class,

- transport,

- version,

- interaction style,

- delivery semantics,

- ordering semantics,

- timeout model,

- retry model,

- authentication mechanism,

- payload limits,

- streaming support,

- callback support,

- and lifecycle.

17.11 Protocol Profile Identity

Every reusable Protocol Profile shall have stable identity and Version.

17.12 Protocol Classes

Canonical protocol classes may include:

- synchronous request-response,

- asynchronous request-status-result,

- server streaming,

- client streaming,

- bidirectional streaming,

- webhook callback,

- polling,

- event subscription,

- queue command,

- queue event,

- local process,

- MCP,

- file exchange,

- browser-assisted,

- and human-assisted.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.13 Transport

Transport may include:

- HTTPS,

- HTTP/2,

- HTTP/3,

- WebSocket,

- Server-Sent Events,

- local socket,

- standard input and output,

- message broker,

- file system,

- or protocol-specific channel.

17.14 Transport Security

Transport security shall be explicit.

Secure transport does not replace:

- payload validation,

- identity,

- authority,

- or data-class eligibility.

17.15 Protocol Version

Every protocol interaction shall preserve the relevant protocol or API Version where known.

17.16 Interaction Style

Interaction style may be:

- immediate,

- deferred,

- streamed,

- event-driven,

- polled,

- or human-mediated.

17.17 Delivery Semantics

Delivery semantics may include:

- at most once,

- at least once,

- effectively once through idempotency,

- best effort,

- Provider-defined,

- or unknown.

Universal exactly-once delivery shall not be claimed without proof.

17.18 Ordering Semantics

Ordering may be:

- total,

- partitioned,

- per-object,

- per-session,

- best effort,

- unordered,

- or unknown.

17.19 Protocol Maturity

Protocol maturity may be:

- experimental,

- preview,

- production,

- restricted,

- deprecated,

- legacy,

- or retired.

17.20 API

An API is a defined machine-to-machine interface exposing one or more operations.

An API shall be represented through canonical Contracts rather than only through SDK code.

17.21 API Contract

An API Contract defines the externally visible interface required for interaction.

It shall include or reference:

- apiContractId,

- Provider or service,

- Product,

- base endpoint class,

- API Version,

- operations,

- schemas,

- authentication mechanism,

- error model,

- rate limits,

- lifecycle,

- and provenance.

17.22 API Contract Identity

Every API Contract shall have stable identity and Version.

17.23 API Operation

An API Operation is one bounded endpoint or method invocation.

It shall include or reference:

- apiOperationId,

- method or procedure,

- path or target,

- request schema,

- response schema,

- interaction style,

- side-effect class,

- idempotency support,

- pagination support,

- streaming support,

- timeout model,

- and error mappings.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.24 API Operation Identity

Every reusable API Operation shall have stable identity.

17.25 API Method

API methods may include:

- GET,

- POST,

- PUT,

- PATCH,

- DELETE,

- RPC method,

- Graph operation,

- or Provider-specific invocation.

Method semantics shall not be inferred from the method name alone.

17.26 API Path

The endpoint path shall remain implementation-specific.

It shall not become the canonical Capability ID.

17.27 Read Operation

A Read Operation retrieves state without intended external mutation.

Read operations may still create:

- Provider usage,

- logs,

- rate-limit consumption,

- or data exposure.

17.28 Write Operation

A Write Operation creates or changes external state.

It requires explicit side-effect classification.

17.29 Delete Operation

A Delete Operation is consequential.

It shall require:

- exact target identity,

- authority,

- idempotency where possible,

- and verification.

17.30 Submission Operation

A Submission Operation sends work for immediate or deferred execution.

Provider acceptance does not imply completion.

17.31 Status Operation

A Status Operation retrieves current or historical state for an existing external job or object.

17.32 Cancellation Operation

A Cancellation Operation requests that external work stop.

Cancellation request and confirmed cancellation shall remain distinct.

17.33 Result Operation

A Result Operation retrieves the completed Output or references after external execution.

17.34 API Side-Effect Class

An API Operation shall declare whether it may:

- read,

- create,

- update,

- delete,

- publish,

- send,

- purchase,

- subscribe,

- unsubscribe,

- or execute code.

17.35 Safe Operation

A Safe Operation does not intend to alter external state.

Safe does not mean free of privacy or cost consequence.

17.36 Idempotent Operation

An idempotent operation may be repeated without creating additional unintended effect under defined conditions.

17.37 Non-Idempotent Operation

A non-idempotent operation may create repeated effects.

Retry requires stronger controls.

17.38 API Schema

API request and response schemas shall be versioned and validated.

17.39 Request Schema

The Request Schema defines the allowed external payload.

It shall not replace the canonical request schema.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.40 Response Schema

The Response Schema defines the expected external response structure.

17.41 Error Schema

The Error Schema defines Provider or service failure payloads.

Unknown error shapes shall fail safely.

17.42 Callback Schema

The Callback Schema defines externally delivered event or job-update payloads.

17.43 API Versioning

API Versioning may use:

- path,

- header,

- media type,

- query parameter,

- schema field,

- or Provider-managed alias.

17.44 API Version Preservation

The exact observed API Version shall remain in the Protocol Receipt.

17.45 Unversioned API

An externally unversioned API shall be treated as more volatile.

Conformance evidence should expire sooner.

17.46 API Deprecation

Deprecation shall identify:

- affected operations,

- replacement,

- deadline,

- migration impact,

- and affected Connections.

17.47 API Retirement

Retired API Versions shall be excluded from new execution.

Historical interactions shall remain interpretable.

17.48 Request Envelope

A Request Envelope is the canonical transport-facing wrapper for one outbound invocation.

It shall include or reference:

- requestEnvelopeId,

- operation,

- Connection,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- Execution,

- Attempt,

- correlation,

- causation,

- idempotency key,

- schema Version,

- payload reference,

- deadline,

- timeout,

- classification,

- and provenance.

17.49 Request Envelope Identity

Every material Request Envelope shall have stable identity.

17.50 Payload Reference

The Envelope may contain:

- inline payload,

- protected payload reference,

- Asset reference,

- or structured fields.

Large or sensitive payloads should not be duplicated unnecessarily.

17.51 Request Classification

The Request Envelope shall preserve the effective Data Classification.

17.52 Request Authority

The Request Envelope shall reference the authority and policy decision permitting dispatch.

It shall not contain broad reusable authority tokens unnecessarily.

17.53 Request Deadline

The Envelope shall preserve the applicable dispatch or completion deadline.

17.54 Request Timeout

The timeout shall be explicit and Operation-specific.

17.55 Request Fingerprint

A Request Fingerprint may support:

- idempotency,

- deduplication,

- audit,

- and conflict detection.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.56 Request Mutation

Once dispatched, the material Request Envelope Version shall be immutable.

17.57 Response Envelope

A Response Envelope is the canonical wrapper for one inbound synchronous or retrieved response.

It shall include or reference:

- responseEnvelopeId,

- Request Envelope,

- external request ID,

- status,

- schema Version,

- payload reference,

- warnings,

- usage,

- timing,

- receivedAt,

- and provenance.

17.58 Response Envelope Identity

Every material Response Envelope shall have stable identity.

17.59 Transport Status

Transport status shall remain distinct from canonical execution outcome.

17.60 Application Status

The external service may return an application-level state inside a successful transport response.

17.61 Partial Response

A partial response shall be marked explicitly.

It shall not become final Output automatically.

17.62 Empty Response

An empty response may be valid for some operations.

It shall be interpreted according to the API Contract.

17.63 Malformed Response

Malformed responses shall produce:

- schema failure,

- integration defect,

- or unknown external outcome

according to operation state.

17.64 Response Warning

Warnings shall remain visible and may affect:

- quality,

- rights,

- cost,

- or future eligibility.

17.65 Command Envelope

A Command Envelope represents an instruction requesting that a recipient perform an operation.

It shall include:

- commandId,

- command type,

- target,

- requested action,

- authority,

- idempotency,

- deadline,

- correlation,

- causation,

- schema Version,

- and payload reference.

17.66 Command Identity

Every Command shall have stable identity.

17.67 Command Versus Event

A Command requests that something happen.

An Event states that something is believed to have happened.

The two shall not be conflated.

17.68 Command Recipient

A Command shall identify the intended recipient or routing scope.

17.69 Command Expiry

Expired Commands shall not execute without explicit revalidation.

17.70 Command Rejection

Recipients may reject a Command because of:

- validation,

- authority,

- state conflict,

- policy,

- or capacity.

17.71 Event Envelope

An Event Envelope represents an immutable statement about an observed state change or occurrence.

It shall include or reference:

- eventId,

- event type,

- source,

- subject,

- event time,

- observed time,

- schema Version,

- correlation,

- causation,

- sequence or version,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- classification,

- payload reference,

- and provenance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.72 Event Identity

Every Event shall have stable identity.

17.73 Event Type

Event Type shall be canonical and versioned.

17.74 Event Source

The source shall identify the system or Principal that emitted the Event.

17.75 Event Subject

The subject identifies the object or resource affected.

17.76 Event Time

Event Time is when the external or canonical occurrence is believed to have happened.

17.77 Observed Time

Observed Time is when Omnira received or created the Event.

The two may differ significantly.

17.78 Event Sequence

Sequence may be:

- global,

- per-subject,

- per-job,

- per-session,

- or unavailable.

17.79 Event Version

Object Version may help reject stale updates.

17.80 Event Immutability

Published Event content shall not be edited in place.

Corrections require a new Event.

17.81 Event Correction

A correction Event shall reference the Event or state it corrects.

17.82 Event Retraction

A retraction indicates that a prior Event should no longer be treated as valid evidence.

The original remains historically visible.

17.83 Event Completeness

An Event may provide:

- complete state,

- partial change,

- or notification requiring a follow-up read.

17.84 Notification Event

A notification Event indicates that something changed but may not contain authoritative state.

The recipient may need reconciliation.

17.85 State-Carrying Event

A state-carrying Event includes enough state for the defined consumer use.

It still requires schema and source validation.

17.86 Event Trust

External Events shall be treated as untrusted until:

- source is authenticated,

- schema is validated,

- scope is resolved,

- and semantic checks pass.

17.87 Correlation Context

Correlation Context links protocol interactions belonging to the same logical work.

It may include:

- correlationId,

- requestId,

- planId,

- stepId,

- executionId,

- attemptId,

- jobId,

- sessionId,

- and traceId.

17.88 Correlation Identity

Correlation identifiers shall remain stable across retries and callbacks where they represent the same logical operation.

17.89 Causation Context

Causation identifies which prior command, request, event or decision caused the current interaction.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.90 Trace Context

Trace Context supports distributed observability.

Trace propagation shall not expose protected data.

17.91 External Correlation ID

Provider correlation identifiers shall be preserved exactly where supplied.

17.92 Correlation Loss

If an external callback lacks direct correlation, the system may resolve through:

- Provider job ID,

- Account,

- Asset ID,

- idempotency key,

- or controlled lookup.

Ambiguous correlation shall remain unresolved.

17.93 Synchronous API

A Synchronous API attempts to return its primary response during the initiating connection.

It is appropriate when:

- execution is short,

- response size is bounded,

- timeout risk is acceptable,

- and no long-lived Provider state is required.

17.94 Synchronous Request Lifecycle

Representative states include:

- prepared,

- dispatched,

- acknowledged,

- responding,

- received,

- parsed,

- failed,

- timed out,

- or unknown.

17.95 Synchronous Success

Synchronous success means the expected transport response arrived and passed protocol validation.

It does not automatically mean:

- Quality accepted,

- Asset durable,

- cost confirmed,

- or business complete.

17.96 Synchronous Timeout

Timeout after dispatch may create unknown outcome when the operation has side effects or Provider work may continue.

17.97 Synchronous Retry

Retry is permitted only when:

- operation semantics allow it,

- idempotency is preserved,

- Budget remains,

- and external completion ambiguity is resolved.

17.98 Long Work Through Synchronous API

Long-running work should not be forced through a synchronous connection merely for implementation convenience.

17.99 Asynchronous API

An Asynchronous API accepts work and returns an external job or operation reference before final completion.

17.100 Asynchronous Job

An Asynchronous Job is a canonical record representing deferred external or internal work.

It shall include or reference:

- asynchronousJobId,

- external job ID,

- Connection,

- Provider Account,

- Capability,

- Execution,

- Attempt,

- submitted request,

- current state,

- callback configuration,

- Polling Policy,

- deadline,

- timeout,

- Budget Reservation,

- Capacity Reservation where applicable,

- Outputs,

- usage,

- and provenance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.101 Asynchronous Job Identity

Every Asynchronous Job shall have stable identity.

17.102 External Job Reference

The exact external job reference shall be durable before the dispatching worker releases ownership.

17.103 Job Submission

Job submission shall preserve:

- Request Envelope,

- idempotency key,

- Connection,

- external response,

- and submission time.

17.104 Submission Accepted

Submission Accepted means the external system acknowledged responsibility for the job.

It does not imply the job started or will succeed.

17.105 Submission Unknown

If the worker loses connection before receiving a job ID, the state may be unknown.

The system shall reconcile before duplicate submission.

17.106 Job Lifecycle

Canonical Asynchronous Job states may include:

- proposed,

- submitting,

- submission unknown,

- accepted,

- queued,

- scheduled,

- running,

- partially complete,

- awaiting external dependency,

- awaiting callback,

- result available,

- ingesting,

- evaluating,

- succeeded,

- failed,

- cancellation requested,

- cancelled,

- expired,

- unknown,

- reconciliation required,

- and archived.

17.107 Proposed Job

The canonical job exists but has not been submitted.

17.108 Submitting Job

Dispatch is in progress.

17.109 Submission-Unknown Job

It is unclear whether the external system accepted the request.

17.110 Accepted Job

The Provider returned a valid job or operation identifier.

17.111 Queued Job

The Provider reports waiting for capacity.

17.112 Scheduled Job

The Provider has assigned a future execution slot where supported.

17.113 Running Job

The external system reports active processing.

17.114 Partially Complete Job

Some usable or intermediate Outputs exist.

Final completion remains unsatisfied.

17.115 Awaiting-Dependency Job

The external system waits for another operation, Asset or human action.

17.116 Awaiting-Callback Job

Omnira expects an external callback or completion notification.

17.117 Result-Available Job

The external system reports that result content can be retrieved.

17.118 Ingesting Job

Omnira is downloading, validating or storing the Output.

17.119 Evaluating Job

Required Quality evaluation remains active.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.120 Succeeded Job

Succeeded means the job’s defined canonical completion conditions have been satisfied.

Provider completion alone may be insufficient.

17.121 Failed Job

The job has a confirmed terminal failure.

17.122 Cancellation-Requested Job

A cancellation request was sent.

External execution may still continue.

17.123 Cancelled Job

Cancellation is confirmed under available evidence.

17.124 Expired Job

The external job or result is no longer available or valid according to known Provider semantics.

17.125 Unknown Job

Current external state cannot be established.

17.126 Reconciliation-Required Job

Internal and external evidence conflict or remain incomplete.

17.127 Archived Job

The active lifecycle is complete and retained for history.

17.128 Job State Transition

Every state transition shall be:

- valid,

- attributable,

- version-aware,

- and evented.

17.129 Invalid Transition

Invalid transitions shall be rejected or quarantined.

A late queued callback shall not revert a succeeded job.

17.130 External State Mapping

Provider-native state shall be preserved beside canonical state.

17.131 Job Progress

Progress may be:

- exact percentage,

- stage,

- item count,

- estimated,

- unknown,

- or Provider-defined.

17.132 Progress Confidence

Provider progress shall not be assumed linear or exact.

17.133 Job Deadline

The canonical deadline may differ from Provider timeout.

17.134 Job Timeout

Job Timeout defines when the system stops expecting ordinary completion and begins escalation or reconciliation.

17.135 Job Expiry

Result expiry may occur after completion.

The Fabric shall ingest required Assets before expiry.

17.136 Job Ownership

Canonical job ownership belongs to the Execution system.

Provider ownership of processing remains external.

17.137 Job Worker Ownership

Workers may temporarily own polling, ingestion or reconciliation through leases.

17.138 Job Checkpoint

Durable Checkpoints shall preserve:

- external job ID,

- current state,

- next poll time,

- callback state,

- and result references.

17.139 Job Recovery

After restart, Omnira shall recover active jobs without resubmitting them blindly.

17.140 Job Completion Contract

The Completion Contract may require:

- terminal Provider state,

- Output retrieval,

- checksum,

- usage,

- cost state,

- evaluation,

- and required evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.141 Job Partial Completion

Partial Outputs shall remain versioned and distinct from final accepted Outputs.

17.142 Job Result Set

One job may produce:

- one Output,

- several variants,

- a manifest,

- or several Assets.

The result cardinality shall be explicit.

17.143 Job Failure Detail

Failure shall preserve:

- external code,

- canonical category,

- retryability,

- cost,

- partial Outputs,

- and refund state where relevant.

17.144 Job Cancellation

Cancellation policy shall define:

- whether supported,

- when permitted,

- cost effect,

- partial Output handling,

- and verification.

17.145 Cancellation Unsupported

When the Provider does not support cancellation, Omnira shall not claim that local stop cancelled the external job.

17.146 Cancellation Pending

The system shall preserve pending state until external evidence confirms outcome.

17.147 Job Retry

Retry creates a new Attempt and usually a new external job.

The original job remains historically visible.

17.148 Job Fallback

Fallback to another resource requires a new Routing or Fallback Decision.

17.149 Callback Contract

A Callback Contract defines how an external system reports state or completion to Omnira.

It shall include or reference:

- callbackContractId,

- source,

- event types,

- schema,

- authentication,

- delivery semantics,

- ordering,

- retry behaviour,

- timeout,

- and lifecycle.

17.150 Callback Contract Identity

Every Callback Contract shall have stable identity and Version.

17.151 Callback Endpoint

A Callback Endpoint is the concrete receiving address or logical target.

It shall be:

- Environment-specific,

- scoped,

- authenticated,

- rate-limited,

- and observable.

17.152 Callback Correlation

Callbacks shall correlate through:

- event ID,

- job ID,

- request ID,

- idempotency key,

- or another durable external reference.

17.153 Callback Authentication

Callback authentication may use:

- signature,

- shared-secret reference,

- asymmetric signature,

- mutual TLS,

- Provider token,

- or approved equivalent.

17.154 Callback Signature

Signature validation shall include the exact signed bytes and Provider-defined canonicalisation rules.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.155 Callback Timestamp

Timestamp validation may reduce replay risk.

Clock tolerance shall be explicit.

17.156 Callback Replay Protection

Previously processed callbacks shall not duplicate canonical effects.

17.157 Callback Schema Validation

The callback payload shall be validated before state mutation.

17.158 Callback Subject Validation

The callback shall identify an object belonging to the expected:

- Provider,

- Account,

- Connection,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- or Execution.

17.159 Callback Account Validation

A valid event for the wrong Provider Account shall not update the current job.

17.160 Callback Environment Validation

Sandbox callbacks shall not mutate production state.

17.161 Callback State Validation

The proposed transition shall be checked against the canonical state machine.

17.162 Duplicate Callback

A duplicate callback may be acknowledged without repeating downstream effects.

17.163 Late Callback

A late callback shall not overwrite newer verified state.

17.164 Out-of-Order Callback

Out-of-order callbacks shall be resolved through:

- sequence,

- object Version,

- Provider timestamp,

- or reconciliation.

17.165 Missing Callback

Missing callbacks shall trigger polling or reconciliation where completion matters.

17.166 Callback Retry

Providers may retry callbacks after:

- timeout,

- non-success response,

- or internal failure.

Omnira receivers shall remain idempotent.

17.167 Callback Acknowledgement

Acknowledgement should occur only after the event is durably accepted for processing.

Business completion need not occur before acknowledgement.

17.168 Fast Acknowledgement

Webhook endpoints should validate and durably enqueue work quickly where architecture permits.

17.169 Slow Callback Processing

Expensive downstream processing should not hold the Provider connection unnecessarily.

17.170 Callback Dead Letter

Unprocessable callbacks shall be quarantined with:

- raw protected payload reference,

- validation result,

- source,

- and remediation state.

17.171 Callback Reconciliation

A callback may trigger a follow-up Provider read before canonical state changes when:

- payload is incomplete,

- event is only a notification,

- or trust requires authoritative retrieval.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.172 Webhook

A Webhook is an externally initiated HTTP or equivalent event delivery to an Omnira-controlled endpoint.

17.173 Webhook Endpoint

A Webhook Endpoint shall include or reference:

- webhookEndpointId,

- Environment,

- accepted sources,

- Callback Contract,

- authentication method,

- rate limits,

- lifecycle,

- and owner.

17.174 Webhook Endpoint Identity

Every persistent Webhook Endpoint shall have stable identity.

17.175 Webhook Subscription

A Webhook Subscription represents registration with an external system.

It shall include:

- subscriptionId,

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Connection,

- event types,

- target endpoint,

- external subscription ID,

- status,

- expiry,

- and provenance.

17.176 Webhook Subscription Identity

Every Subscription shall have stable identity.

17.177 Subscription Creation

Creating a webhook Subscription is an external side effect.

It requires authority and verification.

17.178 Subscription Renewal

Some webhook Subscriptions expire and require renewal.

17.179 Subscription Revocation

Revocation shall stop future expected delivery but may not prevent in-flight retries.

17.180 Subscription Reconciliation

Omnira shall periodically or conditionally verify that required external Subscriptions still exist.

17.181 Webhook Receipt

A Webhook Receipt records one received delivery.

It shall include:

- webhookReceiptId,

- endpoint,

- source,

- event ID,

- receivedAt,

- signature result,

- schema result,

- deduplication result,

- correlation result,

- processing state,

- and provenance.

17.182 Receipt Identity

Every Webhook Receipt shall have stable identity.

17.183 Raw Webhook Evidence

Raw payload and headers may be retained as protected evidence according to policy.

17.184 Webhook Redaction

Sensitive headers and payload fields shall be redacted before ordinary logging.

17.185 Webhook Delivery Attempt

A Provider may send several Delivery Attempts for one logical Event.

Each receipt may be preserved while canonical processing occurs once.

17.186 Unknown Webhook Source

Unknown or unauthenticated sources shall be rejected or quarantined.

17.187 Invalid Signature

Invalid signature shall prevent canonical mutation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.188 Missing Signature

Missing signature shall fail when the Callback Contract requires one.

17.189 Expired Timestamp

A stale signed Event may be rejected as replay unless delayed delivery is valid under contract.

17.190 Webhook Rate Limiting

Endpoints shall limit abusive or accidental delivery volume without losing legitimate critical Events.

17.191 Webhook Denial of Service

Webhook infrastructure shall use:

- bounded payloads,

- concurrency limits,

- queueing,

- and source controls.

17.192 Webhook Payload Size

Payload-size limits shall be explicit.

Large Assets should be referenced rather than embedded.

17.193 Webhook URL Rotation

Changing callback URLs requires:

- Provider Subscription update,

- verification,

- and migration period where necessary.

17.194 Webhook Secret Rotation

Signing-secret rotation shall support overlapping validity where Provider and policy require it.

17.195 Polling

Polling is repeated status retrieval from an external system.

It may supplement or replace callbacks.

17.196 Polling Policy

A Polling Policy shall include or reference:

- pollingPolicyId,

- applicable operation,

- initial delay,

- interval,

- backoff,

- maximum interval,

- maximum polls,

- deadline,

- rate-limit behaviour,

- terminal-state rules,

- and provenance.

17.197 Polling Policy Identity

Every reusable Polling Policy shall have stable identity and Version.

17.198 Initial Poll Delay

The first poll should reflect expected Provider processing time.

17.199 Fixed Polling

Fixed Polling uses one repeated interval.

17.200 Adaptive Polling

Adaptive Polling changes interval based on:

- Provider state,

- elapsed time,

- queue position,

- rate limits,

- and expected duration.

17.201 Provider-Directed Polling

Provider guidance may define minimum or recommended interval.

17.202 Polling Backoff

Intervals may increase for long jobs.

17.203 Polling Jitter

Jitter prevents synchronised bursts across many jobs.

17.204 Polling Maximum

Every Polling Policy shall have finite bounds or a transition to long-term reconciliation.

17.205 Polling Rate Limit

Polling shall not consume Provider quota irresponsibly.

17.206 Polling Cost

Some status requests may incur cost or usage.

That cost shall be attributable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.207 Polling and Callback Cooperation

Callbacks and polling may coexist.

A callback may cancel future polls after durable processing.

17.208 Callback-First Strategy

The system waits primarily for callback and polls after a timeout.

17.209 Poll-First Strategy

The system polls ordinarily and uses callback as an additional signal.

17.210 Hybrid Strategy

The system may poll slowly while awaiting callback.

17.211 Polling Deduplication

Concurrent workers shall not poll the same job unnecessarily.

17.212 Poll Lease

One worker or coordinated service should own the next poll through a durable lease.

17.213 Poll Result

Every meaningful status observation shall preserve:

- external state,

- time,

- source,

- and canonical mapping.

17.214 Poll Failure

Poll failure shall not change the job to failed automatically.

17.215 Poll Timeout

A status request timeout may leave the external job state unknown.

17.216 Polling Stop

Polling shall stop when:

- canonical terminal state is verified,

- job is cancelled,

- result expired,

- policy stops,

- or Incident ownership takes over.

17.217 Status Observation

A Job Status Observation is one point-in-time external-state observation.

It shall include:

- observationId,

- job,

- source,

- Provider state,

- canonical interpretation,

- observedAt,

- confidence,

- and provenance.

17.218 Observation Identity

Every material Observation shall have stable identity.

17.219 Observation Freshness

Status observations become stale.

Freshness shall be explicit.

17.220 Conflicting Observations

Conflicting callback and poll observations shall trigger version-aware resolution or reconciliation.

17.221 Streaming

Streaming delivers partial data before final completion.

Streaming shall remain a protocol property.

It shall not alter the Capability or Completion Contract silently.

17.222 Stream Session

A Stream Session shall include or reference:

- streamSessionId,

- Connection,

- protocol,

- Execution,

- Attempt,

- resource,

- openedAt,

- state,

- sequence model,

- backpressure policy,

- cancellation policy,

- and provenance.

17.223 Stream Session Identity

Every Stream Session shall have stable identity.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.224 Stream States

States may include:

- opening,

- open,

- receiving,

- paused,

- closing,

- closed,

- interrupted,

- failed,

- cancelled,

- and unknown.

17.225 Stream Event

A Stream Event shall include:

- streamEventId,

- session,

- event type,

- sequence,

- payload reference,

- receivedAt,

- and provenance.

17.226 Stream Event Identity

Every Stream Event shall have stable identity or deduplication identity.

17.227 Token Stream

A Token Stream delivers text fragments.

17.228 Audio Stream

An Audio Stream delivers audio frames or chunks.

17.229 Video Stream

A Video Stream may deliver frames, segments or preview updates.

17.230 Status Stream

A Status Stream delivers state changes rather than Output content.

17.231 Tool-Call Stream

A Tool-call stream may interleave text and Tool invocation instructions.

17.232 Stream Ordering

Ordering shall be verified through sequence where available.

17.233 Missing Stream Event

A sequence gap shall be detected.

The system may:

- request resume,

- reconcile,

- fail,

- or retain partial Output.

17.234 Duplicate Stream Event

Duplicate events shall not duplicate canonical content.

17.235 Stream Backpressure

Consumers shall signal or enforce bounded intake.

Unbounded memory buffering is prohibited.

17.236 Slow Consumer

A slow consumer may cause:

- buffering,

- reduced quality,

- Provider disconnect,

- or controlled cancellation.

17.237 Stream Resume

Resume is permitted only when supported by:

- Provider cursor,

- sequence,

- replay endpoint,

- or durable intermediate state.

17.238 Stream Reconnect

Reconnect shall not assume continuity without sequence validation.

17.239 Stream Cancellation

Closing the local stream shall not be represented as external cancellation unless confirmed.

17.240 Stream Final Event

A final Event shall indicate that no further content is expected.

It does not by itself prove Quality acceptance.

17.241 Stream Partial Output

Partial streamed content may be shown or used only when the Capability and Quality Contract permit it.

17.242 Stream Assembly

Fragments shall be assembled deterministically and checked for:

- order,

- completeness,

- encoding,

- and final state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.243 Stream Usage

Usage may arrive:

- incrementally,

- at finalisation,

- or later through billing.

The state shall remain explicit.

17.244 Stream Error

A stream error shall preserve:

- partial content,

- external job state,

- cost exposure,

- and retryability.

17.245 Stream Unknown Outcome

Connection loss may leave the Provider operation running.

Reconciliation may be required.

17.246 Server-Sent Events

Server-Sent Events may support one-way streaming.

The Adapter shall handle:

- reconnect identifiers,

- event types,

- and terminal markers.

17.247 WebSocket

WebSocket supports long-lived full-duplex communication.

It requires:

- session identity,

- heartbeat,

- reconnect,

- ordering,

- backpressure,

- and closure semantics.

17.248 WebSocket Heartbeat

Heartbeat detects connection liveness.

It does not prove application progress.

17.249 WebSocket Reconnect

Reconnect shall revalidate:

- session,

- authentication,

- sequence,

- and authority.

17.250 Bidirectional Streaming

Client and server may send interleaved messages.

Every message shall preserve direction, type and sequence.

17.251 Queue

A Queue transports Commands, Events or work messages between producers and consumers.

Queue architecture is expanded here only as it relates to protocol use.

Distributed coordination and broader event architecture remain governed by the platform’s canonical execution model.

17.252 Queue Message

A Queue Message shall include or reference:

- messageId,

- message type,

- schema Version,

- producer,

- intended consumer or topic,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- correlation,

- causation,

- idempotency or deduplication key,

- createdAt,

- availableAt,

- expiry,

- delivery count,

- classification,

- payload reference,

- and provenance.

17.253 Queue Message Identity

Every Queue Message shall have stable identity.

17.254 Command Message

A Command Message requests work from a consumer.

17.255 Event Message

An Event Message distributes an observed fact.

17.256 Work Message

A Work Message assigns a bounded processing unit.

17.257 Notification Message

A Notification Message indicates that another source should be queried.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.258 Message Schema

Message schemas shall be versioned and validated.

17.259 Message Availability Time

A message may be delayed until a future time.

17.260 Message Expiry

Expired messages shall not execute consequential work.

17.261 Message Priority

Priority may influence delivery order according to queue policy.

It shall not create authority.

17.262 Queue Subscription

A Queue Subscription defines which consumer receives which message classes.

It shall include:

- subscriptionId,

- queue or topic,

- consumer identity,

- filters,

- delivery semantics,

- acknowledgement policy,

- retry policy,

- dead-letter policy,

- and lifecycle.

17.263 Subscription Identity

Every persistent Queue Subscription shall have stable identity.

17.264 Queue Consumer

A Queue Consumer shall have a Service Principal identity and scoped authority.

17.265 Queue Producer

A Queue Producer shall be authorised to emit the message type and scope.

17.266 Delivery Attempt

A Delivery Attempt represents one broker-to-consumer transfer.

It shall include:

- deliveryAttemptId,

- message,

- consumer,

- deliveredAt,

- lease or visibility timeout,

- acknowledgement state,

- error,

- and provenance.

17.267 Delivery Attempt Identity

Every Delivery Attempt shall have stable identity.

17.268 At-Least-Once Delivery

A message may be delivered repeatedly until acknowledged.

Consumers shall be idempotent.

17.269 At-Most-Once Delivery

A message may be lost if delivery fails.

This semantic is unsuitable for some critical operations without additional recovery.

17.270 Exactly-Once Claim

Exactly-once claims shall identify the precise boundary.

The platform shall not infer exactly-once external side effects from broker guarantees.

17.271 Message Acknowledgement

Acknowledgement shall occur only after the message is durably and safely processed to the defined boundary.

17.272 Early Acknowledgement

Acknowledging before durable processing may lose work.

17.273 Late Acknowledgement

Acknowledging after expensive non-idempotent work may cause duplicate redelivery if the worker fails.

17.274 Visibility Timeout

Visibility timeout or lease shall match expected processing duration and support renewal.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.275 Message Redelivery

Redelivery shall preserve the same logical Message identity.

17.276 Delivery Count

Delivery count may influence quarantine or Incident handling.

17.277 Poison Message

A Poison Message repeatedly fails because of invalid or incompatible payload.

It shall be isolated from unrelated work.

17.278 Dead-Letter Queue

Dead-letter state shall preserve:

- original Message,

- failure history,

- consumer,

- and remediation owner.

17.279 Message Replay

Replay may reprocess a Message.

Replay shall not automatically repeat external side effects.

17.280 Replay Authority

Manual replay of consequential work requires explicit authority and state review.

17.281 Queue Ordering

Queue ordering may be:

- global,

- partitioned,

- per-key,

- best effort,

- or absent.

17.282 Ordering Key

An Ordering Key may preserve sequence for:

- one job,

- one Asset,

- one target account,

- or one Workflow.

17.283 Parallel Consumers

Parallel consumers shall respect ordering and target-specific concurrency requirements.

17.284 Queue Partition

Partitions may improve scale while limiting ordering scope.

17.285 Partition Key

Partition keys shall not leak sensitive information unnecessarily.

17.286 Queue Backpressure

Queue saturation shall signal producers and Admission Control.

17.287 Queue Overflow

Overflow behaviour shall be explicit:

- reject,

- delay,

- spill,

- shed,

- or fail.

17.288 Queue Isolation

Queues or partitions may be isolated by:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Provider,

- Capability,

- Environment,

- or risk class.

17.289 Cross-Tenant Queue

Shared queue infrastructure shall preserve strict metadata, payload and credential isolation.

17.290 Queue Payload Protection

Protected payloads may be stored by reference rather than directly in broker messages.

17.291 Queue Encryption

Queue transport and storage protection shall match Data Classification requirements.

17.292 MCP

Model Context Protocol is an integration protocol for exposing Tools, Resources, prompts and related capabilities to clients.

MCP shall be treated as an integration mechanism.

It shall not define Omnira’s Agent identity, authority or canonical Tool model.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.293 MCP Server

An MCP Server is a protocol endpoint exposing one or more MCP capabilities.

It shall include or reference:

- mcpServerId,

- owner,

- transport,

- endpoint,

- implementation Version,

- trust class,

- Connection,

- lifecycle,

- and inventory.

17.294 MCP Server Identity

Every persistent MCP Server shall have stable identity.

17.295 MCP Server Owner

The owner may be:

- Omnira,

- user,

- Project,

- Tenant,

- external Provider,

- or third party.

17.296 MCP Trust Class

Trust classes may include:

- Omnira-managed,

- user-managed local,

- Project-managed local,

- verified external,

- unverified external,

- experimental,

- and prohibited.

17.297 MCP Transport

MCP transport may include:

- standard input and output,

- HTTP,

- streaming HTTP,

- WebSocket,

- or future approved transport.

17.298 MCP Server Lifecycle

Lifecycle may include:

- discovered,

- proposed,

- validating,

- active,

- restricted,

- degraded,

- suspended,

- deprecated,

- retired,

- and archived.

17.299 MCP Session

An MCP Session represents one active protocol relationship between an Omnira client and an MCP Server.

It shall include:

- mcpSessionId,

- server,

- client,

- Connection,

- negotiated protocol Version,

- openedAt,

- capabilities,

- state,

- authentication reference,

- and provenance.

17.300 MCP Session Identity

Every MCP Session shall have stable identity.

17.301 MCP Session States

States may include:

- opening,

- negotiating,

- active,

- degraded,

- closing,

- closed,

- interrupted,

- failed,

- and unknown.

17.302 MCP Negotiation

Session negotiation shall preserve:

- protocol Version,

- supported Features,

- server metadata,

- and client capabilities.

17.303 MCP Session Reconnect

Reconnect shall revalidate:

- server identity,

- inventory,

- protocol Version,

- authentication,

- and policy.

17.304 MCP Session Isolation

Sessions shall remain scoped by:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- and Principal.

17.305 MCP Capability Discovery

Discovery may reveal:

- Tools,

- Resources,

- prompts,

- and server capabilities.

Discovery does not create authority.

17.306 MCP Tool Definition

An MCP Tool Definition shall include or reference:

- mcpToolId,

- server,

- external tool name,

- description,

- input schema,

- output expectations,

- side-effect class,

- discoveredAt,

- schema Version,

- trust state,

- and mapping.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.307 MCP Tool Identity

Canonical Tool identity shall remain separate from the external MCP Tool name.

17.308 MCP Tool Description

Tool descriptions are untrusted metadata.

They shall not override:

- policy,

- Agent instructions,

- user intent,

- or authority.

17.309 MCP Tool Input Schema

The discovered schema shall be validated before use.

17.310 MCP Tool Output Schema

Output schema may be:

- explicit,

- inferred,

- free-form,

- or unknown.

Unstructured output requires cautious handling.

17.311 MCP Tool Side Effect

Each Tool shall be classified as potentially:

- read-only,

- create,

- update,

- delete,

- publish,

- send,

- execute,

- or unknown.

17.312 Unknown MCP Side Effect

A Tool with unknown side effects shall not receive production authority.

17.313 MCP Tool Mapping

A governed Capability or Tool Mapping shall connect the external Tool to Omnira’s canonical model.

17.314 MCP Tool Admission

Admission should require:

- server trust,

- schema validation,

- side-effect classification,

- scope,

- Connection policy,

- tests,

- and maturity.

17.315 MCP Tool Invocation

An MCP Invocation shall include or reference:

- mcpInvocationId,

- session,

- Tool,

- canonical Tool Call,

- input,

- authority,

- target scope,

- idempotency,

- timeout,

- result,

- and provenance.

17.316 MCP Invocation Identity

Every MCP Invocation shall have stable identity.

17.317 MCP Invocation Validation

Before invocation, Omnira shall validate:

- Tool identity,

- schema,

- Project scope,

- target,

- authority,

- classification,

- and side-effect policy.

17.318 MCP Invocation Result

The result shall preserve:

- server response,

- content blocks,

- warnings,

- errors,

- side effects,

- and canonical interpretation.

17.319 MCP Tool Error

MCP Tool errors shall map to canonical Error Classification while preserving external detail.

17.320 MCP Tool Timeout

Timeout shall preserve uncertainty about whether the Tool continued or changed state.

17.321 MCP Tool Cancellation

Cancellation support shall be explicit.

Local session closure does not prove Tool cancellation.

17.322 MCP Read-Only Connection

A read-only Connection shall block Tools classified as mutating.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.323 MCP Tool Inventory Drift

Inventory drift occurs when:

- Tool appears,

- Tool disappears,

- schema changes,

- description changes,

- or side-effect understanding changes.

17.324 MCP Inventory Version

Every discovered inventory Snapshot shall have Version or checksum.

17.325 MCP Tool Schema Drift

Material schema drift shall invalidate prior conformance until reviewed.

17.326 MCP Tool Removal

Removed Tools shall become unavailable for new execution.

Historical Invocations remain resolvable.

17.327 MCP Tool Rename

A renamed external Tool shall not automatically become a new canonical Tool if identity continuity can be verified.

17.328 MCP Resource

An MCP Resource is a server-exposed data object or reference.

It shall be treated as external data.

17.329 MCP Resource Definition

A Resource Definition should include:

- resourceId,

- server,

- URI or external identifier,

- name,

- media type,

- classification,

- mutability,

- discoveredAt,

- and provenance.

17.330 MCP Resource Identity

External URI alone may be insufficient canonical identity.

Server and Connection context shall remain attached.

17.331 MCP Resource Read

Reading a Resource requires:

- authority,

- classification eligibility,

- and Project scope.

17.332 MCP Resource Mutation

Where protocol or server permits mutation, the action shall be treated as a consequential Tool operation.

17.333 MCP Resource Subscription

Resource-change subscriptions shall use governed Event handling and deduplication.

17.334 MCP Prompt

An MCP Prompt is a server-provided prompt template or content package.

It is not a canonical system instruction.

17.335 MCP Prompt Definition

A Prompt Definition should include:

- promptId,

- server,

- external name,

- parameters,

- content class,

- discoveredAt,

- trust,

- and Version.

17.336 MCP Prompt Trust

Server prompts shall be treated as untrusted content.

They shall not gain privileged instruction precedence.

17.337 MCP Prompt Use

A prompt may be used only when:

- explicitly mapped,

- reviewed,

- scoped,

- and compatible with the Agent or Workflow.

17.338 MCP Prompt Injection

Prompt content may contain malicious or irrelevant instructions.

It shall be isolated from policy and authority layers.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.339 MCP Logging

MCP logs shall preserve:

- server,

- session,

- Tool,

- request,

- timing,

- result,

- and error

without exposing secrets or unnecessary protected data.

17.340 MCP Health

MCP health shall distinguish:

- transport,

- session,

- inventory,

- Tool availability,

- and Connection policy.

17.341 MCP Server Healthy

A transport-level healthy server may still expose:

- invalid schemas,

- unauthorised Tools,

- or degraded operations.

17.342 MCP Conformance

Production MCP use requires conformance appropriate to:

- Tool class,

- side effects,

- data,

- and Project.

17.343 MCP Local Server

A local server shall not be trusted automatically.

It may have broad:

- file,

- shell,

- repository,

- network,

- or credential access.

17.344 MCP Remote Server

A remote MCP server is an external data-processing boundary.

17.345 MCP Server Permissions

Permissions shall be narrower than the server’s maximum technical capability.

17.346 MCP Tool Filtering

The client shall expose only permitted Tools to the requesting Agent or Workflow.

17.347 MCP Dynamic Discovery

Dynamically discovered Tools shall remain unavailable until policy and validation complete.

17.348 MCP Server Prompt Prohibition

No MCP server may alter Omnira’s canonical system authority through its metadata.

17.349 MCP Cross-Project Isolation

One Project’s MCP session, Resources and results shall not leak into another Project.

17.350 MCP Session Credential Isolation

Credentials used for one MCP Server or Project shall not be reused broadly.

17.351 MCP Failure Containment

A failing or malicious MCP Server may be:

- suspended,

- disconnected,

- restricted,

- or isolated.

17.352 MCP Fallback

Fallback to another MCP Server or direct API requires a Routing or Plan decision.

17.353 Event Subscription

An Event Subscription defines which Events a consumer receives.

It shall include:

- eventSubscriptionId,

- source,

- Event types,

- filters,

- consumer,

- delivery channel,

- replay position,

- acknowledgement policy,

- and lifecycle.

17.354 Event Subscription Identity

Every persistent Event Subscription shall have stable identity.

17.355 Event Filter

Filters may include:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- object type,

- Capability,

- Provider,

- state,

- or severity.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.356 Event Filter Security

Filters shall not expose unauthorised Events through broad subscription.

17.357 Subscription Start Position

Start position may be:

- latest,

- earliest retained,

- specific offset,

- specific time,

- or snapshot boundary.

17.358 Event Replay Position

Replay position shall be durable when delivery guarantees require it.

17.359 Subscription Pause

Paused subscriptions stop active delivery according to broker semantics.

Events may accumulate or be skipped depending on contract.

17.360 Subscription Resume

Resume shall define replay behaviour.

17.361 Subscription Expiry

Expired subscriptions shall not silently continue.

17.362 Event Consumer

Consumers shall validate Event schema and authority before acting.

17.363 Event-Driven Side Effect

An Event-triggered side effect requires:

- explicit Workflow authority,

- idempotency,

- target verification,

- and current policy.

17.364 Event Does Not Grant Authority

An Event may trigger evaluation of an authorised Workflow.

It does not itself grant new authority.

17.365 Event Fan-Out

One Event may trigger several consumers.

Fan-out shall remain bounded and observable.

17.366 Event Loop

Event loops may occur when services respond to each other repeatedly.

Loop prevention may use:

- causation,

- workflow identity,

- hop limit,

- and idempotency.

17.367 Event Hop Count

A bounded hop count may prevent uncontrolled propagation.

17.368 Event Storm

A large burst of Events may overload consumers.

Backpressure and aggregation may be required.

17.369 Event Coalescing

Several similar Events may be coalesced only when semantics permit.

17.370 Event Sampling

Operational telemetry Events may be sampled.

Consequential business Events shall not be sampled away.

17.371 Event Retention

Retention shall reflect:

- replay needs,

- audit,

- incident investigation,

- and classification.

17.372 Event Compaction

Compacted streams may preserve latest state by key.

They do not replace full audit history where required.

17.373 Schema Version

Every protocol payload shall identify or resolve a Schema Version.

17.374 Schema Identity

Schema identity shall remain stable across compatible revisions.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.375 Backward Compatibility

A newer consumer can process older payloads.

17.376 Forward Compatibility

An older consumer can safely tolerate newer payloads within defined rules.

17.377 Breaking Schema Change

A breaking change requires:

- new Version,

- migration,

- consumer readiness,

- and rollout control.

17.378 Optional Field Addition

Optional fields may be added when old consumers safely ignore them.

17.379 Required Field Addition

New required fields require migration or Version boundary.

17.380 Field Removal

Field removal requires deprecation and compatibility planning.

17.381 Enum Expansion

Consumers shall handle unknown enum values safely.

17.382 Unknown Field

Unknown fields shall not be promoted into canonical state without validation.

17.383 Unknown Enum Value

Unknown values shall remain unknown rather than map to a convenient existing state.

17.384 Schema Registry

A governed Schema Registry may store:

- schema identity,

- Version,

- compatibility,

- owner,

- lifecycle,

- and consumers.

17.385 Schema Validation

Validation shall occur at protocol boundaries before canonical state mutation.

17.386 Schema Validation Failure

Invalid payloads shall be rejected, quarantined or reconciled.

They shall not be parsed leniently into incorrect state.

17.387 Consumer Compatibility

Deployments shall ensure that active consumers can process emitted Versions.

17.388 Producer Compatibility

Producers shall not emit a Version unsupported by required consumers.

17.389 Mixed-Version Deployment

Mixed Versions require explicit compatibility windows.

17.390 Protocol Migration

Migration may use:

- parallel consumers,

- dual read,

- shadow processing,

- or staged rollout.

Consequential dual write is prohibited unless explicitly safe.

17.391 Idempotency

Protocol idempotency ensures repeated transport attempts do not create unintended repeated logical effects.

17.392 Idempotency Key

The same logical Command or submission shall retain the same key across safe retries.

17.393 Idempotency Scope

Scope shall include enough identity to prevent cross:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- target,

- Capability,

- or Environment collision.

17.394 Idempotency Conflict

The same key with different material payload shall fail.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.395 Provider Idempotency Support

Provider support shall be declared per API Operation.

17.396 Idempotency Unsupported

Internal records and reconciliation shall compensate where external support is absent.

17.397 Idempotency Retention

Retention shall match the replay and duplicate-effect window.

17.398 Idempotency Result

Repeated invocation may return:

- existing result,

- pending job,

- unknown outcome,

- or conflict.

17.399 Deduplication

Deduplication identifies repeated protocol deliveries.

It shall remain separate from Idempotency.

17.400 Deduplication Key

Keys may use:

- Event ID,

- Message ID,

- Provider request ID,

- job ID,

- checksum,

- or compound identity.

17.401 Deduplication Scope

Deduplication shall preserve Tenant, Project and source boundaries.

17.402 Deduplication Record

A record shall preserve:

- key,

- source,

- first receipt,

- processing result,

- and retention.

17.403 Deduplication Collision

Potential collision shall not merge unrelated operations.

17.404 Content Deduplication

Equivalent content may still represent distinct paid jobs.

Execution history shall not be erased.

17.405 Retry

Protocol retry may occur at:

- transport,

- API Operation,

- callback delivery,

- queue delivery,

- polling,

- Tool invocation,

- or full Execution level.

The retry layer shall be explicit.

17.406 Hidden SDK Retry

SDK automatic retry shall be:

- disabled,

- configured,

- or observed.

Hidden retry is prohibited for consequential ambiguity.

17.407 Transport Retry

Transport retry may be safe before confirmed submission.

After possible submission, reconciliation may be required.

17.408 Callback Delivery Retry

Providers may retry Event delivery.

Receivers shall remain idempotent.

17.409 Queue Delivery Retry

Broker redelivery shall preserve Message identity.

17.410 Poll Retry

A failed status poll may retry without resubmitting the external job.

17.411 Full Job Retry

A new Provider job requires a new Attempt.

17.412 Retry Budget

Protocol retries shall remain inside:

- Attempt limit,

- Budget,

- deadline,

- and rate limits.

17.413 Timeout

Timeouts shall be defined separately for:

- connection,

- request,

- stream inactivity,

- callback wait,

- poll request,

- job completion,

- and result ingestion.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.414 Connection Timeout

Limits transport establishment time.

17.415 Read Timeout

Limits waiting for response bytes.

17.416 Stream Idle Timeout

Limits time without stream progress.

17.417 Callback Wait Timeout

Defines when missing callback triggers polling or reconciliation.

17.418 Job Completion Timeout

Defines when ordinary waiting ends.

It does not prove Provider failure.

17.419 Ingestion Timeout

Limits Asset retrieval or parsing time.

17.420 Timeout State

Timeout shall map to a truthful canonical state.

It shall not simplify uncertainty falsely.

17.421 Pagination

Pagination shall preserve completeness and ordering semantics.

17.422 Pagination Contract

A Pagination Contract shall include:

- style,

- cursor or offset,

- page size,

- maximum page size,

- ordering,

- mutation behaviour,

- and completion indicator.

17.423 Cursor Pagination

Cursors shall be treated as opaque external state.

17.424 Offset Pagination

Offset pagination may miss or duplicate items when the collection changes.

17.425 Keyset Pagination

Keyset pagination requires stable ordered keys.

17.426 Pagination Token

Tokens shall be scoped and protected.

They are not credentials but may expose access or state.

17.427 Pagination Resume

Resume shall preserve:

- cursor,

- query,

- filters,

- Account,

- and schema Version.

17.428 Pagination Expiry

Expired cursors may require restart or reconciliation.

17.429 Pagination Duplicate

Overlapping pages shall not duplicate canonical records.

17.430 Pagination Gap

Missing pages shall preserve incomplete enumeration state.

17.431 Complete Enumeration

Completeness shall be explicit.

Reaching one page boundary does not prove complete listing.

17.432 Pagination Bound

Maximum items, pages, cost and time shall be bounded.

17.433 Rate Limit

Protocol clients shall respect Provider and internal Rate Limits.

17.434 Rate-Limit Scope

Scope may be:

- Account,

- endpoint,

- Model,

- Tool,

- operation,

- region,

- IP,

- or subscription.

17.435 Rate-Limit Header

Headers may provide:

- remaining,

- reset,

- limit,

- and retry-after.

They are dynamic evidence.

17.436 Rate-Limit Response

A Rate-Limit response shall remain distinct from:

- quota exhaustion,

- Provider outage,

- and Budget failure.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.437 Distributed Rate Limit

Shared Provider Accounts require coordinated enforcement across workers.

17.438 Backoff

Backoff shall use Provider guidance and Reliability Policy.

17.439 Quota

Protocol use may consume Provider or Project quota.

Quota state remains separate from transport availability.

17.440 Payload Limit

Every Operation shall expose known limits for:

- bytes,

- tokens,

- files,

- images,

- audio,

- video,

- or fields.

17.441 Oversized Payload

Oversized requests shall fail before dispatch or be replanned.

Silent truncation is prohibited for mandatory content.

17.442 Payload Chunking

Chunking requires explicit semantic support.

17.443 Chunk Order

Chunk order and source relation shall be preserved.

17.444 Chunk Completion

All mandatory chunks shall be accounted for before complete result claims.

17.445 Payload Compression

Compression shall preserve acceptable fidelity and declared media type.

17.446 Content Encoding

Character encoding and binary transfer rules shall be explicit.

17.447 Content Type

Declared and observed content type shall be validated.

17.448 Temporary URL

Temporary URLs shall preserve expiry and access scope.

17.449 URL Retrieval

Server-side retrieval shall protect against:

- internal address access,

- unsupported protocols,

- redirect abuse,

- oversized download,

- and malicious files.

17.450 API Authentication Boundary

API authentication shall use Credential References resolved only at the execution boundary.

17.451 Protocol Credential Use

Credentials shall be scoped to:

- Connection,

- Provider Account,

- endpoint,

- Capability,

- and operation where supported.

17.452 Credential in Payload Prohibition

Secrets shall not be placed in ordinary canonical payload fields.

17.453 Credential in URL Prohibition

Sensitive credentials should not appear in URLs where they may leak through logs.

17.454 Credential Rotation

Active protocol clients shall support safe credential rotation.

17.455 Authentication Failure

Authentication failure shall not be retried indefinitely.

17.456 Authorisation Failure

Missing permission shall not be bypassed through another Account silently.

17.457 Webhook Secret

Webhook signing secrets remain managed through the secret architecture.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.458 MCP Authentication

MCP authentication shall be explicit for local and remote servers where applicable.

17.459 Session Authentication

Long-lived sessions shall handle expiry and renewal without losing canonical identity.

17.460 Data Minimisation

Protocol payloads shall contain only the data required for the operation.

17.461 Metadata Minimisation

External metadata shall avoid unnecessary:

- personal names,

- Project strategy,

- internal paths,

- or secret identifiers.

17.462 Data Classification

Every protocol interaction shall preserve effective classification.

17.463 External Processing Boundary

Sending data through API, MCP or webhook response paths constitutes external processing where the target is external.

17.464 Region

Actual or expected region shall remain explicit where relevant.

17.465 Provider Retention

Protocol use shall reflect Provider-side data retention and training terms.

17.466 Prompt Injection

External API content, MCP metadata, webhook payloads and queue messages may contain malicious instructions.

They shall not gain authority.

17.467 Untrusted Event Content

Event payload text shall be treated as data, not system instruction.

17.468 Untrusted Tool Metadata

MCP Tool descriptions and schemas shall be validated and sandboxed conceptually.

17.469 Untrusted Search Result

Search results returned through API or MCP remain source content requiring evaluation.

17.470 Deserialisation Safety

Payload parsing shall avoid unsafe object construction or code execution.

17.471 File Attachment Safety

Inbound files may require:

- type validation,

- malware scan,

- archive constraints,

- and sandboxing.

17.472 Protocol Observability

Observability shall expose:

- request volume,

- response status,

- latency,

- timeouts,

- job states,

- callback delay,

- duplicate delivery,

- schema failure,

- queue backlog,

- stream interruption,

- MCP inventory drift,

- and unknown outcomes.

17.473 Protocol Metric

Metrics may include:

- synchronous success rate,

- submission-unknown rate,

- callback success rate,

- callback duplication rate,

- callback delay,

- poll count,

- job completion time,

- stream gap rate,

- queue redelivery rate,

- schema incompatibility rate,

- and MCP Tool failure rate.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: APIs, MCP, Webhooks and Asynchronous Jobs
text:
17.474 Protocol Trace

Traces shall preserve:

- Request Envelope,

- Response Envelope,

- Command,

- Event,

- job,

- callback,

- poll,

- stream,

- queue,

- and Tool invocation relationships.

17.475 Trace Sampling

Failed, consequential and unknown operations require stronger retention than ordinary high-volume traffic.

17.476 Protocol Logging

Logs shall not expose:

- raw credentials,

- full protected payloads,

- signing secrets,

- or private callback data unnecessarily.

17.477 Protocol Receipt

A Protocol Receipt may include:

- protocol class,

- API or MCP Version,

- operation,

- Connection,

- request ID,

- external job ID,

- Event or Message ID,

- callback state,

- delivery attempts,

- result state,

- timing,

- usage,

- errors,

- and provenance.

17.478 Protocol Health

Protocol Health shall distinguish:

- endpoint reachability,

- authentication,

- schema compatibility,

- callback delivery,

- polling success,

- stream stability,

- and server inventory.

17.479 API Health

API Health may be scoped to one Operation and Connection.

17.480 Webhook Health

Webhook Health may include:

- valid-delivery rate,

- signature failures,

- processing latency,

- and Subscription reconciliation.

17.481 Queue Health

Queue Health may include:

- availability,

- backlog,

- consumer lag,

- redelivery,

- and dead-letter rate.

17.482 MCP Health

MCP Health may include:

- transport,
