18.788 Future Privileged Access Management

Privileged administration may use dedicated access-management workflows.

18.789 Future Multi-Party Recovery

Critical Tenant access may use several recovery trustees.

18.790 Future Federated Agents

External Agents may receive short-lived capability Tokens rather than reusable internal Credentials.

18.791 Future Local Sovereignty

Local-only deployments may keep all authentication keys on user-controlled hardware.

18.792 Future Offline Identity

Offline Nodes may operate through expiring locally verifiable authority snapshots.

18.793 Offline Revocation Limitation

Offline operation shall preserve bounded expiry because immediate central revocation may be unavailable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
18.794 Canonical Identity Contract

The following requirements define canonical identity:

1. Every Principal SHALL have stable identity.

2. Principal SHALL remain distinct from Session.

3. Principal SHALL remain distinct from Credential.

4. Principal SHALL remain distinct from Account.

5. external identities SHALL bind explicitly.

6. external labels SHALL NOT become immutable identity.

7. authentication issuer SHALL be explicit.

8. Agent identity SHALL remain Omnira-owned.

9. Model changes SHALL NOT change Agent identity.

10. Provider changes SHALL NOT change Agent identity.

11. Runtime changes SHALL NOT change Agent identity.

12. Principal lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

13. suspended Principals SHALL not initiate new execution.

14. retired Principals SHALL remain historical.

15. identity changes SHALL be attributable.

16. cross-Tenant identity confusion SHALL be denied.

17. Service Principals SHALL remain distinct from human users.

18. Device Principals SHALL remain independently revocable.

19. external Agents SHALL NOT inherit Omnira identity automatically.

20. Identity SHALL NOT be inferred solely from possession of a Secret.

18.795 Canonical Authentication and Authorisation Contract

The following requirements define access Decisions:

1. Authentication SHALL remain distinct from authorisation.

2. Authorisation SHALL remain distinct from Approval.

3. every access Decision SHALL identify Principal.

4. Tenant SHALL be explicit.

5. Project SHALL be explicit where relevant.

6. action SHALL be explicit.

7. target SHALL be explicit.

8. current Grants SHALL be evaluated.

9. current Mandates SHALL be evaluated where relevant.

10. expiry SHALL be enforced.

11. revocation SHALL be enforced.

12. default-deny SHALL apply where authority is unknown.

13. least privilege SHALL govern.

14. delegation SHALL NOT exceed source authority.

15. Agents SHALL NOT self-authorise.

16. Role SHALL NOT imply universal authority.

17. high-risk operations MAY require step-up authentication.

18. high-risk operations MAY require independent Approval.

19. Decisions SHALL reference current policy.

20. Technical access SHALL NOT create business authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
18.796 Canonical Credential Contract

The following requirements define Credentials:

1. Every Credential SHALL have stable canonical identity.

2. Credential SHALL remain distinct from Secret value.

3. Credential SHALL remain distinct from Principal.

4. Credential SHALL remain distinct from Provider Account.

5. owner SHALL be explicit.

6. custodian SHOULD be explicit where different.

7. Provider or target system SHALL be explicit.

8. Account SHALL be explicit where applicable.

9. Tenant SHALL be explicit.

10. Project scope SHALL be explicit.

11. Environment SHALL be explicit.

12. Credential type SHALL be explicit.

13. lifecycle state SHALL be explicit.

14. expiry SHALL be explicit where applicable.

15. rotation policy SHALL be explicit.

16. Secret Store reference SHALL be explicit without revealing value.

17. Credential Reference SHALL be non-secret.

18. revoked Credential SHALL NOT resolve.

19. compromised Credential SHALL be containable independently.

20. Credential possession SHALL NOT create execution authority.

18.797 Canonical Secret Management Contract

The following requirements define Secret handling:

1. Raw Secrets SHALL use protected storage.

2. Secrets SHALL be encrypted at rest.

3. Secrets SHALL use protected transport.

4. Secret access SHALL require authenticated workload identity.

5. Secret resolution SHALL be purpose-bound.

6. Secret resolution SHALL be scope-bound.

7. Secret resolution SHOULD occur just in time.

8. Secret lifetime in application memory SHALL be minimised.

9. Agents SHALL NOT receive raw Secrets.

10. prompts SHALL NOT contain raw Secrets.

11. ordinary logs SHALL NOT contain raw Secrets.

12. traces SHALL NOT contain raw Secrets.

13. queue messages SHALL NOT contain reusable raw Secrets.

14. ordinary Events SHALL NOT contain raw Secrets.

15. Registry records SHALL NOT contain raw Secrets.

16. permanent Memory SHALL NOT contain raw Secrets.

17. ordinary Evidence summaries SHALL NOT contain raw Secrets.

18. source control SHALL NOT contain raw Secrets.

19. Secret exposure SHALL trigger compromise review.

20. Secret-management failure SHALL NOT fall back to uncontrolled plaintext storage.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 18.798 Canonical Provider Account and Connection Contract
18.799 Canonical Rotation, Revocation and Compromise Contract
text:
18.798 Canonical Provider Account and Connection Contract

The following requirements define Provider access:

1. Every Provider Account SHALL have stable identity.

2. Provider SHALL be explicit.

3. Account owner type SHALL be explicit.

4. Account owner SHALL be explicit.

5. Tenant SHALL be explicit.

6. Project scope SHALL be explicit.

7. billing mode SHALL be explicit where relevant.

8. privacy settings SHALL be explicit where relevant.

9. commercial-use state SHALL be explicit where relevant.

10. Account SHALL remain distinct from Credential.

11. Every Connection SHALL have stable identity and Version.

12. Connection SHALL bind exact Provider.

13. Connection SHALL bind exact Product.

14. Connection SHALL bind exact Account.

15. Connection SHALL bind Credential Reference.

16. Connection SHALL bind Adapter Version.

17. Connection SHALL bind Environment.

18. Connection SHALL bind Tenant and Project scope.

19. activation SHALL verify intended Account where practical.

20. Connection validity SHALL NOT create action authority.

18.799 Canonical Rotation, Revocation and Compromise Contract

The following requirements define Credential lifecycle security:

1. Material Secret replacement SHALL create distinguishable Version.

2. Rotation SHALL identify dependencies.

3. new Credential Version SHALL be verified before normal cutover where practical.

4. overlap SHALL be bounded.

5. old Version SHALL be revoked after cutover.

6. compromised Secrets SHALL NOT be restored during rollback.

7. expiry SHALL be monitored.

8. revocation SHALL be attributable.

9. revocation SHALL stop new resolution.

10. queued work SHALL revalidate.

11. scheduled work SHALL revalidate.

12. active Sessions or Tokens SHOULD be revoked where possible.

13. compromise SHALL create a Compromise Record.

14. compromise response SHALL identify blast radius.

15. dependent Connections SHALL be containable.

16. suspected Provider Account takeover SHALL suspend dependent access.

17. current revocation SHALL survive backup restore.

18. current compromise state SHALL survive backup restore.

19. closure SHALL require verification.

20. Lifecycle automation SHALL NOT broaden Credential scope.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 18.800 Canonical Privileged, Recovery and Break-Glass Contract
text:
18.800 Canonical Privileged, Recovery and Break-Glass Contract

The following requirements define exceptional access:

1. privileged Roles SHALL be explicit.

2. privileged access SHALL use stronger authentication where appropriate.

3. just-in-time privilege SHOULD be preferred.

4. just-enough privilege SHOULD be preferred.

5. elevated Sessions SHALL expire.

6. privilege assignment SHALL be auditable.

7. persistent privileged access SHALL be reviewed.

8. Recovery Credentials SHALL be strongly protected.

9. Recovery SHALL verify legitimate Principal.

10. Recovery SHALL restore access rather than grant unrestricted operational authority.

11. Break-Glass Grants SHALL have stable identity.

12. break-glass Principal SHALL be explicit.

13. emergency purpose SHALL be explicit.

14. scope SHALL be narrow.

15. expiry SHALL be short and automatic.

16. use SHALL be audited.

17. use SHOULD notify responsible owners.

18. post-use review SHALL occur.

19. Agents SHALL NOT activate break glass autonomously.

20. Emergency access SHALL NOT become permanent normal architecture.

18.801 Identity, Credential and Secret Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No identity without a Principal.

- No authentication without an issuer or trusted authentication mechanism.

- No authentication result becomes authorisation automatically.

- No authorisation result replaces required Approval.

- No Credential becomes identity.

- No Secret becomes authority.

- No Provider Account becomes Credential.

- No Connection becomes authority.

- No Agent owns raw Provider Secrets.

- No Model receives reusable authentication material.

- No raw Secret enters ordinary prompts.

- No raw Secret enters permanent Memory.

- No raw Secret enters ordinary logs.

- No raw Secret enters ordinary queue payloads.

- No raw Secret enters canonical Registry metadata.

- No cross-Project Credential access occurs implicitly.

- No cross-Tenant Credential access occurs.

- No successful login to the wrong Account activates a Connection.

- No Credential rotation restores a compromised Secret.

- No revoked Credential becomes active through restore.

- No expired authority survives merely because a Session remains cached.

- No MCP discovery creates Secret access.

- No Tool receives unrelated Secrets through inherited environment.

- No local execution becomes a Credential-governance exception.

- No publication Credential creates publication authority.

- No financial Credential creates spend authority.

- No break-glass access becomes ordinary Agent capability.

- No identity or Credential failure permits uncontrolled fallback.

- No Secret-management convenience outranks least privilege.

- No technical access becomes business authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
18.802 Closing Statement

Identity is the foundation of accountable execution.

Credentials are the technical mechanisms through which authenticated access becomes possible.

Secrets are the protected material that may enable those mechanisms.

Accounts define external ownership and service context.

Connections bind those Accounts to exact Credentials, Adapters, Environments and Projects.

Authority determines whether access may actually be exercised.

Approval determines whether a consequential action may proceed now.

These concepts must remain separate.

For Atlas, this means that Atlas can request intelligence without carrying API keys, passwords, Tokens or Provider Sessions in its reasoning context.

Atlas retains its own Omnira identity regardless of which Model, Provider or Runtime performs the work.

For Arnold, this means that switching between local and external Models does not change Arnold's identity, authority or Project boundaries.

For Familje-Stunden, this means that image, Voice, publication and creative-platform Accounts can remain isolated from private personal Accounts and from unrelated Projects.

For The Prompt, this means that research, generation and publishing may use several external services without giving any one Agent unrestricted Credential access.

For local intelligence, this means that Nodes, Runtimes and Tools authenticate as their own Principals while Local Only policy continues to govern where data may travel.

For Omnira-managed infrastructure, this means that centrally managed Provider access can serve several Projects while retaining Project attribution, isolation and user-visible governance.

The Principal identifies the actor.

The Authentication Method proves identity.

The Authorisation Decision establishes permission.

The Approval establishes bounded user authority where required.

The Credential establishes technical access.

The Secret Store protects Secret material.

The Credential Reference allows the Fabric to reason about access without carrying the Secret.

The Provider Account identifies the external service context.

The Connection binds that context to one exact Credential, Adapter, Environment and scope.

The Credential Use Record proves when protected access was exercised.

The Rotation Plan changes access material safely.

The Revocation Record terminates access.

The Compromise Record preserves security truth.

The Recovery Credential restores legitimate access.

The Break-Glass Grant handles exceptional emergency conditions without turning emergency privilege into normal operation.

No identity without a Principal.

No authentication without an issuer.

No authorisation without scope.

No Credential without ownership.

No Secret without protected storage.

No Connection without exact Account binding.

No Agent access to raw Secret material.

No rotation without Versioning.

No revocation without propagation.

No recovery without verification.

No emergency access without expiry and review.

The user retains ownership.

The Project retains scope.

Omnira retains authority.

The Fabric accesses protected intelligence resources without surrendering identity, security or control.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical architecture, governance model, object model, lifecycle, trust boundaries and conformance requirements for local, private, edge and self-hosted intelligence within the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

It establishes:

- how local, private, edge, offline, on-premises and self-hosted execution remain distinct,

- how user-owned, Tenant-owned, Project-owned and Omnira-managed infrastructure coexist,

- how Runtime Nodes, execution environments, local Model Deployments and private Tools are represented,

- how placement policy selects where work may execute,

- how data custody and processing location remain explicit,

- how local execution remains subject to authority, policy, quality, cost and provenance,

- how Nodes are enrolled, identified, attested, restricted, suspended and retired,

- how Models, Tools and runtime packages are installed, verified, updated and removed,

- how local Model identity remains separate from filenames, aliases and runtime tags,

- how quantisation, fine-tuning, compilation and hardware configuration affect Deployment identity,

- how private and self-hosted resources enter the Capability, Model, Provider and execution-resource Registries,

- how hardware capacity, energy, thermal state, battery, memory, storage and network constraints influence execution,

- how local and edge work is scheduled without degrading the user’s device unexpectedly,

- how confidential and Local Only data is prevented from leaving approved boundaries,

- how offline execution and delayed synchronisation remain canonical,

- how local Assets, logs, caches, Model weights and temporary files are governed,

- how local Tools and runtimes are sandboxed,

- how distributed user-owned Nodes coordinate without becoming one unrestricted trust domain,

- how private clusters and cloud-hosted self-managed infrastructure remain distinguishable,

- how local failure, device loss, corruption and stale state are recovered,

- how local cost, energy and hardware depreciation remain visible,

- how private inference, local retrieval, embeddings, speech, vision and media processing are integrated,

- how local training, fine-tuning and adaptation remain governed,

- how future mobile, workstation, server and edge Nodes participate in Omnira,

- and how Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy local and private execution foundation.

Local is not automatically private.

Private is not automatically secure.

Self-hosted is not automatically user-owned.

User-owned is not automatically trusted.

Offline is not automatically authorised.

A local Model is still a Model resource.

A local Runtime is still an execution dependency.

A private Node is still subject to identity, policy, cost, quality and evidence.

A downloaded Model file is not automatically an admitted Model Version.

A runtime tag is not automatically canonical Model identity.

A machine that is online is not automatically ready.

A Node with technical access to data does not automatically have authority to process it.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
sectionTitles: 19.2 Purpose of Local and Private Intelligence
text:
19.2 Purpose of Local and Private Intelligence

Omnira shall support intelligence resources that do not depend exclusively on external managed Providers.

These resources may run on:

- the user’s laptop,

- a desktop workstation,

- a private GPU rig,

- a home server,

- a mobile device,

- a local network appliance,

- an organisation-owned server,

- an on-premises cluster,

- a dedicated hosted server,

- a self-managed cloud virtual machine,

- a confidential-compute environment,

- or a future edge device.

Local and private resources may provide:

- stronger data custody,

- lower marginal execution cost,

- reduced Provider dependence,

- offline capability,

- lower latency for some workloads,

- custom Model support,

- private retrieval,

- controlled Tool execution,

- hardware reuse,

- and continuity during external Provider disruption.

They may also create risks involving:

- insecure configuration,

- unpatched software,

- malicious Model packages,

- insufficient hardware,

- device loss,

- broad file access,

- cross-Project leakage,

- unavailable backups,

- inaccurate Model identity,

- poor quality,

- hidden energy cost,

- or unsupported operational burden.

The architecture exists to preserve the benefits without hiding the risks.

19.3 Local

Local means that execution occurs on a device or Node physically or logically controlled near the user or organisation.

Local may include:

- personal laptop,

- workstation,

- home server,

- local mobile device,

- or local network server.

Local does not necessarily mean:

- offline,

- isolated,

- user-owned,

- or safe.

19.4 Private

Private means that execution and data handling occur within a defined restricted trust and custody boundary.

A private boundary may be:

- one user device,

- one Tenant network,

- one isolated cluster,

- one dedicated hosted environment,

- or one confidential-compute boundary.

Private shall be defined through evidence and policy.

It shall not be inferred from marketing language.

19.5 Edge

Edge means execution occurs on or near the device, user, sensor, data source or operational environment that produces or consumes the data.

Edge execution may reduce:

- latency,

- network dependence,

- data transfer,

- and central infrastructure load.

Edge does not automatically mean Local Only.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.6 Self-Hosted

Self-hosted means the user, Tenant, Project or Omnira operates the runtime or service rather than relying entirely on a Provider-managed execution service.

Self-hosted infrastructure may run:

- locally,

- on premises,

- in rented dedicated hardware,

- or in public cloud infrastructure.

Self-hosted does not necessarily mean user-owned hardware.

19.7 On-Premises

On-premises means infrastructure is operated within facilities or networks controlled by the user or organisation.

On-premises does not prove:

- security,

- isolation,

- maintenance,

- or data residency

without further evidence.

19.8 Offline

Offline means the Node can perform the defined work without an active external network connection.

Offline execution may still require:

- local credentials,

- cached policy,

- local Models,

- local data,

- and later synchronisation.

19.9 Air-Gapped

Air-gapped means the execution environment is deliberately isolated from ordinary network communication.

Air-gapped environments require controlled:

- import,

- export,

- update,

- evidence transfer,

- and recovery procedures.

19.10 Dedicated Hosted

Dedicated Hosted means infrastructure is rented from an external operator but dedicated to one user, Tenant or defined scope.

The hosting Provider remains part of the trust and physical control boundary.

19.11 Self-Managed Cloud

Self-Managed Cloud means the user, Tenant or Omnira operates software and execution policy on cloud infrastructure.

The cloud infrastructure Provider still controls underlying physical and virtualisation layers.

19.12 Confidential Compute

Confidential Compute uses hardware or platform mechanisms intended to protect data during processing.

Actual guarantees shall be evidenced through:

- supported hardware,

- attestation,

- threat model,

- key release policy,

- and implementation review.

19.13 Local Only

Local Only is a Data Classification and placement restriction.

It means data or work shall remain within approved local or private execution boundaries.

Local Only shall not be weakened automatically because a local resource is unavailable.

19.14 Private Routing Profile

The Private Routing Profile prefers or requires resources meeting defined custody and placement constraints.

Private is not merely a cost preference.

It may exclude otherwise superior external resources.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
sectionTitles: 19.20 Local Execution Is Not Governance Bypass
text:
19.15 Execution Placement

Execution Placement determines the physical, virtual and trust location where work is performed.

Placement shall be:

- explicit,

- policy-conformant,

- attributable,

- and preserved in evidence.

19.16 Placement Is Not Routing Alone

Routing selects an eligible intelligence or execution resource.

Placement determines where that resource operates.

A Model may have several Deployments with different placement properties.

19.17 Placement Is Not Ownership

A user-owned Model Deployment may run on rented infrastructure.

A self-hosted service may run on Omnira-managed hardware.

Ownership and placement shall remain separate.

19.18 Placement Is Not Trust

A resource may be local but untrusted.

A remote dedicated Node may be approved for certain confidential work.

Trust shall be evaluated independently.

19.19 Placement Is Not Data Classification

Data Classification defines protection requirements.

Placement Policy determines which locations satisfy them.

19.20 Local Execution Is Not Governance Bypass

Local resources shall still require:

- Capability eligibility,

- Model or Tool registration,

- authority,

- Budget where applicable,

- scheduling,

- evidence,

- evaluation,

- and Incident handling.

19.21 Local and Private Control Plane

The Local and Private Intelligence Control Plane is the governed collection of services and canonical objects responsible for:

- Node identity,

- Node enrollment,

- runtime inventory,

- Model package admission,

- Tool package admission,

- placement,

- capacity,

- health,

- scheduling,

- sandboxing,

- private networking,

- offline operation,

- synchronisation,

- local storage,

- updates,

- recovery,

- and evidence.

It shall integrate with:

- Capability Registry,

- Model Registry,

- Provider Registry,

- Agent and Tool Registry,

- Connector Registry,

- Identity and Secret Management,

- Policy,

- Planning,

- Routing,

- Scheduling,

- Reliability,

- Cost,

- Quality,

- Assets,

- Observability,

- and Incident Response.

19.22 Canonical Local and Private Objects

The canonical architecture should include or reference:

- Execution Zone,

- Trust Zone,

- Placement Policy,

- Placement Decision,

- Runtime Node,

- Node Identity,

- Node Enrollment,

- Node Attestation,

- Node Trust Profile,

- Node Capability Profile,

- Hardware Profile,

- Runtime,

- Runtime Version,

- Runtime Deployment,

- Execution Environment,

- Sandbox,

- Worker,

- Worker Pool,

- Local Model Package,

- Local Model Installation,

- Model Deployment,

- Tool Package,

- Tool Installation,

- Resource Pool,

- Storage Volume,

- Local Asset Store,

- Network Profile,

- Resource Lease,

- Capacity Record,

- Health Observation,

- Update Plan,

- Rollback Plan,

- Offline Operation,

- Synchronisation Record,

- and Local Execution Receipt.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.23 Execution Zone

An Execution Zone is a governed location or infrastructure boundary in which work may execute.

Examples include:

- user laptop zone,

- private workstation zone,

- home-server zone,

- mobile-device zone,

- Tenant on-premises zone,

- dedicated-hosting zone,

- self-managed cloud zone,

- confidential-compute zone,

- and external managed Provider zone.

19.24 Execution Zone Identity

Every persistent Execution Zone shall have stable canonical identity.

19.25 Zone Ownership

Every Zone shall identify ownership such as:

- user-owned,

- Project-owned,

- Tenant-owned,

- Omnira-owned,

- rented dedicated,

- or external Provider-managed.

19.26 Zone Operator

The operator responsible for maintaining the Zone shall be explicit.

Ownership and operation may differ.

19.27 Zone Custodian

The custodian responsible for physical or administrative custody may differ from the operator.

19.28 Zone Location

Location may include:

- device,

- facility,

- country,

- region,

- cloud region,

- or logical network.

Precision shall match policy need.

19.29 Zone Data Residency

The Zone shall declare which data-residency claims are:

- verified,

- contractually stated,

- inferred,

- or unknown.

19.30 Zone Network Class

A Zone may be:

- internet connected,

- restricted egress,

- private network only,

- intermittently connected,

- offline capable,

- or air-gapped.

19.31 Zone Trust Class

Trust classes may include:

- trusted private,

- controlled private,

- limited,

- unverified,

- experimental,

- compromised,

- and prohibited.

19.32 Zone Lifecycle

Zone lifecycle may include:

- proposed,

- validating,

- active,

- restricted,

- degraded,

- isolated,

- suspended,

- compromised,

- retired,

- and archived.

19.33 Trust Zone

A Trust Zone is a security boundary within which defined trust assumptions apply.

One Execution Zone may contain several Trust Zones.

19.34 Trust-Zone Separation

Examples may include:

- host operating system,

- container sandbox,

- virtual machine,

- confidential enclave,

- user session,

- Project workspace,

- and administrative plane.

19.35 Trust-Zone Crossing

Every data or command crossing a Trust Zone shall be governed as an explicit boundary.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.36 Placement Policy

A Placement Policy defines where a Capability Request, Plan Step or data class may execute.

It shall include or reference:

- placementPolicyId,

- scope,

- allowed Zones,

- prohibited Zones,

- required ownership,

- required trust,

- network constraints,

- data residency,

- hardware constraints,

- fallback rules,

- and Version.

19.37 Placement Policy Identity

Every reusable Placement Policy shall have stable identity and Version.

19.38 Placement Policy Scope

Placement Policies may apply at:

- Platform,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Capability,

- Data Classification,

- Agent,

- Workflow,

- Model,

- Tool,

- or Asset level.

19.39 Allowed Placement

Allowed placement defines eligible Zones.

Eligibility remains subject to:

- resource health,

- authority,

- quality,

- capacity,

- and cost.

19.40 Prohibited Placement

Prohibited placement shall be enforced before data or execution leaves the permitted boundary.

19.41 Required Local Placement

Required Local Placement means the work shall execute only on approved local Nodes.

19.42 Preferred Local Placement

Preferred Local Placement permits external fallback only when policy and user authority allow it.

19.43 Required Private Placement

Required Private Placement may include approved:

- local,

- on-premises,

- dedicated,

- or confidential-compute

Zones.

19.44 Required Offline Placement

Required Offline Placement prohibits dependence on external network services during execution.

19.45 Required Region

A policy may require one or more approved countries or regions.

19.46 Prohibited Region

A region may be excluded because of:

- law,

- policy,

- Provider terms,

- risk,

- or contractual restrictions.

19.47 Placement Fallback

Fallback shall define whether work may move from:

- local to dedicated remote,

- private to external,

- one private Node to another,

- or online to offline mode.

Fallback shall never weaken mandatory placement silently.

19.48 Placement Decision

A Placement Decision selects an eligible Zone and Node for one bounded Step.

It shall include or reference:

- placementDecisionId,

- Plan Version,

- Step,

- data classes,

- selected Zone,

- selected Node,

- selected Runtime,

- policy Versions,

- alternatives,

- reasons,

- validity,

- and provenance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.49 Placement Decision Identity

Every material Placement Decision shall have stable identity.

19.50 Placement Decision Validity

A Decision may become invalid after:

- Node trust change,

- device loss,

- policy change,

- capacity loss,

- network change,

- or Model removal.

19.51 Placement Revalidation

Placement shall be revalidated before execution and during long-running work where material.

19.52 Runtime Node

A Runtime Node is a physical or virtual compute environment capable of hosting one or more Runtimes, Models, Tools or workers.

Examples include:

- laptop,

- desktop,

- server,

- mobile device,

- virtual machine,

- container host,

- or dedicated accelerator appliance.

19.53 Runtime Node Identity

Every Runtime Node shall have stable canonical identity.

19.54 Node Identity Independence

Node identity shall remain separate from:

- hostname,

- IP address,

- operating-system user,

- device owner,

- cloud instance ID,

- and Runtime.

19.55 Physical Node

A Physical Node corresponds to one physical machine or device.

19.56 Virtual Node

A Virtual Node corresponds to a virtual machine, isolated compute instance or equivalent boundary.

19.57 Container Node

A container may be treated as an execution boundary but shall not replace its host Node identity.

19.58 Mobile Node

A Mobile Node is a phone, tablet or wearable-capable execution device.

Its constraints may include:

- battery,

- thermal limits,

- background restrictions,

- storage,

- and intermittent network.

19.59 Workstation Node

A Workstation Node is a user-interactive machine with local execution capacity.

Foreground user experience shall be protected.

19.60 Server Node

A Server Node is intended primarily for sustained background or shared workloads.

19.61 Edge Node

An Edge Node operates near data generation or consumption.

It may be mobile, embedded, local or remotely managed.

19.62 Recovery Node

A Recovery Node is reserved for restoration, validation or emergency operations.

It shall not become ordinary shared capacity automatically.

19.63 Node Owner

Every Node shall identify its owner.

19.64 Node Operator

Every Node shall identify the Principal or organisation responsible for operation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.65 Node Custodian

Physical custody shall remain explicit where material.

19.66 Node Tenant Scope

A Node may be:

- single-user,

- single-Project,

- single-Tenant,

- multi-Project,

- or multi-Tenant.

Shared scope requires stronger isolation.

19.67 Node Project Scope

Project-dedicated Nodes may simplify data isolation.

They shall still enforce canonical Project identity.

19.68 Node Environment

Development, test, staging, production and recovery Node roles shall remain explicit.

19.69 Node Location

Node location may affect:

- data residency,

- latency,

- physical risk,

- and recovery.

19.70 Node Network

The Node shall reference its current or expected Network Profile.

19.71 Node Lifecycle

Node lifecycle may include:

- discovered,

- proposed,

- enrolling,

- validating,

- active,

- restricted,

- degraded,

- offline,

- isolated,

- suspended,

- compromised,

- lost,

- retired,

- wiped,

- and archived.

19.72 Discovered Node

A detected machine is not automatically admitted.

19.73 Proposed Node

The Node has been nominated for Omnira participation.

19.74 Enrolling Node

Identity, ownership, trust and configuration are being established.

19.75 Validating Node

The system is testing:

- identity,

- runtime,

- hardware,

- policy,

- and security.

19.76 Active Node

The Node may be considered for eligible placement.

19.77 Restricted Node

The Node may perform only bounded Capabilities or data classes.

19.78 Degraded Node

The Node remains usable with known limitations.

19.79 Offline Node

The Node is currently disconnected or intentionally offline.

It may still perform locally scheduled work.

19.80 Isolated Node

The Node has been separated from ordinary communication because of policy or Incident.

19.81 Suspended Node

New work is blocked temporarily.

19.82 Compromised Node

The Node is believed or confirmed to be unsafe.

19.83 Lost Node

Physical or administrative control is lost.

19.84 Retired Node

The Node shall not receive new work.

19.85 Wiped Node

Managed sensitive data and credentials have been removed according to policy.

19.86 Archived Node

Historical identity and evidence remain queryable.

19.87 Node Enrollment

Node Enrollment establishes a governed relationship between Omnira and a Runtime Node.

It shall include or reference:

- nodeEnrollmentId,

- Node,

- owner,

- operator,

- Device Principal,

- Zone,

- Environment,

- trust profile,

- bootstrap method,

- enrolledAt,

- and lifecycle.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.88 Node Enrollment Identity

Every Enrollment shall have stable identity.

19.89 Enrollment Bootstrap

Bootstrap may use:

- one-time Token,

- QR code,

- local pairing,

- certificate issuance,

- administrative registration,

- or another approved method.

19.90 Enrollment Authentication

Enrollment shall verify the intended Node and authorised owner or operator.

19.91 Enrollment Scope

Enrollment shall define:

- permitted Projects,

- permitted Capabilities,

- data classes,

- network permissions,

- and administrative roles.

19.92 Enrollment Approval

Shared, production or high-trust Nodes may require explicit approval.

19.93 Enrollment Expiry

Temporary Node enrollment shall expire automatically.

19.94 Node Re-Enrollment

Major identity, ownership or trust changes may require re-enrollment.

19.95 Node Attestation

Node Attestation is evidence about hardware, software or runtime state.

It may include:

- hardware identity,

- secure boot,

- operating-system Version,

- runtime checksum,

- container image,

- configuration,

- or confidential-compute report.

19.96 Attestation Identity

Every material Attestation shall have stable observation identity.

19.97 Attestation Source

The source shall be explicit and trusted according to its guarantees.

19.98 Attestation Freshness

Attestation becomes stale after time or system change.

19.99 Attestation Confidence

Attestation confidence may be:

- hardware-backed,

- platform-verified,

- software-reported,

- operator-verified,

- inferred,

- or unknown.

19.100 Attestation Is Not Absolute Trust

Attestation supports trust evaluation.

It does not prove:

- absence of compromise,

- correct policy,

- or safe Model behaviour.

19.101 Node Trust Profile

A Node Trust Profile describes the security and operational properties of one Node.

It should include or reference:

- nodeTrustProfileId,

- operating-system trust,

- encryption state,

- secure boot,

- patch state,

- administrative exposure,

- network exposure,

- physical custody,

- Secret Store,

- isolation,

- attestation,

- and lifecycle.

19.102 Node Trust Profile Identity

Every profile shall have stable identity and Version.

19.103 Trusted Node

A Trusted Node satisfies the defined requirements for its permitted workload classes.

Trust remains scoped.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.104 Limited Node

A Limited Node may process only:

- Public,

- Project Internal,

- low-risk,

- or development data

according to policy.

19.105 Unverified Node

An Unverified Node shall not receive confidential or consequential production work.

19.106 Compromised Trust State

Compromised trust shall immediately affect placement eligibility.

19.107 Trust Downgrade

A downgrade shall:

- stop new sensitive work,

- reassess active work,

- protect Assets,

- and trigger Incident response where required.

19.108 Node Capability Profile

A Node Capability Profile describes what the Node can technically and operationally support.

It may include:

- CPU architecture,

- CPU cores,

- memory,

- GPU type,

- accelerator memory,

- storage,

- network,

- supported runtimes,

- supported operating systems,

- battery,

- and thermal constraints.

19.109 Hardware Profile

A Hardware Profile shall include or reference:

- hardwareProfileId,

- architecture,

- processors,

- accelerators,

- memory,

- storage,

- network interfaces,

- power characteristics,

- and observedAt.

19.110 Hardware Identity

Hardware serial numbers or platform IDs may be protected identifiers.

They shall not be exposed broadly.

19.111 CPU Resource

CPU capacity may be measured through:

- cores,

- threads,

- instruction set,

- utilisation,

- and sustained throughput.

19.112 GPU Resource

GPU or accelerator capacity may include:

- architecture,

- memory,

- compute capability,

- supported precision,

- driver,

- and utilisation.

19.113 Unified Memory

Some devices share memory between CPU and GPU.

Effective Model capacity shall reflect actual runtime behaviour.

19.114 Accelerator Compatibility

A Model or Runtime may require specific:

- driver,

- instruction set,

- compute library,

- or precision support.

19.115 Memory Capacity

Available memory shall account for:

- operating system,

- user applications,

- runtime overhead,

- Model weights,

- context,

- and safety headroom.

19.116 Storage Capacity

Storage shall account for:

- Model packages,

- caches,

- Assets,

- temporary files,

- logs,

- checkpoints,

- and backups.

19.117 Storage Performance

Throughput and latency may affect:

- Model loading,

- media processing,

- indexing,

- and checkpointing.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.118 Network Capacity

Network Profile shall consider:

- bandwidth,

- latency,

- stability,

- metering,

- and privacy.

19.119 Battery State

Mobile and laptop Nodes shall expose battery state where scheduling depends on it.

19.120 Power Source

The Node may be:

- plugged in,

- battery powered,

- power restricted,

- or unknown.

19.121 Thermal State

Thermal state may affect sustainable capacity.

19.122 Fan and Noise Constraint

A user may restrict high-load work during quiet periods or interactive use.

19.123 Hardware Reservation

Scarce GPU, memory or storage may require a Resource Lease or Reservation.

19.124 Runtime

A Runtime is a software system capable of executing Models, Tools or workflows.

Examples include:

- local Model server,

- inference engine,

- container runtime,

- Python runtime,

- media-processing runtime,

- browser runtime,

- or workflow worker.

19.125 Runtime Identity

Every governed Runtime shall have stable canonical identity.

19.126 Runtime Version

Every material Runtime release shall have explicit Version.

19.127 Runtime Type

Runtime types may include:

- Model inference,

- embedding,

- vector search,

- speech,

- vision,

- media processing,

- code execution,

- Tool execution,

- container,

- browser,

- and workflow.

19.128 Runtime Provider

A Runtime may be:

- open source,

- commercial,

- user-developed,

- Omnira-developed,

- or externally maintained.

Runtime Provider identity remains separate from Model Provider.

19.129 Runtime Deployment

A Runtime Deployment is one installed and configured instance of a Runtime on a Node.

It shall include or reference:

- runtimeDeploymentId,

- Runtime Version,

- Node,

- Environment,

- endpoint,

- configuration,

- trust,

- lifecycle,

- and health.

19.130 Runtime Deployment Identity

Every Runtime Deployment shall have stable identity.

19.131 Runtime Endpoint

The endpoint may be:

- local socket,

- loopback HTTP,

- private-network service,

- process invocation,

- or container interface.

19.132 Runtime Configuration

Configuration may include:

- concurrency,

- memory limit,

- GPU allocation,

- cache path,

- network access,

- Model directory,

- and logging.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
sectionTitles: 19.141 Runtime Health Is Not Node Health
text:
19.133 Runtime Configuration Version

Material configuration changes shall be versioned or attributable.

19.134 Runtime Lifecycle

Runtime lifecycle may include:

- proposed,

- installing,

- validating,

- active,

- restricted,

- degraded,

- updating,

- suspended,

- failed,

- deprecated,

- retired,

- and removed.

19.135 Runtime Installation

Installation shall verify:

- source,

- package,

- checksum,

- signature where available,

- dependencies,

- permissions,

- and compatibility.

19.136 Runtime Validation

Validation shall test:

- startup,

- health,

- supported operations,

- capacity,

- isolation,

- and evidence.

19.137 Runtime Update

Updates shall use a governed Update Plan.

19.138 Runtime Rollback

Rollback shall preserve:

- previous Version,

- configuration,

- Model compatibility,

- and evidence.

19.139 Runtime Removal

Removal shall consider:

- active jobs,

- installed Models,

- cache,

- logs,

- and recovery.

19.140 Runtime Health

Runtime health may include:

- process state,

- endpoint reachability,

- Model load status,

- error rate,

- memory pressure,

- and responsiveness.

19.141 Runtime Health Is Not Node Health

A healthy Node may contain a failed Runtime.

A Runtime may appear healthy while the Node is untrusted.

19.142 Execution Environment

An Execution Environment is a governed runtime context for one class of work.

It shall include or reference:

- environmentId,

- Node,

- Runtime,

- operating-system identity,

- file scope,

- network scope,

- Secret access,

- resource limits,

- and lifecycle.

19.143 Environment Isolation

Development, testing, production and recovery environments shall remain distinct.

19.144 Project Environment

Project-specific environments should restrict:

- file paths,

- databases,

- caches,

- and credentials

to the assigned Project.

19.145 Ephemeral Environment

An Ephemeral Environment is created for one bounded job or session and destroyed afterward.

19.146 Persistent Environment

A Persistent Environment retains state across executions.

Persistent state shall be governed explicitly.

19.147 Sandbox

A Sandbox is an isolation mechanism limiting what executed code, Models or Tools may access.

It may use:

- process restrictions,

- container,

- virtual machine,

- operating-system sandbox,

- capability security,

- or remote execution boundary.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.148 Sandbox Identity

Every reusable Sandbox Profile shall have stable identity and Version.

19.149 Sandbox Policy

Sandbox Policy shall define:

- file access,

- network access,

- process access,

- device access,

- memory,

- CPU,

- time,

- and Secret access.

19.150 Read-Only Sandbox

A read-only Sandbox prevents persistent mutation outside approved temporary space.

19.151 Networkless Sandbox

A networkless Sandbox prevents external network communication.

19.152 Restricted-Egress Sandbox

Restricted egress permits only approved endpoints.

19.153 GPU Sandbox

GPU access shall be limited to assigned devices or partitions where supported.

19.154 Sandbox Escape

Suspected escape is a severe security Incident.

19.155 Sandbox Limitation

Isolation guarantees depend on implementation and host trust.

They shall not be overstated.

19.156 Worker

A Worker is a runtime process or service executing bounded work.

Every Worker shall have:

- Service Principal,

- Node,

- Runtime,

- Environment,

- lease,

- and task identity.

19.157 Worker Identity

Every active Worker instance shall have unique runtime identity.

19.158 Worker Pool

A Worker Pool groups compatible Workers.

It shall preserve:

- Node membership,

- Capability support,

- Project scope,

- trust,

- capacity,

- and health.

19.159 Worker Pool Identity

Every persistent Worker Pool shall have stable identity.

19.160 Dedicated Worker Pool

A Dedicated Pool serves one Project, Tenant or high-risk workload class.

19.161 Shared Worker Pool

A Shared Pool requires strong isolation and attribution.

19.162 Worker Lease

A Worker shall own work through a bounded lease.

19.163 Worker Failure

Worker failure shall not erase:

- Execution identity,

- external job identity,

- Checkpoint,

- or evidence.

19.164 Local Model Package

A Local Model Package is a set of files and metadata required to deploy a Model locally or privately.

It may include:

- weights,

- configuration,

- tokenizer,

- vocabulary,

- architecture definition,

- adapter weights,

- runtime metadata,

- licence,

- and manifest.

19.165 Local Model Package Identity

Every admitted Local Model Package shall have stable canonical identity.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.166 Package Identity Is Not Filename

Filename, folder name or runtime tag alone shall not establish Model identity.

19.167 Package Manifest

A package manifest should include:

- Model Family,

- Model Version,

- source,

- revision,

- file list,

- checksums,

- format,

- precision,

- quantisation,

- licence,

- and compatibility.

19.168 Package Source

The source may be:

- official publisher,

- verified repository,

- trusted mirror,

- local export,

- fine-tuning pipeline,

- or unknown.

Unknown sources require stronger restriction.

19.169 Package Provenance

Provenance shall identify:

- publisher,

- repository,

- revision,

- download time,

- operator,

- transformations,

- and validation.

19.170 Package Checksum

Every material package file should receive a cryptographic checksum.

19.171 Package Signature

Publisher or repository signatures should be verified where available.

19.172 Unsigned Package

Unsigned packages may be admitted only under explicit trust and review policy.

19.173 Package Format

Formats may include:

- framework-native weights,

- safetensors,

- GGUF-like packages,

- ONNX,

- engine-specific binaries,

- or other supported forms.

Format shall remain explicit.

19.174 Weight Precision

Precision may include:

- full precision,

- half precision,

- mixed precision,

- low-bit quantisation,

- or runtime-specific format.

19.175 Quantisation

Quantisation materially affects:

- memory,

- speed,

- quality,

- and compatibility.

Quantisation shall be part of Deployment identity or Package Variant identity.

19.176 Quantisation Source

The system shall preserve who created or published the quantised package.

19.177 Quantisation Method

Method and parameters shall be explicit where known.

19.178 Unknown Quantisation

Unknown quantisation properties reduce reproducibility and trust.

19.179 Fine-Tuned Package

A fine-tuned package shall preserve:

- Base Model,

- training method,

- dataset lineage,

- training configuration,

- rights,

- evaluation,

- and owner.

19.180 Adapter Weights

Parameter-efficient adapters shall remain distinct from the Base Model and Runtime.

19.181 Merged Model

A merged package shall record all contributing Models or adapters where known.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.182 Distilled Model

Distillation lineage and source Models shall remain explicit.

19.183 Converted Package

Format conversion shall create new package provenance and checksum.

19.184 Compiled Engine

Runtime compilation may create hardware-specific executable artefacts.

The compiled engine shall be treated as a Deployment artefact.

19.185 Model Package Licence

The licence shall govern:

- local use,

- commercial use,

- redistribution,

- modification,

- and hosted service use.

19.186 Licence Unknown

Unknown licence shall block commercial or production use where rights are required.

19.187 Restricted Model Package

A package may be restricted because of:

- licence,

- provenance,

- safety,

- quality,

- unsupported architecture,

- or security.

19.188 Malicious Model Risk

Model packages and loading code may contain malicious components.

The system shall avoid unsafe deserialisation and executable package hooks.

19.189 Safe Model Loading

Model-loading formats and libraries shall be selected to reduce arbitrary-code execution risk.

19.190 Model Package Scan

Scanning may inspect:

- file types,

- embedded code,

- manifest,

- known vulnerabilities,

- malware,

- and suspicious structure.

19.191 Package Quarantine

Unverified packages shall remain in a quarantine area without production execution.

19.192 Package Admission

Admission shall require:

- identity resolution,

- provenance,

- checksum,

- licence,

- compatibility,

- security review,

- and Model Registry relationship.

19.193 Local Model Installation

A Local Model Installation records one package installed on one Node or shared storage system.

It shall include or reference:

- installationId,

- Local Model Package,

- Node,

- Runtime Deployment,

- path reference,

- installedAt,

- state,

- and provenance.

19.194 Installation Identity

Every installation shall have stable identity.

19.195 Installation Path

Paths shall be treated as Node-local implementation details.

They shall not become Model identity.

19.196 Installation State

States may include:

- downloading,

- verifying,

- installed,

- validating,

- ready,

- restricted,

- corrupt,

- unavailable,

- removing,

- removed,

- and archived.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.197 Download Resume

Large package downloads may resume from verified boundaries.

19.198 Download Integrity

Resumed downloads shall verify final integrity.

19.199 Installation Validation

Validation may include:

- load test,

- inference test,

- memory test,

- output sanity,

- and benchmark.

19.200 Corrupt Installation

Corrupt packages shall not load.

They shall be quarantined or removed safely.

19.201 Installation Removal

Removal shall ensure:

- no active Deployment depends on it,

- shared files are not deleted accidentally,

- and history remains.

19.202 Model Deployment

A Model Deployment is one executable realisation of a Model Version or Package Variant within a Runtime and Node context.

It shall include or reference:

- modelDeploymentId,

- Model,

- Model Version,

- Local Model Package,

- Runtime Deployment,

- Node,

- configuration,

- precision,

- context limit,

- hardware allocation,

- lifecycle,

- health,

- and evidence.

19.203 Model Deployment Identity

Every Model Deployment shall have stable canonical identity.

19.204 Model Deployment Configuration

Configuration may include:

- context length,

- batch size,

- GPU layers,

- tensor parallelism,

- threads,

- memory map,

- cache type,

- and generation defaults.

19.205 Deployment Configuration Version

Material changes affecting quality, capacity or behaviour shall create a new Deployment Version or identity.

19.206 Loaded Deployment

A Deployment may be installed but not currently loaded.

19.207 Warm Deployment

A Warm Deployment is loaded and ready for low-latency execution.

19.208 Cold Deployment

A Cold Deployment requires Model loading before execution.

19.209 Deployment Readiness

Readiness shall include:

- Runtime health,

- package integrity,

- memory availability,

- successful load,

- and probe result.

19.210 Deployment Health

Health may include:

- ready,

- loading,

- degraded,

- out of memory,

- failed,

- corrupt,

- restricted,

- and unknown.

19.211 Deployment Capacity

Capacity shall reflect:

- context size,

- output size,

- concurrency,

- token throughput,

- and hardware state.

19.212 Deployment Quality

Local Deployment quality may differ from Provider-hosted versions because of:

- quantisation,

- runtime,

- configuration,

- hardware,

- and package revision.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.213 Deployment Benchmark

Benchmark evidence shall be Deployment-specific where those factors matter.

19.214 Deployment Behaviour Fingerprint

A behaviour fingerprint may help detect:

- package change,

- configuration drift,

- or Runtime regression.

19.215 Deployment Drift

Drift may occur after:

- Runtime update,

- driver update,

- package replacement,

- configuration change,

- or hardware change.

19.216 Deployment Pinning

Pinned execution shall identify the exact:

- Model Version,

- Package,

- Runtime Version,

- Node,

- and configuration.

19.217 Deployment Replication

The same Model Package may be deployed to several Nodes.

Each Deployment retains separate identity and health.

19.218 Deployment Migration

Moving a Deployment to another Node creates a new placement and usually a distinct Deployment identity.

19.219 Deployment Eviction

A loaded Model may be evicted from memory.

Eviction shall not imply installation removal.

19.220 Deployment Unload

Unloading releases runtime memory while preserving the installation.

19.221 Deployment Removal

Removal disables future execution while preserving historical evidence.

19.222 Tool Package

A Tool Package is a versioned software package providing one or more Tools.

It may include:

- executable,

- library,

- container image,

- script,

- plugin,

- or MCP server.

19.223 Tool Package Identity

Every governed Tool Package shall have stable identity and Version.

19.224 Tool Package Provenance

Provenance shall include:

- source,

- publisher,

- repository,

- revision,

- checksum,

- signature,

- licence,

- and transformations.

19.225 Tool Package Permissions

Required permissions shall be declared before installation.

19.226 Tool Package Security

Packages shall be reviewed or scanned according to:

- source trust,

- executable code,

- network access,

- file access,

- and privilege.

19.227 Tool Installation

A Tool Installation records one Tool Package installed within a Node or Environment.

19.228 Tool Installation Identity

Every Tool Installation shall have stable identity.

19.229 Tool Deployment

A Tool Deployment represents an executable Tool endpoint or process configuration.

It shall remain separate from Tool Definition and Tool Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.230 Tool Deployment Scope

Tool Deployments shall identify:

- Project,

- Environment,

- Sandbox,

- file scope,

- network scope,

- and Service Principal.

19.231 Local Shell Tool

Shell or command execution is a high-risk Tool class.

It shall use:

- structured arguments,

- restricted identity,

- explicit working directory,

- and sandboxing.

19.232 Local File Tool

File Tools shall be restricted to approved paths and operations.

19.233 Local Repository Tool

Repository Tools shall identify:

- repository,

- branch,

- read or write scope,

- and credential boundary.

19.234 Local Media Tool

Media Tools may process:

- image,

- audio,

- video,

- and document Assets.

Input and Output paths shall remain Project-scoped.

19.235 Local Browser Tool

Browser Tools shall use isolated profiles and restricted sessions.

19.236 Local Search Tool

Local search and retrieval shall preserve:

- index identity,

- source scope,

- freshness,

- and access control.

19.237 Resource Pool

A Resource Pool groups Nodes, Runtimes, Deployments or Workers that can serve compatible work.

It shall preserve member-level:

- trust,

- capacity,

- cost,

- placement,

- and health.

19.238 Local Resource Pool

A Local Resource Pool may include several user-controlled Nodes.

19.239 Private Resource Pool

A Private Pool contains resources inside one approved private boundary.

19.240 Heterogeneous Resource Pool

A heterogeneous pool may combine different:

- GPUs,

- Model variants,

- Runtimes,

- and performance.

Eligibility and quality shall remain member-specific.

19.241 Dedicated Resource Pool

A dedicated pool serves one Project or Tenant.

19.242 Shared Private Pool

A shared private pool requires:

- isolation,

- scheduling fairness,

- and data separation.

19.243 Resource Lease

A Resource Lease grants temporary use of:

- Node,

- GPU,

- Runtime,

- Model Deployment,

- storage,

- or Worker.

It shall include:

- resourceLeaseId,

- resource,

- owner,

- work,

- start,

- expiry,

- capacity,

- and fencing.

19.244 Resource Lease Identity

Every material Resource Lease shall have stable identity.

19.245 Exclusive Lease

An Exclusive Lease prevents conflicting use of the resource.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.246 Shared Lease

A Shared Lease allocates a bounded share.

19.247 Lease Renewal

Renewal requires active ownership and continuing eligibility.

19.248 Lease Expiry

Expired ownership shall not permit continued canonical mutation.

19.249 Lease Recovery

Stale Leases shall be released only after confirming no active valid owner remains.

19.250 Storage Volume

A Storage Volume is a governed persistent or temporary storage resource.

It shall include or reference:

- volumeId,

- Node or Zone,

- owner,

- Project scope,

- capacity,

- encryption,

- lifecycle,

- and health.

19.251 Local Asset Store

A Local Asset Store holds governed Assets inside a local or private Zone.

19.252 Local Asset Store Identity

Every persistent Local Asset Store shall have stable identity.

19.253 Asset Store Scope

Asset Stores may be:

- user,

- Project,

- Tenant,

- or shared private.

Shared stores require access control.

19.254 Asset Store Encryption

Encryption at rest shall match Data Classification requirements.

19.255 Asset Store Backup

Backup policy shall be explicit.

19.256 Asset Store Portability

Assets should be exportable through governed procedures where rights permit.

19.257 Temporary Storage

Temporary storage shall be:

- bounded,

- classified,

- cleaned,

- and recoverable where required.

19.258 Cache

Caches may contain:

- Model weights,

- prompts,

- embeddings,

- Provider responses,

- intermediate media,

- and compiled artefacts.

Cache content shall remain governed.

19.259 Cache Scope

Caches shall include:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Model,

- Deployment,

- and Version

where applicable.

19.260 Cross-Project Cache Prohibition

Protected Project data shall not be reused across Projects through shared caches.

19.261 Cache Expiry

Expiry shall reflect:

- sensitivity,

- staleness,

- storage pressure,

- and reproducibility.

19.262 Cache Invalidation

Changes to:

- data,

- Model,

- Runtime,

- policy,

- or rights

may invalidate cache entries.

19.263 Model Cache

Downloaded or compiled Model caches shall preserve package identity and checksum.

19.264 Prompt Cache

Prompt caches may reveal confidential information.

They shall remain classified and scoped.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.265 Embedding Cache

Embeddings may preserve sensitive semantic information.

They shall receive the source data’s effective protection.

19.266 Local Vector Store

A local vector store shall identify:

- index,

- embedding Model,

- source corpus,

- Project,

- update time,

- and access policy.

19.267 Vector Index Identity

Every governed index shall have stable identity and Version.

19.268 Index Rebuild

Rebuild shall preserve:

- source set,

- embedding Model Version,

- chunking policy,

- and time.

19.269 Index Staleness

Stale indexes shall not be represented as current truth.

19.270 Network Profile

A Network Profile describes connectivity and restrictions for a Node or Zone.

It should include:

- networkProfileId,

- connectivity class,

- allowed ingress,

- allowed egress,

- DNS policy,

- proxy,

- VPN,

- metering,

- and trust.

19.271 Network Profile Identity

Every reusable Network Profile shall have stable identity and Version.

19.272 Internet-Connected Profile

An internet-connected Node may access external services subject to policy.

19.273 Restricted-Egress Profile

Only approved endpoints are reachable.

19.274 Private-Network Profile

The Node communicates only within an approved private network.

19.275 Offline Profile

No external network communication is expected.

19.276 Intermittent Profile

Connectivity may disappear unpredictably.

Execution and synchronisation shall tolerate it.

19.277 Metered Network

Large downloads or uploads may require scheduling or approval.

19.278 Network Trust

Private Wi-Fi or local network presence shall not become identity proof.

19.279 Network Encryption

Node communication shall use approved protected transport.

19.280 Peer Node Communication

Peer-to-peer communication shall authenticate both Nodes and preserve Project scope.

19.281 Node Discovery

Network discovery shall not create trust or enrollment automatically.

19.282 Service Exposure

Local Runtime endpoints should not be exposed beyond required interfaces.

19.283 Loopback Binding

Single-device services should prefer loopback or local sockets where practical.

19.284 Private Address Binding

Private network binding still requires authentication and firewall policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.285 Public Exposure

Publicly reachable local services require explicit approval and stronger security.

19.286 Remote Access

Remote administration shall use:

- authenticated,

- encrypted,

- least-privileged,

- and auditable

mechanisms.

19.287 VPN

VPN membership may support network access.

It does not replace Service Principal identity.

19.288 Firewall Policy

Ingress and egress rules shall be explicit and versioned.

19.289 DNS Policy

DNS configuration may affect:

- endpoint trust,

- data routing,

- and Incident containment.

19.290 Proxy

A proxy may observe or modify traffic.

Its trust boundary shall remain explicit.

19.291 Placement Eligibility

A Node or Deployment is placement-eligible only when:

- policy permits the Zone,

- Node trust is sufficient,

- Runtime is valid,

- resource is healthy,

- capacity exists,

- Capability support is verified,

- authority exists,

- and deadline remains feasible.

19.292 Placement Ranking

After eligibility, ranking may consider:

- privacy,

- cost,

- latency,

- quality,

- energy,

- load,

- locality,

- and user preference.

19.293 Local-First Routing

Local-first means eligible local resources are preferred before external resources.

It shall not force use of an unsuitable local Model.

19.294 Free-First Routing

Free-first may prefer local resources with no immediate Provider charge.

Local execution still has:

- hardware,

- energy,

- maintenance,

- and opportunity cost.

19.295 Privacy-First Routing

Privacy-first prioritises custody and data minimisation.

It may accept higher latency or lower quality only within approved constraints.

19.296 Performance-First Local Routing

The fastest local Deployment may be selected when quality and policy remain satisfied.

19.297 Energy-Aware Routing

The system may consider:

- battery,

- electricity,

- thermal cost,

- and scheduled low-load periods.

19.298 Device-Priority Policy

The user may prioritise:

- interactive responsiveness,

- battery preservation,

- quiet operation,

- or maximum throughput.

19.299 Foreground Protection

Background local work shall not degrade foreground use beyond approved limits.

19.300 User Presence

Some local consequential Tools may require active user presence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.301 Screen-Locked State

Sensitive local execution may pause or continue according to policy when the device is locked.

19.302 Sleep State

Node sleep may suspend work.

The Scheduler shall preserve truthful state.

19.303 Wake Capability

Remote or scheduled wake shall require device support and authority.

19.304 Local Scheduler

A Local Scheduler coordinates work on one Node or private pool.

It shall remain subordinate to the canonical Scheduler and policy.

19.305 Local Queue

A local queue shall preserve:

- Project,

- priority,

- deadline,

- resource requirements,

- and durability.

19.306 Local Concurrency

Concurrency shall account for actual:

- CPU,

- GPU,

- memory,

- I/O,

- and user activity.

19.307 Model Load Scheduling

Model loading may be scheduled separately from inference.

19.308 Warm Model Scheduling

The Scheduler may preserve a warm Model when expected reuse justifies memory cost.

19.309 Model Swap Cost

Switching loaded Models may create significant latency and energy cost.

19.310 Batch Local Work

Background tasks may be batched to reduce repeated Model loading.

19.311 Interactive Local Work

Interactive local tasks should receive responsive capacity without starving critical background recovery.

19.312 Local Job Preemption

Local work may be preempted when:

- Checkpointing exists,

- state remains safe,

- and policy permits.

19.313 Non-Preemptible Local Work

Some compilation, mutation or media operations may not stop safely.

19.314 Local Checkpoint

Checkpoints shall identify:

- Execution,

- Step,

- Runtime,

- Model,

- progress,

- and integrity.

19.315 Checkpoint Portability

A Checkpoint may be Node-specific, Runtime-specific or portable.

The property shall be explicit.

19.316 Local Job Migration

Migration to another Node requires:

- compatible Runtime,

- compatible Model or Tool,

- accessible data,

- valid authority,

- and safe state transfer.

19.317 Sensitive Job Migration

Local Only or confidential work may move only to approved Zones.

19.318 Data Locality

Data Locality describes where required Inputs are stored relative to execution.

Placement may prefer the Node already holding authorised data.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.319 Data Movement

Moving data between Nodes or Zones is a governed operation.

It shall preserve:

- source,

- destination,

- classification,

- encryption,

- authority,

- and provenance.

19.320 Data Transfer Plan

Large or sensitive transfers may require a dedicated Plan Step.

19.321 Transfer Integrity

Transfers should verify:

- checksum,

- completeness,

- and destination identity.

19.322 Transfer Encryption

Protected data shall use approved encryption in transit.

19.323 Transfer Resume

Resumable transfer shall preserve verified boundaries.

19.324 Transfer Failure

Partial data shall not become complete Input.

19.325 Transfer Cleanup

Incomplete temporary copies shall be cleaned safely.

19.326 Offline Operation

An Offline Operation performs work while canonical central services are unavailable or unreachable.

It shall include or reference:

- offlineOperationId,

- Node,

- cached authority,

- policy snapshot,

- Project,

- Plan or task,

- start,

- local state,

- synchronisation requirement,

- and provenance.

19.327 Offline Operation Identity

Every material Offline Operation shall have stable identity.

19.328 Offline Authority

Offline work may use only authority explicitly valid for offline use.

19.329 Offline Policy Snapshot

The exact cached policy Version shall be preserved.

19.330 Offline Credential

Offline Credentials shall be:

- device-bound,

- time-bounded,

- narrowly scoped,

- and revocable when connectivity returns.

19.331 Offline Budget

Paid external work is ordinarily unavailable offline.

Local resource limits may still apply.

19.332 Offline Data Availability

Required data shall exist locally before offline execution begins.

19.333 Offline Model Availability

Required Model Package and Runtime shall be installed and validated.

19.334 Offline Tool Availability

Required Tools shall be installed and sandboxed.

19.335 Offline Completion

Offline local completion remains provisional until required central synchronisation and policy checks occur.

19.336 Offline Side Effect

External publication, purchase or remote mutation cannot be completed offline unless a specific local target exists and policy permits it.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.337 Offline Queue

Events and receipts may be stored locally for later synchronisation.

19.338 Offline Evidence

Evidence shall include:

- local time,

- Node identity,

- policy snapshot,

- Model and Tool Versions,

- and later synchronisation state.

19.339 Clock Reliability

Offline device clocks may drift.

Time confidence shall be preserved.

19.340 Offline Conflict

Changes made independently on several Nodes may conflict.

Conflict resolution shall be explicit.

19.341 Synchronisation

Synchronisation transfers state, evidence, Assets or policy between local Nodes and canonical services.

It shall preserve:

- identity,

- order,

- conflict,

- and provenance.

19.342 Synchronisation Record

A Synchronisation Record shall include:

- synchronisationId,

- source,

- destination,

- object set,

- Versions,

- start,

- completion,

- conflicts,

- and provenance.

19.343 Synchronisation Identity

Every material synchronisation process shall have stable identity.

19.344 Push Synchronisation

The Node sends local state to the central system.

19.345 Pull Synchronisation

The Node receives current policy, registry state or work.

19.346 Bidirectional Synchronisation

Bidirectional synchronisation requires conflict strategy.

19.347 Synchronisation Checkpoint

A durable position may identify the last confirmed shared state.

19.348 Duplicate Synchronisation

Repeated transfer shall be idempotent.

19.349 Synchronisation Ordering

Late older data shall not overwrite newer canonical state automatically.

19.350 Synchronisation Conflict

Conflicts may occur in:

- Asset metadata,

- policy,

- schedules,

- registry records,

- or local modifications.

19.351 Conflict Resolution

Resolution may be:

- canonical wins,

- local wins with approval,

- merge,

- manual review,

- or branch creation.

19.352 Canonical Authority During Sync

Canonical governed records remain authoritative unless the object’s ownership explicitly allows local authority.

19.353 Local Event Replay

Local Events may replay after reconnection.

They shall not duplicate external side effects.

19.354 Synchronisation Security

Both source and destination shall authenticate.

Protected data shall remain encrypted.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.355 Synchronisation Backpressure

Large sync workloads shall not overload the Node or central services.

19.356 Offline Revocation Gap

A disconnected Node may not receive immediate revocation.

Offline authority shall be designed with bounded risk.

19.357 Revocation Reconciliation

On reconnection, the Node shall apply current revocation and assess work performed after the effective revocation time.

19.358 Policy Drift During Offline Work

Offline work completed under stale policy may require review before acceptance.

19.359 Local Execution Receipt

A Local Execution Receipt preserves what occurred on a local or private resource.

It shall include or reference:

- localExecutionReceiptId,

- Node,

- Zone,

- Runtime Deployment,

- Model or Tool Deployment,

- Execution,

- Attempt,

- policy Versions,

- placement,

- capacity,

- timing,

- usage,

- Outputs,

- warnings,

- and provenance.

19.360 Local Execution Receipt Identity

Every receipt shall have stable identity.

19.361 Local Resource Usage

Usage may include:

- CPU time,

- GPU time,

- memory peak,

- energy estimate,

- disk I/O,

- network transfer,

- and storage.

19.362 Local Usage Confidence

Measurements may be:

- hardware-reported,

- runtime-reported,

- operating-system measured,

- estimated,

- or unknown.

19.363 Local Cost

Local cost may include:

- electricity,

- hardware depreciation,

- rented infrastructure,

- storage,

- maintenance,

- and opportunity cost.

19.364 Local Is Not Free

The user interface shall not represent local execution as universally free.

19.365 Marginal Local Cost

Marginal cost may be near zero for some work but shall remain an estimate.

19.366 Hardware Depreciation

Depreciation may be included in advanced economic models.

It shall not be fabricated where no policy exists.

19.367 Energy Cost

Energy estimates should identify:

- power,

- duration,

- unit price,

- and confidence.

19.368 Cloud Self-Hosted Cost

Self-managed cloud Nodes may create:

- compute,

- accelerator,

- storage,

- network,

- and idle-time costs.

19.369 Idle Cost

A dedicated or cloud Node may incur cost while unused.

19.370 Model Loading Cost

Loading and compiling Models consumes time and energy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.371 Local Quality

Local quality shall be evaluated according to the same Capability and Quality Contracts as external execution.

19.372 Local Quality Assumption Prohibition

Privacy advantage does not justify unmeasured quality claims.

19.373 Deployment-Specific Evaluation

Evaluations should identify:

- Model Package,

- Runtime,

- configuration,

- hardware,

- and context limits.

19.374 Quantisation Evaluation

Quantised variants shall receive separate quality evidence where material.

19.375 Local Hallucination Risk

Local Models may have different knowledge, safety and instruction-following properties.

Routing shall reflect observed evidence.

19.376 Local Structured Output

Structured-output support shall be tested per Runtime and Model Deployment.

19.377 Local Tool Calling

Tool-calling capability shall be verified.

A prompt-emulated Tool call is not the same as native structured Tool invocation.

19.378 Local Multilingual Quality

Swedish and other required language quality shall be measured.

19.379 Local Context Limits

Configured context may exceed reliable quality.

Effective tested limits shall remain distinct from theoretical maximum.

19.380 Local Safety

Local Models may lack Provider moderation or safety layers.

Omnira policy and evaluation remain responsible.

19.381 Local Privacy

Local execution may reduce external disclosure.

It may still expose data through:

- logs,

- caches,

- local malware,

- shared accounts,

- backups,

- remote administration,

- or synchronisation.

19.382 Data Custody

Data custody identifies who can administratively or physically access data.

19.383 Data Processing Location

Processing location shall be recorded separately from storage location.

19.384 Data Storage Location

Inputs, temporary files, Outputs and logs may be stored in different locations.

Each shall be governed.

19.385 Local Prompt Retention

Prompt and context retention shall be explicit.

19.386 Runtime Logging

Runtime logs shall avoid storing full protected prompts and Outputs by default.

19.387 Crash Dump

Crash dumps may contain sensitive memory.

They shall be protected or disabled according to risk.

19.388 Swap and Hibernation

Operating-system swap and hibernation may contain sensitive data.

Encryption and policy shall account for it.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.389 Shared Memory

Shared-memory mechanisms may leak data across processes if isolation is weak.

19.390 Clipboard

Local workflows shall avoid placing sensitive data in clipboard unnecessarily.

19.391 Local Backup

Backups may copy:

- Models,

- Assets,

- logs,

- caches,

- and Secrets.

Backup scope and encryption shall be explicit.

19.392 Cloud Backup Risk

A local device backed up to a cloud service may no longer satisfy strict Local Only requirements unless policy allows it.

19.393 Local Deletion

Deletion shall account for:

- active file,

- cache,

- backup,

- snapshot,

- and synchronised copies.

19.394 Secure Wipe

Secure wipe guarantees vary by storage technology.

Claims shall remain evidence-based.

19.395 Cryptographic Erasure

Destroying encryption keys may provide stronger practical deletion for encrypted volumes.

19.396 Node Security

Every active Node shall implement security appropriate to its permitted workload.

Controls may include:

- operating-system patching,

- disk encryption,

- strong authentication,

- firewall,

- least privilege,

- malware protection,

- and secure boot.

19.397 Operating-System Patch State

Patch state shall influence trust and placement.

19.398 Unsupported Operating System

Unsupported systems should be restricted from sensitive production work.

19.399 Administrative Privilege

Ordinary Model and Tool work shall not run with unrestricted administrator or root privilege.

19.400 User Account Isolation

Dedicated operating-system users may isolate services and Projects.

19.401 Disk Encryption

Portable and sensitive Nodes should use approved full-disk or volume encryption.

19.402 Screen Lock

Interactive devices should enforce screen lock according to policy.

19.403 Secure Boot

Secure boot may provide integrity evidence where supported.

19.404 Malware Protection

Malware scanning and endpoint controls may be required according to Node risk.

19.405 Remote Administration

Remote administration shall be:

- restricted,

- authenticated,

- encrypted,

- and logged.

19.406 Open Port

Every exposed port shall have a justified service owner and policy.

19.407 Default Credential Prohibition

Default passwords or shared default keys shall not remain active.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.408 Service Account

Local services shall run under dedicated bounded identities where practical.
