19.409 Secret Isolation

Local Runtimes and Tools shall receive only required Credentials.

19.410 Environment Variable Leakage

Child processes shall not inherit unrelated Secrets.

19.411 File-System Scope

Working directories and permitted paths shall be explicit.

19.412 Home Directory Access

Broad access to the user’s home directory is prohibited unless specifically required and approved.

19.413 Project Directory Access

Tools should be restricted to the exact Project or worktree required.

19.414 Device Access

Camera, microphone, location, Bluetooth, USB and other device permissions shall be Capability- and task-specific.

19.415 Network Egress

Models and Tools shall not receive unrestricted egress by default.

19.416 Telemetry

Runtime telemetry shall be reviewed for data disclosure and may be disabled where policy requires it.

19.417 Update Channel

Automatic updates may contact external services.

Update policy shall remain explicit.

19.418 Supply-Chain Security

Local intelligence depends on:

- Model packages,

- runtime packages,

- libraries,

- drivers,

- containers,

- operating systems,

- and download sources.

Each forms part of the supply chain.

19.419 Software Bill of Materials

Critical Runtime or Tool packages should have a dependency inventory where practical.

19.420 Dependency Vulnerability

Known vulnerable dependencies may restrict production eligibility.

19.421 Package Repository Trust

Package repositories shall be approved or classified.

19.422 Mirror Trust

Mirrors may alter or replace files.

Checksums and signatures reduce risk.

19.423 Container Image

Container images shall have:

- immutable digest,

- source,

- base image,

- build provenance,

- scan state,

- and lifecycle.

19.424 Mutable Tag

Mutable tags shall not be used as sole production identity.

19.425 Image Digest

Exact image digest should be preserved in evidence.

19.426 Driver

GPU and device drivers affect compatibility, security and performance.

Driver Version shall remain explicit.

19.427 Firmware

Firmware state may affect trust and stability.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.428 Runtime Library

Compute libraries and acceleration frameworks may materially affect results.

19.429 Package Update

Updates shall not occur silently during pinned production execution.

19.430 Auto-Update Restriction

Automatic updates may be disabled or staged for critical environments.

19.431 Update Plan

An Update Plan shall include or reference:

- updatePlanId,

- target,

- current Version,

- new Version,

- compatibility,

- validation,

- backup,

- rollback,

- schedule,

- and owner.

19.432 Update Plan Identity

Every material Update Plan shall have stable identity.

19.433 Update Admission

Updates shall require:

- source validation,

- compatibility review,

- security review,

- and capacity.

19.434 Update Testing

Testing should include:

- startup,

- representative inference,

- Tool execution,

- quality regression,

- performance,

- and recovery.

19.435 Canary Node

A new Version may be deployed to one limited Node first.

19.436 Shadow Execution

A new Runtime or Model Deployment may process copied non-consequential work without becoming authoritative.

19.437 Update Cutover

Cutover shall preserve exact Version transition.

19.438 Rollback Plan

Rollback shall identify:

- prior package,

- configuration,

- data compatibility,

- and trigger.

19.439 Rollback Limitation

Data migrations or cache changes may make rollback incomplete.

19.440 Failed Update

Failed updates shall not leave the Node in ambiguous production eligibility.

19.441 Model Update

A new local Model Version or Package Variant requires new Registry and quality evidence.

19.442 Runtime Update

Runtime updates may change behaviour even when the Model Package remains the same.

19.443 Driver Update

Driver updates may affect stability, performance and reproducibility.

19.444 Operating-System Update

Operating-system updates may affect sandbox, permissions, drivers and Runtimes.

19.445 Local Monitoring

Observability should expose:

- Node health,

- Runtime health,

- Model readiness,

- Tool health,

- capacity,

- temperature,

- battery,

- storage,

- network,

- queue,

- errors,

- and policy state.

19.446 Node Heartbeat

Connected Nodes may send bounded heartbeats.

Heartbeat absence does not prove failure.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.447 Offline Heartbeat

Offline-capable Nodes shall not be marked compromised merely because they are disconnected.

19.448 Health Observation

A Health Observation shall include:

- observationId,

- target,

- state,

- metrics,

- observedAt,

- source,

- confidence,

- and provenance.

19.449 Health Freshness

Health evidence becomes stale.

Routing and placement shall account for it.

19.450 Node Availability

Availability shall distinguish:

- online,

- reachable,

- authenticated,

- schedulable,

- and ready.

19.451 Runtime Availability

Runtime process availability remains separate from Model readiness.

19.452 Capacity Telemetry

Telemetry may include:

- CPU,

- GPU,

- memory,

- disk,

- battery,

- temperature,

- and queue.

19.453 Privacy-Preserving Telemetry

Telemetry shall not include protected content unnecessarily.

19.454 Local Log

Local logs shall be:

- bounded,

- classified,

- rotated,

- and synchronised only when policy permits.

19.455 Central Log Synchronisation

Sensitive local logs may remain local or be redacted before central transfer.

19.456 Metrics Retention

Retention shall support:

- capacity planning,

- Incident review,

- and quality drift

without excessive personal monitoring.

19.457 User Activity Privacy

Device utilisation monitoring shall avoid unnecessary observation of private user activity.

19.458 Local Incident

A Local Incident is a material failure involving a Node, Runtime, Model Package, Tool, local data or private execution boundary.

Examples include:

- Node compromise,

- unauthorised file access,

- Model package corruption,

- malicious Tool,

- out-of-memory crash,

- private-data egress,

- lost device,

- local Asset loss,

- or unverified package execution.

19.459 Local Incident Identity

Every material Local Incident shall have stable identity.

19.460 Node Incident

A Node Incident may involve:

- compromise,

- loss,

- hardware failure,

- overheating,

- storage corruption,

- or unauthorised access.

19.461 Runtime Incident

A Runtime Incident may involve:

- crash,

- schema defect,

- memory leak,

- wrong Model load,

- or unsafe network access.

19.462 Model Package Incident

A package Incident may involve:

- checksum mismatch,

- malicious code,

- wrong licence,

- misidentified Model,

- or quality regression.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.463 Tool Incident

A Tool Incident may involve:

- sandbox escape,

- unintended deletion,

- secret access,

- or cross-Project mutation.

19.464 Placement Incident

A Placement Incident occurs when work or data executes outside an approved Zone.

19.465 Egress Incident

Protected data leaving the approved boundary is a severe Incident.

19.466 Local Asset Incident

Local Assets may be:

- deleted,

- corrupted,

- overwritten,

- or lost before synchronisation.

19.467 Capacity Incident

Capacity Incidents may include:

- memory exhaustion,

- thermal shutdown,

- disk full,

- or GPU failure.

19.468 Local Incident Containment

Containment may include:

- suspend Node,

- isolate network,

- stop Runtime,

- revoke device Credentials,

- disable Tool,

- quarantine package,

- or halt synchronisation.

19.469 Local Incident Investigation

Investigation should inspect:

- Node identity,

- trust evidence,

- processes,

- file access,

- network traffic,

- package provenance,

- Credential use,

- and affected Executions.

19.470 Local Incident Recovery

Recovery may require:

- clean Node rebuild,

- credential rotation,

- package reinstallation,

- Asset restoration,

- policy correction,

- and re-enrollment.

19.471 Node Rebuild

A compromised or corrupted Node should be rebuilt from trusted sources rather than repaired blindly where practical.

19.472 Rebuild Identity

The rebuilt machine may retain canonical Node continuity only when identity and trust continuity are verified.

Otherwise, a new Node identity shall be created.

19.473 Hardware Failure

Hardware failure may leave local work incomplete or inaccessible.

19.474 Storage Failure

Storage failure requires:

- corruption assessment,

- backup recovery,

- and Asset reconciliation.

19.475 Device Loss

Lost-device response shall include:

- Node suspension,

- Session revocation,

- Credential review,

- encryption assessment,

- and data exposure review.

19.476 Device Recovery

A recovered lost device shall not return to active status without fresh validation.

19.477 Private Cluster

A Private Cluster groups several Nodes under one governed administrative boundary.

It shall include or reference:

- clusterId,

- owner,

- operator,

- Nodes,

- network,

- scheduler,

- storage,

- trust,

- and lifecycle.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.478 Private Cluster Identity

Every persistent cluster shall have stable identity.

19.479 Cluster Control Plane

The cluster control plane manages:

- membership,

- scheduling,

- deployment,

- networking,

- storage,

- and health.

It shall use its own Service Principal identity.

19.480 Cluster Worker Node

Worker Nodes shall remain individually identifiable.

19.481 Cluster Membership

Membership changes shall be versioned and validated.

19.482 Cluster Trust

Cluster membership does not make every Node equally trusted.

19.483 Cluster Namespace

Tenant and Project namespaces may support logical isolation.

They shall not be assumed sufficient without enforcement evidence.

19.484 Cluster Network Policy

Network communication shall be restricted by workload and scope.

19.485 Cluster Storage

Shared storage shall preserve Project and Tenant access boundaries.

19.486 Cluster Secret Management

Secrets shall remain outside workload configuration and be resolved through approved mechanisms.

19.487 Cluster Autoscaling

Autoscaling may add or remove Nodes according to demand.

New Nodes require trusted enrollment.

19.488 Cloud Autoscaling

Cloud-created Nodes may incur cost immediately.

Budget and capacity policy remain required.

19.489 Scale to Zero

Idle self-hosted services may stop to reduce cost.

Cold-start latency shall remain visible.

19.490 Cluster Failure Domain

Redundant work should avoid one shared:

- host,

- rack,

- power source,

- network,

- or region

where continuity requires separation.

19.491 Federated Nodes

Federated Nodes participate in one Fabric while remaining under different ownership or administrative boundaries.

19.492 Federation Identity

Each Node and owning domain shall remain explicit.

19.493 Federation Trust

Trust shall be bilateral or policy-based.

Federation does not create universal access.

19.494 Federation Capability

A federated Node may expose only selected Capabilities.

19.495 Federation Data Policy

Data may move to a federated Node only when placement and ownership permit it.

19.496 Federation Revocation

A Node or domain may be removed rapidly from eligibility.

19.497 Peer Discovery

Federated discovery shall not create automatic trust.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.498 Remote Attestation

Remote attestation may support federated trust decisions.

19.499 Mobile Intelligence

Mobile Nodes may support:

- approvals,

- lightweight inference,

- speech,

- image understanding,

- local retrieval,

- notifications,

- device context,

- and controlled actions.

19.500 Mobile Resource Constraints

Mobile scheduling shall account for:

- battery,

- thermal state,

- background execution limits,

- memory,

- network,

- and user interaction.

19.501 Mobile Data Boundary

Private messages, private photos and restricted applications shall remain outside Agent access unless explicitly authorised.

19.502 Mobile Sensor Access

Camera, microphone, location and other sensors require explicit Capability and permission.

19.503 Mobile Voice Processing

Voice may be processed locally where supported.

Raw voice data retention shall follow policy.

19.504 Mobile Offline Assistant

A bounded local assistant may continue selected functions without network access.

19.505 Mobile Approval Node

A mobile device may act as an approval interface without hosting the underlying execution.

19.506 Mobile Execution Node

A mobile device may host lightweight Models or Tools.

Execution capability does not create broader device authority.

19.507 Mobile Background Work

Heavy background work should pause when it would harm battery, temperature or user experience.

19.508 Mobile Device Loss

Loss shall trigger immediate Node, Session and Credential response.

19.509 Workstation Intelligence

A workstation may host:

- larger language Models,

- image Models,

- local retrieval,

- code Tools,

- and media processing.

19.510 Workstation Foreground Use

Omnira shall respect user-defined resource ceilings during active personal use.

19.511 Private Rig

A private GPU rig may serve one or more Nodes or Projects.

It shall have:

- explicit owner,

- network policy,

- Node identity,

- capacity,

- and maintenance responsibility.

19.512 Private Rig Idle Use

Idle hardware may serve background work under approved schedules.

19.513 Private Rig Shared Use

Shared private rigs require Project isolation and cost attribution.

19.514 Home Server

A home server may provide persistent:

- local Models,

- retrieval,

- storage,

- scheduling,

- and private services.

Physical and network security remain part of the trust boundary.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.515 Cloud Private Node

A private cloud Node may provide stronger availability than a personal device.

It remains an external infrastructure dependency.

19.516 Dedicated GPU Server

A dedicated GPU server may host private Deployments.

Hardware allocation and tenancy shall be evidenced.

19.517 Confidential Node

A confidential-compute Node may receive restricted work only when:

- attestation is valid,

- key release policy permits it,

- and the threat model is accepted.

19.518 Air-Gapped Node

An air-gapped Node shall use controlled import and export packages.

19.519 Air-Gap Import

Import shall verify:

- media source,

- package checksum,

- manifest,

- malware,

- and operator.

19.520 Air-Gap Export

Export shall verify:

- authorised content,

- classification,

- checksum,

- and chain of custody.

19.521 Air-Gap Update

Updates require planned offline distribution and rollback.

19.522 Private Retrieval

Private retrieval may use local:

- document stores,

- vector indexes,

- databases,

- and search Tools.

The retrieval system shall preserve source permissions.

19.523 Retrieval Access Control

Index membership shall not bypass source-document permissions.

19.524 Retrieval Provenance

Returned chunks shall preserve:

- source,

- location,

- index,

- embedding Model,

- retrieval time,

- and score.

19.525 Private Embeddings

Embeddings may be generated locally to avoid external data disclosure.

19.526 Embedding Model Identity

The exact embedding Model and Version shall remain attached to the index.

19.527 Embedding Migration

Changing the embedding Model may require complete index rebuild.

19.528 Private Speech

Local speech-to-text or text-to-speech may process sensitive audio without external transfer.

19.529 Voice Quality

Local voice quality shall be evaluated separately from external Provider quality.

19.530 Voice Rights

Local generation does not remove voice, likeness or consent requirements.

19.531 Private Vision

Local vision Models may process images and screenshots inside approved Zones.

19.532 Image Privacy

Local image analysis shall still respect private image and folder exclusions.

19.533 Private Code Intelligence

Code analysis may run locally with repository-scoped Tools and Models.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.534 Code Execution

Generated or analysed code shall execute only in approved Sandboxes.

19.535 Private Media Processing

Transcoding, composition and derivative creation may run locally.

The exact Tool Versions and input checksums shall remain in provenance.

19.536 Local Search

Local search may query indexed private data.

It shall not be conflated with current web search.

19.537 Hybrid Execution

Hybrid execution combines local and external resources within one Plan.

Each Step shall preserve its placement and data boundary.

19.538 Hybrid Data Minimisation

Only required derived or redacted data should leave the local boundary.

19.539 Local Preprocessing

Local preprocessing may:

- redact,

- summarise,

- compress,

- transcode,

- or extract features

before external execution.

19.540 Preprocessing Integrity

Preprocessing shall preserve the information required by the Capability.

19.541 Redaction

Redaction shall identify:

- method,

- removed fields,

- reversibility,

- and validation.

19.542 Derived External Payload

A derived payload remains linked to the protected local source through provenance.

19.543 External Postprocessing

An external Output may return for local evaluation, composition or storage.

19.544 Split Execution

One Capability may require local and external sub-Steps.

Material split shall be explicit in the Execution Graph.

19.545 No Hidden Egress

A local Runtime, Tool or Model package shall not contact external services without declared and permitted network access.

19.546 Telemetry Egress

Diagnostic telemetry counts as external data transfer.

19.547 Licence Verification Egress

Licence checks may require external communication.

The dependency shall be explicit.

19.548 Model Download Egress

Downloading a Model package is separate from inference-time data transfer.

19.549 Update Egress

Automatic update traffic shall remain governed.

19.550 Training and Fine-Tuning

Local or private training, fine-tuning and adaptation are higher-complexity capabilities.

They require explicit:

- dataset,

- rights,

- consent,

- purpose,

- Budget,

- compute,

- evaluation,

- and output governance.

19.551 Training Job

A Training Job shall be represented separately from inference Execution.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.552 Training Dataset

The dataset shall have:

- identity,

- provenance,

- ownership,

- classification,

- rights,

- consent,

- version,

- and retention.

19.553 Training Data Minimisation

Only required data shall enter training.

19.554 Training Rights

Possession of data does not prove the right to train on it.

19.555 Personal Data Training

Training on personal data requires explicit policy and consent where applicable.

19.556 Project Isolation in Training

One Project’s data shall not improve another Project’s Model automatically.

19.557 Fine-Tune Identity

Every fine-tuned Model shall receive distinct Model Version or Variant identity.

19.558 Fine-Tune Lineage

Lineage shall include:

- Base Model,

- dataset,

- method,

- parameters,

- code,

- Runtime,

- hardware,

- and operator.

19.559 Training Checkpoint

Checkpoints are sensitive Model artefacts and shall be governed.

19.560 Training Evaluation

A fine-tuned Model shall not enter production before evaluation.

19.561 Training Cost

Compute, storage and energy shall be recorded.

19.562 Training Reproducibility

Reproducibility may require:

- seeds,

- software Versions,

- dataset Version,

- and hardware.

Limitations shall remain explicit.

19.563 Model Adaptation

Prompt tuning, adapters, retrieval augmentation and memory are distinct from weight training.

19.564 Continuous Learning Prohibition

Production Models shall not update weights automatically from user interactions without explicit governed architecture.

19.565 Derived Learning

Derived Learning may inform future fine-tuning proposals.

It shall not become training data automatically.

19.566 Model Export

Exporting locally trained weights is a consequential action involving rights and data leakage risk.

19.567 Model Deletion

Deleting fine-tuned Models requires dependency and retention review.

19.568 Local Governance

Local infrastructure remains part of Omnira’s governed platform.

Owners and operators shall have defined responsibilities.

19.569 Node Steward

Every production Node should have an accountable steward.

19.570 Runtime Steward

Every Runtime should have an accountable maintainer.

19.571 Model Package Steward

Every admitted private package should have an owner or curator.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.572 Tool Steward

Every local Tool should have an accountable owner.

19.573 Zone Policy Owner

Every Execution Zone shall have an authority responsible for placement rules.

19.574 Shared Infrastructure Agreement

Shared private infrastructure should define:

- ownership,

- maintenance,

- cost,

- access,

- recovery,

- and retirement.

19.575 Node Inventory

The platform shall maintain inventory of:

- Nodes,

- hardware,

- Runtimes,

- Models,

- Tools,

- storage,

- and trust state.

19.576 Inventory Freshness

Disconnected Nodes may have stale inventory.

Freshness shall remain visible.

19.577 Inventory Reconciliation

On reconnect, actual installed resources shall be reconciled with canonical records.

19.578 Shadow Runtime

An unregistered Runtime discovered on a Node shall not become production eligible automatically.

19.579 Shadow Model

An unregistered Model package shall remain quarantined or experimental.

19.580 Shadow Tool

An unregistered executable or MCP server shall not receive Agent access.

19.581 Node Drift

Node drift may include changes to:

- operating system,

- hardware,

- runtime,

- permissions,

- network,

- or storage.

19.582 Configuration Drift

Material drift shall trigger validation or restriction.

19.583 Desired State

A managed Node may have a declared desired configuration.

19.584 Actual State

Observed actual state shall remain distinct from desired state.

19.585 Remediation

Automated remediation may restore approved configuration only within bounded authority.

19.586 Destructive Remediation

Destructive reinstallation, deletion or wipe requires explicit authority.

19.587 Node Retirement

Retirement shall address:

- active jobs,

- Credentials,

- Assets,

- Models,

- Tools,

- storage,

- and audit.

19.588 Node Wipe

Wipe shall use a governed procedure and evidence.

19.589 Hardware Disposal

Disposal shall protect residual data and credentials.

19.590 Node Transfer

Transferring ownership requires:

- data removal,

- credential revocation,

- re-enrollment,

- and new trust assessment.

19.591 Local Policy

Local Policy defines requirements for:

- Node trust,

- package admission,

- placement,

- sandboxing,

- networking,

- storage,

- updates,

- and evidence.

text:
19.592 Platform Local Policy

Platform policy may require:

- stable Node identity,

- encrypted storage,

- registered Runtimes,

- and no untrusted package execution.

19.593 Tenant Local Policy

Tenant policy may define:

- approved facilities,

- Node ownership,

- network,

- and data residency.

19.594 Project Local Policy

Project policy may define:

- allowed Nodes,

- local folders,

- Models,

- Tools,

- and Resource Pools.

19.595 Data-Class Placement Policy

Each Data Classification may define eligible Zone classes.

19.596 Local Only Policy

Local Only policy shall fail closed when no eligible local resource exists.

19.597 Confidential Policy

Confidential work may require:

- trusted Node,

- encrypted storage,

- restricted egress,

- and approved backup.

19.598 Prohibited Data

Prohibited data shall not be processed even locally unless a separate policy explicitly permits it.

19.599 Model Package Policy

Package admission policy may require:

- approved source,

- checksum,

- licence,

- and security scan.

19.600 Tool Package Policy

Tool admission may require stronger sandbox and permission review.

19.601 Update Policy

Updates may be:

- manual,

- scheduled,

- staged,

- or automatic within approved bounds.

19.602 Offline Policy

Offline operation shall define:

- permitted Capabilities,

- maximum duration,

- cached authority,

- and synchronisation requirements.

19.603 Energy Policy

The user or Tenant may define limits for:

- battery,

- power,

- quiet hours,

- and maximum utilisation.

19.604 Local Policy Version

Every Placement and Local Execution shall reference applicable policy Versions.

19.605 Local API

The Local Control Plane should expose governed operations such as:

- register Zone,

- enrol Node,

- attest Node,

- inspect inventory,

- register Runtime,

- install Model,

- install Tool,

- validate Deployment,

- reserve resource,

- place Step,

- dispatch local work,

- record receipt,

- synchronise,

- suspend Node,

- update,

- rollback,

- and retire.

19.606 Node API

The Node API should support:

- discover,

- enrol,

- validate,

- activate,

- restrict,

- suspend,

- isolate,

- retire,

- and inspect.

19.607 Runtime API

The Runtime API should support:

- register,

- install,

- start,

- stop,

- update,

- rollback,

- health check,

- and remove.

19.608 Model Package API

The package API should support:

- register source,

- download,

- verify,

- quarantine,

- admit,

- install,

- validate,

- and remove.

19.609 Placement API

The Placement API should support:

- evaluate eligible Zones,

- rank Nodes,

- create Decision,

- revalidate,

- and explain.

19.610 Synchronisation API

The Synchronisation API should support:

- inspect pending state,

- push,

- pull,

- detect conflicts,

- resolve,

- and verify.

19.611 Local Observability API

The observability interface should support:

- Node health,

- Runtime health,

- Deployment readiness,

- capacity,

- temperature,

- storage,

- network,

- and incidents.

19.612 Stage 1 Local Intelligence Objective

Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy local and private execution foundation needed to prove:

- stable Node identity,

- local Runtime registration,

- private Model Deployment identity,

- local Tool execution,

- placement policy,

- Local Only enforcement,

- capacity and health,

- local scheduling,

- Model package provenance,

- sandboxing,

- local execution receipts,

- and recovery.

Stage 1 shall not attempt to create a universal distributed private cloud.

19.613 Stage 1 Execution Zones

Stage 1 should support at minimum:

- user laptop Zone,

- user workstation or private-rig Zone,

- local network or home-server Zone where available,

- and external managed Provider Zone for contrast.

19.614 Stage 1 Node Types

Stage 1 should support:

- interactive laptop or workstation Node,

- persistent private server Node,

- and optional mobile approval Node.

19.615 Stage 1 Runtime Support

Stage 1 should support at minimum:

- one local language-Model Runtime such as Ollama or equivalent,

- one NVIDIA-compatible or accelerator-backed local path where available,

- one local Tool Runtime,

- and one local media-processing Runtime.

19.616 Stage 1 Model Support

Stage 1 should support:

- local text generation,

- local reasoning or code assistance,

- local embeddings,

- and optional local speech or vision

according to available hardware.

19.627 Stage 1 Model Package Admission

Stage 1 shall require:

- known source,

- checksum,

- canonical Model mapping,

- format,

- quantisation,

- licence,

- and validation.

19.628 Stage 1 Tool Admission

Stage 1 shall require:

- Tool identity,

- Version,

- provenance,

- permissions,

- Project scope,

- and Sandbox Profile.

19.629 Stage 1 Local Scheduling

Stage 1 shall account for:

- Node availability,

- memory,

- storage,

- Model load state,

- concurrency,

- battery where applicable,

- and user foreground protection.

19.630 Stage 1 Local Only Enforcement

Stage 1 shall block external fallback for Local Only data.

19.631 Stage 1 Hybrid Execution

Stage 1 may support local preprocessing followed by approved external execution when:

- classification permits it,

- the derived payload is governed,

- and provenance is preserved.

19.632 Stage 1 Offline Support

Stage 1 should support bounded offline inference and local evidence storage.

Full multi-master offline autonomy is outside Stage 1.

19.633 Stage 1 Synchronisation

Stage 1 should synchronise:

- local execution receipts,

- Asset metadata,

- health,

- and inventory

after reconnection.

19.634 Stage 1 Recovery

Stage 1 shall support:

- Node suspension,

- Runtime restart,

- package revalidation,

- Asset recovery,

- and clean re-enrollment.

19.635 Stage 1 Node Acceptance Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Node has stable canonical identity.

2. Node identity remains distinct from hostname.

3. Node identifies owner.

4. Node identifies operator.

5. Node identifies Execution Zone.

6. Node identifies Environment.

7. Device Principal is bound.

8. Node lifecycle is explicit.

9. Discovered Node is not automatically active.

10. Suspended Node receives no new work.

11. Compromised Node is excluded immediately.

12. Lost Node triggers identity response.

13. Retired Node remains historically queryable.

14. Node health has freshness.

15. Node inventory survives service restart.

19.636 Stage 1 Enrollment Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Enrollment has stable identity.

2. Bootstrap Token is single-use.

3. Owner authority is verified.

4. Device identity is verified.

5. Project scope is explicit.

6. Environment is explicit.

7. Trust profile is assigned.

8. Credentials are device-scoped.

9. Enrollment failure creates no active Node.

10. Re-enrollment does not duplicate identity incorrectly.

11. Ownership change requires review.

12. Suspended enrollment blocks connection.

13. Enrollment evidence is retained.

14. Cross-Tenant enrollment is rejected.

15. Historical enrollment remains queryable.

text:
19.637 Stage 1 Trust Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Trust profile has stable identity and Version.

2. Disk encryption state is recorded.

3. Operating-system support state is recorded.

4. Patch state influences eligibility.

5. Local location does not imply trust.

6. Secure boot evidence is scoped.

7. Unverified Node cannot process Confidential data.

8. Trust downgrade stops new sensitive work.

9. Stale attestation reduces eligibility.

10. Compromised trust state opens Incident.

11. Network exposure is included.

12. Secret Store state is included.

13. Administrative privilege is included.

14. Trust claims remain evidence-based.

15. Historical trust state remains queryable.

19.638 Stage 1 Hardware Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. CPU architecture is recorded.

2. Memory total and available remain distinct.

3. GPU identity is recorded where present.

4. Accelerator memory is recorded.

5. Driver Version is recorded.

6. Storage capacity is recorded.

7. Network Profile is recorded.

8. Battery state is recorded where applicable.

9. Thermal state affects capacity.

10. Hardware profile has freshness.

11. Unknown hardware properties remain unknown.

12. Runtime compatibility is validated.

13. Model fit is validated before load.

14. Capacity headroom is preserved.

15. Historical hardware observations remain queryable.

19.639 Stage 1 Runtime Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Runtime has stable identity and Version.

2. Runtime Deployment identifies Node.

3. Endpoint is explicit.

4. Configuration is explicit.

5. Runtime installation verifies source.

6. Runtime health is separate from Node health.

7. Failed Runtime is excluded from placement.

8. Runtime update creates attributable change.

9. Rollback restores prior Version where safe.

10. Runtime removal blocks new execution.

11. Runtime logs exclude protected prompts by default.

12. Runtime network access follows policy.

13. Runtime runs under bounded Service Principal.

14. Runtime state survives restart.

15. Historical Runtime Versions remain queryable.

19.640 Stage 1 Model-Package Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Package has stable identity.

2. Package maps to canonical Model.

3. Model Version is explicit.

4. Source is explicit.

5. Revision is explicit.

6. Checksums are verified.

7. Format is explicit.

8. Precision is explicit.

9. Quantisation is explicit.

10. Licence is explicit.

11. Unknown licence blocks production.

12. Unsafe deserialisation is prohibited.

13. Unverified package remains quarantined.

14. Converted package has new provenance.

15. Historical package metadata remains queryable.

text:
19.641 Stage 1 Model-Installation Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Installation has stable identity.

2. Node is explicit.

3. Runtime is explicit.

4. Path is not Model identity.

5. Download supports integrity validation.

6. Corrupt download does not install.

7. Installation state is durable.

8. Load test is performed.

9. Memory fit is tested.

10. Output sanity is tested.

11. Removal checks active dependencies.

12. Shared package files are not deleted accidentally.

13. Installation drift is detectable.

14. Revalidation follows Runtime update.

15. Historical installation remains queryable.

19.642 Stage 1 Model-Deployment Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Deployment has stable identity.

2. Canonical Model and Version are explicit.

3. Package is explicit.

4. Runtime Deployment is explicit.

5. Node is explicit.

6. Quantisation is preserved.

7. Configuration is preserved.

8. Tested context limit is recorded.

9. Installed and loaded remain distinct.

10. Ready and healthy remain distinct.

11. Warm and cold state remain distinct.

12. Capacity is Deployment-specific.

13. Quality evidence is Deployment-specific.

14. Configuration change creates new attributable Version.

15. Historical Deployment remains queryable.

19.643 Stage 1 Placement Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Placement Policy has stable identity and Version.

2. Data Classification is evaluated.

3. Allowed Zones are enforced.

4. Prohibited Zones are enforced.

5. Node trust is evaluated.

6. Runtime health is evaluated.

7. Model or Tool eligibility is evaluated.

8. Capacity is evaluated.

9. Local Only request cannot route externally.

10. Preferred local request may use approved fallback only.

11. Placement Decision preserves alternatives.

12. Decision validity expires after trust change.

13. Long-running work can revalidate placement.

14. Placement is included in execution provenance.

15. Historical Decisions remain immutable.

19.644 Stage 1 Local-Scheduling Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Offline Node does not receive online-only work.

2. Node availability has freshness.

3. Insufficient memory blocks Model load.

4. Insufficient storage blocks large work.

5. Battery policy delays heavy work.

6. Thermal pressure reduces capacity.

7. Foreground user activity reduces background concurrency.

8. Model load time affects estimate.

9. Warm Model may be preferred.

10. Model swapping cost is considered.

11. Local queue survives restart.

12. Resource Lease prevents conflicting GPU use.

13. Expired Lease prevents stale worker mutation.

14. Interactive work receives governed priority.

15. Background work does not starve recovery.

text:
19.645 Stage 1 Sandbox Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Sandbox Profile has stable identity and Version.

2. File access is restricted.

3. Network access is restricted.

4. Process access is restricted.

5. Device access is restricted.

6. Memory and CPU are bounded.

7. Working directory is explicit.

8. Tool cannot access unrelated Project files.

9. Tool cannot access Secret Store without permission.

10. Read-only mode blocks mutation.

11. Networkless mode blocks egress.

12. Sandbox failure creates Incident.

13. Local execution does not inherit full user environment.

14. Sandbox configuration is preserved in provenance.

15. Historical Sandbox Profile remains queryable.

19.646 Stage 1 Local-Tool Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Tool Definition remains distinct from installation.

2. Tool Version is explicit.

3. Package provenance is explicit.

4. Required permissions are declared.

5. Side-effect class is explicit.

6. Project scope is enforced.

7. Working directory is enforced.

8. Structured arguments are used.

9. Raw shell concatenation is prohibited.

10. Output is bounded.

11. Exit code remains distinct from semantic success.

12. Tool logs exclude Secrets.

13. Tool update triggers conformance review.

14. Suspended Tool cannot execute.

15. Historical Tool executions remain queryable.

19.647 Stage 1 Local-Data Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Local Only data stays inside allowed Zones.

2. Temporary files inherit classification.

3. Prompt caches are Project-scoped.

4. Embeddings inherit source protection.

5. Vector index identifies source corpus.

6. Index identifies embedding Model.

7. Shared cache does not leak cross-Project data.

8. Local backups follow placement policy.

9. Cloud backup is detected as external storage.

10. Data transfer requires explicit destination.

11. Transfer checksum is verified.

12. Incomplete transfer does not become valid Input.

13. Deletion considers cache and backup.

14. Synchronisation preserves classification.

15. Historical data movement remains queryable.

19.648 Stage 1 Offline Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Offline Operation has stable identity.

2. Node is authorised for offline use.

3. Policy Snapshot is preserved.

4. Cached authority has expiry.

5. Required Model is installed.

6. Required data is local.

7. Required Tool is local.

8. External side effect is not claimed offline.

9. Local evidence is stored durably.

10. Device clock confidence is preserved.

11. Reconnection triggers synchronisation.

12. Duplicate sync does not duplicate state.

13. Stale policy work receives review where required.

14. Revocation gap is assessed.

15. Historical offline operation remains queryable.

text:
19.649 Stage 1 Synchronisation Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Synchronisation Record has stable identity.

2. Source and destination are explicit.

3. Object Versions are preserved.

4. Duplicate transfer is idempotent.

5. Older state does not overwrite newer state blindly.

6. Conflict is explicit.

7. Conflict policy is applied.

8. Protected data is encrypted.

9. Both Nodes authenticate.

10. Partial transfer remains incomplete.

11. Checksum verifies completion.

12. Backpressure is enforced.

13. Offline Events do not repeat external side effects.

14. Failed synchronisation can resume safely.

15. Historical synchronisation remains queryable.

19.650 Stage 1 Local-Receipt Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Receipt has stable identity.

2. Node is explicit.

3. Zone is explicit.

4. Runtime Version is explicit.

5. Model or Tool Deployment is explicit.

6. Placement Decision is explicit.

7. Policy Versions are explicit.

8. Start and end times are preserved.

9. Resource usage is preserved.

10. Usage confidence is explicit.

11. Outputs are linked.

12. Warnings are preserved.

13. Local does not become zero cost automatically.

14. Receipt synchronises without duplication.

15. Historical receipt remains immutable.

19.651 Stage 1 Security Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Local service is not publicly exposed by default.

2. Service authentication is enforced.

3. Default Credentials are removed.

4. Runtime does not run as unrestricted administrator.

5. Project file scope is enforced.

6. Secret environment variables are minimised.

7. Model package is scanned or validated.

8. Tool package provenance is checked.

9. Container image digest is preserved.

10. Mutable tag is not sole identity.

11. Telemetry egress follows policy.

12. Crash dumps are protected.

13. Disk encryption is required where policy defines it.

14. Compromised Node is isolated.

15. No local failure authorises external bypass.

19.652 Stage 1 Recovery Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Runtime crash preserves Execution state.

2. Node restart recovers local queue.

3. Model load failure does not corrupt package metadata.

4. Corrupt package is quarantined.

5. Storage failure creates Incident.

6. Lost device suspends Node.

7. Device Credentials are revoked.

8. Local Assets are restored from approved backup where available.

9. Recovered Node receives fresh validation.

10. Clean rebuild uses trusted sources.

11. Re-enrollment preserves or replaces identity correctly.

12. Revoked state is reapplied after restore.

13. Historical receipts survive recovery.

14. Recovery does not broaden Project access.

15. Normal placement resumes only after validation.

text:
19.653 Stage 1 Quality Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Local Model receives same Quality Floor as external resource.

2. Quantised variant receives separate evaluation.

3. Runtime update triggers regression test.

4. Structured output support is verified.

5. Tool-calling support is verified.

6. Swedish quality is evaluated.

7. Context limits are empirically tested.

8. Local privacy does not excuse poor quality.

9. Deployment quality is tied to exact configuration.

10. Behaviour drift is detectable.

11. Local success does not become acceptance automatically.

12. Evaluator identity is preserved.

13. Failed quality may trigger external fallback only when policy permits.

14. Local-only request cannot violate placement to improve quality.

15. Historical evaluations remain linked to Deployment.

19.654 Stage 1 Economic Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Local execution is not labelled universally free.

2. GPU time is measurable or estimated.

3. CPU time is measurable or estimated.

4. Energy estimate has confidence.

5. Cloud self-hosted idle cost is recorded.

6. Storage cost is attributable where applicable.

7. Model download cost is separate from inference.

8. Hardware purchase remains outside execution cost unless policy includes it.

9. Shared rig usage preserves Project attribution.

10. Local retry consumes resource budget.

11. Warm Model memory cost is visible.

12. External fallback requires Budget.

13. Cost comparison includes expected completion.

14. Missing local cost remains unknown.

15. Historical cost evidence remains queryable.

19.655 Applied Example — Local Ollama Text Resource

A local language Model is installed through an Ollama-like Runtime.

Canonical relationships are:

Runtime Node

represents the user’s workstation.

Runtime Deployment

represents the installed local Model service.

Local Model Package

represents the verified Model files and metadata.

Model Deployment

represents the exact Model, package, quantisation, Runtime, Node and configuration.

Connection

provides the governed invocation path.

Capability Mapping

declares verified support for:

- text generation,

- bounded reasoning,

- structured output where tested,

- and local-only processing.

The Runtime tag is preserved as an external identifier.

It does not replace canonical Model identity.

text:
19.656 Applied Example — NVIDIA-Backed Local Deployment

A private workstation has an NVIDIA-compatible GPU.

The Deployment record preserves:

- GPU model,

- accelerator memory,

- driver Version,

- Runtime Version,

- Model Package,

- precision,

- quantisation,

- context configuration,

- and tested concurrency.

A driver update triggers:

- health validation,

- representative benchmark,

- and behaviour regression review.

The Model identity remains unchanged.

The Deployment evidence changes.

19.657 Applied Example — Local Only Project Document

A Project document is classified Local Only.

The Planner creates Steps for:

- local extraction,

- local embedding,

- local retrieval,

- and local reasoning.

Placement Policy permits only approved local Nodes.

When the workstation is offline, the work may wait or execute locally.

When the workstation is unavailable, the Fabric does not send the document to an external Provider.

19.658 Applied Example — Local Preprocessing Before External Reasoning

A Project Internal document may use hybrid execution.

The local Tool:

1. extracts required sections.

2. removes prohibited personal fields.

3. creates a bounded summary.

4. validates redaction.

5. records provenance.

Only the approved derived summary enters the external reasoning Step.

The external Provider never receives the original document.

19.659 Applied Example — Omnira Code Audit

An Omnira repository audit uses:

- local repository Tool,

- local search,

- local reasoning Model,

- and read-only Sandbox.

The Tool may access only the exact repository path.

It cannot access:

- unrelated Projects,

- browser sessions,

- personal files,

- or Secret Stores.

A later modification Plan requires separate write authority.

19.660 Applied Example — GainPilot Local Content Drafting

GainPilot may use a local language Model for:

- exercise-description drafts,

- structured workout templates,

- and internal content variants.

External media generation may remain a separate Step.

Local drafting reduces Provider usage without making the local draft automatically publishable.

19.661 Applied Example — Familje-Stunden Local Composition

Familje-Stunden may use local media Tools to:

- resize accepted images,

- compose pages,

- combine audio,

- create previews,

- and export PDFs.

The Local Execution Receipt preserves:

- Tool Version,

- input Asset checksums,

- output checksums,

- Node,

- Project path,

- and operator or Service Principal.

Local composition does not bypass final child-facing review.

text:
19.662 Applied Example — The Prompt Private Research Archive

The Prompt may store internal research and source notes in a private local index.

Current web retrieval remains external.

The local index is used for:

- prior episode comparison,

- terminology,

- style guidance,

- and duplicate-topic detection.

The index does not replace current-source verification.

19.663 Applied Example — Private Home Server

A home server hosts:

- local Model Runtime,

- embeddings,

- Project vector stores,

- and Asset cache.

The server is:

- user-owned,

- locally operated,

- private-network scoped,

- disk-encrypted,

- and remotely accessible only through approved authentication.

Each Project uses separate:

- storage paths,

- indexes,

- queues,

- and permissions.

19.664 Applied Example — Laptop Unavailable

A Plan prefers the user’s laptop for private inference.

The laptop is offline.

The Placement system evaluates:

- another approved private Node,

- waiting for the laptop,

- or requesting permission for a dedicated remote private Node.

It shall not silently use a public external Provider.

19.665 Applied Example — Mobile Approval Node

A mobile device receives approval requests.

It does not host the video-generation Model.

The mobile Node identity proves the approval interface and user Session.

The Execution occurs on a separate private workstation or external Provider according to the approved Placement Decision.

19.666 Applied Example — Mobile Local Voice

A mobile device performs local speech recognition for an approval command.

The raw voice is processed on-device.

The derived command is sent to Omnira.

The raw recording is deleted according to policy.

Local voice processing does not grant automatic authority to execute the command.

19.667 Applied Example — Model Package Checksum Mismatch

A downloaded package claims to be an approved Model Version.

The checksum does not match the expected manifest.

The package is:

- quarantined,

- excluded from installation,

- recorded as integrity failure,

- and investigated.

The system shall not load it because the filename looks correct.

19.668 Applied Example — Unknown Runtime Tag

A local runtime reports a Model tag that is not in the Model Registry.

The resource is classified:

- discovered,

- unresolved identity,

- experimental,

- and ineligible for production.

An owner may later map and validate it.

sectionTitles: 19.673 Applied Example — Shared Private GPU Rig
19.674 Applied Example — Private Cloud GPU Node
text:
19.669 Applied Example — Quantised Variant

The same Base Model exists as:

- full precision,

- 8-bit,

- and 4-bit local packages.

Each Variant receives:

- separate package identity,

- memory profile,

- throughput evidence,

- and quality evaluation.

The Router may select the 4-bit Deployment for lightweight private drafting.

It may require the 8-bit Deployment for higher-quality analysis.

19.670 Applied Example — Runtime Update Regression

A Runtime update increases generation speed but breaks structured JSON output.

The Deployment health may remain technically active.

Its Capability Mapping for structured output becomes degraded or invalid.

Production structured-output work routes elsewhere until corrected.

19.671 Applied Example — Thermal Throttling

A laptop begins a long local inference batch.

Thermal state rises.

Effective throughput falls.

The Scheduler:

- reduces concurrency,

- updates completion estimate,

- protects interactive use,

- and may pause background work.

It shall not misclassify the Model as permanently failed.

19.672 Applied Example — Low Battery

A mobile or laptop Node is below the configured battery threshold.

Heavy background work is delayed.

Critical offline user work may proceed under explicit policy.

The system records the power-aware scheduling decision.

19.673 Applied Example — Shared Private GPU Rig

Familje-Stunden and GainPilot share one private GPU rig.

The Resource Pool enforces:

- Project queues,

- capacity Reservations,

- separate storage,

- separate local Assets,

- and usage attribution.

GainPilot background work shall not consume capacity reserved for a Familje-Stunden publication deadline.

19.674 Applied Example — Private Cloud GPU Node

A self-managed cloud GPU Node is created for temporary video or Model work.

The Plan includes:

- Budget Reservation,

- Node creation,

- enrollment,

- Runtime installation,

- package verification,

- execution,

- Asset retrieval,

- log collection,

- credential revocation,

- and Node destruction.

Idle billing stops only after verified termination.

19.675 Applied Example — Offline Code Analysis

A laptop disconnects from the network during a local code audit.

The audit continues using:

- cached policy,

- local repository,

- installed Model,

- and local Tools.

The local receipt remains pending synchronisation.

No external search Step is attempted until connectivity returns.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric

sectionTitles: 19.679 Applied Example — Local Vector Index Migration
text:
19.676 Applied Example — Offline Policy Drift

A local Job completes under Policy Version 4.

While offline, central policy advances to Version 5 and blocks the used Tool.

On reconnect, the Output remains evidence.

It does not become accepted automatically.

A policy-drift review determines whether it may be retained or used.

19.677 Applied Example — Device Loss

A laptop containing encrypted local Models and Project data is lost.

The Fabric:

1. marks the Node lost.

2. revokes Sessions and device Credentials.

3. blocks synchronisation.

4. identifies affected local Assets.

5. confirms disk-encryption evidence.

6. assesses backup state.

7. rotates exposed Credentials.

8. opens an Incident.

The user’s canonical identity and Project records remain intact.

19.678 Applied Example — Clean Node Rebuild

A Node is suspected compromised.

Rather than trusting partial cleanup, the operator:

- exports approved evidence,

- revokes credentials,

- wipes the Node,

- reinstalls the operating system,

- installs approved Runtimes,

- verifies Model packages,

- re-enrols the Node,

- and validates trust.

Production eligibility returns only after conformance.

19.679 Applied Example — Local Vector Index Migration

A Project changes its embedding Model.

The old index remains historically tied to the prior Model.

A new index Version is created through:

- source enumeration,

- rechunking where required,

- new embeddings,

- validation,

- and cutover.

The old and new vector spaces are not mixed blindly.

19.680 Applied Example — Air-Gapped Review Node

A sensitive review task runs on an air-gapped Node.

Inputs arrive through a signed Export Package.

The Node validates:

- manifest,

- checksums,

- classification,

- and operator.

Outputs leave through a governed package containing:

- result,

- provenance,

- checksums,

- and review evidence.

No network callback is expected.

19.681 Applied Example — Local Training Proposal

A Project proposes a private fine-tune using historical approved content.

Before training, the Fabric requires:

- dataset inventory,

- rights review,

- personal-data review,

- Base Model licence,

- compute estimate,

- evaluation plan,

- rollback,

- and owner approval.

The existence of spare GPU capacity does not authorise training.

Training requires rights, purpose and approval.

Training data requires identity, rights and classification.

19.746 Future Local and Private Architecture

Future versions may support:

- fully federated user-owned compute,

- secure cross-device orchestration,

- confidential Model execution,

- hardware-backed policy enforcement,

- dynamic private clusters,

- peer-to-peer Model distribution,

- encrypted inference,

- split learning,

- private multi-party computation,

- local Agent swarms,

- mobile on-device multimodal Models,

- energy-aware scheduling,

- and verified execution receipts.

Future evolution must preserve:

- canonical identity,

- Project isolation,

- placement policy,

- evidence,

- and user authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.747 Federated Personal Compute

A user may contribute several devices to one private resource pool.

Each device shall retain:

- identity,

- trust,

- capacity,

- and revocation.

19.748 Cross-Device Handoff

Interactive work may begin on mobile and continue on a workstation.

Context movement shall preserve:

- classification,

- consent,

- and provenance.

19.749 Secure Peer-to-Peer Transfer

Nodes may exchange Model packages or Assets directly using authenticated encrypted transfer.

19.750 Peer Package Verification

Peer delivery shall still verify canonical checksum and source provenance.

19.751 Confidential Inference

Future cryptographic or hardware techniques may reduce exposure during inference.

Actual performance and threat-model limits shall remain explicit.

19.752 Encrypted Model Weights

Encrypted weights may protect intellectual property at rest.

Runtime exposure and key release remain part of the threat model.

19.753 Hardware-Bound Model Licence

Some Models may require licensed hardware or keys.

The restriction shall remain explicit in Deployment eligibility.

19.754 Remote Private Worker

A remote private worker may execute bounded work without exposing general Node access.

19.755 Verifiable Execution

Future Nodes may produce signed evidence of:

- code,

- Model,

- configuration,

- Inputs,

- and result.

Signatures prove origin and integrity, not semantic correctness.

19.756 Private Capacity Exchange

Tenants may share unused private capacity under explicit agreements.

Ownership, data scope, cost and trust shall remain governed.

19.757 Local Agent Swarm

Several local Agents may coordinate on one private cluster.

Agent identities and authority remain separate from the Models serving them.

19.758 On-Device Multimodal Intelligence

Future mobile Models may support:

- voice,

- vision,

- text,

- and device context

without external transfer.

Device permissions remain Capability-specific.

19.759 Energy-Aware Placement

Work may be scheduled according to:

- battery,

- renewable availability,

- electricity price,

- heat,

- and deadline.

19.760 Carbon-Aware Private Compute

Carbon signals may influence flexible workload placement.

Privacy and user priority remain binding.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.761 Predictive Model Warmth

The Scheduler may predict which Models should remain loaded.

Prediction shall not override memory and user-experience limits.

19.762 Dynamic Quantisation Selection

The Fabric may select among verified quantised Variants according to:

- quality,

- latency,

- memory,

- and energy.

The selected Deployment remains explicit.

19.763 Local Quality Adaptation

The system may learn which local Deployments suit which tasks.

Learning shall remain evidence-based and scoped.

19.764 Private Model Marketplace

A future package catalogue may distribute verified private Models and Tools.

Installation shall not equal permission or production admission.

19.765 Remote Attested Node Admission

A Node may prove its configuration remotely before receiving protected work.

19.766 Local Success Criteria

The local and private architecture succeeds when:

- every Node has stable identity,

- every Runtime and Deployment is versioned,

- every Model Package has provenance,

- placement policy is enforced,

- Local Only data remains local,

- local resources are scheduled truthfully,

- Models and Tools are sandboxed,

- local quality is measured,

- offline work remains reconcilable,

- and private execution never bypasses canonical governance.

19.767 Local Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- local is assumed private,

- hostname becomes Node identity,

- runtime tag becomes Model identity,

- unverified packages enter production,

- local Tools receive unrestricted file or network access,

- Local Only data falls back externally,

- offline work has unlimited authority,

- local cost is represented as zero,

- or Node compromise cannot be contained.

19.768 Canonical Execution Zone Contract

The following requirements define canonical Execution Zones:

1. Every Execution Zone SHALL have stable identity.

2. Zone owner SHALL be explicit.

3. Zone operator SHALL be explicit.

4. Zone custody SHALL be explicit where material.

5. Zone location or region SHALL be explicit where required.

6. Network class SHALL be explicit.

7. Trust class SHALL be explicit.

8. Data-residency evidence SHALL be explicit.

9. Zone lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

10. Local, private, edge and self-hosted labels SHALL remain distinct.

11. Zone membership SHALL be versioned.

12. Compromised Zones SHALL be excluded from placement.

13. Shared Zones SHALL preserve Tenant and Project isolation.

14. External infrastructure dependencies SHALL remain visible.

15. Zone policy SHALL be versioned.

16. Zone changes SHALL be attributable.

17. Zone trust SHALL require evidence.

18. Retired Zones SHALL remain historically resolvable.

19. Historical Placement Decisions SHALL preserve Zone identity.

20. Zone location SHALL NOT create authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric

sectionTitles: 19.770 Canonical Node Enrollment and Trust Contract
text:
19.769 Canonical Runtime Node Contract

The following requirements define canonical Runtime Nodes:

1. Every Runtime Node SHALL have stable identity.

2. Node identity SHALL remain distinct from hostname and IP address.

3. Node owner SHALL be explicit.

4. Node operator SHALL be explicit.

5. Device Principal SHALL be explicit.

6. Execution Zone SHALL be explicit.

7. Environment SHALL be explicit.

8. Hardware Profile SHALL be explicit.

9. Network Profile SHALL be explicit.

10. Trust Profile SHALL be explicit.

11. Node lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

12. Node health SHALL include freshness.

13. Discovered Node SHALL NOT become active automatically.

14. Suspended, compromised, lost or retired Nodes SHALL NOT receive new work.

15. Shared Nodes SHALL preserve Tenant and Project isolation.

16. Node changes SHALL be attributable.

17. Re-enrollment SHALL preserve or replace identity explicitly.

18. Node retirement SHALL address Credentials and data.

19. Historical Node state SHALL remain queryable.

20. Node availability SHALL NOT create execution authority.

19.770 Canonical Node Enrollment and Trust Contract

The following requirements define Node enrollment and trust:

1. Every Enrollment SHALL have stable identity.

2. Enrollment SHALL verify owner or operator authority.

3. Enrollment SHALL verify the intended Node.

4. Bootstrap material SHALL be single-use or narrowly bounded.

5. Project and Tenant scope SHALL be explicit.

6. Environment SHALL be explicit.

7. Node trust requirements SHALL be explicit.

8. Attestation source and freshness SHALL be preserved.

9. Attestation SHALL NOT be treated as absolute trust.

10. Trust Profiles SHALL be versioned.

11. Unverified Nodes SHALL fail closed for sensitive work.

12. Trust downgrade SHALL affect placement promptly.

13. Compromise SHALL trigger suspension or isolation.

14. Device loss SHALL trigger Credential and Session review.

15. Recovered Nodes SHALL require fresh validation.

16. Ownership transfer SHALL require new governance.

17. Trust evidence SHALL remain queryable.

18. Historical Enrollment records SHALL remain immutable.

19. Enrollment SHALL NOT grant unrestricted Capability access.

20. Local location SHALL NOT substitute for trust.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.771 Canonical Runtime Contract

The following requirements define canonical Runtimes:

1. Every Runtime SHALL have stable identity.

2. Every Runtime release SHALL have explicit Version.

3. Runtime type SHALL be explicit.

4. Runtime Provider or maintainer SHALL be explicit.

5. Every Runtime Deployment SHALL have stable identity.

6. Deployment SHALL identify Node and Environment.

7. Endpoint SHALL be explicit.

8. Configuration SHALL be attributable.

9. Runtime lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

10. Installation SHALL verify package source and integrity.

11. Health SHALL remain distinct from Node health.

12. Runtime SHALL execute under bounded Service Principal.

13. Network and file access SHALL follow policy.

14. Updates SHALL use governed Plans.

15. Rollback SHALL preserve historical truth.

16. Failed Runtimes SHALL be excluded from placement.

17. Runtime removal SHALL consider active dependencies.

18. Historical Versions SHALL remain queryable.

19. Runtime SHALL NOT become Model identity.

20. Runtime availability SHALL NOT create authority.

19.772 Canonical Local Model Package Contract

The following requirements define canonical Local Model Packages:

1. Every admitted package SHALL have stable identity.

2. Package SHALL map to canonical Model and Version where known.

3. Package source SHALL be explicit.

4. Source revision SHALL be explicit.

5. File checksums SHALL be preserved.

6. Format SHALL be explicit.

7. Precision SHALL be explicit.

8. Quantisation SHALL be explicit.

9. Package licence SHALL be explicit.

10. Package provenance SHALL include transformations.

11. Filename or tag SHALL NOT become canonical identity.

12. Unverified packages SHALL remain quarantined.

13. Unsafe executable loading SHALL be prohibited.

14. Converted packages SHALL receive new provenance.

15. Fine-tuned packages SHALL preserve Base Model lineage.

16. Unknown licence SHALL block restricted production use.

17. Package admission SHALL require compatibility and security review.

18. Removed packages SHALL remain historically resolvable.

19. Package changes SHALL NOT rewrite historical Deployments.

20. Package availability SHALL NOT create authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.773 Canonical Local Model Deployment Contract

The following requirements define local Model Deployments:

1. Every Deployment SHALL have stable identity.

2. Deployment SHALL identify canonical Model and Version.

3. Deployment SHALL identify Local Model Package.

4. Deployment SHALL identify Runtime Deployment.

5. Deployment SHALL identify Runtime Node.

6. Configuration SHALL be explicit.

7. Precision and quantisation SHALL be explicit.

8. Hardware allocation SHALL be explicit.

9. Tested context limit SHALL be explicit.

10. Installed, loaded, warm and ready states SHALL remain distinct.

11. Deployment health SHALL include freshness.

12. Capacity SHALL be Deployment-specific.

13. Quality evidence SHALL be Deployment-specific.

14. Configuration changes affecting behaviour SHALL be versioned.

15. Runtime and driver drift SHALL trigger review.

16. Pinned execution SHALL preserve exact Deployment identity.

17. Replicated Deployments SHALL remain individually identifiable.

18. Removed Deployments SHALL be excluded from new routing.

19. Historical Deployment evidence SHALL remain queryable.

20. Local Deployment SHALL remain a resource, not an Agent identity.

19.774 Canonical Placement Contract

The following requirements define canonical placement:

1. Every reusable Placement Policy SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Policy SHALL identify scope.

3. Allowed Zones SHALL be explicit.

4. Prohibited Zones SHALL be explicit.

5. Required trust SHALL be explicit.

6. Data residency SHALL be explicit where material.

7. Network constraints SHALL be explicit.

8. Ownership constraints SHALL be explicit.

9. Fallback rules SHALL be explicit.

10. Every material Placement Decision SHALL have stable identity.

11. Decision SHALL identify Plan Version and Step.

12. Decision SHALL identify selected Zone and Node.

13. Decision SHALL identify Runtime and resource Deployment.

14. Policy Versions SHALL be preserved.

15. Local Only SHALL fail closed.

16. Placement SHALL be revalidated after material trust change.

17. Data movement SHALL require governed authority.

18. Placement SHALL remain separate from Model identity.

19. Historical Decisions SHALL remain immutable.

20. Placement SHALL NOT weaken classification silently.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
sectionTitles: 19.775 Canonical Local Tool and Sandbox Contract
text:
19.775 Canonical Local Tool and Sandbox Contract

The following requirements define local Tool execution:

1. Every Tool Package SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Package provenance SHALL be explicit.

3. Every Tool Installation SHALL have stable identity.

4. Every Tool Deployment SHALL identify Node and Environment.

5. Side-effect class SHALL be explicit.

6. Required permissions SHALL be explicit.

7. Project and Tenant scope SHALL be explicit.

8. Every Sandbox Profile SHALL have stable identity and Version.

9. File access SHALL be least privileged.

10. Network access SHALL be least privileged.

11. Process and device access SHALL be least privileged.

12. Secret access SHALL be denied unless explicitly required.

13. Shell invocation SHALL use structured arguments.

14. Working directory SHALL be explicit.

15. Read-only policy SHALL block mutation.

16. Sandbox failure SHALL create Incident.

17. Tool updates SHALL trigger conformance review.

18. Suspended Tools SHALL NOT execute.

19. Historical Tool executions SHALL remain queryable.

20. Local Tool possession SHALL NOT create authority.

19.776 Canonical Offline Operation Contract

The following requirements define offline execution:

1. Every Offline Operation SHALL have stable identity.

2. Node and Project SHALL be explicit.

3. Cached authority SHALL be explicitly valid for offline use.

4. Policy Snapshot Version SHALL be preserved.

5. Offline Credential scope and expiry SHALL be explicit.

6. Required Models and Tools SHALL be installed before work.

7. Required data SHALL be locally available.

8. External side effects SHALL NOT be claimed without external verification.

9. Offline evidence SHALL be stored durably.

10. Device time confidence SHALL be preserved.

11. Offline completion MAY remain provisional.

12. Reconnection SHALL trigger synchronisation.

13. Revocation gaps SHALL be assessed.

14. Stale-policy work SHALL receive review where required.

15. Duplicate synchronisation SHALL be idempotent.

16. Conflicts SHALL remain explicit.

17. Offline authority SHALL be bounded in duration and scope.

18. Historical Offline Operations SHALL remain queryable.

19. Offline state SHALL NOT erase central canonical authority.

20. Lack of network SHALL NOT create broader permission.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
sectionTitles: 19.778 Canonical Local Data and Storage Contract
text:
19.777 Canonical Synchronisation Contract

The following requirements define local synchronisation:

1. Every material Synchronisation Record SHALL have stable identity.

2. Source and destination SHALL be explicit.

3. Object identity and Version SHALL be preserved.

4. Both endpoints SHALL authenticate.

5. Data Classification SHALL be preserved.

6. Protected transfers SHALL be encrypted.

7. Transfer integrity SHALL be verified.

8. Partial transfer SHALL remain incomplete.

9. Duplicate transfer SHALL be idempotent.

10. Ordering and checkpoints SHALL be explicit.

11. Older state SHALL NOT overwrite newer state blindly.

12. Conflicts SHALL be explicit.

13. Resolution policy SHALL be versioned.

14. Offline Events SHALL NOT duplicate external side effects.

15. Revocations SHALL be applied on reconnection.

16. Synchronisation SHALL respect backpressure.

17. Failed transfer SHALL support safe resume where practical.

18. Synchronisation evidence SHALL remain attributable.

19. Historical records SHALL remain queryable.

20. Synchronisation SHALL NOT weaken Project or Tenant isolation.

19.778 Canonical Local Data and Storage Contract

The following requirements define local data governance:

1. Every governed Storage Volume SHALL have stable identity.

2. Owner and Project scope SHALL be explicit.

3. Encryption state SHALL be explicit.

4. Capacity and health SHALL be observable.

5. Local Asset Stores SHALL preserve Asset identity and provenance.

6. Temporary files SHALL inherit classification.

7. Caches SHALL be Tenant- and Project-scoped.

8. Prompt caches SHALL remain protected.

9. Embeddings SHALL inherit source-data protection.

10. Vector indexes SHALL identify source corpus and embedding Model.

11. Backups SHALL follow Placement Policy.

12. Cloud backup SHALL be treated as external storage.

13. Data transfer SHALL require explicit destination.

14. Checksums SHOULD verify movement and storage integrity.

15. Deletion SHALL consider caches, backups and snapshots.

16. Crash dumps and swap SHALL be protected.

17. Shared storage SHALL enforce isolation.

18. Historical data movement SHALL remain queryable.

19. Local storage SHALL NOT imply Local Only compliance automatically.

20. Storage availability SHALL NOT create data-processing authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.779 Canonical Local Execution Receipt Contract

The following requirements define local execution evidence:

1. Every Local Execution Receipt SHALL have stable identity.

2. Receipt SHALL identify Node.

3. Receipt SHALL identify Execution Zone.

4. Receipt SHALL identify Runtime Deployment.

5. Receipt SHALL identify Model or Tool Deployment.

6. Receipt SHALL identify Execution and Attempt.

7. Receipt SHALL identify Placement Decision.

8. Receipt SHALL identify policy Versions.

9. Start and end times SHALL be preserved.

10. Resource usage SHALL be preserved where measurable.

11. Usage confidence SHALL be explicit.

12. Outputs and Assets SHALL remain linked.

13. Warnings and degradation SHALL remain visible.

14. Local execution SHALL NOT be represented as universally free.

15. Receipt SHALL preserve offline or synchronisation state.

16. Receipt SHALL NOT expose raw Secrets.

17. Duplicate synchronisation SHALL NOT duplicate the receipt.

18. Historical receipts SHALL remain immutable.

19. Receipts SHALL support quality and cost evaluation.

20. Local execution SHALL remain as auditable as external execution.

19.780 Canonical Local Security Contract

The following requirements define local security:

1. Local Nodes SHALL use stable Device or Service identity.

2. Network location SHALL NOT replace authentication.

3. Protected Nodes SHOULD use encrypted storage.

4. Unsupported operating systems SHALL be restricted.

5. Administrative privilege SHALL be minimised.

6. Default Credentials SHALL be removed.

7. Local services SHALL NOT be publicly exposed by default.

8. File access SHALL be Project-scoped.

9. Network egress SHALL be explicit.

10. Tools SHALL run in approved Sandboxes.

11. Runtimes SHALL NOT inherit unrelated Secrets.

12. Package provenance and integrity SHALL be verified.

13. Mutable package tags SHALL NOT be sole identity.

14. Telemetry and update traffic SHALL follow policy.

15. Crash dumps and temporary memory artefacts SHALL be protected.

16. Trust state SHALL include freshness.

17. Compromised Nodes SHALL be isolated promptly.

18. Lost devices SHALL trigger Credential and Session response.

19. Recovery SHALL use trusted sources.

20. Local execution failure SHALL NOT authorise governance bypass.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.781 Canonical Local Governance Contract

The following requirements define overall local and private governance:

1. Local, private, edge, offline and self-hosted SHALL remain distinct concepts.

2. Every execution location SHALL be represented through a governed Zone.

3. Every Node SHALL have stable identity.

4. Every Runtime, Model and Tool Deployment SHALL be versioned.

5. Every Model Package SHALL have provenance.

6. Placement Policy SHALL govern data and work location.

7. Local Only SHALL fail closed.

8. Local execution SHALL remain subject to authority and approval.

9. Local execution SHALL remain subject to Quality Contracts.

10. Local usage and cost SHALL remain visible.

11. Nodes and resources SHALL use least privilege.

12. Local Models and Tools SHALL NOT receive raw Secrets.

13. Offline work SHALL use bounded cached authority.

14. Synchronisation SHALL preserve identity and conflicts.

15. Shared private resources SHALL preserve Tenant and Project isolation.

16. Updates and drift SHALL be governed.

17. Compromise and loss SHALL be containable.

18. Historical local execution truth SHALL remain reconstructable.

19. No local infrastructure failure SHALL authorise external bypass.

20. User custody SHALL coexist with Omnira governance.

19.782 Local and Private Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No local label becomes proof of privacy.

- No private label becomes proof of security.

- No self-hosted label becomes proof of ownership.

- No hostname, path or runtime tag becomes canonical identity.

- No downloaded Model package becomes production-ready automatically.

- No quantisation or fine-tune remains hidden.

- No local Node receives sensitive work without sufficient trust.

- No installed Model becomes ready without validation.

- No local Tool receives unrestricted file, network or Secret access.

- No Local Only request falls back externally.

- No offline operation receives unlimited authority.

- No synchronisation overwrites conflicts silently.

- No local execution is represented as universally free.

- No local privacy advantage removes Quality evaluation.

- No Node health replaces Runtime or Deployment health.

- No mutable package tag replaces exact Version evidence.

- No shared private pool loses Project attribution.

- No lost or compromised Node remains eligible.

- No restored backup reactivates revoked Credentials blindly.

- No local failure bypasses the Intelligence Fabric.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Local, Private, Edge and Self-Hosted Intelligence
text:
19.783 Closing Statement

Local, private, edge and self-hosted intelligence allow Omnira to use compute that is closer to the user, more private, more controllable and less dependent on external managed Providers.

Those benefits exist only when the local boundary is represented truthfully.

The Execution Zone defines where work may occur.

The Placement Policy defines where it is permitted to occur.

The Runtime Node defines the machine or virtual environment.

The Node Trust Profile defines what may be trusted about it.

The Runtime Deployment defines the software that executes work.

The Local Model Package defines the verified Model artefacts.

The Model Deployment defines the exact Model, package, Runtime, Node and configuration.

The Tool Deployment defines the local operation and its permissions.

The Sandbox limits access.

The Scheduler allocates bounded capacity.

The Resource Lease protects ownership of scarce hardware.

The Local Execution Receipt preserves what happened.

The Synchronisation Record reconciles offline and connected state.

The Quality system determines whether the Output is acceptable.

The Cost system preserves the real economic impact.

The Incident system handles compromise, loss and failure.

For Familje-Stunden, this architecture allows:

- local page composition,

- local media processing,

- private storage of Nova and Pling Assets,

- local review tools,

- and private drafting

without exposing Project data unnecessarily or bypassing final quality review.

For The Prompt, it allows:

- private archives,

- local semantic search,

- local script drafting,

- and local media processing

while preserving the need for current external source verification.

For GainPilot, it allows:

- local structured content generation,

- economical batch drafting,

- private user-data analysis,

- and local embeddings

without turning private health and training data into shared Provider context.

For Omnira, it allows:

- laptops,

- workstations,

- mobile devices,

- private GPU rigs,

- home servers,

- dedicated hosted Nodes,

- self-managed cloud infrastructure,

- local Model runtimes,

- private Tools,

- offline work,

- and future federated devices

to participate in one governed Intelligence Fabric.

The hardware may belong to the user.

The Runtime may be open source.

The Model may be downloaded.

The Node may be offline.

The data may remain private.

The execution must still have identity, authority, policy, evidence and quality.

No local execution without a Node.

No Node without identity.

No private placement without policy.

No Model Deployment without package provenance.

No Tool without bounded permissions.

No offline work without expiring authority.
