No synchronisation without conflict handling.

No Local Only fallback to external processing.

No private claim without evidence.

No self-hosting without operational responsibility.

The user retains custody.

The Project retains isolation.

Omnira retains governance.

The Fabric brings intelligence closer to the user without allowing proximity to replace trust.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical architecture, governance model, object model, lifecycle, planning semantics, quality boundaries and conformance requirements for multimodal production within the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

It establishes:

- how text, image, audio, voice, music, video, animation, document and interactive media production coexist,

- how multimodal production remains Capability-driven and Provider-independent,

- how creative intent is translated into structured Production Specifications,

- how canonical Assets, references, characters, Voices, styles, scenes, timelines and compositions are represented,

- how generation, transformation, editing, assembly, rendering, review and publication remain distinct operations,

- how multimodal Plans become explicit Production Graphs,

- how reference Assets guide identity, style, composition and continuity,

- how character and visual identity remain stable across generated outputs,

- how voice identity, pronunciation, timing and consent remain governed,

- how image, video, audio and document variants are generated and compared,

- how asynchronous Provider jobs and local processing coexist,

- how intermediate Outputs remain distinct from accepted Assets,

- how deterministic and stochastic stages are represented,

- how creative iteration remains bounded by Budget, quality and approval,

- how multimodal quality is evaluated through modality-specific and cross-modal criteria,

- how continuity is maintained across scenes, pages, episodes, campaigns and Projects,

- how technical specifications such as dimensions, duration, codecs, loudness, frame rate and file formats are enforced,

- how rights, licences, attribution, consent and provenance remain attached throughout production,

- how child-facing, public-facing and brand-sensitive content receives stronger review,

- how local, private and external resources are combined without hidden data movement,

- how publication packages are assembled without bypassing final approval,

- how failed or partial media jobs are recovered,

- how multimodal production integrates with Assets, Registries, Scheduling, Cost, Quality, Memory and the Intelligence Graph,

- and how Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy multimodal production foundation.

A generated Output is not automatically an Asset.

An Asset is not automatically approved.

A reference image is not automatically consent.

A Provider preset is not automatically a canonical style.

A character name is not automatically character identity.

A Voice ID is not automatically voice ownership.

A successful render is not automatically production completion.

A technically valid file is not automatically creatively acceptable.

A scene that looks correct in isolation is not automatically continuous with the surrounding work.

A Provider project or workspace is not automatically the canonical Production Project.

A multimodal pipeline shall not hide which steps were human-assisted.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

Asset rights, provenance, consent and ownership are expanded in Chapter 21.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text: Implementation and conformance must be verified separately.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.2 Purpose of Multimodal Production Architecture

Omnira Projects may produce:

- written content,

- structured data,

- illustrations,

- photographs,

- diagrams,

- voice narration,

- sound effects,

- music,

- video,

- animation,

- social-media clips,

- printable documents,

- ebooks,

- web graphics,

- application Assets,

- and composite publication packages.

These Outputs often require several intelligence and Tool resources.

A single finished video may require:

- script generation,

- factual review,

- scene planning,

- image generation,

- image selection,

- character consistency review,

- animation,

- voice synthesis,

- audio cleaning,

- music selection,

- subtitle generation,

- composition,

- rendering,

- quality review,

- and publication packaging.

Without a canonical multimodal architecture, each Project would become dependent on:

- one Provider’s workspace model,

- one editor’s file naming,

- one Tool’s timeline format,

- one image generator’s prompt language,

- or one person’s memory of prior creative decisions.

The architecture exists to make multimodal production:

- repeatable,

- explainable,

- Provider-independent,

- quality-governed,

- rights-aware,

- recoverable,

- and suitable for increasing automation.

20.3 Multimodal Production

Multimodal Production is the governed process of creating, transforming, combining, evaluating and delivering Outputs involving one or more media modalities.

It may contain:

- one modality,

- several coordinated modalities,

- or a composite deliverable.

20.4 Modality

A Modality is a canonical category of content representation.

Canonical modalities may include:

- text,

- structured data,

- code,

- image,

- document,

- audio,

- voice,

- music,

- video,

- animation,

- three-dimensional content,

- interactive content,

- and mixed media.

20.5 Primary Modality

The Primary Modality is the dominant form of the final deliverable.

Examples include:

- video for a reel,

- document for a printable activity,

- image for a social post,

- audio for a narrated story,

- or interactive media for an application experience.

20.6 Supporting Modality

A Supporting Modality contributes to the final deliverable.

Examples include:

- script supporting video,

- narration supporting animation,

- subtitles supporting audio,

- reference images supporting image generation,

- or metadata supporting publication.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 20.11 Production Project Is Not Provider Workspace
text:
20.7 Composite Deliverable

A Composite Deliverable contains several coordinated Assets.

Examples include:

- video plus thumbnail plus caption,

- PDF plus cover image plus preview images,

- audio story plus transcript plus chapter markers,

- social campaign package,

- or application media bundle.

20.8 Production Project

A Production Project is a governed creative-production context within an Omnira Project.

It may represent:

- one book,

- one episode,

- one campaign,

- one monthly theme,

- one video series,

- one application release,

- or one publication package.

20.9 Production Project Identity

Every persistent Production Project shall have stable canonical identity.

20.10 Production Project Scope

A Production Project shall identify:

- Tenant,

- Omnira Project,

- owner,

- audience,

- purpose,

- brand or creative system,

- deliverables,

- schedule,

- Budget,

- rights context,

- and lifecycle.

20.11 Production Project Is Not Provider Workspace

A Provider workspace may support execution.

It shall not replace the canonical Production Project.

20.12 Production Unit

A Production Unit is one bounded creative item inside a Production Project.

Examples include:

- scene,

- page,

- exercise animation,

- reel,

- audio chapter,

- thumbnail,

- or publication post.

20.13 Production Unit Identity

Every governed Production Unit shall have stable identity.

20.14 Production Batch

A Production Batch groups several compatible Production Units for coordinated execution.

Batching may improve:

- consistency,

- cost,

- throughput,

- Model warmth,

- and review efficiency.

20.15 Batch Identity

Every material Production Batch shall have stable identity.

20.16 Production Version

A Production Version is one immutable material state of a Production Unit or Deliverable.

Material changes shall create a new Version.

20.17 Draft

A Draft is an incomplete or unaccepted Production Version.

20.18 Candidate

A Candidate is a Production Version eligible for comparison or review.

20.19 Selected Candidate

A Selected Candidate has been chosen for further production.

Selection does not automatically mean final acceptance.

20.20 Accepted Version

An Accepted Version satisfies the applicable Quality and Approval Contracts.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.21 Final Version

A Final Version is the accepted version designated for delivery or publication.

Final does not mean immutable forever.

Corrections require a new Version.

20.22 Canonical Production Objects

The canonical multimodal object model should include or reference:

- Production Project,

- Production Unit,

- Production Batch,

- Production Specification,

- Creative Brief,

- Audience Profile,

- Brand System,

- Style System,

- Character Definition,

- Character Version,

- Character Reference Set,

- Voice Definition,

- Voice Version,

- Pronunciation Profile,

- Scene Definition,

- Shot Definition,

- Page Definition,

- Timeline,

- Track,

- Segment,

- Composition,

- Layout,

- Prompt Specification,

- Negative Constraint,

- Generation Request,

- Transformation Request,

- Edit Request,

- Render Request,

- Variant Set,

- Candidate,

- Selection Decision,

- Continuity Record,

- Technical Specification,

- Publication Package,

- Production Receipt,

- and Production Incident.

20.23 Production Specification

A Production Specification defines what shall be created and the constraints governing production.

It shall include or reference:

- productionSpecificationId,

- Production Project,

- Production Unit,

- purpose,

- audience,

- Primary Modality,

- Supporting Modalities,

- creative requirements,

- technical requirements,

- brand requirements,

- character requirements,

- rights requirements,

- quality requirements,

- Budget,

- schedule,

- approval,

- and Version.

20.24 Production Specification Identity

Every Production Specification shall have stable identity and Version.

20.25 Specification Immutability

A dispatched Production Specification Version shall remain immutable.

Changes require a new Version.

20.26 Creative Brief

A Creative Brief expresses the intended communication, emotional tone and creative outcome.

It may include:

- message,

- audience,

- mood,

- narrative,

- visual direction,

- voice direction,

- pacing,

- references,

- prohibited elements,

- and desired response.

20.27 Creative Brief Identity

Every persistent Creative Brief shall have stable identity and Version.

20.28 Brief Versus Prompt

A Creative Brief describes canonical creative intent.

A Provider prompt is one implementation-specific instruction derived from that Brief.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.29 Brief Versus Script

A Brief defines intent.

A Script defines exact or provisional spoken or written content.

20.30 Brief Versus Style System

A Brief may reference an existing Style System.

It does not redefine the entire style unless explicitly Versioned.

20.31 Audience Profile

An Audience Profile describes intended consumers of the content.

It may include:

- age group,

- language,

- literacy,

- cultural context,

- accessibility needs,

- platform,

- and sensitivity.

20.32 Audience Profile Identity

Every reusable Audience Profile shall have stable identity and Version.

20.33 Child-Facing Audience

Child-facing production requires stronger controls for:

- safety,

- age appropriateness,

- clarity,

- privacy,

- emotional tone,

- and advertising boundaries.

20.34 Public Audience

Public-facing content requires review for:

- factual accuracy,

- rights,

- brand,

- privacy,

- and reputational consequence.

20.35 Internal Audience

Internal content may still contain confidential or strategic data.

Internal status does not remove rights or Quality requirements.

20.36 Brand System

A Brand System defines stable identity elements for one Project, product or organisation.

It may include:

- name,

- logo,

- colours,

- typography,

- visual motifs,

- tone,

- terminology,

- iconography,

- and prohibited uses.

20.37 Brand System Identity

Every Brand System shall have stable identity and Version.

20.38 Brand Asset

A Brand Asset is a governed Asset such as:

- logo,

- wordmark,

- icon,

- template,

- type treatment,

- or background system.

20.39 Brand Rule

A Brand Rule defines one enforceable brand requirement.

Examples include:

- minimum logo clearance,

- approved colour palette,

- title placement,

- or prohibited distortion.

20.40 Brand Drift

Brand Drift occurs when generated or edited Outputs deviate from the approved Brand System.

20.41 Style System

A Style System defines reusable creative characteristics beyond brand identity.

It may include:

- illustration style,

- realism level,

- line quality,

- lighting,

- colour treatment,

- texture,

- camera language,

- animation behaviour,

- audio mood,

- and compositional rules.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.42 Style System Identity

Every Style System shall have stable identity and Version.

20.43 Style Reference Set

A Style Reference Set contains approved Assets demonstrating the desired style.

20.44 Style Description

A textual Style Description may support generation.

It shall not replace visual evidence when visual consistency is required.

20.45 Provider Style Preset

A Provider preset is implementation-specific.

It may map to a Style System but shall not become canonical style identity.

20.46 Style Strength

A generation request may specify how strongly references or style constraints should influence the Output.

The semantics are Provider-specific and require mapping.

20.47 Style Drift

Style Drift shall be evaluated across:

- colour,

- line,

- texture,

- composition,

- lighting,

- and narrative tone.

20.48 Character Definition

A Character Definition represents a stable fictional, branded or production-specific character identity.

It shall include or reference:

- characterId,

- name,

- role,

- owner,

- visual traits,

- proportions,

- clothing rules,

- colour rules,

- personality,

- voice relationship,

- prohibited changes,

- reference Assets,

- rights,

- and lifecycle.

20.49 Character Identity

Every governed Character shall have stable canonical identity.

20.50 Character Version

Material changes to character design shall create a Character Version.

20.51 Character Design Canon

Character Design Canon defines the approved visual truth for one Character Version.

20.52 Character Reference Set

A Character Reference Set contains approved Assets showing:

- front,

- side,

- back,

- expressions,

- poses,

- clothing,

- scale,

- and contextual use.

20.53 Character Sheet

A Character Sheet is one composite reference Asset presenting canonical traits.

20.54 Character Trait

Character traits may include:

- body proportions,

- face shape,

- eye design,

- hair,

- skin or material,

- clothing,

- accessories,

- and distinctive marks.

20.55 Character Proportion

Relative proportions shall remain stable where identity continuity is required.

20.56 Character Clothing Rule

Clothing may be:

- fixed,

- context-dependent,

- seasonal,

- scene-specific,

- or freely variable within constraints.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.57 Character Accessory

Accessories may be identity-critical or optional.

The distinction shall be explicit.

20.58 Character Expression Set

Approved expressions may support consistent emotional depiction.

20.59 Character Pose Set

Approved poses may guide:

- generation,

- animation,

- and continuity.

20.60 Character Scale Relationship

Relative scale between several Characters shall be explicit where relevant.

20.61 Character Identity Preservation

Identity preservation shall be evaluated across:

- face,

- silhouette,

- proportions,

- colour,

- clothing,

- accessories,

- and behaviour.

20.62 Multi-Character Scene

A Multi-Character Scene contains two or more governed Characters.

Capability support for multiple reference identities shall be verified.

20.63 Character Occlusion

Partial visibility shall not justify unverified identity where the scene depends on character recognition.

20.64 Character Variation

Permitted variation shall be defined.

Examples include:

- clothing for weather,

- pose,

- facial expression,

- lighting,

- or age-appropriate activity.

20.65 Prohibited Character Variation

Prohibited changes may include:

- altered species,

- wrong age,

- missing identity features,

- unsafe clothing,

- or inconsistent body form.

20.66 Character Drift Record

A Character Drift Record documents deviations detected during evaluation.

20.67 Nova and Pling

Nova and Pling may be represented as canonical Character Definitions for Familje-Stunden production.

Their reference Assets, proportions, clothing and interaction rules shall remain Versioned.

Their names alone are insufficient production references.

20.68 Character Is Not Agent

A fictional or visual Character is not an Omnira Agent identity unless separately defined as an operational Agent.

Nova and Pling are creative identities unless an approved architecture establishes otherwise.

20.69 Voice Definition

A Voice Definition represents a stable Voice identity or approved synthetic Voice profile.

It shall include or reference:

- voiceId,

- name,

- owner,

- language,

- accent,

- age impression,

- tone,

- range,

- reference,

- Consent,

- rights,

- Provider mappings,

- and lifecycle.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.70 Voice Identity

Every governed Voice shall have stable canonical identity.

20.71 Voice Version

Material changes in Voice source, style or approved configuration shall create a Voice Version.

20.72 Synthetic Voice

A Synthetic Voice may be:

- Provider stock Voice,

- custom generated Voice,

- cloned Voice,

- locally generated Voice,

- or transformed Voice.

20.73 Stock Voice

A stock Provider Voice shall remain linked to:

- Provider,

- Voice ID,

- licence,

- and available Models.

20.74 Custom Voice

A custom Voice requires stronger:

- ownership,

- Consent,

- source,

- and deletion governance.

20.75 Voice Clone

A Voice Clone shall not be produced or used without explicit verified authority and Consent.

20.76 Voice Mapping

One canonical Voice may map to different Provider implementations only when acceptable identity continuity is verified.

20.77 Voice Provider ID

A Provider Voice ID is an external identifier.

It shall not replace canonical Voice identity.

20.78 Voice Characteristics

Voice characteristics may include:

- timbre,

- pitch,

- pace,

- energy,

- warmth,

- articulation,

- and emotional range.

20.79 Voice Style

Voice Style defines one performance mode such as:

- calm narration,

- energetic advertisement,

- educational explanation,

- bedtime story,

- or character dialogue.

20.80 Voice Consistency

Voice consistency shall be evaluated across:

- scenes,

- chapters,

- episodes,

- and production dates.

20.81 Pronunciation Profile

A Pronunciation Profile defines approved pronunciation for:

- names,

- brands,

- abbreviations,

- specialist terms,

- foreign words,

- and invented language.

20.82 Pronunciation Profile Identity

Every reusable Pronunciation Profile shall have stable identity and Version.

20.83 Phonetic Guidance

Phonetic guidance may be Provider-specific.

The canonical intended pronunciation shall remain Provider-independent.

20.84 Voice Timing

Voice timing includes:

- pauses,

- emphasis,

- sentence pacing,

- segment timing,

- and synchronisation with visuals.

20.85 Voice Performance Direction

Performance direction may specify:

- emotion,

- intensity,

- tempo,

- audience relationship,

- and prohibited delivery styles.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.86 Voice Output

A Voice Output is generated audio associated with one Voice Definition and one text or performance Specification.

20.87 Voice Acceptance

Voice acceptance may require:

- correct identity,

- intelligibility,

- pronunciation,

- emotional fit,

- audio Quality,

- Consent,

- and rights.

20.88 Music Definition

A Music Definition represents a governed musical identity or production requirement.

It may include:

- mood,

- tempo,

- instrumentation,

- structure,

- duration,

- rights,

- and intended use.

20.89 Music Asset

A Music Asset may be:

- original,

- generated,

- licensed,

- stock,

- commissioned,

- or public-domain.

20.90 Music Rights

Music use shall preserve:

- licence,

- attribution,

- territory,

- platform,

- commercial use,

- and expiry where applicable.

20.91 Sound Effect

A Sound Effect is a bounded audio Asset used to support action, transition or atmosphere.

20.92 Audio Bed

An Audio Bed is continuous background sound or music placed beneath narration or dialogue.

20.93 Loudness

Audio loudness targets shall be specified for the intended platform and deliverable.

20.94 Peak Level

Peak limits shall prevent clipping and distortion.

20.95 Noise Floor

Noise and artefacts shall be evaluated when Voice or recording Quality matters.

20.96 Audio Ducking

Audio Ducking reduces background audio beneath speech.

The rule shall be explicit in composition.

20.97 Text Asset

A Text Asset may contain:

- script,

- caption,

- title,

- description,

- transcript,

- subtitle,

- label,

- or body copy.

20.98 Script

A Script defines exact or provisional spoken, displayed or narrated content.

20.99 Script Identity

Every governed Script shall have stable identity and Version.

20.100 Script Structure

A Script may include:

- scenes,

- dialogue,

- narration,

- action,

- visual notes,

- timing,

- and pronunciation guidance.

20.101 Script Approval

A Script may require factual, editorial, legal or child-safety approval before production.

20.102 Caption

A Caption is text accompanying a publication or media Asset.

20.103 Subtitle

A Subtitle is time-aligned text corresponding to spoken or meaningful audio content.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.104 Subtitle Track

A Subtitle Track shall preserve:

- language,

- timing,

- text,

- style,

- and Version.

20.105 Transcript

A Transcript is a textual representation of spoken audio.

It may be:

- source-authored,

- generated from speech,

- or corrected.

20.106 On-Screen Text

On-screen text shall be represented separately from spoken narration where they differ.

20.107 Text Accuracy

Text rendered into images or video shall be verified visually.

Provider text generation inside imagery may be unreliable.

20.108 Image Definition

An Image Definition describes one intended still visual.

It may include:

- subject,

- scene,

- composition,

- style,

- characters,

- camera,

- lighting,

- dimensions,

- text,

- background,

- and negative constraints.

20.109 Image Identity

Every accepted image Asset shall have stable identity.

20.110 Image Variant

A Variant is one generated or edited alternative for the same Image Definition.

20.111 Image Generation

Image Generation creates a new image from:

- text,

- reference images,

- masks,

- structure,

- or combinations.

20.112 Image Transformation

Image Transformation modifies an existing image while preserving defined elements.

20.113 Image Editing

Image Editing applies bounded changes such as:

- remove object,

- replace background,

- adjust clothing,

- correct anatomy,

- extend canvas,

- or add approved text.

20.114 Inpainting

Inpainting changes a selected region while preserving the rest where possible.

20.115 Outpainting

Outpainting extends the image beyond its existing boundaries.

20.116 Background Removal

Background removal produces transparency or a separated subject.

Edge Quality shall be evaluated.

20.117 Upscaling

Upscaling increases image resolution.

It may introduce invented details and requires evaluation.

20.118 Image Restoration

Restoration may repair:

- damage,

- compression,

- blur,

- colour,

- or missing regions.

Restoration shall not be represented as exact recovery when information is invented.

20.119 Image Composition

Image Composition combines several Assets or generated elements into one image.

20.120 Image Layout

Layout defines relative placement of:

- image,

- text,

- logo,

- margins,

- and decorative elements.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.121 Aspect Ratio

Aspect ratio shall be specified independently from absolute dimensions.

20.122 Image Dimensions

Dimensions shall identify width and height in pixels or another relevant unit.

20.123 Resolution

Resolution may refer to pixel count, print density or effective detail.

The meaning shall be explicit.

20.124 Colour Space

Colour space may include:

- sRGB,

- Display P3,

- CMYK,

- or another defined profile.

20.125 Alpha Channel

Transparency requirements shall be explicit.

20.126 Image Format

Formats may include:

- PNG,

- JPEG,

- WebP,

- TIFF,

- SVG,

- PDF,

- or Provider-specific intermediate form.

20.127 Lossless Image Format

Lossless formats should be used when repeated editing or transparency requires them.

20.128 Lossy Image Format

Lossy compression shall remain within approved Quality bounds.

20.129 Print Image

Print images require appropriate:

- dimensions,

- resolution,

- colour,

- bleed,

- and safe area.

20.130 Web Image

Web images may prioritise:

- responsive dimensions,

- compression,

- loading performance,

- and colour consistency.

20.131 Image Accessibility

Meaningful images may require:

- alt text,

- descriptive caption,

- or surrounding context.

20.132 Video Definition

A Video Definition describes one intended moving-image deliverable or Scene.

It may include:

- narrative purpose,

- duration,

- shots,

- characters,

- camera,

- movement,

- style,

- audio,

- text,

- format,

- and platform.

20.133 Video Identity

Every accepted Video Asset shall have stable identity.

20.134 Video Generation

Video Generation creates moving imagery from:

- text,

- image,

- video reference,

- motion reference,

- or combinations.

20.135 Image-to-Video

Image-to-Video animates one or more source images.

It shall preserve reference identity according to the Capability Contract.

20.136 Text-to-Video

Text-to-Video generates scenes directly from textual direction.

It may provide weaker identity continuity than reference-based generation.

20.137 Video-to-Video

Video-to-Video transforms existing motion or footage while preserving defined structure.

20.138 Animation

Animation is deliberate temporal change in visual elements.

It may be:

- frame-based,

- skeletal,

- procedural,

- generated,

- motion-graphic,

- or composite.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.139 Motion Graphic

Motion graphics animate:

- text,

- icons,

- diagrams,

- shapes,

- or brand elements.

20.140 Scene

A Scene is a coherent narrative, visual or temporal unit.

It shall include or reference:

- sceneId,

- Production Unit,

- purpose,

- setting,

- Characters,

- action,

- dialogue,

- timing,

- continuity,

- and Version.

20.141 Scene Identity

Every governed Scene shall have stable identity.

20.142 Shot

A Shot is one continuous or conceptually bounded camera view.

It shall include or reference:

- shotId,

- Scene,

- framing,

- camera position,

- camera movement,

- subject,

- action,

- duration,

- and transition.

20.143 Shot Identity

Every governed Shot shall have stable identity.

20.144 Shot List

A Shot List defines the ordered Shots required for one Scene or video.

20.145 Storyboard

A Storyboard visually represents planned Shots and timing.

Storyboard Assets remain distinct from final media.

20.146 Animatic

An Animatic combines storyboard imagery and provisional timing or audio.

It supports validation before final production.

20.147 Keyframe

A Keyframe represents a significant visual state within animation or video generation.

20.148 Motion Reference

A Motion Reference guides body movement, camera or temporal behaviour.

20.149 Camera Framing

Framing may include:

- extreme close-up,

- close-up,

- medium,

- full-body,

- wide,

- overhead,

- or custom.

20.150 Camera Angle

Angle may include:

- eye level,

- high,

- low,

- top-down,

- profile,

- or three-quarter.

20.151 Camera Movement

Movement may include:

- static,

- pan,

- tilt,

- dolly,

- zoom,

- orbit,

- tracking,

- handheld,

- or generated motion.

20.152 Camera Continuity

Camera position and movement should remain coherent across adjacent Shots when continuity requires it.

20.153 Subject Motion

Subject motion shall specify:

- actor,

- action,

- direction,

- speed,

- and interaction.

20.154 Motion Plausibility

Generated motion shall be evaluated for:

- anatomy,

- physics,

- continuity,

- object permanence,

- and temporal artefacts.

20.155 Frame Rate

Frame rate shall be specified or derived according to delivery requirements.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.156 Video Dimensions

Video width and height shall be explicit.

20.157 Video Aspect Ratio

Common ratios may include:

- 16:9,

- 9:16,

- 1:1,

- 4:5,

- or Project-specific format.

20.158 Video Duration

Duration may be:

- exact,

- bounded range,

- target,

- or Provider-limited.

20.159 Duration Tolerance

Acceptable deviation shall be explicit.

20.160 Video Codec

Codec may include:

- H.264,

- H.265,

- AV1,

- ProRes,

- or another approved codec.

20.161 Video Container

Container may include:

- MP4,

- MOV,

- WebM,

- or another approved format.

20.162 Bitrate

Bitrate requirements may balance:

- Quality,

- file size,

- platform limits,

- and upload reliability.

20.163 Keyframe Interval

Encoding Keyframe interval may affect:

- seeking,

- streaming,

- and editing.

20.164 Audio Codec

Audio within video may use:

- AAC,

- PCM,

- Opus,

- or another approved codec.

20.165 Video Transparency

Video transparency support is format- and platform-specific.

It shall not be assumed.

20.166 Looping Video

Looping requires continuity between end and start frames.

20.167 Thumbnail

A Thumbnail is a distinct image Asset designed to represent a video, article or publication.

20.168 Thumbnail Definition

A Thumbnail Definition may include:

- focal subject,

- title,

- branding,

- emotional signal,

- safe zones,

- and platform dimensions.

20.169 Document Definition

A Document Definition describes one structured document deliverable.

Examples include:

- PDF,

- ebook,

- report,

- printable activity,

- workbook,

- or guide.

20.170 Document Identity

Every accepted Document Asset shall have stable identity.

20.171 Document Page

A Document Page is one ordered visual and semantic unit.

20.172 Page Definition

A Page Definition may include:

- pageId,

- page number,

- purpose,

- layout,

- text,

- images,

- activity,

- accessibility,

- and Version.

20.173 Page Size

Page size may include:

- A4,

- Letter,

- custom print size,

- or responsive digital canvas.

20.174 Page Orientation

Orientation may be:

- portrait,

- landscape,

- or responsive.

20.175 Bleed

Print bleed shall be explicit where required.

20.176 Safe Margin

Content shall remain inside defined safe margins.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.177 Binding Margin

Bound documents may require extra inner margin.

20.178 Document Typography

Typography shall follow:

- Brand System,

- readability,

- language,

- age,

- and print constraints.

20.179 Font Rights

Font use shall respect licence and embedding rights.

20.180 Document Reflow

Reflowable documents differ from fixed-layout documents.

The intended behaviour shall be explicit.

20.181 Fixed Layout

Fixed layout preserves exact spatial composition.

20.182 Reflowable Ebook

Reflowable ebook content shall remain semantically structured.

20.183 PDF Export

PDF export shall validate:

- page count,

- dimensions,

- fonts,

- links,

- images,

- colour,

- and file integrity.

20.184 Document Accessibility

Documents may require:

- reading order,

- headings,

- alt text,

- language metadata,

- contrast,

- and selectable text.

20.185 Interactive Content

Interactive content responds to user input.

Examples include:

- application exercise,

- interactive story,

- quiz,

- animation control,

- or game-like activity.

20.186 Interactive Asset

An Interactive Asset may contain:

- code,

- media,

- state,

- input handling,

- and accessibility behaviour.

20.187 Interaction Definition

Interaction Definition shall describe:

- user action,

- system response,

- state transition,

- feedback,

- error handling,

- and completion.

20.188 Interaction Safety

Child-facing interactions shall avoid:

- dark patterns,

- uncontrolled external links,

- unnecessary data collection,

- and harmful feedback.

20.189 Production Graph

A Production Graph is a specialised Execution Graph representing multimodal production dependencies.

It shall preserve:

- Production Units,

- Steps,

- Inputs,

- Outputs,

- Assets,

- variants,

- selection,

- Quality,

- approvals,

- and publication dependencies.

20.190 Production Graph Identity

Every Production Graph Version shall have stable identity.

20.191 Production Step

A Production Step is one bounded operation in the Production Graph.

Examples include:

- write Script,

- generate image,

- edit image,

- create Voice,

- animate Scene,

- compose audio,

- render video,

- export PDF,

- review,

- or publish.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.192 Production Step Type

Step types may include:

- ideation,

- planning,

- generation,

- transformation,

- editing,

- composition,

- rendering,

- evaluation,

- selection,

- approval,

- packaging,

- publication,

- and archival.

20.193 Creative Planning Step

Creative Planning produces structured direction rather than final media.

20.194 Generation Step

A Generation Step creates new Candidate content using a Model or Provider.

20.195 Transformation Step

A Transformation Step modifies an existing Input while preserving defined properties.

20.196 Editing Step

An Editing Step applies a bounded intentional change.

20.197 Composition Step

A Composition Step combines accepted or provisional elements into a larger unit.

20.198 Render Step

A Render Step materialises a Timeline, document or Composition into a deliverable file.

20.199 Evaluation Step

An Evaluation Step measures technical, creative, safety, rights or continuity criteria.

20.200 Selection Step

A Selection Step chooses among Candidates.

Selection shall be attributable.

20.201 Approval Step

An Approval Step records a human or authorised system Decision.

20.202 Packaging Step

A Packaging Step assembles required Assets and metadata for delivery or publication.

20.203 Publication Step

A Publication Step creates an external side effect and requires appropriate authority.

20.204 Archival Step

An Archival Step preserves final Assets, evidence and production records.

20.205 Step Dependency

A Step may depend on:

- accepted Input,

- Candidate availability,

- evaluation,

- approval,

- Asset ingestion,

- or rights verification.

20.206 Hard Dependency

A Hard Dependency must be satisfied before execution.

20.207 Soft Dependency

A Soft Dependency improves production but may be omitted under approved conditions.

20.208 Conditional Branch

A Production Graph may branch based on:

- Quality,

- Provider failure,

- rights,

- cost,

- or approval.

20.209 Iteration Loop

A bounded Iteration Loop creates revised Candidates until:

- acceptance,

- Budget limit,

- Attempt limit,

- deadline,

- or escalation.

20.210 Unbounded Iteration Prohibition

Creative production shall not retry indefinitely.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.211 Production Checkpoint

A Checkpoint preserves a recoverable state such as:

- accepted Script,

- selected image,

- approved Voice Output,

- completed Scene,

- or rendered draft.

20.212 Parallel Production

Independent Scenes or Assets may be produced in parallel when continuity and resource constraints permit.

20.213 Sequential Production

Steps requiring one accepted Output before the next shall remain sequential.

20.214 Batch Production

Compatible units may share:

- Model,

- Provider,

- style,

- Voice,

- dimensions,

- or review Session.

20.215 Batch Consistency

Batching may improve consistency but can propagate one incorrect Specification across many Outputs.

Preflight validation is mandatory.

20.216 Production Preflight

Preflight validates the Production Specification before paid or consequential execution.

It should check:

- required Inputs,

- reference Assets,

- rights,

- Consent,

- dimensions,

- duration,

- Budget,

- Provider support,

- and Approval.

20.217 Preflight Failure

Missing mandatory production Inputs shall block dispatch.

20.218 Production Intent Envelope

A Production Intent Envelope specialises the Intent Envelope for multimodal work.

It may include:

- audience,

- creative goal,

- emotional goal,

- brand,

- Characters,

- style,

- Modality,

- Quality,

- platform,

- schedule,

- and publication intent.

20.219 Prompt Specification

A Prompt Specification is a canonical description of information to communicate to a generative resource.

It shall include or reference:

- promptSpecificationId,

- Production Specification,

- positive requirements,

- negative constraints,

- references,

- structure,

- language,

- parameter policy,

- and Version.

20.220 Prompt Specification Identity

Every persistent Prompt Specification shall have stable identity and Version.

20.221 Prompt Derivation

Provider prompts shall be derived from the canonical Prompt Specification through Adapter mappings.

20.222 Positive Requirement

A Positive Requirement describes what should appear or occur.

20.223 Negative Constraint

A Negative Constraint describes what shall not appear or occur.

20.224 Negative Constraint Identity

Reusable negative constraints may have stable identity.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.225 Hard Negative Constraint

A Hard Negative Constraint is mandatory.

Violation shall fail acceptance.

20.226 Soft Negative Constraint

A Soft Negative Constraint is preferred but may permit bounded deviation.

20.227 Prompt Section

Prompt Specifications may separate:

- subject,

- setting,

- style,

- composition,

- camera,

- lighting,

- motion,

- text,

- Quality,

- and exclusions.

20.228 Prompt Language

Canonical prompts may be authored in one language and translated for a Provider.

Meaning shall be preserved.

20.229 Provider Prompt

The exact Provider prompt shall be preserved as Execution Evidence when policy permits.

20.230 Prompt Injection Boundary

External reference text and Provider metadata shall not alter authority or canonical requirements.

20.231 Prompt Template

A Prompt Template is a reusable structure for one production class.

20.232 Prompt Template Identity

Every reusable Prompt Template shall have stable identity and Version.

20.233 Template Variable

Variables shall have:

- type,

- allowed values,

- validation,

- and source.

20.234 Prompt Compilation

Prompt Compilation combines:

- Template,

- Brief,

- Character rules,

- Style rules,

- Scene details,

- and Provider mappings.

20.235 Prompt Compilation Receipt

The compilation process should preserve which source requirements produced each material Provider-specific instruction.

20.236 Prompt Compiler

A Prompt Compiler is the governed component that converts canonical Production intent into one Provider-specific prompt package.

The Prompt Compiler shall not invent new creative authority.

20.237 Prompt Compiler Input

Compiler Input may include:

- Prompt Specification,

- Creative Brief,

- Character Definitions,

- Style System,

- reference Assets,

- Technical Specification,

- Provider Capability,

- Model constraints,

- and policy.

20.238 Prompt Compiler Output

Compiler Output may include:

- Provider prompt,

- negative prompt,

- reference ordering,

- Provider parameters,

- control values,

- seed policy,

- attachment mappings,

- and bounded Adapter metadata.

20.239 Compilation Traceability

Every material compiled instruction should be traceable to:

- canonical requirement,

- Adapter mapping,

- Provider limitation,

- or explicitly approved optimisation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.240 Compilation Loss

When a Provider cannot express one canonical requirement, the compiler shall report that limitation rather than silently omit it.

20.241 Compilation Substitution

A Provider-specific approximation may be used only when:

- the canonical requirement remains understandable,

- substitution risk is recorded,

- and acceptance criteria remain valid.

20.242 Prompt Compression

Prompt compression may reduce instruction size.

It shall preserve mandatory semantics.

20.243 Prompt Expansion

Prompt expansion may add Provider-specific descriptive language.

It shall not create new identity, rights, authority or publication requirements.

20.244 Reference Ordering

Where Provider behaviour depends on reference order, the Adapter shall preserve deterministic ordering.

20.245 Reference Weight Mapping

Provider-specific reference weights shall map from canonical influence requirements where possible.

20.246 Unsupported Weighting

When a Provider cannot express required reference weighting, the limitation shall influence eligibility or Quality review.

20.247 Parameter Policy

A Parameter Policy defines allowed generative parameters such as:

- creativity,

- adherence,

- seed,

- guidance,

- steps,

- duration,

- quality tier,

- or Candidate count.

20.248 Provider Parameter

Provider-native parameter names remain Adapter implementation detail.

20.249 Parameter Range Validation

Adapters shall validate parameter ranges before dispatch.

20.250 Default Parameter

Provider defaults shall not be relied upon for material behaviour without explicit mapping.

20.251 Seed

A Seed is a Provider or Model-specific input intended to influence reproducibility or variation.

20.252 Seed Identity

Seeds may be stored as execution parameters.

They are not creative identity.

20.253 Determinism Profile

A Determinism Profile describes expected repeatability for one production operation.

20.254 Determinism Classes

Classes may include:

- deterministic,

- approximately repeatable,

- stochastic with seed,

- stochastic without reliable seed,

- and unknown.

20.255 Seed Does Not Guarantee Reproduction

A fixed seed may still produce different Outputs after:

- Model update,

- Provider update,

- Runtime change,

- parameter change,

- or infrastructure variation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.256 Reproducibility Record

Material production should preserve enough information to estimate whether exact or approximate reproduction is possible.

20.257 Variation Policy

A Variation Policy defines how many and what kinds of alternatives may be generated.

20.258 Variation Dimensions

Variation may occur in:

- composition,

- pose,

- expression,

- camera,

- wording,

- pacing,

- colour,

- motion,

- Voice performance,

- or style intensity.

20.259 Controlled Variation

Controlled Variation changes approved dimensions while preserving mandatory identity and requirements.

20.260 Uncontrolled Variation

Uncontrolled Variation shall not be used when exact continuity is required.

20.261 Candidate Set

A Candidate Set groups alternative Outputs for the same production objective.

20.262 Candidate Set Identity

Every material Candidate Set shall have stable identity.

20.263 Candidate Set Fields

A Candidate Set should include:

- candidateSetId,

- Production Unit,

- generation request,

- Candidate identities,

- variation policy,

- selection criteria,

- Budget,

- and state.

20.264 Candidate Identity

Each Candidate shall have stable identity before comparison.

20.265 Candidate Provenance

Every Candidate shall preserve:

- source Specification,

- Inputs,

- Provider,

- Model or Tool,

- Attempt,

- parameters,

- and creation time.

20.266 Candidate Count

Candidate count shall remain Budget-aware.

20.267 Candidate Overgeneration

Generating many Candidates without evidence that additional variation improves outcomes is an economic anti-pattern.

20.268 Candidate Diversity

Candidate diversity may be measured to avoid near-duplicate alternatives.

20.269 Candidate Similarity

Similarity analysis may identify duplicate or near-duplicate Candidates.

20.270 Candidate Comparison

Candidates may be compared by:

- technical validity,

- creative fit,

- identity consistency,

- brand consistency,

- continuity,

- accessibility,

- rights,

- safety,

- and human preference.

20.271 Candidate Ranking

Candidate ranking may be:

- deterministic,

- Model-assisted,

- human,

- or hybrid.

20.272 Ranking Is Not Acceptance

The highest-ranked Candidate shall not become Accepted automatically unless the applicable acceptance policy permits it.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.273 Selection Decision

A Selection Decision records which Candidate was selected and why.

20.274 Selection Decision Identity

Every material Selection Decision shall have stable identity.

20.275 Selection Evidence

Selection should preserve:

- Candidate Set,

- evaluator,

- rubric,

- scores,

- findings,

- human feedback,

- and Decision.

20.276 Selection Reversal

A previously selected Candidate may be superseded.

Historical selection remains preserved.

20.277 Candidate Rejection

Rejected Candidates may remain as bounded production Evidence according to retention policy.

20.278 Candidate Reuse

A rejected Candidate shall not be reused in another Project merely because the file remains stored.

20.279 Generation Request

A Generation Request asks a generative resource to create new Candidate content.

20.280 Generation Request Identity

Every dispatched Generation Request shall have stable identity.

20.281 Generation Request Fields

It should include:

- generationRequestId,

- Production Specification,

- Prompt Specification,

- references,

- requested Modality,

- technical constraints,

- parameter policy,

- Candidate count,

- Budget,

- and routing constraints.

20.282 Transformation Request

A Transformation Request asks a resource to modify existing Asset content.

20.283 Transformation Preservation Contract

Every Transformation Request shall define what must be preserved.

20.284 Preservation Examples

Preserved properties may include:

- Character identity,

- pose,

- composition,

- text,

- timing,

- Voice identity,

- background,

- or geometry.

20.285 Transformation Change Contract

The Request shall also define what is allowed to change.

20.286 Minimal Change Principle

Where a user requests a local correction, the Fabric should minimise unrelated change.

20.287 Edit Request

An Edit Request defines one bounded creative or technical modification.

20.288 Edit Request Identity

Every material Edit Request shall have stable identity.

20.289 Edit Target

The exact Asset Version or Composition Version shall be explicit.

20.290 Edit Region

Spatial edits may include:

- mask,

- bounding region,

- layer,

- object,

- or semantic target.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.291 Temporal Edit Region

Video and audio edits may identify:

- time range,

- Clip,

- Track,

- Scene,

- or segment.

20.292 Edit Preservation

Unselected regions or Tracks should remain unchanged where the Capability supports it.

20.293 Destructive Edit

Destructive edits overwrite source representation.

They should be avoided where Versioned non-destructive workflows are practical.

20.294 Non-Destructive Edit

Non-destructive edits preserve source Assets and create new Versions or edit instructions.

20.295 Transformation Provenance

Every transformed Asset shall reference its exact source Asset Versions.

20.296 Composition

A Composition combines multiple Assets, Tracks, layers or semantic elements into one coordinated production object.

20.297 Composition Identity

Every governed Composition shall have stable identity and Version.

20.298 Composition Types

Composition types may include:

- image Composition,

- audio Composition,

- video Composition,

- document Composition,

- social package Composition,

- or mixed-media Composition.

20.299 Composition Source

Every component in a Composition shall reference an exact source Asset Version or generated element.

20.300 Composition Order

Layer or Track ordering shall be explicit.

20.301 Layer

A Layer is one ordered visual component within a Composition.

20.302 Layer Identity

Every material Layer should have stable identity inside its Composition Version.

20.303 Layer Properties

A Layer may include:

- source Asset,

- position,

- scale,

- rotation,

- opacity,

- blend,

- crop,

- mask,

- effects,

- and time range.

20.304 Layer Lock

Identity-critical or approved Layers may be locked against automatic modification.

20.305 Timeline

A Timeline is an ordered temporal Composition.

20.306 Timeline Identity

Every governed Timeline shall have stable identity and Version.

20.307 Timeline Timebase

The Timeline shall define:

- time units,

- frame rate or sampling basis,

- start,

- duration,

- and precision.

20.308 Track

A Track contains one ordered class of temporal content.

20.309 Track Types

Track types may include:

- video,

- animation,

- Voice,

- dialogue,

- music,

- sound effect,

- subtitle,

- metadata,

- and marker.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.310 Track Identity

Every material Track shall have stable identity within the Timeline Version.

20.311 Clip

A Clip places all or part of an Asset on a Timeline.

20.312 Clip Fields

A Clip may include:

- source Asset Version,

- source range,

- Timeline range,

- speed,

- gain,

- transform,

- transition,

- and effects.

20.313 Segment

A Segment is a bounded semantic or temporal portion of a Track or Asset.

20.314 Segment Identity

Material Segments should have stable identity when referenced by review or revision.

20.315 Marker

A Marker identifies a meaningful time, frame or production event.

20.316 Marker Uses

Markers may identify:

- Scene boundaries,

- chapter boundaries,

- beats,

- review comments,

- subtitle events,

- or synchronisation points.

20.317 Transition

A Transition defines how one Clip, Shot, page or state changes into another.

20.318 Transition Types

Transitions may include:

- cut,

- fade,

- dissolve,

- wipe,

- animated motion,

- audio crossfade,

- or custom transition.

20.319 Transition Restraint

Transitions should serve creative purpose rather than be added merely because a Tool supports them.

20.320 Synchronisation

Synchronisation aligns several modalities in time or semantic structure.

20.321 Audio-Visual Synchronisation

Audio-visual synchronisation may align:

- speech to animation,

- music to Scene,

- subtitle to Voice,

- action to sound effect,

- and on-screen text to narration.

20.322 Sync Point

A Sync Point is a defined temporal or semantic alignment reference.

20.323 Lip Synchronisation

Lip synchronisation shall be evaluated when visible speaking characters require mouth-to-speech alignment.

20.324 Lip-Sync Limitation

A generated talking character may require manual correction when Provider output cannot meet identity or timing requirements.

20.325 Voice Track

A Voice Track contains one or more governed Voice Clips.

20.326 Voice Clip

A Voice Clip shall reference:

- Script Version,

- Voice Version,

- Provider or local Runtime,

- pronunciation configuration,

- and source audio Asset.

20.327 Dialogue Track

Dialogue Tracks may contain several Voice identities.

Speaker attribution shall be explicit.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.328 Music Track

A Music Track shall reference exact Music Asset Versions and rights state.

20.329 Sound Effect Track

Sound effects shall preserve source and rights provenance.

20.330 Subtitle Track Synchronisation

Subtitle timing shall align with the accepted audio Version.

20.331 Timeline Revision

A Timeline revision creates a new Version when material Clip ordering, timing or source changes.

20.332 Composition Render

Rendering materialises a Composition into an Output representation.

20.333 Render Request

A Render Request defines the exact Composition and technical settings to materialise.

20.334 Render Request Identity

Every material Render Request shall have stable identity.

20.335 Render Profile

A Render Profile defines reusable technical output requirements.

20.336 Render Profile Identity

Every reusable Render Profile shall have stable identity and Version.

20.337 Render Profile Fields

It may include:

- dimensions,

- frame rate,

- codec,

- bitrate,

- colour profile,

- audio codec,

- loudness,

- subtitle mode,

- metadata,

- and file format.

20.338 Render Job

A Render Job is the actual execution of one Render Request.

20.339 Render Job Identity

Every Render Job shall have stable identity.

20.340 Render Job State

States may include:

- prepared,

- queued,

- rendering,

- validating,

- succeeded,

- failed,

- cancelled,

- unknown,

- and reconciliation required.

20.341 Review Proxy

A Review Proxy is a lower-cost or lower-resolution representation used for review before final rendering.

20.342 Proxy Is Not Master

A Review Proxy shall not automatically become the Master Asset.

20.343 Master Render

A Master Render is the high-quality canonical output from which delivery renditions may be derived.

20.344 Distribution Render

A Distribution Render is adapted to one platform, channel or technical target.

20.345 Master Preservation

The Master Render should remain preserved independently from compressed distribution copies.

20.346 Rendition

A Rendition is a derived representation of the same accepted content for a specific delivery context.

20.347 Rendition Provenance

Every Rendition shall link to the exact Master Asset Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.348 Image Rendition

Image renditions may vary in:

- dimensions,

- compression,

- format,

- colour space,

- crop,

- and metadata.

20.349 Video Rendition

Video renditions may vary in:

- dimensions,

- bitrate,

- codec,

- frame rate,

- aspect ratio,

- subtitles,

- and platform metadata.

20.350 Audio Rendition

Audio renditions may vary in:

- codec,

- bitrate,

- sample rate,

- channel layout,

- and loudness target.

20.351 Document Rendition

Document renditions may include:

- print PDF,

- screen PDF,

- ebook,

- individual pages,

- or preview images.

20.352 Text Production Architecture

Text production shall separate:

- ideation,

- factual source use,

- drafting,

- editing,

- approval,

- and publication.

20.353 Text Canon

When exact approved wording matters, one accepted Script or Text Asset Version shall become canonical for downstream production.

20.354 Text Drift

Downstream voice or visual Tools shall not silently rewrite accepted canonical text.

20.355 Structured Data Production

Structured data Outputs shall validate against schemas before downstream use.

20.356 Structured Data Canon

Machine-readable production metadata should remain separate from human-facing copy.

20.357 Code Production

Generated code used in interactive media shall follow code execution and repository governance rather than creative acceptance alone.

20.358 Image Production Architecture

Image production should support:

- Specification,

- references,

- Candidate generation,

- evaluation,

- selection,

- editing,

- acceptance,

- and rendition.

20.359 Image Identity Continuity

Recurring Characters or branded elements shall use approved references and continuity evidence.

20.360 Image Candidate Review

Review should distinguish:

- technical defects,

- visual identity defects,

- creative mismatch,

- unsafe content,

- text errors,

- and rights concerns.

20.361 Image Text Layer Preference

Where exact text matters, separate typography or composition layers are preferred over relying on generative image text.

20.362 Image Regeneration

Regeneration should target the smallest defective component where possible.

20.363 Audio Production Architecture

Audio production shall support:

- source or Script,

- Voice or sound requirement,

- generation or recording,

- cleanup,

- composition,

- loudness validation,

- and acceptance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.364 Speech Production Architecture

Speech production shall preserve:

- exact Script,

- Voice Profile,

- pronunciation,

- emotion,

- timing,

- Consent,

- and Provider provenance.

20.365 Speech Segmentation

Long scripts may be divided into Segments for:

- retry,

- pronunciation correction,

- parallel generation,

- and selective replacement.

20.366 Speech Segment Identity

Every material speech Segment should have stable identity.

20.367 Speech Stitching

Joined Voice Segments shall be checked for:

- consistent tone,

- room or synthetic texture,

- volume,

- pacing,

- and boundary artefacts.

20.368 Pronunciation Retry

Mispronounced words may trigger selective regeneration of one Segment instead of the entire narration.

20.369 Voice Provider Change

Changing Voice Provider requires continuity evaluation before accepted identity reuse.

20.370 Music Production Architecture

Music production shall distinguish:

- original composition,

- generated composition,

- stock licensing,

- human commissioning,

- and editing.

20.371 Music Brief

A Music Brief may define:

- emotional arc,

- genre,

- tempo,

- instrumentation,

- loop behaviour,

- duration,

- and prohibited similarities.

20.372 Generated Music Candidate

Generated music shall enter as Candidate Asset before acceptance.

20.373 Music Similarity Risk

Generated music may require review for potentially problematic similarity or uncertain rights.

20.374 Music Loop

Looping music shall be technically and musically validated at the loop boundary.

20.375 Sound Effect Production

Sound effects may be generated, recorded, licensed or sourced from approved libraries.

20.376 Audio Composition

Voice, music and sound effects shall be mixed through explicit Track relationships.

20.377 Loudness Normalisation

Loudness normalisation shall target the intended delivery context.

20.378 Dialogue Intelligibility

Speech intelligibility shall outrank decorative audio effects where spoken content is material.

20.379 Video Production Architecture

Video production shall coordinate:

- Story,

- Script,

- Storyboard,

- Scenes,

- Shots,

- references,

- generation,

- audio,

- composition,

- render,

- and review.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.380 Story Structure

A Story Structure defines narrative progression across Scenes or sections.

20.381 Story Structure Identity

Every persistent Story Structure shall have stable identity and Version.

20.382 Story Beat

A Story Beat is one meaningful narrative change or moment.

20.383 Story Beat Mapping

Beats may map to:

- Scenes,

- Shots,

- pages,

- Voice Segments,

- or interactive states.

20.384 Storyboard Dependency

High-cost video production should use Storyboards or equivalent previsualisation when doing so materially reduces waste.

20.385 Scene Specification

Every material generated Scene should have a Scene Specification.

20.386 Scene Specification Fields

It should include:

- Scene identity,

- narrative purpose,

- location,

- characters,

- action,

- visual style,

- camera,

- duration,

- references,

- Voice,

- continuity,

- and acceptance criteria.

20.387 Shot Specification

Every generated Shot should define its intended framing, action and duration.

20.388 Shot Boundary

Shots should be split when one Provider cannot reliably satisfy complex multi-action direction in a single generation.

20.389 Shot Candidate

Each generated Shot is a Candidate until accepted.

20.390 Shot Continuity

Adjacent Shots shall be evaluated for:

- character identity,

- clothing,

- object position,

- lighting,

- direction of movement,

- scale,

- and environment.

20.391 Temporal Identity Drift

Generated video may change identity within one Clip.

Temporal identity consistency shall therefore be evaluated across frames, not only at the first frame.

20.392 Temporal Object Drift

Objects may:

- disappear,

- multiply,

- change shape,

- or move impossibly.

These defects shall be included in Quality evaluation.

20.393 Video Reference Frame

Approved frames may be promoted as references for later Shots.

20.394 Keyframe Continuity

Keyframes may establish approved start or end states to improve sequence continuity.

20.395 Scene Transition Continuity

End-state and start-state compatibility should be evaluated when one Scene transitions directly into another.

20.396 Video Revision

Video revision should target:

- one Shot,

- one frame range,

- one audio Track,

- one subtitle Segment,

- or one composition element

where possible.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.397 Full Video Regeneration

Regenerating an entire video should be avoided when only one bounded defect exists.

20.398 Animation Production Architecture

Animation may combine:

- generated imagery,

- rigged Characters,

- deterministic motion,

- generated motion,

- and compositing.

20.399 Deterministic Animation

Deterministic animation should be preferred when exact timing and repeatability are more important than generative variation.

20.400 Generated Animation

Generated animation requires stronger temporal Quality review.

20.401 Character Rig

A Character Rig is an executable or editable representation of a Character for animation.

20.402 Character Rig Identity

Every persistent Rig shall have stable identity and Version.

20.403 Rig Provenance

A Rig shall link to the Character Version and source Assets from which it was created.

20.404 Animation Pose

Animation pose states should preserve Character proportions and identity.

20.405 Motion Safety

Child-facing animation shall avoid unsafe or disturbing generated motion inconsistent with the intended audience.

20.406 Document Production Architecture

Document production shall coordinate:

- content,

- pagination,

- layout,

- typography,

- illustrations,

- activities,

- metadata,

- export,

- and review.

20.407 Document Source Model

The editable source model should remain distinct from exported PDF or ebook representations.

20.408 Page Continuity

Page series shall maintain:

- typography,

- margin system,

- recurring Character scale,

- numbering,

- navigation,

- and visual rhythm.

20.409 Printable Activity

Printable activities shall be validated for:

- instructions,

- age appropriateness,

- sufficient writing space,

- print margins,

- contrast,

- and answerability.

20.410 Document Pagination

Pagination shall be deterministic after the accepted source Version where exact page references matter.

20.411 Document Link Validation

Hyperlinks and internal navigation shall be validated before acceptance.

20.412 Document Font Embedding

Required fonts shall be embedded or substituted according to rights and technical policy.

20.413 Document Image Resolution

Placed images shall meet effective output resolution requirements.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.414 Document Master

The accepted document source and final PDF may both be canonical Assets with distinct representations.

20.415 Interactive Production Architecture

Interactive production shall combine:

- media,

- code,

- state,

- input,

- accessibility,

- and behavioural testing.

20.416 Interactive State

Interactive state transitions shall be explicit and testable.

20.417 Interactive Determinism

Deterministic application behaviour shall not be replaced by generative behaviour without a clear requirement.

20.418 Generative Interaction

When an interactive experience invokes AI dynamically, that inference remains a separate Fabric Capability Request.

20.419 Interactive Safety Boundary

Generated responses inside child-facing interactive systems require stronger content and privacy policy.

20.420 Interactive Offline Behaviour

Offline behaviour shall be explicitly defined when the experience may lose connectivity.

20.421 Accessibility Production

Accessibility is a production requirement rather than a post-production decoration.

20.422 Accessibility Profile

An Accessibility Profile may define:

- captions,

- transcripts,

- alt text,

- contrast,

- text size,

- reading order,

- keyboard access,

- motion reduction,

- and audio descriptions.

20.423 Accessibility Evaluation

Acceptance shall include required accessibility checks.

20.424 Accessibility Variant

Accessible variants may be separate Renditions linked to one canonical Deliverable.

20.425 Multilingual Production

Multilingual content shall preserve source-to-translation relationships.

20.426 Translation Asset

Every accepted translation shall reference the exact source Text Asset Version.

20.427 Translation Review

High-impact translations should receive linguistic review appropriate to audience and context.

20.428 Dubbed Voice

Translated Voice production shall preserve:

- translated Script,

- Voice identity,

- timing,

- and Consent.

20.429 Locale-Specific Asset

Some visual or document Assets may require locale-specific text, dimensions or legal information.

20.430 Continuity

Continuity is the preservation of required identity and state across related production units.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.431 Continuity Profile

A Continuity Profile defines what must remain stable across a defined production scope.

20.432 Continuity Profile Identity

Every reusable Continuity Profile shall have stable identity and Version.

20.433 Continuity Dimensions

Dimensions may include:

- Character identity,

- clothing,

- object state,

- location,

- lighting,

- camera,

- Voice,

- terminology,

- typography,

- style,

- timeline,

- and factual state.

20.434 Continuity Scope

Continuity may apply across:

- Shots,

- Scenes,

- pages,

- chapters,

- episodes,

- campaigns,

- monthly themes,

- or an entire Project.

20.435 Continuity Ledger

A Continuity Ledger records accepted production facts that downstream units must preserve.

20.436 Continuity Ledger Identity

Every persistent Continuity Ledger shall have stable identity and Version.

20.437 Continuity Entry

A Continuity Entry may state:

- Character clothing,

- object location,

- weather,

- time of day,

- emotional state,

- previous action,

- or visual setting.

20.438 Continuity Source

Every material continuity fact should derive from an accepted source rather than informal memory alone.

20.439 Continuity Update

A deliberate canonical change shall create a new continuity state or Version.

20.440 Continuity Conflict

Conflicting continuity facts shall be surfaced before downstream generation.

20.441 Character Continuity

Character identity shall reference the exact Character Version and approved Reference Set.

20.442 Voice Continuity

Voice continuity shall reference the exact Voice Version and relevant performance profile.

20.443 Brand Continuity

Brand continuity shall reference the current applicable Brand System Version.

20.444 Style Continuity

Style continuity shall reference the applicable Style System Version.

20.445 Narrative Continuity

Narrative continuity shall preserve accepted story facts.

20.446 Spatial Continuity

Spatial continuity may preserve:

- direction,

- positions,

- room layout,

- and object relationships.

20.447 Temporal Continuity

Temporal continuity preserves the logical progression of time.

20.448 Continuity Evaluation

Continuity may be evaluated by:

- deterministic checks,

- visual comparison,

- multimodal Models,

- or human review.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.449 Continuity Confidence

Automated continuity findings shall include confidence and exact evidence.

20.450 Continuity Failure

Mandatory continuity failure shall block acceptance.

20.451 Reference Set

A Reference Set is a governed collection of Assets used to guide production.

20.452 Reference Set Identity

Every reusable Reference Set shall have stable identity and Version.

20.453 Reference Types

Reference types may include:

- Character,

- Style,

- Brand,

- layout,

- camera,

- motion,

- Voice,

- music,

- product,

- or environment.

20.454 Reference Role

Every reference should identify why it is being used.

20.455 Reference Influence

A reference may be:

- mandatory identity source,

- strong guide,

- optional inspiration,

- structural guide,

- or negative example.

20.456 Reference Is Not Permission

Possessing a reference Asset does not prove rights to use it for generation or publication.

20.457 Reference Eligibility

Rights, Consent and Classification shall be checked before a reference is sent to an external Provider.

20.458 Reference Locality

Local Only reference Assets shall remain inside approved local execution boundaries.

20.459 Reference Version

Production shall use exact reference Asset Versions.

20.460 Reference Drift

Replacing a reference Asset silently may change downstream identity.

Material replacement requires new Reference Set Version.

20.461 Reference Leakage

External Providers may retain uploaded reference Assets according to their terms.

This risk shall influence eligibility.

20.462 Reference Minimisation

Only references required for the current Step should be disclosed.

20.463 Production Dependency

A Production Dependency is an upstream object whose change may affect downstream work.

20.464 Dependency Types

Dependencies may include:

- Brief,

- Script,

- Character,

- Voice,

- Style,

- Brand,

- reference Asset,

- Scene,

- Timeline,

- rights,

- Consent,

- and technical requirement.

20.465 Dependency Graph

The Production Graph shall allow reverse lookup of downstream objects affected by one changed dependency.

20.466 Impact Analysis

Impact Analysis determines which downstream production units may be invalidated after a change.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.467 Script Impact

Changing approved narration may affect:

- Voice Assets,

- subtitles,

- Scene timing,

- animation,

- captions,

- and final render.

20.468 Character Impact

Changing a Character Version may affect every downstream visual containing that Character.

20.469 Voice Impact

Changing Voice Version may affect all dependent narration or dialogue.

20.470 Rights Impact

Revoked rights may invalidate Assets, compositions, packages and publications.

20.471 Selective Regeneration

Selective Regeneration replaces only downstream outputs affected by one changed or defective dependency.

20.472 Regeneration Scope

Regeneration scope should be determined through dependency and Quality evidence.

20.473 Regeneration Preservation

Unaffected accepted Assets should remain unchanged.

20.474 Cascading Regeneration

A fundamental change may legitimately require broad downstream regeneration.

20.475 Regeneration Decision

Material regeneration shall record:

- cause,

- affected objects,

- retained objects,

- Budget,

- and Decision.

20.476 Quality

Quality is the degree to which a production Output satisfies required technical, creative, semantic, safety, rights and continuity criteria.

20.477 Production Quality Profile

A Production Quality Profile defines applicable dimensions and thresholds.

20.478 Quality Profile Identity

Every reusable Quality Profile shall have stable identity and Version.

20.479 Quality Dimensions

Multimodal Quality dimensions may include:

- technical validity,

- correctness,

- creative fit,

- identity consistency,

- continuity,

- brand compliance,

- style compliance,

- intelligibility,

- timing,

- accessibility,

- safety,

- rights,

- and publication suitability.

20.480 Technical Quality

Technical Quality evaluates whether the file or representation functions correctly.

20.481 Creative Quality

Creative Quality evaluates whether the Output fulfills the intended creative direction.

20.482 Semantic Quality

Semantic Quality evaluates whether the intended meaning is preserved.

20.483 Identity Quality

Identity Quality evaluates whether required Characters, Voices or branded elements remain recognisable and correct.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.484 Cross-Modal Quality

Cross-Modal Quality evaluates consistency among modalities.

20.485 Cross-Modal Examples

Examples include:

- Voice matches Script,

- subtitles match Voice,

- visual action matches narration,

- thumbnail represents video,

- and document image matches activity instructions.

20.486 Safety Quality

Safety Quality evaluates age appropriateness, harmful content and Project-specific safety constraints.

20.487 Rights Quality

Rights Quality determines whether required usage permissions are resolved.

20.488 Accessibility Quality

Accessibility Quality evaluates applicable accessibility requirements.

20.489 Quality Rubric

A Quality Rubric defines how evaluation dimensions are measured.

20.490 Quality Rubric Identity

Every reusable Rubric shall have stable identity and Version.

20.491 Mandatory Criterion

Failure of a mandatory criterion blocks acceptance regardless of aggregate score.

20.492 Weighted Criterion

Weighted criteria may influence ranking without being individually mandatory.

20.493 Quality Threshold

Acceptance thresholds shall be explicit.

20.494 Deterministic Evaluation

Deterministic checks should be used where exact validation is possible.

20.495 Deterministic Image Checks

Examples include:

- dimensions,

- file integrity,

- alpha channel,

- colour profile,

- and file size.

20.496 Deterministic Video Checks

Examples include:

- duration,

- frame rate,

- resolution,

- codec,

- audio Track,

- and corruption.

20.497 Deterministic Audio Checks

Examples include:

- duration,

- sample rate,

- channels,

- clipping,

- and loudness.

20.498 Deterministic Document Checks

Examples include:

- page count,

- dimensions,

- fonts,

- links,

- embedded images,

- and selectable text.

20.499 Model-Assisted Evaluation

Models may evaluate creative or semantic qualities not easily measured deterministically.

20.500 Evaluator Model

Every Model-assisted evaluation shall identify the evaluator Model and Version or Deployment evidence.

20.501 Evaluator Independence

Where practical, evaluation should not depend exclusively on the same generative resource that created the Candidate.

20.502 Multimodal Evaluator

A multimodal evaluator may compare:

- references,

- generated images,

- videos,

- text,

- and audio metadata.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 20.517 One Failure Is Not Universal Learning
text:
20.503 Human Review

Human review remains authoritative where Project policy requires subjective creative acceptance.

20.504 Reviewer Identity

Every material human review shall identify the Reviewer Principal.

20.505 Reviewer Annotation

A Reviewer may attach structured findings to:

- Asset,

- Scene,

- Shot,

- Timeline range,

- page,

- or Candidate.

20.506 Review Annotation

A Review Annotation records one specific review finding.

20.507 Annotation Identity

Every material Review Annotation shall have stable identity.

20.508 Annotation Fields

It may include:

- target,

- time or region,

- category,

- severity,

- comment,

- proposed correction,

- Reviewer,

- and state.

20.509 Annotation State

States may include:

- open,

- accepted,

- rejected,

- resolved,

- superseded,

- and waived.

20.510 Quality Finding

A Quality Finding is a structured result produced by evaluation.

20.511 Finding Severity

Severity may include:

- informational,

- minor,

- major,

- blocking,

- and unknown.

20.512 Quality Evidence

Every acceptance Decision shall link to applicable Quality evidence.

20.513 Quality Inconclusive

Inconclusive evaluation shall not be treated as pass.

20.514 Evaluation Conflict

When evaluators disagree materially, the conflict shall remain visible and may require human review.

20.515 Reviewer Preference

Personal aesthetic preference shall be distinguished from mandatory Project requirements.

20.516 Quality Learning

Repeated Quality evidence may inform future routing or production defaults through governed Derived Learning.

20.517 One Failure Is Not Universal Learning

A single poor Candidate shall not automatically make one Provider globally ineligible.

20.518 Revision

A Revision is a deliberate change to a Production Version in response to creative, technical, Quality or governance feedback.

20.519 Revision Request

A Revision Request defines:

- target Version,

- defect or desired change,

- preservation requirements,

- allowed changes,

- priority,

- and acceptance criteria.

20.520 Revision Request Identity

Every material Revision Request shall have stable identity.

20.521 Revision Scope

Revision should target the smallest meaningful production unit.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.522 Revision Provenance

Every revised Asset shall link to the source Version and Revision Request.

20.523 Revision Loop

Revision loops shall remain bounded by:

- Budget,

- attempts,

- deadline,

- and escalation.

20.524 Revision Escalation

Repeated failure should trigger:

- Provider change,

- human intervention,

- Specification review,

- or cancellation

rather than infinite regeneration.

20.525 Variant

A Variant is an intentionally different approved or Candidate form of the same production concept.

20.526 Variant Versus Revision

A Revision attempts to correct or improve a target.

A Variant intentionally represents an alternative.

20.527 Variant Types

Variants may include:

- platform,

- language,

- age group,

- aspect ratio,

- campaign,

- colour,

- duration,

- or creative direction.

20.528 Variant Identity

Every governed Variant shall have stable identity.

20.529 Variant Relationship

Variants shall link to their common source or Production Unit.

20.530 Platform Variant

A platform-specific Variant may adapt:

- dimensions,

- duration,

- caption,

- title-safe areas,

- audio,

- or file size.

20.531 Content Variant

A content Variant materially changes wording, creative direction or narrative.

20.532 A/B Variant

A/B Variants may support measured publication experiments.

Experiment authority remains separate from production authority.

20.533 Acceptance

Acceptance is the Decision that one Production Version satisfies the applicable completion criteria for its intended use.

20.534 Acceptance Decision

An Acceptance Decision shall identify:

- exact target Version,

- accepted use,

- evaluator or approver,

- Quality evidence,

- rights state,

- Consent state,

- and time.

20.535 Acceptance Decision Identity

Every material Acceptance Decision shall have stable identity.

20.536 Conditional Acceptance

A Version may be accepted for:

- internal review,

- draft use,

- or one bounded channel

while remaining ineligible for public publication.

20.537 Internal Acceptance

Internal acceptance shall not be interpreted as publication eligibility.

20.538 Publication Acceptance

Publication acceptance requires all mandatory publication conditions.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
