20.539 Acceptance Revocation

Acceptance may be revoked if:

- rights change,

- Consent is revoked,

- serious defect is discovered,

- or policy changes.

20.540 Acceptance Supersession

A newer accepted Version may supersede an earlier Version without deleting historical evidence.

20.541 Final Candidate

The final Candidate is the Candidate chosen for final acceptance review.

20.542 Master Asset Acceptance

A Master Asset shall be accepted before downstream distribution renditions are considered final.

20.543 Production Completion

Production Completion occurs only when the Production Specification’s completion criteria are satisfied.

20.544 Completion Criteria

Criteria may require:

- accepted Assets,

- technical validation,

- Quality pass,

- rights clearance,

- Consent,

- packaging,

- and approval.

20.545 Render Success Is Not Completion

One successful Render Job does not establish Production Completion if downstream validation or approval remains outstanding.

20.546 Production Receipt

A Production Receipt summarises one completed production operation or workflow.

20.547 Production Receipt Identity

Every material Production Receipt shall have stable identity.

20.548 Production Receipt Fields

It should include or reference:

- Production Project,

- Production Unit,

- Plan,

- Execution,

- accepted Assets,

- Providers,

- costs,

- evaluations,

- approvals,

- provenance,

- and completion state.

20.549 Production Package

A Production Package is a governed set of exact Asset Versions and metadata prepared for delivery or publication.

20.550 Production Package Identity

Every Production Package shall have stable identity and Version.

20.551 Package Manifest

Every Package should have a Manifest listing its exact contents.

20.552 Package Manifest Fields

The Manifest may include:

- Asset identity,

- Asset Version,

- representation,

- role,

- checksum,

- rights,

- Classification,

- and intended use.

20.553 Package Exactness

A Package shall not reference mutable “latest” Assets when exact deliverables matter.

20.554 Package Types

Packages may include:

- publication package,

- print package,

- social package,

- app media package,

- archive package,

- review package,

- or delivery package.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 20.568 Archive Does Not Require Every Intermediate
text:
20.555 Publication Package

A Publication Package is specifically prepared for one or more external publication targets.

20.556 Publication Package Fields

It may include:

- target Account,

- channel,

- Asset Versions,

- caption,

- title,

- thumbnail,

- schedule,

- disclosures,

- rights Decision,

- approval,

- and metadata.

20.557 Publication Package Is Not Publication

Packaging does not create an external side effect.

20.558 Publication Handoff

Publication Handoff transfers an approved exact Package to a publication Connector or human operator.

20.559 Publication Handoff Authority

Handoff shall require current publication authority.

20.560 Publication Target

The exact Account and channel shall be known before consequential handoff.

20.561 Publication Schedule

Scheduled publication shall revalidate:

- approval,

- rights,

- Consent,

- Account,

- and Package Version

at execution time.

20.562 Publication Verification

After publication, the external result should be verified according to Chapter 17 and Chapter 24 semantics.

20.563 Publication Correction

Correction after publication shall create a new production or publication action rather than rewriting historical evidence.

20.564 Package Invalidation

A Package becomes invalid if one required included Asset becomes:

- revoked,

- superseded,

- rights-ineligible,

- or Consent-invalid.

20.565 Package Rebuild

Invalidated Packages shall be rebuilt from current eligible Asset Versions before reuse.

20.566 Archival Package

An Archival Package preserves exact canonical production state for future reconstruction.

20.567 Archive Content

Archive may include:

- accepted source Assets,

- Master Assets,

- Package Manifest,

- Production Receipt,

- Evaluation Records,

- and required provenance.

20.568 Archive Does Not Require Every Intermediate

Retention policy may omit low-value temporary Candidates.

20.569 Human-Assisted Production

A multimodal workflow may contain human-assisted execution where automation is unavailable, unsafe or economically undesirable.

20.570 Human-Assisted Step

A Human-Assisted Step shall identify:

- operator,

- instructions,

- Input Assets,

- Account,

- expected Output,

- cost,

- evidence,

- and completion criteria.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.571 Human-Assisted Provider

A Provider accessible only through a manual web interface may still participate as a governed resource.

20.572 Manual Provider Job

A manual Provider job should preserve any available:

- native job ID,

- settings,

- Provider workspace,

- screenshot,

- receipt,

- and resulting Asset.

20.573 Manual Evidence

Manual execution shall preserve enough evidence to establish what was done without requiring surveillance of every human action.

20.574 Human-Assisted Cost

External credits and human time may both contribute to estimated production cost.

20.575 Manual Account Verification

The human operator shall confirm the intended external Account before consequential use.

20.576 Human Error Recovery

Manual errors shall enter the same revision and Incident architecture rather than being hidden.

20.577 Manual QA

Stage 1 shall require manual QA before public publication of generated creative media.

20.578 Human Creative Authority

Human creative review shall remain available even when automated evaluators improve.

20.579 Cost

Multimodal production cost aggregates every paid or materially consumed production Step.

20.580 Production Cost Estimate

A Production Cost Estimate shall account for expected:

- generations,

- Candidates,

- retries,

- renders,

- Voice characters,

- video duration,

- storage,

- human work,

- and external credits.

20.581 Cost Per Accepted Asset

Cost efficiency should consider cost per accepted Asset rather than cost per raw generation alone.

20.582 Candidate Waste

Rejected Candidates contribute real cost and should influence future optimisation.

20.583 Selective Revision Economics

Selective regeneration may reduce cost compared with full production restart.

20.584 Local Production Cost

Local production may include:

- GPU use,

- CPU use,

- power,

- storage,

- and opportunity cost.

20.585 Human Review Cost

Human review may be represented as time or financial cost where relevant.

20.586 Budget

Every bounded production workflow shall remain within its approved Budget.

20.587 Candidate Budget

Candidate count may have its own Budget allowance.

20.588 Revision Budget

Revision loops may have independent retry or spend ceilings.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.589 Render Budget

High-cost renders should not begin while cheaper review proxies remain unresolved.

20.590 Budget Escalation

A required increase shall pause and request authority rather than being silently absorbed.

20.591 Cost Forecast Update

Cost forecasts should update after:

- Candidate rejection,

- Provider fallback,

- scope expansion,

- or render changes.

20.592 Latency

Multimodal production latency may span seconds, minutes, hours or human turnaround.

20.593 Production Deadline

A Production Project or Unit may define a hard or soft deadline.

20.594 Critical Path

The Production Graph should identify Steps controlling expected completion time.

20.595 Parallelism

Independent Steps may execute in parallel when Budget and continuity allow.

20.596 Provider Queue Time

Provider queue delay shall remain distinct from actual generation time.

20.597 Human Queue Time

Human review delay shall remain observable.

20.598 Render Time

Rendering latency shall be observable separately from generation latency.

20.599 Capacity

Production may depend on:

- Provider quotas,

- GPU capacity,

- local storage,

- rendering workers,

- human reviewers,

- and API rate limits.

20.600 Production Scheduling

Scheduling shall account for dependencies, deadlines, capacity and authority.

20.601 Batch Scheduling

Batching should not delay urgent work merely to maximise efficiency.

20.602 Priority

Priority may derive from:

- user deadline,

- publication schedule,

- Project importance,

- dependency criticality,

- or Incident recovery.

20.603 Reliability

Multimodal production shall assume partial failure.

20.604 Partial Failure

One Scene, Candidate, Voice Segment, Render or upload may fail while other production units succeed.

20.605 Partial Success Preservation

Successful unaffected outputs should remain preserved when safe.

20.606 Generation Retry

Generation retries shall create new Attempts.

20.607 Transformation Retry

Transformation retries shall preserve exact source Version and change scope.

20.608 Render Retry

A Render retry may reuse the same accepted Composition when failure was purely technical.

20.609 Provider Fallback

Fallback may switch Provider only when:

- Capability remains compatible,

- data remains eligible,

- Budget remains valid,

- rights remain valid,

- and continuity risks are acceptable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.610 Creative Fallback Risk

Switching creative Providers may change style or Character identity even when the same nominal Capability is supported.

20.611 Fallback Evaluation

Creative fallback should receive stronger comparison and continuity review.

20.612 Async Production Job

Long-running Provider generation shall use canonical asynchronous job handling.

20.613 Provider Job Acceptance

Provider acceptance shall not mean Candidate availability.

20.614 Expiring Provider Result

Temporary media URLs shall be ingested durably before expiry.

20.615 Unknown Production Outcome

Timeout after submission may leave the job outcome unknown.

20.616 Unknown Outcome Retry

Unknown side-effect or paid generation status shall be reconciled before retry where duplication matters.

20.617 Duplicate Candidate

Duplicate callbacks shall not create duplicate canonical Candidate identities for the same Provider result.

20.618 Production Reconciliation

A Reconciler shall identify:

- orphan Provider jobs,

- missing Assets,

- incomplete ingest,

- unknown cost,

- and stale workflow state.

20.619 Production Checkpoint Recovery

Recovery should resume from the most recent valid Checkpoint rather than restarting all production.

20.620 Provider Cancellation

Cancellation requested shall remain distinct from confirmed cancellation.

20.621 Cancelled Job Asset

A Provider may still produce an Output after cancellation request.

The result shall be reconciled and governed.

20.622 Production Incident

A Production Incident is a material production failure affecting:

- safety,

- rights,

- data,

- cost,

- publication,

- identity,

- or operational integrity.

20.623 Production Incident Examples

Examples include:

- wrong Character published,

- wrong Account used,

- private reference leaked,

- invalid rights,

- duplicate publication,

- runaway generation cost,

- or corrupted Master Asset.

20.624 Security

Multimodal production processes untrusted Inputs and complex files and shall apply security controls throughout the pipeline.

20.625 Untrusted Media

Uploaded or Provider-generated files shall be treated as untrusted until validated.

20.626 File Validation

Validation may include:

- content-type verification,

- size,

- dimensions,

- codec,

- decompression limits,

- and malware scanning where applicable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.627 Malicious Metadata

Embedded metadata shall not be treated as trusted instructions.

20.628 Prompt Injection in References

Text embedded in documents, webpages or images shall not override Fabric policy.

20.629 Tool Injection

Generated files shall not automatically trigger scripts, macros or external actions.

20.630 Document Macro

Macro-enabled documents require explicit handling policy.

20.631 SVG Security

SVG and other active formats may contain scripts or external references and require safe processing.

20.632 Media Parser Risk

Complex codecs and parsers should run inside appropriately isolated execution boundaries.

20.633 External URL Fetch

Provider result or reference URLs shall be validated before privileged download.

20.634 Reference URL Expiry

A temporary reference URL shall not become canonical identity.

20.635 Privacy

Multimodal production may contain highly sensitive visual, audio and contextual data.

20.636 Privacy-Minimised Production

Only required media and context shall be sent to each production resource.

20.637 Child Media

Child images, Voice or identifying information require stronger privacy and Consent governance.

20.638 Private Photo

A private user photo used as reference shall remain protected according to its Classification and intended purpose.

20.639 Provider Retention

Provider retention and training settings shall influence whether sensitive references may be uploaded.

20.640 Local Only Media

Local Only media shall not be sent to external Providers.

20.641 Derived Sensitive Asset

A generated derivative may remain sensitive because it reveals or depicts protected source information.

20.642 Metadata Privacy

Image, audio and video metadata may reveal:

- location,

- device,

- creator,

- timestamps,

- or private filenames.

Metadata minimisation shall therefore be deliberate.

20.643 Privacy in Review

Human reviewers shall receive only production context necessary for review.

20.644 Rights Integration

Chapter 21 governs canonical rights semantics.

This chapter shall preserve the hooks needed to prevent rights context from being lost during production.

20.645 Rights Before Production

Source and reference rights shall be evaluated before uses requiring such permission.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.646 Rights During Transformation

A transformation does not erase source rights obligations.

20.647 Rights During Composition

Composite Outputs inherit relevant constraints from included components.

20.648 Rights Before Publication

Publication Packages shall fail eligibility when mandatory rights remain unresolved.

20.649 Consent Integration

Consent shall remain linked to every use of protected likeness, Voice or personal data.

20.650 Consent Revocation

Revocation may invalidate:

- reference use,

- further generation,

- accepted Assets,

- Packages,

- or publication.

The affected scope shall be reviewed.

20.651 Synthetic Media

Generated or materially altered media shall retain appropriate synthetic-media classification and disclosure information.

20.652 Disclosure

Required disclosures shall be included in:

- visible content,

- metadata,

- caption,

- or publication package

according to policy.

20.653 Documentary Evidence Boundary

Generated or reconstructed media shall not be represented as unaltered documentary evidence.

20.654 Provenance

Every meaningful production Asset shall preserve production provenance.

20.655 Provenance Chain

The chain may include:

- source Asset,

- reference Asset,

- Prompt Specification,

- Provider prompt,

- Model,

- Adapter,

- Attempt,

- transformation,

- composition,

- render,

- human edit,

- and acceptance.

20.656 Human Contribution

Human creative edits shall be represented where material to provenance or rights.

20.657 Provider Contribution

Provider involvement shall remain attributable without making the Provider the owner of canonical creative identity.

20.658 Local Tool Contribution

Local transformations shall remain visible in provenance where they materially affect the Asset.

20.659 Composition Provenance

A composite shall preserve lineage for every material component.

20.660 Render Provenance

Render provenance shall link the exact Composition Version and Render Profile.

20.661 Production Evidence

Production Evidence shall remain distinct from ordinary logs.

20.662 Evidence Package

A Production Evidence Package may link:

- Request,

- Plan,

- Attempts,

- Assets,

- Provider jobs,

- evaluations,

- approvals,

- cost,

- and completion verification.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.663 Memory Integration

Multimodal production shall not dump prompts, Candidates or review chatter wholesale into permanent Memory.

20.664 Derived Creative Learning

Repeated reviewed findings may become Derived Learning such as:

- one Provider preserves Nova’s identity better for one task,

- one aspect ratio requires different framing,

- or one Voice setting improves pronunciation.

20.665 Learning Scope

Creative learning shall remain:

- Project-scoped,

- Capability-scoped,

- evidence-linked,

- and challengeable.

20.666 Character Memory

Canonical Character identity belongs in governed Character and Asset objects rather than informal Model conversation history.

20.667 Voice Memory

Canonical Voice identity belongs in Voice Profiles and Consent records rather than Provider Session history.

20.668 Style Memory

Style should remain Versioned in the Style System rather than relying on previous prompts.

20.669 Observability

Multimodal production shall be observable across the full Production Graph.

20.670 Production Correlation

Correlation should connect:

- Production Project,

- Production Unit,

- Plan,

- Step,

- Attempt,

- Provider job,

- Asset,

- Evaluation,

- and Package.

20.671 Production Metrics

Metrics may include:

- generation count,

- Candidate acceptance rate,

- retry rate,

- cost per accepted Asset,

- render latency,

- Provider failure,

- continuity failure,

- human review time,

- and publication readiness.

20.672 Quality Metrics

Quality metrics should be task-specific and shall not be reduced to one universal score.

20.673 Cost Metrics

Cost should distinguish:

- Provider,

- Modality,

- Project,

- Production Unit,

- Candidate,

- and accepted Deliverable.

20.674 Drift Metrics

Repeated Character, Voice or Style drift may trigger review of:

- Provider,

- Prompt Compiler,

- Reference Set,

- or Specification.

20.675 Audit

Material production Decisions shall be auditable.

20.676 Auditable Production Events

Audit should cover:

- Character canon change,

- Voice Profile change,

- reference replacement,

- acceptance,

- rights override,

- publication approval,

- Package change,

- and destructive Asset removal.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.677 Production API

The Fabric should expose canonical APIs or equivalent interfaces for multimodal production.

20.678 Production API Operations

Operations may include:

- create Production Project,

- create Production Specification,

- create Production Graph,

- submit Generation Request,

- submit Transformation Request,

- inspect Candidate Set,

- create Selection Decision,

- request Revision,

- render,

- accept Asset,

- create Package,

- and inspect Evidence.

20.679 Provider Independence

The Production API shall not require Provider-native prompt or job objects from ordinary consumers.

20.680 Provider Extension

Provider-specific capabilities may be exposed through optional typed extension metadata without corrupting the canonical core.

20.681 Stage 1 Objective

Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy multimodal production architecture required for current Omnira Projects.

20.682 Stage 1 Modalities

Stage 1 should support at minimum:

- text,

- image,

- Voice,

- document or file Assets,

- and basic composition metadata.

20.683 Stage 1 Deferred Full Video

Advanced video orchestration may remain partially manual or experimental in Stage 1.

The canonical objects shall still support later integration.

20.684 Stage 1 Production Objects

Stage 1 shall implement at minimum:

- Production Project,

- Production Specification,

- Creative Brief,

- Character Profile or Definition,

- Voice Profile or Definition,

- Prompt Specification,

- Generation Request,

- Candidate,

- Candidate Set,

- Selection Decision,

- Technical Specification,

- Production Package,

- and Production Receipt.

20.685 Stage 1 Asset Integration

Every generated output shall enter the canonical Asset and provenance architecture.

20.686 Stage 1 Character References

Familje-Stunden Character reference Assets shall be exact Versioned Inputs.

20.687 Stage 1 Voice

ElevenLabs or an approved replacement may provide the first production Voice path.

20.688 Stage 1 Image

OpenArt may participate as Human-Assisted production where automation is unavailable or unsuitable.

20.689 Stage 1 Automated Image

Ideogram or another suitable image Provider may provide an automated image generation path.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.690 Stage 1 Provider Prompt Compilation

Provider prompts shall derive from canonical Production Specifications rather than being the only source of creative truth.

20.691 Stage 1 Manual QA

Generated public-facing creative media shall receive human QA before publication.

20.692 Stage 1 Publication Separation

Production completion shall not automatically publish.

20.693 Stage 1 Cost

Candidate generation and revisions shall remain Budget-bounded.

20.694 Stage 1 Async

Long-running generation jobs shall use durable asynchronous state.

20.695 Stage 1 Provenance

Every accepted Asset shall preserve exact production lineage.

20.696 Stage 1 Rights and Consent

Rights and Consent shall be checked before public or commercial use.

20.697 Stage 1 Test — Production Specification

Tests shall verify:

1. Production Specification has stable identity.

2. Production Version is immutable after dispatch.

3. audience is explicit.

4. purpose is explicit.

5. Modality is explicit.

6. Character references are exact.

7. technical requirements are explicit.

8. Budget is explicit.

9. Quality requirements are explicit.

10. missing mandatory Input blocks dispatch.

20.698 Stage 1 Test — Prompt Compilation

Tests shall verify:

1. canonical Prompt Specification exists.

2. Provider prompt is derived.

3. Character requirements survive compilation.

4. Style requirements survive compilation.

5. negative constraints survive compilation.

6. unsupported Provider semantics are reported.

7. Provider parameters validate.

8. external reference text cannot alter policy.

9. compilation receipt links source requirements.

10. Provider prompt does not become canonical creative truth.

20.699 Stage 1 Test — Candidate Sets

Tests shall verify:

1. every Candidate has identity.

2. every Candidate has provenance.

3. Candidate Set has identity.

4. Candidate count is Budget-bounded.

5. selection is attributable.

6. ranking is distinct from acceptance.

7. rejected Candidates cannot publish.

8. near-duplicate Candidates can be detected where required.

9. selected Candidate remains Version-specific.

10. selection reversal preserves history.

20.700 Stage 1 Test — Character Continuity

Tests shall verify:

1. Character has canonical identity.

2. Character Version is explicit.

3. reference Assets are exact Versions.

4. Provider ID does not replace Character identity.

5. facial identity is reviewed.

6. proportions are reviewed.

7. clothing rules are reviewed.

8. multi-Character relationships are reviewed.

9. Character drift creates findings.

10. failed identity blocks acceptance when mandatory.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.701 Stage 1 Test — Voice

Tests shall verify:

1. Voice has canonical identity.

2. Voice Version is explicit.

3. Provider Voice ID remains mapping only.

4. Script Version is exact.

5. Consent is valid.

6. pronunciation is evaluated.

7. Voice continuity is evaluated.

8. generated audio becomes Asset.

9. cost is recorded.

10. Project boundary prevents unapproved Voice reuse.

20.702 Stage 1 Test — Images

Tests shall verify:

1. generation uses canonical Specification.

2. Candidate Assets are Versioned.

3. dimensions validate.

4. format validates.

5. Character identity can be evaluated.

6. exact text errors can block acceptance.

7. edits create new Version.

8. source Asset remains linked.

9. rights remain linked.

10. accepted image is distinct from generated output.

20.703 Stage 1 Test — Documents

Tests shall verify:

1. exact page size.

2. page count.

3. safe margins.

4. fonts.

5. image integrity.

6. links.

7. selectable text where required.

8. accessibility requirements.

9. accepted source and PDF remain linked.

10. export failure does not overwrite accepted source.

20.704 Stage 1 Test — Async Production

Tests shall verify:

1. Provider job has durable handle.

2. acceptance is not completion.

3. callback duplication is idempotent.

4. polling works.

5. temporary result is ingested.

6. timeout can create unknown state.

7. reconciliation exists.

8. cost is reconciled.

9. cancelled does not equal cancellation requested.

10. orphan jobs are detected.

20.705 Stage 1 Test — Selective Revision

Tests shall verify:

1. Revision Request has exact target.

2. preservation requirements are explicit.

3. allowed change is explicit.

4. source Version remains intact.

5. new Candidate receives provenance.

6. downstream impact is calculated.

7. unaffected Assets remain accepted.

8. revision cost is bounded.

9. repeated failure escalates.

10. acceptance binds the revised Version.

20.706 Stage 1 Test — Packages

Tests shall verify:

1. Package has stable identity and Version.

2. Manifest contains exact Asset Versions.

3. checksums exist where required.

4. rights are current.

5. Consent is current.

6. Classification permits intended use.

7. approval binds exact Package.

8. mutable “latest” references are absent.

9. invalidated Asset invalidates Package.

10. Package does not publish by itself.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 20.708 Applied Example — Nova and Pling Image
20.709 Applied Example — Nova and Pling Video
20.713 Applied Example — The Prompt News Visual
text:
20.707 Applied Example — Familje-Stunden Monthly Theme

A monthly Familje-Stunden Production Project may contain:

- Story,

- illustrations,

- audio narration,

- printable activities,

- previews,

- social Assets,

- and final Package.

Every component remains Project-scoped and Versioned.

20.708 Applied Example — Nova and Pling Image

A Scene requires Nova and Pling in a school-start environment.

The Fabric uses:

- exact Character Versions,

- approved Reference Sets,

- Scene Specification,

- Style System,

- negative constraints,

- and image Provider capability.

Generated Outputs become Candidates.

Human review selects and accepts one Candidate.

20.709 Applied Example — Nova and Pling Video

An approved Nova and Pling hero image is animated.

The source image remains canonical.

Image-to-Video creates a new Candidate Asset.

Evaluation checks:

- facial identity,

- body consistency,

- unintended morphing,

- motion,

- child-safe behaviour,

- and loop or duration requirements.

20.710 Applied Example — Familje-Stunden Voice Story

An accepted Story Script is segmented.

Each segment uses the approved narrator Voice Profile.

Generated audio is evaluated for:

- pronunciation,

- tone,

- continuity,

- artefacts,

- and child suitability.

Accepted Segments are composed into one narration Master.

20.711 Applied Example — Diploma PDF

A diploma Production Unit combines:

- background Asset,

- child name,

- date,

- typography,

- layout,

- and export profile.

Dynamic personalisation remains separate from the immutable background design.

The final issued diploma becomes its own exact Asset Version.

20.712 Applied Example — The Prompt

A The Prompt production workflow may contain:

- source research,

- Script,

- visual Brief,

- image Candidate,

- Voice,

- short video,

- caption,

- thumbnail,

- and publication Package.

Source evidence remains distinct from generated creative media.

20.713 Applied Example — The Prompt News Visual

A generated visual representing a news topic shall not masquerade as original documentary photography.

Synthetic-media disclosure and source relationships remain explicit.

20.714 Applied Example — GainPilot Exercise Demo

An exercise demonstration Asset may contain:

- exercise definition,

- body positioning,

- movement phases,

- visual animation,

- instructional text,

- and Voice.

Biomechanical correctness becomes a mandatory Quality criterion.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 20.722 Anti-Pattern — Provider Workspace Is Production Project
20.724 Anti-Pattern — Voice ID Is Voice Identity
text:
20.715 Applied Example — OpenArt Human-Assisted Production

OpenArt is used manually for one media task.

The Fabric creates a Human-Assisted Step containing:

- exact Brief,

- references,

- Project Account,

- credit limit,

- Output requirements,

- and evidence.

The resulting file is ingested into the Asset system.

The execution remains labelled human-assisted.

20.716 Applied Example — Ideogram Alternative

An automated image Provider becomes unavailable.

The Router may select another approved image Provider.

The fallback Candidate receives separate provenance and stronger identity/style review before acceptance.

20.717 Applied Example — ElevenLabs Timeout

A Voice generation request times out.

The Fabric does not immediately regenerate.

It checks Provider state first.

If the original generation succeeded, its audio is retrieved and ingested rather than paying for a duplicate Attempt.

20.718 Applied Example — Local Composition

Generated image, Voice and music Assets may be composed locally.

The local Tool creates:

- Timeline,

- Track relationships,

- Render Job,

- Master Asset,

- and provenance

without exposing source media to another external Provider.

20.719 Applied Example — Selective Revision

One Scene in a ten-Scene video contains a malformed hand.

The Revision Request targets that Shot.

The remaining nine accepted Scenes remain unchanged.

The Fabric regenerates only the defective component and downstream render.

20.720 Applied Example — Character Canon Change

Nova receives an intentionally updated seasonal outfit.

A new Character Version is created.

Future Production Specifications may use the new Version.

Historical Assets retain their original Character Version.

20.721 Anti-Pattern — Prompt Is Creative Canon

Prompts are execution artefacts.

Canonical creative truth belongs in structured Production objects.

20.722 Anti-Pattern — Provider Workspace Is Production Project

Provider workspaces may disappear or change.

Omnira retains canonical identity.

20.723 Anti-Pattern — Character Name Is Enough

Recurring visual identity requires Versioned canonical references.

20.724 Anti-Pattern — Voice ID Is Voice Identity

Provider IDs are implementation mappings.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 20.726 Anti-Pattern — Generated Output Is Automatically Asset
20.729 Anti-Pattern — Full Regeneration for Small Defect
20.733 Anti-Pattern — Temporary Result URL Is Master Asset
20.734 Anti-Pattern — Accepted Script Silently Rewritten Downstream
20.735 Anti-Pattern — Child-Facing Output Uses Ordinary Review Only
20.737 Anti-Pattern — Publication Package Uses Latest Assets
20.738 Anti-Pattern — Production History Becomes Permanent Memory
text:
20.725 Anti-Pattern — Reference Image Means Rights

Rights and Consent remain separate.

20.726 Anti-Pattern — Generated Output Is Automatically Asset

Outputs require ingestion and provenance.

20.727 Anti-Pattern — Asset Is Automatically Accepted

Quality and governance remain required.

20.728 Anti-Pattern — Successful Render Means Done

Technical success is only one completion dimension.

20.729 Anti-Pattern — Full Regeneration for Small Defect

Selective revision should be used when dependencies permit.

20.730 Anti-Pattern — Unlimited Candidate Generation

Creative exploration remains Budget-bounded.

20.731 Anti-Pattern — Provider Fallback Ignores Continuity

Equivalent Capability does not imply equivalent creative identity.

20.732 Anti-Pattern — Human-Assisted Work Hidden

Manual execution shall remain explicit.

20.733 Anti-Pattern — Temporary Result URL Is Master Asset

Durable ingestion is required.

20.734 Anti-Pattern — Accepted Script Silently Rewritten Downstream

Canonical text Versions must remain exact.

20.735 Anti-Pattern — Child-Facing Output Uses Ordinary Review Only

Audience risk shall influence Quality and Approval.

20.736 Anti-Pattern — Composite Loses Source Lineage

Every material component shall remain attributable.

20.737 Anti-Pattern — Publication Package Uses Latest Assets

Exact Versions are required.

20.738 Anti-Pattern — Production History Becomes Permanent Memory

Evidence and Memory remain separate.

20.739 Canonical Multimodal Production Contract

The following requirements define Multimodal Production:

1. Every governed Production Project SHALL have stable identity.

2. every material Production Unit SHALL have stable identity.

3. every executable Production Specification SHALL have Version.

4. Creative Brief SHALL remain distinct from Provider prompt.

5. Provider prompt SHALL derive from canonical requirements.

6. every generated Candidate SHALL have provenance.

7. Character identity SHALL remain canonical and Provider-independent.

8. Voice identity SHALL remain canonical and Provider-independent.

9. references SHALL use exact Asset Versions.

10. reference use SHALL remain rights- and Consent-governed.

11. Generation, Transformation, Composition, Render, Acceptance and Publication SHALL remain distinct.

12. Production Graph dependencies SHALL be explicit.

13. iterations SHALL remain bounded.

14. Quality SHALL be evaluated before acceptance.

15. accepted Assets SHALL remain Version-specific.

16. composite Assets SHALL preserve source lineage.

17. Packages SHALL contain exact Asset Versions.

18. publication SHALL remain separately authorised.

19. human-assisted Steps SHALL remain truthful.

20. Multimodal production SHALL remain Provider-independent above Adapter boundaries.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.740 Canonical Character and Voice Contract

The following requirements define recurring creative identity:

1. Every governed Character SHALL have stable identity.

2. material design changes SHALL create Character Version.

3. Character Reference Sets SHALL be Versioned.

4. recurring production SHALL reference exact Character Version.

5. Provider prompts SHALL NOT become Character identity.

6. Character names SHALL NOT substitute for references where visual continuity matters.

7. every governed Voice SHALL have stable identity.

8. material Voice changes SHALL create Voice Version.

9. Provider Voice IDs SHALL remain mappings.

10. Voice use SHALL preserve rights and Consent.

11. Voice cloning SHALL require explicit authority.

12. Character and Voice continuity SHALL be evaluated.

13. drift SHALL be recorded.

14. mandatory identity failure SHALL block acceptance.

15. Character Assets SHALL remain Project-scoped unless reuse is authorised.

16. Voice Assets SHALL remain Project-scoped unless reuse is authorised.

17. Model change SHALL NOT change canonical Character identity.

18. Provider change SHALL NOT change canonical Voice identity automatically.

19. historical production SHALL preserve the Versions actually used.

20. Creative identity SHALL remain owned by the Project rather than the Provider.

20.741 Canonical Prompt and Generation Contract

The following requirements define generative production:

1. Every persistent Prompt Specification SHALL have identity and Version.

2. Prompt Specification SHALL derive from Production Specification.

3. positive requirements SHALL be explicit.

4. negative constraints SHALL be explicit.

5. references SHALL be explicit.

6. Provider prompts SHALL be compiled through Adapter mappings.

7. compilation SHALL preserve source traceability.

8. unsupported semantics SHALL be reported.

9. Provider parameters SHALL validate.

10. Provider defaults SHALL NOT silently become canonical creative Decisions.

11. Seed SHALL NOT be treated as guaranteed reproducibility.

12. every Generation Request SHALL have stable identity.

13. Candidate count SHALL be bounded.

14. every Candidate SHALL have stable identity.

15. every Candidate SHALL preserve exact execution provenance.

16. ranking SHALL remain distinct from acceptance.

17. generated text in imagery SHALL receive visual validation where exact wording matters.

18. Provider output SHALL NOT become final merely because generation succeeded.

19. fallback generation SHALL preserve mandatory constraints.

20. Generative flexibility SHALL NOT override canonical creative requirements.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 20.743 Canonical Quality, Revision and Acceptance Contract
text:
20.742 Canonical Composition and Render Contract

The following requirements define Composition and Render:

1. Every governed Composition SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. every material source shall reference exact Asset Version.

3. layer ordering SHALL be explicit.

4. Timeline SHALL have stable identity and Version.

5. Tracks SHALL remain typed and attributable.

6. Clips SHALL reference exact source Asset Versions.

7. timing SHALL be explicit.

8. synchronisation SHALL be explicit where required.

9. Render Request SHALL identify exact Composition Version.

10. Render Profile SHALL be Versioned.

11. Render Job SHALL have stable identity.

12. render success SHALL remain distinct from production acceptance.

13. Review Proxy SHALL remain distinct from Master.

14. Master SHALL remain distinct from Distribution Rendition.

15. Renditions SHALL link to exact Master Version.

16. technical validation SHALL follow render.

17. source lineage SHALL survive composition.

18. local composition SHALL remain governed.

19. re-rendering SHALL preserve exact accepted source state.

20. Composition SHALL NOT hide component rights, provenance or Classification.

20.743 Canonical Quality, Revision and Acceptance Contract

The following requirements define production Quality:

1. Every material production class SHALL define Quality criteria.

2. mandatory criteria SHALL be explicit.

3. deterministic validation SHALL be used where possible.

4. Model-assisted evaluation SHALL be attributable.

5. human review SHALL be attributable.

6. Character continuity SHALL be evaluated where required.

7. Voice continuity SHALL be evaluated where required.

8. cross-modal consistency SHALL be evaluated where required.

9. inconclusive evaluation SHALL NOT equal pass.

10. mandatory failure SHALL block acceptance.

11. every Revision Request SHALL identify exact target Version.

12. revision SHALL define preservation and allowed change.

13. selective revision SHOULD be preferred where appropriate.

14. revised Assets SHALL preserve source lineage.

15. revision loops SHALL be bounded.

16. every Acceptance Decision SHALL bind exact Version.

17. internal acceptance SHALL NOT imply publication eligibility.

18. acceptance MAY be revoked.

19. historical acceptance Decisions SHALL remain preserved.

20. Quality SHALL NOT be inferred solely from Provider reputation or technical success.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 20.744 Canonical Production Package and Publication Handoff Contract
text:
20.744 Canonical Production Package and Publication Handoff Contract

The following requirements define delivery packaging:

1. Every Production Package SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Package Manifest SHALL identify exact Asset Versions.

3. mutable latest references SHALL be prohibited where exact delivery matters.

4. checksums SHOULD be preserved where applicable.

5. rights state SHALL be current.

6. Consent state SHALL be current.

7. Classification SHALL permit intended use.

8. attribution requirements SHALL be represented.

9. disclosure requirements SHALL be represented.

10. exact target Account SHALL be explicit for publication Packages.

11. exact channel SHALL be explicit.

12. publication metadata SHALL be Versioned with the Package.

13. Package creation SHALL NOT publish.

14. Publication Handoff SHALL require current authority.

15. scheduled publication SHALL revalidate current state.

16. invalidated Asset SHALL invalidate affected Package.

17. Package rebuild SHALL create new Version.

18. publication result SHALL be externally verified where practical.

19. archive SHALL preserve exact delivered state.

20. Packaging SHALL NOT bypass Quality, rights, Consent or Approval.

20.745 Multimodal Production Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No Production Project without identity.

- No Production Specification without purpose and audience.

- No Provider workspace becomes canonical Project truth.

- No Character without canonical identity.

- No Character identity defined only by a name or prompt.

- No Voice identity defined only by a Provider ID.

- No Voice cloning without explicit authority and Consent.

- No Prompt as the sole source of creative truth.

- No Candidate without provenance.

- No generated Output automatically becomes accepted Asset.

- No reference Asset treated as permission.

- No transformation without exact source Version.

- No Composition without source lineage.

- No Timeline without exact Asset references.

- No Render without exact Composition Version and Render Profile.

- No technical success treated as creative acceptance.

- No mandatory Quality failure hidden by aggregate score.

- No unbounded creative retry.

- No fallback outside privacy, rights, Quality and Budget constraints.

- No Local Only media sent externally.

- No child-facing public media without stronger review.

- No Human-Assisted Step represented as autonomous execution.

- No Production Package with mutable unknown Asset Versions.

- No publication handoff without current authority.

- No production evidence dumped wholesale into permanent Memory.

- No Provider becomes the owner of Character, Voice, Style or Project identity.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
20.746 Closing Statement

Multimodal production is where intelligence becomes visible, audible, interactive and publishable.

It is also where weak architecture becomes expensive.

A single creative deliverable may pass through:

- Scripts,

- references,

- Models,

- Providers,

- human operators,

- generation systems,

- editing systems,

- local Tools,

- Voice services,

- renderers,

- evaluation systems,

- Asset stores,

- and publication platforms.

Without canonical structure, every one of those systems can become an accidental source of truth.

The Creative Brief preserves intent.

The Audience Profile defines who the production exists for.

The Brand System preserves Project identity.

The Style System preserves recurring creative language.

The Character Definition preserves recurring visual identity.

The Voice Definition preserves recurring spoken identity.

The Production Specification converts creative intent into an executable canonical contract.

The Prompt Specification translates that contract toward generative resources without making prompts the owner of creative truth.

The Production Graph makes dependencies explicit.

The Candidate Set makes stochastic generation reviewable.

The Selection Decision makes creative choice attributable.

The Continuity Profile and Continuity Ledger preserve identity and state across scenes, pages, episodes and campaigns.

The Timeline and Composition make multimodal assembly explicit.

The Render Profile makes technical delivery reproducible.

The Quality system determines whether an Output is actually suitable.

The Revision architecture allows defects to be corrected without destroying accepted work.

The Asset system makes temporary Provider results durable.

The provenance system preserves how each Asset came into existence.

The rights and Consent systems determine whether an Asset may be used.

The Production Package binds exact approved Asset Versions for delivery.

The Publication Handoff preserves the boundary between production and consequence.

For Familje-Stunden, this architecture allows Nova and Pling to remain the same Characters across:

- illustrations,

- Stories,

- monthly themes,

- animation,

- Voice,

- printable material,

- social content,

- and future video.

Their identity does not belong to OpenArt.

It does not belong to Ideogram.

It does not belong to one prompt.

It does not belong to one image file.

It belongs to the Project’s governed Character canon.

For The Prompt, this architecture allows:

- research,

- Script,

- visuals,

- Voice,

- video,

- thumbnails,

- captions,

- and publication Packages

to form one production system without confusing generated creative media with source evidence.

For GainPilot, the same architecture can govern:

- exercise illustrations,

- instructional animation,

- coaching Voice,

- structured programme documents,

- and future interactive exercise experiences

while requiring biomechanical correctness and privacy appropriate to the Project.

For Atlas, multimodal production becomes a Capability it can orchestrate without memorising the quirks of every creative Provider.

Atlas expresses:

- what is needed,

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
- why it is needed,

- who it is for,

- which identity must remain stable,

- which constraints matter,

- and what acceptance means.

The Fabric determines how that production should be implemented.

No production without a Brief.

No Brief without an audience and purpose.

No character without canonical identity.

No Voice without a Profile and authority.

No Scene without a Specification.

No Candidate without provenance.

No composite without source lineage.

No render without technical validation.

No acceptance without Quality evidence.

No Package without exact Asset Versions.

No publication handoff without approved scope.

The user retains creative direction.

The Project retains identity.

Omnira retains governance.

The Fabric turns many modalities into one coherent production without allowing any Provider, prompt or file to become the owner of creative truth.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical architecture, object model, lifecycle, governance boundaries, evidence requirements and conformance rules for Assets, provenance, ownership, custody, licensing, rights, consent, attribution, permitted use, reuse, distribution and synthetic-media disclosure within the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

It establishes:

- how Outputs become governed Assets,

- how source, reference, intermediate, derivative, master, distribution and archive Assets remain distinct,

- how Asset identity remains independent from filenames, URLs, storage paths and Provider IDs,

- how Asset Versions, Renditions, Representations and Packages are modelled,

- how integrity, checksums, manifests and chain of custody are preserved,

- how Asset storage, replication, movement, retention, deletion and recovery remain governed,

- how production lineage becomes machine-readable provenance,

- how execution provenance remains distinct from legal ownership,

- how rights claims, licences, grants, restrictions, terms and policy interact,

- how Provider terms are captured at the exact time and scope of use,

- how commercial-use eligibility is determined,

- how attribution obligations remain attached to Assets and Deliverables,

- how derivative, modification, adaptation, distribution, sublicensing and training rights remain explicit,

- how public-domain, open-licensed, stock, commissioned, user-owned, Provider-generated and unknown-rights Assets remain distinguishable,

- how consent for voice, likeness, image, personal data and performance is represented,

- how consent remains purpose-, Project-, audience-, channel-, territory- and time-bounded,

- how minor and guardian consent require stronger controls,

- how consent revocation affects future and existing use,

- how identity, authority and consent remain separate,

- how possession of media does not prove permission,

- how publication readiness requires both production acceptance and rights eligibility,

- how synthetic and generated media may require disclosure or labelling,

- how watermarks, metadata, signatures and content credentials are preserved,

- how cross-Project reuse remains controlled,

- how training, fine-tuning, indexing, retrieval and memory use require separate rights analysis,

- how human and AI contributions remain attributable,

- how rights uncertainty is represented without fabrication,

- how disputed Assets are quarantined,

- how incidents involving infringement, unauthorised likeness, missing consent or broken lineage are contained,

- and how Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy Asset, provenance, rights and consent foundation.

An Output is not automatically an Asset.

An Asset is not automatically owned by the Project.

Possession is not ownership.

Ownership is not permission for every use.

A licence is not consent.

Consent is not copyright ownership.

A Provider’s technical ability to generate content does not prove that the resulting use is lawful or permitted.

A valid Credential does not prove rights.

A generated image is not automatically commercially usable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
A reference Asset is not automatically reusable outside its approved purpose.

A public URL is not proof of public-domain status.

A watermark is not the complete rights state.

A missing rights record is not permission.

An Asset accepted for internal review is not automatically eligible for publication.

A historical licence does not necessarily cover a new channel, territory or audience.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

Execution evidence, Decision Evidence, Derived Learning and Governed Memory are expanded in Chapter 22.

Implementation and legal conformance must be verified separately.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 21.2 Purpose of Asset and Rights Governance
text:
21.2 Purpose of Asset and Rights Governance

The Intelligence Fabric may create, receive, transform, store and distribute:

- text,

- code,

- images,

- graphics,

- documents,

- audio,

- Voices,

- music,

- video,

- animations,

- datasets,

- prompts,

- templates,

- Models,

- Tool packages,

- manifests,

- captions,

- transcripts,

- and composite Deliverables.

Each item may have different:

- creators,

- owners,

- licensors,

- subjects,

- Providers,

- usage terms,

- consent requirements,

- territories,

- time limits,

- attribution duties,

- confidentiality,

- and downstream restrictions.

Without canonical governance, Omnira could:

- publish a draft rather than the accepted master,

- use a private family image as a public reference,

- reuse a Voice outside its consent scope,

- assume a generated Asset is commercially usable,

- remove required attribution,

- train on Project material without permission,

- mix Assets across Tenants,

- lose the source lineage of a final composite,

- delete the only canonical master,

- or continue using an Asset after consent revocation.

The architecture exists to make every meaningful Asset answer:

- What is this Asset?

- Which Version is it?

- Where did it come from?

- Who or what created it?

- Which Inputs and references contributed?

- Which transformations occurred?

- Which Provider, Model, Tool or human was involved?

- Who owns or claims rights?

- Which licence or grant applies?

- Which uses are permitted?

- Which uses are prohibited?

- Which attribution is required?

- Which consent supports identifiable people, Voices or performances?

- When do those permissions expire?

- Which Projects, channels, audiences and territories are covered?

- What happens if the rights or consent state changes?

21.3 Asset

An Asset is a governed, identifiable and durable unit of content, media, software, data or artefact that Omnira may store, reference, transform, evaluate, deliver or reuse.

An Asset shall have:

- stable identity,

- Version,

- ownership or custody metadata,

- classification,

- provenance,

- integrity evidence,

- lifecycle,

- and use eligibility.

21.4 Output

An Output is content or data produced by one Execution, Attempt, Provider job, Tool or human contribution.

An Output may become:

- rejected evidence,

- temporary intermediate,

- Candidate,

- or governed Asset.

Output identity and Asset identity shall remain distinct.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.5 Output-to-Asset Admission

An Output becomes a governed Asset only after required:

- retrieval,

- integrity validation,

- type validation,

- classification,

- provenance capture,

- storage,

- rights-state assignment,

- and lifecycle assignment.

21.6 Asset Is Not File

One Asset may have several files, Renditions or storage locations.

One file may be an implementation representation of one Asset Version.

File identity shall not replace Asset identity.

21.7 Asset Is Not URL

A URL is a location or access mechanism.

URLs may:

- expire,

- redirect,

- change,

- or disappear.

Canonical Asset identity shall remain independent.

21.8 Asset Is Not Filename

Filenames are human-readable labels.

They may be changed without changing the Asset.

21.9 Asset Is Not Storage Path

Storage paths are implementation details.

Moving an Asset shall not create a new Asset identity unless the content or governed meaning changes.

21.10 Asset Is Not Provider Object

A Provider Asset ID is an external identifier.

The canonical Asset remains Omnira-owned.

21.11 Asset Is Not Ownership

Asset registration records what exists.

It does not automatically determine who legally owns it.

21.12 Asset Is Not Rights Clearance

An Asset may exist in Omnira while its rights remain:

- unresolved,

- restricted,

- disputed,

- expired,

- or prohibited.

21.13 Asset Control Plane

The Asset Control Plane is the governed collection of services and canonical objects responsible for:

- Asset identity,

- Versioning,

- storage,

- integrity,

- metadata,

- Renditions,

- lineage,

- custody,

- retention,

- movement,

- deletion,

- recovery,

- packaging,

- rights,

- consent,

- disclosure,

- and eligibility.

It shall integrate with:

- Production,

- Execution,

- Provider and Model Registries,

- Quality,

- Identity,

- Data Classification,

- Policy,

- Cost,

- Publication,

- Search,

- Retrieval,

- Memory,

- Observability,

- and Incident Response.

21.14 Canonical Asset and Rights Objects

The canonical architecture should include or reference:

- Asset,

- Asset Version,

- Asset Representation,

- Asset Rendition,

- Asset Manifest,

- Asset Set,

- Asset Collection,

- Source Asset,

- Reference Asset,

- Intermediate Asset,

- Candidate Asset,

- Master Asset,

- Distribution Asset,

- Archive Asset,

- Temporary Asset,

- Quarantined Asset,

- Asset Location,

- Storage Object,

- Integrity Record,

- Checksum,

- Signature,

- Content Credential,

- Chain-of-Custody Record,

- Provenance Record,

- Provenance Relationship,

- Creation Record,

- Transformation Record,

- Contribution Record,

- Rights Profile,

- Rights Claim,

- Ownership Claim,

- Licence,

- Usage Grant,

- Restriction,

- Attribution Requirement,

- Terms Snapshot,

- Rights Decision,

- Consent Subject,

- Consent Grant,

- Guardian Authority,

- Revocation Record,

- Disclosure Requirement,

- Synthetic-Media Label,

- Rights Incident,

- and Asset Receipt.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.15 Asset Identity

Every Asset shall have stable canonical identity.

21.16 Asset Version

An Asset Version represents one materially distinct state of an Asset.

Changes requiring a new Version may include:

- content,

- structure,

- media samples,

- code,

- metadata affecting meaning,

- rights state,

- or accepted production status.

21.17 Asset Version Identity

Every Asset Version shall have stable identity.

21.18 Immutable Version

A released or accepted Asset Version shall not be edited in place.

Changes shall create a new Version.

21.19 Mutable Working State

An editing application may maintain mutable working state.

That state shall not replace canonical Versioning.

21.20 Asset Revision

A Revision records the change from one Version to another.

It shall preserve:

- prior Version,

- change reason,

- actor,

- Tool,

- time,

- and impact.

21.21 Asset Fork

A Fork creates a new lineage branch from an existing Asset Version.

Examples include:

- alternate language,

- different Project adaptation,

- experimental edit,

- or channel variant.

21.22 Asset Merge

A Merge combines contributions or branches.

The resulting Version shall preserve all contributing lineage.

21.23 Asset Representation

An Asset Representation is one encoded or structured representation of the same governed content.

Examples include:

- editable source,

- rendered file,

- thumbnail,

- proxy,

- waveform,

- transcript,

- or structured metadata.

21.24 Representation Identity

Every persistent Representation shall have stable identity.

21.25 Representation Equivalence

Representations may share semantic content while differing technically.

Equivalence shall be declared, not assumed.

21.26 Asset Rendition

A Rendition is a derived representation adapted for a particular technical or distribution purpose.

Examples include:

- low-resolution preview,

- web image,

- print image,

- portrait video,

- compressed audio,

- or captioned copy.

21.27 Rendition Identity

Every Rendition shall have stable identity.

21.28 Master Representation

The Master Representation is the highest-authority technical source for future derivatives.

It may be:

- editable,

- lossless,

- high resolution,

- or otherwise canonical.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.29 Distribution Representation

A Distribution Representation is prepared for a channel or recipient.

21.30 Proxy Representation

A Proxy is intended for review or low-cost processing.

It shall not become the master accidentally.

21.31 Thumbnail

A Thumbnail is a small visual representation for navigation.

It shall preserve its relationship to the source Asset.

21.32 Transcript Representation

A transcript may represent the spoken content of audio or video.

It is not identical to the source media.

21.33 Caption Representation

Captions include timing and accessibility information beyond plain transcript text.

21.34 Waveform Representation

A waveform supports audio navigation.

It does not replace the audio Asset.

21.35 Structured Representation

Structured metadata may represent:

- scenes,

- tracks,

- pages,

- segments,

- or annotations.

It shall identify the source Version.

21.36 Asset Type

Asset types may include:

- text,

- structured data,

- code,

- image,

- vector,

- document,

- audio,

- Voice,

- music,

- video,

- animation,

- 3D,

- Model,

- Tool package,

- dataset,

- manifest,

- template,

- and composite package.

21.37 Asset Media Type

Media type shall reflect the actual content.

Declared type and observed type may differ.

21.38 Asset Extension

File extension is a hint.

It shall not replace content validation.

21.39 Asset Schema

Structured Assets shall identify schema and schema Version.

21.40 Asset Language

Language shall be explicit where applicable.

21.41 Asset Audience

Audience restrictions may affect:

- child suitability,

- internal use,

- public use,

- or regulated distribution.

21.42 Asset Classification

Every Asset shall inherit or receive a Data Classification.

Classification may be:

- Public,

- Project Internal,

- Confidential,

- Local Only,

- or Prohibited.

21.43 Classification Inheritance

A derivative shall inherit the strongest relevant classification unless policy explicitly permits reduction after verified transformation.

21.44 Classification Reduction

Classification reduction requires:

- authorised transformation,

- validation,

- reason,

- and Decision.

21.45 Asset Owner

Asset Owner identifies the Principal or entity holding the canonical ownership relationship claimed or established inside Omnira.

Ownership claims may remain disputed or uncertain.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.46 Asset Custodian

The Custodian is responsible for holding or protecting the Asset.

Custody does not imply ownership.

21.47 Asset Controller

The Controller determines how the Asset may be used within a defined domain.

Control may derive from:

- ownership,

- licence,

- contract,

- role,

- or policy.

21.48 Asset Operator

The Operator performs storage, transformation or delivery actions.

Operation does not imply ownership.

21.49 Asset Subject

An Asset Subject is a person, character, organisation, object, location or concept represented in the Asset.

21.50 Human Subject

Assets containing identifiable humans may require:

- privacy review,

- likeness rights,

- consent,

- and restricted use.

21.51 Minor Subject

A minor subject requires stronger guardian, privacy and publication controls.

21.52 Fictional Subject

Fictional characters may still be protected by:

- copyright,

- trademark,

- contract,

- or Project policy.

21.53 Brand Subject

Logos, marks and trade dress may require separate rights analysis.

21.54 Asset Creator

Asset Creator identifies the person, Agent, Provider, Model, Tool or combination that produced the Asset or Output.

21.55 Human Creator

A human creator shall be represented as a Human Principal or external contributor.

21.56 Agent Creator

An Agent may be attributed as an orchestrating or contributing system.

The Agent remains distinct from the Model used.

21.57 Model Contribution

A Model may be recorded as a generation resource.

It does not become the legal owner by default.

21.58 Tool Contribution

A Tool may transform or compose an Asset.

Its Version shall remain in provenance.

21.59 Provider Contribution

The Provider supplied the execution environment or service.

Provider involvement does not by itself determine ownership.

21.60 Joint Contribution

One Asset may have several human and machine contributors.

21.61 Source Asset

A Source Asset is an Input whose content materially contributes to another Asset.

21.62 Source Asset Identity

The exact source Version shall be preserved.

21.63 Reference Asset

A Reference Asset guides production without necessarily being copied directly into the Output.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.64 Reference Role

Reference roles may include:

- identity,

- style,

- composition,

- motion,

- Voice,

- colour,

- brand,

- or negative example.

21.65 Reference Use

Use of a reference may still require:

- permission,

- licence,

- consent,

- or confidential treatment.

21.66 Intermediate Asset

An Intermediate Asset supports production but is not the final Deliverable.

Examples include:

- mask,

- isolated stem,

- storyboard panel,

- temporary render,

- extracted frame,

- or working document.

21.67 Candidate Asset

A Candidate Asset is proposed for review.

It is not accepted automatically.

21.68 Accepted Asset

An Accepted Asset has an Acceptance Decision for a defined use.

21.69 Master Asset

A Master Asset is the accepted authoritative source for derivatives or distribution.

21.70 Distribution Asset

A Distribution Asset is prepared for one target channel or recipient.

21.71 Archive Asset

An Archive Asset is preserved for historical, legal, recovery or reproducibility purposes.

21.72 Temporary Asset

A Temporary Asset is retained for a bounded time.

Its expiry and dependency shall be explicit.

21.73 Ephemeral Output

An ephemeral Output may be discarded after validation if no policy requires retention.

21.74 Quarantined Asset

A Quarantined Asset is isolated because of:

- malware,

- unknown source,

- disputed rights,

- missing consent,

- corruption,

- or policy failure.

21.75 Rejected Asset

A Rejected Asset remains available as evidence or negative reference according to retention policy.

21.76 Superseded Asset

A Superseded Asset Version has been replaced by a newer governing Version.

21.77 Revoked Asset

A Revoked Asset is blocked from further use because of:

- rights,

- consent,

- Incident,

- or owner Decision.

21.78 Asset Lifecycle

Asset lifecycle may include:

- discovered,

- received,

- ingesting,

- validating,

- admitted,

- candidate,

- accepted,

- restricted,

- quarantined,

- superseded,

- revoked,

- expired,

- archived,

- pending deletion,

- deleted,

- and destroyed.

21.79 Discovered Asset

A discovered file or external object is not automatically governed or eligible.

21.80 Received Asset

The Asset or Output has entered an Omnira-controlled boundary.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.81 Ingesting Asset

The system is downloading, copying, validating or registering it.

21.82 Validating Asset

The system is checking:

- integrity,

- type,

- metadata,

- policy,

- provenance,

- and rights state.

21.83 Admitted Asset

The Asset has sufficient metadata and storage to participate in governed workflows.

21.84 Restricted Asset

Use is limited to defined:

- Projects,

- purposes,

- audiences,

- channels,

- territories,

- or time periods.

21.85 Expired Asset

The Asset or its permitted-use window has expired.

21.86 Pending-Deletion Asset

Deletion is approved but not yet complete across all locations.

21.87 Deleted Asset

The active representation is removed from ordinary use.

Historical metadata may remain.

21.88 Destroyed Asset

The content is deleted or rendered inaccessible according to the defined destruction procedure.

21.89 Asset Admission

Asset admission shall establish:

- identity,

- Version,

- type,

- classification,

- integrity,

- source,

- storage,

- rights state,

- consent state where applicable,

- and lifecycle.

21.90 Asset Ingestion

Ingestion may include:

1. receive or retrieve.

2. authenticate source.

3. validate size.

4. validate media type.

5. scan for malware.

6. calculate checksum.

7. inspect metadata.

8. assign classification.

9. capture provenance.

10. resolve rights state.

11. store durably.

12. create Representations.

13. mark lifecycle.

21.91 Ingestion Identity

Every material ingestion process shall have stable identity.

21.92 Ingestion Source

Sources may include:

- user upload,

- Provider output,

- local Tool,

- external URL,

- repository,

- camera,

- microphone,

- scanner,

- import package,

- or human contribution.

21.93 Ingestion Trust

Source trust shall influence validation depth.

21.94 Provider Output Ingestion

Provider Outputs with temporary URLs shall be ingested before expiry when required.

21.95 User Upload

User upload does not prove ownership or rights.

The user may be asked to classify and attest intended use.

21.96 External URL Ingestion

External URLs shall be treated as untrusted.

Retrieval shall protect against:

- malicious redirects,

- internal-network access,

- oversized downloads,

- and unsupported protocols.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.97 Local File Ingestion

Local file access shall remain path- and Project-scoped.

21.98 Import Package

An import package may contain:

- Assets,

- manifest,

- checksums,

- rights metadata,

- and consent evidence.

Package validation shall precede admission.

21.99 Duplicate Ingestion

Duplicate content may map to:

- same Asset Version,

- another Representation,

- or a distinct Asset with equivalent bytes.

The Decision shall preserve semantic context.

21.100 Content Deduplication

Content checksum may detect identical bytes.

It shall not erase:

- distinct ownership,

- Project context,

- rights,

- or execution history.

21.101 Semantic Deduplication

Semantically similar content shall not be merged automatically.

21.102 Asset Manifest

An Asset Manifest describes the files, Representations, checksums and relationships constituting an Asset or Package.

21.103 Manifest Identity

Every Manifest shall have stable identity and Version.

21.104 Manifest Entry

Each entry should identify:

- Asset or Representation,

- role,

- path or location,

- size,

- media type,

- checksum,

- and Version.

21.105 Manifest Integrity

The Manifest may itself be checksummed or signed.

21.106 Asset Set

An Asset Set is a governed group of related Assets.

Examples include:

- Character Reference Set,

- Scene Asset Set,

- training dataset,

- publication package,

- or monthly content bundle.

21.107 Asset Set Identity

Every Asset Set shall have stable identity and Version.

21.108 Asset Collection

A Collection groups Assets for discovery or management.

Collection membership does not change Asset ownership.

21.109 Asset Collection Identity

Every persistent Collection shall have stable identity.

21.110 Collection Membership

Membership shall be Versioned or attributable.

21.111 Asset Location

An Asset Location identifies where one Representation is stored or accessible.

It shall include or reference:

- assetLocationId,

- Representation,

- storage system,

- region,

- path or object key,

- access class,

- encryption,

- lifecycle,

- and health.

21.112 Asset Location Identity

Every persistent Asset Location shall have stable identity.

21.113 Primary Location

The Primary Location is the authoritative storage location for one Representation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.114 Replica Location

A Replica preserves availability or locality.

21.115 Cache Location

A Cache Location may be temporary and non-authoritative.

21.116 External Location

An External Location is controlled by another system or Provider.

21.117 Temporary Location

A Temporary Location has an expiry or uncertain durability.

21.118 Local Location

A Local Location resides on an approved local Node or private Zone.

21.119 Cloud Location

A Cloud Location resides in externally operated infrastructure.

21.120 Region

Location region shall be explicit where data residency matters.

21.121 Storage Object

A Storage Object is the implementation-level object containing bytes or structured content.

21.122 Storage Object Identity

Storage object identifiers shall not replace Asset identity.

21.123 Storage System

A Storage System may be:

- local file system,

- object store,

- document store,

- database,

- content-addressed store,

- archive,

- or Provider library.

21.124 Storage-System Trust

Trust shall consider:

- operator,

- encryption,

- access control,

- region,

- retention,

- backup,

- and deletion.

21.125 Encryption at Rest

Protected Assets shall use encryption appropriate to their classification.

21.126 Encryption Key Reference

Key identity may be preserved without exposing key material.

21.127 Storage Access

Storage access shall be governed by:

- Principal,

- Project,

- purpose,

- operation,

- and classification.

21.128 Read Access

Read access permits retrieval within defined scope.

21.129 Write Access

Write access permits creation or change.

It shall not imply delete authority.

21.130 Delete Access

Delete authority shall remain narrow and consequential.

21.131 Public Access

Public access shall require explicit publication or distribution Decision.

21.132 Signed Access URL

A signed URL is a temporary access mechanism.

It shall not become durable public status.

21.133 Asset Transfer

Asset transfer moves or copies content between Locations or Zones.

21.134 Transfer Record

A Transfer Record shall preserve:

- source,

- destination,

- Asset Version,

- actor,

- authority,

- encryption,

- checksum,

- time,

- and result.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 21.151 Restore Does Not Reactivate Revoked Asset
text:
21.135 Transfer Identity

Every material Transfer shall have stable identity.

21.136 Transfer Integrity

The destination shall verify integrity before becoming authoritative.

21.137 Transfer Confidentiality

Protected Assets shall remain encrypted in transit.

21.138 Transfer Classification

Classification shall travel with the Asset.

21.139 Transfer Rights

Transfer to another party or Provider may require distribution or processing permission.

21.140 Asset Replication

Replication creates another governed Location for the same Representation.

21.141 Replica Consistency

Replica state and freshness shall be explicit.

21.142 Asset Migration

Migration changes authoritative storage or format.

It shall preserve:

- Asset identity,

- Version,

- integrity,

- provenance,

- rights,

- and access policy.

21.143 Storage Migration

Storage-system migration shall include:

- inventory,

- copy,

- checksum,

- cutover,

- rollback,

- and source cleanup.

21.144 Format Migration

Format migration creates a derived Representation or Asset Version.

It may affect:

- quality,

- editability,

- metadata,

- and rights obligations.

21.145 Asset Backup

Backup protects against loss.

Backup is another storage and rights boundary.

21.146 Backup Identity

Material backup sets should have stable identity or manifest.

21.147 Backup Encryption

Backup protection shall match Asset classification.

21.148 Backup Region

Backup location may affect data residency and consent.

21.149 Backup Retention

Backup retention shall be explicit.

21.150 Backup Restore

Restore shall reapply current:

- rights,

- consent,

- revocation,

- and deletion state.

21.151 Restore Does Not Reactivate Revoked Asset

Restored bytes shall not return a revoked Asset to active use automatically.

21.152 Asset Retention

Retention defines how long Asset content and metadata remain stored.

21.153 Retention Policy

Retention may depend on:

- classification,

- rights,

- consent,

- Project need,

- legal requirement,

- audit,

- or storage cost.

21.154 Minimum Retention

Some evidence or accepted masters may require minimum retention.

21.155 Maximum Retention

Personal, private or temporary media may require deletion after a defined period.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.156 Retention Hold

A hold suspends deletion because of:

- Incident,

- dispute,

- audit,

- legal request,

- or recovery.

21.157 Asset Expiry

Expiry may result from:

- licence,

- consent,

- subscription,

- Provider retention,

- temporary URL,

- or Project policy.

21.158 Asset Deletion

Deletion shall identify all known:

- Locations,

- caches,

- replicas,

- backups,

- packages,

- and derivatives.

21.159 Deletion Request

A Deletion Request shall include:

- target,

- reason,

- authority,

- scope,

- deadline,

- and dependencies.

21.160 Deletion Identity

Every material Deletion Request shall have stable identity.

21.161 Soft Deletion

Soft deletion removes ordinary visibility while retaining recoverability.

21.162 Hard Deletion

Hard deletion removes active content from defined Locations.

21.163 Destruction

Destruction may include:

- object deletion,

- key destruction,

- media wipe,

- or Provider deletion request.

21.164 Deletion Verification

Deletion completion shall be verified per Location where possible.

21.165 Provider Deletion

Provider-side deletion may have:

- delay,

- retention exception,

- backup persistence,

- or unknown completion.

The state shall remain explicit.

21.166 Derived-Asset Deletion

Deleting a source does not automatically delete derivatives.

Policy shall determine required propagation.

21.167 Consent-Based Deletion

Consent revocation may require future-use blocking and, in some cases, deletion.

The required effect shall be determined by policy and applicable obligations.

21.168 Asset Integrity

Integrity means the Asset content is complete and unaltered relative to its recorded Version.

21.169 Integrity Record

An Integrity Record shall include:

- integrityRecordId,

- Asset Version,

- algorithm,

- checksum or signature,

- createdAt,

- verifier,

- result,

- and provenance.

21.170 Checksum

A checksum is a content-derived value used to verify integrity.

21.171 Checksum Algorithm

The algorithm and Version shall be explicit.

21.172 Weak Checksum

Weak or legacy checksums may support accidental-corruption detection but not strong integrity claims.

21.173 Strong Checksum

Approved cryptographic checksums should be used for canonical integrity.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.174 Multiple Checksums

Several algorithms may be preserved during migration or interoperability.

21.175 Signature

A digital signature may prove that a specific key signed content or metadata.

21.176 Signature Identity

Every signature record shall identify:

- signer,

- key,

- algorithm,

- signed content,

- time,

- and verification result.

21.177 Signature Is Not Truth

A signature proves origin or integrity under the key’s trust.

It does not prove the content is accurate, lawful or accepted.

21.178 Content Credential

A Content Credential is machine-readable provenance or authenticity metadata attached to or associated with media.

It may include:

- creator,

- edits,

- generation,

- signatures,

- and tool information.

21.179 Content Credential Preservation

Content credentials should be preserved where technically and legally appropriate.

21.180 Metadata Stripping

Distribution platforms may strip metadata.

Canonical provenance shall therefore not depend solely on embedded metadata.

21.181 Watermark

A watermark may communicate:

- ownership,

- preview status,

- Provider origin,

- synthetic content,

- or restricted use.

21.182 Visible Watermark

Visible watermarks may be mandatory for:

- review,

- unlicensed previews,

- or disclosure.

21.183 Invisible Watermark

Invisible watermark claims shall be treated according to actual evidence and detection capability.

21.184 Watermark Removal

Removing a required watermark may violate:

- Provider terms,

- licence,

- policy,

- or law.

It shall require explicit rights eligibility.

21.185 Integrity Failure

Checksum or signature mismatch shall quarantine or invalidate the affected Representation.

21.186 Corrupt Asset

Corruption may be:

- partial,

- complete,

- recoverable,

- or unknown.

21.187 Repair

Repair creates a new Version or Representation and preserves the corrupt source as evidence where policy requires it.

21.188 Provenance

Provenance is the governed record of where an Asset came from, how it was created, which inputs contributed, which transformations occurred and which actors or resources participated.

21.189 Provenance Is Not Ownership

Provenance describes lineage.

It does not alone determine legal ownership.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.190 Provenance Is Not Quality

Complete lineage does not prove the Asset is correct or acceptable.

21.191 Provenance Is Not Consent

Knowing whose Voice or likeness appears does not prove permission.

21.192 Provenance Record

A Provenance Record shall include or reference:

- provenanceRecordId,

- subject Asset Version,

- creation or source event,

- source Assets,

- reference Assets,

- Provider,

- Model,

- Tool,

- Adapter,

- Runtime,

- human contributors,

- transformations,

- prompts or specifications,

- time,

- environment,

- and evidence.

21.193 Provenance Record Identity

Every material Provenance Record shall have stable identity.

21.194 Provenance Relationship

Relationship types may include:

- created from,

- derived from,

- transformed from,
