- composed from,

- referenced,

- trained from,

- fine-tuned from,

- transcribed from,

- translated from,

- rendered from,

- restored from,

- replaced by,

- and superseded by.

21.195 Provenance Graph

The Provenance Graph connects Assets, Versions, Executions, resources, people, rights and Decisions.

21.196 Provenance Completeness

Completeness may be:

- complete,

- materially complete,

- partial,

- minimal,

- unknown,

- or disputed.

21.197 Missing Provenance

Missing provenance shall reduce eligibility for:

- publication,

- commercial reuse,

- training,

- or high-trust use.

21.198 Source Provenance

Source provenance identifies where original content entered Omnira.

21.199 Generation Provenance

Generation provenance identifies:

- Provider,

- Model,

- Model Version,

- prompt or Specification,

- parameters,

- references,

- and Attempt.

21.200 Transformation Provenance

Transformation provenance identifies:

- source Version,

- Tool,

- Tool Version,

- settings,

- human operator,

- and Output Version.

21.201 Composition Provenance

Composition provenance identifies every:

- Layer,

- Track,

- Clip,

- source Asset,

- transform,

- and Timeline Version.

21.202 Human Contribution Record

A Human Contribution Record shall identify:

- contributor,

- role,

- action,

- target,

- source,

- output,

- Tool,

- time,

- and agreement or rights context.

21.203 AI Contribution Record

An AI Contribution Record may identify:

- Agent,

- Model,

- Provider,

- Capability,

- and bounded contribution.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.204 Mixed Contribution

Mixed human and AI authorship shall not be simplified to one false creator label.

21.205 Prompt Provenance

Prompts may be protected evidence.

Their retention shall follow:

- privacy,

- trade secret,

- Project,

- and Provider policies.

21.206 Reference Provenance

Every reference shall identify:

- exact Asset Version,

- role,

- use,

- and rights state.

21.207 Training Provenance

Training lineage shall identify:

- Base Model,

- dataset,

- dataset Versions,

- method,

- code,

- Runtime,

- and resulting Model.

21.208 Retrieval Provenance

Retrieved content shall preserve:

- source Asset,

- location,

- index,

- query,

- time,

- and relevance evidence.

21.209 Publication Provenance

Publication evidence shall identify:

- exact Asset Version,

- Package,

- channel,

- Account,

- publication time,

- and external identifier.

21.210 Chain of Custody

Chain of Custody records who or what possessed, transferred, stored or controlled an Asset through material stages.

21.211 Chain-of-Custody Record

The record shall include:

- custodyRecordId,

- Asset Version,

- prior custodian,

- new custodian,

- Location,

- transfer,

- time,

- integrity result,

- and authority.

21.212 Custody Identity

Every material custody transition shall have stable identity.

21.213 Custody Is Not Ownership

A Provider may hold temporary custody without owning the Asset.

21.214 Custody Gap

Unexplained custody gaps reduce trust and may block sensitive use.

21.215 Evidence Package

An Evidence Package may bundle:

- provenance,

- checksums,

- rights,

- consent,

- acceptance,

- and custody

for one Asset or Deliverable.

21.216 Rights

Rights are legally, contractually or policy-recognised permissions, interests or restrictions governing an Asset, subject or use.

Omnira shall represent rights states without pretending to provide final legal judgement where uncertainty remains.

21.217 Rights Profile

A Rights Profile summarises the rights state of one Asset Version or Asset Set.

It shall include or reference:

- rightsProfileId,

- Asset,

- ownership claims,

- licences,

- usage grants,

- restrictions,

- attribution,

- consent,

- territories,

- channels,

- duration,

- commercial use,

- derivative use,

- training use,

- disclosure,

- and eligibility.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.218 Rights Profile Identity

Every Rights Profile shall have stable identity and Version.

21.219 Rights State

Rights states may include:

- cleared,

- cleared with conditions,

- internally permitted,

- restricted,

- unresolved,

- disputed,

- expired,

- revoked,

- prohibited,

- and not applicable.

21.220 Cleared

Cleared means sufficient evidence supports the defined intended use.

Clearance shall always be scoped.

21.221 Cleared with Conditions

Conditions may include:

- attribution,

- watermark,

- channel limit,

- territory,

- time,

- audience,

- commercial restriction,

- or disclosure.

21.222 Internally Permitted

Internal use may be allowed while public distribution remains prohibited.

21.223 Unresolved

Required evidence or interpretation is missing.

21.224 Disputed

Two or more parties or records conflict materially.

21.225 Prohibited

The intended use is not allowed under current policy or evidence.

21.226 Rights Claim

A Rights Claim is an assertion that a Principal or entity owns, controls or may exercise a defined right.

It shall include:

- rightsClaimId,

- claimant,

- Asset or subject,

- right type,

- basis,

- scope,

- validity,

- evidence,

- status,

- and provenance.

21.227 Rights Claim Identity

Every material Rights Claim shall have stable identity.

21.228 Claim Basis

Basis may include:

- authorship,

- employment,

- assignment,

- contract,

- licence,

- commission,

- inheritance,

- Provider terms,

- or statutory status.

21.229 Claim Status

States may include:

- asserted,

- verified,

- partially verified,

- disputed,

- rejected,

- expired,

- and superseded.

21.230 Ownership Claim

An Ownership Claim asserts ownership of copyright, Asset, account, trademark or another right.

21.231 Ownership Is Divisible

Different rights may be held by different parties.

Examples include:

- copyright,

- master recording,

- composition,

- performance,

- likeness,

- trademark,

- and distribution.

21.232 Copyright Owner

The copyright owner may differ from:

- creator,

- commissioner,

- custodian,

- or Project operator.

21.233 Commissioned Work

Commissioning a work does not automatically prove transfer of all rights.

The governing agreement shall be preserved.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 21.237 Publicly Available Is Not Public Domain
text:
21.234 Employee or Contractor Work

Rights may depend on:

- employment terms,

- contractor agreement,

- jurisdiction,

- and assignment.

21.235 Joint Ownership

Several parties may hold rights.

Use may require one or several permissions.

21.236 Public Domain

Public-domain status shall be supported by evidence appropriate to:

- jurisdiction,

- term,

- work type,

- and source.

21.237 Publicly Available Is Not Public Domain

Availability on the internet does not remove rights.

21.238 Licence

A Licence grants permission to use an Asset, work, service or right under defined conditions.

21.239 Licence Identity

Every governed Licence shall have stable identity and Version.

21.240 Licence Source

Licence source may be:

- direct contract,

- Provider terms,

- open licence,

- stock library,

- marketplace,

- commissioning agreement,

- employment agreement,

- or statutory permission.

21.241 Licence Grantor

The grantor shall be explicit.

21.242 Licence Grantee

The grantee may be:

- user,

- Project,

- Tenant,

- Omnira,

- or another entity.

21.243 Licence Scope

Licence scope may include:

- Asset,

- territory,

- duration,

- channel,

- audience,

- media,

- language,

- commercial use,

- modification,

- distribution,

- sublicensing,

- and training.

21.244 Licence Term

The effective start and expiry shall be explicit.

21.245 Perpetual Licence

Perpetual does not necessarily mean irrevocable or unrestricted.

21.246 Revocable Licence

Revocation conditions shall be explicit.

21.247 Exclusive Licence

Exclusive rights may prevent others from exercising the same granted right.

21.248 Non-Exclusive Licence

Non-exclusive rights may coexist with other licences.

21.249 Transferable Licence

Transferability shall not be assumed.

21.250 Sublicensable Licence

Sublicensing permission shall be explicit.

21.251 Worldwide Licence

Worldwide scope shall be evidenced.

21.252 Territory-Limited Licence

Distribution shall remain inside approved territories.

21.253 Channel-Limited Licence

A licence may permit:

- website,

- social media,

- print,

- streaming,

- application,

- advertising,

- or internal use

with different conditions.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.254 Audience-Limited Licence

Use may be limited to:

- subscribers,

- employees,

- students,

- customers,

- or private recipients.

21.255 Commercial Use

Commercial-use permission shall be explicit.

The existence of revenue does not automatically make every use identical.

21.256 Non-Commercial Use

Non-commercial restrictions may prohibit advertising, subscription or business use.

21.257 Promotional Use

Promotional use may differ from ordinary editorial or product use.

21.258 Editorial Use

Editorial-only Assets may not be used for advertising or endorsements.

21.259 Advertising Use

Advertising rights may require broader or separate permission.

21.260 Internal Use

Internal use may permit:

- review,

- analysis,

- training of staff,

- or development

without external distribution.

21.261 Public Distribution

Public distribution requires explicit publication eligibility.

21.262 Modification Right

Modification permission determines whether the Asset may be edited.

21.263 Adaptation Right

Adaptation may include:

- translation,

- remix,

- derivative media,

- localisation,

- or format change.

21.264 Derivative Right

The right to create derivative works shall be explicit.

21.265 Distribution Right

Distribution permission governs copies or delivery to others.

21.266 Display Right

Display permission may apply to public or private visual presentation.

21.267 Performance Right

Performance rights may apply to:

- music,

- script,

- Voice,

- or audiovisual works.

21.268 Synchronisation Right

Synchronisation rights govern pairing music with visual media.

21.269 Mechanical Right

Music reproduction may require specific rights in some contexts.

21.270 Master Recording Right

The recording and the underlying composition may have separate owners.

21.271 Broadcast Right

Broadcast or stream rights may differ by territory and channel.

21.272 Embedding Right

Fonts, media or components may have specific embedding restrictions.

21.273 Redistribution Right

Redistributing source files may be prohibited even when rendered use is permitted.

21.274 Source-File Right

Editable source access may have different conditions from final-output use.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.275 Training Right

Permission to use an Asset for Model training shall be explicit.

Ordinary viewing or generation permission does not imply training rights.

21.276 Fine-Tuning Right

Fine-tuning may require separate permission from retrieval or analysis.

21.277 Embedding Right for Retrieval

Creating embeddings or indexes may constitute a governed processing use.

Permission shall be assessed separately.

21.278 Memory Use Right

Admitting content into persistent Governed Memory may require broader retention and reuse permission.

21.279 Reference-Generation Right

Using an Asset as a generation reference may require different permission from simply displaying it.

21.280 Style-Reference Right

Using a protected work as style guidance may involve policy and legal risk.

Omnira shall preserve the source and intended use rather than assume permission.

21.281 Attribution Requirement

Attribution obligations define required credit.

They may include:

- creator name,

- source,

- licence name,

- URL,

- copyright notice,

- or modification disclosure.

21.282 Attribution Requirement Identity

Every reusable requirement shall have stable identity.

21.283 Attribution Placement

Attribution may be required:

- on the Asset,

- in caption,

- in credits,

- in metadata,

- in documentation,

- or in a linked page.

21.284 Attribution Text

Exact required text should be preserved where known.

21.285 Modification Notice

Some licences require disclosure of modifications.

21.286 No-Endorsement Restriction

Use shall not imply endorsement where prohibited.

21.287 No-Derivatives Restriction

Modification and derivative creation are prohibited.

21.288 Share-Alike Restriction

Derivative distribution may require a compatible licence.

21.289 Source-Availability Requirement

Some software or content licences may require source or notice availability.

21.290 Trademark Restriction

Use of marks may be restricted even when surrounding content is licensed.

21.291 Moral Rights

Attribution, integrity or author rights may persist separately from economic rights.

The system shall preserve relevant claims and restrictions where known.

21.292 Privacy Right

Privacy interests may restrict use even when copyright permission exists.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.293 Publicity or Likeness Right

Use of a person’s identity, face, Voice or persona may require consent or other authority.

21.294 Contract Restriction

A contract may impose restrictions beyond general copyright law.

21.295 Platform Restriction

A publication platform may restrict:

- synthetic media,

- music,

- advertising,

- or disclosure.

21.296 Provider Terms

Provider terms govern use of the Provider and may affect Outputs.

They shall be captured as Versioned evidence.

21.297 Terms Snapshot

A Terms Snapshot records the relevant Provider terms at a specific time.

It shall include or reference:

- termsSnapshotId,

- Provider,

- Product,

- Account or plan,

- jurisdiction,

- effective date,

- retrievedAt,

- source,

- relevant clauses or structured interpretation,

- and checksum or archive reference.

21.298 Terms Snapshot Identity

Every Terms Snapshot shall have stable identity and Version.

21.299 Plan-Specific Terms

Rights may differ by:

- free plan,

- paid plan,

- enterprise plan,

- trial,

- or managed account.

21.300 Account-Specific Terms

User-owned and Omnira-managed Accounts may have different rights or restrictions.

21.301 Provider Output Rights

Output-rights claims shall preserve:

- Provider,

- Model or Product,

- Account plan,

- terms Version,

- generation date,

- and applicable restrictions.

21.302 Provider Training Use

Provider retention or training use of Inputs and Outputs shall remain explicit.

21.303 Provider Ownership Claim

Some Providers may disclaim or retain certain rights.

The exact claim shall be preserved rather than generalised.

21.304 Provider Indemnity

Indemnity terms, if any, may depend on:

- plan,

- usage controls,

- policy compliance,

- and excluded content.

The system shall not assume indemnity without evidence.

21.305 Provider Watermark Requirement

Required watermark or metadata obligations shall remain attached.

21.306 Provider Attribution Requirement

Provider credit may be required under some plans or products.

21.307 Provider Commercial Restriction

Free or experimental services may restrict commercial use.

21.308 Provider Geography Restriction

Use may be restricted by territory or user location.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.309 Provider Terms Change

A terms change shall affect future eligibility and may require review of continuing use.

21.310 Historical Terms

Historical Outputs shall remain linked to the terms in force at creation.

21.311 Terms Unavailability

If terms cannot be retrieved or verified, rights state shall remain unresolved.

21.312 Open Licence

An Open Licence grants reuse under defined public conditions.

The exact licence and Version shall be preserved.

21.313 Open-Source Software Licence

Software Assets may require:

- notices,

- source availability,

- attribution,

- copyleft,

- patent,

- or redistribution compliance.

21.314 Permissive Software Licence

Permissive does not mean obligation-free.

Notices and attribution may remain required.

21.315 Copyleft Software Licence

Distribution or network use may trigger source or licensing obligations.

21.316 Dataset Licence

Datasets may have terms distinct from the individual content they contain.

21.317 Model Licence

Model weights and Outputs may be governed by different terms.

21.318 Font Licence

Font licences may distinguish:

- desktop use,

- web embedding,

- application embedding,

- document embedding,

- and redistribution.

21.319 Stock Asset Licence

Stock libraries may restrict:

- seat count,

- impressions,

- print runs,

- templates,

- merchandise,

- or resale.

21.320 Music Library Licence

Music rights may depend on:

- channel,

- monetisation,

- territory,

- account,

- and subscription status.

21.321 Subscription Expiry

A subscription may permit continued use of previously licensed Assets or may not.

The actual licence shall determine eligibility.

21.322 Template Licence

Templates may permit final-output use while prohibiting source redistribution.

21.323 Marketplace Asset

Marketplace assets shall preserve:

- seller,

- licence,

- purchase record,

- Product,

- and Version.

21.324 Purchase Receipt

Purchase evidence may support rights.

It does not alone describe all licence conditions.

21.325 Usage Grant

A Usage Grant is a canonical permission allowing a defined Principal, Project or Tenant to use an Asset or subject in a defined manner.

It shall include:

- usageGrantId,

- grantor,

- grantee,

- Asset or subject,

- permitted uses,

- prohibited uses,

- Project,

- channels,

- audience,

- territory,

- duration,

- conditions,

- revocation,

- and evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 21.327 Usage Grant Is Not Licence Source
text:
21.326 Usage Grant Identity

Every Usage Grant shall have stable identity.

21.327 Usage Grant Is Not Licence Source

The Grant may derive from a Licence, contract, owner Decision or Consent.

The basis shall remain linked.

21.328 Project-Limited Grant

The Asset may be used only in one Project.

21.329 Campaign-Limited Grant

The grant may be limited to one campaign or production.

21.330 Deliverable-Limited Grant

The grant may permit one exact Deliverable.

21.331 Channel-Limited Grant

The grant may permit one social account, website or publication channel.

21.332 Time-Limited Grant

The grant shall expire automatically.

21.333 Territory-Limited Grant

Geographic scope shall remain explicit.

21.334 Purpose-Limited Grant

The Asset may be used only for:

- education,

- marketing,

- internal review,

- product operation,

- or another defined purpose.

21.335 Audience-Limited Grant

The grant may prohibit public or child-facing use.

21.336 Non-Transferable Grant

Another Project or Tenant cannot inherit it automatically.

21.337 Revocable Grant

Revocation conditions shall be explicit.

21.338 Irrevocable Grant

Irrevocability shall not be assumed and may still have scope limits.

21.339 Restriction

A Restriction prohibits or limits one use.

Restrictions may derive from:

- licence,

- consent,

- policy,

- contract,

- law,

- Provider terms,

- or owner Decision.

21.340 Restriction Identity

Every material Restriction shall have stable identity.

21.341 Prohibited Use

Examples may include:

- commercial advertising,

- political use,

- adult content,

- biometric training,

- public distribution,

- merchandise,

- or cross-Project reuse.

21.342 Required Review

A restriction may require human or legal review before use.

21.343 Required Attribution

A restriction may require credit before publication.

21.344 Required Disclosure

A restriction may require synthetic-media or AI-use disclosure.

21.345 Required Watermark

A watermark may be mandatory for previews or generated media.

21.346 Required Removal Date

Some Assets must be removed after expiry.

21.347 Rights Decision

A Rights Decision determines whether one intended use is permitted under current evidence and policy.

It shall include or reference:

- rightsDecisionId,

- Asset Version,

- intended use,

- Project,

- channel,

- audience,

- territory,

- time,

- applicable Claims,

- Licences,

- Grants,

- restrictions,

- consent,

- terms,

- decision,

- conditions,

- confidence,

- reviewer,

- and provenance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.348 Rights Decision Identity

Every material Rights Decision shall have stable identity.

21.349 Rights Decision States

States may include:

- eligible,

- eligible with conditions,

- ineligible,

- unresolved,

- disputed,

- expired,

- and superseded.

21.350 Intended Use

Rights eligibility shall always be evaluated against a specific intended use.

21.351 Internal-Review Decision

Internal review may be permitted while publication remains unresolved.

21.352 Publication Decision

Publication requires:

- channel,

- audience,

- territory,

- commercial context,

- and duration.

21.353 Reuse Decision

Reuse in another Project or campaign requires a new evaluation.

21.354 Training Decision

Training or fine-tuning requires a dedicated Rights Decision.

21.355 Retrieval Decision

Indexing and retrieval use may require a separate Decision.

21.356 Rights Confidence

Confidence may be:

- verified,

- strongly supported,

- conditionally supported,

- uncertain,

- disputed,

- or unknown.

21.357 Rights Reviewer

A rights reviewer may be:

- authorised human,

- specialist,

- owner,

- or legal reviewer

according to policy.

21.358 Automated Rights Evaluation

Automation may detect missing metadata or incompatible terms.

It shall not fabricate legal certainty.

21.359 Rights Decision Expiry

A Decision may expire after:

- licence expiry,

- terms change,

- consent change,

- channel change,

- Project change,

- or new dispute.

21.360 Consent

Consent is a voluntary, informed and scoped permission from an authorised subject or representative for a defined use of identity, likeness, Voice, performance, personal data or other protected interest.

Consent shall remain separate from:

- copyright,

- ownership,

- authentication,

- and general authority.

21.361 Consent Subject

A Consent Subject is the person or represented individual whose protected attributes or data are being used.

21.362 Consent Subject Identity

Every governed Consent Subject shall have stable identity or a protected pseudonymous reference.

21.363 Human Subject Identity

Identity evidence shall be sufficient for the required purpose while minimising personal data.

21.364 Subject Representation

A subject may be represented through:

- Human Principal,

- external person record,

- performer record,

- guardian-linked minor,

- or pseudonymous participant.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.365 Consent Grant

A Consent Grant records permission for a defined use.

It shall include or reference:

- consentGrantId,

- subject,

- grantor,

- authority basis,

- grantee,

- purpose,

- Asset or data scope,

- modality,

- likeness,

- Voice,

- performance,

- Project,

- channel,

- audience,

- territory,

- start,

- expiry,

- revocation,

- compensation where relevant,

- evidence,

- and Version.

21.366 Consent Grant Identity

Every Consent Grant shall have stable identity and Version.

21.367 Consent Grantor

The grantor may be:

- the subject,

- guardian,

- authorised representative,

- rights holder,

- or another legally authorised party.

21.368 Consent Grantee

The grantee may be:

- Project,

- Tenant,

- user,

- Omnira,

- producer,

- or publisher.

21.369 Informed Consent

Consent evidence should demonstrate that the grantor understood:

- purpose,

- media,

- audience,

- distribution,

- duration,

- and material risks.

21.370 Voluntary Consent

Consent shall not be represented as valid when coercion or material misunderstanding is known.

21.371 Specific Consent

Consent shall be specific enough to evaluate the intended use.

21.372 Broad Consent

Broad consent shall not be interpreted beyond its actual language and authority.

21.373 Purpose Limitation

Consent for one purpose shall not authorise another purpose automatically.

21.374 Project Limitation

Consent may apply only to one Project.

21.375 Campaign Limitation

Consent may apply only to one campaign or release.

21.376 Channel Limitation

Consent may permit:

- website,

- social media,

- streaming,

- print,

- application,

- or internal use

with different conditions.

21.377 Audience Limitation

Consent may exclude:

- advertising,

- adult audiences,

- political messaging,

- or child-facing distribution.

21.378 Territory Limitation

Consent may be limited geographically.

21.379 Time Limitation

Consent shall expire when its term ends.

21.380 Modality Limitation

Consent for a photograph does not automatically permit Voice cloning.

Consent for Voice does not automatically permit likeness synthesis.

21.381 Likeness Consent

Likeness consent governs use of recognisable appearance or persona.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.382 Voice Consent

Voice consent governs use of recorded, cloned, synthesised or imitated Voice.

21.383 Performance Consent

Performance consent governs use of a recorded or generated performance associated with the subject.

21.384 Recording Consent

Recording permission shall remain distinct from publication permission.

21.385 Editing Consent

Consent may limit:

- manipulation,

- synthetic alteration,

- context changes,

- or misleading edits.

21.386 Synthetic-Likeness Consent

Synthetic or generated likeness may require explicit permission beyond ordinary image use.

21.387 Voice-Cloning Consent

Voice cloning should require explicit consent for:

- creation,

- storage,

- generation,

- permitted Scripts,

- channels,

- and duration.

21.388 Training Consent

Using a person’s Voice, likeness or data to train or adapt a Model requires explicit scope.

21.389 Biometric Consent

Biometric processing may require stronger controls and separate permission.

21.390 Personal-Data Consent

Consent may govern collection, analysis, storage or sharing of personal data.

Other lawful bases may exist, but they shall remain separately represented.

21.391 Revocable Consent

Consent may be revocable according to its basis and applicable obligations.

21.392 Irrevocable Consent Claim

Irrevocability shall be treated cautiously and remain bounded by the actual agreement and law.

21.393 Consent Evidence

Evidence may include:

- signed agreement,

- recorded statement,

- digital approval,

- Provider consent record,

- guardian form,

- or contractual clause.

21.394 Consent Evidence Identity

Every material Consent Evidence item shall have stable identity and protected storage.

21.395 Consent Form Version

The exact form or terms presented shall be preserved.

21.396 Consent Timestamp

Grant time and effective time shall remain explicit.

21.397 Consent Expiry

Expiry shall block future use unless renewed.

21.398 Consent Renewal

Renewal creates a new Consent Version or Grant.

21.399 Consent Amendment

Material scope changes require a new amendment or consent.

21.400 Consent Revocation

Revocation shall identify:

- subject,

- grant,

- scope,

- effective time,

- future-use effect,

- existing-publication effect,

- deletion requirement,

- and evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 21.408 Consent Is Not Assumed from Participation
21.409 Consent Is Not Assumed from Public Posting
text:
21.401 Consent Revocation Identity

Every material revocation shall have stable identity.

21.402 Future-Use Revocation

New use shall stop at the effective time.

21.403 Existing-Publication Review

Existing publications may require:

- removal,

- replacement,

- restricted continuation,

- or no change

depending on policy and obligation.

21.404 Derived Asset Review

Revocation shall identify affected derivatives and Models.

21.405 Consent Propagation

Consent changes shall propagate to:

- Asset eligibility,

- production references,

- publication packages,

- scheduled work,

- and memory or training use.

21.406 Consent Conflict

Conflicting consent records shall result in unresolved or restrictive status.

21.407 Missing Consent

Missing required consent shall block use.

21.408 Consent Is Not Assumed from Participation

Appearing in a recording or providing source material does not automatically prove all intended uses.

21.409 Consent Is Not Assumed from Public Posting

Public posting does not automatically permit cloning, training, remixing or advertising use.

21.410 Guardian Authority

Guardian Authority records that one adult or entity may grant consent for a minor or dependent subject.

21.411 Guardian Authority Identity

Every Guardian Authority record shall have stable identity.

21.412 Guardian Relationship

The relationship and authority basis shall be explicit.

21.413 Guardian Verification

Verification shall be proportionate to the use and risk.

21.414 Minor Consent

Where appropriate, a minor’s assent may be recorded in addition to guardian consent.

21.415 Minor Privacy

Minor data and media shall receive stronger minimisation, retention and access controls.

21.416 Minor Publication

Public publication of a minor’s image, Voice or personal information requires explicit, narrow approval.

21.417 Minor Synthetic Media

Synthetic likeness or Voice involving minors should receive the strongest review and may be prohibited by policy.

21.418 Guardian Revocation

Guardian authority or consent changes shall propagate promptly.

21.419 Age Transition

When a minor reaches legal adulthood, future use may require renewed consent depending on scope and policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 21.437 Disclosure Is Not a Rights Cure
text:
21.420 Deceased Subject

Rights and consent may continue through estates, contracts or local law.

The state shall remain subject to review.

21.421 Collective Consent

Group recordings may require individual or collective permissions.

21.422 Crowd and Background Subjects

Background individuals may require:

- release,

- masking,

- restricted use,

- or contextual review.

21.423 Incidental Capture

Incidental capture does not automatically remove privacy or likeness obligations.

21.424 Anonymisation

Anonymisation may reduce identity risk when effective and verified.

21.425 Pseudonymisation

Pseudonymisation reduces direct identification but remains personal data in many contexts.

21.426 Redaction Consent Effect

Redaction may change consent requirements only after validation.

21.427 Synthetic Media

Synthetic Media is content generated or materially altered through computational methods in a way that creates or changes represented people, Voices, events or environments.

21.428 Generated Media

Generated media may contain entirely synthetic or mixed content.

21.429 Materially Altered Media

Material alteration changes meaning, identity, context or perceived reality.

21.430 Ordinary Editing

Cropping, colour adjustment or compression may not require the same disclosure as material synthesis.

The distinction shall be policy-defined.

21.431 Synthetic-Media Label

A Synthetic-Media Label records that disclosure is required or recommended.

It shall include:

- labelId,

- Asset Version,

- disclosure type,

- placement,

- text,

- channel,

- audience,

- and basis.

21.432 Label Identity

Every label requirement shall have stable identity.

21.433 Disclosure Requirement

Disclosure may be required because of:

- policy,

- platform terms,

- advertising,

- public trust,

- likeness,

- or legal obligation.

21.434 Visible Disclosure

Visible disclosure may appear:

- on-screen,

- in caption,

- in credits,

- or in description.

21.435 Metadata Disclosure

Metadata may include machine-readable generation or edit information.

21.436 Audio Disclosure

Audio-only content may require spoken or description-based disclosure.

21.437 Disclosure Is Not a Rights Cure

Labelling synthetic media does not make unauthorised use permissible.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.438 Misleading Context

An accurate Asset may still be misleading when presented in a false context.

21.439 Documentary Representation

Generated or reconstructed content shall not be presented as unaltered documentary evidence without clear disclosure.

21.440 Simulation

Simulations shall be labelled according to audience and purpose.

21.441 Avatar Disclosure

Synthetic avatars may require disclosure that the person or performance is not live or original.

21.442 AI-Assistance Disclosure

Projects may require disclosure of AI assistance even when content is not fully synthetic.

21.443 Asset Eligibility

Asset Eligibility determines whether an Asset may be used for a defined operation.

Eligibility shall consider:

- lifecycle,

- integrity,

- classification,

- rights,

- consent,

- quality,

- audience,

- channel,

- territory,

- time,

- and policy.

21.444 Use Eligibility

Use classes may include:

- internal review,

- development,

- reference,

- generation,

- transformation,

- training,

- composition,

- distribution,

- publication,

- advertising,

- and archival.

21.445 Reference Eligibility

An Asset may be eligible for visual review but not Provider upload.

21.446 Generation Eligibility

An Asset may be used as an Input or reference only when rights and consent permit that processing.

21.447 Transformation Eligibility

Modification rights and preserve constraints shall be satisfied.

21.448 Composition Eligibility

Each component shall be eligible for the composite’s intended use.

21.449 Publication Eligibility

Publication requires:

- accepted Asset Version,

- cleared or conditionally cleared rights,

- required consent,

- completed attribution,

- disclosure,

- channel compatibility,

- and approval.

21.450 Advertising Eligibility

Advertising use may require broader:

- likeness,

- music,

- stock,

- and endorsement rights.

21.451 Training Eligibility

Training use requires explicit rights, consent and dataset policy.

21.452 Retrieval Eligibility

Persistent indexing and semantic retrieval require permitted processing and retention.

21.453 Memory Eligibility

Content admitted into Governed Memory shall satisfy:

- retention,

- confidentiality,

- consent,

- Project scope,

- and reuse permission.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.454 Cross-Project Eligibility

Reuse across Projects requires:

- ownership or licence compatibility,

- consent compatibility,

- classification compatibility,

- and explicit authority.

21.455 Cross-Tenant Eligibility

Cross-Tenant reuse is prohibited by default.

21.456 Public Reuse

A Public Asset may still have licence and attribution obligations.

21.457 Internal Asset Reuse

Project Internal Assets shall remain Project-scoped unless policy permits broader use.

21.458 Confidential Asset Reuse

Confidential Assets require explicit purpose and authority.

21.459 Local Only Asset Use

Local Only Assets shall not be uploaded to external Providers.

21.460 Prohibited Asset Use

Prohibited Assets shall not be processed except under a separately approved exception.

21.461 Rights Resolution Pipeline

A representative rights-resolution pipeline may:

1. identify Asset and Version.

2. identify source.

3. identify creator and claimant.

4. retrieve licence or terms.

5. identify Provider plan.

6. identify intended use.

7. identify channel, audience, territory and time.

8. identify required consent.

9. identify attribution and disclosure.

10. evaluate restrictions.

11. create Rights Decision.

12. enforce conditions.

13. preserve evidence.

21.462 Conservative Resolution

Unknown or conflicting evidence shall not be resolved optimistically.

21.463 Rights Inheritance

Derivatives may inherit:

- source restrictions,

- attribution,

- licence,

- consent,

- and disclosure requirements.

21.464 Rights Transformation

A transformation does not automatically remove source obligations.

21.465 Composite Rights

A composite Deliverable shall satisfy the combined rights of all included components.

21.466 Most Restrictive Component

One restricted component may limit the entire composite.

21.467 Rights Substitution

A restricted component may be replaced by an eligible alternative.

21.468 Rights Clearance Gate

The gate shall fail when mandatory evidence is missing.

21.469 Rights Override

Overrides shall require:

- authorised reviewer,

- reason,

- legal or policy basis,

- scope,

- expiry,

- and audit.

Some prohibited states shall not be overrideable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.470 Rights Policy

Rights Policy defines mandatory rules for:

- Asset use,

- licence evidence,

- consent,

- attribution,

- disclosure,

- training,

- and publication.

21.471 Platform Rights Policy

Platform policy may require:

- no publication with unresolved rights,

- no Voice cloning without explicit consent,

- and no cross-Tenant reference reuse.

21.472 Tenant Rights Policy

Tenant policy may define:

- approved licences,

- Provider plans,

- disclosure,

- and legal review thresholds.

21.473 Project Rights Policy

Project policy may define:

- ownership,

- Brand Assets,

- Characters,

- Voices,

- stock libraries,

- and approved reference sources.

21.474 Child-Facing Rights Policy

Child-facing Projects may prohibit:

- uncertain likeness,

- unauthorised children’s media,

- hidden advertising,

- and weak guardian evidence.

21.475 Voice Policy

Voice policy may define:

- approved subjects,

- consent requirements,

- Provider,

- retention,

- and prohibited Scripts.

21.476 Likeness Policy

Likeness policy may define:

- approved subjects,

- synthetic alteration,

- advertising use,

- and disclosure.

21.477 Training Policy

Training policy may prohibit default use of Project content for Model improvement.

21.478 Retrieval Policy

Retrieval policy may permit internal indexing while prohibiting external embedding.

21.479 Open-Source Policy

Software and Model use may require licence scanning and notice preservation.

21.480 Attribution Policy

Attribution may be generated automatically from canonical requirements.

21.481 Disclosure Policy

Disclosure may vary by:

- channel,

- audience,

- synthetic content type,

- and materiality.

21.482 Policy Version

Every Rights Decision shall reference applicable policy Versions.

21.483 Asset API

The Asset Control Plane should expose governed operations such as:

- create Asset,

- create Version,

- ingest Output,

- register Representation,

- calculate checksum,

- add Location,

- transfer,

- replicate,

- classify,

- restrict,

- accept,

- revoke,

- archive,

- delete,

- and inspect lineage.

21.484 Provenance API

The Provenance API should support:

- create Record,

- add source,

- add reference,

- add transformation,

- add contribution,

- add custody transition,

- inspect lineage,

- and export evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.485 Rights API

The Rights API should support:

- register Claim,

- register Licence,

- register Terms Snapshot,

- create Usage Grant,

- add Restriction,

- evaluate intended use,

- record Decision,

- and expire or revoke.

21.486 Consent API

The Consent API should support:

- register Subject,

- register Guardian Authority,

- create Consent Grant,

- attach evidence,

- amend,

- renew,

- revoke,

- and inspect affected Assets.

21.487 Attribution API

The Attribution API should support:

- calculate requirements,

- generate credits,

- validate placement,

- and confirm completion.

21.488 Disclosure API

The Disclosure API should support:

- determine requirement,

- create label,

- attach metadata,

- validate channel placement,

- and record evidence.

21.489 Stage 1 Asset Objective

Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy Asset, provenance, rights and consent foundation required for representative Omnira production.

Stage 1 shall prove:

- stable Asset identity,

- immutable Asset Versions,

- durable storage,

- checksums,

- Representations,

- source and derivative lineage,

- Provider and human contribution records,

- rights profiles,

- Terms Snapshots,

- commercial-use eligibility,

- attribution,

- Voice and likeness consent,

- guardian consent,

- publication-rights gates,

- revocation,

- deletion,

- and Asset evidence export.

Stage 1 shall not attempt to replace professional legal review.

21.490 Stage 1 Asset Types

Stage 1 should support at minimum:

- text,

- image,

- document,

- audio,

- Voice,

- video,

- captions,

- metadata,

- Model package,

- Tool package,

- and Production Package.

21.491 Stage 1 Asset Object

The Stage 1 Asset should include:

- assetId,

- type,

- Project,

- owner or controller,

- classification,

- lifecycle,

- current Version,

- Rights Profile,

- createdAt,

- and provenance.

21.492 Stage 1 Asset Version Object

The Stage 1 Asset Version should include:

- assetVersionId,

- Asset,

- Version,

- content identity,

- media type,

- size,

- checksum,

- source,

- createdAt,

- creator,

- acceptance state,

- and lifecycle.

21.493 Stage 1 Representation Object

The Stage 1 Representation should include:

- representationId,

- Asset Version,

- role,

- format,

- dimensions or duration,

- Location,

- checksum,

- lifecycle,

- and provenance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.494 Stage 1 Asset Location Object

The Stage 1 Location should include:

- locationId,

- Representation,

- storage system,

- region,

- object reference,

- access class,

- encryption state,

- durability,

- and lifecycle.

21.495 Stage 1 Provenance Record

The Stage 1 Provenance Record should include:

- provenanceRecordId,

- Asset Version,

- Production or Execution,

- source Assets,

- reference Assets,

- Provider,

- Model,

- Tool,

- Adapter,

- human contributors,

- transformation,

- time,

- and evidence.

21.496 Stage 1 Rights Profile

The Stage 1 Rights Profile should include:

- rightsProfileId,

- Asset Version,

- owner or claimant,

- Licence references,

- Provider Terms Snapshot,

- permitted use,

- prohibited use,

- commercial use,

- modification,

- distribution,

- training,

- attribution,

- consent,

- disclosure,

- rights state,

- and Version.

21.497 Stage 1 Terms Snapshot

The Stage 1 Terms Snapshot should include:

- termsSnapshotId,

- Provider,

- Product,

- plan,

- effective date,

- retrievedAt,

- source reference,

- relevant structured terms,

- checksum,

- and Version.

21.498 Stage 1 Consent Grant

The Stage 1 Consent Grant should include:

- consentGrantId,

- subject,

- grantor,

- authority basis,

- grantee,

- purpose,

- modality,

- Asset or data scope,

- Project,

- channels,

- audience,

- territory,

- start,

- expiry,

- revocation,

- and evidence.

21.499 Stage 1 Rights Decision

The Stage 1 Rights Decision should include:

- rightsDecisionId,

- Asset Version,

- intended use,

- Project,

- channel,

- audience,

- territory,

- time,

- rights evidence,

- consent evidence,

- decision,

- conditions,

- reviewer,

- and validity.

21.500 Stage 1 Asset Receipt

The Stage 1 Asset Receipt should include:

- assetReceiptId,

- Asset Version,

- ingestion,

- integrity,

- Locations,

- provenance,

- classification,

- rights state,

- consent state,

- acceptance,

- and lifecycle.

21.501 Stage 1 Storage

Stage 1 shall support:

- one durable local or private Asset store,

- one managed object-storage path where applicable,

- Project-scoped access,

- checksums,

- replication or backup,

- and controlled deletion.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.502 Stage 1 Provider Output Capture

Stage 1 shall ingest required Provider Outputs before temporary access expires.

21.503 Stage 1 Provenance Capture

Stage 1 shall preserve:

- Request,

- Execution,

- Attempt,

- Provider,

- Model,

- Adapter,

- Tool,

- prompts or Specifications,

- Inputs,

- references,

- and human review.

21.504 Stage 1 Rights Sources

Stage 1 should support:

- user-owned Assets,

- Project-created Assets,

- commissioned human work,

- Provider-generated Outputs,

- stock Assets,

- open-licensed Assets,

- public-domain claims,

- and unknown-rights Assets.

21.505 Stage 1 Consent Types

Stage 1 should support:

- likeness consent,

- Voice consent,

- recording consent,

- synthetic-use consent,

- training consent,

- guardian consent,

- and revocation.

21.506 Stage 1 Publication Gate

A Stage 1 publication package shall fail when:

- Asset Version is not accepted,

- rights are unresolved,

- required consent is missing,

- attribution is incomplete,

- disclosure is missing,

- or the Package contains a revoked Asset.

21.507 Stage 1 Asset Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Asset has stable identity.

2. Asset identity remains distinct from filename.

3. Asset identity remains distinct from URL.

4. Asset identity remains distinct from storage path.

5. Asset type is explicit.

6. Project is explicit.

7. classification is explicit.

8. lifecycle is explicit.

9. owner or controller is explicit.

10. current Version is explicit.

11. Output does not become Asset automatically.

12. discovered file is not active automatically.

13. revoked Asset is excluded from new use.

14. archived Asset remains queryable.

15. historical Asset state remains reconstructable.

21.508 Stage 1 Version Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Asset Version has stable identity.

2. content change creates new Version.

3. accepted Version is immutable.

4. Revision references prior Version.

5. Fork preserves parent Version.

6. Merge preserves all contributors.

7. rejected Version remains evidence.

8. superseded Version is excluded from new publication.

9. rights-state change is attributable.

10. consent-state change is attributable.

11. filename change does not create false new Asset.

12. storage move does not rewrite Version.

13. format conversion creates derived Representation or Version.

14. historical Version remains retrievable.

15. Version chain remains machine-readable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.509 Stage 1 Representation Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Representation has stable identity.

2. Representation references exact Asset Version.

3. role is explicit.

4. format is explicit.

5. media type is validated.

6. dimensions or duration are recorded.

7. master and proxy remain distinct.

8. thumbnail does not replace source.

9. transcript remains distinct from audio.

10. caption remains distinct from transcript.

11. distribution Rendition remains derivative.

12. editable source is preserved where required.

13. checksum is recorded.

14. Location is explicit.

15. historical Representations remain queryable.

21.510 Stage 1 Ingestion Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Ingestion has stable identity.

2. source is authenticated where possible.

3. size limit is enforced.

4. media type is validated.

5. malware scanning is applied according to risk.

6. checksum is calculated.

7. metadata is inspected.

8. classification is assigned.

9. provenance is captured.

10. rights state is assigned.

11. consent state is assigned where applicable.

12. durable storage is confirmed.

13. temporary URL expiry is handled.

14. failed validation creates quarantine.

15. historical ingestion evidence remains queryable.

21.511 Stage 1 Integrity Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Integrity Record has stable identity.

2. checksum algorithm is explicit.

3. checksum matches stored bytes.

4. transfer verifies destination checksum.

5. corrupted Representation is quarantined.

6. signature identifies signer and key.

7. invalid signature does not prove authenticity.

8. content credential is preserved where available.

9. metadata stripping does not erase canonical provenance.

10. Manifest is checksummed.

11. backup restore verifies integrity.

12. duplicate bytes do not erase distinct rights context.

13. repaired Asset creates new Version.

14. integrity failure creates Incident where material.

15. historical Integrity Records remain queryable.

21.512 Stage 1 Storage Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Location has stable identity.

2. storage system is explicit.

3. region is explicit where material.

4. access class is explicit.

5. encryption state is explicit.

6. Project access is enforced.

7. public access requires explicit Decision.

8. signed URL remains temporary.

9. replica state is visible.

10. cache is non-authoritative.

11. backup is encrypted.

12. restore reapplies revocation.

13. deletion covers known Locations.

14. storage migration preserves checksum.

15. historical Locations remain queryable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.513 Stage 1 Provenance Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Provenance Record has stable identity.

2. subject Asset Version is explicit.

3. source Assets are explicit.

4. reference Assets are explicit.

5. Provider is explicit.

6. Model and Version are explicit.

7. Tool and Version are explicit.

8. Adapter is explicit.

9. human contributions are explicit.

10. Production Specification is linked.

11. prompt evidence is protected.

12. transformations are ordered.

13. composite links every component.

14. missing provenance reduces eligibility.

15. historical lineage remains immutable.

21.514 Stage 1 Custody Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Custody Record has stable identity.

2. prior custodian is explicit.

3. new custodian is explicit.

4. Location is explicit.

5. transfer authority is explicit.

6. integrity is verified.

7. external Provider custody is recorded.

8. temporary human custody is recorded where material.

9. custody does not imply ownership.

10. custody gap creates uncertainty.

11. cross-Project transfer is rejected without authority.

12. air-gapped transfer preserves chain of custody.

13. returned Asset preserves original lineage.

14. deleted custody Location is recorded.

15. historical custody remains queryable.

21.515 Stage 1 Rights-Profile Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Rights Profile has stable identity and Version.

2. Asset Version is explicit.

3. claimant is explicit.

4. ownership status is explicit.

5. Licence references are explicit.

6. Provider Terms Snapshot is explicit.

7. commercial-use state is explicit.

8. modification right is explicit.

9. distribution right is explicit.

21.610 Future Asset and Rights Architecture

Future versions may support:

- cryptographically verifiable provenance,

- standardised content credentials,

- automated licence interpretation,

- rights-policy compilation,

- dynamic consent enforcement,

- decentralised rights registries,

- programmable usage grants,

- royalty attribution,

- synthetic-media authenticity signals,

- privacy-preserving identity verification,

- and rights-aware Model training.

Future evolution must preserve:

- canonical Asset identity,

- exact Versions,

- scoped permission,

- consent,

- human authority,

- and uncertainty.

21.611 Verifiable Provenance

Future Assets may carry signed provenance chains.

Verification shall still remain separate from semantic truth and rights clearance.

21.612 Standard Content Credentials

Standardised credentials may improve interoperability.

Canonical Omnira evidence shall remain authoritative for internal Decisions.

21.613 Rights Policy Compiler

A future compiler may convert licences, consent and policies into enforceable eligibility rules.

Human review remains necessary for ambiguity.

21.614 Automated Licence Classification

Models may extract licence terms.

Extracted interpretation shall preserve source, confidence and reviewer state.

21.615 Dynamic Consent Token

A subject may issue a machine-verifiable token expressing bounded consent.

The token shall remain revocable and purpose-limited.

21.616 Decentralised Rights Registry

External registries may publish ownership or licence claims.

Registration shall not become unquestioned truth.

21.617 Royalty Tracking

Future systems may attribute revenue or usage to contributing rights holders.

21.618 Usage Metering

Usage Grants may define:

- number of impressions,

- downloads,

- renders,

- or publications.

Metering accuracy shall remain explicit.

21.619 Programmable Licence

Human-readable terms shall remain available.

Technical and legal feasibility shall remain explicit.

21.632 Asset Success Criteria

The Asset architecture succeeds when:

- every Asset has stable identity,

- every accepted state has an immutable Version,

- storage and URLs remain implementation details,

- integrity is verifiable,

- lineage is reconstructable,

- rights and consent are scoped,

- attribution and disclosure are enforceable,

- cross-Project reuse is controlled,

- revocation propagates,

- and publication uses exact eligible Versions.

21.633 Asset Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- files or URLs become canonical identity,

- Outputs become Assets automatically,

- rights are inferred from possession,

- consent is assumed,

- Provider terms are not Versioned,

- attribution is lost,

- disputed Assets remain publishable,

- cross-Project reuse is silent,

- or historical lineage cannot be reconstructed.

text:
21.634 Canonical Asset Contract

The following requirements define canonical Assets:

1. Every Asset SHALL have stable identity.

2. Asset identity SHALL remain independent from filename.

3. Asset identity SHALL remain independent from URL.

4. Asset identity SHALL remain independent from storage path.

5. Asset SHALL identify Project and Tenant scope.

6. Asset type SHALL be explicit.

7. Data Classification SHALL be explicit.

8. Owner, controller or unresolved ownership state SHALL be explicit.

9. Asset lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

10. Current Version SHALL be explicit.

11. Output SHALL NOT become Asset automatically.

12. Admission SHALL require integrity and provenance.

13. Rights state SHALL be linked.

14. Consent state SHALL be linked where applicable.

15. Revoked Assets SHALL NOT receive new use.

16. Quarantined Assets SHALL NOT enter production.

17. Archived Assets SHALL remain historically resolvable.

18. Asset changes SHALL be attributable.

19. Historical state SHALL remain queryable.

20. Asset existence SHALL NOT create permission.

21.635 Canonical Asset Version Contract

The following requirements define Asset Versions:

1. Every Asset Version SHALL have stable identity.

2. Version SHALL identify parent Asset.

3. Content identity SHALL be explicit.

4. Media type SHALL be explicit.

5. Size or structure SHALL be explicit where applicable.

6. Integrity checksum SHALL be preserved.

7. Creator or creation source SHALL be explicit.

8. Creation time SHALL be explicit.

9. Lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

10. Acceptance state SHALL be explicit.

11. Accepted Versions SHALL be immutable.

12. Material changes SHALL create new Versions.

13. Revision SHALL identify prior Version.

14. Forks SHALL preserve lineage.

15. Merges SHALL preserve all contributors.

sectionTitles: 21.651 Asset, Provenance, Rights and Consent Invariants
text:
21.651 Asset, Provenance, Rights and Consent Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No Output becomes an Asset automatically.

- No file, URL, filename or storage path becomes canonical Asset identity.

- No Asset possession becomes ownership.

- No ownership claim becomes permission for every use.

- No licence becomes consent.

- No consent becomes copyright ownership.

- No public availability becomes public-domain proof.

- No generated Asset becomes rights-free automatically.

- No Provider capability becomes commercial-use permission.

- No current Provider terms overwrite historical terms evidence.

- No reference Asset becomes reusable outside its scope automatically.

- No private image or Voice becomes training material automatically.

- No recording consent becomes publication or cloning consent automatically.

- No minor media receives ordinary low-risk treatment.

- No unresolved rights become cleared silently.

- No required attribution or disclosure disappears in a derivative.

- No revoked Asset returns through backup restore.

- No composite is eligible when one mandatory component is ineligible.

- No publication package contains an uncleared Asset.

- No rights, consent or Asset failure bypasses the Intelligence Fabric.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
21.652 Closing Statement

Assets are the durable things Omnira creates, receives, transforms, stores and delivers.

Provenance explains where those Assets came from.

Rights define which uses are permitted.

Consent defines which human or protected-subject uses are authorised.

Integrity proves that the recorded Version matches the stored content.

Custody explains who or what held the Asset.

Acceptance determines whether the Asset is good enough for a defined purpose.

Publication Eligibility determines whether it may be used publicly.

These are separate truths.

The Asset defines the governed object.

The Asset Version defines its immutable state.

The Representation defines its technical form.

The Location defines where it is stored.

The Integrity Record proves its content identity.

The Provenance Record preserves creation and transformation lineage.

The Chain-of-Custody Record preserves possession and transfer.

The Rights Profile summarises the permitted-use state.

The Licence defines granted rights and conditions.

The Terms Snapshot preserves Provider-specific obligations.

The Usage Grant binds permission to a Project, purpose, channel, audience, territory and time.

The Consent Grant binds human permission to an exact use.

The Guardian Authority protects minors and dependent subjects.

The Attribution Requirement preserves credit.

The Disclosure Requirement preserves transparency.

The Rights Decision evaluates one intended use.

The Publication Package contains only exact eligible Versions.

For Familje-Stunden, this architecture ensures that:

- Nova and Pling remain Project-governed character Assets,

- private family photos do not become public references,

- children’s likenesses require strong guardian authority,

- narration Voices remain inside their Consent Grants,

- music and fonts preserve their licences,

- and every public package contains only accepted and cleared material.

For The Prompt, it ensures that:

- source evidence remains distinct from generated illustration,

- screenshots and articles are not reused merely because they are online,

- synthetic visuals are disclosed when required,

- and publication Packages preserve exact source, Asset and rights lineage.

For GainPilot, it ensures that:

- exercise footage,

- performers,

- Voices,

- music,

- animations,

- logos,

- and coaching materials

remain traceable, eligible and commercially governed.

For Omnira, it ensures that:

- user uploads,

- Provider Outputs,

- local creations,

- human contributions,

- open-source packages,

- stock media,

- Models,

- Tools,

- datasets,

- and publication Deliverables

participate through one canonical Asset architecture.

The user may own the source.

The Project may hold a licence.

A Provider may generate an Output.

A human may contribute an edit.

Omnira may store the Asset.

A platform may distribute it.

A subject may grant or revoke consent.

None of those facts should be collapsed into one vague claim that the content is “ours.”

No Asset without identity.

No Version without integrity.

No derivative without lineage.

No Provider Output without terms evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
No commercial use without rights eligibility.

No likeness or Voice use without valid authority.

No minor media without guardian governance.

No attribution obligation left to memory.

No synthetic-media disclosure hidden when required.

No publication with unresolved mandatory rights.

No revocation without propagation.

No deletion without custody and Location review.

The user retains ownership and consent authority.

The Project retains scope and purpose.

Omnira retains provenance and enforcement.

The Fabric preserves what was created, who contributed, what may be done with it and what must never be assumed.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical architecture, object model, lifecycle, boundaries, governance requirements and conformance rules for execution evidence, evaluation evidence, Decision Evidence, Derived Learning and Governed Memory within the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

It establishes:

- how every meaningful Execution remains reconstructable,

- how evidence differs from logs, telemetry, provenance, Assets and ordinary application data,

- how Execution Records, Attempt Records, Receipts and Evidence Bundles remain distinct,

- how Provider responses, Tool results, human contributions and external state observations become governed evidence,

- how evidence confidence, completeness, freshness, integrity and trust are represented,

- how facts remain distinguishable from claims, observations, interpretations and Decisions,

- how evaluation evidence remains linked to exact Outputs, Assets, Models, Providers and Deployments,

- how Decision Evidence explains why Omnira selected, approved, rejected, retried, stopped or escalated an action,

- how Derived Learning is formed from evidence without becoming unquestioned truth,

- how learning remains scoped to the correct Tenant, Project, Capability, resource and time period,

- how confidence, validity, expiry, challenge and replacement are preserved,

- how Governed Memory differs from raw chat history, logs, vector indexes and arbitrary stored context,

- how Memory admission requires purpose, authority, classification, provenance and retention,

- how Atlas and other Agents retrieve Memory without receiving unrestricted historical data,

- how Agent identity and Memory remain independent from the Model currently serving the Agent,

- how working memory, episodic memory, semantic memory, procedural memory and policy memory remain distinct,

- how Project Memory remains isolated from Personal, Tenant and Platform Memory,

- how private, confidential and Local Only evidence remains protected,

- how consent, rights and retention limit memory use,

- how incorrect or outdated Memory is challenged, corrected, superseded, expired or deleted,

- how contradictory evidence remains visible rather than overwritten silently,

- how Memory retrieval preserves source citations and confidence,

- how Derived Learning influences Routing, Planning, Quality, Reliability and Cost without bypassing policy,

- how feedback and outcomes are converted into evaluation rather than raw reinforcement,

- how Model-generated summaries are prevented from becoming canonical fact automatically,

- how human knowledge remains attributable,

- how system self-observation remains bounded,

- how event streams, audit records, Metrics and traces support but do not replace governed evidence,

- how evidence and Memory survive provider, Model and infrastructure changes,

- how incidents involving corrupted evidence, false Memory, leakage or unauthorised learning are contained,

- and how Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy evidence, learning and Memory foundation.

A log is not automatically evidence.

Evidence is not automatically fact.

A Provider response is not automatically true.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
An accepted Output is not automatically permanent Memory.

Provenance is not evaluation.

Evaluation is not Decision Evidence.

Decision Evidence is not Derived Learning.

Derived Learning is not Governed Memory.

Governed Memory is not a raw transcript archive.

A vector embedding is not Memory authority.

A high confidence score is not certainty.

Repeated occurrence is not proof of universality.

An Agent’s statement is not canonical truth merely because the Agent produced it.

A human correction shall not disappear behind a later Model summary.

A newer Memory item does not automatically invalidate an older one without scope and evidence.

Deletion from an index does not prove deletion from every evidence store.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

Data classification, privacy and isolation are expanded in Chapter 23.

Approval, authority and bounded autonomy are expanded in Chapter 24.

Observability, audit and Incident Response are expanded in Chapter 25.

Implementation and operational conformance must be verified separately.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
sectionTitles: 22.2 Purpose of Evidence, Learning and Memory Governance
text:
22.2 Purpose of Evidence, Learning and Memory Governance

The Intelligence Fabric performs work through:

- Agents,

- Models,

- Providers,

- Tools,

- Adapters,

- Connectors,

- local Nodes,

- human operators,

- scheduled workflows,

- external services,

- and publication systems.

Those systems produce:

- requests,

- Plans,

- Attempts,

- Outputs,

- provider-job states,

- Costs,

- Quality results,

- approvals,

- incidents,

- external side effects,

- user feedback,

- and business outcomes.

Without canonical evidence governance, Omnira could:

- forget why a Provider was selected,

- retry a paid job whose outcome is unknown,

- treat a generated answer as verified fact,

- learn from a failed or rejected Output,

- propagate one Project’s preference into another Project,

- preserve outdated information indefinitely,

- expose private transcripts through Agent context,

- lose links between a Memory claim and its sources,

- overwrite contradictory evidence,

- or allow one Model’s summary to become permanent system truth.

The architecture exists to ensure that Omnira can answer:

- What happened?

- What was intended?

- Which Plan and policy applied?

- Which resource executed the work?

- What did the Provider or Tool return?

- Which external state was verified?

- What did the human approve or reject?

- Which evidence supported the Decision?

- What was learned?

- How confident is that learning?

- Which scope does it apply to?

- When does it expire?

- Who may retrieve it?

- How can it be challenged or replaced?

- What remains unknown?

22.3 Evidence

Evidence is a governed record or artefact that supports reconstruction, verification, evaluation or explanation of a claim, event, state, Decision or outcome.

Evidence may be:

- direct,

- indirect,

- machine-generated,

- human-generated,

- Provider-generated,

- externally verified,

- inferred,

- or disputed.

22.4 Evidence Is Not Truth

Evidence supports a conclusion.

It does not guarantee that the conclusion is correct.

22.5 Evidence Is Not Log Data

Logs may provide evidence.

Ordinary debug or operational log entries do not become canonical evidence automatically.

22.6 Evidence Is Not Provenance Alone

Provenance explains origin and transformation lineage.

Evidence may additionally support:

- quality,

- external state,

- authority,

- cost,

- or Decision reasoning.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
sectionTitles: 22.15 Evidence, Learning and Memory Control Plane
22.16 Canonical Evidence, Learning and Memory Objects
text:
22.7 Evidence Is Not Memory

Evidence may be retained without being admitted into Agent-accessible Memory.

22.8 Evidence Is Not Learning

Learning is a derived and governed interpretation of evidence.

22.9 Learning Is Not Automatic

The existence of repeated evidence does not authorise automatic creation of a permanent rule.

22.10 Governed Memory

Governed Memory is an authorised, scoped, attributable, classified, reviewable and lifecycle-controlled representation of knowledge, preference, procedure, context or historical fact intended for future retrieval.

Governed Memory shall remain linked to evidence or an authorised human source.

22.11 Memory Is Not Transcript Storage

A transcript archive may support audit or reconstruction.

It shall not become the canonical Memory layer by default.

22.12 Memory Is Not Prompt Context

Prompt context is the bounded data supplied to one Model invocation.

It may include retrieved Memory.

It is not itself durable Memory.

22.13 Memory Is Not Vector Storage

A vector store may index Memory or evidence.

The vector store does not define canonical truth, ownership or authority.

22.14 Memory Is Not Agent Identity

Agent identity remains stable even when its Memory changes.

Memory remains independently governed.

22.15 Evidence, Learning and Memory Control Plane

The Evidence, Learning and Memory Control Plane is the governed collection of services and canonical objects responsible for:

- evidence capture,

- integrity,

- classification,

- evaluation,

- Decision explanation,

- outcome verification,

- learning derivation,

- Memory admission,

- Memory retrieval,

- challenge,

- correction,

- supersession,

- expiry,

- retention,

- deletion,

- and audit.

It shall integrate with:

- Capability Requests,

- Planning,

- Routing,

- Scheduling,

- Execution,

- Providers,

- Models,

- Tools,

- Assets,

- Rights,

- Consent,

- Identity,

- Policy,

- Quality,

- Reliability,

- Cost,

- Approvals,

- Observability,

- and Incident Response.

22.16 Canonical Evidence, Learning and Memory Objects

The canonical architecture should include or reference:

- Evidence Item,

- Evidence Source,

- Evidence Claim,

- Evidence Bundle,

- Execution Record,

- Attempt Record,

- Execution Receipt,

- Provider Response Record,

- Tool Result Record,

- Human Action Record,

- External State Observation,

- Outcome Verification,

- Evaluation Record,

- Quality Finding,

- Feedback Record,

- Decision Evidence,

- Decision Rationale,

- Decision Trace,

- Derived Learning,

- Learning Candidate,

- Learning Review,

- Learning Policy,

- Memory Domain,

- Memory Item,

- Memory Version,

- Memory Source Link,

- Memory Admission Decision,

- Memory Retrieval Record,

- Memory Challenge,

- Memory Correction,

- Memory Supersession,

- Memory Expiry,

- Memory Deletion Record,

- Memory Index Entry,

- and Evidence Incident.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.17 Evidence Item

An Evidence Item is one canonical unit supporting reconstruction, validation or reasoning.

It shall include or reference:

- evidenceItemId,

- type,

- subject,

- claim or event,

- source,

- producer,

- observedAt,

- recordedAt,

- scope,

- classification,

- integrity,

- confidence,

- freshness,

- lifecycle,

- and provenance.

22.18 Evidence Item Identity

Every material Evidence Item shall have stable canonical identity.

22.19 Evidence Type

Evidence types may include:

- request evidence,

- Plan evidence,

- execution evidence,

- Provider evidence,

- Tool evidence,

- human evidence,

- external state evidence,

- cost evidence,

- quality evidence,

- authority evidence,

- rights evidence,

- publication evidence,

- Incident evidence,

- and outcome evidence.

22.20 Direct Evidence

Direct Evidence originates from the system or event being observed.

Examples include:

- Provider job status,

- external publication ID,

- signed response,

- file checksum,

- or human approval record.

22.21 Indirect Evidence

Indirect Evidence supports a conclusion through interpretation or correlation.

Examples include:

- inferred Provider outage,

- likely duplicate publication,

- or estimated user preference.

22.22 Primary Evidence

Primary Evidence is the most direct authoritative source available for the claim.

22.23 Secondary Evidence

Secondary Evidence reports or interprets another source.

22.24 Corroborating Evidence

Corroborating Evidence independently supports the same claim.

22.25 Contradictory Evidence

Contradictory Evidence conflicts with another Evidence Item.

It shall remain visible and linked.

22.26 Negative Evidence

Negative Evidence records the absence of an expected result or signal.

Absence shall not be interpreted beyond what the observation can prove.

22.27 Human Evidence

Human Evidence may include:

- approval,

- rejection,

- correction,

- observation,

- attestation,

- review,

- or manual result entry.

22.28 Machine Evidence

Machine Evidence may include:

- API response,

- Tool Output,

- checksum,

- Metric,

- trace,

- or structured validation result.

22.29 Provider Evidence

Provider Evidence originates from an external Provider.

It remains subject to:

- Provider trust,

- Account identity,

- timestamp,

- response integrity,

- and possible inconsistency.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.30 Model-Generated Evidence

Model-generated text may describe or classify evidence.

It shall not become primary evidence of external truth automatically.

22.31 External State Evidence

External State Evidence records an observation about an external system.

Examples include:

- post published,

- file exists,

- invoice issued,

- job completed,

- email sent,

- or repository commit present.

22.32 Evidence Scope

Every Evidence Item shall identify applicable:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- Capability,

- Execution,

- Asset,

- resource,

- and time range

where relevant.

22.33 Evidence Classification

Evidence shall receive Data Classification based on its content and source.

22.34 Evidence Producer

The producer may be:

- Human Principal,

- Service Principal,

- Agent,

- Provider,

- Tool,

- Node,

- or external system.

22.35 Evidence Source

The Evidence Source identifies where the observation or artefact originated.

22.36 Evidence Source Identity

Every persistent Evidence Source shall have stable identity.

22.37 Source Trust

Source trust may be:

- authoritative,

- verified,

- high,

- moderate,

- low,

- unknown,

- disputed,

- or compromised.

22.38 Source Trust Is Scoped

A Provider may be authoritative for its own job status but not for independent Quality evaluation.

22.39 Evidence Subject

The subject identifies what the evidence is about.

22.40 Evidence Claim

An Evidence Claim is a structured proposition supported or contradicted by Evidence Items.

It shall include or reference:

- evidenceClaimId,

- statement,

- subject,

- scope,

- time,

- supporting Evidence,

- contradicting Evidence,

- confidence,

- status,

- and provenance.

22.41 Evidence Claim Identity

Every material Evidence Claim shall have stable identity.

22.42 Claim Status

States may include:

- proposed,

- supported,

- strongly supported,

- verified,

- contradicted,

- disputed,

- unresolved,

- expired,

- and superseded.

22.43 Verified Claim

Verified means the claim satisfies the defined verification policy for its scope.

It does not mean universal certainty.

22.44 Unresolved Claim

Required evidence remains incomplete or conflicting.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.45 Disputed Claim

Material evidence or authorised human Decisions conflict.

22.46 Evidence Confidence

Confidence estimates how strongly the available evidence supports a claim.

It shall preserve:

- method,

- scale,

- source quality,

- evidence count,

- contradictions,

- and uncertainty.

22.47 Confidence Scale

A canonical confidence scale may include:

- unknown,

- very low,

- low,

- moderate,

- high,

- very high,

- and verified under defined policy.

22.48 Confidence Is Not Probability Automatically

A confidence label shall not be represented as a precise probability unless the method supports that interpretation.

22.49 Evidence Freshness

Freshness indicates how current the Evidence Item is relative to the claim.

22.50 Freshness Window

The valid freshness window may depend on:

- Provider status,

- pricing,

- user preference,

- publication state,

- hardware health,

- or stable architecture fact.

22.51 Stale Evidence

Stale Evidence may remain historically useful while becoming ineligible for current Decisions.

22.52 Evidence Validity

Validity defines the time and conditions under which the Evidence Item may support a Decision.

22.53 Evidence Integrity

Evidence integrity confirms that the stored evidence matches the recorded content.

22.54 Evidence Checksum

Material evidence artefacts should have checksums.

22.55 Evidence Signature

Signed evidence may strengthen origin and integrity claims.

22.56 Evidence Tamper State

States may include:

- intact,

- modified with attribution,

- corrupted,

- disputed,

- missing,

- and unknown.

22.57 Evidence Completeness

Completeness may be:

- complete,

- materially complete,

- partial,

- minimal,

- unknown,

- or unavailable.

22.58 Evidence Lifecycle

Evidence lifecycle may include:

- captured,

- validating,

- admitted,

- restricted,

- challenged,

- disputed,

- superseded,

- expired,

- archived,

- pending deletion,

- and deleted.

22.59 Captured Evidence

Captured Evidence has entered the system but may not yet be validated.

22.60 Admitted Evidence

Admitted Evidence satisfies the minimum governance requirements for its intended use.

22.61 Restricted Evidence

Restricted Evidence may be used only within defined scopes.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.62 Challenged Evidence

A challenge asserts that the evidence or its interpretation may be wrong or incomplete.

22.63 Superseded Evidence

Newer or stronger evidence may supersede its use for current Decisions without erasing history.

22.64 Archived Evidence

Archived Evidence remains available for audit or historical interpretation.

22.65 Evidence Bundle

An Evidence Bundle is a governed collection of Evidence Items supporting one Execution, Asset, Decision, Incident or outcome.

It shall include or reference:

- evidenceBundleId,

- subject,

- Evidence Items,

- completeness,

- integrity,

- classification,

- lifecycle,

- and provenance.

22.66 Evidence Bundle Identity

Every material Evidence Bundle shall have stable identity.

22.67 Execution Evidence Bundle

An Execution Evidence Bundle may contain:

- Request,

- Intent Envelope,

- Plan,

- Routing Decision,

- Placement Decision,

- approvals,

- Attempt records,

- Provider responses,

- Tool results,

- Costs,

- Outputs,

- evaluations,

- and external outcome verification.

22.68 Decision Evidence Bundle

A Decision Evidence Bundle contains the evidence used for one Decision.

22.69 Incident Evidence Bundle

An Incident Evidence Bundle preserves relevant Events, logs, state, Assets and Decisions.

22.70 Evidence Bundle Immutability

Released Bundle Versions shall not be edited in place.

22.71 Execution Record

An Execution Record is the canonical historical record of one Execution.

It shall include or reference:

- executionId,

- Capability Request,

- Intent Envelope,

- Plan Version,

- Execution Graph,

- Principal,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- authority,

- policy Versions,

- routing,

- placement,

- Attempts,

- Outputs,

- Costs,

- state transitions,

- completion,

- and evidence.
