22.72 Execution Record Identity

Execution identity shall remain stable throughout the lifecycle.

22.73 Execution Record Is Not Receipt

The Execution Record may contain detailed canonical state.

The Execution Receipt is a summarised immutable result representation.

22.74 Execution State History

Every material state transition shall be preserved.

22.75 Execution Start

Start evidence shall identify:

- authorised Plan,

- selected resources,

- Budget,

- and initiating Principal.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.76 Execution Completion

Completion shall distinguish:

- technical completion,

- Output availability,

- semantic success,

- external side-effect completion,

- business completion,

- and acceptance.

22.77 Execution Failure

Failure evidence shall identify:

- failing Step,

- Attempt,

- error class,

- recovery state,

- and unresolved consequences.

22.78 Execution Cancellation

Cancellation shall preserve:

- requestor,

- effective time,

- affected Attempts,

- external jobs,

- Costs,

- and remaining unknowns.

22.79 Execution Timeout

Timeout does not prove that external work did not complete.

22.80 Unknown Outcome

Unknown Outcome is a valid execution and evidence state when the system cannot establish whether a consequential operation completed.

It shall remain explicit until reconciled or resolved.

22.81 Attempt Record

An Attempt Record describes one bounded invocation of a resource.

It shall include or reference:

- attemptId,

- Execution,

- Step,

- resource,

- Provider,

- Account,

- Connection,

- Credential Reference,

- request payload evidence,

- start,

- end,

- result,

- usage,

- cost,

- error,

- retry relation,

- and provenance.

22.82 Attempt Record Identity

Every Attempt shall have stable identity.

22.83 Attempt Is Not Execution

One Execution may contain several Attempts.

22.84 Attempt Input Evidence

The exact canonical Input and Adapter-produced request should remain attributable.

22.85 Attempt Output Evidence

The raw or structured Provider or Tool result shall remain linked according to policy.

22.86 Attempt Result State

States may include:

- succeeded,

- failed,

- timed out,

- cancelled,

- rejected,

- unknown outcome,

- externally pending,

- and superseded.

22.87 Attempt Retry Relation

Retries shall identify which prior Attempt they follow and why.

22.88 Attempt Fallback Relation

Fallback Attempts shall identify the resource or method replaced.

22.89 Attempt Cost Evidence

Estimated and actual cost shall remain attributable to the exact Attempt.

22.90 Attempt Usage Evidence

Usage may include:

- tokens,

- images,

- seconds,

- characters,

- compute,

- storage,

- calls,

- or human time.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
sectionTitles: 22.101 Exit Status Is Not Semantic Success
text:
22.91 Provider Response Record

A Provider Response Record captures the Provider’s response or acknowledged state.

It shall include or reference:

- providerResponseRecordId,

- Attempt,

- Provider,

- Account,

- endpoint,

- request correlation,

- external job ID,

- status,

- payload reference,

- receivedAt,

- integrity,

- and provenance.

22.92 Provider Response Identity

Every material Provider Response Record shall have stable identity.

22.93 Provider Acknowledgement

Acknowledgement proves receipt or acceptance according to the Provider’s semantics.

It does not necessarily prove completion.

22.94 Provider Completion

Provider-reported completion shall remain distinct from Omnira verification and acceptance.

22.95 Provider Error

Provider error evidence shall preserve:

- code,

- category,

- retry guidance,

- request correlation,

- and response time.

22.96 Provider Callback Evidence

Callback evidence shall include:

- source authentication,

- Subscription,

- event ID,

- job ID,

- timestamp,

- payload integrity,

- and processing result.

22.97 Provider Poll Evidence

Polling observations shall preserve sequence and time.

22.98 Provider Status Conflict

Conflicting callback, polling and dashboard states shall remain visible until reconciled.

22.99 Tool Result Record

A Tool Result Record captures one Tool Invocation and its result.

It shall include or reference:

- toolResultRecordId,

- Tool,

- Tool Version,

- Invocation,

- Node,

- Sandbox,

- Inputs,

- outputs,

- exit status,

- semantic validation,

- side effects,

- time,

- and provenance.

22.100 Tool Result Identity

Every material Tool Result Record shall have stable identity.

22.101 Exit Status Is Not Semantic Success

A zero exit code does not prove the intended change occurred correctly.

22.102 Tool Side-Effect Evidence

Consequential Tool use shall preserve:

- target,

- before state,

- requested mutation,

- after state,

- and verification.

22.103 Tool Read Evidence

Read operations may preserve:

- source identity,

- Version,

- range,

- and checksum

without storing unnecessary full content.

22.104 Human Action Record

A Human Action Record captures a material human contribution or Decision.

It shall include or reference:

- humanActionRecordId,

- Principal,

- role,

- action,

- target,

- scope,

- time,

- authority,

- evidence,

- and result.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.105 Human Action Identity

Every material Human Action shall have stable identity.

22.106 Human Approval Evidence

Approval evidence shall identify:

- approver,

- approved scope,

- conditions,

- expiry,

- and exact target Version.

22.107 Human Rejection Evidence

Rejection evidence shall preserve:

- target,

- reasons,

- annotations,

- and permitted next actions.

22.108 Human Correction Evidence

A correction shall preserve:

- prior claim,

- corrected claim,

- source,

- actor,

- and time.

22.109 Human Attestation

An attestation is a human assertion.

Its authority and evidence basis shall remain explicit.

22.110 Manual Result Entry

Manual entry shall be labelled as human-provided rather than system-verified.

22.111 External State Observation

An External State Observation records one observation of an external system.

It shall include or reference:

- observationId,

- external system,

- subject,

- observed state,

- method,

- observer,

- observedAt,

- confidence,

- freshness,

- and evidence.

22.112 External Observation Identity

Every material External State Observation shall have stable identity.

22.113 Observation Method

Methods may include:

- API read,

- webhook,

- browser inspection,

- file retrieval,

- database query,

- Provider dashboard,

- human confirmation,

- or independent service.

22.114 Observation Authority

The observing method shall be authorised and appropriate to the claim.

22.115 Observation Freshness

External state may change immediately after observation.

Freshness shall remain visible.

22.116 Outcome Verification

Outcome Verification determines whether the intended real-world or external outcome occurred.

It shall include or reference:

- outcomeVerificationId,

- Execution,

- intended outcome,

- external target,

- observations,

- verifier,

- decision,

- confidence,

- time,

- and provenance.

22.117 Outcome Verification Identity

Every material Outcome Verification shall have stable identity.

22.118 Technical Outcome

A Technical Outcome may be:

- file created,

- API request accepted,

- or job completed.

22.119 Business Outcome

A Business Outcome may be:

- content published,

- customer received delivery,

- payment settled,

- subscriber converted,

- or user accepted the result.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.120 User Outcome

A User Outcome describes whether the user’s intended need was satisfied.

22.121 Outcome Is Not Output

An Output may exist without achieving the intended Outcome.

22.122 Publication Outcome

Publication completion requires external verification such as:

- post ID,

- URL,

- account,

- timestamp,

- and visibility state.

22.123 Delivery Outcome

Delivery may require evidence that the intended recipient or system received the Asset.

22.124 Mutation Outcome

A mutation requires verification of the target state after the operation.

22.125 Outcome Unknown

Unknown remains valid when verification cannot establish completion.

22.126 Evaluation Record

An Evaluation Record captures an assessment of an Output, Asset, Execution, resource or outcome.

It shall include or reference:

- evaluationRecordId,

- target,

- target Version,

- evaluator,

- rubric,

- method,

- evidence,

- findings,

- score,

- mandatory failures,

- confidence,

- decision,

- and time.

22.127 Evaluation Record Identity

Every material Evaluation Record shall have stable identity.

22.128 Evaluation Target

Targets may include:

- Output,

- Candidate,

- Asset,

- Model Deployment,

- Provider,

- Tool,

- Plan,

- Execution,

- or Outcome.

22.129 Evaluator

The evaluator may be:

- human,

- Model,

- Tool,

- rule engine,

- benchmark,

- or composite process.

22.130 Evaluator Identity

Evaluator identity and Version shall be explicit.

22.131 Evaluation Method

Methods may include:

- deterministic validation,

- benchmark,

- rubric review,

- pairwise comparison,

- human review,

- external ground truth,

- or statistical analysis.

22.132 Evaluation Evidence

Evaluation shall reference the exact evidence inspected.

22.133 Quality Finding

A Quality Finding is one specific evaluation result.

It shall include:

- findingId,

- criterion,

- target,

- severity,

- evidence,

- result,

- confidence,

- and remediation.

22.134 Quality Finding Identity

Every material Quality Finding shall have stable identity.

22.135 Mandatory Failure

A mandatory failure blocks acceptance regardless of average score.

22.136 Advisory Finding

An advisory finding suggests improvement without blocking use.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.137 Evaluation Score

Scores shall identify:

- scale,

- direction,

- weighting,

- and interpretation.

22.138 Evaluation Confidence

Confidence shall reflect:

- evidence quality,

- evaluator reliability,

- ambiguity,

- and agreement.

22.139 Evaluation Disagreement

Conflicting evaluations shall remain visible.

22.140 Evaluation Supersession

A new evaluation may supersede a prior current Decision while preserving history.

22.141 Evaluation Is Not Memory

Evaluation results may inform learning.

They shall not become permanent Memory automatically.

22.142 Feedback Record

A Feedback Record captures user or stakeholder response to an Output, interaction or outcome.

It shall include or reference:

- feedbackRecordId,

- contributor,

- target,

- feedback type,

- content,

- rating,

- scope,

- time,

- consent,

- and provenance.

22.143 Feedback Record Identity

Every material Feedback Record shall have stable identity.

22.144 Explicit Feedback

Explicit Feedback is intentionally provided by a human.

22.145 Implicit Feedback

Implicit Feedback is inferred from behaviour such as:

- selection,

- abandonment,

- edit,

- repetition,

- or rejection.

It shall remain labelled as inferred.

22.146 Feedback Scope

Feedback may apply to:

- one Output,

- one workflow,

- one Provider,

- one style,

- one Project,

- or one user preference.

22.147 Feedback Is Not Universal Preference

One action shall not become a global preference automatically.

22.148 Negative Feedback

Negative Feedback may identify:

- factual error,

- poor style,

- wrong timing,

- high cost,

- or unwanted behaviour.

22.149 Positive Feedback

Positive Feedback may support reuse.

It does not prove universal quality.

22.150 Feedback Consent

Personalisation and long-term preference learning may require explicit consent or policy.

22.151 Decision Evidence

Decision Evidence is the governed set of evidence supporting one selection, approval, rejection, escalation, retry, fallback, pause, stop or acceptance Decision.

It shall include or reference:

- decisionEvidenceId,

- Decision,

- subject,

- alternatives,

- constraints,

- policy Versions,

- Evidence Items,

- rationale,

- confidence,

- decision maker,

- and time.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.152 Decision Evidence Identity

Every material Decision Evidence record shall have stable identity.

22.153 Decision Rationale

The rationale explains how evidence, policy and constraints led to the Decision.

22.154 Decision Trace

A Decision Trace records the ordered evaluation path.

It may include:

- candidate generation,

- eligibility,

- ranking,

- exclusions,

- approvals,

- and final selection.

22.155 Decision Maker

The Decision Maker may be:

- human,

- policy engine,

- Router,

- Planner,

- evaluator,

- Agent,

- or composite authority.

22.156 Decision Authority

The Decision Maker shall have authority for the Decision class.

22.157 Decision Alternatives

Material alternatives considered should remain visible.

22.158 Excluded Alternative

An excluded alternative shall preserve the exclusion reason.

22.159 Selected Alternative

Selection shall identify the evidence and policy supporting it.

22.160 Decision Confidence

Confidence applies to the Decision’s supporting evidence and expected result.

It does not replace authority.

22.161 Decision Validity

A Decision may be valid only for:

- one Execution,

- one time window,

- one Asset Version,

- one policy Version,

- or one external state.

22.162 Decision Revalidation

Material state change may require a new Decision.

22.163 Routing Decision Evidence

Routing evidence may include:

- Candidate eligibility,

- quality evidence,

- cost,

- privacy,

- reliability,

- latency,

- and profile.

22.164 Planning Decision Evidence

Planning evidence may include:

- decomposition,

- dependencies,

- authority,

- placement,

- Budget,

- and fallback strategy.

22.165 Approval Decision Evidence

Approval evidence shall preserve the exact scope and conditions approved.

22.166 Retry Decision Evidence

Retry Decisions shall consider:

- error class,

- idempotency,

- prior cost,

- unknown outcome,

- and remaining Budget.

22.167 Fallback Decision Evidence

Fallback evidence shall show that mandatory constraints remain satisfied.

22.168 Acceptance Decision Evidence

Acceptance evidence shall preserve:

- target Version,

- Quality findings,

- rights,

- consent,

- and intended use.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
sectionTitles: 22.171 Decision Evidence Is Not Raw Chain of Thought
text:
22.169 Stop Decision Evidence

The reason for stopping may include:

- Budget,

- authority,

- safety,

- policy,

- repeated failure,

- or user cancellation.

22.170 Escalation Decision Evidence

Escalation shall identify:

- unresolved issue,

- required authority,

- affected scope,

- and available options.

22.171 Decision Evidence Is Not Raw Chain of Thought

The canonical record shall preserve concise, structured rationale and material evidence.

It shall not depend on hidden internal reasoning traces.

22.172 Explainability

Explainability provides a human- and machine-readable account of:

- what was decided,

- why,

- under which constraints,

- and with which evidence.

22.173 Explanation Audience

Different explanations may be produced for:

- user,

- operator,

- administrator,

- auditor,

- developer,

- or machine consumer.

22.174 Explanation Privacy

Explanations shall not expose:

- raw Secrets,

- protected prompts,

- unrelated personal data,

- or another Project’s evidence.

22.175 Derived Learning

Derived Learning is a governed conclusion, pattern, preference, performance observation, heuristic or procedural improvement inferred from evidence.

It shall include or reference:

- derivedLearningId,

- statement,

- type,

- scope,

- source Evidence,

- derivation method,

- confidence,

- limitations,

- validity,

- expiry,

- challenge state,

- owner,

- and provenance.

22.176 Derived Learning Identity

Every Derived Learning item shall have stable identity and Version.

22.177 Learning Type

Learning types may include:

- user preference,

- Project preference,

- workflow performance,

- Provider performance,

- Model suitability,

- quality pattern,

- cost pattern,

- reliability pattern,

- scheduling pattern,

- procedural improvement,

- risk signal,

- and domain knowledge.

22.178 Learning Candidate

A Learning Candidate is a proposed conclusion not yet admitted for operational use.

22.179 Learning Candidate Identity

Every material Learning Candidate shall have stable identity.

22.180 Learning Derivation

Derivation methods may include:

- explicit human statement,

- repeated evaluation,

- statistical aggregation,

- comparative benchmark,

- Incident review,

- feedback analysis,

- or authorised expert conclusion.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.181 Explicit Human Learning

A verified user statement may support a preference or factual Memory item.

Its scope shall still be explicit.

22.182 Statistical Learning

Statistical Learning shall preserve:

- sample size,

- period,

- population,

- exclusions,

- uncertainty,

- and method.

22.183 Comparative Learning

Comparative Learning may conclude that one resource performs better for one task class.

It shall not become a universal ranking.

22.184 Incident Learning

Incident review may produce:

- new control,

- safer procedure,

- routing restriction,

- or detection rule.

22.185 Procedural Learning

Procedural Learning describes a better sequence or method for future work.

22.186 Domain Learning

Domain Learning describes a fact or interpretation about the Project’s subject matter.

It requires evidence suitable for that knowledge class.

22.187 Preference Learning

Preference Learning captures choices such as:

- tone,

- style,

- timing,

- Provider ownership,

- review depth,

- or notification behaviour.

22.188 Preference Scope

Preference may apply to:

- one user,

- one Project,

- one channel,

- one Capability,

- or one production class.

22.189 Preference Strength

Preference strength may be:

- suggestion,

- default,

- strong preference,

- mandatory user rule,

- or prohibited option.

22.190 Preference Source

Source may be:

- explicit statement,

- repeated selection,

- repeated rejection,

- or inferred behaviour.

22.191 Inferred Preference

Inferred preference shall remain lower confidence than explicit instruction unless confirmed.

22.192 Resource Performance Learning

Performance Learning may include:

- quality,

- latency,

- cost,

- reliability,

- revision burden,

- and user acceptance.

22.193 Provider Learning

Provider Learning shall remain scoped to:

- Product,

- Account,

- region,

- Model,

- time period,

- and task class.

22.194 Model Learning

Model suitability shall identify exact Model Version or Deployment where material.

22.195 Tool Learning

Tool performance shall identify Tool Version and Environment.

22.196 Local Resource Learning

Local performance shall identify:

- Node,

- Runtime,

- Model Deployment,

- hardware,

- and configuration.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.197 Learning Confidence

Learning confidence shall reflect:

- evidence quality,

- evidence volume,

- contradictions,

- freshness,

- method,

- and review.

22.198 Learning Limitations

Every material Derived Learning item shall describe known limitations.

22.199 Learning Validity

Validity defines where and when the conclusion may be used.

22.200 Learning Expiry

Derived Learning shall expire when:

- evidence ages,

- Provider changes,

- Model changes,

- policy changes,

- Project changes,

- or a defined review period ends.

22.201 Learning Review

A Learning Review evaluates whether a Learning Candidate may influence operations or Memory.

It shall include or reference:

- learningReviewId,

- target,

- reviewer,

- evidence,

- scope,

- confidence,

- decision,

- conditions,

- and time.

22.202 Learning Review Identity

Every material Learning Review shall have stable identity.

22.203 Learning Review States

States may include:

- admitted,

- admitted with conditions,

- rejected,

- revision required,

- expired,

- and superseded.

22.204 Automatic Learning Admission

Automatic admission may be permitted only for low-risk, well-defined and reversible learning classes.

22.205 Human Learning Review

High-impact learning affecting:

- authority,

- privacy,

- publication,

- spend,

- or cross-Project behaviour

shall require human review.

22.206 Learning Policy

Learning Policy defines:

- eligible evidence,

- minimum sample,

- confidence threshold,

- review requirement,

- scope,

- expiry,

- and prohibited derivations.

22.207 Learning Policy Identity

Every Learning Policy shall have stable identity and Version.

22.208 Learning Isolation

Learning derived from one Tenant or Project shall not influence another without explicit authority and appropriate anonymisation or aggregation.

22.209 Personal Learning

Personal preferences remain bound to the user and authorised contexts.

22.210 Project Learning

Project Learning may influence future work inside that Project.

22.211 Tenant Learning

Tenant-wide Learning requires broader authority and evidence.

22.212 Platform Learning

Platform Learning should use:

- aggregated,

- minimised,

- rights-compatible,

- privacy-protected,

- and policy-approved

evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.213 Cross-Project Learning

Cross-Project transfer is prohibited by default.

22.214 Cross-Tenant Learning

Cross-Tenant learning is prohibited unless a separately approved privacy-preserving framework exists.

22.215 Learning From Rejected Outputs

Rejected Outputs may support negative learning when the rejection reason is clear and attributable.

22.216 Learning From Accepted Outputs

Acceptance may support positive learning.

It does not prove optimality.

22.217 Learning From Silence

Lack of feedback shall not be interpreted as approval automatically.

22.218 Learning From Success

Technical success shall not become business-success learning without Outcome Verification.

22.219 Learning From Failure

Failure shall be classified before producing a general conclusion.

22.220 Learning From One Incident

One severe Incident may justify an immediate safety restriction.

It shall remain labelled as precautionary when evidence is limited.

22.221 Learning From Provider Outage

Temporary outage evidence shall not become a permanent Provider-quality conclusion.

22.222 Learning From Cost

Cost learning shall preserve:

- currency,

- price Version,

- Provider Account,

- and time.

22.223 Learning From Quality

Quality learning shall preserve:

- rubric,

- evaluator,

- Output class,

- and target audience.

22.224 Learning From Human Correction

Human correction should receive strong weight within the corrected scope.

22.225 Learning Challenge

A Learning Challenge asserts that a Derived Learning item may be:

- incorrect,

- outdated,

- overbroad,

- under-supported,

- or mis-scoped.

22.226 Learning Challenge Identity

Every material Learning Challenge shall have stable identity.

22.227 Challenge Source

The challenger may be:

- user,

- administrator,

- Reviewer,

- system evaluation,

- Incident,

- or contradictory evidence.

22.228 Challenge Effect

A challenged Learning item may be:

- suspended,

- restricted,

- retained with warning,

- or sent for review.

22.229 Learning Correction

A correction creates a new Version with updated evidence and scope.

22.230 Learning Supersession

Supersession preserves the old item while marking a newer item as governing.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.231 Learning Revocation

Revocation blocks operational use immediately.

22.232 Learning Deletion

Deletion may remove content while preserving minimal audit metadata.

22.233 Governed Memory Domain

A Memory Domain is a canonical boundary defining ownership, purpose, scope and access for Memory Items.

Domains may include:

- Personal Memory,

- Project Memory,

- Tenant Memory,

- Agent Memory,

- Workflow Memory,

- Platform Memory,

- and Recovery Memory.

22.234 Memory Domain Identity

Every Memory Domain shall have stable identity and Versioned policy.

22.235 Personal Memory

Personal Memory stores user-specific preferences, context and authorised facts.

It shall not become visible to unrelated Tenants or Projects.

22.236 Project Memory

Project Memory stores knowledge and preferences authorised for one Project.

22.237 Tenant Memory

Tenant Memory stores organisation-wide knowledge approved for Tenant use.

22.238 Agent Memory

Agent Memory stores role-relevant knowledge for one Agent identity.

It remains bounded by Project, Tenant and policy.

22.239 Workflow Memory

Workflow Memory stores reusable state or lessons for one workflow class.

22.240 Platform Memory

Platform Memory stores broadly applicable platform knowledge.

It shall exclude Project-confidential content by default.

22.241 Recovery Memory

Recovery Memory stores critical continuity information required to restore systems or governance.

22.242 Memory Domain Ownership

Every Memory Domain shall identify:

- owner,

- controller,

- administrators,

- permitted readers,

- permitted writers,

- and policy.

22.243 Memory Domain Scope

Scope may include:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Agent,

- Capability,

- workflow,

- environment,

- data class,

- and time.

22.244 Memory Item

A Memory Item is one governed unit of retrievable knowledge or context.

It shall include or reference:

- memoryItemId,

- Memory Domain,

- statement or structured content,

- type,

- subject,

- scope,

- source links,

- classification,

- confidence,

- validity,

- expiry,

- authority,

- lifecycle,

- and provenance.

22.245 Memory Item Identity

Every Memory Item shall have stable identity.

22.246 Memory Version

Every material Memory change shall create a new Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
sectionTitles: 22.258 Memory Is Not Authority Source by Default
text:
22.247 Memory Content

Memory content may be:

- structured fact,

- preference,

- procedure,

- relationship,

- constraint,

- summary,

- decision,

- or historical episode.

22.248 Memory Type

Memory types may include:

- working,

- episodic,

- semantic,

- procedural,

- preference,

- relational,

- policy,

- operational,

- and recovery.

22.249 Working Memory

Working Memory stores short-lived context needed for current or near-current execution.

It shall have short retention and narrow scope.

22.250 Episodic Memory

Episodic Memory records meaningful past events or interactions.

It shall preserve:

- time,

- participants,

- scope,

- and evidence.

22.251 Semantic Memory

Semantic Memory represents facts, concepts and relationships.

It requires evidence and validity suitable for the claim.

22.252 Procedural Memory

Procedural Memory represents approved methods, workflows or operating instructions.

22.253 Preference Memory

Preference Memory stores explicit or reviewed preferences.

22.254 Relational Memory

Relational Memory represents governed relationships among:

- people,

- Projects,

- Assets,

- resources,

- and organisations.

22.255 Policy Memory

Policy Memory exposes current governing rules to authorised Agents.

The authoritative Policy service remains the source of truth.

22.256 Operational Memory

Operational Memory stores current operational facts such as:

- active branch,

- working directory,

- current milestone,

- or known recovery state.

It shall expire or update as operations change.

22.257 Recovery Memory

Recovery Memory preserves critical instructions such as:

- canonical repository,

- protected backup,

- migration state,

- or recovery restrictions.

22.258 Memory Is Not Authority Source by Default

Memory may describe authority.

The authoritative Identity, Policy and Approval systems determine current authority.

22.259 Memory Statement

A Memory Statement is a human-readable proposition stored in a Memory Item.

22.260 Structured Memory

Structured Memory may include typed fields and relationships rather than only narrative text.

22.261 Memory Subject

Every factual Memory Item should identify its subject.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.262 Memory Scope

Every Memory Item shall identify where it applies.

22.263 Memory Classification

Memory shall retain or increase the classification of its source evidence.

22.264 Memory Source Link

A Memory Source Link connects the Memory Item to:

- Evidence Items,

- human statements,

- Assets,

- Decisions,

- policies,

- or external sources.

22.265 Memory Source Link Identity

Every material source relationship shall have stable identity.

22.266 Source Link Requirement

Material factual or learned Memory shall have at least one authoritative or attributable source.

22.267 Source Independence

Several independent sources may increase confidence.

22.268 Source Contradiction

Contradictory sources shall remain linked and visible.

22.269 Memory Confidence

Memory confidence describes support for the Memory Item.

It shall not replace the underlying evidence.

22.270 Memory Validity

Validity defines the conditions under which retrieval may treat the item as current.

22.271 Memory Effective Time

A Memory Item may become effective at a defined time.

22.272 Memory Expiry

Memory shall expire automatically when its validity window ends.

22.273 Stable Memory

Some architectural doctrines may have long validity.

They shall still remain Versioned and challengeable.

22.274 Volatile Memory

Volatile information such as:

- prices,

- Provider status,

- branch state,

- current role holder,

- or device health

shall have short validity.

22.275 Historical Memory

Historical Memory may remain true about the past after it ceases to describe the present.

22.276 Memory Lifecycle

Memory lifecycle may include:

- proposed,

- validating,

- admitted,

- active,

- restricted,

- challenged,

- suspended,

- superseded,

- expired,

- revoked,

- archived,

- pending deletion,

- and deleted.

22.277 Proposed Memory

Proposed Memory has not yet passed admission requirements.

22.278 Active Memory

Active Memory may participate in authorised retrieval.

22.279 Restricted Memory

Restricted Memory may be retrieved only under narrower conditions.

22.280 Suspended Memory

Suspended Memory is temporarily excluded from retrieval.

22.281 Superseded Memory

Superseded Memory remains historical but does not govern current retrieval by default.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.282 Expired Memory

Expired Memory shall not be presented as current without explicit historical context.

22.283 Archived Memory

Archived Memory remains available for audit or historical lookup.

22.284 Memory Admission

Memory Admission determines whether evidence, feedback or Derived Learning may enter a Memory Domain.

It shall evaluate:

- purpose,

- authority,

- source,

- confidence,

- classification,

- scope,

- rights,

- consent,

- retention,

- expiry,

- and risk.

22.285 Memory Admission Decision

A Memory Admission Decision shall include or reference:

- memoryAdmissionDecisionId,

- candidate,

- target Domain,

- sources,

- policy Versions,

- reviewer,

- decision,

- conditions,

- expiry,

- and provenance.

22.286 Memory Admission Identity

Every material Memory Admission Decision shall have stable identity.

22.287 Admission States

States may include:

- admitted,

- admitted with conditions,

- rejected,

- deferred,

- review required,

- and expired.

22.288 Explicit Human Memory

A user may explicitly ask Omnira to remember a fact or preference.

The system shall still determine:

- scope,

- classification,

- retention,

- and permitted consumers.

22.289 Automatic Memory Admission

Automatic admission shall be limited to low-risk, well-defined and reversible classes.

22.290 Prohibited Automatic Memory

The following shall not enter long-term Memory automatically:

- raw Secrets,

- Credentials,

- private messages,

- unverified personal data,

- transient Provider errors,

- raw chain-of-thought,

- complete private transcripts,

- unreviewed Model claims,

- or unrelated Project content.

22.291 Raw Prompt Prohibition

Raw prompts shall not be admitted into permanent Memory merely because they were used in an Execution.

22.292 Raw Output Prohibition

Raw Model Outputs shall not become Memory without evaluation and admission.

22.293 Transcript Minimisation

Conversation history may be summarised into scoped Memory only when:

- relevant,

- authorised,

- attributable,

- and reviewable.

22.294 Memory Summary

A Memory Summary is a derived representation of one or more sources.

It shall preserve source links and limitations.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.295 Summary Drift

Repeated summarisation may distort meaning.

Canonical source links shall remain available.

22.296 Memory Granularity

Memory should be stored at the smallest meaningful and retrievable scope.

22.297 Overbroad Memory

Overbroad statements shall be rejected or narrowed.

22.298 Memory Duplication

Duplicate or overlapping Memory Items should be linked or reconciled rather than multiplied silently.

22.299 Memory Consolidation

Consolidation may combine several compatible Items into a new Version.

All source relationships shall remain.

22.300 Memory Conflict

A Memory Conflict occurs when active Items make incompatible claims within overlapping scope.

22.301 Conflict Detection

Conflict detection may use:

- exact fields,

- temporal overlap,

- entity relationships,

- semantic comparison,

- and human challenge.

22.302 Conflict Resolution

Resolution may:

- narrow scope,

- identify different time periods,

- supersede one Item,

- retain both as disputed,

- or request human review.

22.303 No Silent Overwrite

Conflicting Memory shall not be overwritten without an attributable Decision.

22.304 Memory Correction

A Memory Correction creates a new Version or replacement item.

It shall preserve:

- prior statement,

- corrected statement,

- source,

- actor,

- and reason.

22.305 Memory Challenge

A Memory Challenge asserts that an Item is:

- incorrect,

- incomplete,

- outdated,

- misclassified,

- unauthorised,

- or overbroad.

22.306 Memory Challenge Identity

Every material Memory Challenge shall have stable identity.

22.307 Challenge Effect

A challenge may:

- add warning,

- suspend retrieval,

- require review,

- or trigger immediate correction.

22.308 User Correction Priority

A user correction about their own preference or personal context should receive strong priority within their authority.

It shall not override external legal or technical facts automatically.

22.309 Expert Correction

A qualified expert correction may supersede weaker evidence within the expert’s domain.

22.310 Automated Correction

Automated correction shall require sufficient evidence and policy.

22.311 Memory Supersession

Supersession identifies a newer governing Memory Item while preserving the prior Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.312 Memory Revocation

Revocation removes future retrieval eligibility immediately.

22.313 Memory Deletion

Deletion removes the Memory content from defined stores according to policy.

22.314 Memory Deletion Record

A Memory Deletion Record shall include:

- deletionRecordId,

- target,

- reason,

- authority,

- Locations,

- indexes,

- completion,

- and time.

22.315 Memory Deletion Identity

Every material deletion process shall have stable identity.

22.316 Memory Retention

Retention shall be based on:

- purpose,

- Project need,

- personal preference,

- classification,

- rights,

- consent,

- audit,

- and policy.

22.317 Minimum Retention

Some recovery or governance Memory may require minimum retention.

22.318 Maximum Retention

Sensitive personal or operational Memory may require automatic expiry.

22.319 Memory Hold

A hold may preserve Memory during:

- Incident,

- dispute,

- recovery,

- or audit.

22.320 Memory Retrieval

Memory Retrieval selects eligible Memory Items for one bounded request or Agent context.

It shall consider:

- Principal,

- Agent,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Capability,

- purpose,

- classification,

- authority,

- relevance,

- confidence,

- freshness,

- and token Budget.

22.321 Memory Retrieval Record

A Memory Retrieval Record shall include or reference:

- memoryRetrievalRecordId,

- requester,

- Agent,

- Request,

- Domain,

- query,

- candidate Items,

- selected Items,

- exclusions,

- ranking,

- time,

- and provenance.

22.322 Memory Retrieval Identity

Every material retrieval shall have stable identity.

22.323 Retrieval Eligibility

Only active and authorised Memory Items may be retrieved.

22.324 Retrieval Relevance

Relevance shall be evaluated inside the correct scope.

22.325 Retrieval Confidence

Low-confidence Memory should be labelled or excluded according to task risk.

22.326 Retrieval Freshness

Stale Memory shall not be presented as current without warning.

22.327 Retrieval Purpose

The same Memory Item may be eligible for one purpose and prohibited for another.

22.328 Retrieval Minimisation

Only the minimum necessary Memory shall enter Model context.

22.329 Retrieval Explanation

The system should be able to explain which Memory Items influenced the response or Plan.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.330 Retrieval Citations

Material factual Memory supplied to an Agent should preserve source references where practical.

22.331 Retrieval Ranking

Ranking may consider:

- scope match,

- authority,

- relevance,

- confidence,

- freshness,

- specificity,

- and recency.

22.332 Scope Before Similarity

A semantically similar Memory Item from the wrong Project shall not be retrieved.

22.333 Authority Before Relevance

Highly relevant content remains ineligible without authority.

22.334 Freshness Before Convenience

Outdated operational Memory shall not be preferred merely because it is easy to retrieve.

22.335 Memory Index

A Memory Index supports discovery.

It shall not become the authoritative Memory store.

22.336 Memory Index Entry

A Memory Index Entry should include:

- memoryIndexEntryId,

- Memory Item,

- Domain,

- embedding or search representation,

- classification,

- lifecycle,

- and Version.

22.337 Index Identity

Every governed index shall have stable identity and Version.

22.338 Embedding Model

The exact embedding Model and Version shall remain attached to the index.

22.339 Index Scope

Indexes shall preserve:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Domain,

- classification,

- and access policy.

22.340 Index Freshness

Index state shall identify the latest incorporated Memory Version.

22.341 Index Deletion

Deleted or revoked Memory shall be removed from active indexes promptly.

22.342 Index Rebuild

Rebuilding an index shall preserve canonical Memory identity and permissions.

22.343 Search Representation

Search text, keywords or embeddings may be derived from Memory.

They inherit its protection.

22.344 Semantic Leakage

Embeddings may reveal sensitive semantic content.

They shall be treated according to source classification.

22.345 Memory Context Builder

The Memory Context Builder creates a bounded context package for an Agent or Model.

It shall include or reference:

- selected Memory Items,

- source summaries,

- confidence,

- freshness,

- exclusions,

- and token allocation.

22.346 Context Builder Identity

The Context Builder shall have a stable Service Principal and Version.

22.347 Context Compilation

Compilation may:

- summarise,

- order,

- deduplicate,

- redact,

- and format

eligible Memory.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.348 Context Compilation Provenance

The exact Memory Versions used shall remain attributable.

22.349 Context Token Budget

Memory shall not crowd out:

- current user intent,

- critical evidence,

- policy,

- or Tool results.

22.350 Context Priority

Priority may be:

1. current user instruction.

2. mandatory policy.

3. current Request and Plan.

4. verified current state.

5. scoped Memory.

6. lower-confidence historical context.

22.351 Memory Conflict in Context

Conflicting Memory shall be presented with uncertainty or withheld pending resolution.

22.352 Memory Injection Resistance

Retrieved content remains data.

It shall not override system or policy instructions.

22.353 Atlas Memory Relationship

Atlas may retrieve governed Memory through authorised Memory services.

Atlas shall not own all Memory storage or bypass Domain boundaries.

22.354 Atlas Identity Persistence

Atlas identity, role and authority remain stable when its serving Model changes.

22.355 Atlas Working Memory

Atlas may use bounded working Memory for current orchestration.

22.356 Atlas Project Memory

Atlas may retrieve Project Memory only when acting inside the relevant Project scope.

22.357 Atlas Personal Memory

Personal Memory access shall follow the user’s explicit permissions and purpose.

22.358 Atlas Platform Memory

Platform doctrine and approved architecture may be retrieved across Projects according to policy.

22.359 Atlas Memory Write

Atlas may propose Memory Items.

Admission shall follow Memory Policy.

22.360 Atlas Cannot Self-Authorise Memory

Atlas shall not grant itself broader retention or cross-Project access.

22.361 Other Agent Memory

Specialised Agents such as Arnold may have dedicated Memory Domains.

Their Memory remains subordinate to Project and Tenant policy.

22.362 Arnold Memory Example

Arnold may retain:

- approved training preferences,

- current programme state,

- exercise constraints,

- and coaching procedures.

It shall not receive unrelated Omnira or Familje-Stunden Memory.

22.363 Agent Memory Portability

Agent Memory shall remain available when the underlying Model or Provider changes.

22.364 Model Session Memory

Provider-managed conversation state is not canonical Agent Memory.

It may be used only as an implementation aid under policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.365 Provider Memory Feature

Provider-hosted Memory features shall not become authoritative without:

- scope,

- exportability,

- deletion,

- provenance,

- and privacy review.

22.366 Memory and Planning

Planning may use Memory for:

- preferences,

- prior workflow outcomes,

- known constraints,

- and Project procedures.

22.367 Memory Does Not Override Intent

Current explicit user instruction outranks conflicting ordinary preference Memory.

22.368 Memory and Routing

Routing may use Derived Learning about:

- resource quality,

- cost,

- reliability,

- and user preference.

22.369 Routing Learning Bound

Learned routing shall remain subordinate to:

- security,

- privacy,

- rights,

- authority,

- Quality Floor,

- Budget,

- and profile.

22.370 Memory and Scheduling

Scheduling may use Memory about:

- preferred work windows,

- recurring deadlines,

- resource availability patterns,

- and review timing.

22.371 Memory and Cost

Economic learning may support estimates and optimisation.

It shall not create spending authority.

22.372 Memory and Quality

Quality learning may inform:

- Provider selection,

- review depth,

- or Candidate count.

It shall not remove mandatory evaluation.

22.373 Memory and Reliability

Reliability learning may adjust:

- timeout,

- retry,

- polling,

- or fallback

within approved policy.

22.374 Memory and Rights

Rights and consent states shall remain sourced from authoritative control planes.

Memory may summarise them but shall not replace them.

22.375 Memory and Policy

Current Policy service state outranks stale Policy Memory.

22.376 Memory and Observability

Observability may provide evidence for learning.

Metrics shall not enter Memory without derivation and review.

22.377 Memory and Incident Response

Incidents may create:

- temporary restrictions,

- recovery Memory,

- and reviewed procedural learning.

22.378 Memory and Intelligence Graph

The Intelligence Graph may represent:

- Memory Item supported by Evidence,

- Memory supersedes Memory,

- Derived Learning applies to Capability,

- Agent may access Memory Domain,

- and Decision used Memory Item.

The Memory Control Plane remains authoritative.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.379 Memory and Assets

Memory may reference Assets.

It shall not copy protected Asset content unnecessarily.

22.380 Memory and Personal Data

Personal Memory shall be:

- minimised,

- purpose-limited,

- access-controlled,

- and deletable according to policy.

22.381 Sensitive Inference

The system shall not infer and store sensitive personal traits automatically without explicit lawful and policy basis.

22.382 Health Memory

Health-related Memory requires stronger classification and purpose control.

22.383 Financial Memory

Financial details require strong protection and narrow retrieval.

22.384 Family Memory

Family and child-related Memory requires strong privacy and scope controls.

22.385 Private Message Memory

Private messages shall not become persistent Memory by default.

22.386 Location Memory

Detailed location history shall not be retained beyond approved purpose.

22.387 Voice Memory

Raw voice recordings shall not become general Memory.

Derived preferences may be retained only when authorised.

22.388 Image Memory

Private photos shall not become general visual Memory or training references automatically.

22.389 Secret Memory Prohibition

Secrets, passwords, API keys and Tokens shall never be stored as ordinary Memory Items.

22.390 Credential Reference Memory

An Agent may know that an approved Connection exists.

It shall not retrieve raw Credential material.

22.391 Rights and Consent for Memory

Memory admission may require:

- retention rights,

- consent,

- Project scope,

- and permitted reuse.

22.392 Evidence Retention

Evidence retention may differ from Memory retention.

22.393 Raw Evidence Archive

Raw evidence may remain in restricted archive while only a minimised Memory summary is retrievable.

22.394 Audit Evidence Retention

Audit evidence may require longer retention than operational Memory.

22.395 Legal Hold

A legal or dispute hold may prevent evidence deletion.

It shall not make the evidence broadly retrievable.

22.396 Evidence Access

Evidence access shall be governed by:

- Principal,

- role,

- purpose,

- Project,

- classification,

- and time.

22.397 Evidence Reader

An Evidence Reader may inspect evidence without permission to alter or admit Memory.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.398 Evidence Writer

Evidence writers may append governed records.

They shall not rewrite historical evidence.

22.399 Evidence Administrator

Administrative authority shall not include unrestricted content access automatically.

22.400 Memory Reader

A Memory Reader may retrieve eligible Items.

22.401 Memory Writer

A Memory Writer may propose or create Items under policy.

22.402 Memory Approver

A Memory Approver may admit high-impact Memory.

22.403 Memory Auditor

An Auditor may inspect Memory lineage and access history.

22.404 Separation of Duties

High-risk Memory admission may require different:

- proposer,

- reviewer,

- and approver.

22.405 Evidence Immutability

Material historical evidence shall be append-only or Versioned.

22.406 Evidence Correction

Incorrect evidence metadata may be corrected through an attributable amendment.

Original content shall remain preserved where required.

22.407 Evidence Redaction

Protected content may be redacted for a derived view.

The original restricted evidence may remain separately governed.

22.408 Evidence Deletion

Deletion may be required for:

- privacy,

- consent,

- retention,

- or source obligations.

Minimal audit metadata may remain where permitted.

22.409 Evidence Deletion Record

Every material evidence deletion shall be attributable and verifiable.

22.410 Memory Access Record

Every material Memory access should preserve:

- requester,

- Agent,

- Domain,

- Items,

- purpose,

- time,

- and result.

22.411 Memory Access Identity

Every material access record shall have stable identity.

22.412 Memory Write Record

Every Memory creation or change shall preserve:

- actor,

- source,

- Decision,

- Version,

- and time.

22.413 Memory Retrieval Privacy

Ordinary user-facing responses should not expose internal Memory identifiers unless useful or requested.

22.414 Memory Transparency

Users should be able to understand:

- what important Memory exists,

- why it exists,

- who may use it,

- and how to correct or delete it.

22.415 Memory Inspection

Authorised users should be able to inspect active Memory by Domain and scope.

22.416 Memory Export

Users or Tenant administrators may export authorised Memory with provenance and classification.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.417 Memory Portability

Portable Memory should use Provider-independent formats.

22.418 Memory Import

Imported Memory shall be treated as untrusted until:

- source,

- scope,

- classification,

- rights,

- and evidence

are validated.

22.419 Legacy Memory

Legacy notes, profiles or transcripts shall not become canonical Memory automatically.

22.420 Memory Migration

Migration shall preserve:

- identity,

- Version,

- source links,

- classification,

- access policy,

- and lifecycle.

22.421 Memory Backup

Memory backup shall preserve encryption, scope and revocation state.

22.422 Memory Restore

Restore shall reapply current:

- deletion,

- revocation,

- expiry,

- and access control.

22.423 No Revoked Memory Reactivation

Restored backups shall not reactivate revoked or expired Memory.

22.424 Evidence and Memory Availability

Availability shall remain distinct from trust and eligibility.

22.425 Evidence Store Outage

Execution may continue according to policy only when required evidence can be durably captured later or locally.

Consequential work may need to pause.

22.426 Memory Store Outage

Agents may operate with reduced context.

They shall not fabricate missing Memory.

22.427 Degraded Memory Mode

Degraded mode shall disclose:

- unavailable Domains,

- freshness limits,

- and increased uncertainty.

22.428 Offline Memory

Offline Nodes may use a bounded encrypted Memory subset.

22.429 Offline Memory Snapshot

The snapshot shall preserve:

- Domain,

- Items,

- Versions,

- policy,

- expiry,

- and creation time.

22.430 Offline Memory Revocation Gap

Disconnected Nodes may retain stale Memory temporarily.

Expiry and reconciliation shall bound risk.

22.431 Memory Synchronisation

Memory synchronisation shall preserve:

- identity,

- Version,

- conflicts,

- deletion,

- and access policy.

22.432 Duplicate Memory Synchronisation

Repeated sync shall be idempotent.

22.433 Memory Conflict During Sync

Conflicts shall not use universal last-write-wins.

22.434 Local Memory Proposal

Offline or local Agents may propose Memory.

Central admission may remain pending until reconnection.

22.435 Evidence Metrics

Metrics may include:

- evidence completeness,

- missing receipt rate,

- unknown outcome duration,

- verification latency,

- contradictory claim count,

- and evidence retention volume.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.436 Learning Metrics

Metrics may include:

- Learning Candidates,

- admission rate,

- challenge rate,

- supersession rate,

- confidence distribution,

- and operational impact.

22.437 Memory Metrics

Metrics may include:

- active Items,

- stale Items,

- expired Items,

- retrieval frequency,

- conflict count,

- access denial,

- and deletion completion.

22.438 Memory Quality Metric

Memory quality may consider:

- source coverage,

- confidence,

- specificity,

- freshness,

- conflict,

- and retrieval usefulness.

22.439 Memory Precision

Precision measures whether retrieved Memory was relevant and correct for the request.

22.440 Memory Recall

Recall measures whether important eligible Memory was retrieved.

22.441 Memory Harm Metric

The system should monitor:

- wrong-context retrieval,

- stale guidance,

- privacy leakage,

- over-personalisation,

- and false certainty.

22.442 Learning Benefit Metric

Learning benefit may consider:

- Quality improvement,

- cost reduction,

- fewer revisions,

- reduced failure,

- and user acceptance.

22.443 Learning Regression

A learned rule may worsen outcomes.

Rollback and challenge shall be supported.

22.444 Evidence Dashboard

A dashboard may show:

- incomplete Executions,

- unknown outcomes,

- missing external verification,

- disputed claims,

- and evidence incidents.

22.445 Memory Dashboard

A dashboard may show:

- Domains,

- active Items,

- source quality,

- expiry,

- conflicts,

- and recent access.

22.446 Learning Dashboard

A dashboard may show:

- proposed learning,

- evidence,

- confidence,

- scope,

- review,

- and impact.

22.447 Evidence Incident

An Evidence Incident is a material failure involving:

- missing,

- corrupted,

- fabricated,

- altered,

- mis-scoped,

- leaked,

- or inaccessible evidence.

22.448 Evidence Incident Identity

Every material Evidence Incident shall have stable identity.

22.449 Missing Evidence Incident

Required evidence may be absent because of:

- callback loss,

- logging failure,

- storage failure,

- manual omission,

- or Provider expiry.

22.450 Corrupted Evidence Incident

Integrity mismatch may invalidate the affected record.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.451 Fabricated Evidence Incident

Fabricated or falsely attributed evidence is severe.

22.452 Evidence Leakage Incident

Protected evidence exposed outside its scope requires containment.

22.453 Evidence Misclassification Incident

Incorrect classification may cause overexposure or unnecessary restriction.

22.454 Decision Evidence Incident

A Decision may lack sufficient evidence or contain an incorrect rationale.

22.455 Learning Incident

A Learning Incident occurs when Derived Learning is:

- false,

- overbroad,

- improperly shared,

- unauthorised,

- or operationally harmful.

22.456 Memory Incident

A Memory Incident may include:

- wrong-user Memory,

- cross-Project leakage,

- stale Memory treated as current,

- deleted Memory retrieved,

- or unauthorised sensitive inference.

22.457 Memory Poisoning

Memory Poisoning occurs when false or malicious content is admitted to influence future behaviour.

22.458 Prompt-Based Memory Poisoning

Instructions inside external content shall not create Memory writes automatically.

22.459 Provider-Based Memory Poisoning

Provider Outputs shall not become Memory solely because they appear confident.

22.460 Cross-Project Memory Leakage

Retrieval of another Project’s Memory is a severe isolation Incident.

22.461 Secret in Memory Incident

Discovery of raw Credential material in Memory requires immediate containment and rotation review.

22.462 Memory Incident Containment

Containment may include:

- suspend Item,

- disable Domain,

- revoke access,

- quarantine source,

- rebuild index,

- or stop affected workflows.

22.463 Memory Incident Investigation

Investigation should inspect:

- source evidence,

- admission Decision,

- retrieval records,

- Agent contexts,

- affected Outputs,

- and downstream Decisions.

22.464 Memory Incident Recovery

Recovery may require:

- correction,

- supersession,

- index rebuild,

- affected-output review,

- policy change,

- and user notification.

22.465 Learning Rollback

A harmful learned rule shall be disabled or reverted without deleting historical evidence.

22.466 Evidence Reconstruction

Missing canonical evidence may be reconstructed from:

- Provider records,

- external state,

- local receipts,

- Assets,

- logs,

- and human attestation.

Reconstruction shall be labelled as such.

Reconstructed evidence may have lower confidence than original capture.

- integrity,

- unknown-outcome preservation,

- immutable Decisions,

22.472 Tenant Memory Policy

- permitted Domains,

- administrators,

- retention,

- and cross-Project prohibition.

22.473 Project Memory Policy

Project policy may define:

- approved knowledge classes,

- Agent access,

- user preferences,

- and expiry.

22.474 Personal Memory Policy

Personal Memory shall remain user-controlled within platform safety and legal requirements.

22.475 Agent Memory Policy

Each Agent shall have explicit:

- readable Domains,

- writable proposal classes,

- and prohibited content.

High-risk Memory may include:

- health,

- finance,

- identity,

- minors,

- legal,

- credentials,

- and authority.

It requires stronger controls.

22.477 Memory Expiry Policy

Volatile items shall receive short expiry by default.

22.478 Memory Review Policy

Some Domains may require periodic review.

22.479 Evidence Policy Version

Every Execution and Decision shall reference applicable evidence-policy Versions where material.

22.480 Memory Policy Version

Every admission and retrieval shall reference applicable Memory-policy Versions.

- add contradiction,

- verify outcome,

- challenge,

- amend,

- archive,

- record Tool result,

- record human action,

- record state transition,

- attach evidence,

- Secrets,

- private message contents,

- complete raw transcripts,

- unverified personal traits,

- another Project’s confidential data,

- and hidden reasoning traces.

22.525 Stage 1 Security Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. evidence is classified.

2. Memory inherits source protection.

3. raw Secrets are excluded.

4. Credential values are excluded.

5. private messages are excluded by default.

22.526 Stage 1 Recovery Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Execution evidence survives worker restart.

2. Provider job identity survives service restart.

3. local evidence can synchronise after reconnection.

4. duplicate sync does not duplicate evidence.

5. missing evidence may be reconstructed and labelled.

6. corrupted evidence is quarantined.

7. Memory index can rebuild from canonical store.

8. index rebuild preserves permissions.

9. backup restore reapplies revocation.

11. deleted Memory remains deleted.

12. conflicting versions remain visible.

13. Learning rollback restores prior operational rule.

14. recovery does not broaden access.

22.527 Applied Example — Unknown Video Outcome

A Provider video submission times out after the request leaves Omnira.

The Attempt state becomes:

unknown outcome.

Evidence preserves:

- request correlation,

- Provider Account,

- submission time,

- estimated cost,

- idempotency key,

- and timeout.

The Fabric does not submit the same paid job again automatically.

It first:

- polls the Provider,

- checks callbacks,

- inspects Provider history,

- or requests human verification.

A later Provider job discovery resolves the Outcome without erasing the original uncertainty.

22.528 Applied Example — Familje-Stunden Character Learning

Several Nova image Candidates are reviewed.

Evidence shows that one Provider configuration repeatedly causes:

- wrong hair colour,

- missing clothing details,

- and inconsistent facial proportions.

A Learning Candidate proposes:

This Provider configuration is unsuitable for high-fidelity Nova character Scenes.

The learning is scoped to:

- Familje-Stunden,

- Nova,

- image generation,

- exact Provider Product,

- exact Model Version,

- and current reference method.

It does not become a universal statement about the Provider.

text:
22.529 Applied Example — Pling Reference Improvement

Review evidence shows that a three-view Reference Set produces stronger Pling consistency than one front-view image.

Derived Learning recommends:

Use the approved multi-view Reference Set for future Pling Scenes.

The Learning item references:

- Candidate evaluations,

- identity scores,

- human review,

- and exact Reference Set Versions.

It expires for review after major Provider or Model change.

22.530 Applied Example — The Prompt Source Reliability

Several research Executions reveal that one source frequently publishes corrections after initial release.

A Learning Candidate proposes:

Treat early claims from this source as requiring corroboration.

The learning is scoped to:

- The Prompt,

- current-news research,

- that source,

- and a defined time period.

It does not prohibit the source or mark all its content false.

22.531 Applied Example — GainPilot Programme State

GainPilot Memory stores:

- current training programme,

- start date,

- previous plan Version,

- known constraints,

- and user-approved goals.

The source links include:

- programme creation Decision,

- user confirmation,

- completed workout history,

- and later modifications.

Arnold retrieves this Memory to avoid repeating the same programme indefinitely.

The Memory does not give Arnold authority to change the programme without the applicable change gate.

22.532 Applied Example — Explicit User Preference

The user states:

Use local or user-owned resources first when they meet required quality and privacy.

A Preference Memory item is created with:

- explicit human source,

- user scope,

- relevant Projects,

- strong preference level,

- and policy limitations.

The preference does not override:

- Local Only requirements,

- rights,

- Quality Floor,

- deadline,

- or mandatory security controls.

22.533 Applied Example — Formatting Preference

The user explicitly requires book chapters to be delivered as:

- one filename block,

- one uninterrupted chapter block,

- no surrounding commentary.

This may be admitted as a workflow preference Memory item for the Intelligence Fabric book-production context.

It shall not become a universal formatting rule for unrelated tasks.

text:
22.534 Applied Example — Omnira Repository Recovery Memory

A Recovery Memory item records that the active Omnira Git repository currently resides in a specific verified location while an organised Project workspace exists elsewhere.

The Memory includes:

- current path,

- intended migration target,

- do-not-overwrite constraint,

- requirement to preserve `.git`,

- and review date.

Because repository state may change, the Memory receives expiry or revalidation requirements.

22.535 Applied Example — Provider Quality Learning

A text Provider performs well for:

- structured architecture drafting,

- long context,

- and consistent terminology.

It performs poorly for:

- image generation,

- which it does not support.

The Derived Learning remains capability-specific.

The Provider does not receive one universal quality score.

22.536 Applied Example — Routing Profile Learning

Evidence shows that Economy routing saves initial call cost but causes repeated revisions for critical child-facing illustrations.

A reviewed Learning item may recommend:

For canonical Nova and Pling hero images, use Balanced or Premium within approved Budget.

It shall not redefine the Economy profile globally.

22.537 Applied Example — Human Correction

A user corrects an operational Memory item:

The GainPilot canonical repository is in the Projects folder, while one unfinished local branch temporarily remains in Developer.

The correction creates a new Memory Version.

The prior Memory remains historical.

Future retrieval receives the corrected scoped state.

22.538 Applied Example — Conflicting Project Paths

Two Evidence Items report different repository paths.

The Memory system evaluates:

- timestamps,

- Git status,

- active branch,

- and user confirmation.

Until resolved, the Memory is marked:

conflicted.

An Agent shall not perform destructive migration based on one stale path.

22.539 Applied Example — Publication Verification

A social publication Connector reports success.

Outcome Verification checks:

- external post ID,

- target Account,

- timestamp,

- media,

- and visibility.

Only then does the Execution receive:

externally verified completion.

The Connector response alone remains Provider evidence.

text:
22.540 Applied Example — Failed Publication with Existing Post

A publication request times out.

A later external observation finds the post already exists.

The system:

- resolves the unknown outcome,

- prevents duplicate publication,

- records external identifier,

- and creates Learning about the platform’s delayed response behaviour.

The Learning does not remove idempotency safeguards.

22.541 Applied Example — Rejected Voice Segment

A Voice segment is rejected for incorrect pronunciation.

The rejection evidence includes:

- Script Segment,

- Voice Profile,

- pronunciation dictionary,

- audio Asset,

- Reviewer annotation,

- and Provider configuration.

Derived Learning may recommend a different pronunciation syntax for that exact Provider.

The rejected audio does not become Voice Memory.

22.542 Applied Example — Local Model Context Limit

A local Model advertises a large context window.

Evaluation evidence shows quality degrades above a lower threshold on the user’s exact Deployment.

Derived Learning stores the tested reliable limit for:

- that Model Version,

- quantisation,

- Runtime,

- Node,

- and configuration.

The theoretical maximum remains separate.

22.543 Applied Example — Cost Estimate Learning

Repeated video jobs show that Provider generation often requires two Candidates before acceptance.

A cost-learning item may update expected total cost for that production class.

The estimate remains:

- Provider-specific,

- Model-specific,

- Project-specific where necessary,

- and time-bounded.

22.544 Applied Example — Incident Learning

An Asset was nearly lost because a temporary Provider URL expired before ingestion.

Incident review creates Procedural Learning:

Prioritise durable ingestion immediately after result availability for temporary media URLs.

The learning becomes a Scheduler rule only after review and conformance.

22.545 Applied Example — Child-Facing Safety Memory

Familje-Stunden Project Memory includes an approved rule:

Scenes for very young children shall avoid intense fear, threatening imagery and confusing danger without reassuring resolution.

The rule is sourced from:

- Project policy,

- audience definition,

- and editorial approval.

It is not inferred from one generated image.

sectionTitles: 22.546 Applied Example — The Prompt Generated Visual Disclosure
text:
22.546 Applied Example — The Prompt Generated Visual Disclosure

A Project Memory item records that generated illustrations used in news content must not be represented as documentary photography.

The source is:

- Project editorial policy,

- rights policy,

- and accepted disclosure standard.

The rule remains authoritative until superseded by approved policy.

22.547 Applied Example — Atlas Memory Retrieval

Atlas receives a Request concerning Omnira architecture.

The Memory Context Builder retrieves:

- approved platform doctrine,

- current canonical book status,

- relevant Project constraints,

- and recent verified implementation state.

It excludes:

- unrelated family data,

- GainPilot health records,

- private messages,

- and expired repository locations.

22.548 Applied Example — Arnold Memory Retrieval

Arnold receives a question about the user’s training plan.

It retrieves:

- active programme,

- recent completed sessions,

- known injuries or constraints,

- user goals,

- and approved coaching preferences.

It does not retrieve:

- Omnira investor discussions,

- Familje-Stunden production notes,

- or unrelated personal correspondence.

22.549 Applied Example — Memory Challenge

The user says:

That preference is no longer correct.

The system creates a Memory Challenge.

The challenged preference is suspended.

A corrected Memory Version is admitted after confirming the new scope.

Future Agents no longer use the outdated preference.

22.550 Applied Example — Expired Operational Memory

A Memory Item says:

The current branch is `fix/example`.

The item expires after a short period.

Before Git mutation, the Agent verifies the live branch rather than trusting stale Memory.

22.551 Applied Example — Historical Memory

A historical Memory item records that a book was approved on a specific date.

It remains true about the past even if a later Version supersedes the book.

Retrieval shall present it as historical status.

22.552 Applied Example — Rights-Limited Memory

A confidential contractor agreement may support a Rights Decision.

The full agreement remains restricted evidence.

A minimised Memory item may state:

Commercial use approved for the specified Deliverables until the defined date.

The Memory preserves a source link without exposing the full contract to ordinary Agents.

22.553 Applied Example — Deleted Personal Memory

The user requests deletion of one personal preference.

The system:

- revokes retrieval,

- removes the canonical Memory content,

- removes index entries,

- clears caches,

- updates backups according to policy,

- and records deletion evidence.

The deleted preference shall not reappear after index rebuild.

22.554 Applied Example — Memory Import

An old notes file contains Project facts and preferences.

Import creates Memory Candidates.

Each candidate receives:

- source reference,

- classification,

- scope,

- confidence,

- and review.

The entire file does not become one trusted Memory blob.

22.555 Applied Example — Provider-Managed Conversation History

A Provider retains conversation history.

Omnira treats that history as external Provider state.

Canonical Agent Memory remains in Omnira-controlled storage.

Provider history may be disabled, minimised or used only under explicit policy.

Retrieved content remains untrusted data.

22.612 Anti-Pattern — Platform Learning Uses Tenant Data Silently

Cross-Tenant use requires explicit architecture and authority.

22.613 Anti-Pattern — Learning Failure Bypasses the Fabric

No learning or Memory failure authorises uncontrolled execution.

22.614 Future Evidence, Learning and Memory Architecture

Future versions may support:

- cryptographically verifiable Execution Receipts,

- federated evidence stores,

- privacy-preserving aggregate learning,

- causal performance analysis,

- calibrated confidence,

- contradiction-aware knowledge graphs,

- automated Memory decay,

- user-controlled Memory wallets,

- selective disclosure,

- policy-bound Agent learning,

- and portable Agent Memory.

Future evolution must preserve:

- evidence lineage,

- scope,

- authority,

- classification,

- challenge,

- and user control.

22.615 Verifiable Execution Receipt

Future Receipts may be signed by:

- Provider,

- Node,

- Adapter,

- or Omnira service.

Signatures prove bounded origin and integrity, not semantic truth.

22.616 Federated Evidence

Evidence may remain inside different Tenant or local boundaries while supporting verified claims.

22.617 Selective Disclosure

A system may prove a property without exposing all underlying evidence.

22.618 Zero-Knowledge Evidence

Future cryptographic methods may prove bounded claims while preserving confidentiality.

Actual guarantees shall remain explicit.

22.619 Causal Learning

Causal analysis may distinguish correlation from likely cause.

It shall preserve assumptions and uncertainty.

22.620 Calibrated Confidence

Confidence may be calibrated against historical correctness for defined claim classes.

22.621 Automated Contradiction Graph

The Intelligence Graph may detect conflicting claims and temporal transitions automatically.

22.622 Memory Decay

Low-value or stale Memory may reduce retrieval priority or expire according to policy.

22.623 Memory Reinforcement

Repeated verified use may increase confidence without removing challengeability.

22.624 User Memory Wallet

Users may inspect, export, amend and selectively share Personal Memory.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.625 Portable Agent Memory

Agent Memory may move across Model and Provider implementations through canonical export.

22.626 Policy-Bound Learning Agent

A specialised Learning Agent may propose Derived Learning.

It shall have no authority to admit high-impact Memory independently.

22.627 Continuous Evaluation

Resources may be evaluated continuously through sampled production Outcomes.

Evaluation shall preserve user privacy and Project scope.

22.628 Shadow Learning

New learned policies may be tested in shadow mode before affecting execution.

22.629 Learning Canary

A learned routing or planning rule may apply to a limited workload first.

22.630 Learning Rollback Automation

Automatic rollback may occur when defined regression thresholds are reached.

22.631 Privacy-Preserving Aggregation

Platform learning may use aggregated signals that minimise Tenant and user exposure.

22.632 Differential Privacy

Privacy-preserving statistical techniques may reduce disclosure risk.

Their limitations and utility impact shall remain explicit.

22.633 Federated Learning

Model or policy updates may be derived across Nodes without centralising raw data.

Rights, consent and attack risks remain governed.

22.634 Memory Digital Twin

A future representation may show:

- current Memory,

- sources,

- conflicts,

- confidence,

- and downstream influence.

22.635 Decision Simulation

The system may simulate how different Memory or Learning would affect Planning or Routing before activation.

22.636 Evidence-Based Self-Improvement

Omnira may improve procedures through reviewed evidence.

It shall not rewrite foundational authority or policy autonomously.

22.637 Evidence Success Criteria

The evidence architecture succeeds when:

- every meaningful Execution is reconstructable,

- every Attempt remains attributable,

- unknown outcomes remain explicit,

- external state is verified,

- evaluations reference exact targets,

- Decisions preserve evidence and alternatives,

- and historical truth cannot be rewritten silently.

22.638 Learning Success Criteria

The learning architecture succeeds when:

- conclusions are evidence-based,

- scope is explicit,

- confidence and limitations are visible,

- expiry is enforced,

- challenges are supported,

- rollback is possible,

- and one Project’s experience does not contaminate another.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.639 Memory Success Criteria

The Memory architecture succeeds when:

- Memory is intentional rather than accidental,

- Domains preserve ownership and scope,

- sources remain linked,

- retrieval is authorised and minimised,

- stale or conflicting Memory is handled safely,

- users can correct and delete Memory,

- and Agent identity survives Model changes without surrendering privacy.

22.640 Evidence Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- Executions cannot be reconstructed,

- Attempts lack resource or Account identity,

- Provider completion is treated as external outcome,

- timeout becomes ordinary failure,

- Decision rationale lacks evidence,

- or evidence can be altered without attribution.

22.641 Learning Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- raw Outputs become learning,

- one event becomes universal policy,

- cross-Project evidence is reused silently,

- confidence lacks method,

- challenged learning remains active without review,

- or learning modifies authority, privacy or spend outside policy.

22.642 Memory Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- raw transcripts become permanent Memory,

- vector indexes become authoritative,

- wrong-Project Memory is retrieved,

- expired Memory is treated as current,

- deleted Memory reappears,

- Agents self-authorise retention,

- or source lineage is missing.

22.643 Canonical Evidence Item Contract

The following requirements define canonical Evidence Items:

1. Every Evidence Item SHALL have stable identity.

2. Evidence type SHALL be explicit.

3. Subject SHALL be explicit.

4. Source SHALL be explicit.

5. Producer SHALL be explicit.

6. Observation time SHALL be explicit.

7. Recording time SHALL be explicit.

8. Tenant and Project scope SHALL be explicit.

9. Classification SHALL be explicit.

10. Integrity SHALL be explicit.

11. Confidence SHALL be explicit.

12. Freshness SHALL be explicit.

13. Lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

14. Direct and indirect evidence SHALL remain distinct.

15. Supporting and contradicting evidence SHALL remain linked.

16. Evidence SHALL NOT become truth automatically.

17. Stale evidence SHALL NOT support current Decisions silently.

18. Evidence changes SHALL be attributable.

19. Historical Evidence SHALL remain queryable.

20. Evidence SHALL remain distinct from Memory and Learning.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.644 Canonical Execution Record Contract

The following requirements define canonical Execution Records:

1. Every Execution SHALL have stable identity.

2. Request and Intent Envelope SHALL be linked.

3. Exact Plan Version SHALL be linked.

4. Tenant, Project and Principal SHALL be explicit.

5. Authority and policy Versions SHALL be explicit.

6. Routing and Placement Decisions SHALL be linked.

7. Every Attempt SHALL be linked.

8. State transitions SHALL be durable.

9. Outputs and Assets SHALL be linked.

10. Costs and usage SHALL be linked.

11. Cancellation and pause SHALL be attributable.

12. Technical completion and business completion SHALL remain distinct.

13. Unknown Outcome SHALL remain a valid state.

14. External side effects SHALL require verification.

15. Execution Record SHALL remain distinct from Receipt.

16. Historical state SHALL NOT be rewritten.

17. Corrections SHALL use attributable amendments.

18. Evidence Bundle SHALL be linked.

19. Execution SHALL remain reconstructable after restart.

20. No Execution failure SHALL erase prior evidence.

22.645 Canonical Attempt Record Contract

The following requirements define canonical Attempts:
