1. Every Attempt SHALL have stable identity.

2. Execution and Step SHALL be explicit.

3. Resource SHALL be explicit.

4. Provider, Account and Connection SHALL be explicit where applicable.

5. Credential Reference SHALL be preserved without Secret material.

6. Input evidence SHALL be attributable.

7. Start and end SHALL be explicit.

8. Result state SHALL be explicit.

9. External job identity SHALL be preserved.

10. Usage SHALL be attributable.

11. Cost SHALL be attributable.

12. Error class SHALL be explicit.

13. Retry relationship SHALL be explicit.

14. Fallback relationship SHALL be explicit.

15. Unknown outcome SHALL NOT be converted to failure automatically.

16. Provider acknowledgement SHALL remain distinct from completion.

17. Attempt SHALL remain distinct from Execution.

18. Historical Attempts SHALL remain immutable.

19. Attempt evidence SHALL remain queryable.

20. Attempt failure SHALL NOT authorise unbounded retry.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.646 Canonical Outcome Verification Contract

The following requirements define Outcome Verification:

1. Every material Outcome Verification SHALL have stable identity.

2. Intended outcome SHALL be explicit.

3. External target SHALL be explicit.

4. Observation method SHALL be explicit.

5. Observer or verifier SHALL be explicit.

6. Observation time SHALL be explicit.

7. Evidence SHALL be linked.

8. Confidence SHALL be explicit.

9. Technical, external, business and user outcomes SHALL remain distinct.

10. Output existence SHALL NOT prove intended outcome.

11. Provider completion SHALL NOT prove publication or delivery.

12. Consequential mutation SHALL verify after state.

13. Unknown outcome SHALL remain valid.

14. Later verification SHALL preserve prior uncertainty.

15. Conflicting observations SHALL remain visible.

16. Verification freshness SHALL be explicit.

17. Verification policy SHALL be Versioned.

18. Historical Outcome Decisions SHALL remain immutable.

19. Verification SHALL remain human- and machine-readable.

20. No outcome SHALL be claimed without sufficient evidence.

22.647 Canonical Evaluation Contract

The following requirements define Evaluation Records:

1. Every Evaluation Record SHALL have stable identity.

2. Exact target and Version SHALL be explicit.

3. Evaluator identity and Version SHALL be explicit.

4. Method and Rubric SHALL be explicit.

5. Evidence inspected SHALL be linked.

6. Findings SHALL be structured.

7. Mandatory failures SHALL remain distinct from scores.

8. Score scale and interpretation SHALL be explicit.

9. Confidence SHALL be explicit.

10. Human and automated evaluations SHALL remain distinct.

11. Disagreement SHALL remain visible.

12. Supersession SHALL preserve prior evaluations.

13. Evaluation SHALL NOT become Memory automatically.

14. Evaluation SHALL NOT create authority.

15. Acceptance SHALL reference exact Evaluation evidence.

16. Stale Evaluation SHALL NOT support changed targets.

17. Evaluation changes SHALL be attributable.

18. Historical Evaluations SHALL remain immutable.

19. Evaluation SHALL remain distinct from provenance.

20. Evaluation SHALL remain explainable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.648 Canonical Decision Evidence Contract

The following requirements define Decision Evidence:

1. Every material Decision Evidence record SHALL have stable identity.

2. Decision type SHALL be explicit.

3. Subject SHALL be explicit.

4. Alternatives SHALL be explicit where material.

5. Selected option SHALL be explicit.

6. Excluded options SHALL preserve reasons.

7. Constraints SHALL be explicit.

8. Policy Versions SHALL be explicit.

9. Evidence Items SHALL be linked.

10. Rationale SHALL be structured and concise.

11. Decision maker SHALL be explicit.

12. Decision authority SHALL be verified.

13. Confidence and limitations SHALL be explicit.

14. Validity SHALL be bounded.

15. Revalidation triggers SHALL be explicit.

16. Explanation SHALL respect classification and privacy.

17. Raw hidden reasoning SHALL NOT be required.

18. Decision evidence SHALL remain immutable.

19. Historical Decisions SHALL remain queryable.

20. No Decision SHALL be presented as evidence-free preference.

22.649 Canonical Derived Learning Contract

The following requirements define Derived Learning:

1. Every Derived Learning item SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Statement SHALL be explicit.

3. Learning type SHALL be explicit.

4. Tenant and Project scope SHALL be explicit.

5. Capability, resource or workflow scope SHALL be explicit.

6. Source Evidence SHALL be linked.

7. Derivation method SHALL be explicit.

8. Confidence SHALL be explicit.

9. Limitations SHALL be explicit.

10. Effective time SHALL be explicit.

11. Expiry or review date SHALL be explicit.

12. Contradictory evidence SHALL remain linked.

13. Learning review SHALL be attributable.

14. Automatic admission SHALL be limited by policy.

15. High-impact Learning SHALL require human review.

16. Challenges SHALL be supported.

17. Corrections SHALL create new Versions.

18. Supersession and rollback SHALL preserve history.

19. Cross-Project use SHALL be prohibited by default.

20. Derived Learning SHALL NOT create authority, rights or consent.

22.650 Canonical Memory Domain Contract

The following requirements define Memory Domains:

1. Every Memory Domain SHALL have stable identity.

2. Domain type SHALL be explicit.

3. Owner and controller SHALL be explicit.

4. Tenant and Project scope SHALL be explicit.

5. Agent scope SHALL be explicit where applicable.

6. Permitted readers SHALL be explicit.

7. Permitted writers SHALL be explicit.

8. Permitted Memory types SHALL be explicit.

9. Classification limits SHALL be explicit.

10. Retention policy SHALL be explicit.

11. Admission policy SHALL be explicit.

12. Retrieval policy SHALL be explicit.

13. Challenge and deletion policy SHALL be explicit.

14. Personal, Project, Tenant and Platform Domains SHALL remain distinct.

15. Cross-Project access SHALL be denied by default.

16. Cross-Tenant access SHALL be denied by default.

17. Domain policy SHALL be Versioned.

18. Retired Domains SHALL remain historically resolvable.

19. Domain ownership SHALL NOT create unrestricted content access.

20. Memory Domain SHALL remain independent from Model Provider.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.651 Canonical Memory Item Contract

The following requirements define Memory Items:

1. Every Memory Item SHALL have stable identity.

2. Every material change SHALL create a Version.

3. Domain SHALL be explicit.

4. Memory type SHALL be explicit.

5. Subject SHALL be explicit.

6. Content SHALL be clear or structured.

7. Tenant, Project and Agent scope SHALL be explicit.

8. Classification SHALL be explicit.

9. Source links SHALL be present.

10. Confidence SHALL be explicit.

11. Effective time SHALL be explicit.

12. Expiry or review date SHALL be explicit.

13. Lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

14. Authority for admission SHALL be explicit.

15. Contradictions SHALL remain visible.

16. Corrections SHALL preserve prior Versions.

17. Revoked or expired Items SHALL NOT be retrieved as current.

18. Historical Items SHALL remain queryable.

19. Memory SHALL NOT contain raw Secrets.

20. Memory Item SHALL NOT become authority or policy source automatically.

22.652 Canonical Memory Admission Contract

The following requirements define Memory Admission:

1. Every material Admission Decision SHALL have stable identity.

2. Candidate SHALL be explicit.

3. Target Domain SHALL be explicit.

4. Purpose SHALL be explicit.

5. Source evidence SHALL be linked.

6. Scope SHALL be explicit.

7. Classification SHALL be evaluated.

8. Authority SHALL be verified.

9. Rights and consent SHALL be evaluated where applicable.

10. Confidence SHALL meet policy.

11. Retention SHALL be explicit.

12. Expiry SHALL be explicit.

13. Reviewer SHALL be explicit.

14. Conditions SHALL be enforceable.

15. Raw prompts SHALL NOT be admitted automatically.

16. Raw Outputs SHALL NOT be admitted automatically.

17. Raw transcripts SHALL NOT become permanent Memory by default.

18. Secrets and Credentials SHALL be prohibited.

19. Historical Admission Decisions SHALL remain immutable.

20. Admission SHALL remain distinct from retrieval.

22.653 Canonical Memory Retrieval Contract

The following requirements define Memory Retrieval:

1. Every material Retrieval Record SHALL have stable identity.

2. Requester and Agent SHALL be explicit.

3. Current Request and purpose SHALL be explicit.

4. Domain SHALL be explicit.

5. Candidate Items SHALL be recorded where policy permits.

6. Selected Items SHALL be recorded.

7. Exclusions SHALL preserve reasons.

8. Tenant and Project eligibility SHALL be enforced first.

9. Authority SHALL precede relevance ranking.

10. Classification SHALL be enforced.

11. Lifecycle SHALL be enforced.

12. Confidence SHALL be considered.

13. Freshness SHALL be considered.

14. Current explicit user instruction SHALL outrank ordinary preference Memory.

15. Policy service SHALL outrank stale Policy Memory.

16. Retrieval SHALL be minimised.

17. Source references SHALL be preserved.

18. Token Budget SHALL be bounded.

19. Historical Retrieval Records SHALL remain queryable.

20. Retrieval SHALL NOT expose another Domain’s protected Memory.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
sectionTitles: 22.654 Canonical Memory Challenge and Correction Contract
22.655 Canonical Evidence and Memory Security Contract
text:
22.654 Canonical Memory Challenge and Correction Contract

The following requirements define Memory challenge and correction:

1. Every material Memory Challenge SHALL have stable identity.

2. Challenger SHALL be explicit.

3. Target Item and Version SHALL be explicit.

4. Challenge reason SHALL be explicit.

5. Supporting evidence SHALL be linked.

6. Challenge effect SHALL be explicit.

7. High-risk challenged Memory MAY be suspended immediately.

8. Review SHALL be attributable.

9. Correction SHALL create a new Version.

10. Prior Version SHALL remain historical.

11. Supersession SHALL identify the governing Item.

12. Unresolved conflict SHALL remain visible.

13. No silent overwrite SHALL occur.

14. User corrections SHALL receive appropriate priority within their authority.

15. Contradictory external facts SHALL require evidence review.

16. Revocation SHALL block future retrieval.

17. Deletion SHALL address stores and indexes.

18. Restore SHALL NOT reactivate revoked state.

19. Historical challenge and correction evidence SHALL remain queryable.

20. Memory SHALL remain challengeable regardless of confidence.

22.655 Canonical Evidence and Memory Security Contract

The following requirements define security:

1. Evidence and Memory SHALL receive Data Classification.

2. Access SHALL be Principal-, Tenant-, Project- and purpose-scoped.

3. Secrets and Credential values SHALL be excluded.

4. Private messages SHALL NOT become Memory by default.

5. Sensitive personal inference SHALL NOT be stored automatically.

6. Search indexes SHALL preserve access controls.

7. Embeddings SHALL inherit source protection.

8. Prompt injection SHALL NOT create Memory writes.

9. Provider Outputs SHALL NOT self-admit.

10. Cross-Project retrieval SHALL be prohibited by default.

11. Cross-Tenant learning SHALL be prohibited by default.

12. Access and mutation SHALL be auditable.

13. Deletion and revocation SHALL propagate to indexes and caches.

14. Backups SHALL preserve lifecycle state.

15. Offline snapshots SHALL be encrypted and expiring.

16. Explanations SHALL minimise protected content.

17. Evidence integrity failures SHALL trigger containment.

18. Memory poisoning SHALL trigger review and Incident response.

19. Recovery SHALL NOT broaden authority.

20. No evidence or Memory failure SHALL authorise bypass of the Fabric.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
sectionTitles: 22.656 Canonical Evidence, Learning and Memory Governance Contract
22.657 Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory Invariants
text:
22.656 Canonical Evidence, Learning and Memory Governance Contract

The following requirements define overall governance:

1. Evidence SHALL remain distinct from truth.

2. Provenance SHALL remain distinct from Evaluation.

3. Evaluation SHALL remain distinct from Decision Evidence.

4. Decision Evidence SHALL remain distinct from Derived Learning.

5. Derived Learning SHALL remain distinct from Governed Memory.

6. Memory SHALL remain distinct from transcript, prompt and vector storage.

7. Every material object SHALL have stable identity.

8. Scope, classification and lifecycle SHALL be explicit.

9. Source evidence SHALL remain linked.

10. Confidence, freshness and limitations SHALL remain visible.

11. Unknown and disputed states SHALL be valid.

12. Human correction SHALL remain attributable.

13. Agents SHALL propose rather than self-authorise high-impact Memory.

14. Agent identity SHALL remain independent from Model and Provider.

15. Cross-Project and cross-Tenant boundaries SHALL be enforced.

16. Deletion, revocation and expiry SHALL propagate.

17. Historical truth SHALL remain reconstructable.

18. Learning SHALL remain reversible.

19. Memory SHALL remain user- and policy-governed.

20. No evidence, learning or Memory layer SHALL become an unreviewed source of authority.

22.657 Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No log entry becomes canonical evidence automatically.

- No evidence becomes unquestioned truth.

- No Provider response becomes external Outcome Verification automatically.

- No timeout becomes ordinary failure automatically.

- No Output becomes Derived Learning automatically.

- No accepted Output becomes permanent Memory automatically.

- No evaluation becomes Decision Evidence without a Decision relationship.

- No Decision Evidence becomes Memory automatically.

- No single event becomes a universal rule.

- No confidence score becomes certainty.

- No raw transcript becomes long-term Memory by default.

- No raw prompt or hidden reasoning becomes canonical Memory.

- No vector index becomes the Memory source of truth.

- No semantically similar Memory crosses Project or Tenant scope.

- No Agent self-authorises permanent high-impact Memory.

- No Model or Provider owns Agent identity or canonical Memory.

- No conflicting Memory is overwritten silently.

- No revoked, expired or deleted Memory remains actively retrievable.

- No learning changes authority, rights, consent or spend outside policy.

- No evidence, learning or Memory failure bypasses the Intelligence Fabric.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
22.658 Closing Statement

Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory allow Omnira to improve without losing accountability.

Evidence records what was observed.

The Execution Record preserves what was attempted.

The Attempt Record preserves which resource performed the work.

The Provider Response Record preserves what the external service reported.

The Tool Result Record preserves what local or connected Tools returned.

The Human Action Record preserves what people approved, rejected or corrected.

Outcome Verification determines whether the intended external or business state actually occurred.

The Evaluation Record determines how well the result satisfied defined criteria.

Decision Evidence explains why Omnira selected, approved, retried, rejected, stopped or escalated.

Derived Learning turns repeated, reviewed evidence into bounded conclusions.

The Memory Admission Decision determines what may be retained for future use.

The Memory Item preserves that retained knowledge with sources, scope, confidence, validity and expiry.

The Memory Retrieval Record explains what context influenced an Agent or Decision.

The Memory Challenge ensures that wrong or outdated knowledge can be corrected.

The Memory Supersession preserves history without allowing stale truth to govern the present.

For Familje-Stunden, this architecture ensures that:

- Nova and Pling continuity learning remains Project-scoped,

- child-facing safety rules remain sourced and reviewable,

- rejected illustrations can improve future selection without becoming canonical references,

- and private family material never becomes general Memory automatically.

For The Prompt, it ensures that:

- source reliability patterns remain time- and source-scoped,

- generated visuals remain distinct from documentary evidence,

- publication completion is externally verified,

- and one successful news format does not become an unquestioned universal template.

For GainPilot, it ensures that:

- Arnold remembers the current programme,

- programme age and change history remain explicit,

- user goals and constraints remain sourced,

- and coaching improvements arise from verified outcomes rather than repeated assumptions.

For Atlas, it ensures that:

- platform doctrine remains available across Model changes,

- Project context remains isolated,

- user preferences remain bounded,

- operational state expires when stale,

- and Memory never replaces current authority, policy or evidence.

For Omnira, it ensures that:

- Agents,

- Models,

- Providers,

- local Nodes,

- Tools,

- humans,

- workflows,

- Assets,

- Decisions,

- Incidents,

- and outcomes

contribute to one governed body of evidence without collapsing into one uncontrolled data archive.

The Execution may finish.

The Provider may change.

The Model may be replaced.

The Agent may continue.

The user may correct the system.

The Project may evolve.

The evidence must remain.

The learning must remain bounded.

The Memory must remain challengeable.

No meaningful Execution without evidence.

No external Outcome without verification.

No Evaluation without an exact target.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Execution Evidence, Learning and Governed Memory
text:
No Decision without material evidence.

No Learning without sources.

No Memory without admission.

No Memory retrieval without scope.

No confidence without uncertainty.

No correction without history.

No deletion without propagation.

No Agent identity tied to one Model.

No improvement without governance.

The user retains correction and deletion authority.

The Project retains scope and knowledge boundaries.

Omnira retains evidence and Memory governance.

The Fabric learns from what happened without allowing yesterday’s inference to become tomorrow’s unquestioned truth.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical architecture, object model, policy hierarchy, lifecycle, enforcement boundaries and conformance requirements for data classification, privacy and isolation within the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

It establishes:

- how every meaningful data object receives a governed protection state,

- how Public, Project Internal, Confidential, Local Only and Prohibited classifications are defined and enforced,

- how data category, sensitivity, classification, handling policy and legal status remain distinct,

- how classification is assigned automatically and tightened by authorised humans,

- how the Fabric is prohibited from lowering classification without explicit authority and evidence,

- how classification propagates through derived data, embeddings, summaries, caches, logs, prompts, Outputs, Assets and Memory,

- how aggregated information may become more sensitive than its individual Inputs,

- how declassification, redaction, anonymisation and disclosure decisions remain governed,

- how purpose limitation and data minimisation constrain collection, processing, storage and retrieval,

- how personal, family, child, health, financial, biometric, location, communication and Credential-related data receive stronger controls,

- how private messages and private correspondence remain outside general Agent access,

- how raw Secrets, passwords, Tokens and private keys remain prohibited from ordinary Model context and Memory,

- how user, Project, Tenant, Agent, Workflow, environment, Node, Provider, Account, storage, cache, index and Memory isolation remain explicit,

- how Tenant and Project boundaries are enforced before routing, retrieval and execution,

- how local execution differs from Local Only classification,

- how data residency, custody, processing location and storage location remain distinct,

- how cross-boundary transfer, Provider upload, remote execution, backup and synchronisation are controlled,

- how access remains purpose-, capability-, role-, Project-, data-type-, device- and time-bounded,

- how privacy-preserving transformation is represented and verified,

- how pseudonymisation differs from anonymisation,

- how re-identification risk is assessed,

- how telemetry, observability, logs, traces, evidence and analytics remain privacy-governed,

- how consent, rights, authority, privacy and classification interact without collapsing into one concept,

- how deletion, retention, revocation and restoration preserve current privacy state,

- how privacy incidents, isolation failures and cross-Project leakage are contained and investigated,

- how Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy classification, privacy and isolation foundation,

- and how future multi-Tenant growth shall preserve the same canonical guarantees.

Classification is not consent.

Consent is not access authority.

Access authority is not ownership.

Ownership is not permission for every processing purpose.

Privacy is not secrecy alone.

Encryption is not isolation by itself.

Local execution is not automatically Local Only.

Publicly available data is not automatically Public within Omnira.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
A redacted copy is not automatically anonymous.

A pseudonym is not anonymity.

An embedding is not non-sensitive merely because it cannot be read directly.

A summary may remain as sensitive as its source.

A log may contain more private data than the operation it describes.

A shared database is not a shared trust domain.

A filtered query is not sufficient Tenant isolation unless enforcement is structural and verified.

An administrator role does not automatically permit unrestricted content access.

A Model context window is a temporary disclosure boundary.

A Provider Account is a custody and policy boundary.

A backup is another copy of the data.

A deleted index entry is not proof that all data copies are deleted.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

Approval, authority and bounded autonomy are expanded in Chapter 24.

Observability, audit and Incident Response are expanded in Chapter 25.

Implementation, legal applicability and operational conformance must be verified separately.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 23.2 Purpose of Data Classification, Privacy and Isolation
text:
23.2 Purpose of Data Classification, Privacy and Isolation

Omnira coordinates intelligence across:

- users,

- Projects,

- Tenants,

- Agents,

- Models,

- Providers,

- Accounts,

- Devices,

- local Nodes,

- cloud services,

- Tools,

- Connectors,

- Assets,

- Memory,

- and external systems.

Those systems may process:

- public source material,

- internal Project plans,

- private family information,

- children’s images,

- training and health records,

- financial information,

- business strategy,

- unpublished media,

- source code,

- Credentials,

- personal communications,

- location information,

- Voice recordings,

- biometric-like identifiers,

- legal documents,

- and confidential customer data.

Without canonical classification and isolation, the Fabric could:

- send Local Only material to an external Provider,

- retrieve one Project’s Memory into another Project,

- expose a family image to a business Agent,

- place raw Credentials in a Model prompt,

- preserve private data in logs after the source was deleted,

- infer sensitive traits and retain them without authority,

- reuse embeddings across Tenants,

- restore revoked data from backup,

- allow one Provider Account to mix several Project libraries,

- or treat administrative convenience as permission.

The architecture exists to ensure that every processing operation can answer:

- What data is involved?

- Which classification applies?

- Which categories and subjects are represented?

- Which purpose permits processing?

- Which Principal, Agent and Project are acting?

- Which Capabilities are required?

- Which environments, Nodes, Providers and Accounts are eligible?

- Where may the data be processed?

- Where may it be stored?

- How long may it remain?

- Which transformations are permitted?

- Which disclosure or transfer is occurring?

- Which evidence supports the Decision?

- Which obligations apply after deletion, revocation or policy change?

23.3 Data

Data is any recorded, represented, transmitted, inferred or generated information processed by Omnira.

Data may exist as:

- text,

- structured fields,

- documents,

- code,

- images,

- audio,

- video,

- embeddings,

- indexes,

- metadata,

- logs,

- traces,

- Metrics,

- Model context,

- Memory,

- or derived conclusions.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.4 Data Object

A Data Object is a governed unit of information to which classification, scope, access, retention and processing policy can be applied.

Examples include:

- Asset Version,

- document,

- message,

- field,

- record,

- dataset,

- prompt context,

- Output,

- Evidence Item,

- Memory Item,

- cache entry,

- log event,

- or database row.

23.5 Data Object Identity

Every persistent governed Data Object shall have stable identity or a stable relationship to a canonical object.

23.6 Classification

Classification is the governed protection level assigned to data according to sensitivity, harm potential, privacy, contractual obligations, policy and intended use.

23.7 Classification Is Not Data Type

An image may be Public, Confidential or Local Only.

A data type does not determine one universal classification.

23.8 Classification Is Not Category

Health data is a Data Category.

Confidential may be its Classification.

The two shall remain distinct.

23.9 Classification Is Not Access Control

Classification defines required protection.

Access Control determines which Principal may perform which action.

23.10 Classification Is Not Location

Classification may constrain placement.

It does not itself identify where the data is stored.

23.11 Classification Is Not Encryption

Encryption is one control used to enforce classification requirements.

23.12 Privacy

Privacy is the governed protection of people, relationships, communications, behaviour, identity and personal context from unnecessary collection, use, disclosure, inference, retention or control.

23.13 Isolation

Isolation is the enforced separation of data, execution, identity, storage, Memory, Credentials and authority across defined boundaries.

23.14 Data Boundary

A Data Boundary is a canonical scope within which defined data may be accessed or processed.

Boundaries may include:

- user,

- household,

- Project,

- Tenant,

- Agent,

- workflow,

- environment,

- Node,

- Zone,

- Provider Account,

- storage system,

- or legal region.

23.15 Privacy Boundary

A Privacy Boundary defines where personal or sensitive information may be collected, viewed, inferred, retained or disclosed.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 23.18 Data Classification and Privacy Control Plane
23.19 Canonical Classification, Privacy and Isolation Objects
text:
23.16 Trust Boundary

A Trust Boundary defines where different security assumptions apply.

Privacy and trust boundaries may overlap but are not identical.

23.17 Isolation Boundary

An Isolation Boundary defines which resources and data must remain separated despite sharing infrastructure.

23.18 Data Classification and Privacy Control Plane

The Data Classification, Privacy and Isolation Control Plane is the governed collection of services and canonical objects responsible for:

- data categorisation,

- classification,

- handling policy,

- purpose definition,

- minimisation,

- access eligibility,

- placement constraints,

- transfer control,

- isolation,

- retention,

- deletion,

- redaction,

- anonymisation,

- privacy review,

- disclosure,

- and Incident response.

It shall integrate with:

- Identity,

- Tenancy,

- Projects,

- Capability Requests,

- Planning,

- Routing,

- Placement,

- Providers,

- Models,

- Tools,

- Connections,

- Credentials,

- Assets,

- Rights,

- Consent,

- Memory,

- Evidence,

- Observability,

- Approvals,

- and Incidents.

23.19 Canonical Classification, Privacy and Isolation Objects

The canonical architecture should include or reference:

- Data Object,

- Data Category,

- Data Subject,

- Data Classification,

- Classification Label,

- Classification Assignment,

- Classification Decision,

- Classification Rule,

- Handling Profile,

- Purpose Definition,

- Processing Purpose,

- Processing Activity,

- Privacy Policy,

- Privacy Constraint,

- Access Scope,

- Data Boundary,

- Isolation Boundary,

- Tenant Boundary,

- Project Boundary,

- Agent Boundary,

- Environment Boundary,

- Storage Boundary,

- Provider Boundary,

- Transfer Decision,

- Disclosure Record,

- Data Flow,

- Retention Policy,

- Retention Decision,

- Deletion Record,

- Redaction Specification,

- Redacted Representation,

- Pseudonymisation Record,

- Anonymisation Record,

- Re-Identification Risk Assessment,

- Privacy Review,

- Isolation Test,

- Isolation Evidence,

- and Privacy Incident.

23.20 Canonical Classification Levels

The canonical Data Classification levels are:

1. Public.

2. Project Internal.

3. Confidential.

4. Local Only.

5. Prohibited.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.21 Classification Ordering

The canonical levels form an increasing protection ordering for default enforcement:

Public

less restrictive than:

Project Internal

less restrictive than:

Confidential

less externally transferable than:

Local Only.

Prohibited is not merely a higher secrecy level.

It represents data or processing that is disallowed under the applicable policy.

23.22 Classification Precedence

When several classifications apply, the effective Classification shall be the most restrictive relevant state unless a valid, explicit and evidenced Decision defines otherwise.

23.23 Public

Public data is approved for public disclosure and ordinary external processing under applicable rights, policy and purpose constraints.

23.24 Public Does Not Mean Unrestricted

Public data may still have:

- copyright,

- attribution,

- terms,

- accuracy,

- audience,

- retention,

- or platform restrictions.

23.25 Public Source Material

Material found on a public website is not automatically classified Public within Omnira.

The system shall consider:

- intended use,

- personal data,

- rights,

- context,

- and source restrictions.

23.26 Public Asset

An Asset becomes Public only after explicit approval or policy-supported classification.

23.27 Project Internal

Project Internal data is intended for authorised use inside one Project or its approved operational relationships.

It shall not be disclosed publicly or reused across Projects automatically.

23.28 Project Internal Examples

Examples may include:

- drafts,

- internal notes,

- ordinary plans,

- non-sensitive prompts,

- unpublished scheduling data,

- Project analytics,

- and routine production metadata.

23.29 Project Internal Boundary

Project Internal data shall remain inside:

- the owning Project,

- authorised Agents,

- approved Providers,

- approved storage,

- and permitted operational systems.

23.30 Confidential

Confidential data could cause material harm, privacy loss, commercial damage, legal exposure, identity risk or safety impact if accessed or disclosed improperly.

23.31 Confidential Examples

Examples may include:

- private user data,

- health information,

- financial information,

- confidential strategy,

- customer records,

- unpublished contracts,

- private family images,

- source code with sensitive logic,

- and protected correspondence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 23.34 Local Only Is a Placement Restriction
23.35 Local Only Is Not Device-Specific Automatically
23.39 Prohibited Does Not Mean Delete Immediately in Every Case
text:
23.32 Confidential Processing

Confidential processing may require:

- stronger identity,

- least privilege,

- approved Provider terms,

- encrypted storage,

- restricted logging,

- and explicit placement.

23.33 Local Only

Local Only data shall remain within approved local, private or self-hosted boundaries defined by policy.

It shall not be sent to ordinary external managed Providers.

23.34 Local Only Is a Placement Restriction

Local Only constrains processing and storage placement.

It may also require:

- restricted network,

- local Model,

- local Tool,

- and local evidence handling.

23.35 Local Only Is Not Device-Specific Automatically

A Local Only policy may permit:

- one laptop,

- one private rig,

- one on-premises server,

- or a defined private cluster.

The eligible Zones shall be explicit.

23.36 Local Only Failure

When no eligible local resource exists, the Fabric shall:

- wait,

- request a policy change,

- request an approved private alternative,

- or stop.

It shall not silently route externally.

23.37 Prohibited

Prohibited data or processing shall not be collected, stored, inferred, transferred, generated or used under the current policy.

23.38 Prohibited Examples

Examples may include:

- raw passwords in Model context,

- unauthorised private messages,

- prohibited biometric inference,

- unauthorised child sexual content,

- unlawfully obtained data,

- data outside the Project’s legal or policy authority,

- or information explicitly excluded by the user.

23.39 Prohibited Does Not Mean Delete Immediately in Every Case

Some prohibited content may need temporary isolated handling for:

- Incident response,

- lawful reporting,

- quarantine,

- or deletion verification.

Such handling shall be narrowly authorised.

23.40 Classification Label

A Classification Label is the machine- and human-readable representation of a Data Classification applied to a Data Object.

23.41 Classification Label Identity

Every reusable Classification Label shall have stable identity and Version.

23.42 Classification Assignment

A Classification Assignment binds a Classification Label to one Data Object or scope.

It shall include or reference:

- classificationAssignmentId,

- Data Object,

- assigned Classification,

- source,

- rule,

- classifier,

- confidence,

- effective time,

- expiry or review,

- and provenance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.43 Classification Assignment Identity

Every material Classification Assignment shall have stable identity.

23.44 Classification Source

Classification may originate from:

- explicit user designation,

- Project policy,

- Tenant policy,

- data category,

- source inheritance,

- automatic classifier,

- Provider metadata,

- legal requirement,

- or human review.

23.45 Explicit User Tightening

An authorised user may increase protection.

The Fabric shall apply the tighter classification promptly.

23.46 Automatic Tightening

The Fabric may increase classification automatically when new evidence indicates greater sensitivity.

23.47 Automatic Lowering Prohibition

The Fabric shall not lower classification automatically merely because:

- content was summarised,

- names were removed,

- a Provider labelled it safe,

- or an embedding was created.

23.48 Classification Lowering

Lowering classification requires:

- authorised Principal,

- defined purpose,

- transformation evidence,

- risk review,

- and attributable Decision.

23.49 Classification Confidence

Automatic classification shall preserve confidence and method.

23.50 Unknown Classification

Unknown classification shall default to a restrictive handling state appropriate to the context.

23.51 Classification Review

Low-confidence or high-risk classifications shall require review.

23.52 Classification Conflict

Conflicting assignments shall produce the most restrictive effective handling until resolved.

23.53 Classification Version

Material classification changes shall be Versioned or recorded as state transitions.

23.54 Classification Effective Time

Classification may change over time.

Historical processing shall remain linked to the effective Classification at the time.

23.55 Classification Expiry

Some temporary heightened states may expire after review.

Expiry shall not reduce protection without an explicit governing rule.

23.56 Classification Rule

A Classification Rule maps evidence, categories or contexts to a Classification.

It shall include or reference:

- classificationRuleId,

- scope,

- conditions,

- assigned level,

- exceptions,

- priority,

- Version,

- and owner.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.57 Classification Rule Identity

Every Rule shall have stable identity and Version.

23.58 Rule Priority

Higher-authority or more-specific Rules shall outrank general defaults.

23.59 Data Category

A Data Category describes the semantic or regulatory nature of data.

Categories may include:

- identity,

- contact,

- authentication,

- communication,

- family,

- child,

- health,

- fitness,

- financial,

- employment,

- education,

- location,

- device,

- behavioural,

- biometric,

- legal,

- commercial,

- source code,

- intellectual property,

- and operational telemetry.

23.60 Data Category Identity

Every canonical Data Category shall have stable identity and Version.

23.61 Multi-Category Data

One Data Object may belong to several categories.

23.62 Category Inheritance

Derived data may inherit all material source categories.

23.63 Category Discovery

Automatic category detection shall preserve confidence and limitations.

23.64 Identity Data

Identity Data may include:

- name,

- user ID,

- government identifier,

- account identifier,

- or identity evidence.

23.65 Contact Data

Contact Data may include:

- email,

- phone,

- address,

- and messaging handles.

23.66 Authentication Data

Authentication Data may include:

- username,

- Session ID,

- Token metadata,

- authentication event,

- or device identity.

23.67 Credential Material

Credential Material includes:

- passwords,

- private keys,

- API keys,

- access Tokens,

- refresh Tokens,

- recovery codes,

- and Secret values.

Credential Material shall be stored only in approved Secret systems.

23.68 Credential Reference

A Credential Reference may be used in ordinary workflow objects without exposing Secret value.

23.69 Communication Data

Communication Data may include:

- email,

- private message,

- chat,

- voicemail,

- call transcript,

- or correspondence metadata.

23.70 Private Communication

Private communication shall not become general Agent context or Memory by default.

23.71 Project Communication

Project communication may be processed only inside approved:

- Accounts,

- channels,

- Projects,

- purposes,

- and retention.

23.72 Family Data

Family Data includes information about:

- partner,

- children,

- household,

- relationships,

- routines,

- and private events.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.73 Child Data

Child Data receives stronger protection because of vulnerability, consent and long-term harm risk.

23.74 Child Data Default

Child-related personal data should default to Confidential or Local Only according to purpose and policy.

23.75 Health Data

Health Data may include:

- diagnoses,

- symptoms,

- medications,

- injuries,

- biological measures,

- treatment,

- and health-related inference.

23.76 Fitness Data

Fitness Data may include:

- workouts,

- performance,

- weight,

- body measurements,

- nutrition,

- recovery,

- and programme history.

Fitness Data may become health-sensitive depending on context.

23.77 Financial Data

Financial Data may include:

- account information,

- transactions,

- income,

- debt,

- investments,

- invoices,

- payment instruments,

- and financial planning.

23.78 Payment Instrument Data

Full payment-card or banking Credentials shall remain outside ordinary Agent and Model access.

23.79 Employment Data

Employment Data may include:

- work history,

- salary,

- performance,

- contracts,

- and workplace records.

23.80 Education Data

Education Data may include:

- grades,

- assignments,

- enrolment,

- learning difficulties,

- and school information.

23.81 Location Data

Location Data may include:

- exact coordinates,

- address,

- route,

- geofence,

- city,

- workplace,

- or recurring movement.

23.82 Detailed Location

Precise or historical location requires stronger minimisation and retention.

23.83 Coarse Location

City or region may require less protection but remains personal context.

23.84 Device Data

Device Data may include:

- model,

- operating-system Version,

- network state,

- storage,

- battery,

- installed applications,

- and device identifiers.

23.85 Device Identifier

Stable device identifiers may enable tracking and shall be protected.

23.86 Behavioural Data

Behavioural Data may include:

- clicks,

- usage patterns,

- habits,

- timing,

- preferences,

- and inferred intent.

23.87 Behavioural Inference

Behavioural inference shall remain lower confidence and purpose-limited unless confirmed.

23.88 Biometric Data

Biometric Data may include:

- face templates,

- Voiceprints,

- fingerprints,

- gait,

- or other persistent bodily identifiers.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.89 Biometric-Like Data

Character or Voice similarity embeddings may function like biometric identifiers even when not legally classified identically.

The system shall treat re-identification risk seriously.

23.90 Legal Data

Legal Data may include:

- contracts,

- disputes,

- claims,

- legal advice,

- court records,

- and compliance documents.

23.91 Commercial Data

Commercial Data may include:

- pricing,

- strategy,

- forecasts,

- customer information,

- and product plans.

23.92 Source Code

Source code may be:

- Public,

- Project Internal,

- Confidential,

- or Local Only

depending on repository and content.

23.93 Intellectual Property

Intellectual Property data may include:

- manuscripts,

- designs,

- Characters,

- Models,

- inventions,

- processes,

- and proprietary methods.

23.94 Operational Telemetry

Operational Telemetry may reveal:

- user activity,

- system architecture,

- Project names,

- file paths,

- and sensitive workflow details.

23.95 Metadata

Metadata may be as sensitive as content.

Examples include:

- sender,

- recipient,

- timestamp,

- location,

- file path,

- device,

- and Account.

23.96 Derived Data

Derived Data is produced through:

- summarisation,

- analysis,

- classification,

- embedding,

- aggregation,

- prediction,

- or inference.

23.97 Derived Data Classification

Derived Data shall inherit the strongest relevant source protection unless a governed transformation proves reduced risk.

23.98 Summary Classification

A summary remains as sensitive as the facts it preserves.

23.99 Embedding Classification

Embeddings shall inherit source classification and Project scope.

23.100 Index Classification

A search or vector index shall inherit the combined sensitivity of its contents.

23.101 Aggregate Data

Aggregated data may reduce or increase sensitivity.

23.102 Aggregation Risk

Aggregation may reveal:

- patterns,

- rare behaviour,

- business strategy,

- or re-identifiable groups.

23.103 Inferred Data

Inferred Data shall preserve:

- derivation method,

- confidence,

- source categories,

- and purpose.

23.104 Sensitive Inference

Automatic inference of sensitive traits shall be prohibited or strongly restricted unless explicitly authorised.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.105 Data Subject

A Data Subject is a person whose personal information is represented or inferable.

23.106 Data Subject Identity

The system may use a protected pseudonymous subject identifier when full identity is unnecessary.

23.107 Subject Relationship

Data may concern:

- user,

- child,

- partner,

- employee,

- customer,

- contractor,

- audience member,

- or third party.

23.108 Third-Party Data

A user’s authority over their own account does not automatically permit broad processing of other people’s data.

23.109 Data Controller Role

The entity determining processing purpose and means shall be represented where applicable.

23.110 Data Processor Role

A service processing data on behalf of another controller shall be represented where applicable.

23.111 Subprocessor Role

External Providers and infrastructure may act as subprocessors or analogous service roles.

The exact relationship shall remain explicit.

23.112 Data Custodian

The Custodian stores or protects data.

Custody does not create processing purpose.

23.113 Data Owner

Data ownership claims shall remain distinct from privacy rights and control roles.

23.114 Purpose Definition

A Purpose Definition describes why data is processed.

It shall include or reference:

- purposeId,

- statement,

- owner,

- scope,

- eligible data,

- prohibited data,

- operations,

- recipients,

- retention,

- and Version.

23.115 Purpose Definition Identity

Every reusable Purpose Definition shall have stable identity and Version.

23.116 Purpose Limitation

Data collected for one purpose shall not be reused for another purpose automatically.

23.117 Primary Purpose

The Primary Purpose is the direct reason for the processing.

23.118 Secondary Purpose

A Secondary Purpose requires separate compatibility or authority evaluation.

23.119 Compatible Purpose

Purpose compatibility shall be evidenced and policy-governed.

23.120 Incompatible Purpose

Incompatible purposes require new authority, consent or prohibition.

23.121 Processing Purpose

Every material processing operation shall reference an authorised Purpose Definition.

23.122 Purpose Is Not Capability

A Capability describes what the system can do.

A Purpose explains why it may do it in this context.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.123 Purpose Is Not Consent

Consent may support a purpose.

Other authority or policy may also exist.

The concepts shall remain separate.

23.124 Processing Activity

A Processing Activity is one governed collection, access, analysis, transformation, transfer, storage, retrieval, disclosure or deletion operation.

It shall include or reference:

- processingActivityId,

- purpose,

- Principal,

- Agent,

- Project,

- Data Objects,

- categories,

- classifications,

- operation,

- recipients,

- placement,

- retention,

- and evidence.

23.125 Processing Activity Identity

Every material Processing Activity shall have stable identity.

23.126 Collection

Collection introduces data into Omnira-controlled processing.

23.127 Access

Access allows an authorised Principal or service to view or retrieve data.

23.128 Use

Use applies data to one defined task or Decision.

23.129 Analysis

Analysis derives findings, patterns or conclusions.

23.130 Transformation

Transformation changes representation, content or sensitivity.

23.131 Disclosure

Disclosure makes data available to another Principal, system, Provider or audience.

23.132 Transfer

Transfer moves data between Locations, Zones, Providers or jurisdictions.

23.133 Storage

Storage retains data beyond transient execution.

23.134 Retrieval

Retrieval selects stored data for a new bounded context.

23.135 Deletion

Deletion removes data from defined stores and active use.

23.136 Processing Necessity

Every processing operation should use only data necessary for the purpose.

23.137 Data Minimisation

Data Minimisation limits:

- fields,

- records,

- duration,

- precision,

- copies,

- recipients,

- and context.

23.138 Input Minimisation

Only required Inputs shall be supplied to a Model, Tool or Provider.

23.139 Context Minimisation

Model context shall exclude unrelated:

- Memory,

- history,

- messages,

- files,

- and personal information.

23.140 Field Minimisation

Structured requests should omit unneeded fields.

23.141 Temporal Minimisation

Data shall not be retained longer than required.

23.142 Precision Minimisation

Coarse location or age range should be used instead of exact data when sufficient.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.143 Recipient Minimisation

Data shall be disclosed only to the required Provider, Account, service or human.

23.144 Copy Minimisation

Unnecessary duplicates, caches and exports shall be avoided.

23.145 Model Context Boundary

Every Model invocation creates a disclosure boundary.

The context shall include only:

- authorised,

- relevant,

- classified,

- and minimised

data.

23.146 Provider Input Boundary

Data sent to a Provider shall be limited to the exact Attempt.

23.147 Provider Project Library

Persistent Provider-side libraries shall not be used by default when transient invocation is sufficient.

23.148 Provider Retention

Provider retention settings and terms shall affect eligibility.

23.149 Provider Training Use

Providers that may use Inputs or Outputs for training shall be evaluated against classification and policy.

23.150 Provider Account Boundary

Each Provider Account shall identify:

- owner,

- plan,

- Tenant,

- Projects,

- retention,

- training settings,

- and trust.

23.151 Shared Provider Account

Shared Accounts create elevated cross-Project and cross-Tenant risk.

They require explicit isolation controls.

23.152 Dedicated Provider Account

Dedicated Accounts may reduce mixing but do not remove Provider custody.

23.153 User-Owned Provider Account

User-owned Accounts remain subject to Project policy and evidence requirements.

23.154 Omnira-Managed Provider Account

Omnira-managed Accounts shall preserve Tenant and Project attribution.

23.155 Provider Conversation State

Provider-hosted chat or session history shall not become canonical Memory.

It may retain data beyond one Execution and therefore requires explicit policy.

23.156 Provider File Store

Files uploaded to Provider-managed storage shall have:

- purpose,

- Project,

- retention,

- deletion,

- and access

defined.

23.157 External Processing Eligibility

External processing is eligible only when:

- classification permits it,

- purpose permits it,

- rights and consent permit it,

- Provider and Account are approved,

- retention is acceptable,

- location is acceptable,

- and minimisation has been applied.

23.158 External Processing Denial

One failed eligibility condition shall block the external route.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 23.160 Local Does Not Remove Privacy Risk
text:
23.159 Local Processing Eligibility

Local processing still requires:

- authorised Node,

- trusted Runtime,

- approved Tool or Model,

- Project scope,

- and evidence.

23.160 Local Does Not Remove Privacy Risk

Local data may leak through:

- backups,

- logs,

- malware,

- shared accounts,

- screen capture,

- remote administration,

- or broad file permissions.

23.161 Handling Profile

A Handling Profile defines required controls for one Classification or data context.

It shall include or reference:

- handlingProfileId,

- classification,

- allowed processing,

- allowed storage,

- approved Zones,

- approved Providers,

- encryption,

- logging,

- retention,

- review,

- and Version.

23.162 Handling Profile Identity

Every Handling Profile shall have stable identity and Version.

23.163 Public Handling Profile

Public data may use approved external resources and ordinary distribution paths.

Rights and purpose still apply.

23.164 Project Internal Handling Profile

Project Internal data should use:

- Project-scoped access,

- approved Providers,

- bounded retention,

- and no public disclosure without reclassification.

23.165 Confidential Handling Profile

Confidential data may require:

- stronger identity,

- limited Providers,

- encryption,

- no ordinary payload logging,

- short temporary retention,

- and explicit access records.

23.166 Local Only Handling Profile

Local Only data requires:

- approved local or private Zones,

- no ordinary external Provider egress,

- local storage,

- local evidence handling,

- and controlled synchronisation.

23.167 Prohibited Handling Profile

Prohibited data shall be blocked, quarantined or deleted according to Incident and policy procedures.

23.168 Access Scope

Access Scope defines the exact boundary within which a Principal may perform an operation.

It may include:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Capability,

- data category,

- Classification,

- Asset,

- folder,

- Account,

- device,

- time,

- and operation.

23.169 Access Scope Identity

Every reusable or granted Access Scope shall have stable identity and Version.

23.170 Read Scope

Read Scope defines which Data Objects may be viewed or retrieved.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.171 Write Scope

Write Scope defines which Data Objects may be created or modified.

23.172 Delete Scope

Delete Scope shall remain narrower than ordinary write access.

23.173 Share Scope

Share or disclosure authority shall remain separate from read access.

23.174 Export Scope

Export authority permits data to leave one controlled system or boundary.

23.175 Training Scope

Training or fine-tuning access shall remain distinct from ordinary processing.

23.176 Memory Scope

Memory admission and retrieval require dedicated scope.

23.177 Administrative Scope

Administrative access to configuration shall not imply content access.

23.178 Break-Glass Access

Emergency access shall be:

- rare,

- time-bounded,

- justified,

- highly audited,

- and reviewed afterward.

23.179 Least Privilege

Every Principal, Agent, Tool and service shall receive the minimum access required.

23.180 Just-in-Time Access

Temporary access should be granted only when required and expire automatically.

23.181 Time-Bounded Access

Access validity shall include start and expiry.

23.182 Purpose-Bound Access

Access shall be valid only for approved purposes.

23.183 Capability-Bound Access

An Agent approved to summarise shall not automatically receive authority to delete or publish.

23.184 Device-Bound Access

Some access may be restricted to:

- one Node,

- one mobile approval device,

- one workstation,

- or one recovery device.

23.185 Environment-Bound Access

Development, test, staging and production access shall remain distinct.

23.186 Session-Bound Access

A Session may constrain data and actions further than the Principal’s general role.

23.187 Tenant Boundary

The Tenant Boundary separates ownership, policy, identity, Credentials, data, Memory, cost and execution among Tenants.

23.188 Tenant Identity

Every Tenant shall have stable identity.

23.189 Tenant Isolation

Tenant isolation shall apply to:

- database rows,

- object storage,

- caches,

- queues,

- indexes,

- logs,

- Metrics,

- Provider Accounts,

- Memory,

- and administrative operations.

23.190 Tenant Context

Every Tenant-scoped request shall carry verified Tenant context.

23.191 Tenant Context Source

Tenant context shall derive from trusted identity and routing.

It shall not be accepted solely from untrusted request fields.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.192 Tenant Context Propagation

Tenant identity shall propagate through every:

- Request,

- Plan,

- Step,

- Attempt,

- Event,

- Asset,

- Evidence Item,

- Cost Record,

- and Memory access.

23.193 Tenant Context Loss

Loss or ambiguity of Tenant context shall fail closed.

23.194 Shared Infrastructure

Shared infrastructure may host several Tenants only when enforced isolation is verified.

23.195 Tenant Data Store

Tenant storage may be:

- physically separate,

- logically separate,

- schema-separated,

- row-separated,

- or cryptographically separated.

The isolation guarantee shall be explicit.

23.196 Row-Level Isolation

Row-level policies shall be enforced centrally and tested continuously.

23.197 Application Filter Insufficiency

Application-layer filters alone shall not be treated as sufficient Tenant isolation for high-risk data.

23.198 Tenant Storage Prefix

Object-storage keys shall include non-guessable and policy-enforced Tenant scope.

23.199 Tenant Encryption

Tenant-specific encryption keys may strengthen isolation.

23.200 Tenant Queue Isolation

Queue messages shall preserve Tenant identity and prevent cross-Tenant consumption.

23.201 Tenant Cache Isolation

Cache keys shall include Tenant identity and relevant policy Versions.

23.202 Tenant Search Isolation

Search and vector queries shall filter Tenant eligibility before similarity ranking.

23.203 Tenant Log Isolation

Logs shall not expose one Tenant’s payloads to another Tenant’s operator.

23.204 Tenant Metric Isolation

Metrics should avoid labels that reveal another Tenant’s sensitive information.

23.205 Tenant Backup Isolation

Backups shall preserve Tenant scope and deletion state.

23.206 Tenant Restore Isolation

Restore shall not copy one Tenant’s data into another Tenant.

23.207 Tenant Export

Tenant export shall contain only authorised data and preserve classification.

23.208 Tenant Deletion

Tenant deletion shall address:

- active stores,

- indexes,

- caches,

- backups,

- Provider libraries,

- and external processors.

23.209 Project Boundary

The Project Boundary separates operational context, data, Assets, Memory, Credentials, Agents and workflows within one Tenant or user domain.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.210 Project Identity

Every Project shall have stable identity.

23.211 Project Isolation

Project isolation shall apply even when the same user owns several Projects.

23.212 Project Context

Every Project-scoped Request shall carry verified Project identity.

23.213 Project Context Loss

Ambiguous Project context shall fail closed for data access and mutation.

23.214 Cross-Project Read

Cross-Project read requires explicit authority and purpose.

23.215 Cross-Project Write

Cross-Project mutation shall be prohibited by default.

23.216 Cross-Project Reference Reuse

Reference Assets, prompts, embeddings or Memory shall not cross Projects silently.

23.217 Project Credentials

Project-specific Connections and Credentials shall remain isolated.

23.218 Shared Credential

A shared Credential may support several Projects only when explicitly configured and auditable.

23.219 Project Provider Account

Provider Accounts may be dedicated or shared.

Project attribution shall always remain explicit.

23.220 Project Storage

Project storage paths, object keys and database records shall preserve Project identity.

23.221 Project Cache

Cache entries shall include Project scope.

23.222 Project Search

Search results shall enforce Project eligibility before relevance.

23.223 Project Memory

Memory Domains shall prevent one Project’s confidential context from entering another Project.

23.224 Project Logs

Operational logs should preserve Project correlation without exposing full protected payloads.

23.225 Project Export

Exports shall contain only the intended Project’s eligible data.

23.226 Project Migration

Migration shall preserve:

- Project identity,

- classification,

- provenance,

- access,

- and deletion state.

23.227 Agent Boundary

The Agent Boundary defines which data, Memory, Tools and authority one Agent identity may access.

23.228 Agent Identity

Every Agent shall have stable Omnira-owned identity.

23.229 Agent Scope

Agent scope may include:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- role,

- Capabilities,

- Memory Domains,

- Tools,

- and data classes.

23.230 Agent Context Isolation

One Agent’s context shall not be visible to another Agent unless explicitly shared.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.231 Agent Memory Isolation

Agent Memory remains bounded by its authorised Domains.

23.232 Agent Tool Isolation

Tools available to one Agent shall not become available to all Agents automatically.

23.233 Agent Secret Isolation

Agents receive Credential References or bounded Tool capabilities, not raw Secret values.

23.234 Agent-to-Agent Transfer

Data exchanged between Agents is a governed disclosure.

It shall preserve:

- source,

- destination,

- purpose,

- classification,

- and minimisation.

23.235 Delegation

An Agent may delegate only within its authority and data scope.

23.236 Delegation Does Not Expand Access

A delegated Agent shall not receive broader access than the delegating authority permits.

23.237 Workflow Boundary

A Workflow Boundary defines the data, state, Tools and authority available to one workflow instance.

23.238 Workflow Identity

Every workflow instance shall have stable identity.

23.239 Workflow State Isolation

Workflow state shall be isolated across:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- execution,

- and version.

23.240 Workflow Input Isolation

One workflow’s Inputs shall not become another workflow’s context automatically.

23.241 Workflow Output Isolation

Outputs shall remain associated with the originating Project and Request.

23.242 Workflow Retry Isolation

Retries shall use the same governed scope and not broaden data access.

23.243 Workflow Cache Isolation

Reusable workflow cache shall be keyed by:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- policy,

- data Version,

- and resource Version.

23.244 Environment Boundary

Development, test, staging, production and recovery environments shall remain isolated.

23.245 Development Data

Production personal or confidential data shall not enter development environments by default.

23.246 Test Data

Test environments should use:

- synthetic,

- minimised,

- anonymised,

- or specifically approved

data.

23.247 Production Data

Production data shall not be copied to test for convenience.

23.248 Staging Data

Staging may use representative but minimised datasets under explicit policy.

23.249 Recovery Environment

Recovery may access sensitive data only for bounded restoration purposes.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.250 Environment Credential Isolation

Credentials shall not be shared across environments by default.

23.251 Environment Provider Isolation

Provider Accounts or workspaces should remain environment-specific where risk requires it.

23.252 Node Boundary

A Runtime Node is an isolation and custody boundary.

Node access shall be scoped by:

- Device Principal,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- Tool,

- and data class.

23.253 Node File Isolation

Tools shall access only approved file paths.

23.254 Node User Isolation

Dedicated operating-system users or containers may enforce Project boundaries.

23.255 Node Process Isolation

Processes shall not read unrelated process memory or environment variables.

23.256 Node Device Isolation

Camera, microphone, location, USB and screen capture require explicit Capability and permission.

23.257 Node Clipboard Isolation

Sensitive data shall not be placed in clipboard unnecessarily.

23.258 Node Temporary File Isolation

Temporary files shall remain Project-scoped and classified.

23.259 Node Swap and Hibernation

Swap and hibernation may contain sensitive memory and require encryption.

23.260 Node Backup Isolation

Local backups shall preserve Project and data-class boundaries.

23.261 Storage Boundary

A Storage Boundary defines access, encryption, location, replication and retention for stored data.

23.262 Database Isolation

Database controls may include:

- separate database,

- separate schema,

- row-level security,

- encryption,

- and restricted service roles.

23.263 Object Storage Isolation

Object storage shall use:

- Tenant and Project prefixes,

- access policies,

- encryption,

- and signed access.

23.264 File-System Isolation

File permissions and Sandbox policies shall protect Project directories.

23.265 Memory Store Isolation

Canonical Memory storage shall enforce Domain, Tenant and Project access.

23.266 Evidence Store Isolation

Evidence may require stricter access than ordinary operational data.

23.267 Analytics Store Isolation

Analytics pipelines shall minimise and aggregate data before broader use.

23.268 Cache Boundary

Caches are storage systems and shall receive the same scope discipline as primary stores.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.269 Shared Cache Risk

Shared caches can leak:

- prompts,

- Outputs,

- embeddings,

- decisions,

- and existence of records.

23.270 Cache Key Composition

Cache keys shall include relevant:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- user,

- classification,

- purpose,

- Model,

- policy,

- and Version.

23.271 Cache Value Classification

Cached values inherit source protection.

23.272 Cache Expiry

Sensitive cache entries shall have short retention.

23.273 Cache Invalidation

Deletion, revocation, policy change and source update shall invalidate affected entries.

23.274 Negative Cache

Negative results may still reveal sensitive existence or access state.

23.275 Search Isolation

Search shall enforce access before:

- lexical ranking,

- semantic ranking,

- reranking,

- and result generation.

23.276 Vector Index Isolation

Vector indexes shall preserve:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Domain,

- source Asset,

- classification,

- and deletion state.

23.277 Shared Vector Index

Shared physical indexes may be used only with verified structural filtering and leakage testing.

23.278 Semantic Side Channel

Similarity scores may reveal the presence of protected data.

Results and score exposure shall be minimised.

23.279 Retrieval Snippet

Snippets shall reveal only authorised source ranges.

23.280 Index Metadata

Index metadata shall not expose:

- private filenames,

- subjects,

- Project names,

- or counts

to unauthorised consumers.

23.281 Memory Isolation

Memory retrieval shall enforce:

- Domain,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Agent,

- purpose,

- classification,

- lifecycle,

- and freshness.

23.282 Prompt Isolation

Prompt assembly shall exclude unrelated Memory and historical context.

23.283 Conversation Isolation

Conversations shall remain scoped to:

- user,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Agent,

- and Session.

23.284 Conversation Reuse

Conversation history shall not be reused across Projects automatically.

23.285 Session Isolation

Session state shall not leak between users, devices or Tenants.

23.286 Browser Isolation

Browser automation shall use isolated profiles and sessions.

23.287 Cookie Isolation

Authentication cookies shall remain Account- and profile-scoped.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.288 Publication Account Isolation

Project publication Accounts shall not be mixed with private user Accounts without explicit authority.

23.289 Provider Boundary

A Provider Boundary includes:

- Provider,

- Product,

- Account,

- region,

- storage,

- retention,

- training,

- and access.

23.290 Provider Isolation Evaluation

Eligibility shall consider whether the Provider isolates:

- Accounts,

- workspaces,

- Projects,

- files,

- sessions,

- and Models.

23.291 Provider Shared Model

A shared hosted Model may process many customers’ data.

Input isolation and retention guarantees shall remain explicit.

23.292 Provider Human Access

Potential Provider staff access shall be considered for Confidential data.

23.293 Provider Region

Processing and storage region shall be explicit where required.

23.294 Provider Subprocessors

Subprocessor or infrastructure dependencies shall be captured where material.

23.295 Provider Data Export

Data leaving Omnira for a Provider is a governed transfer.

23.296 Provider Output Return

Outputs returning from a Provider inherit:

- source classification,

- Provider custody evidence,

- and rights state.

23.297 Provider Deletion

Provider-side deletion may remain pending or partially unverifiable.

23.298 Provider Account Termination

Termination shall address:

- stored files,

- conversation history,

- generated Assets,

- logs,

- and Tokens.

23.299 Data Residency

Data Residency identifies where data is stored or processed geographically or jurisdictionally.

23.300 Storage Residency

Storage Residency identifies persistent Location.

23.301 Processing Residency

Processing Residency identifies where computation occurs.

23.302 Backup Residency

Backup copies may exist in different regions from primary storage.

23.303 Provider Control Plane Residency

Provider metadata or control-plane data may reside outside the selected processing region.

23.304 Residency Evidence

Residency claims shall be:

- verified,

- contractually stated,

- inferred,

- or unknown.

23.305 Residency Policy

A policy may require:

- country,

- region,

- on-premises,

- private cloud,

- or local device.

23.306 Cross-Border Transfer

Cross-border transfer shall be represented as a material Data Flow where applicable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.307 Data Flow

A Data Flow describes movement or access between systems, boundaries or Principals.

It shall include or reference:

- dataFlowId,

- source,

- destination,

- Data Objects,

- classifications,

- categories,

- purpose,

- transfer method,

- region,

- recipient,

- retention,

- and evidence.

23.308 Data Flow Identity

Every material Data Flow shall have stable identity.

23.309 Ingress Flow

Ingress brings data into Omnira or one Project boundary.

23.310 Egress Flow

Egress sends data outside the current boundary.

23.311 Internal Flow

Internal Flow crosses an internal service or Zone boundary.

23.312 Cross-Project Flow

Cross-Project Flow requires explicit authority and minimisation.

23.313 Cross-Tenant Flow

Cross-Tenant Flow is prohibited by default.

23.314 Model Context Flow

Supplying context to a Model is a Data Flow.

23.315 Tool Input Flow

Supplying data to a Tool is a Data Flow.

23.316 Human Review Flow

Providing data to a Reviewer is a Data Flow.

23.317 Publication Flow

Publication intentionally changes visibility and requires separate authority.

23.318 Backup Flow

Backup copies data into another storage and retention boundary.

23.319 Synchronisation Flow

Synchronisation transfers state between Nodes or control planes.

23.320 Transfer Decision

A Transfer Decision determines whether a Data Flow is permitted.

It shall include or reference:

- transferDecisionId,

- source,

- destination,

- Data Objects,

- classifications,

- purpose,

- policy Versions,

- minimisation,

- encryption,

- recipient,

- decision,

- conditions,

- and provenance.

23.321 Transfer Decision Identity

Every material Transfer Decision shall have stable identity.

23.322 Transfer Eligibility

Transfer requires:

- authorised purpose,

- eligible recipient,

- compatible classification,

- approved region,

- secure transport,

- rights and consent,

- and retention.

23.323 Transfer Denial

Denied transfer shall fail before payload disclosure.

23.324 Transfer Minimisation

The transferred representation should contain only required data.

23.325 Transfer Encryption

Protected data shall use approved transport encryption.

23.326 Transfer Integrity

Checksum or equivalent verification should be used where material.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.327 Transfer Expiry

Temporary transfer links and access shall expire.

23.328 Disclosure Record

A Disclosure Record documents that data was made available to another party, system or audience.

It shall include or reference:

- disclosureRecordId,

- Data Objects,

- discloser,

- recipient,

- purpose,

- legal or policy basis,

- time,

- scope,

- retention,

- and evidence.

23.329 Disclosure Record Identity

Every material disclosure shall have stable identity.

23.330 Internal Disclosure

Internal disclosure may still require purpose and access checks.

23.331 External Disclosure

External disclosure includes Provider processing, delivery and publication.

23.332 Public Disclosure

Public disclosure requires:

- publication authority,

- reclassification or Public eligibility,

- rights,

- consent,

- and review.

23.333 Disclosure Is Not Transfer Only

Viewing through a shared screen, Reviewer interface or remote Tool may constitute disclosure without copying files.

23.334 Privacy Constraint

A Privacy Constraint defines one mandatory limitation on processing.

Examples include:

- no external processing,

- no training,

- no retention,

- no exact location,

- no private-message access,

- no public disclosure,

- or no child likeness.

23.335 Privacy Constraint Identity

Every reusable Privacy Constraint shall have stable identity and Version.

23.336 User Privacy Preference

The user may define stricter preferences than the Platform default.

23.337 Project Privacy Policy

Each Project may define additional privacy constraints.

23.338 Tenant Privacy Policy

Tenant policy may impose organisation-wide requirements.

23.339 Platform Privacy Policy

Platform policy defines non-negotiable minimum protections.

23.340 Policy Precedence

The most restrictive applicable privacy requirement shall govern unless an authorised exception exists.

23.341 Privacy Exception

An exception shall include:

- exact scope,

- reason,

- authority,

- duration,

- affected data,

- conditions,

- and review.

23.342 Permanent Exception Prohibition

Broad permanent privacy exceptions should be prohibited.

23.343 Data Collection Policy

Collection policy shall define:

- permitted sources,

- data categories,

- purpose,

- consent,

- and retention.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.344 Passive Collection

Passive or background collection requires stronger justification and user control.

23.345 Sensor Collection

Camera, microphone, location and device sensors require explicit Capability and permission.

23.346 Installed Application List

Installed application inventory may reveal sensitive interests or behaviour.

Collection shall be purpose-limited.

23.347 Notification Content

Notification content may expose private communication and shall be excluded or strongly restricted.

23.348 Screenshot Collection

Screenshots may contain:

- private messages,

- banking data,

- personal photos,

- and Credentials.

Capture requires explicit scope and review.

23.349 Screen Redaction

Sensitive regions should be excluded or redacted before processing when practical.

23.350 Data Accuracy

Personal and operational data should be accurate enough for the intended use.

23.351 Accuracy Challenge

Users shall be able to correct materially wrong personal or Project data.

23.352 Source Attribution

Derived personal data shall remain linked to its source and confidence.

23.353 Inference Transparency

Material inferred data should be labelled as inferred.

23.354 Profiling

Profiling combines data to evaluate or predict behaviour, interests or characteristics.

It requires explicit policy and purpose.

23.355 High-Impact Profiling

Profiling affecting:

- employment,

- finance,

- health,

- access,

- or significant opportunity

requires stronger governance.

23.356 Manipulative Personalisation

Personalisation shall not exploit sensitive vulnerability or hidden inference.

23.357 Privacy by Default

The default state shall minimise:

- access,

- collection,

- retention,

- sharing,

- and visibility.

23.358 Privacy by Design

Privacy requirements shall be part of:

- architecture,

- schemas,

- APIs,

- queues,

- storage,

- and testing.

23.359 Data Protection Impact Review

High-risk processing may require a structured Privacy Review before implementation or activation.

23.360 Privacy Review

A Privacy Review evaluates:

- purpose,

- necessity,

- data categories,

- subjects,

- classification,

- recipients,

- retention,

- rights,

- consent,

- security,

- and residual risk.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 23.376 Redaction Does Not Alter Source Automatically
text:
23.361 Privacy Review Identity

Every material Privacy Review shall have stable identity.

23.362 Privacy Review States

States may include:

- approved,

- approved with conditions,

- revision required,

- rejected,

- expired,

- and superseded.

23.363 High-Risk Processing

High-risk processing may include:

- child data,

- biometrics,

- health data,

- financial data,

- private communications,

- precise location,

- large-scale profiling,

- or cross-Tenant aggregation.

23.364 Residual Risk

Residual risk shall remain explicit after controls are applied.

23.365 Privacy Risk Owner

Every accepted material residual risk shall have an accountable owner.

23.366 Redaction

Redaction removes or obscures selected content from a derived representation.

23.367 Redaction Specification

A Redaction Specification shall include:

- redactionSpecificationId,

- source,

- target categories or fields,

- method,

- irreversible or reversible state,

- validation,

- purpose,

- and Version.

23.368 Redaction Specification Identity

Every Redaction Specification shall have stable identity and Version.

23.369 Field Redaction

Structured fields may be removed or replaced.

23.370 Text Redaction

Text spans may be removed, masked or generalised.

23.371 Image Redaction

Faces, screens, names or locations may be blurred, covered or removed.

23.372 Audio Redaction

Names, Voices or sensitive segments may be muted, replaced or distorted.

23.373 Video Redaction

Video redaction shall preserve temporal tracking across Frames.

23.374 Metadata Redaction

Metadata such as location, creator or device may be removed.

23.375 Redacted Representation

A Redacted Representation is a derivative linked to its source and Redaction Specification.

23.376 Redaction Does Not Alter Source Automatically

The protected source remains separately governed unless deletion is required.

23.377 Redaction Validation

Validation shall verify that targeted information is not recoverable through ordinary access.

23.378 Redaction Failure

Incomplete redaction shall block the lower-classification use.

23.379 Reversible Redaction

Reversible masking remains sensitive and requires key or mapping protection.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.380 Pseudonymisation

Pseudonymisation replaces direct identifiers with controlled aliases while preserving possible re-linkage.

23.381 Pseudonymisation Record

A Pseudonymisation Record shall include:

- pseudonymisationId,

- source,

- method,

- mapping custody,

- scope,

- reversibility,

- and validation.

23.382 Pseudonymisation Identity

Every material pseudonymisation process shall have stable identity.

23.383 Pseudonym Mapping

The mapping between identity and pseudonym shall be stored separately with stronger access controls.

23.384 Pseudonymised Data

Pseudonymised data remains protected and may still be personal.

23.385 Anonymisation

Anonymisation aims to make identification no longer reasonably possible under the accepted threat model.

23.386 Anonymisation Record
