An Anonymisation Record shall include:

- anonymisationId,

- source,

- method,

- removed identifiers,

- generalisation,

- aggregation,

- threat model,

- risk assessment,

- validation,

- and Version.

23.387 Anonymisation Identity

Every material anonymisation process shall have stable identity.

23.388 Anonymisation Is Not Name Removal

Removing names alone rarely proves anonymity.

23.389 Re-Identification Risk

Risk may arise from:

- rare combinations,

- location,

- timestamps,

- free text,

- images,

- Voice,

- device identifiers,

- and external datasets.

23.390 Re-Identification Risk Assessment

The assessment shall include:

- attacker assumptions,

- available auxiliary data,

- uniqueness,

- linkage risk,

- impact,

- and reviewer.

23.391 Re-Identification Assessment Identity

Every material assessment shall have stable identity.

23.392 Anonymous Classification

Data may receive reduced classification only after successful anonymisation review.

23.393 Anonymisation Expiry

Anonymisation claims may become weaker as external data and techniques evolve.

Review may be required.

23.394 Aggregation

Aggregation combines records into statistics or summaries.

23.395 Small-Group Risk

Small groups may remain re-identifiable.

23.396 Suppression

Rare or sensitive groups may be suppressed.

23.397 Generalisation

Precision may be reduced through:

- age bands,

- coarse location,

- time ranges,

- or category grouping.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 23.414 Separation of Content and Metadata Access
text:
23.398 Noise Addition

Statistical noise may reduce disclosure risk.

Accuracy trade-offs shall remain explicit.

23.399 Privacy-Preserving Analytics

Analytics should prefer:

- minimised fields,

- aggregation,

- bounded retention,

- and role-separated access.

23.400 Analytics Purpose

Analytics data shall not be repurposed for personal profiling automatically.

23.401 Telemetry Privacy

Telemetry shall collect the minimum required for reliability and performance.

23.402 Content Logging Prohibition

Full prompts, Outputs, messages or documents shall not be logged by default.

23.403 Structured Logging

Logs should record:

- identifiers,

- states,

- timings,

- error classes,

- and bounded metadata

rather than protected payloads.

23.404 Log Classification

Logs inherit the sensitivity of included data.

23.405 Log Redaction

Credential values, personal content and private file paths shall be redacted.

23.406 Trace Privacy

Distributed traces may expose:

- request paths,

- Project IDs,

- Provider endpoints,

- and payload fragments.

Trace attributes shall be minimised.

23.407 Metric Privacy

Metrics should avoid:

- names,

- emails,

- Asset titles,

- message content,

- or high-cardinality personal identifiers.

23.408 Debug Mode

Debug mode shall not disable privacy controls silently.

23.409 Temporary Diagnostic Capture

Expanded capture requires:

- Incident scope,

- approval,

- short expiry,

- protected storage,

- and cleanup.

23.410 Evidence Privacy

Execution evidence shall preserve reconstructability without exposing unnecessary full content.

23.411 Memory Privacy

Memory shall store the minimum durable representation required for future use.

23.412 Audit Privacy

Audit access shall remain role- and purpose-limited.

23.413 Administrative Metadata

Administrators may inspect health and identifiers without viewing protected content where practical.

23.414 Separation of Content and Metadata Access

Operational roles should not receive content access merely to manage infrastructure.

23.415 Retention Policy

A Retention Policy defines how long data remains stored and retrievable.

It shall include or reference:

- retentionPolicyId,

- scope,

- data categories,

- classifications,

- minimum period,

- maximum period,

- triggers,

- holds,

- deletion method,

- and Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.416 Retention Policy Identity

Every Retention Policy shall have stable identity and Version.

23.417 Purpose-Based Retention

Retention shall be no longer than necessary for the authorised purpose.

23.418 Evidence Retention

Evidence may require longer retention than Model context or temporary Inputs.

23.419 Memory Retention

Memory retention shall remain distinct from source-data retention.

23.420 Provider Retention

Provider-side retention shall be included in the effective retention picture.

23.421 Backup Retention

Backup periods shall remain visible.

23.422 Temporary File Retention

Temporary media, prompts and transformations shall expire automatically.

23.423 Cache Retention

Cache retention shall be shorter than canonical source retention unless justified.

23.424 Legal or Dispute Hold

A hold may suspend deletion without broadening access or processing purpose.

23.425 Retention Decision

A Retention Decision applies policy to one Data Object or set.

It shall include:

- retentionDecisionId,

- target,

- policy,

- start,

- expiry,

- hold,

- review,

- and provenance.

23.426 Retention Decision Identity

Every material Retention Decision shall have stable identity.

23.427 Deletion Trigger

Deletion may be triggered by:

- expiry,

- user request,

- consent revocation,

- Project closure,

- Account termination,

- policy change,

- or Incident.

23.428 Deletion Propagation

Deletion shall address:

- canonical store,

- replicas,

- caches,

- indexes,

- Memory,

- logs,

- Provider storage,

- backups,

- and derived objects

according to policy.

23.429 Deletion Is Not Forgetting Automatically

Audit metadata may remain where permitted.

Active content retrieval shall stop.

23.430 Deletion Record

A Deletion Record shall preserve:

- deletionRecordId,

- target,

- authority,

- reason,

- Locations,

- processors,

- completion,

- residual copies,

- and time.

23.431 Deletion Record Identity

Every material Deletion Record shall have stable identity.

23.432 Incomplete Deletion

Incomplete deletion shall remain explicit.

23.433 Backup Deletion Delay

Backup expiration may delay full physical deletion.

The data shall remain inaccessible for ordinary use.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.434 Provider Deletion Uncertainty

Provider deletion may be:

- confirmed,

- requested,

- pending,

- partially confirmed,

- or unknown.

23.435 Restore Rules

Restore shall reapply current:

- classification,

- revocation,

- expiry,

- deletion,

- and access.

23.436 No Deleted Data Reactivation

Restored copies shall not return deleted or revoked data to ordinary use.

23.437 Privacy Request

A Privacy Request may concern:

- access,

- correction,

- export,

- restriction,

- deletion,

- or objection

according to applicable policy and law.

23.438 Privacy Request Identity

Every material Privacy Request shall have stable identity.

23.439 Requester Verification

Identity and authority shall be verified proportionately.

23.440 Data Discovery

The system should be able to identify relevant data across:

- Assets,

- Memory,

- Evidence,

- logs,

- indexes,

- Providers,

- and backups.

23.441 Privacy Export

Exports shall be:

- scoped,

- classified,

- understandable,

- and secure.

23.442 Correction Request

Corrections shall preserve history and propagate to active derived state where required.

23.443 Restriction Request

Restricted data shall remain stored if required but excluded from defined processing.

23.444 Deletion Request

Deletion shall follow retention, evidence and legal constraints without fabricating completion.

23.445 Isolation Test

An Isolation Test verifies that one boundary cannot access another boundary’s data or authority.

It shall include or reference:

- isolationTestId,

- boundary type,

- source scope,

- target scope,

- operation,

- expected denial,

- result,

- environment,

- time,

- and evidence.

23.446 Isolation Test Identity

Every material Isolation Test shall have stable identity.

23.447 Tenant Isolation Test

A Tenant isolation test attempts unauthorised cross-Tenant access.

23.448 Project Isolation Test

A Project isolation test attempts cross-Project retrieval, mutation or cache access.

23.449 Agent Isolation Test

An Agent test verifies Memory, Tool and data restrictions.

23.450 Environment Isolation Test

An environment test verifies separation between development and production.

23.451 Storage Isolation Test

A storage test verifies object, row, schema or path enforcement.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.452 Cache Isolation Test

A cache test verifies keys and eviction do not leak data.

23.453 Search Isolation Test

A search test verifies eligibility filtering before ranking.

23.454 Provider Isolation Test

A Provider test verifies that files, sessions and outputs remain in the correct Account or workspace.

23.455 Credential Isolation Test

A Credential test verifies that one Project cannot resolve another Project’s Secret.

23.456 Memory Isolation Test

A Memory test verifies Domain and Project boundaries.

23.457 Queue Isolation Test

A queue test verifies that workers cannot consume another Tenant’s messages.

23.458 Log Isolation Test

A log test verifies that payloads and identifiers do not leak to unauthorised viewers.

23.459 Backup Isolation Test

A backup test verifies restore scope and Tenant segregation.

23.460 Isolation Evidence

Isolation Evidence preserves:

- test,

- environment,

- configuration,

- result,

- failures,

- and remediation.

23.461 Isolation Evidence Identity

Every material Isolation Evidence record shall have stable identity.

23.462 Continuous Isolation Verification

Critical isolation controls should be tested continuously or on every material change.

23.463 Isolation Regression

A change to schema, cache, Provider Account, index or policy may introduce isolation regression.

23.464 Isolation Failure

Any verified cross-Tenant or unauthorised cross-Project access is a severe Incident.

23.465 Privacy Incident

A Privacy Incident is a material event involving unauthorised:

- access,

- disclosure,

- inference,

- retention,

- transfer,

- loss,

- or processing.

23.466 Privacy Incident Identity

Every material Privacy Incident shall have stable identity.

23.467 Classification Incident

A Classification Incident occurs when data receives insufficient protection or incorrect handling.

23.468 Egress Incident

An Egress Incident occurs when protected data leaves an approved boundary.

23.469 Cross-Tenant Incident

Cross-Tenant access or disclosure is a severe isolation failure.

23.470 Cross-Project Incident

Cross-Project leakage is severe when Projects are expected to remain isolated.

23.471 Credential Exposure Incident

Credential exposure requires:

- containment,

- rotation,

- access review,

- and evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.472 Private Message Incident

Unauthorised processing of private communications requires immediate containment.

23.473 Child Data Incident

Child data incidents receive elevated severity and review.

23.474 Biometric Incident

Biometric or Voice identity leakage may create long-term harm.

23.475 Location Incident

Precise location exposure may create physical safety risk.

23.476 Logging Incident

Protected payloads in logs require:

- access restriction,

- redaction,

- deletion,

- and downstream review.

23.477 Memory Leakage Incident

Wrong-scope Memory retrieval requires:

- context review,

- Output review,

- index audit,

- and policy correction.

23.478 Provider Incident

A Provider may retain or expose data outside expected terms or region.

23.479 Backup Incident

Lost, unencrypted or cross-Tenant backup data requires Incident response.

23.480 Privacy Incident Containment

Containment may include:

- revoke access,

- stop workflow,

- isolate Node,

- suspend Provider path,

- rotate Credential,

- quarantine data,

- disable index,

- and block publication.

23.481 Privacy Incident Investigation

Investigation should identify:

- affected Data Objects,

- subjects,

- classifications,

- scope,

- Principals,

- recipients,

- duration,

- copies,

- downstream Outputs,

- and cause.

23.482 Privacy Incident Notification

Notification requirements shall be determined by policy, contract and applicable law.

The system shall preserve evidence without fabricating legal conclusions.

23.483 Privacy Incident Recovery

Recovery may require:

- deletion,

- correction,

- reclassification,

- Credential rotation,

- index rebuild,

- Provider deletion,

- user communication,

- and policy change.

23.484 Isolation Remediation

Remediation shall address the root cause, not only the observed leak.

23.485 Privacy Policy

Privacy Policy defines rules for:

- collection,

- use,

- inference,

- disclosure,

- retention,

- access,

- deletion,

- and transparency.

23.486 Privacy Policy Identity

Every Privacy Policy shall have stable identity and Version.

23.487 Classification Policy

Classification Policy defines levels, assignment, inheritance, lowering and review.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.488 Isolation Policy

Isolation Policy defines mandatory boundaries and enforcement mechanisms.

23.489 Data-Flow Policy

Data-Flow Policy defines eligible transfers and recipients.

23.490 Provider Privacy Policy

Provider policy defines which data classes may use which Providers, Accounts and Products.

23.491 Memory Privacy Policy

Memory policy defines which data may be retained and retrieved.

23.492 Logging Privacy Policy

Logging policy defines permitted fields, redaction and retention.

23.493 Analytics Privacy Policy

Analytics policy defines aggregation, subject protection and reuse.

23.494 Local Only Policy

Local Only Policy defines approved Zones, Nodes, storage and synchronisation.

23.495 Prohibited Data Policy

Prohibited Data Policy defines blocking, quarantine, Incident and deletion actions.

23.496 Child Data Policy

Child Data Policy defines:

- classification,

- consent,

- access,

- Provider eligibility,

- retention,

- and publication.

23.497 Private Communication Policy

Private communications shall remain excluded by default unless the user explicitly opens a bounded workflow.

23.498 Financial Data Policy

Financial Data may require:

- local or restricted processing,

- no ordinary logging,

- and stronger approval.

23.499 Health Data Policy

Health Data may require:

- Confidential or Local Only handling,

- limited Agent access,

- and narrow retention.

23.500 Policy Version

Every material Processing Activity shall reference applicable policy Versions.

23.501 Classification API

The Classification Control Plane should expose governed operations such as:

- classify Data Object,

- inspect classification,

- tighten classification,

- propose lowering,

- review,

- record Decision,

- and propagate changes.

23.502 Data Category API

The Category API should support:

- assign category,

- detect category,

- review,

- add subject,

- and inspect inheritance.

23.503 Purpose API

The Purpose API should support:

- create Purpose Definition,

- bind processing,

- evaluate compatibility,

- restrict,

- expire,

- and audit.

23.504 Privacy Review API

The Privacy Review API should support:

- create review,

- add data flow,

- assess risk,

- define controls,

- approve,

- reject,

- and revalidate.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.505 Transfer API

The Transfer API should support:

- propose flow,

- evaluate eligibility,

- minimise payload,

- approve,

- deny,

- execute,

- and verify.

23.506 Isolation API

The Isolation API should support:

- define boundary,

- inspect policy,

- test,

- record evidence,

- detect regression,

- and isolate affected resources.

23.507 Retention API

The Retention API should support:

- assign policy,

- calculate expiry,

- place hold,

- release hold,

- delete,

- and verify.

23.508 Privacy Request API

The Privacy Request API should support:

- receive request,

- verify requester,

- discover data,

- export,

- correct,

- restrict,

- delete,

- and record completion.

23.509 Stage 1 Classification Objective

Stage 1 shall implement:

- the five canonical Classification levels,

- automatic classification assistance,

- explicit user tightening,

- no automatic lowering,

- classification inheritance,

- Handling Profiles,

- and policy-enforced routing.

23.510 Stage 1 Privacy Objective

Stage 1 shall implement:

- purpose limitation,

- data minimisation,

- sensitive-category handling,

- Provider privacy eligibility,

- retention,

- deletion,

- redaction,

- and privacy review.

23.511 Stage 1 Isolation Objective

Stage 1 shall implement verified isolation across:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Agent,

- Environment,

- storage,

- cache,

- search,

- Memory,

- Credentials,

- and Provider Accounts.

23.512 Stage 1 Classification Assignment Object

The Stage 1 Classification Assignment should include:

- assignmentId,

- Data Object,

- category,

- Classification,

- source,

- classifier,

- confidence,

- effective time,

- review date,

- and provenance.

23.513 Stage 1 Handling Profile Object

The Stage 1 Handling Profile should include:

- handlingProfileId,

- Classification,

- allowed Providers,

- approved Zones,

- encryption,

- logging,

- retention,

- Memory eligibility,

- transfer rules,

- and Version.

23.514 Stage 1 Purpose Definition Object

The Stage 1 Purpose Definition should include:

- purposeId,

- owner,

- statement,

- Project,

- eligible data categories,

- permitted operations,

- recipients,

- retention,

- and Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.515 Stage 1 Processing Activity Object

The Stage 1 Processing Activity should include:

- processingActivityId,

- purpose,

- Principal,

- Agent,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Data Objects,

- categories,

- classifications,

- operation,

- Provider or Tool,

- placement,

- retention,

- and evidence.

23.516 Stage 1 Transfer Decision Object

The Stage 1 Transfer Decision should include:

- transferDecisionId,

- source,

- destination,

- Data Objects,

- classifications,

- purpose,

- recipient,

- Provider Account,

- region,

- minimisation,

- encryption,

- decision,

- conditions,

- and policy Versions.

23.517 Stage 1 Isolation Boundary Object

The Stage 1 Isolation Boundary should include:

- isolationBoundaryId,

- type,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Agent or Environment,

- protected resources,

- permitted Principals,

- enforcement mechanisms,

- lifecycle,

- and Version.

23.518 Stage 1 Privacy Review Object

The Stage 1 Privacy Review should include:

- privacyReviewId,

- Processing Activity,

- purposes,

- categories,

- subjects,

- classifications,

- flows,

- recipients,

- retention,

- controls,

- residual risk,

- reviewer,

- decision,

- and Version.

23.519 Stage 1 Retention Decision Object

The Stage 1 Retention Decision should include:

- retentionDecisionId,

- target,

- policy,

- start,

- expiry,

- hold state,

- deletion method,

- and provenance.

23.520 Stage 1 Deletion Record Object

The Stage 1 Deletion Record should include:

- deletionRecordId,

- target,

- authority,

- reason,

- canonical store,

- replicas,

- caches,

- indexes,

- Provider copies,

- backup state,

- completion,

- and time.

23.521 Stage 1 Supported Sensitive Categories

Stage 1 shall explicitly support policies for:

- Credentials,

- private communications,

- family and child data,

- health and fitness data,

- financial data,

- exact location,

- private images,

- private Voice,

- source code,

- and confidential business information.

23.522 Stage 1 Default Classification

Stage 1 should default:

- approved public source material to Public only after review,

- ordinary Project work to Project Internal,

- personal or sensitive data to Confidential,

- user-designated local material to Local Only,

- and disallowed Secrets or private-message content in ordinary contexts to Prohibited.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.523 Stage 1 Automatic Classification

Automatic classification may propose:

- category,

- Classification,

- confidence,

- and reasons.

High-risk data shall fail closed when confidence is insufficient.

23.524 Stage 1 Provider Eligibility

Each Provider Product and Account shall declare maximum eligible Classification.

23.525 Stage 1 External Egress

External egress shall require a Transfer Decision for Confidential or Local Only-sensitive paths.

23.526 Stage 1 Local Only Enforcement

Local Only data shall be blocked from ordinary external Adapters and Provider Accounts.

23.527 Stage 1 Project Isolation

Every canonical object, queue message, cache entry, index entry and storage object shall preserve Project identity.

23.528 Stage 1 Tenant Isolation

Multi-Tenant paths shall enforce Tenant context at database, storage, queue, cache and search boundaries.

23.529 Stage 1 Memory Isolation

Memory retrieval shall filter Tenant and Project before semantic ranking.

23.530 Stage 1 Logging

Stage 1 shall prohibit full protected payload logging by default.

23.531 Stage 1 Retention

Stage 1 shall implement automatic expiry for:

- temporary prompts,

- Provider transfer copies,

- review proxies,

- local temporary files,

- and volatile operational Memory.

23.532 Stage 1 Deletion

Stage 1 deletion shall address canonical stores, indexes and caches.

Provider and backup deletion state shall remain visible.

23.533 Stage 1 Redaction

Stage 1 should support:

- structured-field redaction,

- text redaction,

- image-region redaction,

- and metadata removal.

23.534 Stage 1 Privacy Review

High-risk Stage 1 workflows shall require privacy review before activation.

23.535 Stage 1 Classification Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Classification Assignment has stable identity.

2. Data Object is explicit.

3. source is explicit.

4. classifier is explicit.

5. confidence is explicit.

6. effective time is explicit.

7. Public remains distinct from publicly available.

8. Project Internal remains Project-scoped.

9. Confidential receives stronger handling.

10. Local Only blocks external routing.

11. Prohibited blocks ordinary processing.

12. user may tighten classification.

13. Fabric cannot lower automatically.

14. conflicting assignments use restrictive handling.

15. historical Classification remains queryable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.536 Stage 1 Category Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Data Category has stable identity.

2. one Data Object may have several categories.

3. Credentials are detected.

4. private communication is detected.

5. child data is detected.

6. health data is detected.

7. financial data is detected.

8. exact location is detected.

9. private image context is preserved.

10. metadata categories are represented.

11. derived data inherits categories.

12. inference remains labelled.

13. confidence is preserved.

14. category change is attributable.

15. historical categories remain queryable.

23.537 Stage 1 Handling-Profile Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Handling Profile has stable identity and Version.

2. Classification is explicit.

3. allowed Providers are explicit.

4. approved Zones are explicit.

5. encryption is explicit.

6. logging policy is explicit.

7. retention is explicit.

8. Memory eligibility is explicit.

9. transfer rules are explicit.

10. Public profile does not remove rights checks.

11. Confidential profile limits logging.

12. Local Only profile blocks external egress.

13. Prohibited profile blocks processing.

14. policy change triggers revalidation.

15. historical Profiles remain queryable.

23.538 Stage 1 Purpose Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Purpose Definition has stable identity and Version.

2. owner is explicit.

3. statement is explicit.

4. Project is explicit.

5. eligible categories are explicit.

6. permitted operations are explicit.

7. recipients are explicit.

8. retention is explicit.

9. secondary use requires compatibility review.

10. Capability does not replace purpose.

11. consent does not replace purpose.

12. purpose change creates new Version.

13. expired purpose blocks new processing.

14. Processing Activity references purpose.

15. historical Purpose Definitions remain queryable.

23.539 Stage 1 Processing-Activity Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Processing Activity has stable identity.

2. Principal is explicit.

3. Agent is explicit.

4. Tenant and Project are explicit.

5. Data Objects are explicit.

6. categories are explicit.

7. classifications are explicit.

8. operation is explicit.

9. Provider or Tool is explicit.

text:
23.559 Applied Example — Omnira Platform Architecture Book

The Omnira Intelligence Fabric manuscript is Project Internal during drafting.

After formal approval, selected canonical versions may become:

- Project Internal,

- Tenant-wide,

- or Public

through explicit publication and rights Decisions.

Draft notes, internal review comments and implementation secrets remain non-public.

A public final PDF does not automatically make all underlying source files Public.

23.560 Applied Example — Familje-Stunden Child Photo

A parent submits a child’s photo for one personalised activity.

The photo is classified:

Confidential

or:

Local Only

according to the selected workflow.

The Purpose Definition permits:

- one personalised Deliverable,

- private delivery,

- no public publication,

- no cross-Project reuse,

- no training,

- and deletion after the configured period.

The image is excluded from ordinary character-reference libraries and Platform Learning.

23.561 Applied Example — Familje-Stunden Nova and Pling Assets

Canonical Nova and Pling reference illustrations are Project Internal or Confidential depending on release status.

Approved public promotional images may be Public.

Private working references, source Layers and rejected Candidates remain Project-scoped.

A public Nova image does not authorise GainPilot or another Tenant to reuse the Character.

23.562 Applied Example — Child-Facing Story Review

A Reviewer receives only:

- the current story pages,

- necessary character references,

- and review rubric.

The Reviewer does not receive:

- subscriber data,

- family photos,

- payment information,

- or unrelated Project Memory.

23.563 Applied Example — The Prompt Research Workflow

Public news articles may be retrieved for research.

The resulting internal Script and source analysis remain Project Internal until approved.

Private source correspondence remains Confidential.

Generated visual media remains classified according to publication state and source Inputs.

23.564 Applied Example — The Prompt Screenshot

A screenshot of a source page may contain:

- personal notifications,

- browser tabs,

- account name,

- cookies,

- or unrelated private content.

A Redaction Specification removes those regions before external analysis or publication.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.565 Applied Example — GainPilot Training Data

Workout history, body weight, injuries and health constraints are classified Confidential.

They may be processed by Arnold inside GainPilot.

They shall not be retrieved by:

- Familje-Stunden,

- The Prompt,

- or general Platform Agents

without explicit authority.

23.566 Applied Example — GainPilot Local Analysis

The user chooses Local Only handling for detailed health and training analysis.

The Planner selects:

- approved local Model,

- local data store,

- local embeddings,

- and local evidence.

External fallback is blocked.

A high-quality external Model may be suggested only as a policy-change option.

23.567 Applied Example — User Preference Memory

A formatting preference for canonical book chapters is stored as Project or workflow Memory.

It is not sensitive personal data.

It remains scoped to the relevant production workflow and does not justify retrieving private personal history.

23.568 Applied Example — Private Messages

A user opens a bounded workflow to inspect one Project-related conversation.

The system receives:

- explicit account,

- conversation,

- time range,

- purpose,

- and permitted actions.

Unrelated private messages remain inaccessible.

The content is not admitted to permanent Memory automatically.

23.569 Applied Example — Notification Content

Mobile notification metadata may indicate that a Project service has responded.

The system may process:

- application,

- time,

- and generic event type

without reading private message body when the purpose does not require it.

23.570 Applied Example — Mobile Screenshot

A screenshot is requested for troubleshooting.

Before external analysis, the workflow:

1. identifies the active application.

2. detects private-message or banking regions.

3. redacts protected content.

4. preserves a Local Only original.

5. sends only the redacted derivative.

6. records the Transfer Decision.

The Provider never receives the unredacted image.

23.571 Applied Example — Exact Location

A pharmacy reminder requires only a geofence.

The system stores:

- approved place,

- coarse trigger radius,

- and task

rather than continuous detailed location history.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.572 Applied Example — Provider Routing

A Confidential Project document requires summarisation.

The Router evaluates:

- approved local Model,

- enterprise Provider Account with no training,

- ordinary consumer Provider,

- and manual local review.

The consumer Account is ineligible.

The local or approved enterprise path may proceed.

23.573 Applied Example — Shared Provider Account

Two Projects use one Provider Account.

The Adapter creates:

- separate external workspaces,

- Project-specific files,

- Project tags,

- and deletion schedules.

If the Provider cannot enforce adequate separation, the Account becomes ineligible for Confidential use.

23.574 Applied Example — Local Only Memory

A Local Only Memory Domain contains private device-recovery instructions.

The index, canonical store and Context Builder all run on approved local Nodes.

The Memory is never synchronised to ordinary cloud search.

23.575 Applied Example — Cross-Project Search Attempt

A GainPilot search query is semantically similar to a Familje-Stunden document.

Project filtering excludes the Familje-Stunden source before similarity ranking.

The model never receives the protected snippet.

23.576 Applied Example — Cache Leakage Prevention

Two Tenants submit identical prompt text.

The cache key still includes:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Provider Account,

- Classification,

- and policy Version.

One Tenant cannot receive another Tenant’s cached Output or learn that it exists.

23.577 Applied Example — Repository Tool

A code Agent is authorised for one Omnira repository path.

The Sandbox denies access to:

- personal folders,

- GainPilot repository,

- Familje-Stunden Assets,

- browser profiles,

- and Secret Stores

unless separately granted.

23.578 Applied Example — Development Environment

A developer needs realistic data for testing.

The system creates a synthetic dataset matching:

- schema,

- approximate distribution,

- and edge cases.

Production customer or family data is not copied into development.

23.579 Applied Example — Provider Temporary Storage

A Provider stores uploaded images for thirty days.

The Confidential workflow requires deletion within twenty-four hours.

The Provider path becomes ineligible unless:

- immediate deletion is supported,

- evidence is captured,

- and remaining backup retention is acceptable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.580 Applied Example — Generated Summary

A Confidential contract is summarised.

The summary remains Confidential because it preserves:

- parties,

- obligations,

- price,

- and dates.

Shorter length does not lower classification.

23.581 Applied Example — Anonymised Analytics

GainPilot wants aggregate workout adherence statistics.

The analytics pipeline:

- removes direct identifiers,

- groups by broad categories,

- suppresses small groups,

- assesses re-identification,

- and prohibits individual-level retrieval.

Only after review may the aggregate receive a lower classification.

23.582 Applied Example — Pseudonymised User Record

A research dataset replaces user identity with a pseudonym.

The mapping remains in a separate encrypted store.

The dataset remains Confidential because authorised re-linkage is possible.

23.583 Applied Example — Deleted Memory

The user deletes a personal preference.

The deletion propagates to:

- canonical Memory,

- search index,

- vector index,

- cache,

- offline snapshots,

- and future context.

Backup copies remain inaccessible until expiry.

Restore does not reactivate the item.

23.584 Applied Example — Consent Revocation

A Voice subject revokes consent.

The Consent Control Plane updates eligibility.

Privacy and isolation controls:

- block future Voice processing,

- remove Voice references from active Provider libraries,

- restrict affected Assets,

- and prevent Memory retrieval for new production.

23.585 Applied Example — Child Data Incident

A child photo appears in an ordinary debug log.

The Incident response:

1. restricts log access.

2. stops the affected logging path.

3. deletes or redacts the payload.

4. identifies every viewer and copy.

5. reviews Provider and backup exposure.

6. updates logging controls.

7. verifies remediation.

23.586 Applied Example — Wrong-Tenant Query

A malformed service request carries an incorrect Tenant field.

The trusted Session context and database policy conflict with the request field.

The operation fails closed.

The request does not return another Tenant’s data.

23.587 Applied Example — Backup Restore

A backup contains a Memory Item deleted after the backup date.

During restore, the current deletion ledger is reapplied.

The bytes are not returned to active indexes or Agent retrieval.

text:
23.588 Applied Example — Public Website Content

A webpage is publicly accessible but contains personal contact information.

The research workflow may quote necessary public facts.

It shall not collect or retain unrelated personal details merely because they are visible.

23.589 Applied Example — Open-Source Repository

A public open-source repository is classified Public for ordinary code analysis.

Private fork changes, Tokens, local configuration and unpublished branches remain Project Internal or Confidential.

23.590 Applied Example — Investor Materials

An investor deck may be Confidential before a controlled meeting.

A specific exported version may receive a Usage Grant for named recipients.

The underlying financial model and internal notes remain more restricted.

23.591 Applied Example — Human Reviewer

A human Reviewer sees a watermarked proxy rather than the editable master.

The access expires after review.

Download is blocked where unnecessary.

The Reviewer’s annotations remain Project Internal evidence.

23.592 Applied Example — Platform Learning

Omnira considers learning that one Provider has high failure rates.

Platform Learning may use:

- aggregated,

- minimised,

- Tenant-separated,

- and non-content Metrics.

Raw Tenant prompts and Outputs are not centralised for this purpose.

Availability does not determine Omnira Classification.

Consent and handling remain separate.

23.595 Anti-Pattern — Classification Equals Rights

Confidential data may be processed through approved controls.

23.599 Anti-Pattern — Prohibited Means Ordinary High Sensitivity

Prohibited indicates disallowed processing, not merely stronger encryption.

23.600 Anti-Pattern — User May Lower Any Classification Informally

Lowering requires authority, evidence and policy.

23.645 Anti-Pattern — User Ownership Authorises Third-Party Data Processing

Other subjects retain privacy interests.

23.646 Anti-Pattern — Public URL Allows Bulk Collection

Purpose, minimisation and rights remain.

23.647 Anti-Pattern — Declassification Without Transformation Evidence

Lowering protection requires verified risk reduction.

23.648 Anti-Pattern — Isolation Tested Only Once

Schema, cache and deployment changes may regress controls.

23.649 Anti-Pattern — Cross-Tenant Incident Treated as Ordinary Bug

Isolation breaches require severe Incident handling.

23.650 Anti-Pattern — Privacy Review Performed After Launch

High-risk processing shall be reviewed before activation.

23.651 Anti-Pattern — Privacy Failure Authorises Manual Workaround

Manual work remains governed by the same boundaries.

23.652 Anti-Pattern — Classification Failure Bypasses the Fabric

Unknown or disputed data shall fail safely.

23.653 Future Classification, Privacy and Isolation Architecture

Future versions may support:

- attribute-based access control,

- policy-as-code,

- cryptographic Tenant separation,

- confidential computing,

- privacy-preserving retrieval,

- selective disclosure,

- differential privacy,

- federated analytics,

- verifiable deletion,

- encrypted search,

- secure enclaves,

- data lineage automation,

- and user-controlled privacy dashboards.

Future evolution must preserve:

- purpose,

- classification,

- scope,

- minimisation,

- isolation,

- challenge,

- and human authority.

23.654 Attribute-Based Access Control

Future access may evaluate:

- Principal,

- role,

- Project,

- Capability,

- device,

- classification,

- purpose,

- location,

- time,

- and risk.

23.655 Policy-as-Code

Privacy and isolation rules may be compiled into enforceable service policies.

Human-readable policy shall remain authoritative and reviewable.

23.656 Cryptographic Tenant Separation

Tenant-specific keys may reduce the impact of storage or administrative compromise.

23.657 Confidential Computing

Protected processing may occur inside hardware-backed environments.

Attestation and threat-model limits shall remain explicit.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.658 Encrypted Retrieval

Search over encrypted or protected data may reduce infrastructure exposure.

Performance and leakage limitations shall remain visible.

23.659 Private Information Retrieval

Future methods may reduce disclosure of the user’s query to storage or Provider systems.

23.660 Differential Privacy

Aggregate statistics may use calibrated noise to reduce subject exposure.

Accuracy and privacy parameters shall remain explicit.

23.661 Federated Analytics

Analytics may occur locally with only approved aggregate results shared centrally.

23.662 Federated Learning

Model or routing learning may use local updates without centralising raw data.

Poisoning, rights and re-identification remain governed.

23.663 Selective Disclosure

The system may prove a required attribute without revealing complete source data.

23.664 Privacy-Preserving Identity Verification

A user may prove age, authority or membership without exposing unnecessary identity details.

23.665 Verifiable Deletion

Future storage systems may produce stronger evidence that data has been deleted or cryptographically erased.

23.666 Dynamic Classification

Classification may update automatically as:

- context,

- combinations,

- recipients,

- or threats

change.

Automatic lowering remains restricted.

23.667 Contextual Integrity

Privacy policy may evaluate whether a data flow is appropriate to the relationship and purpose, not only whether access exists.

23.668 Privacy Digital Twin

A future privacy model may visualise:

- Data Objects,

- subjects,

- flows,

- Providers,

- regions,

- retention,

- and risks.

23.669 Automated Flow Discovery

The system may infer Data Flows from execution evidence.

Discovered flows shall require validation.

23.670 Data-Lineage Enforcement

Lineage may automatically propagate classification and deletion requirements.

23.671 Privacy Budget

Statistical or aggregate processing may use bounded privacy budgets.

The budget method and limitations shall remain explicit.

23.672 Re-Identification Monitoring

Anonymised datasets may be periodically reassessed against new external data and techniques.

23.673 User Privacy Dashboard

Users may inspect:

- active data categories,

- Projects,

- Providers,

- Memory,

- retention,

- permissions,

- and deletion state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.674 Tenant Privacy Dashboard

Tenant administrators may inspect policy and metadata without unrestricted content access.

23.675 Consent and Privacy Integration

Consent changes may update processing eligibility and retention automatically.

23.676 Rights and Privacy Integration

Rights to use an Asset shall not override subject privacy constraints.

23.677 Privacy-Aware Routing

Routing may prefer resources with stronger:

- retention,

- region,

- isolation,

- and account controls.

23.678 Privacy-Aware Planning

The Planner may insert:

- local preprocessing,

- redaction,

- aggregation,

- or human review

before external execution.

23.679 Privacy-Aware Memory

Memory admission may automatically reject data lacking suitable retention purpose.

23.680 Privacy-Aware Observability

Metrics and traces may adapt collection to Classification and Incident mode.

23.681 Classification Success Criteria

The classification architecture succeeds when:

- every material Data Object has a protection state,

- categories and Classification remain distinct,

- inheritance is reliable,

- users may tighten protection,

- lowering requires authority,

- and Routing enforces the result.

23.682 Privacy Success Criteria

The privacy architecture succeeds when:

- processing has explicit purpose,

- collection and context are minimised,

- personal and child data receive stronger controls,

- Provider disclosures remain visible,

- retention and deletion propagate,

- and users can understand and correct important data use.

23.683 Isolation Success Criteria

The isolation architecture succeeds when:

- Tenant and Project scope are structural,

- Agents retrieve only eligible data,

- Credentials remain separated,

- caches and indexes cannot leak,

- Provider Accounts preserve scope,

- and isolation regressions are detected before harm.

23.684 Classification Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- data lacks Classification,

- public availability becomes Public automatically,

- derived data loses source protection,

- Local Only falls back externally,

- or the Fabric lowers protection without authority.

23.685 Privacy Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- processing lacks purpose,

- excessive context is sent to Models,

- private communications are collected by default,

- sensitive inferences become permanent facts,

- retention is indefinite,

- or deletion does not propagate.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.686 Isolation Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- Tenant context is optional,

- Project filtering occurs after retrieval,

- caches omit scope,

- vector indexes leak,

- Provider libraries mix Projects,

- or administrative convenience grants unrestricted access.

23.687 Canonical Data Classification Contract

The following requirements define canonical Classification:

1. Every material Data Object SHALL have a Classification.

2. The canonical levels SHALL be Public, Project Internal, Confidential, Local Only and Prohibited.

3. Classification SHALL remain distinct from Data Category.

4. Classification SHALL remain distinct from rights and consent.

5. Classification source SHALL be explicit.

6. Automatic classification method and confidence SHALL be explicit.

7. Unknown Classification SHALL fail to restrictive handling.

8. Users MAY tighten Classification within their authority.

9. The Fabric SHALL NOT lower Classification automatically.

10. Lowering SHALL require authority, evidence and Decision.

11. Conflicting assignments SHALL use the most restrictive effective handling.

12. Derived data SHALL inherit source protection.

13. Aggregation SHALL receive independent sensitivity review.

14. Embeddings and indexes SHALL inherit protection.

15. Historical Classification SHALL remain linked to past processing.

16. Classification changes SHALL propagate.

17. Expired or superseded assignments SHALL remain queryable.

18. Classification SHALL influence Routing and Placement.

19. Classification SHALL NOT create processing authority.

20. No Classification failure SHALL authorise uncontrolled use.

23.688 Canonical Public Classification Contract

The following requirements define Public data:

1. Public SHALL require approved public eligibility.

2. Publicly available SHALL NOT become Public automatically.

3. Public data MAY still have rights and attribution requirements.

4. Public data MAY still contain personal information requiring minimisation.

5. Public classification SHALL identify intended scope.

6. Public source retrieval SHALL preserve provenance.

7. Public data MAY use approved external Providers.

8. Public data SHALL remain subject to purpose.

9. Public Assets SHALL reference exact approved Versions.

10. Draft or source material SHALL NOT inherit Public status automatically.

11. Public release SHALL be attributable.

12. Revoked public status SHALL affect future use.

13. Historical publication evidence SHALL remain.

14. Public classification SHALL NOT authorise training automatically.

15. Public classification SHALL NOT authorise cross-Tenant reuse automatically.

16. Public classification SHALL NOT remove Provider terms.

17. Public classification SHALL NOT remove consent requirements.

18. Public classification SHALL remain reviewable.

19. Historical Public Decisions SHALL remain queryable.

20. Public SHALL describe disclosure eligibility, not absence of governance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.689 Canonical Project Internal Contract

The following requirements define Project Internal data:

1. Project identity SHALL be explicit.

2. Access SHALL remain inside authorised Project scope.

3. Public disclosure SHALL require a new Decision.

4. Cross-Project reuse SHALL require explicit authority.

5. Project Internal data MAY use approved Providers.

6. Provider Account and workspace SHALL preserve Project attribution.

7. Storage SHALL preserve Project scope.

8. Cache SHALL preserve Project scope.

9. Search SHALL filter Project before ranking.

10. Memory SHALL remain Project-scoped.

11. Logs SHALL minimise payload content.

12. Exports SHALL remain Project-bound.

13. Retention SHALL follow Project purpose.

14. Project closure SHALL trigger retention review.

15. Derived data SHALL remain Project Internal unless reclassified.

16. Accepted public derivatives SHALL NOT expose protected sources.

17. Project Internal SHALL remain distinct from Confidential.

18. Historical access SHALL remain auditable.

19. Project policy SHALL be Versioned.

20. Project ownership SHALL NOT create cross-Project permission.

23.690 Canonical Confidential Contract

The following requirements define Confidential data:

1. Confidential data SHALL receive stronger access controls.

2. Purpose SHALL be explicit.

3. Recipient SHALL be explicit.

4. Provider eligibility SHALL be explicit.

5. Account plan and retention SHALL be evaluated.

6. Encryption at rest and in transit SHALL be required where applicable.

7. Ordinary payload logging SHALL be prohibited.

8. Temporary copies SHALL have short retention.

9. Memory admission SHALL require review or policy.

10. Search and embeddings SHALL preserve Confidential scope.

11. Human review SHALL be limited to authorised reviewers.

12. Data transfer SHALL require a governed Decision.

13. Backup SHALL preserve encryption and scope.

14. Deletion SHALL address all known copies.

15. Confidential data SHALL NOT become Platform Learning automatically.

16. Derived summaries SHALL remain Confidential unless approved otherwise.

17. Access SHALL be auditable.

18. Incidents SHALL receive elevated response.

19. Historical Decisions SHALL remain queryable.

20. Confidential handling SHALL remain compatible with user and Project authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.691 Canonical Local Only Contract

The following requirements define Local Only data:

1. Local Only SHALL identify approved Execution Zones.

2. Local Only SHALL identify approved storage.

3. Ordinary external managed Providers SHALL be ineligible.

4. External fallback SHALL fail closed.

5. Local Models and Tools SHALL still be registered and governed.

6. Node trust SHALL be sufficient.

7. Local logs and caches SHALL preserve classification.

8. Local backups SHALL remain inside approved boundaries.

9. Offline snapshots SHALL be encrypted.

10. Synchronisation SHALL be explicitly allowed or denied.

11. Local Only Memory SHALL remain in approved stores and indexes.

12. Provider suggestions MAY be presented only as policy-change options.

13. Temporary external transfer SHALL require explicit reclassification or exception.

14. Local Only SHALL NOT mean one fixed device unless policy states it.

15. Local Only SHALL NOT remove quality requirements.

16. Local Only SHALL NOT remove authority requirements.

17. Local Only SHALL NOT remove rights or consent requirements.

18. Node loss or failure SHALL NOT authorise egress.

19. Historical placement evidence SHALL remain queryable.

20. Local Only SHALL remain a mandatory placement boundary.

23.692 Canonical Prohibited Data Contract

The following requirements define Prohibited data and processing:

1. Prohibited state SHALL be explicit.

2. Prohibition basis SHALL be explicit.

3. Ordinary collection SHALL be blocked.

4. Ordinary storage SHALL be blocked.

5. Model context SHALL exclude prohibited data.

6. Memory SHALL exclude prohibited data.

7. Training and analytics SHALL exclude prohibited data.

8. Transfer and disclosure SHALL be blocked.

9. Quarantine MAY be used for Incident handling.

10. Quarantine access SHALL be narrowly authorised.

11. Deletion or reporting procedure SHALL be explicit.

12. Prohibited state SHALL outrank cost and convenience.

13. User request SHALL NOT override non-waivable prohibition.

14. Automatic classifiers MAY trigger provisional prohibition.

15. Human review MAY resolve false positives.

16. Prohibition changes SHALL be attributable.

17. Historical Incident evidence MAY remain.

18. Prohibited data SHALL NOT enter general logs.

19. Prohibited data SHALL NOT become Agent context.

20. No failure SHALL convert Prohibited data into permitted processing.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.693 Canonical Purpose and Minimisation Contract

The following requirements define purpose and minimisation:

1. Every material Processing Activity SHALL reference a Purpose Definition.

2. Purpose SHALL identify owner and scope.

3. Eligible data categories SHALL be explicit.

4. Permitted operations SHALL be explicit.

5. Recipients SHALL be explicit.

6. Retention SHALL be explicit.

7. Secondary use SHALL require compatibility or new authority.

8. Only necessary fields SHALL be processed.

9. Only necessary records SHALL be processed.

10. Only necessary precision SHALL be processed.

11. Only necessary recipients SHALL receive data.

12. Only necessary copies SHALL be retained.

13. Model context SHALL be minimised.

14. Memory retrieval SHALL be minimised.

15. Provider uploads SHALL be minimised.

16. Logs and traces SHALL be minimised.

17. Minimisation Decisions SHALL be attributable.

18. Failure to minimise MAY block processing.

19. Historical Purpose Versions SHALL remain queryable.

20. Capability availability SHALL NOT replace purpose.

23.694 Canonical Tenant Isolation Contract

The following requirements define Tenant isolation:

1. Every Tenant SHALL have stable identity.

2. Tenant context SHALL derive from trusted identity.

3. Tenant context SHALL propagate through every canonical object.

4. Missing or conflicting Tenant context SHALL fail closed.

5. Database access SHALL enforce Tenant scope structurally.

6. Object storage SHALL enforce Tenant scope.

7. Queue messages SHALL enforce Tenant scope.

8. Cache keys SHALL include Tenant scope.

9. Search SHALL filter Tenant before ranking.

10. Memory SHALL filter Tenant before retrieval.

11. Credentials SHALL remain Tenant-scoped.

12. Provider Accounts SHALL preserve Tenant attribution.

13. Logs SHALL not expose another Tenant’s content.

14. Backups SHALL preserve Tenant boundaries.

15. Restore SHALL preserve Tenant boundaries.

16. Cross-Tenant access SHALL be denied by default.

17. Cross-Tenant aggregation SHALL require separate approved architecture.

18. Isolation tests SHALL run continuously or after material change.

19. Cross-Tenant leakage SHALL be a severe Incident.

20. Tenant administration SHALL NOT grant unrestricted content access automatically.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric

text:
23.695 Canonical Project Isolation Contract

The following requirements define Project isolation:

1. Every Project SHALL have stable identity.

2. Project context SHALL derive from trusted Request state.

3. Project context SHALL propagate through Plans, Attempts, Assets, Evidence and Memory.

4. Missing or ambiguous Project context SHALL fail closed.

5. Storage SHALL preserve Project scope.

6. Database access SHALL preserve Project scope.

7. Cache SHALL preserve Project scope.

8. Search SHALL filter Project before ranking.

9. Memory SHALL filter Project before retrieval.

10. Credentials SHALL remain Project-scoped unless explicitly shared.

11. Provider workspaces SHALL preserve Project attribution.

12. Reference Assets SHALL remain Project-scoped.

13. Agent access SHALL remain Project-scoped.

14. Cross-Project read SHALL require authority.

15. Cross-Project mutation SHALL be prohibited by default.

16. Cross-Project Learning SHALL be prohibited by default.

17. Export SHALL preserve Project boundaries.

18. Isolation tests SHALL cover every shared subsystem.

19. Cross-Project leakage SHALL trigger Incident response.

20. Common ownership SHALL NOT dissolve Project isolation.

23.696 Canonical Agent and Workflow Isolation Contract

The following requirements define Agent and workflow isolation:

1. Every Agent SHALL have stable identity.

2. Agent role and Project scope SHALL be explicit.

3. Readable Memory Domains SHALL be explicit.

4. Writable Memory proposal classes SHALL be explicit.

5. Tool access SHALL be explicit.

6. Data categories SHALL be explicit.

7. Agent context SHALL be minimised.

8. Agent-to-Agent disclosure SHALL be recorded.

9. Delegation SHALL NOT broaden authority.

10. Model changes SHALL NOT broaden Agent access.

11. Provider session history SHALL NOT become shared Agent Memory.

12. Every workflow instance SHALL have stable identity.

13. Workflow Inputs and state SHALL remain isolated.

14. Retry SHALL preserve the same scope.

15. Workflow cache SHALL preserve Tenant and Project.

16. Outputs SHALL remain linked to the originating workflow and Project.

17. Agent and workflow denial SHALL be auditable.

18. Cross-Agent leakage SHALL trigger review.

19. Historical access SHALL remain queryable.

20. Agent or workflow convenience SHALL NOT override privacy boundaries.

sectionTitles: 23.697 Canonical Storage, Cache and Search Isolation Contract
text:
23.697 Canonical Storage, Cache and Search Isolation Contract

The following requirements define data-store isolation:

1. Every persistent store SHALL identify Tenant and Project scope.

2. Access SHALL be enforced structurally.

3. Encryption state SHALL be explicit.

4. Public access SHALL require explicit authority.

5. Cache entries SHALL inherit classification.

6. Cache keys SHALL include relevant scope and policy.

7. Deletion and revocation SHALL invalidate caches.

8. Search SHALL enforce eligibility before ranking.

9. Vector indexes SHALL preserve source identity and scope.

10. Embeddings SHALL inherit protection.

11. Snippets SHALL reveal only authorised ranges.

12. Metadata SHALL not expose protected existence.

13. Index rebuild SHALL preserve lifecycle and access.

14. Deleted data SHALL leave active indexes.

15. Backups SHALL preserve scope and encryption.

16. Restore SHALL reapply current deletion and revocation.

17. Shared infrastructure SHALL receive isolation tests.

18. Isolation regressions SHALL block release.

19. Historical access evidence SHALL remain queryable.

20. Storage availability SHALL NOT create access authority.

23.698 Canonical Provider Privacy Contract

The following requirements define Provider privacy governance:

1. Every Provider Product SHALL declare eligible Classification.

2. Every Provider Account SHALL identify owner and scope.

3. Account plan and Terms Snapshot SHALL be explicit.

4. Retention settings SHALL be explicit.

5. Training-use settings SHALL be explicit.

6. Region and custody SHALL be explicit where material.

7. Shared Account risk SHALL be represented.

8. Provider file and session storage SHALL be governed.

9. Only minimised Inputs SHALL be sent.

10. Provider upload SHALL require an eligible Purpose.

11. Local Only data SHALL be denied.

12. Confidential data SHALL require approved Product and Account.

13. Temporary Provider copies SHALL have deletion policy.

14. Output SHALL inherit source protection.

15. Provider callbacks and logs SHALL remain scoped.

16. Account termination SHALL address retained data.

17. Provider changes SHALL trigger revalidation.

18. Missing privacy evidence SHALL reduce eligibility.

19. Historical Transfers SHALL remain queryable.

20. Provider capability SHALL NOT create permission to process.

23.700 Canonical Redaction, Pseudonymisation and Anonymisation Contract
text:
23.699 Canonical Data Flow and Transfer Contract

The following requirements define Data Flows and transfers:

1. Every material Data Flow SHALL have stable identity.

2. Source SHALL be explicit.

3. Destination SHALL be explicit.

4. Data Objects SHALL be explicit.

5. Classification and categories SHALL be explicit.

6. Purpose SHALL be explicit.

7. Recipient SHALL be explicit.

8. Region SHALL be explicit where material.

9. Retention SHALL be explicit.

10. Minimisation SHALL be applied.

11. Encryption SHALL be applied where required.

12. Rights and consent SHALL be evaluated.

13. Transfer Decision SHALL precede disclosure.

14. Denied transfer SHALL send no payload.

15. Integrity SHALL be verified where material.

16. Disclosure SHALL be recorded.

17. Temporary access SHALL expire.

18. Historical Decisions SHALL remain immutable.

19. Cross-Tenant transfer SHALL be prohibited by default.

20. Data movement SHALL NOT occur merely because systems are connected.

23.700 Canonical Redaction, Pseudonymisation and Anonymisation Contract

The following requirements define privacy-preserving transformation:

1. Every material transformation SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Source Asset or Data Object SHALL be explicit.

3. Purpose SHALL be explicit.

4. Target fields, regions or identifiers SHALL be explicit.

5. Method SHALL be explicit.

6. Reversibility SHALL be explicit.

7. Mapping custody SHALL be explicit for pseudonymisation.

8. Threat model SHALL be explicit for anonymisation.

9. Validation SHALL be required.

10. Failed validation SHALL block reduced handling.

11. Pseudonymised data SHALL remain protected.

12. Name removal SHALL NOT be treated as anonymity.

13. Images, Voice, free text and metadata SHALL be assessed.

14. Re-identification risk SHALL be reviewed.

15. Small-group risk SHALL be assessed.

16. Reduced Classification SHALL require a Decision.

17. Source lineage SHALL remain preserved.

18. Historical transformations SHALL remain queryable.

19. Future revalidation SHALL be possible.

20. Privacy transformation SHALL NOT fabricate anonymity.

23.701 Canonical Retention and Deletion Contract

The following requirements define retention and deletion:

1. Every Retention Policy SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Purpose SHALL determine retention.

3. Minimum and maximum periods SHALL be explicit.

4. Provider and backup retention SHALL be represented.

5. Temporary files and caches SHALL expire.

6. Holds SHALL suspend deletion without broadening use.

7. Every material Deletion Record SHALL have stable identity.

8. Target and authority SHALL be explicit.

9. Canonical stores SHALL be addressed.

10. Replicas SHALL be addressed.

11. Caches SHALL be addressed.

12. Indexes SHALL be addressed.

13. Memory SHALL be addressed.

14. Provider copies SHALL be addressed.

15. Backups SHALL be assessed.

16. Incomplete deletion SHALL remain explicit.

17. Restore SHALL reapply current lifecycle state.

18. Deleted data SHALL NOT return to ordinary retrieval.

19. Historical deletion evidence SHALL remain queryable.

20. Deletion SHALL NOT erase accountability.

23.702 Canonical Logging and Observability Privacy Contract

The following requirements define privacy-safe observability:

1. Full protected payload logging SHALL be prohibited by default.

2. Credential values SHALL never enter ordinary logs.

3. Private communication content SHALL be excluded by default.

4. Logs SHALL preserve Tenant and Project correlation.

5. Logs SHALL inherit classification.

6. Trace attributes SHALL be minimised.

13. Log retention SHALL be explicit.

14. Deletion and revocation SHALL propagate where required.

16. Administrators SHALL receive metadata-only views where practical.

17. Debug mode SHALL NOT disable privacy controls.

18. Logging incidents SHALL trigger containment.

19. Historical access SHALL remain auditable.

The following requirements define Privacy Review:

2. Processing Activity SHALL be explicit.

3. Purpose SHALL be explicit.

4. Data Subjects SHALL be explicit.

5. Data categories SHALL be explicit.

6. Classifications SHALL be explicit.

7. Data Flows SHALL be explicit.

8. Providers and recipients SHALL be explicit.

9. Storage and processing regions SHALL be explicit where material.

10. Retention SHALL be explicit.

11. Rights and consent SHALL be considered.

13. Minimisation SHALL be evaluated.

14. Residual risk SHALL be explicit.

The following requirements define Incident handling:

23.705 Canonical Classification, Privacy and Isolation Governance Contract

The following requirements define overall governance:

1. Classification, privacy, consent, rights and authority SHALL remain distinct.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 23.706 Data Classification, Privacy and Isolation Invariants
text:
23.706 Data Classification, Privacy and Isolation Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No publicly available data becomes Public automatically.

- No Classification becomes consent, rights or authority.

- No user may weaken non-waivable protection informally.

- No automatic system lowers Classification without evidence and authority.

- No derivative, summary, embedding or index loses source protection automatically.

- No Local Only data routes to an ordinary external Provider.

- No Prohibited data enters ordinary Model context or Memory.

- No Tenant or Project context is optional.

- No similarity search occurs before access eligibility.

- No cache, queue, log, index or backup exists outside isolation policy.

- No Agent receives raw Secrets.

- No private communication becomes general context automatically.

- No child data receives ordinary low-risk handling.

- No pseudonym becomes proof of anonymity.

- No redaction lowers protection without validation.

- No Provider Account becomes a universal Project workspace.

- No deletion ends at one database row.

- No backup restore reactivates deleted or revoked data.

- No administrator role grants unrestricted content access automatically.

- No privacy, classification or isolation failure bypasses the Intelligence Fabric.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
23.707 Closing Statement

Data classification, privacy and isolation determine where Omnira may think, what it may remember, which resources it may use and which boundaries it must never cross.

Classification defines the required protection.

Data Category defines the kind of information involved.

Purpose defines why processing is permitted.

The Handling Profile defines how the data must be protected.

The Access Scope defines who or what may act.

The Tenant Boundary separates organisations.

The Project Boundary separates operational worlds.

The Agent Boundary limits intelligence roles.

The Workflow Boundary limits one execution path.

The Environment Boundary separates development from production.

The Node Boundary limits local access.

The Provider Boundary defines external custody.

The Storage Boundary protects durable copies.

The Cache and Index Boundaries protect derived and accelerated access.

The Data Flow describes where information moves.

The Transfer Decision determines whether that movement is permitted.

The Retention Decision determines how long the data may remain.

The Redaction, Pseudonymisation and Anonymisation Records preserve privacy transformations without overstating their guarantees.

The Privacy Review evaluates high-risk processing before activation.

The Isolation Test proves that architectural boundaries work in practice.

The Privacy Incident preserves accountability when they fail.

For Familje-Stunden, this architecture ensures that:

- private family photos remain private,

- children’s information receives stronger protection,

- Nova and Pling Assets remain Project-scoped,

- child-facing review sees only necessary material,

- and public content does not expose private working sources.

For The Prompt, it ensures that:

- public research remains distinguishable from private source correspondence,

- screenshots are redacted,

- generated visuals remain correctly classified,

- and analytics do not become hidden personal profiling.

For GainPilot, it ensures that:

- health, fitness and body data remain Confidential or Local Only,

- Arnold retrieves only GainPilot-relevant Memory,

- programme history does not leak into unrelated Projects,

- and local processing preferences cannot be overridden silently.

For Atlas, it ensures that:

- broad orchestration authority does not become universal data access,

- Personal Memory remains purpose-limited,

- Project context remains isolated,

- Secrets remain inside Credential systems,

- and current user intent does not cause accidental disclosure of unrelated history.

For Omnira, it ensures that:

- users,

- Tenants,

- Projects,

- Agents,

- workflows,

- Providers,

- Nodes,

- Assets,

- Evidence,

- Memory,

- caches,

- indexes,

- logs,

- and backups

participate in one governed data architecture.

The data may be Public.

It may be Project Internal.

It may be Confidential.

It may be Local Only.

It may be Prohibited.

The Fabric must know which state applies before it routes, retrieves, stores, learns, transfers or acts.

No processing without purpose.

No purpose without scope.

No scope without identity.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
No disclosure without eligibility.

No retrieval before isolation.

No transfer before minimisation.

No external Provider for Local Only data.

No Model context containing raw Secrets.

No Project Memory in the wrong Project.

No child data without stronger protection.

No declassification without evidence.

No anonymisation claim without risk review.

No retention without expiry or justification.

No deletion without propagation.

No isolation guarantee without testing.

The user retains privacy authority.

The Project retains its protected context.

The Tenant retains its boundary.

Omnira retains policy and enforcement.

The Fabric may move intelligence across resources, but it shall never move protected data across a boundary merely because the technology allows it.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical architecture, object model, policy hierarchy, lifecycle, enforcement boundaries and conformance requirements for approval, authority and bounded autonomy within the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

It establishes:

- how human, Agent, Service and Device Principals receive authority,

- how authentication, identity, role, permission, authority, approval, consent and ownership remain distinct,

- how every consequential action is linked to an authorised Principal and exact scope,

- how Authority Grants remain bounded by Tenant, Project, Capability, resource, data category, Classification, action, cost, time and risk,

- how one-time approval differs from standing authority,

- how Plan approval differs from execution authorisation,

- how approval of a Budget does not approve unrelated spending,

- how approval of content does not approve publication,

- how approval of a Provider does not approve every Model, Account or data class,

- how approval of one Asset Version does not approve later revisions,

- how bounded job approval permits the Fabric to operate inside an exact envelope,

- how retries, fallbacks and replanning remain inside approved limits,

- how deviations trigger pause, denial or escalation,

- how new Providers, new Accounts, higher Budget, broader data disclosure, publication, deletion, overwrite and irreversible side effects require separate authority,

- how Authority Levels describe general operating posture without replacing explicit Grants,

- how human review, dual control, quorum, separation of duties and step-up authentication are applied,

- how delegated authority remains narrower than the delegator’s authority,

- how Agents may act autonomously only inside explicit Mandates,

- how standing Mandates remain revocable, expiring and observable,

- how approval requests present understandable scope, consequences, cost, data movement and alternatives,

- how Approval Decisions bind to exact object Versions and policy state,

- how stale approvals are invalidated,

- how approval replay and duplicate execution are prevented,

- how emergency and break-glass authority remain exceptional,

- how mobile approvals remain secure and limited,

- how revocation, suspension, expiry and Project closure propagate,

- how authority is preserved across Model and Provider changes without becoming broader,

- how approval evidence remains reconstructable,

- how denied actions remain denied despite technical capability,

- how Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy authority and approval foundation,

- and how later autonomy may increase only through evidence, policy and explicit human delegation.

Authentication is not authorisation.

Identity is not authority.

A role is not an unlimited permission set.

Access is not approval.

Approval is not consent.

Consent is not execution authority.

Ownership is not permission to ignore policy.

A successful login is not approval for a consequential action.

A Project role is not authority in another Project.

A Capability is not permission to use it.

A Provider Connection is not authority to disclose data to that Provider.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
A Budget is not approval to spend it on any purpose.

A Plan is not authorised merely because it is technically valid.

A human-readable “yes” without exact scope is not sufficient evidence for high-risk execution.

Approval of a draft does not approve the final Asset automatically.

Approval of an Asset does not approve publication automatically.

Approval of publication does not prove external publication completion.

A standing Mandate is not unlimited autonomy.

A high Authority Level is not a universal override.

An Agent shall never become its own source of authority.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

Observability, audit and Incident Response are expanded in Chapter 25.

Developer experience, testing and conformance are expanded in Chapter 26.

Implementation and operational conformance must be verified separately.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 24.2 Purpose of Approval, Authority and Bounded Autonomy
text:
24.2 Purpose of Approval, Authority and Bounded Autonomy

The Intelligence Fabric may perform actions such as:

- reading Project data,

- summarising information,

- generating content,

- calling paid Providers,

- changing files,

- committing code,

- sending messages,

- scheduling work,

- publishing media,

- modifying external Accounts,

- purchasing credits,

- changing system settings,

- deleting Assets,

- rotating Credentials,

- moving data,

- and coordinating other Agents.

Those actions differ in:

- consequence,

- reversibility,

- cost,

- privacy,

- legal effect,

- audience,

- external visibility,

- operational risk,

- and required human judgement.

Without canonical authority governance, Omnira could:

- execute a technically valid but unauthorised Plan,

- spend beyond the user’s intended Budget,

- retry a paid action after an unknown outcome,

- publish the wrong Asset Version,

- send Confidential data to an unapproved Provider,

- allow one Agent to approve its own work,

- reuse an old approval after the content changed,

- delete files because a broad role allowed write access,

- infer standing permission from repeated past approval,

- delegate more authority than the delegator possessed,

- or continue acting after authority was revoked.

The architecture exists to ensure that every consequential action can answer:

- Who is acting?

- Which identity was authenticated?

- Which Tenant and Project are in scope?

- Which action is proposed?

- Which exact objects and Versions are affected?

- Which Capability is required?

- Which authority permits the action?

- Which policy applies?

- Which risk class applies?

- Which data will be read or disclosed?

- Which external systems, Providers and Accounts are involved?

- What will it cost?

- Is the action reversible?

- Which approval or Mandate authorises it?

- When does that authority expire?

- Which deviations require escalation?

- How can the action be stopped or revoked?

- Which evidence proves that the resulting execution remained inside scope?

24.3 Principal

A Principal is a canonical identity capable of receiving, exercising, delegating, approving or being denied authority.

Principal types may include:

- Human Principal,

- Agent Principal,

- Service Principal,

- Device Principal,

- Provider Principal,

- External Organisation Principal,

- and composite approval group.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.4 Human Principal

A Human Principal represents an identified person.

A Human Principal may act as:

- user,

- Project owner,

- Reviewer,

- Approver,

- administrator,

- operator,

- contributor,

- or auditor.

24.5 Agent Principal

An Agent Principal represents an Omnira-owned Agent identity.

The Agent remains distinct from:

- Model,

- Provider,

- Runtime,

- Session,

- and human operator.

24.6 Service Principal

A Service Principal represents a non-human service component.

Examples include:

- Router,

- Planner,

- Scheduler,

- Adapter,

- publication Connector,

- or background worker.

24.7 Device Principal

A Device Principal represents a registered device or trusted execution Node.

Device identity may support:

- approval,

- step-up verification,

- local execution,

- or recovery.

24.8 Composite Principal

A Composite Principal represents a group whose authority requires several members.

Examples include:

- two-person approval,

- quorum,

- owner plus finance reviewer,

- or administrator plus Project owner.

24.9 Principal Identity

Every Principal shall have stable identity.

24.10 Principal State

Principal states may include:

- active,

- restricted,

- suspended,

- disabled,

- compromised,

- expired,

- and retired.

24.11 Principal State Enforcement

A suspended, disabled, compromised or expired Principal shall not exercise new authority.

24.12 Authentication

Authentication establishes that an actor controls or satisfies the required identity mechanism.

Authentication may use:

- password,

- passkey,

- hardware key,

- biometric unlock,

- signed service credential,

- device attestation,

- Session Token,

- or another approved method.

24.13 Authentication Is Not Authorisation

Authentication establishes identity confidence.

It does not determine which action is permitted.

24.14 Authentication Assurance

Authentication Assurance describes the strength of the authentication event.

Levels may include:

- low,

- standard,

- strong,

- phishing-resistant,

- device-bound,

- and hardware-backed.

24.15 Step-Up Authentication

Step-Up Authentication requires stronger assurance for a consequential action.

Examples include:

- Credential export,

- large spend,

- deletion,

- account recovery,

- Project ownership change,

- publication to a sensitive channel,

- or break-glass use.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.16 Authentication Freshness

High-risk actions may require recent authentication.

24.17 Session Authentication

A Session carries authenticated identity for a bounded period.

Session state shall include:

- Principal,

- authentication method,

- assurance,

- issued time,

- expiry,

- device,

- and risk signals.

24.18 Session Is Not Permanent Authority

Session validity shall not extend expired or revoked Authority Grants.

24.19 Authorisation

Authorisation determines whether a Principal may perform a defined action under current policy and context.

24.20 Authority

Authority is the governed power to decide, approve, direct or execute a defined action within an explicit scope.

24.21 Permission

A Permission is one specific allowed operation.

Examples include:

- read Asset,

- create draft,

- invoke Model,

- modify file,

- publish post,

- approve Budget,

- or revoke Grant.

24.22 Permission Is Not Complete Authority

A Permission may still require:

- purpose,

- approval,

- Budget,

- data eligibility,

- policy,

- or separation of duties.

24.23 Role

A Role is a named collection of expected responsibilities and candidate Permissions.

Examples include:

- Project Owner,

- Editor,

- Reviewer,

- Publisher,

- Finance Approver,

- Agent Operator,

- Security Administrator,

- and Auditor.

24.24 Role Assignment

A Role Assignment binds a Role to a Principal in a defined scope.

It shall include or reference:

- roleAssignmentId,

- Principal,

- Role,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- environment,

- start,

- expiry,

- conditions,

- and issuer.

24.25 Role Assignment Identity

Every Role Assignment shall have stable identity.

24.26 Role Is Not Universal Authority

Role Permissions remain constrained by:

- Project,

- environment,

- policy,

- risk,

- and exact action context.

24.27 Role Inheritance

Role inheritance shall be explicit and acyclic where possible.

24.28 Role Combination

Several Roles may combine.

Conflicting restrictions shall resolve to the more restrictive result unless policy defines otherwise.

24.29 Authority Domain

An Authority Domain is a canonical area in which Decisions or actions may be authorised.

Domains may include:

- Project operations,

- finance,

- publication,

- data access,

- privacy,

- rights,

- security,

- infrastructure,

- Credential management,

- Agent configuration,

- and incident response.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.30 Authority Domain Identity

Every Authority Domain shall have stable identity and Version.
