24.31 Authority Scope

Authority Scope defines exactly where a Grant applies.

Scope dimensions may include:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- environment,

- Capability,

- action type,

- resource type,

- Provider,

- Provider Account,

- Model,

- Tool,

- data category,

- Classification,

- Asset,

- folder,

- repository,

- publication channel,

- financial account,

- device,

- geography,

- audience,

- time,

- and frequency.

24.32 Scope Intersection

Effective authority is the intersection of all applicable scope restrictions.

24.33 Missing Scope

Missing or ambiguous scope shall fail closed for consequential actions.

24.34 Authority Grant

An Authority Grant gives a Principal permission to perform or approve defined actions under explicit conditions.

It shall include or reference:

- authorityGrantId,

- grantor,

- grantee,

- Authority Domain,

- Permissions,

- scope,

- limits,

- conditions,

- effective time,

- expiry,

- delegation rights,

- revocation,

- policy Versions,

- and provenance.

24.35 Authority Grant Identity

Every Authority Grant shall have stable identity and Version.

24.36 Grantor

The Grantor must possess authority to issue the Grant.

24.37 Grantee

The Grantee may be:

- Human Principal,

- Agent Principal,

- Service Principal,

- Device Principal,

- or Composite Principal.

24.38 Grant Basis

A Grant may derive from:

- ownership,

- administrator role,

- Project role,

- contract,

- policy,

- explicit user delegation,

- or emergency authority.

24.39 Grant Validity

A Grant is valid only when:

- issuer authority remains valid,

- effective time has begun,

- expiry has not passed,

- conditions are satisfied,

- Principal is active,

- and no revocation or suspension applies.

24.40 Grant Scope Narrowing

A narrower Grant may be derived from a broader Grant.

24.41 Grant Scope Expansion

Scope expansion requires a new authorised Grant.

It shall not occur through interpretation.

24.42 Negative Grant

A Negative Grant or explicit Denial blocks a defined action despite broader Roles or Permissions.

24.43 Denial Precedence

Explicit Denial shall outrank ordinary allow Grants unless a higher-authority exception is explicitly permitted.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.44 Grant Condition

Conditions may include:

- approval,

- Budget availability,

- specific device,

- strong authentication,

- defined time window,

- eligible Provider,

- required review,

- or successful Quality Gate.

24.45 Grant Limit

Limits may include:

- maximum cost,

- number of actions,

- duration,

- data volume,

- retry count,

- publication frequency,

- or affected objects.

24.46 Grant Expiry

Every standing Grant should have an expiry or review date.

24.47 Grant Suspension

Suspension temporarily prevents use without deleting the historical Grant.

24.48 Grant Revocation

Revocation terminates future use of the Grant.

24.49 Grant Supersession

A new Grant may supersede an earlier one while preserving history.

24.50 Grant Propagation

Revocation, expiry or restriction shall propagate to:

- active Sessions,

- approval tokens,

- queued work,

- Mandates,

- and delegated Grants.

24.51 Delegation

Delegation allows one Principal to grant a subset of its authority to another Principal.

24.52 Delegation Authority

A Principal may delegate only when the source Grant explicitly permits delegation.

24.53 Delegation Scope

Delegated scope shall be equal to or narrower than the source authority.

24.54 Delegation Depth

Maximum delegation depth shall be explicit.

24.55 Subdelegation

Subdelegation requires explicit permission.

24.56 Delegation Expiry

Delegated authority shall not outlive the source Grant.

24.57 Delegation Revocation

Revoking the source Grant shall revoke dependent delegated Grants unless policy defines a narrower transition.

24.58 Delegation Evidence

Delegation shall preserve:

- source Grant,

- grantor,

- grantee,

- scope,

- reason,

- time,

- expiry,

- and conditions.

24.59 Impersonation

Impersonation allows an authorised Principal to act through another identity context.

It shall be exceptional, visible and auditable.

24.60 Hidden Impersonation Prohibition

The acting Principal and represented Principal shall both remain visible.

24.61 Service Delegation

A human or Agent may delegate bounded execution to a Service Principal.

The service does not inherit unrelated authority.

24.62 Agent Delegation

An Agent may delegate to another Agent only within:

- its own Grant,

- approved Plan,

- Project,

- data scope,

- and allowed delegation depth.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 24.63 Agent Delegation Does Not Create Autonomy
text:
24.63 Agent Delegation Does Not Create Autonomy

Delegation remains subordinate to the approved Mandate and Plan.

24.64 Approval

Approval is an attributable Decision by an authorised Principal that permits a defined action, Plan, Version, Budget, scope or exception.

24.65 Approval Is Contextual

Approval shall bind to:

- exact subject,

- exact Version,

- exact scope,

- exact limits,

- and applicable policy state.

24.66 Approval Request

An Approval Request asks one or more authorised Principals to approve a defined matter.

It shall include or reference:

- approvalRequestId,

- requester,

- approver requirements,

- subject,

- subject Version,

- action,

- purpose,

- scope,

- consequences,

- reversibility,

- data disclosure,

- Providers and Accounts,

- estimated cost,

- Budget impact,

- alternatives,

- risks,

- deadline,

- expiry,

- and evidence.

24.67 Approval Request Identity

Every Approval Request shall have stable identity and Version.

24.68 Approval Subject

Approval subjects may include:

- Request,

- Plan,

- Step,

- Execution,

- Asset,

- content,

- Budget,

- Provider,

- Connection,

- Credential operation,

- publication,

- deletion,

- policy exception,

- Mandate,

- or Incident action.

24.69 Approval Subject Version

The exact approved Version shall be explicit.

24.70 Approval Request Change

Material changes shall create a new Approval Request Version.

24.71 Material Approval Change

Material changes may include:

- content,

- cost,

- Provider,

- Account,

- data disclosure,

- target,

- timing,

- audience,

- publication channel,

- or reversibility.

24.72 Approval Summary

The request shall provide a concise, understandable summary.

24.73 Approval Detail

The approver shall be able to inspect detailed:

- Plan,

- object changes,

- data flows,

- cost,

- risks,

- and evidence.

24.74 Approval Diff

When an existing object changes, the request should show the exact material diff.

24.75 Approval Consequence

The request shall explain what happens if approved.

24.76 Denial Consequence

The request should explain what work will stop, defer or change if denied.

24.77 Approval Alternative

Material alternatives should be shown where practical.

Examples include:

- cheaper Provider,

- local execution,

- draft-only mode,

- reduced scope,

- delayed execution,

- or manual operation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.78 Approval Risk Summary

Risk should identify:

- privacy,

- security,

- financial,

- publication,

- rights,

- reliability,

- and reversibility.

24.79 Approval Data Disclosure

The request shall identify which data will be disclosed to which systems or people.

24.80 Approval Cost

Estimated cost shall include:

- initial execution,

- candidate count,

- retries,

- fallback,

- storage,

- and human review

where material.

24.81 Approval Time Window

Approval validity shall include start and expiry.

24.82 Approval Deadline

A request may expire if not decided by the required time.

24.83 Approval Decision

An Approval Decision records the authorised response to an Approval Request.

It shall include or reference:

- approvalDecisionId,

- Approval Request Version,

- approver,

- authority basis,

- decision,

- approved scope,

- conditions,

- limits,

- exclusions,

- effective time,

- expiry,

- authentication assurance,

- rationale,

- and provenance.

24.84 Approval Decision Identity

Every Approval Decision shall have stable identity.

24.85 Approval Decision States

States may include:

- approved,

- approved with conditions,

- partially approved,

- denied,

- deferred,

- revision required,

- expired,

- withdrawn,

- revoked,

- and superseded.

24.86 Approved

Approved permits the exact defined action or scope.

24.87 Approved with Conditions

Conditions shall be enforceable before or during execution.

24.88 Partial Approval

Partial approval shall identify approved and denied portions explicitly.

24.89 Denied

Denied actions shall not execute.

24.90 Deferred

Deferred requests remain undecided and unauthorised.

24.91 Revision Required

The requester must submit a new or amended request.

24.92 Approval Withdrawal

The requester may withdraw a pending request.

24.93 Approval Revocation

An approver or higher authority may revoke an approval before or during execution where policy permits.

24.94 Approval Rationale

The rationale should be concise and attributable.

24.95 Approval Conditions

Conditions may include:

- maximum Budget,

- approved Provider,

- approved Account,

- no external data disclosure,

- human review before publication,

- specific Asset Version,

- retry count,

- deadline,

- or rollback plan.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 24.111 Plan Approval Is Not Unlimited Replanning
text:
24.96 Approval Exclusion

Exclusions define what remains unauthorised.

Examples include:

- no publication,

- no deletion,

- no Provider change,

- no cross-Project use,

- or no Budget increase.

24.97 Approval Evidence

Approval evidence shall preserve:

- identity,

- authority,

- authentication,

- exact request,

- exact Decision,

- time,

- conditions,

- and scope.

24.98 Approval Signature

High-risk approvals may require a cryptographic or strongly authenticated signature.

24.99 Approval Token

An Approval Token is a bounded machine-verifiable artefact representing an active Approval Decision.

It shall include or reference:

- tokenId,

- Decision,

- subject,

- scope,

- limits,

- issuedAt,

- expiry,

- nonce,

- audience,

- and signature.

24.100 Approval Token Identity

Every Approval Token shall have stable identity or unique cryptographic identity.

24.101 Approval Token Audience

The token shall be valid only for the intended service or execution audience.

24.102 Approval Token Replay Protection

Tokens shall use:

- unique nonce,

- bounded use count,

- exact subject,

- expiry,

- and consumed state.

24.103 Approval Token Is Not Transferable

Approval Tokens shall not be reused by unrelated Executions.

24.104 Approval Token Consumption

Consumption shall be recorded atomically where consequence requires it.

24.105 Approval Token Revocation

Revoked Decisions shall invalidate unconsumed Tokens.

24.106 One-Time Approval

A One-Time Approval permits one exact action or Execution.

24.107 Single-Use Approval

Single-use authority shall be consumed after successful admission of the authorised action.

24.108 Per-Step Approval

A Plan may require approval before one specific Step.

24.109 Per-Execution Approval

One Execution is approved as a whole within stated limits.

24.110 Plan Approval

Plan Approval permits execution of one exact Plan Version inside stated bounds.

24.111 Plan Approval Is Not Unlimited Replanning

Material replanning requires revalidation or new approval.

24.112 Content Approval

Content Approval confirms that one exact content or Asset Version is acceptable for the stated use.

24.113 Publication Approval

Publication Approval permits release of an exact approved Asset or Package to an exact channel and Account.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 24.114 Content Approval Is Not Publication Approval
24.116 Budget Approval Is Not Payment Execution
text:
24.114 Content Approval Is Not Publication Approval

These Decisions shall remain separate.

24.115 Budget Approval

Budget Approval permits reservation or spend within a defined purpose and scope.

24.116 Budget Approval Is Not Payment Execution

Actual purchase, transfer or charge may require separate authority.

24.117 Provider Approval

Provider Approval permits use of a defined Provider Product under stated classifications and purposes.

24.118 Provider Account Approval

A Provider Account may require separate approval because of:

- owner,

- plan,

- billing,

- retention,

- workspace,

- or Tenant scope.

24.119 Model Approval

A specific Model, Deployment or Version may require approval for:

- high-risk tasks,

- sensitive data,

- or production use.

24.120 Tool Approval

A Tool may be approved for:

- read-only,

- bounded write,

- local execution,

- or defined repositories.

24.121 Credential Approval

Credential actions may require approval for:

- creation,

- rotation,

- export,

- revocation,

- sharing,

- or scope expansion.

24.122 Data Access Approval

Access Approval permits defined read or processing access.

24.123 Data Transfer Approval

Transfer Approval permits a defined Data Flow.

24.124 Deletion Approval

Deletion Approval permits deletion of exact objects and Locations under stated recovery conditions.

24.125 Overwrite Approval

Overwrite Approval permits replacing existing content or state.

It shall remain distinct from ordinary write authority.

24.126 Policy Exception Approval

An exception permits deviation from one explicit policy rule within exact bounds.

24.127 Emergency Approval

Emergency Approval permits urgent actions under an Incident procedure.

24.128 Approval Bundle

An Approval Bundle groups several related Approval Requests or Decisions.

It shall include or reference:

- approvalBundleId,

- purpose,

- items,

- dependencies,

- required approvers,

- quorum,

- expiry,

- and state.

24.129 Approval Bundle Identity

Every Approval Bundle shall have stable identity and Version.

24.130 Bundle Atomicity

A Bundle may be:

- all-or-nothing,

- partially approvable,

- or dependency-ordered.

The semantics shall be explicit.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.131 Approval Dependency

One approval may depend on another.

Examples include:

- rights approval before publication,

- Budget approval before paid execution,

- or privacy approval before Provider transfer.

24.132 Approval Order

Required approval order shall be explicit.

24.133 Approval Quorum

A quorum defines how many members of an approval group must approve.

24.134 Quorum Identity

The eligible approver group and membership Version shall be explicit.

24.135 Dual Control

Dual Control requires two independent authorised Principals.

24.136 Two-Person Rule

High-risk actions may require two distinct people.

An Agent shall not satisfy a human two-person rule.

24.137 Separation of Duties

Different stages may require different Principals.

Examples include:

- creator and Reviewer,

- requester and Approver,

- developer and production deployer,

- or finance requester and finance Approver.

24.138 Self-Approval Restriction

A Principal shall not approve its own high-risk request where policy requires independent review.

24.139 Agent Self-Approval Prohibition

An Agent shall not approve authority expansion, policy exceptions or high-risk actions for itself.

24.140 Conflict of Interest

A known conflict may disqualify an Approver for one Decision.

24.141 Approval Group

An Approval Group is a governed collection of eligible Approvers.

It shall include:

- groupId,

- members,

- Roles,

- quorum,

- scope,

- and Version.

24.142 Approval Group Identity

Every Approval Group shall have stable identity and Version.

24.143 Approver Eligibility

Eligibility shall be evaluated at Decision time.

24.144 Approver Substitution

Substitute Approvers shall be explicitly configured.

24.145 Approval Escalation

An unresolved request may escalate to a higher-authority Principal or group.

24.146 Escalation Path

Escalation shall identify:

- trigger,

- next Approver,

- deadline,

- and preserved context.

24.147 Escalation Does Not Broaden Scope

Escalation changes Decision authority, not the proposed action scope.

24.148 Approval Notification

Notification informs eligible Approvers that a Decision is required.

Notification itself does not approve anything.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.149 Approval Channel

Approval channels may include:

- Omnira interface,

- mobile application,

- secure web interface,

- hardware device,

- or signed external workflow.

24.150 Insecure Approval Channel

Ordinary email reply, unauthenticated chat or copied link may be insufficient for high-risk approval.

24.151 Mobile Approval

Mobile approval may be used for bounded Decisions.

It shall preserve:

- Principal,

- device,

- authentication assurance,

- exact scope,

- and Decision evidence.

24.152 Mobile Approval Minimisation

The mobile interface shall show sufficient context without exposing unnecessary protected data.

24.153 Mobile Approval Step-Up

Large spend, deletion, recovery and authority changes may require stronger verification than device unlock alone.

24.154 Voice Approval

Voice may assist navigation or request preparation.

High-risk approval shall require a reliable authenticated confirmation mechanism.

24.155 Ambiguous Natural-Language Approval

Ambiguous phrases such as:

- “go ahead,”

- “do it,”

- or “looks good”

shall not authorise broader consequential scope than the displayed request.

24.156 Confirmation Binding

The system shall bind the human response to the exact visible Approval Request.

24.157 Approval Fatigue

The architecture shall reduce unnecessary prompts without hiding material decisions.

24.158 Approval Grouping

Low-risk related actions may be grouped when scope remains understandable.

24.159 Approval Decomposition

High-risk or materially different actions shall be separated.

24.160 Dark-Pattern Prohibition

Approval interfaces shall not:

- preselect risky options,

- hide cost,

- obscure data disclosure,

- pressure acceptance,

- or make denial materially confusing.

24.161 Approval Accessibility

Approval interfaces should support:

- clear language,

- readable layout,

- keyboard access,

- screen readers,

- and understandable consequences.

24.162 Approval Localisation

Translated approval text shall preserve legal and operational meaning.

24.163 Approval Explainability

The approver should understand:

- what,

- why,

- where,

- who,

- how much,

- how long,

- and what can go wrong.

24.164 Authority Level

An Authority Level describes the general operating posture permitted for a Principal or Agent.

Authority Levels do not replace explicit Grants, policy, approvals or scope.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 24.175 L4 — Execute Approved Operational Actions Within a Mandate
text:
24.165 Canonical Authority Levels

The canonical operating levels are:

- L0 — Observe,

- L1 — Recommend,

- L2 — Prepare,

- L3 — Execute Low-Risk Reversible Actions,

- L4 — Execute Approved Operational Actions Within a Mandate,

- L5 — Manage a Delegated Domain Within Strict Boundaries,

- L6 — Exceptional Sovereign or Recovery Authority.

24.166 L0 — Observe

L0 permits:

- read-only observation,

- status inspection,

- and evidence collection

within explicit data access scope.

24.167 L0 Restrictions

L0 shall not:

- modify,

- publish,

- spend,

- approve,

- delete,

- or create external side effects.

24.168 L1 — Recommend

L1 permits:

- analysis,

- recommendations,

- alternatives,

- risk summaries,

- and approval preparation.

24.169 L1 Restrictions

L1 shall not execute consequential actions.

24.170 L2 — Prepare

L2 permits creation of:

- drafts,

- Plans,

- files in non-authoritative workspace,

- proposed changes,

- publication Packages,

- and Approval Requests.

24.171 L2 Restrictions

Prepared work shall not become effective, published or externally committed without further authority.

24.172 L3 — Execute Low-Risk Reversible Actions

L3 permits explicitly approved classes of:

- reversible,

- low-cost,

- low-impact,

- and Project-scoped

actions.

24.173 L3 Examples

Examples may include:

- create draft file,

- update temporary workspace,

- run read-only test,

- produce local preview,

- or organise non-authoritative data.

24.174 L3 Exclusions

L3 does not automatically permit:

- publication,

- deletion,

- payment,

- Credential mutation,

- Account changes,

- or Confidential external disclosure.

24.175 L4 — Execute Approved Operational Actions Within a Mandate

L4 permits operational execution inside a defined Mandate.

The Mandate shall specify:

- actions,

- Projects,

- Budgets,

- Providers,

- data classes,

- side effects,

- time,

- and escalation.

24.176 L4 Example

A publishing workflow may prepare and publish approved content to one Project Account under an active publication Mandate.

24.177 L4 Restrictions

L4 shall stop when:

- content changes materially,

- target Account changes,

- Budget exceeds limit,

- approval expires,

- or policy changes.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 24.178 L5 — Manage a Delegated Domain Within Strict Boundaries
24.181 L6 — Exceptional Sovereign or Recovery Authority
text:
24.178 L5 — Manage a Delegated Domain Within Strict Boundaries

L5 permits broader operational management of one defined domain.

Examples may include:

- scheduling,

- prioritisation,

- resource allocation,

- low-risk retries,

- approved Provider selection,

- and bounded Budget management.

24.179 L5 Requirements

L5 requires:

- mature policy,

- strong evidence,

- monitoring,

- incident response,

- periodic review,

- and human revocation.

24.180 L5 Restrictions

L5 does not provide universal authority across Projects or domains.

24.181 L6 — Exceptional Sovereign or Recovery Authority

L6 represents exceptional owner, platform or recovery authority.

It may permit:

- ownership transfer,

- root recovery,

- policy restoration,

- or emergency containment.

24.182 L6 Restrictions

L6 shall:

- be rare,

- strongly authenticated,

- time-bounded where possible,

- highly audited,

- and unavailable to ordinary Agents.

24.183 Authority Level Mapping

Every Agent or Principal may have different Levels in different Domains.

24.184 No Universal Level

A Principal may be L4 for Project scheduling and L1 for finance.

24.185 Level Is Not Grant

No Level alone authorises an action.

24.186 Level Change

Increasing an Authority Level requires explicit approval and evidence.

24.187 Level Downgrade

Authority may be reduced immediately for:

- Incident,

- poor performance,

- user Decision,

- policy change,

- or Project state.

24.188 Autonomy

Autonomy is the ability of an Agent or system to choose and perform actions without requiring a new human Decision for every Step.

24.189 Bounded Autonomy

Bounded Autonomy permits independent operation only inside explicit:

- scope,

- authority,

- Budget,

- policy,

- risk,

- data,

- time,

- and outcome boundaries.

24.190 Autonomy Is Not Independence

An autonomous Agent remains subordinate to:

- human authority,

- Platform policy,

- Project policy,

- and active Mandates.

24.191 Autonomy Is Not Unlimited Delegation

An Agent shall not expand its own operating envelope.

24.192 Autonomy Envelope

An Autonomy Envelope defines the complete boundary inside which independent operation is permitted.

It shall include or reference:

- autonomyEnvelopeId,

- Principal or Agent,

- Authority Domain,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Capabilities,

- permitted actions,

- prohibited actions,

- data categories,

- Classifications,

- Providers,

- Accounts,

- Models,

- Tools,

- Budget,

- time,

- frequency,

- retry,

- fallback,

- side-effect,

- reversibility,

- Quality,

- monitoring,

- and escalation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.193 Autonomy Envelope Identity

Every Autonomy Envelope shall have stable identity and Version.

24.194 Autonomy Envelope Versioning

Any material boundary change shall create a new Version.

24.195 Autonomy Envelope Owner

Every Envelope shall have an accountable human or governance owner.

24.196 Autonomy Envelope Expiry

Every Envelope shall have expiry or mandatory review.

24.197 Autonomy Envelope Suspension

An Envelope may be suspended without deleting its history.

24.198 Mandate

A Mandate is an active Authority Grant authorising an Agent or Service to pursue a defined operational objective within an Autonomy Envelope.

24.199 Mandate Identity

Every Mandate shall have stable identity and Version.

24.200 Mandate Purpose

A Mandate shall state the objective and expected outcomes.

24.201 Mandate Scope

A Mandate shall include exact:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Capability,

- action,

- resource,

- data,

- cost,

- time,

- and side-effect scope.

24.202 Mandate Limits

Limits shall be measurable and enforceable.

24.203 Mandate Conditions

Conditions may include:

- valid Quality Gate,

- no unresolved Incident,

- approved Provider health,

- fresh user approval,

- or Budget availability.

24.204 Mandate Exclusions

Exclusions shall identify actions that always require separate approval.

24.205 Mandatory Separate Approval

The following should require separate approval unless an explicit high-assurance Mandate states otherwise:

- new Provider,

- new Provider Account,

- higher Budget,

- publication,

- deletion,

- overwrite,

- Credential export,

- access expansion,

- policy exception,

- ownership change,

- external sharing,

- and irreversible action.

24.206 Standing Mandate

A Standing Mandate permits repeated actions within recurring boundaries.

24.207 Standing Mandate Examples

Examples may include:

- publish two approved Project posts per day,

- perform nightly read-only health checks,

- generate draft analytics reports,

- or reconcile Provider jobs hourly.

24.208 Standing Mandate Frequency

Maximum frequency and volume shall be explicit.

24.209 Standing Mandate Cost

Maximum cost per action and per period shall be explicit.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.210 Standing Mandate Review

Standing Mandates shall receive periodic review.

24.211 Standing Mandate Revocation

The user or authorised owner shall be able to revoke the Mandate promptly.

24.212 Bounded Job Approval

Bounded Job Approval authorises one job or workflow to operate independently inside exact limits.

It shall define:

- objective,

- Plan Version,

- allowed Steps,

- Providers,

- Accounts,

- data scope,

- Budget,

- retry count,

- fallback options,

- deadline,

- and escalation triggers.

24.213 Bounded Job Operation

The Fabric may execute, retry and use eligible fallback inside the approved boundaries without requesting approval for each ordinary Step.

24.214 Bounded Job Deviation

The Fabric shall stop or escalate when:

- Plan changes materially,

- Provider changes outside the approved set,

- Budget rises,

- data disclosure broadens,

- Quality Floor changes,

- target changes,

- publication becomes required,

- deletion becomes required,

- or outcome becomes unknown beyond the approved policy.

24.215 Bounded Job Completion

Completion shall preserve evidence that all actions remained inside the approved envelope.

24.216 Execution Authorisation

Execution Authorisation is the machine-enforceable Decision that one exact Execution may begin or continue.

It shall be derived from:

- Principal identity,

- active Grants,

- Approval Decisions,

- Mandate,

- Plan Version,

- policy,

- Budget,

- data eligibility,

- and current state.

24.217 Execution Authorisation Identity

Every material Execution Authorisation shall have stable identity.

24.218 Authorisation Evaluation

Authorisation shall occur:

- before execution,

- before each consequential Step,

- and after material state change.

24.219 Authorisation Inputs

The evaluator shall consider:

- acting Principal,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Capability,

- action,

- target,

- Version,

- data,

- Provider,

- Account,

- Budget,

- time,

- risk,

- and active Incidents.

24.220 Authorisation Decision States

States may include:

- authorised,

- authorised with conditions,

- denied,

- approval required,

- reauthentication required,

- policy review required,

- and indeterminate.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.221 Authorisation Indeterminate

Indeterminate shall fail closed for consequential actions.

24.222 Authorisation Cache

Low-risk authorisation results may be cached briefly.

Cache keys shall include:

- Principal,

- Grant Versions,

- policy Versions,

- Project,

- action,

- target,

- and time.

24.223 Authorisation Cache Invalidation

Revocation, policy change, role change, Incident or object Version change shall invalidate affected results.

24.224 Continuous Authorisation

Long-running workflows shall revalidate authority at checkpoints.

24.225 Queued Work Authorisation

Queued work shall be reauthorised before execution begins.

24.226 Delayed Execution

An approval may expire before delayed work starts.

The work shall not execute.

24.227 Scheduled Execution

Scheduled actions shall validate:

- active Mandate,

- exact schedule,

- target state,

- content Version,

- Account,

- and Budget

at run time.

24.228 Long-Running Execution

Long-running work shall revalidate authority before:

- expensive stages,

- external side effects,

- publication,

- deletion,

- and final delivery.

24.229 Plan Change

A changed Plan shall receive new authorisation when material.

24.230 Non-Material Plan Adjustment

Minor internal scheduling or equivalent-resource adjustment may remain authorised when explicitly allowed.

24.231 Material Plan Adjustment

Material changes include:

- new Provider,

- changed data flow,

- changed target,

- increased cost,

- increased risk,

- changed side effect,

- or changed completion contract.

24.232 Retry Authority

Retry authority shall be defined separately from initial execution authority.

24.233 Technical Retry

A technical retry may be allowed within:

- error class,

- count,

- time,

- cost,

- and idempotency boundaries.

24.234 Quality Retry

A quality-driven regeneration creates a new Candidate and may require separate Candidate Budget.

24.235 Retry After Unknown Outcome

Retry after unknown outcome shall require reconciliation or explicit authority.

24.236 Retry Cost

Cumulative retry cost shall count against the approved Budget.

24.237 Retry Scope

Retry shall not broaden data, Provider or action scope.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 24.255 Manual Interface Does Not Broaden Authority
text:
24.238 Fallback Authority

Fallback is permitted only among approved eligible alternatives.

24.239 Fallback Provider Set

The approved Provider set shall be explicit.

24.240 Fallback Model Set

The approved Model or Deployment set shall be explicit where material.

24.241 Fallback Data Review

Fallback shall revalidate:

- Classification,

- privacy,

- rights,

- consent,

- retention,

- and region.

24.242 Fallback Cost Review

Fallback shall remain inside the approved Budget.

24.243 Fallback Quality Review

Fallback shall preserve the Quality Floor.

24.244 Pinned Routing Authority

Pinned routing shall not switch Providers or Models silently.

24.245 Private Routing Authority

Private routing shall not fall back to ordinary external Providers.

24.246 Replanning Authority

The Planner may replan only inside the authorised change envelope.

24.247 Escalation Trigger

Escalation triggers may include:

- Budget threshold,

- repeated failure,

- unknown outcome,

- policy conflict,

- low confidence,

- rights uncertainty,

- privacy uncertainty,

- Quality failure,

- Provider outage,

- or deadline risk.

24.248 Escalation Record

Every material escalation shall preserve:

- trigger,

- current state,

- required Decision,

- alternatives,

- deadline,

- and affected work.

24.249 Pause

Pause suspends future Steps while preserving state.

24.250 Stop

Stop terminates further authorised activity for the current Execution or Mandate.

24.251 Abort

Abort attempts immediate termination.

External work may still require reconciliation.

24.252 Human Takeover

A human may take over a workflow.

The handoff shall preserve:

- state,

- authority,

- evidence,

- and pending risks.

24.253 Human-Assisted Mandate

A Mandate may include defined manual Steps.

Manual operation shall remain truthful and attributable.

24.254 Manual Procedure Authority

A human operator receives authority only for the exact procedure and scope.

24.255 Manual Interface Does Not Broaden Authority

Operating a Provider dashboard manually shall not allow unapproved work.

24.256 Risk Class

Risk Class describes the consequence and control requirement of an action.

Canonical classes may include:

- R0 — No Material Side Effect,

- R1 — Low and Reversible,

- R2 — Moderate Operational,

- R3 — Consequential,

- R4 — High Impact,

- R5 — Critical or Sovereign.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.257 R0 — No Material Side Effect

Examples include:

- read public metadata,

- calculate estimate,

- inspect status,

- or generate non-persistent preview.

24.258 R1 — Low and Reversible

Examples include:

- create draft,

- update temporary workspace,

- or add non-public annotation.

24.259 R2 — Moderate Operational

Examples include:

- call a paid Provider within a small Budget,

- modify Project Internal files with Version control,

- or schedule approved work.

24.260 R3 — Consequential

Examples include:

- publish content,

- send external message,

- commit code to an active branch,

- or create a customer-facing Asset.

24.261 R4 — High Impact

Examples include:

- delete canonical data,

- rotate production Credentials,

- deploy to production,

- make substantial purchase,

- or process highly sensitive data externally.

24.262 R5 — Critical or Sovereign

Examples include:

- transfer Project ownership,

- disable platform security,

- access root recovery,

- delete Tenant data,

- or override non-waivable policy.

24.263 Risk Classification

Risk shall consider:

- impact,

- reversibility,

- scope,

- data sensitivity,

- cost,

- legal effect,

- external visibility,

- and recovery difficulty.

24.264 Risk Aggregation

Several low-risk actions may become higher risk when accumulated.

24.265 Cumulative Risk

Frequency, volume or combined scope may require stronger approval.

24.266 Dynamic Risk

Risk may increase because of:

- Incident,

- unusual device,

- new Provider,

- changed Account,

- unusual spend,

- or unexpected target.

24.267 Action Class

An Action Class is a canonical category of operation.

Examples include:

- observe,

- analyse,

- generate,

- transform,

- write,

- send,

- publish,

- purchase,

- transfer,

- delete,

- overwrite,

- configure,

- delegate,

- approve,

- and recover.

24.268 Action Class Identity

Every Action Class shall have stable identity and Version.

24.269 Read Action

Read authority shall specify:

- scope,

- data category,

- Classification,

- and purpose.

24.270 Analyse Action

Analysis authority does not automatically permit Memory admission or external disclosure.

24.271 Generate Action

Generation authority permits candidate creation.

It does not automatically approve Asset admission or publication.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.272 Transform Action

Transformation authority shall identify source, preserve constraints and output scope.

24.273 Write Action

Write authority permits creation or modification inside exact targets.

24.274 Send Action

Send authority creates an external communication side effect.

24.275 Publish Action

Publish authority makes content visible through a defined channel.

24.276 Purchase Action

Purchase authority creates financial commitment.

24.277 Transfer Action

Transfer authority moves data, Assets or funds across a boundary.

24.278 Delete Action

Delete authority removes data or state.

24.279 Overwrite Action

Overwrite authority replaces existing state and may destroy recoverability.

24.280 Configure Action

Configure authority changes system or Project behaviour.

24.281 Delegate Action

Delegation authority changes another Principal’s Permissions.

24.282 Approve Action

Approval authority permits issuing Approval Decisions in a defined domain.

24.283 Recover Action

Recovery authority may restore or change critical state under strong controls.

24.284 Reversibility

Reversibility describes whether an action can be undone reliably.

24.285 Fully Reversible

The prior state can be restored with high confidence and low cost.

24.286 Partially Reversible

Some effects can be restored while others persist.

24.287 Compensatable

The action cannot be rolled back directly but a compensating action is available.

24.288 Irreversible

The action or its external consequences cannot be reliably undone.

24.289 Reversibility Evidence

Claims of reversibility shall identify:

- backup,

- Version,

- rollback method,

- compensation,

- and limitations.

24.290 Reversibility Is Not Permission

A reversible action may still require approval.

24.291 Destructive Action

A destructive action removes, replaces or invalidates data, access or state.

24.292 Destructive Action Requirements

Destructive actions should require:

- exact target,

- impact preview,

- authority,

- strong authentication,

- recovery plan,

- and evidence.

24.293 Soft Delete

Soft Delete may reduce immediate risk while preserving recovery.

24.294 Hard Delete

Hard Delete requires stronger authority and confirmation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.295 Bulk Delete

Bulk deletion shall display:

- count,

- scope,

- dependencies,

- and residual copies.

24.296 Deletion Cooling-Off Period

High-impact deletion may use an approval or recovery delay.

24.297 Overwrite Preview

Overwrite approval should show the current and proposed Versions.

24.298 Backup Requirement

A backup or Version checkpoint may be mandatory before destructive action.

24.299 Backup Does Not Remove Approval

Recoverability reduces impact but does not create authority.

24.300 Financial Authority

Financial Authority governs:

- Provider spend,

- subscriptions,

- purchases,

- transfers,

- refunds,

- credits,

- and Budget changes.

24.301 Financial Scope

Financial Grants shall identify:

- payer,

- Project,

- funding source,

- currency,

- amount,

- period,

- purpose,

- and vendor.

24.302 Spend Limit

Spend limits may apply:

- per Attempt,

- per Execution,

- per day,

- per month,

- per Project,

- per Provider,

- or per Principal.

24.303 Aggregate Spend

Cumulative spend shall be evaluated against all relevant limits.

24.304 Cost Reservation

A reservation is not final spend but reduces available authorised Budget.

24.305 Cost Overrun

Expected overrun shall pause work before the limit is exceeded where practical.

24.306 Provider Price Change

A material price change may invalidate approval.

24.307 Currency Conversion

Budget evaluation shall identify exchange-rate source and margin where relevant.

24.308 Subscription Purchase

Starting or upgrading a subscription requires explicit scope and recurrence disclosure.

24.309 Recurring Spend

Recurring charges shall include:

- amount,

- frequency,

- renewal,

- cancellation,

- and owner.

24.310 Free Trial

A free trial that converts to paid service shall be treated as recurring financial commitment.

24.311 Managed Credits

Use of Omnira-managed credits shall remain Project-attributable.

24.312 User-Owned Account Spend

User-owned Account usage still requires Project Budget authority.

24.313 Refund Authority

Refund or credit requests may require separate authority.

24.314 Financial Approval Separation

The requester and Approver may require separation above defined thresholds.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.315 Publication Authority

Publication Authority governs release to external audiences.

24.316 Publication Scope

Publication Grants shall identify:

- Project,

- Account,

- channel,

- audience,

- content class,

- schedule,

- geography,

- and frequency.

24.317 Publication Asset Version

The exact Asset or Package Version shall be approved.

24.318 Publication Account

The exact external Account shall be explicit.

24.319 Publication Timing

Approval may apply to:

- immediate,

- scheduled,

- or defined window

publication.

24.320 Publication Frequency

Standing publication Mandates shall define maximum frequency.

24.321 Publication Metadata

Caption, title, tags, links and visibility settings are part of the approved publication payload.

24.322 Publication Revision

Material content or metadata changes require reapproval.

24.323 Publication Preview

The approver should see a channel-representative preview.

24.324 Publication Visibility

Visibility may be:

- private,

- unlisted,

- subscriber-only,

- internal,

- or public.

24.325 Publication Audience Change

Changing audience or visibility is material.

24.326 Publication Verification

Publication authority does not equal publication completion.

External verification remains required.

24.327 Unpublish Authority

Removing public content may require separate authority and evidence.

24.328 Edit-After-Publish Authority

Editing published content shall be separately governed.

24.329 Social Reply Authority

Replying to Project comments may be authorised within one opened workflow.

Private-message replies remain separately restricted.

24.330 Bulk Publication

Bulk publication requires stronger preview, limits and rollback planning.

24.331 Content Authority

Content authority governs creation and acceptance of editorial or creative material.

24.332 Draft Authority

Drafting may be broadly delegated.

24.333 Canonical Acceptance Authority

Marking content canonical requires an authorised Reviewer or owner.

24.334 Character Authority

Changes to canonical Character Profiles require Project-specific approval.

24.335 Voice Authority

Voice Profile or consent changes require exact authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.336 Brand Authority

Brand Profile changes require authorised Project governance.

24.337 Code Authority

Code authority governs repository reads, modifications, commits, pushes, pull requests, merges and deployments.

24.338 Repository Scope

Code Grants shall identify exact:

- repository,

- branch,

- worktree,

- path,

- environment,

- and operation.

24.339 Read-Only Code Authority

Read authority shall not permit file modification.

24.340 Modify Code Authority

Modification authority may be limited to:

- branch,

- directory,

- file class,

- or task.

24.341 Commit Authority

Commit creation is a distinct action from file modification.

24.342 Push Authority

Push authority is distinct from commit authority.

24.343 Pull Request Authority

Creating or updating a pull request is distinct from pushing a branch.

24.344 Merge Authority

Merge authority shall remain separate and may require checks or review.

24.345 Deployment Authority

Deployment is distinct from merge.

24.346 Production Deployment

Production deploys require stronger approval than local builds.

24.347 Migration Authority

Database or infrastructure migrations require exact environment and rollback scope.

24.348 Force Operation

Force push, destructive reset or history rewrite shall require exceptional authority.

24.349 Code Approval Diff

Approval should display the exact diff or immutable commit reference.

24.350 Working Tree Change

Approval tied to a commit shall not authorise later uncommitted changes.

24.351 Credential Authority

Credential authority governs:

- create,

- read metadata,

- use,

- rotate,

- revoke,

- export,

- and delete.

24.352 Secret Read Prohibition

Agents and ordinary operators should not receive raw Secret values.

24.353 Credential Use Grant

A Principal may receive bounded use of a Connection without reading the Secret.

24.354 Credential Rotation

Rotation authority shall identify:

- target Credential,

- dependent systems,

- rollout,

- rollback,

- and verification.

24.355 Credential Export

Export requires exceptional authority and strong authentication.

24.356 Credential Sharing

Sharing a Credential across Projects or Tenants requires explicit governance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.357 Provider Connection Authority

Creating or changing a Connection may affect:

- data,

- billing,

- region,

- and Account ownership.

24.358 System Authority

System authority governs:

- device settings,

- network,

- storage,

- process control,

- restart,

- and software installation.

24.359 Device Restart

Restart authority may be low or high risk depending on active work.

24.360 Network Change

Wi-Fi, VPN, firewall and network changes may interrupt work or alter privacy boundaries.

24.361 Screen Capture

Screenshot authority shall be:

- task-specific,

- device-specific,

- and time-bounded.

24.362 Microphone and Camera

Sensor access requires explicit Capability and permission.

24.363 Installed Application Inventory

Application-list access shall be purpose-limited.

24.364 Location Authority

Location access shall specify precision, duration and purpose.

24.365 Notification Authority

Notification metadata and content permissions shall remain distinct.

24.366 Mobile System Changes

Mobile settings such as:

- restart,

- Do Not Disturb,

- Wi-Fi,

- or system configuration

should require approval until a mature Mandate exists.

24.367 Data Authority

Data authority governs read, processing, transfer, publication, retention and deletion.

24.368 Data Access Grant

The Grant shall identify:

- categories,

- Classification,

- Project,

- purpose,

- operations,

- and time.

24.369 Data Disclosure Authority

Disclosure authority remains separate from read authority.

24.370 Data Retention Authority

Storing data beyond the current Execution requires retention authority.

24.371 Memory Admission Authority

Creating permanent Memory requires an eligible Memory Admission Decision.

24.372 Training Authority

Using data for training or fine-tuning requires separate authority.

24.373 Cross-Project Data Authority

Cross-Project access requires explicit scope.

24.374 Cross-Tenant Data Authority

Cross-Tenant access is prohibited by default.

24.375 Approval Policy

Approval Policy defines which actions require which form of approval.

It shall include or reference:

- approvalPolicyId,

- scope,

- action classes,

- risk classes,

- thresholds,

- required Approvers,

- authentication assurance,

- quorum,

- separation of duties,

- expiry,

- and Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.376 Approval Policy Identity

Every Approval Policy shall have stable identity and Version.

24.377 Platform Approval Policy

Platform policy defines non-waivable minimum controls.

24.378 Tenant Approval Policy

Tenant policy may add stricter requirements.

24.379 Project Approval Policy

Project policy may define:

- owners,

- publishers,

- Budget thresholds,

- review gates,

- and standing Mandates.

24.380 Agent Approval Policy

Each Agent shall have explicit approval requirements by action class.

24.381 Risk-Based Approval Policy

Approval strength should increase with consequence and uncertainty.

24.382 Threshold Policy

Thresholds may apply to:

- spend,

- data volume,

- deletion count,

- publication audience,

- or action frequency.

24.383 Approval Policy Precedence

The most restrictive applicable requirement shall govern.

24.384 Approval Exception Policy

Exceptions shall be narrow, expiring and attributable.

24.385 Approval Policy Change

Policy changes may invalidate pending and active approvals.

24.386 Policy Grandfathering

Grandfathering shall be explicit.

It shall not be assumed.

24.387 Approval State Machine

Approval Request states may include:

- draft,

- submitted,

- awaiting approver,

- partially decided,

- approved,

- denied,

- revision required,

- expired,

- withdrawn,

- revoked,

- and superseded.

24.388 Draft Approval Request

A draft has no authority effect.

24.389 Submitted Approval Request

Submitted means the request is ready for eligible review.

24.390 Awaiting Approver

The system is waiting for required Decisions.

24.391 Partially Decided

Some but not all required Decisions exist.

24.392 Approved Request

All required approvals and conditions are satisfied.

24.393 Expired Request

No new execution may use the request.

24.394 Superseded Request

A newer Version replaces it.

24.395 Approval Decision Finality

A Decision may be:

- final,

- revocable,

- appealable,

- or conditionally final.

24.396 Approval Appeal

A denied request may be resubmitted or appealed according to policy.

24.397 Approval Race

Concurrent Decisions shall be reconciled against:

- request Version,

- quorum,

- withdrawal,

- revocation,

- and expiry.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.398 Stale Approval

An approval becomes stale when material context changes.

24.399 Stale Approval Triggers

Triggers may include:

- Asset Version change,

- Plan Version change,

- Provider change,

- Account change,

- Budget change,

- policy change,

- rights change,

- consent change,

- Classification change,

- or Incident.

24.400 Approval Revalidation

Stale approvals shall be revalidated before use.

24.401 Approval Idempotency

Repeated submission of the same Decision shall not create duplicate authority.

24.402 Duplicate Approval Event

Duplicate approval callbacks or notifications shall be deduplicated.

24.403 Approval Correlation

Every request, Decision, Token and Execution Authorisation shall share stable correlation.

24.404 Approval Availability

Approval-system outage shall not cause fail-open execution.

24.405 Offline Approval

Offline approval may be supported through signed, expiring and replay-protected artefacts.

24.406 Offline Approval Risk

Offline approval shall not be used for dynamic context that cannot be verified.

24.407 Approval Synchronisation

Offline Decisions shall be reconciled before consequential execution.

24.408 Approval Store

Approval records shall use durable, append-only or Versioned storage.

24.409 Approval Confidentiality

Approval content may contain sensitive:

- Plans,

- Costs,

- data flows,

- and Assets.

Access shall be scoped.

24.410 Approval Retention

Approval evidence shall remain available for audit and dispute according to policy.

24.411 Approval Deletion

Personal data may be minimised or deleted while preserving required Decision evidence.

24.412 Authority Evaluation Service

The Authority Evaluation Service is the canonical service that determines effective authority.

It shall evaluate:

- identity,

- Roles,

- Grants,

- Denials,

- approvals,

- Mandates,

- policy,

- risk,

- and current state.

24.413 Authority Evaluation Service Identity

The service shall have stable Service Principal identity and Version.

24.414 Central Policy Decision

Material authorisation logic should not be duplicated inconsistently across Adapters and applications.

24.415 Local Enforcement

Execution components shall still enforce the Decision at the action boundary.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 24.433 Current Authority Does Not Rewrite History
text:
24.416 Policy Decision Point

The Policy Decision Point evaluates whether an action is authorised.

24.417 Policy Enforcement Point

The Policy Enforcement Point blocks or permits the action.

24.418 Policy Information Point

The Policy Information Point supplies:

- identity,

- Project,

- Classification,

- risk,

- Budget,

- and resource state.

24.419 Policy Administration Point

The Policy Administration Point manages approved policy Versions.

24.420 Defence in Depth

Authority should be enforced at:

- Planner,

- Scheduler,

- Adapter,

- Tool,

- storage,

- Provider Connector,

- and external side-effect boundary.

24.421 Adapter Enforcement

Adapters shall reject calls lacking valid Execution Authorisation.

24.422 Tool Enforcement

Tools shall verify exact:

- Project,

- target,

- operation,

- and authority.

24.423 Storage Enforcement

Storage shall enforce read, write and delete separately.

24.424 Publication Enforcement

Publication Connectors shall require exact Asset Version and target Account authority.

24.425 Financial Enforcement

Billing or purchase systems shall enforce Budget and approval Tokens.

24.426 Queue Enforcement

Workers shall verify authority at consumption time.

24.427 Event Enforcement

Events shall not be interpreted as authority unless they carry valid references to canonical Decisions.

24.428 Human Operator Enforcement

Manual operators shall receive an exact authorised procedure and scope.

24.429 Authority Evidence

Every consequential action shall preserve evidence of the authority used.

24.430 Authority Snapshot

An Authority Snapshot records the effective authority state at one Decision or execution point.

It may include:

- Principal,

- Roles,

- Grants,

- Denials,

- policy Versions,

- approvals,

- Mandate,

- and time.

24.431 Authority Snapshot Identity

Every material Authority Snapshot shall have stable identity.

24.432 Historical Authority

Historical actions shall remain linked to the authority valid at the time.

24.433 Current Authority Does Not Rewrite History

Later revocation does not imply that a previously authorised action was unauthorised at execution time.

24.434 Retroactive Invalidity

If a Grant was fraudulent or compromised, the system may classify prior actions as disputed without rewriting evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.435 Authority Drift

Authority Drift occurs when actual system access becomes broader than canonical Grants.

24.436 Authority Drift Detection

The system should compare:

- configured Permissions,

- Provider roles,

- storage policies,

- Tool scopes,

- and canonical Grants.

24.437 Orphan Permission

An external Permission without a corresponding canonical Grant shall be reviewed or removed.

24.438 Orphan Grant

A canonical Grant that cannot be enforced technically shall not be treated as active.

24.439 Excess Privilege

Permissions broader than required shall be reduced.

24.440 Dormant Authority

Unused high-risk Grants should expire or require review.

24.441 Authority Review

Periodic review should inspect:

- Principals,

- Roles,

- Grants,

- Mandates,

- Tokens,

- and external Permissions.

24.442 Access Certification

Owners may certify that current authority remains appropriate.

24.443 Agent Performance Review

Autonomy expansion should consider:

- reliability,

- Quality,

- policy compliance,

- incident history,

- cost accuracy,

- and human correction rate.

24.444 Autonomy Promotion

Increasing autonomy shall require:

- evidence,

- controlled testing,

- explicit approval,

- and rollback.

24.445 Autonomy Demotion

Authority shall be reduced promptly after:

- Incident,

- repeated error,

- policy breach,

- user Decision,

- or context change.

24.446 Shadow Mode

A proposed autonomous policy may operate in shadow mode without executing side effects.

24.447 Recommendation Comparison

Shadow Decisions may be compared with human Decisions.

24.448 Canary Autonomy

A new Mandate may apply to a small, low-risk subset first.

24.449 Autonomy Rollback

Rollback shall restore the prior active Mandate or lower Level.

24.450 No Authority Learning Without Review

Derived Learning shall not expand authority automatically.

24.451 Evidence-Informed Authority

Evidence may support a proposal to broaden or narrow authority.

A human or authorised governance process shall decide.

24.452 Human Override

An authorised human may stop or restrict Agent activity.

24.453 Human Override Limit

Human override shall not bypass non-waivable safety or legal policy merely because the person requests it.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 24.468 Incident Authority Does Not Permit Unrelated Work
text:
24.454 Emergency Stop

An Emergency Stop shall suspend defined:

- Agents,

- workflows,

- Providers,

- publications,

- or Project actions.

24.455 Emergency Stop Identity

Every stop action shall have stable identity and evidence.

24.456 Global Emergency Stop

A global stop shall require exceptional authority and may preserve read-only recovery access.

24.457 Project Emergency Stop

A Project owner may stop Project execution within their authority.

24.458 Agent Emergency Stop

An Agent may be disabled without disabling unrelated platform services.

24.459 Provider Emergency Stop

A Provider path may be suspended after privacy, security or reliability Incident.

24.460 Break-Glass Authority

Break-Glass Authority permits exceptional access or action during urgent recovery.

It shall be:

- strongly authenticated,

- time-bounded,

- purpose-bounded,

- highly audited,

- and reviewed afterward.

24.461 Break-Glass Trigger

Triggers may include:

- active security Incident,

- owner lockout,

- failed recovery,

- data-loss risk,

- or critical service outage.

24.462 Break-Glass Approval

Break-glass use may require:

- two-person approval,

- owner confirmation,

- or post-event review

depending on urgency.

24.463 Break-Glass Scope

The scope shall be the minimum required.

24.464 Break-Glass Expiry

Authority shall expire automatically.

24.465 Break-Glass Evidence

Evidence shall include:

- trigger,

- actor,

- actions,

- data accessed,

- duration,

- and outcome.

24.466 Break-Glass Review

Post-event review shall determine:

- appropriateness,

- residual access,

- required rotation,

- and policy changes.

24.467 Incident Authority

Incident roles may receive temporary authority for:

- containment,

- evidence preservation,

- Credential rotation,

- or service isolation.

24.468 Incident Authority Does Not Permit Unrelated Work

Emergency authority remains Incident-scoped.

24.469 Recovery Authority

Recovery operations shall preserve:

- current revocation,

- deletion,

- Project,

- Tenant,

- and policy state.

24.470 Owner Authority

Project or Tenant ownership may include broad governance authority.

It does not permit bypass of non-waivable Platform safety and isolation rules.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.471 Ownership Transfer

Ownership transfer requires:

- strong authentication,

- exact target,

- receiving Principal,

- acceptance,

- and evidence.

24.472 Ownership Recovery

Recovery shall use verified recovery procedures and independent evidence.

24.473 Multi-Tenant Authority

Authority shall remain Tenant-scoped by default.

24.474 Tenant Administrator

A Tenant Administrator may manage:

- members,

- Roles,

- policy,

- and billing

without universal content access automatically.

24.475 Project Owner

A Project Owner governs one Project.

They shall not gain access to another Tenant or Project automatically.

24.476 Platform Administrator

Platform administration may govern infrastructure.

Content access shall remain separately granted.

24.477 Support Operator

Support authority should use:

- metadata views,

- temporary access,

- user consent,

- and redaction.

24.478 Auditor

An Auditor may inspect evidence and policy without mutation authority.

24.479 External Reviewer

An External Reviewer receives only the exact review package and time-bounded access.

24.480 Contractor Authority

Contractor authority shall be narrow, expiring and Project-specific.

24.481 Departed Principal

Authority shall be revoked promptly when a person leaves the role or organisation.

24.482 Device Loss

Authority Tokens and Sessions on a lost device shall be revoked.

24.483 Compromised Principal

Compromise shall suspend active authority and trigger review.

24.484 Agent Model Change

Changing the Agent’s serving Model shall not broaden authority.

24.485 Agent Provider Change

Changing Provider shall not broaden:

- data access,

- Tool access,

- Budget,

- or Mandate.

24.486 Agent Version Change

Material Agent logic changes may require revalidation of high-risk Mandates.

24.487 Approval and Rights

Rights clearance does not create execution authority.

Publication requires both rights eligibility and publication authority.

24.488 Approval and Consent

Consent permits defined use of protected subjects or data.

It does not authorise a Principal to execute unrelated actions.

24.489 Approval and Privacy

Approval cannot lower mandatory Classification without a valid classification Decision.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.490 Approval and Security

An authorised action may still be blocked by active security policy or Incident state.

24.491 Approval and Quality

Approval may require a passed Quality Gate.

Approval shall not fabricate Quality evidence.

24.492 Approval and Reliability

Unknown outcome, partial completion or stale state may invalidate further action.

24.493 Approval and Cost

Budget approval shall remain linked to actual Cost Records and cumulative spend.

24.494 Approval and Memory

Memory may describe prior approvals.

The Approval Control Plane remains authoritative.

24.495 Approval and Evidence

Every material Decision shall preserve structured evidence and rationale.

24.496 Approval and Intelligence Graph

The Intelligence Graph may represent:

- Principal has Grant,

- Grant permits Action,

- Approval authorises Plan,

- Mandate governs Agent,

- Decision supersedes Decision,

- and Execution used Authority Snapshot.

The Authority Control Plane remains authoritative.

24.497 Approval Observability

Operational views should expose:

- pending approvals,

- expiring approvals,

- active Mandates,

- denied actions,

- authority failures,

- and emergency access.

24.498 Approval Metric

Metrics may include:

- request count,

- approval latency,

- denial rate,

- expiry rate,

- revision rate,

- and stale-approval rate.

24.499 Autonomy Metric

Metrics may include:

- autonomous actions,

- escalations,

- boundary violations,

- manual corrections,

- rollback rate,

- and stop frequency.

24.500 Authority Metric

Metrics may include:

- active Grants,

- dormant Grants,

- excess privileges,

- orphan Permissions,

- and expired authority.

24.501 Approval Fatigue Metric

Repeated low-value prompts may indicate poor policy design.

24.502 Approval Quality Metric

Quality may consider whether Approvers received:

- sufficient context,

- accurate cost,

- exact target,

- and understandable consequences.

24.503 Boundary Violation Metric

Any attempted action outside a Mandate shall be recorded.

24.504 Denied Action Metric

Denied actions may indicate:

- correct enforcement,

- configuration problem,

- or attempted misuse.

24.505 Approval Dashboard

A dashboard may show:

- pending requests,

- requested action,

- risk,

- cost,

- data flow,

- expiry,

- and required Approvers.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.506 Mandate Dashboard

A Mandate dashboard may show:

- Agent,

- Project,

- actions,

- Budget,

- usage,

- expiry,

- incidents,

- and revocation control.

24.507 Authority Dashboard

An authority dashboard may show:

- Roles,

- Grants,

- Denials,

- delegation chains,

- and external permission drift.

24.508 Approval Incident

An Approval Incident is a material failure involving:

- missing approval,

- wrong approver,

- stale approval,

- replay,

- scope mismatch,

- forged Decision,

- or unauthorised execution.

24.509 Approval Incident Identity

Every material Approval Incident shall have stable identity.

24.510 Missing Approval Incident

A consequential action executed without required approval is severe.

24.511 Wrong-Version Approval Incident

An action used approval for a different Asset, Plan or policy Version.

24.512 Scope-Expansion Incident

Execution exceeded:

- Project,

- Provider,

- Budget,

- data,

- target,

- or action scope.

24.513 Approval Replay Incident

A consumed or expired approval was reused.

24.514 Forged Approval Incident

Approval evidence was altered or fabricated.

24.515 Approver Compromise Incident

A compromised Principal issued Decisions.

24.516 Authority Drift Incident

External Permissions exceeded canonical Grants.

24.517 Agent Autonomy Incident

An Agent acted outside its Mandate.

24.518 Financial Authority Incident

Spend exceeded or bypassed Budget approval.

24.519 Publication Authority Incident

Content was published:

- without approval,

- to wrong Account,

- with wrong Version,

- or outside schedule.

24.520 Destructive Authority Incident

Deletion or overwrite occurred without exact authority.

24.521 Credential Authority Incident

Credential material was exposed, exported or changed without authority.

24.522 Break-Glass Abuse Incident

Emergency authority was used outside the Incident purpose.

24.523 Incident Containment

Containment may include:

- stop Agent,

- revoke Tokens,

- suspend Grants,

- disable Provider path,

- freeze publication,

- rotate Credentials,

- or isolate Project.

24.524 Approval Incident Investigation

Investigation should inspect:

- Principal,

- authentication,

- Grant chain,

- Approval Request,

- Decision,

- Token,

- Plan,

- Execution,

- and external outcome.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.525 Approval Incident Recovery

Recovery may require:

- revoke action,

- unpublish,

- restore data,

- refund,

- rotate Credential,

- correct policy,

- and notify affected owners.

24.526 Authority Incident Learning

Incident learning may recommend narrower scope or stronger controls.

It shall not expand authority automatically.

24.527 Approval API

The Approval Control Plane should expose governed operations such as:

- create Approval Request,

- submit,

- inspect,

- approve,

- deny,

- partially approve,

- request revision,

- withdraw,

- revoke,

- expire,

- and export evidence.

24.528 Authority API

The Authority API should support:

- create Grant,

- assign Role,

- add Denial,

- delegate,

- suspend,

- revoke,

- evaluate,

- and inspect effective authority.

24.529 Mandate API

The Mandate API should support:

- propose Mandate,

- approve,

- activate,

- inspect usage,

- pause,

- narrow,

- revoke,

- expire,

- and review.

24.530 Execution Authorisation API

The API should support:

- request authorisation,

- validate Token,

- consume approval,

- revalidate,

- deny,

- and explain Decision.

24.531 Approval Search API

Search should support:

- Principal,

- Project,

- action,

- risk,

- state,

- subject,

- expiry,

- and approver.

24.532 Authority Graph API

The API should support inspection of:

- Grant chains,

- delegation,

- Role inheritance,

- Denials,

- and effective Permissions.

24.533 Emergency API

Emergency operations should support:

- stop,

- isolate,

- break-glass request,

- temporary Grant,

- and post-event review.

24.534 Stage 1 Authority Objective

Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy authority foundation required for representative Omnira operations.

Stage 1 shall prove:

- stable Principals,

- Roles,

- Authority Grants,

- explicit Denials,

- Approval Requests,

- Approval Decisions,

- Approval Tokens,

- Mandates,

- Execution Authorisation,

- revocation,

- expiry,

- and authority evidence.

24.535 Stage 1 Approval Objective

Stage 1 shall require explicit human approval for consequential actions, including:

- paid execution,

- publication,

- external message sending,

- destructive file change,

- Credential change,

- new Provider or Account,

- Confidential external processing,

- system-setting changes,

- and Budget increase.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.536 Stage 1 Bounded Autonomy Objective

Stage 1 may permit bounded autonomy for:

- draft generation,

- read-only analysis,

- approved low-risk file preparation,

- technical retries,

- reconciliation,

- and approved local processing.

Stage 1 shall not grant unrestricted autonomous publication, deletion, spending or policy change.

24.537 Stage 1 Principal Object

The Stage 1 Principal should include:

- principalId,

- type,

- Tenant,

- user or service relationship,

- state,

- authentication methods,

- and lifecycle.

24.538 Stage 1 Role Assignment Object

The Stage 1 Role Assignment should include:

- roleAssignmentId,

- Principal,

- Role,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- environment,

- start,

- expiry,

- issuer,

- and state.

24.539 Stage 1 Authority Grant Object

The Stage 1 Authority Grant should include:

- authorityGrantId,

- grantor,

- grantee,

- Domain,

- Permissions,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- action classes,

- resource scope,

- data scope,

- Budget limits,

- start,

- expiry,

- delegation,

- and Version.

24.540 Stage 1 Approval Request Object

The Stage 1 Approval Request should include:

- approvalRequestId,

- requester,

- subject,

- subject Version,

- action,

- purpose,

- Project,

- scope,

- Provider and Account,

- data disclosure,

- estimated cost,

- Budget impact,

- risk,

- reversibility,

- alternatives,

- required Approvers,

- expiry,

- and Version.

24.541 Stage 1 Approval Decision Object

The Stage 1 Approval Decision should include:

- approvalDecisionId,

- request Version,

- approver,

- authority basis,

- decision,

- approved scope,

- conditions,

- limits,

- exclusions,

- authentication assurance,

- effective time,

- expiry,

- and rationale.

24.542 Stage 1 Approval Token Object

The Stage 1 Approval Token should include:

- tokenId,

- Decision,

- subject,

- Execution,

- audience,

- scope,

- limits,

- use count,

- issuedAt,

- expiry,

- nonce,

- and signature.

24.543 Stage 1 Mandate Object

The Stage 1 Mandate should include:

- mandateId,

- owner,

- Agent or Service,

- objective,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Capabilities,

- actions,

- prohibited actions,

- Providers,

- Accounts,

- data classes,

- Budget,

- retry,

- fallback,

- time,

- frequency,

- escalation,

- state,

- and Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.544 Stage 1 Execution Authorisation Object

The Stage 1 Execution Authorisation should include:

- authorisationId,

- Execution,

- Plan Version,

- acting Principal,

- Project,

- Grant references,

- Approval references,

- Mandate,

- policy Versions,

- Budget state,

- decision,

- conditions,

- issuedAt,

- expiry,

- and evidence.

24.545 Stage 1 Approval Policies

Stage 1 should implement policies for:

- Provider spend,

- publication,

- external messages,

- code mutation,

- commit and push,

- deletion,

- overwrite,

- Credential operations,

- Confidential data transfer,

- Local Only policy changes,

- and mobile system settings.

24.546 Stage 1 Authority Levels

Stage 1 Agents should begin at:

- L0,

- L1,

- or L2

for most consequential domains.

L3 may be granted for narrowly defined reversible tasks.

L4 and above require reviewed Mandates and production evidence.

24.547 Stage 1 Human Approval

Human approval shall be required before:

- first paid Provider use,

- new recurring spend,

- publication,

- deleting canonical Assets,

- changing production Credentials,

- external Confidential processing,

- or expanding Agent authority.

24.548 Stage 1 Approval Interface

The interface shall show:

- exact action,

- exact Project,

- exact target Version,

- Provider and Account,

- data disclosure,

- cost,

- risk,

- reversibility,

- conditions,

- and expiry.

24.549 Stage 1 Mobile Approval

Mobile approvals shall support:

- approve,

- deny,

- request revision,

- inspect cost,

- inspect target,

- and revoke active Mandate.

High-risk authority changes shall require step-up authentication.

24.550 Stage 1 Revocation

Stage 1 shall support immediate revocation of:

- Grant,

- Role,

- Approval Token,

- Mandate,

- Session,

- Provider path,

- and Agent execution.

24.551 Stage 1 Emergency Stop

Stage 1 shall support:

- Agent stop,

- Project stop,

- publication stop,

- and Provider stop.

24.552 Stage 1 Audit Evidence

Every consequential action shall preserve:

- Principal,

- Request,

- Decision,

- Grant,

- Mandate,

- Token,

- Plan,

- Execution,

- and outcome.

24.553 Stage 1 Principal Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Principal has stable identity.

2. Principal type is explicit.

3. Tenant relationship is explicit.

4. state is explicit.

5. authentication methods are explicit.

6. suspended Principal cannot act.

7. disabled Principal cannot approve.

8. compromised Principal Tokens are revoked.

9. Agent remains distinct from Model.

10. Service remains distinct from Agent.

11. Device identity is explicit.

12. retired Principal remains historical.

13. Principal change is attributable.

14. duplicate identity is detected.

15. historical Principal state remains queryable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.554 Stage 1 Role Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Role has stable identity and Version.

2. Role Assignment has stable identity.

3. Principal is explicit.

4. Tenant is explicit.

5. Project is explicit.

6. environment is explicit.

7. start is explicit.

8. expiry is explicit.

9. issuer is explicit.

10. Role does not create universal authority.

11. Role combination respects Denials.

12. expired Role is inactive.

13. revoked Role invalidates access.

14. Role change is attributable.

15. historical Role Assignments remain queryable.

24.555 Stage 1 Authority-Grant Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Grant has stable identity and Version.

2. grantor is explicit.

3. grantee is explicit.

4. grantor authority is verified.

5. Authority Domain is explicit.

6. Permissions are explicit.

7. Tenant and Project are explicit.

8. action scope is explicit.

9. data scope is explicit.

10. resource scope is explicit.

11. limits are explicit.

12. expiry is explicit.

13. delegation right is explicit.

14. revocation propagates.

15. historical Grants remain queryable.

24.556 Stage 1 Denial Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Denial has stable identity.

2. subject Principal is explicit.

3. action is explicit.

4. scope is explicit.

5. reason is explicit.

6. effective time is explicit.

7. expiry is explicit.

8. Denial outranks ordinary Grant.

9. exception requires higher authority.

10. denied action fails before execution.

11. denial is explainable.

12. denial is auditable.

13. revoked Denial is attributable.

14. conflicting policies fail restrictive.

15. historical Denials remain queryable.

24.557 Stage 1 Delegation Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. source Grant is explicit.

2. source Grant permits delegation.

3. delegate is explicit.

4. delegated scope is narrower or equal.

5. delegated expiry does not exceed source.

6. delegation depth is enforced.

7. subdelegation is denied unless explicit.

8. revoking source revokes dependent Grant.

9. Agent delegation preserves Project.

10. delegation does not broaden data access.

11. delegation does not broaden Budget.

12. delegation does not add publication authority.

13. delegation evidence is immutable.

14. expired delegation cannot authorise queued work.

15. historical chain remains queryable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.558 Stage 1 Approval-Request Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Approval Request has stable identity and Version.

2. requester is explicit.

3. subject is explicit.

4. exact subject Version is explicit.

5. action is explicit.

6. purpose is explicit.

7. Project is explicit.

8. scope is explicit.

9. Provider and Account are explicit where applicable.

10. data disclosure is explicit.

11. cost and Budget impact are explicit.

12. risk is explicit.

13. reversibility is explicit.

14. required Approvers are explicit.

15. expiry is explicit.

24.559 Stage 1 Approval-Decision Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Approval Decision has stable identity.

2. exact Request Version is explicit.

3. approver is explicit.

4. approver eligibility is verified.

5. authority basis is explicit.

6. decision state is explicit.

7. approved scope is explicit.

8. conditions are explicit.

9. limits are explicit.

10. exclusions are explicit.

11. authentication assurance is explicit.

12. effective time is explicit.

13. expiry is explicit.

14. rationale is attributable.

15. historical Decisions remain immutable.

24.560 Stage 1 Approval-Version Tests

Representative tests should include:

1. Asset change invalidates old content approval.

2. Plan change invalidates old Plan approval.

3. Provider change triggers reapproval.

4. Account change triggers reapproval.

5. Budget increase triggers reapproval.

6. Classification change triggers revalidation.

7. consent change triggers revalidation.

24.580 Applied Example — Familje-Stunden August Publication

The August Familje-Stunden Package contains:

- approved PDF,

- approved audio,

- approved cover,

- metadata,

- Familje-Stunden Project,

- production Account,

- subscriber channel,

- release date,

- exact Package checksum,

- and visibility.

The Mandate permits:

- maximum spend,

- no publication,

- and mandatory human review.

The Agent may select Candidates for review.

It may not replace canonical Nova or Pling references or publish the image independently.
