24.582 Applied Example — Familje-Stunden Child Photo

A personalised activity uses a child’s photo.

The workflow requires:

- valid Consent Grant,

- Confidential or Local Only handling,

- exact parent-approved Deliverable,

- no public publication,

- no training,

- and deletion after the defined period.

Approval of the personalised worksheet does not authorise storage beyond the retention period.

24.583 Applied Example — The Prompt Daily Posting Mandate

The Prompt may receive a Standing Mandate to publish up to two approved posts per day.

The Mandate defines:

- Project Accounts,

- channels,

- content policy,

- source requirements,

- maximum spend,

- publication windows,

- and stop conditions.

Each post still requires:

- accepted Script,

- accepted media,

- rights eligibility,

- and exact publication payload.

The Mandate does not permit private-message replies or new Account connections.

24.584 Applied Example — Duplicate News Script

A workflow detects that a new Script is materially similar to a recently published Script.

The publication Mandate includes a duplicate-content prohibition.

The workflow pauses and escalates rather than publishing again.

Technical ability and schedule do not override the Mandate boundary.

24.585 Applied Example — GainPilot Programme Change

Arnold may analyse programme age and recommend a change at L1 or prepare a proposed Plan at L2.

Changing the user’s active programme requires:

- exact proposed Plan,

- rationale,

- affected schedule,

- and user approval

until an approved coaching Mandate permits bounded changes.

The Agent may not infer standing authority from prior accepted programme updates.

24.586 Applied Example — GainPilot Workout Adjustment

A Mandate may permit Arnold to replace one unavailable exercise with an approved equivalent when:

- target muscle group remains,

- injury constraints remain satisfied,

- equipment is available,

- and intensity remains within range.

Changing the programme goal or weekly structure requires escalation.

24.587 Applied Example — Local Only Training Analysis

The user classifies detailed health and training data as Local Only.

Atlas or Arnold may select local Models and Tools inside the approved Mandate.

No external fallback is permitted.

A proposal to use an external Provider requires a separate policy and Transfer Decision.

A video workflow requests approval for:

- one Provider,

- one Account,

- three Candidates,

- maximum cost,

- approved references,

- and no publication.

Technical retries are allowed twice.

A fourth Candidate or another Provider requires new approval.

24.589 Applied Example — ElevenLabs Narration

The Approval Request identifies:

- Script Version,

- Voice Profile,

- Provider Account,

- character count,

- estimated cost,

- Consent Grant,

- and permitted reuse.

The Approval Decision permits narration generation only.

- exact Project,

- exact reference Assets,

- maximum credits,

- exact Scene,

- and required downloads.

The manual operation remains attributable.

24.591 Applied Example — New Provider Request

The Router finds a cheaper Provider not present in the approved Provider set.

It may recommend the Provider.

It may not use it until:

- Provider Registry review,

- terms review,

- privacy eligibility,

- Connection approval,

- and Budget approval

are complete.

24.592 Applied Example — Provider Account Change

The approved Provider remains the same, but the Account changes from user-owned paid plan to a free Account.

Because:

- terms,

- retention,

- commercial rights,

- and billing

may differ, the old approval does not transfer automatically.

A Provider silently updates the Model serving one alias.

The Model Registry detects Version drift.

High-risk Mandates pause until:

- evaluation,

- policy,

- and approval

are revalidated.

24.594 Applied Example — Code Modification

A code Agent is approved to modify files in one worktree.

The Grant permits:

- read,

- edit,

- test,

- and create an unstaged diff.

It does not permit:

- push,

- merge,

- deploy,

- delete unrelated files,

- or modify another repository.

24.595 Applied Example — Commit and Push

After review, the user approves one exact diff and commit subject.

The Agent creates the commit.

Push remains a separate action unless explicitly included.

A later file change invalidates the original diff approval.

24.596 Applied Example — Pull Request Merge

A pull request has passing checks.

Passing checks do not create merge authority.

- authorised Approver,

- exact commit,

- target branch,

- and merge method.

24.597 Applied Example — Production Deployment

A merged change is ready for deployment.

Deployment Approval identifies:

- environment,

- release Version,

- migration status,

- rollback,

- monitoring,

- and maintenance window.

Merge approval does not authorise production deployment.

24.598 Applied Example — File Deletion

An Agent proposes deleting duplicate preview images.

The Approval Request shows:

- exact paths,

- count,

- checksums,

- duplicate evidence,

- canonical retained copies,

- and recovery state.

Deletion authority applies only to listed files.

The Agent may not delete adjacent folders for convenience.

24.599 Applied Example — Repository Migration

A repository must move from one directory to another.

The bounded migration approval defines:

- source path,

- target path,

- `.git` preservation,

- no-overwrite rule,

- checksum or Git verification,

- rollback,

- and source retention until confirmation.

The Agent may not merge unrelated organised workspace content automatically.

24.600 Applied Example — Credential Rotation

A Provider Credential is suspected to be exposed.

Incident authority permits:

- revoke old Credential,

- create replacement,

- update approved Connection references,

- and verify service recovery.

It does not permit exporting the new Secret to ordinary logs or Agent Memory.

24.601 Applied Example — Subscription Upgrade

A Provider offers a higher plan.

The Approval Request shows:

- monthly cost,

- billing owner,

- renewal,

- cancellation,

- additional rights,

- and Project allocation.

Approval of one generation does not approve the subscription upgrade.

24.602 Applied Example — Mobile System Restart

A mobile Node becomes unresponsive.

Atlas may recommend restart at L1.

The user approves the exact device restart.

The approval does not permit:

- factory reset,

- data deletion,

- network changes,

- or unrelated system settings.

24.605 Applied Example — Scheduled Publication After Revocation

A post is approved and scheduled.

Before publication, the user revokes the Mandate.

The Connector revalidates authority at run time and blocks publication.

24.606 Applied Example — Approval Expiry

A Budget approval expires at midnight.

A queued Provider job begins after midnight.

The job is denied and returned for reapproval.

24.607 Applied Example — Price Increase

A Provider raises the estimated cost above the approved maximum.

The Fabric pauses.

It may present:

- lower Candidate count,

- alternate approved Provider,

- delayed execution,

- or higher Budget request.

24.608 Applied Example — Unknown Payment Outcome

A purchase request times out after submission.

The system records unknown outcome.

It does not repeat the purchase merely because the approval Token remains valid.

Reconciliation determines whether the charge occurred.

24.609 Applied Example — Partial Approval

A user approves:

- Script generation,

- image generation,

- and local composition

but denies video generation.

The Plan executes only the approved branches.

The denied video branch remains blocked.

24.610 Applied Example — Approval with Conditions

A publication is approved with conditions:

- correct one spelling error,

- preserve all other content,

- and use the approved account.

The corrected Version requires automated diff verification.

Any additional material edit triggers new review.

24.611 Applied Example — Dual Approval for Tenant Deletion

Deleting an entire Tenant requires:

- Tenant owner approval,

- Platform recovery approval,

- strong authentication,

- waiting period,

- export option,

- and verified deletion Plan.

One administrator cannot complete the action alone.

24.680 Future Approval and Authority Architecture

Future versions may support:

- policy-as-code authorisation,

- cryptographically signed approvals,

- capability tokens,

- decentralised identity,

- continuous risk-based authentication,

- programmable Mandates,

- formal authority proofs,

- privacy-preserving approval,

- hardware-backed mobile approval,

- multi-party computation,

- and autonomous-domain certification.

Future evolution must preserve:

- explicit human ownership,

- bounded scope,

- revocation,

- evidence,

- and non-waivable policy.

24.681 Policy-as-Code Authority

Human-readable policy may compile into machine-enforceable authorisation rules.

The compiled form shall remain traceable to an approved Version.

24.682 Capability Token

A Capability Token may grant one exact action without exposing broad Account Credentials.

24.683 Attenuated Token

A Token may be narrowed when delegated.

It shall not be broadened.

24.684 Cryptographic Approval

Approvals may be signed with:

- passkey,

- hardware key,

- device key,

- or organisational certificate.

24.685 Verifiable Approval Chain

A service may verify:

- Approver identity,

- Grant chain,

- Request Version,

- and Token integrity.

24.688 Behavioural Risk Signal

24.689 Programmable Mandate

A Mandate may encode machine-verifiable:

- Budget,

- time,

- actions,

- Providers,

- and escalation.

24.690 Formal Authority Proof

24.692 Hardware-Backed Approval

A trusted device may bind approval to:

- Principal,

- exact request hash,

- and secure display.

24.693 Multi-Party Approval

High-risk actions may use threshold signatures or distributed approval.

24.694 Autonomous-Domain Certification

A mature domain may receive a certification describing:

- tested controls,

- risk limits,

- monitoring,

- and permitted autonomy.

24.695 Certification Expiry

- Agent change,

- policy change,

- Incident,

- or defined time.

24.696 Continuous Mandate Evaluation

The system may continuously assess:

- boundary compliance,

- cost,

- incidents,

- and Quality

to maintain or suspend a Mandate.

24.697 Automated Authority Narrowing

The Fabric may automatically narrow or suspend authority when risk increases.

It shall not automatically broaden authority.

24.698 Dynamic Budget Mandate

A future Mandate may adjust spend inside a human-approved formula and maximum ceiling.

24.699 Outcome-Based Mandate

A Mandate may continue only while verified outcomes meet defined thresholds.

24.700 Reputation-Aware Delegation

Agent or service history may influence recommended scope.

Reputation shall not replace explicit authority.

24.701 Consent-Aware Authorisation

Consent state may automatically block actions that were otherwise authorised.

24.702 Rights-Aware Authorisation

Rights eligibility may automatically block publication or training.

24.711 Approval Success Criteria

The approval architecture succeeds when:

- every material request identifies exact scope,

- Approvers understand consequences,

- Decisions bind to exact Versions,

- stale approvals are invalidated,

- Tokens cannot replay,

- and denied actions remain blocked.

24.712 Authority Success Criteria

The authority architecture succeeds when:

- every action has an accountable Principal,

- Grants are scoped and expiring,

- delegation cannot broaden authority,

- Denials are enforceable,

- revocation propagates,

- and external Permissions match canonical governance.

24.713 Bounded Autonomy Success Criteria

Bounded autonomy succeeds when:

- Agents operate without unnecessary interruption,

- all actions remain inside explicit Mandates,

- deviations trigger escalation,

- cost and data boundaries are enforced,

- humans can stop the system,

- and autonomy can be reduced without losing evidence.

24.714 Approval Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- approval lacks exact subject Version,

- cost or disclosure is hidden,

- natural-language ambiguity authorises broad action,

- or approval can be replayed.

24.736 Approval, Authority and Bounded Autonomy Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No authentication event becomes action authority.

- No Role becomes universal permission.

- No access Grant becomes approval for a consequential action.

- No approval becomes consent, rights or ownership.

- No Budget becomes unrestricted spending authority.

- No content approval becomes publication authority automatically.

- No Plan approval survives material Plan change silently.

- No Approval Decision applies to an unspecified Version.

- No Approval Token may be replayed or transferred.

- No Agent approves its own authority expansion.

- No delegated authority exceeds the source Grant.

- No Authority Level overrides explicit Denial or policy.

- No standing Mandate lacks scope, limits, expiry and revocation.

- No retry or fallback escapes the approved envelope.

- No unknown outcome authorises blind repetition.

- No scheduled action relies on stale authority.

- No deletion or overwrite follows from ordinary write access.

- No emergency authority becomes permanent.

- No revoked authority returns through cache, queue, device or backup.

- No approval or authority failure bypasses the Intelligence Fabric.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
24.737 Closing Statement

Approval, authority and bounded autonomy determine who may decide, who may act and how far Omnira may proceed without asking again.

Identity defines who or what is acting.

Authentication establishes confidence in that identity.

The Role describes expected responsibility.

The Authority Grant defines permitted power.

The Denial defines what remains forbidden.

The Approval Request describes the exact Decision required.

The Approval Decision binds an authorised human or governance process to an exact scope and Version.

The Approval Token carries that Decision safely to the execution boundary.

The Authority Level describes the general operating posture.

The Autonomy Envelope defines every boundary that shall constrain independent action.

The Mandate activates bounded autonomy for one objective or domain.

The Execution Authorisation proves that one exact Plan may begin or continue.

The Escalation Record preserves every deviation that requires human judgement.

The Revocation Record ensures that authority can stop.

The Emergency Stop protects the user and Project when the system must halt immediately.

The Break-Glass procedure permits exceptional recovery without converting emergency access into ordinary power.

For Familje-Stunden, this architecture ensures that:

- Atlas may prepare August content without publishing it,

- Nova and Pling Assets cannot become canonical without review,

- child-facing media receives the correct Approvers,

- private family material remains outside publication authority,

- and one approved Package cannot be replaced silently before release.

For The Prompt, it ensures that:

- research, Script generation and visual production may operate through bounded workflows,

- daily publication remains tied to exact Project Accounts and policies,

- duplicate or materially changed content is escalated,

- and private-message access never appears inside a general social publishing Mandate.

For GainPilot, it ensures that:

- Arnold may analyse programme history and prepare recommendations,

- workout substitutions remain inside approved coaching bounds,

- active programme changes remain user-governed,

- health and Local Only constraints cannot be bypassed,

- and coaching autonomy can increase only after evidence and explicit delegation.

For Atlas, it ensures that:

- broad intelligence does not become unlimited authority,

- Project orchestration does not become cross-Project access,

- Model or Provider changes do not broaden its Permissions,

- Memory does not create authority,

- and every consequential action remains tied to a human-owned governance chain.

For Omnira, it ensures that:

- humans,

- Agents,

- Services,

- Devices,

- Providers,

- Tools,

- workflows,

- publication systems,

- financial systems,

- storage systems,

- and recovery procedures

participate through one canonical authority architecture.

The user may approve an objective.

The Project owner may define a Mandate.

The Planner may create a valid Plan.

The Router may select an eligible resource.

The Agent may operate inside the approved Envelope.

The Adapter may execute the authorised call.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
The Provider may return a result.

The Connector may create an external side effect.

None of those components may expand the authority granted by the user.

No action without a Principal.

No Principal action without authority.

No authority without scope.

No approval without an exact subject.

No consequential execution without current authorisation.

No standing autonomy without a Mandate.

No Mandate without limits.

No retry without bounded authority.

No fallback outside the approved set.

No publication from content approval alone.

No deletion from write access alone.

No spend beyond the approved Budget.

No delegation beyond the delegator.

No Agent self-authorisation.

No stale approval at the execution boundary.

No emergency access without evidence and expiry.

The user retains sovereign decision authority.

The Project retains operational and financial boundaries.

Omnira retains policy, enforcement and revocation.

The Fabric may act independently only where the human has deliberately defined the space in which independent action is permitted.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical architecture, object model, lifecycle, governance boundaries, operating practices and conformance requirements for observability, audit and Incident Response within the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

It establishes:

- how the Fabric observes Requests, Plans, Executions, Attempts, Providers, Models, Tools, Agents, Nodes, queues, Assets, Memory and external side effects,

- how Metrics, logs, traces, Events, health signals, evidence and audit records remain distinct,

- how observability supports understanding without becoming an uncontrolled copy of protected data,

- how every material Execution receives end-to-end correlation,

- how technical state remains distinguishable from semantic success, accepted quality, external completion and business outcome,

- how service health, resource health, Provider health, Model health and workflow health are measured,

- how latency, throughput, saturation, error, quality, cost, privacy and authority signals remain visible,

- how telemetry remains scoped by Tenant, Project, Agent, Environment, resource and Classification,

- how structured logging avoids exposing full prompts, Outputs, private messages and Secrets,

- how distributed traces preserve causal execution paths across local and external systems,

- how Metrics and dashboards preserve operational truth without fabricating certainty,

- how alerting distinguishes symptoms, causes, risks, anomalies and confirmed Incidents,

- how alerts remain actionable, deduplicated, prioritised and owned,

- how audit records preserve who did what, to which object, under which authority, when and with what result,

- how audit differs from ordinary logs and immutable execution evidence,

- how user, Agent, administrator and emergency actions remain attributable,

- how audit integrity, retention, access and export are governed,

- how authority changes, approvals, data transfers, publication, deletion, Credential operations and policy changes receive elevated audit,

- how Incident detection, declaration, classification, containment, investigation, recovery and closure are governed,

- how privacy, security, reliability, quality, cost, rights, consent and authority Incidents remain distinguishable,

- how Incident severity and priority are determined,

- how command, ownership, communication and escalation operate,

- how evidence is preserved without exposing unnecessary content,

- how unknown outcomes, partial completion and delayed external effects are reconciled,

- how post-Incident learning becomes reviewed Derived Learning rather than folklore,

- how corrective actions remain owned, testable and traceable,

- how chaos testing, game days, fault injection and recovery exercises validate resilience,

- how Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy observability, audit and Incident Response foundation,

- and how future autonomy shall remain observable, stoppable and accountable.

A Metric is not an Event.

An Event is not a log line.

A log line is not an audit record.

An audit record is not complete execution evidence.

A trace is not proof of business completion.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
A health check is not proof of semantic correctness.

An alert is not an Incident automatically.

An Incident is not merely an exception.

An error is not always a failure.

A failed Attempt is not always a failed Execution.

A successful Attempt is not always a successful Outcome.

A Provider-reported completion is not automatically an accepted Asset.

A dashboard is not the source of truth.

Absence of telemetry is not proof of health.

High availability is not correctness.

Low latency is not quality.

Averages are not sufficient for tail behaviour.

A high alert count is not proof of good monitoring.

A complete audit trail does not justify unrestricted access to its contents.

An administrator’s ability to operate infrastructure does not automatically permit reading user content.

Incident urgency does not erase classification, authority or evidence requirements.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

Developer experience, testing and conformance are expanded in Chapter 26.

Stage 1 implementation architecture is expanded in Chapter 27.

Rollout, migration, anti-patterns and future evolution are expanded in Chapter 28.

Implementation and operational conformance must be verified separately.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 25.2 Purpose of Observability, Audit and Incident Response
text:
25.2 Purpose of Observability, Audit and Incident Response

The Intelligence Fabric coordinates work across:

- user interfaces,

- Agents,

- Planner,

- Router,

- Scheduler,

- Admission Controller,

- Provider Adapters,

- Model Deployments,

- local Nodes,

- Tools,

- MCP servers,

- webhooks,

- queues,

- Asset stores,

- Memory,

- approval services,

- publication systems,

- and external platforms.

Those systems may fail through:

- unavailable Providers,

- incorrect Routing,

- queue backlog,

- latency spikes,

- Model regression,

- corrupted Assets,

- duplicate publication,

- wrong-Project access,

- Credential exposure,

- Budget overrun,

- stale approval,

- privacy leakage,

- rights failure,

- consent revocation,

- unknown external outcome,

- and human error.

Without canonical observability and Incident Response, Omnira could:

- know that something failed but not which Step,

- know that a Provider returned success but not whether publication occurred,

- detect high latency without seeing queue saturation,

- see cost growth without identifying retry storms,

- lose the relationship between a user action and an external side effect,

- hide privacy leakage inside ordinary logs,

- allow cross-Project retrieval to remain unnoticed,

- react repeatedly to duplicate alerts,

- restore service without resolving the underlying risk,

- or close an Incident without proving recovery.

The architecture exists to ensure that Omnira can answer:

- What is happening now?

- What happened previously?

- Which components participated?

- Which Tenant and Project were affected?

- Which Request, Plan, Execution and Attempt are involved?

- Which Provider, Account, Model, Tool and Node were used?

- Where is latency being introduced?

- Which queue or resource is saturated?

- Which error class occurred?

- Which authority and policy applied?

- Which data crossed which boundary?

- Which side effects occurred?

- Which outcomes remain unknown?

- Who detected the problem?

- Who owns the response?

- What was contained?

- What remains at risk?

- How was recovery verified?

- Which changes prevent recurrence?

- Which learning may safely influence future behaviour?

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.3 Observability

Observability is the capability to understand internal system state and behaviour from governed external signals and recorded evidence.

Observability shall support:

- detection,

- diagnosis,

- explanation,

- forecasting,

- capacity planning,

- reliability management,

- security monitoring,

- privacy monitoring,

- cost governance,

- and Incident Response.

25.4 Monitoring

Monitoring evaluates known signals, thresholds and expected conditions.

Monitoring is a subset of observability.

25.5 Telemetry

Telemetry is machine-produced operational data emitted by systems and resources.

Telemetry may include:

- Metrics,

- logs,

- traces,

- health observations,

- profiles,

- events,

- and resource measurements.

25.6 Metric

A Metric is a numerical measurement aggregated over dimensions and time.

Examples include:

- request count,

- latency,

- queue depth,

- error rate,

- token usage,

- cost,

- GPU utilisation,

- and approval delay.

25.7 Log

A log is a timestamped structured or textual record produced by a component.

Logs may support:

- debugging,

- operation,

- security,

- and reconstruction.

Logs are not automatically canonical evidence or audit records.

25.8 Trace

A Trace is a causal representation of one distributed operation across services, Steps, Attempts and external calls.

25.9 Span

A Span represents one bounded operation inside a Trace.

25.10 Event

An Event is a canonical statement that something meaningful occurred.

Examples include:

- Execution started,

- approval granted,

- Provider callback received,

- Asset accepted,

- publication verified,

- Grant revoked,

- or Incident declared.

25.11 Health Signal

A Health Signal describes the observed ability of a component or resource to serve its intended function.

25.12 Audit

Audit is the governed, attributable and reviewable record of material actions, Decisions, authority use and changes to protected or consequential state.

25.13 Incident

An Incident is an unplanned event or condition that causes or threatens material harm to:

- availability,

- reliability,

- correctness,

- privacy,

- security,

- rights,

- authority,

- cost,

- user trust,

- Project continuity,

- or external outcomes.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 25.15 Observability, Audit and Incident Response Control Plane
25.16 Canonical Observability, Audit and Incident Objects
text:
25.14 Incident Response

Incident Response is the governed lifecycle for:

- detection,

- triage,

- declaration,

- containment,

- investigation,

- recovery,

- communication,

- closure,

- and learning.

25.15 Observability, Audit and Incident Response Control Plane

The Observability, Audit and Incident Response Control Plane is the governed collection of services and canonical objects responsible for:

- telemetry collection,

- correlation,

- normalisation,

- aggregation,

- health evaluation,

- alerting,

- audit recording,

- Incident management,

- evidence preservation,

- escalation,

- response coordination,

- recovery verification,

- and post-Incident learning.

It shall integrate with:

- Capability Requests,

- Planning,

- Routing,

- Cost,

- Quality,

- Reliability,

- Scheduling,

- Adapters,

- Credentials,

- Assets,

- Rights,

- Consent,

- Memory,

- Classification,

- Authority,

- Approvals,

- and Developer Conformance.

25.16 Canonical Observability, Audit and Incident Objects

The canonical architecture should include or reference:

- Telemetry Record,

- Metric Definition,

- Metric Point,

- Metric Series,

- Log Record,

- Trace,

- Span,

- Correlation Context,

- Operational Event,

- Health Observation,

- Health Evaluation,

- Service Level Indicator,

- Service Level Objective,

- Error Budget,

- Dashboard,

- Query,

- Alert Rule,

- Alert Instance,

- Alert Group,

- Notification,

- On-Call Assignment,

- Audit Event,

- Audit Record,

- Audit Trail,

- Audit Export,

- Incident,

- Incident Severity,

- Incident Priority,

- Incident Timeline,

- Incident Role Assignment,

- Incident Evidence Bundle,

- Containment Action,

- Recovery Action,

- Verification Record,

- Communication Record,

- Post-Incident Review,

- Corrective Action,

- Runbook,

- Playbook,

- Chaos Experiment,

- Game Day,

- and Observability Incident.

25.17 Observability Scope

Every observability signal shall identify applicable scope where relevant.

Scope may include:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- Agent,

- Request,

- Execution,

- Attempt,

- workflow,

- Provider,

- Account,

- Model,

- Tool,

- Node,

- queue,

- Asset,

- Memory Domain,

- and Incident.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.18 Scope Before Aggregation

Aggregation shall not erase Tenant, Project or authority boundaries.

25.19 Scope Ambiguity

Ambiguous scope shall reduce trust and may require quarantine of the telemetry.

25.20 Correlation Context

Correlation Context is the canonical set of identifiers and Versions used to relate activity across components.

It should include or reference:

- correlationId,

- traceId,

- Request ID,

- Execution ID,

- Attempt ID,

- Tenant ID,

- Project ID,

- Agent ID,

- workflow ID,

- Plan Version,

- policy Versions,

- and Incident ID where applicable.

25.21 Correlation Context Identity

Every material operation shall carry stable correlation.

25.22 Correlation Propagation

Correlation shall propagate through:

- API calls,

- queue messages,

- webhook subscriptions,

- Provider requests,

- callbacks,

- local Tool invocations,

- Asset creation,

- audit records,

- and external verification.

25.23 Correlation Loss

Loss of correlation shall be visible as an observability defect.

25.24 External Correlation

Provider request IDs, job IDs and event IDs shall be linked to Omnira correlation without replacing canonical identity.

25.25 User Correlation

User-facing activity may reference a safe operation identifier without exposing internal infrastructure details.

25.26 Telemetry Record

A Telemetry Record is one governed operational observation.

It shall include or reference:

- telemetryRecordId,

- type,

- producer,

- scope,

- correlation,

- observedAt,

- recordedAt,

- value or payload,

- classification,

- integrity,

- retention,

- and provenance.

25.27 Telemetry Record Identity

Every persistent material Telemetry Record shall have stable identity or a stable series relationship.

25.28 Telemetry Producer

The producer may be:

- Service,

- Agent,

- Tool,

- Provider Adapter,

- Node,

- Runtime,

- database,

- queue,

- or external platform.

25.29 Observed Time

Observed time identifies when the state or event occurred.

25.30 Recorded Time

Recorded time identifies when Omnira stored the telemetry.

25.31 Ingestion Delay

The difference between observed and recorded time shall remain measurable.

25.32 Clock Source

Telemetry shall identify or inherit the relevant clock source.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.33 Monotonic Duration

Elapsed time should be measured using a monotonic clock where possible.

25.34 Wall-Clock Timestamp

Human and distributed correlation requires an authoritative wall-clock timestamp.

25.35 Clock Skew

Clock skew shall be detected, bounded and visible.

25.36 Time Zone

Canonical operational timestamps should use UTC.

Local time may be displayed for users and schedules.

25.37 Time Precision

Precision shall match the operational need without creating misleading accuracy.

25.38 Telemetry Integrity

Material telemetry should include integrity controls appropriate to its risk.

25.39 Telemetry Loss

Telemetry loss shall be measured rather than hidden.

25.40 Telemetry Sampling

Sampling may reduce volume.

The sampling method and excluded signal classes shall remain explicit.

25.41 Mandatory Unsampled Signals

The following should not be omitted through ordinary sampling:

- authority changes,

- Approval Decisions,

- publication,

- deletion,

- Credential operations,

- privacy boundary violations,

- cross-Tenant access,

- Incident state changes,

- and emergency authority use.

25.42 Telemetry Classification

Telemetry inherits the sensitivity of included content and metadata.

25.43 Telemetry Minimisation

Operational usefulness shall be achieved with the minimum protected payload.

25.44 Metric Definition

A Metric Definition describes one canonical measurement.

It shall include or reference:

- metricDefinitionId,

- name,

- description,

- unit,

- type,

- dimensions,

- aggregation,

- source,

- scope,

- retention,

- and Version.

25.45 Metric Definition Identity

Every Metric Definition shall have stable identity and Version.

25.46 Metric Name

Metric names shall be:

- stable,

- meaningful,

- non-secret,

- and implementation-independent where practical.

25.47 Metric Unit

The unit shall be explicit.

Examples include:

- seconds,

- milliseconds,

- bytes,

- requests,

- tokens,

- currency,

- percentage,

- and count.

25.48 Metric Type

Metric types may include:

- counter,

- gauge,

- histogram,

- summary,

- distribution,

- rate,

- and derived ratio.

25.49 Counter

A Counter increases over time and may reset after process restart.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.50 Gauge

A Gauge represents a current measured value.

Examples include:

- queue depth,

- active workers,

- memory usage,

- and remaining credits.

25.51 Histogram

A Histogram records a distribution over defined buckets.

25.52 Distribution

A Distribution preserves statistical shape across observations.

25.53 Rate

A Rate represents change per time unit.

25.54 Ratio

A Ratio compares two governed measurements.

The numerator and denominator shall be explicit.

25.55 Metric Point

A Metric Point records one value at one time and dimensional scope.

25.56 Metric Series

A Metric Series groups Metric Points sharing the same definition and dimensions.

25.57 Metric Dimension

Dimensions may include:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- Provider,

- Model,

- Capability,

- action class,

- error class,

- risk class,

- and result state.

25.58 High-Cardinality Dimension

High-cardinality values such as:

- user ID,

- Request ID,

- filename,

- URL,

- message ID,

- or Asset title

should not be ordinary Metric dimensions.

25.59 Metric Cardinality Control

Cardinality limits shall protect:

- cost,

- performance,

- privacy,

- and query reliability.

25.60 Metric Aggregation

Aggregation shall identify:

- function,

- interval,

- scope,

- and missing-data semantics.

25.61 Average

Average alone shall not be used to represent tail-sensitive performance.

25.62 Percentile

Percentiles such as:

- p50,

- p90,

- p95,

- p99,

- and p99.9

shall be used where latency or quality distributions matter.

25.63 Tail Latency

Tail latency shall be monitored separately from typical latency.

25.64 Missing Data

Missing Metric data shall remain distinct from zero.

25.65 Metric Freshness

Dashboards and Decisions shall display Metric freshness where material.

25.66 Derived Metric

A Derived Metric is calculated from canonical Metric Series.

Its formula and Version shall be explicit.

25.67 Metric Baseline

A baseline describes expected behaviour over a relevant period.

25.68 Baseline Scope

Baselines shall remain scoped to:

- resource,

- Environment,

- Project,

- Capability,

- and time pattern.

25.69 Seasonal Baseline

Time-of-day, weekday and campaign seasonality may affect expected values.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.70 Static Threshold

A static threshold triggers when a Metric crosses a fixed boundary.

25.71 Dynamic Threshold

A dynamic threshold adapts to a governed baseline.

It shall preserve method, sensitivity and limitations.

25.72 Anomaly Score

An anomaly score indicates deviation.

It does not prove failure.

25.73 Golden Signals

The Fabric should observe at minimum:

- latency,

- traffic,

- errors,

- saturation,

- quality,

- cost,

- and policy denial.

25.74 Latency Metric

Latency shall be decomposed into phases where possible.

25.75 Traffic Metric

Traffic may include:

- Requests,

- Executions,

- Attempts,

- tokens,

- Assets,

- and external events.

25.76 Error Metric

Errors shall be classified rather than counted only as one total.

25.77 Saturation Metric

Saturation may include:

- queue age,

- worker occupancy,

- concurrency,

- GPU memory,

- Provider quota,

- and connection-pool pressure.

25.78 Quality Metric

Quality Metrics may include:

- mandatory failure rate,

- acceptance rate,

- human revision rate,

- benchmark score,

- and identity consistency.

25.79 Cost Metric

Cost Metrics may include:

- estimated cost,

- actual cost,

- reserved cost,

- cost variance,

- cost per accepted Asset,

- and retry waste.

25.80 Policy Denial Metric

Denied or blocked operations shall be measured by reason class without exposing protected details.

25.81 Security Metric

Security Metrics may include:

- failed authentication,

- revoked Token use,

- Secret access denial,

- and anomalous authority requests.

25.82 Privacy Metric

Privacy Metrics may include:

- blocked egress,

- redaction failure,

- wrong-scope retrieval,

- and retention expiry backlog.

25.83 Rights Metric

Rights Metrics may include:

- unresolved Assets,

- expired licences,

- missing consent,

- and blocked publication packages.

25.84 Approval Metric

Approval Metrics may include:

- pending count,

- decision latency,

- expiry,

- denial,

- and stale approval.

25.85 Memory Metric

Memory Metrics may include:

- retrieval relevance,

- stale Memory use,

- conflict count,

- and wrong-scope denial.

25.86 Audit Metric

Audit Metrics may include:

- missing mandatory records,

- delayed ingestion,

- integrity failure,

- and access-review exceptions.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.87 Log Record

A Log Record is one timestamped structured record produced by a component.

It shall include or reference:

- logRecordId or stream identity,

- severity,

- producer,

- correlation,

- scope,

- message template,

- structured fields,

- observedAt,

- classification,

- and retention.

25.88 Log Severity

Canonical severities may include:

- trace,

- debug,

- informational,

- notice,

- warning,

- error,

- critical,

- and emergency.

25.89 Log Severity Meaning

Severity shall reflect operational impact and required response.

It shall not be used inconsistently across components.

25.90 Structured Log

Structured logs should use typed fields rather than relying solely on free text.

25.91 Log Message Template

Templates shall avoid dynamic protected content in the message body.

25.92 Log Field

Fields may include:

- operation,

- state,

- duration,

- error class,

- resource ID,

- correlation,

- and bounded result metadata.

25.93 Payload Logging

Full payload logging shall be prohibited by default.

25.94 Prompt Logging

Full prompts shall not enter ordinary logs by default.

25.95 Output Logging

Full Model Outputs shall not enter ordinary logs by default.

25.96 Private Message Logging

Private communications shall not enter ordinary logs.

25.97 Credential Logging

Passwords, Tokens, keys and Secret values shall never enter ordinary logs.

25.98 Sensitive Header Logging

Authentication and Provider headers shall be redacted.

25.99 URL Logging

URLs may contain:

- Tokens,

- query data,

- filenames,

- user IDs,

- and signed access.

They shall be sanitised.

25.100 File Path Logging

File paths may reveal:

- user names,

- Project names,

- private directories,

- and internal architecture.

Only necessary path context shall be retained.

25.101 Error Logging

Errors shall preserve:

- class,

- code,

- component,

- operation,

- retryability,

- and correlation

without exposing unnecessary payload.

25.102 Stack Trace

Stack traces may be restricted to developer or Incident views.

25.103 Debug Logging

Debug logging shall be time-bounded and Environment-scoped.

25.104 Production Debug Capture

Expanded production capture requires:

- approval,

- Incident scope,

- short retention,

- access restriction,

- and cleanup.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.105 Log Sampling

High-volume informational logs may be sampled.

Errors, authority events and material side effects should not be sampled away.

25.106 Log Rotation

Log rotation shall prevent unbounded local storage growth.

25.107 Log Retention

Retention shall reflect:

- operational need,

- Classification,

- audit requirement,

- and privacy.

25.108 Log Integrity

Material security and audit-supporting logs may require append-only or tamper-evident storage.

25.109 Log Access

Access shall be role-, Project-, Tenant- and purpose-scoped.

25.110 Log Export

Exports shall be minimised and classified.

25.111 Log Deletion

Deletion and retention changes shall remain attributable.

25.112 Trace

A Trace represents one end-to-end causal operation.

It shall include or reference:

- traceId,

- root operation,

- Request,

- Execution,

- spans,

- scope,

- start,

- end,

- result,

- and sampling state.

25.113 Trace Identity

Every material distributed operation should have stable Trace identity.

25.114 Root Span

The Root Span represents the top-level operation.

25.115 Child Span

A Child Span represents an operation caused by another Span.

25.116 Span Identity

Every Span shall have identity unique inside its Trace.

25.117 Span Parent

Parent relationships shall preserve causal structure.

25.118 Span Link

Span links may connect:

- asynchronous work,

- retries,

- batches,

- or fan-out.

They shall remain distinct from parent-child causality.

25.119 Span Attributes

Attributes may include:

- component,

- Capability,

- Provider,

- Model,

- Step,

- result,

- and bounded resource metadata.

25.120 Span Events

Span Events may record:

- retry,

- callback,

- checkpoint,

- approval,

- and state transition.

25.121 Span Status

Span status may be:

- unset,

- succeeded,

- failed,

- cancelled,

- timed out,

- or unknown.

25.122 Span Duration

Span duration shall use reliable elapsed-time measurement.

25.123 Trace Sampling

Sampling shall preserve high-risk and failed workflows according to policy.

25.124 Head Sampling

Head sampling decides at Trace start.

25.125 Tail Sampling

Tail sampling decides after observing outcome.

It may preserve:

- failures,

- slow traces,

- high-cost traces,

- or policy violations.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.126 Trace Baggage

Cross-service baggage shall be minimised and shall not carry Secrets or protected payload.

25.127 Trace Context Trust

Inbound trace identifiers from untrusted systems shall be validated and isolated.

25.128 Trace Discontinuity

Missing spans or broken propagation shall remain visible.

25.129 External Provider Span

An external call Span shall identify:

- Provider,

- Product,

- Account,

- Adapter,

- request correlation,

- start,

- acknowledgement,

- completion,

- and result.

25.130 Queue Span

Queue traces should distinguish:

- enqueue,

- queue wait,

- dequeue,

- lease,

- processing,

- acknowledgement,

- and redelivery.

25.131 Human Review Span

Human review may be represented as a long asynchronous Span or linked workflow state.

Human identity and privacy shall remain protected.

25.132 Approval Span

Approval waiting time shall remain separate from execution latency.

25.133 Evaluation Span

Evaluation cost and latency shall remain visible.

25.134 Publication Span

Publication traces shall include:

- submission,

- external acknowledgement,

- verification,

- and final visibility state.

25.135 Critical Path

The critical path is the sequence determining end-to-end completion time.

25.136 Critical-Path Analysis

Parallel Steps shall not be added naively when calculating end-to-end latency.

25.137 Trace-to-Evidence Link

Trace data may support Execution Evidence.

Canonical evidence shall remain separately governed.

25.138 Operational Event

An Operational Event records a meaningful system state change.

It shall include or reference:

- eventId,

- event type,

- producer,

- subject,

- prior state,

- new state,

- correlation,

- observedAt,

- recordedAt,

- scope,

- and provenance.

25.139 Operational Event Identity

Every material Event shall have stable identity.

25.140 Event Version

Event schema Version shall be explicit.

25.141 Event Ordering

Global ordering shall not be assumed.

Relevant partition or subject ordering shall be represented.

25.142 Duplicate Event

Events shall support deduplication by stable identity.

25.143 Late Event

Late arrival shall not rewrite history silently.

25.144 Event Correction

Incorrect Events shall be corrected through compensating or amendment Events.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.145 Event Replay

Replay shall preserve:

- original event time,

- replay time,

- source,

- and idempotency.

25.146 Health Observation

A Health Observation records one measured state of a component or resource.

It shall include or reference:

- healthObservationId,

- subject,

- dimension,

- state,

- measurement,

- observedAt,

- freshness,

- source,

- confidence,

- and scope.

25.147 Health Observation Identity

Every material Health Observation shall have stable identity.

25.148 Health Dimension

Health dimensions may include:

- availability,

- readiness,

- liveness,

- correctness,

- latency,

- saturation,

- quota,

- data freshness,

- quality,

- privacy,

- and authority.

25.149 Liveness

Liveness indicates whether a component is operating and making progress.

25.150 Readiness

Readiness indicates whether a component is eligible to receive work.

25.151 Availability

Availability indicates whether the service can provide its intended function.

25.152 Correctness Health

Correctness Health indicates whether observed outputs and state transitions satisfy required semantics.

25.153 Quality Health

Quality Health indicates whether outputs satisfy current Quality Floors.

25.154 Privacy Health

Privacy Health indicates whether data flows and retention remain inside policy.

25.155 Authority Health

Authority Health indicates whether Grants, Tokens and external Permissions remain aligned.

25.156 Economic Health

Economic Health indicates whether cost, Budget and quota remain within acceptable bounds.

25.157 Health State

Canonical health states may include:

- healthy,

- degraded,

- at risk,

- unhealthy,

- unavailable,

- unknown,

- quarantined,

- and maintenance.

25.158 Unknown Health

Unknown shall remain distinct from healthy.

25.159 Health Freshness

Old health observations shall not be treated as current.

25.160 Health Confidence

Health confidence shall reflect:

- observation method,

- freshness,

- source trust,

- and agreement.

25.161 Health Evaluation

A Health Evaluation combines observations into a current operational assessment.

It shall include or reference:

- healthEvaluationId,

- subject,

- observations,

- policy,

- state,

- confidence,

- reason,

- evaluatedAt,

- and validity.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.162 Health Evaluation Identity

Every material Health Evaluation shall have stable identity.

25.163 Composite Health

Composite health shall consider dependencies and critical functions.

25.164 Dependency Health

A service may be healthy internally but unable to serve because a dependency is unavailable.

25.165 Partial Health

Different Capabilities may have different health on the same Provider or Node.

25.166 Provider Health

Provider Health shall remain scoped to:

- Product,

- Account,

- region,

- Model,

- endpoint,

- and Capability.

25.167 Model Health

Model Health may include:

- availability,

- output validity,

- benchmark drift,

- context-limit behaviour,

- and safety compliance.

25.168 Tool Health

Tool Health may include:

- invocation success,

- semantic success,

- dependency availability,

- and Sandbox integrity.

25.169 Node Health

Node Health may include:

- CPU,

- memory,

- GPU,

- disk,

- network,

- thermal state,

- battery,

- and process health.

25.170 Queue Health

Queue Health may include:

- depth,

- age,

- redelivery,

- dead-letter count,

- throughput,

- and consumer availability.

25.171 Storage Health

Storage Health may include:

- availability,

- integrity,

- latency,

- capacity,

- replication,

- and deletion backlog.

25.172 Memory Health

Memory Health may include:

- retrieval availability,

- index freshness,

- conflict count,

- wrong-scope denial,

- and stale-item rate.

25.173 Approval Health

Approval Health may include:

- service availability,

- queue delay,

- stale Decisions,

- and Token validation failures.

25.174 Service Level Indicator

A Service Level Indicator is a defined measurement of service behaviour relevant to users or dependent systems.

It shall include or reference:

- sliId,

- service or Capability,

- definition,

- good-event criteria,

- total-event criteria,

- measurement source,

- window,

- and Version.

25.175 SLI Identity

Every SLI shall have stable identity and Version.

25.176 Availability SLI

Availability may measure the proportion of eligible Requests receiving valid service.

25.177 Latency SLI

Latency may measure the proportion of operations completing under a target.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 25.194 Error Budget Is Not Financial Budget
text:
25.178 Correctness SLI

Correctness may measure validated outcomes rather than transport success only.

25.179 Freshness SLI

Freshness may measure data or index age.

25.180 Durability SLI

Durability may measure preservation of accepted Assets or evidence.

25.181 Quality SLI

Quality may measure acceptance or mandatory-failure rate.

25.182 Privacy SLI

A Privacy SLI may measure compliant data flows or timely deletion completion.

25.183 Authority SLI

An Authority SLI may measure correct enforcement of required approvals.

25.184 Service Level Objective

A Service Level Objective defines a target for one or more SLIs over a window.

It shall include or reference:

- sloId,

- SLI,

- target,

- window,

- scope,

- owner,

- consequence,

- and Version.

25.185 SLO Identity

Every SLO shall have stable identity and Version.

25.186 SLO Scope

SLOs shall remain scoped to:

- Capability,

- Project class,

- Environment,

- Provider path,

- or user-facing service.

25.187 SLO Window

Windows may be:

- rolling,

- calendar,

- release,

- or campaign-based.

25.188 SLO Target

Targets shall be achievable, meaningful and tied to user impact.

25.189 SLO Exclusion

Exclusions shall be narrow, explicit and reviewable.

25.190 Error Budget

An Error Budget represents the allowed amount of SLO non-conformance within a window.

25.191 Error Budget Identity

Every Error Budget shall have stable identity and state.

25.192 Error Budget Consumption

Consumption shall be measured from the governing SLI.

25.193 Error Budget Policy

Budget state may affect:

- release pace,

- autonomy,

- Provider eligibility,

- experimentation,

- or required remediation.

25.194 Error Budget Is Not Financial Budget

Reliability Error Budget and monetary Budget shall remain distinct.

25.195 Burn Rate

Burn Rate measures how quickly the Error Budget is being consumed.

25.196 Fast Burn

Fast burn may require immediate response.

25.197 Slow Burn

Slow burn may require planned remediation before exhaustion.

25.198 SLO Breach

A breach is a service-governance condition.

It may or may not correspond to one Incident.

25.199 Dashboard

A Dashboard is a governed visual or structured view of operational state.

It shall include or reference:

- dashboardId,

- purpose,

- audience,

- scope,

- queries,

- freshness,

- owner,

- and Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.200 Dashboard Identity

Every production Dashboard shall have stable identity and Version.

25.201 Dashboard Audience

Audiences may include:

- user,

- Project owner,

- operator,

- developer,

- security,

- finance,

- auditor,

- and Incident team.

25.202 Dashboard Scope

Dashboards shall default to the minimum authorised Tenant and Project scope.

25.203 Dashboard Freshness

Every view should communicate data freshness where material.

25.204 Dashboard Unknown State

Missing data shall not appear as healthy zero.

25.205 Dashboard Drill-Down

Drill-down shall preserve access control and Classification.

25.206 User Dashboard

A user-facing dashboard may show:

- active jobs,

- progress,

- approvals,

- cost,

- outcome,

- and current issues.

25.207 Project Dashboard

A Project dashboard may show:

- content workflows,

- publication status,

- Budget,

- Provider health,

- and Incident state.

25.208 Platform Dashboard

A platform dashboard may show aggregated health without exposing protected Project content.

25.209 Provider Dashboard

Provider views may show:

- latency,

- error,

- quota,

- cost,

- and quality

by Product, Account and Capability.

25.210 Model Dashboard

Model views may show:

- availability,

- quality,

- latency,

- cost,

- and drift.

25.211 Queue Dashboard

Queue views may show:

- depth,

- oldest age,

- throughput,

- failures,

- and dead letters.

25.212 Approval Dashboard

Approval views may show:

- pending,

- expiring,

- denied,

- stale,

- and average decision time.

25.213 Privacy Dashboard

Privacy views may show:

- external transfers,

- Local Only blocks,

- deletion backlog,

- and redaction failure.

25.214 Authority Dashboard

Authority views may show:

- active Mandates,

- expiring Grants,

- excess Permissions,

- and revoked Token attempts.

25.215 Incident Dashboard

Incident views may show:

- active Incidents,

- severity,

- owner,

- affected services,

- and next update.

25.216 Dashboard as Projection

A Dashboard is a projection of canonical data.

It shall not become the authoritative state store.

25.217 Observability Query

An Observability Query defines how telemetry is selected, aggregated and presented.

It shall include:

- queryId,

- source,

- filters,

- scope,

- formula,

- time window,

- and Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.218 Query Identity

Every production-critical Query should have stable identity and Version.

25.219 Query Validation

Changes to critical Queries shall be tested against known data.

25.220 Query Access

Queries shall enforce Tenant, Project and role boundaries.

25.221 Query Cost

Unbounded queries may harm the observability system and shall be controlled.

25.222 Alert Rule

An Alert Rule evaluates telemetry or state and creates an Alert Instance when defined conditions are met.

It shall include or reference:

- alertRuleId,

- name,

- scope,

- condition,

- evaluation window,

- severity,

- owner,

- notification policy,

- suppression,

- and Version.

25.223 Alert Rule Identity

Every Alert Rule shall have stable identity and Version.

25.224 Alert Condition

Conditions may use:

- threshold,

- rate,

- absence,

- anomaly,

- state transition,

- policy violation,

- or composite logic.

25.225 Alert Evaluation Window

The window shall balance detection speed and noise.

25.226 Alert Severity

Alert severity shall represent likely consequence and required urgency.

25.227 Alert Owner

Every Alert Rule shall have an accountable owner or owning team.

25.228 Alert Runbook

Every high-severity Alert Rule should link to a Runbook.

25.229 Alert Instance

An Alert Instance represents one active or historical evaluation breach.

It shall include or reference:

- alertInstanceId,

- Rule Version,

- scope,

- detectedAt,

- state,

- severity,

- evidence,

- deduplication key,

- owner,

- and Incident link.

25.230 Alert Instance Identity

Every Alert Instance shall have stable identity.

25.231 Alert State

States may include:

- firing,

- acknowledged,

- suppressed,

- resolved,

- expired,

- and converted to Incident.

25.232 Alert Acknowledgement

Acknowledgement means a responsible Principal has seen the alert.

It does not prove remediation.

25.233 Alert Resolution

Resolution means the triggering condition no longer applies according to the Rule.

It does not necessarily mean the underlying cause is fixed.

25.234 Alert Deduplication

Repeated signals for the same condition should create one grouped alert where appropriate.

25.235 Alert Group

An Alert Group collects related Alert Instances.

It shall include:

- groupId,

- deduplication key,

- members,

- root scope,

- state,

- and owner.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.236 Alert Correlation

Related symptoms across services may be correlated into one Incident candidate.

25.237 Root-Cause Alert

Root-cause alerts should be preferred over multiple downstream symptom alerts where possible.

25.238 Symptom Alert

User-impacting symptoms may still require notification even when root cause is known.

25.239 Alert Suppression

Suppression may be used during:

- maintenance,

- known Incident,

- deployment,

- or dependency outage.

Suppression shall be scoped and expiring.

25.240 Alert Silence

A silence prevents notifications but shall not erase Alert Instances or Metrics.

25.241 Maintenance Window

Maintenance windows shall identify:

- affected services,

- start,

- end,

- owner,

- and expected effects.

25.242 Alert Escalation

Unacknowledged or worsening alerts may escalate to another Principal or Incident declaration.

25.243 Alert Notification

Notification delivers alert context to an eligible recipient.

It shall preserve:

- Rule,

- scope,

- severity,

- time,

- impact,

- and Runbook link.

25.244 Notification Channel

Channels may include:

- Omnira interface,

- mobile push,

- email,

- secure messaging,

- paging service,

- and voice call.

25.245 Notification Minimisation

Notifications shall avoid exposing protected content unnecessarily.

25.246 Notification Delivery Evidence

High-severity notifications should preserve delivery and acknowledgement state.

25.247 Alert Fatigue

Alert fatigue occurs when excessive or low-value alerts reduce response effectiveness.

25.248 Actionable Alert

An actionable alert should identify:

- what is wrong,

- likely impact,

- scope,

- owner,

- immediate checks,

- and escalation path.

25.249 Non-Actionable Alert

Non-actionable alerts should be converted to dashboard or analytic signals rather than pages.

25.250 Paging Policy

Paging shall be reserved for conditions requiring timely human intervention.

25.251 Business-Hours Alert

Some alerts may wait for normal review when impact is low.

25.252 Automated Containment Alert

Certain high-confidence conditions may trigger bounded automatic containment under policy.

25.253 Automated Containment Limits

Automation shall not:

- delete evidence,

- broaden authority,

- expose Secrets,

- or perform irreversible remediation

without required approval.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.254 On-Call Assignment

An On-Call Assignment identifies who owns response during a time period.

It shall include or reference:

- onCallAssignmentId,

- role,

- Principal,

- service or domain,

- start,

- end,

- escalation,

- and backup.

25.255 On-Call Identity

Every assignment shall have stable identity.

25.256 On-Call Handoff

Handoffs shall preserve active alerts, Incidents, risks and pending actions.

25.257 On-Call Availability

A listed owner who cannot be reached shall trigger escalation.

25.258 Audit Event

An Audit Event records one material action, Decision or governance change.

It shall include or reference:

- auditEventId,

- event type,

- actor,

- represented Principal where applicable,

- authority basis,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- action,

- target,

- target Version,

- prior state,

- new state,

- time,

- result,

- correlation,

- and provenance.

25.259 Audit Event Identity

Every Audit Event shall have stable identity.

25.260 Audit Actor

The actual acting Principal shall be explicit.

25.261 Represented Principal

Impersonation or delegated action shall preserve both acting and represented identities.

25.262 Audit Authority Basis

The Grant, Approval, Mandate or emergency authority used shall be linked.

25.263 Audit Target

The exact object or resource affected shall be explicit.

25.264 Audit Target Version

Material changes shall identify the prior and resulting Versions.

25.265 Audit Result

Result states may include:

- succeeded,

- failed,

- denied,

- partially completed,

- unknown,

- and reversed.

25.266 Audit Denial

Denied consequential actions should be audited when relevant to security or governance.

25.267 Audit Prior State

Prior state should be preserved for material configuration or authority changes.

25.268 Audit New State

Resulting state should be preserved or referenced.

25.269 Audit Diff

A structured diff should be preserved for:

- policy,

- Role,

- Grant,

- Mandate,

- configuration,

- content acceptance,

- and code changes

where practical.

25.270 Audit Reason

Human and automated Decisions should preserve a bounded reason or rationale.

25.271 Audit Record

An Audit Record is the canonical stored representation of one or more Audit Events and associated integrity evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.272 Audit Record Identity

Every Audit Record shall have stable identity.

25.273 Audit Trail

An Audit Trail is the ordered set of Audit Records relevant to one subject, Principal, Project, Execution or time period.

25.274 Audit Trail Identity

Material exported or reviewed Audit Trails should have stable identity and query definition.

25.275 Audit Completeness

Completeness shall be explicit.

Missing mandatory Audit Events are an Incident or conformance failure.

25.276 Audit Immutability

Material Audit Records shall be append-only or tamper-evident.

25.277 Audit Amendment

Incorrect metadata may be amended through a linked correction record.

The original shall remain.

25.278 Audit Integrity

Audit integrity may use:

- checksums,

- hash chains,

- signatures,

- write-once storage,

- or external anchoring.

25.279 Audit Sequence

Sequence integrity may help detect removal or reordering.

25.280 Audit Timestamp

Audit timestamps shall use trusted time and preserve ingestion delay.

25.281 Audit Access

Audit access shall be role-, Tenant-, Project- and purpose-scoped.

25.282 Auditor Role

An Auditor may inspect records without mutation authority.

25.283 Audit Administrator

Audit-system administration shall not automatically grant content access.

25.284 Audit Privacy

Audit records may contain:

- identity,

- Project names,

- file paths,

- cost,

- and action details.

Views shall be minimised by audience.

25.285 Audit Retention

Retention may be longer than ordinary logs.

It shall remain policy-defined.

25.286 Audit Deletion

Where deletion is required, minimal integrity and accountability metadata may remain according to policy.

25.287 Audit Export

An Audit Export is a governed package of records for review, compliance or dispute.

It shall include:

- exportId,

- query scope,

- time range,

- records,

- redactions,

- integrity,

- requester,

- and purpose.

25.288 Audit Export Identity

Every Audit Export shall have stable identity.

25.289 Audit Export Redaction

Exports shall hide unrelated or unauthorised data.

25.290 Audit Export Integrity

Exports should include checksum or signature.

25.291 Audit Query

Audit queries shall be Versioned or preserved when used for formal review.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 25.304 Execution Evidence Is Not Audit Replacement
text:
25.292 Mandatory Audit Classes

The following shall receive canonical audit:

- authentication and step-up events,

- Role and Grant changes,

- Approval Requests and Decisions,

- Mandate activation and revocation,

- publication,

- deletion,

- overwrite,

- Credential creation, rotation, revocation and export,

- data transfer,

- classification lowering,

- rights and consent Decisions,

- Memory admission and deletion,

- policy changes,

- emergency authority,

- Incident state changes,

- and Tenant ownership changes.

25.293 Optional Audit Classes

Lower-risk read or preview actions may use sampled or policy-defined audit when appropriate.

25.294 Read Audit

Sensitive data reads may require audit even when no mutation occurs.

25.295 Bulk Read Audit

Bulk export, indexing or broad search shall receive elevated audit.

25.296 Failed Access Audit

Repeated denied access may indicate misconfiguration or attempted misuse.

25.297 Publication Audit

Publication audit shall include:

- Asset Version,

- target Account,

- payload,

- Approval,

- Connector,

- and external verification.

25.298 Deletion Audit

Deletion audit shall include:

- target,

- authority,

- Locations,

- completion,

- residual copies,

- and recovery state.

25.299 Credential Audit

Credential audit shall preserve metadata and action without storing Secret values.

25.300 Authority Audit

Authority audit shall show effective Grants, Denials, delegation and external Permission state.

25.301 Incident Audit

Every Incident lifecycle transition and material response action shall be audited.

25.302 Audit Is Not Observability Replacement

Audit records do not replace Metrics, traces or health signals.

25.303 Observability Is Not Audit Replacement

Operational logs do not provide sufficient governance evidence automatically.

25.304 Execution Evidence Is Not Audit Replacement

Execution Evidence explains work.

Audit explains accountable action and governance changes.

They may link but remain distinct.

25.305 Incident Detection

Incident detection may originate from:

- Alert Rule,

- user report,

- human observation,

- Provider notification,

- audit anomaly,

- security signal,

- privacy review,

- quality failure,

- cost anomaly,

- or external outcome discrepancy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.306 Incident Candidate

An Incident Candidate is a condition under review before formal declaration.

25.307 Incident Declaration

Declaration confirms that the condition requires governed Incident Response.

25.308 Incident Identity

Every Incident shall have stable identity.

25.309 Incident Object

An Incident shall include or reference:

- incidentId,

- title,

- summary,

- type,

- severity,

- priority,

- state,

- detectedAt,

- declaredAt,

- affected Tenants,

- Projects,

- users,

- services,

- Capabilities,

- data,

- Assets,

- external systems,

- owner,

- commander,

- evidence,

- containment,

- recovery,

- communications,

- and timeline.

25.310 Incident Type

Incident types may include:

- reliability,

- availability,

- correctness,

- quality,

- privacy,

- security,

- authority,

- financial,

- rights,

- consent,

- data integrity,

- Asset loss,

- Provider,

- publication,

- Memory,

- and multi-domain.

25.311 Reliability Incident

A Reliability Incident affects continuity, completion or recoverability.

25.312 Availability Incident

An Availability Incident prevents eligible service use.

25.313 Correctness Incident

A Correctness Incident produces materially wrong system state or outcomes.

25.314 Quality Incident

A Quality Incident allows outputs below mandatory standards into downstream use.

25.315 Privacy Incident

A Privacy Incident involves unauthorised access, disclosure, inference, retention or transfer.

25.316 Security Incident

A Security Incident involves compromise, attack, unauthorised access or control failure.

25.317 Authority Incident

An Authority Incident involves execution outside valid Grants, approvals or Mandates.

25.318 Financial Incident

A Financial Incident involves unauthorised or materially incorrect spend, billing or credit use.

25.319 Rights Incident

A Rights Incident involves unauthorised use, missing licence, attribution failure or disputed ownership.

25.320 Consent Incident

A Consent Incident involves missing, expired, revoked or mis-scoped consent.

25.321 Data Integrity Incident

A Data Integrity Incident involves corruption, inconsistency, loss or unauthorised alteration.

25.322 Asset Loss Incident

An Asset Loss Incident threatens or causes loss of canonical or accepted Assets.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.323 Provider Incident

A Provider Incident arises from external service failure or unexpected behaviour.

25.324 Publication Incident

A Publication Incident involves wrong content, wrong Account, duplicate post, missing publication or unauthorised visibility.

25.325 Memory Incident

A Memory Incident involves wrong, stale, leaked, poisoned or deleted Memory affecting behaviour.

25.326 Multi-Domain Incident

One Incident may affect several domains.

All material impacts shall remain represented.

25.327 Incident Severity

Severity describes actual or potential impact.

Canonical severities may include:

- SEV0 — Sovereign or Catastrophic,

- SEV1 — Critical,

- SEV2 — High,

- SEV3 — Moderate,

- SEV4 — Low,

- and SEV5 — Informational Review.

25.328 SEV0 — Sovereign or Catastrophic

Examples may include:

- widespread Tenant data exposure,

- loss of platform control,

- unrecoverable destruction of critical user data,

- or compromise of sovereign recovery authority.

25.329 SEV1 — Critical

Examples may include:

- active cross-Tenant leakage,

- production Credential compromise,

- unauthorised public publication with major impact,

- or major service outage affecting critical operations.

25.330 SEV2 — High

Examples may include:

- substantial Project outage,

- Confidential data sent to wrong Provider,

- repeated unauthorised spend,

- or accepted corrupt Assets.

25.331 SEV3 — Moderate

Examples may include:

- limited Project disruption,

- delayed publication,

- isolated quality failure,

- or recoverable workflow corruption.

25.332 SEV4 — Low

Examples may include:

- minor degraded experience,

- non-critical alerting defect,

- or limited internal workflow delay.

25.333 SEV5 — Informational Review

Examples may include:

- near miss,

- minor policy warning,

- or low-risk conformance observation.

25.334 Severity Basis

Severity shall consider:

- user harm,

- data sensitivity,

- affected scope,

- duration,

- reversibility,

- financial impact,

- external visibility,

- legal or contractual risk,

- and trust impact.

25.335 Potential Severity

Potential impact may justify higher initial severity before full scope is known.

25.336 Confirmed Severity

Severity may be adjusted as evidence improves.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.337 Severity Downgrade

Downgrade shall preserve the original classification and rationale.

25.338 Severity Upgrade

Worsening impact shall trigger immediate reassessment.

25.339 Incident Priority

Priority describes response urgency and resource allocation.

Priority may consider severity, active harm, spread, recoverability and time sensitivity.

25.340 Severity Is Not Priority

A severe historical Incident may have lower current response priority after containment.

A moderate active leak may require immediate priority.

25.341 Incident State

Canonical Incident states may include:

- suspected,

- investigating,

- declared,

- active,

- contained,

- recovering,

- monitoring,

- resolved,

- closed,

- reopened,

- and archived.

25.342 Suspected

Evidence suggests a possible Incident but scope remains uncertain.

25.343 Investigating

The condition is under active triage.

25.344 Declared

The Incident lifecycle and roles are activated.

25.345 Active

Harm or material degradation is ongoing.

25.346 Contained

Spread or new harm is prevented, but recovery is incomplete.

25.347 Recovering

Systems, data or workflows are being restored.

25.348 Monitoring

Recovery is implemented and being observed for stability.

25.349 Resolved

The immediate impact and governing conditions are no longer active.

25.350 Closed

Required review, communication and action ownership are complete.

25.351 Reopened

New evidence shows the Incident remains active or recurred.

25.352 Incident Detection Time

Detected time identifies when Omnira or a person first identified the condition.

25.353 Incident Start Time

Start time estimates when impact began.

25.354 Incident Declaration Time

Declaration time identifies when governed response began.

25.355 Incident Containment Time

Containment time identifies when further harm was stopped.

25.356 Incident Recovery Time

Recovery time identifies when intended service or state was restored.

25.357 Incident Resolution Time

Resolution time identifies when the Incident met closure conditions.

25.358 Time-to-Detect

Time-to-Detect measures delay between start and detection.

25.359 Time-to-Acknowledge

Time-to-Acknowledge measures delay before ownership.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.360 Time-to-Contain

Time-to-Contain measures delay before spread or harm is bounded.

25.361 Time-to-Recover

Time-to-Recover measures delay before service or state restoration.

25.362 Time-to-Resolve

Time-to-Resolve measures total duration until resolution.

25.363 Incident Scope

Incident scope shall include:

- Tenants,

- Projects,

- users,

- services,

- Agents,

- Providers,

- Accounts,

- Assets,

- data categories,

- regions,

- and time.

25.364 Scope Unknown

Unknown scope shall remain explicit and may justify restrictive containment.

25.365 Affected User

Affected users shall be identified where possible without overexposing personal data.

25.366 Affected Project

Every affected Project shall be represented separately where impact differs.

25.367 Affected Tenant

Cross-Tenant impact shall receive elevated response.

25.368 Affected Data

Affected data shall identify:

- categories,

- Classification,

- copies,

- recipients,

- and retention.

25.369 Affected Asset

Affected Assets and Versions shall be identified.

25.370 Affected External State

External posts, messages, purchases or mutations shall be identified.

25.371 Incident Commander

The Incident Commander coordinates response and Decision flow.

The role may be held by an authorised human or, for low-risk bounded events, a governed automation.

High-severity Incident command shall remain human-owned.

25.372 Incident Commander Identity

The assigned commander shall be explicit.

25.373 Technical Lead

The Technical Lead coordinates diagnosis and remediation.

25.374 Communications Lead

The Communications Lead coordinates stakeholder updates.

25.375 Scribe

The Scribe maintains timeline, Decisions and evidence.

25.376 Privacy Lead

A Privacy Lead may be required for personal-data Incidents.

25.377 Security Lead

A Security Lead may be required for compromise or attack.

25.378 Project Owner

The affected Project owner may provide business and content authority.

25.379 Provider Liaison

A Provider liaison may coordinate external support or escalation.

25.380 Role Assignment

Incident role assignments shall be recorded with:

- Principal,

- role,

- start,

- end,

- and authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.381 Role Separation

One person may hold several roles in small Incidents, but accountability shall remain explicit.

25.382 Incident Command Channel

A dedicated communication channel may be created for active response.

25.383 Incident Channel Classification

The channel shall match the Incident’s data sensitivity.

25.384 Incident Timeline

The Incident Timeline is the ordered record of:

- observations,

- Decisions,

- actions,

- state changes,

- communications,

- and outcomes.

25.385 Incident Timeline Identity

Every Incident Timeline shall have stable identity.

25.386 Timeline Entry

Each entry should include:

- time,

- actor,

- event,

- evidence,

- Decision,

- and result.

25.387 Timeline Correction

Corrections shall preserve the original entry and amendment.

25.388 Timeline Time Source

Time discrepancies shall remain visible.

25.389 Incident Evidence Bundle

The Incident Evidence Bundle preserves all material evidence required for investigation and review.

It may include:

- logs,

- traces,

- Metrics,

- audit records,

- Provider responses,

- Assets,

- screenshots,

- configuration,

- authority records,

- and human statements.

25.390 Incident Evidence Identity

Every Incident Evidence Bundle shall have stable identity and Version.

25.391 Evidence Preservation

Evidence shall be preserved before destructive remediation where practical.

25.392 Evidence Hold

A hold may suspend ordinary deletion and retention expiry for relevant evidence.

25.393 Evidence Minimisation

Evidence collection shall remain limited to the affected scope.

25.394 Evidence Integrity

Checksums, signatures or write-once storage may protect critical evidence.

25.395 Evidence Access

Access shall remain role- and purpose-limited.

25.396 Evidence Redaction

Derived review views may redact unrelated personal or Secret information.

25.397 Evidence Chain of Custody

Manual exports and device captures shall preserve custody.

25.398 Evidence Reconstruction

Missing evidence may be reconstructed and labelled with lower confidence.

25.399 Triage

Triage determines whether the condition is an Incident and identifies initial severity, scope and ownership.

25.400 Triage Questions

Initial triage should determine:

- what changed,

- who is affected,

- whether harm is ongoing,

- whether data is exposed,

- whether authority is compromised,

- whether external side effects occurred,

- and whether containment is available.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.401 Triage Decision

The triage Decision may:

- dismiss,

- monitor,

- create a problem record,

- declare Incident,

- or escalate immediately.

25.402 False Positive

A false positive alert shall remain available for Rule improvement.

25.403 Near Miss

A near miss is a condition that could have caused material harm but was prevented or narrowly avoided.

25.404 Near-Miss Review

Near misses may justify corrective action even without user impact.

25.405 Containment

Containment prevents additional harm, spread or unauthorised action.

It may be:

- automatic,

- manual,

- temporary,

- or permanent.

25.406 Containment Action

A Containment Action shall include or reference:

- containmentActionId,

- Incident,

- actor,

- authority,

- target,

- action,

- start,

- result,

- side effects,

- and evidence.

25.407 Containment Action Identity

Every material Containment Action shall have stable identity.

25.408 Service Isolation

A service may be isolated from traffic.

25.409 Provider Suspension

A Provider, Account, Model or Adapter path may be disabled.

25.410 Agent Suspension

An Agent may be paused or reduced to observe-only mode.

25.411 Project Stop

One Project may be stopped without affecting unrelated Projects.
