25.412 Publication Freeze

Publication Connectors may be disabled.

25.413 Credential Revocation

Suspected Credentials may be revoked or rotated.

25.414 Network Isolation

A Node or service may be disconnected from external networks.

25.415 Queue Pause

Queue consumption may pause while preserving messages.

25.416 Input Block

New Requests of an affected class may be rejected or deferred.

25.417 Output Quarantine

Generated Outputs may be prevented from Asset admission or publication.

25.418 Memory Suspension

Affected Memory Items or Domains may be excluded from retrieval.

25.419 Rights Quarantine

Disputed Assets may be blocked from use.

25.420 Data Access Restriction

Affected data may be restricted to Incident responders.

25.421 Containment Reversibility

Containment actions should be reversible where possible.

25.422 Containment Cost

Operational and business cost shall be considered but shall not outrank safety or privacy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.423 Over-Containment

Containment may affect more scope than required.

The excess impact shall be visible and reduced when safe.

25.424 Under-Containment

Containment that allows continued harm is insufficient.

25.425 Investigation

Investigation identifies:

- timeline,

- scope,

- trigger,

- contributing conditions,

- root causes,

- and affected outcomes.

25.426 Hypothesis

Investigation hypotheses shall be labelled and tested.

25.427 Confirmed Fact

Confirmed facts shall link to evidence.

25.428 Assumption

Assumptions shall remain explicit.

25.429 Unknown

Unknowns shall be tracked until resolved or accepted.

25.430 Root Cause

Root Cause is the underlying condition whose correction materially reduces recurrence.

An Incident may have several root causes.

25.431 Trigger

The trigger is the event that initiated the failure.

It may not be the root cause.

25.432 Contributing Factor

A contributing factor increased likelihood, duration or impact.

25.433 Detection Gap

A Detection Gap explains why the Incident was not identified sooner.

25.434 Control Gap

A Control Gap identifies a missing or ineffective preventive or containment mechanism.

25.435 Process Gap

A Process Gap identifies an operational or governance weakness.

25.436 Human Error

Human action may contribute.

The review shall examine system conditions, interface design and safeguards rather than stopping at blame.

25.437 Provider Cause

Provider failure may be a cause but internal dependency design and fallback policy still require review.

25.438 Model Cause

A Model regression may be a cause.

Exact Model, Deployment, prompt, input and evaluation state shall be preserved.

25.439 Configuration Cause

Configuration drift may cause unexpected behaviour.

25.440 Authority Cause

Overbroad or stale authority may enable harm.

25.441 Privacy Cause

Missing minimisation, wrong classification or improper transfer may cause exposure.

25.442 Data Cause

Corrupt, stale or mis-scoped data may cause incorrect outcomes.

25.443 Memory Cause

Wrong or poisoned Memory may influence Planning or execution.

25.444 Cost Cause

Retry storms, pricing changes or reservation leaks may cause economic harm.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.445 Race Condition

Concurrent state changes may create inconsistent outcomes.

25.446 Unknown Outcome Cause

Network or Provider uncertainty may create duplicate-action risk.

25.447 Investigation Query

Material queries and tools used during investigation should be preserved where practical.

25.448 Reproduction

Reproduction may confirm cause.

Production data shall not be copied into unsafe environments.

25.449 Safe Reproduction

Synthetic or minimised test cases should be preferred.

25.450 Recovery

Recovery restores intended service, data, authority or external state after containment.

25.451 Recovery Action

A Recovery Action shall include or reference:

- recoveryActionId,

- Incident,

- actor,

- authority,

- target,

- action,

- prerequisites,

- rollback,

- result,

- and evidence.

25.452 Recovery Action Identity

Every material Recovery Action shall have stable identity.

25.453 Service Recovery

Service may be restored gradually through:

- shadow,

- canary,

- limited traffic,

- or full activation.

25.454 Data Recovery

Data recovery may restore:

- Assets,

- configuration,

- Memory,

- Evidence,

- or database state.

25.455 Authority Recovery

Authority state may require:

- revocation cleanup,

- new Grants,

- Token invalidation,

- and access certification.

25.456 Credential Recovery

Credential recovery may require:

- rotation,

- dependency update,

- Session revocation,

- and verification.

25.457 External-State Recovery

External posts, messages or purchases may require:

- correction,

- unpublish,

- refund,

- follow-up,

- or compensation.

25.458 Recovery Point

The exact restored Version or state shall be explicit.

25.459 Recovery Time

Recovery completion time shall be recorded.

25.460 Recovery Verification

Recovery shall not be declared complete without verification against defined success criteria.

25.461 Verification Record

A Verification Record shall include or reference:

- verificationRecordId,

- Incident,

- target,

- expected state,

- method,

- evidence,

- verifier,

- result,

- confidence,

- and time.

25.462 Verification Record Identity

Every material Verification Record shall have stable identity.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.463 Technical Verification

Technical verification may confirm:

- service responds,

- data restored,

- Token revoked,

- or queue drained.

25.464 Semantic Verification

Semantic verification may confirm:

- correct Asset,

- correct Project,

- correct user state,

- or valid publication.

25.465 User Verification

Affected users or owners may confirm that intended service has been restored.

25.466 External Verification

External platforms or Providers may require independent confirmation.

25.467 Recovery Monitoring

A monitoring period shall confirm stability after recovery.

25.468 Recovery Regression

Recurrence during monitoring may reopen the Incident.

25.469 Rollback

Rollback returns to a known prior state.

It shall identify:

- target Version,

- data impact,

- compatibility,

- and limitations.

25.470 Rollforward

Rollforward applies a corrective Version rather than restoring the previous one.

25.471 Compensation

Compensation creates a new balancing action when direct rollback is impossible.

25.472 Recovery Does Not Erase Incident

Restoration shall not delete evidence or history.

25.473 Incident Communication

Communication provides accurate, scoped and timely information to affected parties and responders.

25.474 Communication Record

A Communication Record shall include or reference:

- communicationRecordId,

- Incident,

- audience,

- sender,

- channel,

- content Version,

- time,

- approval,

- and delivery state.

25.475 Communication Record Identity

Every material Incident communication shall have stable identity.

25.476 Internal Communication

Internal updates may include:

- current impact,

- actions,

- owner,

- risks,

- and next update.

25.477 User Communication

User communication should be:

- factual,

- understandable,

- transparent about uncertainty,

- and clear about required action.

25.478 Tenant Communication

Tenant administrators may receive aggregated impact and affected-scope details.

25.479 Provider Communication

Provider escalation should preserve:

- case ID,

- severity,

- Account,

- evidence,

- and requested action.

25.480 Public Communication

Public status communication requires authorised messaging and privacy review.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.481 Communication Cadence

Active high-severity Incidents should have a defined update cadence.

25.482 No-Change Update

When no material change exists, the update may state that investigation continues.

25.483 Uncertainty Disclosure

Unknown scope or outcome shall not be presented as certainty.

25.484 Speculation Prohibition

Unverified root causes shall not be communicated as confirmed facts.

25.485 Blame Prohibition

Incident communication should avoid unsupported blame.

25.486 Sensitive Detail Minimisation

Communication shall not expose:

- Secrets,

- private data,

- exploit details,

- or unrelated Tenant information.

25.487 Notification Obligation

Privacy, security, contractual or legal notification requirements shall be evaluated separately.

25.488 Communication Approval

External high-impact communication may require authorised approval.

25.489 Status Page

A status page may publish current service impact without exposing protected architecture.

25.490 Status Component

Status components should map to user-understandable Capabilities.

25.491 Status Accuracy

Status shall reflect verified impact and freshness.

25.492 Incident Resolution

Resolution requires evidence that:

- active harm is stopped,

- required service is restored,

- external state is reconciled,

- authority is corrected,

- and monitoring criteria are satisfied.

25.493 Resolution Criteria

Criteria shall be defined per Incident.

Examples include:

- no further leakage,

- correct Asset restored,

- duplicate publication removed,

- Credentials rotated,

- and queues stable.

25.494 Incident Closure

Closure requires:

- resolved state,

- completed communications,

- evidence preservation,

- owner confirmation,

- and assigned corrective actions.

25.495 Closure Is Not Forgetting

Closed Incidents remain available for audit and learning.

25.496 Incident Reopen

New impact or evidence may reopen a closed Incident.

25.497 Post-Incident Review

A Post-Incident Review is the structured evaluation of what happened, why, how response performed and what must change.

It shall include or reference:

- reviewId,

- Incident,

- summary,

- impact,

- timeline,

- root causes,

- contributing factors,

- detection,

- containment,

- recovery,

- communication,

- learning,

- and Corrective Actions.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.498 Post-Incident Review Identity

Every material review shall have stable identity and Version.

25.499 Blameless Review

The review should focus on systems, incentives, interfaces and safeguards rather than personal blame.

Intentional misuse remains accountable.

25.500 Impact Summary

Impact shall identify:

- users,

- Projects,

- Tenants,

- duration,

- data,

- financial effect,

- external effect,

- and trust impact.

25.501 What Went Well

Successful controls and response actions should be preserved.

25.502 What Went Poorly

Delays, gaps, ambiguity and failed controls should be documented.

25.503 Where Luck Helped

Near misses and accidental protection should be explicit.

25.504 Detection Review

The review shall assess:

- whether monitoring detected the condition,

- whether alerts were actionable,

- and whether signals existed earlier.

25.505 Response Review

The review shall assess:

- command,

- ownership,

- escalation,

- evidence,

- containment,

- and communication.

25.506 Recovery Review

The review shall assess:

- restore method,

- verification,

- regressions,

- and user confirmation.

25.507 Governance Review

The review shall assess:

- authority,

- approval,

- classification,

- rights,

- consent,

- and policy.

25.508 Corrective Action

A Corrective Action is a governed task intended to reduce recurrence, impact or detection time.

It shall include or reference:

- correctiveActionId,

- Incident,

- description,

- owner,

- priority,

- due date,

- verification,

- state,

- and evidence.

25.509 Corrective Action Identity

Every Corrective Action shall have stable identity.

25.510 Corrective Action Type

Types may include:

- prevention,

- detection,

- containment,

- recovery,

- documentation,

- training,

- policy,

- architecture,

- and cleanup.

25.511 Corrective Action Owner

Every action shall have one accountable owner.

25.512 Corrective Action Due Date

Due dates shall reflect risk and effort.

25.513 Corrective Action State

States may include:

- proposed,

- accepted,

- in progress,

- blocked,

- completed,

- verified,

- deferred,

- rejected,

- and superseded.

25.514 Corrective Action Verification

Completion shall require proof that the change works.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.515 Action Closure

An action shall not close merely because code was merged or documentation was written.

25.516 Risk Acceptance

A residual risk may be accepted by an authorised owner.

The scope, rationale and review date shall be explicit.

25.517 Deferred Action

Deferral shall preserve:

- reason,

- risk,

- owner,

- and next review.

25.518 Derived Learning

Incident learning may produce:

- routing restrictions,

- new alerts,

- new tests,

- narrower Mandates,

- updated Runbooks,

- or architectural changes.

Derived Learning shall follow Chapter 22 governance.

25.519 Incident Learning Scope

Learning shall remain scoped to the affected:

- Provider,

- Model,

- Project,

- Capability,

- or failure class.

25.520 No Automatic Universal Rule

One Incident shall not create a universal policy automatically unless the risk justifies a reviewed precautionary control.

25.521 Runbook

A Runbook is an operational procedure for diagnosis, containment, recovery or verification of a known condition.

It shall include or reference:

- runbookId,

- trigger,

- scope,

- prerequisites,

- steps,

- authority,

- safety checks,

- rollback,

- verification,

- owner,

- and Version.

25.522 Runbook Identity

Every Runbook shall have stable identity and Version.

25.523 Runbook Trigger

The conditions for use shall be explicit.

25.524 Runbook Scope

The exact service, Project, Provider or Incident class shall be explicit.

25.525 Runbook Preconditions

Required access, authority, backups and evidence shall be listed.

25.526 Runbook Step

Each Step should define:

- action,

- expected result,

- failure handling,

- and evidence.

25.527 Runbook Safety Check

Safety checks shall prevent:

- wrong-Project action,

- wrong Environment,

- data loss,

- and authority bypass.

25.528 Runbook Rollback

Rollback or stop conditions shall be explicit.

25.529 Runbook Verification

The procedure shall define how success is proven.

25.530 Runbook Ownership

Every Runbook shall have an owner and review date.

25.531 Runbook Test

Critical Runbooks shall be exercised periodically.

25.532 Stale Runbook

A Runbook that no longer matches architecture or permissions shall be marked stale or retired.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.533 Playbook

A Playbook coordinates response across several roles or systems for a broader Incident class.

25.534 Playbook Identity

Every Playbook shall have stable identity and Version.

25.535 Privacy Playbook

A Privacy Playbook may cover:

- containment,

- scope discovery,

- Provider deletion,

- subject impact,

- and notification review.

25.536 Credential Playbook

A Credential Playbook may cover:

- revocation,

- rotation,

- dependency update,

- Session invalidation,

- and verification.

25.537 Publication Playbook

A Publication Playbook may cover:

- freeze,

- identify posts,

- unpublish,

- correct,

- notify,

- and verify.

25.538 Data-Loss Playbook

A Data-Loss Playbook may cover:

- stop writes,

- preserve media,

- verify backups,

- recover,

- and validate integrity.

25.539 Provider-Outage Playbook

A Provider-outage Playbook may cover:

- health verification,

- fallback eligibility,

- queue handling,

- cost,

- and user communication.

25.540 Unknown-Outcome Playbook

An unknown-outcome Playbook may cover:

- stop duplicate action,

- reconcile Provider state,

- inspect external target,

- and resolve status.

25.541 Observability Incident

An Observability Incident is a material failure of telemetry, alerting, audit or monitoring.

Examples include:

- missing Metrics,

- broken trace propagation,

- audit ingestion failure,

- false healthy dashboard,

- alert delivery failure,

- or uncontrolled payload logging.

25.542 Observability Incident Identity

Every material Observability Incident shall have stable identity.

25.543 Monitoring Blind Spot

A blind spot exists when a material failure can occur without useful detection.

25.544 Telemetry Pipeline Failure

Telemetry collection, transport or storage may fail independently from the observed system.

25.545 Audit Pipeline Failure

Loss of mandatory Audit Events is a high-risk governance failure.

25.546 Dashboard Misrepresentation

Incorrect Queries or stale data may display false health.

25.547 Alert Delivery Failure

A firing alert may fail to reach the responsible person.

25.548 Excessive Alerting

Noise may hide critical conditions.

25.549 Missing Correlation

Broken context may prevent diagnosis or audit linkage.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.550 Telemetry Privacy Leak

Observability data may expose protected content.

25.551 Observability Recovery

Recovery may require:

- restore pipeline,

- replay buffered telemetry,

- reconstruct gaps,

- correct Queries,

- and notify affected operators.

25.552 Meta-Monitoring

The observability system itself shall be monitored.

25.553 Dead-Man Signal

Critical telemetry producers may emit heartbeat or absence signals.

25.554 Audit Heartbeat

Audit ingestion may use continuity checks to detect missing records.

25.555 Synthetic Monitoring

Synthetic monitoring performs controlled test operations to verify service behaviour.

25.556 Synthetic Request

Synthetic Requests shall be clearly labelled and isolated from user data.

25.557 End-to-End Synthetic Test

An end-to-end test may verify:

- Request,

- Planning,

- Routing,

- Provider,

- Asset,

- and external outcome

using non-production test targets.

25.558 Synthetic Publication

Publication tests shall use private or dedicated test Accounts.

25.559 Synthetic Approval

Approval tests shall not create real authority outside the test Environment.

25.560 Probe

A Probe performs a bounded check of availability or correctness.

25.561 Readiness Probe

Readiness probes shall verify ability to accept appropriate work.

25.562 Liveness Probe

Liveness probes shall detect stuck or non-progressing components.

25.563 Deep Health Check

Deep checks may exercise dependencies.

They shall be rate-limited and non-destructive.

25.564 Canary Request

A canary Request verifies a new Version with limited real or synthetic traffic.

25.565 Shadow Observation

Shadow mode evaluates Decisions without executing side effects.

25.566 Chaos Experiment

A Chaos Experiment intentionally introduces a controlled fault to verify resilience and response.

It shall include or reference:

- chaosExperimentId,

- hypothesis,

- scope,

- fault,

- safeguards,

- authority,

- start,

- stop conditions,

- observations,

- and result.

25.567 Chaos Experiment Identity

Every Chaos Experiment shall have stable identity and Version.

25.568 Chaos Hypothesis

The expected system behaviour shall be explicit.

25.569 Chaos Scope

Experiments shall begin with the smallest safe scope.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.570 Chaos Safeguard

Safeguards may include:

- automatic stop,

- traffic limit,

- isolated Environment,

- backup,

- and on-call presence.

25.571 Chaos Authority

Production chaos requires explicit approval.

25.572 Chaos Data Protection

Experiments shall not expose protected data or broaden access.

25.573 Chaos Stop Condition

Unexpected impact shall stop the experiment.

25.574 Chaos Evidence

Metrics, logs, traces and response actions shall be preserved.

25.575 Game Day

A Game Day is a coordinated exercise that tests Incident detection, command, communication and recovery.

It shall include:

- scenario,

- roles,

- objectives,

- systems,

- safeguards,

- timeline,

- and review.

25.576 Game Day Identity

Every Game Day shall have stable identity.

25.577 Tabletop Exercise

A tabletop exercise tests Decisions and communication without changing systems.

25.578 Recovery Drill

A recovery drill verifies restoration from backup or checkpoint.

25.579 Credential Drill

A Credential drill verifies rotation and dependency recovery.

25.580 Privacy Drill

A privacy drill tests data-scope discovery, containment and communication.

25.581 Publication Drill

A publication drill tests freeze, unpublish and correction.

25.582 Unknown-Outcome Drill

An unknown-outcome drill tests duplicate prevention and reconciliation.

25.583 Drill Evidence

Exercise results shall create Corrective Actions where gaps exist.

25.584 Profiling

Profiling measures internal resource or code behaviour.

It may include:

- CPU,

- memory,

- allocation,

- lock,

- and GPU profiles.

25.585 Profiling Privacy

Profiles may expose code paths, data shapes or user identifiers.

Collection shall be scoped and protected.

25.586 Continuous Profiling

Continuous profiling may be enabled for approved services with bounded overhead.

25.587 Performance Regression

Regression detection shall compare compatible Versions and workloads.

25.588 Model Drift

Model drift occurs when behaviour changes materially over time or across Versions.

25.589 Model Drift Detection

Detection may use:

- benchmarks,

- sampled production evaluation,

- schema compliance,

- and human acceptance.

25.590 Provider Drift

Provider drift may include changes in:

- latency,

- error,

- terms,

- Model alias,

- output format,

- or quota.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.591 Adapter Drift

Adapter drift may arise from external API changes or local code changes.

25.592 Policy Drift

Policy drift occurs when enforced behaviour differs from canonical policy.

25.593 Authority Drift

Authority drift occurs when actual external Permissions exceed canonical Grants.

25.594 Configuration Drift

Configuration drift occurs when runtime state differs from approved configuration.

25.595 Data Drift

Data drift occurs when input distributions change materially.

25.596 Quality Drift

Quality drift occurs when acceptance or mandatory-failure rates worsen.

25.597 Cost Drift

Cost drift occurs when actual economic behaviour changes materially.

25.598 Drift Observation

Drift shall be scoped, evidenced and time-bounded.

25.599 Drift Alert

Drift alerts shall avoid reacting to small expected variation.

25.600 Drift Response

Response may include:

- re-evaluation,

- Routing restriction,

- rollback,

- approval review,

- or Incident declaration.

25.601 Cost Observability

Cost observability shall connect spend to:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Request,

- Execution,

- Attempt,

- Provider,

- Model,

- Tool,

- Asset,

- and outcome.

25.602 Estimated Cost Metric

Estimated cost shall remain distinguishable from actual cost.

25.603 Cost Variance

Variance shall be measured by workflow and resource.

25.604 Cost Per Accepted Output

Cost effectiveness should consider accepted outputs rather than calls only.

25.605 Retry Waste

Failed and duplicate Attempt cost shall remain visible.

25.606 Reservation Leak

Reserved funds or capacity not released shall be detected.

25.607 Budget Burn

Spend velocity shall be compared with approved Budget and period.

25.608 Managed Credit Health

Managed credits shall expose:

- balance,

- reservation,

- usage,

- expiry,

- and allocation.

25.609 User-Owned Account Cost

User-owned Provider usage shall still be observable and Project-attributable.

25.610 Financial Alert

Alerts may trigger on:

- overspend risk,

- unusual rate,

- price change,

- or duplicate charge.

25.611 Quality Observability

Quality observability shall connect evaluations to:

- exact Output,

- Asset Version,

- Provider,

- Model,

- prompt,

- reference,

- and human review.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.612 Acceptance Rate

Acceptance rate shall be scoped to production class and Quality Floor.

25.613 Revision Rate

Human revision rate may indicate resource or prompt weakness.

25.614 Mandatory-Failure Rate

Mandatory failures shall remain distinct from low scores.

25.615 Identity Consistency Metric

Character or Voice consistency may be monitored for defined Projects.

25.616 Factuality Metric

Factual accuracy may require source-grounded evaluation rather than Model self-rating.

25.617 Publication Defect Metric

Defects discovered after publication shall be linked back to production evidence.

25.618 Quality Alert

A Quality alert may trigger when:

- mandatory failures increase,

- acceptance declines,

- or drift appears.

25.619 Privacy Observability

Privacy observability shall monitor:

- external data flows,

- Local Only blocks,

- wrong-scope access,

- retention expiry,

- redaction,

- and deletion.

25.620 Egress Metric

External transfer volume shall be grouped by Classification and Provider.

25.621 Wrong-Scope Denial

Denied cross-Project or cross-Tenant access should be measured and reviewed.

25.622 Deletion Backlog

Expired or requested deletion pending completion shall remain visible.

25.623 Redaction Failure Metric

Failed redaction validation shall trigger review.

25.624 Provider Retention Metric

Provider-side pending deletion and retention uncertainty shall remain visible.

25.625 Privacy Alert

High-severity alerts may include:

- Local Only egress,

- cross-Tenant retrieval,

- child-data exposure,

- or Secret in telemetry.

25.626 Authority Observability

Authority observability shall monitor:

- active Grants,

- Mandates,

- Token use,

- denied actions,

- stale approvals,

- and external Permission drift.

25.627 Mandate Usage

Mandate activity shall show:

- actions,

- cost,

- frequency,

- deviations,

- and expiry.

25.628 Approval Replay Metric

Rejected replay attempts shall be measured.

25.629 Stale Approval Metric

Attempts to use stale Decisions shall remain visible.

25.630 Excess Privilege Metric

External or runtime permissions broader than canonical Grants shall be detected.

25.631 Emergency Authority Metric

Break-glass use shall always generate high-visibility audit and review.

25.735 Applied Example — Wrong August Package

A release Connector publishes an older August Package Version.

Detection may originate from:

- Manifest mismatch,

- checksum mismatch,

- user report,

- or publication verification.

The Incident response:

1. freezes further publication.

2. identifies the exact published Version.

3. verifies affected subscribers.

4. restores the approved Package.

5. records the external correction.

6. reviews approval and Version binding.

7. adds a publication-integrity control.

25.736 Applied Example — Nova Character Drift

Several generated Nova images pass transport validation but fail identity consistency.

Quality Metrics show:

- falling acceptance,

- higher revision,

- and specific mandatory failures.

The condition may trigger a Quality Incident when rejected Candidates are incorrectly promoted.

The investigation preserves:

- Model Version,

- Provider,

- reference Assets,

- prompt,

- evaluations,

- and approval state.

25.737 Applied Example — Pling Missing from Hero Image

A hero generation completes successfully but Pling is absent.

The Provider Attempt is successful.

The Production Step is semantically failed.

The Asset remains a rejected Candidate.

Transport success shall not inflate Quality or completion Metrics.

25.738 Applied Example — Familje-Stunden Child Photo Leak

A child photo appears in an ordinary log field.

The Privacy Alert creates a high-severity Incident.

Containment includes:

- restrict log access,

- stop the logging path,

- identify every copy,

- delete or redact affected records,

- inspect exports and backups,

- and verify that the original workflow remains protected.

The Incident review adds a payload-field denylist and test.

25.739 Applied Example — The Prompt Duplicate Publication

A publication call times out.

The workflow retries without reconciling external state.

Two identical posts appear.

The Incident Timeline links:

- initial Attempt,

- timeout,

- missing unknown-outcome state,

- retry,

- external post IDs,

- and user report.

Corrective Actions include:

- idempotency,

- external verification before retry,

- and duplicate-content alerting.

25.740 Applied Example — The Prompt Source Failure

A news source becomes unavailable during research.

The Provider or Tool health becomes degraded for that source.

The workflow may:

- use approved alternate sources,

- defer publication,

- or request review

according to policy.

The outage shall not be represented as proof that the source is unreliable permanently.

25.741 Applied Example — The Prompt Generated Visual Mislabelled

A generated illustration is published as if it were documentary photography.

This is a publication and disclosure Incident.

Containment may include:

- edit caption,

- replace image,

- or unpublish.

The review inspects:

- disclosure policy,

- Asset metadata,

- publication payload,

- and approval preview.

25.742 Applied Example — GainPilot Programme Stagnation

The user remains on the same programme for many months.

No technical failure occurs.

Operational and outcome observability reveals:

- unchanged programme Version,

- programme age,

- missing progression review,

- and repeated similar sessions.

This may create a product correctness or coaching-quality problem rather than an infrastructure Incident.

The corrective action adds programme-age observability and a review trigger.

25.743 Applied Example — GainPilot Health Data Egress

A Local Only training analysis is accidentally routed to an external Provider.

The Transfer Decision should have blocked the Attempt.

The Incident response:

1. stops the Provider path.

2. identifies exact data disclosed.

3. requests Provider deletion.

4. reviews Account retention.

5. suspends affected Mandate.

6. verifies local-only enforcement.

7. notifies the user according to policy.

25.744 Applied Example — Arnold Wrong Memory

Arnold retrieves an outdated programme state and recommends an invalid exercise.

The Incident investigation links:

- Memory Item,

- expiry,

- retrieval record,

- Agent context,

- recommendation,

- and user correction.

The Memory Item is suspended.

The index is rebuilt if necessary.

A corrective action adds current-programme verification before advice.

25.745 Applied Example — Omnira Repository Path Error

An Agent operates in an outdated repository path.

Observability records:

- working directory,

- repository identity,

- branch,

- and expected Project path.

A mismatch alert stops mutation before damage.

The event remains an operational near miss if no file was changed.

25.746 Applied Example — Repository Migration Incident

A migration process begins copying into a target directory containing unrelated organised content.

A no-overwrite invariant fails.

The workflow stops automatically.

The Incident review inspects:

- source verification,

- target inventory,

- `.git` preservation,

- and rollback state.

The architecture shall prefer containment over “finishing” an ambiguous migration.

25.747 Applied Example — Paid Video Retry Storm

A Provider returns temporary errors.

Multiple workers retry the same job.

Cost and rate Metrics spike.

The Incident response:

- opens the circuit breaker,

- pauses queue consumption,

- deduplicates jobs,

- reconciles unknown outcomes,

- and checks Budget.

The review adds distributed retry coordination and reservation cleanup.

25.748 Applied Example — ElevenLabs Quota Exhaustion

Narration jobs begin failing because the Account quota is exhausted.

Provider Health may remain healthy generally.

Account Health becomes unavailable for the Voice Capability.

The Scheduler should defer, fallback only within approved bounds, or request additional Budget.

Repeated immediate retries are prohibited.

25.749 Applied Example — OpenArt Human Queue Delay

A human-assisted OpenArt workflow waits longer than expected.

The Provider is not technically down.

Human queue observability shows:

- unassigned work,

- review age,

- and missed deadline risk.

The user receives an accurate “waiting for human production” state rather than “generating.”

25.750 Applied Example — Local Ollama Model Load Failure

A local Model fails to load because GPU memory is insufficient.

Node Health shows:

- available VRAM,

- current Model residency,

- load error,

- and thermal state.

The Scheduler may unload an eligible Model, queue work or escalate.

Local Only data shall not fall back externally.

25.751 Applied Example — Provider Callback Delay

A video Provider finishes the job, but the callback arrives late.

Polling finds the result first.

The Trace preserves:

- completion,

- polling discovery,

- late callback,

- deduplication,

- and Asset ingestion.

The late Event does not trigger duplicate processing.

25.752 Applied Example — Audit Pipeline Failure

The audit store stops accepting records while ordinary logs continue.

Meta-monitoring detects the gap.

Consequential actions such as:

- publication,

- deletion,

- Credential change,

- and authority mutation

may pause until canonical audit is restored or a durable fallback is active.

25.753 Applied Example — Approval Notification Failure

A high-cost generation Approval Request is created, but the mobile notification fails.

The request remains pending.

No execution occurs.

Alerting detects notification delivery failure and provides another approved channel.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric

25.754 Applied Example — Stale Approval Use

A publication Package changes after approval.

The Connector attempts execution with the old Approval Token.

The Policy Enforcement Point rejects it.

The denial is audited and may generate a low- or moderate-severity governance alert.

25.755 Applied Example — Credential Exposure

A Provider Token appears in a debug trace.

Containment includes:

- revoke Token,

- disable affected debug export,

- identify every viewer and Location,

- rotate Credential,

- validate dependent Connections,

- and search for further exposure.

The Incident is not closed until the old Token is unusable.

25.756 Applied Example — Cross-Project Search Leak

A GainPilot Agent receives a Familje-Stunden snippet through a shared vector index.

The event is a severe Project-isolation Incident.

Containment includes:

- disable index,

- suspend affected retrieval,

- review contexts and Outputs,

- rebuild with structural filters,

- and test every Project boundary.

25.757 Applied Example — Wrong Social Account

The Prompt content is published to a private personal Account rather than the Project Account.

The Incident combines:

- authority,

- privacy,

- publication,

- and external-state impact.

The exact Account, Asset, caption and visibility are verified.

The content is removed or corrected under explicit authority.

25.758 Applied Example — Unknown Purchase Outcome

A Provider credit purchase times out.

The system does not know whether the charge succeeded.

The Incident or reconciliation workflow checks:

- billing history,

- invoice,

- credit balance,

- and payment state

before any repeat purchase.

25.759 Applied Example — Storage Capacity Warning

The local Mac has critically low free space.

Capacity Metrics show increasing risk to:

- builds,

- Asset ingestion,

- Git operations,

- and evidence storage.

A warning becomes an Incident only when impact or imminent loss requires coordinated response.

Cleanup shall preserve protected Project material and current work.

25.760 Applied Example — External SSD Failure

An external SSD is detected by USB but not exposed as a usable disk.

The response preserves:

- device identifiers,

- system logs,

- error timing,

- and read-only diagnostics.

Write, repair and repeated probing remain prohibited when professional data recovery is the governing decision.

A Project publication is delayed by Provider outage.

The user receives:

- current state,

An Agent attempts an action outside its Mandate.

The Policy Enforcement Point blocks it.

Authority observability records:

- requested action,

- scope mismatch,

- Agent,

- Mandate,

Repeated attempts may suspend the Agent and trigger Incident review.

A recovery operator invokes break-glass authority after owner lockout.

Audit records preserve:

- identity verification,

- scope,

- actions,

- data accessed,

- Credential rotation,

- expiry,

- and post-event review.

Break-glass usage always appears in high-visibility observability.

Current authority, consent and deletion must be reapplied.

25.841 Anti-Pattern — Closed Incident Data Available to Every Developer

Access shall narrow after response.

25.842 Anti-Pattern — Observability Failure Bypasses the Fabric

No blind execution path is authorised merely because monitoring is unavailable.

25.843 Future Observability, Audit and Incident Architecture

Future versions may support:

- autonomous causal diagnosis,

- privacy-preserving telemetry,

- cryptographically verifiable audit,

- cross-Provider trace standards,

- adaptive SLOs,

- intent-aware alerting,

- predictive Incident detection,

- digital twins,

- automated containment proofs,

- formal recovery verification,

- and federated Incident learning.

Future evolution must preserve:

- scope,

- identity,

- evidence,

- Classification,

- authority,

- human control,

- and uncertainty.

25.844 Causal Diagnosis

Future systems may infer likely causal chains from traces, Metrics, Events and changes.

Inferences shall remain labelled and evidence-linked.

25.845 Change Correlation

Deployments, policy changes, Provider changes and configuration drift may be correlated with Incident onset.

25.846 Predictive Incident Detection

Forecasts may identify:

- capacity exhaustion,

- quota risk,

- deadline failure,

- or quality drift

before user impact.

25.847 Predictive Alert Uncertainty

Prediction confidence and false-positive cost shall remain visible.

25.848 Intent-Aware Observability

The system may compare actual behaviour with the original Intent Envelope and Completion Contract.

25.849 Outcome-Aware SLO

Future SLOs may measure verified user outcomes rather than technical responses alone.

25.850 Adaptive SLO

Objectives may adapt by:

- Capability,

- risk,

- Project,

- and user expectation

through approved policy.

25.851 Privacy-Preserving Metrics

Aggregation, selective disclosure or secure computation may reduce exposure.

25.852 Federated Telemetry

Local Nodes may retain raw telemetry while sharing approved aggregates.

25.853 Differentially Private Analytics

Statistical privacy techniques may protect aggregate platform learning.

Accuracy limits shall remain explicit.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.854 Confidential Observability

Secure enclaves or protected processing may analyse sensitive telemetry.

25.855 Verifiable Audit Log

Hash chains, signatures or external anchoring may strengthen tamper evidence.

25.856 Selective Audit Proof

A system may prove that an authorised action occurred without exposing unrelated records.

25.857 Cross-Provider Trace Interoperability

Standard trace context may improve external correlation.

Canonical Omnira identity remains authoritative.

25.858 Incident Digital Twin

A digital twin may model:

- dependencies,

- current state,

- affected scope,

- containment,

- and recovery options.

25.859 Response Simulation

The system may simulate containment and recovery impact before execution.

25.860 Automated Containment Proposal

Agents may propose containment based on evidence.

High-impact actions remain approval-bound.

25.861 Bounded Automatic Containment

Low-risk reversible containment may execute under an explicit Mandate.

25.862 Formal Recovery Proof

Future systems may verify that restored state satisfies defined invariants.

25.863 Continuous Control Verification

Privacy, authority, isolation and reliability controls may be tested continuously.

25.864 Observability Policy Compiler

Human-readable telemetry policy may compile into collectors, filters, retention and alerts.

25.865 Automated Runbook Execution

Safe Runbook Steps may execute automatically inside an approved Incident Mandate.

25.866 Runbook Decision Point

Human approval remains required where Steps become destructive, externally visible or irreversible.

25.867 Incident Copilot

An Incident Agent may:

- summarise evidence,

- maintain timeline,

- suggest hypotheses,

- and prepare updates.

It shall not fabricate facts or become Incident Commander automatically.

25.868 Audit Copilot

An Audit Agent may identify:

- gaps,

- drift,

- and unusual authority use

without receiving unnecessary content.

25.869 Cross-Incident Learning

Reviewed patterns may improve controls across Projects only when privacy and scope permit.

25.870 Federated Incident Learning

Tenants may share anonymised failure patterns without sharing raw data.

25.871 SLO-Based Autonomy

Autonomy may narrow automatically when error budgets are exhausted.

It shall not broaden automatically.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.872 Dynamic Incident Severity

Severity may update from verified impact signals.

25.873 User-Controlled Incident Preferences

Users may choose notification detail and cadence within mandatory requirements.

25.874 Observability Success Criteria

The observability architecture succeeds when:

- every material Execution is correlated end to end,

- service and workflow state can be understood,

- Metrics expose distributions and saturation,

- logs remain privacy-safe,

- traces preserve causality,

- health remains scoped and fresh,

- alerts are actionable,

- and observability failures are detected.

25.875 Audit Success Criteria

The audit architecture succeeds when:

- every consequential action has an accountable actor,

- authority basis is linked,

- exact targets and Versions are preserved,

- records are tamper-evident,

- access is scoped,

- required Events are complete,

- and historical governance state is reconstructable.

25.876 Incident Response Success Criteria

Incident Response succeeds when:

- material harm is detected,

- ownership is assigned,

- scope and severity remain explicit,

- containment stops further impact,

- evidence is preserved,

- recovery is verified,

- users receive accurate communication,

- and Corrective Actions reduce recurrence.

25.877 Observability Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- correlation is missing,

- protected payloads enter ordinary telemetry,

- missing data appears healthy,

- tail latency is invisible,

- dashboards are stale without warning,

- or alerts have no owner.

25.878 Audit Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- actor or authority is missing,

- mandatory records can be edited silently,

- Secret values are stored,

- audit access is unrestricted,

- or ingestion gaps remain undetected.

25.879 Incident Response Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- Incidents lack owner,

- severity ignores privacy or authority impact,

- containment destroys evidence,

- recovery lacks verification,

- communication hides uncertainty,

- or learning is not converted into owned action.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.880 Canonical Telemetry Contract

The following requirements define canonical telemetry:

1. Every material Telemetry Record SHALL have identity or stable series membership.

2. Producer SHALL be explicit.

3. Tenant, Project and Environment SHALL be explicit where applicable.

4. Correlation SHALL be preserved.

5. Observed and recorded time SHALL remain distinct.

6. Clock source and skew SHALL be understood.

7. Classification SHALL be explicit.

8. Retention SHALL be explicit.

9. Sampling state SHALL be explicit.

10. Missing telemetry SHALL remain distinct from zero.

11. Freshness SHALL be visible.

12. Telemetry loss SHALL be measurable.

13. High-risk governance Events SHALL not be sampled away.

14. Protected payload SHALL be minimised.

15. Secrets SHALL be prohibited.

16. Telemetry access SHALL be scoped.

17. Historical data SHALL remain queryable according to retention.

18. Telemetry changes SHALL be Versioned where material.

19. Telemetry SHALL remain distinct from audit and evidence.

20. Observability collection SHALL NOT create new processing authority.

25.881 Canonical Metric Contract

The following requirements define Metrics:

1. Every Metric Definition SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Name SHALL be stable and meaningful.

3. Unit SHALL be explicit.

4. Metric type SHALL be explicit.

5. Dimensions SHALL be explicit.

6. Aggregation SHALL be explicit.

7. Source SHALL be explicit.

8. Scope SHALL be explicit.

9. Retention SHALL be explicit.

10. Missing values SHALL not become zero automatically.

11. High-cardinality protected dimensions SHALL be controlled.

12. Averages SHALL not replace distributions where tails matter.

13. p95 and p99 SHOULD be available for critical latency.

14. Derived formulas SHALL be Versioned.

15. Quality, cost and transport success SHALL remain distinct.

16. Metric freshness SHALL be visible.

17. Baselines SHALL be scoped.

18. Anomaly SHALL not become confirmed failure automatically.

19. Historical Definitions SHALL remain queryable.

20. Metrics SHALL NOT become the sole source of operational truth.

25.882 Canonical Logging Contract

The following requirements define logs:

1. Logs SHALL be structured where practical.

2. Severity SHALL be consistent.

3. Producer SHALL be explicit.

4. Correlation SHALL be present.

5. Tenant, Project and Environment SHALL be present where applicable.

6. Message templates SHALL avoid dynamic protected content.

7. Full prompts SHALL be prohibited by default.

8. Full Outputs SHALL be prohibited by default.

9. Private communications SHALL be prohibited by default.

10. Secret values SHALL never be logged.

11. Authentication headers and signed URLs SHALL be sanitised.

12. File paths SHALL be minimised.

13. Stack traces SHALL be access-controlled.

14. Debug mode SHALL be bounded.

15. Sampling SHALL not omit material failures or governance Events.

16. Retention SHALL be explicit.

17. Access SHALL be scoped.

18. Export SHALL preserve Classification.

19. Historical access SHALL remain auditable.

20. Logs SHALL NOT substitute for canonical audit or evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.883 Canonical Trace Contract

The following requirements define traces:

1. Every material distributed operation SHOULD have stable Trace identity.

2. Root operation SHALL be explicit.

3. Request and Execution SHALL be linked.

4. Parent-child causality SHALL be preserved.

5. Asynchronous links SHALL remain explicit.

6. Queue wait SHALL remain distinct from processing.

7. Provider and Tool calls SHALL be represented.

8. Approval and human-review wait SHALL be represented.

9. Evaluation and external verification SHALL be represented.

10. Span status SHALL be explicit.

11. Duration SHALL use reliable elapsed time.

12. Sampling state SHALL be explicit.

13. Failed and high-risk traces SHALL be preserved according to policy.

14. Baggage SHALL exclude Secrets and protected payload.

15. External trace context SHALL be validated.

16. Broken propagation SHALL be detected.

17. Critical path SHALL be derivable.

18. Historical traces SHALL remain queryable according to retention.

19. Trace SHALL remain distinct from business Outcome Verification.

20. A completed Trace SHALL NOT prove accepted completion automatically.

25.884 Canonical Health Contract

The following requirements define health:

1. Every material Health Observation SHALL have stable identity.

2. Subject SHALL be explicit.

3. Health dimension SHALL be explicit.

4. Observation time SHALL be explicit.

5. Freshness SHALL be explicit.

6. Source SHALL be explicit.

7. Confidence SHALL be explicit.
