sectionTitles: 25.901 Observability, Audit and Incident Response Invariants
text:
25.901 Observability, Audit and Incident Response Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No Metric becomes an Event automatically.

- No log line becomes canonical audit automatically.

- No trace becomes proof of business completion.

- No Provider success becomes accepted Output automatically.

- No missing telemetry becomes healthy zero.

- No average hides mandatory tail analysis.

- No alert becomes Incident without triage.

- No alert silence erases history.

- No high-severity alert lacks ownership.

- No audit event lacks actor, target and authority basis.

- No Secret enters ordinary logs, traces, Metrics or audit payload.

- No Incident lacks stable identity and explicit state.

- No severity ignores privacy, authority or irreversibility.

- No containment destroys required evidence.

- No recovery is complete without verification.

- No user communication presents speculation as fact.

- No Post-Incident Review ends with unowned actions.

- No corrective action closes without evidence.

- No Runbook governs production without Version and authority.

- No observability, audit or Incident failure bypasses the Intelligence Fabric.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
25.902 Closing Statement

Observability allows Omnira to understand what is happening.

Audit allows Omnira to prove who acted, under which authority and against which exact state.

Incident Response allows Omnira to contain harm, recover safely and improve without rewriting history.

The Metric measures behaviour.

The log records bounded operational detail.

The Trace preserves causal execution.

The Event records meaningful state change.

The Health Observation reports one measured condition.

The Health Evaluation determines whether a resource or service is fit for purpose.

The SLI defines what is measured.

The SLO defines the required objective.

The Error Budget defines tolerated non-conformance.

The Dashboard presents authorised operational state.

The Alert Rule identifies conditions requiring attention.

The Audit Event preserves accountable action.

The Audit Trail preserves historical governance.

The Incident defines coordinated response to material harm.

The Incident Timeline preserves what was known and done.

The Containment Action stops further impact.

The Recovery Action restores intended state.

The Verification Record proves that recovery is real.

The Communication Record preserves what affected people were told.

The Post-Incident Review explains what happened and why.

The Corrective Action converts learning into accountable change.

The Runbook makes known response repeatable.

The Chaos Experiment and Game Day prove that resilience exists outside documentation.

For Familje-Stunden, this architecture ensures that:

- August releases use the correct Package Version,

- Nova and Pling quality drift is detected before publication,

- child data never disappears into ordinary logs,

- subscriber-visible delivery is externally verified,

- and publication mistakes can be contained and corrected with full evidence.

For The Prompt, it ensures that:

- research, generation and publication remain end-to-end traceable,

- duplicate posts are detected and reconciled,

- generated visuals remain distinguishable from documentary evidence,

- source and Provider failures remain scoped,

- and daily automation never hides wrong-account or wrong-content publication.

For GainPilot, it ensures that:

- Arnold’s recommendations remain linked to current programme state,

- programme stagnation becomes visible,

- health and training data remain protected,

- Local Only routing failures are detected,

- and coaching quality is measured through user outcomes rather than transport success.

For Atlas, it ensures that:

- every Plan, Routing Decision and delegated action remains observable,

- Memory influence remains attributable,

- authority boundaries remain visible,

- Model and Provider drift are detected,

- and autonomous behaviour can be stopped when evidence indicates risk.

For Omnira, it ensures that:

- users,

- Tenants,

- Projects,

- Agents,

- Models,

- Providers,

- Tools,

- Nodes,

- queues,

- Assets,

- Memory,

- approvals,

- publications,

- and external systems

participate in one accountable operational truth.

The system may be fast.

It may be available.

It may be correct.

It may be cheap.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
It may be private.

It may be authorised.

It may be recoverable.

None of those qualities should be assumed from one green indicator.

No operation without correlation.

No health claim without fresh evidence.

No latency claim without distribution.

No alert without ownership.

No audit without actor and authority.

No Incident without scope and command.

No containment without evidence preservation.

No recovery without verification.

No communication without truth about uncertainty.

No learning without corrective ownership.

No autonomy without observability.

The user retains the right to know what happened.

The Project retains its operational history.

Omnira retains audit, response and recovery governance.

The Fabric shall never claim that intelligence is under control unless it can observe the work, prove the authority, detect the harm and demonstrate the recovery.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical architecture, object model, workflows, quality gates, lifecycle controls and conformance requirements for developer experience, testing and implementation assurance within the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

It establishes:

- how developers interact with the Fabric without bypassing its governance,

- how canonical schemas, APIs, SDKs, command-line tools, local environments and documentation remain aligned,

- how implementation contracts become executable tests,

- how component tests, integration tests, contract tests, conformance tests, system tests and acceptance tests remain distinct,

- how Provider, Model, Tool, Adapter, Connector, Agent, workflow and local Node integrations are tested,

- how test data remains isolated from production data,

- how paid Provider tests remain bounded and attributable,

- how publishing, deletion, messaging, purchasing and other external side effects remain disabled or safely redirected during testing,

- how deterministic fixtures coexist with probabilistic Model evaluation,

- how Quality evaluation differs from software correctness,

- how golden tests, benchmark suites, rubrics, statistical tests and human review are governed,

- how test environments preserve Tenant, Project, Credential, data and authority isolation,

- how local development remains representative without requiring unrestricted production access,

- how mocks, stubs, fakes, simulators, emulators, sandboxes and live tests remain distinguishable,

- how Provider-specific behaviour is validated without leaking into canonical business logic,

- how schema and protocol compatibility are tested,

- how API, event, queue, webhook, callback and Tool contracts remain Versioned,

- how retries, timeouts, unknown outcomes, duplicate delivery and partial completion are tested,

- how privacy, rights, consent, classification, authority, Budget and provenance controls receive first-class conformance tests,

- how performance, load, stress, endurance, capacity and latency tests remain bounded,

- how security tests address Secrets, supply chain, Sandbox escape, prompt injection, Tool misuse and cross-scope access,

- how test evidence remains attributable and reviewable,

- how builds, releases, migrations and deployments receive quality gates,

- how failed tests block promotion according to risk,

- how exceptions remain explicit, expiring and approved,

- how conformance certification applies to Adapters, Connectors, Models, Providers, Tools, Agents, workflows and services,

- how external drift invalidates prior certification when necessary,

- how regression suites preserve previously fixed behaviour,

- how developer productivity is improved without weakening architecture,

- how Stage 1 shall implement the smallest trustworthy developer and conformance foundation,

- and how future autonomous development remains bounded by the same evidence and authority model.

A successful build is not proof of correctness.

A passing unit test is not proof of system conformance.

A working demo is not production readiness.

A mock response is not evidence that the Provider behaves the same way.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
A Provider sandbox is not always equivalent to production.

A deterministic snapshot is not sufficient for probabilistic intelligence quality.

A Model benchmark is not a software contract test.

A high benchmark score is not proof of policy compliance.

A manual test without recorded evidence is not canonical conformance.

A test environment is not permitted to use production data merely because it is non-public.

A development Credential is not a production Credential.

A test Account is not a user Account.

A successful API response is not proof of external outcome.

A timeout test is incomplete if unknown outcome is not represented.

A retry test is incomplete if cost, idempotency and duplicate side effects are ignored.

A test suite that cannot fail meaningfully is not assurance.

A flaky test is not harmless when it hides real regressions.

A waived test is not permanently removed from governance.

A certification is not eternal.

A release tag is not approval to deploy.

Developer convenience shall never become an implicit exception to privacy, authority or Project isolation.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

Stage 1 implementation architecture is expanded in Chapter 27.

Rollout, migration, anti-patterns and future evolution are expanded in Chapter 28.

Implementation, tooling and operational conformance must be verified separately.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 26.2 Purpose of Developer Experience, Testing and Conformance
text:
26.2 Purpose of Developer Experience, Testing and Conformance

The Intelligence Fabric depends on many independently changing components, including:

- canonical schemas,

- control-plane services,

- Agents,

- Models,

- Providers,

- Adapters,

- Connectors,

- local Runtimes,

- Tools,

- MCP servers,

- queues,

- webhooks,

- Asset stores,

- Memory systems,

- approval services,

- and external publication platforms.

Those components may fail through:

- schema mismatch,

- incorrect mapping,

- stale Provider assumptions,

- broken retry logic,

- missing idempotency,

- unsupported cancellation,

- wrong data classification,

- Credential leakage,

- cross-Project access,

- unbounded cost,

- incorrect rights handling,

- missing provenance,

- false success reporting,

- incompatible Model updates,

- and unsafe developer shortcuts.

Without a canonical developer and conformance architecture, Omnira could:

- implement the same contract differently in several services,

- allow Provider SDKs to bypass the Adapter boundary,

- accept incompatible event Versions,

- test only happy paths,

- use production Accounts for experiments,

- incur uncontrolled Provider spend,

- publish or delete during automated testing,

- treat probabilistic quality as deterministic correctness,

- certify an integration once and never re-evaluate it,

- or ship a release whose observable behaviour contradicts the approved architecture.

The architecture exists to ensure that developers can answer:

- Which canonical contracts govern this component?

- Which schemas and Versions are supported?

- Which test environment is safe?

- Which data and Credentials may be used?

- Which side effects are permitted?

- Which test types are required?

- Which Provider behaviours are simulated?

- Which behaviours are verified live?

- Which failures are covered?

- Which policy invariants are executable?

- Which conformance profile applies?

- Which evidence proves compliance?

- Which exceptions remain open?

- Which release gates must pass?

- Which drift conditions invalidate prior results?

- How can a developer reproduce a failure locally?

- How can a change be rolled back safely?

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 26.4 Developer Experience Is Not Convenience Alone
text:
26.3 Developer Experience

Developer Experience is the complete set of interfaces, tools, environments, documentation, feedback loops and guardrails through which people and coding Agents build, test, inspect and evolve the Intelligence Fabric.

26.4 Developer Experience Is Not Convenience Alone

Good developer experience reduces unnecessary friction.

It shall not hide:

- authority,

- policy,

- cost,

- privacy,

- or operational consequence.

26.5 Developer Interface

A Developer Interface is a governed interaction surface for building or operating the Fabric.

Examples include:

- API,

- SDK,

- CLI,

- local service,

- schema package,

- test harness,

- dashboard,

- code generator,

- and documentation portal.

26.6 Developer Identity

Every developer, coding Agent and automation acting on implementation state shall have a stable Principal identity.

26.7 Developer Authority

Developer authority shall remain scoped to:

- repository,

- branch,

- worktree,

- Environment,

- service,

- data,

- Credential,

- and operation.

26.8 Developer Environment

A Developer Environment is an isolated workspace used to create, run, test or inspect implementation changes.

Types may include:

- local,

- remote development,

- containerised,

- ephemeral preview,

- test,

- integration,

- staging,

- and production diagnostic.

26.9 Developer Environment Identity

Every governed shared or ephemeral Developer Environment should have stable identity.

26.10 Local Development

Local Development occurs on an approved local Node.

It shall preserve:

- Project scope,

- file access,

- Secret boundaries,

- test data isolation,

- and reproducibility.

26.11 Remote Development

Remote Development uses hosted or remote compute.

Its data and Credential eligibility shall be explicit.

26.12 Ephemeral Environment

An Ephemeral Environment is created for a bounded branch, pull request, test or review and destroyed afterward.

26.13 Environment Parity

Environment Parity describes how closely a lower Environment represents production behaviour.

26.14 Parity Is Not Identity

Development and production should share contracts and architecture where practical.

They shall not share unrestricted data, Credentials or external side effects.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.15 Developer Control Plane

The Developer Control Plane is the governed collection of services and artefacts responsible for:

- schemas,

- SDKs,

- CLI,

- local setup,

- environment creation,

- test orchestration,

- fixture management,

- conformance evaluation,

- build evidence,

- release gates,

- and developer documentation.

26.16 Canonical Developer and Conformance Objects

The canonical architecture should include or reference:

- Developer Environment,

- Environment Profile,

- Schema Package,

- API Definition,

- SDK Package,

- CLI Package,

- Code Generator,

- Example Project,

- Test Suite,

- Test Case,

- Test Run,

- Test Result,

- Test Fixture,

- Test Dataset,

- Mock Definition,

- Stub Definition,

- Fake Service,

- Simulator,

- Emulator,

- Provider Sandbox Profile,

- Golden Dataset,

- Benchmark Suite,

- Evaluation Suite,

- Load Profile,

- Fault Scenario,

- Conformance Profile,

- Conformance Requirement,

- Conformance Test,

- Conformance Run,

- Conformance Result,

- Certification,

- Certification Scope,

- Certification Exception,

- Regression Record,

- Build Record,

- Release Candidate,

- Promotion Decision,

- and Developer Incident.

26.17 Canonical Contract

A Canonical Contract defines required behaviour, structure, state, constraints or interoperability for one Fabric concept or boundary.

26.18 Contract Sources

Canonical Contracts may originate from:

- approved architecture chapters,

- canonical schemas,

- API definitions,

- event specifications,

- policy definitions,

- state machines,

- and invariants.

26.19 Contract Identity

Every executable Canonical Contract shall have stable identity and Version.

26.20 Contract Version

Material contract changes shall create a new Version.

26.21 Contract Status

Contract states may include:

- draft,

- proposed,

- approved,

- active,

- deprecated,

- superseded,

- retired,

- and archived.

26.22 Contract Scope

Scope may include:

- service,

- Adapter,

- Connector,

- Provider Product,

- Model,

- Tool,

- Agent,

- workflow,

- event,

- API,

- or data object.

26.23 Contract Requirement

A Contract Requirement is one testable normative statement.

It shall include or reference:

- requirementId,

- source contract,

- statement,

- severity,

- scope,

- verification method,

- and Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.24 Requirement Identity

Every material Contract Requirement shall have stable identity.

26.25 Mandatory Requirement

A mandatory requirement shall block certification or release when unsatisfied unless a valid exception exists.

26.26 Advisory Requirement

An advisory requirement may recommend improvement without blocking certification.

26.27 Conditional Requirement

A conditional requirement becomes mandatory when its triggering condition applies.

26.28 Non-Applicable Requirement

Non-applicability shall be justified and evidenced.

It shall not be selected merely to avoid testing.

26.29 Executable Invariant

An Executable Invariant is a canonical invariant expressed as machine-verifiable logic or test.

Examples include:

- no Local Only egress,

- no missing Project scope,

- no Secret in logs,

- no publication without exact approval,

- and no retry after unknown outcome without reconciliation.

26.30 Human-Verified Requirement

Some requirements require human judgement.

Examples include:

- understandable approval presentation,

- visual identity continuity,

- editorial quality,

- and user trust.

26.31 Mixed Verification

A requirement may combine:

- deterministic test,

- automated evaluation,

- and human review.

26.32 Schema Package

A Schema Package contains Versioned canonical data schemas.

It shall include or reference:

- package identity,

- schema Versions,

- compatibility policy,

- generators,

- examples,

- validation rules,

- and checksums.

26.33 Schema Package Identity

Every Schema Package shall have stable identity and Version.

26.34 Schema Format

Formats may include:

- JSON Schema,

- Protocol Buffers,

- OpenAPI schemas,

- GraphQL schema,

- TypeScript definitions,

- database schema,

- or another approved representation.

26.35 Canonical Schema Source

One declared source shall generate or govern derived language bindings where practical.

26.36 Schema Duplication

Manually duplicated schema definitions should be avoided.

26.37 Schema Validation

All boundary Inputs and Outputs shall be validated against the applicable schema.

26.38 Schema Compatibility

Compatibility may be:

- backward,

- forward,

- full,

- none,

- or conditionally compatible.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.39 Backward Compatibility

A newer consumer remains able to process older valid data.

26.40 Forward Compatibility

An older consumer remains able to process newer data within defined tolerance.

26.41 Breaking Change

A breaking change alters behaviour or structure in a way incompatible with existing consumers.

26.42 Non-Breaking Change

A non-breaking change preserves defined compatibility.

26.43 Semantic Breaking Change

A field may retain its type while changing meaning.

Semantic compatibility shall be reviewed separately from structural compatibility.

26.44 Schema Default

Defaults shall be explicit and shall not hide omitted mandatory information.

26.45 Unknown Field Handling

Unknown fields shall be:

- ignored,

- preserved,

- rejected,

- or quarantined

according to the contract.

26.46 Unknown Enum Handling

Unknown enum values shall not be mapped silently to an unrelated known value.

26.47 Null Handling

Null, absent, empty and unknown shall remain distinguishable where material.

26.48 Schema Migration

Migration shall preserve:

- identity,

- provenance,

- Classification,

- lifecycle,

- and historical interpretation.

26.49 API Definition

An API Definition describes one governed service interface.

It shall include or reference:

- API identity,

- operations,

- Inputs,

- Outputs,

- errors,

- authentication,

- authority,

- idempotency,

- rate limits,

- and Version.

26.50 API Definition Identity

Every API Definition shall have stable identity and Version.

26.51 API Operation

Every operation shall define:

- purpose,

- request schema,

- response schema,

- error states,

- authority,

- side effects,

- idempotency,

- and observability.

26.52 API Error Contract

Errors shall use canonical categories and preserve Provider-native detail only as bounded metadata.

26.53 API Idempotency Contract

Consequential operations shall define:

- idempotency key,

- replay behaviour,

- retention,

- and conflict response.

26.54 API Pagination

Pagination shall define:

- ordering,

- cursor semantics,

- stability,

- and scope.

26.55 API Filtering

Filters shall not bypass Tenant, Project or authority constraints.

26.56 API Versioning

Versioning may use:

- path,

- header,

- schema,

- operation Version,

- or capability negotiation.

The method shall be consistent.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.57 API Deprecation

Deprecation shall include:

- replacement,

- notice,

- migration path,

- and retirement date.

26.58 Event Contract

An Event Contract defines:

- event identity,

- type,

- schema,

- producer,

- consumer expectations,

- ordering,

- deduplication,

- retention,

- and Version.

26.59 Event Contract Identity

Every Event Contract shall have stable identity and Version.

26.60 Event Consumer Compatibility

Consumers shall tolerate supported event Versions without fabricating unknown semantics.

26.61 Event Replay Conformance

Replayed Events shall preserve original identity and event time.

26.62 Queue Contract

A Queue Contract defines:

- message schema,

- partitioning,

- ordering,

- lease,

- acknowledgement,

- retry,

- dead-letter,

- and deduplication.

26.63 Webhook Contract

A Webhook Contract defines:

- subscription,

- event types,

- authentication,

- signature,

- retry,

- ordering,

- replay protection,

- and reconciliation.

26.64 Tool Contract

A Tool Contract defines:

- Tool identity,

- input schema,

- output schema,

- permissions,

- side effects,

- Environment,

- timeouts,

- and error semantics.

26.65 Agent Contract

An Agent Contract defines:

- identity,

- role,

- authority,

- Inputs,

- Outputs,

- Memory access,

- Tool access,

- escalation,

- and prohibited behaviour.

26.66 Workflow Contract

A Workflow Contract defines:

- objective,

- Inputs,

- state machine,

- Steps,

- dependencies,

- retries,

- compensation,

- completion,

- and evidence.

26.67 SDK Package

An SDK Package provides language-specific access to canonical APIs and objects.

It shall include or reference:

- package identity,

- language,

- supported API Versions,

- generated types,

- authentication helpers,

- error types,

- observability hooks,

- and examples.

26.68 SDK Package Identity

Every SDK Package shall have stable identity and Version.

26.69 SDK Source

Generated SDK code should derive from canonical API and schema definitions where practical.

26.70 SDK Abstraction

The SDK shall expose Fabric concepts rather than Provider-specific implementation details above the Adapter boundary.

26.71 SDK Authentication

The SDK shall support approved authentication without exposing raw Secrets unnecessarily.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.72 SDK Authority Context

The SDK shall require or derive:

- Principal,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- purpose,

- and authority context

for governed operations.

26.73 SDK Error Handling

SDK errors shall preserve canonical categories and correlation.

26.74 SDK Retry

SDKs shall not perform hidden retries that bypass canonical Reliability Policy.

26.75 SDK Timeout

Timeouts shall be configurable within policy and shall not imply external failure.

26.76 SDK Telemetry

SDKs should emit bounded correlation and operational telemetry.

26.77 SDK Compatibility

SDK Version compatibility with API Versions shall be declared.

26.78 SDK Deprecation

Deprecated methods shall identify replacement and removal schedule.

26.79 CLI Package

A CLI Package provides governed command-line interaction with the Fabric.

It shall include:

- command identity,

- configuration,

- authentication,

- scope display,

- dry-run,

- output formats,

- and audit integration.

26.80 CLI Package Identity

Every CLI Package shall have stable identity and Version.

26.81 CLI Scope Visibility

The CLI shall clearly display:

- Environment,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Account,

- and destructive target

before consequential actions.

26.82 CLI Dry Run

Dry-run mode shall display intended actions without creating side effects.

26.83 CLI Confirmation

High-risk confirmation shall bind to exact scope.

Generic interactive confirmation shall not replace formal Approval where required.

26.84 CLI Non-Interactive Mode

Automation mode shall require explicit Tokens, scopes and exit codes.

26.85 CLI Output

Output formats may include:

- human-readable,

- JSON,

- structured table,

- and machine event stream.

26.86 CLI Secret Handling

Secrets shall not appear in command history, process listings or ordinary output.

26.87 CLI Exit Code

Exit codes shall distinguish:

- success,

- validation failure,

- denial,

- partial result,

- timeout,

- unknown outcome,

- and internal failure.

26.88 Code Generator

A Code Generator creates types, clients, validators, fixtures or service skeletons from canonical definitions.

26.89 Code Generator Identity

Every Code Generator shall have stable identity and Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.90 Generated Code Provenance

Generated artefacts shall preserve generator and source-schema Versions.

26.91 Generated Code Modification

Manual edits to generated code should be prohibited or clearly separated.

26.92 Example Project

An Example Project demonstrates approved integration patterns.

It shall avoid:

- production Credentials,

- real personal data,

- uncontrolled spend,

- and unsafe side effects.

26.93 Reference Implementation

A Reference Implementation demonstrates one conformant implementation.

It does not become the only permitted internal architecture unless declared.

26.94 Developer Documentation

Developer Documentation shall describe:

- concepts,

- setup,

- contracts,

- examples,

- testing,

- errors,

- security,

- and migration.

26.95 Documentation Identity

Canonical documentation sets should have stable Version and release relationship.

26.96 Documentation Source

Documentation should derive from or link to canonical contracts.

26.97 Documentation Accuracy

Documentation shall be tested against current APIs and examples where practical.

26.98 Documentation Drift

Outdated documentation is a conformance defect.

26.99 Quick Start

A Quick Start should achieve a safe first successful operation without requiring production privileges.

26.100 Setup Validation

Setup tools should verify:

- Runtime,

- dependencies,

- Environment,

- Credentials by reference,

- network,

- and Project scope.

26.101 Developer Bootstrap

Bootstrap shall be:

- reproducible,

- idempotent,

- and reversible.

26.102 Dependency Locking

Dependencies should be pinned or constrained according to supply-chain policy.

26.103 Reproducible Build

A Reproducible Build produces materially equivalent artefacts from the same source and declared inputs.

26.104 Build Environment

The build Environment, compiler, dependencies and generator Versions shall be attributable.

26.105 Build Record

A Build Record shall include or reference:

- buildId,

- source commit,

- branch,

- repository,

- Environment,

- toolchain,

- dependencies,

- tests,

- artefacts,

- checksums,

- and result.

26.106 Build Record Identity

Every release-relevant Build Record shall have stable identity.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.107 Build Artefact

Build artefacts shall have:

- stable identity,

- Version,

- checksum,

- provenance,

- and Classification.

26.108 Build Cache

Build caches shall remain scoped and non-authoritative.

26.109 Build Cache Poisoning

Untrusted or cross-Project cache content shall not be reused without integrity verification.

26.110 Test

A Test is a defined procedure that evaluates whether an implementation, object or system satisfies expected behaviour.

26.111 Test Suite

A Test Suite is a governed collection of related Tests.

It shall include or reference:

- testSuiteId,

- purpose,

- scope,

- requirements,

- Environment,

- fixtures,

- owner,

- and Version.

26.112 Test Suite Identity

Every material Test Suite shall have stable identity and Version.

26.113 Test Case

A Test Case defines:

- preconditions,

- Inputs,

- operation,

- expected result,

- assertions,

- cleanup,

- and evidence.

26.114 Test Case Identity

Every material Test Case shall have stable identity and Version.

26.115 Test Run

A Test Run is one execution of a Test Suite or Test Case.

It shall include or reference:

- testRunId,

- Suite Version,

- source commit,

- Environment,

- configuration,

- fixtures,

- start,

- end,

- results,

- logs,

- cost,

- and evidence.

26.116 Test Run Identity

Every Test Run shall have stable identity.

26.117 Test Result

A Test Result records one outcome.

States may include:

- passed,

- failed,

- skipped,

- blocked,

- inconclusive,

- flaky,

- quarantined,

- and not applicable.

26.118 Passed

Passed means the observed result satisfied defined assertions.

26.119 Failed

Failed means at least one mandatory assertion was unsatisfied.

26.120 Skipped

Skipped means the Test did not execute.

The reason shall be explicit.

26.121 Blocked

Blocked means a prerequisite prevented execution.

26.122 Inconclusive

Inconclusive means the available evidence cannot establish pass or fail.

26.123 Flaky

Flaky means repeated executions produce inconsistent results without intended input change.

26.124 Quarantined Test

A quarantined Test remains visible but does not govern ordinary release gating temporarily.

Quarantine requires:

- owner,

- reason,

- expiry,

- and remediation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.125 Not Applicable

Not Applicable requires a justified condition showing that the requirement does not apply.

26.126 Test Severity

Tests may be classified as:

- release blocking,

- certification blocking,

- warning,

- informational,

- or experimental.

26.127 Test Evidence

Test Evidence may include:

- assertions,

- logs,

- traces,

- Metrics,

- screenshots,

- Assets,

- external IDs,

- and human review.

26.128 Test Reproducibility

A failed Test should be reproducible or preserve enough evidence to investigate.

26.129 Test Isolation

Tests shall not depend on unrelated test order or shared mutable state unless explicitly designed.

26.130 Test Cleanup

Tests shall clean up temporary resources without deleting required evidence.

26.131 Test Idempotency

Repeated Test Runs shall not create unintended cumulative side effects.

26.132 Test Determinism

Deterministic Tests should produce consistent results for the same controlled inputs.

26.133 Probabilistic Test

A Probabilistic Test evaluates behaviour with expected statistical variation.

26.134 Probabilistic Assertion

Assertions may use:

- thresholds,

- confidence intervals,

- distributions,

- acceptance rates,

- or repeated sampling.

26.135 Single-Sample Limitation

One Model Output shall not prove stable probabilistic behaviour.

26.136 Test Oracle

A Test Oracle determines the expected result.

Oracles may be:

- exact expected value,

- invariant,

- schema,

- reference implementation,

- external ground truth,

- human rubric,

- or statistical criterion.

26.137 Oracle Authority

The Oracle source and limitations shall be explicit.

26.138 False Oracle

An incorrect expected result may cause a valid implementation to fail or an invalid implementation to pass.

26.139 Oracle Review

High-impact Oracles shall be reviewed and Versioned.

26.140 Test Pyramid

The test strategy should combine:

- unit tests,

- component tests,

- integration tests,

- contract tests,

- system tests,

- end-to-end tests,

- conformance tests,

- security tests,

- performance tests,

- and human acceptance tests.

26.141 Unit Test

A Unit Test evaluates one small code unit in isolation.

26.142 Component Test

A Component Test evaluates one service or module with controlled dependencies.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.143 Integration Test

An Integration Test evaluates interaction among two or more real components.

26.144 Contract Test

A Contract Test verifies that a producer or consumer satisfies a declared interface contract.

26.145 System Test

A System Test evaluates the integrated Fabric or a substantial subsystem.

26.146 End-to-End Test

An End-to-End Test evaluates the full path from Request to verified Completion or intended Outcome.

26.147 Conformance Test

A Conformance Test verifies a canonical requirement independent of one implementation’s internal design.

26.148 Acceptance Test

An Acceptance Test verifies that the system satisfies user, Project or business criteria.

26.149 Regression Test

A Regression Test preserves behaviour associated with a previously fixed defect or approved capability.

26.150 Smoke Test

A Smoke Test checks whether critical basic functionality operates.

26.151 Sanity Test

A Sanity Test checks a narrow changed area before deeper testing.

26.152 Exploratory Test

Exploratory Testing uses human investigation to discover unexpected behaviour.

26.153 Property-Based Test

A Property-Based Test generates many Inputs to verify invariants.

26.154 Mutation Test

Mutation Testing changes code intentionally to determine whether the test suite detects defects.

26.155 Metamorphic Test

A Metamorphic Test verifies relationships among outputs when exact expected values are difficult to define.

26.156 Differential Test

A Differential Test compares two implementations, Versions or Providers under the same Inputs.

26.157 Snapshot Test

A Snapshot Test compares structured output with a stored representation.

26.158 Snapshot Limitation

Snapshots shall not replace semantic assertions.

26.159 Golden Test

A Golden Test compares results with an approved canonical example or dataset.

26.160 Golden Dataset

A Golden Dataset contains approved Inputs, expected properties, reference Outputs or evaluations.

It shall include or reference:

- datasetId,

- purpose,

- scope,

- samples,

- source,

- rights,

- Classification,

- review,

- and Version.

26.161 Golden Dataset Identity

Every Golden Dataset shall have stable identity and Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.162 Golden Sample

A Golden Sample shall preserve:

- input,

- expected behaviour,

- evaluation,

- scope,

- and provenance.

26.163 Golden Dataset Drift

Golden examples may become outdated when policy, Models or requirements change.

26.164 Benchmark Suite

A Benchmark Suite measures comparative performance under controlled conditions.

It shall include or reference:

- benchmarkSuiteId,

- task classes,

- datasets,

- Metrics,

- evaluation,

- environment,

- and Version.

26.165 Benchmark Suite Identity

Every Benchmark Suite shall have stable identity and Version.

26.166 Benchmark Reproducibility

Benchmark settings shall preserve:

- Model,

- Provider,

- Account,

- parameters,

- Runtime,

- hardware,

- and time.

26.167 Benchmark Contamination

A Model may have seen public benchmark data during training.

Results shall be interpreted cautiously.

26.168 Benchmark Gaming

Optimisation for a narrow benchmark may reduce general usefulness.

26.169 Evaluation Suite

An Evaluation Suite assesses intelligence quality, safety or usefulness.

It shall include or reference:

- evaluationSuiteId,

- task class,

- rubric,

- evaluators,

- sample policy,

- thresholds,

- and Version.

26.170 Evaluation Suite Identity

Every Evaluation Suite shall have stable identity and Version.

26.171 Deterministic Evaluation

Deterministic evaluation may test:

- schema,

- exact facts,

- required fields,

- prohibited terms,

- or file integrity.

26.172 Model-Based Evaluation

A Model may evaluate another Model’s Output.

Evaluator identity, Version and limitations shall be explicit.

26.173 Human Evaluation

Human evaluation shall preserve:

- Reviewer,

- rubric,

- target,

- evidence,

- result,

- and disagreement.

26.174 Pairwise Evaluation

Pairwise evaluation compares Candidates without requiring one absolute score.

26.175 Blind Evaluation

Reviewers may be blinded to Provider or Model identity to reduce bias.

26.176 Inter-Rater Agreement

Agreement among human or Model evaluators should be measured where material.

26.177 Evaluation Threshold

Thresholds shall distinguish:

- release blocking,

- route eligibility,

- advisory,

- and experimental use.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.178 Quality Floor Test

A Quality Floor Test verifies mandatory minimum requirements.

26.179 Factuality Test

Factuality tests should use reliable sources or known ground truth.

26.180 Identity Consistency Test

Identity consistency tests may compare generated media with canonical Reference Sets.

26.181 Rights and Consent Test

Tests shall verify that required Rights and Consent objects exist and remain valid.

26.182 Policy Conformance Test

Policy tests verify that actions are allowed or denied correctly.

26.183 Authority Conformance Test

Authority tests verify Grants, approvals, Tokens, Mandates and revocation.

26.184 Privacy Conformance Test

Privacy tests verify classification, minimisation, transfer and isolation.

26.185 Cost Conformance Test

Cost tests verify estimate, reservation, actual usage, retry accumulation and Budget enforcement.

26.186 Reliability Conformance Test

Reliability tests verify retry, timeout, fallback, circuit breaker, reconciliation and recovery.

26.187 Scheduling Conformance Test

Scheduling tests verify admission, fairness, quota, concurrency, deadline and recurrence.

26.188 Evidence Conformance Test

Evidence tests verify reconstructability, provenance, Decision Evidence and unknown-state preservation.

26.189 Asset Conformance Test

Asset tests verify identity, checksum, Version, lineage, rights, consent and durability.

26.190 Memory Conformance Test

Memory tests verify admission, scope, retrieval, expiry, challenge and deletion.

26.191 Observability Conformance Test

Observability tests verify correlation, Metrics, logs, traces, alerts and audit completeness.

26.192 Test Fixture

A Test Fixture is a controlled object, configuration or Environment state used by Tests.

26.193 Fixture Identity

Every reusable Test Fixture shall have stable identity and Version.

26.194 Fixture Scope

Fixtures shall identify:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- Classification,

- and intended Tests.

26.195 Fixture Determinism

Fixtures should be immutable or recreated predictably.

26.196 Fixture Provenance

Fixture origin and transformation shall remain attributable.

26.197 Synthetic Fixture

A Synthetic Fixture is generated specifically for testing and does not represent a real person or production object.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.198 Sanitised Fixture

A Sanitised Fixture derives from real data after approved transformation.

It remains subject to re-identification review.

26.199 Production Data Prohibition

Production personal or Confidential data shall not enter ordinary development or test Environments by default.

26.200 Test Dataset

A Test Dataset is a governed set of samples used by one or more Test Suites.

26.201 Test Dataset Identity

Every Test Dataset shall have stable identity and Version.

26.202 Dataset Split

Training, tuning, validation and test splits shall remain distinct when applicable.

26.203 Test Leakage

Using test data to tune the system may invalidate independent evaluation.

26.204 Dataset Rights

Test data shall have valid rights for:

- storage,

- use,

- evaluation,

- and sharing.

26.205 Dataset Consent

Data representing people may require valid Consent.

26.206 Dataset Classification

Datasets shall receive Data Classification and Handling Profile.

26.207 Dataset Retention

Retention shall be explicit.

26.208 Fixture Secret Prohibition

Real Credentials shall not be embedded in fixtures.

26.209 Secret Placeholder

Secret placeholders shall be clearly invalid and non-sensitive.

26.210 Test Credential

A Test Credential is an approved Credential limited to a test Account or Environment.

26.211 Test Credential Scope

Test Credentials shall not access production resources.

26.212 Test Credential Rotation

Shared Test Credentials should be rotated and monitored.

26.213 Credential Injection

Test Credentials shall be injected through approved Secret mechanisms.

26.214 Mock

A Mock verifies expected interactions with a dependency.

26.215 Stub

A Stub returns controlled responses without modelling full behaviour.

26.216 Fake

A Fake implements simplified but functional behaviour.

26.217 Simulator

A Simulator models the behaviour of an external system or resource.

26.218 Emulator

An Emulator reproduces a target Runtime or protocol more completely.

26.219 Mock Definition

A Mock Definition shall include or reference:

- mockId,

- target contract,

- expected calls,

- responses,

- state,

- errors,

- and Version.

26.220 Mock Identity

Every reusable Mock Definition shall have stable identity and Version.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.221 Mock Fidelity

Mock Fidelity describes how closely the mock represents real behaviour.

26.222 Low-Fidelity Mock

A low-fidelity mock supports narrow deterministic testing.

26.223 High-Fidelity Simulator

A high-fidelity simulator may reproduce:

- asynchronous states,

- retries,

- rate limits,

- callbacks,

- and failures.

26.224 Mock Limitation

Mocks shall not be treated as evidence of live Provider compatibility.

26.225 Contract-Driven Mock

Mocks should derive from canonical and Provider contract definitions where practical.

26.226 Stateful Mock

Stateful mocks may represent:

- queued job,

- processing,

- completion,

- cancellation,

- and expiry.

26.227 Error Injection

Mocks and simulators should support canonical and Provider-native failures.

26.228 Latency Injection

Dependencies should support controlled delay and timeout.

26.229 Duplicate Injection

Event and callback simulators should support duplicate delivery.

26.230 Reordering Injection

Async simulators should support out-of-order Events.

26.231 Partial Response Injection

Simulators should support incomplete or malformed responses.

26.232 Unknown-Outcome Injection

Tests shall support request acceptance followed by lost response or uncertain external state.

26.233 Provider Sandbox

A Provider Sandbox is a Provider-managed or isolated test Environment.

It shall be described by a Sandbox Profile.

26.234 Provider Sandbox Profile

The profile shall include or reference:

- Provider,

- Product,

- Account,

- capabilities,

- limitations,

- billing,

- data retention,

- rate limits,

- and production differences.

26.235 Sandbox Profile Identity

Every Sandbox Profile shall have stable identity and review date.

26.236 Sandbox Limitation

A sandbox may differ in:

- Models,

- latency,

- capacity,

- rights,

- billing,

- callbacks,

- and moderation.

26.237 Live Test

A Live Test calls a real Provider, Tool, service or external platform.

26.238 Live Test Authority

Live Tests require explicit:

- Account,

- Budget,

- data,

- side-effect,

- and Environment authority.

26.239 Live Test Tag

Every Live Test shall be clearly tagged and separable from ordinary test runs.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.240 Live Test Budget

Maximum spend shall be explicit.

26.241 Live Test Data

Live Tests should use synthetic or approved low-risk data.

26.242 Live Test Side Effects

Side effects shall be:

- disabled,

- redirected,

- private,

- temporary,

- or explicitly approved.

26.243 Live Publication Test

Publication tests shall use:

- dedicated test Account,

- private visibility,

- unique marker,

- and cleanup verification.

26.244 Live Message Test

Message tests shall use dedicated test recipients.

26.245 Live Purchase Test

Purchase tests should use Provider sandbox billing or the smallest approved bounded amount.

26.246 Live Deletion Test

Deletion tests shall target synthetic test objects only.

26.247 Live Credential Test

Credential tests shall not expose raw Secret values.

26.248 Live Test Cleanup

Cleanup shall verify external state and preserve evidence.

26.249 Live Test Unknown Outcome

A timed-out Live Test shall reconcile external state before repetition.

26.250 Provider Contract Test

A Provider Contract Test verifies actual Provider behaviour against the Adapter’s declared assumptions.

26.251 Provider Response Schema Test

The test verifies response structures and optional fields.

26.252 Provider State Test

The test verifies native job states and their canonical mapping.

26.253 Provider Error Test

The test verifies known error codes and retry semantics.

26.254 Provider Rate-Limit Test

The test verifies headers, reset timing and throttling behaviour within safe limits.

26.255 Provider Usage Test

The test verifies usage and cost reporting.

26.256 Provider Cancellation Test

The test verifies whether cancellation is:

- accepted,

- effective,

- partial,

- unsupported,

- or uncertain.

26.257 Provider Idempotency Test

The test verifies duplicate request handling.

26.258 Provider Callback Test

The test verifies:

- authentication,

- delivery,

- duplicate behaviour,

- ordering,

- and retry.

26.259 Provider Polling Test

The test verifies polling state progression and quota impact.

26.260 Provider Asset Expiry Test

The test verifies temporary URL expiry and durable ingestion requirements.

26.261 Provider Terms Test

Terms and retention assumptions may require manual review rather than automated testing.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.262 Adapter Conformance

Adapter Conformance verifies that one Adapter Version satisfies the canonical Adapter contract.

26.263 Connector Conformance

Connector Conformance verifies one configured Connector Instance against its Adapter, Provider and scope.

26.264 Model Conformance

Model Conformance verifies that a Model or Deployment satisfies declared capability and policy requirements.

26.265 Tool Conformance

Tool Conformance verifies schema, permissions, Sandbox, side effects and error handling.

26.266 Agent Conformance

Agent Conformance verifies role, authority, Tool use, Memory use, output and escalation.

26.267 Workflow Conformance

Workflow Conformance verifies state, Steps, retry, compensation, approval, completion and evidence.

26.268 Service Conformance

Service Conformance verifies API, policy, observability, security and operational behaviour.

26.269 Conformance Profile

A Conformance Profile defines the requirements applicable to one component class or deployment.

It shall include or reference:

- conformanceProfileId,

- subject type,

- requirement set,

- mandatory Tests,

- Environment,

- thresholds,

- evidence,

- expiry,

- and Version.

26.270 Conformance Profile Identity

Every Conformance Profile shall have stable identity and Version.

26.271 Core Profile

The Core Profile defines minimum requirements for all Fabric components.

26.272 Provider Adapter Profile

The Provider Adapter Profile adds:

- mapping,

- errors,

- usage,

- retries,

- async jobs,

- and Provider drift.

26.273 Local Runtime Profile

The Local Runtime Profile adds:

- Node scope,

- process isolation,

- hardware,

- Model loading,

- and offline behaviour.

26.274 Tool Profile

The Tool Profile adds:

- permissions,

- file scope,

- command execution,

- side effects,

- and Sandbox.

26.275 MCP Profile

The MCP Profile adds:

- server identity,

- capability discovery,

- schema validation,

- trust,

- and untrusted output handling.

26.276 Human-Assisted Profile

The Human-Assisted Profile adds:

- manual states,

- instructions,

- evidence,

- Account scope,

- and truthful completion.

26.277 Publication Profile

The Publication Profile adds:

- exact Asset,

- Account,

- approval,

- idempotency,

- verification,

- and correction.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.278 Agent Profile

The Agent Profile adds:

- identity,

- role,

- authority,

- Memory,

- Tool use,

- escalation,

- and no self-authorisation.

26.279 Workflow Profile

The Workflow Profile adds:

- state machine,

- idempotency,

- retries,

- compensation,

- and Completion Contract.

26.280 High-Risk Profile

The High-Risk Profile adds stronger:

- authentication,

- audit,

- human review,

- isolation,

- and rollback.

26.281 Conformance Requirement

A Conformance Requirement binds one Canonical Contract Requirement to a Profile.

26.282 Conformance Test

A Conformance Test verifies one or more Requirements using a declared method.

26.283 Conformance Test Identity

Every Conformance Test shall have stable identity and Version.

26.284 Conformance Run

A Conformance Run executes the applicable Test set for one exact subject Version.

It shall include or reference:

- conformanceRunId,

- subject,

- subject Version,

- Profile Version,

- Environment,

- Test Runs,

- evidence,

- exceptions,

- and result.

26.285 Conformance Run Identity

Every Conformance Run shall have stable identity.

26.286 Conformance Result

Conformance states may include:

- conformant,

- conditionally conformant,

- non-conformant,

- expired,

- suspended,

- and inconclusive.

26.287 Conformant

All mandatory Requirements are satisfied.

26.288 Conditionally Conformant

Mandatory Requirements are satisfied subject to explicit bounded conditions or approved exceptions.

26.289 Non-Conformant

At least one mandatory Requirement is unsatisfied without a valid exception.

26.290 Expired Conformance

The result is no longer current because its validity period ended.

26.291 Suspended Conformance

An Incident, drift or change temporarily invalidates operational eligibility.

26.292 Inconclusive Conformance

Evidence is insufficient to determine compliance.

26.293 Certification

A Certification is a governed assertion that one exact subject Version satisfies one Conformance Profile for a defined period and scope.

26.294 Certification Identity

Every Certification shall have stable identity and Version.

26.295 Certification Subject

The subject may be:

- Adapter Version,

- Connector Instance,

- Model Deployment,

- Provider Product,

- Tool Version,

- Agent Version,

- workflow Version,

- service release,

- or Environment.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.296 Certification Scope

Scope shall identify:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Environment,

- Capability,

- data classes,

- Providers,

- Accounts,

- and use cases.

26.297 Certification Issuer

The issuer shall have authority and competence for the Profile.

26.298 Certification Evidence

Certification shall link to:

- Conformance Run,

- Test Runs,

- exceptions,

- review,

- and approval.

26.299 Certification Validity

Validity shall include start and expiry.

26.300 Certification Conditions

Conditions may include:

- only Public data,

- only one Account,

- no cancellation,

- manual QA required,

- or maximum Budget.

26.301 Certification Revocation

A Certification may be revoked after:

- Incident,

- drift,

- misrepresentation,

- or failed revalidation.

26.302 Certification Suspension

Suspension blocks new eligible use pending review.

26.303 Certification Renewal

Renewal requires new evidence appropriate to changes and elapsed time.

26.304 Certification Portability

Certification for one Account, region or Deployment shall not transfer automatically.

26.305 Certification Exception

A Certification Exception permits a bounded unmet Requirement temporarily.

It shall include or reference:

- exceptionId,

- Requirement,

- subject,

- reason,

- risk,

- compensating control,

- owner,

- approval,

- expiry,

- and remediation.

26.306 Certification Exception Identity

Every Exception shall have stable identity.

26.307 Exception Scope

Scope shall be as narrow as possible.

26.308 Exception Expiry

Every Exception shall expire automatically.

26.309 Exception Renewal

Renewal requires new review and evidence.

26.310 Exception Visibility

Active Exceptions shall be visible in:

- Certification,

- dashboards,

- release gates,

- and operational eligibility.

26.311 Compensating Control

A compensating control reduces risk while the primary Requirement remains unsatisfied.

26.312 Waiver

A Waiver acknowledges that a Requirement will not be met for a defined scope.

Waivers shall be rare and higher-authority than temporary exceptions.

26.313 Permanent Waiver Prohibition

Broad permanent waivers should be prohibited.

26.314 Conformance Drift

Conformance Drift occurs when runtime behaviour or external dependencies no longer match certified assumptions.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.315 Drift Sources

Drift may arise from:

- Provider API change,

- Model alias update,

- SDK update,

- Tool dependency change,

- configuration change,

- policy change,

- infrastructure change,

- or data distribution change.

26.316 Drift Detection

Detection may use:

- scheduled contract tests,

- schema monitoring,

- benchmark comparison,

- health signals,

- and manual review.

26.317 Drift Impact

Material drift may:

- suspend Certification,

- narrow eligibility,

- trigger re-evaluation,

- or create Incident.

26.318 Regression

A Regression is a change that causes previously satisfied behaviour to become unsatisfied.

26.319 Regression Record

A Regression Record shall include or reference:

- regressionId,

- affected requirement,

- first known bad Version,

- last known good Version,

- evidence,

- impact,

- fix,

- and Test.

26.320 Regression Record Identity

Every material Regression Record shall have stable identity.

26.321 Regression Test Requirement

Every fixed material regression should produce a persistent Regression Test.

26.322 Last Known Good

The last known conformant Version shall remain identifiable.

26.323 First Known Bad

The earliest known non-conformant Version should be identified where practical.

26.324 Bisectability

Build and Test evidence should support change isolation.

26.325 Test Coverage

Test Coverage measures which code, paths, contracts, risks or Requirements are exercised.

26.326 Code Coverage

Code coverage may include:

- statement,

- branch,

- condition,

- and path coverage.

26.327 Requirement Coverage

Requirement Coverage measures which canonical Requirements have Tests.

26.328 Risk Coverage

Risk Coverage measures which failure and harm classes are exercised.

26.329 Integration Coverage

Integration Coverage measures which component combinations are tested.

26.330 Provider Coverage

Provider Coverage measures which Products, Accounts, Models and operations are verified.

26.331 Coverage Limitation

High numerical code coverage does not prove meaningful assurance.

26.332 Coverage Gap

Uncovered mandatory Requirements shall remain visible.

26.333 Traceability Matrix

A Traceability Matrix links:

- architecture requirement,

- schema,

- implementation,

- Test,

- result,

- defect,

- and Certification.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.334 Traceability Matrix Identity

Every release-relevant matrix should have stable identity and Version.

26.335 Bidirectional Traceability

The system should answer:

- which Tests prove this Requirement,

- and which Requirements justify this Test.

26.336 Orphan Test

A Test without an understood Requirement or risk may be reviewed for value.

26.337 Orphan Requirement

A mandatory Requirement without verification is a conformance gap.

26.338 Test Plan

A Test Plan defines the required Test activities for one change, release or Certification.

It shall include or reference:

- testPlanId,

- scope,

- risks,

- Requirements,

- Environments,

- Test Suites,

- data,

- side effects,

- schedule,

- owners,

- and exit criteria.

26.339 Test Plan Identity

Every material Test Plan shall have stable identity and Version.

26.340 Risk-Based Testing

Test depth shall increase with:

- consequence,

- complexity,

- novelty,

- uncertainty,

- and change scope.

26.341 Change Impact Analysis

Every material change should identify affected:

- contracts,

- services,

- Providers,

- workflows,

- data,

- and Tests.

26.342 Test Selection

Test selection may use change impact while preserving mandatory broad suites for high-risk releases.

26.343 Test Exit Criteria

Exit criteria shall define when testing is sufficient for the intended promotion.

26.344 Test Entry Criteria

Entry criteria shall define prerequisites such as:

- build success,

- fixture readiness,

- Environment health,

- and Credential availability.

26.345 Continuous Integration

Continuous Integration automatically builds and tests changes in an isolated Environment.

26.346 CI Identity

Every CI workflow shall have stable configuration identity and Version.

26.347 CI Principal

CI shall operate through a dedicated Service Principal.

26.348 CI Authority

CI authority shall be limited to required:

- repository,

- artefact,

- test,

- and reporting operations.

26.349 CI Secret Scope

CI Secrets shall be Environment- and workflow-scoped.

26.350 CI Fork Safety

Untrusted contributions shall not receive production or privileged Secrets.

26.351 CI Test Isolation

Parallel jobs shall not share mutable state unintentionally.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.352 CI Cache

Caches shall be scoped by:

- repository,

- branch or lockfile,

- toolchain,

- and trust level.

26.353 CI Artefact

Test reports, logs and build outputs shall have retention and Classification.

26.354 CI Failure

Release-blocking failures shall stop promotion.

26.355 CI Retry

Automatic CI retry shall not hide deterministic failures.

26.356 Flaky Retry Evidence

Repeated Test outcomes shall remain visible.

26.357 CI Timeout

Timeout shall remain distinct from Test failure.

26.358 Continuous Delivery

Continuous Delivery prepares release-ready artefacts after passing required gates.

26.359 Continuous Deployment

Continuous Deployment promotes automatically into an Environment under an approved Mandate.

High-risk production deployment may remain human-approved.

26.360 Release Candidate

A Release Candidate is one immutable artefact set proposed for promotion.

It shall include or reference:

- releaseCandidateId,

- source commit,

- build,

- artefacts,

- schemas,

- migrations,

- Tests,

- Certifications,

- known issues,

- and Version.

26.361 Release Candidate Identity

Every Release Candidate shall have stable identity.

26.362 Release Manifest

The Release Manifest shall list exact:

- artefacts,

- checksums,

- dependencies,

- configuration,

- and migration Versions.

26.363 Release Evidence

Release Evidence shall include:

- Build Record,

- Test Runs,

- Conformance Runs,

- security results,

- and approvals.

26.364 Release Gate

A Release Gate evaluates whether promotion may proceed.

Gate classes may include:

- build,

- unit,

- integration,

- conformance,

- security,

- privacy,

- performance,

- migration,

- approval,

- and operational readiness.

26.365 Release Gate Identity

Every Release Gate shall have stable identity and Version.

26.366 Mandatory Gate

A mandatory failed Gate blocks promotion.

26.367 Conditional Gate

A conditional Gate applies when the release affects its scope.

26.368 Gate Exception

A Gate exception requires the same bounded governance as Certification Exceptions.

26.369 Promotion Decision

A Promotion Decision authorises moving one exact Release Candidate into one exact Environment.

It shall include or reference:

- promotionDecisionId,

- candidate,

- source Environment,

- target Environment,

- gates,

- approver,

- conditions,

- schedule,

- rollback,

- and evidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.370 Promotion Decision Identity

Every Promotion Decision shall have stable identity.

26.371 Promotion Is Not Deployment Completion

Promotion authority remains distinct from verified deployment outcome.

26.372 Environment Promotion

Promotion should proceed through defined stages.

Examples include:

- development,

- integration,

- staging,

- canary,

- and production.

26.373 Skipped Environment

Skipping a normal Environment requires explicit justification and approval.

26.374 Canary Release

A Canary Release exposes a limited scope to the new Version.

26.375 Canary Scope

Scope may be limited by:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- traffic percentage,

- Capability,

- or internal users.

26.376 Canary Metrics

Canary evaluation shall monitor:

- errors,

- latency,

- quality,

- cost,

- privacy,

- and authority.

26.377 Canary Abort

Threshold breach shall stop or roll back the canary.

26.378 Blue-Green Deployment

Blue-green deployment maintains old and new Environments for controlled switching.

26.379 Feature Flag

A Feature Flag controls exposure of a capability or implementation path.

26.380 Feature Flag Identity

Every governed Feature Flag shall have stable identity and Version.

26.381 Feature Flag Scope

Flags shall be scoped and shall not become hidden permanent architecture.

26.382 Feature Flag Authority

High-risk flags require governed change and audit.

26.383 Flag Cleanup

Retired flags shall be removed after safe rollout.

26.384 Migration Test

Migration Tests verify schema, data, configuration or storage transitions.

26.385 Forward Migration

Forward migration applies the new representation.

26.386 Backward Migration

Backward migration restores compatibility or prior state where supported.

26.387 Migration Rehearsal

High-risk migrations shall be rehearsed on representative non-production data.

26.388 Migration Checksum

Data migrations should verify counts, checksums or invariants.

26.389 Migration Idempotency

Repeated migration execution shall not corrupt state.

26.390 Migration Partial Failure

Partial failure shall preserve checkpoint and recovery path.

26.391 Migration Rollback

Rollback limitations shall be explicit.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.392 Data Migration Privacy

Production data shall not be copied into unapproved test Environments.

26.393 Performance Test

A Performance Test measures latency, throughput, resource use or cost under controlled load.

26.394 Performance Test Identity

Every material Performance Test profile shall have stable identity and Version.

26.395 Load Test

A Load Test evaluates expected workload.

26.396 Stress Test

A Stress Test evaluates behaviour beyond expected capacity.

26.397 Spike Test

A Spike Test evaluates sudden demand change.

26.398 Endurance Test

An Endurance Test evaluates sustained operation over time.

26.399 Scalability Test

A Scalability Test evaluates behaviour as resources or workload grow.

26.400 Capacity Test

A Capacity Test identifies safe operating limits.

26.401 Soak Test

A Soak Test identifies leaks, drift or degradation during long execution.

26.402 Performance Environment

Load tests shall use an Environment that can represent production behaviour without harming users.

26.403 Production Load Test

Production testing requires explicit approval, safeguards and stop conditions.

26.404 Load Profile

A Load Profile shall include:

- workload classes,

- rates,

- concurrency,

- payload sizes,

- duration,

- and distribution.

26.405 Load Profile Identity

Every Load Profile shall have stable identity and Version.

26.406 Performance Baseline

Baseline shall identify compatible hardware, software and Provider state.

26.407 Tail Performance

Performance gates shall consider p95, p99 and worst-case behaviour where material.

26.408 Queue Performance

Tests shall measure queue wait, oldest age, throughput and fairness.

26.409 Provider Performance

External Provider tests shall respect quota and cost.

26.410 Local Performance

Local tests shall preserve:

- hardware,

- Model residency,

- Runtime,

- quantisation,

- and thermal state.

26.411 Performance Cost

The cost of testing itself shall be bounded.

26.412 Performance Regression Gate

Material regression beyond approved tolerance shall block or require review.

26.413 Reliability Test

Reliability Testing verifies operation under failure and recovery conditions.

26.414 Fault Injection

Fault Injection introduces controlled failure.

Examples include:

- timeout,

- connection loss,

- Provider error,

- storage failure,

- callback loss,

- queue redelivery,

- and process crash.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.415 Fault Scenario

A Fault Scenario shall include:

- scenarioId,

- hypothesis,

- fault,

- scope,

- expected behaviour,

- safeguards,

- and Version.

26.416 Fault Scenario Identity

Every Fault Scenario shall have stable identity and Version.

26.417 Retry Test

Retry Tests shall verify:

- eligible error,

- count,

- backoff,

- Budget,

- idempotency,

- and stop condition.

26.418 Non-Retryable Test

Policy, rights, consent and authority denials shall not be retried unchanged.

26.419 Unknown-Outcome Test

Unknown-outcome tests shall verify:

- state preservation,

- duplicate prevention,

- reconciliation,

- and later resolution.

26.420 Circuit-Breaker Test

Circuit-breaker tests shall verify:

- opening,

- half-open probing,

- recovery,

- and scope.

26.421 Bulkhead Test

Bulkhead tests verify that one failing Provider, Project or workload does not exhaust all shared resources.

26.422 Fallback Test

Fallback tests shall verify:

- eligibility,

- quality,

- cost,

- privacy,

- and authority.

26.423 Checkpoint Test

Long-running workflows shall restore from checkpoints correctly.

26.424 Crash Recovery Test

Service or worker restart shall preserve durable state.

26.425 Queue Redelivery Test

Redelivery shall not duplicate consequential side effects.

26.426 Dead-Letter Test

Failed messages shall enter the correct dead-letter process with evidence.

26.427 Callback-Loss Test

Polling or reconciliation shall recover when callbacks are lost.

26.428 Duplicate-Callback Test

Duplicate events shall remain idempotent.

26.429 Out-of-Order Test

State mapping shall handle late or out-of-order events safely.

26.430 Cancellation Test

Cancellation tests shall verify:

- request,

- Provider support,

- local stop,

- cost,

- external state,

- and final canonical state.

26.431 Partial-Completion Test

Partial results shall remain explicit and shall not become full success.

26.432 Disaster-Recovery Test

Disaster-recovery tests verify restoration of:

- services,

- data,

- Credentials,

- authority,

- and evidence.

26.433 Backup Restore Test

Restore shall reapply current:

- revocation,

- deletion,

- expiry,

- and policy.

26.434 Recovery-Time Test

Recovery Time Objective may be tested against representative failure.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.435 Recovery-Point Test

Recovery Point Objective may be tested through data-loss simulation.

26.436 Security Test

Security Testing evaluates resistance to unauthorised access, misuse, compromise and supply-chain risk.

26.437 Static Analysis

Static Analysis evaluates source or artefacts without execution.

26.438 Dynamic Analysis

Dynamic Analysis evaluates the running system.

26.439 Dependency Scan

Dependency scanning identifies known vulnerable or prohibited packages.

26.440 Secret Scan

Secret scanning detects exposed Credentials or high-risk patterns.

26.441 Licence Scan

Licence scanning identifies dependency and Asset licence obligations.

26.442 Software Bill of Materials

A Software Bill of Materials lists components in a build or package.

26.443 SBOM Identity

Every release-relevant SBOM shall have stable identity and checksum.

26.444 Package Signature

Packages and release artefacts should be signed or integrity-protected.

26.445 Supply-Chain Test

Supply-chain tests verify:

- source,

- dependency integrity,

- build provenance,

- and publication control.

26.446 Sandbox Test

Sandbox tests verify that code or Tools cannot escape allowed:

- process,

- file,

- network,

- device,

- and Credential boundaries.

26.447 File-Scope Test

Tools shall be denied access outside approved paths.

26.448 Network-Egress Test

Components shall be denied unapproved endpoints.

26.449 SSRF Test

External URL handling shall resist server-side request forgery.

26.450 Redirect Test

Redirects shall not bypass endpoint or egress policy.

26.451 Header-Injection Test

Headers and metadata shall be sanitised.

26.452 Prompt-Injection Test

External content shall not override:

- policy,

- authority,

- Tool scope,

- or Memory admission.

26.453 Tool-Injection Test

Tool Outputs shall remain untrusted until validated.

26.454 MCP Trust Test

MCP servers shall not receive automatic trust based only on protocol compatibility.

26.455 Secret-Exfiltration Test

Tests shall verify that Models, Tools and logs cannot reveal Secrets.

26.456 Cross-Tenant Test

Attempts to access another Tenant’s data shall fail structurally.

26.457 Cross-Project Test

Attempts to retrieve or mutate another Project shall fail.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.458 Privilege-Escalation Test

Agents and Services shall not expand their own authority.

26.459 Approval-Bypass Test

Consequential actions shall fail without valid current approval.

26.460 Token-Replay Test

Consumed, expired or wrong-audience Tokens shall fail.

26.461 Session-Isolation Test

Sessions shall not leak identity or data.

26.462 Browser-Isolation Test

Browser profiles, cookies and Accounts shall remain isolated.

26.463 Malicious-File Test

Uploaded or generated files shall be scanned or isolated according to policy.

26.464 Archive-Bomb Test

Compressed inputs shall be bounded against resource exhaustion.

26.465 Deserialisation Test

Untrusted structured data shall not enable code execution or unsafe object construction.

26.466 Privacy Test

Privacy Testing verifies appropriate collection, use, disclosure, retention and deletion.

26.467 Classification Test

Classification assignment and inheritance shall be tested.

26.468 Minimisation Test

Model and Provider Inputs shall exclude unnecessary fields and context.

26.469 Local-Only Test

Local Only data shall fail every ordinary external route.

26.470 Prohibited-Data Test

Prohibited data shall be blocked from ordinary processing.

26.471 Redaction Test

Redaction shall remove targeted content and metadata.

26.472 Pseudonymisation Test

Mappings shall remain separated and protected.

26.473 Anonymisation Test

Re-identification risk shall be evaluated.

26.474 Retention Test

Data shall expire according to policy.

26.475 Deletion Test

Deletion shall propagate across:

- canonical stores,

- caches,

- indexes,

- Provider copies,

- and restoration paths.

26.476 Restore-Deletion Test

Restored backups shall not reactivate deleted data.

26.477 Logging-Privacy Test

Protected payloads and Secrets shall not enter ordinary telemetry.

26.478 Memory-Privacy Test

Memory admission and retrieval shall preserve scope and classification.

26.479 Rights Test

Rights Testing verifies:

- licence,

- permitted use,

- attribution,

- expiry,

- and territory

where applicable.

26.480 Consent Test

Consent Testing verifies:

- subject,

- purpose,

- scope,

- validity,

- expiry,

- and revocation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.481 Rights Revocation Test

Revoked rights shall block future use and publication.

26.482 Consent Revocation Test

Revoked consent shall propagate to affected workflows and Assets.

26.483 Commercial-Use Test

Commercial use shall be denied when licence evidence is insufficient.

26.484 Attribution Test

Required attribution shall appear in the correct Deliverable or metadata.

26.485 Cost Test

Cost Testing verifies economic controls without assuming Provider estimates are always exact.

26.486 Cost Estimate Test

The estimator shall account for:

- Model,

- units,

- Candidates,

- retries,

- storage,

- and review.

26.487 Cost Reservation Test

Reservations shall reduce available Budget and release correctly.

26.488 Actual Usage Test

Actual Provider usage shall reconcile with Attempt and invoice evidence.

26.489 Missing Usage Test

Missing usage shall become unknown rather than zero.

26.490 Retry-Cost Test

Cumulative retries shall count against Budget.

26.491 Price-Change Test

Price drift shall trigger revalidation where material.

26.492 Currency Test

Currency conversion and rounding shall be explicit.

26.493 Managed-Credit Test

Credit reservation, consumption and expiry shall be verified.

26.494 User-Owned Account Test

User-owned Account usage shall remain Project-attributable.

26.495 Approval Test

Approval Testing verifies request presentation, Decision binding, Token use and stale-state handling.

26.496 Approval-Request Test

The request shall display:

- exact action,

- Project,

- target,

- Provider,

- data,

- cost,

- risk,

- and expiry.

26.497 Approval-Version Test

Material target changes shall invalidate old approvals.

26.498 Approval-Token Test

Tokens shall be:

- signed,

- scoped,

- expiring,

- audience-bound,

- and replay-protected.

26.499 Mandate Test

Mandates shall enforce:

- actions,

- limits,

- Budget,

- frequency,

- Providers,

- and exclusions.

26.500 Revocation Test

Revocation shall stop:

- queued work,

- scheduled work,

- cached authority,

- and active Tokens.

26.501 Emergency-Stop Test

Emergency stop shall block new work and preserve evidence.

26.502 Break-Glass Test

Break-glass authority shall remain:

- exceptional,

- expiring,

- audited,

- and unavailable to ordinary Agents.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.503 Agent Test

Agent Testing evaluates role behaviour, authority, Tool use, Memory use, output and escalation.

26.504 Agent Identity Test

The Agent shall retain stable identity across Model changes.

26.505 Agent Model-Swap Test

Changing Model shall not broaden authority or data access.

26.506 Agent Provider-Swap Test

Changing Provider shall preserve:

- policy,

- Project,

- Budget,

- and Memory boundaries.

26.507 Agent Tool-Scope Test

The Agent shall use only approved Tools and operations.

26.508 Agent Memory Test

The Agent shall retrieve only eligible Memory and cite relevant sources where required.

26.509 Agent Current-Instruction Test

Current explicit user instruction shall outrank ordinary stale preference Memory.

26.510 Agent Self-Authority Test

The Agent shall not create or approve its own expanded Mandate.

26.511 Agent Escalation Test

The Agent shall escalate when:

- scope changes,

- confidence falls,

- Budget rises,

- or authority is insufficient.

26.512 Agent Hallucination Test

Tests should detect unsupported claims in task classes where ground truth exists.

26.513 Agent Tool-Result Test

The Agent shall not treat untrusted Tool output as policy or instruction.

26.514 Agent Refusal Test

The Agent shall refuse or pause prohibited actions accurately.

26.515 Agent Recovery Test

After interruption, the Agent shall restore only governed state and not fabricate progress.

26.516 Workflow Test

Workflow Testing verifies complete state and transition behaviour.

26.517 State-Machine Test

Every allowed and prohibited transition shall be tested.

26.518 Invalid-Transition Test

Invalid state changes shall fail safely.

26.519 Workflow Idempotency Test

26.520 Workflow Compensation Test

Compensation shall execute only when permitted and shall preserve evidence.

26.521 Workflow Pause Test

26.522 Workflow Resume Test

Resume shall revalidate authority, policy and current external state.

26.523 Workflow Deadline Test

Missed deadlines shall create the correct state and escalation.

26.524 Workflow Recurrence Test

- authority,

- Budget,

- state,

- and data validation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:

- assignment,

- instructions,

- result,

- and evidence.

26.526 Workflow Publication Test

26.527 Workflow Unknown-Outcome Test

Unknown external state shall block blind repetition.

26.528 Adapter Test

Adapter Testing verifies canonical-to-native and native-to-canonical behaviour.

26.529 Adapter Manifest Test

The manifest shall be complete, Versioned and internally consistent.

26.530 Adapter Binding Test

Only declared Capability and Operation Bindings shall be accepted.

26.531 Adapter Request-Mapping Test

Canonical Inputs shall map correctly without silent omission or invention.

26.532 Adapter Response-Mapping Test

Native responses shall map to canonical objects accurately.

Provider states shall map to:

- queued,

- running,

- succeeded,

- failed,

- cancelled,

- partial,

- expired,

- or unknown

without false certainty.

26.534 Adapter Error-Mapping Test

Native errors shall map to canonical Reliability categories.

26.535 Adapter Usage-Mapping Test

Usage and cost fields shall preserve units and uncertainty.

26.536 Adapter Provenance Test

Provider-native references shall link to canonical provenance.

26.537 Adapter Asset Test

Temporary Provider assets shall be ingested durably before expiry where required.

26.538 Adapter Streaming Test

- partial data,

- backpressure,

- disconnect,

- cancellation,

- and completion.

26.539 Adapter Retry Test

The Adapter shall not hide retries outside canonical policy.

26.540 Adapter Secret Test

Credentials shall be resolved at execution boundary and absent from logs and payload records.

26.541 Adapter Endpoint Test

Only allowlisted endpoints and controlled redirects shall be used.

26.542 Adapter Drift Test

Provider schema or enum changes shall be detected.

26.543 Connector Test

26.544 Connector Scope Test

Tenant, Project, Environment and Account scope shall be enforced.

26.545 Connector Credential Test

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:

- authentication,

- quota,

- endpoint,

- capability,

- and Provider state.

26.548 Connector Revocation Test

Revoked Connections shall fail immediately.

- process control,

- Model loading,

- hardware,

- privacy,

- streaming,

- cancellation,

- authority snapshot,

- expiry,

- and later reconciliation.

Each Tool shall receive explicit authority and scope.

26.561 MCP Disconnect Test

Disconnect shall preserve in-flight state correctly.

- broader files,

- policy control,

- or Memory admission.
