26.564 Manual-State Test

States shall include:

- queued for human,

- assigned,

- in progress,

- awaiting evidence,

- completed,

- rejected,

- and unknown.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:

- Project,

- task,

- Budget,

- Inputs,

- Outputs,

Completion shall require suitable evidence.

26.581 Publication Stale-Approval Test

26.582 Publication Unknown-Outcome Test

- transactions,

- isolation,

- retention,

- backup,

26.585 Concurrency Test

Concurrent writes shall preserve invariants.

Database policies shall prevent cross-Tenant access.

26.587 Project Row-Isolation Test

Project filters shall be structural and enforced.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:

Object keys, access policy, signed URLs and deletion shall be tested.

26.595 Test Correlation

Test logs shall remain scoped and retain failure evidence.

26.597 Test Trace

Integration and end-to-end Tests should preserve traces.

Test Metrics may include:

- duration,

- flakiness,

- cost,

- coverage,

High-risk live Tests shall receive canonical audit.

A Test Dashboard may show:

- current Runs,

- failures,

- flaky Tests,

- coverage,

- conformance,

- and release Gates.

Flaky Tests shall be:

- owned,

- measured,

- quarantined temporarily,

- and repaired.

Flakiness shall be tracked by Suite and component.

26.603 Flaky Test Retry

Retries may gather evidence but shall not replace fixing the cause.

26.604 Quarantine Expiry

Quarantined Tests shall return to blocking status or receive explicit renewal.

26.605 Test Debt

Test Debt includes:

- missing coverage,

- stale fixtures,

- slow suites,

- quarantined Tests,

26.606 Test Debt Owner

Material Test Debt shall have owner, risk and review date.

26.607 Test Runtime

Test runtime should be optimised without removing required assurance.

26.608 Parallel Testing

Parallelism shall preserve isolation and deterministic fixtures.

26.609 Test Sharding

Suites may be sharded while preserving complete result aggregation.

26.610 Incremental Testing

Changed-area testing may provide fast feedback.

Full required suites shall still run before relevant promotion.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.611 Developer Feedback Loop

Developers should receive:

- fast validation,

- clear errors,

- exact failed Requirement,

- reproduction command,

- and relevant evidence.

Failure messages shall explain:

- what failed,

- expected behaviour,

- actual behaviour,

- scope,

- and next diagnostic step.

26.613 Reproduction Command

A Test Result should provide a safe reproduction method where practical.

26.614 Local Test Harness

A Local Test Harness runs representative Tests on developer Nodes.

26.615 Harness Identity

Every Test Harness shall have stable identity and Version.

26.616 Harness Configuration

Configuration shall declare:

- Environment,

- fixtures,

- Providers,

- live-test policy,

- and side-effect policy.

The default shall:

- use mocks or local resources,

- disable publication,

- disable deletion,

- disable real purchasing,

- and avoid production data.

Live mode shall require explicit opt-in and visible scope.

26.619 Fixture Reset

The Harness shall support reliable fixture reset.

26.620 Network Recording

Recorded Provider interactions may support replay if:

- Secrets are removed,

- rights permit retention,

- and drift limitations are understood.

26.621 Record-and-Replay Test

Recorded responses shall preserve source Version and date.

26.622 Replay Limitation

Replay cannot prove current Provider behaviour.

26.623 Contract Snapshot

A Provider Contract Snapshot records observed schemas, states and headers for comparison.

26.624 Contract Snapshot Identity

Every Contract Snapshot shall have stable identity and date.

26.625 Schema Drift Monitor

Schema Drift Monitoring compares current Provider behaviour with certified assumptions.

26.626 Drift Tolerance

Allowed additions or changes shall be explicit.

26.627 Breaking Drift Alert

Breaking drift shall suspend affected operations where safety requires it.

26.628 Cost-Safe Testing

Testing shall avoid uncontrolled Provider spend.

26.629 Test Budget

Every paid Test Suite shall have:

- Budget owner,

- maximum cost,

- Account,

- period,

- and alerts.

26.630 Cost Estimate Before Test

Expected cost shall be computed before live execution.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.631 Test Cost Record

Actual cost shall be linked to the Test Run.

26.632 Cost Overrun

Overrun shall stop remaining paid Tests where practical.

26.633 Candidate Count

Probabilistic evaluation shall use enough samples for confidence while respecting Budget.

26.634 Cached Evaluation

Cached results may accelerate unchanged comparisons but shall preserve Version and validity.

26.635 Side-Effect-Safe Testing

Automated Tests shall use controlled targets for consequential actions.

26.636 Test Namespace

External test objects should use unique namespaces or identifiers.

26.637 Test Account

Dedicated Accounts shall be used for:

- publication,

- messaging,

- storage,

- and billing

where available.

26.638 Test Recipient

Messages shall go only to approved Test recipients.

26.639 Test Visibility

Published Test content should be private, hidden or clearly marked.

26.640 Test Cleanup Verification

Cleanup shall verify that external test artefacts no longer remain active.

26.641 No Production Mutation by Default

CI and local Tests shall not mutate production by default.

26.642 Production Diagnostic Test

Production diagnostics shall be read-only unless explicit Incident authority permits otherwise.

26.643 Developer Access

Developer access shall use least privilege and separate Environments.

26.644 Production Access

Production access shall be:

- rare,

- justified,

- time-bounded,

- and audited.

26.645 Support Access

Support and debugging should use metadata, redaction and temporary grants.

26.646 Pairing with Coding Agents

Coding Agents may assist with:

- analysis,

- implementation,

- test generation,

- and documentation

inside explicit repository and Tool scope.

26.647 Coding Agent Identity

Every coding Agent shall have stable identity and Version.

26.648 Coding Agent Repository Scope

The Agent shall operate only in the approved repository, branch, worktree and path.

26.649 Coding Agent Diff Scope

The task shall define expected files and unrelated-change handling.

26.650 Coding Agent Test Duty

The Agent shall run relevant Tests and report actual results.

26.651 Coding Agent Evidence

Commands, changed files, Tests and unresolved issues shall remain attributable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.652 Coding Agent No-Fabrication Rule

The Agent shall not claim:

- tests passed,

- files exist,

- build succeeded,

- or deployment completed

without evidence.

26.653 Coding Agent Commit Authority

Editing, staging, committing, pushing and merging shall remain distinct authorities.

26.654 Coding Agent Safety Stop

The Agent shall stop when:

- repository is unexpected,

- branch is wrong,

- unrelated changes create ambiguity,

- destructive scope expands,

- or required authority is absent.

26.655 Generated Test Review

Agent-generated Tests shall be reviewed for meaningful assertions.

26.656 Test Overfitting

Tests shall not be written merely to accept current faulty behaviour.

26.657 Architecture Conformance Review

Implementation review shall compare the change against canonical architecture, not only local style.

26.658 Code Review

Code Review evaluates:

- correctness,

- readability,

- contracts,

- security,

- privacy,

- tests,

- and operational impact.

26.659 Review Identity

Every release-relevant review shall identify Reviewer and target Version.

26.660 Review Independence

High-risk changes may require a Reviewer independent from the author.

26.661 Review Diff

Review shall bind to an exact diff or commit.

26.662 Review Update

Material changes after review require re-review.

26.663 Automated Review

Static tools and Agents may support review.

They do not replace required human approval automatically.

26.664 Review Checklist

Checklists may include:

- architecture,

- tests,

- migration,

- observability,

- rollback,

- data,

- authority,

- and cost.

26.665 Security Review

Security-sensitive changes require specialised review.

26.666 Privacy Review

High-risk data changes require Privacy Review.

26.667 Provider Review

New Provider integrations require:

- contract,

- terms,

- data,

- cost,

- reliability,

- and Adapter review.

26.668 Model Review

New Model or Deployment use requires capability and evaluation evidence.

26.669 Tool Review

New Tools require permission, Sandbox and side-effect review.

26.670 Release Review

Release review examines all required Gates and open exceptions.

26.671 Definition of Ready

A work item is ready for implementation when:

- objective,

- scope,

- architecture,

- authority,

- dependencies,

- acceptance criteria,

- and Test Plan

are sufficiently defined.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.672 Definition of Done

A work item is done only when:

- implementation is complete,

- Tests pass,

- contracts are updated,

- documentation is updated,

- observability exists,

- migration is verified,

- and required evidence is recorded.

26.673 Done Is Not Deployed

Completion of implementation remains distinct from deployment and external Outcome.

26.674 Developer Incident

A Developer Incident is a material failure caused or discovered during development, testing, build or release.

Examples include:

- production data in test,

- exposed Secret,

- wrong repository mutation,

- unsafe live Test,

- broken release Gate,

- or incorrect Certification.

26.675 Developer Incident Identity

Every material Developer Incident shall have stable identity.

26.676 Test Environment Incident

A Test Environment may leak, mutate or interfere with production.

26.677 CI Credential Incident

CI may expose or misuse a Credential.

26.678 Build Integrity Incident

A build may contain unverified or altered dependencies.

26.679 False-Pass Incident

A Test or Gate may report pass despite failure.

26.680 False-Fail Incident

A valid release may be blocked by incorrect Test or Environment state.

26.681 Certification Incident

A component may be certified based on incomplete, stale or fabricated evidence.

26.682 Live-Test Incident

A live Test may publish, spend, message or delete outside its approved scope.

26.683 Developer Incident Containment

Containment may include:

- revoke Credentials,

- stop CI,

- disable test Account,

- quarantine artefact,

- freeze release,

- and preserve logs.

26.684 Developer Incident Review

The review shall inspect:

- Environment,

- authority,

- fixtures,

- Secrets,

- Tests,

- Gates,

- and affected external state.

- register Requirement,

- register Test,

- start Run,

- attach evidence,

- evaluate,

- certify,

- suspend,

- revoke,

- and renew.

- select Suite,

- provision Environment,

- load fixtures,

- execute,

- collect evidence,

- clean up,

- and report.

- evidence lookup,

text:

26.729 Applied Example — Text Provider Swap

Atlas requests structured architecture drafting through a canonical Capability Request.

The test runs the same Request against two certified text Provider Adapters.

Conformance verifies:

- Atlas receives no Provider-native object,

- schema remains identical,

- cost and latency remain attributable,

- errors map canonically,

- and Agent authority remains unchanged.

Provider-specific wording variation is evaluated through the approved quality rubric rather than exact string equality.

26.730 Applied Example — Provider Returns HTTP 200 with Failed Job

A Provider returns HTTP 200.

The response body reports:

failed.

The Adapter Test verifies that:

- transport success is recorded,

- operation state becomes failed,

- the Execution does not become successful,

- and the Provider-native error remains linked.

26.731 Applied Example — Missing Usage

A Provider completes an image generation but omits usage information.

The Adapter shall return:

usage unknown.

The Test fails if the implementation invents zero cost.

26.732 Applied Example — Lost Callback

A Provider job completes, but the callback is never delivered.

The Test verifies that:

- polling discovers completion,

- the External Job Handle remains stable,

- the late or missing callback does not create duplicate work,

- and the Asset is ingested once.

26.733 Applied Example — Duplicate Callback

The same signed callback arrives three times.

The callback handler shall:

- authenticate each delivery,

- deduplicate by event or job identity,

- process the state change once,

- and preserve duplicate-delivery telemetry.

26.734 Applied Example — Unsupported Cancellation

A Provider does not support cancellation after submission.

The Connector Test verifies that:

- cancellation request is recorded,

- canonical state does not become cancelled falsely,

- external job remains pending or running,

- and the user sees the limitation.

26.735 Applied Example — Expired Asset URL

A generated Asset URL expires after one hour.

The Test verifies that the ingestion Step:

- downloads the Asset,

- validates checksum and media,

- stores it durably,

- and records Provider source

before expiry.

- bounded character count,

- test Account,

The workflow runs with debug logging.

The Test scans logs and traces.

- no automatic duplicate purchase occurs,

- billing reconciliation runs,

- automatic test generation,

- formal verification,

- proof-carrying builds,

- hermetic development Environments,

- digital twins,

- synthetic Provider ecosystems,

- autonomous regression analysis,

- privacy-preserving benchmark federation,

- continuous certification,

- and self-validating Agents.

Future evolution must preserve:

- human ownership,

- explicit scope,

- evidence,

- reproducibility,

- and bounded authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.847 Machine-Readable Architecture

Canonical requirements may compile into:

- schemas,

- policy tests,

- conformance suites,

- and documentation.

26.848 Automatic Test Generation

Agents may generate candidate Tests from approved Requirements.

Generated Tests shall receive review and traceability.

26.849 Formal Specification

Critical state machines and invariants may receive mathematical or formal representation.

26.850 Model Checking

Model checking may explore state combinations for:

- retries,

- approvals,

- queues,

- and distributed coordination.

26.851 Property Verification

Property-based methods may prove or strongly test invariants across broad Inputs.

26.852 Proof-Carrying Build

A build may include machine-verifiable evidence that required Gates passed.

26.853 Hermetic Environment

A hermetic Environment controls all declared dependencies and network access.

26.854 Reproducible Environment

Environment definitions may recreate local, CI and certification conditions.

26.855 Developer Environment Attestation

A trusted Environment may attest:

- toolchain,

- dependency,

- isolation,

- and policy state.

26.856 Continuous Certification

Certification may update continuously from:

- scheduled contract Tests,

- drift monitoring,

- and production evaluation.

26.857 Certification Confidence

Future Certification may include confidence based on evidence freshness and coverage.

26.858 Provider Digital Twin

A Provider simulator may model:

- states,

- latency,

- quota,

- billing,

- and failure

from observed evidence.

26.859 Workflow Digital Twin

A workflow model may simulate:

- cost,

- latency,

- failure,

- and authority

before execution.

26.860 Synthetic Data Generator

Synthetic data may preserve schema and statistical properties without reproducing real identities.

26.861 Privacy-Preserving Benchmark Federation

Tenants may contribute aggregate evaluation without sharing raw Inputs or Outputs.

26.862 Differential Test Agent

An Agent may compare Versions, Providers or Models and propose regressions.

26.863 Automated Root-Cause Analysis

Test telemetry may identify likely failing changes.

Inferences shall remain evidence-linked.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.864 Autonomous Test Repair

Agents may propose repairs for stale fixtures or Tests.

They shall not weaken assertions merely to pass.

26.865 Self-Validating Agent

An Agent may evaluate its own outputs against deterministic and independent checks.

Self-validation shall not replace external governance.

26.866 Runtime Contract Enforcement

Contracts may be enforced continuously in production, not only during pre-release testing.

26.867 Policy Shadow Evaluation

New policy Versions may be evaluated in shadow mode before activation.

26.868 Release Simulation

The system may simulate migration, traffic and dependency effects before promotion.

26.869 Formal Approval Binding

Approval hashes may bind directly to release artefacts and Test evidence.

26.870 Conformance Marketplace

Future external Adapter or Tool developers may publish packages with signed conformance evidence.

Omnira shall still verify trust, scope and current validity.

26.871 Third-Party Certification

Independent certification may supplement but not replace Omnira’s requirements.

26.872 Cross-Language Conformance

Equivalent SDKs may run one shared language-neutral conformance suite.

26.873 Protocol Fuzzing

Automated fuzzing may test APIs, events, webhooks, MCP and file parsers.

26.874 Semantic Fuzzing

Generated Inputs may target ambiguous capability, policy and intent boundaries.

26.875 Adversarial Agent Testing

Red-team suites may test:

- authority manipulation,

- prompt injection,

- Memory poisoning,

- and unsafe Tool selection.

26.876 Cost-Aware Test Optimisation

Test selection may optimise spend while preserving mandatory assurance.

26.877 Risk-Adaptive Suites

Changes affecting high-risk domains may trigger expanded Tests automatically.

26.878 Observability-Driven Testing

Production evidence may identify new realistic failure scenarios.

26.879 Incident-to-Test Automation

Every material Incident may automatically create a candidate Regression Test.

26.880 Developer Experience Success Criteria

Developer experience succeeds when:

- setup is reproducible,

- scopes are visible,

- safe defaults prevent accidental harm,

- failures are understandable,

- local and CI feedback is fast,

- and governance is integrated rather than bolted on.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.881 Testing Success Criteria

Testing succeeds when:

- deterministic contracts are executable,

- probabilistic quality is evaluated appropriately,

- failure and unknown states are covered,

- external side effects remain bounded,

- regressions become permanent Tests,

- and results are reproducible and attributable.

26.882 Conformance Success Criteria

Conformance succeeds when:

- every eligible component satisfies a declared Profile,

- mandatory Requirements map to evidence,

- Certifications bind to exact Versions and scope,

- drift invalidates stale assumptions,

- exceptions remain narrow and expiring,

- and non-conformant components cannot enter production silently.

26.883 Developer Experience Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- developers require production Credentials for ordinary setup,

- Environments are ambiguous,

- safe dry-run is absent,

- or documentation contradicts current contracts.

26.884 Testing Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- only happy paths are tested,

- live Tests create uncontrolled side effects,

- skipped Tests appear as passed,

- or unknown outcomes are converted into ordinary failures.

26.885 Conformance Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- Certification lacks exact subject Version,

- mandatory Requirements have no Tests,

- exceptions lack expiry,

- or drift does not affect eligibility.

26.886 Canonical Developer Environment Contract

The following requirements define Developer Environments:

1. Every governed Environment SHALL have identity.

2. Environment type SHALL be explicit.

3. Tenant and Project scope SHALL be explicit.

4. Allowed data classes SHALL be explicit.

5. Allowed Credentials SHALL be explicit.

6. Allowed external side effects SHALL be explicit.

7. Network egress SHALL be controlled.

8. File and storage scope SHALL be controlled.

9. Production data SHALL be prohibited by default.

10. Production Credentials SHALL be prohibited by default.

11. Bootstrap SHALL be reproducible.

12. Setup SHALL be idempotent.

13. Environment configuration SHALL be Versioned.

14. Ephemeral Environments SHALL expire.

15. Cleanup SHALL preserve required evidence.

16. Shared Environments SHALL enforce isolation.

17. Environment health SHALL be observable.

18. Environment drift SHALL be detectable.

19. Historical configuration SHALL remain queryable.

20. Developer Environment SHALL NOT create authority outside its declared scope.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.887 Canonical Schema and Contract Contract

The following requirements define schemas and executable contracts:

1. Every canonical schema SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. One authoritative source SHALL be declared.

3. Required fields SHALL be enforceable.

4. Unknown fields SHALL follow explicit policy.

5. Unknown enum values SHALL remain distinguishable.

6. Null, absent, empty and unknown SHALL remain distinct where material.

7. Structural compatibility SHALL be evaluated.

8. Semantic compatibility SHALL be evaluated.

9. Breaking changes SHALL create a new Version.

10. Migration path SHALL be defined.

11. Contract Requirements SHALL have stable identity.

12. Mandatory and advisory Requirements SHALL remain distinct.

13. Applicability SHALL be explicit.

14. Requirements SHALL link to verification.

15. Executable invariants SHALL derive from approved architecture.

16. Generated bindings SHALL preserve source provenance.

17. Historical Versions SHALL remain resolvable.

18. Deprecation SHALL include replacement and timeline.

19. Contract drift SHALL be detected.

20. Implementation convenience SHALL NOT redefine canonical semantics.

26.888 Canonical SDK and CLI Contract

The following requirements define SDKs and CLI tools:

1. Every package SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Supported API and schema Versions SHALL be declared.

3. Generated types SHALL derive from canonical definitions where practical.

4. Authentication SHALL avoid Secret exposure.

5. Tenant and Project context SHALL be explicit.

6. Authority context SHALL be explicit.

7. Errors SHALL preserve canonical categories.

8. Hidden retries SHALL be prohibited.

9. Timeout SHALL not imply external failure automatically.

10. Correlation SHALL be emitted.

11. Dry-run SHALL create no side effects.

12. Destructive actions SHALL display exact scope.

13. Machine output SHALL be structured.

14. Exit codes SHALL distinguish denial, timeout and unknown outcome.

15. Command history SHALL not expose Secrets.

16. Deprecated operations SHALL provide migration guidance.

17. Examples SHALL be tested.

18. Package provenance SHALL be recorded.

19. Historical Versions SHALL remain traceable.

20. SDK or CLI convenience SHALL NOT bypass policy enforcement.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 26.891 Canonical Fixture and Test Data Contract
text:
26.889 Canonical Test Case Contract

The following requirements define Test Cases:

1. Every material Test Case SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Requirement or risk SHALL be linked.

3. Preconditions SHALL be explicit.

4. Inputs SHALL be explicit.

5. Environment SHALL be explicit.

6. Fixtures SHALL be explicit.

7. Operation SHALL be explicit.

8. Expected result SHALL be explicit.

9. Assertions SHALL be explicit.

10. Cleanup SHALL be explicit.

11. Side-effect policy SHALL be explicit.

12. Cost limit SHALL be explicit for paid Tests.

13. Evidence SHALL be captured.

14. Result states SHALL remain distinct.

15. Skipped SHALL not become passed.

16. Inconclusive SHALL not become passed.

17. Flaky SHALL remain visible.

18. Reproduction method SHOULD be available.

19. Historical Versions SHALL remain queryable.

20. Test Case SHALL NOT be weakened merely to match faulty implementation.

26.890 Canonical Test Run Contract

The following requirements define Test Runs:

1. Every Test Run SHALL have stable identity.

2. Suite and Case Versions SHALL be explicit.

3. Source commit or subject Version SHALL be explicit.

4. Environment SHALL be explicit.

5. Configuration SHALL be explicit.

6. Fixtures and datasets SHALL be explicit.

7. Provider Accounts and live-test mode SHALL be explicit.

8. Start and end SHALL be explicit.

9. Results SHALL be complete.

10. Skips, blocks and inconclusive outcomes SHALL be explicit.

11. Logs and traces SHALL be linked.

12. Cost SHALL be linked.

13. Side effects SHALL be linked.

14. Cleanup SHALL be verified.

15. Correlation SHALL be preserved.

16. Test retry history SHALL remain visible.

17. Integrity SHALL be verifiable.

18. Retention SHALL be explicit.

19. Historical Runs SHALL remain queryable.

20. A Test Run SHALL NOT claim behaviour it did not execute.

26.891 Canonical Fixture and Test Data Contract

The following requirements define fixtures and test data:

1. Every reusable Fixture or Dataset SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Purpose SHALL be explicit.

3. Tenant, Project and Environment SHALL be explicit.

4. Classification SHALL be explicit.

5. Provenance SHALL be explicit.

6. Rights SHALL be explicit.

7. Consent SHALL be explicit where applicable.

8. Synthetic data SHALL be preferred.

9. Production data SHALL be prohibited by default.

10. Sanitised data SHALL receive re-identification review.

11. Real Secrets SHALL be prohibited.

12. Reset SHALL be deterministic.

13. Parallel use SHALL remain isolated.

14. Retention SHALL be explicit.

15. Deletion SHALL be supported.

16. Test leakage SHALL be prevented.

17. Dataset splits SHALL remain distinct where applicable.

18. Change SHALL create a new Version.

19. Historical data Versions SHALL remain traceable.

20. Test data convenience SHALL NOT weaken privacy or Project isolation.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.892 Canonical Mock and Simulator Contract

The following requirements define mocks and simulators:

1. Every reusable Mock or Simulator SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Target Contract SHALL be explicit.

3. Fidelity SHALL be described.

4. Supported states SHALL be explicit.

5. Supported errors SHALL be explicit.

6. Latency injection SHALL be supported where relevant.

7. Duplicate delivery SHALL be supported where relevant.

8. Reordering SHALL be supported where relevant.

9. Partial and malformed response SHALL be supported.

10. Unknown outcome SHALL be supported.

11. Usage and cost uncertainty SHALL be supported.

12. Stateful behaviour SHALL be deterministic.

13. Contract changes SHALL trigger update.

14. Mock limitations SHALL be documented.

15. Recorded responses SHALL be sanitised.

16. Replay source and date SHALL be explicit.

17. Mocks SHALL not contain production Secrets.

18. Historical Versions SHALL remain traceable.

19. Live verification SHALL supplement high-risk assumptions.

20. Mock success SHALL NOT certify live Provider behaviour.

26.893 Canonical Live Test Contract

The following requirements define live external Tests:

1. Every Live Test SHALL be explicitly tagged.

2. Provider, Product and Account SHALL be explicit.

3. Tenant, Project and Environment SHALL be explicit.

4. Data SHALL be synthetic or specifically approved.

5. Classification SHALL be eligible.

6. Purpose SHALL be explicit.

7. Budget SHALL be explicit.

8. Maximum side effect SHALL be explicit.

9. Publication SHALL use dedicated private test targets.

10. Messaging SHALL use approved recipients.

11. Purchase SHALL use sandbox or minimal approved amount.

12. Deletion SHALL use synthetic objects.

13. Start and stop conditions SHALL be explicit.

14. Unknown outcome SHALL trigger reconciliation.

15. Cleanup SHALL be verified.

16. Cost and usage SHALL be recorded.

17. Secrets SHALL remain protected.

18. Audit SHALL be preserved.

19. Historical Runs SHALL remain queryable.

20. Live Test SHALL NOT execute by default in ordinary local or CI workflows.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 26.895 Canonical Security and Privacy Testing Contract
text:
26.894 Canonical Evaluation and Benchmark Contract

The following requirements define intelligence evaluation:

1. Every Evaluation or Benchmark Suite SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Task class SHALL be explicit.

3. Dataset SHALL be explicit.

4. Rubric SHALL be explicit.

5. Evaluator identity and Version SHALL be explicit.

6. Thresholds SHALL be explicit.

7. Mandatory failures SHALL remain distinct from average score.

8. Probabilistic behaviour SHALL use sufficient samples.

9. Statistical method SHALL be explicit.

10. Confidence and limitations SHALL be explicit.

11. Human and Model evaluation SHALL remain distinct.

12. Pairwise and absolute scoring SHALL remain distinct.

13. Benchmark contamination risk SHALL be considered.

14. Exact Provider, Model and configuration SHALL be preserved.

15. Hardware and Runtime SHALL be preserved for local tests.

16. Cost and latency SHALL be measured.

17. Evaluation disagreement SHALL remain visible.

18. Golden data SHALL be Versioned.

19. Historical results SHALL remain queryable.

20. Benchmark performance SHALL NOT create production authority automatically.

26.895 Canonical Security and Privacy Testing Contract

The following requirements define security and privacy assurance:

1. Dependency scanning SHALL be performed.

2. Secret scanning SHALL be performed.

3. SBOM SHALL be produced for release artefacts.

4. Build provenance SHALL be preserved.

5. Package integrity SHALL be verified.

6. Sandbox boundaries SHALL be tested.

7. File and network scope SHALL be tested.

8. SSRF and redirect controls SHALL be tested.

9. Prompt and Tool injection SHALL be tested.

10. Secret exfiltration SHALL be tested.

11. Cross-Tenant and cross-Project isolation SHALL be tested.

12. Approval and authority bypass SHALL be tested.

13. Classification and Local Only enforcement SHALL be tested.

14. Minimisation and logging privacy SHALL be tested.

15. Retention and deletion propagation SHALL be tested.

16. Restore SHALL preserve deletion and revocation.

17. Rights and consent expiry SHALL be tested.

18. Security and privacy failures SHALL block applicable release.

19. Historical evidence SHALL remain queryable.

20. Security Testing SHALL NOT itself create uncontrolled access or data exposure.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 26.897 Canonical Agent and Workflow Testing Contract
text:
26.896 Canonical Reliability Testing Contract

The following requirements define reliability assurance:

1. Retryable and non-retryable failures SHALL remain distinct.

2. Retry count and duration SHALL be bounded.

3. Retry cost SHALL be measured.

4. Idempotency SHALL be tested.

5. Timeout SHALL preserve uncertainty where required.

6. Unknown outcome SHALL be tested.

7. Reconciliation SHALL precede repeat side effect.

8. Duplicate delivery SHALL be tested.

9. Out-of-order delivery SHALL be tested.

10. Callback loss SHALL be tested.

11. Circuit breaker SHALL be tested.

12. Bulkhead isolation SHALL be tested.

13. Fallback eligibility SHALL be revalidated.

14. Checkpoint and crash recovery SHALL be tested.

15. Cancellation semantics SHALL be tested.

16. Partial completion SHALL remain explicit.

17. Backup and restore SHALL be tested.

18. Recovery verification SHALL be explicit.

19. Historical failure evidence SHALL remain queryable.

20. Reliability recovery SHALL NOT broaden authority, privacy or Budget.

26.897 Canonical Agent and Workflow Testing Contract

The following requirements define Agent and workflow assurance:

1. Every Agent and workflow Version SHALL be explicit.

2. Agent identity SHALL remain independent from Model and Provider.

3. Role and authority SHALL be tested.

4. Tenant and Project scope SHALL be tested.

5. Memory access SHALL be tested.

6. Tool access SHALL be tested.

7. Current user instruction precedence SHALL be tested.

8. Agent self-authorisation SHALL be denied.

9. Unsupported claims SHALL be evaluated where ground truth exists.

10. Escalation SHALL be tested.

11. Workflow state transitions SHALL be complete.

12. Invalid transitions SHALL be denied.

13. Idempotency SHALL be tested.

14. Retry and fallback SHALL be bounded.

15. Pause and resume SHALL preserve state and revalidate.

16. Human Steps SHALL remain attributable.

17. External side effects SHALL be verified.

18. Unknown outcome SHALL block blind repetition.

19. Historical Runs SHALL remain reconstructable.

20. Helpful output SHALL NOT compensate for authority or privacy failure.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 26.898 Canonical Adapter and Connector Conformance Contract
text:
26.898 Canonical Adapter and Connector Conformance Contract

The following requirements define integration conformance:

1. Every Adapter and Connector SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Adapter Manifest SHALL validate.

3. Capability and Operation Bindings SHALL be exact.

4. Unsupported operations SHALL fail before dispatch.

5. Canonical Inputs SHALL map without silent semantic loss.

6. Native responses SHALL map accurately.

7. Unknown states SHALL remain unknown.

8. Transport success SHALL remain distinct from operation success.

9. Native errors SHALL map canonically.

10. Usage and cost units SHALL be preserved.

11. Missing usage SHALL remain unknown.

12. Secret resolution SHALL occur at execution boundary.

13. Hidden retries SHALL be prohibited.

14. Endpoint and redirect policy SHALL be enforced.

15. Async jobs, callbacks and polling SHALL be tested.

16. Streaming and cancellation SHALL be tested where supported.

17. Provider-native objects SHALL not become canonical directly.

18. Connector scope SHALL enforce Tenant, Project and Account.

19. Drift SHALL trigger revalidation.

20. Historical Versions and evidence SHALL remain queryable.

26.899 Canonical Conformance Profile Contract

The following requirements define Conformance Profiles:

1. Every Profile SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Subject type SHALL be explicit.

3. Scope SHALL be explicit.

4. Applicable Requirements SHALL be explicit.

5. Mandatory and advisory Requirements SHALL remain distinct.

6. Conditional applicability SHALL be explicit.

7. Required Tests SHALL be explicit.

8. Required Environment SHALL be explicit.

9. Thresholds SHALL be explicit.

10. Evidence requirements SHALL be explicit.

11. Human review requirements SHALL be explicit.

12. Expiry or revalidation triggers SHALL be explicit.

13. Profile changes SHALL create a new Version.

14. Subject-specific Profiles MAY extend Core Profile.

15. High-risk Profiles SHALL require stronger controls.

16. Non-applicability SHALL require justification.

17. Historical Profiles SHALL remain resolvable.

18. Profile ownership SHALL be explicit.

19. Profile approval SHALL be attributable.

20. A Profile SHALL NOT be weakened to accommodate one failing implementation silently.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.900 Canonical Certification Contract

The following requirements define Certification:

1. Every Certification SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Exact subject and Version SHALL be explicit.

3. Conformance Profile Version SHALL be explicit.

4. Scope SHALL be explicit.

5. Environment SHALL be explicit.

6. Test and Conformance Runs SHALL be linked.

7. Mandatory failures SHALL block Certification.

8. Exceptions SHALL be explicit.

9. Compensating controls SHALL be explicit.

10. Issuer SHALL be authorised.

11. Conditions SHALL be explicit.

12. Start and expiry SHALL be explicit.

13. Drift triggers SHALL be explicit.

14. Suspension SHALL be supported.

15. Revocation SHALL be supported.

16. Renewal SHALL require current evidence.

17. Certification SHALL not transfer across Account, region or Deployment automatically.

18. Historical Certifications SHALL remain immutable.

19. Operational eligibility SHALL reference current Certification.

20. Certification SHALL NOT become eternal trust.

26.901 Canonical Exception Contract

The following requirements define conformance and release exceptions:

1. Every Exception SHALL have stable identity.

2. Unmet Requirement SHALL be explicit.

3. Subject and scope SHALL be explicit.

4. Reason SHALL be explicit.

5. Risk SHALL be explicit.

6. Compensating control SHALL be explicit.

7. Owner SHALL be explicit.

8. Approver SHALL be explicit.

9. Effective time SHALL be explicit.

10. Expiry SHALL be explicit.

11. Remediation SHALL be explicit.

12. Renewal SHALL require new review.

13. Exception SHALL remain visible in Certification and release evidence.

14. Exception SHALL not broaden unrelated scope.

15. High-risk Requirements MAY prohibit exception.

16. Expired Exception SHALL no longer permit eligibility.

17. Closure SHALL require verification.

18. Historical Exceptions SHALL remain queryable.

19. Permanent broad waivers SHOULD be prohibited.

20. Exception SHALL NOT become silent normal behaviour.

26.902 Canonical CI and Build Contract

The following requirements define CI and build assurance:

1. Every CI workflow SHALL have stable configuration identity and Version.

2. CI SHALL use a dedicated Service Principal.

3. Repository and branch scope SHALL be explicit.

4. Secrets SHALL be workflow- and Environment-scoped.

5. Untrusted contributions SHALL not receive privileged Secrets.

6. Build toolchain SHALL be attributable.

7. Dependencies SHALL be locked or constrained.

8. Generated code SHALL preserve provenance.

9. Build artefacts SHALL have checksums.

10. SBOM SHALL be linked where required.

11. Test Runs SHALL be linked.

12. Caches SHALL be integrity- and scope-controlled.

13. Parallel jobs SHALL remain isolated.

14. Failures SHALL remain visible.

15. Automatic retry SHALL not erase original result.

16. Release-relevant Builds SHALL be reproducible where practical.

17. Artefact retention SHALL be explicit.

18. Build promotion SHALL require release Gates.

19. Historical Build Records SHALL remain queryable.

20. CI authority SHALL NOT include production mutation by default.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 26.903 Canonical Release Gate and Promotion Contract
text:
26.903 Canonical Release Gate and Promotion Contract

The following requirements define release promotion:

1. Every Release Candidate SHALL have stable identity.

2. Source commit SHALL be immutable.

3. Build artefacts and checksums SHALL be explicit.

4. Schemas and migrations SHALL be explicit.

5. Test and Conformance evidence SHALL be linked.

6. Known issues and Exceptions SHALL be explicit.

7. Every Release Gate SHALL have stable identity and Version.

8. Mandatory failed Gates SHALL block promotion.

9. Conditional Gates SHALL apply based on change impact.

10. Gate exceptions SHALL follow governed Exception policy.

11. Promotion Decision SHALL bind to exact Candidate.

12. Source and target Environments SHALL be explicit.

13. Approver SHALL be authorised.

14. Conditions and schedule SHALL be explicit.

15. Rollback or recovery SHALL be explicit.

16. Canary or staged release SHALL be supported.

17. Deployment outcome SHALL be verified separately.

18. Material post-gate changes SHALL invalidate the Decision.

19. Historical promotion evidence SHALL remain queryable.

20. Build or merge success SHALL NOT become deployment authority automatically.

26.904 Canonical Regression Contract

The following requirements define regression governance:

1. Every material Regression SHALL have stable identity.

2. Affected Requirement SHALL be explicit.

3. Impact SHALL be explicit.

4. First known bad Version SHOULD be identified.

5. Last known good Version SHOULD be identified.

6. Evidence SHALL be linked.

7. Root cause SHALL be investigated.

8. Fix SHALL be linked.

9. Persistent Regression Test SHALL be added.

10. Test SHALL fail before the fix where reproducible.

11. Test SHALL pass after the fix.

12. Similar paths SHALL be reviewed.

13. Certification impact SHALL be evaluated.

14. Release eligibility SHALL be evaluated.

15. Incident relationship SHALL be linked where applicable.

16. Regression closure SHALL require verification.

17. Flaky reproduction SHALL remain explicit.

18. Historical state SHALL remain queryable.

19. Lessons MAY become reviewed Derived Learning.

20. A fixed defect SHALL NOT be allowed to lose its Regression Test silently.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 26.906 Developer Experience, Testing and Conformance Invariants
text:
26.905 Canonical Developer Governance Contract

The following requirements define overall developer governance:

1. Canonical architecture SHALL remain the source of implementation Requirements.

2. Developer tools SHALL expose scope and authority.

3. Safe defaults SHALL prevent production side effects.

4. Production data and Credentials SHALL be prohibited by default.

5. Schemas and contracts SHALL be Versioned.

6. Tests SHALL map to Requirements and risks.

7. Deterministic and probabilistic assurance SHALL remain distinct.

8. Mocks SHALL not replace live contract verification entirely.

9. Paid and consequential Tests SHALL be bounded.

10. Privacy, authority, cost and provenance SHALL be first-class Test dimensions.

11. Failed mandatory Tests SHALL block applicable promotion.

12. Exceptions SHALL be narrow, expiring and visible.

13. Certifications SHALL bind to exact subject Versions and scope.

14. Drift SHALL trigger revalidation.

15. Regressions SHALL create persistent Tests.

16. Coding Agents SHALL remain scoped and evidence-bound.

17. Documentation SHALL remain current and tested.

18. Builds and releases SHALL preserve provenance.

19. Historical conformance evidence SHALL remain reconstructable.

20. No developer, test or release failure SHALL authorise bypass of the Intelligence Fabric.

26.906 Developer Experience, Testing and Conformance Invariants

The following invariants shall remain true:

- No developer convenience becomes a policy exception automatically.

- No production Credential enters ordinary local or CI testing.

- No production personal data enters ordinary test Environments by default.

- No mock response becomes proof of live Provider behaviour.

- No sandbox becomes proof of production equivalence.

- No single Model sample becomes proof of stable quality.

- No benchmark score becomes production authority.

- No skipped, blocked or inconclusive Test becomes passed.

- No flaky failure disappears through retry without evidence.

- No quarantined Test remains unowned or unexpired.

- No live paid Test runs without Budget and Account scope.

- No publication, message, purchase or deletion Test targets uncontrolled production state.

- No timeout becomes ordinary failure when external outcome may be unknown.

- No Adapter hides retries, Secrets or Provider-native semantics.

- No Agent Test ignores authority, privacy or escalation.

- No Certification applies beyond exact Version, scope and validity.

- No Exception lacks owner, risk, compensating control and expiry.

- No failed mandatory Gate promotes silently.

- No fixed material regression loses its Regression Test.

- No developer, test or conformance failure bypasses the Intelligence Fabric.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
26.907 Closing Statement

Developer experience determines whether Omnira can be built safely and repeatedly.

Testing determines whether implementations satisfy their intended behaviour.

Conformance determines whether those implementations satisfy the canonical architecture.

The Schema Package defines the structures.

The API Definition defines the service boundary.

The SDK and CLI expose governed developer interaction.

The Developer Environment preserves safe and reproducible work.

The Test Fixture creates controlled state.

The Mock and Simulator create bounded dependency behaviour.

The Live Test verifies real external behaviour.

The Unit Test verifies small implementation logic.

The Integration Test verifies connected components.

The Contract Test verifies interface compatibility.

The System Test verifies the combined platform.

The End-to-End Test verifies the path from Request to Outcome.

The Evaluation Suite verifies intelligence quality.

The Security and Privacy Tests verify protected boundaries.

The Reliability Tests verify failure, retry and recovery.

The Conformance Profile defines what a component must satisfy.

The Conformance Run assembles the evidence.

The Certification binds that evidence to one exact Version and scope.

The Exception preserves a temporary gap without hiding it.

The Build Record preserves implementation provenance.

The Release Gate prevents unverified promotion.

The Promotion Decision authorises one exact Release Candidate.

The Regression Test ensures that corrected failures remain corrected.

For Familje-Stunden, this architecture ensures that:

- Nova and Pling identity tests remain tied to approved references,

- child-facing safety failures block acceptance,

- private family and child data never enters ordinary development fixtures,

- publication tests use private dedicated Accounts,

- and the correct August Package Version is verified before release.

For The Prompt, it ensures that:

- research claims remain source-grounded,

- generated visual disclosure is tested,

- duplicate Scripts and publications become regressions rather than recurring surprises,

- Provider and publication failures preserve unknown outcome,

- and live social tests never use private personal Accounts by default.

For GainPilot, it ensures that:

- programme age and active Plan context remain available to Arnold,

- exercise substitution remains bounded,

- health and fitness data retain Confidential or Local Only handling,

- local Model paths are tested against exact hardware and Runtime,

- and coaching quality remains distinct from technical response success.

For Atlas, it ensures that:

- Provider swaps remain invisible above the Adapter boundary,

- Agent identity and authority survive Model changes,

- Memory and Tool access remain tested,

- unsupported authority triggers escalation,

- and Atlas can never claim that code, Tests or deployments succeeded without evidence.

For Omnira, it ensures that:

- developers,

- coding Agents,

- schemas,

- SDKs,

- APIs,

- Adapters,

- Connectors,

- Models,

- Providers,

- Tools,

- workflows,

- Environments,

- builds,

- releases,

participate in one executable architecture.

The architecture chapter states what must be true.

The Canonical Contract expresses the requirement.

The Test verifies observable behaviour.

The Conformance Run assembles proof.

The Certification declares bounded eligibility.

The Release Gate protects promotion.

The observability system verifies runtime reality.

The Incident system responds when reality differs from the proof.

No implementation without a contract.

No contract without Version.

No Test without expected behaviour.

No live Test without bounded side effects.

No paid Test without Budget.

No Provider assumption without contract evidence.

No Model quality claim without evaluation.

No Agent certification without authority and Memory tests.

No workflow certification without failure and unknown-outcome tests.

No release without mandatory Gates.

No Certification without exact scope.

No Exception without expiry.

No regression fix without a permanent Test.

No developer productivity at the cost of user trust.

The developer retains a clear and safe path to build.

The Project retains its data and implementation boundaries.

Omnira retains canonical conformance and release governance.

The Fabric shall not call itself implementation-ready merely because the code runs.

It becomes implementation-ready only when the contracts are executable, the failures are tested, the evidence is preserved and every promoted component proves that it behaves inside the architecture the user approved.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical Stage 1 implementation architecture for the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

It translates the architectural contracts established in Chapters 1 through 26 into the first deployable implementation boundary.

It establishes:

- which Intelligence Fabric components SHALL exist in Stage 1,

- which capabilities SHALL be operational before broader autonomy is introduced,

- which services SHALL be canonical,

- which functions MAY initially remain modular components inside a shared service,

- which persistence boundaries SHALL exist,

- which schemas SHALL become executable,

- how Atlas and other Agents SHALL access the Fabric,

- how Capability Requests SHALL enter the system,

- how Planning, Routing, Budgeting, Approval, Execution and Evidence SHALL connect,

- how Providers SHALL be registered and invoked,

- how local Models and local Nodes SHALL participate,

- how Credentials SHALL remain outside Agent context,

- how external and local intelligence SHALL coexist behind one capability-first interface,

- how synchronous and asynchronous work SHALL be handled,

- how MCP, APIs, queues, webhooks and manual-assisted integrations SHALL enter through governed boundaries,

- how text, code, image, Voice and multimodal workloads SHALL be represented,

- how Assets SHALL be ingested,

- how provenance SHALL be created,

- how Quality SHALL be evaluated,

- how Memory SHALL receive only governed Derived Learning,

- how Data Classification SHALL constrain routing,

- how approval SHALL bind to exact execution scope,

- how cost SHALL be estimated, reserved and reconciled,

- how logs, traces, audit and Incidents SHALL be produced,

- how developer conformance SHALL be enforced,

- which Providers and Runtime paths SHALL be implemented first,

- which features SHALL explicitly remain outside Stage 1,

- how the implementation SHALL remain migratable toward later stages,

- and what evidence SHALL prove that Stage 1 is complete.

Stage 1 is not a prototype that may ignore canonical contracts.

Stage 1 is the minimum production-capable Intelligence Fabric foundation.

Stage 1 shall prefer:

- correctness over breadth,

- explicit scope over convenience,

- bounded autonomy over unrestricted Agent freedom,

- clear interfaces over distributed complexity,

- durable evidence over hidden state,

- local and free-first options where suitable,

- Provider independence over direct SDK coupling,

- and reversible implementation choices over premature optimisation.

Stage 1 shall not attempt to implement every future feature described in this book.

Stage 1 shall implement enough of every mandatory control plane to ensure that later expansion does not require abandoning the architecture.

The implementation may begin as a modular monolith or small set of cohesive services where operational simplicity is beneficial.

Canonical boundaries SHALL exist even when process boundaries do not yet exist.

A module boundary is sufficient where distribution would create unnecessary complexity.

A database table is not a domain boundary by itself.

A microservice is not automatically better architecture.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
A message bus is not required merely because future scale may require one.

A direct internal function call may be valid when:

- the canonical interface remains explicit,

- the module boundary is maintained,

- observability remains intact,

- and later extraction remains possible.

Stage 1 SHALL NOT encode Provider-specific assumptions into Atlas.

Stage 1 SHALL NOT expose raw API keys to Agents.

Stage 1 SHALL NOT allow unrestricted MCP discovery to become authority.

Stage 1 SHALL NOT allow arbitrary external Providers to be used merely because a Connector exists.

Stage 1 SHALL NOT automatically publish generated outputs.

Stage 1 SHALL NOT automatically lower Data Classification.

Stage 1 SHALL NOT automatically admit raw execution histories into permanent Memory.

Stage 1 SHALL NOT silently retry unknown external side effects.

Stage 1 SHALL NOT treat Provider acceptance as Completion.

Stage 1 SHALL NOT claim unrestricted autonomous operation.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

Chapter 28 defines rollout, migration, anti-patterns and future evolution beyond this implementation boundary.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.2 Stage 1 Mission

The mission of Stage 1 is to create one trustworthy Intelligence Fabric path through which Omnira may request, select, execute, evaluate and record intelligence work without depending directly on one Model, one Provider or one execution location.

Stage 1 shall prove that Omnira can:

1. receive a Capability Request.

2. classify its data and execution requirements.

3. resolve available capabilities.

4. identify eligible Models, Providers, Accounts, Tools and local Runtime resources.

5. generate an executable Plan.

6. estimate cost and resource requirements.

7. determine whether approval is required.

8. route according to policy.

9. execute through a canonical Adapter boundary.

10. handle synchronous or asynchronous results.

11. ingest resulting Assets.

12. evaluate Quality.

13. reconcile actual cost and usage.

14. preserve Execution Evidence and provenance.

15. produce governed Derived Learning where justified.

16. return a canonical Completion result to the requesting Agent or user.

27.3 Stage 1 Architectural Position

The Intelligence Fabric SHALL exist as a shared Omnira platform service.

It SHALL NOT be owned by Atlas.

Atlas SHALL be one major consumer.

Other consumers may include:

- Arnold,

- future Project Agents,

- workflow services,

- Omnira user interfaces,

- publication systems,

- test harnesses,

- and administrative control planes.

27.4 Atlas Boundary

Atlas SHALL express:

- intent,

- Project context,

- desired Capability,

- constraints,

- Quality requirements,

- Budget preferences,

- privacy requirements,

- and expected Output.

Atlas SHALL NOT need to know:

- concrete Provider API endpoints,

- API keys,

- Provider-specific request schemas,

- raw Model identifiers,

- retry headers,

- webhook formats,

- or Provider-native job state machines.

27.5 Fabric Responsibility

The Fabric SHALL determine:

- what resources are eligible,

- how work is planned,

- which resource is selected,

- how execution occurs,

- how failures are handled,

- how cost is governed,

- how evidence is produced,

- and whether Completion requirements are satisfied.

27.6 Stage 1 Completion Definition

Stage 1 is complete only when representative workflows can use the Fabric end to end without bypassing its canonical boundaries.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.7 Stage 1 Mandatory Domains

Stage 1 SHALL implement operational support for:

- Capability Registry,

- Model Registry,

- Provider Registry,

- Agent and Tool Resource Registry,

- Provider Account and Connection Registry,

- Credential references,

- Capability Request intake,

- Intent Envelope validation,

- Planning,

- Execution Graphs,

- Routing,

- Cost estimation,

- Budget enforcement,

- Approval,

- Execution,

- synchronous APIs,

- asynchronous Provider jobs,

- polling,

- webhook ingestion,

- durable work queues,

- local Runtime execution,

- MCP client integration,

- Asset ingestion,

- provenance,

- Quality evaluation,

- Evidence,

- Data Classification,

- privacy policy,

- Tenant and Project isolation,

- bounded authority,

- observability,

- audit,

- Incident hooks,

- testing,

- and conformance.

27.8 Stage 1 Representative Modalities

Stage 1 SHALL support at minimum:

- text,

- reasoning,

- code-oriented text generation,

- image generation,

- Voice generation,

- generic file and Asset processing,

- search or retrieval capability,

- Tool invocation,

- and local Model execution.

27.9 Stage 1 Deferred Modalities

Full production support may be deferred for:

- advanced video orchestration,

- music generation,

- fully autonomous browser production,

- complex multi-Agent marketplaces,

- custom Model training,

- large-scale fine-tuning,

- distributed GPU clusters,

- federated learning,

- and autonomous external purchasing.

The architecture SHALL leave room for them.

27.10 Stage 1 Deployment Philosophy

Stage 1 SHOULD minimise operational complexity.

The preferred initial shape is:

- one Fabric application or small cohesive service group,

- one primary relational database,

- one durable object or Asset store,

- one queue,

- one Secret system,

- one observability stack,

- and optional local Runtime Nodes.

27.11 Modular Monolith

A modular monolith is acceptable for Stage 1 when internal boundaries follow canonical domains.

27.12 Module Extraction

A module SHALL be extractable later without changing canonical contracts.

27.13 Premature Microservice Prohibition

Stage 1 SHALL NOT create separate network services merely to mirror every chapter or object.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.14 Shared Process

The following MAY initially share one process:

- Registry,

- Planner,

- Router,

- Cost Engine,

- Policy Evaluation,

- Evidence assembly,

- and orchestration.

Their data models and interfaces SHALL remain explicit.

27.15 Separately Isolated Components

The following SHOULD have stronger process or trust isolation where practical:

- Secret resolution,

- untrusted Tool execution,

- local process execution,

- webhook ingress,

- browser-assisted operation,

- and arbitrary file processing.

27.16 Stage 1 Logical Architecture

The Stage 1 logical architecture consists of:

1. Fabric API.

2. Identity and Context Boundary.

3. Capability and Resource Registries.

4. Policy and Classification Engine.

5. Planner.

6. Cost and Budget Engine.

7. Routing Engine.

8. Approval Control.

9. Execution Orchestrator.

10. Adapter Layer.

11. Connector Layer.

12. Async Job Manager.

13. Queue and Worker Layer.

14. MCP Client.

15. Local Runtime Manager.

16. Asset and Provenance Service.

17. Quality Evaluation Service.

18. Evidence Service.

19. Memory Admission Boundary.

20. Observability and Audit.

21. Incident Hooks.

22. Developer and Conformance Harness.

27.17 Fabric API

The Fabric API is the canonical entry boundary for intelligence execution.

27.18 Fabric API Responsibilities

It SHALL:

- authenticate the caller,

- resolve Principal identity,

- resolve Tenant and Project,

- validate Intent Envelope,

- create Capability Request,

- assign correlation,

- initiate policy evaluation,

- start Planning,

- expose status,

- return Completion result,

- and expose Evidence references.

27.19 Fabric API Non-Responsibilities

It SHALL NOT:

- embed Provider SDK semantics,

- resolve raw Credentials into caller context,

- select Provider by hard-coded name,

- bypass approval,

- or fabricate synchronous completion for asynchronous work.

27.20 Stage 1 API Style

Stage 1 MAY use HTTP and JSON as the primary public internal API.

Internal module calls MAY use native language interfaces.

Canonical schemas SHALL remain transport-neutral.

27.21 Stage 1 API Operations

The first API SHOULD include operations equivalent to:

- submit Capability Request,

- inspect Request,

- inspect Plan,

- approve or deny,

- inspect Execution,

- cancel Execution,

- retrieve result,

- inspect Asset,

- inspect Evidence,

- query Registry,

- inspect Connector health,

- and inspect current Cost state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.22 Capability Request Submission

Request submission SHALL return:

- Request identity,

- correlation identity,

- initial state,

- whether approval may be required,

- and status location or equivalent handle.

27.23 Asynchronous API

Long-running work SHALL return a durable canonical handle rather than holding the client connection indefinitely.

27.24 Request Status

Request status SHALL remain distinct from Execution and Provider job status.

27.25 Canonical Request States

Stage 1 Capability Request states SHOULD include:

- received,

- validating,

- planning,

- awaiting approval,

- ready,

- executing,

- evaluating,

- completed,

- failed,

- cancelled,

- unknown,

- and blocked.

27.26 Intent Envelope

The Stage 1 Intent Envelope SHALL contain enough information to drive policy and planning.

27.27 Stage 1 Intent Envelope Fields

It SHOULD include or reference:

- intentEnvelopeId,

- requester Principal,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- purpose,

- Capability,

- desired Output type,

- Input references,

- Classification,

- Routing Profile,

- Quality Floor,

- maximum Budget,

- deadline,

- privacy constraints,

- preferred or prohibited resources,

- approval expectations,

- and metadata.

27.28 Intent Validation

Validation SHALL occur before Planning.

27.29 Unknown Intent Field

Unknown optional fields MAY be preserved.

Unknown mandatory semantics SHALL cause validation failure.

27.30 Request Idempotency

Request submission SHALL support idempotency for clients that may retry.

27.31 Request Deduplication

Deduplication SHALL not merge distinct human intents merely because their text is identical.

27.32 Tenant Context

Tenant context SHALL derive from trusted identity or explicit platform scope.

27.33 Project Context

Project context SHALL be mandatory for Project-scoped work.

27.34 Missing Project

Missing Project SHALL fail closed when the requested Capability uses:

- Project Memory,

- Project Assets,

- Project Credentials,

- Project Budget,

- or external Project Accounts.

27.35 Identity Service Integration

The Fabric SHALL consume canonical Principal identity rather than inventing its own authentication model.

27.36 Service Principal

Internal Fabric modules and workers SHALL use Service Principal identity.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.37 Agent Principal

Atlas and every Agent SHALL have stable Agent Principal identity.

27.38 Resource Registry Layer

Stage 1 SHALL maintain separate canonical registries for:

- Capabilities,

- Models,

- Providers,

- Tools,

- Runtime Nodes,

- Agents,

- Provider Accounts,

- Connections,

- and Adapter Versions.

27.39 Registry Persistence

Registry records SHOULD be stored in the primary relational database initially.

27.40 Registry Read Path

Planning and Routing SHALL read through canonical Registry interfaces.

27.41 Registry Write Path

Registry mutation SHALL require authenticated administrative or governed configuration authority.

27.42 Registry Cache

Read-heavy Registry objects MAY be cached.

Cache invalidation SHALL occur on Version change.

27.43 Capability Registry Stage 1

The Capability Registry SHALL be the primary semantic discovery mechanism.

27.44 Capability Examples

Initial capability identifiers may represent:

- text.generate,

- text.reason,

- code.generate,

- image.generate,

- voice.generate,

- search.web,

- retrieval.project,

- tool.invoke,

- asset.transform,

- and model.local.generate.

27.45 Capability Hierarchy

Capabilities MAY have parent and child relationships.

Routing SHALL use exact requirements, not string-prefix assumptions alone.

27.46 Capability Requirement

A Request MAY include:

- required,

- preferred,

- prohibited,

- and optional capability features.

27.47 Capability Feature

Examples include:

- structured output,

- streaming,

- image reference input,

- Voice Profile support,

- JSON schema output,

- Tool calling,

- long context,

- or local execution.

27.48 Model Registry Stage 1

The Model Registry SHALL describe intelligence resources independently from Provider Accounts.

27.49 Model Registry Minimum Fields

A Model Record SHOULD include:

- modelId,

- providerId,

- productId,

- native identifier,

- canonical display name,

- model family,

- Version or alias state,

- supported Capabilities,

- context limits,

- modalities,

- pricing reference,

- quality evidence,

- privacy properties,

- lifecycle state,

- and last verification.

27.50 Model Alias

Provider aliases SHALL be distinguishable from immutable Model Versions.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.51 Alias Drift

Alias changes SHALL trigger Registry drift state and potential re-evaluation.

27.52 Local Model Record

Local Models SHALL appear in the Model Registry alongside external Models.

27.53 Local Model Provider

Local runtime infrastructure MAY be represented as an Omnira Local Provider abstraction.

27.54 Provider Registry Stage 1

The Provider Registry SHALL represent external or local service organisations and execution systems.

27.55 Provider Minimum Fields

A Provider Record SHOULD include:

- providerId,

- name,

- Provider type,

- trust state,

- supported Products,

- legal or Terms references,

- privacy evidence,

- commercial-rights evidence,

- regions,

- lifecycle,

- and review date.

27.56 Provider Product

Different Products from one Provider SHALL remain distinguishable.

27.57 Provider Account Registry

Each Account SHALL identify:

- accountId,

- Provider,

- owner type,

- Tenant,

- Project scope,

- plan,

- billing mode,

- region,

- privacy settings,

- training setting,

- commercial-use status,

- and lifecycle.

27.58 Account Owner Type

Stage 1 SHALL support:

- user-owned,

- Tenant-owned,

- Project-owned,

- and Omnira-managed

Accounts where applicable.

27.59 User-Owned Account

User-owned Credentials SHALL remain under user authority while still being governed by Fabric policy.

27.60 Omnira-Managed Account

Omnira-managed Accounts SHALL preserve Project and Tenant attribution for cost and data use.

27.61 Connection Registry

A Connection binds:

- Provider Account,

- Credential Reference,

- Adapter Version,

- Environment,

- Project or Tenant scope,

- and allowed Capabilities.

27.62 Connection Minimum Fields

A Connection SHOULD include:

- connectionId,

- providerId,

- productId,

- accountId,

- credentialRef,

- adapterId,

- adapterVersion,

- Environment,

- Tenant,

- Project scope,

- allowed Capabilities,

- health,

- state,

- and Version.

27.63 Credential Reference

Connections SHALL store Credential References only.

27.64 Credential Resolution Boundary

Raw Secret resolution SHALL occur only at the Adapter or approved Tool execution boundary.

27.65 Credential Store

Stage 1 SHALL use an approved Secret Store.

The implementation MAY initially use:

- operating-system secure storage,

- environment-injected secure secret service,

- Vault-compatible storage,

- or another approved system.

Plaintext files SHALL NOT be canonical Credential storage.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.66 Secret Retrieval

Secret retrieval SHALL be:

- scoped,

- auditable,

- short-lived,

- and unavailable to ordinary Agent context.

27.67 Secret Cache

If Secret values are cached in memory, the cache SHALL be:

- process-local,

- short-lived,

- non-logged,

- and cleared on revocation where practical.

27.68 Tool Registry Stage 1

The Tool Registry SHALL describe executable capabilities distinct from Models.

27.69 Tool Minimum Fields

A Tool SHOULD include:

- toolId,

- name,

- Version,

- Capability Bindings,

- input schema,

- output schema,

- side-effect class,

- authority requirements,

- Environment requirements,

- Sandbox requirements,

- and lifecycle.

27.70 MCP Tool

MCP-discovered Tools SHALL be mapped into canonical Tool Records before Agent exposure.

27.71 Runtime Node Registry

Stage 1 SHALL register local Nodes capable of intelligence or Tool execution.

27.72 Runtime Node Minimum Fields

A Node SHOULD include:

- nodeId,

- owner,

- Tenant,

- device class,

- operating system,

- hardware capabilities,

- Runtime services,

- network state,

- trust state,

- availability,

- and health.

27.73 Stage 1 Local Nodes

Representative Nodes MAY include:

- Mac laptop,

- Windows workstation,

- private AI rig,

- or future server.

27.74 Node Availability

The Scheduler SHALL not assume that personal Nodes are continuously online.

27.75 Node Start Requirement

When a required Local Only Node is offline, the Fabric SHALL:

- wait,

- notify,

- or request the user to start it

rather than violating placement policy.

27.76 Policy Engine

Stage 1 SHALL implement one central policy evaluation layer.

27.77 Policy Domains

The policy layer SHALL evaluate at minimum:

- Data Classification,

- Provider eligibility,

- Routing constraints,

- Budget,

- authority,

- approval,

- rights,

- consent,

- local placement,

- and publication restrictions.

27.78 Policy Result

Policy evaluation SHALL return:

- permitted,

- permitted with conditions,

- denied,

- approval required,

- or indeterminate.

27.79 Indeterminate Policy

Indeterminate SHALL fail closed for consequential actions.

27.80 Policy Version

Every Decision SHALL reference applicable policy Versions.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.81 Policy Representation

Stage 1 MAY represent policy through:

- typed application rules,

- configuration,

- or a policy engine.

Human-readable canonical policy SHALL remain authoritative.

27.82 Premature Policy Language

A full general-purpose policy DSL is not required for Stage 1.

27.83 Classification Engine

Stage 1 SHALL classify every material Input and Asset.

27.84 Classification Levels

The five canonical levels SHALL be implemented:

- Public,

- Project Internal,

- Confidential,

- Local Only,

- Prohibited.

27.85 Classification Default

Unknown sensitive data SHALL receive restrictive treatment.

27.86 Automatic Classifier

An automatic classifier MAY propose:

- Data Category,

- Classification,

- confidence,

- and reasons.

27.87 User Tightening

Users SHALL be able to tighten Classification.

27.88 Automatic Lowering

Automatic lowering SHALL be prohibited.

27.89 Classification Propagation

Classification SHALL propagate to:

- prompts,

- Provider Inputs,

- generated Outputs,

- Assets,

- embeddings,

- Evidence,

- and Memory proposals.

27.90 Project Isolation

Every persisted object SHALL include Tenant and Project scope where applicable.

27.91 Database Enforcement

Stage 1 SHOULD use structural access enforcement such as:

- scoped repository methods,

- row-level security,

- separate schemas,

- or equivalent controls.

Application filters alone SHALL NOT be the only high-risk isolation mechanism.

27.92 Object Storage Isolation

Asset keys SHALL include canonical scope and shall not depend solely on human-readable filenames.

27.93 Queue Isolation

Queue messages SHALL preserve Tenant and Project identity.

27.94 Cache Isolation

Cache keys SHALL include Tenant and Project where data or Decisions are scoped.

27.95 Search Isolation

Search and vector retrieval SHALL apply access eligibility before similarity ranking.

27.96 Planner

The Planner SHALL convert one Capability Request into one Versioned Execution Plan.

27.97 Planner Input

The Planner SHALL receive:

- Intent Envelope,

- available Capabilities,

- policy constraints,

- Budget,

- Routing Profile,

- Quality requirements,

- data placement,

- deadline,

- and resource health.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.98 Planner Output

The Planner SHALL produce:

- Plan identity,

- Plan Version,

- Steps,

- dependencies,

- required Capabilities,

- expected Inputs and Outputs,

- resource constraints,

- approval gates,

- Budget allocation,

- fallback policy,

- completion criteria,

- and evidence requirements.

27.99 Plan Persistence

Every executable Plan SHALL be stored durably before execution.

27.100 Plan Immutability

An approved Plan Version SHALL be immutable.

Replanning creates a new Version.

27.101 Plan Step

Every Step SHALL have:

- stepId,

- operation,

- Capability,

- Inputs,

- expected Outputs,

- dependency list,

- side-effect class,

- retry policy,

- Quality requirements,

- Budget,

- and state.

27.102 Step State

Canonical Stage 1 Step states SHOULD include:

- pending,

- ready,

- blocked,

- queued,

- running,

- awaiting external completion,

- awaiting human,

- evaluating,

- succeeded,

- failed,

- cancelled,

- skipped,

- unknown,

- and reconciliation required.

27.103 Execution Graph

The Plan SHALL be represented as a directed execution graph.

27.104 Acyclic Default

Stage 1 SHOULD prefer acyclic execution graphs.

Loops MAY be represented through bounded retry or explicit iteration constructs.

27.105 Cycle Prohibition

Unbounded graph cycles SHALL be rejected.

27.106 Completion Contract

Every Plan SHALL define Completion conditions.

27.107 Completion Contract Examples

Completion may require:

- valid text Output,

- accepted Asset,

- external publication verification,

- cost reconciliation,

- or human approval.

27.108 Planner and Provider Independence

The Planner SHALL reason in Capabilities and resource requirements.

It SHALL NOT produce raw Provider SDK calls.

27.109 Cost Engine

Stage 1 SHALL implement cost estimation before paid execution.

27.110 Cost Sources

Cost estimates may derive from:

- token pricing,

- per-image pricing,

- per-character pricing,

- per-second pricing,

- subscription allocation,

- local electricity approximation,

- manual credit use,

- and fixed task cost.

27.111 Estimated Cost

Every paid Plan SHALL carry estimated cost.

27.112 Cost Range

When exact cost is unknown, the estimate SHALL support:

- minimum,

- expected,

- maximum,

- and confidence.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.113 Budget Object

Stage 1 SHALL support:

- per Request Budget,

- per Execution Budget,

- Project Budget,

- and optional global user Budget.

27.114 Budget Reservation

Paid execution SHOULD reserve estimated funds or credits before dispatch.

27.115 Budget Release

Unused reservation SHALL be released.

27.116 Actual Cost

Actual cost SHALL be reconciled after Provider usage becomes available.

27.117 Missing Cost

Missing Provider usage SHALL remain unknown rather than zero.

27.118 Cost Ledger

Cost Records SHALL be append-only or Versioned.

27.119 Cost Attribution

Every cost SHALL map to:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Request,

- Execution,

- Attempt,

- Provider,

- Account,

- and Capability.

27.120 Retry Cost

Retries SHALL consume the same approved Budget unless separately approved.

27.121 Fallback Cost

Fallback SHALL remain inside Budget.

27.122 Cost Ceiling

The Execution Orchestrator SHALL stop before dispatching work that would knowingly exceed the authorised maximum.

27.123 Routing Engine

The Routing Engine SHALL select from currently eligible resources.

27.124 Routing Inputs

Routing SHALL evaluate:

- Capability,

- mandatory features,

- Data Classification,

- privacy,

- rights,

- consent,

- authority,

- Routing Profile,

- Quality evidence,

- health,

- latency,

- capacity,

- cost,

- Budget,

- deadline,

- local availability,

- Provider Account,

- and certification.

27.125 Eligibility Before Ranking

Ineligible resources SHALL be removed before scoring.

27.126 Security Precedence

Security, permissions, data protection, rights and task requirements SHALL outrank price.

27.127 Routing Profiles

Stage 1 SHALL implement:

- Economy,

- Balanced,

- Premium,

- Private,

- and Pinned.

27.128 Economy

Economy SHALL prefer the lowest-cost eligible resource meeting the Quality Floor.

27.129 Balanced

Balanced SHALL optimise across:

- quality,

- cost,

- latency,

- and reliability.

27.130 Premium

Premium SHALL prioritise higher Quality while respecting Budget and policy.

27.131 Private

Private SHALL prefer or require approved private and local resources according to policy.

27.132 Pinned

Pinned SHALL restrict execution to the specified eligible resource or resource set.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.133 Free-First Behaviour

Economy and Balanced MAY prefer:

- local resources,

- free quotas,

- user-owned subscriptions,

- or zero-incremental-cost resources

when they satisfy all mandatory requirements.

27.134 Free Does Not Override Quality

A free resource below the Quality Floor SHALL be ineligible.

27.135 Free Does Not Override Privacy

A free external service SHALL not receive Local Only data.

27.136 User-Owned Subscription

A paid subscription already owned by the user MAY have low incremental cost while remaining a Provider with external custody.

27.137 Routing Score

Stage 1 MAY calculate a weighted score after eligibility filtering.

27.138 Routing Evidence

Every Routing Decision SHALL record:

- eligible candidates,

- excluded candidates and reason classes,

- selected resource,

- Routing Profile,

- key scores,

- policy Versions,

- and timestamp.

27.139 Deterministic Tie Break

Tie-breaking SHOULD be stable and explainable.

27.140 Resource Health

Unhealthy resources SHALL be excluded or penalised according to severity.

27.141 Certification Requirement

Production Routes SHALL require current Conformance Certification for the relevant subject and use case where Stage 1 has implemented certification.

27.142 Approval Engine

Stage 1 SHALL implement bounded approval before consequential execution.

27.143 Approval Categories

Approval SHALL be required at minimum for:

- first paid external execution,

- Budget increases,

- publication,

- external messaging,

- deletion,

- overwrite,

- production Credential mutation,

- new Provider Connection,

- new external Confidential transfer,

- and authority expansion.

27.144 Draft-Only Work

Low-risk draft generation MAY operate under pre-approved Stage 1 Mandates.

27.145 Bounded Job Approval

Approval MAY authorize:

- exact Plan Version,

- maximum cost,

- approved Providers,

- retry count,

- fallback set,

- and deadline.

27.146 Approval Token

Execution SHALL consume machine-verifiable Approval Tokens where applicable.

27.147 Stale Approval

Approval SHALL be invalidated by material changes including:

- Plan Version,

- Provider,

- Account,

- Budget,

- target Asset,

- data disclosure,

- or policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.148 Approval Service Availability

Consequential actions SHALL fail closed if approval state cannot be verified.

27.149 Execution Orchestrator

The Execution Orchestrator SHALL own canonical runtime progression of Plans.

27.150 Orchestrator Responsibilities

It SHALL:

- create Execution,

- admit Steps,

- request Routing,

- enforce Budget,

- request approval,

- create Attempts,

- dispatch through Adapter or Tool boundary,

- track async work,

- trigger evaluation,

- reconcile cost,

- persist Evidence,

- and update Completion state.

27.151 Orchestrator Non-Responsibilities

It SHALL NOT:

- know raw Provider credentials,

- implement Provider-specific request bodies,

- perform direct external publication without a Connector,

- or write permanent Memory directly.

27.152 Execution

Every Plan run SHALL create a unique Execution.

27.153 Execution Minimum Fields

An Execution SHOULD include:

- executionId,

- Request,

- Plan Version,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Principal,

- state,

- startedAt,

- completedAt,

- Budget,

- Routing Profile,

- policy Versions,
