- Approval references,

- and Evidence Bundle.

27.154 Execution State

Canonical Stage 1 states SHOULD include:

- prepared,

- awaiting approval,

- admitted,

- running,

- waiting,

- evaluating,

- partially complete,

- completed,

- failed,

- cancelled,

- unknown,

- and reconciliation required.

27.155 Attempt

Every resource invocation SHALL create an Attempt.

27.156 Attempt Identity

Each Attempt SHALL have unique stable identity.

27.157 Attempt Minimum Fields

An Attempt SHOULD include:

- attemptId,

- Execution,

- Step,

- resource,

- Provider,

- Account,

- Model or Tool,

- Adapter Version,

- request correlation,

- idempotency key,

- startedAt,

- state,

- usage,

- cost,

- error,

- and native references.

27.158 Attempt State

Canonical states SHOULD include:

- prepared,

- dispatched,

- accepted,

- running,

- streaming,

- succeeded,

- failed,

- timed out,

- cancelled,

- unknown,

- and reconciled.

27.159 Attempt and Step

One Step MAY have several Attempts.

Attempt failure does not automatically mean Step failure.

27.160 Execution Locking

The Orchestrator SHALL prevent simultaneous conflicting progression of the same Step.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.161 Distributed Lease

If several workers process the same queue, Stage 1 SHALL use:

- lease,

- visibility timeout,

- row lock,

- or equivalent concurrency control.

27.162 Fencing

High-risk distributed work SHOULD use fencing or Version checks to prevent stale workers from committing state.

27.163 Queue

Stage 1 SHALL use a durable queue for work that cannot safely remain process-local.

27.164 Queue Candidates

Queue usage SHOULD include:

- long-running execution,

- Provider polling,

- webhook processing,

- Asset ingestion,

- evaluation,

- and reconciliation.

27.165 Queue Semantics

Stage 1 SHOULD assume at-least-once delivery.

27.166 Exactly-Once Prohibition

The implementation SHALL NOT claim end-to-end exactly-once semantics.

27.167 Idempotent Consumer

Queue consumers SHALL be idempotent.

27.168 Queue Message

A queue message SHALL contain:

- messageId,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- correlation,

- operation,

- target identity,

- attempt count,

- availableAt,

- and payload reference.

Large protected payloads SHOULD be referenced rather than embedded.

27.169 Queue Retry

Queue retry SHALL be distinct from Provider retry.

27.170 Dead-Letter Queue

Repeatedly unprocessable messages SHALL enter a dead-letter state.

27.171 Dead-Letter Review

Dead-letter messages SHALL remain queryable and replayable after correction.

27.172 Outbox Pattern

Stage 1 SHOULD use a transactional outbox when canonical state change and asynchronous message emission must remain consistent.

27.173 Inbox Pattern

Consumers SHOULD preserve deduplication or Inbox records for material messages.

27.174 Worker

Workers SHALL operate as Service Principals.

27.175 Worker Scope

Workers SHALL validate Tenant, Project, authority and current state before execution.

27.176 Scheduler

Stage 1 SHALL include basic scheduling for delayed and recurring internal Fabric work.

27.177 Stage 1 Scheduling Use

Initial scheduling MAY support:

- Provider polling,

- retry,

- reconciliation,

- retention cleanup,

- conformance re-check,

- and recurring approved workflows.

27.178 Scheduler Is Not Full Autonomy

A scheduled job SHALL still require current authority and policy at execution time.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.179 Scheduler Queue

Scheduled work SHOULD enter the same durable execution path as immediate work.

27.180 Admission Control

Before expensive or constrained execution, Stage 1 SHALL check:

- capacity,

- quota,

- Budget,

- health,

- concurrency,

- and deadline.

27.181 Capacity Limit

Capacity limits MAY be configured per:

- Provider Account,

- Model,

- Node,

- Project,

- or Capability.

27.182 Rate Limit

Provider rate-limit state SHALL be tracked.

27.183 Retry-After

Provider retry-after guidance SHALL be respected where valid.

27.184 Quota

Quota SHALL remain distinct from Budget.

27.185 Local Capacity

Local Node capacity MAY include:

- CPU,

- RAM,

- GPU,

- VRAM,

- disk,

- and Model residency.

27.186 Local Resource Reservation

Heavy local work MAY reserve capacity before execution.

27.187 Adapter Layer

All Provider-native communication SHALL occur through Versioned Adapters.

27.188 Adapter Interface

The canonical Stage 1 Adapter interface SHOULD support operations equivalent to:

- validate configuration,

- inspect capabilities,

- estimate usage where possible,

- execute synchronous operation,

- submit asynchronous operation,

- inspect job,

- cancel job where supported,

- retrieve result,

- and verify health.

27.189 Adapter Input

Adapters SHALL accept canonical operation requests.

27.190 Adapter Output

Adapters SHALL return canonical operation responses or canonical state updates.

27.191 Native Preservation

Provider-native references MAY be retained in bounded evidence.

They SHALL NOT leak into higher-level business logic.

27.192 Adapter Error Mapping

Every Adapter SHALL map native errors into canonical categories.

27.193 Stage 1 Error Categories

Canonical categories SHOULD include:

- invalid request,

- unauthenticated,

- unauthorised,

- quota exhausted,

- rate limited,

- unavailable,

- timeout,

- provider failure,

- malformed response,

- unsupported capability,

- content rejected,

- cancellation unsupported,

- unknown outcome,

- and internal mapping failure.

27.194 Retryability

Error categories SHALL include retryability guidance but SHALL not trigger retry independently of Reliability Policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.195 Adapter Usage Mapping

Usage SHALL be normalised into canonical units where possible.

27.196 Unknown Usage

Unknown usage SHALL remain unknown.

27.197 Adapter Version

Every Attempt SHALL record exact Adapter Version.

27.198 Adapter Configuration

Provider endpoint, region and feature configuration SHALL be externalised from business logic.

27.199 Adapter Health

Each Adapter and Connector SHALL expose health.

27.200 Connector Layer

A Connector represents one configured use of an Adapter, Account, Credential and scope.

27.201 Connector Activation

A Connection SHALL not become active until a bounded verification succeeds.

27.202 Connection Verification

Verification SHOULD check:

- authentication,

- expected Account,

- supported Capability,

- region where relevant,

- and safe test operation.

27.203 Connection Deactivation

Revoked Credentials or policy changes SHALL deactivate affected Connections.

27.204 Connection Health

Health MAY be:

- healthy,

- degraded,

- unavailable,

- unauthorised,

- quota exhausted,

- suspended,

- or unknown.

27.205 Stage 1 External Text Providers

Stage 1 SHALL implement at least two external text or reasoning Provider paths.

27.206 External Text Provider Independence

The exact Provider choices MAY evolve.

The architecture SHALL require two distinct functioning external Provider integrations before Stage 1 completion.

27.207 Text Provider Capability

Both SHOULD support:

- text generation,

- reasoning-oriented tasks,

- structured Output or schema mode where practical,

- usage reporting,

- and bounded error mapping.

27.208 Text Streaming

At least one Stage 1 text Provider path SHOULD support streaming.

27.209 Structured Output

Stage 1 SHOULD support canonical structured Output validation independently from Provider-specific schema features.

27.210 Provider-Native Tool Calling

Provider-native Tool calling MAY be supported later or through a constrained Stage 1 path.

It SHALL not bypass the canonical Tool Registry and authority layer.

27.211 ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs SHALL be the first Voice Provider candidate in Stage 1 unless implementation review identifies a blocking reason.

27.212 ElevenLabs Scope

The initial Voice integration SHOULD support:

- text-to-speech,

- Voice Profile reference,

- canonical audio settings,

- usage,

- cost,

- output Asset ingestion,

- consent checks,

- and provenance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.213 Voice Cloning

Unrestricted Voice cloning SHALL remain outside default Stage 1 operation.

27.214 Voice Consent

Any Voice identity use requiring consent SHALL be blocked without valid Consent evidence.

27.215 OpenArt

OpenArt SHALL be represented as the first multimodal production candidate where useful.

27.216 OpenArt Integration Mode

If no suitable stable automated API exists for the required production workflow, Stage 1 SHALL represent OpenArt through a Human-Assisted Connector rather than pretending automation.

27.217 Human-Assisted Connector

The Connector SHALL support:

- queued human state,

- exact instructions,

- Account,

- Project,

- Inputs,

- Budget or credits,

- evidence upload,

- output ingestion,

- and completion verification.

27.218 Human-Assisted Truthfulness

Human-assisted work SHALL remain labelled as human-assisted throughout Evidence and UI.

27.219 Image Provider

Stage 1 SHALL implement at least one automated image generation Provider path.

27.220 Image Provider Candidate

Ideogram or another suitable Provider MAY serve as the initial automated image alternative.

27.221 Image Generation Capability

The image Adapter SHOULD support:

- prompt,

- aspect ratio,

- dimensions where supported,

- style controls where relevant,

- reference Inputs where supported,

- Candidate count,

- asynchronous or synchronous state,

- usage,

- and Asset ingestion.

27.222 Image Candidate

Every generated image SHALL become a Candidate Asset Version before acceptance.

27.223 Image Quality Review

Manual QA SHALL remain mandatory before publication in Stage 1.

27.224 Local Runtime

Stage 1 SHALL implement at least one local Model Runtime path.

27.225 Ollama

Ollama MAY be the first local Runtime because of its simple local Model execution interface.

27.226 NVIDIA Runtime

An NVIDIA local inference path MAY be integrated where appropriate for the available workstation or future private rig.

27.227 Local Runtime Adapter

Local Models SHALL use the same canonical Adapter or Runtime boundary rather than being called directly by Atlas.

27.228 Local Model Discovery

Installed local Models MAY be discovered automatically.

Discovery SHALL NOT grant production eligibility automatically.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.229 Local Model Certification

A local Model SHALL require:

- capability evidence,

- hardware compatibility,

- privacy state,

- quality evidence,

- and conformance

before production routing.

27.230 Local Model Identity

Exact local Model identity SHALL include:

- model family,

- Version,

- quantisation or build,

- Runtime,

- and checksum where practical.

27.231 Local Model Context

Context limit SHALL be verified rather than assumed from metadata only.

27.232 Local Streaming

Local streaming SHOULD use the same canonical Stream interface as external text Providers.

27.233 Local Cancellation

Cancellation semantics SHALL be represented truthfully.

27.234 Local Only Execution

Local Only Inputs SHALL route only to eligible local or private resources.

27.235 Local Offline Execution

Offline local operation MAY proceed if:

- required policy is available,

- authority remains valid,

- resources are present,

- and later reconciliation is possible.

27.236 Offline Authority Expiry

Expired approval or Mandate SHALL prevent consequential offline execution.

27.237 MCP Stage 1

Stage 1 SHALL implement a governed MCP client.

27.238 MCP Scope

The initial MCP implementation SHOULD support:

- approved server registration,

- connection,

- initialization,

- capability negotiation,

- Tool discovery,

- Resource discovery where required,

- schema snapshot,

- Tool invocation,

- progress,

- and cancellation where supported.

27.239 Stage 1 MCP Server Classes

MCP servers MAY be:

- local stdio,

- approved HTTP,

- or another supported transport.

Local stdio SHOULD receive stronger process isolation.

27.240 MCP Server Registry

Every approved MCP server SHALL have a canonical server record.

27.241 MCP Discovery Snapshot

Discovery SHALL create a Versioned snapshot.

27.242 Dynamic Discovery

Newly discovered Tools SHALL not become automatically authorised.

27.243 MCP Tool Promotion

A discovered Tool SHALL pass:

- schema validation,

- permission review,

- side-effect classification,

- Project scope,

- and Conformance

before Agent use.

27.244 MCP Prompt

MCP Prompts SHALL be treated as templates or content.

They SHALL NOT become system policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.245 MCP Resource

Resource URIs SHALL be validated against approved scope.

27.246 MCP Sampling

Server-initiated unrestricted sampling SHALL remain disabled in Stage 1 unless explicitly routed back through the Fabric as a new Capability Request.

27.247 MCP Elicitation

Server-initiated requests for user input or authority SHALL NOT bypass Omnira approval.

27.248 MCP Environment

Local MCP processes SHALL receive minimal:

- environment variables,

- file access,

- network access,

- and Credentials.

27.249 Search Capability

Stage 1 MAY support web or external search as a Capability through approved Providers or Tools.

27.250 Search Result

Search results SHALL remain data, not trusted instructions.

27.251 Search Provenance

Search Outputs SHOULD preserve:

- source,

- URL or source identity,

- retrieval time,

- snippet,

- and Provider.

27.252 Retrieval Capability

Project retrieval SHALL use the governed Asset and Memory stores.

27.253 Retrieval Scope

Tenant and Project filtering SHALL occur before semantic ranking.

27.254 Retrieval Result

Each result SHALL preserve:

- source object,

- source Version,

- snippet or reference,

- relevance,

- Classification,

- and provenance.

27.255 Vector Store

Stage 1 MAY use one shared vector infrastructure if structural Project and Tenant isolation is enforced.

27.256 Embedding Provider

Embedding generation SHALL pass through the Fabric or an internal governed embedding service.

27.257 Embedding Classification

Embeddings inherit source Classification.

27.258 Local Embedding

Local embeddings SHOULD be available for Local Only Memory where practical.

27.259 Async Job Manager

Stage 1 SHALL implement canonical external asynchronous job handling.

27.260 External Job Handle

Every submitted Provider job SHALL receive a durable External Job Handle before the system loses execution context.

27.261 External Job Handle Fields

It SHOULD include:

- externalJobHandleId,

- Provider,

- Account,

- native job ID,

- Execution,

- Step,

- Attempt,

- submittedAt,

- state,

- polling policy,

- callback expectation,

- result expiry,

- and reconciliation state.

27.262 Async Submission

Provider acceptance SHALL update the Attempt to accepted or queued, not succeeded.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.263 Async State Mapping

Provider-native states SHALL map into canonical job states.

27.264 Stage 1 Async States

They SHOULD include:

- prepared,

- submitting,

- accepted,

- queued,

- running,

- partial,

- succeeded pending ingestion,

- failed,

- cancellation requested,

- cancelled,

- expired,

- unknown,

- reconciliation required,

- and closed.

27.265 Polling Worker

Stage 1 SHALL implement durable polling for Providers that require it.

27.266 Polling Backoff

Polling SHALL use:

- Provider guidance,

- bounded backoff,

- jitter,

- quota awareness,

- and stop conditions.

27.267 Polling Termination

Polling SHALL stop when:

- terminal state is verified,

- maximum duration is exceeded,

- job expires,

- cancellation is confirmed,

- or escalation is required.

27.268 Callback and Polling

Callbacks and polling MAY coexist.

Duplicate Completion detection SHALL be idempotent.

27.269 Webhook Ingress

Stage 1 SHALL implement a generic governed webhook ingress path.

27.270 Webhook Verification

Signature or equivalent authenticity verification SHALL occur before trusted processing.

27.271 Raw Body Preservation

Where signature schemes require exact bytes, raw request body SHALL be preserved transiently for verification.

27.272 Webhook Durable Intake

After verification and basic validation, the webhook SHALL be durably recorded before downstream processing.

27.273 Webhook Fast Response

Webhook handlers SHOULD acknowledge quickly after durable intake.

27.274 Webhook Business Logic

Substantial workflow logic SHALL occur asynchronously, not directly in the ingress request.

27.275 Webhook Event

Every accepted webhook SHALL map to a canonical Event or Provider event record.

27.276 Webhook Deduplication

Duplicate delivery SHALL be expected.

27.277 Event ID

Provider event ID SHALL be preserved where available.

27.278 Missing Provider Event ID

When no stable event ID exists, a bounded deduplication strategy MAY use:

- job ID,

- event type,

- timestamp window,

- and payload hash.

27.279 Webhook Replay Protection

Timestamp and signature replay protections SHALL be implemented where supported.

27.280 Unknown Event Type

Unknown event types SHALL be quarantined or recorded without side effects.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.281 Callback Before Submission Response

The implementation SHALL tolerate callback arrival before the original submitter has processed its response.

27.282 Result Retrieval

A success callback MAY trigger durable result retrieval and Asset ingestion.

27.283 Expiring Result URL

Temporary result URLs SHALL not be treated as durable Assets.

27.284 Asset Service

Stage 1 SHALL implement a canonical Asset Service.

27.285 Asset Responsibilities

The Asset Service SHALL manage:

- Asset identity,

- Versions,

- files,

- checksums,

- media metadata,

- Classification,

- provenance,

- rights,

- consent references,

- acceptance state,

- and retention.

27.286 Asset Store

Binary files SHOULD be stored in object or file storage.

Metadata SHOULD be stored in the relational database.

27.287 Asset Identity

The Asset is the logical object.

Asset Version represents immutable content state.

27.288 Asset Version Fields

An Asset Version SHOULD include:

- assetVersionId,

- Asset,

- media type,

- checksum,

- size,

- storage location,

- createdAt,

- creator,

- source Attempt,

- Classification,

- lifecycle,

- and provenance.

27.289 Asset Checksum

Every durable file SHALL receive a checksum.

27.290 Asset Ingestion

Provider Outputs SHALL be ingested before canonical success where the Provider result is temporary.

27.291 Asset Validation

Ingestion SHOULD validate:

- expected media type,

- size,

- checksum,

- corruption,

- and policy.

27.292 Asset Candidate State

Generated content SHALL initially enter Candidate state.

27.293 Asset Acceptance

Acceptance requires Quality and governance checks defined by the workflow.

27.294 Asset Rejection

Rejected Candidates MAY remain temporarily for evidence or comparison according to retention policy.

27.295 Asset Provenance

Every generated or transformed Asset SHALL link to:

- source Inputs,

- Plan,

- Execution,

- Step,

- Attempt,

- Provider,

- Model or Tool,

- Adapter,

- parameters,

- and evaluation.

27.296 Rights Metadata

Stage 1 SHALL store known:

- licence,

- commercial-use eligibility,

- attribution,

- Provider terms,

- and unresolved rights state.

27.297 Consent Metadata

Assets representing protected people or Voice identities SHALL link applicable Consent records.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.298 Provenance Service

Stage 1 SHALL distinguish different evidence classes.

27.299 Execution Record

Execution Record SHALL describe what was executed.

27.300 Asset Provenance

Asset Provenance SHALL describe how one Asset was created.

27.301 Evaluation Record

Evaluation Record SHALL describe Quality assessment.

27.302 Decision Evidence

Decision Evidence SHALL describe why a material Decision was made.

27.303 Derived Learning

Derived Learning SHALL capture reviewed generalisable findings.

27.304 Governed Memory

Governed Memory SHALL hold approved durable knowledge or preference.

27.305 No Raw Memory Dump

Raw prompts, intermediate chains, full logs and every Model Output SHALL NOT be admitted wholesale into permanent Memory.

27.306 Evidence Bundle

Every material Execution SHOULD produce an Evidence Bundle.

27.307 Evidence Bundle Fields

It SHOULD include or reference:

- Request,

- Plan Version,

- Routing Decision,

- Approval,

- Attempts,

- Provider native references,

- usage,

- Cost Records,

- Assets,

- evaluations,

- policy Decisions,

- and Completion Verification.

27.308 Evidence Storage

Structured Evidence SHALL be stored independently from ordinary logs.

27.309 Evidence Retention

Retention SHALL match governance and Project needs.

27.310 Evidence Privacy

Evidence SHALL minimise unnecessary raw protected content.

27.311 Quality Evaluation Service

Stage 1 SHALL implement a canonical evaluation boundary.

27.312 Quality Evaluation Types

It SHALL support at minimum:

- deterministic validation,

- rule-based evaluation,

- Model-based evaluation where appropriate,

- and human review.

27.313 Quality Floor

Every production Capability path SHALL define a Quality Floor or explicit acceptance criterion.

27.314 Deterministic Validation

Deterministic checks MAY include:

- schema,

- dimensions,

- file integrity,

- required fields,

- prohibited omissions,

- and exact constraints.

27.315 Model-Based Evaluation

Model evaluation SHALL record:

- evaluator Model,

- Provider,

- rubric,

- score,

- confidence,

- and limitations.

27.316 Human Evaluation

Human evaluation SHALL record Reviewer identity and result.

27.317 Candidate Comparison

Stage 1 MAY support several Candidates followed by ranking and human acceptance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.318 Mandatory Failure

One mandatory failure SHALL prevent acceptance regardless of average score.

27.319 Quality Result

Quality result SHOULD include:

- passed,

- failed,

- review required,

- and inconclusive.

27.320 Quality and Routing

Historical Quality evidence MAY influence Routing.

It SHALL not create unsupported permanent Provider preference without reviewed Derived Learning.

27.321 Manual QA

Before external publication, Stage 1 SHALL require human QA for generated creative media.

27.322 Text QA

Production-critical text MAY require human review depending on Project policy.

27.323 Memory Admission Boundary

Stage 1 SHALL implement a separate Memory admission interface.

27.324 Memory Proposal

The Fabric MAY propose a Memory Item after Execution.

It SHALL NOT write permanent Memory directly without admission evaluation.

27.325 Memory Admission Input

The Memory layer SHALL receive:

- proposed content,

- source Evidence,

- Project,

- Domain,

- Classification,

- confidence,

- validity,

- and purpose.

27.326 Memory Admission Decision

The Memory system SHALL decide:

- accept,

- reject,

- narrow,

- expire,

- challenge,

- or require review.

27.327 Derived Learning Requirement

Derived Learning SHALL include:

- supporting evidence,

- scope,

- confidence,

- validity,

- and replacement conditions.

27.328 Provider Learning Example

A finding that one Provider performs poorly on one image task MAY become Project-scoped Derived Learning after repeated evidence.

It SHALL not become universal truth automatically.

27.329 Planning Memory

The Planner MAY read approved routing or Project Memory through governed retrieval.

27.330 Memory Influence Evidence

Material Memory Items influencing a Plan SHOULD be recorded in Decision Evidence.

27.331 Observability

Stage 1 SHALL emit end-to-end correlation.

27.332 Trace Boundary

A Trace SHOULD span:

- Request,

- Planning,

- Routing,

- approval,

- queueing,

- Provider or Tool Attempt,

- evaluation,

- Asset ingestion,

- and Completion.

27.333 Structured Logs

Logs SHALL use structured fields.

27.334 Secret Redaction

Raw Credentials SHALL never enter ordinary logs.

27.335 Prompt Logging

Full prompts SHALL be disabled by default.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.336 Output Logging

Full Outputs SHALL be disabled by default.

27.337 Metrics

Stage 1 SHALL expose Metrics for:

- Request count,

- Execution count,

- Attempt count,

- latency,

- errors,

- queue depth,

- queue age,

- Provider health,

- retry count,

- unknown outcomes,

- cost,

- Quality,

- approval delay,

- and audit health.

27.338 Provider Metrics

Metrics SHALL distinguish:

- Provider,

- Product,

- Account,

- Model,

- and Capability.

27.339 Project Metrics

Project-level Metrics SHALL preserve Tenant isolation.

27.340 Local Node Metrics

Local Node telemetry SHALL include enough data for scheduling while minimising private device data.

27.341 Audit

Stage 1 SHALL create canonical Audit Events for consequential actions.

27.342 Mandatory Stage 1 Audit Events

They SHALL include:

- authentication-sensitive operations,

- Provider Connection creation,

- Credential mutation,

- Approval Decision,

- Mandate activation,

- paid execution,

- external Confidential transfer,

- publication,

- deletion,

- policy change,

- classification lowering,

- Incident action,

- and emergency stop.

27.343 Audit Store

The Audit Store SHALL be append-only or tamper-evident.

27.344 Audit Failure

If mandatory Audit storage is unavailable, high-risk actions SHOULD pause unless a durable fallback is available.

27.345 Incident Integration

Stage 1 SHALL implement Incident creation hooks.

27.346 Automatic Incident Candidates

The system SHOULD be capable of generating Incident candidates for:

- cross-Tenant access,

- Local Only egress,

- Secret leakage,

- unauthorised publication,

- Budget breach,

- audit outage,

- repeated unknown outcome,

- and major Provider failure.

27.347 Incident Command

Full autonomous Incident command is outside Stage 1.

Human-owned Incident handling SHALL remain primary.

27.348 Automated Containment

Stage 1 MAY automatically perform low-risk containment such as:

- disable a broken Connector,

- stop retry storm,

- freeze a queue,

- or block further publication.

High-impact containment SHALL remain approval-bound unless an emergency Mandate exists.

27.349 Developer Harness

Stage 1 SHALL ship with a developer Test Harness.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.350 Test Harness Default

The default Harness SHALL:

- use synthetic data,

- use mocks or local resources,

- disable public publication,

- disable production deletion,

- disable uncontrolled spend,

- and display active Project and Environment.

27.351 Integration Fixtures

Stage 1 SHALL include fixtures for:

- text Request,

- async image generation,

- Voice generation,

- Local Only text,

- Provider timeout,

- callback duplication,

- unknown outcome,

- wrong Project,

- expired approval,

- and Budget exhaustion.

27.352 Provider Simulators

Stage 1 SHOULD include simulators for:

- synchronous success,

- synchronous error,

- 202-style asynchronous job,

- callback,

- callback loss,

- duplicate callback,

- malformed response,

- rate limit,

- timeout,

- and unknown external outcome.

27.353 Live Provider Tests

Each production Provider Adapter SHALL have a bounded live contract test.

27.354 Live Test Cost

Live tests SHALL use an explicit test Budget.

27.355 Conformance Profiles

Stage 1 SHALL implement at minimum:

- Core Service Profile,

- Provider Adapter Profile,

- Connector Profile,

- Local Runtime Profile,

- MCP or Tool Profile,

- Human-Assisted Profile,

- Agent Profile,

- Workflow Profile,

- and Publication Profile.

27.356 Certification

Production-eligible Stage 1 components SHALL have current Conformance results.

27.357 Certification Simplicity

Stage 1 Certification MAY initially be an internal signed or database-backed record.

It does not require external certification infrastructure.

27.358 Stage 1 Primary Database

A relational database SHOULD act as the canonical transactional state store.

27.359 Database Candidate

PostgreSQL is an appropriate Stage 1 choice where available.

The canonical architecture SHALL remain database-product-independent.

27.360 Primary Database Domains

The database SHOULD contain structured records for:

- Requests,

- Plans,

- Executions,

- Attempts,

- Registries,

- Connections,

- policies,

- approvals,

- costs,

- Assets,

- Evidence,

- evaluations,

- events,

- audit,

- Incidents,

- and Conformance.

27.361 Database Migration

All schema changes SHALL be Versioned and migration-tested.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.362 Database Transaction

Transactional consistency SHOULD protect critical state transitions.

27.363 Optimistic Concurrency

Version columns or equivalent SHOULD protect concurrent mutation.

27.364 Event Outbox

The database SHOULD support an outbox table or equivalent for durable event emission.

27.365 Object Storage

Binary and large Asset content SHALL not be stored directly in ordinary relational rows unless justified.

27.366 Object Store Candidate

Stage 1 MAY use:

- local filesystem abstraction,

- S3-compatible storage,

- cloud object storage,

- or private object storage

behind one Asset storage interface.

27.367 Storage Location

Every Asset Version SHALL know its storage Location and custody boundary.

27.368 Signed Access

Temporary external access SHALL use short-lived scoped references where supported.

27.369 Storage Encryption

Confidential and Local Only storage SHALL use approved encryption appropriate to the Environment.

27.370 Queue Technology

Stage 1 MAY use:

- database-backed durable queue,

- Redis-compatible queue,

- managed queue,

- or dedicated broker.

The chosen implementation SHALL satisfy the canonical queue contract.

27.371 Simple Queue Preference

A database-backed queue MAY be preferable during initial Stage 1 if throughput requirements are moderate and transactional simplicity is valuable.

27.372 Queue Extraction

The queue interface SHALL permit migration to a dedicated broker later.

27.373 Cache

Stage 1 MAY use an in-memory or external cache.

The cache SHALL remain non-authoritative.

27.374 Cache Use

Caches MAY accelerate:

- Registry reads,

- policy reads,

- health state,

- and low-risk routing calculations.

27.375 Cache Exclusion

Approvals, revocations and high-risk authority decisions SHALL not depend on stale long-lived cache entries.

27.376 Search Store

Project retrieval MAY use a vector database or PostgreSQL vector extension during Stage 1.

27.377 Search Abstraction

The retrieval interface SHALL not expose vendor-specific vector database semantics to Agents.

27.378 Search Deletion

Deleted or revoked sources SHALL be removed from active retrieval.

27.379 Event Bus

A separate distributed event bus is OPTIONAL in Stage 1.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.380 Internal Events

Canonical Events MAY initially travel through:

- outbox,

- queue,

- or internal dispatcher.

27.381 Event Contract Preservation

Internal implementation choice SHALL not change Event schemas or semantics.

27.382 Stage 1 Service Boundaries

A practical initial deployment MAY contain the following modules:

- API Module,

- Registry Module,

- Policy Module,

- Planner Module,

- Routing Module,

- Cost Module,

- Approval Module,

- Execution Module,

- Adapter Module,

- Async Module,

- Asset Module,

- Evaluation Module,

- Evidence Module,

- Audit Module,

- and Conformance Module.

27.383 Worker Process

A separate Worker process SHOULD handle durable asynchronous Steps.

27.384 Webhook Process

Webhook ingress MAY run in the main application or a separate ingress process.

Security isolation SHOULD guide the decision.

27.385 Local Node Agent

Each local Node SHOULD run a minimal Omnira Runtime Agent or equivalent service.

27.386 Node Agent Responsibilities

It SHOULD:

- authenticate to Omnira,

- report health,

- advertise approved local resources,

- receive bounded jobs,

- resolve local Tool execution,

- stream progress,

- preserve local evidence,

- and stop on revocation.

27.387 Node Agent Non-Responsibilities

It SHALL NOT:

- decide Project policy,

- self-authorise external fallback,

- read unrelated files,

- or expose arbitrary device control.

27.388 Node Registration

New Node registration SHALL require user or administrator approval.

27.389 Node Trust

Node trust SHOULD include:

- identity,

- ownership,

- Environment,

- software Version,

- and last verification.

27.390 Node Heartbeat

Nodes SHOULD send bounded heartbeat and capacity state.

27.391 Offline Node

Missing heartbeat SHALL move the Node to unavailable or unknown after timeout.

27.392 Local Job Dispatch

Jobs sent to a Node SHALL include:

- Execution,

- Step,

- Capability,

- input references,

- authority,

- policy,

- and deadline.

27.393 Local Secret Access

Local jobs SHALL receive only Credentials required for the exact operation.

27.394 Local File Access

Input file references SHALL be resolved through approved Project paths or Asset storage.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 27.409 Provider Abstraction Does Not Mean Secrecy
text:
27.395 Device Permissions

Camera, microphone, location, screen and system actions remain outside general Stage 1 intelligence execution unless explicitly implemented as governed Tools.

27.396 Stage 1 Agent Integration

Atlas SHALL call the Fabric through the same canonical Request interface used by other Agents.

27.397 Agent SDK

A lightweight Agent SDK SHOULD simplify:

- Capability Request creation,

- status subscription,

- approval handling,

- result retrieval,

- and Evidence inspection.

27.398 Agent Request Context

The SDK SHALL automatically include:

- Agent identity,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- and correlation

from trusted Session context.

27.399 Agent Provider Opacity

The Agent SDK SHALL not require Provider names for normal capability-first requests.

27.400 Pinned Agent Request

A user MAY intentionally request Pinned execution.

The Agent MAY pass that preference without learning raw Credential detail.

27.401 Agent Streaming

Streaming text may be forwarded from the Fabric to the Agent or UI through canonical stream events.

27.402 Streaming Partial Output

Partial stream content SHALL not become final Output automatically.

27.403 Streaming Persistence

Stage 1 MAY persist:

- final Output,

- bounded stream metadata,

- and errors

without storing every token event permanently.

27.404 Stream Disconnect

Client disconnect SHALL not automatically cancel underlying execution.

27.405 Stream Cancellation

Explicit cancellation SHALL create a canonical cancellation request.

27.406 User Interface

Stage 1 SHOULD expose enough UI to make Fabric behaviour understandable.

27.407 Stage 1 UI Views

The UI SHOULD support:

- Request status,

- current Plan summary,

- selected routing profile,

- estimated cost,

- approval,

- execution progress,

- Provider class or resource class,

- result,

- actual cost,

- and Evidence summary.

27.408 Provider Transparency

Users SHOULD be able to inspect which Provider and Account class was ultimately used.

27.409 Provider Abstraction Does Not Mean Secrecy

Provider independence SHALL not hide meaningful data custody, cost or rights information from users.

27.410 Cost UI

The user SHOULD see estimated and actual cost.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.411 Local UI

The user SHOULD see when work requires a local Node and whether that Node is online.

27.412 Approval UI

The user SHALL see exact:

- Project,

- action,

- data transfer,

- Provider or resource,

- cost ceiling,

- retry scope,

- and side effects.

27.413 Evidence UI

A basic Evidence view SHOULD show:

- what executed,

- what resource was used,

- what Assets were produced,

- Quality result,

- cost,

- and any unresolved uncertainty.

27.414 Admin UI

A minimal administrative interface SHOULD support:

- Registry inspection,

- Connection management,

- Provider health,

- Model health,

- certification,

- and Incident status.

27.415 Stage 1 Security Architecture

Security SHALL be built into every boundary rather than added after Provider integration.

27.416 Network Egress

Server-side Provider calls SHOULD use an allowlist or controlled egress policy.

27.417 Endpoint Validation

Adapter endpoint configuration SHALL be validated.

27.418 Redirect Control

Redirects SHALL not bypass approved destination policy.

27.419 TLS

External production Provider communication SHALL use authenticated encrypted transport.

27.420 Webhook TLS

Webhook endpoints SHALL use secure transport.

27.421 SSRF Defence

User- or Provider-supplied URLs SHALL not be fetched blindly from privileged network context.

27.422 File Download

External result downloads SHALL enforce:

- size limits,

- content type,

- timeout,

- redirect policy,

- and scanning where appropriate.

27.423 Decompression

Compressed data SHALL have expansion limits.

27.424 Content-Type Validation

Declared content type SHALL not be trusted without validation where risk is material.

27.425 Injection Defence

External text, Tool results and MCP content SHALL remain data.

They SHALL not modify policy or authority.

27.426 Model Prompt Construction

System policy and external retrieved content SHALL remain structurally distinguishable.

27.427 Tool Output

Tool output SHALL not be executed recursively unless an explicit Plan requires it.

27.428 Secrets

No raw Secret SHALL be included in:

- prompts,

- Model context,

- ordinary logs,

- Evidence summaries,

- queue payloads,

- or Memory.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.429 Credential Rotation

Stage 1 SHALL support Credential rotation without changing Connection identity where possible.

27.430 Credential Revocation

Revocation SHALL make new Adapter resolution fail immediately.

27.431 Session Security

Administrative and approval Sessions SHALL have bounded lifetime.

27.432 Step-Up Authentication

High-risk actions SHOULD support stronger authentication.

27.433 Security Headers

User-facing web surfaces SHOULD implement appropriate modern browser security controls.

27.434 Dependency Security

Stage 1 builds SHALL include dependency and Secret scanning.

27.435 SBOM

Release artefacts SHOULD include an SBOM.

27.436 Stage 1 Privacy Architecture

Privacy decisions SHALL happen before Provider dispatch.

27.437 Provider Privacy Eligibility

Each Provider Product and Account SHALL declare supported maximum Classification or explicit policy profile.

27.438 Local Only Egress Guard

The Adapter dispatch layer SHALL include a final Local Only enforcement check.

27.439 Confidential External Transfer

Confidential external transfer SHALL require an eligible Provider Account and current policy Decision.

27.440 Purpose Binding

Every Provider dispatch SHALL reference the governing processing purpose.

27.441 Data Minimisation

The Planner and Adapter SHALL minimise data before external dispatch.

27.442 Context Trimming

Only relevant Memory and Asset fragments SHALL enter Model context.

27.443 Temporary Files

Temporary transformation and download files SHALL expire.

27.444 Provider File Retention

When Provider file storage exists, the Connector SHALL record retention and deletion capability.

27.445 Stage 1 Rights Architecture

Generated and source Assets SHALL preserve rights metadata sufficient to block uncertain commercial use.

27.446 Rights Unknown

Rights unknown SHALL not be interpreted as permitted commercial publication.

27.447 Provider Commercial Rights

Provider plan and Terms evidence SHALL be associated with relevant generated Assets.

27.448 Source Rights

Reference Assets SHALL preserve their own usage rights.

27.449 Consent Architecture

Consent SHALL be checked before processing protected:

- Voice,

- likeness,

- child data,

- or other subject-dependent Assets

where policy requires it.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.450 Stage 1 Reliability Architecture

The Stage 1 reliability model SHALL assume that:

- networks fail,

- Providers timeout,

- workers crash,

- callbacks duplicate,

- state becomes stale,

- and external side effects may become uncertain.

27.451 Retry Policy

Retry SHALL be centralised in canonical Reliability Policy.

27.452 Adapter Retry Prohibition

Adapters SHALL not perform uncontrolled hidden retry.

27.453 Retry Count

Every retryable Step SHALL define maximum count.

27.454 Retry Backoff

Backoff SHOULD include jitter for shared external services.

27.455 Unknown Outcome

Unknown external side-effect outcome SHALL become explicit state.

27.456 Reconciliation

Reconciliation SHALL run before a potentially duplicating retry.

27.457 Circuit Breaker

Stage 1 SHOULD support circuit-breaker behaviour for failing Provider paths.

27.458 Circuit Scope

Circuit state SHOULD be scoped to:

- Provider,

- Product,

- Account,

- Capability,

- and potentially region.

27.459 Bulkhead

One failing Provider or Project SHOULD not consume all Worker capacity.

27.460 Timeout Layers

Stage 1 SHALL distinguish:

- client timeout,

- service timeout,

- Provider request timeout,

- async job deadline,

- and workflow deadline.

27.461 Cancellation

Cancellation SHALL be best-effort and truthfully represented.

27.462 Cancellation Requested

Cancellation requested SHALL not equal cancelled.

27.463 Provider Unsupported Cancellation

Unsupported cancellation SHALL remain visible.

27.464 Worker Crash

Durable state SHALL allow another Worker to resume or reconcile.

27.465 Orphan Job Reconciler

Stage 1 SHALL periodically scan for:

- accepted jobs with no active poll,

- running Steps with expired leases,

- unknown jobs,

- and incomplete Asset ingestion.

27.466 Reconciler

The Reconciler SHOULD be a first-class background service or Worker function.

27.467 Reconciliation Evidence

Every reconciliation action SHALL remain attributable.

27.468 Stage 1 Quality Architecture

Quality SHALL be part of execution Completion, not an optional downstream report.

27.469 Quality Evaluation Timing

Evaluation MAY occur:

- during generation,

- after result retrieval,

- before Asset acceptance,

- and before publication.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.470 Quality Retry

A quality retry SHALL create a new Candidate and new Attempt.

27.471 Quality Retry Budget

Quality retries SHALL consume approved Budget.

27.472 Human Review Queue

Stage 1 SHOULD support a simple human-review queue.

27.473 Review Assignment

A review item SHALL identify:

- Project,

- Asset,

- rubric,

- required Decision,

- and deadline.

27.474 Review Completion

Review result SHALL be durable.

27.475 Stage 1 Publication Boundary

Publication SHALL remain a separate Connector class from generation.

27.476 Publication Connector

A publication Connector SHALL require:

- exact Account,

- exact Asset or Package Version,

- approval,

- rights,

- consent,

- and idempotency.

27.477 Publication Stage 1 Default

Automatic public publishing SHALL remain disabled by default.

27.478 Approval Before Publish

Human approval SHALL occur immediately before or as part of the bounded publication operation.

27.479 External Verification

The Connector SHALL verify:

- external ID,

- Account,

- visibility,

- and content

where practical.

27.480 Publication Unknown Outcome

Timeout after submission SHALL trigger reconciliation rather than blind retry.

27.481 Stage 1 Project Examples

The architecture SHALL be validated with real representative Project scenarios.

27.482 Familje-Stunden Scenario

A Stage 1 Familje-Stunden workflow SHOULD demonstrate:

- Project-scoped request,

- image generation,

- Voice generation,

- child-safe policy,

- Asset ingestion,

- human QA,

- cost visibility,

- and no automatic publication.

27.483 Familje-Stunden Image References

Nova and Pling reference Assets SHALL remain Project-scoped and included through canonical Asset references.

27.484 Familje-Stunden Voice

Narration SHALL use approved Voice Profiles and Consent evidence.

27.485 Familje-Stunden Human Review

Creative media SHALL require human acceptance.

27.486 The Prompt Scenario

A Stage 1 The Prompt workflow SHOULD demonstrate:

- research or retrieval,

- text reasoning,

- source provenance,

- Script generation,

- image generation,

- human QA,

- and publication approval boundary.

27.487 The Prompt Source Evidence

Material research outputs SHALL preserve source references.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.488 The Prompt Publication

Publication MAY initially remain manual or approval-gated.

27.489 GainPilot Scenario

A Stage 1 GainPilot workflow SHOULD demonstrate:

- Local Only or Confidential training context,

- Project Memory retrieval,

- local or approved external reasoning,

- Agent identity persistence,

- and no cross-Project retrieval.

27.490 GainPilot Local Execution

A Local Only health-related Request SHALL demonstrate local Model routing.

27.491 Atlas Scenario

Atlas SHALL demonstrate that it can request the same Capability without naming a Provider.

27.492 Atlas Provider Swap

Two eligible external text Providers SHALL be swappable without Atlas code changes.

27.493 Atlas Local Fallback

Where policy permits, Atlas MAY route from external to local or local to external according to the selected Routing Profile.

Local Only rules remain mandatory.

27.494 Stage 1 Repository Architecture

The codebase SHOULD group Fabric implementation by canonical domain rather than Provider.

27.495 Preferred High-Level Structure

A practical repository structure MAY contain conceptual areas equivalent to:

- fabric/api,

- fabric/domain,

- fabric/registry,

- fabric/policy,

- fabric/planning,

- fabric/routing,

- fabric/cost,

- fabric/approval,

- fabric/execution,

- fabric/adapters,

- fabric/connectors,

- fabric/runtime,

- fabric/assets,

- fabric/evaluation,

- fabric/evidence,

- fabric/observability,

- fabric/audit,

- fabric/incidents,

- fabric/conformance,

- and fabric/tests.

27.496 Provider Directory

Provider-specific code SHOULD exist only beneath Adapter or Connector boundaries.

27.497 Domain Import Rule

Core domain modules SHALL not import Provider SDK packages directly.

27.498 Adapter Import Rule

Provider SDKs MAY be imported by Provider-specific Adapter implementations.

27.499 Secret Import Rule

Only approved execution-boundary modules SHALL access Secret resolution APIs.

27.500 UI Import Rule

UI layers SHALL not import Provider SDKs or raw Secret interfaces.

27.501 Schema Location

Canonical schemas SHOULD have one stable package or directory.

27.502 Generated Types

Language types SHOULD derive from the canonical schema package where practical.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.503 Architecture Tests

Stage 1 SHOULD include automated dependency-boundary tests.

27.504 Boundary Test Example

A test SHALL fail if Atlas imports a Provider-specific SDK directly.

27.505 Boundary Test Example Two

A test SHALL fail if a domain object includes a raw API key field.

27.506 Boundary Test Example Three

A test SHALL fail if publication code accepts an Asset without Approval reference.

27.507 Configuration Architecture

Stage 1 configuration SHALL separate:

- code,

- Environment configuration,

- Project policy,

- Provider configuration,

- and Secrets.

27.508 Environment Configuration

Environment configuration MAY define:

- database,

- queue,

- object storage,

- observability,

- and enabled Adapter modules.

27.509 Project Configuration

Project configuration MAY define:

- default Routing Profile,

- Budget,

- allowed Providers,

- Local Only preferences,

- Quality Floors,

- and publication policy.

27.510 Provider Configuration

Provider configuration MAY define:

- endpoint,

- region,

- Product feature flags,

- and Account mapping.

27.511 Secret Configuration

Secrets SHALL not be stored in ordinary configuration files.

27.512 Configuration Versioning

Material configuration changes SHALL be attributable and Versioned.

27.513 Feature Flags

Feature flags MAY control experimental Stage 1 components.

27.514 Feature Flag Safety

Experimental Provider paths SHALL be disabled by default for production Projects.

27.515 Stage 1 Boot Sequence

At startup, the Fabric SHOULD:

1. load canonical configuration.

2. establish database connectivity.

3. establish queue connectivity.

4. establish Asset storage.

5. load policy Versions.

6. load Registry state.

7. register enabled Adapter implementations.

8. verify migrations.

9. start observability.

10. start Workers and reconciliation.

11. expose readiness only after mandatory dependencies are healthy.

27.516 Readiness

The Fabric SHALL distinguish readiness from liveness.

27.517 Partial Readiness

A Provider outage SHALL not necessarily make the entire Fabric unavailable.

Capability-level health SHALL be represented.

27.518 Readiness Dependency

Database or authority-store failure MAY make consequential execution unavailable even if the process is live.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.519 Stage 1 Startup Migration

Database migrations SHALL run through an explicit controlled process rather than hidden application mutation where production risk exists.

27.520 Shutdown

Graceful shutdown SHOULD:

- stop admission,

- finish or release active leases,

- persist state,

- close streams,

- and stop Workers safely.

27.521 Crash Safety

A hard process crash SHALL not lose canonical Execution or external job identity.

27.522 Deployment Environment

Stage 1 SHOULD support:

- local development,

- integration,

- staging,

- and production.

27.523 Production Stage 1

Production SHALL initially serve a small controlled set of Projects and Agents.

27.524 Single-User First

Stage 1 MAY begin with one primary user while preserving Tenant and Project identity structurally.

27.525 Multi-Tenant Readiness

Schemas and authorization SHALL avoid assumptions that only one user or Tenant will ever exist.

27.526 Project Isolation From Day One

Even single-user Stage 1 SHALL enforce Project boundaries.

27.527 Stage 1 Infrastructure as Code

Infrastructure configuration SHOULD be Version-controlled where practical.

27.528 Infrastructure Secrets

Secrets SHALL remain external to source control.

27.529 Stage 1 Backups

The primary database and canonical Asset store SHALL have verified backup procedures.

27.530 Backup Verification

Backups SHALL be tested through restoration.

27.531 Backup Scope

Backup SHALL preserve:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- encryption,

- audit,

- and deletion state.

27.532 Recovery Documentation

Stage 1 SHALL include recovery Runbooks.

27.533 Disaster Scenario

At least one disaster-recovery exercise SHOULD prove restoration of:

- database,

- Asset metadata,

- Evidence,

- and active configuration.

27.534 Stage 1 CI

Continuous Integration SHALL run:

- lint,

- static checks,

- unit tests,

- schema validation,

- contract tests,

- privacy tests,

- isolation tests,

- and relevant conformance tests.

27.535 Stage 1 Integration CI

A controlled integration pipeline SHOULD run:

- database,

- queue,

- object storage,

- Worker,

- and mock Provider tests.

27.536 Live Provider CI

Paid live Provider tests SHOULD not run on every ordinary commit.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.537 Scheduled Live Tests

Live contract tests MAY run:

- manually before release,

- on a schedule,

- or when Provider drift is suspected.

27.538 Live Test Safety

Live tests SHALL use dedicated Accounts or tightly bounded production-compatible test scopes.

27.539 Release Candidate

Every Stage 1 release SHALL bind to:

- source commit,

- Build Record,

- schemas,

- migrations,

- Test Runs,

- conformance,

- and known exceptions.

27.540 Deployment Gate

Production promotion SHALL require:

- passing mandatory tests,

- migration verification,

- security checks,

- privacy checks,

- and operator approval according to risk.

27.541 Rollback

Stage 1 deployment SHALL have a rollback or rollforward Plan.

27.542 Database Compatibility

Deployments SHOULD preserve at least temporary compatibility during migration where rollback depends on it.

27.543 Observability Before Traffic

New components SHALL emit enough telemetry before they receive production work.

27.544 Stage 1 Performance Target

Performance targets SHALL be defined per Capability rather than one universal number.

27.545 Interactive Text

Interactive text SHOULD prioritise:

- low admission delay,

- streaming,

- and responsive cancellation.

27.546 Image Generation

Image generation MAY tolerate longer async completion while preserving progress state.

27.547 Voice Generation

Voice generation SHOULD expose:

- queue,

- Provider processing,

- ingestion,

- and evaluation latency.

27.548 Local Model Cold Start

Local Model load time SHALL be observable separately from inference time.

27.549 Stage 1 Capacity

Capacity SHALL initially favour bounded queues over aggressive horizontal scaling.

27.550 Overload

When resources are saturated, the Fabric SHALL:

- queue,

- defer,

- reject,

- or request alternative route

rather than silently degrading policy.

27.551 Stage 1 Failure Philosophy

Every failure SHALL preserve enough state to answer:

- what was attempted,

- what may have happened externally,

- what it cost,

- whether retry is safe,

- and what the user should do next.

27.552 User-Facing Failure

User-facing failure messages SHALL distinguish:

- validation,

- approval required,

- unavailable resource,

- Budget,

- timeout,

- unknown outcome,

- Quality failure,

- and policy denial.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
sectionTitles: 27.566 Stage 1 Migration of Existing Agent Calls
text:
27.553 Internal Error Detail

Sensitive internal errors SHALL remain available to authorised operators without exposing them to ordinary users.

27.554 Stage 1 Manual Override

Manual operator actions SHALL still pass through authority and audit.

27.555 Manual Database Edit

Direct production database edits SHOULD be prohibited except through exceptional recovery procedure.

27.556 Manual Provider Dashboard

Manual Provider actions SHALL be represented through Human-Assisted or Incident procedures when they materially affect canonical state.

27.557 Drift Reconciliation

If external state changes manually, the Fabric SHALL reconcile rather than silently overwrite canonical truth.

27.558 Stage 1 Metrics of Success

Stage 1 SHOULD measure:

- percentage of Requests using canonical Fabric path,

- Provider independence,

- local execution usage,

- free-first savings,

- approval latency,

- routing success,

- cost-estimate accuracy,

- quality acceptance,

- retry rate,

- unknown outcome rate,

- Asset provenance completeness,

- and policy-denial correctness.

27.559 Fabric Adoption Metric

The percentage of Agent intelligence calls bypassing the Fabric SHOULD trend toward zero.

27.560 Direct Provider Call Detection

Architecture tests and code search SHOULD detect direct Provider calls outside approved Adapter modules.

27.561 Credential Exposure Metric

Raw Credential exposure incidents SHALL remain zero.

27.562 Cross-Project Leak Target

Cross-Project retrieval or execution leakage target SHALL be zero.

27.563 Local Only Egress Target

Local Only external egress target SHALL be zero.

27.564 Publication Without Approval Target

Unauthorised publication target SHALL be zero.

27.565 Evidence Completeness Target

Every production Execution SHOULD link to a complete Evidence Bundle.

27.566 Stage 1 Migration of Existing Agent Calls

Existing direct Agent-to-Provider calls SHALL be inventoried.

27.567 Migration Inventory

The inventory SHOULD identify:

- caller,

- Capability,

- Provider,

- SDK,

- Credential location,

- data type,

- cost,

- side effects,

- and migration priority.

27.568 Migration Priority

Highest-priority migrations SHOULD include:

- Atlas core reasoning calls,

- high-cost media generation,

- sensitive-data calls,

- and workflows with publication or external side effects.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.569 Compatibility Wrapper

Temporary compatibility wrappers MAY translate existing Agent calls into Capability Requests.

27.570 Wrapper Limitation

Compatibility wrappers SHALL not become permanent Provider-specific backdoors.

27.571 Provider Migration

Existing Provider Credentials SHALL be moved into canonical Connection and Secret management.

27.572 Credential Migration

Credential values SHALL not be copied into new configuration files.

27.573 Existing Asset Migration

Existing generated Assets MAY be registered gradually.

New Stage 1 Assets SHALL always use canonical provenance from launch.

27.574 Existing Memory Migration

Existing Memory SHALL not be bulk-reclassified as Derived Learning automatically.

27.575 Legacy Evidence

Legacy execution history MAY be marked:

- imported,

- incomplete,

- or unverifiable

rather than fabricated into canonical completeness.

27.576 Stage 1 Migration Gate

A workflow SHALL not be considered migrated until:

- direct Provider dependency is removed,

- canonical Request is used,

- Adapter path is used,

- Credentials are governed,

- Cost is recorded,

- Evidence is created,

- and policy is enforced.

27.577 Stage 1 Non-Goals

Stage 1 SHALL NOT require:

- full autonomous company management,

- unrestricted Agent delegation,

- universal Provider support,

- every image and video tool,

- every local Model Runtime,

- globally distributed infrastructure,

- zero human review,

- or fully automatic purchasing.

27.578 No Universal Model Router

Stage 1 routing SHALL focus on registered and certified resources only.

27.579 No Provider Marketplace

Automatic discovery and execution against arbitrary third-party Providers SHALL remain outside Stage 1.

27.580 No Automatic Key Import

The Fabric SHALL not scan devices for arbitrary API keys.

27.581 No Unbounded MCP

Unapproved MCP servers SHALL not be dynamically exposed to Agents.

27.582 No Autonomous Browser Root Access

Browser automation SHALL not receive unrestricted personal browser profiles.

27.583 No Private Message General Access

Private communication remains excluded unless one bounded workflow explicitly authorises it.

27.584 No Automatic Publication

Generated Assets SHALL not be published without policy and approval.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.585 No Automatic Authority Promotion

Successful history SHALL not automatically increase Agent Authority Level.

27.586 No Automatic Permanent Learning

Operational outcomes SHALL not automatically become global Memory.

27.587 No Autonomous Provider Purchasing

Provider subscription or credit purchases remain human-approved.

27.588 No Complex Distributed Saga Platform

Stage 1 MAY implement bounded compensation and recovery without building a universal distributed saga engine.

27.589 No Event Sourcing Requirement

Selective immutable Event history MAY be used.

Full platform event sourcing is not mandatory.

27.590 No Premature CQRS Requirement

Read and write models MAY remain combined until scale or complexity justifies separation.

27.591 No Custom Orchestrator DSL Requirement

Execution Plans MAY use typed data structures rather than a new programming language.

27.592 No General Workflow Marketplace

Stage 1 workflows SHALL remain governed Omnira workflows.

27.593 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario One

A text Request from Atlas SHALL:

1. enter through Fabric API.

2. carry Project context.

3. resolve text Capability.

4. evaluate two external Providers and one local option.

5. apply Routing Profile.

6. estimate cost.

7. obtain approval when required.

8. execute through one Adapter.

9. validate Output.

10. record cost and Evidence.

11. return canonical text result.

12. preserve Provider opacity to Atlas.

27.594 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Two

A Local Only reasoning Request SHALL:

1. classify Input as Local Only.

2. exclude every ordinary external Provider.

3. identify eligible local Nodes.

4. wait if the Node is offline.

5. execute locally when available.

6. preserve local evidence.

7. return canonical Output.

8. produce zero external data egress.

27.595 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Three

An async image generation Request SHALL:

1. create Plan.

2. obtain bounded Budget approval.

3. select eligible image Provider.

4. submit async job.

5. persist External Job Handle.

6. receive callback or poll.

7. handle duplicates idempotently.

8. retrieve Asset before URL expiry.

9. checksum and store Asset.

10. evaluate Quality.

11. require human QA.

12. reconcile actual cost.

13. return Candidate or Accepted Asset.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.596 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Four

A Voice generation Request SHALL:

1. resolve approved Voice Profile.

2. validate Consent.

3. estimate character cost.

4. select ElevenLabs Connection.

5. execute through Adapter.

6. ingest audio.

7. preserve Voice provenance.

8. record usage.

9. require appropriate human review.

10. block cross-Project Voice reuse.

27.597 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Five

An OpenArt human-assisted job SHALL:

1. create canonical Step.

2. determine automation unavailable or unsuitable.

3. route to Human-Assisted Connector.

4. present exact Project instructions.

5. expose bounded credits or Budget.

6. record human operator.

7. ingest resulting Asset.

8. preserve manual evidence.

9. evaluate Quality.

10. never label the work as API automation.

27.598 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Six

An MCP Tool Request SHALL:

1. use approved MCP server.

2. load approved discovery snapshot.

3. expose only authorised Tool.

4. validate Tool Input.

5. enforce Project scope.

6. invoke server.

7. treat returned content as untrusted.

8. validate Output.

9. record Tool evidence.

10. prevent Tool output from changing policy.

27.599 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Seven

A Provider timeout after consequential submission SHALL:

1. move Attempt to unknown.

2. block blind retry.

3. schedule reconciliation.

4. inspect Provider or external state.

5. resolve succeeded, failed or still unknown.

6. charge actual cost if incurred.

7. preserve the uncertainty period in Evidence.

27.600 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Eight

A duplicate webhook SHALL:

1. verify signature.

2. preserve delivery identity.

3. deduplicate processing.

4. acknowledge safely.

5. avoid duplicate Asset ingestion.

6. avoid duplicate cost entry.

7. preserve duplicate-delivery telemetry.

27.601 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Nine

A stale Approval Token SHALL:

1. fail validation after Plan change.

2. prevent execution.

3. create an auditable denial.

4. request new approval.

5. preserve the old Decision historically.

27.602 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Ten

A cross-Project retrieval attempt SHALL:

1. carry requesting Project identity.

2. apply access filter before ranking.

3. exclude another Project’s embeddings.

4. return no protected snippet.

5. record the denial.

6. raise Incident if structural isolation failed.

27.603 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Eleven

A Budget overrun forecast SHALL:

1. update estimated remaining cost.

2. compare with approved ceiling.

3. pause before new paid Attempt.

4. provide alternatives.

5. request higher Budget only if needed.

6. never exceed the bound knowingly.

27.604 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Twelve

A Provider becomes unhealthy SHALL:

1. update health.

2. remove or penalise resource.

3. re-evaluate fallback.

4. preserve Classification.

5. preserve Quality Floor.

6. preserve Budget.

7. escalate if no eligible route remains.

27.605 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Thirteen

A Model alias changes SHALL:

1. detect changed native Model identity where possible.

2. mark drift.

3. suspend high-risk certification when required.

4. run evaluation.

5. update Model Registry.

6. require reapproval where policy requires it.

27.606 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Fourteen

A Credential is revoked SHALL:

1. mark Credential unavailable.

2. invalidate Connector health.

3. prevent future dispatch.

4. stop queued operations requiring it.

5. preserve historical Attempts.

6. allow rotation without exposing raw Secret.

27.607 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Fifteen

Audit storage fails SHALL:

1. detect the outage.

2. mark audit health unavailable.

3. pause high-risk actions.

4. continue only safe operations permitted by policy.

5. restore durable audit path.

6. reconcile buffered records where supported.

27.608 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Sixteen

A local Node crashes mid-generation SHALL:

1. detect lost heartbeat.

2. expire job lease.

3. mark Attempt unknown or failed according to state.

4. preserve local evidence already received.

5. avoid external fallback for Local Only data.

6. permit local retry after recovery if safe.

27.609 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Seventeen

A generated Asset fails Quality SHALL:

1. preserve Provider Attempt as successful.

2. preserve Candidate Asset.

3. mark evaluation failed.

4. prevent Asset acceptance.

5. allow quality retry inside Budget.

6. require human review when retry limits are reached.

27.610 Stage 1 Acceptance Scenario Eighteen

A publication workflow SHALL:

1. use exact Accepted Asset Version.

2. verify rights.

3. verify Consent.

4. verify Classification permits publication.

5. verify target Account.

6. consume Approval Token.

7. submit through publication Connector.

8. reconcile timeout safely.

9. verify external result.

10. record publication Evidence.

3. identity, Tenant and Project context.

- schemas,

- domain types,

- IDs,

- Versions,

- database,

- migrations,

- Project context,

- and architectural dependency rules.

- Capability Registry,

- Model Registry,

- Provider Registry,

- Account Registry,

- Connection Registry,

- Tool Registry,

- Node Registry,

- and Secret References.

- Policy,

- Classification,

- Planner,

- Routing,

- Cost,

- Budget,

- and Approval.

27.648 Phase C Exit

Phase D SHALL create:

- Execution Orchestrator,

- Attempts,

- Workers,

- queues,

- leases,

- retries,

- reconciliation,

- and Adapter interface.

Phases MAY overlap where dependencies allow.

Canonical boundary order SHALL not be violated.

Production Provider execution SHALL not be enabled before:

- Cost,

- and authority

are enforceable.

27.662 Permanent Memory Before Admission Prohibition

- cost,

- backups,

- recovery,

- audit,

- Incidents,
