Authority:

- Approval Requests work,

- Approval Decisions work,

- Approval Tokens work,

- revocation works,

- bounded job approval works.

Execution:

- Execution Orchestrator works,

- Attempts work,

- queue works,

- Worker works,

- leases work,

- retries work,

- unknown outcomes work,

- reconciliation works.

Integrations:

- external text Provider A works,

- external text Provider B works,

- one local Runtime works,

- one automated image Provider works,

- ElevenLabs Voice works or has an approved replacement,

- OpenArt human-assisted path works or has an approved replacement,

- constrained MCP works.

Assets:

- Asset Service works,

- checksum works,

- durable ingestion works,

- provenance works,

- Candidate and Accepted states work.

Quality:

- deterministic validation works,

- Evaluation Records work,

- human QA works,

- Quality retries work.

Memory:

- Memory Proposal works,

- admission works,

- rejection works,

- deletion works,

- Derived Learning remains evidence-linked.

Operations:

- correlation works,

- Metrics work,

- logs work,

- traces work,

- audit works,

- audit health monitoring works,

- Incident hooks work.

Developer assurance:

- mock suite works,

- live Provider contract tests work,

- conformance Profiles exist,

- Certifications exist,

- migration tests pass,

- backup restore is verified,

- release Gates work.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
27.810 Closing Statement

Stage 1 is where the Omnira Intelligence Fabric stops being architecture alone and becomes the governed execution foundation of the platform.

The Capability Request gives Agents a Provider-independent way to ask for intelligence.

The Intent Envelope gives the Fabric enough context to understand purpose, scope, privacy, Quality, Budget and constraints.

The Registries describe what intelligence resources exist.

The Policy Engine determines what is allowed.

The Planner determines what work must occur.

The Cost Engine determines what that work may cost.

The Router determines which eligible resources should perform it.

The Approval Control Plane determines whether consequential execution may proceed.

The Execution Orchestrator turns the approved Plan into durable work.

The Queue and Worker layer make long-running and failure-prone operations recoverable.

The Adapter layer translates canonical intelligence into Provider-native operations.

The Connector layer binds those Adapters to exact Accounts, Credentials, Environments and Projects.

The Async Job Manager preserves external work beyond one process or network connection.

The Webhook and Polling paths reconcile distributed Provider state.

The Local Runtime Manager gives local Models first-class status without making them governance exceptions.

The MCP client makes Tool ecosystems available without allowing protocol discovery to become authority.

The Asset Service turns temporary external results into durable Omnira objects.

The Quality Service determines whether those outputs are actually usable.

The Evidence Service preserves how each material result came into existence.

The Memory Admission Boundary ensures that execution history does not silently become permanent belief.

The Classification and Privacy controls determine where data may travel.

The Authority controls determine who may cause consequential actions.

The Observability layer makes the execution understandable.

The Audit layer makes it accountable.

The Incident layer makes failures containable and recoverable.

The Conformance layer proves that implementations match the architecture.

For Familje-Stunden, Stage 1 means that:

- Nova and Pling references may flow through governed multimodal production,

- Voice generation may use approved Profiles and Consent,

- child and family data may remain protected,

- generated images become traceable Assets,

- costs remain visible,

- and human review remains mandatory before public release.

For The Prompt, Stage 1 means that:

- research and reasoning may route among several intelligence resources,

- source evidence remains linked,

- text and image generation share one orchestration layer,

- Provider failures remain recoverable,

- and publication remains separately governed.

For GainPilot, Stage 1 means that:

- Arnold may request reasoning without owning a Provider integration,

- Local Only training and health context may remain on approved local Nodes,

- Project Memory cannot leak into another Project,

- Model changes do not change Arnold’s identity,

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
- and coaching intelligence may later expand without replacing the execution foundation.

For Atlas, Stage 1 means that:

- Atlas says what intelligence is needed,

- the Fabric decides how it should be implemented,

- Atlas no longer needs raw Model names or API keys,

- local and external resources can coexist,

- Provider changes do not rewrite Atlas,

- and every material execution becomes costed, governed, evidenced and recoverable.

For Omnira, Stage 1 creates the first complete operational loop:

Intent.

Capability.

Policy.

Plan.

Budget.

Route.

Approval.

Execution.

Evaluation.

Asset.

Evidence.

Learning.

Completion.

No Provider-specific intelligence above the Fabric boundary.

No raw Credential in Agent context.

No Route before eligibility.

No paid Attempt without Budget.

No consequential action without authority.

No async job without durable identity.

No retry without state awareness.

No Local Only data without local enforcement.

No generated Asset without provenance.

No accepted Asset without Quality.

No publication from generation alone.

No permanent learning without governed admission.

No production trust without conformance.

No operation without observability.

No consequence without audit.

No failure without a recovery path.

The user retains intent, Budget and authority.

The Project retains scope, data and policy.

Atlas retains intelligence orchestration without infrastructure coupling.

Omnira retains governance, identity and platform ownership.

The Fabric becomes the one place where capability, resource, cost, privacy, quality, authority and execution meet.

Stage 1 shall be considered complete only when Omnira can use intelligence from multiple external and local resources through that one governed architecture without needing to know which underlying implementation happens to serve the request.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.1 Chapter Status

This chapter defines the canonical rollout, migration, adoption, transition, deprecation, anti-pattern and future-evolution architecture for the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

It establishes:

- how the Fabric SHALL move from architecture into operational use,

- how existing direct Agent-to-Provider paths SHALL be inventoried,

- how legacy Provider integrations SHALL migrate behind the Fabric boundary,

- how Credentials SHALL migrate without unnecessary Secret exposure,

- how Provider Accounts and Connections SHALL be canonicalised,

- how existing Models, Tools, local Runtimes and MCP servers SHALL enter the Registries,

- how legacy workflows SHALL migrate without losing operational continuity,

- how Assets SHALL be imported without fabricated provenance,

- how historical execution data SHALL be represented when canonical evidence is incomplete,

- how existing Memory SHALL be preserved without pretending that it originated through the new governance model,

- how current Project behaviour SHALL remain stable while infrastructure changes underneath it,

- how Atlas and other Agents SHALL transition away from direct Provider knowledge,

- how compatibility wrappers SHALL remain temporary,

- how shadow mode, dual execution, canaries and phased routing SHALL reduce migration risk,

- how Stage 1 SHALL be introduced without requiring a complete platform rewrite,

- how migration SHALL remain reversible until verification is complete,

- how users and Project owners SHALL retain control throughout transition,

- how data, cost, privacy, rights, consent and authority SHALL remain enforced during migration,

- how observability SHALL determine rollout health,

- how rollback and rollforward SHALL operate,

- how drift between legacy and canonical systems SHALL be detected,

- how deprecated integration paths SHALL be retired,

- how direct Provider bypass SHALL be eliminated gradually but decisively,

- how rollout SHALL differ across Atlas, Familje-Stunden, The Prompt, GainPilot and future Projects,

- how anti-patterns SHALL be identified before they become permanent architecture,

- how emergency exceptions SHALL avoid becoming permanent technical debt,

- how later stages SHALL evolve from Stage 1 without invalidating canonical identities or contracts,

- how the Fabric MAY scale into distributed execution, richer multimodal orchestration, advanced local intelligence, continuous benchmarking and broader Agent autonomy,

- how future standards, Providers and protocols SHALL be absorbed through canonical interfaces,

- how architectural decisions SHALL be revisited without rewriting history,

- how deprecation SHALL remain visible and time-bounded,

- how future intelligence improvements SHALL remain subordinate to policy, privacy, authority and user intent,

- and how Omnira SHALL preserve the doctrine of No Intelligence Without Fabric as the platform evolves.

Migration is not a file move alone.

Rollout is not deployment alone.

A compatibility layer is not completion.

A legacy workflow that still requires a direct Provider SDK is not fully migrated.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
A Provider Connection copied into a new database is not canonicalisation unless scope, Account, Credential, policy and evidence are correct.

An imported Asset does not gain provenance that never existed.

An old Model interaction does not become canonical Execution Evidence retroactively.

A new routing layer does not justify breaking Project behaviour.

A successful canary does not prove universal readiness.

A shadow Decision does not create authority.

A dual-run Output does not automatically become production Output.

A rollback shall not restore revoked authority, deleted data or expired Consent.

A migration shall not resurrect obsolete Credentials.

A feature flag shall not become a permanent hidden fork.

A temporary Provider bypass shall not become a second architecture.

A future protocol shall not bypass canonical policy because it is fashionable.

A new Agent framework shall not become the owner of Agent identity.

A new Model router shall not become the owner of routing policy.

A new vector database shall not become the owner of Memory semantics.

A new orchestration engine shall not become the owner of Plan semantics.

A new multimodal Provider shall not become the owner of Asset identity.

A new local Runtime shall not become a privacy exception.

A stronger Model shall not receive broader authority automatically.

A cheaper Provider shall not lower Data Classification.

A faster workflow shall not remove provenance.

An autonomous workflow shall not remove user stop authority.

Future evolution SHALL extend the Fabric.

It SHALL NOT route around it.

This chapter is normative after formal approval.

It closes the canonical first edition of the Omnira Intelligence Fabric architecture.

Implementation sequencing, delivery planning and repository-specific execution SHALL be derived from this book without weakening its contracts.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.2 Purpose of Rollout and Migration

The Intelligence Fabric enters an existing Omnira ecosystem.

Existing systems may already contain:

- direct Model calls,

- Provider SDK integrations,

- manually stored API keys,

- Agent-specific Provider configuration,

- Project-specific scripts,

- local Model commands,

- browser-assisted workflows,

- manual creative workflows,

- publication routines,

- Asset folders,

- Memory records,

- scheduling logic,

- retry logic,

- cost assumptions,

- and external Accounts.

The migration architecture exists to move those systems into one governed Fabric without:

- interrupting valuable Project work unnecessarily,

- losing data,

- fabricating historical evidence,

- expanding access,

- changing user-visible behaviour accidentally,

- hiding cost,

- weakening privacy,

- or creating permanent compatibility debt.

28.3 Migration Objective

The primary migration objective is:

Every production intelligence operation SHALL eventually enter through a canonical Capability Request and execute through governed Fabric resources.

28.4 Migration Unit

The preferred migration unit is one coherent workflow or Capability path.

Examples include:

- Atlas text reasoning,

- The Prompt research,

- Familje-Stunden image generation,

- Familje-Stunden Voice narration,

- GainPilot coaching reasoning,

- local Model inference,

- publication,

- or MCP Tool invocation.

28.5 Migration Is Incremental

The Fabric SHALL support incremental migration.

A complete platform cutover in one event is not required.

28.6 Migration Is Governed

Every migration SHALL have:

- scope,

- owner,

- source state,

- target state,

- risks,

- data impact,

- authority impact,

- rollback,

- verification,

- and completion criteria.

28.7 Migration Plan

A Migration Plan is the canonical object describing transition from one implementation state to another.

It SHALL include or reference:

- migrationPlanId,

- objective,

- owner,

- source architecture,

- target architecture,

- affected Projects,

- affected Capabilities,

- affected Agents,

- affected Providers,

- affected Accounts,

- affected Credentials,

- data objects,

- dependencies,

- migration phases,

- verification,

- rollback,

- deadline,

- and state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.8 Migration Plan Identity

Every material Migration Plan SHALL have stable identity and Version.

28.9 Migration State

Canonical Migration Plan states MAY include:

- proposed,

- approved,

- inventorying,

- preparing,

- shadowing,

- canary,

- migrating,

- verifying,

- partially migrated,

- completed,

- paused,

- rolled back,

- failed,

- superseded,

- and archived.

28.10 Migration Owner

Every migration SHALL have one accountable owner.

28.11 Migration Scope

Scope SHALL identify exact:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- repository,

- service,

- Agent,

- Capability,

- Provider path,

- Account,

- data,

- and Environment.

28.12 Migration Boundary

Unrelated systems SHALL remain outside the migration unless explicitly included.

28.13 Migration Dependency

Dependencies SHALL be identified before cutover.

28.14 Migration Precondition

A migration SHALL not begin consequential cutover until required target controls exist.

28.15 Migration Postcondition

A migration is complete only when defined target invariants are verified.

28.16 Migration Evidence

Every material migration SHALL produce evidence of:

- source state,

- changes,

- target state,

- tests,

- data checks,

- policy checks,

- rollback readiness,

- and completion.

28.17 Migration Record

A Migration Record SHALL preserve actual transition history.

It SHALL remain distinct from the Migration Plan.

28.18 Migration Record Identity

Every material Migration Record SHALL have stable identity.

28.19 Source Architecture Inventory

Before migration, Omnira SHALL identify existing intelligence paths.

28.20 Inventory Scope

The inventory SHOULD capture:

- caller,

- Agent,

- Project,

- Capability,

- Provider,

- Product,

- Model,

- SDK,

- endpoint,

- Credential source,

- Account,

- Input data,

- Output type,

- cost,

- retry logic,

- fallback logic,

- side effects,

- Memory use,

- publication,

- and observability.

28.21 Direct Provider Call

A Direct Provider Call is any intelligence call that bypasses the Fabric’s canonical Adapter and Routing architecture.

28.22 Direct Provider Call Registry

During migration, known direct calls SHOULD be registered as migration debt.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.23 Migration Debt

Migration Debt is a known legacy path not yet fully governed by the Fabric.

28.24 Migration Debt Identity

Every material Migration Debt item SHOULD have stable identity.

28.25 Migration Debt Fields

It SHOULD include:

- debtId,

- source,

- Project,

- Capability,

- risk,

- owner,

- temporary controls,

- target migration,

- due date,

- and state.

28.26 Migration Debt State

States MAY include:

- identified,

- controlled,

- in migration,

- blocked,

- resolved,

- accepted temporarily,

- and expired.

28.27 Migration Debt Priority

Priority SHOULD increase with:

- sensitive data,

- high spend,

- broad authority,

- external side effects,

- publication,

- private Accounts,

- or unstable Provider dependencies.

28.28 High-Priority Legacy Paths

The first migrations SHOULD include:

- Atlas core reasoning,

- Project-sensitive reasoning,

- paid multimodal generation,

- publication paths,

- external message paths,

- and workflows with weak Credential handling.

28.29 Low-Priority Legacy Paths

Low-risk internal experiments MAY remain temporarily outside production migration scope when they are:

- clearly non-production,

- isolated,

- non-sensitive,

- non-consequential,

- and time-bounded.

28.30 Inventory Completeness

Unknown legacy integrations SHALL remain a migration risk.

28.31 Repository Search

Code search SHOULD identify:

- Provider SDK imports,

- direct HTTP endpoints,

- API key names,

- Model names,

- Tool subprocesses,

- MCP configuration,

- and publication SDKs.

28.32 Configuration Search

Configuration SHOULD be inspected for:

- Provider endpoints,

- Account IDs,

- Model aliases,

- embedded Credentials,

- and direct routing flags.

28.33 Runtime Observation

Observability SHOULD identify intelligence traffic not represented in the inventory.

28.34 Cost Observation

Provider billing MAY reveal hidden legacy call paths.

28.35 Network Observation

Controlled egress telemetry MAY reveal direct Provider access outside Adapters.

28.36 Migration Discovery Shall Be Non-Destructive

Discovery SHALL prefer read-only inspection.

28.37 No Secret Dump for Inventory

Credential discovery SHALL record location and reference.

It SHALL NOT dump Secret values into migration reports.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.38 Legacy Credential Inventory

Existing Credentials SHALL be classified by:

- Provider,

- Account,

- owner,

- Project use,

- Environment,

- storage location,

- scope,

- age,

- and status.

28.39 Unknown Credential Ownership

Credentials with uncertain owner or Project SHALL not become active Fabric Connections automatically.

28.40 Credential Canonicalisation

A legacy Credential is canonicalised only when:

- owner is identified,

- Account is identified,

- scope is defined,

- Secret is stored in approved storage,

- Connection is registered,

- and old exposure paths are retired.

28.41 Credential Rotation During Migration

High-risk legacy Credentials SHOULD be rotated when moved into the Fabric.

28.42 Credential Reuse

A Credential MAY remain the same Secret during low-risk migration if safe.

Its storage and access model SHALL still change.

28.43 Credential Exposure Review

If legacy code embedded Secrets in:

- source control,

- logs,

- documentation,

- chat,

- or scripts,

rotation SHALL be considered mandatory.

28.44 Credential History

Historical Secret values SHALL not be copied into canonical Evidence.

28.45 Legacy Provider Account Inventory

Existing Accounts SHALL be mapped to canonical Provider Account records.

28.46 Account Ownership Verification

Migration SHALL verify whether each Account is:

- personal,

- Project-owned,

- Tenant-owned,

- organisation-owned,

- or Omnira-managed.

28.47 Account Terms Review

Material Accounts SHOULD be reviewed for:

- billing,

- retention,

- training settings,

- commercial rights,

- region,

- and usage policy.

28.48 Account Scope Migration

One legacy Account used by several Projects SHALL not automatically become a shared unrestricted Connection.

28.49 Shared Account

A shared Account MAY remain shared if policy permits.

Each Project’s Connection and authority SHALL remain explicit.

28.50 Provider Registry Migration

Legacy Provider definitions SHALL be mapped into the Provider Registry.

28.51 Model Registry Migration

Known Models SHALL be registered with:

- native identifier,

- family,

- Provider,

- Capability evidence,

- and lifecycle state.

28.52 Unknown Model Version

Historical aliases whose exact underlying Version is unknown SHALL be recorded as unresolved historical identity.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.53 No Fabricated Model Version

Migration SHALL NOT invent immutable Model identity where evidence does not exist.

28.54 Tool Inventory

Legacy Tools SHALL be mapped by:

- Tool identity,

- command,

- schema,

- file scope,

- network scope,

- side effect,

- authority,

- and Project.

28.55 Unregistered Tool

A legacy Tool SHALL not become production-eligible until it passes Tool conformance.

28.56 Local Runtime Inventory

Existing local AI Runtimes SHALL be inventoried.

28.57 Local Runtime Properties

Inventory SHOULD capture:

- Node,

- Runtime,

- installed Models,

- hardware,

- network behaviour,

- storage,

- file permissions,

- and launch method.

28.58 Local Runtime Canonicalisation

Local execution becomes canonical when it uses:

- Node identity,

- Runtime identity,

- Model Registry,

- canonical Attempt,

- policy,

- and Evidence.

28.59 Legacy Shell Command

A direct shell call to a local Model MAY be wrapped temporarily.

It SHALL eventually migrate behind a local Runtime Adapter or Tool contract.

28.60 MCP Inventory

Existing MCP servers SHALL be inventoried by:

- server identity,

- transport,

- package,

- Version,

- Tools,

- Resources,

- Prompts,

- file access,

- network access,

- Credentials,

- and trust.

28.61 MCP Migration

A legacy MCP server SHALL not become Agent-accessible through the Fabric until:

- server identity is registered,

- discovery snapshot exists,

- schemas validate,

- Tools are classified,

- scope is approved,

- and conformance passes.

28.62 Agent Inventory

Agents SHALL be inventoried by:

- identity,

- Project,

- role,

- current Models,

- Providers,

- Tools,

- Memory,

- authority,

- and direct integrations.

28.63 Agent Identity Preservation

Migration SHALL preserve Agent identity even when all underlying Models or Providers change.

28.64 Agent Provider Decoupling

Direct Provider references SHALL move from Agent configuration into Fabric resource and routing policy.

28.65 Agent Capability Mapping

Legacy Agent functions SHOULD be mapped to canonical Capabilities.

28.66 Atlas Migration

Atlas SHALL migrate from direct intelligence implementation knowledge toward Capability Requests.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.67 Atlas Migration Principle

Atlas SHOULD retain:

- strategic role,

- context,

- intent,

- coordination,

- and user interaction

while losing:

- API key knowledge,

- endpoint knowledge,

- SDK coupling,

- and raw Provider routing logic.

28.68 Compatibility Adapter for Atlas

A temporary Atlas compatibility interface MAY translate existing calls into Capability Requests.

28.69 Atlas Compatibility Wrapper

The wrapper SHALL:

- preserve current call shape where necessary,

- create canonical Request,

- attach Project,

- attach classification,

- attach Budget,

- and return canonical result.

28.70 Atlas Compatibility Wrapper Expiry

The wrapper SHALL have an owner and retirement criterion.

28.71 No New Direct Atlas Integration

After Fabric migration begins, new Atlas Provider integrations SHALL be prohibited outside the Fabric.

28.72 Project Agent Migration

Project Agents SHALL migrate independently by Capability path.

28.73 Arnold Migration

Arnold SHOULD migrate reasoning, local intelligence and Tool use through the Fabric without changing Arnold’s canonical coaching identity.

28.74 Workflow Inventory

Legacy workflows SHALL be inventoried by:

- trigger,

- Steps,

- Provider calls,

- human Steps,

- retries,

- state,

- side effects,

- publication,

- and Completion.

28.75 Workflow Canonicalisation

A workflow becomes Fabric-governed when:

- it creates canonical Requests or Plans,

- every intelligence call uses registered resources,

- external side effects use Connectors,

- cost is recorded,

- authority is enforced,

- and Evidence exists.

28.76 Partial Workflow Migration

A workflow MAY be partially migrated.

The boundary between canonical and legacy Steps SHALL be explicit.

28.77 Legacy Step

A Legacy Step is a workflow Step still executed by pre-Fabric infrastructure.

28.78 Legacy Step Evidence

Legacy Steps SHALL be labelled as legacy and may have incomplete Evidence.

28.79 Legacy Step Risk

Legacy Steps with:

- payment,

- publication,

- deletion,

- sensitive data,

- or private Accounts

SHOULD be migrated early.

28.80 Legacy Workflow State

Migration SHALL preserve active workflow state where feasible.

28.81 In-Flight Workflow Cutover

In-flight work SHOULD generally finish on its original execution path unless:

- active risk requires migration,

- the Provider path is unsafe,

- or the state can be transferred without ambiguity.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.82 Mid-Execution Migration

Moving a live external job between orchestration systems SHALL require explicit reconciliation.

28.83 No Duplicate Execution During Cutover

Cutover SHALL prevent both legacy and Fabric systems from executing the same consequential Step independently.

28.84 Execution Ownership

Every in-flight Step SHALL have one canonical execution owner.

28.85 Ownership Transfer

If ownership transfers, the handoff SHALL preserve:

- current state,

- external IDs,

- idempotency,

- authority,

- and Evidence.

28.86 Shadow Mode

Shadow Mode allows the Fabric to compute:

- Plan,

- Routing Decision,

- cost estimate,

- policy result,

- or evaluation

without controlling production execution.

28.87 Shadow Purpose

Shadow Mode SHALL be used to compare new decisions with current behaviour safely.

28.88 Shadow No-Side-Effect

Shadow execution SHALL not create external side effects unless separately authorised as a test.

28.89 Shadow Routing

Shadow Routing MAY compare which Provider the Fabric would select against the legacy Provider choice.

28.90 Shadow Cost

Shadow Cost MAY compare predicted cost with actual legacy cost.

28.91 Shadow Policy

Shadow Policy MAY identify legacy operations that the new Fabric would block.

28.92 Shadow Authority

Shadow authority evaluation SHALL NOT create execution permission.

28.93 Shadow Evidence

Shadow results SHALL be labelled non-authoritative.

28.94 Shadow Success

Shadow agreement is useful evidence but is not required when the legacy system itself is unsafe or wrong.

28.95 Dual Run

Dual Run executes the same non-consequential workload through legacy and Fabric paths for comparison.

28.96 Dual Run Scope

Dual Run SHOULD use:

- read-only,

- synthetic,

- draft,

- or non-public work

unless duplicate side effects are impossible.

28.97 Dual Run Cost

Dual Run SHALL account for duplicate cost.

28.98 Dual Run Data

Both execution paths SHALL independently satisfy data eligibility.

28.99 Dual Run Result

Results MAY be compared for:

- Quality,

- latency,

- cost,

- correctness,

- and provenance.

28.100 Dual Run Publication Prohibition

Public publication SHALL NOT normally execute through both paths.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.101 Canary Migration

Canary Migration routes a small bounded subset of production traffic through the Fabric.

28.102 Canary Scope

Canary scope MAY be defined by:

- Project,

- user,

- Capability,

- request class,

- data class,

- Provider,

- percentage,

- or time window.

28.103 Canary Eligibility

High-risk data SHOULD not be the first canary unless the controls being validated specifically concern that risk and approval exists.

28.104 Canary Success Metrics

Canary evaluation SHOULD include:

- completion,

- latency,

- Quality,

- cost,

- retry,

- unknown outcome,

- policy denial,

- user correction,

- and Incident rate.

28.105 Canary Abort Threshold

Abort criteria SHALL be defined before rollout.

28.106 Canary Expansion

Canary scope MAY expand only after evidence supports it.

28.107 Percentage Rollout

Percentage-based rollout SHALL preserve deterministic assignment where comparison matters.

28.108 Project-Based Rollout

Project-based migration MAY be preferable when Projects have materially different policies.

28.109 Capability-Based Rollout

Capability-based migration MAY be preferable when one shared service provides the same Capability to several Projects.

28.110 Provider-Based Rollout

Provider-based migration MAY migrate one Adapter at a time.

28.111 Agent-Based Rollout

Agent-based migration MAY migrate Atlas before Arnold or vice versa according to risk and dependency.

28.112 Feature Flag Rollout

Feature flags MAY control Fabric adoption during migration.

28.113 Feature Flag Identity

Every migration-relevant feature flag SHALL have stable identity and owner.

28.114 Feature Flag Scope

Flags SHALL identify exact:

- Environment,

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Capability,

- and user group

where applicable.

28.115 Feature Flag Expiry

Migration flags SHALL have cleanup criteria.

28.116 Permanent Flag Prohibition

A migration flag SHALL not remain permanently because no one wants to remove legacy code.

28.117 Cutover

Cutover makes the Fabric path authoritative for a defined scope.

28.118 Cutover Preconditions

Before cutover:

- Fabric path passes conformance,

- observability is active,

- rollback is possible,

- source state is understood,

- data and authority are verified,

- and owners are informed.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.119 Cutover Window

A planned cutover MAY use a defined operational window.

28.120 Cutover Freeze

High-risk migrations MAY briefly freeze mutation to prevent conflicting state.

28.121 Cutover Verification

Immediately after cutover, the team SHALL verify:

- request flow,

- routing,

- Provider dispatch,

- result handling,

- cost,

- Evidence,

- and user-facing behaviour.

28.122 Post-Cutover Monitoring

Enhanced monitoring SHOULD remain active after cutover.

28.123 Rollback

Rollback restores the previous operational path when the new path is unsafe or materially defective.

28.124 Rollback Plan

Every high-risk migration SHALL define rollback before cutover.

28.125 Rollback Trigger

Triggers MAY include:

- critical Incident,

- unacceptable Quality,

- privacy failure,

- authority failure,

- cost anomaly,

- data corruption,

- or unresolved unknown outcomes.

28.126 Rollback Is Not Historical Rewind

Rollback restores service path.

It SHALL not erase events that already occurred.

28.127 External Side Effect Rollback

External actions MAY require compensation rather than technical rollback.

28.128 Rollback Authority

Rollback SHALL require appropriate operational authority.

28.129 Rollback Data

Rollback SHALL preserve current:

- deletion,

- Consent,

- rights,

- revocation,

- and authority.

28.130 Rollback Credential Safety

Old revoked Credentials SHALL NOT be reactivated merely because old code expected them.

28.131 Rollback Schema Compatibility

Database migrations SHALL account for rollback compatibility where needed.

28.132 Rollforward

Rollforward fixes the new architecture while remaining on the new path.

28.133 Rollforward Preference

When data transformation is irreversible, rollforward MAY be safer than rollback.

28.134 Rollback Evidence

Rollback SHALL be recorded and verified.

28.135 Rollout Verification

Rollout Verification establishes that the new Fabric path satisfies defined migration and operational criteria.

28.136 Verification Categories

Verification SHOULD include:

- functional,

- data,

- privacy,

- authority,

- cost,

- performance,

- Quality,

- Evidence,

- and user-facing behaviour.

28.137 Functional Verification

The migrated workflow SHALL still achieve its intended purpose.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
sectionTitles: 28.149 Migration Completion Does Not Require Deleting History
text:
28.138 Data Verification

Input, output and persisted state SHALL remain correct.

28.139 Privacy Verification

No new data flow SHALL violate Classification or purpose.

28.140 Authority Verification

No action SHALL receive broader authority through migration.

28.141 Cost Verification

Cost SHALL remain visible and within expected boundaries.

28.142 Quality Verification

Output Quality SHALL meet the existing or newly approved Quality Floor.

28.143 Evidence Verification

Canonical Evidence SHALL exist for new executions.

28.144 User Experience Verification

Users SHALL understand changed states, approvals and costs.

28.145 Legacy Behaviour Difference

Intentional behaviour changes SHALL be documented.

They SHALL not be hidden inside infrastructure migration.

28.146 Migration Regression

A migration regression is a previously working behaviour that becomes materially worse after migration.

28.147 Migration Regression Record

Material regressions SHALL create Regression Records and Tests.

28.148 Migration Completion

A migration scope is complete only when:

- target path is authoritative,

- required data is canonical,

- Credentials are governed,

- direct bypass is removed or disabled,

- observability works,

- Evidence works,

- tests pass,

- and rollback debt is resolved.

28.149 Migration Completion Does Not Require Deleting History

Legacy records MAY remain for historical reconstruction.

28.150 Legacy Path Retirement

After verified migration, the legacy execution path SHOULD be disabled.

28.151 Legacy Path Deletion

Code deletion MAY occur only after:

- verification,

- rollback decision,

- retention needs,

- and repository safeguards

are satisfied.

28.152 Deprecation

Deprecation marks a component or contract as scheduled for replacement or retirement.

28.153 Deprecation Record

A Deprecation Record SHALL include:

- deprecationId,

- subject,

- replacement,

- reason,

- announcedAt,

- migration guidance,

- deadline,

- owner,

- and state.

28.154 Deprecation Identity

Every material Deprecation Record SHALL have stable identity.

28.155 Deprecation States

States MAY include:

- announced,

- migrating,

- restricted,

- blocked for new use,

- retired,

- and archived.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.156 New Use After Deprecation

Deprecated components SHOULD be blocked from new adoption before existing use is removed.

28.157 Deprecation Deadline

Deadline SHALL be explicit and reviewable.

28.158 Deprecation Extension

Extension requires:

- reason,

- risk,

- owner,

- and new date.

28.159 Retirement

Retirement removes a subject from active eligibility.

28.160 Retired Provider

A retired Provider remains in historical Evidence but cannot receive new work.

28.161 Retired Model

A retired Model remains resolvable historically.

28.162 Retired Adapter

An old Adapter Version may remain installed only for historical decoding or rollback where safe.

28.163 Retired Connection

A retired Connection cannot resolve Credentials for new dispatch.

28.164 Retired Tool

A retired Tool cannot be exposed to Agents.

28.165 Retired MCP Server

A retired MCP server cannot receive new Sessions.

28.166 Retired Workflow

A retired workflow may remain visible for historical executions.

28.167 Contract Deprecation

Canonical APIs, schemas and Events SHALL support explicit Version deprecation.

28.168 Breaking Migration

Breaking migrations SHALL include:

- migration path,

- compatibility period,

- affected consumers,

- and rollback or rollforward.

28.169 Data Migration

Data migration transforms existing canonical or legacy data into a target representation.

28.170 Data Migration Identity

Every material data migration SHALL have stable identity and Version.

28.171 Data Migration Source

Source schema and source state SHALL be explicit.

28.172 Data Migration Target

Target schema and expected invariants SHALL be explicit.

28.173 Data Migration Mapping

Field and semantic mappings SHALL be documented.

28.174 Missing Legacy Field

Missing historical information SHALL remain unknown or absent.

It SHALL not be fabricated.

28.175 Legacy Provenance

Imported Assets without full production history SHALL be marked with imported or incomplete provenance state.

28.176 Provenance Confidence

Imported provenance MAY include confidence and evidence source.

28.177 Historical Asset Import

Existing Assets MAY be imported with:

- Asset identity,

- checksum,

- source folder,

- known creator,

- known date,

- known Project,

- known rights,

- and incomplete provenance marker.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.178 Import Does Not Recreate Execution

An Asset existing before Fabric SHALL not receive a fictional Provider Attempt or Execution.

28.179 Legacy Rights

Rights state SHALL be:

- verified,

- probable,

- unknown,

- disputed,

- or restricted

based on available evidence.

28.180 Unknown Rights

Unknown rights SHALL remain blocking for uses requiring proven rights.

28.181 Legacy Consent

Consent SHALL not be inferred solely because an Asset exists.

28.182 Legacy Classification

Imported data SHALL receive a conservative Classification when uncertainty exists.

28.183 Historical Execution Import

Existing logs MAY be imported as historical execution references.

28.184 Incomplete Historical Execution

Historical execution MAY be marked:

- legacy,

- incomplete,

- unverified,

- or partially reconstructable.

28.185 No Fabricated Audit

Legacy logs SHALL not become canonical Audit Events unless their integrity and semantics support that transformation.

28.186 Legacy Cost Import

Historical Provider spend MAY be imported as aggregate Cost Records if exact attribution is unavailable.

28.187 Cost Attribution Confidence

Imported cost SHALL preserve confidence and scope.

28.188 Memory Migration

Existing Memory SHALL be categorised before admission into the new governed Memory architecture.

28.189 Legacy Memory Categories

Existing Memory MAY include:

- user preference,

- Project fact,

- architecture decision,

- temporary context,

- derived operational belief,

- and unknown-origin note.

28.190 Memory Origin

Origin SHALL be preserved when known.

28.191 Unknown Memory Origin

Unknown-origin Memory SHOULD receive lower trust and review.

28.192 Memory Canonicalisation

Legacy Memory becomes canonical only after:

- Project scope,

- Domain,

- Classification,

- evidence,

- confidence,

- validity,

- and admission

are resolved sufficiently.

28.193 No Bulk Truth Promotion

Large legacy Memory stores SHALL not be promoted wholesale into high-confidence canonical Memory.

28.194 Legacy Project Knowledge

Approved Project books and canonical documents MAY receive stronger authority than informal Memory.

28.195 Knowledge Edition

Future Atlas Knowledge Editions MAY ingest approved Omnira books through governed knowledge processes without changing the book’s source authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.196 Document as Source

Canonical architecture books SHALL remain source documents.

Derived indexes and embeddings SHALL remain projections.

28.197 Search Index Migration

Search indexes MAY be rebuilt from canonical source objects.

28.198 Index Rebuild Preference

Rebuilding from source is preferable to migrating opaque legacy vector state when feasible.

28.199 Index Migration

If vector state is migrated, source identity and Project scope SHALL remain verifiable.

28.200 Deleted Source During Migration

Deleted or revoked sources SHALL not be reintroduced through index import.

28.201 Event Migration

Legacy events MAY be translated into canonical Events only where semantics are well understood.

28.202 Event Translation Record

Translation SHALL preserve:

- source event,

- target event,

- mapping Version,

- and uncertainty.

28.203 Unknown Legacy Event

Unknown events SHALL remain archival data rather than being forced into incorrect canonical types.

28.204 Queue Migration

In-flight queue work SHALL be handled through one explicit transfer strategy.

28.205 Queue Drain Strategy

The legacy queue MAY drain before new work enters the Fabric.

28.206 Queue Transfer Strategy

Pending items MAY be translated into canonical queue messages if state and idempotency are known.

28.207 Queue Abandon Strategy

Low-value obsolete queue work MAY be cancelled under explicit authority.

28.208 Queue Duplicate Prevention

New and old queues SHALL not process the same consequential work.

28.209 Scheduled Job Migration

Recurring jobs SHALL receive new canonical schedule and Mandate references.

28.210 Schedule Cutover

Only one scheduler SHALL own each recurrence after cutover.

28.211 Missed Schedule

Migration SHALL define handling for schedules occurring during transition.

28.212 Webhook Migration

Webhook endpoints MAY require staged transition.

28.213 Webhook Dual Delivery

Provider support for multiple endpoints MAY allow temporary dual delivery.

Downstream processing SHALL remain deduplicated.

28.214 Webhook Endpoint Replacement

When only one endpoint is supported, cutover SHALL coordinate:

- subscription update,

- signature Secret,

- verification,

- and fallback.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.215 Webhook Secret Rotation

Webhook migration SHOULD rotate shared Secrets when old endpoint exposure is uncertain.

28.216 Webhook Replay

Buffered or retried legacy events SHALL remain idempotent after migration.

28.217 External Job Migration

Existing async Provider jobs SHALL remain tied to the system that owns their durable state unless transferred explicitly.

28.218 External Job Transfer

Transfer SHALL preserve:

- Provider,

- Account,

- native job ID,

- state,

- result Location,

- cost,

- and idempotency.

28.219 Unknown External Job

Uncertain jobs SHALL remain reconciliation-required.

28.220 Publication Migration

Publication architecture SHALL migrate separately from generation.

28.221 Publication Account Inventory

Every publication Account SHALL be verified.

28.222 Publication Credential Migration

Publication Credentials SHALL move into approved Secret and Connection management.

28.223 Publication Approval Migration

Legacy “approved” flags SHALL not automatically become canonical Approval Decisions.

28.224 Legacy Publication History

Historical posts MAY be imported as external Asset or publication references.

28.225 Publication Verification Migration

Future publications SHALL use canonical external verification after cutover.

28.226 Manual Workflow Migration

Manual workflows SHALL be modelled truthfully before automation is increased.

28.227 Manual Procedure Inventory

Manual workflows SHOULD capture:

- operator,

- Account,

- Inputs,

- outputs,

- cost,

- evidence,

- and completion criteria.

28.228 Manual-to-Assisted Migration

A manual workflow MAY first become Human-Assisted before full API automation.

28.229 Human-Assisted Value

Human-Assisted representation provides:

- canonical state,

- cost,

- evidence,

- scope,

- and future automation path.

28.230 No False Automation

Migration SHALL not hide manual intervention to make progress appear more automated.

28.231 Cost Migration

Economic governance SHALL migrate before broad paid routing.

28.232 Historical Budget

Legacy spending caps MAY be converted into Project Budget configuration after owner review.

28.233 Missing Historical Cost

Unknown historical cost SHALL not block migration of future calls.

It SHALL remain unknown historically.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.234 Subscription Migration

Existing subscriptions SHALL be registered with:

- owner,

- Provider,

- plan,

- renewal,

- cost,

- cancellation,

- and Project allocation

where relevant.

28.235 Free Tier Migration

Free quotas SHALL be represented as economic resources rather than assumed unlimited.

28.236 Billing Account Change

Changing billing owner during migration requires explicit approval.

28.237 Policy Migration

Legacy implicit rules SHALL be converted into explicit policy.

28.238 Implicit Policy

Examples include:

- “never use external Provider for this Project,”

- “always ask before spending,”

- or “do not publish automatically.”

28.239 Policy Extraction

Observed legacy behaviour MAY suggest policy.

It SHALL not become canonical without review.

28.240 Project Policy Migration

Project-specific constraints SHALL remain distinct from platform policy.

28.241 User Preference Versus Policy

Preference such as “prefer local when possible” SHALL remain distinct from mandatory Local Only policy.

28.242 Authority Migration

Existing roles and permissions SHALL be mapped into canonical Principals, Roles, Grants and Mandates.

28.243 Authority Conservatism

When legacy authority is ambiguous, migration SHALL choose narrower authority.

28.244 No Authority Expansion Through Migration

Migration SHALL never broaden authority merely to preserve old convenience.

28.245 Existing Automation

Legacy automated actions SHALL receive explicit Mandates before continuing under Fabric control.

28.246 Automation Without Owner

Legacy automation without accountable owner SHALL be paused or assigned before migration.

28.247 Standing Permission Review

Repeated historical user approval SHALL not become Standing Mandate automatically.

28.248 Approval Migration

Pending legacy approvals MAY be completed in legacy system or reissued canonically.

28.249 Approval Reissue

High-risk approvals SHOULD be reissued in canonical form.

28.250 Revocation Migration

Revoked permissions SHALL remain revoked.

28.251 Deleted Principal

Deleted or departed Principals SHALL not become active during identity import.

28.252 Device Migration

Local Nodes SHALL be registered through explicit pairing or approval.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.253 Device Trust Migration

Past device familiarity SHALL not automatically create trusted Node status.

28.254 Node Software

Node Agent installation SHALL be verified before execution eligibility.

28.255 Mobile Node Migration

Mobile intelligence SHALL adopt the same Node and authority contracts as other execution resources.

28.256 Browser Workflow Migration

Browser-assisted workflows SHALL use isolated profiles and canonical Account identity.

28.257 Personal Browser State

Personal cookies and Sessions SHALL not be imported into Project automation automatically.

28.258 Browser Profile Creation

A Project browser profile SHOULD be explicitly provisioned.

28.259 Browser Session Migration

If existing Project Sessions are migrated, Account ownership and scope SHALL be verified.

28.260 Rollout Cohort

A Rollout Cohort is a defined group receiving a new Fabric capability.

It SHALL include or reference:

- cohortId,

- scope,

- criteria,

- feature,

- start,

- end,

- owner,

- and metrics.

28.261 Rollout Cohort Identity

Every production Rollout Cohort SHOULD have stable identity.

28.262 Internal Cohort

The first cohort MAY include only the platform owner or internal Projects.

28.263 Project Cohort

A Project MAY form one rollout cohort.

28.264 Capability Cohort

One Capability MAY be enabled across several Projects gradually.

28.265 Risk Cohort

Lower-risk workloads SHOULD often precede high-risk workloads.

28.266 Cohort Exit

A cohort exits when success or rollback criteria are met.

28.267 Rollout Gate

A Rollout Gate determines whether expansion may continue.

28.268 Rollout Gate Inputs

Inputs MAY include:

- conformance,

- Incidents,

- Quality,

- cost,

- latency,

- user corrections,

- policy denials,

- and migration regressions.

28.269 Stop-the-Line

Critical governance or isolation failure SHALL stop rollout expansion.

28.270 Rollout Pause

A rollout MAY pause without rolling back existing stable cohorts.

28.271 Rollout Resume

Resume requires evidence that blocking conditions are resolved.

28.272 Rollout Communication

Affected users SHALL understand material changes in:

- provider usage,

- cost visibility,

- approval,

- local execution,

- and data handling.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.273 Silent Infrastructure Migration

Low-impact internal changes MAY remain invisible to users if user-facing behaviour and custody do not materially change.

28.274 Data Custody Change

Any migration changing data custody SHOULD be visible where material.

28.275 Provider Change During Migration

Changing Provider MAY require user or Project approval depending on policy.

28.276 Default Provider Removal

Removing one Provider SHOULD not force Agent code changes.

28.277 Routing Migration

Routing logic MAY initially reproduce existing fixed Provider selection before becoming adaptive.

28.278 Fixed Route First

A fixed canonical Route is acceptable during initial migration if:

- Provider is registered,

- policy is enforced,

- cost is recorded,

- and Routing Decision exists.

28.279 Adaptive Routing Later

Adaptive scoring SHOULD be enabled after enough evidence exists.

28.280 Routing Learning During Migration

Historical Provider assumptions SHALL not be promoted into scoring weights without evidence.

28.281 Quality Baseline

Before route migration, existing Quality SHOULD be measured where possible.

28.282 Cost Baseline

Existing cost SHOULD be measured where possible.

28.283 Latency Baseline

Existing latency SHOULD be measured where possible.

28.284 Failure Baseline

Existing error and retry behaviour SHOULD be measured.

28.285 Baseline Imperfection

Missing baseline data SHALL remain visible.

Migration SHALL not invent comparison confidence.

28.286 Provider Swap Safety

A Provider swap SHALL preserve:

- Capability,

- Quality Floor,

- data eligibility,

- rights,

- authority,

- and Budget.

28.287 Provider Swap User Impact

Material differences in:

- style,

- latency,

- cost,

- or rights

SHOULD be assessed.

28.288 Model Upgrade Migration

Model upgrades SHALL be treated as resource Version changes, not automatic improvements.

28.289 Model Upgrade Shadowing

High-impact Model changes SHOULD run shadow or benchmark evaluation first.

28.290 Model Downgrade

A cheaper Model MAY be used only when Quality Floor remains satisfied.

28.291 Model Alias Retirement

Aliases SHOULD be resolved to stable Registry identity as far as Provider evidence permits.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.292 Adapter Upgrade

Adapter Versions SHALL be rolled out independently from core Agents.

28.293 Adapter Canary

New Adapter Versions SHOULD receive bounded traffic first when consequences are material.

28.294 Adapter Rollback

Old Adapter Version MAY remain available temporarily for rollback if safe.

28.295 Connector Upgrade

Changing Adapter Version SHALL revalidate Connector conformance.

28.296 Tool Upgrade

Tool Version changes SHALL revalidate:

- schema,

- permissions,

- side effects,

- and Sandbox.

28.297 MCP Server Upgrade

Server changes SHALL trigger discovery diff and revalidation.

28.298 Prompt Template Migration

Prompt templates MAY move from Agent-specific code into governed Agent or Capability configuration.

28.299 Prompt Identity

Material prompt templates SHOULD have Version identity.

28.300 Prompt Migration

Migration SHALL preserve:

- purpose,

- policy separation,

- input variables,

- and evaluation.

28.301 Prompt Is Not Policy

System governance SHALL not depend on prompt text alone.

28.302 System Prompt Evolution

Agent instruction evolution SHALL be tested independently from Provider migration.

28.303 Context Assembly Migration

Legacy context assembly SHALL migrate toward governed retrieval and Intent Envelope construction.

28.304 Context Scope Verification

Migration SHALL ensure that context remains Project-scoped.

28.305 Context Minimisation

New Fabric context assembly SHOULD reduce unnecessary data exposure.

28.306 Memory Context Migration

Legacy conversation history SHOULD not be copied wholesale into every Fabric Request.

28.307 User Preference Migration

Stable explicit preferences MAY become governed Memory after review.

28.308 Temporary Conversation State

Temporary context SHOULD remain Session-scoped.

28.309 Data Retention Migration

Legacy indefinite retention SHOULD be reviewed during migration.

28.310 Retention Mapping

Every major data class SHOULD receive target retention.

28.311 Legacy Deletion Requests

Past deletion requests SHALL be respected during import.

28.312 Restore During Migration

Backup restore performed during migration SHALL reapply current deletion and revocation state.

28.313 Object Storage Migration

Assets MAY move between storage systems behind stable Asset identity.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.314 Storage Migration Requirement

Migration SHALL preserve:

- checksum,

- Asset Version,

- Classification,

- encryption,

- lifecycle,

- and provenance.

28.315 Storage Dual Read

Temporary dual-read MAY support migration.

28.316 Storage Dual Write

Dual-write SHOULD be used cautiously because divergence risk increases.

28.317 Storage Source of Truth

At every phase, the authoritative storage Location SHALL be explicit.

28.318 Storage Verification

Checksums SHALL verify copied Assets.

28.319 Source Retention

High-value source copies SHOULD remain until target verification completes.

28.320 Source Deletion

Source deletion SHALL require separate completion Decision when data-loss risk exists.

28.321 Database Migration

Database changes SHALL preserve canonical IDs and Versions.

28.322 Table Reorganisation

Internal table changes SHALL not alter domain identity.

28.323 Database Split

Future service extraction MAY split tables across databases.

Canonical object identity SHALL remain stable.

28.324 Database Merge

Combining stores SHALL preserve Tenant and Project isolation.

28.325 Schema Backfill

Backfilled fields SHALL distinguish:

- known historical value,

- derived value,

- default,

- and unknown.

28.326 Default Backfill Risk

Using one default to hide missing historical semantics SHALL be avoided.

28.327 Audit Migration

Audit systems SHALL migrate without breaking historical integrity.

28.328 Audit Chain Continuity

If audit storage technology changes, continuity evidence SHOULD link old and new systems.

28.329 Historical Audit Archive

Legacy audit archives MAY remain read-only rather than being rewritten.

28.330 Observability Migration

Metrics, logs and traces MAY move to new infrastructure without changing their canonical meaning.

28.331 Metric Renaming

Metric migration SHALL preserve mapping or historical continuity where important.

28.332 Trace Migration

Trace IDs SHALL remain stable across one Execution even during component migration.

28.333 Dashboard Migration

Dashboards SHALL be validated against canonical sources after data pipeline changes.

28.334 Alert Migration

Alert Rules SHALL not silently disappear during observability migration.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
sectionTitles: 28.348 Migration Speed Is Not Primary Objective
text:
28.335 Incident Process Migration

Existing incident procedures MAY be mapped into canonical Incident objects gradually.

28.336 Historical Incident Import

Past Incidents MAY be imported with incomplete evidence markers.

28.337 Runbook Migration

Legacy troubleshooting notes MAY become canonical Runbooks after review and testing.

28.338 Documentation Migration

Implementation docs SHALL distinguish:

- canonical architecture,

- current implementation,

- migration state,

- and deprecated paths.

28.339 Documentation Version

Migration docs SHALL identify applicable software Version or period.

28.340 Temporary Documentation

Temporary migration guidance SHALL have expiry or removal criterion.

28.341 Migration Dashboard

A Migration Dashboard SHOULD show:

- scope,

- current phase,

- direct-call count,

- migrated workflows,

- remaining debt,

- incidents,

- test state,

- and retirement readiness.

28.342 Direct Provider Bypass Metric

The number and volume of direct Provider calls outside Fabric SHOULD trend toward zero.

28.343 Legacy Credential Metric

The count of production Credentials outside approved Secret management SHOULD trend toward zero.

28.344 Legacy Account Metric

Unregistered Provider Accounts used by production SHOULD trend toward zero.

28.345 Legacy Asset Metric

New Assets without canonical provenance SHOULD trend toward zero after migration start.

28.346 Migration Incident Metric

Incidents caused by migration SHOULD be tracked separately.

28.347 Migration Cost Metric

Migration SHOULD account for:

- engineering,

- duplicate Provider calls,

- temporary infrastructure,

- and human review.

28.348 Migration Speed Is Not Primary Objective

Fast migration SHALL not outrank correctness and recoverability.

28.349 Rollout Success Criterion

A rollout is successful when:

- target behaviour is correct,

- user harm is absent or acceptable,

- governance works,

- and migration debt decreases.

28.350 Rollout Failure Criterion

A rollout has failed when:

- direct bypass grows,

- policy weakens,

- user-visible reliability materially regresses,

- or temporary exceptions become permanent.

28.351 Project-Specific Rollout — Familje-Stunden

Familje-Stunden SHOULD migrate creative workflows in a sequence that protects canonical character identity, child safety and publication review.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.352 Familje-Stunden Phase One

Initial migration SHOULD cover:

- text generation,

- image generation,

- Voice generation,

- Asset provenance,

- and human QA.

28.353 Familje-Stunden Phase Two

Later migration MAY cover:

- automated packaging,

- subscriber delivery preparation,

- publication scheduling,

- and richer multimodal workflows.

28.354 Familje-Stunden Publication Gate

Public release SHALL remain human-approved throughout Stage 1 rollout.

28.355 Familje-Stunden Child Data

Workflows involving child data SHALL use restrictive rollout cohorts and stronger verification.

28.356 Familje-Stunden Reference Assets

Nova and Pling canonical references SHALL be imported as Project Assets with verified identity and source information.

28.357 Familje-Stunden Legacy Art

Older artwork with uncertain provenance SHALL be marked accordingly rather than promoted as fully evidenced.

28.358 Familje-Stunden Voice Profiles

Voice assets SHALL migrate only after:

- profile ownership,

- consent,

- Provider Account,

- and reuse scope

are clear.

28.359 Familje-Stunden Rollout Success

Success requires:

- stable character identity,

- safe child-facing content,

- correct Asset Versions,

- visible cost,

- and no automatic public publication.

28.360 Project-Specific Rollout — The Prompt

The Prompt SHOULD migrate research and content generation before autonomous publication expands.

28.361 The Prompt Phase One

Initial migration SHOULD cover:

- search and retrieval,

- source provenance,

- Script generation,

- image generation,

- and Quality evaluation.

28.362 The Prompt Phase Two

Later rollout MAY cover:

- publication packaging,

- schedule,

- account-specific publishing,

- and bounded comment response.

28.363 The Prompt Source Migration

Legacy research context SHALL become source-linked Evidence where recoverable.

28.364 The Prompt Generated Media

Generated visual Assets SHALL migrate into canonical provenance and disclosure handling.

28.365 The Prompt Publication Rollout

Publication SHOULD begin:

- manual,

- then approval-gated Connector,

- then bounded Mandate

only after evidence supports it.

28.366 The Prompt Duplicate Protection

Duplicate-content checks SHOULD be active before autonomous publication rollout.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.367 The Prompt Rollout Success

Success requires:

- grounded research,

- no duplicate publishing,

- correct Account,

- disclosure compliance,

- and verified external completion.

28.368 Project-Specific Rollout — GainPilot

GainPilot SHOULD prioritise privacy, current programme context and Local Only enforcement.

28.369 GainPilot Phase One

Initial migration SHOULD cover:

- reasoning requests,

- programme context retrieval,

- local intelligence,

- and Project Memory isolation.

28.370 GainPilot Phase Two

Later rollout MAY cover:

- bounded programme adjustments,

- scheduled coaching analysis,

- and richer autonomous recommendations.

28.371 GainPilot Health Data

High-sensitivity data SHOULD use local-first rollout.

28.372 GainPilot Local Node

A local Runtime SHOULD be proven before any Local Only workflow is considered migrated.

28.373 GainPilot Arnold Identity

Arnold SHALL remain the same Agent despite Provider or Model changes.

28.374 GainPilot Rollout Success

Success requires:

- current Plan awareness,

- no cross-Project data,

- privacy-preserving execution,

- and no unsupported programme changes.

28.375 Platform-Specific Rollout — Atlas

Atlas is the most important initial Fabric consumer and SHOULD migrate incrementally.

28.376 Atlas Phase One

Atlas Phase One SHOULD route:

- ordinary text generation,

- reasoning,

- architecture drafting,

- and structured Outputs

through Fabric.

28.377 Atlas Phase Two

Atlas Phase Two MAY add:

- local intelligence,

- search,

- MCP,

- multimodal production,

- and richer Project workflows.

28.378 Atlas Phase Three

Later Atlas rollout MAY add broader bounded autonomous orchestration.

28.379 Atlas Migration Success

Atlas migration succeeds when:

- Provider knowledge is removed from Agent logic,

- cost is visible,

- local and external routing coexist,

- Credentials are isolated,

- and Evidence exists.

28.380 Omnira-Wide Rollout Order

A practical platform rollout SHOULD follow:

1. read-only and draft intelligence.

2. paid but non-consequential generation.

3. local intelligence.

4. governed Tools.

5. multimodal Asset production.

6. Human-Assisted workflows.

7. external side effects.

8. publication.

9. recurring bounded autonomy.

10. broader delegated operational domains.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
sectionTitles: 28.393 Anti-Pattern — Copy Existing Architecture Into New Names
28.395 Anti-Pattern — One Provider Wrapper Called Fabric
text:
28.381 Autonomy Last

Broader autonomy SHALL follow governance maturity rather than precede it.

28.382 Migration Readiness Review

Before migrating a Capability, Omnira SHOULD review:

- source dependencies,

- target implementation,

- policy,

- Credentials,

- cost,

- test coverage,

- observability,

- and rollback.

28.383 Migration Acceptance Test

Each migrated workflow SHALL have an acceptance test.

28.384 Migration Acceptance Criteria

Criteria SHOULD include:

- correct functionality,

- correct routing,

- correct scope,

- correct cost,

- correct Evidence,

- and absence of legacy bypass.

28.385 Legacy Bypass Detection

Code and Runtime telemetry SHOULD detect bypass after cutover.

28.386 Bypass Alert

Production direct Provider access after migration MAY trigger a governance alert or Incident depending on risk.

28.387 Emergency Legacy Fallback

A legacy path MAY be retained temporarily for emergency fallback only if:

- explicitly approved,

- isolated,

- monitored,

- time-bounded,

- and unable to bypass current policy.

28.388 Emergency Fallback Expiry

Emergency fallback SHALL have retirement date.

28.389 Emergency Fallback Invocation

Use SHALL be audited.

28.390 No Hidden Legacy Fallback

Fallback SHALL not occur silently merely because the Fabric path fails.

28.391 Anti-Pattern — Big-Bang Rewrite

Rewriting all Omnira intelligence systems before validating one Fabric path creates unnecessary risk.

28.392 Anti-Pattern — Migration Without Inventory

Unknown dependencies cause hidden regressions.

28.393 Anti-Pattern — Copy Existing Architecture Into New Names

Canonicalisation requires semantic redesign where legacy assumptions violate the Fabric.

28.394 Anti-Pattern — Provider-Centric Migration

Migration SHALL be Capability- and workflow-aware, not merely SDK replacement.

28.395 Anti-Pattern — One Provider Wrapper Called Fabric

A wrapper around one Provider does not satisfy the architecture.

28.396 Anti-Pattern — Router Before Registry

Routing without governed resource identity becomes hard-coded selection.

28.397 Anti-Pattern — Registry Before Scope

A Resource without Tenant, Project, Account and lifecycle semantics is incomplete.

28.481 Future Evolution Principle

Future Intelligence Fabric evolution SHALL preserve canonical semantics while allowing implementation technology to change.

28.482 Stable Core Concepts

The following concepts SHOULD remain stable across future stages:

- Capability Request,

- Intent Envelope,

- Capability,

- Provider,

- Model,

- Tool,

- Agent,

- Plan,

- Execution,

- Attempt,

- Routing Decision,

- Cost Record,

- Approval,

- Asset,

- Evidence,

- Memory,

- Classification,

- Mandate,

- Incident,

- and Conformance.

chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
sectionTitles: 28.496 Stage Labels Are Not Authority Levels
text:
28.483 Evolution Through Versioning

Material semantic changes SHALL use Versioned contracts rather than silent mutation.

28.484 Architectural Compatibility

Future services SHALL remain compatible with historical canonical records where practical.

28.485 Evolution Decision

An Evolution Decision records approval for material architecture change.

It SHALL include or reference:

- evolutionDecisionId,

- subject,

- rationale,

- affected contracts,

- migration,

- compatibility,

- risks,

- approval,

- and Version.

28.486 Evolution Decision Identity

Every material Evolution Decision SHALL have stable identity.

28.487 Architecture Decision Record

Architecture Decision Records MAY preserve implementation choices supporting the canonical book.

28.488 Book Authority

Implementation ADRs SHALL not silently override this canonical book.

28.489 Book Revision

Material canonical change SHALL require an approved book revision or successor specification.

28.490 Backward-Compatible Extension

Future fields and Capabilities SHOULD prefer additive extension where semantics permit.

28.491 Breaking Evolution

Breaking evolution requires explicit migration and deprecation.

28.492 Future Stage Model

Later stages MAY be organised by maturity rather than fixed calendar dates.

28.493 Stage 2 Direction

A likely Stage 2 MAY expand:

- Provider coverage,

- continuous evaluation,

- richer local intelligence,

- multimodal orchestration,

- deeper Tool integration,

- and selective bounded autonomy.

28.494 Stage 3 Direction

A later stage MAY expand:

- private AI infrastructure,

- distributed local Nodes,

- stronger continuous learning,

- automated operational workflows,

- and cross-Project executive coordination under governance.

28.495 Stage 4 Direction

A mature stage MAY support:

- certified third-party Agents,

- dynamic provider ecosystems,

- complex private compute,

- multi-region execution,

- and broader delegated domain autonomy.

28.496 Stage Labels Are Not Authority Levels

Implementation maturity stages SHALL remain distinct from L0–L6 Authority Levels.

28.497 Future Provider Expansion

The Fabric SHOULD be able to add Providers without modifying Agent business logic.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
sectionTitles: 28.502 Provider Diversity Is Not Mandatory Duplication
text:
28.498 New Provider Process

Future Provider onboarding SHOULD follow:

1. Provider Registry review.

2. Product definition.

3. Account model.

4. privacy and terms review.

5. Adapter implementation.

6. live contract test.

7. capability evaluation.

8. cost integration.

9. Conformance.

10. controlled rollout.

28.499 Provider Removal

Provider removal SHOULD require:

- dependency inventory,

- route replacement,

- Asset retention review,

- Credential revocation,

- and deprecation.

28.500 Multi-Provider Strategy

The Fabric SHOULD avoid relying on one Provider for every critical Capability where practical.

28.501 Provider Diversity

Provider diversity can improve:

- resilience,

- cost control,

- privacy options,

- and capability coverage.

28.502 Provider Diversity Is Not Mandatory Duplication

Every Capability does not require several Providers if one route is uniquely appropriate.

28.503 Continuous Provider Evaluation

Future stages MAY run scheduled evaluation across Providers.

28.504 Continuous Evaluation Safety

Evaluation SHALL use:

- bounded data,

- test Budget,

- non-public Outputs,

- and governed datasets.

28.505 Adaptive Routing

Routing MAY become increasingly evidence-driven.

28.506 Adaptive Routing Inputs

Future routing MAY incorporate:

- recent Quality,

- task-specific benchmark performance,

- live latency,

- cost,

- reliability,

- user preference,

- resource locality,

- and sustainability metrics.

28.507 Adaptive Routing Boundaries

Machine-learned ranking SHALL occur only after policy eligibility.

28.508 No Learned Policy Override

A learned Router SHALL never override:

- Local Only,

- authority,

- Consent,

- rights,

- or prohibited Provider rules.

28.509 Routing Model

A future routing Model MAY predict best resources.

Its own behaviour SHALL be observable and testable.

28.510 Router Explainability

Material Routing Decisions SHOULD remain explainable through evidence even when ML assists ranking.

28.511 Routing Feedback

User acceptance, Quality and cost MAY update routing evidence.

28.512 Feedback Bias

Observed feedback SHALL account for:

- selection bias,

- reviewer variation,

- task distribution,

- and Provider availability.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.513 Future Model Registry

The Model Registry MAY support:

- benchmark histories,

- safety profiles,

- context behaviour,

- quantisation variants,

- fine-tunes,

- and Deployment-specific evidence.

28.514 Model Family Relationships

Future Models MAY represent:

- base Model,

- fine-tune,

- adapter,

- quantisation,

- distillation,

- and deployment lineage.

28.515 Fine-Tuned Model

A fine-tuned Model SHALL remain a new governed Model identity.

28.516 Custom Model Training

Future training MAY occur through the Fabric under explicit:

- data,

- rights,

- Consent,

- Budget,

- and Model governance.

28.517 Training Data

Training datasets SHALL require stronger provenance and use authority than ordinary inference Inputs.

28.518 Model Distillation

Distillation SHALL preserve source rights and data policy.

28.519 Model Export

Exporting a Model MAY require separate intellectual-property and privacy governance.

28.520 Local Intelligence Expansion

Future local intelligence MAY include:

- larger Models,

- multimodal Models,

- embeddings,

- image generation,

- speech,

- computer vision,

- and private Agents.

28.521 Private AI Rig

A private AI rig SHALL join the Fabric as governed Nodes and Runtimes.

28.522 GPU Pool

Several local or private GPUs MAY form a governed resource pool.

28.523 GPU Scheduler

A future GPU Scheduler MAY manage:

- placement,

- VRAM,

- Model residency,

- batching,

- power,

- and priority.

28.524 GPU Scheduler Authority

Scheduling resources SHALL not alter data eligibility or Agent authority.

28.525 Local Model Residency

Models MAY remain loaded based on predicted demand.

28.526 Local Cache Privacy

Model and embedding caches SHALL inherit relevant security controls.

28.527 Edge Intelligence

Phones, laptops, desktops, vehicles and edge devices MAY participate as Nodes.

28.528 Edge Constraints

Routing MAY consider:

- battery,

- connectivity,

- thermal state,

- privacy,

- and user activity.

28.529 Offline Agent Operation

Future Agents MAY operate locally while offline inside bounded authority snapshots.

28.530 Offline Conflict

Offline changes SHALL reconcile before they overwrite newer canonical state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.531 Offline Side Effects

External side effects are naturally unavailable offline and SHALL not be fabricated.

28.532 Mobile Intelligence

Mobile intelligence MAY expose:

- approvals,

- local Tools,

- context,

- capture,

- location,

- and execution

through the same Fabric governance.

28.533 Mobile Sensor Access

Sensor Capabilities SHALL remain explicitly permissioned.

28.534 Mobile Private Data

Private messages and private media SHALL remain excluded unless explicitly governed.

28.535 Vehicle Intelligence

Future vehicle Nodes MAY provide bounded status or context.

They SHALL not receive broad device authority automatically.

28.536 Multimodal Evolution

Future Fabric versions MAY orchestrate:

- image,

- video,

- Voice,

- music,

- animation,

- 3D,

- and interactive media.

28.537 Multimodal Plan

A multimodal Plan MAY contain specialised Steps for:

- script,

- storyboard,

- image references,

- Voice,

- music,

- animation,

- composition,

- subtitles,

- encoding,

- QA,

- and publication.

28.538 Cross-Modal Provenance

Derived media SHALL preserve lineage across source modalities.

28.539 Character Consistency

Future systems MAY use:

- Reference Sets,

- embeddings,

- identity evaluators,

- and human review

to maintain recurring characters.

28.540 Voice Consistency

Voice identity SHALL preserve:

- Voice Profile,

- Consent,

- Provider,

- Model,

- settings,

- and reuse scope.

28.541 Video Provider

Video Providers SHALL enter through the same Adapter, Asset, Cost and Quality architecture.

28.542 Long Video Job

Long-running video generation SHALL use durable async orchestration.

28.543 Video Asset Chain

Video provenance MAY include:

- storyboard,

- reference images,

- audio,

- prompts,

- motion generation,

- editing,

- and final composition.

28.544 Music Generation

Music generation SHALL preserve rights and commercial-use evidence.

28.545 External Creative Suites

Creative suites without stable APIs MAY remain Human-Assisted Connectors.

28.546 Automation Upgrade

A Human-Assisted Connector MAY become an API Connector later without changing the surrounding Plan semantics.

28.547 Human-to-API Migration

Historical manual evidence SHALL remain truthful after automation becomes available.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.548 Future Tool Ecosystem

The Tool Registry MAY expand to:

- code execution,

- browser automation,

- databases,

- design tools,

- commerce,

- communication,

- and device control.

28.549 Tool Capability Granularity

High-risk Tools SHOULD expose narrow canonical actions rather than one broad “execute anything” operation.

28.550 Tool Composition

Plans MAY compose several Tools.

Authority SHALL apply to each side effect.

28.551 Tool Sandboxing

Future Tool execution MAY use:

- containers,

- VMs,

- WASM,

- microVMs,

- or secure enclaves.

28.552 Tool Provenance

Tool-produced Assets and changes SHALL remain attributable.

28.553 Browser Agent Evolution

Browser automation MAY become more capable after:

- profile isolation,

- Account identity,

- page trust,

- approval,

- and replay-safe side effects

are mature.

28.554 Browser Observation

Page content SHALL remain untrusted external data.

28.555 Browser Action

Clicks, submissions, purchases and publication SHALL remain explicit side effects.

28.556 MCP Evolution

The MCP ecosystem MAY expand substantially.

The Fabric SHALL retain canonical control.

28.557 MCP Server Certification

Future MCP servers MAY receive reusable Certification profiles.

28.558 MCP Marketplace

A future MCP marketplace MAY list available servers.

Discovery SHALL not create trust or authority.

28.559 MCP Sampling Evolution

Server-initiated sampling MAY be supported only by translating it into Fabric-governed Capability Requests.

28.560 MCP Elicitation Evolution

Elicitation MAY integrate with approval UI without allowing servers to collect arbitrary user data.

28.561 MCP Resource Subscription

Future resource subscriptions SHALL preserve Project, Classification and event governance.

28.562 Future Agent Protocols

New Agent-to-Agent protocols MAY be integrated through the same identity and authority architecture.

28.563 External Agent

An external Agent SHALL be treated as a governed resource, not as a trusted Omnira Principal automatically.

28.564 External Agent Identity

External Agent identity SHALL include:

- operator,

- protocol,

- endpoint,

- Version,

- Capabilities,

- and trust.

28.565 Agent Delegation Protocol

Future delegation SHALL carry canonical scope and authority rather than plain natural-language instruction.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.566 Agent-to-Agent Contract

Agent collaboration SHOULD preserve:

- sender,

- recipient,

- purpose,

- scope,

- data,

- authority,

- cost,

- and Evidence.

28.567 Third-Party Agent Marketplace

Future marketplaces SHALL require:

- certification,

- isolation,

- billing,

- data handling,

- and revocation.

28.568 Agent Reputation

Operational history MAY inform selection.

Reputation SHALL not override mandatory policy.

28.569 Agent Model Independence

Agents SHALL continue to retain identity independent of current Model.

28.570 Agent Runtime Mobility

One Agent MAY execute across:

- cloud,

- local,

- mobile,
