- and private Nodes

without changing its canonical identity.

28.571 Agent State Portability

Portable state SHALL remain scoped and encrypted.

28.572 Agent Memory Portability

Memory SHALL remain in Omnira governance rather than one Model provider’s conversation store.

28.573 Future Workflow Engine

A richer workflow engine MAY replace Stage 1 orchestration internals.

28.574 Workflow Engine Boundary

The engine SHALL consume canonical Plans and state rather than redefining them silently.

28.575 Workflow DSL

A future DSL MAY express Plans.

It SHALL compile to canonical Execution Graph semantics.

28.576 Workflow Template

Reusable workflow templates MAY be Project-independent where policy and Assets are parameterised.

28.577 Workflow Marketplace

Future reusable workflows MAY be shared across Projects after conformance.

28.578 Workflow Package

A workflow package SHOULD declare:

- required Capabilities,

- Tools,

- data,

- Budget,

- approvals,

- and side effects.

28.579 Workflow Versioning

Every published workflow package SHALL be Versioned.

28.580 Workflow Certification

High-risk workflows SHALL require current Certification.

28.581 Future Event Architecture

A dedicated Event Bus MAY support:

- scale,

- decoupling,

- replay,

- and projections.

28.582 Event Bus Migration

Moving to a broker SHALL not alter Event identity or semantics.

28.583 Event Partitioning

Future partitioning MAY use:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- subject,

- or workflow

according to ordering needs.

28.584 Event Replay

Replay SHALL remain idempotent and policy-aware.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.585 Selective Event Sourcing

Some domains MAY adopt event sourcing where historical state reconstruction has strong value.

28.586 Event Sourcing Scope

Event sourcing SHALL not become mandatory for every Fabric object.

28.587 CQRS Evolution

Read projections MAY separate from transactional models as scale demands.

28.588 CQRS Boundary

Read models SHALL remain projections.

28.589 Future Distributed Execution

The Fabric MAY scale from modular monolith to distributed services.

28.590 Service Extraction Trigger

Extraction SHOULD be driven by:

- scale,

- team ownership,

- security isolation,

- failure isolation,

- deployment cadence,

- or technology need.

28.591 Extraction Is Not Goal

Microservice count SHALL not be used as maturity evidence.

28.592 Registry Service Extraction

Registries MAY become a separate service.

28.593 Routing Service Extraction

Routing MAY become a low-latency dedicated service.

28.594 Execution Service Extraction

Execution orchestration MAY separate from synchronous Request handling.

28.595 Asset Service Extraction

Large media workloads MAY justify independent Asset infrastructure.

28.596 Audit Service Extraction

Audit MAY receive isolated storage and access control.

28.597 Policy Service Extraction

Policy MAY become a central high-assurance decision service.

28.598 Cross-Service Identity

Canonical IDs SHALL remain stable across extraction.

28.599 Cross-Service Transactions

Distributed transactions SHALL be avoided where durable event coordination or sagas are more appropriate.

28.600 Saga Evolution

Complex multi-system workflows MAY adopt explicit Sagas.

28.601 Compensation Evolution

Compensation SHALL remain semantically truthful and separately evidenced.

28.602 Distributed Locking

Future distributed concurrency MAY require:

- leases,

- fencing,

- or consensus-backed coordination.

28.603 Exactly-Once Future Claim

Even future distributed infrastructure SHOULD avoid claiming exactly-once end-to-end side effects unless formally proven for the relevant scope.

28.604 Multi-Region Evolution

Future production MAY span regions.

28.605 Region Policy

Data residency SHALL constrain regional execution.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.606 Region Failover

Failover SHALL not move protected data into an ineligible region.

28.607 Region Cost

Regional pricing MAY influence routing after eligibility.

28.608 Region Health

Health SHALL remain region-specific.

28.609 Multi-Region Identity

Canonical objects SHALL not receive different identities merely because replicas exist.

28.610 Data Replication

Replication SHALL preserve:

- Classification,

- encryption,

- deletion,

- and Tenant scope.

28.611 Sovereign Storage

Some Tenants MAY require region- or jurisdiction-bound storage.

28.612 Private Cloud

The Fabric MAY support private-cloud deployments through the same canonical contracts.

28.613 Hybrid Cloud

Local, private and public resources MAY coexist in one Plan.

28.614 Placement Policy

Placement SHALL remain explicit and policy-governed.

28.615 Confidential Computing

Future sensitive workloads MAY use trusted execution environments.

28.616 Confidential Computing Evidence

Attestation MAY become part of resource eligibility.

28.617 Hardware Attestation

Nodes MAY provide hardware-backed trust evidence.

28.618 Attestation Is Not Full Trust

Attestation proves selected properties, not overall semantic safety.

28.619 Future Secret Architecture

Secret handling MAY evolve toward:

- hardware-backed keys,

- dynamic Credentials,

- workload identity,

- short-lived Tokens,

- and delegated capability Tokens.

28.620 Dynamic Credential

Short-lived Credentials SHOULD reduce long-lived Secret exposure.

28.621 Workload Identity

Services MAY authenticate directly without static API keys where Providers support it.

28.622 Secretless Provider Integration

Some Providers MAY support delegated OAuth or workload federation.

28.623 Secret Migration

Credential mechanism changes SHALL preserve Connection identity where practical.

28.624 Future Economic Governance

The Cost Engine MAY evolve into broader economic optimisation.

28.625 Cost Forecasting

Future models MAY forecast:

- workload,

- credits,

- subscriptions,

- local compute cost,

- and provider spend.

28.626 Subscription Optimisation

The Fabric MAY recommend plan changes based on observed usage.

28.627 Autonomous Subscription Change

Actual subscription purchase or cancellation SHALL remain within explicit financial authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.628 Credit Allocation

Omnira-managed credits MAY be allocated dynamically across Projects under Budget policy.

28.629 Internal Cost

Future economics MAY include:

- infrastructure,

- GPU depreciation,

- storage,

- energy,

- human review,

- and opportunity cost.

28.630 Cost of Quality

Routing MAY optimise cost per accepted result rather than cost per call.

28.631 Cost of Failure

Retry waste and rejected Candidates SHOULD influence resource selection.

28.632 Economic Learning

Cost learning SHALL remain evidence-based and scoped.

28.633 Future Quality Architecture

Quality evaluation MAY become continuous and task-specific.

28.634 Continuous Evaluation

Production samples MAY be evaluated under privacy and cost policy.

28.635 Quality Model

A future Quality Model MAY predict likely acceptance before expensive execution.

28.636 Quality Prediction Use

Prediction MAY assist routing and Candidate count.

28.637 Quality Prediction Limitation

Prediction SHALL not replace mandatory deterministic gates or human review where required.

28.638 Human Preference Learning

User choices MAY improve Project-specific ranking.

28.639 Preference Learning Governance

Preference learning SHALL preserve:

- scope,

- source,

- confidence,

- and challenge.

28.640 Quality Floor Evolution

Quality Floors MAY differ by:

- Project,

- medium,

- audience,

- and side effect.

28.641 Automatic Candidate Selection

The Fabric MAY select among Candidates automatically when policy and evidence permit.

28.642 Automatic Canonical Acceptance

High-risk creative acceptance SHOULD remain human-governed until mature evidence and Mandates justify change.

28.643 Future Rights Architecture

Rights governance MAY integrate:

- licence databases,

- content credentials,

- provenance standards,

- and automated rights checks.

28.644 Content Credentials

Assets MAY carry signed provenance metadata.

28.645 Synthetic Media Metadata

Generated media MAY embed machine-readable origin information.

28.646 Rights Verification Service

Future systems MAY query authoritative rights sources.

28.647 Rights Uncertainty

Automated checks SHALL still preserve unknown or disputed state.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.648 Consent Evolution

Consent MAY become more granular and user-managed.

28.649 Consent Dashboard

Users MAY inspect and revoke active use permissions.

28.650 Consent Propagation

Revocation SHALL trigger affected Asset, Memory and workflow review.

28.651 Future Privacy Architecture

Privacy may become increasingly automated while remaining conservative.

28.652 Privacy-Preserving Routing

Routing MAY prefer:

- local,

- regional,

- encrypted,

- or confidential-compute resources

based on data.

28.653 Automated Data Classification

Classification Models MAY improve with use.

Automatic lowering SHALL remain prohibited unless explicit governance later changes this rule.

28.654 Sensitive Entity Detection

Future classifiers MAY detect:

- personal data,

- health data,

- child data,

- Secrets,

- financial data,

- and biometrics.

28.655 Context Redaction

Automated minimisation MAY redact or transform data before external inference.

28.656 Local Transformation Before External Use

Sensitive raw data MAY be processed locally into safer derived context before eligible external execution.

28.657 Transformation Evidence

Such transformations SHALL remain attributable.

28.658 Privacy Budget

Future systems MAY track cumulative privacy exposure as a governance concept distinct from financial Budget.

28.659 Privacy Budget Is Not Permission

A numerical privacy metric SHALL not override categorical policy.

28.660 Future Memory Architecture

Memory MAY become richer but SHALL remain governed.

28.661 Memory Graph

A future Intelligence Graph MAY represent relationships among:

- Projects,

- people,

- decisions,

- Assets,

- sources,

- workflows,

- and learning.

28.662 Graph Is Projection

The Intelligence Graph SHALL not replace source records automatically.

28.663 Memory Conflict Resolution

Conflicting Memory MAY use:

- recency,

- source authority,

- confidence,

- and human review.

28.664 Temporal Memory

Future Memory MAY support validity intervals and historical truth.

28.665 Contextual Memory

Memory retrieval MAY adapt to task, Project and Agent role.

28.666 Memory Compression

Large histories MAY be compressed into Derived Learning.

Compression SHALL preserve source linkage.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.667 Memory Forgetting

Expired, revoked or invalidated Memory SHALL stop influencing active behaviour.

28.668 Memory Portability

Memory SHOULD remain portable across Providers and Models.

28.669 Memory Encryption

Sensitive Memory MAY require Project- or user-specific encryption keys.

28.670 Future Approval Architecture

Approval MAY become more efficient without weakening informed consent or authority.

28.671 Approval Templates

Recurring action classes MAY use predefined Approval Templates.

28.672 Approval Simulation

The UI MAY preview consequences before approval.

28.673 Risk-Adaptive Approval

Low-risk familiar actions MAY use lighter interaction while high-risk actions receive stronger confirmation.

28.674 Approval Automation

Some Decisions MAY become policy-driven under Standing Mandates.

28.675 No Invisible Approval

Automated authority SHALL always derive from explicit prior human delegation.

28.676 Cryptographic Approval

Future approvals MAY use signed artefacts bound to exact Plan hashes.

28.677 Hardware Approval

High-risk approval MAY use hardware-backed confirmation.

28.678 Multi-Party Approval

Critical actions MAY require quorum or threshold signatures.

28.679 Future Autonomy

Autonomy MAY expand only after:

- reliability,

- Quality,

- policy,

- audit,

- Incident Response,

- and user trust

are proven.

28.680 Autonomy Promotion Path

A future autonomy promotion SHOULD follow:

1. recommendation only.

2. preparation only.

3. shadow execution.

4. low-risk reversible execution.

5. bounded standing Mandate.

6. domain management.

7. periodic recertification.

28.681 Autonomy Evidence

Promotion SHALL consider:

- success rate,

- correction rate,

- boundary violations,

- Incident history,

- cost accuracy,

- and user satisfaction.

28.682 Autonomy Demotion

Authority MAY automatically narrow after policy-defined risk conditions.

28.683 Autonomy Expansion Approval

Authority SHALL not automatically broaden based solely on performance.

28.684 Future Executive Intelligence

Executive Intelligence MAY use Fabric evidence to coordinate Projects.

28.685 Executive Intelligence Boundary

Executive Intelligence MAY decide priorities and recommend actions.

Actual intelligence execution SHALL still use Fabric Capabilities.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.686 Cross-Project Intelligence

Cross-Project aggregation SHALL require explicit authority and data policy.

28.687 Project Confidentiality

Executive views SHALL not dissolve Project privacy.

28.688 Future Manager Layer

Manager Agents MAY coordinate workflows, budgets and review queues through the Fabric.

28.689 Manager Authority

Managers SHALL receive domain-specific Mandates rather than universal Agent power.

28.690 Future Business Automation

Omnira MAY eventually manage broad operational workflows for Projects.

28.691 Business Automation Boundary

Actions such as:

- publishing,

- messaging,

- purchasing,

- scheduling,

- and file mutation

SHALL remain separately governed Capabilities.

28.692 Full Autonomous Company Operation

A future autonomous operating mode MAY exist only through layered Mandates, budgets, audit and user stop authority.

28.693 User Sovereignty

No future stage SHALL remove the user’s ability to:

- inspect,

- restrict,

- revoke,

- stop,

- and challenge

Agent authority within applicable platform and safety constraints.

28.694 Future User-Owned Intelligence

Users MAY connect their own Models, Accounts and private compute.

28.695 User-Owned Provider

User ownership SHALL not exempt Provider use from Project policy.

28.696 User-Owned Local Node

User ownership SHALL not exempt local execution from Asset, Evidence or Quality governance.

28.697 Future Omnira-Managed Intelligence

Omnira MAY offer managed Plans or credits across Providers.

28.698 Managed Provider Abstraction

Users MAY interact with one Omnira billing layer while underlying Provider evidence remains traceable.

28.699 Managed Routing Transparency

Omnira-managed routing SHALL still expose material data custody and rights information.

28.700 Future Third-Party Extensions

Third-party developers MAY build:

- Adapters,

- Tools,

- Agents,

- workflow packages,

- evaluators,

- and local Runtime integrations.

28.701 Extension Package

Every extension SHOULD declare:

- identity,

- Version,

- publisher,

- permissions,

- Capabilities,

- dependencies,

- data access,

- side effects,

- and conformance.

28.702 Extension Signing

Packages MAY be signed.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.703 Extension Trust

Publisher reputation SHALL not replace verification.

28.704 Extension Sandbox

Third-party code SHALL receive stronger isolation.

28.705 Extension Revocation

Compromised packages SHALL be revocable.

28.706 Extension Update

Updates SHALL not receive expanded permissions automatically.

28.707 Future Conformance

Conformance MAY become increasingly automated and continuous.

28.708 Continuous Certification

Runtime evidence MAY maintain Certification freshness.

28.709 Certification Expiry

Time, drift or Incident MAY still suspend eligibility.

28.710 Formal Verification

Critical policy and state machines MAY receive formal proofs.

28.711 Proof Scope

Formal proof applies only to the specified model and assumptions.

28.712 Runtime Verification

Production invariants MAY be continuously checked.

28.713 Policy Conformance Monitor

A runtime monitor MAY detect actions inconsistent with active policy.

28.714 Architecture Conformance Monitor

Dependency and network observation MAY detect Fabric bypass.

28.715 Future Observability

Observability MAY incorporate:

- causal graphs,

- predictive health,

- anomaly detection,

- cost forecasting,

- and autonomous incident assistance.

28.716 Observability Intelligence

Models MAY analyse telemetry.

Their conclusions SHALL remain evidence-linked.

28.717 Incident Copilot Evolution

Incident Agents MAY:

- correlate evidence,

- draft timelines,

- propose containment,

- and prepare communication.

28.718 Incident Commander Boundary

High-impact Incident command SHALL remain human-governed until separately authorised.

28.719 Automatic Low-Risk Recovery

Well-understood reversible failures MAY recover automatically under Runbook Mandates.

28.720 Future Audit

Audit MAY use stronger cryptographic integrity and selective disclosure.

28.721 Audit Proof

Users or auditors MAY verify that required Decisions occurred without receiving unrelated protected data.

28.722 Future Resilience

The Fabric MAY support:

- multi-provider failover,

- multi-region failover,

- local fallback,

- persistent job recovery,

- and disaster automation.

28.723 Resilience Without Policy Escape

Failover SHALL always preserve governance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.724 Future Sustainability

Routing MAY consider environmental cost where reliable evidence exists.

28.725 Sustainability Metric

Energy or carbon estimates SHALL remain separate from Quality and privacy requirements.

28.726 Sustainable Routing

Lower-energy resources MAY be preferred after mandatory eligibility.

28.727 Future Regulatory Evolution

New laws, standards or Provider terms MAY require policy changes.

28.728 Regulatory Update

Regulatory change SHALL enter through reviewed policy and architecture change, not ad hoc Agent instructions.

28.729 Jurisdiction

Tenant or Project jurisdiction MAY constrain:

- data residency,

- Providers,

- retention,

- and rights.

28.730 Future Standard Adoption

The Fabric SHOULD adopt useful external standards where they strengthen interoperability.

28.731 Standard Boundary

External standards SHALL map into canonical Omnira semantics.

28.732 Standard Supremacy Prohibition

An external protocol SHALL not override user or Project policy.

28.733 Future API Evolution

Public or internal Fabric APIs MAY gain broader Capability discovery and workflow submission.

28.734 API Stability

Stable canonical operations SHOULD change slowly.

28.735 Capability Negotiation

Clients MAY negotiate supported schema and Capability Versions.

28.736 Future SDKs

SDKs MAY exist for several languages and Agent frameworks.

28.737 SDK Conformance

Every SDK SHALL implement the same core semantics.

28.738 Future CLI

CLI MAY become a full operational interface while preserving authority.

28.739 Future UI

The user interface MAY expose:

- Fabric decisions,

- cost,

- privacy,

- providers,

- approvals,

- local Nodes,

- and autonomy

in increasingly understandable ways.

28.740 Fabric Explainability

Users SHOULD be able to understand why a route or approval was chosen without seeing hidden reasoning.

28.741 Decision Explanation

Explanations SHOULD cite:

- policy,

- constraints,

- evidence,

- and major trade-offs.

28.742 Future User Controls

Users MAY configure:

- default Routing Profile,

- Provider preferences,

- privacy posture,

- budgets,

- local-first behaviour,

- and approval thresholds.

28.743 User Preference Boundaries

Preferences SHALL not weaken non-waivable policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
sectionTitles: 28.760 Open Source Does Not Mean Free of Risk
text:
28.744 Future Project Templates

Projects MAY inherit approved Fabric policy templates.

28.745 Project Template

A template MAY define:

- allowed Providers,

- default Budget,

- Quality Floors,

- publication authority,

- retention,

- and local-first rules.

28.746 Template Override

Projects MAY tighten inherited policy.

Loosening platform minimums SHALL be prohibited.

28.747 Future Tenant Administration

Multi-Tenant Omnira MAY support delegated governance.

28.748 Tenant Policy

Tenant policy MAY constrain all Projects inside the Tenant.

28.749 Project Policy

Project policy MAY be stricter.

28.750 Policy Precedence

The more restrictive applicable policy SHALL govern unless an explicit higher-level exception mechanism exists.

28.751 Future Federation

Independent Omnira installations MAY exchange bounded Capabilities or Agents.

28.752 Federated Identity

Federation SHALL require verifiable external identity and trust.

28.753 Federated Data

Data SHALL not cross installations without explicit transfer authority.

28.754 Federated Agent

An Agent from another Fabric SHALL not become a local trusted Principal automatically.

28.755 Federated Capability

Remote intelligence MAY appear as an external Provider-like resource.

28.756 Future Marketplace Economics

Omnira MAY support billing across third-party resources.

28.757 Marketplace Settlement

Financial settlement SHALL remain separate from Capability selection.

28.758 Future Licensing

Commercial distribution of extensions MAY require licence metadata.

28.759 Future Open Source Integration

Open-source Models and Tools SHALL still require:

- licence,

- integrity,

- conformance,

- and operational review.

28.760 Open Source Does Not Mean Free of Risk

Security, data and commercial obligations remain.

28.761 Future Proprietary Integration

Closed Providers SHALL still expose enough metadata for governance.

28.762 Unknown Provider Internal Behaviour

Opaque Provider implementation SHALL increase uncertainty rather than disappear from evaluation.

28.763 Future Migration Between Providers

Provider exit SHALL be a normal supported lifecycle.

28.764 Provider Exit Plan

Critical Providers SHOULD have an exit strategy where practical.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.765 Asset Portability

Canonical Assets SHOULD remain accessible independent of Provider retention.

28.766 Memory Portability

Canonical Memory SHALL remain Provider-independent.

28.767 Workflow Portability

Plans and workflows SHOULD reference Capabilities rather than one Provider.

28.768 Agent Portability

Agents SHALL remain portable across Models.

28.769 Future Cost Shock

A Provider price increase SHALL not force architecture change.

28.770 Future Provider Shutdown

Provider discontinuation SHALL trigger route and Connection migration.

28.771 Provider Shutdown Assets

Existing Assets and Evidence SHALL remain accessible where Omnira has ingested them.

28.772 Future Account Loss

Loss of one external Account SHALL not erase canonical Project history.

28.773 Future Credential Compromise

Credential replacement SHALL not change historical identity.

28.774 Future Node Loss

Loss of one local Node SHALL not corrupt canonical state.

28.775 Future Model Removal

Removed local Models SHALL remain historical Registry records.

28.776 Future Architecture Replatforming

The Fabric MAY change:

- database,

- queue,

- object store,

- observability,

- orchestration engine,

- policy engine,

- or deployment platform

without redefining its canonical domain model unnecessarily.

28.777 Replatforming Rule

Technology replacement SHALL occur behind stable interfaces.

28.778 Replatforming Evidence

Migration SHALL verify semantic equivalence.

28.779 Replatforming Rollback

High-risk replatforming SHALL retain recovery path.

28.780 Future Monolith-to-Service Evolution

The Stage 1 modular monolith MAY remain indefinitely if it satisfies scale, reliability and governance.

Distribution is optional.

28.781 Future Service-to-Monolith Consolidation

Services MAY also be recombined if complexity outweighs benefit.

28.782 Architecture Serves Goals

Deployment style SHALL remain subordinate to user and platform outcomes.

28.783 Future Performance Evolution

Optimisation MAY include:

- caching,

- batching,

- speculative execution,

- prewarming,

- parallel Candidates,

- and streaming.

28.784 Cache Governance

Caching SHALL preserve:

- Project,

- Classification,

- Version,

- and expiry.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.785 Batch Governance

Batching SHALL not mix incompatible Tenant or data scopes.

28.786 Speculative Execution

Speculative Provider calls MAY increase cost.

They require economic policy.

28.787 Speculative Side Effect Prohibition

Speculation SHALL not be used for irreversible side effects.

28.788 Parallel Candidate Generation

Parallel generation MAY improve latency at higher cost.

Budget SHALL govern it.

28.789 Prewarming Local Models

Prewarming MAY improve latency while consuming local resources.

28.790 Future Capacity Planning

Forecasts MAY drive Node, Provider and subscription planning.

28.791 Future Scheduling

Scheduling MAY become deadline-aware and globally optimised.

28.792 Scheduling Policy

Optimisation SHALL remain subordinate to Project priority, fairness and Budget.

28.793 Future Quota Markets

Internal allocation mechanisms MAY distribute scarce capacity among Projects.

28.794 Quota Allocation

Scarcity management SHALL remain transparent and policy-governed.

28.795 Future Reliability Evolution

Recovery may become increasingly automated.

28.796 Predictive Provider Failure

The Fabric MAY shift traffic before confirmed outage when evidence supports risk.

28.797 Prediction Uncertainty

Predictive Routing SHALL retain uncertainty.

28.798 Multi-Path Redundancy

Critical workflows MAY use redundant non-side-effect execution.

28.799 Redundant Generation

Two Providers MAY generate Candidates for comparison.

Cost SHALL remain explicit.

28.800 Redundant Publication Prohibition

Publication SHALL not use redundant side-effect execution without idempotent design and explicit reason.

28.801 Future Unknown Outcome Reduction

Providers with stronger idempotency and status APIs MAY receive reliability preference.

28.802 Reliability Reputation

Historical recovery quality MAY influence Routing.

28.803 Future Data Architecture

The Fabric MAY evolve toward richer knowledge and analytics systems.

28.804 Operational Analytics

Operational analytics SHALL use minimised, scoped data.

28.805 Cross-Project Analytics

Cross-Project aggregation SHALL require explicit purpose and authority.

28.806 User Analytics

User behaviour SHALL not be collected merely because it may improve routing.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.807 Analytics Consent

Relevant consent and privacy policy SHALL apply.

28.808 Future Data Lake

A data lake SHALL not become an uncontrolled copy of Fabric data.

28.809 Data Lake Governance

Any analytics store SHALL preserve:

- Tenant,

- Project,

- Classification,

- retention,

- and access.

28.810 Future Evaluation Lake

Evaluation data MAY have separate storage and retention.

28.811 Future Synthetic Data

Synthetic data MAY support testing and evaluation without exposing real Project data.

28.812 Synthetic Data Provenance

Synthetic datasets SHALL record generation method and limitations.

28.813 Future Digital Twins

Digital twins MAY model:

- Providers,

- workflows,

- Agents,

- Projects,

- and infrastructure.

28.814 Digital Twin Is Simulation

Simulation results SHALL not be treated as production fact.

28.815 Future Planning

Planner capabilities MAY become increasingly sophisticated.

28.816 Planner Search

The Planner MAY explore several Plan alternatives.

28.817 Plan Optimisation

Optimisation MAY consider:

- Quality,

- cost,

- latency,

- privacy,

- reliability,

- and human review.

28.818 Planner Self-Evaluation

The Planner MAY evaluate Plan risks before execution.

28.819 Planner Authority Boundary

A better Plan does not create authority.

28.820 Planner Learning

Historical outcomes MAY inform future Planning after reviewed learning.

28.821 Future Intent Understanding

Intent parsing MAY become more automated.

28.822 Ambiguous Intent

High-impact ambiguity SHALL still require user clarification or approval.

28.823 Intent Memory

User preferences MAY help interpret ordinary requests.

They SHALL not override explicit current instruction.

28.824 Future Natural-Language Policy

Users MAY define policies conversationally.

Those policies SHALL compile into explicit reviewable rules.

28.825 Policy Confirmation

Material policy changes SHALL show their interpreted scope before activation.

28.826 Future Governance Automation

Governance MAY become easier, not weaker.

28.827 Automatic Policy Proposal

The Fabric MAY suggest tighter controls based on incidents or use.

28.828 Automatic Policy Tightening

Some emergency safety controls MAY narrow access automatically under approved policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
sectionTitles: 28.832 Compliance Is Not One Universal Mode
text:
28.829 Automatic Policy Loosening

Automatic loosening SHOULD remain prohibited.

28.830 Future Compliance

Tenant-specific compliance requirements MAY map into Conformance Profiles.

28.831 Compliance Profile

A profile MAY define additional:

- retention,

- region,

- audit,

- approval,

- and Provider requirements.

28.832 Compliance Is Not One Universal Mode

Different Projects and jurisdictions may require different controls.

28.833 Future Auditors

External auditors MAY access selective proofs and exports.

28.834 Auditor Access

Audit access SHALL not become broad production access.

28.835 Future Insurance or Assurance

Operational evidence MAY support external assurance without exposing unnecessary user data.

28.836 Future Disaster Recovery

Recovery MAY use:

- replicated metadata,

- offsite backups,

- alternate regions,

- and private Nodes.

28.837 Recovery Independence

Critical backups SHOULD not depend solely on the same Provider as production.

28.838 Recovery Drills

Future systems SHALL continue exercising recovery.

28.839 Future Project Growth

The Fabric SHALL scale from a few Projects to many without dissolving Project boundaries.

28.840 Project Template Scaling

Templates MAY reduce configuration duplication.

28.841 Project Budget Scaling

Budget governance MAY aggregate across portfolios while preserving Project attribution.

28.842 Project Provider Policies

Different Projects MAY intentionally use different Providers.

28.843 Project Agent Families

Several Agents MAY collaborate within one Project under separate roles.

28.844 Future Organisation Structure

Tenants MAY have:

- departments,

- teams,

- portfolios,

- and Project groups.

28.845 Organisational Hierarchy

Authority SHALL follow explicit hierarchy and scope.

28.846 Future User Collaboration

Several humans MAY jointly own or operate Projects.

28.847 Collaborative Approval

Approval groups MAY reflect organisational roles.

28.848 Future Child and Family Projects

Projects involving children SHALL continue to receive stronger privacy and consent defaults.

28.849 Future Health Projects

Health-related Projects SHALL receive stronger privacy and local-processing options.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.850 Future Financial Projects

Financial workflows SHALL require stronger authority and auditing.

28.851 Future High-Risk Domains

The Fabric SHALL support stricter Profiles rather than inventing parallel architectures.

28.852 Architecture Review Cadence

The canonical architecture SHOULD receive periodic review.

28.853 Review Triggers

Review MAY be triggered by:

- major Provider change,

- new protocol,

- major Incident,

- regulatory change,

- scaling limit,

- new autonomy stage,

- or implementation mismatch.

28.854 Architecture Drift

Architecture Drift occurs when implementation behaviour differs materially from canonical contracts.

28.855 Drift Detection

Drift MAY be detected by:

- code dependency tests,

- Conformance,

- audit,

- operational evidence,

- or manual review.

28.856 Drift Classification

Drift MAY be:

- intentional pending approval,

- accidental,

- emergency,

- deprecated,

- or non-conformant.

28.857 Drift Correction

Unapproved drift SHALL be corrected or brought through canonical architecture change.

28.858 Emergency Drift

Emergency implementation changes SHALL receive retrospective review.

28.859 Architecture Debt

Known deviations MAY become Architecture Debt only if:

- explicit,

- owned,

- bounded,

- temporary,

- and safe enough to tolerate.

28.860 Architecture Debt Record

It SHOULD include:

- debtId,

- violated contract,

- reason,

- risk,

- compensating control,

- owner,

- due date,

- and state.

28.861 Architecture Debt Expiry

High-risk architecture debt SHALL not remain open indefinitely.

28.862 Debt Closure

Closure requires verified conformance.

28.863 Future Book Revision

A future Intelligence Fabric v2 may revise this architecture.

28.864 Revision Requirement

Revision SHALL preserve:

- prior Version,

- changelog,

- migration guidance,

- and rationale.

28.865 Canonical Supersession

A new canonical edition MAY supersede this edition.

Historical executions SHALL remain interpreted according to the contract active at their time.

28.866 Canonical Changelog

Material contract changes SHALL appear in a changelog.

28.867 Compatibility Statement

New editions SHOULD state:

- compatible areas,

- breaking areas,

- migration requirements,

- and deprecated concepts.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.868 No Silent Canonical Rewrite

Historical canonical documents SHALL not be edited silently to match future implementation.

28.869 Future Knowledge Integration

Approved books MAY become machine-consumable knowledge for Atlas and other Agents.

28.870 Knowledge Projection

Embeddings, graphs and summaries SHALL retain source links to the canonical book.

28.871 Machine Interpretation

Machine-derived summaries SHALL not outrank source chapters.

28.872 Knowledge Versioning

Agent knowledge SHALL identify which book Version it derives from.

28.873 Future Self-Documentation

The Fabric MAY generate implementation documentation from canonical schemas and contracts.

28.874 Generated Documentation

Generated documentation SHALL link to source Version.

28.875 Future Self-Audit

The Fabric MAY continuously evaluate its own conformance.

28.876 Self-Audit Limits

Self-audit SHALL be independently testable and shall not certify itself without required governance.

28.877 Future Self-Healing

Low-risk components MAY repair known failures automatically.

28.878 Self-Healing Boundary

Self-healing SHALL not:

- broaden authority,

- delete Evidence,

- lower privacy,

- or create unapproved spend.

28.879 Future Self-Optimisation

The Fabric MAY tune:

- routing,

- batching,

- local Model residency,

- queue priority,

- and Candidate count

inside explicit policy.

28.880 Self-Optimisation Evidence

Optimisation changes SHALL be observable and reversible.

28.881 Future Autonomous Fabric Operations

The Fabric itself MAY receive bounded operational Mandates for:

- health recovery,

- capacity management,

- certification refresh,

- and cost optimisation.

28.882 Fabric Self-Authority Prohibition

The Fabric SHALL not grant itself broader authority.

28.883 Future Human Experience

The long-term user experience SHOULD make complex governance understandable without requiring infrastructure expertise.

28.884 User Intent First

Users SHOULD express goals and constraints rather than Provider-specific implementation detail.

28.885 Expert Override

Advanced users MAY pin resources or inspect technical details.

28.886 Expert Override Boundary

Technical override SHALL not bypass non-waivable security and isolation policy.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.887 Progressive Disclosure

Interfaces SHOULD show simple summaries first with deeper technical detail available.

28.888 Cost Transparency

Users SHOULD always be able to understand paid implications before consequential spend.

28.889 Data Transparency

Users SHOULD understand when data leaves local or Project-controlled boundaries.

28.890 Provider Transparency

Abstraction SHALL not hide who processed protected data.

28.891 Autonomy Transparency

Users SHOULD understand what Agents may do without asking again.

28.892 Revocation Simplicity

Users SHOULD be able to stop or narrow autonomy easily.

28.893 Future Competitive Advantage

The Fabric’s strategic value lies not in one Provider integration but in:

- persistent Agent identity,

- capability-first routing,

- cost control,

- privacy-aware placement,

- multimodal orchestration,

- provenance,

- governed Memory,

- and bounded autonomy.

28.894 Provider Commoditisation

As Models become interchangeable, canonical capability and governance become more valuable.

28.895 Model Improvement

Model improvements SHOULD strengthen outcomes without requiring platform redesign.

28.896 Provider Failure

Provider failure SHOULD degrade one route, not break Agent identity.

28.897 Local Compute Improvement

New local hardware SHOULD become an additional resource, not a parallel architecture.

28.898 New Protocol Improvement

New protocols SHOULD become Adapter or Connector opportunities, not governance bypasses.

28.899 Future Family of Intelligence

The Fabric SHOULD eventually coordinate:

- external AI,

- local AI,

- human intelligence,

- deterministic Tools,

- search,

- retrieval,

- Agents,

- and specialised services

through one canonical resource model.

28.900 Human Intelligence as Resource

Human-assisted work SHALL remain a legitimate first-class resource class.

28.901 Human Replacement Is Not Goal

Automation SHOULD be used where it improves outcomes, cost, speed or consistency without sacrificing governance.

28.902 Human Review Value

Human judgement remains especially important for:

- child-facing content,

- publication,

- identity consistency,

- ambiguous rights,

- high-impact decisions,

- and strategic work.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.903 Future Fully Automated Low-Risk Work

Low-risk repetitive work MAY become highly autonomous.

28.904 Future High-Risk Human Gate

High-risk irreversible work MAY remain human-approved indefinitely.

28.905 Architecture Neutrality

The Fabric SHALL not assume that maximum autonomy is the desired end state for every Capability.

28.906 Stage Transition

Transition from one maturity stage to another SHALL require explicit readiness evidence.

28.907 Stage Readiness

Readiness SHOULD include:

- conformance,

- reliability,

- privacy,

- cost,

- quality,

- audit,

- incidents,

- and user control.

28.908 Stage Regression

A Project MAY move back to lower autonomy or narrower capability after Incident or preference change.

28.909 Maturity Is Reversible

More automation is not an irreversible progression.

28.910 Future Legacy

Every future implementation SHALL eventually become legacy.

Therefore:

- identity,

- evidence,

- migration,

- and deprecation

must be designed from the beginning.

28.911 Migration Success Criteria

Migration architecture succeeds when:

- existing useful workflows continue,

- direct Provider coupling decreases,

- Credentials become governed,

- Project scope remains correct,

- Assets gain truthful canonical identity,

- new Evidence is complete,

- legacy uncertainty remains labelled,

- and old paths retire safely.

28.912 Rollout Success Criteria

Rollout succeeds when:

- adoption expands through bounded cohorts,

- canaries provide useful evidence,

- failures trigger pause or rollback,

- users retain control,

- and governance works before autonomy grows.

28.913 Anti-Pattern Success Criteria

Anti-pattern governance succeeds when:

- architectural shortcuts are detected,

- temporary exceptions remain temporary,

- Provider-specific coupling stays contained,

- and implementation does not quietly diverge from the book.

28.914 Future Evolution Success Criteria

Future evolution succeeds when:

- new Models and Providers enter without rewriting Agents,

- new protocols map into canonical boundaries,

- local and external intelligence coexist,

- scale can increase without losing isolation,

- autonomy can expand without losing authority,

- and historical truth remains reconstructable.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.915 Migration Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- migrations fabricate provenance,

- legacy authority is broadened,

- Credentials are exposed,

- dual execution creates duplicate side effects,

- or direct Provider bypass remains hidden after declared completion.

28.916 Rollout Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- canaries have no abort criteria,

- user-visible impact is not monitored,

- failed rollout cannot be stopped,

- or temporary feature flags become permanent hidden architectures.

28.917 Evolution Failure Conditions

The architecture is non-conformant when:

- new technology bypasses canonical contracts,

- stronger Models receive wider authority automatically,

- new protocols define policy,

- or implementation convenience silently replaces source architecture.

28.918 Canonical Migration Plan Contract

The following requirements define Migration Plans:

1. Every material Migration Plan SHALL have stable identity and Version.

2. Objective SHALL be explicit.

3. Owner SHALL be explicit.

4. Source architecture SHALL be explicit.

5. Target architecture SHALL be explicit.

6. Affected Tenant and Projects SHALL be explicit.

7. Affected Capabilities SHALL be explicit.

8. Affected Agents SHALL be explicit.

9. Affected Providers and Accounts SHALL be explicit.

10. Affected Credentials SHALL be explicit by reference.

11. Affected data SHALL be explicit.

12. Dependencies SHALL be explicit.

13. Migration phases SHALL be explicit.

14. Verification SHALL be explicit.

15. Rollback SHALL be explicit.

16. Completion criteria SHALL be explicit.

17. Authority changes SHALL be explicit.

18. Data custody changes SHALL be explicit.

19. Historical evidence SHALL remain preserved.

20. Migration SHALL NOT broaden authority or invent provenance.

28.919 Canonical Migration Inventory Contract

The following requirements define legacy inventory:

1. Every known production intelligence path SHALL be inventoried.

2. Caller SHALL be explicit.

3. Project SHALL be explicit.

4. Capability SHALL be explicit.

5. Provider and Product SHALL be explicit where known.

6. Model SHALL be explicit where known.

7. SDK or protocol SHALL be explicit.

8. Credential location SHALL be identified without exposing Secret value.

9. Account SHALL be identified where possible.

10. data classes SHALL be identified.

11. cost SHALL be identified where possible.

12. retries SHALL be identified.

13. side effects SHALL be identified.

14. Memory use SHALL be identified.

15. publication SHALL be identified.

16. direct Fabric bypass SHALL be flagged.

17. unknown fields SHALL remain unknown.

18. migration priority SHALL be assigned.

19. owner SHALL be assigned.

20. Inventory SHALL NOT require destructive inspection.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.920 Canonical Credential Migration Contract

The following requirements define Credential migration:

1. Every migrated Credential SHALL map to one canonical Credential Reference.

2. owner SHALL be explicit.

3. Provider Account SHALL be explicit.

4. Tenant and Project scope SHALL be explicit.

5. Environment SHALL be explicit.

6. Secret SHALL move into approved storage.

7. raw Secret SHALL not enter migration reports.

8. exposed legacy Secrets SHOULD be rotated.

9. old references SHALL be retired.

10. code SHALL resolve Credentials only through approved boundary.

11. logs SHALL not contain Secret values.

12. backups and config copies SHALL be reviewed.

13. revoked Credentials SHALL remain revoked.

14. departed-owner Credentials SHALL be reviewed.

15. personal and Project Accounts SHALL remain distinct.

16. migration SHALL be audited.

17. rollback SHALL not reactivate compromised Secrets.

18. Connection health SHALL be verified after migration.

19. historical Secret values SHALL not be retained unnecessarily.

20. Credential migration SHALL NOT become a broad sharing mechanism.

28.921 Canonical Legacy Data Import Contract

The following requirements define import of legacy data:

1. Every imported object SHALL preserve source identity where available.

2. import source SHALL be explicit.

3. import time SHALL be explicit.

4. Project SHALL be explicit.

5. Classification SHALL be explicit.

6. checksum SHALL be used for files where practical.

7. known provenance SHALL be preserved.

8. unknown provenance SHALL remain unknown.

9. rights SHALL remain explicit.

10. Consent SHALL remain explicit.

11. historical Version SHALL not be invented.

12. legacy execution SHALL not be fabricated.

13. audit SHALL not be fabricated.

14. derived fields SHALL be labelled.

15. defaulted fields SHALL be labelled where material.

16. deleted objects SHALL not be reactivated.

17. revoked objects SHALL not be reactivated.

18. historical uncertainty SHALL remain visible.

19. import SHALL be reversible until verified where practical.

20. Legacy import SHALL NOT manufacture canonical certainty.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.922 Canonical Shadow and Dual-Run Contract

The following requirements define comparative migration:

1. Shadow Mode SHALL have stable rollout identity.

2. shadow scope SHALL be explicit.

3. shadow results SHALL be non-authoritative.

4. shadow work SHALL not create consequential side effects.

5. shadow cost SHALL be visible.

6. shadow data SHALL satisfy policy independently.

7. comparison Metrics SHALL be explicit.

8. Dual Run SHALL be limited to safe workloads.

9. duplicate external side effects SHALL be prevented.

10. dual-run cost SHALL be bounded.

11. results SHALL remain independently attributable.

12. user-facing Output source SHALL be explicit.

13. shadow disagreement SHALL remain visible.

14. legacy behaviour SHALL not automatically be treated as correct.

15. Fabric behaviour SHALL not automatically be treated as correct.

16. comparison SHALL use approved Quality criteria.

17. evidence SHALL be retained according to policy.

18. transition decision SHALL be attributable.

19. shadow mode SHALL have exit criteria.

20. Shadow and Dual Run SHALL NOT create hidden production authority.

28.923 Canonical Canary Rollout Contract

The following requirements define canary rollout:

1. Every Canary SHALL have stable identity.

2. scope SHALL be explicit.

3. cohort SHALL be explicit.

4. start and end SHALL be explicit.

5. owner SHALL be explicit.

6. success Metrics SHALL be explicit.

7. abort thresholds SHALL be explicit.

8. rollback SHALL be defined.

9. Quality SHALL be monitored.

10. cost SHALL be monitored.

11. latency SHALL be monitored.

12. policy denials SHALL be monitored.

13. privacy SHALL be monitored.

14. authority SHALL be monitored.

15. Incidents SHALL be monitored.

16. user corrections SHOULD be monitored.

17. expansion SHALL require evidence.

18. pause SHALL be supported.

19. historical Canary evidence SHALL remain queryable.

20. Canary success SHALL NOT imply universal readiness automatically.

28.924 Canonical Cutover Contract

The following requirements define cutover:

1. Cutover scope SHALL be explicit.

2. target Fabric path SHALL be conformant.

3. source state SHALL be known.

4. in-flight work SHALL have ownership.

5. duplicate processing SHALL be prevented.

6. current authority SHALL be verified.

7. current Classification SHALL be verified.

8. Credentials SHALL be verified.

9. observability SHALL be active.

10. rollback or rollforward SHALL be defined.

11. cutover time SHALL be recorded.

12. owner SHALL be present.

13. enhanced monitoring SHALL follow cutover.

14. data integrity SHALL be verified.

15. user-facing behaviour SHALL be verified.

16. cost SHALL be verified.

17. legacy bypass SHALL be disabled where applicable.

18. direct Provider calls SHALL be monitored.

19. completion SHALL be explicitly declared.

20. Cutover SHALL NOT be considered complete from deployment alone.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.925 Canonical Rollback Contract

The following requirements define rollback:

1. Every high-risk migration SHALL define rollback or justified rollforward-only recovery.

2. rollback trigger SHALL be explicit.

3. rollback target SHALL be explicit.

4. actor and authority SHALL be explicit.

5. current deletion state SHALL be preserved.

6. current Consent SHALL be preserved.

7. current rights restrictions SHALL be preserved.

8. current revocation SHALL be preserved.

9. compromised Credentials SHALL not be restored.

10. external side effects SHALL be reconciled.

11. database compatibility SHALL be evaluated.

12. queue ownership SHALL be evaluated.

13. in-flight jobs SHALL be reconciled.

14. audit and Evidence SHALL be preserved.

15. Incident state SHALL remain.

16. result SHALL be verified.

17. user impact SHALL be assessed.

18. rollback SHALL be observable.

19. historical rollback evidence SHALL remain immutable.

20. Rollback SHALL NOT rewrite history.

28.926 Canonical Deprecation Contract

The following requirements define deprecation:

1. Every material Deprecation SHALL have stable identity.

2. subject SHALL be explicit.

3. replacement SHALL be explicit where available.

4. reason SHALL be explicit.

5. owner SHALL be explicit.

6. announcement time SHALL be explicit.

7. migration guidance SHALL be explicit.

8. deadline SHALL be explicit.

9. new use SHOULD be blocked before final retirement.

10. existing use SHALL be inventoried.

11. extensions SHALL require explicit review.

12. retirement state SHALL be explicit.

13. historical identity SHALL remain resolvable.

14. old Credentials SHALL be revoked when no longer needed.

15. old Adapters SHALL not receive new traffic.

16. old Tools SHALL not remain Agent-visible.

17. migration debt SHALL remain visible.

18. deadline changes SHALL be attributable.

19. retirement SHALL be verified.

20. Deprecation SHALL NOT become indefinite coexistence by default.

28.927 Canonical Architecture Debt Contract

The following requirements define temporary architectural deviations:

1. Every material Architecture Debt item SHALL have stable identity.

2. violated or deferred contract SHALL be explicit.

3. reason SHALL be explicit.

4. risk SHALL be explicit.

5. affected scope SHALL be explicit.

6. owner SHALL be explicit.

7. compensating control SHALL be explicit.

8. due date SHALL be explicit.

9. current state SHALL be explicit.

10. production impact SHALL be explicit.

11. privacy impact SHALL be explicit.

12. authority impact SHALL be explicit.

13. cost impact SHALL be explicit.

14. exception approval SHALL be explicit where required.

15. expiry SHALL be explicit.

16. overdue high-risk debt SHALL escalate.

17. closure SHALL require conformance verification.

18. historical debt SHALL remain queryable.

19. debt SHALL not silently become canonical.

20. Architecture Debt SHALL NOT justify new dependent bypasses.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
sectionTitles: 28.930 Canonical Local and Edge Evolution Contract
text:
28.928 Canonical Provider Evolution Contract

The following requirements define future Provider evolution:

1. New Providers SHALL enter through Provider Registry.

2. Provider Products SHALL have stable identity.

3. Accounts SHALL remain separate from Providers.

4. Adapters SHALL be Versioned.

5. Credentials SHALL remain by reference.

6. Capability evidence SHALL be required.

7. privacy evidence SHALL be required.

8. rights evidence SHALL be required.

9. cost model SHALL be defined.

10. health SHALL be observable.

11. Conformance SHALL precede production eligibility.

12. rollout SHALL be bounded.

13. Provider changes SHALL not modify Agent identity.

14. Provider removal SHALL preserve historical evidence.

15. Provider shutdown SHALL not erase canonical Assets.

16. user-owned Accounts SHALL remain governed.

17. Omnira-managed Accounts SHALL remain Project-attributable.

18. Provider diversity MAY improve resilience.

19. new Provider technology SHALL map into existing policy.

20. Provider innovation SHALL NOT bypass the Fabric boundary.

28.929 Canonical Model Evolution Contract

The following requirements define future Model evolution:

1. Every Model or Deployment SHALL have stable identity.

2. aliases SHALL remain distinct from immutable Versions.

3. Model changes SHALL be detectable.

4. Capabilities SHALL be explicit.

5. Quality evidence SHALL be Version-specific.

6. local and external Models SHALL share canonical semantics.

7. fine-tunes SHALL receive distinct identity.

8. quantisation SHALL be explicit where material.

9. Runtime SHALL be explicit for local Models.

10. context limits SHALL be verified.

11. privacy eligibility SHALL be explicit.

12. cost SHALL be explicit or estimated.

13. Conformance SHALL be maintained.

14. high-risk Model changes MAY require reapproval.

15. Model upgrade SHALL not broaden authority.

16. Model downgrade SHALL not weaken Quality Floor.

17. historical executions SHALL preserve original Model identity.

18. retired Models SHALL remain resolvable historically.

19. learned routing SHALL remain policy-subordinate.

20. Model capability SHALL NOT become permission.

28.930 Canonical Local and Edge Evolution Contract

The following requirements define future local intelligence:

1. Every Node SHALL have stable identity.

2. owner SHALL be explicit.

3. trust state SHALL be explicit.

4. Runtime SHALL be explicit.

5. hardware SHALL be attributable.

6. local Models SHALL be registered.

7. local Tools SHALL be registered.

8. Local Only SHALL remain structurally enforced.

9. offline authority SHALL be bounded.

10. network egress SHALL be policy-controlled.

11. file access SHALL be scoped.

12. device sensors SHALL require explicit Capabilities.

13. Node health SHALL be observable.

14. Node loss SHALL not cause forbidden external fallback.

15. mobile and edge Nodes SHALL reuse canonical contracts.

16. private GPU pools SHALL remain policy-governed.

17. hardware attestation MAY inform trust.

18. attestation SHALL not replace Quality or authority.

19. historical Node executions SHALL remain reconstructable.

20. Local ownership SHALL NOT create governance exemption.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.931 Canonical Agent Evolution Contract

The following requirements define future Agents:

1. Agent identity SHALL remain Omnira-owned.

2. Agent role SHALL remain explicit.

3. Agent authority SHALL remain bounded.

4. Model identity SHALL remain separate.

5. Provider identity SHALL remain separate.

6. Runtime location SHALL remain separate.

7. Memory SHALL remain Omnira-governed.

8. Tool access SHALL be explicit.

9. Project scope SHALL be explicit.

10. delegation SHALL be bounded.

11. external Agents SHALL not become trusted automatically.

12. Agent protocols SHALL carry canonical scope.

13. performance MAY inform recommended autonomy.

14. performance SHALL not self-expand authority.

15. Agent migration between Models SHALL preserve identity.

16. Agent migration between Nodes SHALL preserve identity.

17. Agent updates MAY require Mandate revalidation.

18. historical Agent Versions SHALL remain queryable.

19. third-party Agents SHALL require Conformance.

20. Agent intelligence SHALL NOT own governance.

28.932 Canonical Workflow Evolution Contract

The following requirements define future workflow evolution:

1. Workflow identity SHALL remain stable across implementation changes.

2. workflow Versions SHALL be explicit.

3. Plans SHALL remain canonical.

4. state transitions SHALL remain governed.

5. retries SHALL remain bounded.

6. compensation SHALL remain explicit.

7. human Steps SHALL remain truthful.

8. external side effects SHALL remain separately authorised.

9. workflow engines MAY change behind canonical semantics.

10. workflow DSLs MAY compile to canonical Plan structures.

11. reusable templates MAY be shared after conformance.

12. scheduling SHALL revalidate authority.

13. recurring workflows SHALL use Mandates.

14. migration SHALL preserve in-flight state carefully.

15. historical workflow executions SHALL remain reconstructable.

16. workflow packages SHALL declare required Capabilities.

17. workflow marketplaces SHALL not create automatic trust.

18. future automation SHALL preserve Evidence.

19. high-risk workflow changes SHALL require review.

20. Workflow convenience SHALL NOT become authority expansion.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.933 Canonical Autonomy Evolution Contract

The following requirements define future autonomy:

1. Autonomy SHALL expand only through explicit governance.

2. Authority Level SHALL remain domain-specific.

3. Autonomy Envelope SHALL remain explicit.

4. Mandate SHALL remain explicit.

5. Budget SHALL remain bounded.

6. data scope SHALL remain bounded.

7. Provider scope SHALL remain bounded.

8. side effects SHALL remain bounded.

9. expiry SHALL remain explicit.

10. revocation SHALL remain immediate.

11. performance evidence SHOULD precede promotion.

12. Incident history SHALL influence review.

13. user correction rate SHOULD influence review.

14. shadow mode SHOULD precede material new autonomy.

15. canary autonomy MAY precede broad autonomy.

16. automatic narrowing MAY occur under approved policy.

17. automatic broadening SHALL not occur without authority.

18. human stop SHALL remain available.

19. high-risk irreversible actions MAY remain human-gated permanently.

20. Autonomy SHALL NOT become the platform’s default measure of success.

28.934 Canonical Future Architecture Contract

The following requirements govern future evolution:

1. Canonical identities SHALL remain stable where semantics remain the same.

2. Material semantic changes SHALL create new Versions.

3. historical evidence SHALL not be rewritten.

4. new Providers SHALL use Adapters.

5. new protocols SHALL use Connectors or governed resource boundaries.

6. new Agents SHALL use canonical Principal and Agent identity.

7. new Models SHALL use Model Registry.

8. new Tools SHALL use Tool Registry.

9. new local Runtimes SHALL use Node and Runtime contracts.

10. new workflows SHALL use canonical Planning and Execution.

11. new media SHALL use Asset and provenance architecture.

12. new learning SHALL use Memory admission.

13. new autonomy SHALL use Authority and Mandates.

14. new side effects SHALL use explicit authority.

15. new data processing SHALL use Classification and privacy.

16. new economic models SHALL remain Project-attributable.

17. new deployment architectures SHALL preserve Tenant and Project isolation.

18. new implementation technology SHALL remain Conformance-tested.

19. architecture changes SHALL be documented and migrated.

20. Future capability SHALL NOT become a reason to bypass the Fabric.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.935 Rollout, Migration and Evolution Invariants

The following invariants SHALL remain true:

- No migration invents provenance that did not exist.

- No migration broadens authority silently.

- No migration exposes raw Credentials for convenience.

- No imported Asset becomes historically more certain than the evidence allows.

- No deleted or revoked object returns through migration.

- No shadow execution creates hidden consequential side effects.

- No dual run duplicates public or financial actions.

- No canary lacks owner, scope and abort criteria.

- No cutover is complete without verification.

- No rollback rewrites history.

- No deprecated path accepts new production adoption indefinitely.

- No emergency legacy fallback becomes permanent.

- No direct Provider bypass remains hidden after migration completion.

- No future Provider gains special access above canonical policy.

- No future Model receives broader authority automatically.

- No future protocol becomes governance.

- No future Agent framework owns Omnira Agent identity.

- No future local Runtime becomes a privacy exception.

- No future workflow engine replaces canonical execution semantics silently.

- No future evolution bypasses the Intelligence Fabric.

28.936 Canonical Final Doctrine

The Omnira Intelligence Fabric is not a Model router.

It is not an API gateway.

It is not a Provider abstraction library.

It is not a prompt manager.

It is not a queue.

It is not a workflow engine.

It is not an Agent framework.

It is not a vector database.

It is not a local Model Runtime.

It is not a multimodal production suite.

It is not a Credential vault.

It is not an approval service.

It is not an observability platform.

It is not a Memory system.

It is not one Provider.

It is not one protocol.

It is the governed architecture that makes all of those resources usable as parts of one coherent intelligence system.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.937 Canonical Final System Relationship

The canonical relationship is:

The user defines intent and authority.

The Project defines scope and policy.

The Agent interprets and coordinates intent.

The Fabric determines governed implementation.

The Capability Registry defines what may be requested.

The Resource Registries define what exists.

The Planner determines what must happen.

The Policy layer determines what may happen.

The Cost layer determines what it may economically consume.

The Router determines which eligible resources should perform it.

The Approval layer determines whether consequential work may proceed.

The Execution layer coordinates actual work.

The Adapter and Connector layers isolate external and local implementation.

The Asset layer preserves durable results.

The Evaluation layer determines whether results are good enough.

The Evidence layer preserves what actually happened.

The Memory boundary determines what may influence future work.

The Observability layer reveals current behaviour.

The Audit layer preserves accountability.

The Incident layer handles failure and harm.

The Conformance layer ensures implementations match the architecture.

Migration and evolution ensure the architecture survives technological change.

28.938 Canonical Final Project Relationship

For Familje-Stunden:

The Fabric SHALL allow:

- text,

- images,

- Voice,

- future video,

- local intelligence,

- external intelligence,

- human-assisted production,

- and publication

to participate in one governed creative pipeline.

Nova and Pling remain Project-owned character identities.

Their reference Assets remain canonical Project knowledge.

No Provider owns their identity.

No image Model owns their appearance.

No Voice Provider owns their narrative role.

No video Provider owns their future animation workflow.

The Fabric preserves:

- Project scope,

- rights,

- Consent,

- cost,

- provenance,

- Quality,

- and human publication authority.

28.939 Canonical Final The Prompt Relationship

For The Prompt:

The Fabric SHALL coordinate:

- research,

- source retrieval,

- reasoning,

- Script generation,

- visual generation,

- future video,

- publication,

- and performance learning

without allowing one Provider to become the architecture.

Sources remain distinguishable from generated interpretation.

Generated visuals remain distinguishable from documentary evidence.

Publication remains separate from generation.

Provider failures remain recoverable.

Cost remains visible.

Routing may improve over time.

The user retains publication and strategic authority.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.940 Canonical Final GainPilot Relationship

For GainPilot:

The Fabric SHALL allow Arnold to remain one persistent coaching Agent while intelligence resources evolve underneath it.

Arnold may use:

- local Models,

- approved external Models,

- retrieval,

- Tools,

- Project Memory,

- and future specialised fitness intelligence

without changing identity.

Health and training data remain governed by:

- Classification,

- Project scope,

- Local Only policy,

- Consent where applicable,

- and user authority.

The Fabric SHALL prevent:

- cross-Project leakage,

- unsupported programme changes,

- privacy escape through fallback,

- and Provider-specific lock-in.

28.941 Canonical Final Atlas Relationship

For Atlas:

The Fabric becomes the execution substrate through which intelligence is obtained.

Atlas SHALL know:

- what needs to be done,

- why it needs to be done,

- which Project it belongs to,

- what constraints matter,

- what Quality is required,

- and what authority the user has granted.

Atlas SHALL not need to know:

- which API key is used,

- which endpoint receives the request,

- which retry header exists,

- which Provider job state means “running,”

- which local process hosts a Model,

- or how one Provider encodes an Asset.

Atlas remains the orchestrating intelligence.

The Fabric remains the governed implementation layer.

28.942 Canonical Final Omnira Relationship

For Omnira:

The Intelligence Fabric SHALL become the canonical boundary through which intelligence resources are:

- discovered,

- described,

- selected,

- authorised,

- executed,

- evaluated,

- costed,

- evidenced,

- observed,

- and evolved.

It SHALL permit Omnira to change:

- Models,

- Providers,

- local hardware,

- Tool ecosystems,

- Agent frameworks,

- protocols,

- storage,

- queues,

- cloud platforms,

- and multimodal services

without changing the fundamental relationship among:

- user intent,

- Project scope,

- authority,

- data,

- cost,

- Quality,

- and evidence.

28.943 Canonical Final Migration Doctrine

Migration SHALL preserve truth.

Unknown history remains unknown.

Partial provenance remains partial.

Legacy state remains legacy until canonicalised.

Current deletion overrides old backups.

Current revocation overrides old Credentials.

Current Consent overrides historical convenience.

Current policy overrides deprecated defaults.

Current authority governs new execution.

No migration shall claim certainty it cannot prove.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
sectionTitles: 28.946 Final Invariants of the Omnira Intelligence Fabric
text:
28.944 Canonical Final Rollout Doctrine

Rollout SHALL preserve control.

Start narrow.

Observe.

Compare.

Canary.

Verify.

Expand.

Pause when evidence weakens.

Rollback when harm exceeds tolerance.

Retire legacy paths when the Fabric path is proven.

Do not confuse deployment with adoption.

Do not confuse adoption with conformance.

Do not confuse conformance with autonomy.

Do not confuse autonomy with success.

28.945 Canonical Final Evolution Doctrine

Evolution SHALL preserve architecture.

New Models are resources.

New Providers are resources.

New Tools are resources.

New Nodes are resources.

New protocols are integration mechanisms.

New workflow engines are implementations.

New Agent frameworks are implementations.

New multimodal platforms are implementations.

They SHALL all enter through the same governed Fabric concepts.

Technology may change quickly.

Canonical meaning shall change deliberately.

28.946 Final Invariants of the Omnira Intelligence Fabric

The following final invariants SHALL govern the entire book:

- No Intelligence Without Fabric.

- No Capability without canonical identity.

- No resource without Registry identity.

- No Provider without explicit Product and Account context.

- No Model identity conflated with Agent identity.

- No Agent identity owned by a Provider.

- No Connection without scope.

- No Credential exposed to ordinary Agent context.

- No raw Secret in prompt, log, queue, Evidence summary or Memory.

- No external processing without Data Classification.

- No Local Only external egress.

- No Project retrieval before access filtering.

- No Tenant boundary based on convention alone.

- No Routing before eligibility.

- No cheapness above security, privacy, rights, authority or Quality.

- No Premium route above Budget.

- No Pinned route with silent fallback.

- No Private route with silent public egress.

- No paid Attempt without bounded economic authority.

- No retry without state and idempotency analysis.

- No unknown external outcome converted into false certainty.

- No Provider acceptance treated as Completion.

- No cancellation request treated as confirmed cancellation.

- No queue delivery treated as exactly once.

- No callback trusted without verification.

- No MCP discovery treated as permission.

- No external Tool description treated as policy.

- No human-assisted work represented as automation.

- No temporary Provider result treated as durable Asset.

- No Asset without provenance.

- No accepted Output without applicable Quality evaluation.

- No publication from generation authority alone.

- No publication without exact target and authority.

- No deletion from ordinary write authority.

- No Memory admission from raw execution dump.

- No Derived Learning without evidence and scope.

- No learning that silently expands authority.

- No autonomy without Mandate.

- No Mandate without limits, expiry and revocation.

- No Agent self-authorisation.

- No high-risk action without current authority.

- No stale approval at execution boundary.

- No observability claim without fresh evidence.

- No audit without actor and authority.

- No Incident closure without recovery verification.

- No conformance claim without executable evidence.

- No Certification without exact Version and scope.

- No migration that fabricates historical certainty.

- No legacy bypass that becomes permanent architecture.

- No future technology that bypasses canonical governance.

title: Omnira Intelligence Fabric
chapterTitle: Rollout, Migration, Anti-Patterns and Future Evolution
text:
28.947 Final Architecture Promise

The Omnira Intelligence Fabric promises that intelligence may improve without requiring Omnira to surrender control.

Models may become more capable.

Providers may become cheaper.

Local hardware may become stronger.

Agents may become more autonomous.

Multimodal systems may become dramatically better.

Protocols may change.

Tools may multiply.

New platforms may appear.

Old platforms may disappear.

The Fabric SHALL absorb those changes through stable governed contracts.

The user shall not need to rebuild Atlas because a Provider changes.

The Project shall not need to lose its history because a Model changes.

An Agent shall not lose its identity because execution moves from cloud to local hardware.

A workflow shall not lose its authority boundaries because automation improves.

An Asset shall not lose its provenance because it moves between storage systems.

A Memory Item shall not become universal truth because one Provider produced it.

A cheaper route shall not weaken privacy.

A faster route shall not weaken Quality.

A stronger Agent shall not receive unlimited authority.

A future protocol shall not erase governance.

28.948 Final Closing Statement

Omnira is intended to operate intelligence, not merely consume Models.

That requires a layer capable of separating intent from implementation.

The Intelligence Fabric is that layer.

The user asks for an outcome.

Atlas or another Agent interprets the need.

The Capability Request expresses the need canonically.

The Project provides scope.

Policy determines what is allowed.

The Planner creates the work.

The Cost Engine determines economic boundaries.

The Router selects eligible intelligence.

The Approval system preserves human authority.

The Execution system makes the work durable.

The Adapter layer isolates Provider change.

The Connector layer binds Accounts and Credentials safely.

The Local Runtime layer gives private compute equal architectural status.

The Tool and MCP layers extend what intelligence can do without creating automatic trust.

The Asset system preserves generated and transformed results.

The Quality system determines whether those results are acceptable.

The Provenance system preserves how they were produced.

The Evidence system preserves what actually happened.

The Memory boundary determines what should matter later.

The Observability system reveals system behaviour.

The Audit system preserves accountable history.

The Incident system contains failure and harm.

The Conformance system ensures implementation matches architecture.

The migration system ensures Omnira can reach that future without destroying the present.

The evolution model ensures that the architecture can survive technologies that do not exist yet.

For Stage 1, the goal is intentionally narrower:

Build the first trustworthy path.

Route one Capability through several eligible resources.

Use local intelligence where appropriate.

Use external intelligence where appropriate.

Know what it costs.

Know where the data goes.

Know which Account is used.

Know which Model or Tool acted.

Know whether the result is good enough.

Know whether a human approved the consequence.

Know whether the action actually completed.

Know what evidence exists.

Know how to recover when it fails.

Then expand.

No intelligence path should become more powerful than the governance surrounding it.

No Agent should become more autonomous than the authority granted to it.

No Provider should become more important than the Capability it serves.

No implementation should become more authoritative than the architecture it implements.

The user retains intent.

The user retains authority.

The Project retains scope.

The Agent retains identity.

Omnira retains governance.

The Intelligence Fabric retains implementation independence.

This is the canonical architecture of the Omnira Intelligence Fabric.

No Intelligence Without Fabric.

title: Omnira Intelligence Graph
text:
1.1 Produktvision

Detta kapitel bygger på Product Vision v1.0. Det definierar vad Intelligence Graph är, vilka upplevelser den ska ge, produktens tre huvudlägen, det visuella grundkonceptet, hierarkin, projektmodellen och de tio designprinciper som resten av boken vilar på.

Omnira Intelligence Graph ska vara det visuella nervsystemet för hela Omnira. När grafen öppnas ska användaren direkt känna: hela mitt AI-operativsystem lever, och jag förstår vad det gör.

Grafen ska förena tre saker som normalt är separata: systemarkitektur, operativ övervakning och visuell intelligens. Den ska kunna visa både hur Omnira är uppbyggt och vad Atlas, Manager, agents och workflows faktiskt gör i realtid.

Den får vara visuellt imponerande, men aldrig på bekostnad av korrekt data, läsbarhet, prestanda, felsökning, tillgänglighet eller projektisolering.

Grafen är inte en dekorativ visualisering. Den är ett operativt gränssnitt för att förstå, övervaka och styra Omnira.

1.2 Den centrala upplevelsen

Intelligence Graph ska ge användaren fem tydliga upplevelser.

Systemet känns levande

Omnira ska upplevas som ett aktivt, intelligent system snarare än en samling statiska tabeller och dashboards. Det åstadkoms genom lågmäld andning i centrala noder, verkliga runtime-signaler, kontrollerad edge-aktivitet, mjuka tillståndsövergångar, nya noder som växer fram från sin parent samt tydlig respons när Atlas delegerar eller ett workflow aktiveras. Den levande känslan ska vara kontrollerad — en stabil graf får aldrig se stressad ut utan anledning.

Användaren ser vad som händer nu

Live Operations ska snabbt besvara: Vad körs? Vem arbetar? Vad väntar? Vad har misslyckats? Vad behöver mitt godkännande? Vad har precis slutförts? Vilken execution eller agent orsakar en flaskhals? Användaren ska inte behöva tolka en massa rörliga prickar för att förstå läget.

Atlas känns som en verklig central intelligens

Atlas ska vara den största och mest visuellt unika noden — inte bara en ikon med ett namn. Noden ska kännas som en aktiv intelligens som observerar projekten, resonerar, delegerar, tar emot signaler, kommunicerar med Manager och följer pågående operationer. Atlas ska kunna vara lugn och levande utan att fejka pågående arbete. När Atlas faktiskt arbetar ska dess visuella tillstånd förändras utifrån verkliga events.

Problem ska synas omedelbart

Failures, timed-out executions och väntande approvals ska bryta igenom den normala visuella hierarkin. Atlas är störst, men ett kritiskt fel ska ändå kunna dra blicken först — genom varningsfärg, statusring, puls, kontrast, tydlig label och aktivitet i berörd path.

En större nod är strukturellt viktigare. En starkare signal är operativt viktigare. De två systemen får inte blandas ihop.

Grafen ska kunna imponera utan att förlora trovärdighet

Grafen ska ha visuell wow-känsla och kunna demonstrera Omniras kapacitet. Men den får aldrig animera falsk aktivitet, påstå att ett workflow körs när det inte gör det, använda slumpmässiga partiklar som ser ut som runtime-events, visa relationer som inte finns, blanda projektdata eller låta en gammal historisk execution se live ut. Det ska alltid gå att förstå skillnaden mellan visuell presentation, aktuell aktivitet, historisk data och simulerad replay.

title: Omnira Intelligence Graph
text:
1.3 Produktens tre huvudlägen

Intelligence Graph ska inte vara en enda graf med tre filter. De tre lägena ska vara olika visuella produkter som delar samma designspråk.

System Map
